   1: # Governance — project structure as security primitive
   2: 
   3: Status: living document. Companion to
   4: [`PRINCIPLES.md`](./PRINCIPLES.md),
   5: [`SOVEREIGNTY.md`](./SOVEREIGNTY.md), and
   6: [`SECURITY.md`](./SECURITY.md).
   7: 
   8: Last updated: 2026-05-08.
   9: 
  10: > Engineering alone doesn't keep a project free of corporations;
  11: > structure does. A perfectly-engineered codebase still falls if
  12: > the entity holding the trademark accepts an acquisition, the
  13: > maintainer accepts a NSL gag order alone, or the license permits
  14: > a closed-source corporate fork.
  15: 
  16: This document is the project-structure complement to the engineering
  17: controls in `SOVEREIGNTY.md`. It specifies the legal, procedural,
  18: and ceremonial commitments that prevent corporate capture by
  19: structure rather than by code.
  20: 
  21: ---
  22: 
  23: ## License — AGPLv3
  24: 
  25: **License:** GNU Affero General Public License v3 or later.
  26: 
  27: **Why AGPL specifically (not MIT, not Apache, not GPL):**
  28: 
  29: - **MIT / Apache permit closed forks.** A corporation can take
  30:   the One Link codebase, add proprietary surveillance, ship as a
  31:   closed-source competitor. We refuse to make that legal.
  32: - **GPL covers binary distribution.** Modern services run as
  33:   hosted SaaS without distributing the binary; GPL leaves a
  34:   loophole.
  35: - **AGPL closes the SaaS loophole.** Anyone who modifies One Link
  36:   and offers it as a network service must publish their modified
  37:   source.
  38: 
  39: The trade-off: AGPL deters some corporate adoption (which is
  40: fine; we're not optimizing for corporate adoption). It strongly
  41: encourages forks to publish their source, which is what "for the
  42: people" requires.
  43: 
  44: **Implementation:**
  45: - `LICENSE` file at repo root contains the AGPL-3.0-or-later text.
  46: - Every source file carries a header:
  47:   ```
  48:   // SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
  49:   // Copyright (c) <year> <Trademark Holder> and contributors.
  50:   ```
  51: - No CLA (Contributor License Agreement) that transfers ownership.
  52:   Contributors retain copyright on their contributions; the
  53:   cumulative work is collectively licensed AGPL.
  54: 
  55: ---
  56: 
  57: ## Trademark holding — non-profit only
  58: 
  59: **Holder:** a non-profit organization (501(c)(3) in the US, or
  60: equivalent in another jurisdiction). Specifically NOT an
  61: individual maintainer, NOT a company, NOT a foundation that
  62: takes corporate sponsorship with influence.
  63: 
  64: **Why non-profit:**
  65: - An individual can be coerced, bought, or compromised. A
  66:   non-profit has board oversight and statutory restrictions.
  67: - A for-profit company can be acquired. A 501(c)(3) cannot be
  68:   acquired in the conventional sense; its assets must transfer
  69:   to another non-profit on dissolution.
  70: - A non-profit's books are public (Form 990 filings).
  71: 
  72: **Until the non-profit exists** (we're pre-incorporation as of
  73: 2026-05-08): the trademark is held by the founding maintainer
  74: under a published trust deed that obligates transfer to the
  75: non-profit upon incorporation.
  76: 
  77: **Use rules** (binding on the holder):
  78: 1. The "One Link" mark may be used only for software adhering to
  79:    `PRINCIPLES.md` and this `GOVERNANCE.md`.
  80: 2. Forks that violate the principles must not use the name "One
  81:    Link."
  82: 3. The mark may not be sold, licensed for-fee, or transferred to
  83:    a for-profit entity. Transfer to another non-profit with
  84:    identical principles is permitted upon dissolution.
  85: 
  86: ---
  87: 
  88: ## Release signing — multi-maintainer threshold
  89: 
  90: **Scheme:** Ed25519 signatures. Releases require **≥2-of-N**
  91: maintainer signatures to be valid. N starts at 3 (founding
  92: maintainers). Quorum can grow as the project grows; a single
  93: maintainer signing alone is never sufficient.
  94: 
  95: **Why threshold:**
  96: - Single-maintainer signing means a single key compromise =
  97:   malicious release. Threshold means an attacker needs to
  98:   compromise 2 simultaneously.
  99: - A maintainer under coercion (NSL, blackmail, etc.) cannot ship
 100:   a backdoored release alone. The other maintainers serve as
 101:   attestation that the release wasn't compelled.
 102: 
 103: **Key custody:**
 104: - Each maintainer's release-signing key lives on a hardware
 105:   security module (YubiKey 5C / similar) that the maintainer
 106:   physically possesses.
 107: - Air-gapped key generation. Public keys published in source
 108:   (`docs/maintainer_keys.md`).
 109: - Rotation: every 2 years, or on suspected compromise. Rotation
 110:   ceremony requires the existing quorum to sign the new keys.
 111: 
 112: **Service Worker enforcement:**
 113: - The SW (per `SECURITY.md`) verifies every update against the
 114:   pinned multi-key threshold. A release signed by 1-of-N is
 115:   rejected. A release signed by ≥2-of-N proceeds.
 116: 
 117: ---
 118: 
 119: ## Refuse-acquisition charter
 120: 
 121: **Binding text** (incorporated into the non-profit's charter once
 122: established; binding-by-published-policy until then):
 123: 
 124: > The One Link project, the entity holding its trademark, and
 125: > the keys signing its releases SHALL NOT be sold, transferred,
 126: > or operationally controlled by any for-profit entity. Offers
 127: > of acquisition shall be declined publicly. The signing keys
 128: > shall not be transferred outside the maintainer pool. The
 129: > trademark shall not be licensed to a for-profit entity. This
 130: > charter may be amended only by unanimous vote of all current
 131: > maintainers AND a public 90-day comment period.
 132: 
 133: **Practical effect:** even if a corporation offers $1B for One
 134: Link, the answer is "no" by binding charter. Maintainers who
 135: would accept the offer can leave the project (free to fork under
 136: AGPL); they cannot take the trademark, the canonical signing
 137: keys, or the canonical release pipeline with them.
 138: 
 139: ---
 140: 
 141: ## Funding posture
 142: 
 143: **What we accept:**
 144: - Individual donations (small, recurring, anonymous if desired).
 145: - Crowdfunding (Open Collective, Liberapay, similar).
 146: - Grants from non-profit foundations (with no influence clauses).
 147: 
 148: **What we refuse:**
 149: - Corporate sponsorship with seat-at-the-table influence.
 150: - Sponsorship that requires logo placement in the app
 151:   (advertising-by-stealth).
 152: - Investment of any kind. We're not a startup.
 153: - Any funding that requires us to deviate from
 154:   `PRINCIPLES.md`.
 155: 
 156: **Sustainability model:** the project costs are tiny by design (a
 157: $5/mo VPS for the canonical rendezvous; domain registration; CI
 158: minutes). Annual budget target: under $5,000. Funded entirely by
 159: small donations from users.
 160: 
 161: If we ever need substantially more (paid maintainers, security
 162: audits), the path is:
 163: 1. Public budget proposal.
 164: 2. Public funding round (donation drive).
 165: 3. If raised, books published quarterly.
 166: 4. If not raised, scope adjusts to fit available funds.
 167: 
 168: We never accept money to ship a feature corporate sponsors want.
 169: 
 170: ---
 171: 
 172: ## Maintainer covenant
 173: 
 174: Every maintainer signs a published covenant (as a Git-committed
 175: text file with a maintainer's signature) before being added to
 176: the threshold quorum. The covenant binds:
 177: 
 178: 1. Custody of one's signing key on personal HSM.
 179: 2. Refusal to sign any release the maintainer hasn't reviewed.
 180: 3. Refusal to sign under coercion (NSL, gag order, etc.); the
 181:    correct response is to recuse and notify other maintainers,
 182:    who then collectively decide whether to halt the release
 183:    pipeline temporarily.
 184: 4. Public disclosure of any conflict of interest (employment by
 185:    relevant corporations, ownership of relevant equity, etc.).
 186: 5. Two-week notice on resignation, with secure handoff of public
 187:    responsibilities.
 188: 
 189: A maintainer who breaches the covenant is removed from the
 190: quorum by the remaining maintainers. Their signing key is
 191: revoked; outstanding releases re-signed.
 192: 
 193: ---
 194: 
 195: ## Warrant canary
 196: 
 197: **The mechanism:**
 198: 
 199: A canary statement is published at a known canonical URL
 200: (`/canary.txt` on the project's primary domain, plus mirrored
 201: elsewhere) and updated on a fixed cadence (monthly, on the 1st).
 202: The statement reads, in part:
 203: 
 204: ```
 205: One Link Warrant Canary — <month> <year>
 206: 
 207: As of <date>, the One Link project maintainers have NOT received:
 208:   - Any National Security Letter, FISA order, or equivalent
 209:     in any jurisdiction
 210:   - Any compelled-access request requiring secrecy
 211:   - Any subpoena targeting user data we do not hold (see note 1)
 212:   - Any takedown order against the canonical release pipeline
 213: 
 214: Note 1: One Link by design does not hold user message content,
 215: contact graphs, or any per-user identifying information beyond
 216: what's in the public release commit log. We have no user data to
 217: disclose.
 218: 
 219: Signed by ≥2-of-N maintainers, the keys for which are pinned in
 220: docs/maintainer_keys.md.
 221: 
 222:   -- Maintainer A: <signature>
 223:   -- Maintainer B: <signature>
 224: ```
 225: 
 226: **The signal:**
 227: - A **fresh canary** signed monthly = no compelled access has been
 228:   received.
 229: - A **stale canary** (more than ~6 weeks old) = something happened.
 230:   We deliberately don't lie ("we received nothing" when we did);
 231:   we just stop signing.
 232: - The absence is the message. Users monitoring the canary URL
 233:   see staleness automatically.
 234: 
 235: **Limitations (named honestly):**
 236: - Some legal regimes can compel a fake canary. We mitigate by
 237:   threshold-signing: it's harder to compel ≥2 of N maintainers in
 238:   different jurisdictions to lie.
 239: - We commit to maintainers across multiple jurisdictions to avoid
 240:   single-jurisdiction compulsion risk.
 241: 
 242: ---
 243: 
 244: ## Maintainer geographic distribution
 245: 
 246: The threshold quorum is designed to be **multi-jurisdictional**.
 247: At least 2 of the N maintainers must reside in different
 248: jurisdictions. This makes a single-government compulsion order
 249: insufficient to forge a release or fake the canary.
 250: 
 251: This is documented in `docs/maintainer_keys.md` as
 252: non-identifying jurisdiction tags (e.g., "EU - non-Schengen,"
 253: "North America - non-US," "South America"). Specific identities
 254: are public; specific addresses are not.
 255: 
 256: ---
 257: 
 258: ## Code of conduct + community governance
 259: 
 260: The community follows the Contributor Covenant 2.1 (industry
 261: standard, well-tested) with one addition: the principles in
 262: `PRINCIPLES.md` are non-negotiable. Contributors who advocate for
 263: violating them (e.g., proposing telemetry "for the user's own
 264: good") are not breaching the CoC, but their proposals will not
 265: merge.
 266: 
 267: Decisions on disputed merges go through:
 268: 1. Public PR discussion (default).
 269: 2. Maintainer rough-consensus.
 270: 3. If unresolved: full maintainer vote with quorum.
 271: 4. Major architectural changes: 30-day public RFC + comment period.
 272: 
 273: ---
 274: 
 275: ## Project amnesty / sunset clause
 276: 
 277: If the project becomes structurally compromised (e.g.,
 278: maintainer quorum compromised; canary chain broken; codebase
 279: shipped a backdoor in a release that 2-of-N signed maliciously),
 280: the project's structural commitment is to:
 281: 
 282: 1. **Publicly disclose the compromise** within 7 days of
 283:    discovery, with full forensic detail.
 284: 2. **Revoke the canonical signing keys**. No further releases
 285:    from the compromised pipeline.
 286: 3. **Recommend users uninstall** until a clean fork is
 287:    established under new keys + new maintainer quorum.
 288: 4. **Publish post-mortem** with root-cause analysis and
 289:    structural changes.
 290: 5. **Sunset the trademark** rather than transfer it to a
 291:    compromised entity. The mark goes dormant; a clean
 292:    community fork can adopt a new name.
 293: 
 294: The reputational cost is real and unrecoverable. That's the
 295: point: the cost prevents shortcuts.
 296: 
 297: ---
 298: 
 299: ## Audit cadence
 300: 
 301: Per `PRINCIPLES.md`, every quarter:
 302: 
 303: 1. **Verify the canary chain.** Each signed canary cross-checks
 304:    against the prior month's; gaps trigger investigation.
 305: 2. **Audit financial books.** Public; reviewed by an independent
 306:    non-profit auditor annually.
 307: 3. **Re-verify maintainer covenants.** Each maintainer re-signs
 308:    the covenant annually, with an opportunity to declare new
 309:    conflicts of interest.
 310: 4. **Threshold key health check.** Each signing key still
 311:    accessible to its maintainer; each HSM still functional.
 312: 5. **Re-publish the warrant canary** (per the monthly cadence).
 313: 
 314: A governance document that doesn't get audited becomes
 315: decoration. The audit cadence is the difference between a
 316: charter and a charter that holds.
 317: 
 318: ---
 319: 
 320: ## What this collectively prevents
 321: 
 322: | Capture vector | Prevention |
 323: |---|---|
 324: | Maintainer accepts acquisition | Refuse-acquisition charter |
 325: | Maintainer is bought / blackmailed | Threshold-quorum signing (single key insufficient) |
 326: | Maintainer is compelled to ship backdoor (NSL etc.) | Multi-jurisdictional quorum + warrant canary |
 327: | For-profit fork goes proprietary | AGPLv3 license blocks closed-source distribution |
 328: | Trademark sold | Non-profit holding + use-rule restriction |
 329: | CDN compromised | Pinned release key + signed updates |
 330: | CA compromised | Pinned release key (HTTPS not the trust root) |
 331: | OS keychain compelled disclosure | OPFS-stored identity, not OS keychain |
 332: | Single maintainer compromised | Threshold quorum |
 333: | All maintainers compromised | Project amnesty / sunset clause; community fork |
 334: 
 335: This is what governance buys that engineering cannot.

  71: 
  72: ## Part 1 — The Vision
  73: 
  74: ### What we are building
  75: 
  76: Living Presence is a **continuous, variable-intensity channel between
  77: trusted people**, expressed through whatever surfaces are appropriate
  78: at any given moment.
  79: 
  80: - At low intensity: ambient awareness. Mom is at home; her presence
  81:   is faintly felt without any active session.
  82: - At medium intensity: passive contact. A photo arrives, a thought
  83:   is shared, a voice note plays through a speaker as she walks past.
  84: - At high intensity: full conversation. Face, voice, gaze, gesture,
  85:   through whichever surfaces are present.
  86: - At decay: the conversation goes back to ambient, leaves an async
  87:   trace if conditions require, resumes when both parties return.
  88: 
  89: The user experiences this as: **one button labelled "Call Mom",
  90: which always works.**
  91: 
  92: The button does not pick a codec. It does not pick a device. It does
  93: not show an error. It does not buffer. It does not ring busy. It
  94: does not say "reconnecting." If conditions are bad, the call gently
  95: changes form. If both parties are not present, it leaves a capsule.
  96: If conditions recover, it resumes.
  97: 
  98: This is the only surface.
  99: 
 100: ### Why this is different from every call product
 101: 
 102: | Product | Breaks which law |
 103: |---|---|
 104: | Zoom / Teams / Meet / WebEx | *Just works* (error toasts, quality bars, "reconnecting..." overlays, cloud-SFU dependency) |
 105: | FaceTime | *We are one* (per-device opt-in via Continuity, walled garden, cloud-relay) |
 106: | Signal / WhatsApp / Telegram | *For the people* (works for the tech-comfortable; grandma on a flaky network gets dropped calls) |
 107: | Discord | *We are one* (separate identity per device, no organic body) |
 108: | Push-to-talk (Voxer / Zello) | *For the people* (async-only is a different product, not a fallback) |
 109: 
 110: The composition we are designing — **all three laws holding
 111: simultaneously, on a sovereign P2P substrate, with cryptographic
 112: frame-level provenance, across an arbitrary intensity dial** — has
 113: no shipping counterpart.
 114: 
 115: ### Why now
 116: 
 117: The substrate to build on is shipped:
 118: 
 119: - One Link v0.21.0-alpha: 39 native crates, hybrid WebRTC + QUIC
 120:   transport, post-quantum identity, hardware attestation, onion
 121:   routing, macaroon capabilities, CRDT state, linked-mesh.
 122: - OneField: voice.cl (1616 LOC) and video.cl (1107 LOC) define the
 123:   math, wire format, predicates, and tests for the alien-tier
 124:   semantic channel.
 125: - Coherence Lang: the compiler, the four numerical rails, the
 126:   property fuzzer at 850M trials/sec, the native CUDA path.
 127: - ACE: the relational memory substrate that conversations can
 128:   optionally live inside.
 129: 
 130: No other team has all of these. The substrate alone is years of
 131: work. The application that exercises all of it is the wedge.
 132: 
 133: ---
 134: 
 135: ## Part 2 — The Doctrine of Invisibility
 136: 
 137: The single most leverage-y artifact in the project. Every PR is
 138: reviewed against it. Adding to this list is engineering work that
 139: must be paid for somewhere else (in the engines) to remove a surface
 140: from the user.
 141: 
 142: ### What we refuse to ship
 143: 
 144: - **No advanced settings.** Anywhere. There is no "advanced" tier.
 145:   Every option is a doctrine failure to be paid down.
 146: - **No codec picker.** The Compiler chooses. The user never knows
 147:   the word "codec."
 148: - **No device picker mid-call.** The Body Engine moves between
 149:   surfaces. The user does not pick "use my phone's mic."
 150: - **No relay picker.** The Route Brain chooses. No "use TURN"
 151:   toggle.
 152: - **No "your connection is unstable" toast.** Replace with: the
 153:   Compiler descends a rung; the picture softens; nothing pops up.
 154: - **No "reconnecting..." overlay.** Replace with: the Immune System
 155:   prewarms a backup route invisibly. If the call drops, the Compiler
 156:   goes to async capsule with no UI event.
 157: - **No quality bars.** No bitrate readout. No latency display.
 158: - **No error codes.** Ever. Including for engineers — the daemon
 159:   logs codes locally but the UI never surfaces them.
 160: - **No "call failed."** Calls do not fail. They convert to async.
 161: - **No busy signal.** Replace with: capsule offer.
 162: - **No "user not registered."** Replace with: invite flow that
 163:   gives the recipient an invitation across whatever side channels
 164:   exist (SMS, email, QR, NFC).
 165: - **No "verify your phone number."** Replace with: QR pairing
 166:   (`ol_pair_qr`, Row 2).
 167: - **No CAPTCHA.** Ever. The substrate uses macaroon capabilities
 168:   and rate-limiting at the protocol layer.
 169: - **No "click to allow microphone access."** Ask once at install,
 170:   in plain language, with rationale.
 171: - **No "this app needs an update to call."** Updates are
 172:   background, signed, gated by the Service Worker pubkey pinning
 173:   (C2 fix).
 174: - **No analytics consent banner.** We do not collect telemetry
 175:   about users. We collect *call vitals* locally for the Immune
 176:   System to learn from; they never leave the device.
 177: - **No "subscribe for HD."** Quality is determined by network and
 178:   engines, not by tier.
 179: - **No paywall.** Calls are free for the people. Federated relay
 180:   funds itself; see Part 13.
 181: - **No "your call is being recorded for quality."** No silent
 182:   recording. Ever.
 183: - **No "missed call" badge with a number.** Replace with: the
 184:   capsule itself in the chat surface. There are no "missed
 185:   events"; there are only conversation states.
 186: 
 187: ### What the engines must produce instead
 188: 
 189: - **State-of-network must be sensed, not surfaced.** The Immune
 190:   System reads `_pair_health`, fragility scores, relay EWMA. It
 191:   acts. It does not tell the user.
 192: - **Transitions must be smooth.** Frame-level crossfade (200ms)
 193:   between device handoff. Codec changes happen at I-frame boundaries
 194:   with no visible artifact.
 195: - **Failures must convert.** Every failure mode the Compiler is
 196:   aware of maps to a rung on the ladder. The lowest rung is
 197:   async-capsule, which is always achievable (it requires only the
 198:   existing courier-bundle infrastructure to deliver).
 199: - **Trust must be visible without being noisy.** A single calm
 200:   provenance dot on the call surface. Tap to reveal: who, what,
 201:   where, how, recording state. Never a popup, never a banner.
 202: - **Identity must be felt, not entered.** First-call SAS
 203:   verification reuses the `ol_pair_qr` 5-word SAS — visible briefly
 204:   ("you and Alex share: amber river canyon meadow stone"), tap to
 205:   confirm, never appears again unless keys rotate.
 206: 
 207: ### The review rule
 208: 
 209: Every PR introducing user-visible string, setting, toggle, banner,
 210: or status indicator must reference this section in the description
 211: with a justification *for* the surface being a doctrine exception.
 212: Default answer is no.
 213: 
 214: ---
 215: 
 216: ## Part 3 — Architecture Overview
 217: 
 218: ### The mental model
 219: 
 220: ```
 221:                     ┌──────────────────────────┐
 222:                     │      ONE BUTTON          │
 223:                     │      "Call Mom"          │
 224:                     └───────────┬──────────────┘
 225:                                 │
 226:                 ┌───────────────▼───────────────┐
 227:                 │     INTENSITY DIAL (Part 5)   │
 228:                 │   {ambient · low · med · high}│
 229:                 │   CRDT-backed shared state    │
 230:                 └───────────────┬───────────────┘
 231:                                 │
 232:         ┌───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐
 233:         │           NINE HIDDEN ENGINES (Part 4)        │
 234:         │                                               │
 235:         │  Immune ──> Compiler ──> Body ──> Route       │
 236:         │     │           │           │        │        │
 237:         │     └───────────┴───────────┴────────┘        │
 238:         │                  │                            │
 239:         │  Reality ──> Priority ──> Predictive          │
 240:         │                  │                            │
 241:         │            Semantic ──> OneField R&D          │
 242:         └───────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
 243:                                 │
 244:         ┌───────────────────────▼───────────────────────┐
 245:         │            EXISTING SUBSTRATE (Part 9)        │
 246:         │  WebRTC | QUIC | TCP | onion | linked-mesh    │
 247:         │  PQ identity | macaroons | confidential       │
 248:         │  duress | CRDT | ChunkRatchet | hwkey         │
 249:         │  39 native Rust crates                        │
 250:         └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 251: ```
 252: 
 253: ### How a call flows (high-level)
 254: 
 255: 1. User taps "Call Mom" on any device they own.
 256: 2. The Body Engine writes to the shared `CallSession` CRDT: "user
 257:    intends to reach `mom_master_vk` at intensity HIGH."
 258: 3. The Compiler picks the highest viable rung based on negotiated
 259:    capability intersection + last-known network conditions.
 260: 4. The Route Brain prewarms one or more paths.
 261: 5. The signaling layer emits CALL_INVITE messages to all of Mom's
 262:    active devices.
 263: 6. Mom's Body Engine listens on all devices. The device most likely
 264:    to be where Mom is (based on prior LWW state) renders the ring
 265:    first; others fan out after 3 seconds.
 266: 7. Mom accepts on whichever surface she's at. The CRDT updates;
 267:    other devices stop ringing.
 268: 8. Media negotiation completes. The Immune System starts its tick
 269:    loop. The Reality Engine signs every frame from the moment
 270:    capture begins.
 271: 9. The call runs at whatever rung is sustainable. The Compiler
 272:    moves up or down as conditions change. Every transition is
 273:    crossfaded.
 274: 10. End conditions: user-initiated hangup, mutual hangup, or
 275:     Immune-System-converted-to-async. All three are graceful.
 276: 11. If async: the in-flight buffer becomes a voice note + chat
 277:     record; live-resumable flag set for 10 minutes.
 278: 12. If conditions recover within the window: resume offer appears.
 279: 
 280: The user sees: the button → a face → a face for as long as
 281: conditions allow → either a clean hangup or a calm capsule offer.
 282: 
 283: ### Layered architecture diagram
 284: 
 285: ```
 286: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 287: │                       PRESENTATION LAYER                        │
 288: │         "Call Mom" button + face surface + capsule offer        │
 289: │        (web/index.html + desktop wrapper + mobile shell)        │
 290: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 291:                                   │
 292: ┌─────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
 293: │                       CALL STATE LAYER                          │
 294: │              CallSession (CRDT) — Part 5                        │
 295: │   intensity | participants | active_surfaces | health | trust   │
 296: └─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
 297:                                   │
 298: ┌─────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
 299: │                       ENGINE LAYER                              │
 300: │    9 controllers reading CallSession, writing requests          │
 301: │    Immune | Compiler | Body | Route | Reality | Priority |      │
 302: │    Predictive | Semantic | OneField                             │
 303: └─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
 304:                                   │
 305: ┌─────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
 306: │                       MEDIA LAYER                               │
 307: │   RTP/SRTP audio/video tracks | semantic-delta channel          │
 308: │   jitter buffer | AEC | AGC | crossfade | frame provenance      │
 309: └─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
 310:                                   │
 311: ┌─────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────┐
 312: │                       TRANSPORT LAYER (EXISTING)                │
 313: │      WebRTC DTLS-SRTP | QUIC | TCP peer | onion | mesh radio    │
 314: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 315: ```
 316: 
 317: ### Engine responsibility map
 318: 
 319: | Engine | Reads | Writes | Tick rate |
 320: |---|---|---|---|
 321: | Immune | CallSession, _pair_health, _relay_metrics, homology, attestation | ImmuneDecision events | 100 ms |
 322: | Compiler | CallSession, ImmuneDecision, capability intersection | Rung change requests | Event-driven |
 323: | Body | CallSession, device states (linked-mesh), ISAC presence | Surface role updates (CRDT writes) | 500 ms |
 324: | Route | _relay_metrics, ol_routing scores, fragility | Path prewarm + switch | 200 ms |
 325: | Reality | Every emitted media frame | FrameProvenance tag | Per-frame |
 326: | Priority | Compiler rung, available bandwidth | QoS class per stream | On rung change |
 327: | Predictive | Received frames, model confidence | Locally-rendered ahead frames | Per-frame |
 328: | Semantic | Negotiated caps, model-pack hash | Encoded delta stream | Per-frame |
 329: | OneField R&D | Experimental cap flag | PINN waveform spec | Per-symbol |
 330: 
 331: ---
 332: 
 333: ## Part 4 — The Nine Engines
 334: 
 335: Each engine specified below has: purpose, data structures, state
 336: machine, integration points (what it reads, what it writes), graduation
 337: mode at launch, thresholds, soak-test pattern.
 338: 
 339: ---
 340: 
 341: ### 4.1 Call Immune System
 342: 
 343: **Purpose:** Watches the call's vital signs. Requests representation
 344: changes when the user is being or about to be harmed.
 345: 
 346: **Architectural firewall:** Never touches media directly. Emits
 347: *requests* to downstream engines (Compiler, Route, Body) each of which
 348: has refusal authority.
 349: 
 350: #### Data structures
 351: 
 352: ```python
 353: # src/one_link/call_immune.py — NEW MODULE
 354: 
 355: from dataclasses import dataclass
 356: from enum import Enum
 357: from typing import Optional
 358: 
 359: class PathClass(Enum):
 360:     LOCAL  = 0     # same device (multi-device body internal)
 361:     LAN    = 1     # local network
 362:     DIRECT = 2     # P2P direct via WAN
 363:     RELAY  = 3     # via federated relay
 364:     ONION  = 4     # via onion circuit
 365:     MESH   = 5     # OneField radio mesh (future)
 366: 
 367: class DeviceRole(Enum):
 368:     MIC      = 0
 369:     CAM      = 1
 370:     DISPLAY  = 2
 371:     SPEAKER  = 3
 372:     RELAY    = 4
 373:     HELPER   = 5
 374:     INACTIVE = 6
 375: 
 376: class ThermalState(Enum):
 377:     NOMINAL  = 0
 378:     WARM     = 1
 379:     HOT      = 2
 380:     CRITICAL = 3
 381: 
 382: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 383: class CapabilitySnapshot:
 384:     semantic_media_v1: bool
 385:     predictive_continuity_v1: bool
 386:     onefield_radio_v1: bool
 387:     confidential_tier: int      # 0 = software, 1 = TPM, 2 = SGX/SEV, 3 = SE
 388:     model_pack_hash: Optional[str]
 389: 
 390: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 391: class CallVitals:
 392:     """Snapshot of all health signals at a single 100ms tick.
 393:        Pure read; no I/O. Composes from existing daemon state.
 394:        Hashable for soak-replay determinism."""
 395:     call_id: str
 396:     peer_fp: str
 397:     tick: int                          # monotonic, 100ms per
 398: 
 399:     # Transport health (from _PairHealth + _relay_metrics)
 400:     rtt_ewma_ms: float
 401:     loss_rate_ewma: float              # 0.0..1.0
 402:     jitter_ms: float                   # frame-arrival std-dev
 403:     bandwidth_estimate_kbps: float
 404: 
 405:     # Path topology (from ol_routing + ol_homology)
 406:     path_class: PathClass
 407:     path_fragility_score: float        # 0=robust 1=critical
 408:     backup_routes_warm: int
 409: 
 410:     # Device state (from linked-mesh)
 411:     own_device_role: DeviceRole
 412:     own_battery_pct: Optional[float]
 413:     own_thermal_state: ThermalState
 414:     peer_device_present: bool
 415: 
 416:     # Media health (from in-call instrumentation)
 417:     audio_frames_received: int
 418:     audio_frames_dropped: int
 419:     video_frames_received: int
 420:     video_frames_predicted: int
 421:     confirm_ratio_voice: float
 422:     confirm_ratio_video: float
 423: 
 424:     # Trust state (from attestation)
 425:     path_attested: bool
 426:     capability_state: CapabilitySnapshot
 427: 
 428:     def vitals_hash(self) -> str:
 429:         """BLAKE3 over canonical encoding. Used by ImmuneDecision."""
 430:         import hashlib
 431:         return hashlib.blake2b(repr(self).encode(), digest_size=16).hexdigest()
 432: 
 433: 
 434: class ImmuneAction(Enum):
 435:     HOLD                   = 0
 436:     PREWARM_BACKUP_ROUTE   = 1
 437:     SWITCH_ROUTE           = 2
 438:     REQUEST_LOWER_FIDELITY = 3
 439:     REQUEST_VOICE_ONLY     = 4
 440:     SUGGEST_DEVICE_HANDOFF = 5
 441:     CONVERT_TO_ASYNC       = 6
 442:     EMERGENCY_REKEY        = 7
 443: 
 444: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 445: class ImmuneDecision:
 446:     action: ImmuneAction
 447:     reason_code: str              # "loss_above_p90", "fragility_critical", etc.
 448:     triggered_by: list[str]       # field names that crossed threshold
 449:     confidence: float             # 0..1 for SHADOW-mode learning
 450:     tick: int
 451:     vitals_hash: str
 452: ```
 453: 
 454: #### State machine
 455: 
 456: ```
 457:                        ┌─────────────────────────┐
 458:                        │  TickLoop @ 100ms       │
 459:                        │  (call lifecycle scope) │
 460:                        └────────────┬────────────┘
 461:                                     │
 462:                        ┌────────────▼────────────┐
 463:                        │  Sense: build CallVitals│
 464:                        └────────────┬────────────┘
 465:                                     │
 466:                   ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
 467:                   │                 │                 │
 468:         ┌─────────▼────────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌────────▼─────────┐
 469:         │ Transport Health │ │ Path Brain  │ │ Device Wellness  │
 470:         │ Controller       │ │ Controller  │ │ Controller       │
 471:         └─────────┬────────┘ └──────┬──────┘ └────────┬─────────┘
 472:                   │                 │                 │
 473:                   └─────────────────┼─────────────────┘
 474:                                     │
 475:                        ┌────────────▼────────────┐
 476:                        │ Arbitrator              │
 477:                        │ (highest-severity wins) │
 478:                        └────────────┬────────────┘
 479:                                     │
 480:                        ┌────────────▼────────────┐
 481:                        │ ImmuneDecision          │
 482:                        │ → Presence Compiler     │
 483:                        │ → Route Brain           │
 484:                        │ → Multi-Device Body     │
 485:                        │ → audit_log.append()    │
 486:                        └─────────────────────────┘
 487: ```
 488: 
 489: Three sub-controllers run in parallel each tick. The Arbitrator
 490: selects the highest-severity action.
 491: 
 492: **Severity ordering** (highest first):
 493: ```
 494: EMERGENCY_REKEY > CONVERT_TO_ASYNC > SWITCH_ROUTE >
 495: REQUEST_VOICE_ONLY > REQUEST_LOWER_FIDELITY >
 496: SUGGEST_DEVICE_HANDOFF > PREWARM_BACKUP_ROUTE > HOLD
 497: ```
 498: 
 499: #### Thresholds with hysteresis
 500: 
 501: ```python
 502: class TransportHealthController:
 503:     # Two thresholds per signal: trigger + recover.
 504:     # Recover < trigger / 2 enforces hysteresis.
 505: 
 506:     RTT_PREWARM_TRIGGER_MS = 400.0   # prewarm backup
 507:     RTT_PREWARM_RECOVER_MS = 180.0
 508:     RTT_SWITCH_TRIGGER_MS  = 800.0   # switch active
 509:     RTT_SWITCH_RECOVER_MS  = 350.0
 510: 
 511:     LOSS_DEGRADE_TRIGGER   = 0.05    # 5% loss
 512:     LOSS_DEGRADE_RECOVER   = 0.02
 513:     LOSS_VOICE_TRIGGER     = 0.15
 514:     LOSS_VOICE_RECOVER     = 0.05
 515:     LOSS_ASYNC_TRIGGER     = 0.35
 516:     LOSS_ASYNC_RECOVER     = 0.10
 517: 
 518:     JITTER_DEGRADE_MS      = 80.0
 519: 
 520:     def decide(self, v: CallVitals, last: Optional[ImmuneDecision]) -> ImmuneDecision:
 521:         ...
 522: ```
 523: 
 524: **How thresholds are tuned:** Defaults are *initial* values. After 1k
 525: call-minutes of dogfooding (Tier γ SHADOW mode), pull the actual
 526: distribution of `_pair_health.latency_ewma_ms` and `loss_rate_ewma`
 527: from the audit log. Set `PREWARM = p90`, `SWITCH = p99`. This is the
 528: same methodology that tuned the relay-bandit thresholds in v0.21.
 529: Reuse the existing audit-log infrastructure.
 530: 
 531: #### Integration points
 532: 
 533: | Subscribes (existing) | Where |
 534: |---|---|
 535: | `Daemon._pair_health[peer_fp]` | every tick |
 536: | `Daemon._relay_metrics[relay_id]` | every tick |
 537: | `routing_native.homology_score(path)` | every tick |
 538: | `confidential_native.current_tier()` | on capability event |
 539: | `Daemon._linked_devices()` | on device-state event |
 540: | `MediaPipeline.frame_stats()` | every tick (NEW) |
 541: 
 542: | Publishes (new) | Where |
 543: |---|---|
 544: | `PresenceCompiler.request(action)` | each tick if action != HOLD |
 545: | `RouteBrain.request(action)` | each tick if action ∈ {PREWARM, SWITCH} |
 546: | `MultiDeviceBody.suggest(action)` | each tick if action == HANDOFF |
 547: | `audit_log.append(decision)` | every tick, including HOLD |
 548: 
 549: #### Graduation modes
 550: 
 551: - **SHADOW (Tier γ):** controller landed, decisions written to audit
 552:   log, no actions emitted. Run for 1k call-minutes of dogfooding.
 553: - **ASSIST (Tier δ):** controller can emit `REQUEST_LOWER_FIDELITY`,
 554:   `PREWARM_BACKUP_ROUTE` only. Cannot switch or convert to async
 555:   without user-equivalent confirmation.
 556: - **AUTOPILOT (Tier η):** all actions enabled. Soak gate ≥95%
 557:   survival on 50k random network scenarios.
 558: 
 559: #### Three non-obvious invariants
 560: 
 561: 1. **The Arbitrator must be pure.** Given the same `CallVitals` it
 562:    must always emit the same `ImmuneDecision`. The `vitals_hash` in
 563:    each decision allows soak-replay to verify this.
 564: 2. **Every decision is logged, even HOLDs.** This is the dataset for
 565:    graduating SHADOW → ASSIST → AUTOPILOT.
 566: 3. **The system can refuse to act.** If `confirm_ratio_voice > 0.98`
 567:    and `loss_rate_ewma < 0.02`, it returns HOLD even if RTT crosses
 568:    the prewarm threshold. The threshold is necessary but not
 569:    sufficient. The Immune System reasons about whether the user is
 570:    *currently* being harmed.
 571: 
 572: #### Soak harness
 573: 
 574: ```python
 575: # tests/test_call_immune_soak.py — NEW
 576: 
 577: @pytest.mark.parametrize("iters", [int(os.getenv("ONE_LINK_SOAK_ITERS", "2000"))])
 578: def test_immune_system_survives_random_degradation(iters):
 579:     """For N random call-degradation scenarios:
 580:        1) Call ends in {alive, graceful_async, user_terminated}.
 581:           NEVER dead_unrecoverable.
 582:        2) No decision oscillates >3 times in any 1-second window.
 583:        3) Median decision latency < 50ms.
 584:        4) When fragility_score > 0.8, action ∈ {prewarm, switch, async} ≥ 95%.
 585:        5) Reality Engine provenance never drops in a transition."""
 586:     ...
 587: ```
 588: 
 589: Acceptance gate: ≥95% call survival, <1% oscillation, <50ms decision
 590: latency. Run 2k by default, 50k nightly via `ONE_LINK_SOAK_ITERS`.
 591: 
 592: ---
 593: 
 594: ### 4.2 Presence Compiler
 595: 
 596: **Purpose:** Compiles "this user wants to be present to that user at
 597: intensity X" into a concrete media representation that is sustainable
 598: on the current path with the current devices.
 599: 
 600: **Surface to user:** invisible. The user sees a face, hears a voice,
 601: or sees the capsule. They never see "you are now on rung 4."
 602: 
 603: #### Data structures
 604: 
 605: ```python
 606: # src/one_link/presence_compiler.py — NEW MODULE
 607: 
 608: from dataclasses import dataclass
 609: from enum import Enum
 610: 
 611: class Rung(Enum):
 612:     """Representation rungs, ordered by fidelity (0 = highest)."""
 613:     RAW_AV             = 0   # full WebRTC video + audio
 614:     OPUS_VIDEO         = 1   # adaptive bitrate Opus + VP9
 615:     SEMANTIC_DELTA_AV  = 2   # neural codec voice + face deltas (Tier ζ+)
 616:     FACE_STILL_MOTION  = 3   # face still + lip-sync from audio
 617:     AUDIO_ONLY         = 4   # Opus audio, video off
 618:     PUSH_TO_TALK       = 5   # discrete utterances
 619:     CONCEPT_TEXT       = 6   # ConceptFrame semantic transmission
 620:     ASYNC_CAPSULE      = 7   # call → voice note + chat
 621:     AMBIENT_PRESENCE   = 8   # below "call" — presence dot only
 622: 
 623: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 624: class RungSpec:
 625:     rung: Rung
 626:     name: str
 627:     min_kbps: float
 628:     min_confirm_ratio: float | None       # None = doesn't need predictive
 629:     requires_caps: list[str]
 630:     audio_codec: str | None
 631:     video_codec: str | None
 632:     semantic_channel: bool
 633: 
 634: LADDER: list[RungSpec] = [
 635:     RungSpec(Rung.RAW_AV,            "raw_av",            1000.0, None, ["WEBRTC_AV_V1"],            "opus", "vp9",  False),
 636:     RungSpec(Rung.OPUS_VIDEO,        "opus_video",         300.0, None, ["WEBRTC_AV_V1"],            "opus", "vp9",  False),
 637:     RungSpec(Rung.SEMANTIC_DELTA_AV, "semantic_delta_av",   30.0, 0.95, ["SEMANTIC_MEDIA_V1"],       None,   None,   True),
 638:     RungSpec(Rung.FACE_STILL_MOTION, "face_still_motion",   10.0, 0.90, ["SEMANTIC_MEDIA_V1"],       "opus", None,   True),
 639:     RungSpec(Rung.AUDIO_ONLY,        "audio_only",          16.0, None, ["WEBRTC_AV_V1"],            "opus", None,   False),
 640:     RungSpec(Rung.PUSH_TO_TALK,       "push_to_talk",         3.0, None, ["WEBRTC_AV_V1"],            "opus", None,   False),
 641:     RungSpec(Rung.CONCEPT_TEXT,       "concept_text",         0.1, None, ["SEMANTIC_MEDIA_V1"],       None,   None,   True),
 642:     RungSpec(Rung.ASYNC_CAPSULE,      "async_capsule",        0.0, None, [],                           None,   None,   False),
 643:     RungSpec(Rung.AMBIENT_PRESENCE,   "ambient_presence",     0.0, None, [],                           None,   None,   False),
 644: ]
 645: ```
 646: 
 647: #### Compiler logic
 648: 
 649: ```python
 650: class PresenceCompiler:
 651:     def __init__(self, session: CallSession, audit_log: AuditLog):
 652:         self.session = session
 653:         self.audit_log = audit_log
 654:         self.current_rung: Rung = Rung.RAW_AV
 655:         self.last_ascent_tick: int = 0
 656:         ASCENT_HYSTERESIS_TICKS = 100   # 10 seconds at 100ms tick
 657: 
 658:     def viable_rungs(self) -> list[RungSpec]:
 659:         """Apply capability-intersection mask + bandwidth filter."""
 660:         peer_caps = self.session.peer_capabilities
 661:         bw = self.session.last_vitals.bandwidth_estimate_kbps
 662:         return [
 663:             r for r in LADDER
 664:             if all(c in peer_caps for c in r.requires_caps)
 665:             and r.min_kbps <= bw
 666:         ]
 667: 
 668:     def request(self, action: ImmuneAction) -> None:
 669:         """Receive request from Immune System or user."""
 670:         target = self._action_to_rung(action)
 671:         self._transition_to(target)
 672: 
 673:     def _transition_to(self, target: Rung) -> None:
 674:         """Descend aggressively, ascend slowly."""
 675:         if target.value > self.current_rung.value:
 676:             # Descend immediately
 677:             self._do_transition(target)
 678:         elif target.value < self.current_rung.value:
 679:             # Ascend only after hysteresis window
 680:             if self.session.tick - self.last_ascent_tick < ASCENT_HYSTERESIS_TICKS:
 681:                 return
 682:             self._do_transition(target)
 683:             self.last_ascent_tick = self.session.tick
 684: 
 685:     def _do_transition(self, target: Rung) -> None:
 686:         # Emit transition event with 200ms crossfade for media-track changes
 687:         ...
 688: ```
 689: 
 690: #### Two invariants
 691: 
 692: 1. **Monotone-descent / slow-ascent.** Drops happen instantly; rises
 693:    require 10 seconds of stable conditions. Prevents oscillation
 694:    that the user would feel as flicker.
 695: 2. **Capability mask is enforced first.** Rung 2 (semantic) is
 696:    invisible to the Compiler unless both peers advertise
 697:    `SEMANTIC_MEDIA_V1` AND model-pack hashes match.
 698: 
 699: #### Rung 7 → conversation continuity
 700: 
 701: When the Compiler descends to `ASYNC_CAPSULE`, it does *not* end
 702: the call. It does:
 703: 
 704: 1. Emit `CallSession.convert_to_async()` event.
 705: 2. Persist the in-flight buffer as a voice note via the existing
 706:    v0.9.2 voice-message infrastructure
 707:    ([tests/test_voice_messages_v092.py](../tests/test_voice_messages_v092.py)).
 708: 3. Hand the conversation context to the chat layer
 709:    ([src/one_link/state.py](../src/one_link/state.py)).
 710: 4. Set `live_resumable_until = now + 10 minutes`.
 711: 5. Both parties' chat surfaces show a calm "voice note in progress"
 712:    indicator until the buffer flushes; then a "tap to resume" affordance
 713:    appears.
 714: 
 715: If conditions recover inside the window, the resume affordance
 716: triggers a new call invite with `resume_of = <prior_call_id>` so the
 717: ACE memory substrate (if present) can stitch them into one
 718: conversation object.
 719: 
 720: #### Integration points
 721: 
 722: | Reads | Source |
 723: |---|---|
 724: | `CallSession.intensity` | the dial |
 725: | `CallSession.peer_capabilities` | via CAP negotiation |
 726: | `ImmuneDecision` requests | from Immune System |
 727: | `CallVitals.bandwidth_estimate_kbps` | from media pipeline |
 728: 
 729: | Writes | Target |
 730: |---|---|
 731: | `CallSession.current_rung` | CRDT (LWW) |
 732: | MediaPipeline rung-change events | RTP/SRTP track reconfigure |
 733: | `audit_log` | per transition |
 734: 
 735: ---
 736: 
 737: ### 4.3 Multi-Device Body Engine
 738: 
 739: **Purpose:** Makes "your devices are organs" architecturally real. The
 740: user is one entity; their devices are surfaces that present them.
 741: 
 742: **The hardest engine to build right.** Cross-device, cross-network
 743: state convergence with sub-200ms handoff atomicity.
 744: 
 745: #### Shared state (CRDT)
 746: 
 747: ```python
 748: # src/one_link/body_engine.py — NEW MODULE
 749: 
 750: from dataclasses import dataclass
 751: from typing import Optional
 752: 
 753: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 754: class SurfaceCapability:
 755:     has_mic: bool
 756:     has_cam: bool
 757:     has_display: bool
 758:     has_speaker: bool
 759:     can_relay: bool
 760:     mic_quality_score: float       # 0..1, learned from prior calls
 761:     cam_quality_score: float
 762:     display_size_px: tuple[int, int] | None
 763:     is_battery_powered: bool
 764:     is_charging: Optional[bool]
 765: 
 766: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 767: class DeviceCallState:
 768:     device_id: str               # HKDF-derived subkey id
 769:     capability: SurfaceCapability
 770:     role: DeviceRole             # MIC | CAM | DISPLAY | SPEAKER | RELAY | HELPER | INACTIVE
 771:     alive_at_ms: int             # monotonic clock from device
 772:     battery_pct: Optional[float]
 773:     thermal_state: ThermalState
 774:     network_class: PathClass     # what does this device see?
 775: 
 776: @dataclass
 777: class ParticipantState:
 778:     """CRDT-merged state for one participant in a call."""
 779:     master_vk: bytes
 780:     active_devices: dict[str, DeviceCallState]  # OR-set keyed by device_id
 781:     primary_mic: 'LWWRegister[str]'             # device_id
 782:     primary_cam: 'LWWRegister[str]'
 783:     primary_display: 'LWWRegister[str]'
 784:     primary_speaker: 'LWWRegister[str]'
 785:     preferred_relay: 'LWWRegister[str]'
 786:     last_seen_location: 'LWWRegister[str]'      # opaque token from ISAC or app context
 787: 
 788: @dataclass
 789: class CallSession:
 790:     """Top-level CRDT for the call. Each device publishes its own
 791:        fragment; merge converges."""
 792:     call_id: str
 793:     intensity: 'LWWRegister[Intensity]'         # AMBIENT | LOW | MED | HIGH
 794:     participants: dict[bytes, ParticipantState] # keyed by master_vk
 795:     current_rung: 'LWWRegister[Rung]'
 796:     started_at_ms: int
 797:     ended_at_ms: Optional[int]
 798:     resume_of: Optional[str]                    # prior call_id if resuming
 799:     conversation_id: Optional[str]              # ACE conversation object
 800:     audit_path: 'LWWSet[FrameProvenance]'       # frame attestations
 801: ```
 802: 
 803: All structures use the existing `ol_crdt` lattice machinery:
 804: [src/one_link/crdt.py](../src/one_link/crdt.py) + native crate.
 805: 
 806: #### Surface arbitration algorithm
 807: 
 808: When multiple devices could play a role (e.g., both phone and laptop
 809: have a mic), the Body Engine picks by score:
 810: 
 811: ```
 812: score(device, role=MIC) =
 813:     role_quality_score(device, MIC)               * 0.40
 814:   + (1 - thermal_penalty(device.thermal_state))   * 0.20
 815:   + battery_penalty(device)                       * 0.15
 816:   + network_class_score(device.network_class)     * 0.15
 817:   + recency_score(device.alive_at_ms)             * 0.10
 818: ```
 819: 
 820: Each device computes the score locally and writes its preference into
 821: the CRDT LWW register. The lattice converges; both devices observe the
 822: same winner; ties go to lexicographic device_id (deterministic).
 823: 
 824: #### Crossfade protocol (the genuinely hard part)
 825: 
 826: Mic moves phone → laptop. Both are on different networks. Without
 827: care, the receiver hears a glottal seam.
 828: 
 829: ```
 830:         Phone mic         Laptop mic        Receiver buffer
 831:         ─────────         ──────────        ───────────────
 832: T=0     producing →                          fading_in phone
 833: T=1     producing →                          phone (steady)
 834:                           (request to take over emitted)
 835:                           (200ms crossfade window starts)
 836: T=2     producing →       producing →        jitter buffer picks
 837:                                               best frame per slot
 838: T=2.2   stopped           producing →        laptop (steady)
 839:                                               fade-in phone
 840:                                               complete
 841: ```
 842: 
 843: Protocol:
 844: 
 845: 1. Old surface (phone) receives `surface_handoff_request(MIC, target=laptop, fade_ms=200)`.
 846: 2. Both devices emit RTP packets *simultaneously* for 200 ms.
 847: 3. Receiver's jitter buffer, per output slot, selects the higher-
 848:    confidence frame (each frame carries a `produce_confidence` field
 849:    in the FrameProvenance header).
 850: 4. After 200 ms, old surface stops. New surface continues.
 851: 5. Reality Engine badge updates: `cam: desktop · mic: phone → laptop`.
 852: 
 853: No "switching device..." indicator. The user experiences continuous
 854: audio with a millisecond-level seam at worst, indistinguishable from
 855: the codec's normal frame-boundary artifacts.
 856: 
 857: #### Integration points
 858: 
 859: | Reads | Source |
 860: |---|---|
 861: | `linked_mesh.devices()` | row 8 substrate |
 862: | `ISAC.presence_probe()` | for "user is in this room" hints |
 863: | device hardware events (charging, thermal) | OS APIs |
 864: 
 865: | Writes | Target |
 866: |---|---|
 867: | `CallSession.participants[me].primary_*` | CRDT LWW |
 868: | Surface-handoff RTP frames | media pipeline |
 869: 
 870: #### Graduation modes
 871: 
 872: - **OFF (Tier α-δ):** single-device per participant. The substrate
 873:   is in place; the algorithm is dormant.
 874: - **ASSIST (Tier ε):** the Body Engine *suggests* a handoff
 875:   ("your laptop has a better mic, switch?"); user confirms.
 876: - **AUTOPILOT (Tier θ):** automatic, crossfaded, invisible.
 877: 
 878: ---
 879: 
 880: ### 4.4 Route Consciousness Engine
 881: 
 882: **Purpose:** Predicts the future of every available path. Prewarms
 883: backups before primaries die. Switches before the user feels pain.
 884: 
 885: **Substrate-heavy:** most signals exist already.
 886: 
 887: #### Data structures
 888: 
 889: ```python
 890: # src/one_link/route_brain.py — NEW MODULE
 891: 
 892: @dataclass
 893: class RouteCandidate:
 894:     path_id: str
 895:     path_class: PathClass
 896:     rtt_ewma_ms: float
 897:     loss_rate_ewma: float
 898:     bandwidth_kbps: float
 899:     fragility_score: float            # ol_homology
 900:     tau_c_score: float                # ol_routing
 901:     attested: bool
 902:     warm: bool                        # connection already established
 903:     last_used_ms: Optional[int]
 904:     cost_score: float                 # composite
 905: 
 906: @dataclass
 907: class RouteState:
 908:     active: RouteCandidate
 909:     warm_backups: list[RouteCandidate]    # sorted by cost_score
 910:     cold_alternatives: list[RouteCandidate]
 911: ```
 912: 
 913: #### Decision algorithm
 914: 
 915: ```python
 916: class RouteBrain:
 917:     def __init__(self, session: CallSession):
 918:         self.session = session
 919:         self.state: RouteState = ...
 920: 
 921:     def on_immune_request(self, action: ImmuneAction) -> None:
 922:         if action == ImmuneAction.PREWARM_BACKUP_ROUTE:
 923:             self._prewarm_top_alternative()
 924:         elif action == ImmuneAction.SWITCH_ROUTE:
 925:             self._switch_to_warmest_backup()
 926: 
 927:     def _prewarm_top_alternative(self) -> None:
 928:         # Compute cost_score for all cold alternatives
 929:         # Establish full handshake on top-1
 930:         # Move it into warm_backups
 931:         ...
 932: 
 933:     def _switch_to_warmest_backup(self) -> None:
 934:         # Issue media-redirect to peer's signaling channel
 935:         # Receive ACK
 936:         # Crossfade media to new path (using same 200ms protocol as Body)
 937:         ...
 938: ```
 939: 
 940: #### Composite cost score
 941: 
 942: ```
 943: cost(path) =
 944:     rtt_score(path.rtt_ewma_ms)               * 0.25
 945:   + loss_score(path.loss_rate_ewma)           * 0.30
 946:   + (1 - path.fragility_score)                * 0.20
 947:   + path.tau_c_score                          * 0.10
 948:   + attestation_score(path.attested)          * 0.10
 949:   + warmth_score(path.warm)                   * 0.05
 950: ```
 951: 
 952: Same scoring style as `_pick_best_relay()` (existing). Reused with
 953: call-specific weights.
 954: 
 955: #### Integration points
 956: 
 957: | Reads | Source |
 958: |---|---|
 959: | `Daemon._relay_metrics` | existing |
 960: | `routing_native.candidate_paths(peer_fp)` | existing (Row 4) |
 961: | `ol_homology.fragility_score(path)` | existing |
 962: | `ol_prefetch` predicted-load | existing (Row 4D) |
 963: 
 964: | Writes | Target |
 965: |---|---|
 966: | Path-switch signaling messages | new wire type `MEDIA_REDIRECT` |
 967: | Warmth state per candidate | local to engine |
 968: | `audit_log` per decision | shared |
 969: 
 970: ---
 971: 
 972: ### 4.5 Cryptographic Reality Engine
 973: 
 974: **Purpose:** Every media segment carries a verifiable provenance tag.
 975: The receiver always knows: who made this frame, on what device, by what
 976: method (real / repaired / predicted / reconstructed), over what path,
 977: with recording in what state.
 978: 
 979: **The single most important safety system.** Makes advanced media safe
 980: instead of creepy.
 981: 
 982: #### Frame provenance schema
 983: 
 984: ```python
 985: # src/one_link/frame_provenance.py — NEW MODULE
 986: 
 987: from enum import Enum
 988: 
 989: class FrameKind(Enum):
 990:     REAL          = 0   # captured live from physical sensor
 991:     REPAIRED      = 1   # missing samples filled by PLC
 992:     PREDICTED     = 2   # rendered ahead by Predictive Continuity
 993:     RECONSTRUCTED = 3   # rendered from semantic delta + model
 994:     BLANK         = 4   # placeholder (camera off, etc.)
 995: 
 996: class RecordingState(Enum):
 997:     NOT_RECORDING       = 0
 998:     RECORDING_LOCAL     = 1   # only this device's side
 999:     RECORDING_REMOTE    = 2   # peer is recording (consent required)
1000:     RECORDING_MUTUAL    = 3   # both sides agreed
1001: 
1002: @dataclass(frozen=True)
1003: class FrameProvenance:
1004:     """32-byte HMAC tag attached to every media segment.
1005:        Verifiable by the receiver against the sender's macaroon chain."""
1006:     schema_version: int               # 1
1007:     segment_hash: bytes               # BLAKE3-256 of segment content
1008:     device_id: str                    # which sender device produced it
1009:     frame_kind: FrameKind
1010:     path_class: PathClass             # local / lan / direct / relay / onion
1011:     recording_state: RecordingState
1012:     timestamp_us: int
1013:     produce_confidence: float         # for Body crossfade selection
1014:     capability_chain_id: bytes        # which macaroon chain attests this
1015:     hmac: bytes                       # over canonical(self) using chain key
1016: ```
1017: 
1018: #### Wire format
1019: 
1020: The provenance tag is **inline** with every media frame. It piggybacks
1021: on the per-chunk header in the existing `ol_aead` AEAD pipeline. No
1022: new framing.
1023: 
1024: ```
1025: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1026: │ Outer transport (DTLS-SRTP or QUIC)                          │
1027: │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
1028: │ │ Media frame (RTP packet or QUIC datagram)               │ │
1029: │ │ ┌────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
1030: │ │ │ FrameProvenance(32B)│ AEAD(content)                  │ │ │
1031: │ │ └────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
1032: │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
1033: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1034: ```
1035: 
1036: #### Verification flow
1037: 
1038: 1. Sender's device holds a per-call macaroon chain rooted in the
1039:    device subkey (`ol_capability` chain).
1040: 2. For each frame: compute `hmac = HMAC-SHA256(chain_key,
1041:    canonical(provenance_minus_hmac))`.
1042: 3. Embed in frame header.
1043: 4. Receiver caches the chain root on call setup.
1044: 5. For each frame: recompute, compare.
1045: 6. Mismatch → drop the frame, log, increment counter; if 3 mismatches
1046:    within a 1-second window → `ImmuneAction.EMERGENCY_REKEY`.
1047: 
1048: The cost is one HMAC per frame. At 50 audio fps + 30 video fps = 80
1049: HMACs/sec per direction. On any modern CPU this is <0.1% CPU. SIMD
1050: HMAC-SHA256 in `ol_aead` makes it negligible.
1051: 
1052: #### UI surface (the only visible piece)
1053: 
1054: ```
1055: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
1056: │  📞  Mom                                  │
1057: │                                           │
1058: │  ┌─────────────────────────┐              │
1059: │  │                         │   • Mom      │
1060: │  │                         │              │
1061: │  │      [face video]       │              │
1062: │  │                         │              │
1063: │  │                         │              │
1064: │  └─────────────────────────┘              │
1065: │                                           │
1066: │  🟢                                        │
1067: └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
1068: 
1069: Tap the green dot →
1070: 
1071: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
1072: │   Trust                                   │
1073: │                                           │
1074: │   Real                                    │
1075: │   Local network                           │
1076: │   Not recording                           │
1077: │   You verified Mom on Mar 4                │
1078: │                                           │
1079: └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
1080: ```
1081: 
1082: When the Compiler descends to `FACE_STILL_MOTION` (rung 3, semantic),
1083: the dot changes color and the detail shows "Reconstructed from model
1084: (same Mom you verified)". When the Route Brain switches from LAN to
1085: relay, "Local network" → "Via relay". The user is never lied to.
1086: 
1087: #### Integration points
1088: 
1089: | Reads | Source |
1090: |---|---|
1091: | Capability chain for this call | `ol_capability` |
1092: | Frame data | media pipeline |
1093: | Recording state | session |
1094: | Path class | Route Brain current state |
1095: 
1096: | Writes | Target |
1097: |---|---|
1098: | Provenance tag inline in every frame | media pipeline |
1099: | UI badge state | presentation layer |
1100: | Mismatch counter | audit log |
1101: 
1102: #### Graduation modes
1103: 
1104: **AUTOPILOT day one.** This is a safety system. It is never opt-in,
1105: never opt-out (you cannot disable it without disabling the call).
1106: 
1107: ---
1108: 
1109: ### 4.6 Human Signal Priority Engine
1110: 
1111: **Purpose:** Under bandwidth pressure, the human survives. Voice
1112: beats video; intelligibility beats fidelity; faces beat backgrounds;
1113: files cede to media.
1114: 
1115: **Architecture:** transport-layer detail, not a feature. Ships
1116: AUTOPILOT day one.
1117: 
1118: #### QoS class hierarchy
1119: 
1120: ```python
1121: class QoSClass(Enum):
1122:     P0_VOICE                  = 0   # intelligibility-critical
1123:     P1_TIMING                 = 1   # turn-taking signals, ack pings
1124:     P2_FACE_PRIMARY           = 2   # primary face region (semantic)
1125:     P3_GESTURE                = 3   # hands, body pose
1126:     P4_FILE_INFLIGHT          = 4   # files in transit
1127:     P5_VIDEO_BACKGROUND       = 5   # background pixels
1128:     P6_AMBIENT                = 6   # background environmental data
1129: ```
1130: 
1131: #### Stream mapping
1132: 
1133: Each QoS class gets its own QUIC stream (or RTP SSRC for WebRTC paths).
1134: Loss in one class never blocks another.
1135: 
1136: ```
1137: QUIC connection
1138: ├── stream 0: control / signaling
1139: ├── stream 1: P0_VOICE  ← priority 1 (highest weight)
1140: ├── stream 2: P1_TIMING ← priority 2
1141: ├── stream 3: P2_FACE
1142: ├── stream 4: P3_GESTURE
1143: ├── stream 5: P4_FILE
1144: ├── stream 6: P5_BACKGROUND
1145: └── stream 7: P6_AMBIENT
1146: ```
1147: 
1148: QUIC's existing priority/weight mechanism (`ol_quic`) carries the
1149: weighting to the wire. When bandwidth drops, P5 and P6 cede first.
1150: 
1151: #### Integration points
1152: 
1153: | Reads | Source |
1154: |---|---|
1155: | Current rung | Compiler |
1156: | Active streams | media pipeline |
1157: 
1158: | Writes | Target |
1159: |---|---|
1160: | Per-stream priority | QUIC stack |
1161: 
1162: ---
1163: 
1164: ### 4.7 Predictive Continuity Engine
1165: 
1166: **Purpose:** When a frame doesn't arrive, the receiver renders an
1167: educated guess. When the real frame arrives, the system corrects.
1168: Prediction repairs continuity; it never lies about reality (the
1169: Reality Engine flags every predicted frame).
1170: 
1171: #### Substrate
1172: 
1173: OneField's `voice.cl` and `video.cl` already define:
1174: - `PredictiveState`
1175: - `should_render_predictively(state, ...)`
1176: - `step_predictive_render(state)`
1177: - `on_delta_arrival(state, novelty) → confirmed | corrected`
1178: - `confirm_ratio()` — the dashboard metric
1179: 
1180: Lookahead cap: 4 voice frames, 8 video frames (per `voice.cl` /
1181: `video.cl` spec).
1182: 
1183: #### Algorithm sketch
1184: 
1185: ```python
1186: # src/one_link/predictive_continuity.py — NEW MODULE
1187: 
1188: @dataclass
1189: class PredictiveState:
1190:     last_real_frame: MediaFrame
1191:     last_real_frame_at_us: int
1192:     predicted_count_since_real: int
1193:     confirm_count: int
1194:     correct_count: int
1195:     model_confidence: float
1196: 
1197: class PredictiveContinuity:
1198:     MAX_LOOKAHEAD_AUDIO_FRAMES = 4
1199:     MAX_LOOKAHEAD_VIDEO_FRAMES = 8
1200: 
1201:     def on_frame_due(self, state: PredictiveState) -> MediaFrame:
1202:         if state.predicted_count_since_real >= self.MAX_LOOKAHEAD_AUDIO_FRAMES:
1203:             # We've predicted past our budget. Render silence/freeze + flag.
1204:             return BlankFrame(kind=FrameKind.BLANK)
1205:         predicted = self._extrapolate(state)
1206:         state.predicted_count_since_real += 1
1207:         # Tag with FrameKind.PREDICTED — Reality Engine signs it as such
1208:         return predicted
1209: 
1210:     def on_real_frame_arrives(self, state: PredictiveState, real: MediaFrame) -> None:
1211:         novelty = self._compute_novelty(state.last_real_frame, real)
1212:         if novelty < CONFIRM_THRESHOLD:
1213:             state.confirm_count += 1
1214:         else:
1215:             state.correct_count += 1
1216:             self._emit_correction(real)
1217:         state.last_real_frame = real
1218:         state.predicted_count_since_real = 0
1219: ```
1220: 
1221: `confirm_ratio = confirm_count / (confirm_count + correct_count)`. When
1222: this exceeds 0.98, the receiver is effectively rendering ahead of the
1223: sender — predictive negative latency in production.
1224: 
1225: #### Integration with Reality Engine
1226: 
1227: Every predicted frame's `FrameProvenance.frame_kind = PREDICTED`. The
1228: Reality badge changes from "Real" to "Reconstructed (predicted)" until
1229: real frames resume. No silent fakery.
1230: 
1231: #### Graduation modes
1232: 
1233: - **OFF (Tier α-δ):** standard codec PLC only.
1234: - **ASSIST (Tier η):** voice predictive only. A/B against Opus PLC.
1235: - **AUTOPILOT (Tier η+):** voice + video predictive.
1236: 
1237: ---
1238: 
1239: ### 4.8 Semantic Video / Voice Engine
1240: 
1241: **Purpose:** The alien tier. Transmit *intent* and *meaning*, not
1242: pixels and samples. The receiver reconstructs presence from a shared
1243: model + a tiny delta on the wire.
1244: 
1245: **Research-grade.** The math + protocol ship in OneField source today
1246: ([voice.cl](../../../OneField%20Mesh/onefield/app/builtin/voice.cl),
1247: [video.cl](../../../OneField%20Mesh/onefield/app/builtin/video.cl)).
1248: Trained model weights do not exist yet; producing them is
1249: research-grade GPU work on curated datasets.
1250: 
1251: #### Wire format
1252: 
1253: Voice: `ArticulatoryFrame` (state) + `VoiceDelta` (change).
1254: 
1255: ```
1256: VoiceDelta:
1257:   schema:  u16 (1)
1258:   seq:     u32
1259:   speaker: u8   (which speaker model)
1260:   bits:    [0..60]  delta bits packed; rest = silence
1261: ```
1262: 
1263: At 50 fps: max 3 kbps, typical 0.5-1.5 kbps. Compare Opus 16k = 16 kbps.
1264: 
1265: Video: `Scene` (graph) + `VideoDelta` (graph mutation).
1266: 
1267: ```
1268: VideoDelta:
1269:   schema:    u16 (1)
1270:   seq:       u32
1271:   scene_id:  u32
1272:   face_pose: [6 floats] (head pose 6DoF)
1273:   expr:      [16 floats] (FACS-coded expression)
1274:   gaze:      [2 floats]
1275:   mouth:     [22 floats] (visemes)
1276:   hands:     optional [n × pose]
1277:   scene_cuts: optional bool
1278: ```
1279: 
1280: Typical: ~24 bytes/frame stable talking-head. ~1 KB keyframe.
1281: 
1282: #### Capability negotiation
1283: 
1284: ```
1285: CAP: SEMANTIC_MEDIA_V1
1286:   model_pack_hash: "blake3:abc..."   # both peers must match
1287:   model_pack_version: "voice-1.0,video-1.0"
1288:   model_pack_entropy_bits: 512        # for quantum-resistance claim
1289: ```
1290: 
1291: If hashes don't match: Compiler masks rungs 2, 3, 6 from the ladder.
1292: The user never knows the option existed. The call uses Opus/VP9.
1293: 
1294: #### Model pack distribution
1295: 
1296: Out-of-band over the existing file transfer pipeline. Model packs:
1297: - Are signed by a trusted model-pack issuer (initial: project root).
1298: - Are content-addressed by BLAKE3 hash.
1299: - Have versioned schemas; backward-compatible model loaders.
1300: - Are sized ~10-50 MB voice, ~50-200 MB video.
1301: - Are cached locally per-device.
1302: - Refuse to load if the issuer signature fails.
1303: 
1304: #### Integration with Reality Engine
1305: 
1306: Semantic-reconstructed frames get `FrameKind.RECONSTRUCTED`. The
1307: provenance tag carries the `model_pack_hash` so the receiver can prove
1308: which model produced the reconstruction. If a sender swaps models
1309: mid-call, the chain breaks; the Immune System rekeys.
1310: 
1311: #### Honest research dependencies
1312: 
1313: | What | Status |
1314: |---|---|
1315: | Math, wire format, predicates, tests | Shipped in voice.cl / video.cl |
1316: | Trained articulatory model (voice) | Does not exist |
1317: | Trained scene-graph model (video) | Does not exist |
1318: | Encoder/decoder ported to Rust crate | Not started |
1319: | Model-pack signing infrastructure | Not started |
1320: 
1321: Cannot ship Tier ζ+ without these. Path: train voice model first
1322: (smaller, faster iteration), port via `ol_codegen` to `ol_semantic`
1323: Rust crate using the existing 1M-iter byte-equivalence gate, then
1324: video.
1325: 
1326: #### Graduation modes
1327: 
1328: - **OFF (Tier α-ε):** capability not advertised.
1329: - **EXPERIMENTAL (Tier ζ):** voice-only, capability-gated, A/B
1330:   against Opus 32k on 20-call corpus. Measure intelligibility MOS.
1331:   Do not promise quality.
1332: - **OPT-IN (Tier θ):** voice + video, both peers must have model
1333:   packs. Compiler will pick semantic rungs when network can't
1334:   sustain Opus/VP9.
1335: 
1336: ---
1337: 
1338: ### 4.9 OneField R&D Engine
1339: 
1340: **Purpose:** Bridge to OneField. When OneField hardware is present
1341: (HackRF mesh, future PINN waveform synth), the call can route over
1342: the physics-level substrate. Today: stub; later: full mesh radio.
1343: 
1344: **Future surface.** Listed here for architectural completeness; no
1345: active build target until OneField hardware is operational.
1346: 
1347: #### What it would enable
1348: 
1349: - Calls with no internet at all (mesh-radio peer-to-peer).
1350: - Frequency-agnostic operation (VLF for through-water, mmWave for
1351:   clear-air bursts).
1352: - Negative-SNR reception with shared model prior (~–25 dB SNR
1353:   feasibility per OneField proof).
1354: - Bounded-latency conversations across arbitrary RTT (intent-as-
1355:   channel + Predictive Continuity scaled to seconds-of-prediction).
1356: 
1357: #### Capability gate
1358: 
1359: ```
1360: CAP: ONEFIELD_RADIO_V1
1361:   hardware_class: enum {HACKRF_PRO, FUTURE_NATIVE_RF}
1362:   band_set: bitfield (which bands the device can transmit/receive)
1363:   compliance_region: enum (FCC, ETSI, ...)  // for safety rails
1364: ```
1365: 
1366: Same capability-gating, opt-in model as Semantic Engine. Never default.
1367: 
1368: #### Honest status
1369: 
1370: The HackRF Pro has not yet arrived in the OneField project. The
1371: field-test harness exists; the radio does not. Tier θ+ depends on
1372: this hardware. Do not block earlier tiers on it.
