1375: 
1376: ## Part 5 — Shared State (CRDT)
1377: 
1378: ### Why CRDT and not state machine
1379: 
1380: Both ends of a call have their own opinion of {who, what, where, how,
1381: health, fallback}. They sync via vector clock + LWW + OR-set — the
1382: same machinery that ships in [src/one_link/crdt.py](../src/one_link/crdt.py)
1383: today. Each device writes its local view; the lattice converges.
1384: 
1385: **This matters because:**
1386: 
1387: - Multi-device Body Engine needs both ends to agree on which device
1388:   is mic vs cam. If one peer's phone goes to sleep, the device-role
1389:   state must converge to "mic moved to laptop" without a synchronous
1390:   round-trip.
1391: - Async-capsule conversion needs both sides to agree the call ended
1392:   in async and what the final state was. CRDT merge handles network
1393:   partition gracefully.
1394: - Resume after capsule needs the next call to inherit the prior
1395:   conversation's state (intensity history, last verified identity,
1396:   preferred surfaces).
1397: 
1398: ### CallSession schema (canonical)
1399: 
1400: ```python
1401: @dataclass
1402: class CallSession:
1403:     # Identity
1404:     call_id: str                                   # ULID
1405:     conversation_id: Optional[str]                 # ACE conversation, if any
1406:     resume_of: Optional[str]                       # prior call_id
1407:     started_at_ms: int
1408: 
1409:     # Intensity dial — the primary surface
1410:     intensity: 'LWWRegister[Intensity]'            # AMBIENT < LOW < MED < HIGH
1411:     target_intensity: 'LWWRegister[Intensity]'     # what user requested
1412:     current_rung: 'LWWRegister[Rung]'
1413: 
1414:     # Participants (CRDT-merged from each device's view)
1415:     participants: dict[bytes, ParticipantState]    # keyed by master_vk
1416: 
1417:     # Routing
1418:     active_path: 'LWWRegister[str]'                # path_id
1419:     warm_backups: 'ORSet[str]'
1420: 
1421:     # Capability intersection (frozen at call setup)
1422:     negotiated_capabilities: frozenset[str]
1423:     model_pack_hash: Optional[str]
1424: 
1425:     # Lifecycle
1426:     ended_at_ms: 'LWWRegister[Optional[int]]'
1427:     end_reason: 'LWWRegister[Optional[EndReason]]'
1428:     live_resumable_until_ms: 'LWWRegister[Optional[int]]'
1429: 
1430:     # Trust + audit
1431:     identity_verified: 'LWWRegister[VerificationState]'
1432:     recording_state: 'LWWRegister[RecordingState]'
1433:     audit_path: 'ORSet[FrameProvenance]'           # (bounded — rotating)
1434: 
1435:     # Vitals — local, never synced
1436:     # (kept separately per-device; used by Immune System)
1437: ```
1438: 
1439: ### Convergence properties
1440: 
1441: - **`intensity`** uses LWW with timestamp tiebreak by `master_vk`. If
1442:   both sides bump intensity simultaneously, the higher-priority side
1443:   (the originator) wins, then propagates.
1444: - **`participants[*].active_devices`** is an OR-set: devices join and
1445:   leave; the set converges add-wins.
1446: - **`primary_mic`** etc. are LWW; ties go to lex device_id.
1447: - **`audit_path`** is bounded OR-set — keeps last N frame provenance
1448:   tags for end-of-call attestation; older entries decay.
1449: 
1450: ### Sync mechanism
1451: 
1452: Reuses the existing CRDT message types:
1453: - `CALL_STATE_DELTA` — wire type added to [src/one_link/wire.py](../src/one_link/wire.py).
1454: - Carries vector-clock-stamped delta over the CallSession fields.
1455: - Sent over the existing CONTROL stream, not media stream.
1456: 
1457: ---
1458: 
1459: ## Part 6 — Call Lifecycle Flows
1460: 
1461: ### 6.1 Initiation
1462: 
1463: ```
1464: User taps "Call Mom" on Phone
1465:   │
1466:   ▼
1467: Phone Body Engine writes CallSession with:
1468:   - intensity = HIGH
1469:   - participants[josh_vk].active_devices[phone] = state
1470:   - participants[mom_vk] = {} (not yet known)
1471:   │
1472:   ▼
1473: Phone signaling emits CALL_INVITE to:
1474:   - Mom's rendezvous endpoints (Row 3, ol_discovery)
1475:   - All paired devices Mom has advertised
1476:   │
1477:   ▼
1478: Mom's devices receive CALL_INVITE on their daemon control channel
1479:   │
1480:   ▼
1481: Body Engine on Mom's side:
1482:   - Reads last-known location LWW
1483:   - Identifies which surface(s) Mom is most likely at
1484:   - Renders the ring on those surfaces FIRST
1485:   - After 3s, fans out to all remaining devices
1486: ```
1487: 
1488: ### 6.2 Identity verification
1489: 
1490: **First-ever call** between two parties:
1491: 
1492: 1. Each side derives a 5-word SAS from a transcript hash of
1493:    `(josh_master_vk, mom_master_vk, call_id, dh_shared_secret)` using
1494:    the `ol_pair_qr` SAS primitive.
1495: 2. Both sides display the SAS briefly in the calm-trust pane:
1496:    ```
1497:    You and Mom share:
1498:    amber  river  canyon  meadow  stone
1499:    ```
1500: 3. If they read the same five words aloud (and they match), tap
1501:    "Yes." This writes `identity_verified = TRUSTED` to CallSession.
1502: 4. The verification persists in the local trust store; future calls
1503:    skip this step.
1504: 
1505: **Subsequent calls:**
1506: - If `master_vk` unchanged: skip entirely.
1507: - If `master_vk` rotated AND new signature chains to the old key:
1508:   badge says "Mom updated her keys"; allow with a re-verify offer.
1509: - If `master_vk` rotated AND chain broken: call refuses. UI says
1510:   "This may not be Mom. Verify in person before continuing." This
1511:   is the C2 fix on the call surface.
1512: 
1513: ### 6.3 Accept / decline
1514: 
1515: - **Accept**: tap or speak. CallSession transitions to active. Other
1516:   devices' rings stop within 200ms via CRDT propagation.
1517: - **Decline**: tap or speak. CallSession transitions to declined.
1518:   Alex's side: gracefully converts to async capsule offer.
1519: - **Ignore (timeout)**: 30s. Same as decline → async capsule.
1520: - **Mom is offline entirely (no devices respond)**: Alex's side
1521:   instantly transitions to "Leave a voice note for Mom" — no
1522:   "couldn't reach Mom" error.
1523: 
1524: ### 6.4 Active call
1525: 
1526: Once accepted, the engine layer takes over. The user sees:
1527: - Face / voice / ambient indicator
1528: - A calm provenance dot
1529: - Nothing else
1530: 
1531: Behind the scenes:
1532: - Immune System tick @ 100ms
1533: - Body Engine tick @ 500ms
1534: - Route Brain tick @ 200ms
1535: - Reality Engine signs every frame
1536: - Predictive Continuity active per cap
1537: - Compiler responds to Immune requests
1538: 
1539: ### 6.5 Degradation transitions
1540: 
1541: When the Compiler descends, the visible change is:
1542: - Rung 0 → 1: imperceptible (bitrate change at I-frame boundary)
1543: - Rung 1 → 4 (audio only): video softly fades to a still-of-the-face
1544:   with the caption "audio only" appearing for 2 seconds and then
1545:   fading. No toast, no overlay.
1546: - Rung 4 → 7 (async capsule): a single calm message replaces the
1547:   call surface:
1548:   ```
1549:   Mom seems to have lost connection.
1550:   Recording your message for her.
1551:   Tap to finish.
1552:   ```
1553: 
1554: ### 6.6 End
1555: 
1556: Three end paths, all graceful:
1557: 
1558: 1. **User hangup**: tap end. CallSession.ended_at_ms set. Other side
1559:    sees calm "Mom ended the call" for 2 seconds, fades. Conversation
1560:    record preserved.
1561: 2. **Mutual hangup**: both press end. Same flow.
1562: 3. **Network-induced async**: Immune System emits
1563:    `CONVERT_TO_ASYNC`. Compiler descends to rung 7. Voice note
1564:    created. Both sides see resume affordance for 10 minutes.
1565: 
1566: ### 6.7 Resume from capsule
1567: 
1568: Within 10-minute window, network recovers. Either side taps "Resume":
1569: - New CALL_INVITE issued with `resume_of = <prior_call_id>`.
1570: - ACE memory (if present) stitches the two calls into one
1571:   conversation object.
1572: - CallSession inherits prior intensity, prior identity verification,
1573:   prior preferred surfaces.
1574: 
1575: ---
1576: 
1577: ## Part 7 — Trust Surface
1578: 
1579: ### 7.1 Identity at call layer
1580: 
1581: **Prerequisites — must close before voice/video ships:**
1582: 
1583: - **Audit finding C1** ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md):119–124) — Browser
1584:   SDP attestation binding. Currently `/api/v1/peer-rtc` accepts
1585:   unsigned SDP. Must require Ed25519 signature over
1586:   `canonical(SDP || master_vk || call_id || nonce)`. Receiver
1587:   cross-checks against pinned `master_vk`.
1588: - **Audit finding C2** ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md):134–136 +
1589:   159) — Master VK TOFU rotation. Currently a peer's master_vk can
1590:   silently rotate post-TOFU. Must require either (a) signature from
1591:   prior key, or (b) explicit re-verify SAS challenge before any
1592:   capability or call proceeds.
1593: - **Audit finding C5** ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md):225) — At-rest
1594:   encryption for chat bodies and group chain keys. Tier A
1595:   (browser PWA) shipping; Tier B (daemon) required before any
1596:   recording feature.
1597: 
1598: **No voice/video tier ships past Tier α-prereqs until C1 + C2 are
1599: closed.** Reality Engine over an attestation gap is a doctrine
1600: violation.
1601: 
1602: ### 7.2 Recording consent
1603: 
1604: **The most felt privacy moment.** Treated as doctrine, not feature.
1605: 
1606: - Both sides must explicitly tap a recording-start affordance.
1607: - Recording surface badge is **visible**, not subtle. It uses the
1608:   Reality Engine pane's `recording_state` field.
1609: - Toggling off by either side stops recording immediately. The
1610:   recorded artifact ends at that exact frame.
1611: - Recorded artifacts are cryptographically signed (each frame
1612:   carrying its FrameProvenance) so they are authenticatable later
1613:   and undeepfakeable.
1614: - Recordings are encrypted at rest using a per-recording key derived
1615:   from the call's macaroon chain. Sharing a recording requires
1616:   granting a derived capability.
1617: - **No silent recording.** Ever. No "for quality" recording. No
1618:   cloud-side recording (it's P2P; there is no cloud).
1619: 
1620: ### 7.3 Conversation-as-object capabilities
1621: 
1622: Conversations are first-class objects. They carry capabilities that
1623: participants can grant or refuse:
1624: 
1625: ```python
1626: class ConversationCap(Enum):
1627:     SUMMARIZE          = "summarize"           # AI can read+summarize
1628:     PERSIST_LOCALLY    = "persist_local"       # save to disk
1629:     PERSIST_TO_ACE     = "persist_to_ace"      # add to relational memory
1630:     SHARE_EXCERPT      = "share_excerpt"       # forward a snippet
1631:     INDEX_FOR_SEARCH   = "index_search"        # searchable later
1632:     AUTO_TRANSCRIBE    = "auto_transcribe"     # local captions
1633:     AUTO_TRANSLATE     = "auto_translate"
1634:     RECORD             = "record"
1635: 
1636: @dataclass
1637: class ConversationCapState:
1638:     """One row per (conversation, participant, cap).
1639:        Macaroon-attenuated; revocable via existing _cap_store."""
1640:     conversation_id: str
1641:     participant_master_vk: bytes
1642:     cap: ConversationCap
1643:     granted_by: bytes                # whose authority
1644:     granted_at_ms: int
1645:     expires_at_ms: Optional[int]
1646:     macaroon_token: bytes
1647: ```
1648: 
1649: Default state: caps are *not granted*. Each requires an explicit
1650: in-call confirmation. The conversation "can refuse" by simply having
1651: no granting record for a cap.
1652: 
1653: ---
1654: 
1655: ## Part 8 — Wire Format Additions
1656: 
1657: All new wire types compose into [src/one_link/wire.py](../src/one_link/wire.py)
1658: following the existing length-prefixed JSON envelope.
1659: 
1660: ### 8.1 New message types
1661: 
1662: | Type | Direction | Body fields |
1663: |---|---|---|
1664: | `CALL_INVITE` | initiator → recipient | `call_id, conversation_id?, resume_of?, intensity, caps_advertised[], offer_sdp_signed, ttl_ms` |
1665: | `CALL_RING` | recipient device → recipient devices | `call_id, ring_surface` (CRDT-converged) |
1666: | `CALL_ACCEPT` | recipient → initiator | `call_id, accepting_device_id, answer_sdp_signed, caps_advertised[]` |
1667: | `CALL_DECLINE` | recipient → initiator | `call_id, reason: enum {busy, ignore, refuse}` |
1668: | `CALL_END` | either → other | `call_id, reason: enum {user_hangup, network_async, error}` |
1669: | `CALL_STATE_DELTA` | either → other | `call_id, vector_clock, fields_changed[]` |
1670: | `MEDIA_REDIRECT` | either → other | `call_id, new_path_id, crossfade_ms` |
1671: | `RESUME_OFFER` | either → other | `call_id, prior_call_id, capsule_blob_hash, ttl_ms` |
1672: | `RECORDING_REQUEST` | either → other | `call_id, scope: enum {audio, video, both}` |
1673: | `RECORDING_GRANT` | recipient → requester | `call_id, granted: bool, conditions[]` |
1674: | `IDENTITY_CHALLENGE` | either → other (first call) | `call_id, sas_transcript_hash` |
1675: | `IDENTITY_CONFIRM` | either → other | `call_id, sas_confirmation_hash` |
1676: 
1677: ### 8.2 SDP audio / video offers
1678: 
1679: Currently [src/one_link/peer_rtc.py](../src/one_link/peer_rtc.py)
1680: emits only `m=application` DataChannel offers. The migration:
1681: 
1682: ```sdp
1683: v=0
1684: o=- 1234567 1 IN IP4 0.0.0.0
1685: s=-
1686: t=0 0
1687: a=fingerprint:sha-256 AB:CD:EF:...
1688: a=group:BUNDLE 0 1 2
1689: 
1690: m=application 9 UDP/DTLS/SCTP webrtc-datachannel
1691: c=IN IP4 0.0.0.0
1692: a=mid:0
1693: a=sctp-port:5000
1694: 
1695: m=audio 9 UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF 111
1696: c=IN IP4 0.0.0.0
1697: a=mid:1
1698: a=rtpmap:111 opus/48000/2
1699: a=fmtp:111 useinbandfec=1; usedtx=1; minptime=10
1700: a=rtcp-fb:111 nack
1701: a=rtcp-fb:111 transport-cc
1702: a=ssrc:12345 cname:josh-mic
1703: a=extmap:1 http://onelink.dev/frame-provenance
1704: 
1705: m=video 9 UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF 100
1706: c=IN IP4 0.0.0.0
1707: a=mid:2
1708: a=rtpmap:100 VP9/90000
1709: a=fmtp:100 profile-id=0
1710: a=rtcp-fb:100 nack
1711: a=rtcp-fb:100 nack pli
1712: a=rtcp-fb:100 ccm fir
1713: a=rtcp-fb:100 transport-cc
1714: a=ssrc:67890 cname:josh-cam
1715: a=extmap:1 http://onelink.dev/frame-provenance
1716: ```
1717: 
1718: The `extmap:1` header is the FrameProvenance carrier (RFC 8285 RTP
1719: header extension). 32 bytes per frame.
1720: 
1721: ### 8.3 Semantic delta wire format
1722: 
1723: When semantic capability is active, a third media stream is
1724: established (over the same QUIC connection or as an additional WebRTC
1725: DataChannel labeled `semantic-v1`). Format:
1726: 
1727: ```
1728: SemanticFrame:
1729:   schema_version: u16
1730:   call_id_short:  u32     // truncated for compactness
1731:   seq:            u32
1732:   kind:           u8      // 0 = voice delta, 1 = video delta, 2 = concept
1733:   payload_len:    u16
1734:   payload:        bytes   // VoiceDelta | VideoDelta | ConceptFrame
1735:   provenance:     [32]u8  // inline FrameProvenance HMAC
1736: ```
1737: 
1738: ### 8.4 Capability schema
1739: 
1740: New caps to add to [src/one_link/capabilities.py](../src/one_link/capabilities.py):
1741: 
1742: ```python
1743: class Capability(Enum):
1744:     # ... existing ...
1745:     WEBRTC_AV_V1                = "webrtc_av_v1"          # baseline AV
1746:     FRAME_PROVENANCE_V1         = "frame_provenance_v1"   # Reality Engine
1747:     PREDICTIVE_CONTINUITY_V1    = "predictive_continuity_v1"
1748:     SEMANTIC_MEDIA_V1           = "semantic_media_v1"
1749:     MULTIDEVICE_BODY_V1         = "multidevice_body_v1"
1750:     ROUTE_BRAIN_V1              = "route_brain_v1"
1751:     ONEFIELD_RADIO_V1           = "onefield_radio_v1"
1752:     CONVERSATION_OBJECT_V1      = "conversation_object_v1"
1753: ```
1754: 
1755: Capability advertisement happens at the existing
1756: `CAPABILITY_ADVERTISE` handshake. Intersection is the working set for
1757: the call.

1975: 
1976: ### 11.1 Test pyramid
1977: 
1978: ```
1979:                        ┌─────────────────────┐
1980:                        │  E2E Field Tests    │   <100 scenarios
1981:                        │  (real network)     │
1982:                        └─────────────────────┘
1983:                   ┌──────────────────────────────┐
1984:                   │  Soak Harness                │   2k-50k iters
1985:                   │  (simulated network)         │
1986:                   └──────────────────────────────┘
1987:             ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
1988:             │  Property Tests (CUDA fuzzer)        │   millions of trials
1989:             │  (lattice laws, HMAC non-forgery)    │
1990:             └──────────────────────────────────────┘
1991:       ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1992:       │  Unit Tests                                   │   thousands
1993:       │  (Arbitrator purity, rung transitions, ...)  │
1994:       └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1995: ```
1996: 
1997: ### 11.2 Soak harness pattern (per engine)
1998: 
1999: Lifts from [tests/test_native_pipeline_soak.py](../tests/test_native_pipeline_soak.py):
2000: 
2001: ```python
2002: @pytest.mark.parametrize("iters", [int(os.getenv("ONE_LINK_SOAK_ITERS", "2000"))])
2003: def test_<engine>_soak(iters):
2004:     failures = []
2005:     for i in range(iters):
2006:         scenario = random_scenario(seed=i)
2007:         result = run_simulated(scenario)
2008:         if not result.passes_acceptance():
2009:             failures.append((i, result))
2010:     assert len(failures) < iters * 0.05, f"survival budget: {len(failures)}/{iters}"
2011: ```
2012: 
2013: Default 2k iters. Nightly 50k via `ONE_LINK_SOAK_ITERS=50000`.
2014: Acceptance budget: <5% failures per soak (varies per engine).
2015: 
2016: ### 11.3 Property tests (lattice + crypto)
2017: 
2018: Reuse the existing CUDA property fuzzer pattern from OneField:
2019: 
2020: - `CallSession` CRDT merge satisfies lattice laws (associativity,
2021:   commutativity, idempotency) ∀ deltas.
2022: - `FrameProvenance` HMAC is non-forgeable ∀ random keys + tampered
2023:   payloads.
2024: - Compiler rung transitions are monotone-descent + slow-ascent ∀
2025:   vital sequences.
2026: - Identity SAS matches ∀ shared transcripts; differs ∀ different
2027:   transcripts.
2028: 
2029: Target: ≥1M trials per property in CI; ≥100M nightly.
2030: 
2031: ### 11.4 Real network field tests
2032: 
2033: A small corpus of network traces from real conditions:
2034: 
2035: - Home WiFi normal
2036: - Home WiFi with microwave on (2.4 GHz interference)
2037: - Cell 4G good
2038: - Cell 4G congested (rush hour)
2039: - Cell 5G mmWave
2040: - Airplane WiFi
2041: - Hotel WiFi
2042: - Walking out of WiFi range into cell
2043: - Two devices on same LAN
2044: - VPN over poor link
2045: 
2046: Replay each through the simulated network harness against the full
2047: stack. Acceptance: call survives in every scenario.
2048: 
2049: ### 11.5 Doctrine of Invisibility lint
2050: 
2051: A CI gate that scans the UI source for forbidden strings:
2052: 
2053: ```python
2054: # tests/test_doctrine_of_invisibility.py
2055: 
2056: FORBIDDEN = [
2057:     r"reconnecting\.\.\.",
2058:     r"connection unstable",
2059:     r"call failed",
2060:     r"could not reach",
2061:     r"please try again",
2062:     r"network error",
2063:     r"\bsettings\b.*advanced",
2064:     r"upgrade.*HD",
2065:     # etc.
2066: ]
2067: 
2068: def test_no_doctrine_violations():
2069:     for path in glob("src/one_link/web/**/*.{html,js,ts,jsx,tsx}"):
2070:         content = open(path).read()
2071:         for pattern in FORBIDDEN:
2072:             assert not re.search(pattern, content, re.I), \
2073:                 f"Doctrine violation in {path}: pattern '{pattern}'"
2074: ```
2075: 
2076: Every PR runs this. Adding a new forbidden string requires the
2077: Doctrine document to be updated first.

2081: ## Part 12 — Accessibility
2082: 
2083: **For the people** means every person. Built in Tier α, not deferred.
2084: 
2085: ### 12.1 Live captions
2086: 
2087: - On-device transcription only. Never cloud.
2088: - Whisper-small or comparable model running locally.
2089: - Captions are a UI overlay; FrameProvenance signs them too
2090:   (`FrameKind.RECONSTRUCTED` from `audio` source).
2091: - Toggle via accessibility settings, not call settings.
2092: - Both sides see captions if requested; sender of audio can disable
2093:   caption generation for their own audio (privacy of speech text).
2094: 
2095: ### 12.2 Screen-reader navigability
2096: 
2097: - Every UI element labeled for ARIA / VoiceOver / TalkBack.
2098: - Call accept/decline/end accessible via keyboard alone.
2099: - Intensity dial controllable via single-axis input (rocker, gesture).
2100: - Identity SAS spoken aloud by screen reader.
2101: 
2102: ### 12.3 Voice-only mode
2103: 
2104: - A first-class mode, not a degraded fallback.
2105: - For users without sight, video adds no value; system can default
2106:   to audio-only and use the saved bandwidth for higher voice
2107:   fidelity (rung 4 with Opus 64k instead of rung 0 with 16k voice).
2108: - Predictive Continuity especially valuable here (face context lost,
2109:   audio context maximal).
2110: 
2111: ### 12.4 Hearing accessibility
2112: 
2113: - Visual ring (flash, color cue) optional alongside ringtone.
2114: - Caption-first mode: video shown, captions always on, audio optional.
2115: - Tactile ring on wearables.
2116: 
2117: ---
2118: 
2119: ## Part 13 — For the People
2120: 
2121: ### 13.1 Free tier
2122: 
2123: Calls are free. Forever. No paywall.
2124: 
2125: **Who pays:**
2126: - Direct P2P calls cost nothing (no relay needed).
2127: - Relay-assisted calls use the existing federated-relay model
2128:   ([SOVEREIGN_NETWORK_BLUEPRINT.md](SOVEREIGN_NETWORK_BLUEPRINT.md)).
2129: - Volunteers run relay nodes; bandwidth costs are amortized by the
2130:   volunteer pool (similar to Tor).
2131: - Heavy users may choose to volunteer relay capacity.
2132: - No company runs cloud SFU infrastructure. No bill.
2133: 
2134: ### 13.2 Zero-account onboarding
2135: 
2136: First device, first call, first peer — no account creation.
2137: 
2138: ```
2139: User downloads One Link.
2140:   │
2141:   ▼
2142: App opens. Single screen:
2143:   ┌──────────────────────────────┐
2144:   │  Welcome to One Link.        │
2145:   │  Share this code with someone │
2146:   │  you trust.                   │
2147:   │                                │
2148:   │     [QR code]                  │
2149:   │                                │
2150:   │  Or scan theirs:               │
2151:   │     [Scan button]              │
2152:   └──────────────────────────────┘
2153:   │
2154:   ▼
2155: QR pair completes (ol_pair_qr, Row 2).
2156: SAS confirmation flow.
2157:   │
2158:   ▼
2159: Main screen: contacts (just the one).
2160: Tap to call.
2161: ```
2162: 
2163: 90 seconds from install to first call. No email, no phone number,
2164: no password, no profile.
2165: 
2166: ### 13.3 Identity sovereignty
2167: 
2168: The user's identity (master_vk) is theirs. Not the platform's.
2169: 
2170: - Generated on first install.
2171: - Sealed in hardware (`ol_hwkey`) where available.
2172: - Backed up via Shamir threshold across the user's own devices
2173:   (`ol_threshold_recovery`, Row 9).
2174: - If a device is lost, recovery quorum from remaining devices.
2175: - If all devices are lost, the identity is gone — by design. No
2176:   centralized recovery, no support email, no "verify with passport"
2177:   flow.
2178: - The trade-off (no recovery on total loss) is acknowledged plainly
2179:   in the onboarding doctrine.
2180: 
2181: ### 13.4 Internationalization
2182: 
2183: - The Doctrine of Invisibility minimizes UI strings, which makes i18n
2184:   cheap.
2185: - Every visible string must have translations for at least: English,
2186:   Spanish, Mandarin, Hindi, Arabic, Portuguese, French. Day-one ship.
2187: - No region-locked features.
2188: - No "this feature is unavailable in your country."
2189: 
2190: ### 13.5 Low-end devices
2191: 
2192: - The Compiler ladder degrades to handle low-end hardware naturally
2193:   (a 2GB-RAM Android phone defaults to audio-only).
2194: - Semantic Engine model packs available in size tiers (10 MB voice,
2195:   50 MB voice, 200 MB video). User device selects largest pack that
2196:   fits.
2197: - OneField R&D path is the long-term answer to bandwidth poverty:
2198:   3 kbps voice on a $20 mesh-radio module reaches every village.
2199:

2202: ## Part 14 — Honest Limits & Dependencies
2203: 
2204: ### 14.1 Open audit findings (BLOCKERS for ship)
2205: 
2206: | Finding | Severity | Status | Blocks |
2207: |---|---|---|---|
2208: | C1 — Browser SDP attestation unsigned | CRITICAL | In flight | Tier α |
2209: | C2 — Master VK silent rotation post-TOFU | CRITICAL | In flight | Tier α |
2210: | C5 — At-rest chat/group encryption | CRITICAL | Partial (Tier A only) | Tier β recording feature |
2211: | H7-H15 | HIGH | Open per May-14 audit | Various, not call-blocking |
2212: 
2213: Voice/video MUST NOT ship past Tier α-pre until C1 + C2 are closed
2214: and regression-tested.
2215: 
2216: ### 14.2 Research-grade dependencies
2217: 
2218: | Dependency | Status | Tier blocked |
2219: |---|---|---|
2220: | Articulatory voice model weights | Does not exist | ζ |
2221: | Scene-graph video model weights | Does not exist | θ |
2222: | PINN waveform synth weights | Does not exist | OneField R&D |
2223: | HackRF Pro hardware | Not yet acquired | OneField R&D |
2224: 
2225: None of these block Tier α-η. The product is shippable without any
2226: of them; the alien tier requires them.
2227: 
2228: ### 14.3 Platform constraints
2229: 
2230: - **iOS**: Background audio capture restricted. Native Swift wrapper
2231:   required for full functionality; PWA path has limited capability.
2232:   Plan: ship Mac + Android + PWA first; iOS native last.
2233: - **Android**: Generally permissive but battery management aggressive
2234:   in low-end OEM skins. Plan: foreground service for active calls.
2235: - **Browser**: WebRTC stack varies; Chrome / Edge / Firefox tested
2236:   baseline. Safari may need polyfills.
2237: 
2238: ### 14.4 Network constraints
2239: 
2240: - **NAT traversal**: Existing ICE infrastructure handles 80%+ of
2241:   cases. Symmetric NAT requires relay (federated, free).
2242: - **Firewalls**: QUIC over UDP/443 is the most-portable transport.
2243:   Fallback to TLS-over-TCP/443 for restrictive networks.
2244: 
2245: ### 14.5 Patent landscape
2246: 
2247: Neural codec IP is contested:
2248: - Google: Lyra family patents
2249: - Meta: Encodec / SoundStream patents
2250: - NVIDIA: Maxine face-reenactment patents
2251: 
2252: OneField's S_ONE → coherence-prior derivation provides an
2253: independent-invention foundation, but a defensive patent pool
2254: (extending [PATENTS.md](../../../OneField%20Mesh/PATENTS.md)) and
2255: careful publication-first strategy is essential before the Semantic
2256: Engine ships externally.
2257: 
2258: ### 14.6 Honest non-claims
2259: 
2260: - "Quantum-resistant info-theoretic privacy" claim from
2261:   [VOICE_VIDEO_ALIEN_TECH.md](../../../OneField%20Mesh/docs/VOICE_VIDEO_ALIEN_TECH.md)
2262:   needs rewriting. It is a large symmetric pre-shared key, not a new
2263:   quantum-immune primitive. Defensible technically, but the framing
2264:   must be tightened before any external pitch.
2265: - "1000× better than Zoom" — true for specific metrics (bandwidth per
2266:   intelligible call-minute under bad networks; call survival under
2267:   network failure), not uniformly. Pitch the experience, not the
2268:   number.

2272: ## Part 15 — Glossary
2273: 
2274: | Term | Meaning |
2275: |---|---|
2276: | **Ambient presence** | The lowest-intensity rung; faint awareness without active session. |
2277: | **AEAD** | Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data; one-shot encrypt-and-sign primitive. |
2278: | **Body Engine** | Multi-Device Body Engine; arbitrates surface roles across user's devices. |
2279: | **Call Immune System** | The 100ms-tick controller that watches vitals and requests representation changes. |
2280: | **Capability (cap)** | Macaroon-attenuable token granting a specific right (file send, semantic media, recording). |
2281: | **CallSession** | The top-level CRDT object representing one call. |
2282: | **CallVitals** | Per-tick read-only snapshot of all health signals. |
2283: | **Compiler** | Presence Compiler; picks the active rung. |
2284: | **Confirm ratio** | Predictive Continuity metric: fraction of predicted frames that match real arrivals. |
2285: | **Crossfade protocol** | 200ms overlap window during route or surface handoff. |
2286: | **CRDT** | Conflict-Free Replicated Data Type; lattice-based eventual consistency. |
2287: | **Doctrine of Invisibility** | The list of surfaces we refuse to ship, and what engines must do instead. |
2288: | **EWMA** | Exponentially Weighted Moving Average; smoothing of streaming statistics. |
2289: | **FrameProvenance** | 32-byte per-frame HMAC tag attesting kind / device / path / recording state. |
2290: | **Hysteresis** | Two-threshold trigger preventing oscillation between two states. |
2291: | **Intensity dial** | The continuous variable of presence; "call" is one position. |
2292: | **Linked mesh** | Row 8: user's own devices act as one identity to outsiders, separately addressable to user. |
2293: | **LWW Register** | Last-Writer-Wins CRDT; tie-broken by (timestamp, master_vk). |
2294: | **Master VK** | Master Verification Key; the long-lived identity public key. |
2295: | **Macaroon** | Attenuable HMAC-chained capability token (`ol_capability`). |
2296: | **OR-set** | Observed-Remove set; CRDT add-wins lattice. |
2297: | **Provenance dot** | The calm UI indicator that opens the trust pane. |
2298: | **Reality Engine** | Cryptographic Reality Engine; signs every frame. |
2299: | **Rung** | One of 9 representations on the Compiler ladder (raw_av down to ambient_presence). |
2300: | **SAS** | Short Authentication String; 5-word verification on first call. |
2301: | **Semantic delta** | Wire format that carries change-in-meaning, not change-in-pixels. |
2302: | **Surface** | An ephemeral output (a TV, a speaker, a watch) — distinct from a *device*. |
2303: | **τ_c** | Coherence time field; the unifying physics primitive in OneField. |
2304: | **TOFU** | Trust-On-First-Use; pinning identity on first contact. |
2305: | **Vector clock** | Per-node logical clock used for CRDT happens-before. |

   1: # One Link Validation Gates
   2: 
   3: Status: in_progress
   4: Last updated: 2026-05-07
   5: 
   6: These gates turn the We Are One doctrine into release criteria. A release is
   7: not production-ready for normal people until these behaviors are proven by
   8: automated tests or explicit manual evidence.
   9: 
  10: ## 1. File Transfer Gate
  11: 
  12: - Zero-byte, one-byte, text, binary, large, and huge-file cases.
  13: - Filenames with spaces and supported Unicode.
  14: - Duplicate file sends transmit no unnecessary bytes when CDC is available.
  15: - Renamed duplicate files are recognized by content.
  16: - Interrupted sends become paused/resumable, not silently failed.
  17: - Daemon/UI restart preserves transfer ledger state.
  18: - Receiver write failure does not create a completed file.
  19: - Corrupt chunks are rejected and retried.
  20: - Final manifest/hash verification is mandatory.
  21: 
  22: ## 2. Compatibility Gate
  23: 
  24: - Current client to previous compatible minor version.
  25: - Previous compatible minor version to current client.
  26: - Unknown optional fields are ignored safely.
  27: - Unsupported required features return a structured reason.
  28: - File transfer falls back from CDC to baseline mode when needed.
  29: - Chat remains available when advanced transfer features differ.
  30: - Group features degrade cleanly where possible.
  31: 
  32: ## 3. Security Gate
  33: 
  34: - Bad signature rejected.
  35: - Bad AEAD tag rejected.
  36: - Replay frame rejected.
  37: - Too-old sequence rejected.
  38: - Bad timestamp rejected.
  39: - Key-change warning generated and surfaced.
  40: - Path traversal rejected.
  41: - Local HTTP API requires token.
  42: - Unauthorized peer cannot send files or request folder data.
  43: - Blocked peer remains blocked across reconnect.
  44: 
  45: ## 4. Reliability Gate
  46: 
  47: - Peer disappears mid-send.
  48: - Peer changes IP/port.
  49: - Peer returns after delay.
  50: - Connection reset.
  51: - Latency spike.
  52: - Frame truncation.
  53: - Multiple concurrent transfers.
  54: - UI reload during transfer.
  55: - Daemon restart during transfer.
  56: - Transfer status never spins forever without watchdog intervention.
  57: 
  58: ## 5. Storage Gate
  59: 
  60: - Blob writes are atomic.
  61: - Partial temp files are cleaned up.
  62: - Corrupt stored blob is detected.
  63: - Missing blob is reported, not treated as complete.
  64: - Cache audit reports verified and corrupt counts.
  65: - Duplicate blobs are stored once.
  66: 
  67: ## 6. Mesh Gate
  68: 
  69: - Self peers are suppressed.
  70: - Duplicate endpoints collapse to one device identity.
  71: - Stale peers disappear automatically.
  72: - Paired offline devices remain visible as paired devices, not ghosts.
  73: - Reachability status is structured.
  74: - Chunk availability can be reconciled across multiple trusted devices.
  75: 
  76: ## 7. UX Gate
  77: 
  78: - First-run user knows how to pair.
  79: - Selected direct conversation or group is obvious.
  80: - File send has an obvious button and drag/drop.
  81: - Group settings include members, rename, invite, and leave.
  82: - Recoverable version drift does not create a giant panic banner.
  83: - Advanced warnings use human language.
  84: - Normal cleanup is automatic.
  85: 
  86: ## Current Phase 1 Focus
  87: 
  88: - Protocol compatibility negotiation.
  89: - Replay-window primitive.
  90: - Blob-store corruption and temp cleanup.
  91: - Transfer fault classification.
  92: - Peer registry stability.

   1: # One Setup: First-Run Experience
   2: 
   3: Status: design target
   4: 
   5: One Link should not have a weak tutorial. It should have a beautiful first-run experience that helps a person become ready, safe, and confident without feeling taught.
   6: 
   7: The goal is not to explain the app. The goal is to make One Link work for the person in front of it.
   8: 
   9: Core promise:
  10: 
  11: > Your devices become one private fabric. No account. No cloud dependency. No confusion. You are One.
  12: 
  13: ## Product Bar
  14: 
  15: This is the bar a billion-dollar product team would hold:
  16: 
  17: - The user reaches a real win in under 60 seconds.
  18: - The user can skip setup without punishment.
  19: - The app teaches by doing, not by lecturing.
  20: - Every screen has one obvious primary action.
  21: - Advanced concepts are proven visually, not explained in walls of text.
  22: - Privacy, trust, recovery, and device safety are part of setup from the beginning.
  23: - The experience feels calm, premium, human, and inevitable.
  24: 
  25: This should feel less like "here is a tutorial" and more like "One Link just woke up around me."
  26: 
  27: ## Doctrine Alignment
  28: 
  29: The existing Doctrine of Invisibility rejects onboarding tours, coach marks, and tip popups. This document respects that.
  30: 
  31: One Setup is not a tour. It is a setup flow that performs real work:
  32: 
  33: - creates or confirms identity
  34: - names the current device
  35: - pairs another trusted device
  36: - sends a first message or file
  37: - proves the route and privacy state
  38: - explains recovery only when the user has enough trust context
  39: 
  40: After first run, there must be no nagging tutorial popups. The app may show quiet contextual empty states and one-line next actions, but it must not become a classroom.
  41: 
  42: ## Audience Modes
  43: 
  44: One Setup needs two explanation layers.
  45: 
  46: ### Human Mode
  47: 
  48: Default for everyone.
  49: 
  50: Purpose:
  51: 
  52: - explain what One Link is doing in plain language
  53: - avoid system jargon
  54: - focus on confidence, safety, and useful actions
  55: - show proof without making the user decode engineering terms
  56: 
  57: Human Mode phrases:
  58: 
  59: - "Add your phone"
  60: - "Trust this device"
  61: - "Send a test message"
  62: - "Sent directly"
  63: - "No account was used"
  64: - "Freeze a lost device"
  65: - "Clear app traces"
  66: - "One Link picked the best path"
  67: 
  68: Human Mode must answer:
  69: 
  70: - What should I do next?
  71: - Is this safe?
  72: - Did it work?
  73: - Where did my file/message go?
  74: - What can I do if a device is lost?
  75: 
  76: ### Technical Mode
  77: 
  78: Optional, available from Settings and Details disclosures.
  79: 
  80: Purpose:
  81: 
  82: - give technical users a precise view of what happened
  83: - expose diagnostics, route details, trust material summaries, and audit events
  84: - help developers, admins, and power users verify the system
  85: - never be required for normal use
  86: 
  87: Entry points:
  88: 
  89: - Settings > Setup > Technical view
  90: - Privacy proof > Details
  91: - Activity > One Now > Details
  92: - Device card > Advanced
  93: - Transfer details disclosure
  94: 
  95: Technical Mode phrases:
  96: 
  97: - root identity
  98: - device certificate
  99: - self-mesh enrollment
 100: - trust code / SAS
 101: - secure channel
 102: - route candidate
 103: - remote instruction
 104: - capability scope
 105: - replay protection
 106: - audit event
 107: - transport path
 108: - CDC/native fast path
 109: 
 110: Technical Mode must answer:
 111: 
 112: - Which identity/device key was used?
 113: - Which device certificate was enrolled?
 114: - Which route was selected and why?
 115: - Was the channel authenticated?
 116: - Was replay protection active?
 117: - Which capabilities allowed the action?
 118: - Which audit event proves it happened?
 119: - What fallback path was used if direct transport failed?
 120: 
 121: Technical Mode should be a separate layer, not a separate product. The same setup step can render both a plain explanation and a technical receipt.
 122: 
 123: ## System Translation Map
 124: 
 125: One Link has advanced systems under the hood. The setup experience must translate each one into words people understand.
 126: 
 127: | Real system | Human words | Technical view |
 128: | --- | --- | --- |
 129: | Root identity | Your One identity | Root identity, recovery material, signing authority |
 130: | Device certificate | This device belongs to you | Device cert, issuer, fingerprint, expiry/revocation |
 131: | Self-mesh | Your personal device fabric | Self-mesh device graph, presence, target selection |
 132: | Pairing invite | Add a device | Short-lived invite, QR payload, expiry, nonce |
 133: | SAS verification | Check the trust code | Transcript-bound SAS, authentication confirmation |
 134: | Secure channel | Private trusted connection | Encrypted session, peer fingerprint, replay window |
 135: | Comms fabric | Best private path | Route candidates, score, transport, fallback |
 136: | Remote instruct | Ask another device to do this | Signed command, capability scope, nonce, audit id |
 137: | File send | Send a file | Transfer id, route, CDC chunks, wire bytes, cache savings |
 138: | Folder sync | Keep this folder matched | Folder root, watcher, manifest, conflict policy |
 139: | Privacy proof | What happened receipt | Route truth, channel state, audit event, policy decisions |
 140: | Clear traces | Clear app history here | Trace categories, local records, retention policy |
 141: | Freeze device | Block a lost device | Freeze command, authority proof, propagation status |
 142: | Revoke device | Permanently remove trust | Revocation record, cert invalidation, audit event |
 143: | Recovery device | A trusted way back in | Recovery authority, quorum or trusted-device policy |
 144: 
 145: The user should never need the right column to succeed. The right column exists so technical people can verify and trust the system.
 146: 
 147: ## Expert System Inventory
 148: 
 149: One Setup should be built by understanding the whole One Link system, not by guessing at generic onboarding patterns.
 150: 
 151: The setup flow must know how these systems work:
 152: 
 153: - identity creation and import
 154: - current-device naming
 155: - root identity and device certificate minting
 156: - self-mesh enrollment
 157: - self-mesh presence and best-device selection
 158: - QR/code pairing
 159: - trust-code verification
 160: - peer/device list rendering
 161: - secure channel establishment
 162: - chat send path
 163: - file send path
 164: - received file inbox
 165: - sent transfer status
 166: - folder sync setup
 167: - local/no-router guide
 168: - courier fallback
 169: - remote instruction policy
 170: - capability scopes
 171: - privacy proof and audit events
 172: - trace clearing and local wipe semantics
 173: - stolen/lost device freeze
 174: - permanent revocation
 175: - recovery-device flow
 176: - calls/video readiness
 177: - camera/mic permissions
 178: - desktop packaged app behavior
 179: - mobile/browser peer behavior
 180: 
 181: If a setup step talks about one of these systems, it must use the real API/state behind that system. No fake completed checkmarks.

 204: ## Modes
 205: 
 206: One Setup has three modes.
 207: 
 208: ### 1. Full Setup
 209: 
 210: Shown on first launch when the app detects no completed setup and no trusted peer.
 211: 
 212: Purpose:
 213: 
 214: - make this device ready
 215: - pair one additional device if possible
 216: - produce the first successful transfer or message
 217: - show privacy proof
 218: 
 219: ### 2. Quick Start
 220: 
 221: For users who do not want setup.
 222: 
 223: Purpose:
 224: 
 225: - skip the full flow
 226: - land in the app immediately
 227: - keep a small Setup checklist available in Activity or Settings
 228: 
 229: The skip button must be clear:
 230: 
 231: **Skip for now**
 232: 
 233: Skipping should set `one_setup_skipped_at_ms`, not `one_setup_completed`.
 234: 
 235: ### 3. Resume Setup
 236: 
 237: Available from Activity, Settings, and empty states.
 238: 
 239: Purpose:
 240: 
 241: - let the user continue setup later
 242: - never force them back into a modal
 243: - show progress as plain completed items
 244: 
 245: ## First Launch Decision
 246: 
 247: On first launch, One Link should decide what the person needs.
 248: 
 249: Inputs:
 250: 
 251: - paired peers count
 252: - self-mesh devices count
 253: - root identity exists
 254: - display name exists
 255: - onboarding/setup completion flags
 256: - camera permission availability
 257: - mic permission availability
 258: - local network permission/connectivity state
 259: - inbox has files
 260: - outgoing transfers exist
 261: - app traces exist
 262: - recovery contact/device exists
 263: - current device has been seen before
 264: 
 265: Decision examples:
 266: 
 267: - No identity, no devices: show One Setup.
 268: - Identity exists, no paired devices: show Add Device step.
 269: - One trusted device exists, no successful send: show First Send step.
 270: - Successful send exists, no safety review: show Safety step quietly.
 271: - User skipped: go straight to the app and show one Setup checklist chip.
 272: - Returning user: never show the full-screen setup automatically.
 273: 
 274: ## Primary User Journey
 275: 
 276: The ideal first-run journey:
 277: 
 278: 1. Welcome
 279: 2. Name this device
 280: 3. Create or confirm One identity
 281: 4. Add phone or laptop
 282: 5. Verify trust
 283: 6. Send first thing
 284: 7. See privacy proof
 285: 8. Safety and recovery
 286: 9. Finish into the real app
 287: 
 288: This is the only flow we should consider "complete."

 490: ## Screen 5: Verify Trust
 491: 
 492: Purpose:
 493: 
 494: Make security understandable and meaningful.
 495: 
 496: Headline:
 497: 
 498: **Check the trust code**
 499: 
 500: Body:
 501: 
 502: Both devices should show the same code.
 503: 
 504: Visual:
 505: 
 506: - six-digit SAS code in large type
 507: - optional visual pattern/art
 508: - device names on both sides
 509: - "What if it does not match?" disclosure
 510: 
 511: Primary action:
 512: 
 513: **Codes match**
 514: 
 515: Secondary action:
 516: 
 517: **Codes do not match**
 518: 
 519: Helpful actions:
 520: 
 521: - **Read code aloud**
 522: - **Show visual code**
 523: 
 524: Behavior:
 525: 
 526: - `Codes match` enrolls the device.
 527: - `Codes do not match` cancels pairing, records rejected trust event, and explains calmly.
 528: - The flow must never auto-trust a device without a clear user confirmation.
 529: 
 530: Copy for mismatch:
 531: 
 532: Stop here. The devices did not prove they are talking directly to each other. Try again when both screens are in front of you.
 533: 
 534: Security requirements:
 535: 
 536: - SAS must be bound to the actual pairing transcript.
 537: - Trust confirmation must be explicit.
 538: - Replayed invite codes must fail.
 539: - Expired invites must fail.
 540: - All trust decisions must be audit-visible.

 642: ## Screen 8: Safety And Recovery
 643: 
 644: Purpose:
 645: 
 646: Teach stolen-device safety without making the user afraid.
 647: 
 648: Headline:
 649: 
 650: **If a device is lost**
 651: 
 652: Body:
 653: 
 654: You can freeze a trusted device from another trusted device.
 655: 
 656: Primary action:
 657: 
 658: **Review safety**
 659: 
 660: Secondary action:
 661: 
 662: **Do this later**
 663: 
 664: Safety checklist:
 665: 
 666: - Freeze a lost device
 667: - Revoke a device permanently
 668: - Clear app traces on this device
 669: - Keep original computer files unless user chooses otherwise
 670: - Recover a device if it was a mistake
 671: 
 672: Recommended setup:
 673: 
 674: - choose one recovery device
 675: - explain that recovery requires an already trusted device or recovery key
 676: - do not allow random remote "mark stolen" without authority
 677: 
 678: Important copy:
 679: 
 680: Freezing protects your One Link access. It does not erase your whole computer.
 681: 
 682: Security requirements:
 683: 
 684: - freeze requires authenticated trusted authority
 685: - revoke requires stronger confirmation
 686: - stolen-device action must be visible in audit
 687: - recovery must not let an attacker unfreeze themselves
 688: - local wipe must explain exactly what it clears
 689:

 891: - Your phone is nearby. Add it?
 892: - First message sent. View privacy proof?
 893: - Desktop is faster for this file. Use it?
 894: - Laptop has not checked in for 3 days. Review?
 895: - You have duplicate received files. Collapse list?
 896: - Everything is quiet.
 897: 
 898: One Now must never feel like an ad banner. It is the system being helpful.
 899: 
 900: ## Skip Behavior
 901: 
 902: Skip must be first-class.
 903: 
 904: When the user clicks **Skip for now**:
 905: 
 906: - close setup immediately
 907: - set `one_setup_skipped_at_ms`
 908: - do not set completed
 909: - do not show setup automatically again for at least 7 days
 910: - keep checklist available
 911: - use empty states instead of popups
 912: 
 913: If the user skips during an in-progress pairing:
 914: 
 915: - ask whether to cancel pairing
 916: - revoke/expire pending invite
 917: - leave no half-trusted device
 918: 
 919: If the user skips after identity creation:
 920: 
 921: - keep identity
 922: - mark remaining steps as recommended
 923: 
 924: If the user skips after pairing:
 925: 
 926: - keep trusted device
 927: - recommend first send
 928: 
 929: ## Accessibility
 930: 
 931: Requirements:
 932: 
 933: - full keyboard navigation
 934: - visible focus rings
 935: - Esc behavior consistent
 936: - screen-reader labels for every input and primary button
 937: - no icon-only required actions
 938: - QR code has code fallback
 939: - SAS code can be copied and read aloud
 940: - text contrast passes WCAG AA
 941: - motion reduced when `prefers-reduced-motion`
 942: - progress must not rely on color alone
 943: 
 944: Onboarding name input must have:
 945: 
 946: - visible label or screen-reader label
 947: - placeholder
 948: - validation message
 949: 
 950: ## Visual Direction
 951: 
 952: Tone:
 953: 
 954: - calm
 955: - private
 956: - premium
 957: - direct
 958: - human
 959: 
 960: Layout:
 961: 
 962: - full-screen or centered setup shell
 963: - narrow readable content
 964: - one primary action
 965: - secondary action visible but quiet
 966: - device cards over text-heavy explanations
 967: - real status receipts
 968: - concise copy
 969: 
 970: Avoid:
 971: 
 972: - marketing feature grids
 973: - giant paragraphs
 974: - nested cards
 975: - purple-only palette
 976: - cluttered settings language
 977: - scary security warnings unless there is actual risk
 978: 
 979: Device card fields:
 980: 
 981: - device name
 982: - device type
 983: - trust state
 984: - last seen
 985: - role: this device / trusted device / pending
 986: 
 987: Trust receipt fields:
 988: 
 989: - encrypted
 990: - identity verified
 991: - route used
 992: - replay protection
 993: - audit recorded
 994: 
 995: ## Copy Principles
 996: 
 997: Use:
 998: 
 999: - "Add your phone"
1000: - "Codes match"
1001: - "Freeze a lost device"
1002: - "Clear app traces"
1003: - "No account needed"
1004: - "Sent directly"
1005: - "Your devices are ready"
1006: 
1007: Avoid:
1008: 
1009: - "cryptographic identity root"
1010: - "self-mesh enrollment certificate"
1011: - "remote instruction capability"
1012: - "transport operator guide"
1013: - "daemon"
1014: - "SAS" unless paired with "trust code"
1015: 
1016: Technical language can exist in Details disclosures, never in the main path.
1017:

1052: ## API Requirements
1053: 
1054: Needed endpoints or endpoint capabilities:
1055: 
1056: - read setup status
1057: - write setup status
1058: - create root identity
1059: - import identity
1060: - name current device
1061: - mint short-lived device invite
1062: - poll pairing status
1063: - confirm trust code match
1064: - reject trust code
1065: - send test message
1066: - send generated test file
1067: - fetch privacy proof for last setup action
1068: - fetch safety status
1069: - configure recovery device
1070: - mark setup complete
1071: - mark setup skipped
1072: - fetch setup checklist
1073: - fetch technical setup diagnostics
1074: - rerun technical setup diagnostics
1075: - export setup receipt
1076: 
1077: Every mutation must return:
1078: 
1079: - success/failure
1080: - user-safe message
1081: - next suggested step
1082: - audit event id where relevant

1084: ## Settings Integration
1085: 
1086: Settings should include a dedicated Setup page.
1087: 
1088: Name:
1089: 
1090: **Setup**
1091: 
1092: Default view:
1093: 
1094: - Human Mode checklist
1095: - Resume setup
1096: - Add device
1097: - Review safety
1098: - Privacy proof
1099: 
1100: Technical toggle:
1101: 
1102: **Show technical setup details**
1103: 
1104: When enabled, Settings shows:
1105: 
1106: - identity status
1107: - device certificate status
1108: - self-mesh device graph
1109: - current route candidates
1110: - last secure channel proof
1111: - last transfer proof
1112: - replay protection status
1113: - capability scopes
1114: - recent setup audit events
1115: - run diagnostics button
1116: - export technical receipt button
1117: 
1118: Technical receipt export:
1119: 
1120: - JSON for machines
1121: - Markdown for humans
1122: - must redact secrets by default
1123: - explicit "include sensitive material" should not exist unless a future security design proves it safe
1124: 
1125: The Settings page should make One Link feel powerful without making the main UI complicated.
1126: 
1127: ## Dual Copy Examples
1128: 
1129: Every major event should have Human Mode and Technical Mode copy.
1130: 
1131: ### Identity Created
1132: 
1133: Human:
1134: 
1135: Your One identity is ready. This device can now add your other devices.
1136: 
1137: Technical:
1138: 
1139: Root identity exists. Local device certificate minted and bound to current device.
1140: 
1141: ### Device Paired
1142: 
1143: Human:
1144: 
1145: Your phone is trusted.
1146: 
1147: Technical:
1148: 
1149: Device certificate enrolled under root identity. Trust-code confirmation completed. Audit event recorded.
1150: 
1151: ### First Message Sent
1152: 
1153: Human:
1154: 
1155: Message sent privately to your trusted device.
1156: 
1157: Technical:
1158: 
1159: Secure channel active. Message dispatched to selected peer target. Replay protection enabled.
1160: 
1161: ### File Sent
1162: 
1163: Human:
1164: 
1165: File sent. One Link only moved the pieces it needed.
1166: 
1167: Technical:
1168: 
1169: Transfer completed through selected route. CDC/cache savings recorded. Wire bytes and effective speed available in transfer proof.
1170: 
1171: ### Device Frozen
1172: 
1173: Human:
1174: 
1175: This device is blocked from One Link until you recover it.
1176: 
1177: Technical:
1178: 
1179: Freeze command accepted from trusted authority, signed, audited, and propagated to known devices.
1180: 
1181: ### Traces Cleared
1182: 
1183: Human:
1184: 
1185: One Link cleared this app's local history for the selected area. Your original computer files were not deleted.
1186: 
1187: Technical:
1188: 
1189: Selected local trace categories cleared. File-system originals untouched. Audit event recorded.
1190: 
1191: ## Failure States
1192: 
1193: Failures must be calm and recoverable.
1194: 
1195: ### Pairing Timeout
1196: 
1197: Message:
1198: 
1199: The invite expired. Create a fresh one when both devices are nearby.
1200: 
1201: Action:
1202: 
1203: **Create new invite**
1204: 
1205: ### Trust Code Mismatch
1206: 
1207: Message:
1208: 
1209: The codes did not match, so One Link stopped before trusting anything.
1210: 
1211: Action:
1212: 
1213: **Try again**
1214: 
1215: ### Network Not Available
1216: 
1217: Message:
1218: 
1219: One Link cannot see another device yet.
1220: 
1221: Actions:
1222: 
1223: - **Use same Wi-Fi**
1224: - **Use cable**
1225: - **Use code**
1226: - **Pair later**
1227: 
1228: ### Permission Blocked
1229: 
1230: Message:
1231: 
1232: One Link needs camera permission on the device scanning the QR.
1233: 
1234: Actions:
1235: 
1236: - **Use code instead**
1237: - **Open permission help**
1238: 
1239: ### First Send Failed
1240: 
1241: Message:
1242: 
1243: The device is trusted, but the send did not finish. One Link can retry or use another path.
1244: 
1245: Actions:
1246: 
1247: - **Retry**
1248: - **Use best path**
1249: - **Show details**
1250: 
1251: ## Security Red-Team Cases
1252: 
1253: The setup flow must defend against:
1254: 
1255: - invite replay
1256: - expired invite reuse
1257: - QR screenshot reuse
1258: - pairing race with malicious nearby device
1259: - trust code mismatch ignored by user
1260: - device name spoofing
1261: - duplicate device names causing confusion
1262: - unauthorized freeze/revoke
1263: - malicious "lost device" report
1264: - recovery device compromise
1265: - local trace wipe being misrepresented as full disk wipe
1266: - remote action capability escalation
1267: - pairing started by background page without user awareness
1268: 
1269: Required mitigations:
1270: 
1271: - short-lived invites
1272: - explicit trust confirmation
1273: - show device name and fingerprint fragment
1274: - clear pending state
1275: - audit every trust decision
1276: - stronger confirmation for revoke/wipe
1277: - freeze is reversible only through trusted authority
1278: - no silent remote access
1279: 
1280: ## Test Plan
1281: 
1282: Unit tests:
1283: 
1284: - setup state transitions
1285: - skip vs complete semantics
1286: - identity created only once
1287: - device name validation
1288: - invite expiration
1289: - trust-code mismatch rejection
1290: - privacy proof generation
1291: - audit event emission
1292: 
1293: UI tests:
1294: 
1295: - all setup buttons wired
1296: - skip works from every step
1297: - back/continue works from every step
1298: - QR fallback code visible
1299: - trust mismatch path visible
1300: - details disclosures hidden by default
1301: - checklist appears after skip
1302: - checklist disappears or marks complete after finish
1303: - empty states point to correct setup actions
1304: - keyboard-only completion path
1305: - Esc behavior
1306: 
1307: Integration tests:
1308: 
1309: - two daemon pairing
1310: - root identity created
1311: - device cert minted
1312: - trusted device enrolled
1313: - first message over actual channel
1314: - generated test file transfer
1315: - privacy proof references actual transfer
1316: - freeze/revoke visible after enrollment
1317: 
1318: Performance tests:
1319: 
1320: - setup status endpoint latency
1321: - invite creation latency
1322: - QR render latency
1323: - pairing poll interval avoids waste
1324: - first message dispatch latency
1325: - first file dispatch latency
1326: 
1327: Manual QA:
1328: 
1329: - first launch on clean profile
1330: - returning launch after complete
1331: - returning launch after skip
1332: - offline/no-router path
1333: - small window
1334: - high DPI
1335: - keyboard only
1336: - screen reader basics
1337: - reduced motion
1338: 
1339: ## Completion Criteria
1340: 
1341: One Setup is complete only when:
1342: 
1343: - first-run user can skip immediately
1344: - first-run user can complete the main setup path
1345: - setup performs real identity/device/send/proof work
1346: - no fake success states exist
1347: - every setup action has backend/API support
1348: - trust decisions are explicit and audited
1349: - failure states are recoverable
1350: - empty states point to useful next actions
1351: - setup checklist reflects real system state
1352: - tests cover skip, complete, pairing, first send, privacy proof, and safety review
1353: - the old passive four-slide onboarding is removed or replaced
1354: 
1355: ## Build Order
1356: 
1357: Recommended implementation order:
1358: 
1359: 1. Add setup state model and API status endpoint.
1360: 2. Replace old onboarding markup with One Setup shell.
1361: 3. Implement skip/complete persistence.
1362: 4. Wire device naming.
1363: 5. Wire identity create/import.
1364: 6. Wire add-device invite and pairing status.
1365: 7. Wire trust-code confirmation and rejection.
1366: 8. Wire first test message.
1367: 9. Wire generated test file.
1368: 10. Wire privacy proof receipt.
1369: 11. Wire safety/recovery review.
1370: 12. Add permanent Setup checklist.
1371: 13. Connect empty states and One Now.
1372: 14. Add exhaustive tests.
1373: 15. Remove stale onboarding copy and tests.
1374: 
1375: ## North Star
1376: 
1377: The user should finish setup thinking:
1378: 
1379: > I did not make an account. I did not learn a complicated system. My devices found each other, trusted each other, sent something, showed me proof, and gave me a way to protect myself if something goes wrong.
1380: 
1381: That is One Link.
1382: 
1383: For the people.
1384: 
1385: Just works.
1386: 
1387: We are One.
1388:

1391: # Product Design Addendum
1392: 
1393: This addendum turns One Setup from a product spec into a design and implementation pack.
1394: 
1395: It covers:
1396: 
1397: - wireframes
1398: - final user copy
1399: - motion and animation rules
1400: - personalization rules
1401: - success metrics
1402: - expanded security/abuse cases
1403: - families, teams, and shared-computer edge cases
1404: - accessibility depth
1405: - implementation tickets mapped to system areas
1406: - automated walkthrough requirements
1407: 
1408: ## Screen Wireframes
1409: 
1410: These are layout blueprints, not visual mocks. The actual UI should use the One Link design system and stay quiet, dense, and calm.
1411: 
1412: ### Welcome
1413: 
1414: ```text
1415: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1416: │                                              │
1417: │                 [One glyph]                  │
1418: │                                              │
1419: │                 You are One                  │
1420: │                                              │
1421: │  Your devices can talk directly, privately,  │
1422: │  and without an account.                     │
1423: │                                              │
1424: │      [ Set up One Link ]   [ Skip for now ]  │
1425: │                                              │
1426: │      No account   Encrypted   Works nearby   │
1427: │                                              │
1428: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1429: ```
1430: 
1431: Rules:
1432: 
1433: - no carousel
1434: - no feature list
1435: - no screenshot gallery
1436: - no marketing headline
1437: - the One Link name and promise must be obvious within one second
1438: 
1439: ### Name Device
1440: 
1441: ```text
1442: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1443: │  Step 1 of 6                                 │
1444: │                                              │
1445: │  Name this device                            │
1446: │  This name appears only to devices you trust.│
1447: │                                              │
1448: │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
1449: │  │ Alex's laptop                          │  │
1450: │  └────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
1451: │                                              │
1452: │  ┌────────────── Device card ─────────────┐  │
1453: │  │ Alex's laptop                          │  │
1454: │  │ This device                            │  │
1455: │  │ Ready to add your other devices        │  │
1456: │  └────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
1457: │                                              │
1458: │        [ Continue ]     [ Use default ]      │
1459: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1460: ```
1461: 
1462: Rules:
1463: 
1464: - show the result as a device card immediately
1465: - never ask the user to understand identity keys here
1466: - duplicate names get a friendly warning, not a hard block
1467: 
1468: ### Identity
1469: 
1470: ```text
1471: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1472: │  Step 2 of 6                                 │
1473: │                                              │
1474: │  Create your One identity                    │
1475: │  This lets your devices belong to you        │
1476: │  without an account.                         │
1477: │                                              │
1478: │  ┌────────────── Proof card ──────────────┐  │
1479: │  │ Account needed: No                     │  │
1480: │  │ Stored: On your devices                │  │
1481: │  │ Used for: Trusting your devices        │  │
1482: │  └────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
1483: │                                              │
1484: │      [ Create identity ]  [ I already have one ] │
1485: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1486: ```
1487: 
1488: Rules:
1489: 
1490: - identity creation should feel like setup, not security ceremony
1491: - raw recovery material stays hidden
1492: - import path is available but not dominant
1493: 
1494: ### Add Device
1495: 
1496: ```text
1497: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1498: │  Step 3 of 6                                 │
1499: │                                              │
1500: │  Add your phone or laptop                    │
1501: │  Open One Link on another device and scan.   │
1502: │                                              │
1503: │       ┌──────── QR code ────────┐            │
1504: │       │                         │            │
1505: │       │                         │            │
1506: │       └─────────────────────────┘            │
1507: │                                              │
1508: │       Code: 482 913     expires in 02:00     │
1509: │                                              │
1510: │  [ Use code instead ] [ Pair later ]         │
1511: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1512: ```
1513: 
1514: When a device is detected:
1515: 
1516: ```text
1517: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1518: │  Alex's laptop  ─────────────  Alex's phone  │
1519: │  This device                    Waiting      │
1520: │                                              │
1521: │              Check the code next             │
1522: │                                              │
1523: │                  [ Continue ]                │
1524: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1525: ```
1526: 
1527: Rules:
1528: 
1529: - the QR is the default
1530: - code fallback is always visible
1531: - expiration is visible
1532: - detected device appears before trust, clearly marked pending
1533: 
1534: ### Verify Trust
1535: 
1536: ```text
1537: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1538: │  Step 4 of 6                                 │
1539: │                                              │
1540: │  Check the trust code                        │
1541: │  Both devices should show this same code.    │
1542: │                                              │
1543: │                 482 913                      │
1544: │                                              │
1545: │  Alex's laptop                  Alex's phone │
1546: │  This device                    Pending      │
1547: │                                              │
1548: │  [ Codes match ] [ Codes do not match ]      │
1549: │                                              │
1550: │  [ Read aloud ] [ Show visual code ]         │
1551: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1552: ```
1553: 
1554: Rules:
1555: 
1556: - "Codes match" must be deliberate
1557: - mismatch must stop trust immediately
1558: - never phrase mismatch as user error
1559: 
1560: ### First Success
1561: 
1562: ```text
1563: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1564: │  Step 5 of 6                                 │
1565: │                                              │
1566: │  Send something to yourself                  │
1567: │  One Link will choose the best private path. │
1568: │                                              │
1569: │  ┌──────────── Target device ─────────────┐  │
1570: │  │ Alex's phone                           │  │
1571: │  │ Trusted and nearby                     │  │
1572: │  └────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
1573: │                                              │
1574: │  [ Send test message ] [ Send a file ]       │
1575: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1576: ```
1577: 
1578: Success state:
1579: 
1580: ```text
1581: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1582: │  Sent privately                              │
1583: │                                              │
1584: │  Encrypted        Yes                        │
1585: │  Trusted device   Alex's phone               │
1586: │  Account used     No                         │
1587: │  Route            Direct/local when possible │
1588: │                                              │
1589: │  [ View privacy proof ] [ Continue ]         │
1590: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1591: ```
1592: 
1593: Rules:
1594: 
1595: - default to test message
1596: - generated test file is second
1597: - user file picker is optional
1598: - proof is compact until expanded
1599: 
1600: ### Safety
1601: 
1602: ```text
1603: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1604: │  Step 6 of 6                                 │
1605: │                                              │
1606: │  If a device is lost                         │
1607: │  You can freeze it from another trusted      │
1608: │  device.                                    │
1609: │                                              │
1610: │  ┌──────────── Safety card ───────────────┐  │
1611: │  │ Freeze lost device                     │  │
1612: │  │ Revoke permanently                     │  │
1613: │  │ Clear app traces here                  │  │
1614: │  │ Keep original files unless you choose  │  │
1615: │  └────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
1616: │                                              │
1617: │  [ Review safety ] [ Do this later ]         │
1618: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1619: ```
1620: 
1621: Rules:
1622: 
1623: - safety should feel empowering, not scary
1624: - explain what freeze does and does not do
1625: - do not bury abuse protection
1626: 
1627: ### Finish
1628: 
1629: ```text
1630: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1631: │                                              │
1632: │              One Link is ready               │
1633: │                                              │
1634: │  ✓ Identity ready                            │
1635: │  ✓ This device named                         │
1636: │  ✓ Trusted device paired                     │
1637: │  ✓ First message sent                        │
1638: │  ✓ Privacy proof available                   │
1639: │                                              │
1640: │              [ Start using One Link ]        │
1641: └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1642: ```
1643: 
1644: Rules:
1645: 
1646: - land the user where their success happened
1647: - Chat if first message
1648: - Files if first file
1649: - Activity if setup skipped after safety

1852: 
1853: Technical Mode copy should be precise but still readable.

1856: 
1857: Root identity exists. Local device certificate minted and bound to this device.

1862: - local device fingerprint
1863: - certificate status
1864: - created at
1865: - recovery status

1868:

1870: 
1871: Fields:
1872: 
1873: - invite id
1874: - expires at
1875: - pending device fingerprint fragment
1876: - pairing transcript id
1877: - replay state
1878: 
1879: ### Trust
1880: 
1881: Trust-code confirmation accepted. Device certificate enrolled under root identity. Audit event recorded.

1888: - audit event id

1919: ## Motion And Animation Rules
1920: 
1921: Motion should make One Link feel alive, not busy.
1922: 
1923: Allowed:
1924: 
1925: - gentle fade between setup steps
1926: - device card slides in when a device is detected
1927: - connection line pulses while pairing is pending
1928: - trust confirmation completes with a short glow/check
1929: - transfer progress uses a restrained progress bar
1930: - success receipt settles into place
1931: 
1932: Avoid:
1933: 
1934: - bouncing UI
1935: - constant loops
1936: - confetti
1937: - dramatic warning animations
1938: - large layout shifts
1939: - motion tied to reading essential information
1940: 
1941: Durations:
1942: 
1943: - step transition: 160-220 ms
1944: - device detected: 220-280 ms
1945: - success confirmation: 260-360 ms
1946: - progress updates: no faster than necessary, coalesced to animation frames
1947: 
1948: Reduced motion:
1949: 
1950: - replace movement with opacity changes
1951: - no pulsing connection line
1952: - no sliding device cards
1953: 
1954: Motion principle:
1955: 
1956: The system should feel responsive, not performative.
1957: 
1958: ## Personalization Rules
1959: 
1960: One Setup should adapt without becoming creepy.
1961: 
1962: Signals allowed:
1963: 
1964: - local device type
1965: - current OS name
1966: - existing device names
1967: - setup completion state
1968: - paired device count
1969: - transfer history counts
1970: - local permission state
1971: - current network reachability
1972: - active risks
1973: 
1974: Signals avoided:
1975: 
1976: - reading user documents for personalization
1977: - inferring sensitive identity details
1978: - uploading behavior
1979: - cloud analytics
1980: 
1981: Examples:
1982: 
1983: - If on Windows desktop: suggest "Alex's PC" or "Desktop".
1984: - If a phone peer appears: say "Add your phone".
1985: - If no camera scan is possible: default to code entry.
1986: - If no network route is available: show local/no-router options.
1987: - If user already sent a file: skip first file and show privacy proof.
1988: - If user has many received duplicates: suggest collapsed view, not during first setup.
1989:

1993: 2. active setup task
1994: 3. first success
1995: 4. privacy proof
1996: 5. recovery

2038: ## Expanded Security And Abuse Cases
2039: 
2040: ### False Lost-Device Claims
2041: 
2042: Risk:
2043: 
2044: Someone tries to freeze a device they do not own or should not control.
2045: 
2046: Requirement:
2047: 
2048: - freeze requires trusted authority
2049: - show which trusted device requested freeze
2050: - allow review from another trusted device
2051: - record audit event
2052: - recovery cannot be completed by the frozen device alone
2053: 
2054: ### Coercive Device Revocation
2055: 
2056: Risk:
2057: 
2058: An abusive person forces or tricks another person into revoking a device.
2059: 
2060: Requirement:
2061: 
2062: - revoke copy must be clear and slow
2063: - require stronger confirmation
2064: - explain consequences
2065: - preserve audit record
2066: - offer "freeze first" as safer reversible action
2067: 
2068: ### Shared Computer
2069: 
2070: Risk:
2071: 
2072: Multiple people use the same OS account or machine.
2073: 
2074: Requirement:
2075: 
2076: - make device ownership clear
2077: - local traces warning must be explicit
2078: - offer app lock/session lock where available
2079: - setup should not expose paired device details on locked screen
2080: 
2081: ### Family Device
2082: 
2083: Risk:
2084: 
2085: A tablet or laptop belongs to a family, not one person.
2086: 
2087: Requirement:
2088: 
2089: - device name can reflect shared ownership
2090: - trust copy should say "devices you trust", not "devices you own" everywhere
2091: - technical mode shows exact identity/device owner state
2092: 
2093: ### Team/Work Device
2094: 
2095: Risk:
2096: 
2097: Work devices may have policies or multiple admins.
2098: 
2099: Requirement:
2100: 
2101: - avoid promising full local control if OS policy can override
2102: - technical receipt should show local-only proof, not compliance claims
2103: - allow setup skip and technical export for admin review
2104: 
2105: ### Attacker Nearby During Pairing
2106: 
2107: Risk:
2108: 
2109: Malicious device attempts to race pairing.
2110: 
2111: Requirement:
2112: 
2113: - pending device card must be visibly pending
2114: - trust code required
2115: - device name alone never proves trust
2116: - expired/replayed invite fails
2117: 
2118: ### QR Screenshot Reuse
2119: 
2120: Risk:
2121: 
2122: An invite QR is captured and reused.
2123: 
2124: Requirement:
2125: 
2126: - short expiration
2127: - nonce-bound invite
2128: - one-time use
2129: - clear expired state
2130: 
2131: ### User Misunderstands Clear Traces
2132: 
2133: Risk:
2134: 
2135: User thinks "clear traces" deletes original files.
2136: 
2137: Requirement:
2138: 
2139: - always say "One Link history on this device"
2140: - always say original computer files are not deleted unless a separate file action says so
2141: - preview categories before clearing
2142:
