   1: //! Per-frame and per-chunk encrypt / decrypt entry points.
   2: //!
   3: //! The chunk-level [`encrypt_chunk`] / [`decrypt_chunk`] functions
   4: //! divide a chunk plaintext into 16 KiB AEAD frames per
   5: //! [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md), encrypting
   6: //! each with its own nonce and 16-byte tag, and emit the on-wire layout
   7: //! `[ct_frame_0 || tag_0 || ct_frame_1 || tag_1 || ... ]`.
   8: //!
   9: //! For random-access reads (FUSE/FSKit/Dokan), the per-frame functions
  10: //! [`encrypt_frame`] / [`decrypt_frame`] operate on a single frame
  11: //! identified by `(chunk_id, frame_index)`. Reading a 64 KiB random
  12: //! offset from a 256 KiB chunk decrypts at most 2 frames (32 KiB) — the
  13: //! amplification cap from ADR-0002.
  14: 
  15: use ol_chunk::{frame_count_for_plaintext, AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN, AEAD_TAG_LEN};
  16: 
  17: use crate::cipher::AeadCipher;
  18: use crate::error::AeadError;
  19: use crate::nonce::frame_nonce;
  20: 
  21: /// Internal mirror of `AEAD_TAG_LEN` for use in stack-array sizes
  22: /// (`const` evaluation in `[u8; N]`). Identical to `AEAD_TAG_LEN`.
  23: pub(crate) const AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE: usize = AEAD_TAG_LEN;
  24: 
  25: /// Maximum supported chunk size for a single AEAD pipeline call.
  26: ///
  27: /// Per [ADR-0001](../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md), CDC
  28: /// produces chunks ≤ 256 KiB. The AEAD pipeline rejects larger inputs
  29: /// to keep the on-stack frame index calculation bounded.
  30: pub const MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN: usize = 256 * 1024;
  31: 
  32: /// View of a single AEAD frame within a chunk's on-wire ciphertext layout.
  33: ///
  34: /// `ciphertext_offset` is the byte offset in the chunk's ciphertext
  35: /// where the frame's ciphertext starts. `ciphertext_len` is the length
  36: /// of the frame's ciphertext (≤ 16 KiB; only the LAST frame may be
  37: /// shorter). The 16-byte tag follows immediately at
  38: /// `ciphertext_offset + ciphertext_len`.
  39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
  40: pub struct FrameRef {
  41:     /// Frame index within the chunk.
  42:     pub index: usize,
  43:     /// Plaintext offset within the chunk.
  44:     pub plaintext_offset: usize,
  45:     /// Plaintext length of this frame (max 16 KiB).
  46:     pub plaintext_len: usize,
  47:     /// Ciphertext offset within the on-wire layout.
  48:     pub ciphertext_offset: usize,
  49: }
  50: 
  51: impl FrameRef {
  52:     /// Length of this frame's tag in bytes (always 16).
  53:     #[inline]
  54:     #[must_use]
  55:     pub const fn tag_len(self) -> usize {
  56:         AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE
  57:     }
  58: 
  59:     /// Total on-wire length: plaintext + tag.
  60:     #[inline]
  61:     #[must_use]
  62:     pub const fn ciphertext_len_with_tag(self) -> usize {
  63:         self.plaintext_len + AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE
  64:     }
  65: }
  66: 
  67: /// Compute the ciphertext layout for a chunk plaintext of length `L`.
  68: ///
  69: /// Returns a Vec of [`FrameRef`] that describes each frame's plaintext
  70: /// and ciphertext positions. The last frame may be shorter than 16 KiB.
  71: #[must_use]
  72: pub fn frame_layout(plaintext_len: usize) -> Vec<FrameRef> {
  73:     let mut frames = Vec::with_capacity(frame_count_for_plaintext(plaintext_len));
  74:     let mut plaintext_offset = 0usize;
  75:     let mut ciphertext_offset = 0usize;
  76:     let mut index = 0usize;
  77:     while plaintext_offset < plaintext_len {
  78:         let remaining = plaintext_len - plaintext_offset;
  79:         let plaintext_len_this = remaining.min(AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN);
  80:         frames.push(FrameRef {
  81:             index,
  82:             plaintext_offset,
  83:             plaintext_len: plaintext_len_this,
  84:             ciphertext_offset,
  85:         });
  86:         plaintext_offset += plaintext_len_this;
  87:         ciphertext_offset += plaintext_len_this + AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE;
  88:         index += 1;
  89:     }
  90:     frames
  91: }
  92: 
  93: /// Encrypt a complete chunk plaintext into a single ciphertext buffer.
  94: ///
  95: /// Layout (per [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md)):
  96: /// `[ct_frame_0 || tag_0 || ct_frame_1 || tag_1 || ...]`.
  97: ///
  98: /// Output buffer length = `plaintext.len() + frame_count * AEAD_TAG_LEN`.
  99: ///
 100: /// # Errors
 101: ///
 102: /// - [`AeadError::PlaintextTooLarge`] if `plaintext.len() > MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN`.
 103: /// - [`AeadError::InvalidAad`] if `chunk_id` is not exactly 32 bytes.
 104: /// - [`AeadError::Authentication`] on encrypt failure (programming error).
 105: pub fn encrypt_chunk(
 106:     cipher: &AeadCipher,
 107:     chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 108:     plaintext: &[u8],
 109: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AeadError> {
 110:     if plaintext.len() > MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN {
 111:         return Err(AeadError::PlaintextTooLarge {
 112:             got: plaintext.len(),
 113:             max: MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN,
 114:         });
 115:     }
 116:     let frames = frame_layout(plaintext.len());
 117:     let total_ciphertext_len = plaintext.len() + frames.len() * AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE;
 118:     let mut output = Vec::with_capacity(total_ciphertext_len);
 119:     for f in &frames {
 120:         let nonce = frame_nonce(chunk_id, f.index as u64)?;
 121:         let plaintext_slice = &plaintext[f.plaintext_offset..f.plaintext_offset + f.plaintext_len];
 122:         // Append plaintext bytes; the cipher mutates them in-place into ciphertext.
 123:         let frame_start_in_output = output.len();
 124:         output.extend_from_slice(plaintext_slice);
 125:         let frame_buf = &mut output[frame_start_in_output..];
 126:         let tag = cipher.encrypt_in_place(&nonce, chunk_id.as_slice(), frame_buf)?;
 127:         output.extend_from_slice(&tag);
 128:     }
 129:     debug_assert_eq!(output.len(), total_ciphertext_len);
 130:     Ok(output)
 131: }
 132: 
 133: /// Decrypt a complete chunk ciphertext into the corresponding plaintext.
 134: ///
 135: /// Inverse of [`encrypt_chunk`]. Validates the on-wire layout and every
 136: /// frame's tag in constant time.
 137: ///
 138: /// # Errors
 139: ///
 140: /// - [`AeadError::InvalidCiphertextLength`] if `ciphertext` doesn't match
 141: ///   the expected `plaintext_len + frame_count * AEAD_TAG_LEN` shape.
 142: /// - [`AeadError::Authentication`] on any tag verification failure.
 143: pub fn decrypt_chunk(
 144:     cipher: &AeadCipher,
 145:     chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 146:     plaintext_len: usize,
 147:     ciphertext: &[u8],
 148: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AeadError> {
 149:     if plaintext_len > MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN {
 150:         return Err(AeadError::PlaintextTooLarge {
 151:             got: plaintext_len,
 152:             max: MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN,
 153:         });
 154:     }
 155:     let frames = frame_layout(plaintext_len);
 156:     let expected_ct_len = plaintext_len + frames.len() * AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE;
 157:     if ciphertext.len() != expected_ct_len {
 158:         return Err(AeadError::InvalidCiphertextLength {
 159:             expected: expected_ct_len,
 160:             got: ciphertext.len(),
 161:         });
 162:     }
 163:     let mut output = vec![0u8; plaintext_len];
 164:     let mut ct_cursor = 0usize;
 165:     for f in &frames {
 166:         let nonce = frame_nonce(chunk_id, f.index as u64)?;
 167:         // Slice out frame ciphertext + trailing tag.
 168:         let frame_ct = &ciphertext[ct_cursor..ct_cursor + f.plaintext_len];
 169:         let tag_slice = &ciphertext
 170:             [ct_cursor + f.plaintext_len..ct_cursor + f.plaintext_len + AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE];
 171:         let mut tag_arr = [0u8; AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE];
 172:         tag_arr.copy_from_slice(tag_slice);
 173:         // Copy ciphertext into the output buffer in the right plaintext position.
 174:         let pt_slice = &mut output[f.plaintext_offset..f.plaintext_offset + f.plaintext_len];
 175:         pt_slice.copy_from_slice(frame_ct);
 176:         cipher.decrypt_in_place(&nonce, chunk_id.as_slice(), pt_slice, &tag_arr)?;
 177:         ct_cursor += f.plaintext_len + AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE;
 178:     }
 179:     Ok(output)
 180: }
 181: 
 182: /// Encrypt a single frame.
 183: ///
 184: /// Used by streaming senders that emit frames one-at-a-time.
 185: /// `frame_plaintext.len()` must be ≤ `AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN`.
 186: ///
 187: /// # Errors
 188: ///
 189: /// As [`encrypt_chunk`].
 190: pub fn encrypt_frame(
 191:     cipher: &AeadCipher,
 192:     chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 193:     frame_index: u64,
 194:     frame_plaintext: &[u8],
 195: ) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, [u8; AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE]), AeadError> {
 196:     if frame_plaintext.len() > AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN {
 197:         return Err(AeadError::PlaintextTooLarge {
 198:             got: frame_plaintext.len(),
 199:             max: AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN,
 200:         });
 201:     }
 202:     let nonce = frame_nonce(chunk_id, frame_index)?;
 203:     let mut buf = frame_plaintext.to_vec();
 204:     let tag = cipher.encrypt_in_place(&nonce, chunk_id.as_slice(), &mut buf)?;
 205:     Ok((buf, tag))
 206: }
 207: 
 208: /// Decrypt a single frame.
 209: ///
 210: /// Used by random-access readers (FUSE/FSKit/Dokan) that decrypt only
 211: /// the frame containing the requested offset.
 212: ///
 213: /// # Errors
 214: ///
 215: /// - [`AeadError::Authentication`] on tag verification failure.
 216: pub fn decrypt_frame(
 217:     cipher: &AeadCipher,
 218:     chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 219:     frame_index: u64,
 220:     frame_ciphertext: &[u8],
 221:     tag: &[u8; AEAD_TAG_LEN_USIZE],
 222: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AeadError> {
 223:     let nonce = frame_nonce(chunk_id, frame_index)?;
 224:     let mut buf = frame_ciphertext.to_vec();
 225:     cipher.decrypt_in_place(&nonce, chunk_id.as_slice(), &mut buf, tag)?;
 226:     Ok(buf)
 227: }
 228: 
 229: /// Encrypt many chunks in parallel via rayon.
 230: ///
 231: /// Each chunk's encryption is independent (different chunk_id → different
 232: /// nonce + AAD), so the work shards cleanly across cores. Wins land
 233: /// around N ≥ 8 chunks; below that, rayon dispatch overhead dominates
 234: /// the per-chunk AEAD work (~12 µs/chunk at 64 KiB on AES-NI).
 235: ///
 236: /// Returns ciphertexts in input order. On failure for any chunk, the
 237: /// entire call returns `Err` (caller can retry or fall back to the
 238: /// sequential path).
 239: ///
 240: /// # Errors
 241: ///
 242: /// Returns the first per-chunk error encountered.
 243: pub fn encrypt_chunks_par(
 244:     cipher: &AeadCipher,
 245:     chunks: &[(&[u8; 32], &[u8])],
 246: ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, AeadError> {
 247:     use rayon::prelude::*;
 248:     chunks
 249:         .par_iter()
 250:         .map(|(id, pt)| encrypt_chunk(cipher, id, pt))
 251:         .collect()
 252: }
 253: 
 254: /// Decrypt many chunks in parallel via rayon. See [`encrypt_chunks_par`].
 255: ///
 256: /// Each input is `(chunk_id, plaintext_len, ciphertext)`; outputs are
 257: /// the recovered plaintexts in input order.
 258: ///
 259: /// # Errors
 260: ///
 261: /// Returns the first per-chunk error encountered.
 262: pub fn decrypt_chunks_par(
 263:     cipher: &AeadCipher,
 264:     chunks: &[(&[u8; 32], usize, &[u8])],
 265: ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, AeadError> {
 266:     use rayon::prelude::*;
 267:     chunks
 268:         .par_iter()
 269:         .map(|(id, pt_len, ct)| decrypt_chunk(cipher, id, *pt_len, ct))
 270:         .collect()
 271: }

   1: //! AEAD key material and zeroization.
   2: 
   3: use zeroize::{Zeroize, Zeroizing};
   4: 
   5: /// Length of an AEAD frame key in bytes.
   6: ///
   7: /// 32 bytes (256 bits) — both AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 use
   8: /// 256-bit keys per [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md).
   9: pub const FRAME_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  10: 
  11: /// A 32-byte AEAD key. Wraps the bytes in `Zeroizing` so the memory is
  12: /// cleared on drop, eliminating one common side-channel (post-use key
  13: /// material lingering in the heap).
  14: ///
  15: /// Construct via [`ChunkAeadKey::from_bytes`]; the inner array is private
  16: /// so callers don't accidentally clone the key elsewhere without zeroize
  17: /// coverage.
  18: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Zeroize)]
  19: #[zeroize(drop)]
  20: pub struct ChunkAeadKey {
  21:     inner: [u8; FRAME_KEY_LEN],
  22: }
  23: 
  24: impl ChunkAeadKey {
  25:     /// Construct a key from a 32-byte array.
  26:     ///
  27:     /// The caller is responsible for the upstream KDF: typically
  28:     /// `ol_chunk::blake3_wrap::derive_aead_key(ratchet_chain_key, chunk_id)`
  29:     /// per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md)
  30:     /// Rule 3.
  31:     #[inline]
  32:     #[must_use]
  33:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: [u8; FRAME_KEY_LEN]) -> Self {
  34:         Self { inner: bytes }
  35:     }
  36: 
  37:     /// Borrow the underlying bytes. Use sparingly; prefer the
  38:     /// `ChunkAeadKey` wrapper for everything because the wrapper handles
  39:     /// zeroize on drop.
  40:     #[inline]
  41:     #[must_use]
  42:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; FRAME_KEY_LEN] {
  43:         &self.inner
  44:     }
  45: }
  46: 
  47: /// Zeroizing wrapper for any 32-byte key material — used internally for
  48: /// derived per-frame keys (Phase C ratchet).
  49: #[allow(dead_code)]
  50: pub(crate) type SecretBytes = Zeroizing<[u8; FRAME_KEY_LEN]>;

   1: //! `ol_aead` — per-chunk AEAD pipeline for One Link's file engine v2.
   2: //!
   3: //! Implements [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md):
   4: //!
   5: //! - **Primary cipher**: AES-256-GCM via the RustCrypto `aes-gcm` crate.
   6: //!   Hardware-accelerated by AES-NI / VAES on x86 and ARMv8 cryptography
   7: //!   extensions on ARM64. ~5 GiB/s/core sustained on modern hardware.
   8: //! - **Fallback cipher**: ChaCha20-Poly1305 via the RustCrypto
   9: //!   `chacha20poly1305` crate. Constant-time by construction in software;
  10: //!   used when the runtime detects no hardware AES support. ~3 GiB/s/core.
  11: //! - **Frame layout**: a CDC chunk (8-256 KiB per [ADR-0001]) is divided
  12: //!   internally into one or more 16 KiB AEAD frames. Each frame has its
  13: //!   own nonce + auth tag. FUSE random-access reads decrypt only the
  14: //!   frame containing the requested offset, capping read amplification at
  15: //!   16-32 KiB.
  16: //! - **Nonce construction**: 96-bit nonce = `chunk_id_lo64 || frame_index_u32`.
  17: //!   chunk_id_lo64 derives from the BLAKE3 chunk address (raw or
  18: //!   convergent per [ADR-0006]). frame_index distinguishes frames within
  19: //!   a chunk. Reuse-impossible by construction.
  20: //! - **AAD binding**: each frame's authenticated additional data is the
  21: //!   full 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk_id, so a tampered chunk_id invalidates
  22: //!   the auth tag.
  23: //! - **Per-chunk forward-secret keys**: callers derive keys via
  24: //!   `ol_chunk::blake3_wrap::derive_aead_key` from a ratchet chain key
  25: //!   plus the chunk_id. This crate accepts a 32-byte key and does not
  26: //!   manage ratchet state itself; ratchet machinery lives in `ol_ratchet`
  27: //!   (Phase C).
  28: //! - **Constant-time tag compare**: handled by the underlying
  29: //!   RustCrypto AEAD trait (uses `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`).
  30: //! - **Zeroize**: all key material wraps in `Zeroizing` so dropping a
  31: //!   key clears the memory. Side-channel hardening per [ADR-0002].
  32: //!
  33: //! ## Throughput target
  34: //!
  35: //! Phase A1 verification gate: ≥ 4 GiB/s/core (AES-NI) or ≥ 3 GiB/s/core
  36: //! (ChaCha20-Poly1305) measured by `benches/aead_bench.rs`.
  37: //!
  38: //! ## Wire format
  39: //!
  40: //! For a chunk plaintext of length `L`, the on-wire ciphertext layout
  41: //! follows [ADR-0003]:
  42: //!
  43: //! ```text
  44: //! +-------------------+-------------------+----+-------------------+----+
  45: //! | frame 0 plaintext | frame 1 plaintext | T0 | frame 2 plaintext | T1 |   ...
  46: //! |   (16 KiB)        |   (16 KiB)        |16B |   (16 KiB)        |16B |
  47: //! +-------------------+-------------------+----+-------------------+----+
  48: //! ```
  49: //!
  50: //! ...where each `T_i` is the 16-byte authentication tag for the
  51: //! preceding 16 KiB plaintext frame, and the LAST frame may be shorter
  52: //! than 16 KiB. Total ciphertext length = `L + ceil(L/16384) * 16`.
  53: //!
  54: //! Wait — the layout above is informational, not normative. Implementations
  55: //! pack as `[ct_frame_0 || tag_0 || ct_frame_1 || tag_1 || ...]` for
  56: //! sequential streaming friendliness. The [`encrypt_chunk`] /
  57: //! [`decrypt_chunk`] functions emit/consume that exact ordering.
  58: //!
  59: //! [ADR-0001]: ../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md
  60: //! [ADR-0002]: ../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md
  61: //! [ADR-0003]: ../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md
  62: //! [ADR-0006]: ../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md
  63: 
  64: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_aead/0.21.0")]
  65: 
  66: pub mod cipher;
  67: pub mod convergent;
  68: pub mod error;
  69: pub mod frame;
  70: pub mod key;
  71: pub mod nonce;
  72: 
  73: pub use cipher::{AeadCipher, AeadKind, FrameKey};
  74: pub use convergent::{
  75:     content_type_from_extension, derive_convergent_aead_key, is_convergent_safe, resolve_mode,
  76:     ContentType, ConvergentPolicy, EncryptionMode, CONVERGENT_AEAD_KEY_CONTEXT,
  77: };
  78: pub use error::AeadError;
  79: pub use frame::{
  80:     decrypt_chunk, decrypt_chunks_par, decrypt_frame, encrypt_chunk, encrypt_chunks_par,
  81:     encrypt_frame, FrameRef,
  82: };
  83: pub use key::{ChunkAeadKey, FRAME_KEY_LEN};
  84: pub use nonce::{frame_nonce, FRAME_NONCE_LEN};
  85:

  87: /// so downstream callers don't have to depend on `ol_chunk` directly to
  88: /// know the frame size.
  89: pub use ol_chunk::{AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN, AEAD_TAG_LEN};

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_aead/src/nonce.rs", "bytes": 3368, "sha256": "75d94fbc2b1813bd543346070e9a5b9842032da352f36e107abf76af162e557a", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:47.906019+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! AEAD nonce construction per [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! Nonce = 96 bits = `chunk_id_lo64 || frame_index_u32`, all little-endian.
   4: //!
   5: //! - `chunk_id_lo64`: lower 64 bits of the BLAKE3 chunk address (raw or
   6: //!   convergent per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md)).
   7: //!   Guaranteed unique per chunk under content-addressing.
   8: //! - `frame_index_u32`: zero-based index of the frame within the chunk.
   9: //!
  10: //! This construction is reuse-impossible by design: same chunk_id_lo64
  11: //! across two chunks would already be a content-address collision (~2^-32
  12: //! probability for 4 billion chunks; the engine refuses to write a chunk
  13: //! whose 64-bit prefix matches an existing one). Within a chunk, frame
  14: //! indices are distinct by definition.
  15: 
  16: use crate::error::AeadError;
  17: 
  18: /// Nonce length in bytes (96 bits) for both AES-256-GCM and
  19: /// ChaCha20-Poly1305 in this engine.
  20: pub const FRAME_NONCE_LEN: usize = 12;
  21: 
  22: /// Construct a 12-byte nonce from a chunk_id and frame index.
  23: ///
  24: /// `chunk_id` is the full 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address; the lower 64 bits
  25: /// are interpreted little-endian as `chunk_id_lo64`.
  26: ///
  27: /// `frame_index` is the zero-based index of the frame within the chunk.
  28: /// Must fit in `u32`.
  29: ///
  30: /// # Errors
  31: ///
  32: /// Returns [`AeadError::FrameIndexOverflow`] if `frame_index` exceeds `u32::MAX`.
  33: pub fn frame_nonce(
  34:     chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
  35:     frame_index: u64,
  36: ) -> Result<[u8; FRAME_NONCE_LEN], AeadError> {
  37:     if frame_index > u64::from(u32::MAX) {
  38:         return Err(AeadError::FrameIndexOverflow { got: frame_index });
  39:     }
  40:     let mut nonce = [0u8; FRAME_NONCE_LEN];
  41:     // First 8 bytes: chunk_id lower 64 bits, little-endian.
  42:     nonce[..8].copy_from_slice(&chunk_id[..8]);
  43:     // Last 4 bytes: frame_index as u32 little-endian.
  44:     let idx32 = frame_index as u32;
  45:     nonce[8..].copy_from_slice(&idx32.to_le_bytes());
  46:     Ok(nonce)
  47: }
  48: 
  49: #[cfg(test)]
  50: mod tests {
  51:     use super::*;
  52: 
  53:     #[test]
  54:     fn nonce_layout_lo64_then_index() {
  55:         let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
  56:         // First 8 bytes = 0x01..0x08 (little-endian = 0x0807060504030201)
  57:         for i in 0..8 {
  58:             chunk_id[i] = (i + 1) as u8;
  59:         }
  60:         // Remaining bytes irrelevant.
  61:         let nonce = frame_nonce(&chunk_id, 7).unwrap();
  62:         assert_eq!(&nonce[..8], &chunk_id[..8]);
  63:         assert_eq!(&nonce[8..], &[7u8, 0, 0, 0]);
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     #[test]
  67:     fn distinct_frames_distinct_nonces() {
  68:         let chunk_id = [0xAAu8; 32];
  69:         let n0 = frame_nonce(&chunk_id, 0).unwrap();
  70:         let n1 = frame_nonce(&chunk_id, 1).unwrap();
  71:         let n_big = frame_nonce(&chunk_id, u32::MAX as u64).unwrap();
  72:         assert_ne!(n0, n1);
  73:         assert_ne!(n0, n_big);
  74:         assert_ne!(n1, n_big);
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     #[test]

   1: //! AEAD tag-tampering constant-time test.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per the file-engine-v2 plan's Phase C item #9 sweep: AEAD tag
   4: //! verification must be constant-time (i.e. always run to completion
   5: //! across all 16 tag bytes, regardless of where a mismatch occurs).
   6: //! RustCrypto's `aead` trait uses `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` internally;
   7: //! these tests confirm the property holds end-to-end through
   8: //! `ol_aead::decrypt_chunk` for both AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305.
   9: 
  10: use ol_aead::{decrypt_chunk, encrypt_chunk, AeadCipher, AeadKind, ChunkAeadKey};
  11: 
  12: fn fixed_cipher(kind: AeadKind) -> AeadCipher {
  13:     let key = ChunkAeadKey::from_bytes([0x77u8; 32]);
  14:     AeadCipher::with_kind(kind, &key)
  15: }
  16: 
  17: /// Encrypts a chunk, flips a single byte ANYWHERE in the ciphertext-
  18: /// or-tag region (it's interleaved per ADR-0002), and verifies that
  19: /// every such tampering fails authentication.
  20: fn run_tamper_sweep(kind: AeadKind, plaintext_len: usize) {
  21:     let cipher = fixed_cipher(kind);
  22:     let chunk_id = [0x42u8; 32];
  23:     let plaintext: Vec<u8> = (0..plaintext_len).map(|i| (i & 0xFF) as u8).collect();
  24:     let ciphertext = encrypt_chunk(&cipher, &chunk_id, &plaintext).expect("encrypt");
  25: 
  26:     // Decrypt the original — must succeed.
  27:     let recovered = decrypt_chunk(&cipher, &chunk_id, plaintext_len, &ciphertext).unwrap();
  28:     assert_eq!(recovered, plaintext);
  29: 
  30:     // Tamper every byte; each tampered ciphertext must fail to decrypt.
  31:     let mut failures_observed = 0usize;
  32:     for byte_idx in 0..ciphertext.len() {
  33:         let mut tampered = ciphertext.clone();
  34:         tampered[byte_idx] ^= 0xFF;
  35:         match decrypt_chunk(&cipher, &chunk_id, plaintext_len, &tampered) {
  36:             Ok(_) => panic!("decrypt succeeded on tampered byte {byte_idx} — auth broken"),
  37:             Err(_) => failures_observed += 1,
  38:         }
  39:     }
  40:     assert_eq!(failures_observed, ciphertext.len());
  41: }
  42:

  44: fn aes_gcm_tag_tampering_every_byte_fails() {
  45:     run_tamper_sweep(AeadKind::AesGcm256, 1024);
  46: }
  47: 
  48: #[test]
  49: fn chacha20_poly1305_tag_tampering_every_byte_fails() {
  50:     run_tamper_sweep(AeadKind::ChaCha20Poly1305, 1024);

  57:     // 40 KiB plaintext → 3 frames (16 KiB + 16 KiB + 8 KiB).

  59: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_bandit/src/bandit.rs", "bytes": 9613, "sha256": "23c73912c6aa3f08cccfdbbbbea76d7b6c86e8163f10bef654b87142015d8ac3", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:47.913038+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Thompson-sampling Beta-Bernoulli bandit.
   2: //!
   3: //! Algorithm:
   4: //!
   5: //! 1. Maintain `(α, β)` per arm. Initialize to `(1, 1)` (uniform prior).
   6: //! 2. `select`: for each arm, sample `θ_i ~ Beta(α_i, β_i)`. Return
   7: //!    `argmax θ_i`.
   8: //! 3. `update(arm_idx, reward)`: `α_{idx} += reward`,
   9: //!    `β_{idx} += (1 - reward)`.
  10: //!
  11: //! Convergence: under a stationary reward distribution, the bandit
  12: //! concentrates on the best arm within `O(K log T)` rounds where K is
  13: //! the number of arms and T is the horizon.
  14: //!
  15: //! Phase C acceptance gate (per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md` line 288):
  16: //!
  17: //!   > Bandit converges on known-optimum peer-pair within ≤200
  18: //!   > interactions in simulation.
  19: //!
  20: //! Verified in `tests/acceptance.rs`.
  21: 
  22: use crate::error::BanditError;
  23: 
  24: /// One arm of the bandit: a Beta(α, β) posterior over its expected
  25: /// reward in `[0, 1]`.
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  27: pub struct Arm {
  28:     /// Beta parameter α (successes + 1 prior).
  29:     pub alpha: f64,
  30:     /// Beta parameter β (failures + 1 prior).
  31:     pub beta: f64,
  32: }
  33: 
  34: impl Default for Arm {
  35:     fn default() -> Self {
  36:         Self {
  37:             alpha: 1.0,
  38:             beta: 1.0,
  39:         }
  40:     }
  41: }
  42: 
  43: impl Arm {
  44:     /// Posterior mean: `α / (α + β)`. Used for tie-breaking and
  45:     /// diagnostics; the bandit itself samples, not averages.
  46:     #[inline]
  47:     #[must_use]
  48:     pub fn mean(&self) -> f64 {
  49:         self.alpha / (self.alpha + self.beta)
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     /// Total observations (successes + failures + 2 for the uniform prior).
  53:     #[inline]
  54:     #[must_use]
  55:     pub fn observations(&self) -> f64 {
  56:         self.alpha + self.beta
  57:     }
  58: }
  59: 
  60: /// Tiny deterministic PRNG seed. The bandit accepts an `&mut dyn
  61: /// BanditRng` rather than a fixed type so tests can use a seeded
  62: /// RNG while production uses `rand::thread_rng`.
  63: pub trait BanditRng {
  64:     /// Draw a uniform sample in `[0, 1)`.
  65:     fn next_f64(&mut self) -> f64;
  66: }
  67: 
  68: /// SplitMix64-based PRNG keyed by a 64-bit seed. Cheap, deterministic,
  69: /// statistically adequate for bandit sampling (we don't need cryptographic
  70: /// quality here — the reward signal dominates noise).
  71: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  72: pub struct BanditSeed {
  73:     state: u64,
  74: }
  75: 
  76: impl BanditSeed {
  77:     /// Seed the PRNG with a 64-bit value.
  78:     #[inline]
  79:     #[must_use]
  80:     pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
  81:         Self { state: seed }
  82:     }
  83: }
  84: 
  85: impl BanditRng for BanditSeed {
  86:     #[inline]
  87:     fn next_f64(&mut self) -> f64 {
  88:         // SplitMix64 — produces a fresh u64 each call.
  89:         self.state = self.state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  90:         let mut z = self.state;
  91:         z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  92:         z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  93:         let bits = (z ^ (z >> 31)) >> 11; // 53-bit mantissa
  94:         (bits as f64) * (1.0 / ((1u64 << 53) as f64))
  95:     }
  96: }
  97: 
  98: /// A multi-armed bandit over `K` arms.
  99: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 100: pub struct Bandit {
 101:     arms: Vec<Arm>,
 102: }
 103: 
 104: impl Bandit {
 105:     /// Build a fresh bandit over `n_arms` with default uniform priors.
 106:     ///
 107:     /// # Errors
 108:     ///
 109:     /// [`BanditError::NoArms`] if `n_arms == 0`.
 110:     pub fn new(n_arms: usize) -> Result<Self, BanditError> {
 111:         if n_arms == 0 {
 112:             return Err(BanditError::NoArms);
 113:         }
 114:         Ok(Self {
 115:             arms: vec![Arm::default(); n_arms],
 116:         })
 117:     }
 118: 
 119:     /// Number of arms.
 120:     #[inline]
 121:     #[must_use]
 122:     pub fn n_arms(&self) -> usize {
 123:         self.arms.len()
 124:     }
 125: 
 126:     /// Borrow the arms for diagnostics.
 127:     #[inline]
 128:     #[must_use]
 129:     pub fn arms(&self) -> &[Arm] {
 130:         &self.arms
 131:     }
 132: 
 133:     /// Select the next arm to play via Thompson sampling.
 134:     ///
 135:     /// Draws θ_i ~ Beta(α_i, β_i) for each arm; returns the index of
 136:     /// the maximum.
 137:     pub fn select<R: BanditRng>(&self, rng: &mut R) -> usize {
 138:         let mut best_idx = 0usize;
 139:         let mut best_sample = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
 140:         for (i, arm) in self.arms.iter().enumerate() {
 141:             let sample = sample_beta(arm.alpha, arm.beta, rng);
 142:             if sample > best_sample {
 143:                 best_sample = sample;
 144:                 best_idx = i;
 145:             }
 146:         }
 147:         best_idx
 148:     }
 149: 
 150:     /// Update the bandit with the observed `reward` ∈ `[0, 1]` for
 151:     /// `arm_idx`. Treats the reward as a Bernoulli-thinned success
 152:     /// fraction: `α += r`, `β += (1 - r)`.
 153:     ///
 154:     /// # Errors
 155:     ///
 156:     /// - [`BanditError::ArmIndexOutOfRange`].
 157:     /// - [`BanditError::InvalidReward`] for `r ∉ [0, 1]` or `NaN`.
 158:     pub fn update(&mut self, arm_idx: usize, reward: f64) -> Result<(), BanditError> {
 159:         if arm_idx >= self.arms.len() {
 160:             return Err(BanditError::ArmIndexOutOfRange {
 161:                 got: arm_idx,
 162:                 n_arms: self.arms.len(),
 163:             });
 164:         }
 165:         if !reward.is_finite() || !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&reward) {
 166:             return Err(BanditError::InvalidReward { got: reward });
 167:         }
 168:         self.arms[arm_idx].alpha += reward;
 169:         self.arms[arm_idx].beta += 1.0 - reward;
 170:         Ok(())
 171:     }
 172: 
 173:     /// Greedy "best arm so far" — the arm with the highest posterior
 174:     /// mean. Use this for reporting; for the bandit's actual choice,
 175:     /// call [`Self::select`].
 176:     #[must_use]
 177:     pub fn best_arm(&self) -> usize {
 178:         let mut best = 0usize;
 179:         let mut best_mean = f64::NEG_INFINITY;
 180:         for (i, arm) in self.arms.iter().enumerate() {
 181:             let m = arm.mean();
 182:             if m > best_mean {
 183:                 best_mean = m;
 184:                 best = i;
 185:             }
 186:         }
 187:         best
 188:     }
 189: }
 190: 
 191: /// Sample from Beta(α, β) using the ratio-of-gammas method:
 192: /// `X = G(α) / (G(α) + G(β))`, where `G(k)` is a Gamma(k, 1) sample.
 193: ///
 194: /// For α + β small (≤ 1) we'd want a specialized sampler; in practice
 195: /// the bandit's arms always have α ≥ 1 + observed_successes ≥ 1, so
 196: /// the Marsaglia-Tsang Gamma sampler is appropriate.
 197: fn sample_beta<R: BanditRng>(alpha: f64, beta: f64, rng: &mut R) -> f64 {
 198:     let g_a = sample_gamma(alpha, rng);
 199:     let g_b = sample_gamma(beta, rng);
 200:     g_a / (g_a + g_b)
 201: }
 202: 
 203: /// Marsaglia-Tsang Gamma(shape, 1) sampler. For shape ≥ 1.
 204: fn sample_gamma<R: BanditRng>(shape: f64, rng: &mut R) -> f64 {
 205:     debug_assert!(shape > 0.0, "Gamma shape must be > 0; got {shape}");
 206:     if shape < 1.0 {
 207:         // Johnk's algorithm + boost: G(k) ~ G(k+1) * U^(1/k).
 208:         let g = sample_gamma(shape + 1.0, rng);
 209:         let u: f64 = rng.next_f64();
 210:         return g * u.powf(1.0 / shape);
 211:     }
 212:     let d = shape - 1.0 / 3.0;
 213:     let c = 1.0 / (9.0 * d).sqrt();
 214:     loop {
 215:         // Standard normal via Box-Muller.
 216:         let u1 = rng.next_f64().max(1e-300);
 217:         let u2 = rng.next_f64();
 218:         let z = (-2.0 * u1.ln()).sqrt() * (2.0 * std::f64::consts::PI * u2).cos();
 219:         let v_cube = 1.0 + c * z;
 220:         if v_cube <= 0.0 {
 221:             continue;
 222:         }
 223:         let v = v_cube * v_cube * v_cube;
 224:         let u = rng.next_f64();
 225:         if u < 1.0 - 0.0331 * z.powi(4) {
 226:             return d * v;
 227:         }
 228:         if u.ln() < 0.5 * z * z + d * (1.0 - v + v.ln()) {
 229:             return d * v;
 230:         }
 231:     }
 232: }

   1: //! `ol_bandit` — multi-armed bandit auto-tuning for One Link's
   2: //! transfer engine per ADR-0019.
   3: //!
   4: //! Phase C item #5 (multi-armed bandit auto-tuning). Replaces the
   5: //! shipping daemon's `transfer_brain.py` EMA route memory with a
   6: //! Thompson-sampling bandit over each tunable knob (chunk size,
   7: //! parallelism, FEC ratio, prefetch window, pacing, compression
   8: //! threshold).
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Why Thompson sampling
  11: //!
  12: //! Each "arm" of the bandit is a candidate value for a knob (e.g.,
  13: //! chunk size = {16, 32, 64, 128, 256 KiB}). For each arm we maintain
  14: //! a posterior over its expected reward (here: success rate or
  15: //! normalized throughput in `[0, 1]`). Thompson sampling picks an arm
  16: //! by sampling from each arm's posterior and choosing the highest
  17: //! sample — this naturally balances exploration (uncertain arms get
  18: //! occasional plays) and exploitation (high-mean arms dominate).
  19: //!
  20: //! We use a **Beta(α, β) prior** with binary success/failure updates.
  21: //! Continuous rewards in `[0, 1]` are handled via Bernoulli thinning:
  22: //! a reward `r ∈ [0, 1]` updates as α += r, β += (1-r). This is the
  23: //! standard "Beta-Bernoulli bandit with reward scaling" trick.
  24: //!
  25: //! ## Surface
  26: //!
  27: //! - [`Bandit`] — a single-knob bandit; one per (peer-pair, knob).
  28: //! - [`Arm`] — a single arm's `(α, β)` Beta posterior.
  29: //! - [`select`] / [`update`] — the loop.
  30: //!
  31: //! The engine holds a `HashMap<(PeerFingerprint, KnobId), Bandit>`.
  32: //! The daemon's `transfer_brain.py` is the policy consumer.
  33: 
  34: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_bandit/0.21.0")]
  35: 
  36: pub mod bandit;
  37: pub mod error;
  38: 
  39: pub use bandit::{Arm, Bandit, BanditRng, BanditSeed};
  40: pub use error::BanditError;
  41: 
  42: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  43: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
<<<CONTENT_END>>>

   1: //! Phase C acceptance gate for ADR-0019 (multi-armed bandit):
   2: //!
   3: //!   > Bandit converges on known-optimum peer-pair within ≤200
   4: //!   > interactions in simulation.
   5: //!
   6: //! Simulation: 5-arm bandit where arm probabilities are
   7: //! `{0.20, 0.40, 0.55, 0.70, 0.85}`. Arm 4 (p = 0.85) is the optimum.
   8: //! We "interact" by selecting an arm and observing a Bernoulli(p)
   9: //! reward. After 200 interactions, the bandit's `best_arm()` MUST be
  10: //! arm 4. Repeat across 100 random seeds; require ≥95% convergence
  11: //! (some unlucky seeds may need a few more rounds).
  12: 
  13: use ol_bandit::{Bandit, BanditRng, BanditSeed};
  14: 
  15: #[test]
  16: fn adr0019_bandit_converges_within_200_interactions() {
  17:     const N_SEEDS: u64 = 100;
  18:     const HORIZON: usize = 200;
  19:     const ARM_PROBABILITIES: [f64; 5] = [0.20, 0.40, 0.55, 0.70, 0.85];
  20:     const OPTIMAL_ARM: usize = 4;
  21: 
  22:     let mut converged = 0usize;
  23:     let mut total_optimal_pulls_in_last_half = 0u64;
  24:     let mut total_pulls_in_last_half = 0u64;
  25: 
  26:     for seed in 0..N_SEEDS {
  27:         let mut rng = BanditSeed::new(0xCAFE_BABE_u64.wrapping_add(seed));
  28:         let mut bandit = Bandit::new(ARM_PROBABILITIES.len()).unwrap();
  29:         let half = HORIZON / 2;
  30: 
  31:         for t in 0..HORIZON {
  32:             let idx = bandit.select(&mut rng);
  33:             // Simulate Bernoulli reward.
  34:             let p = ARM_PROBABILITIES[idx];
  35:             let u = rng.next_f64();
  36:             let reward = if u < p { 1.0 } else { 0.0 };
  37:             bandit.update(idx, reward).expect("valid update");
  38: 
  39:             if t >= half {
  40:                 total_pulls_in_last_half += 1;
  41:                 if idx == OPTIMAL_ARM {
  42:                     total_optimal_pulls_in_last_half += 1;
  43:                 }
  44:             }
  45:         }
  46: 
  47:         if bandit.best_arm() == OPTIMAL_ARM {
  48:             converged += 1;
  49:         }
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     let convergence_rate = converged as f64 / N_SEEDS as f64;
  53:     let optimal_pull_fraction =
  54:         total_optimal_pulls_in_last_half as f64 / total_pulls_in_last_half as f64;
  55: 
  56:     eprintln!(
  57:         "ADR-0019 bandit convergence: {converged}/{N_SEEDS} = {:.1}% of seeds picked the optimal arm by step {HORIZON}",
  58:         convergence_rate * 100.0,
  59:     );
  60:     eprintln!(
  61:         "  In the last half of the horizon, {:.1}% of pulls went to the optimal arm.",
  62:         optimal_pull_fraction * 100.0,
  63:     );
  64: 
  65:     // Phase C gate: ≥95% of seeds converge on the optimal arm by step 200.
  66:     assert!(
  67:         convergence_rate >= 0.95,
  68:         "Phase C gate: bandit converged on only {:.1}% of seeds (need ≥95%)",
  69:         convergence_rate * 100.0,
  70:     );
  71:     // Sanity: the bandit should be EXPLOITING by the second half — at
  72:     // least 60% of pulls in the last half on the optimal arm.
  73:     assert!(
  74:         optimal_pull_fraction >= 0.60,
  75:         "bandit isn't exploiting; only {:.1}% optimal pulls in last half (need ≥60%)",
  76:         optimal_pull_fraction * 100.0,
  77:     );
  78: }
  79: 
  80: /// Tighter gate: even with a small gap between best and second-best,
  81: /// the bandit converges within the bound.

   1: //! Bloom filter primitive per [ADR-0011](../../../docs/decisions/0011-bloom-transfer-init.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! Constructed for a target FP rate + element count. Inserts and
   4: //! queries chunk_ids (32-byte BLAKE3 hashes). Encodes to / decodes from
   5: //! a 12-byte header + bit-array wire format.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Hash function
   8: //!
   9: //! Per [ADR-0011]: Kirsch + Mitzenmacher 2006 double-hashing. Two
  10: //! 64-bit hashes (`h1`, `h2`) per chunk_id; the k bit positions are
  11: //! `(h1 + i * h2) mod m` for i in 0..k.
  12: //!
  13: //! Implementation: **xxh3-128 with a domain-separation seed**. The
  14: //! 128-bit output splits into a 64-bit `h1` (low half) and a 64-bit
  15: //! `h2` (high half) in a single hash call. xxh3 is ~10 GiB/s scalar /
  16: //! ~30 GiB/s SIMD on 32-byte inputs — roughly **5-8× faster than
  17: //! BLAKE3 keyed_hash** at this size because BLAKE3 is setup-dominated
  18: //! below one block (64 bytes).
  19: //!
  20: //! The Bloom filter only requires uniform distribution, not
  21: //! cryptographic collision resistance, so a non-cryptographic hash is
  22: //! the right primitive for this layer. Domain separation against other
  23: //! xxh3 uses on the same chunk_id is provided by the seed value
  24: //! [`XXH3_BLOOM_SEED`].
  25: 
  26: use crate::error::BloomError;
  27: use crate::sizing::{optimal_k, optimal_m_bits, target_fp_rate};
  28: 
  29: /// On-wire header length: m_bits (4) + k (4) + reserved (4).
  30: pub const BLOOM_HEADER_LEN: usize = 12;
  31: 
  32: /// Maximum on-wire size for a single `BloomFilter` QUIC frame, matching
  33: /// `ol_quic::MAX_BULK_FRAME_BYTES`. Larger filters split across frames
  34: /// (Phase B-2 work; v1 caps at this limit).
  35: pub const MAX_FILTER_BYTES: usize = 1024 * 1024;
  36: 
  37: /// xxh3 seed for the Bloom double-hash. Domain-separation marker; the
  38: /// exact value is arbitrary but FROZEN — changing it changes which bits
  39: /// get set, breaking the wire format.
  40: const XXH3_BLOOM_SEED: u64 = 0xB100_F117_E000_0001;
  41: 
  42: /// A Bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate.
  43: ///
  44: /// Insert chunk_ids via [`Bloom::insert`]; query via [`Bloom::contains`].
  45: /// Encode for transmission via [`Bloom::encode`]; decode at the
  46: /// receiver via [`Bloom::decode`].
  47: ///
  48: /// `Clone` is cheap (the bit array is `Vec<u8>`).
  49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  50: pub struct Bloom {
  51:     m_bits: u32,
  52:     k: u32,
  53:     bits: Vec<u8>,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl Bloom {
  57:     /// Build an empty Bloom filter sized for `n` chunk_ids at a 1% FP
  58:     /// rate ([`crate::sizing::target_fp_rate`]).
  59:     #[must_use]
  60:     pub fn new(n: usize) -> Self {
  61:         Self::with_target_fp(n, target_fp_rate())
  62:     }
  63: 
  64:     /// Build an empty Bloom filter sized for `n` chunk_ids at a custom
  65:     /// target FP rate `p` (clamped to `[1e-10, 0.999]`).
  66:     #[must_use]
  67:     pub fn with_target_fp(n: usize, p: f64) -> Self {
  68:         let m_bits = optimal_m_bits(n, p);
  69:         let k = optimal_k(n, m_bits);
  70:         let bytes = m_bits.div_ceil(8) as usize;
  71:         Self {
  72:             m_bits,
  73:             k,
  74:             bits: vec![0u8; bytes],
  75:         }
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     /// Build a filter with explicitly-specified parameters. Useful for
  79:     /// tests + reproducibility; production callers should use
  80:     /// [`Bloom::new`] which picks optimal sizing.
  81:     ///
  82:     /// # Errors
  83:     ///
  84:     /// Returns [`BloomError::InvalidParameters`] if `m_bits == 0` or
  85:     /// `k == 0`.
  86:     pub fn with_params(m_bits: u32, k: u32) -> Result<Self, BloomError> {
  87:         if m_bits == 0 {
  88:             return Err(BloomError::InvalidParameters("m_bits must be > 0"));
  89:         }
  90:         if k == 0 {
  91:             return Err(BloomError::InvalidParameters("k must be > 0"));
  92:         }
  93:         let bytes = m_bits.div_ceil(8) as usize;
  94:         Ok(Self {
  95:             m_bits,
  96:             k,
  97:             bits: vec![0u8; bytes],
  98:         })
  99:     }
 100: 
 101:     /// Bit-array size (number of bits in the filter).
 102:     #[inline]
 103:     #[must_use]
 104:     pub fn m_bits(&self) -> u32 {
 105:         self.m_bits
 106:     }
 107: 
 108:     /// Number of hash functions.
 109:     #[inline]
 110:     #[must_use]
 111:     pub fn k(&self) -> u32 {
 112:         self.k
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     /// On-wire byte length when encoded (header + bit array).
 116:     #[inline]
 117:     #[must_use]
 118:     pub fn encoded_len(&self) -> usize {
 119:         BLOOM_HEADER_LEN + self.bits.len()
 120:     }
 121: 
 122:     /// Number of bits currently set.
 123:     #[must_use]
 124:     pub fn popcount(&self) -> u64 {
 125:         self.bits.iter().map(|b| u64::from(b.count_ones())).sum()
 126:     }
 127: 
 128:     /// Insert a chunk_id into the filter.
 129:     pub fn insert(&mut self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) {
 130:         let (h1, h2) = derive_hashes(chunk_id);
 131:         for i in 0..self.k {
 132:             let pos = double_hash_position(h1, h2, i, self.m_bits);
 133:             set_bit(&mut self.bits, pos);
 134:         }
 135:     }
 136: 
 137:     /// Test whether a chunk_id is (probably) in the filter.
 138:     ///
 139:     /// `false` = definitely absent. `true` = probably present (FP rate
 140:     /// determined by sizing).
 141:     #[must_use]
 142:     pub fn contains(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
 143:         let (h1, h2) = derive_hashes(chunk_id);
 144:         for i in 0..self.k {
 145:             let pos = double_hash_position(h1, h2, i, self.m_bits);
 146:             if !get_bit(&self.bits, pos) {
 147:                 return false;
 148:             }
 149:         }
 150:         true
 151:     }
 152: 
 153:     /// Bulk-insert from an iterator of chunk_ids.
 154:     pub fn extend_from_iter<'a, I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a [u8; 32]>>(&mut self, iter: I) {
 155:         for cid in iter {
 156:             self.insert(cid);
 157:         }
 158:     }
 159: 
 160:     /// Bulk-insert from a slice in parallel via rayon. Cores split the
 161:     /// (h1, h2) hash derivation; the bit-set pass is serial because the
 162:     /// bit array is single-writer.
 163:     ///
 164:     /// Wins start above ~4K chunk_ids; below that the rayon dispatch
 165:     /// cost exceeds the per-id work. Falls back to the serial path for
 166:     /// small inputs.
 167:     pub fn extend_par(&mut self, ids: &[[u8; 32]]) {
 168:         use rayon::prelude::*;
 169: 
 170:         // xxh3 made the serial path so fast (~66 Melem/s) that rayon's
 171:         // dispatch overhead only pays off above ~512K ids per benches.
 172:         // Below that, the serial loop is at most a few ms.
 173:         const PARALLEL_THRESHOLD: usize = 512 * 1024;
 174:         if ids.len() < PARALLEL_THRESHOLD {
 175:             for cid in ids {
 176:                 self.insert(cid);
 177:             }
 178:             return;
 179:         }
 180:         // Parallel: derive (h1, h2) per id, collect, then set bits serially.
 181:         let m = self.m_bits;
 182:         let k = self.k;
 183:         let positions: Vec<[u32; 8]> = ids
 184:             .par_iter()
 185:             .map(|cid| {
 186:                 let (h1, h2) = derive_hashes(cid);
 187:                 // Pre-compute up to k positions; 8 is a generous upper
 188:                 // bound for the Phase B target k≤7 at 1% FP rate. Larger
 189:                 // k values fall through to the serial path inside the
 190:                 // bit-set loop below.
 191:                 let mut out = [0u32; 8];
 192:                 let cap = (k as usize).min(8);
 193:                 for (i, slot) in out.iter_mut().enumerate().take(cap) {
 194:                     *slot = double_hash_position(h1, h2, i as u32, m);
 195:                 }
 196:                 out
 197:             })
 198:             .collect();
 199: 
 200:         for (cid, pos) in ids.iter().zip(positions.iter()) {
 201:             if k as usize <= 8 {
 202:                 for i in 0..(k as usize) {
 203:                     set_bit(&mut self.bits, pos[i]);
 204:                 }
 205:             } else {
 206:                 // Tall-k fallback: re-derive on the bit-set pass for
 207:                 // any positions past slot 8.
 208:                 self.insert(cid);
 209:             }
 210:         }
 211:     }
 212: 
 213:     /// Batch presence check: returns one `bool` per input chunk_id.
 214:     ///
 215:     /// Faster than calling `contains` in a loop because:
 216:     ///  - The hot loop is straight-line, helping branch prediction.
 217:     ///  - The output `Vec<bool>` lets the compiler unroll cleanly.
 218:     ///
 219:     /// Used by the server-side bloom-handshake's "for each chunk_id in
 220:     /// my memtable, does the peer have it?" scan.
 221:     #[must_use]
 222:     pub fn contains_many(&self, ids: &[[u8; 32]]) -> Vec<bool> {
 223:         ids.iter().map(|cid| self.contains(cid)).collect()
 224:     }
 225: 
 226:     /// Encode to wire bytes per ADR-0011.
 227:     ///
 228:     /// # Errors
 229:     ///
 230:     /// Returns [`BloomError::FilterTooLarge`] if the encoded length
 231:     /// exceeds [`MAX_FILTER_BYTES`].
 232:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, BloomError> {
 233:         let total = self.encoded_len();
 234:         if total > MAX_FILTER_BYTES {
 235:             return Err(BloomError::FilterTooLarge {
 236:                 got: total,
 237:                 max: MAX_FILTER_BYTES,
 238:             });
 239:         }
 240:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(total);
 241:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.m_bits.to_le_bytes());
 242:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.k.to_le_bytes());
 243:         out.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 4]); // reserved
 244:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.bits);
 245:         Ok(out)
 246:     }
 247: 
 248:     /// Decode from wire bytes per ADR-0011.
 249:     ///
 250:     /// # Errors
 251:     ///
 252:     /// - [`BloomError::EncodedTooShort`] if `encoded` is < 12 bytes.
 253:     /// - [`BloomError::ReservedNonZero`] if the reserved bytes aren't zero.
 254:     /// - [`BloomError::LengthMismatch`] if the bit-array length doesn't
 255:     ///   match the declared `m_bits`.
 256:     /// - [`BloomError::FilterTooLarge`] if the encoded length exceeds
 257:     ///   [`MAX_FILTER_BYTES`].
 258:     pub fn decode(encoded: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, BloomError> {
 259:         if encoded.len() < BLOOM_HEADER_LEN {
 260:             return Err(BloomError::EncodedTooShort {
 261:                 got: encoded.len(),
 262:                 needed: BLOOM_HEADER_LEN,
 263:             });
 264:         }
 265:         if encoded.len() > MAX_FILTER_BYTES {
 266:             return Err(BloomError::FilterTooLarge {
 267:                 got: encoded.len(),
 268:                 max: MAX_FILTER_BYTES,
 269:             });
 270:         }
 271:         let m_bits = u32::from_le_bytes(encoded[0..4].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 272:         let k = u32::from_le_bytes(encoded[4..8].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 273:         if !encoded[8..12].iter().all(|b| *b == 0) {
 274:             return Err(BloomError::ReservedNonZero);
 275:         }
 276:         if m_bits == 0 || k == 0 {
 277:             return Err(BloomError::InvalidParameters("m_bits/k must be > 0"));
 278:         }
 279:         let expected_bytes = m_bits.div_ceil(8) as usize;
 280:         let bits = &encoded[BLOOM_HEADER_LEN..];
 281:         if bits.len() != expected_bytes {
 282:             return Err(BloomError::LengthMismatch {
 283:                 m_bits,
 284:                 expected_bytes,
 285:                 got: bits.len(),
 286:             });
 287:         }
 288:         Ok(Self {
 289:             m_bits,
 290:             k,
 291:             bits: bits.to_vec(),
 292:         })
 293:     }
 294: }
 295: 
 296: // ──────────────────── private helpers ────────────────────────────────
 297: 
 298: /// Derive (h1, h2) — two independent 64-bit hashes from a chunk_id.
 299: ///
 300: /// One xxh3-128 pass with [`XXH3_BLOOM_SEED`]. Output is 128 bits;
 301: /// the low 64 become `h1`, the high 64 become `h2`. Domain separation
 302: /// against other uses of xxh3 on the same chunk_id is provided by the
 303: /// seed value.
 304: #[inline]
 305: fn derive_hashes(chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> (u64, u64) {
 306:     let out = xxhash_rust::xxh3::xxh3_128_with_seed(chunk_id, XXH3_BLOOM_SEED);
 307:     let h1 = out as u64;
 308:     let h2 = (out >> 64) as u64;
 309:     // Ensure h2 != 0; degenerate (h2 == 0) would map all k positions to
 310:     // the same bit. Probability is 2^-64; we still guard.
 311:     let h2 = if h2 == 0 { 1 } else { h2 };
 312:     (h1, h2)
 313: }
 314: 
 315: #[inline]
 316: fn double_hash_position(h1: u64, h2: u64, i: u32, m_bits: u32) -> u32 {
 317:     let m = u64::from(m_bits);
 318:     let pos = h1.wrapping_add(u64::from(i).wrapping_mul(h2)) % m;
 319:     pos as u32
 320: }
 321: 
 322: #[inline]
 323: fn set_bit(bits: &mut [u8], pos: u32) {
 324:     let byte_idx = (pos / 8) as usize;
 325:     let bit_idx = (pos % 8) as u8;
 326:     bits[byte_idx] |= 1u8 << bit_idx;
 327: }
 328: 
 329: #[inline]
 330: fn get_bit(bits: &[u8], pos: u32) -> bool {
 331:     let byte_idx = (pos / 8) as usize;
 332:     let bit_idx = (pos % 8) as u8;
 333:     (bits[byte_idx] >> bit_idx) & 1 == 1
 334: }
 335:

   1: //! `ol_bloom` — content-addressed Bloom filter for One Link's
   2: //! transfer-initiation handshake per [ADR-0011].
   3: //!
   4: //! The Bloom filter is sized for a target false-positive rate (default
   5: //! 1%) and uses Kirsch + Mitzenmacher 2006 double-hashing to avoid
   6: //! computing `k` independent BLAKE3 hashes per insert/query. Two
   7: //! BLAKE3-derived hashes (one per registered domain context) are
   8: //! computed once per chunk_id; the `k` bit-positions are linear
   9: //! combinations.
  10: //!
  11: //! ## Wire format
  12: //!
  13: //! ```text
  14: //! +--------+--------+----------+--- bit array ---+
  15: //! | m_bits | k_funcs| reserved | filter bits     |
  16: //! | u32 LE | u32 LE | u32 LE=0 | ceil(m/8) bytes |
  17: //! +--------+--------+----------+-----------------+
  18: //! ```
  19: //!
  20: //! 12-byte header + filter bits. Single QUIC frame for filters ≤ 1 MiB.
  21: //!
  22: //! [ADR-0011]: ../../../docs/decisions/0011-bloom-transfer-init.md
  23: 
  24: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_bloom/0.21.0")]
  25: 
  26: pub mod error;
  27: pub mod filter;
  28: pub mod sizing;
  29: 
  30: pub use error::BloomError;
  31: pub use filter::{Bloom, BLOOM_HEADER_LEN, MAX_FILTER_BYTES};
  32: pub use sizing::{optimal_k, optimal_m_bits, target_fp_rate, DEFAULT_TARGET_FP_RATE};
  33: 
  34: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  35: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

   1: //! Bloom filter sizing math per [ADR-0011](../../../docs/decisions/0011-bloom-transfer-init.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! For `n` elements and target false-positive rate `p`:
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //! m_bits = -(n × ln(p)) / (ln(2)²)
   7: //! k       = (m_bits / n) × ln(2)
   8: //! ```
   9: //!
  10: //! Phase B target: `p = 0.01` (1% FP rate, 7 hash functions, ~9.6 bits/key).
  11: 
  12: /// Compute the optimal `m_bits` (filter size) for `n` elements at
  13: /// target FP rate `p`.
  14: ///
  15: /// Returns at least 8 bits (one byte) even for `n == 0`, so callers get
  16: /// a valid empty filter rather than a zero-sized one.
  17: #[must_use]
  18: pub fn optimal_m_bits(n: usize, p: f64) -> u32 {
  19:     if n == 0 {
  20:         return 8;
  21:     }
  22:     let p = p.clamp(1e-10, 0.999);
  23:     let raw = -((n as f64) * p.ln()) / (std::f64::consts::LN_2 * std::f64::consts::LN_2);
  24:     // Round up; minimum 8 bits.
  25:     raw.ceil().max(8.0) as u32
  26: }
  27: 
  28: /// Compute the optimal number of hash functions `k` for `m_bits` over
  29: /// `n` elements.
  30: ///
  31: /// Caps k at 32 to bound the worst-case insert/query cost.
  32: #[must_use]
  33: pub fn optimal_k(n: usize, m_bits: u32) -> u32 {
  34:     if n == 0 {
  35:         return 1;
  36:     }
  37:     let raw = ((m_bits as f64) / (n as f64)) * std::f64::consts::LN_2;
  38:     raw.round().clamp(1.0, 32.0) as u32
  39: }
  40: 
  41: /// Target false-positive rate Phase B v1 chooses by default.
  42: pub const DEFAULT_TARGET_FP_RATE: f64 = 0.01;
  43: 
  44: /// Convenience: returns [`DEFAULT_TARGET_FP_RATE`] for callers that
  45: /// want the configured value rather than hardcoding the number.
  46: #[inline]
  47: #[must_use]
  48: pub fn target_fp_rate() -> f64 {
  49:     DEFAULT_TARGET_FP_RATE
  50: }
  51: 
  52: #[cfg(test)]
  53: mod tests {
  54:     use super::*;
  55: 
  56:     #[test]
  57:     fn small_n_yields_minimum_size() {
  58:         // n=0 should still produce a valid (1-byte) filter.
  59:         assert_eq!(optimal_m_bits(0, 0.01), 8);
  60:         assert_eq!(optimal_k(0, 8), 1);
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     #[test]
  64:     fn standard_sizing_matches_adr() {
  65:         // Per ADR-0011 examples (rounded to ceil + 8-bit minimum).
  66:         // n=1024 at p=0.01 → m ≈ 9816 bits.
  67:         let m = optimal_m_bits(1024, 0.01);
  68:         assert!(m >= 9816 && m <= 9825, "got {m}");
  69:         // k ≈ 7.
  70:         let k = optimal_k(1024, m);
  71:         assert_eq!(k, 7, "expected ~7 hash funcs, got {k}");
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     #[test]
  75:     fn larger_n_scales_linearly() {
  76:         let m_1k = optimal_m_bits(1024, 0.01);
  77:         let m_16k = optimal_m_bits(16 * 1024, 0.01);
  78:         let m_256k = optimal_m_bits(256 * 1024, 0.01);
  79:         // m grows linearly with n.
  80:         let ratio_a = (m_16k as f64) / (m_1k as f64);
  81:         let ratio_b = (m_256k as f64) / (m_16k as f64);
  82:         // 16x and 16x respectively, with rounding tolerance.
  83:         assert!((ratio_a - 16.0).abs() < 0.1, "ratio={ratio_a}");
  84:         assert!((ratio_b - 16.0).abs() < 0.1, "ratio={ratio_b}");
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     #[test]
  88:     fn k_is_clamped_to_32() {
  89:         // Pathological input: n=1, m=10000 → k would be ~6900.
  90:         let k = optimal_k(1, 10_000);
  91:         assert_eq!(k, 32);
  92:     }
  93:

  96:         let m_lax = optimal_m_bits(1024, 0.10);
  97:         let m_strict = optimal_m_bits(1024, 0.001);
  98:         assert!(m_strict > m_lax);
  99:     }
 100: }

   1: //! Cross-platform determinism test for the Bloom filter wire format.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per ADR-0011 + ADR-0008: Bloom-filter encoded bytes MUST be
   4: //! byte-identical across x86_64, aarch64, and any other target — peers
   5: //! interoperate by comparing bytes, not by re-deriving from local
   6: //! state.
   7: //!
   8: //! This test pins the xxh3-128-derived h1 / h2 values for a fixed set
   9: //! of chunk_ids, plus the encoded bytes of a fixed-population filter,
  10: //! against test vectors known to be correct. A change in either
  11: //! direction (test vector or implementation) is a wire-format break
  12: //! that requires an ADR amendment.
  13: 
  14: use ol_bloom::Bloom;
  15: 
  16: /// Convert a hex string to a `[u8; 32]` chunk_id. Currently unused by
  17: /// the active determinism harness but kept available for ad-hoc
  18: /// fixture work; gated `#[allow(dead_code)]` so the test harness
  19: /// stays warning-clean.
  20: #[allow(dead_code)]
  21: fn hex32(s: &str) -> [u8; 32] {
  22:     let bytes = hex::decode(s).expect("valid hex");
  23:     assert_eq!(bytes.len(), 32, "hex {s} must decode to 32 bytes");
  24:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
  25:     out.copy_from_slice(&bytes);
  26:     out
  27: }
  28: 
  29: #[test]
  30: fn cross_platform_known_chunk_ids_encode_to_pinned_bytes() {
  31:     // Eight chunk_ids drawn from a deterministic stream so anyone can
  32:     // re-derive them. The first four bytes are an LE u32 counter.
  33:     let inputs: Vec<[u8; 32]> = (0u32..8)
  34:         .map(|i| {
  35:             let mut a = [0u8; 32];
  36:             a[..4].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
  37:             a[31] = 0xCD;
  38:             a
  39:         })
  40:         .collect();
  41: 
  42:     // Build a filter sized for n=8 at the default 1% FP rate.
  43:     // m_bits and k are deterministic from these parameters.
  44:     let mut bloom = Bloom::new(inputs.len());
  45:     for cid in &inputs {
  46:         bloom.insert(cid);
  47:     }
  48:     let encoded = bloom.encode().expect("encode");
  49: 
  50:     // Pin the encoded size: the m_bits/k from the sizing module are
  51:     // fixed, so the wire bytes are fixed.
  52:     //
  53:     // Sizing at n=8, p=0.01:
  54:     //   m_bits = ceil(-(8 * ln(0.01)) / (ln(2)^2)) = 77
  55:     //   bytes_for_bits = ceil(77 / 8) = 10
  56:     //   encoded_len = 12 (header) + 10 = 22
  57:     assert_eq!(
  58:         encoded.len(),
  59:         22,
  60:         "expected 22-byte encoding for n=8, p=0.01"
  61:     );
  62: 
  63:     // Pin the first 8 bytes of the encoded form (the header carries
  64:     // m_bits + k as u32 LE):
  65:     //   m_bits = 77 → 0x4D 0x00 0x00 0x00
  66:     //   k      = round(ln(2) * 77 / 8) = round(6.674) = 7 → 0x07 0x00 0x00 0x00
  67:     assert_eq!(&encoded[0..4], &[0x4D, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]);
  68:     assert_eq!(&encoded[4..8], &[0x07, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]);
  69:     // Reserved bytes must be zero.
  70:     assert_eq!(&encoded[8..12], &[0, 0, 0, 0]);
  71: 
  72:     // The bit-array bytes [12..22] are determined by xxh3-128 with seed
  73:     // XXH3_BLOOM_SEED = 0xB100_F117_E000_0001, computed over each of
  74:     // the 8 chunk_ids. The h1 / h2 split + the (h1 + i*h2) mod 77
  75:     // formula gives a fixed bit pattern.
  76:     //
  77:     // Pin the bit-array via hex. Any change to:
  78:     //   - the xxh3 seed constant
  79:     //   - the (h1, h2) split (low/high u64)
  80:     //   - the position formula
  81:     //   - the bit-set ordering
  82:     // will fail this assertion.
  83:     let bits = &encoded[12..];
  84:     let bits_hex = hex_encode_lower(bits);
  85:     // Print on failure so the new vector is easy to copy in if the
  86:     // implementation legitimately changes via ADR amendment.
  87:     let expected_hex = pinned_bits_hex();
  88:     assert_eq!(
  89:         bits_hex, expected_hex,
  90:         "Bloom bit-array bytes diverged from pinned vector. \
  91:          If you changed the hash function or seed, update the test \
  92:          vector AND bump the wire-format version per ADR-0011."
  93:     );
  94: }
  95: 
  96: #[test]
  97: fn round_trip_pinned_filter_finds_only_inputs() {
  98:     // Functional check: any chunk_id NOT in the input set should be
  99:     // bloom-rejected with high probability. We assert ≥6 of 8 random
 100:     // outsiders are rejected (the 1% FP rate is per-query; for n=8 the
 101:     // empirical rate is noisier).
 102:     let inputs: Vec<[u8; 32]> = (0u32..8)
 103:         .map(|i| {
 104:             let mut a = [0u8; 32];
 105:             a[..4].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
 106:             a[31] = 0xCD;
 107:             a
 108:         })
 109:         .collect();
 110:     let mut bloom = Bloom::new(inputs.len());
 111:     for cid in &inputs {
 112:         bloom.insert(cid);
 113:     }
 114:     for cid in &inputs {
 115:         assert!(bloom.contains(cid), "inserted id must be present");
 116:     }
 117:     // For very small N (= 8) the empirical FP rate can be inflated.
 118:     // Just confirm at least one outsider is rejected (sanity, not a
 119:     // tight test).
 120:     let mut outsiders = 0;
 121:     let mut rejected = 0;
 122:     for i in 1000u32..1064 {
 123:         let mut a = [0u8; 32];
 124:         a[..4].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
 125:         a[31] = 0xEE;
 126:         outsiders += 1;
 127:         if !bloom.contains(&a) {
 128:             rejected += 1;
 129:         }
 130:     }
 131:     assert!(
 132:         rejected >= outsiders / 2,
 133:         "expected at least half of outsiders rejected; got {rejected}/{outsiders}"
 134:     );
 135: }

 137: fn hex_encode_lower(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
 138:     const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
 139:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
 140:     for &b in bytes {
 141:         out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
 142:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);
 143:     }
 144:     out
 145: }

 161:     // same constant. If you change the hash function: re-run, paste new
 162:     // value, and bump the wire-format version per ADR-0011.
 163:     PINNED_BITS_HEX
 164: }

  68:         for cid in &ids {
  69:             f.insert(cid);
  70:             let now = f.popcount();
  71:             prop_assert!(now >= prev);
  72:             prev = now;
  73:         }
  74:     }
  75: 
  76:     /// Property: any single bit-flip in the encoded bytes that hits a
  77:     /// reserved-zero byte produces a decode error.
  78:     #[test]
  79:     fn reserved_byte_corruption_rejected(
  80:         n in 1usize..100,
  81:         offset in 8usize..12,
  82:     ) {
  83:         let f = Bloom::new(n);
  84:         let mut encoded = f.encode().unwrap();
  85:         encoded[offset] ^= 0x42;
  86:         let result = Bloom::decode(&encoded);
  87:         prop_assert!(matches!(result, Err(BloomError::ReservedNonZero)));
  88:     }
  89: }

   1: //! Canonical decoder. Reads bytes produced by [`crate::CanonEncoder`]
   2: //! and surfaces typed values + length headers to the caller. Decoders
   3: //! refuse to interpret an unknown tag and never silently advance past
   4: //! corrupt input.
   5: 
   6: use crate::error::DecodeError;
   7: use crate::tag::TypeTag;
   8: use crate::varint::{decode_varint, decode_zigzag};
   9: 
  10: /// Read cursor over a canonical byte slice. Maintains position
  11: /// internally so successive `decode_*` calls walk the stream.
  12: #[derive(Debug)]
  13: pub struct CanonDecoder<'a> {
  14:     buffer: &'a [u8],
  15:     position: usize,
  16: }
  17: 
  18: impl<'a> CanonDecoder<'a> {
  19:     /// Build a decoder over `buffer` starting at byte 0.
  20:     #[must_use]
  21:     pub fn new(buffer: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
  22:         Self {
  23:             buffer,
  24:             position: 0,
  25:         }
  26:     }
  27: 
  28:     /// Bytes still ahead of the cursor.
  29:     #[must_use]
  30:     pub fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
  31:         self.buffer.len().saturating_sub(self.position)
  32:     }
  33: 
  34:     /// True iff the cursor is at the end of the buffer.
  35:     #[must_use]
  36:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  37:         self.position >= self.buffer.len()
  38:     }
  39: 
  40:     /// Current byte offset (useful for diagnostics).
  41:     #[must_use]
  42:     pub fn position(&self) -> usize {
  43:         self.position
  44:     }
  45: 
  46:     /// Peek at the next tag byte without advancing the cursor. Useful
  47:     /// for branchy decoders that need to dispatch on type.
  48:     pub fn peek_tag(&self) -> Result<TypeTag, DecodeError> {
  49:         let byte = self.peek_byte()?;
  50:         TypeTag::from_byte(byte)
  51:     }
  52: 
  53:     /// Read a single byte, advancing the cursor.
  54:     fn read_byte(&mut self) -> Result<u8, DecodeError> {
  55:         let byte = self.peek_byte()?;
  56:         self.position += 1;
  57:         Ok(byte)
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     fn peek_byte(&self) -> Result<u8, DecodeError> {
  61:         self.buffer
  62:             .get(self.position)
  63:             .copied()
  64:             .ok_or(DecodeError::UnexpectedEof(self.position))
  65:     }
  66: 
  67:     fn read_tag(&mut self) -> Result<TypeTag, DecodeError> {
  68:         let byte = self.read_byte()?;
  69:         TypeTag::from_byte(byte)
  70:     }
  71: 
  72:     fn expect_tag(&mut self, expected: TypeTag) -> Result<(), DecodeError> {
  73:         let found = self.read_tag()?;
  74:         if found == expected {
  75:             Ok(())
  76:         } else {
  77:             // Rewind so the caller can recover.
  78:             self.position -= 1;
  79:             Err(DecodeError::TagMismatch { expected, found })
  80:         }
  81:     }
  82: 
  83:     fn read_varint(&mut self) -> Result<u64, DecodeError> {
  84:         let (value, n) = decode_varint(self.buffer, self.position)?;
  85:         self.position += n;
  86:         Ok(value)
  87:     }
  88: 
  89:     fn read_zigzag(&mut self) -> Result<i64, DecodeError> {
  90:         let (value, n) = decode_zigzag(self.buffer, self.position)?;
  91:         self.position += n;
  92:         Ok(value)
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     fn read_slice(&mut self, len: usize) -> Result<&'a [u8], DecodeError> {
  96:         if len > self.remaining() {
  97:             return Err(DecodeError::LengthOverflow {
  98:                 claimed: len as u64,
  99:                 remaining: self.remaining(),
 100:             });
 101:         }
 102:         let slice = &self.buffer[self.position..self.position + len];
 103:         self.position += len;
 104:         Ok(slice)
 105:     }
 106: 
 107:     // ─── primitives ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 108: 
 109:     /// Read a `null` marker. Fails if the next tag isn't [`TypeTag::Null`].
 110:     pub fn decode_null(&mut self) -> Result<(), DecodeError> {
 111:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Null)
 112:     }
 113: 
 114:     /// Read a boolean (`True` or `False` tag, no payload).
 115:     pub fn decode_bool(&mut self) -> Result<bool, DecodeError> {
 116:         let tag = self.read_tag()?;
 117:         match tag {
 118:             TypeTag::True => Ok(true),
 119:             TypeTag::False => Ok(false),
 120:             other => {
 121:                 self.position -= 1;
 122:                 Err(DecodeError::TagMismatch {
 123:                     expected: TypeTag::True,
 124:                     found: other,
 125:                 })
 126:             }
 127:         }
 128:     }
 129: 
 130:     /// Read a u64.
 131:     pub fn decode_u64(&mut self) -> Result<u64, DecodeError> {
 132:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::UInt)?;
 133:         self.read_varint()
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     /// Read an i64.
 137:     pub fn decode_i64(&mut self) -> Result<i64, DecodeError> {
 138:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Int)?;
 139:         self.read_zigzag()
 140:     }
 141: 
 142:     /// Read an f32.
 143:     pub fn decode_f32(&mut self) -> Result<f32, DecodeError> {
 144:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Float32)?;
 145:         let bytes = self.read_slice(4)?;
 146:         let mut arr = [0u8; 4];
 147:         arr.copy_from_slice(bytes);
 148:         Ok(f32::from_be_bytes(arr))
 149:     }
 150: 
 151:     /// Read an f64.
 152:     pub fn decode_f64(&mut self) -> Result<f64, DecodeError> {
 153:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Float64)?;
 154:         let bytes = self.read_slice(8)?;
 155:         let mut arr = [0u8; 8];
 156:         arr.copy_from_slice(bytes);
 157:         Ok(f64::from_be_bytes(arr))
 158:     }
 159: 
 160:     /// Read a UTF-8 string.
 161:     pub fn decode_string(&mut self) -> Result<String, DecodeError> {
 162:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::String)?;
 163:         let len = self.read_varint()? as usize;
 164:         let slice = self.read_slice(len)?;
 165:         std::str::from_utf8(slice)
 166:             .map(str::to_owned)
 167:             .map_err(|_| DecodeError::InvalidUtf8)
 168:     }
 169: 
 170:     /// Read a raw byte slice.
 171:     pub fn decode_bytes(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DecodeError> {
 172:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Bytes)?;
 173:         let len = self.read_varint()? as usize;
 174:         Ok(self.read_slice(len)?.to_vec())
 175:     }
 176: 
 177:     /// Read an array header. Returns the element count; caller decodes
 178:     /// each element in turn.
 179:     pub fn decode_array_header(&mut self) -> Result<usize, DecodeError> {
 180:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Array)?;
 181:         Ok(self.read_varint()? as usize)
 182:     }
 183: 
 184:     /// Read a map header. Returns the pair count; caller decodes each
 185:     /// (key, value) in turn.
 186:     pub fn decode_map_header(&mut self) -> Result<usize, DecodeError> {
 187:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Map)?;
 188:         Ok(self.read_varint()? as usize)
 189:     }
 190: 
 191:     /// Read a `None` marker.
 192:     pub fn decode_none(&mut self) -> Result<(), DecodeError> {
 193:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::None)
 194:     }
 195: 
 196:     /// Read a `Some` marker (caller decodes the wrapped value next).
 197:     pub fn decode_some(&mut self) -> Result<(), DecodeError> {
 198:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Some)
 199:     }
 200: 
 201:     /// Read a timestamp (microseconds since the epoch).
 202:     pub fn decode_timestamp(&mut self) -> Result<i64, DecodeError> {
 203:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Timestamp)?;
 204:         self.read_zigzag()
 205:     }
 206: 
 207:     /// Read a UUID (16 bytes, no length prefix).
 208:     pub fn decode_uuid(&mut self) -> Result<[u8; 16], DecodeError> {
 209:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Uuid)?;
 210:         let slice = self.read_slice(16)?;
 211:         let mut out = [0u8; 16];
 212:         out.copy_from_slice(slice);
 213:         Ok(out)
 214:     }
 215: 
 216:     /// Read a node id (length-prefixed bytes).
 217:     pub fn decode_node_id(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DecodeError> {
 218:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::NodeId)?;
 219:         let len = self.read_varint()? as usize;
 220:         Ok(self.read_slice(len)?.to_vec())
 221:     }
 222: 
 223:     /// Read a struct header. Returns `(type_id, field_count)`; caller
 224:     /// decodes the fields.
 225:     pub fn decode_struct_header(&mut self) -> Result<(u32, usize), DecodeError> {
 226:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Struct)?;
 227:         let type_id = self.read_varint()? as u32;
 228:         let fields = self.read_varint()? as usize;
 229:         Ok((type_id, fields))
 230:     }
 231: 
 232:     /// Read an enum-variant header. Returns `(type_id, variant)`;
 233:     /// caller decodes the payload.
 234:     pub fn decode_enum_header(&mut self) -> Result<(u32, u32), DecodeError> {
 235:         self.expect_tag(TypeTag::Enum)?;
 236:         let type_id = self.read_varint()? as u32;
 237:         let variant = self.read_varint()? as u32;
 238:         Ok((type_id, variant))
 239:     }
 240: }

   1: //! Canonical encoder. Produces deterministic bytes that the decoder
   2: //! round-trips to the original value.
   3: 
   4: use crate::error::EncodeError;
   5: use crate::tag::TypeTag;
   6: use crate::varint::{encode_varint, encode_zigzag};
   7: 
   8: /// Streaming encoder that builds a canonical byte sequence into an
   9: /// internal `Vec<u8>`. Callers compose values by calling the
  10: /// per-type `encode_*` methods; the output is the concatenation of
  11: /// every emitted segment.
  12: ///
  13: /// The encoder is single-pass and never re-reads its buffer, so the
  14: /// order of `encode_*` calls IS the order of bytes on the wire.
  15: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  16: pub struct CanonEncoder {
  17:     buffer: Vec<u8>,
  18:     max_size: usize,
  19: }
  20: 
  21: impl CanonEncoder {
  22:     /// Build an empty encoder with a small starting capacity. No size
  23:     /// cap; the buffer grows on demand.
  24:     #[must_use]
  25:     pub fn new() -> Self {
  26:         Self {
  27:             buffer: Vec::with_capacity(256),
  28:             max_size: 0,
  29:         }
  30:     }
  31: 
  32:     /// Build an encoder that returns [`EncodeError::BufferOverflow`]
  33:     /// if any write would push the internal buffer past `max_size`
  34:     /// bytes. Use for accepting attacker-supplied inputs that could
  35:     /// otherwise drive unbounded allocation.
  36:     #[must_use]
  37:     pub fn with_limit(max_size: usize) -> Self {
  38:         let cap = if max_size == 0 {
  39:             256
  40:         } else {
  41:             max_size.min(256)
  42:         };
  43:         Self {
  44:             buffer: Vec::with_capacity(cap),
  45:             max_size,
  46:         }
  47:     }
  48: 
  49:     /// Consume the encoder and return the bytes it produced.
  50:     #[must_use]
  51:     pub fn finish(self) -> Vec<u8> {
  52:         self.buffer
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// Bytes emitted so far. Useful for length checks before
  56:     /// committing a frame.
  57:     #[must_use]
  58:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
  59:         self.buffer.len()
  60:     }
  61: 
  62:     /// True iff the encoder has emitted no bytes yet.
  63:     #[must_use]
  64:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  65:         self.buffer.is_empty()
  66:     }
  67: 
  68:     /// Borrow the in-progress buffer without consuming the encoder.
  69:     #[must_use]
  70:     pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[u8] {
  71:         &self.buffer
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     // ─── primitives ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  75: 
  76:     /// Encode `null`.
  77:     pub fn encode_null(&mut self) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
  78:         self.write_byte(TypeTag::Null.to_byte())
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     /// Encode a boolean.
  82:     pub fn encode_bool(&mut self, value: bool) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
  83:         self.write_byte(if value {
  84:             TypeTag::True.to_byte()
  85:         } else {
  86:             TypeTag::False.to_byte()
  87:         })
  88:     }
  89: 
  90:     /// Encode an unsigned 64-bit int.
  91:     pub fn encode_u64(&mut self, value: u64) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
  92:         self.reserve(1 + 10)?;
  93:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::UInt.to_byte());
  94:         encode_varint(value, &mut self.buffer);
  95:         Ok(())
  96:     }
  97: 
  98:     /// Encode a signed 64-bit int.
  99:     pub fn encode_i64(&mut self, value: i64) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 100:         self.reserve(1 + 10)?;
 101:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::Int.to_byte());
 102:         encode_zigzag(value, &mut self.buffer);
 103:         Ok(())
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     /// Encode an IEEE 754 binary32 with canonical NaN + -0.0 handling.
 107:     pub fn encode_f32(&mut self, value: f32) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 108:         let canonical = canonical_f32(value);
 109:         self.reserve(1 + 4)?;
 110:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::Float32.to_byte());
 111:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(&canonical.to_be_bytes());
 112:         Ok(())
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     /// Encode an IEEE 754 binary64 with canonical NaN + -0.0 handling.
 116:     pub fn encode_f64(&mut self, value: f64) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 117:         let canonical = canonical_f64(value);
 118:         self.reserve(1 + 8)?;
 119:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::Float64.to_byte());
 120:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(&canonical.to_be_bytes());
 121:         Ok(())
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     /// Encode a UTF-8 string.
 125:     pub fn encode_string(&mut self, value: &str) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 126:         let bytes = value.as_bytes();
 127:         self.reserve(1 + 10 + bytes.len())?;
 128:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::String.to_byte());
 129:         encode_varint(bytes.len() as u64, &mut self.buffer);
 130:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(bytes);
 131:         Ok(())
 132:     }
 133: 
 134:     /// Encode a raw byte slice.
 135:     pub fn encode_bytes(&mut self, value: &[u8]) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 136:         self.reserve(1 + 10 + value.len())?;
 137:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::Bytes.to_byte());
 138:         encode_varint(value.len() as u64, &mut self.buffer);
 139:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(value);
 140:         Ok(())
 141:     }

 145:         self.write_byte(TypeTag::None.to_byte())
 146:     }

 151:         self.write_byte(TypeTag::Some.to_byte())
 152:     }

 157:         self.reserve(1 + 10)?;
 158:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::Array.to_byte());
 159:         encode_varint(len as u64, &mut self.buffer);
 160:         Ok(())
 161:     }

 163:     /// Emit a map header. Caller MUST then write `len` (key, value)

 166:         self.reserve(1 + 10)?;

 169:         Ok(())

 180:         self.reserve(1 + 10 + 10)?;

 182:         encode_varint(u64::from(type_id), &mut self.buffer);

 190:         self.reserve(1 + 10 + 10)?;

 208:     pub fn encode_uuid(&mut self, bytes: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 209:         self.reserve(1 + 16)?;
 210:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::Uuid.to_byte());
 211:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(bytes);
 212:         Ok(())
 213:     }
