 215:     /// Encode a node / replica id (length-prefixed bytes).
 216:     pub fn encode_node_id(&mut self, node_id: &[u8]) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 217:         self.reserve(1 + 10 + node_id.len())?;
 218:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::NodeId.to_byte());
 219:         encode_varint(node_id.len() as u64, &mut self.buffer);
 220:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(node_id);
 221:         Ok(())
 222:     }

 224:     /// Encode a vector clock from a pre-sorted `(node_id, counter)`
 225:     /// iterator. Callers MUST sort by `node_id` for canonical output;
 226:     /// the encoder writes entries in iteration order.
 227:     pub fn encode_vector_clock(&mut self, entries: &[(Vec<u8>, u64)]) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 228:         self.reserve(1 + 10)?;
 229:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::VectorClock.to_byte());
 230:         encode_varint(entries.len() as u64, &mut self.buffer);
 231:         for (node_id, counter) in entries {
 232:             self.encode_node_id(node_id)?;
 233:             self.encode_u64(*counter)?;
 234:         }
 235:         Ok(())
 236:     }

 238:     /// Encode an HLC timestamp (wall-time micros, logical counter,
 239:     /// node id).
 240:     pub fn encode_hlc(
 241:         &mut self,
 242:         wall_time: i64,
 243:         logical: u32,
 244:         node_id: &[u8],
 245:     ) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 246:         self.reserve(1 + 10 + 10 + 10 + node_id.len())?;
 247:         self.buffer.push(TypeTag::HLC.to_byte());
 248:         encode_zigzag(wall_time, &mut self.buffer);
 249:         encode_varint(u64::from(logical), &mut self.buffer);
 250:         encode_varint(node_id.len() as u64, &mut self.buffer);
 251:         self.buffer.extend_from_slice(node_id);
 252:         Ok(())
 253:     }

 255:     // ─── internals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
 256: 
 257:     fn write_byte(&mut self, byte: u8) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 258:         self.reserve(1)?;
 259:         self.buffer.push(byte);
 260:         Ok(())
 261:     }
 262: 
 263:     fn reserve(&mut self, n: usize) -> Result<(), EncodeError> {
 264:         if self.max_size > 0 && self.buffer.len() + n > self.max_size {
 265:             Err(EncodeError::BufferOverflow)
 266:         } else {
 267:             Ok(())
 268:         }
 269:     }

 272: /// Collapse every NaN bit pattern to the canonical IEEE 754 quiet NaN
 273: /// and -0.0 to +0.0. Other values pass through untouched.
 274: fn canonical_f32(value: f32) -> f32 {
 275:     if value.is_nan() {
 276:         f32::NAN
 277:     } else if value == 0.0 {
 278:         0.0
 279:     } else {
 280:         value
 281:     }
 282: }
 283: 
 284: /// f64 mirror of [`canonical_f32`].
 285: fn canonical_f64(value: f64) -> f64 {
 286:     if value.is_nan() {
 287:         f64::NAN
 288:     } else if value == 0.0 {
 289:         0.0
 290:     } else {
 291:         value
 292:     }
 293: }

   1: //! Typed encode + decode failure modes for the canonical codec.
   2: 
   3: use thiserror::Error;
   4: 
   5: /// Errors the encoder can surface. The encoder is infallible for the
   6: /// in-memory `Vec<u8>` path; the only knob that produces errors is the
   7: /// optional [`crate::CanonEncoder::with_limit`] cap, which lets
   8: /// callers refuse to allocate more than a budget allows.
   9: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
  10: pub enum EncodeError {
  11:     /// `with_limit(N)` was set and this write would push the buffer
  12:     /// past N bytes.
  13:     #[error("encoder buffer would exceed configured limit")]
  14:     BufferOverflow,
  15: }
  16: 
  17: /// Errors the decoder can return. All variants leave the decoder's
  18: /// read position unchanged so the caller can inspect the error +
  19: /// re-frame if needed.
  20: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
  21: pub enum DecodeError {
  22:     /// Input ended mid-value. Includes the byte offset where the
  23:     /// truncation was detected so log lines pinpoint the breakage.
  24:     #[error("unexpected end of input at byte {0}")]
  25:     UnexpectedEof(usize),
  26: 
  27:     /// Wire byte didn't map to any known [`crate::TypeTag`]. Carries
  28:     /// the raw byte for debug output. Decoders must reject this —
  29:     /// silently skipping an unknown tag would let an attacker hide
  30:     /// extra bytes in the frame.
  31:     #[error("unknown type tag: 0x{0:02X}")]
  32:     UnknownTag(u8),
  33: 
  34:     /// LEB128 varint exceeded 10 bytes (max for a u64). Indicates
  35:     /// either a corrupt input or a malicious oversize-varint attempt.
  36:     #[error("varint too long (>10 bytes); corrupt input")]
  37:     VarintTooLong,
  38: 
  39:     /// Caller expected one tag but the next byte was a different
  40:     /// (valid) tag. Carries both for clear diagnostics.
  41:     #[error("expected tag {expected:?}, found {found:?}")]
  42:     TagMismatch {
  43:         /// The tag the caller expected to see.
  44:         expected: crate::TypeTag,
  45:         /// The tag actually present on the wire.
  46:         found: crate::TypeTag,
  47:     },
  48: 
  49:     /// UTF-8 string field contained invalid UTF-8 bytes.
  50:     #[error("invalid UTF-8 in string field")]
  51:     InvalidUtf8,
  52: 
  53:     /// Length-prefixed field claimed a length larger than the
  54:     /// remaining buffer. Indicates a corrupt or malicious input.
  55:     #[error("length prefix {claimed} exceeds remaining {remaining}")]
  56:     LengthOverflow {
  57:         /// Length the wire frame claimed.

   1: //! `ol_canon` — canonical-bytes encoder for the One Link engine.
   2: //!
   3: //! Ported by hand from `coherence_lang/std/codec/canon.cl` (the
   4: //! algebraic specification). Provides deterministic, self-describing
   5: //! binary encoding that the CRDT lattice, capability calculus, and
   6: //! every wire frame relies on.
   7: //!
   8: //! ## Determinism guarantees
   9: //!
  10: //! - Same value → same bytes, every time, on every platform.
  11: //! - Map / vector-clock keys MUST be pre-sorted by caller (lexicographic
  12: //!   on the encoded key bytes); the encoder writes them in iteration
  13: //!   order to keep the hot path branch-free.
  14: //! - Floats canonicalised: all NaNs collapse to a single quiet-NaN
  15: //!   bit pattern; -0.0 collapses to +0.0.
  16: //! - Integers use LEB128 varints (unsigned) and zigzag-LEB128 (signed)
  17: //!   — same shape RFC 8949 (CBOR) mandates, plus the canonical-ordering
  18: //!   extensions the CL spec adds.
  19: //!
  20: //! ## Type tags
  21: //!
  22: //! Wire format is self-describing: every value starts with a 1-byte
  23: //! [`TypeTag`] discriminant. Decoders refuse to interpret a tag as a
  24: //! different type — no implicit conversions on the wire.
  25: 
  26: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  27: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  28: 
  29: mod decoder;
  30: mod encoder;
  31: mod error;
  32: mod tag;
  33: mod varint;
  34: 
  35: pub use decoder::CanonDecoder;
  36: pub use encoder::CanonEncoder;
  37: pub use error::{DecodeError, EncodeError};
  38: pub use tag::TypeTag;
  39: pub use varint::{decode_varint, decode_zigzag, encode_varint, encode_zigzag};

   1: //! Self-describing type-tag discriminants for the canonical wire
   2: //! format. Values mirror `coherence_lang/std/codec/canon.cl` byte for
   3: //! byte so a future codegen pass can replace this enum with a
   4: //! generated copy without breaking existing encoded blobs.
   5: 
   6: use crate::error::DecodeError;
   7: 
   8: /// Discriminant byte that precedes every encoded value on the wire.
   9: ///
  10: /// Holes in the value space (e.g. 0x03–0x0F between `True` and `UInt`)
  11: /// are reserved for future tags; decoders MUST reject unknown tags
  12: /// rather than silently skipping bytes.
  13: #[repr(u8)]
  14: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
  15: pub enum TypeTag {
  16:     /// Null value (no payload).
  17:     Null = 0x00,
  18:     /// Boolean `false` (no payload).
  19:     False = 0x01,
  20:     /// Boolean `true` (no payload).
  21:     True = 0x02,
  22:     /// Unsigned int, followed by an LEB128 varint.
  23:     UInt = 0x10,
  24:     /// Signed int, followed by a zigzag LEB128 varint.
  25:     Int = 0x11,
  26:     /// IEEE 754 binary32, followed by 4 big-endian bytes.
  27:     Float32 = 0x20,
  28:     /// IEEE 754 binary64, followed by 8 big-endian bytes.
  29:     Float64 = 0x21,
  30:     /// UTF-8 string, length-prefixed varint then bytes.
  31:     String = 0x30,
  32:     /// Raw byte slice, length-prefixed varint then bytes.
  33:     Bytes = 0x31,
  34:     /// Array / list, length-prefixed varint then N encoded values.
  35:     Array = 0x40,
  36:     /// Map, length-prefixed varint then N (key, value) pairs.
  37:     /// **Caller MUST pre-sort keys** for canonical determinism.
  38:     Map = 0x50,
  39:     /// Struct: tag, type-id varint, field-count varint, then fields.
  40:     Struct = 0x60,
  41:     /// Enum variant: tag, type-id varint, variant-id varint, payload.
  42:     Enum = 0x70,
  43:     /// `Option::None` (no payload).
  44:     None = 0x80,
  45:     /// `Option::Some` (followed by the wrapped value).
  46:     Some = 0x81,
  47:     /// Timestamp: zigzag varint of microseconds since the Unix epoch.
  48:     Timestamp = 0x90,
  49:     /// 128-bit UUID, written as 16 raw bytes (no length prefix).
  50:     Uuid = 0x91,
  51:     /// Replica / node identifier: length-prefixed varint then bytes.
  52:     NodeId = 0xA0,
  53:     /// Vector clock: length-prefixed varint then N (key, value) pairs.
  54:     /// Caller-sorted by node-id for canonical form.
  55:     VectorClock = 0xA1,
  56:     /// Hybrid logical clock: wall-time (zigzag varint), logical
  57:     /// (varint), then a length-prefixed node id.
  58:     HLC = 0xA2,
  59: }

  61: impl TypeTag {
  62:     /// Build a `TypeTag` from a wire byte, rejecting unknown tags.

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_canon/src/varint.rs", "bytes": 3823, "sha256": "c14df890d42da2b930d3e99e98e07f20d140701f11e41f794f287f16112ebe9f", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:47.928309+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! LEB128 varint + zigzag-LEB128 signed varint, the wire primitives
   2: //! every length prefix + integer field uses.
   3: //!
   4: //! Encoding: 7 bits per byte, MSB set on continuation. Bytes go LSB
   5: //! first. Max 10 bytes for u64 (9 full-7-bit groups + a 1-bit tail).
   6: 
   7: use crate::error::DecodeError;
   8: 
   9: /// Largest varint length for a u64 input (`ceil(64 / 7) = 10` bytes).
  10: pub(crate) const MAX_VARINT_BYTES: usize = 10;
  11: 
  12: /// Encode an unsigned 64-bit value as an LEB128 varint into `out`.
  13: pub fn encode_varint(mut value: u64, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
  14:     loop {
  15:         let byte = (value & 0x7F) as u8;
  16:         value >>= 7;
  17:         if value == 0 {
  18:             out.push(byte);
  19:             return;
  20:         }
  21:         out.push(byte | 0x80);
  22:     }
  23: }
  24: 
  25: /// Decode an LEB128 varint starting at `pos`. Returns `(value,
  26: /// bytes_consumed)` on success.
  27: pub fn decode_varint(input: &[u8], pos: usize) -> Result<(u64, usize), DecodeError> {
  28:     let mut shift = 0u32;
  29:     let mut value: u64 = 0;
  30:     let mut bytes = 0usize;
  31:     for &byte in input.iter().skip(pos).take(MAX_VARINT_BYTES) {
  32:         bytes += 1;
  33:         let chunk = u64::from(byte & 0x7F);
  34:         // Reject overflow on the 10th byte where shift=63 leaves only
  35:         // 1 bit of headroom.
  36:         if shift >= 64 || chunk.checked_shl(shift).is_none() {
  37:             return Err(DecodeError::VarintTooLong);
  38:         }
  39:         value |= chunk << shift;
  40:         if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
  41:             return Ok((value, bytes));
  42:         }
  43:         shift += 7;
  44:     }
  45:     if bytes == 0 {
  46:         Err(DecodeError::UnexpectedEof(pos))
  47:     } else {
  48:         Err(DecodeError::VarintTooLong)
  49:     }
  50: }
  51: 
  52: /// Encode an i64 as a zigzag-LEB128 varint. The transform is
  53: /// `(n << 1) ^ (n >> 63)` so small negatives stay tiny on the wire.
  54: pub fn encode_zigzag(value: i64, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
  55:     // The cast keeps the sign-bit smear; we then shift left by 1 and
  56:     // XOR with the smear so positive numbers become 2n and negative
  57:     // -(n+1) becomes 2n+1.
  58:     let zigzag = ((value as u64) << 1) ^ ((value >> 63) as u64);
  59:     encode_varint(zigzag, out);
  60: }
  61: 
  62: /// Decode a zigzag-LEB128 signed varint. Inverse of [`encode_zigzag`].
  63: pub fn decode_zigzag(input: &[u8], pos: usize) -> Result<(i64, usize), DecodeError> {
  64:     let (raw, n) = decode_varint(input, pos)?;
  65:     // (raw >> 1) ^ -(raw & 1) — the standard zigzag inverse.
  66:     let value = ((raw >> 1) as i64) ^ -((raw & 1) as i64);
  67:     Ok((value, n))
  68: }

   1: //! Byte-equivalence gate for `ol_canon`. Per the plan: 1M random
   2: //! structured inputs MUST produce byte-identical output across runs.
   3: //!
   4: //! Configurable via ``OL_CANON_GATE_ITERS`` (default 100k for
   5: //! everyday `cargo test`; CI nightly sets 1_000_000 to meet the
   6: //! plan's Phase A1 acceptance number).
   7: 
   8: use ol_canon::{CanonDecoder, CanonEncoder};
   9: 
  10: /// SplitMix64 — deterministic, fast, ample quality for round-trip
  11: /// fuzzing. Same constants as the rest of the workspace's randomized
  12: /// gates so seeds are interchangeable.
  13: fn next_rng(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {
  14:     *state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  15:     let mut z = *state;
  16:     z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  17:     z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  18:     z ^ (z >> 31)
  19: }
  20: 
  21: #[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
  22: enum Value {
  23:     Null,
  24:     Bool(bool),
  25:     U64(u64),
  26:     I64(i64),
  27:     F64(f64),
  28:     String(String),
  29:     Bytes(Vec<u8>),
  30: }
  31: 
  32: fn random_value(state: &mut u64) -> Value {
  33:     match next_rng(state) % 7 {
  34:         0 => Value::Null,
  35:         1 => Value::Bool(next_rng(state) & 1 == 0),
  36:         2 => Value::U64(next_rng(state)),
  37:         3 => Value::I64(next_rng(state) as i64),
  38:         4 => {
  39:             // Reject NaN/Inf so the round-trip equality holds at the
  40:             // bit level. Canonicalisation is tested separately.
  41:             let bits = next_rng(state);
  42:             let f = f64::from_bits(bits);
  43:             if f.is_nan() || f.is_infinite() {
  44:                 Value::F64(0.0)
  45:             } else {
  46:                 Value::F64(f)
  47:             }
  48:         }
  49:         5 => {
  50:             let len = (next_rng(state) % 16) as usize;
  51:             let mut s = String::with_capacity(len);
  52:             for _ in 0..len {
  53:                 // ASCII printable so we don't need full UTF-8 generators
  54:                 let c = b'a' + (next_rng(state) % 26) as u8;
  55:                 s.push(c as char);
  56:             }
  57:             Value::String(s)
  58:         }
  59:         _ => {
  60:             let len = (next_rng(state) % 32) as usize;
  61:             let bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..len).map(|_| (next_rng(state) & 0xFF) as u8).collect();
  62:             Value::Bytes(bytes)
  63:         }
  64:     }
  65: }
  66: 
  67: fn encode(value: &Value) -> Vec<u8> {
  68:     let mut e = CanonEncoder::new();
  69:     match value {
  70:         Value::Null => e.encode_null().unwrap(),
  71:         Value::Bool(v) => e.encode_bool(*v).unwrap(),
  72:         Value::U64(v) => e.encode_u64(*v).unwrap(),
  73:         Value::I64(v) => e.encode_i64(*v).unwrap(),
  74:         Value::F64(v) => e.encode_f64(*v).unwrap(),
  75:         Value::String(v) => e.encode_string(v).unwrap(),
  76:         Value::Bytes(v) => e.encode_bytes(v).unwrap(),
  77:     }
  78:     e.finish()
  79: }
  80: 
  81: fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Value {
  82:     let mut d = CanonDecoder::new(bytes);
  83:     let tag = d.peek_tag().unwrap();
  84:     match tag {
  85:         ol_canon::TypeTag::Null => {
  86:             d.decode_null().unwrap();
  87:             Value::Null
  88:         }
  89:         ol_canon::TypeTag::True | ol_canon::TypeTag::False => Value::Bool(d.decode_bool().unwrap()),
  90:         ol_canon::TypeTag::UInt => Value::U64(d.decode_u64().unwrap()),
  91:         ol_canon::TypeTag::Int => Value::I64(d.decode_i64().unwrap()),
  92:         ol_canon::TypeTag::Float64 => Value::F64(d.decode_f64().unwrap()),
  93:         ol_canon::TypeTag::String => Value::String(d.decode_string().unwrap()),
  94:         ol_canon::TypeTag::Bytes => Value::Bytes(d.decode_bytes().unwrap()),
  95:         other => panic!("unexpected tag: {:?}", other),
  96:     }
  97: }
  98: 
  99: #[test]
 100: fn property_random_values_round_trip_and_are_deterministic() {
 101:     let iters: u64 = std::env::var("OL_CANON_GATE_ITERS")
 102:         .ok()
 103:         .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
 104:         .unwrap_or(100_000);
 105:     let mut state: u64 = 0xC0DE_C0DE_C0DE_C0DE;
 106:     let mut fail = 0u64;
 107:     for _ in 0..iters {
 108:         let value = random_value(&mut state);
 109:         let bytes_a = encode(&value);
 110:         let bytes_b = encode(&value);
 111:         if bytes_a != bytes_b {
 112:             eprintln!("non-deterministic encode for {:?}", value);
 113:             fail += 1;
 114:             continue;
 115:         }
 116:         let decoded = decode(&bytes_a);
 117:         // Float bit-equality: NaN/Inf were filtered above.
 118:         if let (Value::F64(a), Value::F64(b)) = (&value, &decoded) {
 119:             if a.to_bits() != b.to_bits() {
 120:                 eprintln!("f64 round-trip mismatch: {} vs {}", a, b);
 121:                 fail += 1;
 122:                 continue;
 123:             }
 124:         } else if value != decoded {
 125:             eprintln!("round-trip mismatch: {:?} → {:?}", value, decoded);
 126:             fail += 1;
 127:         }
 128:     }
 129:     assert_eq!(
 130:         fail, 0,
 131:         "byte-equivalence gate: {fail} / {iters} round-trips failed"
 132:     );
 133: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_capability/src/capability.rs", "bytes": 14699, "sha256": "b557afc5dda05bc3923c78a177ec80952b7e5a1a6cf4a3ca5ba6091e2aaa98bd", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-14T17:20:15.254664+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}

   1: //! The `Capability` type — macaroon-style cap with HMAC-chained caveats.
   2: 
   3: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
   4: use zeroize::Zeroizing;
   5: 
   6: use crate::caveat::Caveat;
   7: use crate::context::Context;
   8: use crate::error::CapError;
   9: 
  10: /// Length of the root HMAC key in bytes.
  11: pub const ROOT_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  12: /// Length of the cap identifier in bytes.
  13: pub const CAP_ID_LEN: usize = 32;
  14: /// Length of the HMAC chain signature in bytes.
  15: pub const SIGNATURE_LEN: usize = 32;
  16: 
  17: /// Maximum number of caveats accepted by [`Capability::decode`].
  18: /// `verify` re-derives the HMAC chain in O(n caveats), so allowing
  19: /// an attacker-controlled count enables a DoS (audit H15 May 2026).
  20: /// 32 is well above any legitimate delegation chain depth.
  21: pub const MAX_CAVEATS: usize = 32;
  22: 
  23: /// Maximum total wire bytes accepted by [`Capability::decode`]. Acts
  24: /// as a belt-and-suspenders cap for the per-caveat parser plus the
  25: /// `MAX_CAVEATS` count check (audit H15). 8 KiB is comfortable for
  26: /// 32 caveats with reasonable payload sizes.
  27: pub const MAX_WIRE_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024;
  28: 
  29: /// BLAKE3 derive_key context for the root → initial-signature derivation.
  30: const ROOT_HMAC_CONTEXT: &str = "ol-capability-root-v1";
  31: /// BLAKE3 derive_key context for each caveat-step in the chain.
  32: const STEP_HMAC_CONTEXT: &str = "ol-capability-step-v1";
  33: 
  34: /// A 32-byte root HMAC key. Issuer keeps this secret. Zeroized on drop.
  35: pub type RootKey = Zeroizing<[u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN]>;
  36: 
  37: /// A capability: identifier + ordered caveats + HMAC chain signature.
  38: ///
  39: /// Equality compares identifier + caveats + signature; constant-time
  40: /// signature compare is in [`Self::verify`], not in `PartialEq`.
  41: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  42: pub struct Capability {
  43:     /// 32-byte cap identifier. Public; identifies the cap without
  44:     /// revealing the root key. Often `BLAKE3.derive_key("ol-cap-id-v1",
  45:     /// root_key || nonce)` so the issuer can look up the right key.
  46:     id: [u8; CAP_ID_LEN],
  47:     /// Caveats appended in chain order.
  48:     caveats: Vec<Caveat>,
  49:     /// HMAC chain signature; the keyed-hash of the terminal caveat.
  50:     signature: [u8; SIGNATURE_LEN],
  51: }
  52: 
  53: impl Capability {
  54:     /// Mint a fresh root capability with NO caveats.
  55:     ///
  56:     /// `id` identifies the cap (e.g. BLAKE3 of root + a nonce). Pick
  57:     /// a fresh nonce per cap so identical caveat chains don't collide.
  58:     pub fn root(id: [u8; CAP_ID_LEN], root_key: &RootKey) -> Self {
  59:         // Initial signature = derive_key("ol-capability-root-v1", root_key || id)
  60:         let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(ROOT_KEY_LEN + CAP_ID_LEN);
  61:         input.extend_from_slice(&root_key[..]);
  62:         input.extend_from_slice(&id);
  63:         let signature = blake3::derive_key(ROOT_HMAC_CONTEXT, &input);
  64:         Self {
  65:             id,
  66:             caveats: Vec::new(),
  67:             signature,
  68:         }
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     /// Borrow the cap identifier.
  72:     #[inline]
  73:     #[must_use]
  74:     pub fn id(&self) -> &[u8; CAP_ID_LEN] {
  75:         &self.id
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     /// Borrow the caveats in chain order.
  79:     #[inline]
  80:     #[must_use]
  81:     pub fn caveats(&self) -> &[Caveat] {
  82:         &self.caveats
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     /// Borrow the current HMAC chain signature.
  86:     #[inline]
  87:     #[must_use]
  88:     pub fn signature(&self) -> &[u8; SIGNATURE_LEN] {
  89:         &self.signature
  90:     }
  91: 
  92:     /// Attenuate: append a new caveat, advancing the HMAC chain. The
  93:     /// returned cap is verifiable under the SAME root key — the chain
  94:     /// re-derives identically because each step is deterministic in
  95:     /// `(prev_sig, caveat_bytes)`.
  96:     pub fn attenuate(&self, caveat: Caveat) -> Self {
  97:         let caveat_bytes = caveat.encode();
  98:         let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(SIGNATURE_LEN + caveat_bytes.len());
  99:         input.extend_from_slice(&self.signature);
 100:         input.extend_from_slice(&caveat_bytes);
 101:         let new_sig = blake3::derive_key(STEP_HMAC_CONTEXT, &input);
 102: 
 103:         let mut caveats = self.caveats.clone();
 104:         caveats.push(caveat);
 105:         Self {
 106:             id: self.id,
 107:             caveats,
 108:             signature: new_sig,
 109:         }
 110:     }
 111: 
 112:     /// Verify this capability against `root_key` + a runtime `ctx`.
 113:     ///
 114:     /// Two checks:
 115:     /// 1. **Signature check** (constant-time): recompute the HMAC
 116:     ///    chain from `root_key` over the carried caveats; compare to
 117:     ///    the carried signature via `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`.
 118:     /// 2. **Caveat check**: for each caveat, evaluate against `ctx`.
 119:     ///    Any caveat failing rejects the cap.
 120:     ///
 121:     /// # Errors
 122:     ///
 123:     /// - [`CapError::SignatureMismatch`] on signature failure.
 124:     /// - [`CapError::CaveatRejected`] on caveat failure.
 125:     pub fn verify(&self, root_key: &RootKey, ctx: &Context) -> Result<(), CapError> {
 126:         // Re-derive the expected signature.
 127:         let mut expected = {
 128:             let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(ROOT_KEY_LEN + CAP_ID_LEN);
 129:             input.extend_from_slice(&root_key[..]);
 130:             input.extend_from_slice(&self.id);
 131:             blake3::derive_key(ROOT_HMAC_CONTEXT, &input)
 132:         };
 133:         for caveat in &self.caveats {
 134:             let caveat_bytes = caveat.encode();
 135:             let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(SIGNATURE_LEN + caveat_bytes.len());
 136:             input.extend_from_slice(&expected);
 137:             input.extend_from_slice(&caveat_bytes);
 138:             expected = blake3::derive_key(STEP_HMAC_CONTEXT, &input);
 139:         }
 140:         // Constant-time compare.
 141:         if expected.ct_eq(&self.signature).unwrap_u8() != 1 {
 142:             return Err(CapError::SignatureMismatch);
 143:         }
 144:         // Per-caveat check.
 145:         for (idx, caveat) in self.caveats.iter().enumerate() {
 146:             if let Err(reason) = caveat.check(ctx) {
 147:                 return Err(CapError::CaveatRejected { idx, reason });
 148:             }
 149:         }
 150:         Ok(())
 151:     }
 152: 
 153:     /// Returns true iff this cap accepts `ctx` (under `root_key`).
 154:     /// Convenience around [`Self::verify`].
 155:     #[must_use]
 156:     pub fn accepts(&self, root_key: &RootKey, ctx: &Context) -> bool {
 157:         self.verify(root_key, ctx).is_ok()
 158:     }
 159: 
 160:     /// Encode to wire bytes:
 161:     /// `[id (32 B)][caveat_count u32 LE][caveat_1 .. caveat_n][signature (32 B)]`.
 162:     #[must_use]
 163:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
 164:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(CAP_ID_LEN + 4 + 1024 + SIGNATURE_LEN);
 165:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.id);
 166:         let count = u32::try_from(self.caveats.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 167:         out.extend_from_slice(&count.to_le_bytes());
 168:         for caveat in &self.caveats {
 169:             out.extend_from_slice(&caveat.encode());
 170:         }
 171:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.signature);
 172:         out
 173:     }
 174: 
 175:     /// Decode from wire bytes. Does NOT verify the signature — caller
 176:     /// must invoke `verify` separately.
 177:     ///
 178:     /// Bounded on both the caveat count (`MAX_CAVEATS`) and the wire
 179:     /// size (`MAX_WIRE_BYTES`) so an attacker can't ship a malicious
 180:     /// capability that costs O(N) HMAC steps to validate against an
 181:     /// attacker-supplied N (audit H15 May 2026).
 182:     ///
 183:     /// # Errors
 184:     ///
 185:     /// [`CapError::Malformed`] / [`CapError::UnknownCaveat`] on
 186:     /// structural failures, or [`CapError::Malformed`] with a
 187:     /// resource-bound reason if the wire is over-budget.
 188:     pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, CapError> {
 189:         if bytes.len() > MAX_WIRE_BYTES {
 190:             return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 191:                 reason: "wire bytes exceed MAX_WIRE_BYTES",
 192:             });
 193:         }
 194:         if bytes.len() < CAP_ID_LEN + 4 + SIGNATURE_LEN {
 195:             return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 196:                 reason: "wire bytes shorter than minimum header + footer",
 197:             });
 198:         }
 199:         let mut id = [0u8; CAP_ID_LEN];
 200:         id.copy_from_slice(&bytes[..CAP_ID_LEN]);
 201:         let count_bytes = &bytes[CAP_ID_LEN..CAP_ID_LEN + 4];
 202:         let count = u32::from_le_bytes(count_bytes.try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize;
 203:         if count > MAX_CAVEATS {
 204:             return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 205:                 reason: "caveat count exceeds MAX_CAVEATS",
 206:             });
 207:         }
 208: 
 209:         let mut caveats = Vec::with_capacity(count);
 210:         let mut cursor = CAP_ID_LEN + 4;
 211:         for _ in 0..count {
 212:             if bytes.len() < cursor + SIGNATURE_LEN {
 213:                 return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 214:                     reason: "caveat list overruns wire bytes",
 215:                 });
 216:             }
 217:             let (caveat, consumed) = Caveat::decode(&bytes[cursor..bytes.len() - SIGNATURE_LEN])?;
 218:             caveats.push(caveat);
 219:             cursor += consumed;
 220:         }
 221:         if bytes.len() != cursor + SIGNATURE_LEN {
 222:             return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 223:                 reason: "wire bytes do not end with signature exactly",
 224:             });
 225:         }
 226:         let mut signature = [0u8; SIGNATURE_LEN];
 227:         signature.copy_from_slice(&bytes[cursor..cursor + SIGNATURE_LEN]);
 228:         Ok(Self {
 229:             id,
 230:             caveats,
 231:             signature,
 232:         })
 233:     }
 234: }

   1: //! Caveats — typed predicates on the runtime context.
   2: 
   3: use crate::context::Context;
   4: use crate::error::CapError;
   5: 
   6: /// Tag bytes for the wire encoding of each caveat kind. Stable; new
   7: /// kinds get new tags (don't reuse).
   8: mod tag {
   9:     pub(super) const EXPIRES_AT: u8 = 0x01;
  10:     pub(super) const PEER_FINGERPRINT: u8 = 0x02;
  11:     pub(super) const PATH_PREFIX: u8 = 0x03;
  12:     pub(super) const OPERATION_IN: u8 = 0x04;
  13:     pub(super) const AUDIT_TAG: u8 = 0x05;
  14: }
  15: 
  16: /// A single caveat. Caveats compose: a capability's permission is the
  17: /// AND of all its caveats.
  18: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  19: pub enum Caveat {
  20:     /// Cap is valid until this absolute Unix-ms timestamp.
  21:     ExpiresAt(u64),
  22:     /// Cap is bound to a specific peer fingerprint.
  23:     PeerFingerprint([u8; 32]),
  24:     /// Cap restricts operations to paths starting with this prefix.
  25:     PathPrefix(String),
  26:     /// Operation must be one of these names.
  27:     OperationIn(Vec<String>),
  28:     /// Audit tag — doesn't restrict; logged on every use to identify
  29:     /// the delegation chain.
  30:     AuditTag(String),
  31: }
  32: 
  33: impl Caveat {
  34:     /// Wire encoding: `[tag: u8][len: u32 LE][bytes]`.
  35:     pub(crate) fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
  36:         match self {
  37:             Self::ExpiresAt(ms) => {
  38:                 let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 4 + 8);
  39:                 out.push(tag::EXPIRES_AT);
  40:                 out.extend_from_slice(&8u32.to_le_bytes());
  41:                 out.extend_from_slice(&ms.to_le_bytes());
  42:                 out
  43:             }
  44:             Self::PeerFingerprint(fp) => {
  45:                 let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 4 + 32);
  46:                 out.push(tag::PEER_FINGERPRINT);
  47:                 out.extend_from_slice(&32u32.to_le_bytes());
  48:                 out.extend_from_slice(fp);
  49:                 out
  50:             }
  51:             Self::PathPrefix(p) => {
  52:                 let b = p.as_bytes();
  53:                 let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 4 + b.len());
  54:                 out.push(tag::PATH_PREFIX);
  55:                 out.extend_from_slice(&(b.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
  56:                 out.extend_from_slice(b);
  57:                 out
  58:             }
  59:             Self::OperationIn(ops) => {
  60:                 // Encoded as: count u32 LE, then each op as len u32 + bytes.
  61:                 let mut body = Vec::new();
  62:                 body.extend_from_slice(&(ops.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
  63:                 for op in ops {
  64:                     let b = op.as_bytes();
  65:                     body.extend_from_slice(&(b.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
  66:                     body.extend_from_slice(b);
  67:                 }
  68:                 let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 4 + body.len());
  69:                 out.push(tag::OPERATION_IN);
  70:                 out.extend_from_slice(&(body.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
  71:                 out.extend_from_slice(&body);
  72:                 out
  73:             }
  74:             Self::AuditTag(t) => {
  75:                 let b = t.as_bytes();
  76:                 let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 4 + b.len());
  77:                 out.push(tag::AUDIT_TAG);
  78:                 out.extend_from_slice(&(b.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
  79:                 out.extend_from_slice(b);
  80:                 out
  81:             }
  82:         }
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     /// Decode a single caveat from `buf`. Returns the caveat + the
  86:     /// number of bytes consumed.
  87:     pub(crate) fn decode(buf: &[u8]) -> Result<(Self, usize), CapError> {
  88:         if buf.len() < 5 {
  89:             return Err(CapError::Malformed {
  90:                 reason: "caveat header < 5 bytes",
  91:             });
  92:         }
  93:         let tag_byte = buf[0];
  94:         let len = u32::from_le_bytes(buf[1..5].try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize;
  95:         if buf.len() < 5 + len {
  96:             return Err(CapError::Malformed {
  97:                 reason: "caveat truncated",
  98:             });
  99:         }
 100:         let body = &buf[5..5 + len];
 101:         let caveat = match tag_byte {
 102:             tag::EXPIRES_AT => {
 103:                 if body.len() != 8 {
 104:                     return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 105:                         reason: "ExpiresAt body != 8 bytes",
 106:                     });
 107:                 }
 108:                 let ms = u64::from_le_bytes(body.try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 109:                 Self::ExpiresAt(ms)
 110:             }
 111:             tag::PEER_FINGERPRINT => {
 112:                 if body.len() != 32 {
 113:                     return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 114:                         reason: "PeerFingerprint body != 32 bytes",
 115:                     });
 116:                 }
 117:                 let mut fp = [0u8; 32];
 118:                 fp.copy_from_slice(body);
 119:                 Self::PeerFingerprint(fp)
 120:             }
 121:             tag::PATH_PREFIX => {
 122:                 let s = std::str::from_utf8(body).map_err(|_| CapError::Malformed {
 123:                     reason: "PathPrefix body not UTF-8",
 124:                 })?;
 125:                 Self::PathPrefix(s.to_string())
 126:             }
 127:             tag::OPERATION_IN => {
 128:                 if body.len() < 4 {
 129:                     return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 130:                         reason: "OperationIn header < 4 bytes",
 131:                     });
 132:                 }
 133:                 let count = u32::from_le_bytes(body[..4].try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize;
 134:                 let mut ops = Vec::with_capacity(count);
 135:                 let mut cursor = 4usize;
 136:                 for _ in 0..count {
 137:                     if body.len() < cursor + 4 {
 138:                         return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 139:                             reason: "OperationIn entry truncated",
 140:                         });
 141:                     }
 142:                     let l =
 143:                         u32::from_le_bytes(body[cursor..cursor + 4].try_into().expect("4 bytes"))
 144:                             as usize;
 145:                     cursor += 4;
 146:                     if body.len() < cursor + l {
 147:                         return Err(CapError::Malformed {
 148:                             reason: "OperationIn entry body truncated",
 149:                         });
 150:                     }
 151:                     let s = std::str::from_utf8(&body[cursor..cursor + l]).map_err(|_| {
 152:                         CapError::Malformed {
 153:                             reason: "OperationIn entry not UTF-8",
 154:                         }
 155:                     })?;
 156:                     ops.push(s.to_string());
 157:                     cursor += l;
 158:                 }
 159:                 Self::OperationIn(ops)
 160:             }
 161:             tag::AUDIT_TAG => {
 162:                 let s = std::str::from_utf8(body).map_err(|_| CapError::Malformed {
 163:                     reason: "AuditTag body not UTF-8",
 164:                 })?;
 165:                 Self::AuditTag(s.to_string())
 166:             }
 167:             other => return Err(CapError::UnknownCaveat { tag: other }),
 168:         };
 169:         Ok((caveat, 5 + len))
 170:     }
 171: 
 172:     /// Evaluate this caveat against `ctx`. Returns `Ok(())` if the
 173:     /// caveat permits the context; `Err` with a static reason otherwise.
 174:     pub(crate) fn check(&self, ctx: &Context) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
 175:         match self {
 176:             Self::ExpiresAt(ms) => {
 177:                 if let Some(now) = ctx.now_unix_ms {
 178:                     // Audit L9 May 2026: tightened to `>=`. A cap with
 179:                     // `not_after_ms == now` was previously still
 180:                     // valid for the exact millisecond it expired;
 181:                     // inconsistent with `not_before_ms`'s strict `<`
 182:                     // and with caps_grants.py's `>= not_after_ms`
 183:                     // semantics. Symmetric strict-boundary handling
 184:                     // is least-surprise.
 185:                     if now >= *ms {
 186:                         return Err("ExpiresAt: cap expired");
 187:                     }
 188:                 } else {
 189:                     return Err("ExpiresAt: ctx.now_unix_ms not provided");
 190:                 }
 191:             }
 192:             Self::PeerFingerprint(fp) => {
 193:                 if let Some(peer) = ctx.peer {
 194:                     if &peer != fp {
 195:                         return Err("PeerFingerprint: peer mismatch");
 196:                     }
 197:                 } else {
 198:                     return Err("PeerFingerprint: ctx.peer not provided");
 199:                 }
 200:             }
 201:             Self::PathPrefix(p) => {
 202:                 if let Some(path) = ctx.path {
 203:                     if !path.starts_with(p.as_str()) {
 204:                         return Err("PathPrefix: path not under prefix");
 205:                     }
 206:                 } else {
 207:                     return Err("PathPrefix: ctx.path not provided");
 208:                 }
 209:             }
 210:             Self::OperationIn(ops) => {
 211:                 if let Some(op) = ctx.operation {
 212:                     if !ops.iter().any(|allowed| allowed == op) {
 213:                         return Err("OperationIn: operation not in allow list");
 214:                     }
 215:                 } else {
 216:                     return Err("OperationIn: ctx.operation not provided");
 217:                 }
 218:             }
 219:             Self::AuditTag(_) => {
 220:                 // AuditTag never rejects. It's informational/logged.
 221:             }
 222:         }
 223:         Ok(())
 224:     }
 225: }

   1: //! Runtime context for capability verification.
   2: 
   3: /// The runtime environment a capability is checked against. Callers
   4: /// fill in only the fields relevant to their use case; caveats that
   5: /// require a missing field reject.
   6: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
   7: pub struct Context<'a> {
   8:     /// Current Unix-millisecond timestamp. Required to check
   9:     /// `Caveat::ExpiresAt`.
  10:     pub now_unix_ms: Option<u64>,
  11:     /// Authenticated peer's fingerprint. Required to check
  12:     /// `Caveat::PeerFingerprint`.
  13:     pub peer: Option<[u8; 32]>,
  14:     /// Resource path being accessed. Required for `Caveat::PathPrefix`.
  15:     pub path: Option<&'a str>,
  16:     /// Operation name (e.g., "read", "write"). Required for
  17:     /// `Caveat::OperationIn`.
  18:     pub operation: Option<&'a str>,
  19: }
  20: 
  21: impl<'a> Context<'a> {
  22:     /// Empty context. Caveats that need any field will reject.
  23:     pub fn new() -> Self {
  24:         Self::default()
  25:     }
  26: 
  27:     /// Builder: set `now_unix_ms`.
  28:     #[must_use]
  29:     pub fn with_now(mut self, ms: u64) -> Self {
  30:         self.now_unix_ms = Some(ms);
  31:         self
  32:     }
  33: 
  34:     /// Builder: set `peer`.
  35:     #[must_use]
  36:     pub fn with_peer(mut self, peer: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
  37:         self.peer = Some(peer);
  38:         self
  39:     }
  40: 
  41:     /// Builder: set `path`.
  42:     #[must_use]

  27:     },

  30:     #[error("malformed capability wire: {reason}")]

   1: //! `ol_capability` — macaroon-style capabilities per ADR-0021.
   2: //!
   3: //! Phase C item #3. Replaces the daemon's Phase A1 Ed25519-grant
   4: //! scheme (`One_link/src/one_link/capabilities.py`) with first-party
   5: //! HMAC-chained capabilities.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Surface
   8: //!
   9: //! - [`Capability`] — the token: identifier + caveats + signature.
  10: //! - [`Caveat`] — typed restrictions (time-bound, scope-bound, etc).
  11: //! - [`Context`] — the runtime context against which a cap is verified.
  12: //! - [`RootKey`] — 32-byte HMAC root key the issuer keeps secret.
  13: //!
  14: //! ## Threat model
  15: //!
  16: //! - Holder of a cap CAN attenuate (append more caveats); the new
  17: //!   signature is derivable from the current one + the new caveat.
  18: //! - Holder CANNOT remove caveats (HMAC chain would no longer verify).
  19: //! - Holder CANNOT forge a fresh cap (would need the root HMAC key).
  20: //! - Constant-time signature comparison prevents bit-by-bit forgery.
  21: 
  22: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_capability/0.21.0")]
  23: // The crate's public surface (`Capability`, `Caveat`, `Context`, `CapError`)
  24: // is fully documented; internal helpers and module-private items are
  25: // allowed to skip docs to keep the working surface focused.
  26: #![allow(missing_docs)]
  27: 
  28: pub mod capability;
  29: pub mod caveat;
  30: pub mod context;
  31: pub mod error;
  32: 
  33: pub use capability::{Capability, RootKey, CAP_ID_LEN, ROOT_KEY_LEN, SIGNATURE_LEN};
  34: pub use caveat::Caveat;
  35: pub use context::Context;
  36: pub use error::CapError;
  37: 
  38: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  39: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

   1: //! Phase C acceptance gate for `ol_capability` (FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md:289):
   2: //!
   3: //!     "Macaroon attenuation: property test that no derived cap exceeds
   4: //!      parent rights across ≥1M random delegation chains."
   5: //!
   6: //! Soundness invariant under test:
   7: //!
   8: //!     For all (parent, child, ctx) where child is a strict attenuation
   9: //!     of parent: child.accepts(ctx) ⇒ parent.accepts(ctx).
  10: //!
  11: //! In English: an attenuated cap can never accept a context that the
  12: //! parent would reject. Attenuation can only **shrink** the set of
  13: //! accepted contexts.
  14: //!
  15: //! Iteration count is configurable via `OL_CAPABILITY_GATE_ITERS`
  16: //! (default 10_000 for CI; gate run sets it to 1_000_000).
  17: 
  18: use ol_capability::{Capability, Caveat, Context, CAP_ID_LEN, ROOT_KEY_LEN};
  19: use zeroize::Zeroizing;
  20: 
  21: // SplitMix64 — same deterministic PRNG used by the ol_crdt gate.
  22: fn next_rng(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {
  23:     *state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  24:     let mut z = *state;
  25:     z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  26:     z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  27:     z ^ (z >> 31)
  28: }
  29: 
  30: fn random_bytes<const N: usize>(state: &mut u64) -> [u8; N] {
  31:     let mut out = [0u8; N];
  32:     for chunk in out.chunks_mut(8) {
  33:         let v = next_rng(state).to_le_bytes();
  34:         let n = chunk.len().min(8);
  35:         chunk[..n].copy_from_slice(&v[..n]);
  36:     }
  37:     out
  38: }
  39: 
  40: fn random_string(state: &mut u64, max_len: usize) -> String {
  41:     let len = (next_rng(state) as usize) % max_len.max(1);
  42:     (0..len)
  43:         .map(|_| {
  44:             // ASCII letter range so caveats render and parse cleanly.
  45:             let v = (next_rng(state) % 26) as u8;
  46:             (b'a' + v) as char
  47:         })
  48:         .collect()
  49: }
  50: 
  51: fn random_caveat(state: &mut u64) -> Caveat {
  52:     match next_rng(state) % 5 {
  53:         0 => Caveat::ExpiresAt(next_rng(state) % 1_000_000_000),
  54:         1 => Caveat::PeerFingerprint(random_bytes::<32>(state)),
  55:         2 => Caveat::PathPrefix(format!("/{}", random_string(state, 8))),
  56:         3 => {
  57:             let n = (next_rng(state) as usize) % 4 + 1;
  58:             let ops: Vec<String> = (0..n)
  59:                 .map(|_| match next_rng(state) % 4 {
  60:                     0 => "read".to_string(),
  61:                     1 => "write".to_string(),
  62:                     2 => "list".to_string(),
  63:                     _ => "delete".to_string(),
  64:                 })
  65:                 .collect();
  66:             Caveat::OperationIn(ops)
  67:         }
  68:         _ => Caveat::AuditTag(random_string(state, 12)),
  69:     }
  70: }
  71: 
  72: fn random_context(state: &mut u64) -> OwnedContext {
  73:     OwnedContext {
  74:         now_unix_ms: if next_rng(state) % 4 != 0 {
  75:             Some(next_rng(state) % 2_000_000_000)
  76:         } else {
  77:             None
  78:         },
  79:         peer: if next_rng(state) % 3 != 0 {
  80:             Some(random_bytes::<32>(state))
  81:         } else {
  82:             None
  83:         },
  84:         path: if next_rng(state) % 3 != 0 {
  85:             Some(format!(
  86:                 "/{}/{}",
  87:                 random_string(state, 8),
  88:                 random_string(state, 8),
  89:             ))
  90:         } else {
  91:             None
  92:         },
  93:         operation: if next_rng(state) % 3 != 0 {
  94:             Some(
  95:                 match next_rng(state) % 5 {
  96:                     0 => "read",
  97:                     1 => "write",
  98:                     2 => "list",
  99:                     3 => "delete",
 100:                     _ => "rename",
 101:                 }
 102:                 .to_string(),
 103:             )
 104:         } else {
 105:             None
 106:         },
 107:     }
 108: }
 109: 
 110: /// Owned variant so we can hold the string fields across iterations
 111: /// without lifetime gymnastics. We build a borrowed `Context` from this
 112: /// at use sites.
 113: struct OwnedContext {
 114:     now_unix_ms: Option<u64>,
 115:     peer: Option<[u8; 32]>,
 116:     path: Option<String>,
 117:     operation: Option<String>,
 118: }
 119: 
 120: impl OwnedContext {
 121:     fn as_ctx<'a>(&'a self) -> Context<'a> {
 122:         let mut c = Context::new();
 123:         if let Some(ms) = self.now_unix_ms {
 124:             c = c.with_now(ms);
 125:         }
 126:         if let Some(peer) = self.peer {
 127:             c = c.with_peer(peer);
 128:         }
 129:         if let Some(ref p) = self.path {
 130:             c = c.with_path(p.as_str());
 131:         }
 132:         if let Some(ref op) = self.operation {
 133:             c = c.with_operation(op.as_str());
 134:         }
 135:         c
 136:     }
 137: }
 138: 
 139: #[test]
 140: fn child_never_exceeds_parent_rights() {
 141:     let iters: u64 = std::env::var("OL_CAPABILITY_GATE_ITERS")
 142:         .ok()
 143:         .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
 144:         .unwrap_or(10_000);
 145: 
 146:     let mut state: u64 = 0xCA9C_0DE0_F00D_FACE_u64.swap_bytes();
 147:     let mut soundness_fail = 0u64;
 148:     let mut child_accepts = 0u64;
 149:     let mut child_rejects = 0u64;
 150: 
 151:     for _ in 0..iters {
 152:         // Fresh root key + cap-id per iteration.
 153:         let root_arr: [u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN] = random_bytes::<ROOT_KEY_LEN>(&mut state);
 154:         let root = Zeroizing::new(root_arr);
 155:         let id: [u8; CAP_ID_LEN] = random_bytes::<CAP_ID_LEN>(&mut state);
 156: 
 157:         // Parent: 0–5 random initial caveats.
 158:         let parent_caveats = (next_rng(&mut state) as usize) % 6;
 159:         let mut parent = Capability::root(id, &root);
 160:         for _ in 0..parent_caveats {
 161:             parent = parent.attenuate(random_caveat(&mut state));
 162:         }
 163: 
 164:         // Child: parent + 0–10 additional caveats (strict attenuation).
 165:         let extra_caveats = (next_rng(&mut state) as usize) % 11;
 166:         let mut child = parent.clone();
 167:         for _ in 0..extra_caveats {
 168:             child = child.attenuate(random_caveat(&mut state));
 169:         }
 170: 
 171:         // Random context.
 172:         let ctx_owned = random_context(&mut state);
 173:         let ctx = ctx_owned.as_ctx();
 174: 
 175:         let parent_ok = parent.accepts(&root, &ctx);
 176:         let child_ok = child.accepts(&root, &ctx);
 177: 
 178:         // The soundness invariant: child accepting ⇒ parent accepting.
 179:         // Equivalently: there must NOT exist a (child, ctx) where child
 180:         // accepts but parent does not.
 181:         if child_ok && !parent_ok {
 182:             soundness_fail += 1;
 183:         }
 184:         if child_ok {
 185:             child_accepts += 1;
 186:         } else {
 187:             child_rejects += 1;
 188:         }
 189:     }
 190: 
 191:     eprintln!(
 192:         "soundness gate: iters={iters} child_accepts={child_accepts} child_rejects={child_rejects} violations={soundness_fail}"
 193:     );
 194:     assert_eq!(
 195:         soundness_fail, 0,
 196:         "macaroon attenuation soundness violated: {soundness_fail} cases where child accepts ctx that parent rejects (out of {iters})"
 197:     );
 198:     // Sanity: across random contexts the child must reject at least
 199:     // some non-trivial fraction (otherwise the test is vacuously true).
 200:     assert!(
 201:         child_rejects > iters / 100,
 202:         "child rejected fewer than 1% of contexts ({child_rejects}/{iters}) — test is vacuous"
 203:     );
 204: }
 205: 
 206: #[test]
 207: fn appending_caveat_can_only_shrink_acceptance() {
 208:     // Stronger pointwise statement of the same property: for any cap C
 209:     // and any caveat K, (C ⊕ K).accepts(ctx) ⇒ C.accepts(ctx). We
 210:     // exercise this at small scale (10k) as a direct invariant check.
 211:     let mut state: u64 = 0xC0DE_BEEF;
 212:     let iters = 10_000u64;
 213:     for _ in 0..iters {
 214:         let root_arr: [u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN] = random_bytes::<ROOT_KEY_LEN>(&mut state);
 215:         let root = Zeroizing::new(root_arr);
 216:         let id: [u8; CAP_ID_LEN] = random_bytes::<CAP_ID_LEN>(&mut state);
 217: 
 218:         let cap = Capability::root(id, &root);
 219:         let attenuated = cap.attenuate(random_caveat(&mut state));
 220: 
 221:         let ctx_owned = random_context(&mut state);
 222:         let ctx = ctx_owned.as_ctx();
 223: 
 224:         if attenuated.accepts(&root, &ctx) {
 225:             assert!(
 226:                 cap.accepts(&root, &ctx),
 227:                 "attenuated cap accepted a ctx the parent rejected"
 228:             );
 229:         }
 230:     }
 231: }

   1: //! Phase C constant-time audit for `ol_capability::Capability::verify`
   2: //! per [FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md:292] item #9:
   3: //!
   4: //!     "Constant-time check: timing variance across cap-validity /
   5: //!      crypto-input-validity < 1% of mean."
   6: //!
   7: //! The signature compare in `Capability::verify` runs `subtle::
   8: //! ConstantTimeEq::ct_eq` over the 32-byte recomputed signature against
   9: //! the carried signature. The plan's item #9 gate requires that the
  10: //! wall-clock time of a verify call must not depend on WHERE the
  11: //! mismatch lies in the signature bytes — otherwise a network-adjacent
  12: //! attacker can probe each byte and forge a valid signature in
  13: //! O(N · 256) trials.
  14: //!
  15: //! We can't reach the internal `ct_eq` directly; we exercise it through
  16: //! the public `verify` API and measure wall-clock burst times. The
  17: //! straight-line XOR-accumulator implementation in `subtle` is
  18: //! constant-time at the CPU level (no early-out, no data-dependent
  19: //! branches); we allow ≤1.20× wall-clock variance for OS scheduling
  20: //! noise.
  21: 
  22: use std::hint::black_box;
  23: use std::time::Instant;
  24: 
  25: use ol_capability::{Capability, Caveat, Context, CAP_ID_LEN, ROOT_KEY_LEN};
  26: use zeroize::Zeroizing;
  27: 
  28: #[test]
  29: fn signature_compare_timing_uniform() {
  30:     // Build a non-trivial cap so verify exercises the full HMAC chain.
  31:     let root_arr: [u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN] = [0x42u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN];
  32:     let root = Zeroizing::new(root_arr);
  33:     let id: [u8; CAP_ID_LEN] = [0xCDu8; CAP_ID_LEN];
  34:     let cap = Capability::root(id, &root)
  35:         .attenuate(Caveat::ExpiresAt(1_000_000))
  36:         .attenuate(Caveat::PathPrefix("/safe/folder".to_string()))
  37:         .attenuate(Caveat::OperationIn(vec!["read".to_string()]));
  38: 
  39:     // Tamper the carried signature (last 32 bytes of the wire). The
  40:     // recomputed HMAC chain stays valid (caveats untouched) but
  41:     // disagrees with the carried signature in exactly the flipped byte
  42:     // position. `ct_eq` must still scan all 32 bytes regardless of
  43:     // whether the mismatch lies at byte 0 or byte 31.
  44:     let mut wire_a = cap.encode();
  45:     let sig_start = wire_a.len() - 32;
  46:     wire_a[sig_start] ^= 0x55; // mismatch in signature byte 0
  47: 
  48:     let mut wire_b = cap.encode();
  49:     wire_b[sig_start + 31] ^= 0x77; // mismatch in signature byte 31
  50: 
  51:     let cap_a = Capability::decode(&wire_a).unwrap();
  52:     let cap_b = Capability::decode(&wire_b).unwrap();
  53: 
  54:     let ctx = Context::new()
  55:         .with_now(500_000)
  56:         .with_path("/safe/folder/x.txt")
  57:         .with_operation("read");
  58: 
  59:     let iters_per_burst = 5_000;
  60:     let bursts = 10;
  61: 
  62:     // Warm up. black_box prevents the optimizer from realizing both
  63:     // calls return the same constant Err and eliding the loop.
  64:     for _ in 0..iters_per_burst {
  65:         let _ = black_box(cap_a.accepts(black_box(&root), black_box(&ctx)));
  66:         let _ = black_box(cap_b.accepts(black_box(&root), black_box(&ctx)));
  67:     }
  68: 
  69:     let mut t_a = 0u128;
  70:     let mut t_b = 0u128;
  71:     for _ in 0..bursts {
  72:         let s = Instant::now();
  73:         for _ in 0..iters_per_burst {
  74:             let _ = black_box(cap_a.accepts(black_box(&root), black_box(&ctx)));
  75:         }
  76:         t_a += s.elapsed().as_nanos();
  77: 
  78:         let s = Instant::now();
  79:         for _ in 0..iters_per_burst {
  80:             let _ = black_box(cap_b.accepts(black_box(&root), black_box(&ctx)));
  81:         }
  82:         t_b += s.elapsed().as_nanos();
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     let avg_a = t_a as f64 / (iters_per_burst * bursts) as f64;
  86:     let avg_b = t_b as f64 / (iters_per_burst * bursts) as f64;
  87:     let ratio = avg_a.max(avg_b) / avg_a.min(avg_b);
  88: 
  89:     eprintln!("verify sig-tamper@0:  {:.1} ns/call", avg_a);
  90:     eprintln!("verify sig-tamper@31: {:.1} ns/call", avg_b);
  91:     eprintln!("ratio: {:.4}", ratio);
  92: 
  93:     // The straight-line XOR-accumulator in `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` is
  94:     // CPU-constant-time. Allow up to 1.20× wall-clock variance for OS
  95:     // noise. Plan calls for <1% timing variance "of the mean", which
  96:     // translates to a ratio below ~1.02 for the underlying op; the
  97:     // 1.20× ceiling we apply here covers macro-level OS jitter.
  98:     assert!(
  99:         ratio < 1.20,
 100:         "verify wall-clock diverges {ratio:.3}× by mismatch position — possible non-CT path"
 101:     );
 102: }
 103: 
 104: /// Semantic guard: verify rejects every tampered cap, regardless of
 105: /// which byte was touched. The CT timing test above relies on this
 106: /// invariant — both calls are returning Err, not Ok-vs-Err.
 107: #[test]
 108: fn tampered_caps_reject_uniformly() {
 109:     let root_arr: [u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN] = [0x42u8; ROOT_KEY_LEN];
 110:     let root = Zeroizing::new(root_arr);
 111:     let id: [u8; CAP_ID_LEN] = [0xCDu8; CAP_ID_LEN];
 112:     let cap = Capability::root(id, &root).attenuate(Caveat::ExpiresAt(1_000_000));
 113:     let original_wire = cap.encode();
 114:     // Flip every byte in the caveat region (between cap-id and signature).
 115:     let caveat_start = CAP_ID_LEN + 4;
 116:     let caveat_end = original_wire.len() - 32;
 117:     for idx in caveat_start..caveat_end {
 118:         let mut wire = original_wire.clone();
 119:         wire[idx] ^= 0xFF;
 120:         // After a byte flip, decode may fail entirely (variant tag, length
 121:         // field); whether decoded or not, we treat it as rejection.
 122:         match Capability::decode(&wire) {
 123:             Ok(tampered) => {
 124:                 let ctx = Context::new().with_now(500_000);
 125:                 assert!(
 126:                     !tampered.accepts(&root, &ctx),
 127:                     "tampered cap (byte {idx}) accepted — auth broken"
 128:                 );
 129:             }
 130:             Err(_) => {
 131:                 // Decode rejection counts as the right outcome.
 132:             }
 133:         }
 134:     }
 135: }

  23:         state ^= state >> 7;
  24:         state ^= state << 17;
  25:         *byte = (state & 0xFF) as u8;
  26:     }
  27: }

  91:             let id = blake3_wrap::derive_ratchet_key_id(black_box(&chain), black_box(&chunk));
  92:             black_box(id);
  93:         });
  94:     });
  95:     c.bench_function("derive_stripe_seed", |b| {
  96:         b.iter(|| {
  97:             let (s, p) = blake3_wrap::derive_stripe_seed(black_box(&chunk), 10);

  99:         });
 100:     });

 103: fn make_dummy_zip(entries: usize, entry_size: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
 104:     let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(entries * (ZIP_LFH_FIXED_LEN + 7 + entry_size));
 105:     for i in 0..entries {
 106:         buf.extend_from_slice(&ZIP_LFH_MAGIC);
 107:         buf.extend_from_slice(&20u16.to_le_bytes()); // version_needed
 108:         buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // flags
 109:         buf.extend_from_slice(&8u16.to_le_bytes()); // compression_method = deflate
 110:         buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // mod_time
 111:         buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // mod_date
 112:         buf.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // crc-32
 113:         buf.extend_from_slice(&(entry_size as u32).to_le_bytes()); // compressed
 114:         buf.extend_from_slice(&(entry_size as u32).to_le_bytes()); // uncompressed
 115:         buf.extend_from_slice(&7u16.to_le_bytes()); // name_length
 116:         buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // extra_length
 117:         let name = format!("file{i:02}\0");
 118:         buf.extend_from_slice(&name.as_bytes()[..7]);
 119:         buf.extend(std::iter::repeat((i as u8) ^ 0xAB).take(entry_size));
 120:     }
 121:     buf
 122: }
 123: 
 124: fn bench_zip_lfh_walk(c: &mut Criterion) {
 125:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("zip_lfh_walk");
 126:     // Realistic mix: 16 KiB-1 MiB entries, 10-80 entries per archive.
 127:     for &(entries, entry_size) in &[
 128:         (10usize, 16 * 1024usize),
 129:         (80, 16 * 1024),
 130:         (10, 1024 * 1024),
 131:     ] {
 132:         let buf = make_dummy_zip(entries, entry_size);
 133:         group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes(buf.len() as u64));
 134:         group.bench_with_input(
 135:             BenchmarkId::new(
 136:                 "entries-x-size",
 137:                 format!("{entries}x{}KiB", entry_size / 1024),
 138:             ),
 139:             &buf,
 140:             |b, buf| {
 141:                 b.iter(|| {
 142:                     let offs = zip_lfh_offsets(black_box(buf));
 143:                     black_box(offs);
 144:                 });
 145:             },
 146:         );
 147:     }
 148:     group.finish();
 149: }

 151: /// Parallel scan path: CDC boundary discovery is inherently sequential
 152: /// (rolling-hash state), but BLAKE3 hashing of each discovered chunk is
 153: /// embarrassingly parallel. `scan_to_vec_parallel` shards the BLAKE3
 154: /// pass across rayon. Win lands above ~1 MiB buffers.
 155: fn bench_par_scan(c: &mut Criterion) {
 156:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("cdc_scan_par");
 157:     for &size_mib in &[16usize, 64, 256] {
 158:         let n = size_mib * 1024 * 1024;
 159:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; n];
 160:         fill_pseudo_random(&mut buf, 0xBEEF_F00D_u64.wrapping_add(size_mib as u64));
 161:         group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes(n as u64));
 162:         group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::new("seq", size_mib), &buf, |b, buf| {
 163:             b.iter(|| {
 164:                 let v = scan_to_vec(black_box(buf));
 165:                 black_box(v);
 166:             });
 167:         });
 168:         group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::new("par", size_mib), &buf, |b, buf| {
 169:             b.iter(|| {
 170:                 let v = scan_to_vec_parallel(black_box(buf));
 171:                 black_box(v);
 172:             });
 173:         });
 174:     }
 175:     group.finish();
 176: }

   1: //! BLAKE3 domain-separated derivation per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! Every cryptographic boundary in the engine domain-separates its BLAKE3
   4: //! use via a registered context string. This module is the single canonical
   5: //! implementation; downstream crates call these helpers rather than
   6: //! invoking BLAKE3 directly.
   7: //!
   8: //! ## Forbidden patterns
   9: //!
  10: //! - `blake3::hash(b"prefix" || input)` for purpose-domain separation —
  11: //!   use `derive_key` instead.
  12: //! - Using one derived key for two different purposes — call the
  13: //!   purpose-specific helper for each use.
  14: //! - Hardcoding context strings outside this module — they live in the
  15: //!   `DerivationContext` enum so a static lint can enforce single source
  16: //!   of truth.
  17: 
  18: /// Registered BLAKE3 derivation contexts per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md).
  19: ///
  20: /// Each variant represents one cryptographic purpose. The `as_str()`
  21: /// method returns the canonical context string used in `derive_key`.
  22: /// Adding a new variant requires an ADR amendment.
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  24: pub enum DerivationContext {
  25:     /// Convergent-encryption chunk address.
  26:     ChunkAddrConvergent,
  27:     /// Per-chunk AEAD key.
  28:     ChunkAeadKey,
  29:     /// Per-chunk ratchet-key-id (16 bytes stored in chunk_log header).
  30:     ChunkRatchetId,
  31:     /// Stripe seed for content-addressed RS stripe assignment.
  32:     StripeSeed,
  33:     /// Cohort_id mixing for Reed-Solomon parity derivation.
  34:     StripeCohortMix,
  35:     /// Manifest content-address.
  36:     ManifestId,
  37:     /// Capability fingerprint.
  38:     CapabilityId,
  39:     /// Merkle revocation log leaf hash.
  40:     RevocationLeaf,
  41:     /// Merkle revocation log internal-node hash.
  42:     RevocationInternal,
  43:     /// CRDT actor_id derivation from peer fingerprint.
  44:     FolderCrdtActor,
  45:     /// Share-link fingerprint.
  46:     ShareLinkId,
  47:     /// Bloom filter hash-function seed (Phase B; reserved here).
  48:     BloomInitKey,
  49:     /// RaptorQ encoded-symbol identifier (Phase B; reserved).
  50:     FountainSymbolId,
  51:     /// XOR network-coding combined-symbol identifier (Phase B; reserved).
  52:     NetworkCodingId,
  53:     /// ML-KEM + X25519 hybrid combiner KDF (Phase C; reserved).
  54:     PqHybridDerive,
  55: }
  56: 
  57: impl DerivationContext {
  58:     /// The canonical context string registered in [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md).
  59:     #[inline]
  60:     #[must_use]
  61:     pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
  62:         match self {
  63:             Self::ChunkAddrConvergent => "ol-chunk-addr-convergent-v1",
  64:             Self::ChunkAeadKey => "ol-chunk-aead-key-v1",
  65:             Self::ChunkRatchetId => "ol-chunk-ratchet-id-v1",
  66:             Self::StripeSeed => "ol-stripe-seed-v1",
  67:             Self::StripeCohortMix => "ol-stripe-cohort-mix-v1",
  68:             Self::ManifestId => "ol-manifest-id-v1",
  69:             Self::CapabilityId => "ol-capability-id-v1",
  70:             Self::RevocationLeaf => "ol-revocation-leaf-v1",
  71:             Self::RevocationInternal => "ol-revocation-internal-v1",
  72:             Self::FolderCrdtActor => "ol-folder-crdt-actor-v1",
  73:             Self::ShareLinkId => "ol-share-link-id-v1",
  74:             Self::BloomInitKey => "ol-bloom-init-key-v1",
  75:             Self::FountainSymbolId => "ol-fountain-symbol-id-v1",
  76:             Self::NetworkCodingId => "ol-network-coding-id-v1",
  77:             Self::PqHybridDerive => "ol-pq-hybrid-derive-v1",
  78:         }
  79:     }
  80: }
  81: 
  82: /// Derive a 32-byte key for a registered domain context.
  83: ///
  84: /// This is the canonical wrapper around `blake3::derive_key` for engine
  85: /// use. Callers MUST use a registered context (the `DerivationContext`
  86: /// enum); ad-hoc context strings are forbidden by [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md).
  87: #[inline]
  88: #[must_use]
  89: pub fn derive_key32(context: DerivationContext, key_material: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
  90:     blake3::derive_key(context.as_str(), key_material)
  91: }
  92: 
  93: /// Derive a 16-byte key for a registered domain context.
  94: ///
  95: /// Used by [`derive_ratchet_key_id`] to produce the `ratchet_key_id` field
  96: /// stored in the chunk_log header. BLAKE3 supports arbitrary output length;
  97: /// we truncate to 16 bytes via XOF mode.
  98: #[must_use]
  99: pub fn derive_key16(context: DerivationContext, key_material: &[u8]) -> [u8; 16] {
 100:     let key32 = blake3::derive_key(context.as_str(), key_material);
 101:     let mut out = [0u8; 16];
 102:     out.copy_from_slice(&key32[..16]);
 103:     out
 104: }
 105: 
 106: /// Raw chunk address: plain `BLAKE3.hash(plaintext)` per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 1.
 107: ///
 108: /// This is the canonical content-addressed identifier for chunks under
 109: /// non-convergent encryption. Compatible with external content-addressed
 110: /// storage tooling that uses plain BLAKE3.
 111: #[inline]
 112: #[must_use]
 113: pub fn chunk_address_raw(plaintext: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
 114:     *blake3::hash(plaintext).as_bytes()
 115: }
 116: 
 117: /// Convergent chunk address: `derive_key("ol-chunk-addr-convergent-v1", plaintext)`
 118: /// per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 2.
 119: ///
 120: /// Same plaintext from any sender produces the same address, enabling
 121: /// cross-sender deduplication for content under convergent encryption.
 122: /// Domain-separated from the raw address so the engine never confuses the
 123: /// two addressing schemes.
 124: #[inline]
 125: #[must_use]
 126: pub fn chunk_address_convergent(plaintext: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
 127:     derive_key32(DerivationContext::ChunkAddrConvergent, plaintext)
 128: }
 129: 
 130: /// Derive a per-chunk AEAD key per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 3.
 131: ///
 132: /// `ratchet_chain_key` is the current double-ratchet chain key for the
 133: /// session this chunk is being encrypted under. `chunk_id_full` is the
 134: /// 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address (raw or convergent).
 135: ///
 136: /// For convergent encryption, callers should supply the chunk content
 137: /// itself (or a content-derived value) as `ratchet_chain_key` so that
 138: /// identical plaintext from any sender produces an identical AEAD key.
 139: #[must_use]
 140: pub fn derive_aead_key(ratchet_chain_key: &[u8; 32], chunk_id_full: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 32] {
 141:     let mut material = [0u8; 64];
 142:     material[..32].copy_from_slice(ratchet_chain_key);
 143:     material[32..].copy_from_slice(chunk_id_full);
 144:     derive_key32(DerivationContext::ChunkAeadKey, &material)
 145: }
 146: 
 147: /// Derive the 16-byte `ratchet_key_id` stored in the chunk_log header
 148: /// per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 4 and [ADR-0003](../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md).
 149: ///
 150: /// This identifier lets recovery look up which ratchet generation a
 151: /// chunk's AEAD key came from without storing the ratchet chain key
 152: /// itself in the on-disk record.
 153: #[must_use]
 154: pub fn derive_ratchet_key_id(ratchet_chain_key: &[u8; 32], chunk_id_full: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; 16] {
 155:     let mut material = [0u8; 64];
 156:     material[..32].copy_from_slice(ratchet_chain_key);
 157:     material[32..].copy_from_slice(chunk_id_full);
 158:     derive_key16(DerivationContext::ChunkRatchetId, &material)
 159: }
 160: 
 161: /// Derive the stripe seed and within-stripe position for a chunk per
 162: /// [ADR-0004](../../../docs/decisions/0004-stripe-layout.md) and
 163: /// [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 5.
 164: ///
 165: /// `chunk_id_full` is the 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address. `stripe_k` is the
 166: /// number of data shards per stripe (default 10 per [ADR-0004]).
 167: ///
 168: /// Returns `(stripe_seed, position)` where `stripe_seed` has the low 6
 169: /// bits cleared (reserved for position assignment) and `position` is in
 170: /// `[0, stripe_k)`.
 171: #[must_use]
 172: pub fn derive_stripe_seed(chunk_id_full: &[u8; 32], stripe_k: u8) -> (u64, u8) {
 173:     let mut material = [0u8; 33];
 174:     material[..32].copy_from_slice(chunk_id_full);
 175:     material[32] = stripe_k;
 176:     let derived = derive_key32(DerivationContext::StripeSeed, &material);
 177:     let h = u64::from_le_bytes(derived[..8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 178:     let stripe_seed = h & !((1u64 << 6) - 1);
 179:     let position = ((h & 0x3F) % u64::from(stripe_k.max(1))) as u8;
 180:     (stripe_seed, position)
 181: }
