   1: //! Content-defined chunking via FastCDC + Gear-256.
   2: //!
   3: //! Implements the kernel chosen in [ADR-0001](../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md):
   4: //! FastCDC with 8 KiB min / 64 KiB avg / 256 KiB max chunk size, using the
   5: //! reference Gear-256 hash table. SIMD acceleration is dispatched at runtime
   6: //! by the underlying `fastcdc` crate's v2020 implementation; the scalar
   7: //! fallback never falls below 1.2 GiB/s/core on commodity hardware.
   8: //!
   9: //! This module also computes a BLAKE3 hash per chunk while iterating, so
  10: //! callers receive `(start, end, blake3_hash)` triples ready for use as
  11: //! content-addressed identifiers per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md).
  12: //!
  13: //! ## Determinism
  14: //!
  15: //! Two scans of the same input on any platform produce identical
  16: //! `Boundary` sequences. SIMD changes microarchitecture, not byte output.
  17: //! The `tests/cross_platform.rs` fixture pins a known boundary set against
  18: //! a fixed input; CI runs it on Linux x86-64, macOS arm64, and Windows
  19: //! x86-64 to guarantee no cross-platform divergence.
  20: //!
  21: //! ## Throughput
  22: //!
  23: //! Phase A1 verification gate ([ADR-0001]): ≥ 2 GiB/s/core scalar,
  24: //! ≥ 5 GiB/s/core with SIMD. Measured by `benches/cdc_bench.rs` against
  25: //! a 1 GiB pseudo-random buffer.
  26: 
  27: use crate::blake3_wrap;
  28: use crate::error::ChunkError;
  29: 
  30: /// FastCDC chunk size parameters fixed by [ADR-0001].
  31: ///
  32: /// Minimum 8 KiB: chunks below this floor incur metadata overhead
  33: /// (32-byte BLAKE3 + 16-byte ratchet-key-id + bloom slot) that exceeds
  34: /// the savings of dedup. Maximum 256 KiB: above this ceiling, FUSE read
  35: /// amplification gets bad. Average 64 KiB: matches the FastCDC paper's
  36: /// recommended parameter for general-purpose dedup, and matches OneField
  37: /// Mesh `transport/cdc_dedup.cl` family.
  38: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  39: pub struct CdcParams {
  40:     /// Minimum chunk size in bytes. Default 8 KiB.
  41:     pub min_size: u32,
  42:     /// Average chunk size in bytes. Default 64 KiB.
  43:     pub avg_size: u32,
  44:     /// Maximum chunk size in bytes. Default 256 KiB.
  45:     pub max_size: u32,
  46: }
  47: 
  48: impl Default for CdcParams {
  49:     fn default() -> Self {
  50:         Self {
  51:             min_size: 8 * 1024,
  52:             avg_size: 64 * 1024,
  53:             max_size: 256 * 1024,
  54:         }
  55:     }
  56: }
  57: 
  58: impl CdcParams {
  59:     /// Validate FastCDC invariants: min < avg < max, none zero, all within
  60:     /// reasonable bounds (max ≤ 16 MiB for sanity).
  61:     ///
  62:     /// # Errors
  63:     ///
  64:     /// Returns `ChunkError::InvalidParameters` if any invariant is violated.
  65:     pub fn validate(self) -> Result<(), ChunkError> {
  66:         if self.min_size == 0 || self.avg_size == 0 || self.max_size == 0 {
  67:             return Err(ChunkError::InvalidParameters(
  68:                 "min/avg/max sizes must be positive",
  69:             ));
  70:         }
  71:         if self.min_size >= self.avg_size {
  72:             return Err(ChunkError::InvalidParameters(
  73:                 "min_size must be strictly less than avg_size",
  74:             ));
  75:         }
  76:         if self.avg_size >= self.max_size {
  77:             return Err(ChunkError::InvalidParameters(
  78:                 "avg_size must be strictly less than max_size",
  79:             ));
  80:         }
  81:         if self.max_size > 16 * 1024 * 1024 {
  82:             return Err(ChunkError::InvalidParameters("max_size must be ≤ 16 MiB"));
  83:         }
  84:         Ok(())
  85:     }
  86: }
  87: 
  88: /// One CDC boundary: a single chunk's range and its BLAKE3 raw address.
  89: ///
  90: /// `start..end` is the half-open byte range within the input buffer.
  91: /// `length()` returns `end - start`. `raw_address` is the BLAKE3-256 of the
  92: /// chunk plaintext per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md)
  93: /// rule 1 (raw chunk addressing).
  94: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  95: pub struct Boundary {
  96:     /// Inclusive start offset within the input buffer.
  97:     pub start: usize,
  98:     /// Exclusive end offset within the input buffer.
  99:     pub end: usize,
 100:     /// BLAKE3-256 hash of `input[start..end]`.
 101:     pub raw_address: [u8; 32],
 102: }
 103: 
 104: impl Boundary {
 105:     /// Length of this chunk in bytes.
 106:     #[inline]
 107:     pub fn length(&self) -> usize {
 108:         self.end - self.start
 109:     }
 110: }
 111: 
 112: /// Streaming CDC scanner over a byte slice.
 113: ///
 114: /// Iterates chunk boundaries lazily; per-iteration cost is dominated by
 115: /// the underlying FastCDC scan plus a single BLAKE3 hash of the discovered
 116: /// chunk. Callers consume `(start, end, blake3_hash)` triples without
 117: /// holding the whole boundary list in memory.
 118: pub struct ChunkScanner<'a> {
 119:     inner: fastcdc::v2020::FastCDC<'a>,
 120:     buffer: &'a [u8],
 121: }
 122: 
 123: impl<'a> std::fmt::Debug for ChunkScanner<'a> {
 124:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 125:         f.debug_struct("ChunkScanner")
 126:             .field("buffer_len", &self.buffer.len())
 127:             .finish()
 128:     }
 129: }
 130: 
 131: impl<'a> ChunkScanner<'a> {
 132:     /// Create a scanner over `buffer` with the default ADR-0001 parameters.
 133:     pub fn new(buffer: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
 134:         Self::with_params(buffer, CdcParams::default()).expect("default CdcParams are always valid")
 135:     }
 136: 
 137:     /// Create a scanner over `buffer` with custom CDC parameters.
 138:     ///
 139:     /// # Errors
 140:     ///
 141:     /// Returns `ChunkError::InvalidParameters` if `params` violates
 142:     /// FastCDC invariants.
 143:     pub fn with_params(buffer: &'a [u8], params: CdcParams) -> Result<Self, ChunkError> {
 144:         params.validate()?;
 145:         let inner =
 146:             fastcdc::v2020::FastCDC::new(buffer, params.min_size, params.avg_size, params.max_size);
 147:         Ok(Self { inner, buffer })
 148:     }
 149: }
 150: 
 151: impl<'a> Iterator for ChunkScanner<'a> {
 152:     type Item = Boundary;
 153: 
 154:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
 155:         let chunk = self.inner.next()?;
 156:         let start = chunk.offset;
 157:         let end = chunk.offset + chunk.length;
 158:         debug_assert!(end <= self.buffer.len());
 159:         let raw_address = blake3_wrap::chunk_address_raw(&self.buffer[start..end]);
 160:         Some(Boundary {
 161:             start,
 162:             end,
 163:             raw_address,
 164:         })
 165:     }
 166: }
 167: 
 168: /// Convenience: scan a buffer and collect all boundaries into a Vec.
 169: ///
 170: /// Equivalent to `ChunkScanner::new(buffer).collect()`. Useful for tests
 171: /// and one-shot ingest paths that don't need streaming.
 172: #[must_use]
 173: pub fn scan_to_vec(buffer: &[u8]) -> Vec<Boundary> {
 174:     ChunkScanner::new(buffer).collect()
 175: }
 176: 
 177: /// Threshold above which `scan_to_vec_parallel` parallelizes BLAKE3
 178: /// hashing across the discovered boundaries via Rayon. Below this size
 179: /// the threadpool dispatch overhead dominates the win.
 180: const PARALLEL_HASH_MIN_BYTES: usize = 1 * 1024 * 1024;
 181: 
 182: /// Scan a buffer and collect boundaries, hashing chunks in parallel
 183: /// via Rayon for buffers ≥ 1 MiB.
 184: ///
 185: /// FastCDC boundary discovery is inherently sequential (the rolling
 186: /// hash carries state across bytes), but BLAKE3 of each discovered
 187: /// chunk is independent and dominates the cycles/byte budget on multi-
 188: /// core hosts. We split the work into two passes:
 189: ///
 190: ///  1. Sequential: walk the input via FastCDC, emit `(start, end)` ranges.
 191: ///  2. Parallel: hash each `(start, end)` slice via Rayon's work-stealing
 192: ///     pool. The output preserves boundary order.
 193: ///
 194: /// Below `PARALLEL_HASH_MIN_BYTES`, falls back to the single-threaded
 195: /// path.
 196: #[must_use]
 197: pub fn scan_to_vec_parallel(buffer: &[u8]) -> Vec<Boundary> {
 198:     if buffer.len() < PARALLEL_HASH_MIN_BYTES {
 199:         return scan_to_vec(buffer);
 200:     }
 201:     use rayon::prelude::*;
 202: 
 203:     // Pass 1: discover ranges sequentially.
 204:     let params = CdcParams::default();
 205:     let ranges: Vec<(usize, usize)> =
 206:         fastcdc::v2020::FastCDC::new(buffer, params.min_size, params.avg_size, params.max_size)
 207:             .map(|c| (c.offset, c.offset + c.length))
 208:             .collect();
 209: 
 210:     // Pass 2: hash each range in parallel.
 211:     ranges
 212:         .par_iter()
 213:         .map(|&(start, end)| Boundary {
 214:             start,
 215:             end,
 216:             raw_address: blake3_wrap::chunk_address_raw(&buffer[start..end]),
 217:         })
 218:         .collect()
 219: }

 221: #[cfg(test)]
 222: mod tests {
 223:     use super::*;
 224: 
 225:     #[test]
 226:     fn empty_buffer_yields_no_boundaries() {
 227:         let scanner = ChunkScanner::new(b"");
 228:         assert_eq!(scanner.count(), 0);
 229:     }
 230: 
 231:     #[test]
 232:     fn small_buffer_yields_single_chunk() {
 233:         // Buffer well below min_size: FastCDC emits a single trailing chunk.
 234:         let buf = vec![0xABu8; 4096];
 235:         let scanner = ChunkScanner::new(&buf);
 236:         let boundaries: Vec<_> = scanner.collect();
 237:         assert_eq!(boundaries.len(), 1);
 238:         assert_eq!(boundaries[0].start, 0);
 239:         assert_eq!(boundaries[0].end, 4096);
 240:         // Raw address must equal BLAKE3 of the full buffer.
 241:         let expected = blake3::hash(&buf);
 242:         assert_eq!(boundaries[0].raw_address, *expected.as_bytes());
 243:     }
 244: 
 245:     #[test]
 246:     fn one_megabyte_yields_multiple_chunks_in_size_range() {
 247:         // 1 MiB of pseudo-random content via deterministic xorshift.
 248:         let mut rng_state: u64 = 0x1234_5678_DEAD_BEEF;
 249:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; 1024 * 1024];
 250:         for byte in buf.iter_mut() {
 251:             rng_state ^= rng_state << 13;
 252:             rng_state ^= rng_state >> 7;
 253:             rng_state ^= rng_state << 17;
 254:             *byte = (rng_state & 0xFF) as u8;
 255:         }
 256: 
 257:         let boundaries = scan_to_vec(&buf);
 258:         assert!(
 259:             !boundaries.is_empty(),
 260:             "1 MiB random buffer should produce at least one boundary",
 261:         );
 262: 
 263:         // Every chunk respects min/max bounds (except possibly the last one,
 264:         // which may be smaller than min_size when it's the remainder).
 265:         let params = CdcParams::default();
 266:         for (i, b) in boundaries.iter().enumerate() {
 267:             let len = b.length();
 268:             let is_last = i == boundaries.len() - 1;
 269:             assert!(
 270:                 len <= params.max_size as usize,
 271:                 "chunk {i} exceeds max: {len}",
 272:             );
 273:             if !is_last {
 274:                 assert!(
 275:                     len >= params.min_size as usize,
 276:                     "interior chunk {i} below min: {len}",
 277:                 );
 278:             }
 279:         }
 280: 
 281:         // Coverage: chunks tile the buffer exactly.
 282:         assert_eq!(boundaries[0].start, 0);
 283:         assert_eq!(boundaries.last().unwrap().end, buf.len());
 284:         for w in boundaries.windows(2) {
 285:             assert_eq!(w[0].end, w[1].start, "boundaries not contiguous");
 286:         }
 287:     }
 288: 
 289:     #[test]
 290:     fn invalid_params_rejected() {
 291:         let buf = vec![0u8; 1024];
 292:         let bad = CdcParams {
 293:             min_size: 1024,
 294:             avg_size: 1024, // not strictly greater than min
 295:             max_size: 4096,
 296:         };
 297:         let result = ChunkScanner::with_params(&buf, bad);
 298:         assert!(matches!(result, Err(ChunkError::InvalidParameters(_))));
 299:     }
 300: 
 301:     #[test]
 302:     fn deterministic_across_runs() {
 303:         let buf = vec![0xCDu8; 200_000];
 304:         let a = scan_to_vec(&buf);
 305:         let b = scan_to_vec(&buf);
 306:         assert_eq!(a, b, "CDC must be deterministic across runs");
 307:     }
 308: 
 309:     #[test]
 310:     fn boundary_addresses_match_blake3() {
 311:         let buf = (0u8..255).cycle().take(150_000).collect::<Vec<_>>();
 312:         for boundary in scan_to_vec(&buf) {
 313:             let expected = blake3::hash(&buf[boundary.start..boundary.end]);
 314:             assert_eq!(
 315:                 boundary.raw_address,
 316:                 *expected.as_bytes(),
 317:                 "raw_address must equal BLAKE3 of chunk content",
 318:             );
 319:         }
 320:     }
 321: }

   8: /// Errors produced by chunk-layer operations.

  10: pub enum ChunkError {

  12:     /// This is not necessarily an error in itself (a 0-byte buffer is

  18:         /// Minimum length required (typically the CDC min chunk size).

  28:     /// distribution. Frame size must divide the maximum chunk size cleanly.

  31:         /// Frame size in bytes.

   1: //! Format-aware chunking per [ADR-0014](../../../docs/decisions/0014-format-aware-chunking.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! Augments the pure-CDC kernel ([`crate::cdc`]) with structural-boundary
   4: //! injection for well-known container formats. For Phase B v1 this means
   5: //! **ZIP-family archives** (`.zip`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`, `.odt`,
   6: //! `.apk`, `.jar`, `.epub`, `.kra`). Video GOP detection is reserved for
   7: //! Phase B-2.
   8: //!
   9: //! ## Algorithm
  10: //!
  11: //! 1. Detect format from path-extension hint + leading bytes magic.
  12: //! 2. If a structured format is detected, walk the buffer and collect
  13: //!    **forced cut offsets**: positions where the chunk boundary should
  14: //!    be pinned regardless of FastCDC's rolling-hash decision.
  15: //! 3. Run CDC on each `[forced_cut_i .. forced_cut_{i+1})` segment
  16: //!    independently. The forced cuts become hard boundaries.
  17: //!
  18: //! Result: a sender modifies one entry inside a `.xlsx` (a 1 KiB change
  19: //! in a 50 MiB file) and only that entry's chunks change. Pure-CDC would
  20: //! shift every downstream chunk boundary.
  21: //!
  22: //! ## Conservatism
  23: //!
  24: //! - Path-extension hint is preferred but not required. Pure magic
  25: //!   detection (`PK\x03\x04` at offset 0) suffices.
  26: //! - Each ZIP local-file-header (LFH) hit requires a cheap structural
  27: //!   sanity check (`version_needed`, `compression_method`, sane
  28: //!   `name_length` + `extra_length`). False positives are rare and
  29: //!   harmless (degraded dedup, no corruption).
  30: //! - Forced cuts are absorbed by the [`crate::cdc::CdcParams::min_size`]
  31: //!   floor — two LFHs <8 KiB apart only produce one boundary.
  32: 
  33: use crate::blake3_wrap;
  34: use crate::cdc::{Boundary, CdcParams, ChunkScanner};
  35: use crate::error::ChunkError;
  36: 
  37: /// Container formats recognized by the format-aware chunker.
  38: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  39: pub enum ContainerFormat {
  40:     /// ZIP archive family: `.zip`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`, `.odt`,
  41:     /// `.apk`, `.jar`, `.epub`, `.kra`. Local-file-header offsets used
  42:     /// as forced cuts.
  43:     Zip,
  44:     /// ISO Base Media File Format (MP4 / M4V / MOV / 3GP). Top-level
  45:     /// box boundaries used as forced cuts.
  46:     Mp4,
  47:     /// WAV / RIFF audio. `data` chunk start used as a forced cut so
  48:     /// re-tagged audio doesn't shift downstream chunks.
  49:     Wav,
  50:     /// Raw H.264 elementary stream (Annex B format). NAL unit start
  51:     /// codes used as forced cuts; IDR-bearing NAL units (keyframes)
  52:     /// are the highest-priority cuts so re-encoded video preserves
  53:     /// GOP-aligned chunks.
  54:     H264AnnexB,
  55: }
  56: 
  57: /// ZIP local-file-header signature (`PK\x03\x04`).
  58: pub const ZIP_LFH_MAGIC: [u8; 4] = [0x50, 0x4B, 0x03, 0x04];
  59: 
  60: /// ZIP local-file-header fixed-prefix length (signature + 26 fixed bytes).
  61: pub const ZIP_LFH_FIXED_LEN: usize = 30;
  62: 
  63: /// Detect a container format from leading bytes + an optional file
  64: /// extension hint.
  65: ///
  66: /// Returns `None` when no recognized format is detected. Detection is
  67: /// intentionally conservative — ambiguous matches fall back to pure
  68: /// CDC rather than risk false-positive cuts that would tank dedup.
  69: #[must_use]
  70: pub fn detect_format(leading: &[u8], path_extension: Option<&str>) -> Option<ContainerFormat> {
  71:     if leading.starts_with(&ZIP_LFH_MAGIC) {
  72:         return Some(ContainerFormat::Zip);
  73:     }
  74:     // ISO BMFF top-level boxes start with a 4-byte big-endian size
  75:     // followed by a 4-byte ASCII type. The first box in a valid file
  76:     // is almost always ``ftyp`` (or ``styp`` for segmented).
  77:     if leading.len() >= 8 {
  78:         let kind = &leading[4..8];
  79:         if matches!(kind, b"ftyp" | b"styp" | b"moov" | b"mdat" | b"free") {
  80:             return Some(ContainerFormat::Mp4);
  81:         }
  82:     }
  83:     // WAV/RIFF: bytes 0..4 = "RIFF", bytes 8..12 = "WAVE".
  84:     if leading.len() >= 12 && &leading[0..4] == b"RIFF" && &leading[8..12] == b"WAVE" {
  85:         return Some(ContainerFormat::Wav);
  86:     }
  87:     // H.264 Annex B elementary stream: starts with a NAL start code
  88:     // (0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01) or the shorter 3-byte variant. Detect
  89:     // either; downstream scanner walks both forms.
  90:     if leading.len() >= 4 && (leading.starts_with(&[0, 0, 0, 1]) || leading.starts_with(&[0, 0, 1]))
  91:     {
  92:         return Some(ContainerFormat::H264AnnexB);
  93:     }
  94:     if let Some(ext) = path_extension {
  95:         match ext.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
  96:             // Anything with the extension but missing magic falls
  97:             // back to None — refusing to scan minimises false
  98:             // positives on misnamed files.
  99:             "mp4" | "m4v" | "mov" | "3gp" if matches_iso_bmff_extension(leading) => {
 100:                 return Some(ContainerFormat::Mp4);
 101:             }
 102:             "wav"
 103:                 if leading.len() >= 12
 104:                     && &leading[0..4] == b"RIFF"
 105:                     && &leading[8..12] == b"WAVE" =>
 106:             {
 107:                 return Some(ContainerFormat::Wav);
 108:             }
 109:             "h264" | "264" | "avc" => return Some(ContainerFormat::H264AnnexB),
 110:             _ => {}
 111:         }
 112:     }
 113:     None
 114: }
 115: 
 116: /// Scan an H.264 Annex B elementary stream for **keyframe-bearing
 117: /// NAL unit boundaries**. Returns the offsets of NAL units of type
 118: /// IDR (`nal_unit_type == 5`) or SPS (`nal_unit_type == 7`), which
 119: /// together mark the start of every GOP.
 120: ///
 121: /// Returns offsets sorted ascending. Includes the start codes (3 or
 122: /// 4 bytes) so the cut is aligned to the start of the GOP.
 123: ///
 124: /// Sanity-limits: any NAL with a forbidden zero bit set (highest bit
 125: /// of the NAL header) is rejected — that's a transport-error signal.
 126: #[must_use]
 127: pub fn h264_keyframe_offsets(buffer: &[u8]) -> Vec<usize> {
 128:     let mut offsets = Vec::new();
 129:     let mut i = 0usize;
 130:     while i + 4 < buffer.len() {
 131:         // Look for the 4-byte start code (0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01) or the
 132:         // 3-byte one (0x00 0x00 0x01). The 4-byte form is required at
 133:         // the very start; either is legal mid-stream.
 134:         let (start_code_len, nal_byte_idx) =
 135:             if buffer[i] == 0 && buffer[i + 1] == 0 && buffer[i + 2] == 0 && buffer[i + 3] == 1 {
 136:                 (4, i + 4)
 137:             } else if buffer[i] == 0 && buffer[i + 1] == 0 && buffer[i + 2] == 1 {
 138:                 (3, i + 3)
 139:             } else {
 140:                 i += 1;
 141:                 continue;
 142:             };
 143:         if nal_byte_idx >= buffer.len() {
 144:             break;
 145:         }
 146:         let nal_byte = buffer[nal_byte_idx];
 147:         // forbidden_zero_bit (MSB) must be 0.
 148:         if nal_byte & 0x80 != 0 {
 149:             i += start_code_len;
 150:             continue;
 151:         }
 152:         // Low 5 bits are nal_unit_type.
 153:         let nal_type = nal_byte & 0x1F;
 154:         // Type 5 = IDR slice (instantaneous decoder refresh = keyframe).
 155:         // Type 7 = SPS (sequence parameter set, typically right before
 156:         // an IDR). Type 8 = PPS. Per the plan: GOP keyframe detection
 157:         // needs IDR-marked cuts. We also include SPS because the
 158:         // SPS-PPS-IDR triplet is the canonical GOP-start pattern.
 159:         if matches!(nal_type, 5 | 7) {
 160:             offsets.push(i);
 161:         }
 162:         i += start_code_len + 1;
 163:     }
 164:     offsets
 165: }
 166: 
 167: /// Helper: does the leading 8 bytes look plausibly like an ISO BMFF
 168: /// box header (size + 4-letter ASCII type)?
 169: fn matches_iso_bmff_extension(leading: &[u8]) -> bool {
 170:     if leading.len() < 8 {
 171:         return false;
 172:     }
 173:     leading[4..8]
 174:         .iter()
 175:         .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *b == b' ')
 176: }
 177: 
 178: /// Walk an ISO BMFF (MP4 / MOV) buffer and collect top-level box
 179: /// start offsets — every box header `[size:u32 BE][type:4]` becomes
 180: /// a forced cut. Stops on the first malformed header so a
 181: /// non-BMFF buffer that happens to match the leading-bytes check
 182: /// can't drive the scanner off a cliff.
 183: #[must_use]
 184: pub fn mp4_box_offsets(buffer: &[u8]) -> Vec<usize> {
 185:     let mut offsets = Vec::new();
 186:     let mut pos = 0usize;
 187:     while pos + 8 <= buffer.len() {
 188:         let size = u32::from_be_bytes([
 189:             buffer[pos],
 190:             buffer[pos + 1],
 191:             buffer[pos + 2],
 192:             buffer[pos + 3],
 193:         ]) as u64;
 194:         let kind = &buffer[pos + 4..pos + 8];
 195:         // Sanity: the 4-byte type MUST be 4 ASCII chars. Any non-
 196:         // printable rejects the rest of the buffer.
 197:         if !kind.iter().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || *b == b' ') {
 198:             break;
 199:         }
 200:         offsets.push(pos);
 201:         let advance = match size {
 202:             // Size == 1 means a 64-bit extended size in the next 8
 203:             // bytes (rare in practice; bail out if not enough room).
 204:             1 => {
 205:                 if pos + 16 > buffer.len() {
 206:                     break;
 207:                 }
 208:                 let mut be = [0u8; 8];
 209:                 be.copy_from_slice(&buffer[pos + 8..pos + 16]);
 210:                 u64::from_be_bytes(be)
 211:             }
 212:             // Size == 0 means "to end of file". This is the last
 213:             // box; stop after collecting its offset.
 214:             0 => break,
 215:             _ => size,
 216:         };
 217:         // Defensive: a corrupt size field smaller than the header
 218:         // would loop forever. Refuse to advance less than 8 bytes.
 219:         if advance < 8 {
 220:             break;
 221:         }
 222:         pos = pos.saturating_add(advance as usize);
 223:     }
 224:     offsets
 225: }
 226: 
 227: /// Walk a RIFF/WAV buffer and return the offset of the `data` chunk
 228: /// header (length-prefixed RIFF sub-chunk). The data chunk is the
 229: /// dominant payload of a WAV; cutting there isolates the audio
 230: /// samples from the variable-size metadata before it.
 231: #[must_use]
 232: pub fn wav_data_offset(buffer: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
 233:     if buffer.len() < 12 || &buffer[0..4] != b"RIFF" || &buffer[8..12] != b"WAVE" {
 234:         return None;
 235:     }
 236:     let mut pos = 12usize;
 237:     while pos + 8 <= buffer.len() {
 238:         let id = &buffer[pos..pos + 4];
 239:         let size = u32::from_le_bytes([
 240:             buffer[pos + 4],
 241:             buffer[pos + 5],
 242:             buffer[pos + 6],
 243:             buffer[pos + 7],
 244:         ]) as usize;
 245:         if id == b"data" {
 246:             return Some(pos);
 247:         }
 248:         // RIFF sub-chunks are byte-aligned but their size word is
 249:         // not padded; the actual layout pads odd sizes by 1.
 250:         let advance = 8 + size + (size & 1);
 251:         if advance < 8 {
 252:             break;
 253:         }
 254:         pos = pos.saturating_add(advance);
 255:     }
 256:     None
 257: }
 258: 
 259: /// Walk `buffer` and collect ZIP local-file-header offsets that pass the
 260: /// sanity check. Returns a sorted, deduplicated, monotonic list of
 261: /// forced-cut offsets.
 262: ///
 263: /// The first cut is always `0` (start of buffer) is **implicit** and not
 264: /// returned; callers walk forward from offset 0.
 265: ///
 266: /// Uses [`memchr`] to SIMD-scan for the LFH signature's first byte
 267: /// (`0x50` = `'P'`), then checks the full 4-byte sequence + sanity
 268: /// gate at each candidate. On x86 with SSE2/AVX2 this runs at
 269: /// ~10-30 GiB/s through `buffer` — far faster than the 5 GiB/s budget
 270: /// the FastCDC kernel itself runs at.
 271: #[must_use]
 272: pub fn zip_lfh_offsets(buffer: &[u8]) -> Vec<usize> {
 273:     let mut out = Vec::new();
 274:     if buffer.len() < ZIP_LFH_FIXED_LEN {
 275:         return out;
 276:     }
 277:     let mut start = 0usize;
 278:     // SIMD-search for the first signature byte; check full 4-byte
 279:     // sequence + sanity gate at each candidate.
 280:     while let Some(rel) = memchr::memchr(ZIP_LFH_MAGIC[0], &buffer[start..]) {
 281:         let i = start + rel;
 282:         if i + 4 > buffer.len() {
 283:             break;
 284:         }
 285:         if buffer[i..i + 4] == ZIP_LFH_MAGIC && zip_lfh_sanity_check(&buffer[i..]) {
 286:             out.push(i);
 287:             // Skip past the fixed prefix to avoid re-matching the same
 288:             // header. Body false positives are caught by the sanity
 289:             // gate above (cheap), not by trying to parse name_length /
 290:             // extra_length here (would need full ZIP entry parser).
 291:             start = i + ZIP_LFH_FIXED_LEN;
 292:         } else {
 293:             start = i + 1;
 294:         }
 295:         if start >= buffer.len() {
 296:             break;
 297:         }
 298:     }
 299:     out
 300: }
 301: 
 302: /// Cheap structural sanity check on a candidate LFH. `tail` must include
 303: /// at least the 30 fixed bytes after the signature.
 304: ///
 305: /// Validates:
 306: /// - `version_needed` is sane (≤ 100 / a known PKWARE version code).
 307: /// - `compression_method` is a known constant (0 stored, 8 deflate,
 308: ///   9-99 lossless other / future).
 309: /// - `name_length + extra_length` fits within the buffer remainder. We
 310: ///   relax this when we can't see the full entry; the magic + version
 311: ///   + method gate is enough to make false positives statistically
 312: ///   negligible.
 313: fn zip_lfh_sanity_check(tail: &[u8]) -> bool {
 314:     if tail.len() < ZIP_LFH_FIXED_LEN {
 315:         return false;
 316:     }
 317:     let version_needed = u16::from_le_bytes([tail[4], tail[5]]);
 318:     let compression_method = u16::from_le_bytes([tail[8], tail[9]]);
 319:     // Version range: PKWARE specs use 10, 20, 45, 46, 51, 62, 63;
 320:     // tolerate up to 100.
 321:     if version_needed > 100 {
 322:         return false;
 323:     }
 324:     // Known compression methods per PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.10.
 325:     matches!(
 326:         compression_method,
 327:         0 | 1 | 6 | 8 | 9 | 12 | 14 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 93 | 94 | 95 | 96 | 97 | 98 | 99
 328:     )
 329: }
 330: 
 331: /// Run format-aware chunking. Returns the boundaries plus a parallel
 332: /// `Vec<bool>` indicating whether each chunk's *starting* edge was a
 333: /// format-forced cut (vs natural CDC).
 334: ///
 335: /// When `format` is `None` or the buffer doesn't contain any forced
 336: /// cuts, falls back to plain CDC.
 337: ///
 338: /// # Errors
 339: ///
 340: /// Returns the underlying CDC error if `params` are invalid.
 341: pub fn scan_format_aware(
 342:     buffer: &[u8],
 343:     format: Option<ContainerFormat>,
 344:     params: CdcParams,
 345: ) -> Result<FormatAwareChunkSet, ChunkError> {
 346:     params.validate()?;
 347: 
 348:     let forced_cuts = match format {
 349:         Some(ContainerFormat::Zip) => zip_lfh_offsets(buffer),
 350:         Some(ContainerFormat::Mp4) => mp4_box_offsets(buffer),
 351:         Some(ContainerFormat::Wav) => {
 352:             // Single forced cut at the `data` chunk header (if any).
 353:             // The metadata in `fmt ` / `LIST` etc. before it tends
 354:             // to be small, so one cut is enough to isolate the
 355:             // audio body.
 356:             wav_data_offset(buffer).into_iter().collect()
 357:         }
 358:         Some(ContainerFormat::H264AnnexB) => {
 359:             // GOP-aligned cuts at IDR + SPS NAL units. A re-encoded
 360:             // video where only the first few frames changed will
 361:             // still hit the same IDR boundaries downstream, so dedup
 362:             // recovers everything past the edit.
 363:             h264_keyframe_offsets(buffer)
 364:         }
 365:         None => Vec::new(),
 366:     };
 367: 
 368:     // Absorb cuts that are too close together to be useful. Any cut
 369:     // less than `min_size` away from the previous accepted cut (or the
 370:     // start of the buffer) gets dropped to avoid degenerate tiny chunks.
 371:     let mut accepted: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
 372:     let mut last_accepted: usize = 0;
 373:     let min = params.min_size as usize;
 374:     for &c in &forced_cuts {
 375:         if c >= last_accepted + min && c <= buffer.len().saturating_sub(min) {
 376:             accepted.push(c);
 377:             last_accepted = c;
 378:         }
 379:     }
 380: 
 381:     if accepted.is_empty() {
 382:         // No forced cuts → pure CDC.
 383:         let bounds: Vec<Boundary> = ChunkScanner::with_params(buffer, params)?.collect();
 384:         let format_aware = vec![false; bounds.len()];
 385:         return Ok(FormatAwareChunkSet {
 386:             boundaries: bounds,
 387:             format_aware,
 388:         });
 389:     }
 390: 
 391:     // Build segment list `[0, cut_1)`, `[cut_1, cut_2)`, ... `[cut_n, end)`.
 392:     let mut segments: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::with_capacity(accepted.len() + 1);
 393:     let mut prev = 0usize;
 394:     for &c in &accepted {
 395:         segments.push((prev, c));
 396:         prev = c;
 397:     }
 398:     segments.push((prev, buffer.len()));
 399: 
 400:     let mut out_bounds: Vec<Boundary> = Vec::new();
 401:     let mut out_flags: Vec<bool> = Vec::new();
 402:     for (seg_idx, &(s, e)) in segments.iter().enumerate() {
 403:         let segment_buf = &buffer[s..e];
 404:         if segment_buf.is_empty() {
 405:             continue;
 406:         }
 407:         // If the segment is shorter than `max_size`, emit it as a single
 408:         // chunk without running CDC (CDC would just emit one chunk
 409:         // anyway, plus the boundary tail).
 410:         let segment_bounds: Vec<Boundary> = if segment_buf.len() <= params.max_size as usize {
 411:             vec![Boundary {
 412:                 start: 0,
 413:                 end: segment_buf.len(),
 414:                 raw_address: blake3_wrap::chunk_address_raw(segment_buf),
 415:             }]
 416:         } else {
 417:             ChunkScanner::with_params(segment_buf, params)?.collect()
 418:         };
 419: 
 420:         for (chunk_idx, b) in segment_bounds.into_iter().enumerate() {
 421:             // Translate offsets back to the source buffer.
 422:             let translated = Boundary {
 423:                 start: b.start + s,
 424:                 end: b.end + s,
 425:                 raw_address: b.raw_address,
 426:             };
 427:             // The chunk starting at the segment's first byte (chunk_idx
 428:             // == 0) is the format-forced one — unless we're in the very
 429:             // first segment, whose first chunk is the natural start of
 430:             // the buffer (not a forced cut).
 431:             let forced = chunk_idx == 0 && seg_idx > 0;
 432:             out_bounds.push(translated);
 433:             out_flags.push(forced);
 434:         }
 435:     }
 436: 
 437:     Ok(FormatAwareChunkSet {
 438:         boundaries: out_bounds,
 439:         format_aware: out_flags,
 440:     })
 441: }
 442: 
 443: /// Result of [`scan_format_aware`]: boundaries plus a parallel `bool`
 444: /// vector flagging which chunks started at a format-forced cut.
 445: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 446: pub struct FormatAwareChunkSet {
 447:     /// Chunk boundaries in input order.
 448:     pub boundaries: Vec<Boundary>,
 449:     /// `true` if the corresponding chunk's starting edge was a
 450:     /// format-forced cut (vs natural CDC). `format_aware[i]` belongs
 451:     /// to `boundaries[i]`. Always the same length as `boundaries`.
 452:     pub format_aware: Vec<bool>,
 453: }
 454: 
 455: impl FormatAwareChunkSet {
 456:     /// Number of chunks.
 457:     #[inline]
 458:     #[must_use]
 459:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 460:         self.boundaries.len()
 461:     }
 462: 
 463:     /// True if no chunks were produced.
 464:     #[inline]
 465:     #[must_use]
 466:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 467:         self.boundaries.is_empty()
 468:     }
 469: 
 470:     /// Number of chunks whose starting edge was format-forced.
 471:     #[must_use]
 472:     pub fn format_forced_count(&self) -> usize {
 473:         self.format_aware.iter().filter(|b| **b).count()
 474:     }
 475: }

 481:     fn make_dummy_zip(entries: usize, entry_size: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
 482:         // Build a minimum-shape ZIP-like buffer: each entry is an LFH
 483:         // (30 bytes fixed + 8 byte name "file00\x00") followed by
 484:         // `entry_size` arbitrary bytes. Then a few stray bytes. The end
 485:         // doesn't have a central directory; the scanner only cares
 486:         // about LFH offsets.
 487:         let mut buf = Vec::new();
 488:         for i in 0..entries {
 489:             // LFH:
 490:             buf.extend_from_slice(&ZIP_LFH_MAGIC);
 491:             buf.extend_from_slice(&20u16.to_le_bytes()); // version_needed = 20
 492:             buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // flags
 493:             buf.extend_from_slice(&8u16.to_le_bytes()); // compression_method = 8 (deflate)
 494:             buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // mod_time
 495:             buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // mod_date
 496:             buf.extend_from_slice(&0u32.to_le_bytes()); // crc-32
 497:             buf.extend_from_slice(&(entry_size as u32).to_le_bytes()); // compressed_size
 498:             buf.extend_from_slice(&(entry_size as u32).to_le_bytes()); // uncompressed_size
 499:             buf.extend_from_slice(&7u16.to_le_bytes()); // name_length
 500:             buf.extend_from_slice(&0u16.to_le_bytes()); // extra_length
 501:             let name = format!("file{i:02}\0");
 502:             buf.extend_from_slice(&name.as_bytes()[..7]);
 503:             // Entry body.
 504:             buf.extend(std::iter::repeat(0xAB ^ (i as u8)).take(entry_size));
 505:         }
 506:         buf
 507:     }

 595:     #[test]
 596:     fn h264_keyframe_offsets_finds_idr_and_sps() {
 597:         // Build a synthetic stream:
 598:         //   [SPS at offset 0]  (NAL type 7)
 599:         //   [PPS at offset 16] (NAL type 8 — NOT a cut)
 600:         //   [non-IDR slice at 32] (NAL type 1 — NOT a cut)
 601:         //   [IDR slice at 48] (NAL type 5)
 602:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; 64];
 603:         // SPS at 0: 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x67 ...
 604:         buf[0..4].copy_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 1]);
 605:         buf[4] = 0x67; // forbidden_zero=0, ref_idc=11, type=7 (SPS)
 606:                        // PPS at 16: 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x68
 607:         buf[16..20].copy_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 1]);
 608:         buf[20] = 0x68; // type=8 (PPS)
 609:                         // Non-IDR slice at 32: 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x41
 610:         buf[32..36].copy_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 1]);
 611:         buf[36] = 0x41; // type=1 (slice, non-IDR)
 612:                         // IDR slice at 48: 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01 0x65
 613:         buf[48..52].copy_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 1]);
 614:         buf[52] = 0x65; // type=5 (IDR slice)
 615:         let offsets = h264_keyframe_offsets(&buf);
 616:         // Must find the SPS (offset 0) and IDR (offset 48), skip PPS
 617:         // (16) and non-IDR slice (32).
 618:         assert_eq!(offsets, vec![0, 48]);
 619:     }

 683:     #[test]
 684:     fn cdc_equivalence_on_non_zip() {
 685:         // Random binary that does NOT look like ZIP.
 686:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; 512 * 1024];
 687:         for (i, b) in buf.iter_mut().enumerate() {
 688:             *b = (i as u8).wrapping_mul(31).wrapping_add(7);
 689:         }
 690:         let r = scan_format_aware(&buf, Some(ContainerFormat::Zip), CdcParams::default()).unwrap();
 691:         let plain: Vec<Boundary> = ChunkScanner::new(&buf).collect();
 692:         assert_eq!(r.boundaries.len(), plain.len());

   1: //! AEAD frame layout constants per [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! A "chunk" (the CDC output, 8-256 KiB per [ADR-0001](../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md))
   4: //! is the deduplication unit. A "frame" (16 KiB plaintext + 16 byte AEAD
   5: //! tag) is the encryption unit. One chunk holds one or more sequential
   6: //! frames so FUSE random-access reads decrypt only the frame containing
   7: //! the requested offset, capping read amplification at 16-32 KiB.
   8: //!
   9: //! This module defines only the layout constants and pure functions
  10: //! computing frame counts. AEAD encrypt/decrypt itself lives in
  11: //! `ol_aead`. Keeping the constants in `ol_chunk` lets the chunk store
  12: //! validate frame counts without depending on the AEAD crate.
  13: 
  14: /// AEAD frame plaintext payload size in bytes (16 KiB).
  15: ///
  16: /// Joint with the chunk-size distribution from [ADR-0001](../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md):
  17: /// a 64 KiB mean chunk holds 4 frames; max 256 KiB chunk holds 16 frames.
  18: pub const AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN: usize = 16 * 1024;
  19: 
  20: /// AEAD authentication tag length in bytes.
  21: ///
  22: /// 128 bits for both AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 per [ADR-0002](../../../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md).
  23: /// Truncation savings are not worth the security loss.
  24: pub const AEAD_TAG_LEN: usize = 16;
  25: 
  26: /// Compute the number of AEAD frames needed to cover a plaintext chunk
  27: /// of `chunk_plaintext_len` bytes.
  28: ///
  29: /// Rounds up: a chunk of 16,385 bytes needs 2 frames (16,384 + 1 byte).
  30: /// The trailing frame may be shorter than `AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN`.
  31: #[inline]
  32: #[must_use]
  33: pub const fn frame_count_for_plaintext(chunk_plaintext_len: usize) -> usize {
  34:     if chunk_plaintext_len == 0 {
  35:         return 0;
  36:     }
  37:     (chunk_plaintext_len + AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN - 1) / AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN
  38: }
  39: 
  40: /// Compute the on-wire ciphertext length for a chunk: plaintext + per-frame
  41: /// AEAD tags.
  42: #[inline]
  43: #[must_use]
  44: pub const fn ciphertext_len_for_plaintext(chunk_plaintext_len: usize) -> usize {
  45:     chunk_plaintext_len + frame_count_for_plaintext(chunk_plaintext_len) * AEAD_TAG_LEN
  46: }
  47: 
  48: #[cfg(test)]
  49: mod tests {
  50:     use super::*;
  51: 
  52:     #[test]
  53:     fn frame_count_zero_for_empty_chunk() {
  54:         assert_eq!(frame_count_for_plaintext(0), 0);
  55:     }
  56: 
  57:     #[test]
  58:     fn frame_count_one_for_subframe_chunk() {
  59:         assert_eq!(frame_count_for_plaintext(1), 1);
  60:         assert_eq!(frame_count_for_plaintext(AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN), 1);
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     #[test]
  64:     fn frame_count_rounds_up() {
  65:         assert_eq!(frame_count_for_plaintext(AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN + 1), 2);
  66:         // 64 KiB mean chunk = 4 frames per ADR-0002.
  67:         assert_eq!(frame_count_for_plaintext(64 * 1024), 4);
  68:         // 256 KiB max chunk = 16 frames per ADR-0002.
  69:         assert_eq!(frame_count_for_plaintext(256 * 1024), 16);
  70:     }
  71: 
  72:     #[test]
  73:     fn ciphertext_overhead_is_per_frame_tags() {
  74:         // 64 KiB plaintext → 4 tags × 16 = 64 bytes overhead, 0.097%.
  75:         let plain = 64 * 1024;
  76:         let cipher = ciphertext_len_for_plaintext(plain);
  77:         assert_eq!(cipher, plain + 4 * AEAD_TAG_LEN);
  78:     }
  79: }

   1: //! `ol_chunk` — content-defined chunking and content-addressed identifiers
   2: //! for One Link's file engine v2.
   3: //!
   4: //! This crate implements the foundational chunk-layer primitives:
   5: //!
   6: //! 1. **FastCDC kernel** with parameters fixed by [ADR-0001]: 8 KiB minimum,
   7: //!    64 KiB average, 256 KiB maximum chunk size. Gear-256 rolling hash
   8: //!    with the standard FastCDC published mask parameters.
   9: //!
  10: //! 2. **BLAKE3 chunk addressing** in two flavours per [ADR-0006]:
  11: //!    - **raw address**: plain `BLAKE3.hash(plaintext)` — content-addressed
  12: //!      identifier for chunks under non-convergent encryption.
  13: //!    - **convergent address**: `BLAKE3.derive_key("ol-chunk-addr-convergent-v1", plaintext)`
  14: //!      — content-addressed identifier for chunks under convergent
  15: //!      encryption. Cross-sender deduplication holds: same plaintext → same
  16: //!      address from any peer.
  17: //!
  18: //! 3. **Domain-separated subkey derivation** for downstream crates per
  19: //!    [ADR-0006]. The full registered context list is in `blake3_wrap`.
  20: //!
  21: //! 4. **Pure-Rust API**. Pyo3 bindings live in the `one_link_native` umbrella
  22: //!    crate which depends on this crate; this crate has no Python coupling.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## Throughput target
  25: //!
  26: //! Per [ADR-0001] verification gate: ≥ 2 GiB/s/core scalar; ≥ 5 GiB/s/core
  27: //! with AVX-512 / NEON dispatch via the underlying `fastcdc` crate's SIMD
  28: //! features. BLAKE3 hashing is ≥ 3 GiB/s/core via the reference SIMD impl.
  29: //! Joint throughput target: ≥ 1 GiB/s end-to-end ingest on the engine's
  30: //! Phase A1 acceptance hardware.
  31: //!
  32: //! ## Determinism
  33: //!
  34: //! Same input → same chunk boundaries on every architecture. SIMD changes
  35: //! microarchitecture, not byte-output. Cross-platform property tests in
  36: //! `tests/cross_platform.rs` validate this.
  37: //!
  38: //! [ADR-0001]: ../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md
  39: //! [ADR-0006]: ../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md

   1: //! Cross-platform determinism test.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per [ADR-0001](../../../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md) verification
   4: //! gate #2: same input must produce byte-identical chunk boundaries on
   5: //! x86-64, ARM64 (Apple Silicon), and Windows. SIMD changes
   6: //! microarchitecture, not byte output.
   7: //!
   8: //! The fixture below pins:
   9: //!   - A deterministic 1 MiB pseudo-random buffer (xorshift seed = the
  10: //!     value below).
  11: //!   - The expected boundary offsets the FastCDC + Gear-256 kernel must
  12: //!     produce on that buffer for the default ADR-0001 parameters
  13: //!     (8 KiB / 64 KiB / 256 KiB).
  14: //!
  15: //! If this test fails after a Rust compiler upgrade, a `fastcdc` crate
  16: //! upgrade, or a SIMD path enable, that is a determinism regression and
  17: //! must be investigated immediately. The boundaries are part of the
  18: //! engine's wire-format compatibility surface — changing them silently
  19: //! breaks dedup with peers running older builds.
  20: 
  21: use ol_chunk::{scan_to_vec, Boundary};
  22: 
  23: /// Deterministic xorshift fill. Seed pinned for reproducibility.
  24: fn pseudo_random_buf(seed: u64, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
  25:     let mut state = seed;
  26:     let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
  27:     for byte in buf.iter_mut() {
  28:         state ^= state << 13;
  29:         state ^= state >> 7;
  30:         state ^= state << 17;
  31:         *byte = (state & 0xFF) as u8;
  32:     }
  33:     buf
  34: }
  35: 
  36: /// Expected boundaries (start offsets) produced by ADR-0001 kernel on
  37: /// `pseudo_random_buf(0xDEAD_BEEF_CAFE_F00D, 1 MiB)`.
  38: ///
  39: /// These are filled in the first time CI runs on the reference build by
  40: /// reading `boundary.start` for every yielded boundary. After that, this
  41: /// list is the determinism contract: any change here is a wire-format
  42: /// break.
  43: ///
  44: /// For the initial commit we only assert the *count* is stable; once
  45: /// the first reference run happens in CI we'll pin the exact offset list.
  46: const EXPECTED_BOUNDARY_COUNT_RANGE: std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize> = 12..=20;
  47: 
  48: #[test]
  49: fn boundaries_are_within_expected_count_range() {
  50:     let buf = pseudo_random_buf(0xDEAD_BEEF_CAFE_F00D, 1024 * 1024);
  51:     let boundaries: Vec<Boundary> = scan_to_vec(&buf);
  52:     let count = boundaries.len();
  53:     assert!(
  54:         EXPECTED_BOUNDARY_COUNT_RANGE.contains(&count),
  55:         "1 MiB random buffer with default CDC params should produce \
  56:          {EXPECTED_BOUNDARY_COUNT_RANGE:?} boundaries, got {count}",
  57:     );
  58: 
  59:     // Every boundary's BLAKE3 must equal hashing the underlying slice.
  60:     for b in &boundaries {
  61:         let actual = blake3::hash(&buf[b.start..b.end]);
  62:         assert_eq!(b.raw_address, *actual.as_bytes());
  63:     }
  64: 
  65:     // Boundaries tile the buffer exactly.
  66:     assert_eq!(boundaries[0].start, 0);
  67:     assert_eq!(boundaries.last().unwrap().end, buf.len());
  68:     for w in boundaries.windows(2) {
  69:         assert_eq!(w[0].end, w[1].start);
  70:     }
  71: }
  72: 
  73: #[test]
  74: fn determinism_across_repeated_scans() {
  75:     let buf = pseudo_random_buf(0x4242_4242_4242_4242, 256 * 1024);
  76:     let a = scan_to_vec(&buf);
  77:     let b = scan_to_vec(&buf);
  78:     assert_eq!(a, b);
  79: }
  80: 
  81: #[test]
  82: fn distinct_inputs_produce_distinct_addresses() {
  83:     // Two buffers differing in one byte must produce different chunk
  84:     // addresses for any chunk that contains the differing byte. This is
  85:     // the BLAKE3 collision-resistance property carried up to chunk level.
  86:     let buf_a = pseudo_random_buf(0x1, 128 * 1024);
  87:     let mut buf_b = buf_a.clone();
  88:     let mid = buf_b.len() / 2;
  89:     buf_b[mid] = buf_b[mid].wrapping_add(1);
  90: 
  91:     let bounds_a = scan_to_vec(&buf_a);
  92:     let bounds_b = scan_to_vec(&buf_b);
  93: 
  94:     // Find a boundary in A that contains the modified byte.
  95:     let modified = buf_a.len() / 2;
  96:     let containing_a = bounds_a
  97:         .iter()
  98:         .find(|b| b.start <= modified && modified < b.end);
  99:     let containing_b = bounds_b
 100:         .iter()
 101:         .find(|b| b.start <= modified && modified < b.end);
 102:     assert!(containing_a.is_some());
 103:     assert!(containing_b.is_some());
 104: 
 105:     // The chunk address that covers the modified byte MUST differ between
 106:     // the two buffers.
 107:     if let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (containing_a, containing_b) {
 108:         assert_ne!(a.raw_address, b.raw_address);
 109:     }
 110: }

  16:             prop_assert!(*o + 4 <= bytes.len());
  17:         }
  18:         // Offsets must be strictly increasing.
  19:         for w in offsets.windows(2) {
  20:             prop_assert!(w[1] > w[0]);
  21:         }
  22:     }
  23:

  14: fn make_chunk(id_byte: u8, plaintext_len: u32) -> ChunkRecord {
  15:     let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
  16:     chunk_id[0] = id_byte;
  17:     chunk_id[1] = 0xAA;
  18:     let ct_len = plaintext_len as usize + ((plaintext_len as usize + 16383) / 16384) * 16;
  19:     ChunkRecord {
  20:         kind: ChunkRecordKind::ChunkBlob,
  21:         address_kind: ChunkAddressKind::Raw,
  22:         aead_kind: ChunkAeadKind::AesGcm256,
  23:         compressed: false,
  24:         format_aware: false,

  26:         chunk_id,
  27:         ratchet_key_id: [0x55u8; 16],
  28:         stripe_descriptor: StripeDescriptor::NONE,
  29:         ciphertext: vec![0xCDu8; ct_len],
  30:     }
  31: }

   1: //! Chunk-log record format per [ADR-0003](../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! The chunk_log file (managed by [`ol_wal`]) stores records of this
   4: //! shape inside the WAL payload. The WAL header (kind + flags + length +
   5: //! CRC) wraps a 80-byte chunk-record header followed by the AEAD
   6: //! ciphertext bytes. From the perspective of [`ol_wal`]:
   7: //!
   8: //! ```text
   9: //! WAL record:
  10: //!   kind  = ChunkRecordKind (0x01 ChunkBlob, 0x02 StripeParity, 0xFE Tombstone)
  11: //!   flags = ChunkRecord flags (address kind, AEAD kind, compression, format-aware)
  12: //!   payload = [ChunkRecordHeader (80 bytes) || ciphertext (length_ciphertext bytes)]
  13: //! ```
  14: //!
  15: //! ChunkRecordHeader layout:
  16: //!
  17: //! ```text
  18: //! +--------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
  19: //! | Offset | Field                                                            |
  20: //! +--------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
  21: //! | 0      | length_plaintext: u32 LE                                         |
  22: //! | 4      | length_ciphertext: u32 LE                                        |
  23: //! | 8      | chunk_id_full: [u8; 32] (BLAKE3-256, raw or convergent)         |
  24: //! | 40     | ratchet_key_id: [u8; 16]                                         |
  25: //! | 56     | stripe_descriptor: 24 bytes (per ADR-0004)                       |
  26: //! +--------+------------------------------------------------------------------+
  27: //! Total: 80 bytes.
  28: //! ```
  29: 
  30: use crate::error::ChunkStoreError;
  31: use crate::stripe::{StripeDescriptor, STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN};
  32: 
  33: /// Length of the chunk-record header in bytes.
  34: pub const CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN: usize = 80;
  35: 
  36: // ─── kind / flags enums ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  37: 
  38: /// Kind byte for the chunk-log WAL record.
  39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  40: pub enum ChunkRecordKind {
  41:     /// 0x01: a chunk's encrypted content.
  42:     ChunkBlob,
  43:     /// 0x02: a Reed-Solomon parity shard (Phase C onwards).
  44:     StripeParity,
  45:     /// 0xFE: a tombstone reference. The chunk_id was reclaimed; the
  46:     /// address still resolves to "missing on purpose."
  47:     TombstoneRef,
  48: }
  49: 
  50: impl ChunkRecordKind {
  51:     /// On-disk byte.
  52:     #[inline]
  53:     #[must_use]
  54:     pub const fn as_u8(self) -> u8 {
  55:         match self {
  56:             Self::ChunkBlob => 0x01,
  57:             Self::StripeParity => 0x02,
  58:             Self::TombstoneRef => 0xFE,
  59:         }
  60:     }
  61: 
  62:     /// Decode from the on-disk byte.
  63:     #[must_use]
  64:     pub const fn from_u8(b: u8) -> Option<Self> {
  65:         match b {
  66:             0x01 => Some(Self::ChunkBlob),
  67:             0x02 => Some(Self::StripeParity),
  68:             0xFE => Some(Self::TombstoneRef),
  69:             _ => None,
  70:         }
  71:     }
  72: }
  73: 
  74: /// Whether the `chunk_id_full` is the raw BLAKE3 of the plaintext or
  75: /// the convergent-encryption derived address. Per
  76: /// [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md).
  77: ///
  78: /// Default is `Raw` for fresh chunks; per-recipient keys for project /
  79: /// document / non-media content. `Convergent` is opt-in per the Phase B
  80: /// rollout plan — gated by an explicit caller decision based on the
  81: /// content type (raw media = safe to converge; project files = not).
  82: /// See [`convergent_default_for_content_type`] for the production
  83: /// dispatch helper.
  84: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash, Default)]
  85: pub enum ChunkAddressKind {
  86:     /// `BLAKE3.hash(plaintext)`. The conservative default — per-
  87:     /// recipient keys; identical plaintext from two senders produces
  88:     /// different chunk IDs.
  89:     #[default]
  90:     Raw,
  91:     /// `BLAKE3.derive_key("ol-chunk-addr-convergent-v1", plaintext)`.
  92:     /// Opt-in for content types whose well-known plaintexts aren't a
  93:     /// privacy concern (raw media). Enables cross-sender dedup.
  94:     Convergent,
  95: }
  96: 
  97: /// Coarse content-type classifier for the convergent-default dispatch.
  98: /// Returns `Convergent` for content types where two senders sharing
  99: /// the same file SHOULD produce the same chunk IDs (so the dedup
 100: /// dividend is realised), and `Raw` for everything else.
 101: ///
 102: /// Conservative by design: only formats with low correlation between
 103: /// plaintext + recipient identity get convergent. Project files /
 104: /// documents / private payloads stay on raw-BLAKE3.
 105: ///
 106: /// Phase B integration point: the chunk-store ingest path consults
 107: /// this helper, NOT a hardcoded enum, so the policy can evolve
 108: /// without re-spinning every call site.
 109: #[must_use]
 110: pub fn convergent_default_for_content_type(extension: Option<&str>) -> ChunkAddressKind {
 111:     let Some(ext) = extension else {
 112:         return ChunkAddressKind::Raw;
 113:     };
 114:     match ext.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
 115:         // Raw media: the plaintext is the same for every recipient
 116:         // (a JPEG byte stream is fixed), so convergent IDs enable
 117:         // cross-sender dedup without leaking anything that isn't
 118:         // already public.
 119:         "mp4" | "m4v" | "mov" | "3gp" | "mkv" | "webm" | "avi" | "mp3" | "wav" | "flac" | "ogg"
 120:         | "opus" | "aac" | "m4a" | "jpg" | "jpeg" | "png" | "gif" | "webp" | "heic" | "h264"
 121:         | "264" | "avc" => ChunkAddressKind::Convergent,
 122:         // Everything else: project files, docs, archives, code,
 123:         // unknown types. Default to raw-BLAKE3.
 124:         _ => ChunkAddressKind::Raw,
 125:     }
 126: }
 127: 
 128: /// Which AEAD primitive was used to encrypt the ciphertext.
 129: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
 130: pub enum ChunkAeadKind {
 131:     /// AES-256-GCM (primary on x86 / ARM64 with hardware accel).
 132:     AesGcm256,
 133:     /// ChaCha20-Poly1305 (fallback / non-AES platforms).
 134:     ChaCha20Poly1305,
 135: }
 136: 
 137: /// Bit positions in the chunk-record flags byte per [ADR-0003].
 138: pub mod flag_bits {
 139:     /// 0 = raw-BLAKE3, 1 = convergent-BLAKE3.
 140:     pub const ADDRESS_KIND: u8 = 0b0000_0001;
 141:     /// 0 = AES-256-GCM, 1 = ChaCha20-Poly1305.
 142:     pub const AEAD_KIND: u8 = 0b0000_0010;
 143:     /// 0 = no compression, 1 = zstd applied to plaintext before AEAD.
 144:     pub const COMPRESSED: u8 = 0b0000_0100;
 145:     /// 0 = standard CDC, 1 = format-aware boundary used.
 146:     pub const FORMAT_AWARE: u8 = 0b0000_1000;
 147:     /// Bits 4-7 reserved; must be zero.
 148:     pub const RESERVED: u8 = 0b1111_0000;
 149: }
 150: 
 151: // ─── the record itself ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 152: 
 153: /// A complete chunk-log record (header + ciphertext) ready to be wrapped
 154: /// in a [`ol_wal::Record`] and appended to the chunk_log.
 155: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
 156: pub struct ChunkRecord {
 157:     /// Top-level kind (ChunkBlob / StripeParity / TombstoneRef).
 158:     pub kind: ChunkRecordKind,
 159:     /// Whether `chunk_id` is raw or convergent BLAKE3.
 160:     pub address_kind: ChunkAddressKind,
 161:     /// Which AEAD encrypted the ciphertext.
 162:     pub aead_kind: ChunkAeadKind,
 163:     /// Whether the plaintext was zstd-compressed before AEAD.
 164:     pub compressed: bool,
 165:     /// Whether a format-aware boundary was used (vs pure CDC).
 166:     pub format_aware: bool,
 167:     /// Length of the chunk plaintext in bytes (8 KiB - 256 KiB per ADR-0001).
 168:     pub length_plaintext: u32,
 169:     /// 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address.
 170:     pub chunk_id: [u8; 32],
 171:     /// 16-byte ratchet_key_id (per ADR-0006 Rule 4).
 172:     pub ratchet_key_id: [u8; 16],
 173:     /// Stripe descriptor (24 bytes per ADR-0004; `NONE` in Phase A1).
 174:     pub stripe_descriptor: StripeDescriptor,
 175:     /// AEAD ciphertext bytes (length = length_plaintext + frame_count * 16).
 176:     pub ciphertext: Vec<u8>,
 177: }
 178: 
 179: impl ChunkRecord {
 180:     /// Compute the flags byte from the boolean fields.
 181:     #[inline]
 182:     #[must_use]
 183:     pub fn flags_byte(&self) -> u8 {
 184:         let mut f = 0u8;
 185:         if matches!(self.address_kind, ChunkAddressKind::Convergent) {
 186:             f |= flag_bits::ADDRESS_KIND;
 187:         }
 188:         if matches!(self.aead_kind, ChunkAeadKind::ChaCha20Poly1305) {
 189:             f |= flag_bits::AEAD_KIND;
 190:         }
 191:         if self.compressed {
 192:             f |= flag_bits::COMPRESSED;
 193:         }
 194:         if self.format_aware {
 195:             f |= flag_bits::FORMAT_AWARE;
 196:         }
 197:         f
 198:     }
 199: 
 200:     /// Decode the boolean fields back from a flags byte.
 201:     fn parse_flags(
 202:         flags: u8,
 203:     ) -> Result<(ChunkAddressKind, ChunkAeadKind, bool, bool), ChunkStoreError> {
 204:         if flags & flag_bits::RESERVED != 0 {
 205:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 206:                 offset: 0,
 207:                 reason: "reserved flag bits non-zero",
 208:             });
 209:         }
 210:         let address_kind = if flags & flag_bits::ADDRESS_KIND != 0 {
 211:             ChunkAddressKind::Convergent
 212:         } else {
 213:             ChunkAddressKind::Raw
 214:         };
 215:         let aead_kind = if flags & flag_bits::AEAD_KIND != 0 {
 216:             ChunkAeadKind::ChaCha20Poly1305
 217:         } else {
 218:             ChunkAeadKind::AesGcm256
 219:         };
 220:         let compressed = flags & flag_bits::COMPRESSED != 0;
 221:         let format_aware = flags & flag_bits::FORMAT_AWARE != 0;
 222:         Ok((address_kind, aead_kind, compressed, format_aware))
 223:     }
 224: 
 225:     /// Encode to a (kind_byte, flags_byte, payload_bytes) tuple suitable
 226:     /// for [`ol_wal::Record`] construction.
 227:     pub fn encode(&self) -> (u8, u8, Vec<u8>) {
 228:         let mut payload = Vec::with_capacity(CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN + self.ciphertext.len());
 229:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.length_plaintext.to_le_bytes());
 230:         let length_ciphertext = self.ciphertext.len() as u32;
 231:         payload.extend_from_slice(&length_ciphertext.to_le_bytes());
 232:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.chunk_id);
 233:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.ratchet_key_id);
 234:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.stripe_descriptor.encode());
 235:         debug_assert_eq!(payload.len(), CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN);
 236:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.ciphertext);
 237:         (self.kind.as_u8(), self.flags_byte(), payload)
 238:     }
 239: 
 240:     /// Decode from a (kind_byte, flags_byte, payload_bytes) tuple.
 241:     ///
 242:     /// # Errors
 243:     ///
 244:     /// - [`ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord`] if the payload is too short
 245:     ///   or the `length_ciphertext` field doesn't match the actual
 246:     ///   payload remainder.
 247:     pub fn decode(kind: u8, flags: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, ChunkStoreError> {
 248:         let kind = ChunkRecordKind::from_u8(kind).ok_or(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 249:             offset: 0,
 250:             reason: "unknown chunk-record kind",
 251:         })?;
 252:         if payload.len() < CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN {
 253:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 254:                 offset: 0,
 255:                 reason: "payload shorter than chunk-record header",
 256:             });
 257:         }
 258:         let length_plaintext = u32::from_le_bytes(payload[0..4].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 259:         let length_ciphertext = u32::from_le_bytes(payload[4..8].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 260:         let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
 261:         chunk_id.copy_from_slice(&payload[8..40]);
 262:         let mut ratchet_key_id = [0u8; 16];
 263:         ratchet_key_id.copy_from_slice(&payload[40..56]);
 264:         let mut stripe_buf = [0u8; STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN];
 265:         stripe_buf.copy_from_slice(&payload[56..80]);
 266:         let stripe_descriptor = StripeDescriptor::decode(&stripe_buf)?;
 267:         let (address_kind, aead_kind, compressed, format_aware) = Self::parse_flags(flags)?;
 268:         let ciphertext_start = CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN;
 269:         let ciphertext_end = ciphertext_start + length_ciphertext as usize;
 270:         if payload.len() != ciphertext_end {
 271:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 272:                 offset: 0,
 273:                 reason: "length_ciphertext does not match payload length",
 274:             });
 275:         }
 276:         let ciphertext = payload[ciphertext_start..ciphertext_end].to_vec();
 277:         Ok(Self {
 278:             kind,
 279:             address_kind,
 280:             aead_kind,
 281:             compressed,
 282:             format_aware,
 283:             length_plaintext,
 284:             chunk_id,
 285:             ratchet_key_id,
 286:             stripe_descriptor,
 287:             ciphertext,

   5: /// Errors produced by chunk-store operations.

   9:     #[error("WAL: {0}")]

  18:     /// because the CRC may have validated but the higher-level body

<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! `ol_chunk_store` — the integrating chunk store for One Link's file
   2: //! engine v2.
   3: //!
   4: //! Combines:
   5: //!
   6: //! - [`ol_wal`] crash-only WAL (chunk_log + manifest_log files per
   7: //!   [ADR-0003](../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md))
   8: //! - [`ol_chunk`] BLAKE3 derivation (chunk addresses, ratchet_key_id,
   9: //!   stripe seeds per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md))
  10: //! - [`ol_aead`] per-chunk AEAD encrypt/decrypt
  11: //! - In-memory **memtable**: chunk_id → on-disk location
  12: //! - **Bloom filter front**: sub-microsecond chunk-presence checks
  13: //! - Manifest WAL coupling via `chunk_log_anchor` per
  14: //!   [ADR-0005](../../../docs/decisions/0005-manifest-wal-coupling.md)
  15: //! - **Stripe descriptor** support from day one per
  16: //!   [ADR-0004](../../../docs/decisions/0004-stripe-layout.md), even though
  17: //!   the encoder ships in Phase C
  18: //! - **Both raw and convergent** chunk addressing in the chunk_log header
  19: //!   so Phase B can flip the default without a format break
  20: //!
  21: //! ## Surface
  22: //!
  23: //! - [`ChunkStore::open`] — open/create a store rooted at a directory.
  24: //! - [`ChunkStore::write_chunk`] — write a chunk record (writes chunk_log
  25: //!   THEN matching manifest_log entry per ADR-0005 atomicity protocol).
  26: //! - [`ChunkStore::has_chunk`] — bloom + memtable presence check.
  27: //! - [`ChunkStore::read_chunk`] — read a chunk's on-wire ciphertext +
  28: //!   ratchet_key_id + stripe descriptor.
  29: //! - [`ChunkStore::write_manifest`] — append a manifest record (with
  30: //!   `chunk_log_anchor` automatically set to the most-recent chunk_log
  31: //!   offset).
  32: //! - [`ChunkStore::flush`] — durability barrier on both logs.
  33: //! - [`ChunkStore::stats`] — counters for diagnostics.
  34: 
  35: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_chunk_store/0.21.0")]
  36: 
  37: pub mod chunk_record;
  38: pub mod error;
  39: pub mod location;
  40: pub mod manifest_record;
  41: pub mod memtable;
  42: pub mod store;
  43: pub mod stripe;
  44: 
  45: pub use chunk_record::{
  46:     convergent_default_for_content_type, ChunkAddressKind, ChunkAeadKind, ChunkRecord,
  47:     ChunkRecordKind, CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN,
  48: };
  49: pub use error::ChunkStoreError;
  50: pub use location::ChunkLocation;
  51: pub use manifest_record::{ManifestRecord, ManifestRecordKind, MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN};
  52: pub use memtable::Memtable;
  53: pub use store::{ChunkStore, StoreStats};
  54: pub use stripe::{StripeDescriptor, StripeRole, STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN};
  55: 
  56: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  57: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

   1: //! `ChunkLocation` — the in-memory index value for the chunk store.
   2: //!
   3: //! Maps `chunk_id` → on-disk location + per-chunk metadata needed for
   4: //! decrypt without re-reading the chunk_log header.
   5: 
   6: use crate::stripe::StripeDescriptor;
   7: 
   8: /// Where a chunk lives within the chunk_log family.
   9: ///
  10: /// Pure value type; `Copy` for cheap return-by-value from memtable lookup.
  11: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
  12: pub struct ChunkLocation {
  13:     /// chunk_log file id (1-based; `000001.wal`, `000002.wal`, ...).
  14:     pub file_id: u64,
  15:     /// Byte offset within the file where the WAL record header starts.
  16:     /// (Per ADR-0007: this is the offset of the kind byte; the
  17:     /// per-record CRC32C is at the trailing edge.)
  18:     pub wal_offset: u64,
  19:     /// Plaintext length of the chunk in bytes.
  20:     pub length_plaintext: u32,
  21:     /// Ciphertext length (= plaintext length + frame_count * 16).
  22:     pub length_ciphertext: u32,
  23:     /// 16-byte ratchet_key_id for AEAD key reconstitution.
  24:     pub ratchet_key_id: [u8; 16],
  25:     /// Stripe descriptor (per ADR-0004).
  26:     pub stripe_descriptor: StripeDescriptor,
  27: }
  28: 
  29: impl ChunkLocation {
  30:     /// Total on-disk record size including the WAL framing
  31:     /// (8-byte WAL header + 80-byte chunk-record header + ciphertext +
  32:     /// 4-byte CRC trailer).
  33:     #[inline]
  34:     #[must_use]
  35:     pub fn on_disk_record_size(&self) -> u64 {
  36:         const WAL_HEADER_LEN: u64 = 8;
  37:         const WAL_TRAILER_LEN: u64 = 4;
  38:         const CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN: u64 = 80;
  39:         WAL_HEADER_LEN
  40:             + CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN
  41:             + u64::from(self.length_ciphertext)
  42:             + WAL_TRAILER_LEN
  43:     }
  44: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_chunk_store/src/manifest_record.rs", "bytes": 8192, "sha256": "2cd098f9dfa7604cdb4645133b2ba20b77c81a8a2ba291d6f2f0a50388bc892c", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-10T14:16:58.273646+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Manifest-log record format per [ADR-0003] + [ADR-0005].
   2: //!
   3: //! Manifest records are wrapped in [`ol_wal`] records the same way
   4: //! chunk records are. The WAL kind byte distinguishes manifest record
   5: //! types; the WAL flags byte carries record-specific bits; the payload
   6: //! is `[ManifestRecordHeader (52 bytes) || canonical-encoded body]`.
   7: //!
   8: //! Header layout per [ADR-0003]:
   9: //!
  10: //! ```text
  11: //! +--------+------------------------------------------------------+
  12: //! | Offset | Field                                                |
  13: //! +--------+------------------------------------------------------+
  14: //! | 0      | hlc_timestamp: u64 LE (hybrid logical clock)         |
  15: //! | 8      | actor_id: [u8; 32] (peer fingerprint / CRDT actor)   |
  16: //! | 40     | chunk_log_anchor: u64 LE (offset within chunk_log    |
  17: //! |        |   that this manifest commit pairs with — ADR-0005)  |
  18: //! | 48     | reserved: [u8; 4] (must be zero)                     |
  19: //! +--------+------------------------------------------------------+
  20: //! Total: 52 bytes.
  21: //! ```
  22: //!
  23: //! [ADR-0003]: ../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md
  24: //! [ADR-0005]: ../../../docs/decisions/0005-manifest-wal-coupling.md
  25: 
  26: use crate::error::ChunkStoreError;
  27: 
  28: /// Length of the manifest-record header in bytes.
  29: pub const MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN: usize = 52;
  30: 
  31: /// Kind byte for the manifest-log WAL record.
  32: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  33: pub enum ManifestRecordKind {
  34:     /// 0x10: a CRDT op on a folder manifest.
  35:     ManifestVersion,
  36:     /// 0x11: capability grant.
  37:     CapabilityGrant,
  38:     /// 0x12: capability revocation.
  39:     CapabilityRevoke,
  40:     /// 0x13: Merkle revocation log entry.
  41:     MerkleRevocationLogEntry,
  42:     /// 0x14: share-link record.
  43:     ShareLink,
  44:     /// 0xFF: rotation sentinel.
  45:     Sentinel,
  46: }
  47: 
  48: impl ManifestRecordKind {
  49:     /// On-disk byte.
  50:     #[inline]
  51:     #[must_use]
  52:     pub const fn as_u8(self) -> u8 {
  53:         match self {
  54:             Self::ManifestVersion => 0x10,
  55:             Self::CapabilityGrant => 0x11,
  56:             Self::CapabilityRevoke => 0x12,
  57:             Self::MerkleRevocationLogEntry => 0x13,
  58:             Self::ShareLink => 0x14,
  59:             Self::Sentinel => 0xFF,
  60:         }
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// Decode from the on-disk byte.
  64:     #[must_use]
  65:     pub const fn from_u8(b: u8) -> Option<Self> {
  66:         match b {
  67:             0x10 => Some(Self::ManifestVersion),
  68:             0x11 => Some(Self::CapabilityGrant),
  69:             0x12 => Some(Self::CapabilityRevoke),
  70:             0x13 => Some(Self::MerkleRevocationLogEntry),
  71:             0x14 => Some(Self::ShareLink),
  72:             0xFF => Some(Self::Sentinel),
  73:             _ => None,
  74:         }
  75:     }
  76: }
  77: 
  78: /// A complete manifest-log record (header + body) ready for the WAL.
  79: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  80: pub struct ManifestRecord {
  81:     /// Record kind.
  82:     pub kind: ManifestRecordKind,
  83:     /// Per-record-kind flags byte (interpreted by the layer above).
  84:     pub flags: u8,
  85:     /// Hybrid logical clock timestamp.
  86:     pub hlc_timestamp: u64,
  87:     /// 32-byte peer fingerprint (CRDT actor_id).
  88:     pub actor_id: [u8; 32],
  89:     /// Offset within the chunk_log that this manifest commit pairs with.
  90:     /// Zero for records that don't reference a chunk (capability events,
  91:     /// share-links, etc).
  92:     pub chunk_log_anchor: u64,
  93:     /// Canonical-encoded record body (per [`std.codec.canon`] design ref).
  94:     pub body: Vec<u8>,
  95: }
  96: 
  97: impl ManifestRecord {
  98:     /// Encode to a (kind_byte, flags_byte, payload_bytes) tuple.
  99:     pub fn encode(&self) -> (u8, u8, Vec<u8>) {
 100:         let mut payload = Vec::with_capacity(MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN + self.body.len());
 101:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.hlc_timestamp.to_le_bytes());
 102:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.actor_id);
 103:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.chunk_log_anchor.to_le_bytes());
 104:         payload.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 4]); // reserved
 105:         debug_assert_eq!(payload.len(), MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN);
 106:         payload.extend_from_slice(&self.body);
 107:         (self.kind.as_u8(), self.flags, payload)
 108:     }
 109: 
 110:     /// Decode from a (kind_byte, flags_byte, payload_bytes) tuple.
 111:     ///
 112:     /// # Errors
 113:     ///
 114:     /// - [`ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord`] if the payload is too short
 115:     ///   or the reserved bytes are non-zero.
 116:     pub fn decode(kind: u8, flags: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, ChunkStoreError> {
 117:         let kind = ManifestRecordKind::from_u8(kind).ok_or(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 118:             offset: 0,
 119:             reason: "unknown manifest-record kind",
 120:         })?;
 121:         if payload.len() < MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN {
 122:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 123:                 offset: 0,
 124:                 reason: "payload shorter than manifest-record header",
 125:             });
 126:         }
 127:         let hlc_timestamp = u64::from_le_bytes(payload[0..8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 128:         let mut actor_id = [0u8; 32];
 129:         actor_id.copy_from_slice(&payload[8..40]);
 130:         let chunk_log_anchor = u64::from_le_bytes(payload[40..48].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 131:         if !payload[48..52].iter().all(|b| *b == 0) {
 132:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 133:                 offset: 0,
 134:                 reason: "manifest header reserved bytes non-zero",
 135:             });
 136:         }
 137:         let body = payload[MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN..].to_vec();
 138:         Ok(Self {
 139:             kind,
 140:             flags,
 141:             hlc_timestamp,
 142:             actor_id,
 143:             chunk_log_anchor,
 144:             body,
 145:         })
 146:     }
 147: }
