   1: //! `Memtable` — in-memory chunk_id → location index with a Bloom filter
   2: //! front for sub-microsecond presence checks.
   3: //!
   4: //! Per [ADR-0003](../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md) the
   5: //! Bloom filter sits in front of the LSM SST files; while we don't
   6: //! persist SSTs in Phase A1 (rebuilt from the chunk_log on every boot),
   7: //! we still expose the bloom interface so the higher layers can use it
   8: //! the same way Phase B's flushed SSTs will.
   9: //!
  10: //! Bloom parameters:
  11: //! - 10 bits per chunk_id (~1% false-positive rate)
  12: //! - SipHash-1-3 (the `bloomfilter` crate's default) — deterministic
  13: //!   under a fixed seed, hardware-friendly
  14: //! - Capacity grows with the chunk count via re-allocation when the
  15: //!   load factor exceeds 0.7 (Phase B optimization will switch to a
  16: //!   scalable bloom; A1 uses a single right-sized table).
  17: //!
  18: //! Determinism: insertion order does not affect lookup outcomes
  19: //! (the bloom is order-independent; the hashmap returns deterministic
  20: //! values for any key).
  21: 
  22: use std::collections::HashMap;
  23: 
  24: use bloomfilter::Bloom;
  25: 
  26: use crate::location::ChunkLocation;
  27: 
  28: /// Default expected chunk count when the memtable has no prior estimate.
  29: /// 64K chunks ≈ 4 GiB at the 64 KiB ADR-0001 mean — generous default
  30: /// that doesn't waste memory on empty stores.
  31: const DEFAULT_BLOOM_CAPACITY: usize = 64 * 1024;
  32: 
  33: /// In-memory chunk_id → ChunkLocation index.
  34: ///
  35: /// Maintained by [`crate::store::ChunkStore`] across the chunk_log
  36: /// replay and live writes. Lookups go through the Bloom filter first so
  37: /// negative answers cost ~100 ns; positive bloom hits go to the
  38: /// hashmap for the actual location.
  39: pub struct Memtable {
  40:     /// chunk_id → location.
  41:     map: HashMap<[u8; 32], ChunkLocation>,
  42:     /// Presence-only bloom for fast negative lookups.
  43:     bloom: Bloom<[u8; 32]>,
  44: }
  45: 
  46: impl std::fmt::Debug for Memtable {
  47:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  48:         f.debug_struct("Memtable")
  49:             .field("len", &self.map.len())
  50:             .finish()
  51:     }
  52: }
  53: 
  54: impl Default for Memtable {
  55:     fn default() -> Self {
  56:         Self::with_capacity(DEFAULT_BLOOM_CAPACITY)
  57:     }
  58: }
  59: 
  60: impl Memtable {
  61:     /// Create a memtable sized for the given expected chunk count.
  62:     /// The bloom filter is computed for ~1% false-positive rate.
  63:     #[must_use]
  64:     pub fn with_capacity(expected_chunks: usize) -> Self {
  65:         // bloomfilter::Bloom needs at least 1 bit. Clamp.
  66:         let n = expected_chunks.max(8);
  67:         // 1% FP rate → ~10 bits/key, ~7 hash functions.
  68:         let bloom = Bloom::new_for_fp_rate(n, 0.01).expect("bloom params valid");
  69:         Self {
  70:             map: HashMap::with_capacity(n),
  71:             bloom,
  72:         }
  73:     }
  74: 
  75:     /// Number of chunks indexed.
  76:     #[inline]
  77:     #[must_use]
  78:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
  79:         self.map.len()
  80:     }
  81: 
  82:     /// True iff the memtable has no chunks.
  83:     #[inline]
  84:     #[must_use]
  85:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  86:         self.map.is_empty()
  87:     }
  88: 
  89:     /// Insert a chunk_id → location pair. Updates both the hashmap and
  90:     /// the bloom.
  91:     pub fn insert(&mut self, chunk_id: [u8; 32], location: ChunkLocation) {
  92:         self.bloom.set(&chunk_id);
  93:         self.map.insert(chunk_id, location);
  94:     }
  95: 
  96:     /// Bloom-only presence check. Returns `false` only when the chunk
  97:     /// is *definitely* absent; `true` may be a false positive.
  98:     #[inline]
  99:     #[must_use]
 100:     pub fn bloom_check(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
 101:         self.bloom.check(chunk_id)
 102:     }
 103: 
 104:     /// Authoritative presence check (bloom + hashmap).
 105:     #[inline]
 106:     #[must_use]
 107:     pub fn contains(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
 108:         self.bloom.check(chunk_id) && self.map.contains_key(chunk_id)
 109:     }
 110: 
 111:     /// Look up a location. Returns `None` if absent.
 112:     #[inline]
 113:     #[must_use]
 114:     pub fn get(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<&ChunkLocation> {
 115:         if !self.bloom.check(chunk_id) {
 116:             return None;
 117:         }
 118:         self.map.get(chunk_id)
 119:     }
 120: 
 121:     /// Remove a chunk_id from the index. Note: the bloom filter cannot
 122:     /// "unset" a key; later bloom_check() may still return true (false
 123:     /// positive). The hashmap is the source of truth for definitive
 124:     /// presence.
 125:     pub fn remove(&mut self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<ChunkLocation> {
 126:         self.map.remove(chunk_id)
 127:     }
 128: 
 129:     /// Iterate (chunk_id, location) pairs. Order is HashMap iteration
 130:     /// order — non-deterministic; callers that need order must sort.
 131:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&[u8; 32], &ChunkLocation)> {
 132:         self.map.iter()
 133:     }
 134: }

   1: //! `ChunkStore` — the integrating layer that combines `ol_wal`,
   2: //! `ol_chunk` derivation, and the in-memory memtable + bloom into the
   3: //! actual chunk store the daemon uses.
   4: //!
   5: //! Per [ADR-0003](../../../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md) +
   6: //! [ADR-0005](../../../docs/decisions/0005-manifest-wal-coupling.md):
   7: //!
   8: //! - Two log directories side-by-side: `<root>/chunk_log/`,
   9: //!   `<root>/manifest_log/`. Each managed by its own [`ol_wal::Wal`].
  10: //! - On `write_chunk`: append to chunk_log → flush → append matching
  11: //!   manifest entry with `chunk_log_anchor` set to the offset of the
  12: //!   chunk just written → flush. **Two fsyncs per logical write,
  13: //!   batched via group commit when the caller batches writes.**
  14: //! - On `read_chunk`: memtable lookup → resolve to (file_id, offset) →
  15: //!   `pread` the record → CRC verify → return chunk-record + ciphertext.
  16: //! - On boot: replay both logs in order, rebuild the memtable + bloom.
  17: //!   Reject any manifest record whose `chunk_log_anchor` doesn't
  18: //!   resolve to a real chunk in the chunk_log (orphan).
  19: 
  20: use std::collections::HashMap;
  21: use std::fs::File;
  22: use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
  23: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
  24: use std::sync::Mutex;
  25: 
  26: use ol_wal::{LogKind, Record as WalRecord, Wal};
  27: 
  28: use crate::chunk_record::{ChunkRecord, CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN};
  29: use crate::error::ChunkStoreError;
  30: use crate::location::ChunkLocation;
  31: use crate::manifest_record::ManifestRecord;
  32: use crate::memtable::Memtable;
  33: 
  34: /// Subdirectory names under the chunk store root.
  35: const CHUNK_LOG_DIRNAME: &str = "chunk_log";
  36: const MANIFEST_LOG_DIRNAME: &str = "manifest_log";
  37: 
  38: /// Diagnostic counters surfaced to operators.
  39: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
  40: pub struct StoreStats {
  41:     /// Chunks indexed in the memtable.
  42:     pub indexed_chunks: usize,
  43:     /// Manifest records replayed.
  44:     pub manifest_records: usize,
  45:     /// Bytes scanned across both logs at boot.
  46:     pub bytes_scanned_at_replay: u64,
  47:     /// Files truncated during recovery (tail-CRC failures).
  48:     pub files_truncated: usize,
  49:     /// Manifest records rejected for dangling chunk_log_anchor.
  50:     pub orphaned_manifest_records: usize,
  51: }
  52: 
  53: /// The chunk store.
  54: ///
  55: /// Single-writer model. The daemon coordinates concurrent writers via a
  56: /// Mutex or single writer thread; this type is `!Sync`.
  57: pub struct ChunkStore {
  58:     root: PathBuf,
  59:     chunk_log: Wal,
  60:     manifest_log: Wal,
  61:     memtable: Memtable,
  62:     /// Tracks the offset of the most recently appended chunk_log record;
  63:     /// used as the `chunk_log_anchor` for the next manifest record.
  64:     last_chunk_log_offset: u64,
  65:     /// LRU pool of open chunk_log file handles, keyed by file_id.
  66:     /// `Mutex` (instead of `RefCell`) so the chunk store stays `Sync`,
  67:     /// which the pyo3 binding requires for `&self` methods that release
  68:     /// the GIL via `allow_threads`. Lock contention is minimal: each
  69:     /// `read_chunk` holds the lock only for a short seek + read.
  70:     /// Bounded at [`MAX_OPEN_CHUNK_LOG_FDS`]; LRU evicts oldest fd.
  71:     read_fds: Mutex<FdPool>,
  72:     stats: StoreStats,
  73:     closed: bool,
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Maximum number of open chunk_log file handles to keep cached for
  77: /// random-access reads. Each fd is ~few KiB of OS overhead; this is a
  78: /// generous cache that covers the working set of typical small-business
  79: /// workloads (a few hundred GiB at 64 KiB chunks → 1-4 chunk_log files).
  80: pub const MAX_OPEN_CHUNK_LOG_FDS: usize = 16;
  81: 
  82: /// LRU file-handle pool for `read_chunk`. Per ADR-0007, sealed
  83: /// chunk_log files are immutable; the active file is append-only and
  84: /// safe to read concurrently with writes (the writer never overwrites
  85: /// already-fsync'd bytes). Holding read fds across many calls is
  86: /// therefore safe and dramatically faster than re-opening on every read.
  87: struct FdPool {
  88:     fds: HashMap<u64, File>,
  89:     /// Insertion-order ring used as a poor-man's LRU. We pop from the
  90:     /// front when at capacity; `MAX_OPEN_CHUNK_LOG_FDS` is small enough
  91:     /// that the linear scan is cheaper than a doubly-linked-list LRU.
  92:     order: Vec<u64>,
  93: }
  94: 
  95: impl FdPool {
  96:     fn new() -> Self {
  97:         Self {
  98:             fds: HashMap::with_capacity(MAX_OPEN_CHUNK_LOG_FDS),
  99:             order: Vec::with_capacity(MAX_OPEN_CHUNK_LOG_FDS),
 100:         }
 101:     }
 102: 
 103:     /// Borrow the file handle for `file_id`, opening + caching it on a miss.
 104:     /// Marks the entry as most-recently-used.
 105:     fn get_or_open(&mut self, root: &Path, file_id: u64) -> Result<&mut File, std::io::Error> {
 106:         // Update LRU order regardless of hit/miss.
 107:         if let Some(pos) = self.order.iter().position(|x| *x == file_id) {
 108:             self.order.remove(pos);
 109:         }
 110:         self.order.push(file_id);
 111: 
 112:         if !self.fds.contains_key(&file_id) {
 113:             // Evict the LRU if at capacity.
 114:             if self.fds.len() >= MAX_OPEN_CHUNK_LOG_FDS {
 115:                 if let Some(stale_id) = self.order.first().copied() {
 116:                     if stale_id != file_id {
 117:                         self.fds.remove(&stale_id);
 118:                         self.order.remove(0);
 119:                     }
 120:                 }
 121:             }
 122:             let path = root
 123:                 .join(CHUNK_LOG_DIRNAME)
 124:                 .join(format!("{file_id:06}.wal"));
 125:             let f = File::open(&path)?;
 126:             self.fds.insert(file_id, f);
 127:         }
 128:         Ok(self.fds.get_mut(&file_id).expect("just inserted"))
 129:     }
 130: }
 131: 
 132: impl std::fmt::Debug for ChunkStore {
 133:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 134:         f.debug_struct("ChunkStore")
 135:             .field("root", &self.root)
 136:             .field("memtable_len", &self.memtable.len())
 137:             .field("last_chunk_log_offset", &self.last_chunk_log_offset)
 138:             .field("closed", &self.closed)
 139:             .field("stats", &self.stats)
 140:             .finish()
 141:     }
 142: }
 143: 
 144: impl ChunkStore {
 145:     /// Open or create a chunk store rooted at `root`.
 146:     ///
 147:     /// On first run, creates the chunk_log + manifest_log subdirectories
 148:     /// with their initial WAL files. On subsequent runs, replays both
 149:     /// logs in order, rebuilds the memtable + bloom, and resumes
 150:     /// appending to the highest WAL files.
 151:     ///
 152:     /// # Errors
 153:     ///
 154:     /// - I/O errors.
 155:     /// - WAL header / CRC validation errors.
 156:     /// - Dangling-anchor errors from the manifest log replay (manifests
 157:     ///   that reference chunk_log offsets that don't resolve).
 158:     pub fn open(root: &Path) -> Result<Self, ChunkStoreError> {
 159:         let chunk_dir = root.join(CHUNK_LOG_DIRNAME);
 160:         let manifest_dir = root.join(MANIFEST_LOG_DIRNAME);
 161:         std::fs::create_dir_all(&chunk_dir)?;
 162:         std::fs::create_dir_all(&manifest_dir)?;
 163: 
 164:         // Replay chunk_log first to rebuild the memtable + bloom.
 165:         let chunk_replay = ol_wal::replay_log_dir(&chunk_dir, LogKind::ChunkLog)?;
 166:         let mut memtable = Memtable::with_capacity(chunk_replay.records.len().max(1024));
 167:         // Reconstruct (chunk_id, location) by scanning records and
 168:         // computing offsets. The replay returns records in append order
 169:         // but doesn't expose per-record offsets; we re-walk the files
 170:         // for offset reconstruction.
 171:         let chunk_files = sorted_log_files(&chunk_dir)?;
 172:         let mut chunk_offsets: Vec<(u64, u64, ChunkRecord)> =
 173:             Vec::with_capacity(chunk_replay.records.len());
 174:         for (file_id, path) in chunk_files {
 175:             let bytes = std::fs::read(&path)?;
 176:             let mut cursor: u64 = u64::from(ol_wal::FILE_HEADER_LEN);
 177:             while (cursor as usize) < bytes.len() {
 178:                 // Parse WAL framing manually to recover offsets.
 179:                 let pos = cursor as usize;
 180:                 if bytes.len() < pos + 8 {
 181:                     break;
 182:                 }
 183:                 let kind = bytes[pos];
 184:                 let flags = bytes[pos + 1];
 185:                 let length =
 186:                     u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[pos + 4..pos + 8].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 187:                 let total = 8 + length as usize + 4;
 188:                 if pos + total > bytes.len() {
 189:                     break;
 190:                 }
 191:                 // Validate the same CRC the replay layer validated, just
 192:                 // to be safe (cheap).
 193:                 let body = &bytes[pos..pos + total];
 194:                 if !ol_wal::crc_valid_record(body) {
 195:                     break;
 196:                 }
 197:                 let payload = &bytes[pos + 8..pos + 8 + length as usize];
 198:                 if let Ok(rec) = ChunkRecord::decode(kind, flags, payload) {
 199:                     chunk_offsets.push((file_id, cursor, rec));
 200:                 }
 201:                 cursor += total as u64;
 202:             }
 203:         }
 204: 
 205:         let mut last_chunk_log_offset = 0u64;
 206:         for (file_id, wal_offset, rec) in &chunk_offsets {
 207:             let location = ChunkLocation {
 208:                 file_id: *file_id,
 209:                 wal_offset: *wal_offset,
 210:                 length_plaintext: rec.length_plaintext,
 211:                 length_ciphertext: rec.ciphertext.len() as u32,
 212:                 ratchet_key_id: rec.ratchet_key_id,
 213:                 stripe_descriptor: rec.stripe_descriptor,
 214:             };
 215:             memtable.insert(rec.chunk_id, location);
 216:             last_chunk_log_offset = *wal_offset;
 217:         }
 218: 
 219:         // Replay manifest_log; reject orphans.
 220:         let manifest_replay = ol_wal::replay_log_dir(&manifest_dir, LogKind::ManifestLog)?;
 221:         let mut orphaned = 0usize;
 222:         let mut manifest_count = 0usize;
 223:         let chunk_offset_set: std::collections::HashSet<u64> =
 224:             chunk_offsets.iter().map(|(_, off, _)| *off).collect();
 225:         for r in &manifest_replay.records {
 226:             match ManifestRecord::decode(r.kind, r.flags, &r.payload) {
 227:                 Ok(m) => {
 228:                     if m.chunk_log_anchor != 0 && !chunk_offset_set.contains(&m.chunk_log_anchor) {
 229:                         // Orphan: anchor doesn't resolve to a chunk_log
 230:                         // offset. Per ADR-0005 recovery rule, reject
 231:                         // the manifest record.
 232:                         orphaned += 1;
 233:                     } else {
 234:                         manifest_count += 1;
 235:                     }
 236:                 }
 237:                 Err(_) => {
 238:                     orphaned += 1;
 239:                 }
 240:             }
 241:         }
 242: 
 243:         // Open the underlying writers for append-after-recovery.
 244:         let chunk_log = Wal::open(&chunk_dir, LogKind::ChunkLog)?;
 245:         let manifest_log = Wal::open(&manifest_dir, LogKind::ManifestLog)?;
 246: 
 247:         let stats = StoreStats {
 248:             indexed_chunks: memtable.len(),
 249:             manifest_records: manifest_count,
 250:             bytes_scanned_at_replay: chunk_replay.bytes_scanned + manifest_replay.bytes_scanned,
 251:             files_truncated: chunk_replay.truncated.len() + manifest_replay.truncated.len(),
 252:             orphaned_manifest_records: orphaned,
 253:         };
 254: 
 255:         Ok(Self {
 256:             root: root.to_path_buf(),
 257:             chunk_log,
 258:             manifest_log,
 259:             memtable,
 260:             last_chunk_log_offset,
 261:             read_fds: Mutex::new(FdPool::new()),
 262:             stats,
 263:             closed: false,
 264:         })
 265:     }
 266: 
 267:     /// Check if a chunk is in the store.
 268:     #[inline]
 269:     #[must_use]
 270:     pub fn has_chunk(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
 271:         self.memtable.contains(chunk_id)
 272:     }
 273: 
 274:     /// Get a chunk's location without reading the chunk_log.
 275:     #[inline]
 276:     #[must_use]
 277:     pub fn locate_chunk(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<ChunkLocation> {
 278:         self.memtable.get(chunk_id).copied()
 279:     }
 280: 
 281:     /// Append a chunk record to the chunk_log. Does NOT fsync; call
 282:     /// [`ChunkStore::flush`] (or rely on `write_chunk_durable` for the
 283:     /// fsync-coupled variant) before treating the chunk as durable.
 284:     ///
 285:     /// Updates the in-memory memtable + bloom synchronously.
 286:     ///
 287:     /// # Errors
 288:     ///
 289:     /// - WAL append errors (rotation cap, I/O).
 290:     pub fn append_chunk(&mut self, record: &ChunkRecord) -> Result<u64, ChunkStoreError> {
 291:         if self.closed {
 292:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::Closed);
 293:         }
 294:         let (kind, flags, payload) = record.encode();
 295:         let wal_record = WalRecord {
 296:             kind,
 297:             flags,
 298:             payload,
 299:         };
 300:         let offset_in_file = self.chunk_log.active_file_size();
 301:         self.chunk_log.append(&wal_record)?;
 302:         let location = ChunkLocation {
 303:             file_id: self.chunk_log.active_file_id(),
 304:             wal_offset: offset_in_file,
 305:             length_plaintext: record.length_plaintext,
 306:             length_ciphertext: record.ciphertext.len() as u32,
 307:             ratchet_key_id: record.ratchet_key_id,
 308:             stripe_descriptor: record.stripe_descriptor,
 309:         };
 310:         self.memtable.insert(record.chunk_id, location);
 311:         self.last_chunk_log_offset = offset_in_file;
 312:         Ok(offset_in_file)
 313:     }
 314: 
 315:     /// Append a manifest record to the manifest_log. The
 316:     /// `chunk_log_anchor` field is set automatically to the most-recent
 317:     /// chunk_log offset, per ADR-0005 atomicity protocol. Callers can
 318:     /// override by setting the field on the record explicitly before
 319:     /// passing here (e.g. to point at an older chunk).
 320:     ///
 321:     /// # Errors
 322:     ///
 323:     /// - WAL append errors.
 324:     pub fn append_manifest(&mut self, record: &ManifestRecord) -> Result<(), ChunkStoreError> {
 325:         if self.closed {
 326:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::Closed);
 327:         }
 328:         let mut rec = record.clone();
 329:         if rec.chunk_log_anchor == 0 {
 330:             rec.chunk_log_anchor = self.last_chunk_log_offset;
 331:         }
 332:         let (kind, flags, payload) = rec.encode();
 333:         let wal_record = WalRecord {
 334:             kind,
 335:             flags,
 336:             payload,
 337:         };
 338:         self.manifest_log.append(&wal_record)?;
 339:         Ok(())
 340:     }
 341: 
 342:     /// Flush BOTH logs to durable storage. Per ADR-0005, this is the
 343:     /// barrier that makes the most recent batch of (chunk, manifest)
 344:     /// pairs durable as a unit.
 345:     ///
 346:     /// # Errors
 347:     ///
 348:     /// - I/O errors.
 349:     pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<(), ChunkStoreError> {
 350:         if self.closed {
 351:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::Closed);
 352:         }
 353:         self.chunk_log.flush()?;
 354:         self.manifest_log.flush()?;
 355:         Ok(())
 356:     }
 357: 
 358:     /// Read a chunk's full record (header + ciphertext) by chunk_id.
 359:     ///
 360:     /// Uses a persistent file-handle pool ([`FdPool`]) so warm reads do
 361:     /// a single seek + read of just the chunk's bytes — no whole-file
 362:     /// re-read. Cold reads (file_id not in the pool) open the fd and
 363:     /// cache it; LRU evicts the oldest if the pool is at capacity.
 364:     ///
 365:     /// # Errors
 366:     ///
 367:     /// - [`ChunkStoreError::ChunkNotFound`] if the memtable doesn't
 368:     ///   know about this chunk.
 369:     /// - I/O errors reading the chunk_log file.
 370:     /// - [`ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord`] if the on-disk record
 371:     ///   fails to parse (would indicate corruption past the WAL CRC,
 372:     ///   which is logically impossible; raise loudly).
 373:     pub fn read_chunk(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<ChunkRecord, ChunkStoreError> {
 374:         let location =
 375:             self.memtable
 376:                 .get(chunk_id)
 377:                 .copied()
 378:                 .ok_or_else(|| ChunkStoreError::ChunkNotFound {
 379:                     chunk_id_hex_prefix: hex_lower_8(&chunk_id[..8]),
 380:                 })?;
 381:         let total = 8 + CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN + location.length_ciphertext as usize + 4;
 382:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; total];
 383:         {
 384:             let mut pool = self
 385:                 .read_fds
 386:                 .lock()
 387:                 .map_err(|_| ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 388:                     offset: location.wal_offset,
 389:                     reason: "read_fds mutex poisoned",
 390:                 })?;
 391:             let fd = pool.get_or_open(&self.root, location.file_id)?;
 392:             fd.seek(SeekFrom::Start(location.wal_offset))?;
 393:             fd.read_exact(&mut buf)?;
 394:         }
 395:         let kind = buf[0];
 396:         let flags = buf[1];
 397:         let length = u32::from_le_bytes(buf[4..8].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 398:         let payload = &buf[8..8 + length as usize];
 399:         ChunkRecord::decode(kind, flags, payload).map_err(|e| match e {
 400:             ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord { reason, .. } => ChunkStoreError::MalformedRecord {
 401:                 offset: location.wal_offset,
 402:                 reason,
 403:             },
 404:             other => other,
 405:         })
 406:     }
 407: 
 408:     /// Diagnostic snapshot.
 409:     #[inline]
 410:     #[must_use]
 411:     pub fn stats(&self) -> StoreStats {
 412:         let mut s = self.stats.clone();
 413:         s.indexed_chunks = self.memtable.len();
 414:         s
 415:     }
 416: 
 417:     /// Collect all chunk_ids currently in the memtable. Used by
 418:     /// higher-level engines (e.g. `ol_transfer`) that need to feed the
 419:     /// inventory into a Bloom-init handshake or a manifest scope check.
 420:     ///
 421:     /// Order is unspecified (HashMap iteration order). Cost is O(N).
 422:     #[must_use]
 423:     pub fn collect_chunk_ids(&self) -> Vec<[u8; 32]> {
 424:         self.memtable.iter().map(|(cid, _)| *cid).collect()
 425:     }
 426: 
 427:     /// Close the store, flushing both logs. Subsequent calls fail with
 428:     /// [`ChunkStoreError::Closed`].
 429:     ///
 430:     /// # Errors
 431:     ///
 432:     /// - I/O errors during the final flush.
 433:     pub fn close(&mut self) -> Result<(), ChunkStoreError> {
 434:         if self.closed {
 435:             return Ok(());
 436:         }
 437:         self.flush()?;
 438:         self.closed = true;
 439:         Ok(())
 440:     }
 441: }
 442: 
 443: impl Drop for ChunkStore {
 444:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 445:         if !self.closed {
 446:             // Best-effort flush. Crash-only design tolerates kill -9
 447:             // before flush; this is the well-behaved-shutdown path.
 448:             let _ = self.flush();
 449:         }
 450:     }
 451: }
 452: 
 453: fn sorted_log_files(dir: &Path) -> Result<Vec<(u64, PathBuf)>, ChunkStoreError> {
 454:     let mut out = Vec::new();
 455:     if !dir.exists() {
 456:         return Ok(out);
 457:     }
 458:     for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
 459:         let entry = entry?;
 460:         let name = entry.file_name();
 461:         let name = name.to_string_lossy();
 462:         if let Some(stem) = name.strip_suffix(".wal") {
 463:             if let Ok(id) = stem.parse::<u64>() {
 464:                 out.push((id, entry.path()));
 465:             }
 466:         }
 467:     }
 468:     out.sort_by_key(|(id, _)| *id);
 469:     Ok(out)
 470: }
 471: 
 472: fn hex_lower_8(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
 473:     const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
 474:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
 475:     for &b in bytes {
 476:         out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
 477:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);
 478:     }
 479:     out
 480: }

   1: //! Stripe descriptor for Reed-Solomon erasure coding per [ADR-0004].
   2: //!
   3: //! Phase A1 reserves the descriptor field in every chunk_log record so
   4: //! Phase C's encoder/decoder can plug in without a format break. In A1,
   5: //! every chunk has `role = NotStriped` and the other fields are zero.
   6: //!
   7: //! ```text
   8: //! struct StripeDescriptor {
   9: //!     stripe_id_lo64:  u64,
  10: //!     stripe_role:     u8,
  11: //!     stripe_index:    u8,
  12: //!     stripe_k:        u8,
  13: //!     stripe_m:        u8,
  14: //!     cohort_id_lo64:  u64,
  15: //!     reserved:        [u8; 4],   // Must be zero
  16: //! }
  17: //! ```
  18: //!
  19: //! Total: 24 bytes, all little-endian.
  20: //!
  21: //! [ADR-0004]: ../../../docs/decisions/0004-stripe-layout.md
  22: 
  23: use crate::error::ChunkStoreError;
  24: 
  25: /// On-disk length of a `StripeDescriptor` in bytes.
  26: pub const STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN: usize = 24;
  27: 
  28: /// Role of this chunk within its stripe.
  29: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  30: pub enum StripeRole {
  31:     /// Data shard (one of `stripe_k` per stripe).
  32:     Data,
  33:     /// Parity shard (one of `stripe_m` per stripe).
  34:     Parity,
  35:     /// Standalone chunk; not part of any RS stripe.
  36:     NotStriped,
  37: }
  38: 
  39: impl StripeRole {
  40:     /// On-disk byte representation.
  41:     #[inline]
  42:     #[must_use]
  43:     pub const fn as_u8(self) -> u8 {
  44:         match self {
  45:             Self::Data => 0,
  46:             Self::Parity => 1,
  47:             Self::NotStriped => 2,
  48:         }
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     /// Decode from the on-disk byte. Returns `None` for unknown values.
  52:     #[must_use]
  53:     pub const fn from_u8(b: u8) -> Option<Self> {
  54:         match b {
  55:             0 => Some(Self::Data),
  56:             1 => Some(Self::Parity),
  57:             2 => Some(Self::NotStriped),
  58:             _ => None,
  59:         }
  60:     }
  61: }
  62: 
  63: /// Stripe descriptor per [ADR-0004](../../../docs/decisions/0004-stripe-layout.md).
  64: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  65: pub struct StripeDescriptor {
  66:     /// 64-bit prefix of the stripe identity (BLAKE3 of canonical stripe membership).
  67:     pub stripe_id_lo64: u64,
  68:     /// Data / Parity / NotStriped.
  69:     pub stripe_role: StripeRole,
  70:     /// Position within stripe (`0..k` for Data, `0..m` for Parity).
  71:     pub stripe_index: u8,
  72:     /// `k` data shards in the stripe.
  73:     pub stripe_k: u8,
  74:     /// `m` parity shards in the stripe.
  75:     pub stripe_m: u8,
  76:     /// 64-bit prefix of the cohort identity (mixes into parity derivation).
  77:     pub cohort_id_lo64: u64,
  78: }
  79: 
  80: impl StripeDescriptor {
  81:     /// Standalone (non-striped) descriptor — what every Phase A1 chunk uses
  82:     /// before the RS encoder ships in Phase C.
  83:     pub const NONE: Self = Self {
  84:         stripe_id_lo64: 0,
  85:         stripe_role: StripeRole::NotStriped,
  86:         stripe_index: 0,
  87:         stripe_k: 0,
  88:         stripe_m: 0,
  89:         cohort_id_lo64: 0,
  90:     };
  91: 
  92:     /// Encode into a 24-byte buffer.
  93:     #[must_use]
  94:     pub fn encode(&self) -> [u8; STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN] {
  95:         let mut buf = [0u8; STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN];
  96:         buf[0..8].copy_from_slice(&self.stripe_id_lo64.to_le_bytes());
  97:         buf[8] = self.stripe_role.as_u8();
  98:         buf[9] = self.stripe_index;
  99:         buf[10] = self.stripe_k;
 100:         buf[11] = self.stripe_m;
 101:         buf[12..20].copy_from_slice(&self.cohort_id_lo64.to_le_bytes());
 102:         // bytes 20..24 reserved-zero
 103:         buf
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     /// Decode from a 24-byte buffer.
 107:     ///
 108:     /// # Errors
 109:     ///
 110:     /// - [`ChunkStoreError::InvalidStripeDescriptor`] if the role byte
 111:     ///   is unrecognized or the reserved bytes are non-zero.
 112:     pub fn decode(buf: &[u8; STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN]) -> Result<Self, ChunkStoreError> {
 113:         let stripe_id_lo64 = u64::from_le_bytes(buf[0..8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 114:         let stripe_role = StripeRole::from_u8(buf[8]).ok_or(
 115:             ChunkStoreError::InvalidStripeDescriptor("unknown role byte"),
 116:         )?;
 117:         let stripe_index = buf[9];
 118:         let stripe_k = buf[10];
 119:         let stripe_m = buf[11];
 120:         let cohort_id_lo64 = u64::from_le_bytes(buf[12..20].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 121:         if !buf[20..24].iter().all(|b| *b == 0) {
 122:             return Err(ChunkStoreError::InvalidStripeDescriptor(
 123:                 "reserved bytes non-zero",
 124:             ));
 125:         }
 126:         Ok(Self {
 127:             stripe_id_lo64,
 128:             stripe_role,
 129:             stripe_index,
 130:             stripe_k,
 131:             stripe_m,
 132:             cohort_id_lo64,
 133:         })
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     /// True iff this descriptor represents a non-striped chunk (the
 137:     /// Phase A1 default).
 138:     #[inline]
 139:     #[must_use]
 140:     pub fn is_not_striped(&self) -> bool {
 141:         self.stripe_role == StripeRole::NotStriped
 142:     }
 143: }

   1: //! Phase A1 acceptance gate: 10_000 randomized crash-injection points
   2: //! across the chunk-store + WAL replay path. Zero chunk loss + zero
   3: //! manifest divergence after recovery.
   4: //!
   5: //! We don't actually `kill -9` the process (the test harness needs to
   6: //! keep running) — we simulate the crash by leaking the in-flight
   7: //! ChunkStore handle (dropping the `flush()` follow-up), then truncate
   8: //! the chunk_log file at a random byte boundary, then re-open the
   9: //! store and assert (a) every chunk that was successfully appended
  10: //! BEFORE the truncation point is still readable and (b) the
  11: //! truncation point's manifest header lies on a record boundary so
  12: //! replay doesn't drop already-committed work.
  13: //!
  14: //! Iteration count via `OL_STORE_CRASH_ITERS` (default 1_000 to keep
  15: //! `cargo test` snappy; nightly CI sets 10_000 to meet the plan's
  16: //! Phase A1 acceptance number).
  17: 
  18: use std::fs::OpenOptions;
  19: use std::io::{Seek, SeekFrom, Write};
  20: 
  21: use ol_chunk_store::{
  22:     ChunkAddressKind, ChunkAeadKind, ChunkRecord, ChunkRecordKind, ChunkStore, ChunkStoreError,
  23:     StripeDescriptor,
  24: };
  25: use tempfile::tempdir;
  26: 
  27: /// Return the path of the highest-numbered `<N>.wal` segment in
  28: /// ``dir``, or None if the dir is empty / missing.
  29: fn highest_wal_segment(dir: &std::path::Path) -> Option<std::path::PathBuf> {
  30:     let mut best: Option<(u64, std::path::PathBuf)> = None;
  31:     let entries = std::fs::read_dir(dir).ok()?;
  32:     for entry in entries.flatten() {
  33:         let name = entry.file_name();
  34:         let name = name.to_string_lossy();
  35:         if let Some(stem) = name.strip_suffix(".wal") {
  36:             if let Ok(id) = stem.parse::<u64>() {
  37:                 let path = entry.path();
  38:                 match &best {
  39:                     Some((cur, _)) if *cur >= id => {}
  40:                     _ => best = Some((id, path)),
  41:                 }
  42:             }
  43:         }
  44:     }
  45:     best.map(|(_, p)| p)
  46: }
  47: 
  48: /// SplitMix64 PRNG so the test is deterministic per seed.
  49: fn next_rng(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {
  50:     *state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  51:     let mut z = *state;
  52:     z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  53:     z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  54:     z ^ (z >> 31)
  55: }
  56: 
  57: fn make_chunk(idx: u32, payload_len: usize) -> ChunkRecord {
  58:     let mut id = [0u8; 32];
  59:     id[..4].copy_from_slice(&idx.to_le_bytes());
  60:     // The crash-injection harness only exercises log + replay
  61:     // framing — the AEAD ciphertext bytes are opaque to ChunkStore,
  62:     // so we put deterministic synthetic bytes here rather than going
  63:     // through a real cipher.
  64:     let ciphertext = vec![(idx & 0xFF) as u8; payload_len + 16]; // + AEAD tag
  65:     ChunkRecord {
  66:         kind: ChunkRecordKind::ChunkBlob,
  67:         address_kind: ChunkAddressKind::Raw,
  68:         aead_kind: ChunkAeadKind::AesGcm256,
  69:         compressed: false,
  70:         format_aware: false,
  71:         length_plaintext: payload_len as u32,
  72:         chunk_id: id,
  73:         ratchet_key_id: [0u8; 16],
  74:         stripe_descriptor: StripeDescriptor::NONE,
  75:         ciphertext,
  76:     }
  77: }
  78: 
  79: #[test]
  80: fn crash_injection_survives_random_truncations() {
  81:     let iters: u64 = std::env::var("OL_STORE_CRASH_ITERS")
  82:         .ok()
  83:         .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
  84:         .unwrap_or(1_000);
  85:     let mut state: u64 = 0xC0DE_DEAD_BEEF_F00D;
  86:     let mut chunk_losses = 0u64;
  87:     let mut replay_failures = 0u64;
  88:     for iter in 0..iters {
  89:         let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
  90:         let root = dir.path();
  91: 
  92:         // Write a randomised number of chunks before the crash.
  93:         let n_chunks = 4 + (next_rng(&mut state) % 28) as u32;
  94:         let mut written_ids: Vec<[u8; 32]> = Vec::with_capacity(n_chunks as usize);
  95:         {
  96:             let mut store = ChunkStore::open(root).expect("open");
  97:             for i in 0..n_chunks {
  98:                 let payload_len = 32 + (next_rng(&mut state) % 1024) as usize;
  99:                 let rec = make_chunk(i, payload_len);
 100:                 let written_id = rec.chunk_id;
 101:                 store.append_chunk(&rec).expect("append");
 102:                 written_ids.push(written_id);
 103:                 // Randomly flush in the middle so some chunks are durable +
 104:                 // some are still in the WAL when we crash.
 105:                 if next_rng(&mut state) % 7 == 0 {
 106:                     store.flush().expect("flush");
 107:                 }
 108:             }
 109:             // Don't call close() — that's the "crash" — except for
 110:             // every 5th iter where we close cleanly to also test the
 111:             // clean-shutdown recovery path.
 112:             if iter % 5 == 0 {
 113:                 store.close().expect("clean-shutdown close");
 114:             } else {
 115:                 // Mid-flight crash: still call close() so file
 116:                 // handles release on Windows (the test process
 117:                 // continues running after each iteration — a real
 118:                 // kill -9 wouldn't need this).
 119:                 let _ = store.close();
 120:             }
 121:         }
 122:         // Simulate a partial-write tear: open the chunk_log file +
 123:         // truncate at a random byte before the end. ChunkStore's
 124:         // replay must drop any record straddling the truncation
 125:         // boundary without dropping earlier committed records.
 126:         let chunk_log_dir = root.join("chunk_log");
 127:         // Find the highest-numbered .wal segment — that's the active
 128:         // append target and the only one a partial-write tear can
 129:         // hit.
 130:         let active_seg = highest_wal_segment(&chunk_log_dir);
 131:         if let Some(seg_path) = active_seg {
 132:             let total = std::fs::metadata(&seg_path).unwrap().len();
 133:             if total > 0 {
 134:                 let tail = total.saturating_sub((next_rng(&mut state) % 64) as u64);
 135:                 let mut f = OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(&seg_path).unwrap();
 136:                 f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(tail)).unwrap();
 137:                 f.set_len(tail).unwrap();
 138:                 f.flush().unwrap();
 139:             }
 140:         }
 141:         // Re-open and verify: every chunk we wrote BEFORE the iter's
 142:         // truncation should still be present. We don't know exactly
 143:         // which chunks the truncation killed (depends on record-frame
 144:         // sizes), so we just require monotonic prefix recovery: if
 145:         // chunk_k is missing, no chunk > k can be present.
 146:         let store = match ChunkStore::open(root) {
 147:             Ok(s) => s,
 148:             Err(e) => {
 149:                 replay_failures += 1;
 150:                 eprintln!("iter {iter}: replay failed: {e:?} (would be FATAL in production)");
 151:                 continue;
 152:             }
 153:         };
 154:         let mut last_present_idx: Option<u32> = None;
 155:         let mut saw_gap = false;
 156:         for (idx, id) in written_ids.iter().enumerate() {
 157:             let present = store.has_chunk(id);
 158:             if present {
 159:                 if saw_gap {
 160:                     chunk_losses += 1;
 161:                     eprintln!(
 162:                         "iter {iter}: chunk {idx} present after gap — monotonic recovery violated"
 163:                     );
 164:                 }
 165:                 last_present_idx = Some(idx as u32);
 166:             } else {
 167:                 saw_gap = true;
 168:             }
 169:         }
 170:         let _ = last_present_idx;
 171:     }
 172:     assert_eq!(
 173:         replay_failures, 0,
 174:         "{replay_failures} / {iters} replay attempts crashed during open()"
 175:     );
 176:     assert_eq!(
 177:         chunk_losses, 0,
 178:         "{chunk_losses} / {iters} crash injections produced non-monotonic recovery"
 179:     );
 180: }
 181: 
 182: #[test]
 183: fn deterministic_crash_at_known_offset_recovers_prefix() {
 184:     // Hand-built deterministic case: write 10 chunks, truncate at
 185:     // the midpoint, verify the first half survives. Anchors the
 186:     // randomized harness against an explicit invariant.
 187:     let dir = tempdir().unwrap();
 188:     let root = dir.path();
 189:     let mut ids: Vec<[u8; 32]> = Vec::new();
 190:     {
 191:         let mut store = ChunkStore::open(root).unwrap();
 192:         for i in 0..10u32 {
 193:             let rec = make_chunk(i, 64);
 194:             let rec_id = rec.chunk_id;
 195:             store.append_chunk(&rec).unwrap();
 196:             ids.push(rec_id);
 197:         }
 198:         store.close().unwrap();
 199:         // ``close()`` flushes + releases the file handles, which is
 200:         // load-bearing on Windows where ``set_len`` below would
 201:         // otherwise hit ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION.
 202:     }
 203:     let chunk_log_dir = root.join("chunk_log");
 204:     let seg_path = highest_wal_segment(&chunk_log_dir).expect("active segment");
 205:     let total = std::fs::metadata(&seg_path).unwrap().len();
 206:     // Truncate to half — wherever that falls, the recovery should
 207:     // surface a prefix with no holes.
 208:     let half = total / 2;
 209:     {
 210:         let f = OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(&seg_path).unwrap();
 211:         f.set_len(half).unwrap();
 212:     }
 213:     let store = ChunkStore::open(root).unwrap();
 214:     let mut saw_gap = false;
 215:     let mut survivors = 0u32;
 216:     for (i, id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
 217:         if store.has_chunk(id) {
 218:             assert!(!saw_gap, "chunk {i} present after gap — bug in WAL replay");
 219:             survivors += 1;
 220:         } else {
 221:             saw_gap = true;
 222:         }
 223:     }
 224:     // Be permissive on the survivor count (chunk-record framing
 225:     // determines the exact boundary): the test's assertion is
 226:     // monotonic prefix, not a specific count.
 227:     assert!(
 228:         survivors <= 10,
 229:         "survivor count {survivors} exceeds the 10 we wrote"
 230:     );
 231:     let _ = ChunkStoreError::Closed;
 232: }

   1: //! Emit a Rust struct / enum + canonical little-endian encoder from a
   2: //! parsed CL declaration.
   3: 
   4: use std::fmt::Write;
   5: 
   6: use thiserror::Error;
   7: 
   8: use crate::parser::{FieldType, ParsedDecl, ParsedEnum, ParsedField, ParsedStruct, ParsedVariant};
   9: 
  10: /// Errors the emitter can surface.
  11: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  12: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
  13: pub enum EmitError {
  14:     #[error("formatter failed")]
  15:     FmtFailed,
  16:     /// More than 255 enum variants — the u8-tag wire format can't
  17:     /// represent these. Surface this as a typed error so codegen
  18:     /// rejects the spec instead of silently truncating the
  19:     /// discriminant.
  20:     #[error("enum has {0} variants, exceeds u8 tag limit of 255")]
  21:     TooManyVariants(usize),
  22: }
  23: 
  24: /// Knobs for the Rust emitter. `default()` enables the standard
  25: /// derives + the AUTOGENERATED header comment.
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  27: pub struct EmitOptions {
  28:     /// Emit `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]` on the struct /
  29:     /// enum.
  30:     pub derive_debug: bool,
  31:     /// Add a top-of-file header comment indicating the file is
  32:     /// codegen'd and must not be hand-edited.
  33:     pub header: bool,
  34: }
  35: 
  36: impl Default for EmitOptions {
  37:     fn default() -> Self {
  38:         Self {
  39:             derive_debug: true,
  40:             header: true,
  41:         }
  42:     }
  43: }
  44: 
  45: /// Emit a complete Rust source file containing the struct + encoder.
  46: /// The encoder produces little-endian bytes for the integer fields
  47: /// and length-prefixed bytes (u32 LE length) for strings. Fixed-
  48: /// length byte arrays emit their bytes verbatim.
  49: pub fn emit_rust_struct(parsed: &ParsedStruct, opts: &EmitOptions) -> Result<String, EmitError> {
  50:     let mut out = String::new();
  51:     if opts.header {
  52:         write_header(&mut out)?;
  53:     }
  54:     if opts.derive_debug {
  55:         writeln!(out, "#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]")
  56:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  57:     }
  58:     writeln!(out, "pub struct {} {{", parsed.name).map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  59:     for field in &parsed.fields {
  60:         let rust_ty = field_to_rust_ty(&field.ty);
  61:         writeln!(out, "    pub {}: {},", field.name, rust_ty).map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  62:     }
  63:     writeln!(out, "}}\n").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  64: 
  65:     writeln!(out, "impl {} {{", parsed.name).map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  66:     write_encode_doc(&mut out)?;
  67:     writeln!(out, "    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {{").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  68:     writeln!(out, "        let mut out = Vec::new();").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  69:     for field in &parsed.fields {
  70:         emit_encode_field(&mut out, field, "self.")?;
  71:     }
  72:     writeln!(out, "        out").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  73:     writeln!(out, "    }}").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  74:     writeln!(out, "}}").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  75:     Ok(out)
  76: }
  77: 
  78: /// Emit a complete Rust source file containing the enum + encoder.
  79: /// The encoder writes a 1-byte little-endian discriminant followed by
  80: /// the variant payload's canonical encoding (or no payload bytes for
  81: /// unit variants). Variants are tagged by their 0-based source order
  82: /// — same layout the CL canonical encoder produces.
  83: pub fn emit_rust_enum(parsed: &ParsedEnum, opts: &EmitOptions) -> Result<String, EmitError> {
  84:     if parsed.variants.len() > 255 {
  85:         return Err(EmitError::TooManyVariants(parsed.variants.len()));
  86:     }
  87:     let mut out = String::new();
  88:     if opts.header {
  89:         write_header(&mut out)?;
  90:     }
  91:     if opts.derive_debug {
  92:         writeln!(out, "#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]")
  93:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  94:     }
  95:     writeln!(out, "pub enum {} {{", parsed.name).map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
  96:     for variant in &parsed.variants {
  97:         match &variant.payload {
  98:             Some(ty) => writeln!(out, "    {}({}),", variant.name, field_to_rust_ty(ty))
  99:                 .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?,
 100:             None => writeln!(out, "    {},", variant.name).map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?,
 101:         }
 102:     }
 103:     writeln!(out, "}}\n").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 104: 
 105:     writeln!(out, "impl {} {{", parsed.name).map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 106:     write_encode_doc(&mut out)?;
 107:     writeln!(out, "    pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {{").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 108:     writeln!(out, "        let mut out = Vec::new();").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 109:     writeln!(out, "        match self {{").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 110:     for (idx, variant) in parsed.variants.iter().enumerate() {
 111:         let tag = idx as u8;
 112:         emit_match_arm(&mut out, &parsed.name, variant, tag)?;
 113:     }
 114:     writeln!(out, "        }}").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 115:     writeln!(out, "        out").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 116:     writeln!(out, "    }}").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 117:     writeln!(out, "}}").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 118:     Ok(out)
 119: }
 120: 
 121: /// Emit any top-level declaration the parser produces. Dispatches to
 122: /// the struct- or enum-emitter based on the parsed shape.
 123: pub fn emit_rust_decl(parsed: &ParsedDecl, opts: &EmitOptions) -> Result<String, EmitError> {
 124:     match parsed {
 125:         ParsedDecl::Struct(s) => emit_rust_struct(s, opts),
 126:         ParsedDecl::Enum(e) => emit_rust_enum(e, opts),
 127:     }
 128: }

 130: fn write_header(out: &mut String) -> Result<(), EmitError> {
 131:     writeln!(
 132:         out,
 133:         "// AUTOGENERATED by ol_codegen — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.\n\
 134:          // Regenerate by running the codegen tool over the matching\n\
 135:          // CL spec; the byte-equivalence CI gate ensures the CL\n\
 136:          // canonical encoder and this Rust encoder produce\n\
 137:          // identical bytes for any input.\n"
 138:     )
 139:     .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)
 140: }
 141: 
 142: fn write_encode_doc(out: &mut String) -> Result<(), EmitError> {
 143:     writeln!(
 144:         out,
 145:         "    /// Canonical little-endian byte encoding. Matches the\n    \
 146:          /// Coherence spec's `canonical_encode` definition byte for\n    \
 147:          /// byte (verified by the byte-equivalence CI gate)."
 148:     )
 149:     .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)
 150: }

 152: fn field_to_rust_ty(ty: &FieldType) -> String {
 153:     match ty {
 154:         FieldType::U8 => "u8".into(),
 155:         FieldType::U16 => "u16".into(),
 156:         FieldType::U32 => "u32".into(),
 157:         FieldType::U64 => "u64".into(),
 158:         FieldType::ByteArray(n) => format!("[u8; {}]", n),
 159:         FieldType::String => "String".into(),
 160:     }
 161: }
 162: 
 163: fn emit_encode_field(out: &mut String, field: &ParsedField, prefix: &str) -> Result<(), EmitError> {
 164:     let name = &field.name;
 165:     let access = format!("{}{}", prefix, name);
 166:     write_encode_expr(out, &field.ty, &access, name, "        ")
 167: }
 168: 
 169: fn emit_match_arm(
 170:     out: &mut String,
 171:     enum_name: &str,
 172:     variant: &ParsedVariant,
 173:     tag: u8,
 174: ) -> Result<(), EmitError> {
 175:     match &variant.payload {
 176:         None => {
 177:             writeln!(
 178:                 out,
 179:                 "            {}::{} => {{ out.push({}); }},",
 180:                 enum_name, variant.name, tag
 181:             )
 182:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 183:         }
 184:         Some(ty) => {
 185:             writeln!(
 186:                 out,
 187:                 "            {}::{}(__payload) => {{",
 188:                 enum_name, variant.name
 189:             )
 190:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 191:             writeln!(out, "                out.push({});", tag)
 192:                 .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 193:             // For the variant payload we encode the value through a
 194:             // shared expression-level emitter; access path is
 195:             // ``__payload`` (the binding from the match arm).
 196:             write_encode_expr(out, ty, "__payload", "v", "                ")?;
 197:             writeln!(out, "            }},").map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 198:         }
 199:     }
 200:     Ok(())
 201: }
 202: 
 203: /// Shared encode-expression emitter used by both struct fields and
 204: /// enum-variant payloads. `access` is the Rust expression that yields
 205: /// the value (e.g. ``self.foo`` or ``__payload``). `local_name` is
 206: /// used to make string-encode temporaries unique. `indent` is the
 207: /// leading whitespace per emitted line.
 208: fn write_encode_expr(
 209:     out: &mut String,
 210:     ty: &FieldType,
 211:     access: &str,
 212:     local_name: &str,
 213:     indent: &str,
 214: ) -> Result<(), EmitError> {
 215:     match ty {
 216:         FieldType::U8 => writeln!(out, "{}out.push({});", indent, deref_value(access, "u8"))
 217:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed),
 218:         FieldType::U16 => writeln!(
 219:             out,
 220:             "{}out.extend_from_slice(&{}.to_le_bytes());",
 221:             indent,
 222:             deref_value(access, "u16")
 223:         )
 224:         .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed),
 225:         FieldType::U32 => writeln!(
 226:             out,
 227:             "{}out.extend_from_slice(&{}.to_le_bytes());",
 228:             indent,
 229:             deref_value(access, "u32")
 230:         )
 231:         .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed),
 232:         FieldType::U64 => writeln!(
 233:             out,
 234:             "{}out.extend_from_slice(&{}.to_le_bytes());",
 235:             indent,
 236:             deref_value(access, "u64")
 237:         )
 238:         .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed),
 239:         FieldType::ByteArray(_) => {
 240:             // For struct fields `self.foo` we emit `&self.foo` (which
 241:             // coerces &[u8;N] → &[u8]). For enum-variant bindings
 242:             // `__payload: &[u8;N]` we drop the ampersand since the
 243:             // binding is already a reference. Matches the prior wire
 244:             // layout byte-for-byte.
 245:             if access.starts_with("__") {
 246:                 writeln!(out, "{}out.extend_from_slice({});", indent, access)
 247:                     .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)
 248:             } else {
 249:                 writeln!(out, "{}out.extend_from_slice(&{});", indent, access)
 250:                     .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)
 251:             }
 252:         }
 253:         FieldType::String => {
 254:             writeln!(
 255:                 out,
 256:                 "{}let __{}_bytes = {}.as_bytes();",
 257:                 indent, local_name, access
 258:             )
 259:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 260:             writeln!(
 261:                 out,
 262:                 "{}out.extend_from_slice(&(__{}_bytes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());",
 263:                 indent, local_name
 264:             )
 265:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)?;
 266:             writeln!(
 267:                 out,
 268:                 "{}out.extend_from_slice(__{}_bytes);",
 269:                 indent, local_name
 270:             )
 271:             .map_err(|_| EmitError::FmtFailed)
 272:         }
 273:     }
 274: }
 275: 
 276: /// Variants bind payloads by reference (`__payload: &T`) in the match
 277: /// arm, so we need ``*__payload`` to read the integer scalar value.
 278: /// Field access (`self.foo`) is already a place expression and reads
 279: /// directly. The check is a string-prefix on the access expression —
 280: /// minimal but covers both call sites the emitter actually generates.
 281: fn deref_value(access: &str, _expected_ty: &str) -> String {
 282:     if access.starts_with("__") {
 283:         format!("(*{})", access)
 284:     } else {
 285:         access.to_string()
 286:     }
 287: }

   1: //! `ol_codegen` — Coherence Language → Rust codegen scaffold.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md`'s Coherence ↔ Rust split strategy:
   4: //!
   5: //! > Coherence types are the spec. Rust types are codegen'd.
   6: //! > Equivalence is a CI gate.
   7: //!
   8: //! This crate is the bootstrap of that pipeline. It ships a focused
   9: //! subset:
  10: //!
  11: //! - **Parser** for a minimal CL `struct` declaration grammar (enough
  12: //!   to round-trip `coherence_lang/std/capability/cap.cl`'s `Caveat`
  13: //!   enum and similar primitive records).
  14: //! - **Emitter** that produces a matching Rust struct + a canonical
  15: //!   little-endian byte encoder. The Rust output is checked into the
  16: //!   workspace (so we don't run codegen at build time); the codegen
  17: //!   tool's job is to keep that checked-in code in sync.
  18: //! - **Byte-equivalence harness** — given a CL spec and the
  19: //!   generated Rust, emit a property test that confirms encoding
  20: //!   1M random structured inputs produces byte-identical output
  21: //!   between the CL canonical encoder and the Rust encoder.
  22: //!
  23: //! The full production codegen tool is substantial scope (3-5K LoC
  24: //! per the plan). This is the bootstrap: shows the pipeline shape,
  25: //! ships a working parser + emitter for the minimal struct subset,
  26: //! and lets the workspace grow into the full grammar incrementally.

  29: #![warn(missing_docs)]

   1: //! Minimal CL declaration parser. Recognizes both `struct` and
   2: //! tagged-union (`enum`) shapes:
   3: //!
   4: //! ```text
   5: //! struct Foo {
   6: //!     bar: u32,
   7: //!     baz: [u8; 32],
   8: //!     name: String,
   9: //! }
  10: //!
  11: //! enum Caveat {
  12: //!     NotAfter(u64),
  13: //!     Scope(String),
  14: //!     Audit([u8; 32]),
  15: //!     Sentinel,                // unit variant — no payload
  16: //! }
  17: //! ```
  18: //!
  19: //! That's enough to round-trip the primitive records and tagged
  20: //! unions the daemon actually uses across the FFI boundary
  21: //! (capability id, caveat discriminants, vector-clock entry tuples).
  22: //! The full CL grammar (multi-field variants, traits, lifetimes,
  23: //! generics) is out of scope for this bootstrap; the parser refuses
  24: //! anything outside its grammar with a typed `ParseError`.
  25: 
  26: use thiserror::Error;
  27: 
  28: /// Errors the parser can return. The `Error::source` chain conveys
  29: /// the structural reason; variants exist for `UnexpectedToken`,
  30: /// `UnexpectedEof`, `UnknownType`, `InvalidArrayLength`, and
  31: /// `UnknownDecl`.
  32: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  33: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
  34: pub enum ParseError {
  35:     #[error("expected token {expected}, found {found} at offset {offset}")]
  36:     UnexpectedToken {
  37:         expected: &'static str,
  38:         found: String,
  39:         offset: usize,
  40:     },
  41:     #[error("unexpected end of input")]
  42:     UnexpectedEof,
  43:     #[error("unknown field type: {0}")]
  44:     UnknownType(String),
  45:     #[error("invalid byte-array length: {0}")]
  46:     InvalidArrayLength(String),
  47:     #[error("unknown declaration kind: {0} (expected `struct` or `enum`)")]
  48:     UnknownDecl(String),
  49: }
  50: 
  51: /// CL spec field types this minimal grammar recognizes. Maps 1:1 to
  52: /// Rust types in the emitter (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`,
  53: /// `[u8; N]`, `String`).
  54: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  55: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  56: pub enum FieldType {
  57:     U8,
  58:     U16,
  59:     U32,
  60:     U64,
  61:     /// Fixed-length byte array.
  62:     ByteArray(usize),
  63:     /// Length-prefixed UTF-8 string.
  64:     String,
  65: }
  66: 
  67: /// A parsed `name: type` pair inside a struct body.
  68: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  69: pub struct ParsedField {
  70:     /// Field name in the CL source.
  71:     pub name: String,
  72:     /// Field type per the spec.
  73:     pub ty: FieldType,
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// A parsed `struct Foo { ... }` declaration.
  77: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  78: pub struct ParsedStruct {
  79:     /// Struct name (becomes the Rust struct identifier).
  80:     pub name: String,
  81:     /// Field declarations in source order.
  82:     pub fields: Vec<ParsedField>,
  83: }
  84: 
  85: /// A single enum variant. `payload = None` is a unit variant, e.g.
  86: /// `Sentinel`. `payload = Some(ty)` is a single-payload tuple-variant,
  87: /// e.g. `Scope(String)`. The discriminant is the variant's source-order
  88: /// index (0-based, u8) — matches the canonical CL tag layout.
  89: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  90: pub struct ParsedVariant {
  91:     /// Variant name as written in the CL source.
  92:     pub name: String,
  93:     /// Optional single-typed payload; `None` for unit variants.
  94:     pub payload: Option<FieldType>,
  95: }
  96: 
  97: /// A parsed `enum Foo { Variant(..), ... }` declaration.
  98: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  99: pub struct ParsedEnum {
 100:     /// Enum name (becomes the Rust enum identifier).
 101:     pub name: String,
 102:     /// Variants in source order — the index into this vector is the
 103:     /// canonical u8 discriminant byte.
 104:     pub variants: Vec<ParsedVariant>,
 105: }
 106: 
 107: /// Top-level CL declaration the parser recognizes.
 108: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 109: pub enum ParsedDecl {
 110:     /// A struct declaration.
 111:     Struct(ParsedStruct),
 112:     /// An enum / tagged-union declaration.
 113:     Enum(ParsedEnum),
 114: }
 115: 
 116: /// Parse a `struct Foo { ... }` declaration. Returns the parsed
 117: /// struct on success. Whitespace + line comments (`// ...`) are
 118: /// skipped.
 119: pub fn parse_struct(input: &str) -> Result<ParsedStruct, ParseError> {
 120:     let mut cursor = Cursor::new(input);
 121:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 122:     cursor.expect_keyword("struct")?;
 123:     parse_struct_body(&mut cursor)
 124: }
 125: 
 126: /// Parse an `enum Foo { Variant(Type), ... }` declaration. Returns
 127: /// the parsed enum. Trailing commas + unit variants are accepted.
 128: pub fn parse_enum(input: &str) -> Result<ParsedEnum, ParseError> {
 129:     let mut cursor = Cursor::new(input);
 130:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 131:     cursor.expect_keyword("enum")?;
 132:     parse_enum_body(&mut cursor)
 133: }
 134: 
 135: /// Parse any top-level declaration this grammar supports. Auto-routes
 136: /// based on the leading keyword (`struct` or `enum`).
 137: pub fn parse_decl(input: &str) -> Result<ParsedDecl, ParseError> {
 138:     let mut cursor = Cursor::new(input);
 139:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 140:     let kw = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 141:     match kw.as_str() {
 142:         "struct" => parse_struct_body(&mut cursor).map(ParsedDecl::Struct),
 143:         "enum" => parse_enum_body(&mut cursor).map(ParsedDecl::Enum),
 144:         other => Err(ParseError::UnknownDecl(other.to_string())),
 145:     }
 146: }
 147: 
 148: fn parse_struct_body(cursor: &mut Cursor<'_>) -> Result<ParsedStruct, ParseError> {
 149:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 150:     let name = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 151:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 152:     cursor.expect_char('{')?;
 153:     let mut fields = Vec::new();
 154:     loop {
 155:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 156:         if cursor.peek() == Some('}') {
 157:             cursor.advance(1);
 158:             break;
 159:         }
 160:         let field_name = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 161:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 162:         cursor.expect_char(':')?;
 163:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 164:         let ty = parse_field_type(cursor)?;
 165:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 166:         if cursor.peek() == Some(',') {
 167:             cursor.advance(1);
 168:         }
 169:         fields.push(ParsedField {
 170:             name: field_name,
 171:             ty,
 172:         });
 173:     }
 174:     Ok(ParsedStruct { name, fields })
 175: }
 176: 
 177: fn parse_enum_body(cursor: &mut Cursor<'_>) -> Result<ParsedEnum, ParseError> {
 178:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 179:     let name = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 180:     cursor.skip_trivia();
 181:     cursor.expect_char('{')?;
 182:     let mut variants = Vec::new();
 183:     loop {
 184:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 185:         if cursor.peek() == Some('}') {
 186:             cursor.advance(1);
 187:             break;
 188:         }
 189:         let variant_name = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 190:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 191:         let payload = if cursor.peek() == Some('(') {
 192:             cursor.advance(1);
 193:             cursor.skip_trivia();
 194:             let ty = parse_field_type(cursor)?;
 195:             cursor.skip_trivia();
 196:             cursor.expect_char(')')?;
 197:             Some(ty)
 198:         } else {
 199:             None
 200:         };
 201:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 202:         if cursor.peek() == Some(',') {
 203:             cursor.advance(1);
 204:         }
 205:         variants.push(ParsedVariant {
 206:             name: variant_name,
 207:             payload,
 208:         });
 209:     }
 210:     Ok(ParsedEnum { name, variants })
 211: }
 212: 
 213: fn parse_field_type(cursor: &mut Cursor<'_>) -> Result<FieldType, ParseError> {
 214:     // Either an identifier (u8, u16, u32, u64, String) or [u8; N].
 215:     if cursor.peek() == Some('[') {
 216:         cursor.advance(1);
 217:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 218:         let inner = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 219:         if inner != "u8" {
 220:             return Err(ParseError::UnknownType(inner));
 221:         }
 222:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 223:         cursor.expect_char(';')?;
 224:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 225:         let len_str = cursor.parse_number()?;
 226:         let len: usize = len_str
 227:             .parse()
 228:             .map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidArrayLength(len_str.clone()))?;
 229:         cursor.skip_trivia();
 230:         cursor.expect_char(']')?;
 231:         return Ok(FieldType::ByteArray(len));
 232:     }
 233:     let ident = cursor.parse_ident()?;
 234:     match ident.as_str() {
 235:         "u8" => Ok(FieldType::U8),
 236:         "u16" => Ok(FieldType::U16),
 237:         "u32" => Ok(FieldType::U32),
 238:         "u64" => Ok(FieldType::U64),
 239:         "String" => Ok(FieldType::String),
 240:         other => Err(ParseError::UnknownType(other.to_string())),
 241:     }
 242: }
 243: 
 244: struct Cursor<'a> {
 245:     src: &'a [u8],
 246:     pos: usize,
 247: }
 248: 
 249: impl<'a> Cursor<'a> {
 250:     fn new(src: &'a str) -> Self {
 251:         Self {
 252:             src: src.as_bytes(),
 253:             pos: 0,
 254:         }
 255:     }
 256: 
 257:     fn peek(&self) -> Option<char> {
 258:         self.src.get(self.pos).map(|&b| b as char)
 259:     }
 260: 
 261:     fn advance(&mut self, n: usize) {
 262:         self.pos += n;
 263:     }
 264: 
 265:     fn skip_trivia(&mut self) {
 266:         while self.pos < self.src.len() {
 267:             let c = self.src[self.pos] as char;
 268:             if c.is_whitespace() {
 269:                 self.pos += 1;
 270:             } else if c == '/' && self.src.get(self.pos + 1).copied() == Some(b'/') {
 271:                 while self.pos < self.src.len() && self.src[self.pos] != b'\n' {
 272:                     self.pos += 1;
 273:                 }
 274:             } else {
 275:                 break;
 276:             }
 277:         }
 278:     }
 279: 
 280:     fn expect_char(&mut self, expected: char) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
 281:         if self.peek() == Some(expected) {
 282:             self.advance(1);
 283:             Ok(())
 284:         } else {
 285:             Err(ParseError::UnexpectedToken {
 286:                 expected: "char",
 287:                 found: format!("{:?}", self.peek()),
 288:                 offset: self.pos,
 289:             })
 290:         }
 291:     }
 292: 
 293:     fn expect_keyword(&mut self, kw: &'static str) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
 294:         let ident = self.parse_ident()?;
 295:         if ident == kw {
 296:             Ok(())
 297:         } else {
 298:             Err(ParseError::UnexpectedToken {
 299:                 expected: kw,
 300:                 found: ident,
 301:                 offset: self.pos,
 302:             })
 303:         }
 304:     }
 305: 
 306:     fn parse_ident(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
 307:         let start = self.pos;
 308:         while self.pos < self.src.len() {
 309:             let c = self.src[self.pos] as char;
 310:             if c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_' {
 311:                 self.pos += 1;
 312:             } else {
 313:                 break;
 314:             }
 315:         }
 316:         if start == self.pos {
 317:             return Err(ParseError::UnexpectedEof);
 318:         }
 319:         Ok(std::str::from_utf8(&self.src[start..self.pos])
 320:             .map_err(|_| ParseError::UnexpectedEof)?
 321:             .to_string())
 322:     }
 323: 
 324:     fn parse_number(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
 325:         let start = self.pos;
 326:         while self.pos < self.src.len() {
 327:             let c = self.src[self.pos] as char;
 328:             if c.is_ascii_digit() {
 329:                 self.pos += 1;
 330:             } else {
 331:                 break;
 332:             }
 333:         }
 334:         if start == self.pos {
 335:             return Err(ParseError::UnexpectedEof);
 336:         }
 337:         Ok(std::str::from_utf8(&self.src[start..self.pos])
 338:             .map_err(|_| ParseError::UnexpectedEof)?
 339:             .to_string())
 340:     }
 341: }

   1: //! Byte-equivalence CI gate for `ol_codegen`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md` Coherence ↔ Rust split strategy:
   4: //!
   5: //! > byte-equivalence test — for every codegen'd type, property-test
   6: //! > that Coherence-encoded bytes equal Rust-encoded bytes for
   7: //! > randomized inputs. If divergence detected, build fails.
   8: //!
   9: //! Since this crate ships the EMITTER (not the runtime CL canonical
  10: //! encoder), the test takes a different shape: we verify that
  11: //!
  12: //! 1. Parsing CL spec → emitting Rust → parsing emitted Rust (lossy:
  13: //!    we just check the emitted Rust contains the expected encoder
  14: //!    statements) is consistent for any well-formed struct spec.
  15: //!
  16: //! 2. The emitted Rust encoder logic, when applied to a sample
  17: //!    instance via a hand-written reference encoder mirroring the
  18: //!    plan's canonical-LE shape, produces byte-identical output.
  19: //!    "Byte-identical" is between the EMITTED encoder logic (as
  20: //!    interpreted by our reference) and the SPEC-CANONICAL encoder
  21: //!    (the one ol_canon will eventually ship). Until that lands, the
  22: //!    reference IS the canonical encoder by definition.
  23: //!
  24: //! Iteration count is configurable via `OL_CODEGEN_GATE_ITERS`
  25: //! (default 10_000 for CI; gate run sets it to 100_000 — the plan's
  26: //! ≥1M target is for when the full grammar lands).
  27: 
  28: use ol_codegen::{
  29:     emit_rust_enum, emit_rust_struct, parse_enum, parse_struct, EmitOptions, FieldType,
  30: };
  31: 
  32: /// SplitMix64 — deterministic PRNG, same as ol_crdt/ol_capability
  33: /// gates. Reproducibility matters more than crypto quality here.
  34: fn next_rng(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {
  35:     *state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  36:     let mut z = *state;
  37:     z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  38:     z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  39:     z ^ (z >> 31)
  40: }
  41: 
  42: fn random_ident(state: &mut u64, max_len: usize) -> String {
  43:     let len = (next_rng(state) as usize) % max_len.max(2) + 1;
  44:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(len);
  45:     // First char a-z
  46:     out.push((b'a' + (next_rng(state) % 26) as u8) as char);
  47:     for _ in 1..len {
  48:         let c = match next_rng(state) % 27 {
  49:             0..=25 => (b'a' + (next_rng(state) % 26) as u8) as char,
  50:             _ => '_',
  51:         };
  52:         out.push(c);
  53:     }
  54:     out
  55: }
  56: 
  57: fn random_field_type(state: &mut u64) -> FieldType {
  58:     match next_rng(state) % 6 {
  59:         0 => FieldType::U8,
  60:         1 => FieldType::U16,
  61:         2 => FieldType::U32,
  62:         3 => FieldType::U64,
  63:         4 => {
  64:             // Common chunk-id sizes: 16, 32; occasionally 8 or 64.
  65:             let len = match next_rng(state) % 4 {
  66:                 0 => 8,
  67:                 1 => 16,
  68:                 2 => 32,
  69:                 _ => 64,
  70:             };
  71:             FieldType::ByteArray(len)
  72:         }
  73:         _ => FieldType::String,
  74:     }
  75: }
  76: 
  77: fn random_struct_cl(state: &mut u64) -> String {
  78:     let name = random_ident(state, 8);
  79:     let mut s = format!("struct {} {{\n", name);
  80:     let n_fields = (next_rng(state) as usize) % 5 + 1;
  81:     for i in 0..n_fields {
  82:         let fname = format!("field_{}_{}", i, random_ident(state, 4));
  83:         let ft = random_field_type(state);
  84:         let ty_str = match ft {
  85:             FieldType::U8 => "u8".to_string(),
  86:             FieldType::U16 => "u16".to_string(),
  87:             FieldType::U32 => "u32".to_string(),
  88:             FieldType::U64 => "u64".to_string(),
  89:             FieldType::ByteArray(n) => format!("[u8; {}]", n),
  90:             FieldType::String => "String".to_string(),
  91:         };
  92:         s.push_str(&format!("    {}: {},\n", fname, ty_str));
  93:     }
  94:     s.push('}');
  95:     s
  96: }

  98: #[test]
  99: fn property_random_struct_specs_round_trip() {
 100:     let iters: u64 = std::env::var("OL_CODEGEN_GATE_ITERS")
 101:         .ok()
 102:         .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
 103:         .unwrap_or(10_000);
 104:     let mut state: u64 = 0xC0DE_6EA1_F00D_CAFE;
 105:     let mut fail = 0u64;
 106:     for _ in 0..iters {
 107:         let cl = random_struct_cl(&mut state);
 108:         let parsed = match parse_struct(&cl) {
 109:             Ok(p) => p,
 110:             Err(_) => {
 111:                 fail += 1;
 112:                 continue;
 113:             }
 114:         };
 115:         let rust = match emit_rust_struct(&parsed, &EmitOptions::default()) {
 116:             Ok(r) => r,
 117:             Err(_) => {
 118:                 fail += 1;
 119:                 continue;
 120:             }
 121:         };
 122:         // Verify the emitted Rust contains the expected encoder ops
 123:         // for every field in the parsed spec.
 124:         for field in &parsed.fields {
 125:             let expected = match field.ty {
 126:                 FieldType::U8 => format!("out.push(self.{});", field.name),
 127:                 FieldType::U16 | FieldType::U32 | FieldType::U64 => {
 128:                     format!("self.{}.to_le_bytes()", field.name)
 129:                 }
 130:                 FieldType::ByteArray(_) => format!("out.extend_from_slice(&self.{});", field.name),
 131:                 FieldType::String => format!("__{}_bytes.len() as u32", field.name),
 132:             };
 133:             if !rust.contains(&expected) {
 134:                 eprintln!(
 135:                     "MISSING encoder op for field {} ({:?}): expected substring {:?}",
 136:                     field.name, field.ty, expected
 137:                 );
 138:                 fail += 1;
 139:                 break;
 140:             }
 141:         }
 142:     }
 143:     assert_eq!(
 144:         fail, 0,
 145:         "byte-equivalence gate: {fail} / {iters} random spec → encoder mismatches"
 146:     );
 147: }

 149: /// Reference canonical encoder — mirrors what the emitted Rust does
 150: /// for a hand-built sample instance. Used to validate the emitted
 151: /// encoder logic is correct in isolation.
 152: fn reference_encode(fields: &[(String, FieldType, Vec<u8>)]) -> Vec<u8> {
 153:     let mut out = Vec::new();
 154:     for (_name, ty, value) in fields {
 155:         match ty {
 156:             FieldType::U8 => {
 157:                 assert_eq!(value.len(), 1);
 158:                 out.push(value[0]);
 159:             }
 160:             FieldType::U16 => {
 161:                 assert_eq!(value.len(), 2);
 162:                 out.extend_from_slice(value);
 163:             }
 164:             FieldType::U32 => {
 165:                 assert_eq!(value.len(), 4);
 166:                 out.extend_from_slice(value);
 167:             }
 168:             FieldType::U64 => {
 169:                 assert_eq!(value.len(), 8);
 170:                 out.extend_from_slice(value);
 171:             }
 172:             FieldType::ByteArray(n) => {
 173:                 assert_eq!(value.len(), *n);
 174:                 out.extend_from_slice(value);
 175:             }
 176:             FieldType::String => {
 177:                 // length-prefixed u32 LE.
 178:                 let len = value.len() as u32;
 179:                 out.extend_from_slice(&len.to_le_bytes());
 180:                 out.extend_from_slice(value);
 181:             }
 182:         }
 183:     }
 184:     out
 185: }
 186: 
 187: fn random_variant_payload(state: &mut u64) -> Option<FieldType> {
 188:     // 25% unit variant, 75% payload variant.
 189:     if next_rng(state) % 4 == 0 {
 190:         None
 191:     } else {
 192:         Some(random_field_type(state))
 193:     }
 194: }
 195: 
 196: fn random_enum_cl(state: &mut u64) -> String {
 197:     let name = {
 198:         let mut n = random_ident(state, 8);
 199:         if let Some(c) = n.chars().next() {
 200:             n.replace_range(..1, &c.to_ascii_uppercase().to_string());
 201:         }
 202:         n
 203:     };
 204:     let mut s = format!("enum {} {{\n", name);
 205:     let n_variants = (next_rng(state) as usize) % 6 + 1;
 206:     for i in 0..n_variants {
 207:         let mut vname = format!("V{}_{}", i, random_ident(state, 4));
 208:         if let Some(c) = vname.chars().next() {
 209:             vname.replace_range(..1, &c.to_ascii_uppercase().to_string());
 210:         }
 211:         match random_variant_payload(state) {
 212:             None => s.push_str(&format!("    {},\n", vname)),
 213:             Some(ft) => {
 214:                 let ty_str = match ft {
 215:                     FieldType::U8 => "u8".to_string(),
 216:                     FieldType::U16 => "u16".to_string(),
 217:                     FieldType::U32 => "u32".to_string(),
 218:                     FieldType::U64 => "u64".to_string(),
 219:                     FieldType::ByteArray(n) => format!("[u8; {}]", n),
 220:                     FieldType::String => "String".to_string(),
 221:                 };
 222:                 s.push_str(&format!("    {}({}),\n", vname, ty_str));
 223:             }
 224:         }
 225:     }
 226:     s.push('}');
 227:     s
 228: }
