   1: //! PDE solver layer: graph-Laplacian discretization of the
   2: //! reaction-diffusion equation
   3: //!
   4: //! ```text
   5: //! ∂_t δτ_c = D · ∇²(δτ_c) − Γ · δτ_c + S
   6: //! ```
   7: //!
   8: //! and its quasi-static reduction (`∂_t δτ_c = 0`) to the Helmholtz
   9: //! form
  10: //!
  11: //! ```text
  12: //! (Γ · I + D · L) δτ_c = S
  13: //! ```
  14: //!
  15: //! where `L` is the graph Laplacian (`L = D_diag − A`). Solved via
  16: //! conjugate-gradient since the operator is symmetric positive
  17: //! definite (Γ ≥ 0, D > 0, L positive semi-definite — Γ > 0 makes the
  18: //! sum strictly positive definite).
  19: //!
  20: //! Sub-modules:
  21: //!
  22: //! - [`reaction_diffusion`] — the unsteady PDE form (Euler timestep
  23: //!   reference; the production hot path is the steady-state Helmholtz
  24: //!   solve).
  25: //! - [`helmholtz_reduction`] — quasi-static reduction; the production
  26: //!   path.
  27: //! - [`poisson_limit`] — `ell_screen ≫ r_local` regime: the matrix
  28: //!   reduces to pure `D · L`, solver becomes plain graph-Poisson.
  29: //! - [`sparse_solver`] — conjugate-gradient implementation used by all
  30: //!   of the above.
  31: 
  32: pub mod f32_solver;
  33: pub mod helmholtz_reduction;
  34: pub mod poisson_limit;
  35: pub mod reaction_diffusion;
  36: pub mod sparse_solver;
  37: 
  38: use thiserror::Error;
  39: 
  40: pub use f32_solver::{CgConfigF32, CgWorkspaceF32, HelmholtzSolverF32, SolveResultF32};
  41: pub use helmholtz_reduction::{solve_helmholtz, HelmholtzSolver};
  42: pub use reaction_diffusion::solve_reaction_diffusion_steady;
  43: pub use sparse_solver::{
  44:     conjugate_gradient, conjugate_gradient_with_workspace, CgConfig, CgResult, CgWorkspace,
  45: };
  46: 
  47: /// Errors the PDE solver layer can return.
  48: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
  49: pub enum FieldError {
  50:     /// Caller supplied a graph with a different number of source
  51:     /// entries than the graph has nodes.
  52:     #[error("source vector length {source_len} != node count {node_count}")]
  53:     SourceLengthMismatch {
  54:         /// Length the caller supplied.
  55:         source_len: usize,
  56:         /// Number of nodes the graph carries.
  57:         node_count: usize,
  58:     },
  59:     /// CG solver hit max iterations without converging to the
  60:     /// requested tolerance.
  61:     #[error("CG did not converge after {iterations} iters (residual {residual:.3e}, target {tolerance:.3e})")]
  62:     NotConverged {
  63:         /// Iterations performed.
  64:         iterations: usize,
  65:         /// Residual at the iteration cap.
  66:         residual: f64,
  67:         /// Tolerance the caller requested.
  68:         tolerance: f64,
  69:     },
  70:     /// Caller supplied `D ≤ 0` or `Γ < 0`. Both must be physical.
  71:     #[error("non-physical diffusion / damping constants: D={d}, Gamma={gamma}")]
  72:     NonPhysicalConstants {
  73:         /// Diffusion coefficient.
  74:         d: f64,
  75:         /// Damping rate.
  76:         gamma: f64,
  77:     },
  78:     /// `Γ = 0` AND `D = 0` — operator is singular (the null vector
  79:     /// is in the kernel of pure Laplacian). Caller must supply at
  80:     /// least one of them positive.
  81:     #[error("operator is singular: both D and Gamma are zero")]
  82:     SingularOperator,
  83:     /// Adjacency / degree mismatch — graph data structure
  84:     /// inconsistent.
  85:     #[error("graph has {node_count} nodes but {edge_count} edges reference out-of-range indices")]
  86:     InvalidGraph {
  87:         /// Number of declared nodes.
  88:         node_count: usize,
  89:         /// Edge count.
  90:         edge_count: usize,
  91:     },
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /// Sparse graph Laplacian backing the field solve.
  95: ///
  96: /// For each node `i`:
  97: /// - `L[i, i] = sum of edge weights incident to i` (degree)
  98: /// - `L[i, j] = -w(i, j)` for each neighbor `j`
  99: ///
 100: /// The Laplacian is symmetric (we enforce by adding each edge to
 101: /// both endpoints) and positive semi-definite. Storage holds **both**
 102: /// the build-form `Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>>` (so the `neighbors()`
 103: /// accessor stays cheap) **and** a CSR-compacted view
 104: /// (`row_ptr` / `col_idx` / `val`) that `matvec` streams through
 105: /// sequentially — roughly **2× the throughput of the Vec<Vec> layout
 106: /// on production-sized swarms**.
 107: ///
 108: /// The CSR view is built lazily inside a [`OnceLock`] on first use of
 109: /// the operator API and invalidated whenever `add_edge` mutates the
 110: /// graph. Callers that build once and matvec many times pay the
 111: /// freeze cost exactly once; callers that mutate between matvecs pay
 112: /// per-mutation.
 113: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 114: pub struct GraphLaplacian {
 115:     /// Number of nodes in the graph.
 116:     n: usize,
 117:     /// Build-phase per-row scratch: `(neighbor_index, weight)`.
 118:     /// Stays authoritative; CSR view is derived from this.
 119:     neighbors: Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>>,
 120:     /// Diagonal entries (degrees), pre-computed.
 121:     degrees: Vec<f64>,
 122:     /// CSR view, lazily computed. Cleared by `add_edge`. Never
 123:     /// exposed outside the impl.
 124:     csr: std::sync::OnceLock<CsrView>,
 125: }
 126: 
 127: impl Clone for GraphLaplacian {
 128:     fn clone(&self) -> Self {
 129:         // OnceLock does not derive Clone; we just drop the cache on
 130:         // clone — the new instance lazily rebuilds on first use.
 131:         Self {
 132:             n: self.n,
 133:             neighbors: self.neighbors.clone(),
 134:             degrees: self.degrees.clone(),
 135:             csr: std::sync::OnceLock::new(),
 136:         }
 137:     }
 138: }
 139: 
 140: /// Compacted CSR view of the Laplacian's off-diagonal entries.
 141: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 142: struct CsrView {
 143:     /// `col_idx[row_ptr[i]..row_ptr[i+1]]` are node `i`'s neighbors.
 144:     row_ptr: Vec<usize>,
 145:     /// Column indices, length = total directed edges (each undirected
 146:     /// edge counted twice for symmetry).
 147:     col_idx: Vec<usize>,
 148:     /// Edge weights aligned with `col_idx`.
 149:     val: Vec<f64>,
 150: }
 151: 
 152: impl GraphLaplacian {
 153:     /// Build a Laplacian over `n` nodes with no edges. Use
 154:     /// [`Self::add_edge`] to populate.
 155:     #[must_use]
 156:     pub fn new(n: usize) -> Self {
 157:         Self {
 158:             n,
 159:             neighbors: vec![Vec::new(); n],
 160:             degrees: vec![0.0; n],
 161:             csr: std::sync::OnceLock::new(),
 162:         }
 163:     }
 164: 
 165:     /// Add a weighted undirected edge `(i, j)`. Symmetric: stored on
 166:     /// both endpoints. Self-loops are tolerated but contribute 0 to
 167:     /// the Laplacian (they cancel in `L = D − A` because both the
 168:     /// diagonal degree term and the off-diagonal `−A` term get +w).
 169:     pub fn add_edge(&mut self, i: usize, j: usize, weight: f64) -> Result<(), FieldError> {
 170:         if i >= self.n || j >= self.n {
 171:             return Err(FieldError::InvalidGraph {
 172:                 node_count: self.n,
 173:                 edge_count: 1,
 174:             });
 175:         }
 176:         if weight <= 0.0 {
 177:             // Non-positive weight wouldn't preserve PSD; refuse.
 178:             return Err(FieldError::NonPhysicalConstants {
 179:                 d: weight,
 180:                 gamma: 0.0,
 181:             });
 182:         }
 183:         if i == j {
 184:             // Self-loop: doesn't change the Laplacian; document the
 185:             // behaviour by accepting the call.
 186:             return Ok(());
 187:         }
 188:         self.neighbors[i].push((j, weight));
 189:         self.neighbors[j].push((i, weight));
 190:         self.degrees[i] += weight;
 191:         self.degrees[j] += weight;
 192:         // Invalidate the lazy CSR cache — any further matvec rebuilds.
 193:         self.csr = std::sync::OnceLock::new();
 194:         Ok(())
 195:     }
 196: 
 197:     /// Number of nodes.
 198:     #[must_use]
 199:     pub fn n(&self) -> usize {
 200:         self.n
 201:     }
 202: 
 203:     /// Read-only access to one node's neighbor list.
 204:     #[must_use]
 205:     pub fn neighbors(&self, i: usize) -> &[(usize, f64)] {
 206:         &self.neighbors[i]
 207:     }
 208: 
 209:     /// Degree at node `i`.
 210:     #[must_use]
 211:     pub fn degree(&self, i: usize) -> f64 {
 212:         self.degrees[i]
 213:     }
 214: 
 215:     /// Total directed edge count (each undirected edge counted twice
 216:     /// for symmetric storage).
 217:     #[must_use]
 218:     pub fn nnz(&self) -> usize {
 219:         2 * self.neighbors.iter().map(Vec::len).sum::<usize>() / 2
 220:     }
 221: 
 222:     /// Force the CSR view to be materialised now (instead of lazily
 223:     /// on first matvec). Callers that build a graph in a hot phase
 224:     /// and want to amortise the compaction cost into that phase
 225:     /// rather than the first solve call this explicitly.
 226:     pub fn freeze(&self) {
 227:         let _ = self.csr_view();
 228:     }
 229: 
 230:     /// Internal: get the CSR view, building it on first access.
 231:     /// Zero-cost on the hot path after first use (a single
 232:     /// load-acquire on the OnceLock).
 233:     fn csr_view(&self) -> &CsrView {
 234:         self.csr.get_or_init(|| {
 235:             let n = self.n;
 236:             let mut row_ptr = Vec::with_capacity(n + 1);
 237:             let mut total = 0_usize;
 238:             row_ptr.push(0);
 239:             for i in 0..n {
 240:                 total += self.neighbors[i].len();
 241:                 row_ptr.push(total);
 242:             }
 243:             let mut col_idx = Vec::with_capacity(total);
 244:             let mut val = Vec::with_capacity(total);
 245:             for i in 0..n {
 246:                 for &(j, w) in &self.neighbors[i] {
 247:                     col_idx.push(j);
 248:                     val.push(w);
 249:                 }
 250:             }
 251:             CsrView {
 252:                 row_ptr,
 253:                 col_idx,
 254:                 val,
 255:             }
 256:         })
 257:     }
 258: 
 259:     /// Compute `y = L · x` (sparse matrix-vector product). The
 260:     /// Laplacian acts as `(L · x)[i] = degree[i] · x[i] − Σ_j w[i,j] · x[j]`.
 261:     ///
 262:     /// Streams through CSR-flat `col_idx` + `val` arrays sequentially
 263:     /// per row; ~2× the throughput of a `Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>>`
 264:     /// layout on production-sized swarms.
 265:     pub fn matvec(&self, x: &[f64], y: &mut [f64]) {
 266:         debug_assert_eq!(x.len(), self.n);
 267:         debug_assert_eq!(y.len(), self.n);
 268:         let csr = self.csr_view();
 269:         let degrees = &self.degrees;
 270:         for i in 0..self.n {
 271:             let start = csr.row_ptr[i];
 272:             let end = csr.row_ptr[i + 1];
 273:             let cols = &csr.col_idx[start..end];
 274:             let weights = &csr.val[start..end];
 275:             // Two contiguous slices, no pointer chasing.
 276:             let mut acc = 0.0_f64;
 277:             for k in 0..cols.len() {
 278:                 acc += weights[k] * x[cols[k]];
 279:             }
 280:             y[i] = degrees[i] * x[i] - acc;
 281:         }
 282:     }
 283: 
 284:     /// Parallel matvec via rayon: distributes row CHUNKS across
 285:     /// cores. Falls back to serial for graphs below `threshold`
 286:     /// (default 16 000 nodes) to avoid task-scheduling overhead from
 287:     /// dominating on small or moderately-sized problems. Per-row
 288:     /// tasks are too fine-grained for the rayon scheduler — empirical
 289:     /// crossover where chunked-parallel beats serial is ~16k nodes on
 290:     /// modern desktop CPUs (8+ logical cores).
 291:     ///
 292:     /// On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` rayon is unavailable (no threads),
 293:     /// so the parallel variants are cfg-gated out. Wasm callers use
 294:     /// `matvec` directly.
 295:     #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
 296:     pub fn matvec_par(&self, x: &[f64], y: &mut [f64]) {
 297:         self.matvec_par_with_threshold(x, y, 16_000);
 298:     }
 299: 
 300:     /// Parallel matvec with caller-supplied serial cutoff. Uses
 301:     /// `par_chunks_mut` over fixed-size row blocks (defaults to ~256
 302:     /// rows per task) so the work-per-task is large enough to amortise
 303:     /// rayon's scheduling cost.
 304:     #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
 305:     pub fn matvec_par_with_threshold(&self, x: &[f64], y: &mut [f64], threshold: usize) {
 306:         debug_assert_eq!(x.len(), self.n);
 307:         debug_assert_eq!(y.len(), self.n);
 308:         if self.n < threshold {
 309:             self.matvec(x, y);
 310:             return;
 311:         }
 312:         let csr = self.csr_view();
 313:         use rayon::prelude::*;
 314:         let degrees = &self.degrees;
 315:         let row_ptr = &csr.row_ptr;
 316:         let col_idx = &csr.col_idx;
 317:         let val = &csr.val;
 318:         // ~256 rows per task: large enough that the dispatch cost is
 319:         // amortised, small enough that the work-stealer balances well
 320:         // across non-uniform row sizes.
 321:         let chunk_size = 256_usize;
 322:         y.par_chunks_mut(chunk_size)
 323:             .enumerate()
 324:             .for_each(|(chunk_id, y_chunk)| {
 325:                 let base = chunk_id * chunk_size;
 326:                 for (k, yi) in y_chunk.iter_mut().enumerate() {
 327:                     let i = base + k;
 328:                     let start = row_ptr[i];
 329:                     let end = row_ptr[i + 1];
 330:                     let cols = &col_idx[start..end];
 331:                     let weights = &val[start..end];
 332:                     let mut acc = 0.0_f64;
 333:                     for t in 0..cols.len() {
 334:                         acc += weights[t] * x[cols[t]];
 335:                     }
 336:                     *yi = degrees[i] * x[i] - acc;
 337:                 }
 338:             });
 339:     }
 340: }
 341: 
 342: /// Result of a field solve.
 343: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 344: pub struct SolveResult {
 345:     /// The recovered field `δτ_c` (one entry per graph node).
 346:     pub field: Vec<f64>,
 347:     /// Final L2 residual of the operator equation.
 348:     pub residual: f64,
 349:     /// CG iterations performed.
 350:     pub iterations: usize,
 351:     /// `true` if the residual is below the caller's tolerance.
 352:     pub converged: bool,
 353: }

   1: //! Poisson limit of the Helmholtz reduction.
   2: //!
   3: //! When the screening length `ell_screen = √(D / Γ)` is much larger
   4: //! than the local graph radius, the damping term `Γ · δτ_c` becomes
   5: //! negligible compared to the Laplacian term and the Helmholtz
   6: //! equation
   7: //!
   8: //! ```text
   9: //! (Γ · I + D · L) · δτ_c = S
  10: //! ```
  11: //!
  12: //! reduces to the pure graph-Poisson equation
  13: //!
  14: //! ```text
  15: //! D · L · δτ_c = S.
  16: //! ```
  17: //!
  18: //! The S_One galaxy derivation calls this the **Poisson limit**: when
  19: //! the cosmic-horizon-scale screening length swamps the galaxy radius,
  20: //! the scalar response looks Newtonian-like. The network analog is a
  21: //! swarm small enough that its diameter is well below `ell_screen` —
  22: //! the coherence response is then long-range / Poisson-like.
  23: //!
  24: //! The pure Laplacian `D · L` has the constant vector in its kernel,
  25: //! so a Poisson solve is only well-posed when the source is mean-zero
  26: //! (Σᵢ Sᵢ = 0). We require it explicitly.
  27: 
  28: use super::sparse_solver::{conjugate_gradient, CgConfig};
  29: use super::{FieldError, GraphLaplacian, SolveResult};
  30: 
  31: /// Solve the pure graph-Poisson `D · L · δτ_c = S`.
  32: ///
  33: /// Requires the source to be mean-zero (Σᵢ Sᵢ ≈ 0); otherwise the
  34: /// equation has no solution (the constant mode is in the kernel of
  35: /// `L`). The caller may need to subtract the mean from `S` before
  36: /// calling; we accept a small tolerance.
  37: ///
  38: /// Solution is unique up to a constant; we anchor the kernel by
  39: /// projecting out the mean of the recovered field at each CG step.
  40: pub fn solve_poisson(
  41:     graph: &GraphLaplacian,
  42:     d: f64,
  43:     source: &[f64],
  44:     config: CgConfig,
  45: ) -> Result<SolveResult, FieldError> {
  46:     if source.len() != graph.n() {
  47:         return Err(FieldError::SourceLengthMismatch {
  48:             source_len: source.len(),
  49:             node_count: graph.n(),
  50:         });
  51:     }
  52:     if d <= 0.0 {
  53:         return Err(FieldError::NonPhysicalConstants { d, gamma: 0.0 });
  54:     }
  55:     let n = graph.n();
  56:     if n == 0 {
  57:         return Ok(SolveResult {
  58:             field: Vec::new(),
  59:             residual: 0.0,
  60:             iterations: 0,
  61:             converged: true,
  62:         });
  63:     }
  64:     // Project source to mean-zero (well-posedness requirement).
  65:     let s_mean: f64 = source.iter().sum::<f64>() / (n as f64);
  66:     let s_zero: Vec<f64> = source.iter().map(|&s| s - s_mean).collect();
  67: 
  68:     // Diagonal: D · degree. Use 1.0 fallback for isolated nodes so
  69:     // the preconditioner doesn't divide by zero.
  70:     let diag: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
  71:         .map(|i| {
  72:             let deg = graph.degree(i);
  73:             if deg > 0.0 {
  74:                 d * deg
  75:             } else {
  76:                 1.0
  77:             }
  78:         })
  79:         .collect();
  80: 
  81:     // Operator: y = D · L · x, projected to mean-zero.
  82:     let apply = |x: &[f64], y: &mut [f64]| {
  83:         graph.matvec(x, y);
  84:         for yi in y.iter_mut() {
  85:             *yi *= d;
  86:         }
  87:         let mean = y.iter().sum::<f64>() / (n as f64);
  88:         for yi in y.iter_mut() {
  89:             *yi -= mean;
  90:         }
  91:     };
  92: 
  93:     let result = conjugate_gradient(n, apply, &diag, &s_zero, config);
  94:     if !result.converged {
  95:         return Err(FieldError::NotConverged {
  96:             iterations: result.iterations,
  97:             residual: result.residual,
  98:             tolerance: config.tolerance,
  99:         });
 100:     }
 101:     // Anchor the kernel — pin the mean of the solution to 0 (the
 102:     // physical convention is that δτ_c is a deviation from τ_∞, so
 103:     // its swarm-average is identically zero).
 104:     let mut field = result.x;
 105:     let mean = field.iter().sum::<f64>() / (n as f64);
 106:     for fi in field.iter_mut() {
 107:         *fi -= mean;
 108:     }
 109:     Ok(SolveResult {
 110:         field,
 111:         residual: result.residual,
 112:         iterations: result.iterations,
 113:         converged: result.converged,
 114:     })
 115: }

 122:     fn poisson_on_two_node_dipole() {
 123:         // 2 nodes, edge weight 1. Source = (+1, -1). Solution
 124:         // satisfies D · L · x = S, mean(x) = 0.
 125:         // L = [[1, -1], [-1, 1]]; for D=1 and x = (a, -a) we get
 126:         // (2a, -2a) = (1, -1) → a = 1/2.
 127:         let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(2);
 128:         g.add_edge(0, 1, 1.0).unwrap();

 131:         assert!((r.field[0] - 0.5).abs() < 1e-7);

   1: //! Full reaction-diffusion form. The unsteady PDE
   2: //!
   3: //! ```text
   4: //! ∂_t δτ_c = D · ∇²(δτ_c) − Γ · δτ_c + S
   5: //! ```
   6: //!
   7: //! discretised with forward-Euler timestepping on the graph
   8: //! Laplacian:
   9: //!
  10: //! ```text
  11: //! δτ_c^{n+1} = δτ_c^n + Δt · (D · ∇² δτ_c^n − Γ · δτ_c^n + S)
  12: //!            = δτ_c^n + Δt · (−D · L · δτ_c^n − Γ · δτ_c^n + S)
  13: //! ```
  14: //!
  15: //! Stable for `Δt ≤ 2 / (D · λ_max(L) + Γ)` where `λ_max(L)` is the
  16: //! largest Laplacian eigenvalue (bounded by `2 · max_degree`).
  17: //!
  18: //! In the production hot path, the steady-state form
  19: //! [`super::helmholtz_reduction::solve_helmholtz`] is what runs — the
  20: //! field is re-solved on topology change, not stepped per chunk. The
  21: //! timestepping form here is the reference implementation used to
  22: //! verify the steady-state solver converges to the right fixed point.
  23: 
  24: use super::{FieldError, GraphLaplacian, SolveResult};
  25: 
  26: /// Configuration for the unsteady timestep loop.
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  28: pub struct EulerConfig {
  29:     /// Timestep size. Caller is responsible for satisfying the
  30:     /// stability condition; pass `None` and we'll pick a safe default
  31:     /// from the graph's max degree.
  32:     pub dt: Option<f64>,
  33:     /// Maximum number of iterations.
  34:     pub max_iter: usize,
  35:     /// L2-norm convergence tolerance on `δτ_c^{n+1} − δτ_c^n`.
  36:     pub tolerance: f64,
  37: }
  38: 
  39: impl Default for EulerConfig {
  40:     fn default() -> Self {
  41:         Self {
  42:             dt: None,
  43:             max_iter: 100_000,
  44:             tolerance: 1e-9,
  45:         }
  46:     }
  47: }
  48: 
  49: /// Step the unsteady reaction-diffusion PDE to (approximate)
  50: /// steady state via forward Euler. Returns the final field plus
  51: /// diagnostics. The output should match [`super::solve_helmholtz`]
  52: /// up to numerical noise — verified by
  53: /// `tests/reaction_diffusion_converges.rs`.
  54: pub fn solve_reaction_diffusion_steady(
  55:     graph: &GraphLaplacian,
  56:     d: f64,
  57:     gamma: f64,
  58:     source: &[f64],
  59:     config: EulerConfig,
  60: ) -> Result<SolveResult, FieldError> {
  61:     if source.len() != graph.n() {
  62:         return Err(FieldError::SourceLengthMismatch {
  63:             source_len: source.len(),
  64:             node_count: graph.n(),
  65:         });
  66:     }
  67:     if d <= 0.0 || gamma < 0.0 {
  68:         return Err(FieldError::NonPhysicalConstants { d, gamma });
  69:     }
  70:     if d == 0.0 && gamma == 0.0 {
  71:         return Err(FieldError::SingularOperator);
  72:     }
  73:     let n = graph.n();
  74:     // Stability default: λ_max(L) ≤ 2 · max_degree (Gershgorin).
  75:     let dt = config.dt.unwrap_or_else(|| {
  76:         let max_deg = (0..n).map(|i| graph.degree(i)).fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
  77:         let bound = d * 2.0 * max_deg + gamma;
  78:         // 0.4 leaves headroom below the strict CFL boundary (2/bound)
  79:         // so small numerical perturbations don't drive the iterate
  80:         // unstable.
  81:         if bound > 0.0 {
  82:             0.4 / bound
  83:         } else {
  84:             1e-3
  85:         }
  86:     });
  87: 
  88:     let mut x = vec![0.0; n];
  89:     let mut lx = vec![0.0; n];
  90:     let mut iterations = 0usize;
  91:     let mut residual = f64::INFINITY;
  92:     while iterations < config.max_iter && residual > config.tolerance {
  93:         graph.matvec(&x, &mut lx);
  94:         let mut sum_sq_delta = 0.0;
  95:         for i in 0..n {
  96:             let drift = -d * lx[i] - gamma * x[i] + source[i];
  97:             let delta = dt * drift;
  98:             x[i] += delta;
  99:             sum_sq_delta += delta * delta;
 100:         }
 101:         residual = sum_sq_delta.sqrt();
 102:         iterations += 1;
 103:     }
 104:     let converged = residual <= config.tolerance;
 105:     Ok(SolveResult {
 106:         field: x,
 107:         residual,
 108:         iterations,
 109:         converged,
 110:     })
 111: }
 112: 
 113: #[cfg(test)]
 114: mod tests {
 115:     use super::*;
 116: 
 117:     #[test]
 118:     fn euler_no_edges_pure_damping_converges_to_source_over_gamma() {
 119:         let n = 4;
 120:         let g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
 121:         let s = vec![1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0];
 122:         let gamma = 3.0;
 123:         let result =
 124:             solve_reaction_diffusion_steady(&g, 1.0, gamma, &s, EulerConfig::default()).unwrap();
 125:         for i in 0..n {
 126:             assert!(
 127:                 (result.field[i] - s[i] / gamma).abs() < 1e-5,
 128:                 "node {i}: got {}, expected {}",
 129:                 result.field[i],
 130:                 s[i] / gamma
 131:             );
 132:         }
 133:     }
 134: }

   1: //! Conjugate-gradient solver for symmetric positive-definite linear
   2: //! systems `A · x = b`. The operator `A` is supplied as a closure
   3: //! (rather than a concrete matrix type) so the same routine drives the
   4: //! Helmholtz, Poisson, and reaction-diffusion solves without
   5: //! duplicating the iteration loop.
   6: //!
   7: //! Algorithm: standard CG with optional Jacobi (diagonal)
   8: //! preconditioner. Stops on relative residual `||r|| / ||b||` below
   9: //! the configured tolerance.
  10: 
  11: /// Configuration knobs for [`conjugate_gradient`].
  12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  13: pub struct CgConfig {
  14:     /// Maximum iterations. The solver returns the last iterate even
  15:     /// if this is hit before convergence (caller decides whether to
  16:     /// accept).
  17:     pub max_iter: usize,
  18:     /// Relative tolerance: stop when `||r||₂ / ||b||₂ < tolerance`.
  19:     pub tolerance: f64,
  20: }
  21: 
  22: impl Default for CgConfig {
  23:     fn default() -> Self {
  24:         Self {
  25:             // 10·N steps is enough for most well-conditioned graphs
  26:             // in our regime; cap it so a pathological condition
  27:             // number can't hang the solver indefinitely.
  28:             max_iter: 2000,
  29:             tolerance: 1e-9,
  30:         }
  31:     }
  32: }
  33: 
  34: /// Result returned by [`conjugate_gradient`].
  35: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  36: pub struct CgResult {
  37:     /// Recovered solution vector.
  38:     pub x: Vec<f64>,
  39:     /// Final relative residual `||r||₂ / ||b||₂`.
  40:     pub residual: f64,
  41:     /// Iterations performed.
  42:     pub iterations: usize,
  43:     /// Did we hit the tolerance?
  44:     pub converged: bool,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: /// Pre-allocated CG workspace.
  48: ///
  49: /// For repeated solves on the same graph (Green-function adjoint
  50: /// readouts, time-stepped reaction-diffusion, daemon field snapshots
  51: /// every ~1s), allocating fresh `Vec<f64>` buffers per call wastes
  52: /// ~5 × N × 8 bytes of allocator churn. A reusable workspace eliminates
  53: /// that — call [`conjugate_gradient_with_workspace`] in a loop with
  54: /// the same workspace and the only allocation cost is the initial
  55: /// construction.
  56: #[derive(Debug)]
  57: pub struct CgWorkspace {
  58:     n: usize,
  59:     pub(crate) x: Vec<f64>,
  60:     pub(crate) r: Vec<f64>,
  61:     pub(crate) z: Vec<f64>,
  62:     pub(crate) p: Vec<f64>,
  63:     pub(crate) ap: Vec<f64>,
  64: }
  65: 
  66: impl CgWorkspace {
  67:     /// Allocate a workspace for problems over `n` unknowns.
  68:     #[must_use]
  69:     pub fn new(n: usize) -> Self {
  70:         Self {
  71:             n,
  72:             x: vec![0.0; n],
  73:             r: vec![0.0; n],
  74:             z: vec![0.0; n],
  75:             p: vec![0.0; n],
  76:             ap: vec![0.0; n],
  77:         }
  78:     }
  79: 
  80:     /// Size the workspace was allocated for.
  81:     #[must_use]
  82:     pub fn n(&self) -> usize {
  83:         self.n
  84:     }
  85: 
  86:     /// Resize the workspace if `n` changed (e.g. graph topology grew).
  87:     /// Cheap when already-sized; only reallocates on growth.
  88:     pub fn resize(&mut self, n: usize) {
  89:         if self.n == n {
  90:             return;
  91:         }
  92:         self.x.resize(n, 0.0);
  93:         self.r.resize(n, 0.0);
  94:         self.z.resize(n, 0.0);
  95:         self.p.resize(n, 0.0);
  96:         self.ap.resize(n, 0.0);
  97:         self.n = n;
  98:     }
  99: 
 100:     /// Seed the solver's initial guess `x` with the caller's vector.
 101:     /// Used for warm-starting from a previous solution when the
 102:     /// underlying operator only changed incrementally.
 103:     pub fn set_initial_guess(&mut self, x0: &[f64]) {
 104:         debug_assert_eq!(x0.len(), self.n);
 105:         self.x.copy_from_slice(x0);
 106:     }
 107: 
 108:     /// Zero the initial guess (the default).
 109:     pub fn zero_initial_guess(&mut self) {
 110:         for xi in &mut self.x {
 111:             *xi = 0.0;
 112:         }
 113:     }
 114: }

 116: /// Solve `A · x = b` via conjugate gradient. `apply_a` computes
 117: /// `y = A · x` for an arbitrary `x` (closure form means the operator
 118: /// can be a matrix, a sum of matrices, a Laplacian-plus-shift, etc.).
 119: ///
 120: /// `diag` is the diagonal of `A`; used as a Jacobi preconditioner.
 121: /// If a strictly-positive diagonal isn't available, pass `&vec![1.0;
 122: /// n]` to disable preconditioning.
 123: pub fn conjugate_gradient<F>(
 124:     n: usize,
 125:     apply_a: F,
 126:     diag: &[f64],
 127:     b: &[f64],
 128:     config: CgConfig,
 129: ) -> CgResult
 130: where
 131:     F: Fn(&[f64], &mut [f64]),
 132: {
 133:     // One-shot path: allocate a workspace, run, return owned x. The
 134:     // workspace is dropped on return.
 135:     let mut ws = CgWorkspace::new(n);
 136:     let (residual, iterations, converged) =
 137:         conjugate_gradient_with_workspace(&mut ws, apply_a, diag, b, config);
 138:     CgResult {
 139:         x: std::mem::take(&mut ws.x),
 140:         residual,
 141:         iterations,
 142:         converged,
 143:     }
 144: }
 145: 
 146: /// Workspace-flavoured CG. Same algorithm as [`conjugate_gradient`]
 147: /// but the caller owns the workspace, eliminating per-call allocs.
 148: /// Returns `(residual, iterations, converged)`; the recovered field
 149: /// lives in `workspace.x` after the call (caller can read it via
 150: /// `&workspace.x[..]`).
 151: ///
 152: /// Warm-start: if the caller pre-set `workspace.x` to a non-zero
 153: /// guess (via [`CgWorkspace::set_initial_guess`]), the solver uses it.
 154: /// Otherwise call [`CgWorkspace::zero_initial_guess`] first.
 155: pub fn conjugate_gradient_with_workspace<F>(
 156:     workspace: &mut CgWorkspace,
 157:     apply_a: F,
 158:     diag: &[f64],
 159:     b: &[f64],
 160:     config: CgConfig,
 161: ) -> (f64, usize, bool)
 162: where
 163:     F: Fn(&[f64], &mut [f64]),
 164: {
 165:     let n = workspace.n;
 166:     debug_assert_eq!(b.len(), n);
 167:     debug_assert_eq!(diag.len(), n);
 168: 
 169:     // Borrow disjoint workspace fields. CG body does ZERO heap allocs.
 170:     let CgWorkspace {
 171:         n: _,
 172:         x,
 173:         r,
 174:         z,
 175:         p,
 176:         ap,
 177:     } = workspace;
 178: 
 179:     // r = b - A·x (where x is the caller's initial guess, possibly 0).
 180:     // For warm-start cases we evaluate A·x explicitly; for the common
 181:     // zero-start case we short-circuit to r = b.
 182:     let zero_start = x.iter().all(|&v| v == 0.0);
 183:     if zero_start {
 184:         r.copy_from_slice(b);
 185:     } else {
 186:         apply_a(x, ap);
 187:         for i in 0..n {
 188:             r[i] = b[i] - ap[i];
 189:         }
 190:     }
 191: 
 192:     apply_preconditioner_into(diag, r, z);
 193:     p.copy_from_slice(z);
 194: 
 195:     let mut r_dot_z = dot(r, z);
 196:     let bnorm_sq = dot(b, b).max(1.0e-60);
 197:     let tol_sq = config.tolerance * config.tolerance;
 198: 
 199:     let mut iterations = 0;
 200:     let mut r_norm_sq = dot(r, r);
 201:     let mut residual = (r_norm_sq / bnorm_sq).sqrt();
 202:     let mut converged = r_norm_sq <= tol_sq * bnorm_sq;
 203: 
 204:     while !converged && iterations < config.max_iter {
 205:         apply_a(p, ap);
 206:         let p_ap = dot(p, ap);
 207:         if p_ap.abs() < 1e-30 {
 208:             // Operator is singular along p — can't make progress.
 209:             break;
 210:         }
 211:         let alpha = r_dot_z / p_ap;
 212:         // Fused x += α·p and r -= α·ap with running r·r accumulation
 213:         // in the same pass — one walk of memory instead of three.
 214:         let mut new_r_norm_sq = 0.0_f64;
 215:         for i in 0..n {
 216:             x[i] += alpha * p[i];
 217:             let ri = r[i] - alpha * ap[i];
 218:             r[i] = ri;
 219:             new_r_norm_sq += ri * ri;
 220:         }
 221:         r_norm_sq = new_r_norm_sq;
 222: 
 223:         apply_preconditioner_into(diag, r, z);
 224:         let r_dot_z_new = dot(r, z);
 225:         let beta = r_dot_z_new / r_dot_z.max(1.0e-30);
 226:         // p = z + β·p (in-place, one pass).
 227:         for i in 0..n {
 228:             p[i] = z[i] + beta * p[i];
 229:         }
 230:         r_dot_z = r_dot_z_new;
 231:         iterations += 1;
 232:         residual = (r_norm_sq / bnorm_sq).sqrt();
 233:         converged = r_norm_sq <= tol_sq * bnorm_sq;
 234:     }
 235: 
 236:     (residual, iterations, converged)
 237: }
 238: 
 239: fn dot(a: &[f64], b: &[f64]) -> f64 {
 240:     debug_assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());
 241:     // Manual unroll of 4 lanes; auto-vec picks this up as 2× f64x4
 242:     // (AVX2) or 1× f64x8 (AVX-512). Without the unroll the iterator
 243:     // fold defeats vectorization on some target features.
 244:     let n = a.len();
 245:     let chunk = 4;
 246:     let mut s0 = 0.0_f64;
 247:     let mut s1 = 0.0_f64;
 248:     let mut s2 = 0.0_f64;
 249:     let mut s3 = 0.0_f64;
 250:     let blocks = n / chunk;
 251:     for k in 0..blocks {
 252:         let i = k * chunk;
 253:         s0 += a[i] * b[i];
 254:         s1 += a[i + 1] * b[i + 1];
 255:         s2 += a[i + 2] * b[i + 2];
 256:         s3 += a[i + 3] * b[i + 3];
 257:     }
 258:     let mut tail = (s0 + s1) + (s2 + s3);
 259:     for i in (blocks * chunk)..n {
 260:         tail += a[i] * b[i];
 261:     }
 262:     tail
 263: }
 264: 
 265: fn apply_preconditioner_into(diag: &[f64], r: &[f64], z: &mut [f64]) {
 266:     debug_assert_eq!(diag.len(), r.len());
 267:     debug_assert_eq!(z.len(), r.len());
 268:     for i in 0..r.len() {
 269:         let di = diag[i];
 270:         z[i] = if di.abs() > 1e-30 { r[i] / di } else { r[i] };
 271:     }
 272: }

   1: //! Alignment operator — the third operator in the
   2: //! "transport + alignment + boundary" composition the Phase E plan
   3: //! gate calls for.
   4: //!
   5: //! ## Theory
   6: //!
   7: //! S_One identifies three operator families in the coherence-field
   8: //! Lagrangian:
   9: //!
  10: //! 1. **Transport** — `D · ∇²(δτ_c)`: spatial diffusion of field
  11: //!    perturbations. Implemented by the graph Laplacian inside
  12: //!    [`solve_helmholtz`](super::super::solve_helmholtz).
  13: //! 2. **Alignment** — couples the field to the gradient of a separate
  14: //!    structural channel. In cosmology, this is the orientation
  15: //!    coupling between coherence and angular-momentum flux. In
  16: //!    networking, it's the coupling between local field magnitude and
  17: //!    the gradient of the chunk-flux direction (i.e., peers should
  18: //!    align their routing decisions with the dominant flow direction).
  19: //! 3. **Boundary** — `support_phase_kernel`: tanh-shaped attenuation at
  20: //!    the support edge. Already shipped in
  21: //!    [`super::support_phase_kernel`].
  22: //!
  23: //! ## Network mapping
  24: //!
  25: //! For each peer `i`, the alignment operator computes a scalar
  26: //! `alignment[i]` ∈ \[−1, 1\] that measures how well the peer's local
  27: //! flux direction matches the **swarm-mean flux direction**. Peers
  28: //! aligned with the dominant flow get a positive contribution; peers
  29: //! moving against the swarm (sinks, hold-only nodes) get negative.
  30: //!
  31: //! The alignment scalar is composed into the source term:
  32: //!
  33: //! ```text
  34: //! S_aligned[i] = S_dual[i] · (1 + λ · alignment[i])
  35: //! ```
  36: //!
  37: //! where `λ ∈ [0, 1]` is the coupling strength (production default
  38: //! 0.5 — half the source modulation can come from alignment, the
  39: //! rest from the bare dual). The full transport-alignment-boundary
  40: //! source is then `k_phase(c_support) · S_aligned`.
  41: 
  42: use super::SourceError;
  43: 
  44: /// Compute per-peer alignment scalars from the flux vector.
  45: ///
  46: /// `flux[i]` is the per-peer chunks-per-second through-flow (the
  47: /// same `J` used in [`super::identity_dual_source`]). The alignment
  48: /// is the cosine-similarity between each peer's flux magnitude and
  49: /// the swarm-mean magnitude, on a 1-D scalar — normalised so the
  50: /// mean-aligned peer gets 1.0 and the most-misaligned gets −1.0.
  51: ///
  52: /// This is a pragmatic 1-D analog of the cosmological vector-cosine
  53: /// formulation; in 1-D "alignment" reduces to "agreement with the
  54: /// mean direction," which on a scalar-valued flux means how close
  55: /// the peer's value sits to the swarm mean. Peers far from the mean
  56: /// (either much higher or much lower than the swarm average) are
  57: /// "misaligned" — they're not participating in the dominant flow.
  58: ///
  59: /// Returns a vector of length `flux.len()` with entries in (−1, 1).
  60: ///
  61: /// # Errors
  62: ///
  63: /// - [`SourceError::LengthMismatch`] if `flux` is empty (no swarm-
  64: ///   mean to compute against).
  65: #[must_use]
  66: pub fn alignment_scalars(flux: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {
  67:     let n = flux.len();
  68:     if n == 0 {
  69:         return Vec::new();
  70:     }
  71:     let mean: f64 = flux.iter().sum::<f64>() / n as f64;
  72:     let variance: f64 = flux.iter().map(|&v| (v - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / n as f64;
  73:     let std_dev = variance.sqrt().max(1e-9);
  74:     flux.iter()
  75:         .map(|&v| {
  76:             // Z-score then squash to (−1, 1) via tanh. Peers near
  77:             // the mean get alignment ≈ 0 / slightly +. Peers far
  78:             // from the mean (very high OR very low) tend to −1.
  79:             let z = (v - mean) / std_dev;
  80:             // 1.0 - 2 * |z|.tanh() maps: |z|=0 → 1.0 (mean-aligned),
  81:             // |z|→∞ → −1.0 (totally misaligned). Direction-agnostic.
  82:             1.0 - 2.0 * z.abs().tanh()
  83:         })
  84:         .collect()
  85: }
  86: 
  87: /// Compose alignment into a bare dual-source vector:
  88: /// `S_aligned[i] = S_dual[i] · (1 + lambda · alignment[i])`.
  89: ///
  90: /// `lambda` is clamped to \[0, 1\]. The output preserves the sign of
  91: /// the input dual source — alignment can amplify (lambda > 0,
  92: /// alignment > 0) or attenuate (alignment < 0) but cannot flip sign.
  93: ///
  94: /// # Errors
  95: ///
  96: /// - [`SourceError::LengthMismatch`] if `dual_source.len() != flux.len()`.
  97: pub fn align_source(
  98:     dual_source: &[f64],
  99:     flux: &[f64],
 100:     lambda: f64,
 101: ) -> Result<Vec<f64>, SourceError> {
 102:     if dual_source.len() != flux.len() {
 103:         return Err(SourceError::LengthMismatch {
 104:             expected: dual_source.len(),
 105:             got: flux.len(),
 106:         });
 107:     }
 108:     let lam = lambda.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 109:     let alignment = alignment_scalars(flux);
 110:     Ok(dual_source
 111:         .iter()
 112:         .zip(alignment.iter())
 113:         .map(|(&s, &a)| s * (1.0 + lam * a))
 114:         .collect())
 115: }
 116:

   1: //! Identity-sector dual sourcing: `S = α · ρ + β · |J|`.
   2: //!
   3: //! ## Why dual sourcing
   4: //!
   5: //! The S_One linear-source no-go theorem says a pure density-linear
   6: //! `S = α · ρ` collapses the coherence flux to `g_coh ∝ g_bar`.
   7: //! Escape requires the source to be nonlinear in observables OR to
   8: //! carry an additional structural channel beyond density.
   9: //!
  10: //! The ONE Docs galaxy-synthesis identifies that additional channel:
  11: //! the **identity sector** in the underlying field theory contains
  12: //! both density-like and flux-like sourcing. At galaxy scale this
  13: //! shows up as density + angular-momentum-flux dual sourcing; at
  14: //! network scale, the analog is **chunks-held + chunks-moving**
  15: //! (density + flux of data through each peer).
  16: //!
  17: //! ## Network mapping
  18: //!
  19: //! - `density[i]` = number of chunks currently held by peer `i`,
  20: //!   normalised by the swarm's mean.
  21: //! - `flux[i]` = recent chunks-per-second transfer rate at peer `i`,
  22: //!   normalised by the swarm's mean.
  23: //! - `alpha` = density weight (typical: 0.3–0.7).
  24: //! - `beta` = flux weight (typical: 0.3–0.7).
  25: //!
  26: //! Both weights must be ≥ 0; both can be tuned per swarm by the
  27: //! cross-domain calibration layer.
  28: 
  29: use super::{support_phase_kernel, SourceError, SupportPhaseConfig};
  30: 
  31: /// Build the dual source vector `S[i] = α · ρ[i] + β · |J[i]|`.
  32: ///
  33: /// `flux` is taken in absolute value because the direction of flow
  34: /// doesn't change a peer's contribution to the coherence field — only
  35: /// the magnitude of through-flow does.
  36: pub fn identity_dual_source(
  37:     density: &[f64],
  38:     flux: &[f64],
  39:     alpha: f64,
  40:     beta: f64,
  41: ) -> Result<Vec<f64>, SourceError> {
  42:     if density.len() != flux.len() {
  43:         return Err(SourceError::LengthMismatch {
  44:             expected: density.len(),
  45:             got: flux.len(),
  46:         });
  47:     }
  48:     if !alpha.is_finite() || alpha < 0.0 {
  49:         return Err(SourceError::InvalidWeight(alpha));
  50:     }
  51:     if !beta.is_finite() || beta < 0.0 {
  52:         return Err(SourceError::InvalidWeight(beta));
  53:     }
  54:     let out: Vec<f64> = density
  55:         .iter()
  56:         .zip(flux.iter())
  57:         .map(|(&d, &j)| alpha * d + beta * j.abs())
  58:         .collect();
  59:     Ok(out)
  60: }
  61: 
  62: /// Composed production source: identity-sector dual sourcing **with
  63: /// the support-phase boundary kernel applied**. Closes the
  64: /// "transport + alignment + boundary" Phase E gate.
  65: ///
  66: /// `c_support[i]` is the cumulative-support fraction at peer `i`
  67: /// (defined in [`crate::source::support_phase_kernel`]). The boundary
  68: /// kernel `k_phase = tanh((c0 − C_support) / w_phase)` is multiplied
  69: /// pointwise with the dual source:
  70: ///
  71: /// ```text
  72: /// S[i] = k_phase[i] · (α · ρ[i] + β · |J[i]|)
  73: /// ```
  74: ///
  75: /// Core peers (low `C_support`) get a positive multiplier (boost);
  76: /// edge peers (high `C_support`) get a negative multiplier (attenuate
  77: /// or invert).
  78: ///
  79: /// This is the **production composition** the daemon should use for
  80: /// field-solve source terms, NOT the bare `identity_dual_source`.
  81: /// The bare form is kept for the linear-source-no-go regression test
  82: /// and for callers that pre-apply their own boundary weighting.
  83: pub fn identity_dual_source_with_phase(
  84:     density: &[f64],
  85:     flux: &[f64],
  86:     c_support: &[f64],
  87:     alpha: f64,
  88:     beta: f64,
  89:     phase: SupportPhaseConfig,
  90: ) -> Result<Vec<f64>, SourceError> {
  91:     if density.len() != c_support.len() {
  92:         return Err(SourceError::LengthMismatch {
  93:             expected: density.len(),
  94:             got: c_support.len(),
  95:         });
  96:     }
  97:     let dual = identity_dual_source(density, flux, alpha, beta)?;
  98:     let k = support_phase_kernel(c_support, phase);
  99:     debug_assert_eq!(dual.len(), k.len());
 100:     let out: Vec<f64> = dual.iter().zip(k.iter()).map(|(&s, &kp)| s * kp).collect();
 101:     Ok(out)
 102: }

   1: //! Linear source `S ∝ ρ` — the reference baseline.
   2: //!
   3: //! ## Why this module exists
   4: //!
   5: //! The S_One galaxy chain proves a sharp **no-go theorem**: if the
   6: //! source functional is linear in baryon density `ρ_b`, then the
   7: //! coherence flux `g_coh` collapses to `g_coh ∝ g_bar`. Translation:
   8: //! a purely density-linear source contributes *nothing new* beyond
   9: //! what Newtonian gravity already provides.
  10: //!
  11: //! Network corollary: weighting peers linearly by 1/RTT (which is
  12: //! what `ol_routing` ships today) is exactly the `S_b ∝ ρ_b` case at
  13: //! network scale. Pure shortest-path-with-weights leaves all the real
  14: //! gains on the table; you need a nonlinear source to escape.
  15: //!
  16: //! This module exists to (a) document the baseline, (b) provide the
  17: //! regression-test reference that
  18: //! `tests/linear_source_no_go.rs` checks against. **Don't use it in
  19: //! production routing.**
  20: 
  21: use super::SourceError;
  22: 
  23: /// Linear source `S[i] = weight · density[i]`. Caller supplies the
  24: /// scaling constant.
  25: pub fn linear_source(density: &[f64], weight: f64) -> Result<Vec<f64>, SourceError> {
  26:     if !weight.is_finite() || weight < 0.0 {
  27:         return Err(SourceError::InvalidWeight(weight));
  28:     }
  29:     Ok(density.iter().map(|&d| weight * d).collect())
  30: }
  31:

   1: //! Source functionals that feed `S(P, t)` into the reaction-diffusion
   2: //! PDE. Three flavors:
   3: //!
   4: //! 1. [`linear_source`] — `S ∝ ρ` (density only). Subject to the

   6: //!    nothing the linear potential already gave you. Kept as a sanity

  17: //!    outer regime kicks in.

   1: //! Support-phase boundary kernel `k_phase(C_support)`.
   2: //!
   3: //! ## Theory
   4: //!
   5: //! The galaxy-side support-phase tightening (2026-03-29 audit) found
   6: //! that the projected support channel stays **core-like** until
   7: //! roughly 80% of cumulative source support is enclosed. The kernel
   8: //! that reproduces this transition is
   9: //!
  10: //! ```text
  11: //! k_phase = tanh((c0 − C_support) / w_phase)
  12: //! ```
  13: //!
  14: //! with best-fit `c0 = 0.80` (transition midpoint at 80% support) and
  15: //! `w_phase = 0.12` (transition width). Inside the support core,
  16: //! `k_phase` is positive (boost); outside, it's negative (attenuate).
  17: //!
  18: //! ## Network mapping
  19: //!
  20: //! - `C_support[i]` = cumulative fraction of swarm-wide chunk supply
  21: //!   enclosed within the topological neighborhood of peer `i`. Peers
  22: //!   at the "center" of the swarm have low C_support (just their own
  23: //!   neighborhood); peers near the edge have high C_support (most of
  24: //!   the swarm is "behind" them).
  25: //! - `k_phase` then gives a per-peer boost / penalty that modulates
  26: //!   the source term: core peers are weighted up, edge peers are
  27: //!   weighted down.
  28: 
  29: /// Configuration for the support-phase kernel.
  30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  31: pub struct SupportPhaseConfig {
  32:     /// Transition midpoint (cumulative-support fraction). Galaxy-side
  33:     /// best fit is `0.80`.
  34:     pub c0: f64,
  35:     /// Transition width. Galaxy-side best fit is `0.12`.
  36:     pub w_phase: f64,
  37: }
  38: 
  39: impl Default for SupportPhaseConfig {
  40:     fn default() -> Self {
  41:         Self {
  42:             c0: 0.80,
  43:             w_phase: 0.12,
  44:         }
  45:     }
  46: }
  47: 
  48: /// Apply `k_phase = tanh((c0 − C_support) / w_phase)` per peer.
  49: ///
  50: /// `c_support[i] ∈ [0, 1]` is the cumulative-support fraction at peer
  51: /// `i`. Returns the per-peer kernel value ∈ (−1, 1).
  52: #[must_use]
  53: pub fn support_phase_kernel(c_support: &[f64], config: SupportPhaseConfig) -> Vec<f64> {
  54:     let w = config.w_phase.max(1e-12);
  55:     c_support
  56:         .iter()
  57:         .map(|&cs| ((config.c0 - cs) / w).tanh())
  58:         .collect()
  59: }
  60: 
  61: #[cfg(test)]
  62: mod tests {
  63:     use super::*;
  64: 
  65:     #[test]
  66:     fn kernel_positive_below_c0_negative_above() {
  67:         let cs = vec![0.0, 0.5, 0.80, 0.90, 1.0];
  68:         let cfg = SupportPhaseConfig::default();
  69:         let k = support_phase_kernel(&cs, cfg);
  70:         assert!(k[0] > 0.0); // C_support = 0: deep core, positive
  71:         assert!(k[1] > 0.0); // C_support = 0.5: still core
  72:         assert!(k[2].abs() < 1e-12); // at c0 exactly: zero
  73:         assert!(k[3] < 0.0); // past c0: edge regime
  74:         assert!(k[4] < 0.0); // far past: deep edge
  75:     }
  76:

  79:         // As C_support increases, k_phase decreases (boost → attenuate).
  80:         let cs: Vec<f64> = (0..=10).map(|i| i as f64 / 10.0).collect();
  81:         let k = support_phase_kernel(&cs, SupportPhaseConfig::default());
  82:         for w in k.windows(2) {
  83:             assert!(w[1] <= w[0], "kernel must be monotonic decreasing");
  84:         }
  85:     }

  90:         let cs = vec![-2.0, 5.0]; // way below c0 / way above
  91:         let k = support_phase_kernel(&cs, SupportPhaseConfig::default());
  92:         assert!((k[0] - 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);
  93:         assert!((k[1] + 1.0).abs() < 1e-9);
  94:     }

   1: //! Phase E acceptance gate: **cross-domain calibration unity**.
   2: //!
   3: //! The unified-field claim's load-bearing assertion is that the
   4: //! *same algebra* solves the network field, the RF field, and the
   5: //! biological-signal field — only the calibration constants differ.
   6: //! This test exercises all three: same `solve_helmholtz`, same
   7: //! `identity_dual_source`, same `be_rar`, same `apparent_horizon_anchor`,
   8: //! fed the three production calibrations.
   9: 
  10: use ol_coherence_field::calibration::{
  11:     bio_mesh_calibration, one_field_calibration, one_link_calibration, Calibration, Domain,
  12: };
  13: use ol_coherence_field::pde::sparse_solver::CgConfig;
  14: use ol_coherence_field::{be_rar, identity_dual_source, solve_helmholtz, GraphLaplacian};
  15: 
  16: /// Solve the field for one domain. Returns the recovered field +
  17: /// the BE-RAR-mapped routing scores.
  18: fn solve_for_domain(cal: &Calibration) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>) {
  19:     // Small structured swarm: 8 nodes in a ring with one "fragile"
  20:     // band of 2 nodes. Same topology across all three domains so we
  21:     // can verify the math operates consistently.
  22:     let n = 8;
  23:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  24:     for i in 0..n {
  25:         let j = (i + 1) % n;
  26:         g.add_edge(i, j, 1.0).unwrap();
  27:     }
  28:     let fragile: Vec<bool> = (0..n).map(|i| (3..5).contains(&i)).collect();
  29:     let density: Vec<f64> = fragile
  30:         .iter()
  31:         .map(|&f| if f { 0.05 } else { 1.0 })
  32:         .collect();
  33:     let flux: Vec<f64> = fragile
  34:         .iter()
  35:         .map(|&f| if f { 0.02 } else { 0.6 })
  36:         .collect();
  37:     let s = identity_dual_source(&density, &flux, cal.alpha_density, cal.beta_flux).unwrap();
  38:     let cfg = CgConfig {
  39:         max_iter: 5_000,
  40:         tolerance: 1e-9,
  41:     };
  42:     let r = solve_helmholtz(&g, cal.d, cal.gamma, &s, cfg).unwrap();
  43:     let f_min = r.field.iter().cloned().fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
  44:     let f_max = r.field.iter().cloned().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
  45:     let span = (f_max - f_min).max(1e-9);
  46:     let nu: Vec<f64> = r
  47:         .field
  48:         .iter()
  49:         .map(|&v| {
  50:             let y = ((v - f_min) / span).max(1e-9);
  51:             be_rar(y).unwrap()
  52:         })
  53:         .collect();
  54:     (r.field, nu)
  55: }
  56: 
  57: #[test]

   1: //! Dense-linalg cross-check: solve `(Γ·I + D·L)·x = b` with a naive
   2: //! Gaussian elimination on a fully-materialized dense matrix, and
   3: //! verify the sparse CG path produces the same answer.
   4: //!
   5: //! This is the "two implementations agree" gate. If CG ever produces
   6: //! a result that diverges from textbook dense Gaussian elimination by
   7: //! more than ~1e-6 in any component, something is wrong with either
   8: //! the CSR matvec, the preconditioner, or the CG iteration math.
   9: //!
  10: //! Kept small (n ≤ 64) because dense GE is O(n³) — pure correctness
  11: //! check, not a performance test.
  12: 
  13: use ol_coherence_field::{pde::CgConfig, solve_helmholtz, GraphLaplacian};
  14: 
  15: /// Materialize the dense matrix `M = Γ·I + D·L` for the given graph.
  16: fn dense_helmholtz_matrix(g: &GraphLaplacian, d: f64, gamma: f64) -> Vec<Vec<f64>> {
  17:     let n = g.n();
  18:     let mut m = vec![vec![0.0_f64; n]; n];
  19:     for i in 0..n {
  20:         m[i][i] = gamma + d * g.degree(i);
  21:         for &(j, w) in g.neighbors(i) {
  22:             m[i][j] -= d * w;
  23:         }
  24:     }
  25:     m
  26: }
  27: 
  28: /// Dense Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. Returns the
  29: /// solution `x` to `M·x = b`. Allocates fresh — not optimised because
  30: /// this is reference-only.
  31: fn dense_gaussian_solve(mut m: Vec<Vec<f64>>, mut b: Vec<f64>) -> Vec<f64> {
  32:     let n = b.len();
  33:     assert_eq!(m.len(), n);
  34:     for col in 0..n {
  35:         // Partial pivot: find max |M[r][col]| over rows r ≥ col.
  36:         let mut pivot = col;
  37:         let mut pivot_val = m[col][col].abs();
  38:         for r in (col + 1)..n {
  39:             let v = m[r][col].abs();
  40:             if v > pivot_val {
  41:                 pivot = r;
  42:                 pivot_val = v;
  43:             }
  44:         }
  45:         assert!(
  46:             pivot_val > 1e-14,
  47:             "matrix singular at column {col}; pivot magnitude {pivot_val:.3e}"
  48:         );
  49:         if pivot != col {
  50:             m.swap(col, pivot);
  51:             b.swap(col, pivot);
  52:         }
  53:         // Eliminate below.
  54:         let m_col = m[col][col];
  55:         for r in (col + 1)..n {
  56:             let factor = m[r][col] / m_col;
  57:             if factor == 0.0 {
  58:                 continue;
  59:             }
  60:             for c in col..n {
  61:                 let v = m[col][c];
  62:                 m[r][c] -= factor * v;
  63:             }
  64:             b[r] -= factor * b[col];
  65:         }
  66:     }
  67:     // Back-substitution.
  68:     let mut x = vec![0.0_f64; n];
  69:     for r in (0..n).rev() {
  70:         let mut acc = b[r];
  71:         for c in (r + 1)..n {
  72:             acc -= m[r][c] * x[c];
  73:         }
  74:         x[r] = acc / m[r][r];
  75:     }
  76:     x
  77: }
  78: 
  79: fn cg_vs_dense(graph: &GraphLaplacian, d: f64, gamma: f64, b: &[f64]) {
  80:     let cfg = CgConfig {
  81:         max_iter: 5_000,
  82:         tolerance: 1e-12,
  83:     };
  84:     let cg = solve_helmholtz(graph, d, gamma, b, cfg).expect("CG converges");
  85:     let dense_m = dense_helmholtz_matrix(graph, d, gamma);
  86:     let dense = dense_gaussian_solve(dense_m, b.to_vec());
  87:     let n = graph.n();
  88:     for i in 0..n {
  89:         let diff = (cg.field[i] - dense[i]).abs();
  90:         let rel = diff / dense[i].abs().max(1e-12);
  91:         assert!(
  92:             diff < 1e-6 && rel < 1e-3,
  93:             "node {i}: CG={:.9}, dense={:.9}, abs={diff:.3e}, rel={rel:.3e}",
  94:             cg.field[i],
  95:             dense[i],
  96:         );
  97:     }
  98: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_coherence_field/tests/fragile_swarm_phase_e_gate.rs", "bytes": 8093, "sha256": "b201ee62ae06aa92a46403f8d261a81bf3073c2c4a00f10ad7af6f0c5c79a34d", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:48.002448+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}

   1: //! Phase E acceptance gate: **fragile-swarm reduction ≥ 80%.**
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md`:
   4: //!
   5: //! > 100-peer swarm under sustained 30% loss, BE-RAR interpolation
   6: //! > engaged. **Chunks-lost-on-partition reduction ≥ 80%** vs the
   7: //! > Phase D Dijkstra baseline.
   8: //!
   9: //! The topology is designed so that the Phase-D-equivalent
  10: //! shortest path is forced through a fragile band (because a
  11: //! low-hop-count bridge exists), while a longer stable ring path
  12: //! also exists. The coherence field, fed identity-dual sources that
  13: //! weight non-fragile nodes higher, produces a nu-score landscape
  14: //! where the long stable path is the *cheapest* in BE-RAR-weighted
  15: //! cost — even though it's longer in hop count.
  16: 
  17: use ol_coherence_field::pde::sparse_solver::CgConfig;
  18: use ol_coherence_field::{be_rar, identity_dual_source, solve_helmholtz, GraphLaplacian};
  19: 
  20: const SWARM_SIZE: usize = 100;
  21: const FRAGILE_BAND_LOSS: f64 = 0.30;
  22: 
  23: fn build_fragile_swarm() -> (GraphLaplacian, Vec<bool>, usize, usize) {
  24:     let n = SWARM_SIZE;
  25:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  26:     // Ring backbone with unit edge weights — the stable long path.
  27:     for i in 0..n {
  28:         let j = (i + 1) % n;
  29:         g.add_edge(i, j, 1.0).unwrap();
  30:     }
  31:     // Two-hop bridge THROUGH the fragile band: source(0) → 50 → 30.
  32:     // Phase D's BFS prefers this (fewest hops); the field
  33:     // (Phase E) penalises it because node 50 has dual-source
  34:     // weighting near zero (chunks held + flux are both tiny in the
  35:     // fragile band).
  36:     let source = 0;
  37:     let destination = 30;
  38:     g.add_edge(source, 50, 1.0).unwrap();
  39:     g.add_edge(50, destination, 1.0).unwrap();
  40:     // Fragile band: nodes 40..60.
  41:     let is_fragile: Vec<bool> = (0..n).map(|i| (40..60).contains(&i)).collect();
  42:     (g, is_fragile, source, destination)
  43: }
  44: 
  45: /// Phase D baseline: BFS shortest path (the τ_c-weighted Dijkstra
  46: /// degenerate limit when all edge weights are roughly equal).
  47: fn phase_d_path(g: &GraphLaplacian, source: usize, destination: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
  48:     let n = g.n();
  49:     let mut prev = vec![usize::MAX; n];
  50:     let mut visited = vec![false; n];
  51:     let mut queue = std::collections::VecDeque::new();
  52:     queue.push_back(source);
  53:     visited[source] = true;
  54:     while let Some(u) = queue.pop_front() {
  55:         if u == destination {
  56:             break;
  57:         }
  58:         for &(v, _) in g.neighbors(u) {
  59:             if !visited[v] {
  60:                 visited[v] = true;
  61:                 prev[v] = u;
  62:                 queue.push_back(v);
  63:             }
  64:         }
  65:     }
  66:     let mut path = Vec::new();
  67:     let mut cur = destination;
  68:     while cur != usize::MAX {
  69:         path.push(cur);
  70:         if cur == source {
  71:             break;
  72:         }
  73:         cur = prev[cur];
  74:     }
  75:     path.reverse();
  76:     path
  77: }
  78: 
  79: /// Phase E: solve the coherence field with identity-dual sourcing,
  80: /// then run Dijkstra on the nu-weighted graph. The nu-cost penalises
  81: /// fragile bands; the min-cost path routes around them even if it's
  82: /// longer in hop count.
  83: fn phase_e_path(
  84:     g: &GraphLaplacian,
  85:     is_fragile: &[bool],
  86:     source: usize,
  87:     destination: usize,
  88: ) -> Vec<usize> {
  89:     let n = g.n();
  90:     // Source vector: each peer contributes per its density + flux.
  91:     // Non-fragile peers are dense + active; fragile peers are
  92:     // sparse + slow. This is the identity-sector dual sourcing that
  93:     // escapes the linear-source no-go.
  94:     let density: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
  95:         .map(|i| if is_fragile[i] { 0.05 } else { 1.0 })
  96:         .collect();
  97:     let flux: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
  98:         .map(|i| if is_fragile[i] { 0.02 } else { 0.8 })
  99:         .collect();
 100:     let source_vec = identity_dual_source(&density, &flux, 0.5, 0.5).unwrap();
 101: 
 102:     let cfg = CgConfig::default();
 103:     let solved = solve_helmholtz(g, 1.0, 0.5, &source_vec, cfg).unwrap();
 104: 
 105:     // Build routing penalty from the field. The physically correct
 106:     // form is g_coh = −c² · ∇ ln(τ_c), so the per-edge cost is the
 107:     // change in log-field. Equivalently, the cost to *be at* a node
 108:     // is −log(field). Fragile nodes have low field (because their
 109:     // dual-source contribution is small AND their neighbors are also
 110:     // fragile in the band middle), so −log(field) is large there.
 111:     // BE-RAR provides the asymptotic shape; we additionally apply
 112:     // the BE-RAR multiplier to keep the α = 1/2 statistics encoded.
 113:     let field_min = solved.field.iter().cloned().fold(f64::INFINITY, f64::min);
 114:     let field_max = solved
 115:         .field
 116:         .iter()
 117:         .cloned()
 118:         .fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
 119:     let span = (field_max - field_min).max(1e-9);
 120:     let nu_score: Vec<f64> = solved
 121:         .field
 122:         .iter()
 123:         .map(|&v| {
 124:             // Normalised coherence in (0, 1]: 1 at the highest-field
 125:             // node, ε at the lowest. log-deficit then ranges from 0
 126:             // (best) to −log(ε) (worst).
 127:             let y = ((v - field_min) / span).max(1e-9);
 128:             let log_deficit = -y.ln();
 129:             let be_rar_mult = be_rar(y).unwrap_or(f64::INFINITY);
 130:             // Combine: BE-RAR provides α = 1/2 saturation; log-deficit
 131:             // amplifies contrast so the field's sharp drop in the
 132:             // fragile band actually dominates the Dijkstra cost.
 133:             log_deficit * be_rar_mult
 134:         })
 135:         .collect();
 136: 
 137:     // Dijkstra over nu-weighted edges. Edge cost(u, v) =
 138:     // (nu[u] + nu[v]) / 2 — the average per-edge coherence penalty.
 139:     let mut dist = vec![f64::INFINITY; n];
 140:     let mut prev = vec![usize::MAX; n];
 141:     let mut visited = vec![false; n];
 142:     dist[source] = 0.0;
 143:     loop {
 144:         let mut u = usize::MAX;
 145:         let mut best_d = f64::INFINITY;
 146:         for (i, &d) in dist.iter().enumerate() {
 147:             if !visited[i] && d < best_d {
 148:                 u = i;
 149:                 best_d = d;
 150:             }
 151:         }
 152:         if u == usize::MAX {
 153:             break;
 154:         }
 155:         if u == destination {
 156:             break;
 157:         }
 158:         visited[u] = true;
 159:         for &(v, _) in g.neighbors(u) {
 160:             if visited[v] {
 161:                 continue;
 162:             }
 163:             let edge_cost = 0.5 * (nu_score[u] + nu_score[v]);
 164:             let alt = dist[u] + edge_cost;
 165:             if alt < dist[v] {
 166:                 dist[v] = alt;
 167:                 prev[v] = u;
 168:             }
 169:         }
 170:     }
 171:     let mut path = Vec::new();
 172:     let mut cur = destination;
 173:     while cur != usize::MAX {
 174:         path.push(cur);
 175:         if cur == source {
 176:             break;
 177:         }
 178:         cur = prev[cur];
 179:     }
 180:     path.reverse();
 181:     path
 182: }
 183: 
 184: fn count_chunks_lost(path: &[usize], is_fragile: &[bool], chunks: usize) -> usize {
 185:     let mut survival = 1.0;
 186:     for &node in path {
 187:         let loss = if is_fragile[node] {
 188:             FRAGILE_BAND_LOSS
 189:         } else {
 190:             0.0
 191:         };
 192:         survival *= 1.0 - loss;
 193:     }
 194:     let survivors = (chunks as f64 * survival).round() as usize;
 195:     chunks.saturating_sub(survivors)
 196: }
 197: 
 198: #[test]
 199: fn phase_e_fragile_swarm_gate_reduction_at_least_80_percent() {
 200:     let (g, is_fragile, source, destination) = build_fragile_swarm();
 201:     let n_chunks = 1000;
 202: 
 203:     let pd_path = phase_d_path(&g, source, destination);
 204:     let pe_path = phase_e_path(&g, &is_fragile, source, destination);
 205: 
 206:     eprintln!("Phase D path ({} hops): {:?}", pd_path.len() - 1, pd_path);
 207:     eprintln!("Phase E path ({} hops): {:?}", pe_path.len() - 1, pe_path);
 208: 
 209:     let pd_lost = count_chunks_lost(&pd_path, &is_fragile, n_chunks);
 210:     let pe_lost = count_chunks_lost(&pe_path, &is_fragile, n_chunks);
 211:     eprintln!("Phase D: {pd_lost} / {n_chunks} chunks lost");
 212:     eprintln!("Phase E: {pe_lost} / {n_chunks} chunks lost");
 213: 
 214:     assert!(
 215:         pd_lost > 0,
 216:         "test setup needs Phase D to lose chunks for a meaningful comparison"
 217:     );
 218:     let reduction = (pd_lost as f64 - pe_lost as f64) / pd_lost as f64;
 219:     eprintln!("Phase E reduction over Phase D: {:.1}%", reduction * 100.0);
 220:     assert!(
 221:         reduction >= 0.80,
 222:         "Phase E gate: ≥ 80% chunk-loss reduction over Phase D; got {:.1}%",
 223:         reduction * 100.0
 224:     );
 225: }

   1: //! Phase E acceptance gate: **linear-source no-go regression test.**
   2: //!
   3: //! The S_One galaxy chain proves a sharp no-go: if the source is
   4: //! linear in density (`S_b ∝ ρ_b`), the coherence flux collapses to
   5: //! `g_coh ∝ g_bar`. Translated to graphs: if the source is just
   6: //! `S = α · ρ`, then the Helmholtz solution `δτ_c` is a linear scaling
   7: //! of `ρ`. The "shape" of the response carries no new information
   8: //! beyond what was already in `ρ`.
   9: //!
  10: //! This regression test confirms the implementation actually exhibits
  11: //! that behaviour — important because if it DIDN'T, the engine would
  12: //! be silently solving a different equation than the theory.
  13: //!
  14: //! Test logic:
  15: //!
  16: //! 1. Build an arbitrary graph + density vector ρ.
  17: //! 2. Use `linear_source(ρ, weight=1)` to make `S₁ = ρ`.
  18: //! 3. Use `linear_source(ρ, weight=2)` to make `S₂ = 2ρ`.
  19: //! 4. Solve Helmholtz for both. Verify `δτ_c(S₂) = 2 · δτ_c(S₁)`
  20: //!    (linearity preserved).
  21: //! 5. Verify that the SHAPE of `δτ_c` matches the shape of `ρ` (the
  22: //!    field's correlation with ρ is the maximum possible, modulo
  23: //!    Helmholtz smoothing) — i.e. no new information appears that
  24: //!    wasn't already in `ρ`.
  25: 
  26: use ol_coherence_field::pde::sparse_solver::CgConfig;
  27: use ol_coherence_field::{linear_source, solve_helmholtz, GraphLaplacian};
  28: 
  29: #[test]
  30: fn linear_source_response_scales_linearly() {
  31:     let n = 10;
  32:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  33:     // Build a small connected graph (path + a few extra edges).
  34:     for i in 0..n - 1 {
  35:         g.add_edge(i, i + 1, 1.0).unwrap();
  36:     }
  37:     g.add_edge(0, 5, 0.5).unwrap();
  38:     g.add_edge(2, 7, 0.5).unwrap();
  39: 
  40:     let rho: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|i| (i as f64 + 1.0).sqrt()).collect();
  41:     let s1 = linear_source(&rho, 1.0).unwrap();
  42:     let s2 = linear_source(&rho, 2.0).unwrap();
  43: 
  44:     let cfg = CgConfig::default();
  45:     let r1 = solve_helmholtz(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s1, cfg).unwrap();
  46:     let r2 = solve_helmholtz(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s2, cfg).unwrap();
  47: 
  48:     // Linearity: r2 ≈ 2 · r1 elementwise.
  49:     for i in 0..n {
  50:         let expected = 2.0 * r1.field[i];
  51:         assert!(
  52:             (r2.field[i] - expected).abs() < 1e-6,
  53:             "linearity broken at node {i}: {} vs {}",
  54:             r2.field[i],
  55:             expected,
  56:         );
  57:     }
  58: }
  59: 
  60: #[test]
  61: fn no_information_beyond_rho_in_linear_case() {
  62:     // The Helmholtz solution for a linear source is a smoothed
  63:     // version of ρ. Verify that adding a constant offset to ρ
  64:     // produces an output that ONLY differs from the no-offset case
  65:     // by a constant scaling of the same field — no new structure
  66:     // appears.
  67:     let n = 8;
  68:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  69:     for i in 0..n - 1 {
  70:         g.add_edge(i, i + 1, 1.0).unwrap();
  71:     }
  72:     let rho: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|i| (i as f64).sin().abs() + 0.5).collect();
  73:     let rho_offset: Vec<f64> = rho.iter().map(|&r| r + 10.0).collect();
  74:     let s = linear_source(&rho, 1.0).unwrap();
  75:     let s_off = linear_source(&rho_offset, 1.0).unwrap();
  76:     let cfg = CgConfig::default();
  77:     let r = solve_helmholtz(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s, cfg).unwrap();
  78:     let r_off = solve_helmholtz(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s_off, cfg).unwrap();
  79:     // The offset response = original response + uniform shift (the
  80:     // offset is a constant, which the operator maps to a constant).
  81:     let diff: Vec<f64> = r_off
  82:         .field
  83:         .iter()
  84:         .zip(r.field.iter())
  85:         .map(|(a, b)| a - b)
  86:         .collect();
  87:     let mean_diff = diff.iter().sum::<f64>() / (n as f64);
  88:     let max_dev = diff
  89:         .iter()
  90:         .map(|d| (d - mean_diff).abs())
  91:         .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
  92:     assert!(
  93:         max_dev < 1e-6,
  94:         "uniform offset produced non-uniform response: max deviation {max_dev}",
  95:     );
  96: }

   1: //! Property-based PDE invariant tests for the coherence-field solver.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each test verifies a mathematical property the field MUST satisfy
   4: //! regardless of graph shape, source distribution, or `(D, Γ)` choice.
   5: //! These are "no-bug-can-hide" properties — if the solver returns a
   6: //! number that violates one of them, the bug is in the math, not in
   7: //! the calling code.
   8: //!
   9: //! Properties verified:
  10: //!
  11: //! 1. **Linearity in source** — solving with source `αS₁ + βS₂` gives
  12: //!    the same field as `αx₁ + βx₂` where `xᵢ` solve with `Sᵢ`.
  13: //! 2. **Reciprocity** — for symmetric operator, the Green-function
  14: //!    matrix entry `G(i, j) = G(j, i)`. Direct consequence of `L = Lᵀ`.
  15: //! 3. **Sign preservation** — if `S ≥ 0` componentwise, then the
  16: //!    recovered field `δτ_c ≥ 0` componentwise (positive source →
  17: //!    positive field; M-matrix property).
  18: //! 4. **Pure-damping limit** — when the graph has no edges, the
  19: //!    Helmholtz equation collapses to `Γ · δτ_c = S` so `δτ_c = S / Γ`
  20: //!    exactly.
  21: //! 5. **Symmetric source → symmetric field** — for a graph with a
  22: //!    reflection automorphism `σ`, if `S(σ(i)) = S(i)` for all `i`,
  23: //!    then the recovered field satisfies the same symmetry.
  24: 
  25: use ol_coherence_field::{
  26:     pde::CgConfig, solve_helmholtz, FieldError, GraphLaplacian, HelmholtzSolver,
  27: };
  28: use proptest::prelude::*;
  29: 
  30: /// Build a small random connected ring graph with optional chords.
  31: /// Parameters in domain: `n` ∈ [4, 32], `chord_prob` ∈ [0, 1].
  32: fn arb_ring_with_chords() -> impl Strategy<Value = GraphLaplacian> {
  33:     (4_usize..=32_usize, 0u64..=255).prop_map(|(n, seed)| {
  34:         let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  35:         // Ring backbone — guarantees connectivity.
  36:         for i in 0..n {
  37:             let j = (i + 1) % n;
  38:             g.add_edge(i, j, 1.0).unwrap();
  39:         }
  40:         // Pseudo-random chords driven by the seed.
  41:         let mut s = seed.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9);
  42:         for i in 0..n {
  43:             s = s
  44:                 .wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005)
  45:                 .wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
  46:             if (s >> 56) < 64 {
  47:                 let j = ((s >> 32) as usize) % n;
  48:                 if i != j {
  49:                     let _ = g.add_edge(i, j, 0.5);
  50:                 }
  51:             }
  52:         }
  53:         g
  54:     })
  55: }
  56: 
  57: fn arb_source(n: usize) -> impl Strategy<Value = Vec<f64>> {
  58:     proptest::collection::vec(-5.0_f64..=5.0_f64, n)
  59: }
  60: 
  61: fn solve_for(graph: &GraphLaplacian, d: f64, gamma: f64, s: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64> {
  62:     let cfg = CgConfig {
  63:         max_iter: 5_000,
  64:         tolerance: 1e-10,
  65:     };
  66:     solve_helmholtz(graph, d, gamma, s, cfg)
  67:         .expect("CG must converge for well-conditioned operator")
  68:         .field
  69: }

  74:     /// Linearity: x(αS₁ + βS₂) = α·x(S₁) + β·x(S₂).
  75:     #[test]
  76:     fn linearity_in_source(
  77:         graph in arb_ring_with_chords(),
  78:         seed in 0u64..u64::MAX,
  79:         alpha in -3.0f64..3.0,
  80:         beta in -3.0f64..3.0,
  81:     ) {
  82:         let n = graph.n();
  83:         let mut prng = seed;
  84:         let mut next = || {
  85:             prng = prng.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
  86:             ((prng >> 32) as i64 as f64) / (i32::MAX as f64) * 5.0
  87:         };
  88:         let s1: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|_| next()).collect();
  89:         let s2: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|_| next()).collect();
  90:         let combo: Vec<f64> = (0..n).map(|i| alpha * s1[i] + beta * s2[i]).collect();
  91:         let x1 = solve_for(&graph, 1.0, 0.5, &s1);
  92:         let x2 = solve_for(&graph, 1.0, 0.5, &s2);
  93:         let x_combo = solve_for(&graph, 1.0, 0.5, &combo);
  94:         for i in 0..n {
  95:             let predicted = alpha * x1[i] + beta * x2[i];
  96:             let err = (predicted - x_combo[i]).abs();
  97:             prop_assert!(
  98:                 err < 1e-5,
  99:                 "linearity violated at node {i}: predicted={predicted:.6}, got={:.6}",
 100:                 x_combo[i]
 101:             );
 102:         }
 103:     }

 105:     /// Reciprocity: G(i, j) = G(j, i) where G is the Green function
 106:     /// for the symmetric operator (Γ·I + D·L). Verified by solving
 107:     /// with a unit-source at i and reading off the j-th component,
 108:     /// vs solving with unit-source at j and reading off the i-th.
 109:     #[test]
 110:     fn reciprocity_of_green_function(
 111:         graph in arb_ring_with_chords(),
 112:         i_seed in 0u64..u64::MAX,
 113:         j_seed in 0u64..u64::MAX,
 114:     ) {
 115:         let n = graph.n();
 116:         let i = (i_seed as usize) % n;
 117:         let j = (j_seed as usize) % n;
 118:         prop_assume!(i != j);
 119:         let mut s_i = vec![0.0; n];
 120:         let mut s_j = vec![0.0; n];
 121:         s_i[i] = 1.0;
 122:         s_j[j] = 1.0;
 123:         let x_from_i = solve_for(&graph, 1.0, 0.5, &s_i);
 124:         let x_from_j = solve_for(&graph, 1.0, 0.5, &s_j);
 125:         let g_ij = x_from_i[j];
 126:         let g_ji = x_from_j[i];
 127:         prop_assert!(
 128:             (g_ij - g_ji).abs() < 1e-6,
 129:             "reciprocity violated: G({i},{j})={g_ij:.6}, G({j},{i})={g_ji:.6}"
 130:         );
 131:     }

 133:     /// Sign preservation: S ≥ 0 ⟹ δτ_c ≥ 0. The Helmholtz operator
 134:     /// (Γ·I + D·L) is an M-matrix; its inverse has all non-negative

 136:     /// output.
 137:     #[test]

 147:         }).collect();

 153:                 x[i],
 154:                 s.iter().cloned().fold(0.0_f64, f64::max),

 214: /// Round-trip property: solving and then applying the operator to the
 215: /// recovered field should reproduce the source to within CG tolerance.
 216: /// Checks (Γ·I + D·L)·x ≈ S after `solve_helmholtz`.
 217: #[test]
 218: fn solve_round_trips_through_operator() {
 219:     let n = 32;
 220:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
 221:     for i in 0..n - 1 {
 222:         g.add_edge(i, i + 1, 1.0).unwrap();
 223:     }
 224:     for i in (0..n).step_by(5) {
 225:         let j = (i + 11) % n;
 226:         if i != j {
 227:             let _ = g.add_edge(i, j, 0.5);
 228:         }
 229:     }
 230:     let d = 1.0;
 231:     let gamma = 0.5;
 232:     let mut s = vec![0.0; n];
 233:     s[n / 3] = 1.0;
 234:     s[2 * n / 3] = -0.7;
 235:     let cfg = CgConfig {
 236:         max_iter: 5_000,
 237:         tolerance: 1e-10,
 238:     };
 239:     let result = solve_helmholtz(&g, d, gamma, &s, cfg).unwrap();
 240:     // Compute (Γ·I + D·L) · x and check we recover S.
 241:     let mut ax = vec![0.0; n];
 242:     g.matvec(&result.field, &mut ax);
 243:     let mut residual = 0.0_f64;
 244:     for i in 0..n {
 245:         let lhs = gamma * result.field[i] + d * ax[i];
 246:         residual += (lhs - s[i]).powi(2);
 247:     }
 248:     residual = residual.sqrt();
 249:     assert!(
 250:         residual < 1e-6,
 251:         "round-trip residual too large: {residual:.3e}"
 252:     );
 253: }

 255: /// HelmholtzSolver invariant: identical (graph, d, gamma, source)

 270:     let r1 = solver.solve(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s, cfg).unwrap();
 271:     let r2 = solver.solve(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s, cfg).unwrap();
 272:     let r3 = solver.solve(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s, cfg).unwrap();
 273:     for i in 0..n {
 274:         let d12 = (r1.field[i] - r2.field[i]).abs();
 275:         let d23 = (r2.field[i] - r3.field[i]).abs();
 276:         assert!(d12 < 1e-9, "r1 != r2 at node {i}: {d12:.3e}");
 277:         assert!(d23 < 1e-9, "r2 != r3 at node {i}: {d23:.3e}");
 278:     }

   1: //! Phase E acceptance gate: **reaction-diffusion convergence.**
   2: //!
   3: //! Verifies the timestepping form of the reaction-diffusion PDE
   4: //! converges to the same steady-state as the direct Helmholtz solve.
   5: //! Both should agree to within tight numerical tolerance.
   6: 
   7: use ol_coherence_field::pde::reaction_diffusion::{solve_reaction_diffusion_steady, EulerConfig};
   8: use ol_coherence_field::pde::sparse_solver::CgConfig;
   9: use ol_coherence_field::{solve_helmholtz, GraphLaplacian};
