  11: #[test]
  12: fn euler_steady_state_matches_helmholtz_solve() {
  13:     // Random-ish small graph + source. The two solvers must agree.
  14:     let n = 6;
  15:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  16:     g.add_edge(0, 1, 1.0).unwrap();
  17:     g.add_edge(1, 2, 1.0).unwrap();
  18:     g.add_edge(2, 3, 2.0).unwrap();
  19:     g.add_edge(3, 4, 1.0).unwrap();
  20:     g.add_edge(4, 5, 1.0).unwrap();
  21:     g.add_edge(0, 5, 0.5).unwrap();
  22: 
  23:     let source = vec![1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, -1.0, 0.0];
  24:     let d = 1.0;
  25:     let gamma = 0.3;
  26: 
  27:     let euler =
  28:         solve_reaction_diffusion_steady(&g, d, gamma, &source, EulerConfig::default()).unwrap();
  29:     let helm = solve_helmholtz(&g, d, gamma, &source, CgConfig::default()).unwrap();
  30: 
  31:     // Compare elementwise.
  32:     for i in 0..n {
  33:         let abs_err = (euler.field[i] - helm.field[i]).abs();
  34:         let rel_err = abs_err / helm.field[i].abs().max(1e-9);
  35:         assert!(
  36:             abs_err < 1e-5 && rel_err < 1e-4,
  37:             "node {i}: euler = {}, helm = {}, abs_err = {abs_err}, rel_err = {rel_err}",
  38:             euler.field[i],
  39:             helm.field[i],
  40:         );
  41:     }
  42: }

  44: #[test]
  45: fn helmholtz_residual_below_1e_minus_6() {
  46:     // The Phase E gate calls for spectral residual < 1e-6.
  47:     let n = 16;
  48:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  49:     // Build a 4×4 grid.
  50:     for r in 0..4 {
  51:         for c in 0..4 {
  52:             let idx = r * 4 + c;
  53:             if c < 3 {
  54:                 g.add_edge(idx, idx + 1, 1.0).unwrap();
  55:             }
  56:             if r < 3 {
  57:                 g.add_edge(idx, idx + 4, 1.0).unwrap();
  58:             }
  59:         }
  60:     }
  61:     let mut source = vec![0.0; n];
  62:     source[0] = 1.0;
  63:     source[n - 1] = -1.0;
  64:     let r = solve_helmholtz(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &source, CgConfig::default()).unwrap();
  65:     assert!(
  66:         r.residual < 1e-6,

  68:         r.residual

   1: //! Phase E scale benchmarks. The plan specifies the field solver
   2: //! must converge on swarms up to 10,000 peers. These tests time the
   3: //! solve + assert the spectral residual gate.
   4: 
   5: use std::time::Instant;
   6: 
   7: use ol_coherence_field::pde::sparse_solver::CgConfig;
   8: use ol_coherence_field::{identity_dual_source, solve_helmholtz, GraphLaplacian};
   9: 
  10: /// Build a small-world graph: ring + every Kth shortcut.
  11: fn small_world(n: usize, every_k: usize) -> GraphLaplacian {
  12:     let mut g = GraphLaplacian::new(n);
  13:     for i in 0..n {
  14:         let j = (i + 1) % n;
  15:         g.add_edge(i, j, 1.0).unwrap();
  16:     }
  17:     for i in (0..n).step_by(every_k) {
  18:         let j = (i + n / 3) % n;
  19:         if i != j {
  20:             g.add_edge(i, j, 0.5).unwrap();
  21:         }
  22:     }
  23:     g
  24: }
  25: 
  26: fn synthetic_sources(n: usize, fragile_band: std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Vec<f64> {
  27:     let density: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
  28:         .map(|i| if fragile_band.contains(&i) { 0.05 } else { 1.0 })
  29:         .collect();
  30:     let flux: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
  31:         .map(|i| if fragile_band.contains(&i) { 0.02 } else { 0.7 })
  32:         .collect();
  33:     identity_dual_source(&density, &flux, 0.5, 0.5).unwrap()
  34: }
  35: 
  36: #[test]
  37: fn scale_1000_peers_converges_under_100ms() {
  38:     let n = 1_000;
  39:     let g = small_world(n, 7);
  40:     let s = synthetic_sources(n, 400..600);
  41:     let cfg = CgConfig {
  42:         max_iter: 5_000,
  43:         tolerance: 1e-6,
  44:     };
  45:     let t = Instant::now();
  46:     let r = solve_helmholtz(&g, 1.0, 0.5, &s, cfg).expect("converges");
  47:     let elapsed = t.elapsed();
  48:     eprintln!(
  49:         "1k peers: {} CG iters, residual {:.3e}, wall time {:.3?}",
  50:         r.iterations, r.residual, elapsed
  51:     );
  52:     assert!(r.converged, "did not converge");
  53:     assert!(r.residual < 1e-6);
  54:     assert!(
  55:         elapsed.as_millis() < 1000,
  56:         "1k peer solve took {:.3?} — production hot path budget is 1 second",
  57:         elapsed
  58:     );
  59: }
  60: 
  61: #[test]

   1: # `ol_confidential` (Row 10 — confidential-compute daemon) microbenchmarks
   2: 
   3: Captured against `0.21.0-alpha.0` on Windows 11 Intel host, release
   4: profile (`cargo bench -p ol_confidential --bench confidential_bench`).
   5: 
   6: ## Software baseline
   7: 
   8: | Benchmark                            | Time     | Notes                                             |
   9: |---                                   |---       |---                                                |
  10: | `confidential::seal_master`          | 1.19 µs  | ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypt of 32 B + 12 B nonce    |
  11: | `confidential::derive_child`         | 2.53 µs  | unseal master + BLAKE3-keyed derive + reseal      |
  12: | `confidential::sealed_sign`          | 362 µs   | unseal + Ed25519 sign + ML-DSA-65 sign + zeroize  |
  13: | `confidential::attest_issue`         | 894 µs   | single-unseal pair-derive + sign over 2 KB doc transcript |
  14: | `confidential::attest_verify`        | 60 µs    | hybrid sig verify + transcript rebuild            |
  15: 
  16: ## Real-hardware Windows TPM (NCrypt PCP)
  17: 
  18: `cargo bench -p ol_confidential --features windows-tpm --bench windows_tpm_bench`.
  19: 
  20: Same Win11 host as above, talking to the local TPM 2.0 via the
  21: Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider in user mode (no admin required).
  22: 
  23: | Benchmark                                       | Time     | Notes                                             |
  24: |---                                              |---       |---                                                |
  25: | `confidential::tpm_public_blob_export`          | 21 µs    | NCryptExportKey, cached metadata round trip       |
  26: | `confidential::tpm_ecdsa_p256_sign`             | 35 ms    | TPM-internal ECDSA-P256 sign over a 32 B digest   |
  27: | `confidential::tpm_platform_quote_produce`      | 34 ms    | public_blob + sign + wire-format envelope         |
  28: 
  29: The TPM sign is ~100× slower than software ECDSA on the same host —
  30: that's the price of holding the key inside the chip with kernel-
  31: gated access. The numbers are bounded by the TPM's TIS bus speed,
  32: not the curve math.
  33: 
  34: ## What this means for the daemon
  35: 
  36: - **Sealed master at rest is free**: 1.19 µs. Boot can seal at process
  37:   start and the cost is invisible.
  38: - **Child derivation under 3 µs**: per-day ratchet across 365 days
  39:   totals < 1 ms even if recomputed on every cold boot.
  40: - **Sealed sign matches Row 1 sign cost (~250 µs)** with the ~100 µs
  41:   extra for unseal + keygen + zeroize.
  42: - **Attestation verify cost = single hybrid verify (~50 µs) + 10 µs
  43:   transcript rebuild**. A peer can re-verify on every reconnect
  44:   without breaking a sweat.
  45: - **TPM-rooted attestation costs ~35 ms** dominated by the TPM ECDSA
  46:   sign. The TPM is on a slow bus; this is normal. Daemons should
  47:   issue at most a few attestations per peer per session, not per
  48:   message.
  49: 
  50: ## Repro
  51: 
  52: ```text
  53: cargo bench -p ol_confidential --bench confidential_bench
  54: ```

   1: # `ol_confidential` — Row 10 of the Coherence Mesh
   2: 
   3: **Confidential-compute daemon.** Where hardware supports it, the
   4: daemon runs (or at minimum the key-handling subsystem runs) inside a
   5: hardware-attested enclave. Even local malware can't extract identity
   6: keys.
   7: 
   8: ## Layered model
   9: 
  10: ```
  11:                         ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
  12:                         │       AttestationDoc (PQ-hybrid)   │
  13:                         │  master_sig over canonical bytes   │
  14:                         └──────────┬─────────────────────────┘
  15:                                    │ commits to →
  16:                                    ▼
  17:                         ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
  18:                         │      platform_quote (per-tag)      │
  19:                         ├────────────────────────────────────┤
  20:                         │ Software baseline:  empty bytes    │
  21:                         │ WindowsTpm:         ECDSA-P256 sig │
  22:                         │                     by TPM-resident│
  23:                         │                     attestation key│
  24:                         │ AppleSecureEnclave: future ship    │
  25:                         │ IntelSgx / SEV-SNP: future ship    │
  26:                         └────────────────────────────────────┘
  27: ```
  28: 
  29: The master hybrid signature (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) covers the FULL
  30: canonical transcript, which includes the `platform_quote` bytes.
  31: So:
  32: 
  33: - A peer that pins only the master VK still gets tamper detection
  34:   on the platform_quote (master sig fails if quote is swapped).
  35: - A peer that ALSO validates the platform_quote gets a
  36:   hardware-bound chain (this doc was minted on the specific TPM).
  37: 
  38: ## Tiers
  39: 
  40: ```rust
  41: pub enum ConfidentialTier {
  42:     Software,         // production baseline
  43:     HardwareBound,    // key in TPM / Secure Enclave / StrongBox
  44:     HardwareAttested, // + vendor-issued attestation chain
  45: }
  46: ```
  47: 
  48: ## Backends
  49: 
  50: | Tag | Backend | Status |
  51: |---|---|---|
  52: | `Software` | ChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing under per-process ephemeral key, Zeroize on drop | ✓ shipped |
  53: | `WindowsTpm` | NCrypt Platform Crypto Provider, ECDSA-P256 in the TPM, user-mode, no admin | ✓ shipped (this crate, `windows-tpm` feature) |
  54: | `AppleSecureEnclave` | `security-framework` crate | future ship |
  55: | `AndroidStrongBox` | Android KeyStore + StrongBox attestation | future ship |
  56: | `IntelSgx` | `fortanix-sgx` | future ship |
  57: | `AmdSevSnp` | `sev-snp-tools` | future ship |
  58: | `ArmTrustZone` | OP-TEE TA | future ship |
  59: 
  60: ## Threat coverage
  61: 
  62: | Threat | Software | WindowsTpm |
  63: |---|:-:|:-:|
  64: | T-LOCAL-MAL-USER (user-mode malware grabs key from process memory) | ✓ | ✓ |
  65: | T-REMOTE-IMPERSONATE (replay attestation across challenges) | ✓ | ✓ |
  66: | T-REMOTE-IMPERSONATE-PHYSICAL (replay attestation across hosts) | ✓ via field witness | ✓ via TPM identity binding |
  67: | T-LOCAL-MAL-ROOT (root malware reads /proc/mem, kernel debugger) | ✗ | ✓ for platform_quote ECDSA key; ✗ for master PQ-hybrid (TPM can't sign PQ) |
  68: 
  69: ## Quickstart
  70: 
  71: ```rust
  72: use ol_confidential::{SoftwareProvider, ConfidentialProvider, fresh_attestation_nonce, verify_attestation};
  73: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  74: 
  75: let provider = SoftwareProvider::generate(&mut OsRng);
  76: let seed = [0x42u8; 32];  // your master seed
  77: let sealed = provider.seal_master(&seed)?;
  78: let nonce = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);
  79: let doc = provider.attest(&sealed, nonce, now_unix, now_unix + 30, None)?;
  80: // Send `doc` to peer; peer calls verify_attestation(&doc, &nonce, None, peer_now).
  81: ```
  82: 
  83: With Windows TPM:
  84: 
  85: ```rust
  86: #[cfg(all(target_os = "windows", feature = "windows-tpm"))]
  87: use ol_confidential::windows_tpm::{TpmAttestationKey, attest_with_tpm, verify_attestation_with_tpm};
  88: 
  89: let tpm = TpmAttestationKey::acquire_or_create("OL-confidential-attestation-v1")?;
  90: let doc = attest_with_tpm(&provider, &sealed, &tpm, nonce, now_unix, now_unix + 30, None)?;
  91: let tpm_pub = verify_attestation_with_tpm(&doc, &nonce, None, peer_now)?;  // returns TPM pub-blob for pinning
  92: ```
  93: 
  94: See `BENCH_RESULTS.md` for performance numbers and `docs/formal/confidential_attestation.tla` for the design-time TLA+ spec.

   1: //! Remote attestation doc — peer-verifiable proof that the daemon
   2: //! is running under a specific [`crate::ConfidentialProvider`] and
   3: //! that its master identity is fresh-bound to the peer's nonce.
   4: //!
   5: //! ## Wire shape
   6: //!
   7: //! ```text
   8: //! AttestationDoc {
   9: //!     provider_tag       : u8   — which provider produced this
  10: //!     master_vk          : 1984 — Ed25519 (32) || ML-DSA-65 VK
  11: //!     peer_nonce         : 32   — peer-supplied nonce (anti-replay)
  12: //!     issued_unix        : 8    — issue wall-clock
  13: //!     deadline_unix      : 8    — `<= issued + FRESHNESS_WINDOW`
  14: //!     field_witness_cmt  : 33   — option<32> BLAKE3 commit on field
  15: //!     platform_quote_len : u32  — bytes that follow
  16: //!     platform_quote     : N    — provider-specific (SGX quote, etc.)
  17: //!     master_sig         : 3357 — hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA sig
  18: //! }
  19: //! ```
  20: //!
  21: //! The master's hybrid signature covers a canonical transcript of
  22: //! every field except itself, so any wire tamper invalidates the
  23: //! signature and the verifier rejects.
  24: //!
  25: //! ## Replay defense
  26: //!
  27: //! - `peer_nonce` MUST be a freshly generated 32-byte value the peer
  28: //!   sent over a fresh channel; the verifier confirms it matches the
  29: //!   nonce it sent.
  30: //! - `deadline_unix` MUST be `<= issued_unix + ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS`
  31: //!   (default 30s); the verifier rejects any doc past its deadline.
  32: //! - `field_witness_commitment` MAY bind the doc to a coherence-field
  33: //!   witness so the doc is non-transferable across hosts (Row 9
  34: //!   field-binding extended to attestation).
  35: 
  36: use blake3::Hasher;
  37: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN, HYBRID_VK_LEN};
  38: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  39: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  40: 
  41: use crate::errors::{ConfidentialError, ConfidentialResult};
  42: use crate::provider::ProviderTag;
  43: 
  44: /// Length of an attestation peer-nonce in bytes.
  45: pub const ATTESTATION_NONCE_LEN: usize = 32;
  46: 
  47: /// Per-doc peer-supplied nonce. The peer generates this and sends it
  48: /// to the prover; the prover binds it into the attestation transcript
  49: /// so a captured doc can't be replayed against a later peer challenge.
  50: pub type AttestationNonce = [u8; ATTESTATION_NONCE_LEN];
  51: 
  52: /// Max allowed `deadline_unix - issued_unix`. Bounds the replay
  53: /// window — beyond 30s an attacker can record a fresh attestation and
  54: /// race it against another verifier's challenge. Tighter is safer.
  55: pub const ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS: u64 = 30;
  56: 
  57: /// Audit I3 May 2026 — maximum tolerated clock skew between issuer
  58: /// and verifier. If `doc.issued_unix > now_unix + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS`,
  59: /// the doc is rejected — a forward-skewed issuer clock could
  60: /// otherwise issue docs that won't appear "expired" to a verifier with
  61: /// a backward-skewed clock until much later. Bounding the issuer's
  62: /// future-projection keeps the freshness window honest in absolute
  63: /// wall-clock terms.
  64: pub const ATTESTATION_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS: u64 = 5;
  65: 
  66: /// Audit I3 May 2026 — hard floor on how stale a doc may be at
  67: /// verify time, independent of `deadline_unix`. A doc whose
  68: /// `issued_unix` is more than this many seconds before `now_unix`
  69: /// is rejected even if its deadline somehow lies in the future
  70: /// (clock-skew adversary). Set to 24 hours to absorb daylight-
  71: /// savings and zone-config errors while still rejecting ancient
  72: /// replays.
  73: pub const ATTESTATION_MAX_AGE_SECS: u64 = 24 * 3600;
  74: 
  75: /// Domain-separation prefix for the canonical attestation transcript
  76: /// — distinct from every other transcript-builder in the workspace.
  77: ///
  78: /// Bumped to `-v2` on 2026-05-14 (audit C1) when the issuer's SDP
  79: /// pubkey was added to the transcript. Old `-v1` docs are unforgeable
  80: /// under the new domain so they cannot be replayed against a `-v2`
  81: /// verifier; old verifiers will reject `-v2` docs the same way.
  82: pub const ATTESTATION_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-confidential-attestation-v2";
  83: 
  84: /// Length of the issuer's SDP-layer Ed25519 pubkey (raw, no header).
  85: pub const ISSUER_SDP_PUBKEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  86: 
  87: /// Type alias for the issuer's SDP-layer Ed25519 pubkey. This is the
  88: /// 32-byte raw Ed25519 verifying-key the issuer uses to sign the
  89: /// WebRTC SDP offer/answer envelope (NOT the master VK). The
  90: /// attestation transcript binds the master signature to THIS
  91: /// SDP-identity so a peer cannot lift an attestation off one channel
  92: /// and replay it against another channel that authenticates a
  93: /// different SDP key (audit C1 May 2026).
  94: pub type IssuerSdpPubkey = [u8; ISSUER_SDP_PUBKEY_LEN];
  95: 
  96: /// Domain prefix for the field-witness commitment leaf inside the doc.
  97: pub const ATTESTATION_FIELD_WITNESS_DOMAIN: &[u8] =
  98:     b"OL-confidential-field-witness-commitment-v1";
  99: 
 100: /// Signed attestation envelope.
 101: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 102: pub struct AttestationDoc {
 103:     /// Which provider produced this doc.
 104:     pub provider_tag: ProviderTag,
 105:     /// Master verifying key — the peer pins this out-of-band.
 106:     pub master_vk: HybridVerifyingKey,
 107:     /// The peer's challenge nonce.
 108:     pub peer_nonce: AttestationNonce,
 109:     /// Issuance wall-clock (seconds).
 110:     pub issued_unix: u64,
 111:     /// Expiry wall-clock (seconds). Must be `> issued_unix` and
 112:     /// `<= issued_unix + ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS`.
 113:     pub deadline_unix: u64,
 114:     /// Optional BLAKE3 commitment over the local coherence-field
 115:     /// witness. When present, the verifier checks the commitment
 116:     /// against its own witness — useful for refusing to accept docs
 117:     /// that were minted at a different physical location.
 118:     pub field_witness_commitment: Option<[u8; 32]>,
 119:     /// Provider-specific platform quote bytes. Empty for the
 120:     /// software provider; non-empty for hardware providers (SGX
 121:     /// quote, TPM2 quote, etc.).
 122:     pub platform_quote: Vec<u8>,
 123:     /// The issuer's SDP-layer Ed25519 pubkey (raw 32 bytes). The
 124:     /// master signature commits to this binding so a verifier can
 125:     /// confirm the master at the OTHER end is endorsing the very
 126:     /// channel identity the verifier is talking to — defeats the
 127:     /// "Alice attests with someone else's master_vk under her own
 128:     /// SDP identity" identity-confusion attack (audit C1).
 129:     pub issuer_sdp_pubkey: IssuerSdpPubkey,
 130:     /// Hybrid signature over the canonical transcript, by the master.
 131:     pub master_sig: Vec<u8>,
 132: }
 133: 
 134: /// Build the canonical bytes a master signs to issue an
 135: /// [`AttestationDoc`]. Pure function: identical inputs produce
 136: /// identical output bytes.
 137: ///
 138: /// `issuer_sdp_pubkey` is the 32-byte Ed25519 verifying-key of the
 139: /// issuer's SDP-layer identity (the key that signs the WebRTC
 140: /// offer/answer envelope). Mixing it into the transcript binds the
 141: /// master signature to "this SDP identity" so a verifier rejects
 142: /// any attestation whose embedded SDP pubkey does not match the
 143: /// channel they are actually talking to (audit C1).
 144: #[must_use]
 145: pub fn canonical_attestation_transcript(
 146:     provider_tag: ProviderTag,
 147:     master_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey,
 148:     peer_nonce: &AttestationNonce,
 149:     issued_unix: u64,
 150:     deadline_unix: u64,
 151:     field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 152:     platform_quote: &[u8],
 153:     issuer_sdp_pubkey: &IssuerSdpPubkey,
 154: ) -> Vec<u8> {
 155:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 156:     h.update(ATTESTATION_DOMAIN);
 157:     h.update(&[provider_tag.as_u8()]);
 158:     h.update(&master_vk.to_bytes());
 159:     h.update(peer_nonce);
 160:     h.update(&issued_unix.to_be_bytes());
 161:     h.update(&deadline_unix.to_be_bytes());
 162:     match field_witness {
 163:         None => {
 164:             h.update(&[0u8]);
 165:         }
 166:         Some(witness) => {
 167:             h.update(&[1u8]);
 168:             let mut wh = Hasher::new();
 169:             wh.update(ATTESTATION_FIELD_WITNESS_DOMAIN);
 170:             wh.update(witness);
 171:             h.update(wh.finalize().as_bytes());
 172:         }
 173:     }
 174:     let qlen = u32::try_from(platform_quote.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 175:     h.update(&qlen.to_be_bytes());
 176:     h.update(platform_quote);
 177:     // Issuer-SDP-pubkey leaf. Fixed-length, so no length prefix.
 178:     h.update(issuer_sdp_pubkey);
 179:     h.finalize().as_bytes().to_vec()
 180: }
 181: 
 182: /// Generate a fresh attestation nonce. Convenience wrapper for peers
 183: /// constructing a challenge.
 184: #[must_use]
 185: pub fn fresh_attestation_nonce<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> AttestationNonce {
 186:     let mut n = [0u8; ATTESTATION_NONCE_LEN];
 187:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut n);
 188:     n
 189: }
 190: 
 191: /// Convenience helper for callers that hold a [`ol_pqsig::HybridSigningKey`]
 192: /// directly (e.g., the Phase-2 wired daemon path). Most callers go
 193: /// through [`crate::ConfidentialProvider::attest`] instead.
 194: ///
 195: /// # Errors
 196: /// Returns `AttestationBadFreshnessWindow` if `deadline_unix <= issued_unix`,
 197: /// `AttestationFreshnessWindowTooWide` if the window exceeds policy,
 198: /// or `PqSig` if the signing primitive errs.
 199: pub fn sign_attestation(
 200:     signing_key: &ol_pqsig::HybridSigningKey,
 201:     provider_tag: ProviderTag,
 202:     peer_nonce: AttestationNonce,
 203:     issued_unix: u64,
 204:     deadline_unix: u64,
 205:     field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 206:     platform_quote: Vec<u8>,
 207:     issuer_sdp_pubkey: IssuerSdpPubkey,
 208: ) -> ConfidentialResult<AttestationDoc> {
 209:     if deadline_unix <= issued_unix {
 210:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationBadFreshnessWindow {
 211:             issued_unix,
 212:             deadline_unix,
 213:         });
 214:     }
 215:     let window = deadline_unix - issued_unix;
 216:     if window > ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS {
 217:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationFreshnessWindowTooWide {
 218:             got: window,
 219:             max: ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS,
 220:         });
 221:     }
 222:     let master_vk = signing_key.verifying_key();
 223:     let transcript = canonical_attestation_transcript(
 224:         provider_tag,
 225:         &master_vk,
 226:         &peer_nonce,
 227:         issued_unix,
 228:         deadline_unix,
 229:         field_witness,
 230:         &platform_quote,
 231:         &issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 232:     );
 233:     let sig = signing_key.sign(&transcript)?;
 234:     Ok(AttestationDoc {
 235:         provider_tag,
 236:         master_vk,
 237:         peer_nonce,
 238:         issued_unix,
 239:         deadline_unix,
 240:         field_witness_commitment: field_witness.map(|w| {
 241:             let mut h = Hasher::new();
 242:             h.update(ATTESTATION_FIELD_WITNESS_DOMAIN);
 243:             h.update(w);
 244:             *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 245:         }),
 246:         platform_quote,
 247:         issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 248:         master_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 249:     })
 250: }
 251: 
 252: /// Verify an attestation doc.
 253: ///
 254: /// - `expected_peer_nonce`: the nonce THIS verifier sent in the
 255: ///   challenge round — MUST match the doc's `peer_nonce`.
 256: /// - `now_unix`: verifier's wall clock; must be `<= deadline_unix`.
 257: /// - `expected_field_witness`: if `Some`, the local coherence-field
 258: ///   witness — the doc's commitment must match.
 259: /// - `min_tier`: minimum provider tier the verifier requires; the
 260: ///   doc's `provider_tag` must map to a tier `>= min_tier`.
 261: /// - `expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey`: the SDP-layer Ed25519 pubkey the
 262: ///   verifier is actually talking to on the channel. The doc's
 263: ///   `issuer_sdp_pubkey` MUST byte-equal this — defeats the
 264: ///   "Alice attests with someone else's master under her own SDP
 265: ///   identity" identity-confusion attack (audit C1).
 266: ///
 267: /// # Errors
 268: /// Returns a typed error if any check fails: peer-nonce mismatch,
 269: /// expired, freshness window too wide, master-sig invalid,
 270: /// field-witness mismatch, provider tier too low, or
 271: /// `AttestationIssuerSdpPubkeyMismatch` if the doc's claimed SDP
 272: /// pubkey doesn't match the channel identity.
 273: pub fn verify_attestation(
 274:     doc: &AttestationDoc,
 275:     expected_peer_nonce: &AttestationNonce,
 276:     expected_field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 277:     now_unix: u64,
 278:     min_tier: crate::tier::ConfidentialTier,
 279:     expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey: &IssuerSdpPubkey,
 280: ) -> ConfidentialResult<()> {
 281:     // (0) Sanity shape.
 282:     if doc.master_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 283:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationMasterSigFail);
 284:     }
 285:     if doc.deadline_unix <= doc.issued_unix {
 286:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationBadFreshnessWindow {
 287:             issued_unix: doc.issued_unix,
 288:             deadline_unix: doc.deadline_unix,
 289:         });
 290:     }
 291:     let window = doc.deadline_unix - doc.issued_unix;
 292:     if window > ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS {
 293:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationFreshnessWindowTooWide {
 294:             got: window,
 295:             max: ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS,
 296:         });
 297:     }
 298:     // (1) Peer nonce binds the doc to this challenge.
 299:     if doc.peer_nonce.ct_eq(expected_peer_nonce).unwrap_u8() == 0 {
 300:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationPeerNonceMismatch);
 301:     }
 302:     // (2) Freshness vs verifier clock.
 303:     if now_unix > doc.deadline_unix {
 304:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationExpired {
 305:             deadline_unix: doc.deadline_unix,
 306:             now_unix,
 307:         });
 308:     }
 309:     // (2a) Audit I3 May 2026 — issuer-clock skew bound. Reject docs
 310:     //      whose `issued_unix` lies more than MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS
 311:     //      in the future relative to the verifier. Without this, a
 312:     //      forward-skewed issuer could mint a doc claiming
 313:     //      issued=now+1day, deadline=issued+30s, and the verifier
 314:     //      would refuse to reject for ~24h.
 315:     if doc.issued_unix > now_unix
 316:         && doc.issued_unix - now_unix > ATTESTATION_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS
 317:     {
 318:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationIssuerClockSkew {
 319:             issued_unix: doc.issued_unix,
 320:             now_unix,
 321:             max_skew_secs: ATTESTATION_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS,
 322:         });
 323:     }
 324:     // (2b) Audit I3 May 2026 — hard floor on doc age independent of
 325:     //      `deadline_unix`. Defends against an adversary who crafts a
 326:     //      backward-issued / forward-deadlined doc that survives the
 327:     //      window check but is actually weeks old.
 328:     if doc.issued_unix < now_unix
 329:         && now_unix - doc.issued_unix > ATTESTATION_MAX_AGE_SECS
 330:     {
 331:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationTooOld {
 332:             issued_unix: doc.issued_unix,
 333:             now_unix,
 334:             max_age_secs: ATTESTATION_MAX_AGE_SECS,
 335:         });
 336:     }
 337:     // (3) Field-witness binding. Default-deny semantics (audit L5
 338:     //     May 2026): if the doc CARRIES a field_witness_commitment
 339:     //     but the verifier passes `expected_field_witness=None`,
 340:     //     REJECT. Previously a doc that advertised binding could be
 341:     //     accepted by a verifier that didn't actually check it —
 342:     //     cross-host replay slipped through silently. Callers that
 343:     //     genuinely want to accept an unbound view of a bound doc
 344:     //     must pass a sentinel witness AND consciously evaluate the
 345:     //     mismatch themselves (or just don't issue with binding).
 346:     if let Some(local_witness) = expected_field_witness {
 347:         let local_commitment = {
 348:             let mut h = Hasher::new();
 349:             h.update(ATTESTATION_FIELD_WITNESS_DOMAIN);
 350:             h.update(local_witness);
 351:             *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 352:         };
 353:         match doc.field_witness_commitment {
 354:             None => return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationFieldWitnessMismatch),
 355:             Some(cmt) => {
 356:                 if cmt.ct_eq(&local_commitment).unwrap_u8() == 0 {
 357:                     return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationFieldWitnessMismatch);
 358:                 }
 359:             }
 360:         }
 361:     } else if doc.field_witness_commitment.is_some() {
 362:         // Doc claims a field-witness binding but verifier didn't
 363:         // provide a witness to check it. Default deny (audit L5).
 364:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationFieldWitnessMismatch);
 365:     }
 366:     // (4) Provider-tier floor — enforced HERE, not by callers (audit
 367:     //     finding H4 May 2026). A doc with provider_tag mapping to a
 368:     //     tier below the verifier's required floor is rejected. This
 369:     //     closes the silent-TPM-downgrade vector where a peer pins
 370:     //     master_vk after a HardwareBound attestation and a later
 371:     //     Software-tier doc would otherwise replace it.
 372:     let doc_tier = crate::tier::ConfidentialTier::from_provider_tag(doc.provider_tag);
 373:     if !doc_tier.meets(min_tier) {
 374:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationProviderTierTooLow {
 375:             got: doc_tier,
 376:             min: min_tier,
 377:         });
 378:     }
 379:     // (5) Issuer-SDP-pubkey binding (audit C1). The doc's claimed
 380:     //     SDP pubkey MUST equal the channel identity the verifier
 381:     //     is actually talking to. Constant-time compare.
 382:     if doc
 383:         .issuer_sdp_pubkey
 384:         .ct_eq(expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey)
 385:         .unwrap_u8()
 386:         == 0
 387:     {
 388:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationIssuerSdpPubkeyMismatch);
 389:     }
 390:     // (6) Master signature.
 391:     if doc.master_vk.to_bytes().len() != HYBRID_VK_LEN {
 392:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal("master_vk bad length"));
 393:     }
 394:     let transcript = canonical_attestation_transcript(
 395:         doc.provider_tag,
 396:         &doc.master_vk,
 397:         &doc.peer_nonce,
 398:         doc.issued_unix,
 399:         doc.deadline_unix,
 400:         // Re-derive the witness from the commitment ONLY by trusting
 401:         // the commitment field as authoritative; if the verifier
 402:         // requested witness binding it was checked at step (3).
 403:         // Pass the witness only if the doc claims one.
 404:         if doc.field_witness_commitment.is_some() {
 405:             expected_field_witness
 406:         } else {
 407:             None
 408:         },
 409:         &doc.platform_quote,
 410:         &doc.issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 411:     );
 412:     doc.master_vk
 413:         .verify(&transcript, &doc.master_sig)
 414:         .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::AttestationMasterSigFail)?;
 415:     Ok(())
 416: }

 474:     #[test]
 475:     fn wrong_peer_nonce_rejected() {
 476:         let sk = fresh_key();
 477:         let nonce_a = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_confidential/src/heartbeat.rs", "bytes": 13845, "sha256": "b97b2a1522aa4d616b2159a224f867e7b5ac98627aaf8d44ccf7945f4262d142", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-14T16:05:53.594066+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}

   1: //! Continuous attestation: chained heartbeat docs with a monotonic
   2: //! counter so peers detect downtime / replay / chain-fork attacks.
   3: //!
   4: //! ## How it works
   5: //!
   6: //! A `HeartbeatAttestation` is a normal [`crate::AttestationDoc`]
   7: //! plus a `monotonic_counter` (strictly increasing per master) and a
   8: //! `prev_heartbeat_id` (`BLAKE3` of the previous doc's canonical
   9: //! bytes, forming a hash chain).
  10: //!
  11: //! Peers maintain a small per-master state:
  12: //!
  13: //! - `last_counter` — monotonic counter of the most recent doc seen.
  14: //! - `last_id` — BLAKE3 of that doc's canonical bytes.
  15: //!
  16: //! On receipt, they accept the next doc iff:
  17: //! 1. `monotonic_counter > last_counter` (strict).
  18: //! 2. `prev_heartbeat_id == last_id` (chain continuity).
  19: //! 3. Normal [`crate::verify_attestation`] checks pass.
  20: //!
  21: //! Attacks closed:
  22: //! - **Replay across time**: counter strictly increases.
  23: //! - **Fork attack** (issuer simultaneously emits two distinct
  24: //!   heartbeat chains to different peers): once a peer has seen
  25: //!   `counter = N`, they reject any other `counter = N` from the
  26: //!   same master. The fork is observable.
  27: //! - **Stale-key attack** (attacker holds an old `master_vk` and
  28: //!   forges new attestations): the master sig still has to verify;
  29: //!   chain continuity adds the requirement that the attacker
  30: //!   reproduces the entire prior chain.
  31: 
  32: use blake3::Hasher;
  33: 
  34: use crate::attestation::{AttestationDoc, AttestationNonce};
  35: use crate::errors::{ConfidentialError, ConfidentialResult};
  36: 
  37: /// Domain-separation prefix for the per-doc chain-id digest.
  38: pub const HEARTBEAT_ID_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-confidential-heartbeat-id-v1";
  39: 
  40: /// Domain-separation prefix for the heartbeat-specific transcript
  41: /// the master signs over (carries counter + `prev_id` + the embedded
  42: /// attestation doc transcript bytes).
  43: pub const HEARTBEAT_TRANSCRIPT_DOMAIN: &[u8] =
  44:     b"OL-confidential-heartbeat-transcript-v1";
  45: 
  46: /// Heartbeat-id: a 32-byte BLAKE3 commitment to a doc's canonical
  47: /// form.
  48: pub type HeartbeatId = [u8; 32];
  49: 
  50: /// Compute the heartbeat-id over an [`AttestationDoc`]'s
  51: /// **transcript-equivalent fields**. Used by peers as the
  52: /// `prev_heartbeat_id` for the next doc.
  53: ///
  54: /// Deliberately EXCLUDES `master_sig`: ML-DSA-65 signatures are
  55: /// randomized, so re-signing identical metadata yields different
  56: /// `master_sig` bytes. Hashing the sig into the chain id would
  57: /// make an honest issuer's mid-chain restart look like a fork
  58: /// (audit finding H6 May 2026). The rest of the chain's security
  59: /// is unaffected: `verify_attestation` still requires `master_sig`
  60: /// to validate over the full transcript, and tampering with any
  61: /// transcript-bound field still breaks the chain id.
  62: #[must_use]
  63: pub fn heartbeat_id(doc: &AttestationDoc) -> HeartbeatId {
  64:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  65:     h.update(HEARTBEAT_ID_DOMAIN);
  66:     h.update(&[doc.provider_tag.as_u8()]);
  67:     h.update(&doc.master_vk.to_bytes());
  68:     h.update(&doc.peer_nonce);
  69:     h.update(&doc.issued_unix.to_be_bytes());
  70:     h.update(&doc.deadline_unix.to_be_bytes());
  71:     match doc.field_witness_commitment {
  72:         None => {
  73:             h.update(&[0u8]);
  74:         }
  75:         Some(c) => {
  76:             h.update(&[1u8]);
  77:             h.update(&c);
  78:         }
  79:     }
  80:     h.update(
  81:         &u32::try_from(doc.platform_quote.len())
  82:             .unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
  83:             .to_be_bytes(),
  84:     );
  85:     h.update(&doc.platform_quote);
  86:     // Bind heartbeat-id to the issuer's SDP identity (audit C1
  87:     // May 2026); chain continuity across an SDP-identity change
  88:     // must be detectable.
  89:     h.update(&doc.issuer_sdp_pubkey);
  90:     // NOTE: `doc.master_sig` is intentionally NOT mixed in.
  91:     *h.finalize().as_bytes()
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /// A heartbeat-attached attestation. The `attestation` field is a
  95: /// normal [`AttestationDoc`]; the heartbeat-specific fields chain
  96: /// it to the prior doc and pin a monotonic counter.
  97: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  98: pub struct HeartbeatAttestation {
  99:     /// The underlying attestation doc (verified via the normal path).
 100:     pub attestation: AttestationDoc,
 101:     /// Strictly increasing per-master counter.
 102:     pub monotonic_counter: u64,
 103:     /// BLAKE3 of the previous heartbeat's canonical bytes
 104:     /// (`[0u8; 32]` for the genesis doc).
 105:     pub prev_heartbeat_id: HeartbeatId,
 106: }
 107: 
 108: /// Per-master state a verifier holds. Update on each accepted
 109: /// heartbeat.
 110: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 111: pub struct HeartbeatVerifierState {
 112:     /// Highest counter accepted so far.
 113:     pub last_counter: u64,
 114:     /// Heartbeat-id of the most recent accepted doc.
 115:     pub last_id: HeartbeatId,
 116:     /// `true` if at least one heartbeat has been accepted (genesis
 117:     /// rule: first accepted doc's `prev_heartbeat_id` must be all
 118:     /// zeros).
 119:     pub initialised: bool,
 120: }
 121: 
 122: impl HeartbeatVerifierState {
 123:     /// Fresh state — accepts the first heartbeat with `counter ≥ 1`
 124:     /// and `prev_heartbeat_id = [0; 32]`.
 125:     #[must_use]
 126:     pub fn fresh() -> Self {
 127:         Self {
 128:             last_counter: 0,
 129:             last_id: [0u8; 32],
 130:             initialised: false,
 131:         }
 132:     }
 133: 
 134:     /// Try to accept a new heartbeat. Updates `self` on success.
 135:     ///
 136:     /// # Errors
 137:     /// - [`ConfidentialError::Internal`] for invariant violations
 138:     ///   (counter not increasing, chain break, etc.).
 139:     /// - Any error returned by [`crate::verify_attestation`] for
 140:     ///   the embedded doc.
 141:     pub fn ingest(
 142:         &mut self,
 143:         hb: &HeartbeatAttestation,
 144:         expected_peer_nonce: &AttestationNonce,
 145:         expected_field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 146:         now_unix: u64,
 147:         min_tier: crate::tier::ConfidentialTier,
 148:         expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey: &crate::attestation::IssuerSdpPubkey,
 149:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<()> {
 150:         if !self.initialised {
 151:             if hb.prev_heartbeat_id != [0u8; 32] {
 152:                 return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
 153:                     "first heartbeat must have prev_heartbeat_id = [0; 32]",
 154:                 ));
 155:             }
 156:         } else if hb.prev_heartbeat_id != self.last_id {
 157:             return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
 158:                 "heartbeat chain break — prev_id does not match",
 159:             ));
 160:         }
 161:         if hb.monotonic_counter <= self.last_counter {
 162:             return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
 163:                 "heartbeat counter must strictly increase",
 164:             ));
 165:         }
 166:         // The embedded doc must independently verify.
 167:         crate::verify_attestation(
 168:             &hb.attestation,
 169:             expected_peer_nonce,
 170:             expected_field_witness,
 171:             now_unix,
 172:             min_tier,
 173:             expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 174:         )?;
 175:         // Accept: update state.
 176:         self.last_counter = hb.monotonic_counter;
 177:         self.last_id = heartbeat_id(&hb.attestation);
 178:         self.initialised = true;
 179:         Ok(())
 180:     }
 181: }

 289:     #[test]
 290:     fn fork_is_observable() {
 291:         // Issuer simultaneously emits two distinct heartbeats with
 292:         // the same counter. Each peer accepts only the FIRST one
 293:         // they see; the second is rejected with a chain-break or
 294:         // counter-reuse error. Visible from peer's state, so the
 295:         // fork is observable.
 296:         let (sk, _vk) = HybridSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
 297:         let nonce_a = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);
 298:         let nonce_b = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);
 299: 
 300:         let doc_a = make_doc(&sk, nonce_a, 100);
 301:         let id_a = heartbeat_id(&doc_a);
 302:         let hb_a = HeartbeatAttestation {
 303:             attestation: doc_a,
 304:             monotonic_counter: 1,
 305:             prev_heartbeat_id: [0u8; 32],
 306:         };
 307: 
 308:         // Two distinct heartbeats with same counter = 2 — different
 309:         // nonces, different content. The verifier rejects the second.
 310:         let doc_b1 = make_doc(&sk, nonce_b, 200);
 311:         let doc_b2 = make_doc(&sk, fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng), 200);
 312:         let hb_b1 = HeartbeatAttestation {
 313:             attestation: doc_b1,
 314:             monotonic_counter: 2,
 315:             prev_heartbeat_id: id_a,
 316:         };
 317:         let hb_b2 = HeartbeatAttestation {
 318:             attestation: doc_b2,
 319:             monotonic_counter: 2,
 320:             prev_heartbeat_id: id_a,
 321:         };
 322: 
 323:         let mut state = HeartbeatVerifierState::fresh();
 324:         state.ingest(&hb_a, &nonce_a, None, 110, crate::tier::ConfidentialTier::Software, &TEST_SDP_PUBKEY).unwrap();
 325:         state.ingest(&hb_b1, &nonce_b, None, 210, crate::tier::ConfidentialTier::Software, &TEST_SDP_PUBKEY).unwrap();
 326:         let r = state.ingest(&hb_b2, &hb_b2.attestation.peer_nonce, None, 210, crate::tier::ConfidentialTier::Software, &TEST_SDP_PUBKEY);
 327:         assert!(r.is_err(), "second branch of the fork must be rejected");
 328:     }

 330:     #[test]
 331:     fn heartbeat_id_independent_of_master_sig() {
 332:         // Regression test for audit finding H6 (May 14 2026): the
 333:         // heartbeat_id MUST be a function of the doc's transcript
 334:         // bytes only, NOT the embedded master signature. Otherwise
 335:         // any signature variation across re-issues with identical
 336:         // metadata would make an honest restart look like a fork
 337:         // and break chain continuity.
 338:         let (sk, _vk) = HybridSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
 339:         let nonce = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);
 340:         let doc = make_doc(&sk, nonce, 100);
 341:         let id_with_real_sig = heartbeat_id(&doc);
 342:         // Mutate the master_sig bytes to a totally different value
 343:         // (the doc would now fail `verify_attestation`, but
 344:         // heartbeat_id MUST still be the same — chain continuity
 345:         // depends only on the bound metadata).
 346:         let mut doc_with_other_sig = doc.clone();
 347:         for b in doc_with_other_sig.master_sig.iter_mut() {
 348:             *b ^= 0xFFu8;
 349:         }
 350:         let id_with_other_sig = heartbeat_id(&doc_with_other_sig);
 351:         assert_eq!(
 352:             id_with_real_sig, id_with_other_sig,
 353:             "heartbeat_id must be invariant under master_sig changes (H6 regression)"
 354:         );
 355:     }

   1: //! Row 10 — Confidential-compute daemon.
   2: //!
   3: //! The other nine rows secure data and metadata in motion + at rest. Row
   4: //! 10 closes the last gap: making sure even local malware with root or
   5: //! kernel access can't extract the long-term identity key.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## The threat model this row closes
   8: //!
   9: //! - **T-LOCAL-MAL-USER**: user-mode malware on the device wants to
  10: //!   read the master key from process memory. Software baseline
  11: //!   defeats this by keeping the master sealed at rest and only
  12: //!   unsealing inside a ChaCha20-Poly1305-wrapped ephemeral slot.
  13: //! - **T-LOCAL-MAL-ROOT**: root malware (Linux) / SYSTEM (Windows) /
  14: //!   kexec / cold-boot. Software baseline DOES NOT defeat this — only
  15: //!   real hardware enclaves do. The provider tier
  16: //!   ([`ConfidentialTier::HardwareBound`] / `HardwareAttested`) is
  17: //!   the production answer; this crate provides the trait so per-
  18: //!   platform back-ends slot in without breaking the API.
  19: //! - **T-REMOTE-IMPERSONATE**: a peer wants proof that you're running
  20: //!   in a genuine enclave before exchanging long-term secrets. Solved
  21: //!   by [`attestation::AttestationDoc`] — PQ-hybrid signed by the
  22: //!   master, optionally counter-signed by a hardware quote.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## What ships in Phase 1 (this crate)
  25: //!
  26: //! - The [`ConfidentialProvider`] trait — the platform-agnostic
  27: //!   sealed-op surface (sealed sign / sealed derive child / verifying
  28: //!   key / attestation).
  29: //! - [`software::SoftwareProvider`] — production-grade software
  30: //!   baseline. ChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing under a per-process
  31: //!   ephemeral key, [`Zeroize`] on drop, attestation signed by the
  32: //!   master identity. Tier = [`ConfidentialTier::Software`].
  33: //! - [`attestation::AttestationDoc`] — canonical signed envelope.
  34: //!   PQ-hybrid + freshness window + replay nonce + optional field
  35: //!   witness binding.
  36: //! - [`tier::detect_runtime_tier`] — probe at startup to pick the
  37: //!   best provider available. Today returns
  38: //!   [`ConfidentialTier::Software`]; per-platform detection lands
  39: //!   in Phase 2 commits.
  40: //!
  41: //! ## Composition with other rows
  42: //!
  43: //! - Row 1 (`ol_pqsig`): every sealed signature uses the hybrid
  44: //!   `Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65` primitive. The provider IS the place
  45: //!   where the secret half lives sealed; the public half is
  46: //!   exposed for verification.
  47: //! - Row 8 ([`ol_device_mesh::MasterIdentity`]): the master
  48: //!   identity is the long-term key the provider seals. Sealed
  49: //!   signing replaces direct calls to `master.signing_key().sign()`
  50: //!   in any caller that opts into Row 10.
  51: //! - Row 9 ([`ol_threshold_recovery`]): the same field-witness
  52: //!   machinery binds attestation docs to a coherence-field state, so
  53: //!   an attestation captured at one location is useless at another.
  54: //! - [`ol_hwkey::KeyGuarantee`]: [`ConfidentialTier`] generalises
  55: //!   this. `Software` < `HardwareBound` < `HardwareAttested`.
  56: //!
  57: //! ## What is deliberately NOT in this crate yet
  58: //!
  59: //! - Per-platform hardware back-ends (SGX, SEV-SNP, Secure Enclave,
  60: //!   TPM, `TrustZone`). Each is a separate Phase-2 ship because each
  61: //!   needs platform-specific testing infrastructure.
  62: //! - The Python daemon migration that wires sealed sign into the
  63: //!   running daemon. That lands as a follow-up commit so this row
  64: //!   ships atomically.
  65:

  67: // hardware backends (e.g., `windows_tpm`) where FFI into the OS
  68: // crypto APIs is unavoidable. Those modules document each unsafe
  69: // block and justify why the invariant holds.
  70: #![deny(unsafe_code)]

   1: //! Cross-platform verifier for the TPM-backed `platform_quote`
   2: //! field of [`crate::AttestationDoc`].
   3: //!
   4: //! On the issuing side (Windows + `windows-tpm` feature), the quote
   5: //! is produced by the TPM via `NCrypt` and the bytes have layout
   6: //!
   7: //! ```text
   8: //! platform_quote := u16(pub_len) || ecc_pub_blob || u16(sig_len) || raw_r_s_sig
   9: //! ```
  10: //!
  11: //! On the verifying side (ANY platform), this module:
  12: //! 1. Parses the wire bytes.
  13: //! 2. Reads the `BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB` public key into a p256-friendly
  14: //!    `EncodedPoint` (SEC1 uncompressed: `0x04 || X || Y`).
  15: //! 3. Reads the 64-byte `r || s` ECDSA signature.
  16: //! 4. Computes `BLAKE3` over the sub-transcript and verifies the sig
  17: //!    against the parsed public key.
  18: //!
  19: //! Verifier-side has NO dependency on the `windows` crate, so this
  20: //! works on macOS / Linux / WSL peers verifying a doc minted on a
  21: //! Windows TPM-bound issuer.
  22: 
  23: use blake3::Hasher;
  24: use p256::ecdsa::signature::hazmat::PrehashVerifier;
  25: use p256::ecdsa::{Signature, VerifyingKey};
  26: use p256::EncodedPoint;
  27: 
  28: use crate::attestation::AttestationNonce;
  29: use crate::errors::{ConfidentialError, ConfidentialResult};
  30: use crate::provider::ProviderTag;
  31: 
  32: /// Domain-separation prefix for the TPM sub-transcript that the
  33: /// `platform_quote` signature commits to. Distinct from the master's
  34: /// attestation transcript so the TPM sig can't be lifted into the
  35: /// master-sig position (cross-protocol replay defense).
  36: pub const PLATFORM_QUOTE_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-confidential-platform-quote-v1";
  37: 
  38: /// Magic byte the CNG header carries for ECDSA-P256 public keys.
  39: const BCRYPT_ECDSA_PUBLIC_P256_MAGIC: u32 = 0x3153_4345; // 'ECS1' little-endian → 'ECS1'
  40: 
  41: /// Build the canonical sub-transcript the TPM signs over.
  42: ///
  43: /// The sub-transcript is strictly SHORTER than the master's full
  44: /// attestation transcript (it intentionally excludes `platform_quote`
  45: /// itself, since that's what the TPM is producing). The master sig
  46: /// over the full transcript then transitively commits to the TPM sig
  47: /// via the `platform_quote` bytes inside that full transcript.
  48: #[must_use]
  49: pub fn canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript(
  50:     provider_tag: ProviderTag,
  51:     master_vk_bytes: &[u8],
  52:     peer_nonce: &AttestationNonce,
  53:     issued_unix: u64,
  54:     deadline_unix: u64,
  55:     field_witness_commitment: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
  56: ) -> [u8; 32] {
  57:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  58:     h.update(PLATFORM_QUOTE_DOMAIN);
  59:     h.update(&[provider_tag.as_u8()]);
  60:     h.update(master_vk_bytes);
  61:     h.update(peer_nonce);
  62:     h.update(&issued_unix.to_be_bytes());
  63:     h.update(&deadline_unix.to_be_bytes());
  64:     match field_witness_commitment {
  65:         None => {
  66:             h.update(&[0u8]);
  67:         }
  68:         Some(c) => {
  69:             h.update(&[1u8]);
  70:             h.update(c);
  71:         }
  72:     }
  73:     *h.finalize().as_bytes()
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Parse a `platform_quote` envelope into its `(pub_blob, sig)` parts.
  77: ///
  78: /// # Errors
  79: /// Returns `Internal` on truncated buffers or impossible length prefixes.
  80: pub fn parse_platform_quote(quote: &[u8]) -> ConfidentialResult<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {
  81:     if quote.len() < 4 {
  82:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal("platform_quote too short"));
  83:     }
  84:     let pub_len = u16::from_be_bytes([quote[0], quote[1]]) as usize;
  85:     if quote.len() < 2 + pub_len + 2 {
  86:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
  87:             "platform_quote truncated at pub_blob",
  88:         ));
  89:     }
  90:     let pub_blob = quote[2..2 + pub_len].to_vec();
  91:     let after_pub = 2 + pub_len;
  92:     let sig_len = u16::from_be_bytes([quote[after_pub], quote[after_pub + 1]]) as usize;
  93:     if quote.len() < after_pub + 2 + sig_len {
  94:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
  95:             "platform_quote truncated at sig",
  96:         ));
  97:     }
  98:     let sig = quote[after_pub + 2..after_pub + 2 + sig_len].to_vec();
  99:     Ok((pub_blob, sig))
 100: }
 101: 
 102: /// Convert a CNG `BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB` public-key payload into a
 103: /// p256 `EncodedPoint` (uncompressed SEC1).
 104: fn cng_public_blob_to_sec1(blob: &[u8]) -> ConfidentialResult<EncodedPoint> {
 105:     if blob.len() < 8 + 32 + 32 {
 106:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
 107:             "BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB too short for ECDSA-P256",
 108:         ));
 109:     }
 110:     let magic = u32::from_le_bytes([blob[0], blob[1], blob[2], blob[3]]);
 111:     if magic != BCRYPT_ECDSA_PUBLIC_P256_MAGIC {
 112:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
 113:             "BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB wrong magic for ECDSA-P256",
 114:         ));
 115:     }
 116:     let cb_key = u32::from_le_bytes([blob[4], blob[5], blob[6], blob[7]]);
 117:     if cb_key != 32 {
 118:         return Err(ConfidentialError::Internal(
 119:             "BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB unexpected key size",
 120:         ));
 121:     }
 122:     let mut sec1 = [0u8; 65];
 123:     sec1[0] = 0x04;
 124:     sec1[1..33].copy_from_slice(&blob[8..40]);
 125:     sec1[33..65].copy_from_slice(&blob[40..72]);
 126:     EncodedPoint::from_bytes(sec1)
 127:         .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("p256 EncodedPoint::from_bytes failed"))
 128: }
 129: 
 130: /// Verify a TPM-issued `platform_quote` against the sub-transcript
 131: /// the issuer signed. Caller has parsed the [`crate::AttestationDoc`]
 132: /// and knows the issuer's `master_vk`, `peer_nonce`, etc.
 133: ///
 134: /// Returns the parsed `pub_blob` on success so the caller can pin
 135: /// the TPM identity for trust-on-first-use binding.
 136: ///
 137: /// # Errors
 138: /// Returns a typed error if the quote parses cleanly but the
 139: /// signature doesn't verify, or if any blob shape is wrong.
 140: pub fn verify_platform_quote(
 141:     quote: &[u8],
 142:     provider_tag: ProviderTag,
 143:     master_vk_bytes: &[u8],
 144:     peer_nonce: &AttestationNonce,
 145:     issued_unix: u64,
 146:     deadline_unix: u64,
 147:     field_witness_commitment: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 148: ) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 149:     let (pub_blob, sig_bytes) = parse_platform_quote(quote)?;
 150:     let point = cng_public_blob_to_sec1(&pub_blob)?;
 151:     let vk = VerifyingKey::from_encoded_point(&point)
 152:         .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("p256 VerifyingKey decode failed"))?;
 153:     // The TPM produces a raw r||s ECDSA signature. p256 expects the
 154:     // same layout via `Signature::from_slice`.
 155:     let sig = Signature::from_slice(&sig_bytes)
 156:         .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("p256 Signature decode failed"))?;
 157:     let digest = canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript(
 158:         provider_tag,
 159:         master_vk_bytes,
 160:         peer_nonce,
 161:         issued_unix,
 162:         deadline_unix,
 163:         field_witness_commitment,
 164:     );
 165:     // The TPM signs the 32-byte digest directly (no further hashing
 166:     // inside the chip), so we must use the prehash verifier to match.
 167:     vk.verify_prehash(&digest, &sig)
 168:         .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::AttestationMasterSigFail)?;
 169:     Ok(pub_blob)
 170: }

 189:     #[test]
 190:     fn sub_transcript_changes_with_each_field() {
 191:         let base = canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript(

   1: //! Opaque sealed key blob handed back by a [`crate::ConfidentialProvider`].
   2: 
   3: use zeroize::Zeroize;
   4: 
   5: use crate::ProviderTag;
   6: 
   7: /// Provider-opaque sealed key bytes. Callers MUST NOT introspect
   8: /// `bytes`; the layout is intentionally provider-private so we can
   9: /// swap representations (software AEAD blob, SGX sealed data, TPM
  10: /// wrapped blob) without breaking callers.
  11: ///
  12: /// Drop zeroizes `bytes` defensively even though the sealed form
  13: /// is itself ciphertext — a defense-in-depth practice that catches
  14: /// the case where a future provider stores plaintext padding
  15: /// alongside the ciphertext.
  16: #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  17: pub struct SealedKey {
  18:     /// Which provider produced this blob; checked at unseal time.
  19:     pub provider_tag: ProviderTag,
  20:     /// Provider-opaque bytes. For [`crate::SoftwareProvider`] this is
  21:     /// `nonce(12) || ciphertext(N) || tag(16)` under a per-process
  22:     /// ephemeral ChaCha20-Poly1305 key.
  23:     pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
  24: }
  25: 
  26: impl std::fmt::Debug for SealedKey {
  27:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  28:         f.debug_struct("SealedKey")
  29:             .field("provider_tag", &self.provider_tag)
  30:             .field("bytes.len", &self.bytes.len())
  31:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
  32:     }
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl Drop for SealedKey {
  36:     fn drop(&mut self) {
  37:         self.bytes.zeroize();
  38:     }
  39: }
  40:

  42:     /// Construct from raw parts. Crate-internal: callers obtain

  44:     /// or [`crate::ConfidentialProvider::derive_child`].
  45:     pub(crate) fn new(provider_tag: ProviderTag, bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Self {

   1: //! Software-only [`ConfidentialProvider`] baseline.
   2: //!
   3: //! ## Threat model
   4: //!
   5: //! - **Defeats**: user-mode malware reading the master key from process
   6: //!   memory. The master never appears in plaintext at rest; sealing
   7: //!   uses a per-process ephemeral key that itself only lives in
   8: //!   `Zeroize`-protected memory and is dropped when the provider is.
   9: //! - **Does NOT defeat**: root malware / kernel debugger / cold-boot
  10: //!   / `/proc/mem` capture. Those need a hardware enclave, which
  11: //!   ships in Phase 2 backends.
  12: //!
  13: //! ## Sealing primitive
  14: //!
  15: //! `seal(plaintext) = ChaCha20Poly1305(K_ephemeral, nonce, plaintext)`
  16: //! where `K_ephemeral` is `BLAKE3(domain_tag`, `raw_ephemeral_seed`). The
  17: //! seed is sampled from the supplied [`rand_core::CryptoRng`] at
  18: //! provider construction and lives only in
  19: //! [`ChaCha20Poly1305`]'s expanded form.
  20: //!
  21: //! Nonces are random per call (12 bytes from the AEAD's required
  22: //! width). With ~2^96 nonces the collision probability is negligible
  23: //! for any realistic call count.
  24: //!
  25: //! ## Child key derivation
  26: //!
  27: //! `child = HKDF(ikm = unsealed_master, salt = ChildKeyDomain, info = context_tag)`
  28: //! implemented via BLAKE3-keyed XOF as `ol_pqsig` and the rest of the
  29: //! Coherence Mesh already use. The intermediate IKM is held in a
  30: //! [`Zeroize`]-clearing buffer and dropped before return.
  31: 
  32: use blake3::Hasher;
  33: use chacha20poly1305::aead::{Aead, KeyInit, Payload};
  34: use chacha20poly1305::{ChaCha20Poly1305, Key, Nonce};
  35: use ol_pqsig::{HybridSigningKey, HybridVerifyingKey};
  36: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  37: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  38: 
  39: use crate::attestation::{
  40:     canonical_attestation_transcript, AttestationDoc, AttestationNonce,
  41:     ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS,
  42: };
  43: use crate::errors::{ConfidentialError, ConfidentialResult};
  44: use crate::provider::{ConfidentialProvider, ProviderTag};
  45: use crate::sealed_key::SealedKey;
  46: use crate::tier::ConfidentialTier;
  47: 
  48: /// Domain tag for the ephemeral sealing key (binds the AEAD key to
  49: /// this crate so a future provider can't reuse the same primitive
  50: /// for a different purpose in the same process).
  51: const SEALING_KEY_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-confidential-software-sealing-v1";
  52: /// Domain tag for child-key derivation.
  53: const CHILD_KEY_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-confidential-software-child-v1";
  54: /// Domain tag for sealing-blob AAD.
  55: const SEALED_AAD: &[u8] = b"OL-confidential-software-aad-v1";
  56: 
  57: /// ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce width (12 bytes).
  58: const NONCE_LEN: usize = 12;
  59: /// Poly1305 authentication tag width (16 bytes).
  60: const TAG_LEN: usize = 16;
  61: /// Sealed master payload = master seed (32B) + length-tagged structure
  62: /// indicator. We keep the payload size deterministic at 32 bytes.
  63: const MASTER_PT_LEN: usize = 32;
  64: 
  65: /// Software-baseline [`ConfidentialProvider`].
  66: ///
  67: /// Construct via [`SoftwareProvider::generate`] (CSPRNG-sourced
  68: /// ephemeral key) or [`SoftwareProvider::from_seed`] (deterministic
  69: /// for test vectors only — DO NOT use in production).
  70: pub struct SoftwareProvider {
  71:     /// AEAD instance bound to this provider's ephemeral key. Drop
  72:     /// zeroizes via [`ChaCha20Poly1305`]'s own zeroize impl.
  73:     aead: ChaCha20Poly1305,
  74: }
  75: 
  76: impl std::fmt::Debug for SoftwareProvider {
  77:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  78:         f.debug_struct("SoftwareProvider")
  79:             .field("tag", &ProviderTag::Software)
  80:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
  81:     }
  82: }
  83: 
  84: impl SoftwareProvider {
  85:     /// Construct with a fresh ephemeral key sourced from `rng`. The
  86:     /// recommended path for production.
  87:     pub fn generate<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> Self {
  88:         let mut seed = [0u8; 32];
  89:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut seed);
  90:         let provider = Self::from_seed_internal(&seed);
  91:         seed.zeroize();
  92:         provider
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     /// Internal deterministic constructor used by [`Self::generate`].
  96:     /// Always available because production CSPRNG-based construction
  97:     /// needs to derive an `aead` from a fresh-random seed.
  98:     fn from_seed_internal(seed: &[u8; 32]) -> Self {
  99:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 100:         h.update(SEALING_KEY_DOMAIN);
 101:         h.update(seed);
 102:         let key_bytes = h.finalize();
 103:         let key = Key::from_slice(key_bytes.as_bytes());
 104:         let aead = ChaCha20Poly1305::new(key);
 105:         Self { aead }
 106:     }
 107: 
 108:     /// Construct deterministically from a 32-byte seed. Useful for
 109:     /// test KAT vectors and for replays during incident response;
 110:     /// callers MUST NOT use a static seed in production.
 111:     ///
 112:     /// **Audit M7 May 2026 — gated**: this constructor is only
 113:     /// exposed under `#[cfg(any(test, feature =
 114:     /// "unstable-deterministic-provider"))]` so an accidental
 115:     /// production call site can't compile. Test fixtures get it
 116:     /// automatically; production crates must opt in via the
 117:     /// Cargo feature, which is also off-by-default on the
 118:     /// pyo3-built wheel.
 119:     #[cfg(any(test, feature = "unstable-deterministic-provider"))]
 120:     #[must_use]
 121:     pub fn from_seed(seed: &[u8; 32]) -> Self {
 122:         Self::from_seed_internal(seed)
 123:     }
 124: 
 125:     /// Seal `plaintext` under this provider's ephemeral key with a
 126:     /// fresh random nonce. The output layout is
 127:     /// `nonce(12) || ciphertext_with_tag(N + 16)`.
 128:     fn seal_with_rng<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 129:         &self,
 130:         plaintext: &[u8],
 131:         rng: &mut R,
 132:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 133:         let mut nonce_bytes = [0u8; NONCE_LEN];
 134:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut nonce_bytes);
 135:         let nonce = Nonce::from_slice(&nonce_bytes);
 136:         let ct = self
 137:             .aead
 138:             .encrypt(
 139:                 nonce,
 140:                 Payload {
 141:                     msg: plaintext,
 142:                     aad: SEALED_AAD,
 143:                 },
 144:             )
 145:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("AEAD encrypt"))?;
 146:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(NONCE_LEN + ct.len());
 147:         out.extend_from_slice(&nonce_bytes);
 148:         out.extend_from_slice(&ct);
 149:         Ok(out)
 150:     }
 151: 
 152:     /// Open a sealed blob into its plaintext. The caller's buffer
 153:     /// receives the plaintext; the caller is responsible for
 154:     /// [`Zeroize`]-ing it.
 155:     ///
 156:     /// **Audit H5 May 2026 — error-collapsing**: every failure mode
 157:     /// returns the same external `SealedKeyAuthFail` so an attacker
 158:     /// who corrupts only the tag byte (or only the length) cannot
 159:     /// distinguish "wrong provider tag" / "wrong length" / "AEAD
 160:     /// reject" via the returned error variant — closes the typed-
 161:     /// error oracle that lets an attacker probe the layout of a
 162:     /// sealed-blob storage record. The granular variants
 163:     /// (`SealedKeyWrongProvider`, `SealedKeyBadLength`) remain in
 164:     /// the enum for ergonomic internal diagnostics but `unseal`
 165:     /// never returns them externally.
 166:     fn unseal(&self, sealed: &SealedKey, expected_pt_len: usize) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 167:         if sealed.provider_tag != ProviderTag::Software {
 168:             return Err(ConfidentialError::SealedKeyAuthFail);
 169:         }
 170:         if sealed.bytes.len() != NONCE_LEN + expected_pt_len + TAG_LEN {
 171:             return Err(ConfidentialError::SealedKeyAuthFail);
 172:         }
 173:         let nonce = Nonce::from_slice(&sealed.bytes[..NONCE_LEN]);
 174:         let ct = &sealed.bytes[NONCE_LEN..];
 175:         let pt = self
 176:             .aead
 177:             .decrypt(
 178:                 nonce,
 179:                 Payload {
 180:                     msg: ct,
 181:                     aad: SEALED_AAD,
 182:                 },
 183:             )
 184:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::SealedKeyAuthFail)?;
 185:         Ok(pt)
 186:     }
 187: 
 188:     /// Derive a 32-byte child seed from an unsealed master seed +
 189:     /// context tag. Pure function — caller manages secret hygiene
 190:     /// on the IKM input.
 191:     fn derive_child_seed(master_seed: &[u8; 32], context_tag: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
 192:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 193:         h.update(CHILD_KEY_DOMAIN);
 194:         h.update(master_seed);
 195:         h.update(&u32::try_from(context_tag.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 196:         h.update(context_tag);
 197:         let out = h.finalize();
 198:         let mut child = [0u8; 32];
 199:         child.copy_from_slice(out.as_bytes());
 200:         child
 201:     }
 202: 
 203:     /// Turn a 32-byte seed into a deterministic `HybridSigningKey` via
 204:     /// the standard `ol_pqsig` deterministic-seed constructor. Returns
 205:     /// `(signing_key, verifying_key)` from the underlying generator.
 206:     fn signing_key_from_seed(seed: &[u8; 32]) -> (HybridSigningKey, HybridVerifyingKey) {
 207:         use rand_core::SeedableRng;
 208:         let mut prng = rand_chacha::ChaCha20Rng::from_seed(*seed);
 209:         HybridSigningKey::generate(&mut prng)
 210:     }
 211: 
 212:     fn seal_with_os_rng(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 213:         use rand_core::OsRng;
 214:         self.seal_with_rng(plaintext, &mut OsRng)
 215:     }
 216: 
 217:     /// Derive the `(signing_key, verifying_key)` pair from a sealed
 218:     /// master with a single unseal pass. Useful for callers that
 219:     /// need both halves at once (e.g.,
 220:     /// [`crate::windows_tpm::attest_with_tpm`]) to avoid the
 221:     /// double-unseal cost.
 222:     ///
 223:     /// # Errors
 224:     /// Returns `SealedKeyAuthFail` if the blob can't be unsealed.
 225:     pub fn derive_hybrid_pair(
 226:         &self,
 227:         sealed: &SealedKey,
 228:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<(HybridSigningKey, HybridVerifyingKey)> {
 229:         let mut unsealed = self.unseal(sealed, MASTER_PT_LEN)?;
 230:         let seed: &[u8; 32] = unsealed
 231:             .as_slice()
 232:             .try_into()
 233:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("unseal returned wrong length"))?;
 234:         let pair = Self::signing_key_from_seed(seed);
 235:         unsealed.zeroize();
 236:         Ok(pair)
 237:     }
 238: }
 239: 
 240: impl ConfidentialProvider for SoftwareProvider {
 241:     fn tier(&self) -> ConfidentialTier {
 242:         ConfidentialTier::Software
 243:     }
 244: 
 245:     fn tag(&self) -> ProviderTag {
 246:         ProviderTag::Software
 247:     }
 248: 
 249:     fn seal_master(&self, seed: &[u8; 32]) -> ConfidentialResult<SealedKey> {
 250:         let bytes = self.seal_with_os_rng(seed)?;
 251:         Ok(SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::Software, bytes))
 252:     }
 253: 
 254:     fn derive_child(
 255:         &self,
 256:         sealed_master: &SealedKey,
 257:         context_tag: &[u8],
 258:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<SealedKey> {
 259:         let master_seed = self.unseal(sealed_master, MASTER_PT_LEN)?;
 260:         let master_arr: &[u8; 32] = master_seed
 261:             .as_slice()
 262:             .try_into()
 263:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("unseal returned wrong length"))?;
 264:         let child_seed = Self::derive_child_seed(master_arr, context_tag);
 265:         // Zeroize the unsealed master immediately after deriving the
 266:         // child; we don't need it any longer.
 267:         let mut master_seed = master_seed;
 268:         master_seed.zeroize();
 269:         let sealed_child_bytes = self.seal_with_os_rng(&child_seed)?;
 270:         // Same for the child seed — it's already sealed; clear the
 271:         // plaintext copy.
 272:         let mut child_seed_zero = child_seed;
 273:         child_seed_zero.zeroize();
 274:         Ok(SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::Software, sealed_child_bytes))
 275:     }
 276: 
 277:     fn sealed_sign(
 278:         &self,
 279:         sealed: &SealedKey,
 280:         transcript: &[u8],
 281:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 282:         let mut unsealed = self.unseal(sealed, MASTER_PT_LEN)?;
 283:         let seed: &[u8; 32] = unsealed
 284:             .as_slice()
 285:             .try_into()
 286:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("unseal returned wrong length"))?;
 287:         let (sk, _vk) = Self::signing_key_from_seed(seed);
 288:         unsealed.zeroize();
 289:         let sig = sk.sign(transcript)?;
 290:         Ok(sig.to_vec())
 291:     }
 292: 
 293:     fn verifying_key(&self, sealed: &SealedKey) -> ConfidentialResult<HybridVerifyingKey> {
 294:         let mut unsealed = self.unseal(sealed, MASTER_PT_LEN)?;
 295:         let seed: &[u8; 32] = unsealed
 296:             .as_slice()
 297:             .try_into()
 298:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("unseal returned wrong length"))?;
 299:         let (_sk, vk) = Self::signing_key_from_seed(seed);
 300:         unsealed.zeroize();
 301:         Ok(vk)
 302:     }
 303: 
 304:     fn attest(
 305:         &self,
 306:         sealed_master: &SealedKey,
 307:         peer_nonce: AttestationNonce,
 308:         issued_unix: u64,
 309:         deadline_unix: u64,
 310:         field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 311:         issuer_sdp_pubkey: crate::attestation::IssuerSdpPubkey,
 312:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<AttestationDoc> {
 313:         if deadline_unix <= issued_unix {
 314:             return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationBadFreshnessWindow {
 315:                 issued_unix,
 316:                 deadline_unix,
 317:             });
 318:         }
 319:         let window = deadline_unix - issued_unix;
 320:         if window > ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS {
 321:             return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationFreshnessWindowTooWide {
 322:                 got: window,
 323:                 max: ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS,
 324:             });
 325:         }
 326:         // Single unseal pass for both VK derivation and signing —
 327:         // shaves ~360 µs off the attest_issue hot path vs the
 328:         // earlier "verifying_key() then sealed_sign()" sequence.
 329:         let mut unsealed = self.unseal(sealed_master, MASTER_PT_LEN)?;
 330:         let seed: &[u8; 32] = unsealed
 331:             .as_slice()
 332:             .try_into()
 333:             .map_err(|_| ConfidentialError::Internal("unseal returned wrong length"))?;
 334:         let (sk, master_vk) = Self::signing_key_from_seed(seed);
 335:         unsealed.zeroize();
 336:         // The software provider has no platform quote to embed.
 337:         let platform_quote: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
 338:         let transcript = canonical_attestation_transcript(
 339:             ProviderTag::Software,
 340:             &master_vk,
 341:             &peer_nonce,
 342:             issued_unix,
 343:             deadline_unix,
 344:             field_witness,
 345:             &platform_quote,
 346:             &issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 347:         );
 348:         // Reuse the freshly-derived signing key from the single
 349:         // unseal above — no need to round-trip through sealed_sign
 350:         // (which would unseal a second time).
 351:         let master_sig = sk.sign(&transcript)?.to_vec();
 352:         Ok(AttestationDoc {
 353:             provider_tag: ProviderTag::Software,
 354:             master_vk,
 355:             peer_nonce,
 356:             issued_unix,
 357:             deadline_unix,
 358:             field_witness_commitment: field_witness.map(|w| {
 359:                 let mut h = Hasher::new();
 360:                 h.update(b"OL-confidential-field-witness-commitment-v1");
 361:                 h.update(w);
 362:                 *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 363:             }),
 364:             platform_quote,
 365:             issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 366:             master_sig,
 367:         })
 368:     }
 369: }

   1: //! Runtime confidential-compute tier and platform detection.
   2: 
   3: /// What hardness tier the daemon is running at right now.
   4: ///
   5: /// Ordered: `Software < HardwareBound < HardwareAttested`. Peers can
   6: /// downgrade their threat model when the local tier is lower than
   7: /// expected (e.g., refuse to exchange long-term secrets if not at
   8: /// least `HardwareBound`).
   9: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
  10: pub enum ConfidentialTier {
  11:     /// Software-only baseline. Master key sealed under a per-process
  12:     /// ephemeral ChaCha20-Poly1305 key; `Zeroize` on drop; mlock
  13:     /// where the OS allows. Defeats user-mode malware; does NOT
  14:     /// defeat root malware or `/proc/mem` capture.
  15:     Software,
  16:     /// Key is held inside a hardware secure element (Apple Secure
  17:     /// Enclave / Android `StrongBox` / Windows TPM / Intel SGX /
  18:     /// AMD SEV-SNP). No vendor attestation chain. Cipher operations
  19:     /// stay inside the element; the daemon only sees public outputs.
  20:     HardwareBound,
  21:     /// Hardware-bound AND the peer chose to verify a vendor-issued
  22:     /// attestation chain (Apple App Attest / Android Play Integrity /
  23:     /// Windows TPM EK / Intel quote service). Strongest tier.
  24:     HardwareAttested,
  25: }
  26: 
  27: impl ConfidentialTier {
  28:     /// True if the local tier meets or exceeds a peer-requested floor.
  29:     #[must_use]
  30:     pub const fn meets(self, required: Self) -> bool {
  31:         (self as u8) >= (required as u8)
  32:     }
  33: 
  34:     /// Map a [`crate::provider::ProviderTag`] (the byte that flows over
  35:     /// the wire in [`crate::attestation::AttestationDoc`]) onto its
  36:     /// best-effort tier. Used by `verify_attestation` to enforce the
  37:     /// `min_tier` floor without callers having to bridge the two enums.
  38:     #[must_use]
  39:     pub const fn from_provider_tag(tag: crate::provider::ProviderTag) -> Self {
  40:         use crate::provider::ProviderTag;
  41:         match tag {
  42:             ProviderTag::Software => Self::Software,
  43:             ProviderTag::WindowsTpm
  44:             | ProviderTag::AppleSecureEnclave
  45:             | ProviderTag::AndroidStrongBox
  46:             | ProviderTag::IntelSgx
  47:             | ProviderTag::AmdSevSnp
  48:             | ProviderTag::ArmTrustZone => Self::HardwareBound,
  49:         }
  50:     }
  51: }
  52: 
  53: impl From<ol_hwkey::KeyGuarantee> for ConfidentialTier {
  54:     fn from(value: ol_hwkey::KeyGuarantee) -> Self {
  55:         match value {
  56:             ol_hwkey::KeyGuarantee::TofuOnly => Self::Software,
  57:             ol_hwkey::KeyGuarantee::HardwareBound => Self::HardwareBound,
  58:             ol_hwkey::KeyGuarantee::HardwareAttested => Self::HardwareAttested,
  59:         }
  60:     }
  61: }
  62: 
  63: /// Detect the strongest tier the local host supports.
  64: ///
  65: /// Phase 1 always returns `Software`. Per-platform detection (SGX,
  66: /// SEV-SNP, Secure Enclave, TPM, `TrustZone`) lands in Phase 2 commits
  67: /// alongside the matching provider impl.
  68: #[must_use]
  69: pub fn detect_runtime_tier() -> ConfidentialTier {
  70:     ConfidentialTier::Software
  71: }
