   1: //! Windows TPM-hardened [`ConfidentialProvider`] composition.
   2: //!
   3: //! Bundles [`crate::SoftwareProvider`] (for the seal/unseal/sign
   4: //! primitives) with a [`crate::windows_tpm::TpmAttestationKey`] (for
   5: //! TPM-rooted attestation). Every `attest` call produces a doc
   6: //! whose `platform_quote` field carries a TPM-signed ECDSA-P256
   7: //! commitment over the sub-transcript; the master hybrid sig over
   8: //! the full transcript transitively commits to that TPM sig. The
   9: //! tier upgrades to [`ConfidentialTier::HardwareBound`].
  10: //!
  11: //! ## What this gets us
  12: //!
  13: //! - **Peer-verifiable hardware root**: any peer that pins the
  14: //!   `master_vk` can ALSO validate that this doc was minted on a
  15: //!   process that holds the specific TPM key. Cross-platform
  16: //!   verifiers use the pure-Rust `p256` verifier in
  17: //!   [`crate::platform_quote`].
  18: //! - **Cross-host non-transferability**: the TPM identity is
  19: //!   bound to a single physical chip; an attestation captured on
  20: //!   host A can't be re-issued on host B.
  21: //!
  22: //! ## What we explored but didn't ship
  23: //!
  24: //! TPM-wrapped AEAD sealing-key (RSA-OAEP via `NCryptEncrypt` /
  25: //! `NCryptDecrypt`) does NOT work with the Microsoft Platform Crypto
  26: //! Provider on consumer Win11 — the PCP supports TPM-backed keys
  27: //! for SIGNING only, not encryption. True AEAD-key wrap would
  28: //! require either a smart-card KSP, raw tss-esapi (heavy C
  29: //! dependency), or an NCryptSecretAgreement-based ECDH derivation
  30: //! (complex policy plumbing). For Phase 2 first ship, the
  31: //! attestation-key path closes the most valuable threat surface
  32: //! (remote impersonation) without those costs.
  33: 
  34: use ol_pqsig::HybridVerifyingKey;
  35: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  36: 
  37: use crate::attestation::{AttestationDoc, AttestationNonce};
  38: use crate::errors::ConfidentialResult;
  39: use crate::provider::{ConfidentialProvider, ProviderTag};
  40: use crate::sealed_key::SealedKey;
  41: use crate::software::SoftwareProvider;
  42: use crate::tier::ConfidentialTier;
  43: use crate::windows_tpm::TpmAttestationKey;
  44: 
  45: /// Windows TPM-hardened composition over the software baseline.
  46: ///
  47: /// Operates as a normal [`ConfidentialProvider`] but with
  48: /// [`ConfidentialTier::HardwareBound`] and TPM-rooted attestations.
  49: pub struct WindowsHardenedProvider {
  50:     sw: SoftwareProvider,
  51:     tpm: TpmAttestationKey,
  52: }
  53: 
  54: impl std::fmt::Debug for WindowsHardenedProvider {
  55:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  56:         f.debug_struct("WindowsHardenedProvider")
  57:             .field("tier", &self.tier())
  58:             .field("tag", &self.tag())
  59:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
  60:     }
  61: }
  62: 
  63: impl WindowsHardenedProvider {
  64:     /// Build a hardened provider:
  65:     /// - Generate a fresh per-process software AEAD sealing key.
  66:     /// - Acquire or create the TPM-resident ECDSA-P256 attestation
  67:     ///   key under `tpm_key_name`.
  68:     ///
  69:     /// # Errors
  70:     /// Returns `Internal` if the TPM key acquisition fails.
  71:     pub fn create<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
  72:         rng: &mut R,
  73:         tpm_key_name: &str,
  74:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<Self> {
  75:         let sw = SoftwareProvider::generate(rng);
  76:         let tpm = TpmAttestationKey::acquire_or_create(tpm_key_name)?;
  77:         Ok(Self { sw, tpm })
  78:     }
  79: 
  80:     /// Borrow the inner software provider — useful for unit tests
  81:     /// and for callers that need to construct sealed blobs
  82:     /// directly through the software path.
  83:     #[must_use]
  84:     pub fn software(&self) -> &SoftwareProvider {
  85:         &self.sw
  86:     }
  87: 
  88:     /// Borrow the inner TPM attestation key — useful for callers
  89:     /// that need to attest standalone digests outside the
  90:     /// `ConfidentialProvider` trait.
  91:     #[must_use]
  92:     pub fn tpm(&self) -> &TpmAttestationKey {
  93:         &self.tpm
  94:     }
  95: }
  96: 
  97: impl ConfidentialProvider for WindowsHardenedProvider {
  98:     fn tier(&self) -> ConfidentialTier {
  99:         ConfidentialTier::HardwareBound
 100:     }
 101: 
 102:     fn tag(&self) -> ProviderTag {
 103:         ProviderTag::WindowsTpm
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     fn seal_master(&self, seed: &[u8; 32]) -> ConfidentialResult<SealedKey> {
 107:         // Seal under the software AEAD key but stamp the wire tag
 108:         // as WindowsTpm so the sealed blob is bound to this
 109:         // provider's identity (the verifying-key path checks the
 110:         // tag and refuses cross-provider unseals).
 111:         let sw_sealed = self.sw.seal_master(seed)?;
 112:         Ok(SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::WindowsTpm, sw_sealed.bytes.clone()))
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     fn derive_child(
 116:         &self,
 117:         sealed_master: &SealedKey,
 118:         context_tag: &[u8],
 119:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<SealedKey> {
 120:         // Re-tag the input as Software for the inner call, then
 121:         // re-tag the output back to WindowsTpm.
 122:         let sw_in = SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::Software, sealed_master.bytes.clone());
 123:         let sw_out = self.sw.derive_child(&sw_in, context_tag)?;
 124:         Ok(SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::WindowsTpm, sw_out.bytes.clone()))
 125:     }
 126: 
 127:     fn sealed_sign(
 128:         &self,
 129:         sealed: &SealedKey,
 130:         transcript: &[u8],
 131:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 132:         let sw_sealed = SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::Software, sealed.bytes.clone());
 133:         self.sw.sealed_sign(&sw_sealed, transcript)
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     fn verifying_key(&self, sealed: &SealedKey) -> ConfidentialResult<HybridVerifyingKey> {
 137:         let sw_sealed = SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::Software, sealed.bytes.clone());
 138:         self.sw.verifying_key(&sw_sealed)
 139:     }
 140: 
 141:     fn attest(
 142:         &self,
 143:         sealed_master: &SealedKey,
 144:         peer_nonce: AttestationNonce,
 145:         issued_unix: u64,
 146:         deadline_unix: u64,
 147:         field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 148:         issuer_sdp_pubkey: crate::attestation::IssuerSdpPubkey,
 149:     ) -> ConfidentialResult<AttestationDoc> {
 150:         // Route through windows_tpm::attest_with_tpm so the
 151:         // returned doc carries a TPM-signed platform_quote.
 152:         let sw_sealed = SealedKey::new(ProviderTag::Software, sealed_master.bytes.clone());
 153:         crate::windows_tpm::attest_with_tpm(
 154:             &self.sw,
 155:             &sw_sealed,
 156:             &self.tpm,
 157:             peer_nonce,
 158:             issued_unix,
 159:             deadline_unix,
 160:             field_witness,
 161:             issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 162:         )
 163:     }
 164: }

   1: //! Windows TPM-bound attestation key via the `NCrypt` Platform Crypto
   2: //! Provider ("Microsoft Platform Crypto Provider", aka PCP).
   3: //!
   4: //! ## What this module gives us
   5: //!
   6: //! - A **TPM-resident ECDSA-P256 signing key** that the kernel guards.
   7: //!   Key material NEVER leaves the TPM; signing happens inside the
   8: //!   chip. Useful for: peer-verifiable "this attestation was minted
   9: //!   on the same physical box that holds the TPM" guarantee.
  10: //! - A way to **anchor the `platform_quote` field** of
  11: //!   [`crate::AttestationDoc`] in real hardware. The master sig still
  12: //!   covers the entire transcript including `platform_quote` bytes, so
  13: //!   the two-layer binding (software hybrid sig + TPM ECDSA sig over
  14: //!   a sub-transcript) makes the doc bound to BOTH the master and
  15: //!   the specific TPM.
  16: //!
  17: //! ## What it does NOT give us (yet)
  18: //!
  19: //! - The TPM **cannot** sign Ed25519 or ML-DSA-65, so `sealed_sign`
  20: //!   still happens in software. Closing T-LOCAL-MAL-ROOT for the
  21: //!   master sign path is a larger architectural change (split
  22: //!   signing: TPM signs ECDSA, software signs PQ, both validate at
  23: //!   peer) and lands as a separate ship.
  24: //!
  25: //! ## Admin / permission requirements
  26: //!
  27: //! No admin needed. The Platform Crypto Provider runs in user mode
  28: //! and the per-user key store accepts `NCrypt` operations without
  29: //! elevation on consumer Windows.
  30: 
  31: #![allow(unsafe_code)] // FFI into the OS crypto API.
  32:

  34: use windows::Win32::Security::Cryptography::{
  35:     NCryptCreatePersistedKey, NCryptExportKey, NCryptFinalizeKey, NCryptFreeObject,
  36:     NCryptOpenKey, NCryptOpenStorageProvider, NCryptSignHash, CERT_KEY_SPEC,
  37:     NCRYPT_FLAGS, NCRYPT_HANDLE, NCRYPT_KEY_HANDLE, NCRYPT_PROV_HANDLE,

  61: fn wide(s: &str) -> Vec<u16> {

  75: /// A TPM-resident ECDSA-P256 signing key, looked up by per-user key
  76: /// name in the Platform Crypto Provider.
  77: ///
  78: /// On drop, the `NCrypt` key + provider handles are closed (the
  79: /// persisted key itself remains in the user's key store for future
  80: /// runs — that's the whole point of "persisted").

  95: impl Drop for TpmAttestationKey {
  96:     fn drop(&mut self) {
  97:         // SAFETY: handles are valid for the lifetime of `self`;
  98:         // NCryptFreeObject is the documented release call for both
  99:         // provider and key handles. Errors during free are ignored —
 100:         // there's nothing useful to do at drop time.
 101:         unsafe {
 102:             if self.key.0 != 0 {
 103:                 let _ = NCryptFreeObject(NCRYPT_HANDLE(self.key.0));
 104:             }
 105:             if self.provider.0 != 0 {
 106:                 let _ = NCryptFreeObject(NCRYPT_HANDLE(self.provider.0));
 107:             }
 108:         }
 109:     }
 110: }

 112: impl TpmAttestationKey {
 113:     /// Acquire an existing TPM-backed ECDSA-P256 key by name, or
 114:     /// create one if it doesn't exist. Idempotent across runs.
 115:     ///
 116:     /// `key_name` is a per-user identifier. Consumers SHOULD use a
 117:     /// stable string like `"OL-confidential-attestation-v1"` so the
 118:     /// same key persists across daemon restarts.
 119:     ///
 120:     /// # Errors
 121:     /// Returns `Internal` if `NCrypt` fails (TPM unavailable, KSP
 122:     /// refused the create operation, etc.).
 123:     pub fn acquire_or_create(key_name: &str) -> ConfidentialResult<Self> {
 124:         let provider_name_w = wide(PROVIDER_NAME);
 125:         let key_name_w = wide(key_name);
 126:         let alg_w = wide(ECDSA_P256_ALG);
 127: 
 128:         let mut provider = NCRYPT_PROV_HANDLE::default();
 129:         // SAFETY: pointers point at valid wide buffers we own.
 130:         unsafe {
 131:             NCryptOpenStorageProvider(&raw mut provider, PCWSTR(provider_name_w.as_ptr()), 0)
 132:                 .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptOpenStorageProvider: {e}")))?;
 133:         }
 134: 
 135:         let mut key = NCRYPT_KEY_HANDLE::default();
 136:         // SAFETY: provider handle valid; key_name wide-encoded.
 137:         let open_status = unsafe {
 138:             NCryptOpenKey(
 139:                 provider,
 140:                 &raw mut key,
 141:                 PCWSTR(key_name_w.as_ptr()),
 142:                 CERT_KEY_SPEC(0),
 143:                 NCRYPT_FLAGS(0),
 144:             )
 145:         };
 146:         if let Err(e) = open_status {
 147:             if e.code().0 == NTE_BAD_KEYSET {
 148:                 // Key doesn't exist — create + finalize.
 149:                 // SAFETY: provider valid; alg + key_name wide-encoded.
 150:                 unsafe {
 151:                     NCryptCreatePersistedKey(
 152:                         provider,
 153:                         &raw mut key,
 154:                         PCWSTR(alg_w.as_ptr()),
 155:                         PCWSTR(key_name_w.as_ptr()),
 156:                         CERT_KEY_SPEC(0),
 157:                         NCRYPT_FLAGS(0),
 158:                     )
 159:                     .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptCreatePersistedKey: {e}")))?;
 160:                     NCryptFinalizeKey(key, NCRYPT_FLAGS(0))
 161:                         .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptFinalizeKey: {e}")))?;
 162:                 }
 163:             } else {
 164:                 // SAFETY: drop frees provider handle.
 165:                 return Err(internal(format!("NCryptOpenKey: {e}")));
 166:             }
 167:         }
 168:         Ok(Self { provider, key })
 169:     }
 170: 
 171:     /// Export the public key in CNG `BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB` form.
 172:     ///
 173:     /// # Errors
 174:     /// Returns `Internal` if `NCryptExportKey` fails.
 175:     pub fn public_blob(&self) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 176:         let blob_type_w = wide(ECC_PUBLIC_BLOB);
 177:         let mut needed: u32 = 0;
 178:         // SAFETY: key handle valid; output None is the documented
 179:         // "ask for required size" idiom.
 180:         unsafe {
 181:             NCryptExportKey(
 182:                 self.key,
 183:                 None,
 184:                 PCWSTR(blob_type_w.as_ptr()),
 185:                 None,
 186:                 None,
 187:                 &raw mut needed,
 188:                 NCRYPT_FLAGS(0),
 189:             )
 190:             .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptExportKey(size): {e}")))?;
 191:         }
 192:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; needed as usize];
 193:         // SAFETY: buf has exactly `needed` bytes allocated.
 194:         unsafe {
 195:             NCryptExportKey(
 196:                 self.key,
 197:                 None,
 198:                 PCWSTR(blob_type_w.as_ptr()),
 199:                 None,
 200:                 Some(&mut buf),
 201:                 &raw mut needed,
 202:                 NCRYPT_FLAGS(0),
 203:             )
 204:             .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptExportKey: {e}")))?;
 205:         }
 206:         buf.truncate(needed as usize);
 207:         Ok(buf)
 208:     }
 209: 
 210:     /// Sign a 32-byte digest. The TPM produces a raw ECDSA-P256
 211:     /// signature `r || s` (64 bytes, big-endian).
 212:     ///
 213:     /// # Errors
 214:     /// Returns `Internal` if `NCryptSignHash` fails.
 215:     pub fn sign(&self, digest: &[u8; 32]) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 216:         let mut needed: u32 = 0;
 217:         // SAFETY: digest is a 32-byte buffer; None output is the
 218:         // documented "ask for required size" idiom.
 219:         unsafe {
 220:             NCryptSignHash(
 221:                 self.key,
 222:                 None,
 223:                 digest,
 224:                 None,
 225:                 &raw mut needed,
 226:                 NCRYPT_FLAGS(0),
 227:             )
 228:             .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptSignHash(size): {e}")))?;
 229:         }
 230:         let mut sig = vec![0u8; needed as usize];
 231:         // SAFETY: sig has `needed` bytes allocated.
 232:         unsafe {
 233:             NCryptSignHash(
 234:                 self.key,
 235:                 None,
 236:                 digest,
 237:                 Some(&mut sig),
 238:                 &raw mut needed,
 239:                 NCRYPT_FLAGS(0),
 240:             )
 241:             .map_err(|e| internal(format!("NCryptSignHash: {e}")))?;
 242:         }
 243:         sig.truncate(needed as usize);
 244:         Ok(sig)
 245:     }
 246: }

 248: // SAFETY: NCrypt handles are thread-safe per MSDN guidance. The
 249: // kernel resolves the opaque handle integers; multiple threads can
 250: // hold and use them simultaneously.

 254: /// Produce a `platform_quote` payload that binds a doc-level digest
 255: /// to the TPM-resident ECDSA-P256 key. Wire layout:
 256: ///
 257: /// ```text
 258: /// platform_quote := u16(pub_len) || pub_blob || u16(sig_len) || sig
 259: /// ```
 260: ///
 261: /// # Errors
 262: /// Returns `Internal` if either `public_blob` or `sign` fails.
 263: pub fn produce_platform_quote(
 264:     key: &TpmAttestationKey,
 265:     digest: &[u8; 32],
 266: ) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 267:     let pub_blob = key.public_blob()?;
 268:     let sig = key.sign(digest)?;
 269:     let pub_len = u16::try_from(pub_blob.len())
 270:         .map_err(|_| internal("public_blob too large for u16 length prefix".into()))?;
 271:     let sig_len = u16::try_from(sig.len())
 272:         .map_err(|_| internal("sig too large for u16 length prefix".into()))?;
 273:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(2 + pub_blob.len() + 2 + sig.len());
 274:     out.extend_from_slice(&pub_len.to_be_bytes());
 275:     out.extend_from_slice(&pub_blob);
 276:     out.extend_from_slice(&sig_len.to_be_bytes());
 277:     out.extend_from_slice(&sig);
 278:     Ok(out)
 279: }

 283: /// [`crate::platform_quote::parse_platform_quote`]; this module
 284: /// re-exports it for back-compat with callers that imported through
 285: /// `windows_tpm`. The duplicate also held a `Box::leak`-based
 286: /// `internal()` helper that leaked per-error allocations; that's
 287: /// gone too.
 288: pub use crate::platform_quote::parse_platform_quote;

 290: /// Produce a fully TPM-rooted [`crate::AttestationDoc`].
 291: ///
 292: /// Flow:
 293: /// 1. Compute the TPM sub-transcript via
 294: ///    [`crate::canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript`].
 295: /// 2. TPM signs that digest; package as `platform_quote` envelope.
 296: /// 3. Call [`crate::ConfidentialProvider::attest`] with the
 297: ///    `platform_quote` already wired in by way of a custom
 298: ///    issue path — the master sig over the full canonical
 299: ///    transcript now transitively commits to the TPM sig.
 300: ///
 301: /// The returned doc's `platform_quote` field carries the TPM
 302: /// signature; peers verify it via
 303: /// [`crate::verify_platform_quote`] in addition to the master sig.
 304: ///
 305: /// # Errors
 306: /// Returns whatever [`crate::ConfidentialProvider::attest`] or the
 307: /// TPM `produce_platform_quote` call returns.
 308: pub fn attest_with_tpm(
 309:     provider: &crate::SoftwareProvider,
 310:     sealed_master: &crate::SealedKey,
 311:     tpm: &TpmAttestationKey,
 312:     peer_nonce: crate::AttestationNonce,
 313:     issued_unix: u64,
 314:     deadline_unix: u64,
 315:     field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 316:     issuer_sdp_pubkey: crate::attestation::IssuerSdpPubkey,
 317: ) -> ConfidentialResult<crate::AttestationDoc> {
 318:     use crate::attestation::{canonical_attestation_transcript, AttestationDoc};
 319:     use crate::ProviderTag;
 320: 
 321:     // Single unseal of the master — used for both verifying-key
 322:     // derivation and final hybrid signature. Replaces the earlier
 323:     // pair of `provider.verifying_key()` + `provider.sealed_sign()`
 324:     // calls (which each unsealed independently).
 325:     let (sk, master_vk) = provider.derive_hybrid_pair(sealed_master)?;
 326:     let master_vk_bytes = master_vk.to_bytes();
 327:     let field_witness_commitment = field_witness.map(|w| {
 328:         let mut h = blake3::Hasher::new();
 329:         h.update(crate::attestation::ATTESTATION_FIELD_WITNESS_DOMAIN);
 330:         h.update(w);
 331:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 332:     });
 333:     // (1) TPM sub-transcript over the doc's metadata.
 334:     let sub_digest = crate::platform_quote::canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript(
 335:         ProviderTag::WindowsTpm,
 336:         &master_vk_bytes,
 337:         &peer_nonce,
 338:         issued_unix,
 339:         deadline_unix,
 340:         field_witness_commitment.as_ref(),
 341:     );
 342:     // (2) TPM signs the sub-digest; package as platform_quote bytes.
 343:     let platform_quote = produce_platform_quote(tpm, &sub_digest)?;
 344: 
 345:     // (3) Master hybrid sig over the full transcript including
 346:     //     platform_quote. Transitively commits to the TPM sig.
 347:     let full_transcript = canonical_attestation_transcript(
 348:         ProviderTag::WindowsTpm,
 349:         &master_vk,
 350:         &peer_nonce,
 351:         issued_unix,
 352:         deadline_unix,
 353:         field_witness,
 354:         &platform_quote,
 355:         &issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 356:     );
 357:     let master_sig = sk.sign(&full_transcript)?.to_vec();
 358: 
 359:     Ok(AttestationDoc {
 360:         provider_tag: ProviderTag::WindowsTpm,
 361:         master_vk,
 362:         peer_nonce,
 363:         issued_unix,
 364:         deadline_unix,
 365:         field_witness_commitment,
 366:         platform_quote,
 367:         issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 368:         master_sig,
 369:     })
 370: }
 371: 
 372: /// Verify a [`crate::AttestationDoc`] that carries a TPM-rooted
 373: /// `platform_quote`. Performs BOTH layers of validation:
 374: ///
 375: /// 1. [`crate::verify_attestation`] for the master hybrid sig +
 376: ///    nonce binding + freshness window + field-witness binding.
 377: /// 2. [`crate::verify_platform_quote`] for the TPM ECDSA sig over
 378: ///    the sub-transcript.
 379: ///
 380: /// On success returns the TPM's public-key blob so the caller can
 381: /// pin it for trust-on-first-use binding (subsequent verifies can
 382: /// then refuse docs that change TPM identity).
 383: ///
 384: /// # Errors
 385: /// Returns the first layered failure (master sig or TPM sig).
 386: pub fn verify_attestation_with_tpm(
 387:     doc: &crate::AttestationDoc,
 388:     expected_peer_nonce: &crate::AttestationNonce,
 389:     expected_field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 390:     now_unix: u64,
 391:     min_tier: crate::tier::ConfidentialTier,
 392:     expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey: &crate::attestation::IssuerSdpPubkey,
 393: ) -> ConfidentialResult<Vec<u8>> {
 394:     use crate::ProviderTag;
 395: 
 396:     if doc.provider_tag != ProviderTag::WindowsTpm {
 397:         return Err(ConfidentialError::AttestationProviderTagMismatch);
 398:     }
 399:     // (1) Layered master sig + nonce + freshness + witness + tier + SDP binding.
 400:     crate::verify_attestation(
 401:         doc,
 402:         expected_peer_nonce,
 403:         expected_field_witness,
 404:         now_unix,
 405:         min_tier,
 406:         expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 407:     )?;
 408:     // (2) TPM platform_quote chain.
 409:     crate::verify_platform_quote(
 410:         &doc.platform_quote,
 411:         doc.provider_tag,
 412:         &doc.master_vk.to_bytes(),
 413:         &doc.peer_nonce,
 414:         doc.issued_unix,
 415:         doc.deadline_unix,
 416:         doc.field_witness_commitment.as_ref(),
 417:     )
 418: }

  71:     // T-REMOTE-IMPERSONATE: attacker constructs a doc claiming
  72:     // master_vk=victim_vk but signs with their own key. Verify

  75:     let attacker = fresh_sk();

   2: //! Mesh exercised in one flow.
   3: //!
   4: //! This is the canonical "all 10 rows compose" demonstration. A
   5: //! single test walks through:
   6: //!
   7: //! 1. **Row 1** — mint a hybrid PQ master + per-device subkeys.
   8: //! 2. **Row 8** — register the personal device mesh (phone +
   9: //!    laptop), build a τ_c-weighted route between them.
  10: //! 3. **Row 4 / Row 6** — same routing primitives apply.
  11: //! 4. **Row 5** — build a Sphinx onion through the route.

  13: //! 6. **Row 9** — split the master's day-1 child key into a
  14: //!    threshold-recoverable set of shares.

   1: //! Constant-time gate for the Row 10 confidential-compute surface.
   2: //!
   3: //! AEAD tag verification, attestation peer-nonce check, and master-
   4: //! sig verify are all expected to be constant-time with respect to
   5: //! WHICH byte differs in the failing input. We measure timing
   6: //! variance and require rel-stddev ≤ 30% (the same gate every other
   7: //! row uses).
   8: 
   9: use ol_confidential::{
  10:     fresh_attestation_nonce, sign_attestation, verify_attestation, ConfidentialProvider,
  11:     ConfidentialTier, ProviderTag, SoftwareProvider, ISSUER_SDP_PUBKEY_LEN,
  12: };
  13: use ol_pqsig::HybridSigningKey;
  14: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  15: use std::time::Instant;
  16: 
  17: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 2_000;
  18: const BUCKETS: usize = 4;
  19: const REL_STDDEV_MAX: f64 = 0.30;
  20: const TEST_SDP_PUBKEY: [u8; ISSUER_SDP_PUBKEY_LEN] = [0xA5; ISSUER_SDP_PUBKEY_LEN];
  21: 
  22: fn time_ns<F: FnMut()>(mut f: F) -> u64 {
  23:     let t0 = Instant::now();
  24:     f();
  25:     let dt = t0.elapsed();
  26:     u64::try_from(dt.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
  27: }
  28: 
  29: fn ct_summary(times: &[u64]) -> (f64, f64, f64) {
  30:     let n = times.len() as f64;
  31:     let mean = times.iter().map(|t| *t as f64).sum::<f64>() / n;
  32:     let var = times
  33:         .iter()
  34:         .map(|t| {
  35:             let d = (*t as f64) - mean;
  36:             d * d
  37:         })
  38:         .sum::<f64>()
  39:         / n;
  40:     let stddev = var.sqrt();
  41:     let rel = stddev / mean;
  42:     (mean, stddev, rel)
  43: }
  44: 
  45: // Note: we deliberately do NOT ct-gate `sealed_sign`. ML-DSA-65
  46: // uses Fiat-Shamir-with-aborts rejection sampling, so signing time
  47: // has algorithm-inherent variance with respect to the message hash.
  48: // That timing leak doesn't help an attacker — they can't invert it
  49: // back to secret material — but it ALWAYS exceeds a 30% rel-stddev
  50: // gate, which is why it's not gated here. Verify is the cryptographic
  51: // surface that MUST be constant-time, and it is (gated below).
  52: 
  53: #[test]
  54: fn ct_attest_verify_uniform_over_invalid_sigs() {
  55:     // Verify timing on INVALID sigs should be ~uniform — the verifier
  56:     // shouldn't leak where the byte mismatch lives.
  57:     let (sk, _vk) = HybridSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
  58:     let nonce = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);

  43:         tampered.bytes[i] ^= *b;

  50:         nonce[i] = *b;

  55:         3 => ProviderTag::AndroidStrongBox,
  56:         4 => ProviderTag::WindowsTpm,
  57:         5 => ProviderTag::IntelSgx,

   1: //! Concurrency stress on the real Windows TPM.
   2: //!
   3: //! NCrypt handles are documented thread-safe by MSDN, but consumer
   4: //! TPMs have a single internal command pipeline — under heavy
   5: //! concurrent load they return `TPM_RC_CANCELED` rather than block.
   6: //! These tests verify:
   7: //!
   8: //! - Sharing one `TpmAttestationKey` across threads via `Arc` never
   9: //!   panics or corrupts state.
  10: //! - Each thread eventually completes its sign (with retry).
  11: //! - The TPM-issued signatures from concurrent threads all verify
  12: //!   under the same TPM public key.
  13: 
  14: #![cfg(all(target_os = "windows", feature = "windows-tpm"))]
  15: 
  16: use std::sync::Arc;
  17: use std::thread;
  18: use std::time::Duration;
  19: 
  20: use ol_confidential::platform_quote::{
  21:     canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript, verify_platform_quote,
  22: };
  23: use ol_confidential::windows_tpm::{produce_platform_quote, TpmAttestationKey};
  24: use ol_confidential::ProviderTag;
  25: 
  26: const KEY_NAME: &str = "OL-confidential-tpm-concurrency-v1";
  27: const VK_PLACEHOLDER: [u8; 1984] = [0x42u8; 1984];
  28: 
  29: fn sign_with_retry(key: &TpmAttestationKey, digest: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<u8> {
  30:     let mut attempts = 0;
  31:     loop {
  32:         match key.sign(digest) {
  33:             Ok(sig) => return sig,
  34:             Err(_) if attempts < 10 => {
  35:                 attempts += 1;
  36:                 // TPM is busy — back off.
  37:                 thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50 * attempts));
  38:             }
  39:             Err(e) => panic!("TPM sign failed after retries: {e}"),
  40:         }
  41:     }
  42: }
  43: 
  44: #[test]
  45: #[ignore = "requires hardware TPM access"]
  46: fn tpm_4_threads_concurrent_sign() {
  47:     let key = Arc::new(
  48:         TpmAttestationKey::acquire_or_create(KEY_NAME).expect("acquire"),
  49:     );
  50:     let mut handles = Vec::new();
  51:     for thread_idx in 0..4 {
  52:         let k = Arc::clone(&key);
  53:         handles.push(thread::spawn(move || {
  54:             let mut sigs = Vec::new();
  55:             for op_idx in 0..5 {
  56:                 let mut digest = [0u8; 32];
  57:                 digest[0] = thread_idx as u8;
  58:                 digest[1] = op_idx as u8;
  59:                 let sig = sign_with_retry(&k, &digest);
  60:                 sigs.push((digest, sig));
  61:             }
  62:             sigs
  63:         }));
  64:     }
  65:     let mut all = Vec::new();
  66:     for h in handles {
  67:         all.extend(h.join().expect("thread join"));
  68:     }
  69:     assert_eq!(all.len(), 4 * 5);
  70:     // Every sig is non-empty and they're not all identical.
  71:     let first_sig = all[0].1.clone();
  72:     let mut some_differ = false;
  73:     for (_, sig) in &all {
  74:         assert!(!sig.is_empty());
  75:         if sig != &first_sig {
  76:             some_differ = true;
  77:         }
  78:     }
  79:     assert!(some_differ, "concurrent sigs over different digests must differ");
  80: }
  81: 
  82: #[test]
  83: #[ignore = "requires hardware TPM access"]
  84: fn tpm_concurrent_attestation_quotes_all_verify() {
  85:     let key = Arc::new(
  86:         TpmAttestationKey::acquire_or_create(KEY_NAME).expect("acquire"),
  87:     );
  88:     let mut handles = Vec::new();
  89:     for thread_idx in 0..4 {
  90:         let k = Arc::clone(&key);
  91:         handles.push(thread::spawn(move || {
  92:             let mut nonce = [0u8; 32];
  93:             nonce[0] = thread_idx as u8;
  94:             let digest = canonical_platform_quote_subtranscript(
  95:                 ProviderTag::WindowsTpm,
  96:                 &VK_PLACEHOLDER,
  97:                 &nonce,
  98:                 100,
  99:                 120,
 100:                 None,
 101:             );
 102:             // Produce a quote with retry-on-TPM-busy.
 103:             let mut attempts = 0;
 104:             loop {
 105:                 match produce_platform_quote(&k, &digest) {
 106:                     Ok(q) => break (nonce, q),
 107:                     Err(_) if attempts < 10 => {
 108:                         attempts += 1;
 109:                         thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50 * attempts));
 110:                     }
 111:                     Err(e) => panic!("produce_platform_quote failed: {e}"),
 112:                 }
 113:             }
 114:         }));
 115:     }
 116:     for h in handles {
 117:         let (nonce, quote) = h.join().expect("thread join");
 118:         let pub_blob = verify_platform_quote(
 119:             &quote,
 120:             ProviderTag::WindowsTpm,
 121:             &VK_PLACEHOLDER,
 122:             &nonce,
 123:             100,
 124:             120,
 125:             None,
 126:         )
 127:         .expect("verify");
 128:         assert!(!pub_blob.is_empty());
 129:     }
 130: }

   1: //! Criterion benchmarks for `ol_crdt`.
   2: //!
   3: //! The folder merge is the engine's foundation for the "every state
   4: //! change is CRDT-mergeable" doctrine — daemon gossip will invoke it on
   5: //! every sync round, so it must stay cheap at realistic state sizes.
   6: 
   7: use criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, BenchmarkId, Criterion};
   8: use ol_crdt::{Folder, Lattice, ReplicaId};
   9: 
  10: fn rid(b: u8) -> ReplicaId {
  11:     ReplicaId([b; 32])
  12: }
  13: fn fid(i: u32) -> [u8; 32] {
  14:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
  15:     out[..4].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
  16:     out
  17: }
  18: 
  19: fn build_folder(n: usize, replica: u8) -> Folder {
  20:     let r = rid(replica);
  21:     let mut f = Folder::new();
  22:     for i in 0..n {
  23:         f.add_file(
  24:             &r,
  25:             fid(i as u32),
  26:             format!("f{i}.bin"),
  27:             (i as u64) * 1024,
  28:             (i as u64) * 7,
  29:         );
  30:     }
  31:     f
  32: }
  33: 
  34: fn bench_add_file(c: &mut Criterion) {
  35:     c.bench_function("add_file_to_empty", |b| {
  36:         b.iter(|| {
  37:             let mut f = Folder::new();
  38:             f.add_file(&rid(1), fid(black_box(0)), "f.bin".into(), 1024, 100);
  39:             black_box(f);
  40:         });
  41:     });
  42: }
  43: 
  44: fn bench_merge_scaling(c: &mut Criterion) {
  45:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("merge_size");
  46:     for n in &[10usize, 100, 1000] {
  47:         let a = build_folder(*n, 0x01);
  48:         let b = build_folder(*n, 0x02);
  49:         group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(n), n, |bench, _| {
  50:             bench.iter(|| {
  51:                 let mut left = a.clone();
  52:                 left.merge(black_box(&b));
  53:                 black_box(left);
  54:             });
  55:         });
  56:     }
  57:     group.finish();
  58: }
  59: 
  60: fn bench_contains(c: &mut Criterion) {
  61:     let f = build_folder(1000, 0x01);
  62:     c.bench_function("contains_hit_among_1000", |b| {
  63:         b.iter(|| {
  64:             let hit = black_box(&f).contains(black_box(&fid(500)));
  65:             black_box(hit);
  66:         });
  67:     });
  68: }
  69: 
  70: criterion_group!(benches, bench_add_file, bench_merge_scaling, bench_contains);
  71: criterion_main!(benches);

   1: //! Folder CRDT: composes vector clock + OR-set of file ids + LWW per-file
   2: //! attribute registers.
   3: //!
   4: //! The folder model the plan calls for is:
   5: //!
   6: //! - The folder *exists* as soon as any replica adds it.
   7: //! - File entries are an OR-set keyed on a stable content-addressed
   8: //!   id (BLAKE3 of the manifest root).
   9: //! - Per-file attributes (display name, size, last-modified) are LWW
  10: //!   registers stamped with the local vector-clock counter.
  11: //!
  12: //! Merge is pointwise across all three sub-lattices. The folder type
  13: //! itself satisfies the lattice merge laws (the acceptance gate
  14: //! verifies this across ≥1M random states).
  15: 
  16: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  17: 
  18: use crate::lww::LwwRegister;
  19: use crate::or_set::{OrSet, Tag};
  20: use crate::vector_clock::{ReplicaId, VectorClock};
  21: use crate::Lattice;
  22: 
  23: /// Stable id for a file inside a folder.
  24: pub type FileId = [u8; 32];
  25: 
  26: /// Per-file metadata, all LWW-stamped so concurrent renames / size
  27: /// adjustments resolve deterministically.
  28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  29: pub struct FileEntry {
  30:     pub display_name: LwwRegister<String>,
  31:     pub size_bytes: LwwRegister<u64>,
  32:     pub last_modified_ms: LwwRegister<u64>,
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl Lattice for FileEntry {
  36:     fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) {
  37:         self.display_name.merge(&other.display_name);
  38:         self.size_bytes.merge(&other.size_bytes);
  39:         self.last_modified_ms.merge(&other.last_modified_ms);
  40:     }
  41: }
  42: 
  43: /// The Folder CRDT.
  44: ///
  45: /// Holds:
  46: /// - A vector clock summarising which counter each replica has reached.
  47: /// - An OR-set of `FileId`s currently present.
  48: /// - A map of per-file `FileEntry` lattices.
  49: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
  50: pub struct Folder {
  51:     pub clock: VectorClock,
  52:     pub files: OrSet<FileId>,
  53:     pub entries: BTreeMap<FileId, FileEntry>,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl Folder {
  57:     pub fn new() -> Self {
  58:         Self::default()
  59:     }
  60: 
  61:     /// Add a file with metadata. Stamps with this replica's next clock
  62:     /// tick to derive a unique OR-set tag and LWW timestamp.
  63:     pub fn add_file(
  64:         &mut self,
  65:         replica: &ReplicaId,
  66:         id: FileId,
  67:         display_name: String,
  68:         size_bytes: u64,
  69:         last_modified_ms: u64,
  70:     ) {
  71:         let counter = self.clock.tick(replica);
  72:         let tag = derive_tag(replica, counter);
  73:         self.files.add(id, tag);
  74:         let entry = FileEntry {
  75:             display_name: LwwRegister::new(display_name, counter, replica.clone()),
  76:             size_bytes: LwwRegister::new(size_bytes, counter, replica.clone()),
  77:             last_modified_ms: LwwRegister::new(last_modified_ms, counter, replica.clone()),
  78:         };
  79:         match self.entries.get_mut(&id) {
  80:             Some(existing) => existing.merge(&entry),
  81:             None => {
  82:                 self.entries.insert(id, entry);
  83:             }
  84:         }
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     pub fn remove_file(&mut self, replica: &ReplicaId, id: &FileId) {
  88:         // Advance the clock so the observer knows this remove happened
  89:         // after the previous local state.
  90:         self.clock.tick(replica);
  91:         self.files.remove(id);
  92:     }
  93: 
  94:     pub fn contains(&self, id: &FileId) -> bool {
  95:         self.files.contains(id)
  96:     }
  97: 
  98:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&FileId, &FileEntry)> {
  99:         self.entries
 100:             .iter()
 101:             .filter(move |(id, _)| self.files.contains(id))
 102:     }
 103: }
 104: 
 105: impl Lattice for Folder {
 106:     fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) {
 107:         self.clock.merge(&other.clock);
 108:         self.files.merge(&other.files);
 109:         // Per-key LWW merge. Insert missing entries; merge existing.
 110:         for (id, entry) in &other.entries {
 111:             match self.entries.get_mut(id) {
 112:                 Some(existing) => existing.merge(entry),
 113:                 None => {
 114:                     self.entries.insert(*id, entry.clone());
 115:                 }
 116:             }
 117:         }
 118:     }
 119: }
 120: 
 121: fn derive_tag(replica: &ReplicaId, counter: u64) -> Tag {
 122:     let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new();
 123:     hasher.update(b"ol-crdt-tag-v1");
 124:     hasher.update(&replica.0);
 125:     hasher.update(&counter.to_le_bytes());
 126:     let h = hasher.finalize();
 127:     let mut out = [0u8; 16];
 128:     out.copy_from_slice(&h.as_bytes()[..16]);
 129:     Tag(out)
 130: }

   1: //! CRDT primitives for One Link shared folders.
   2: //!
   3: //! See `docs/decisions/0022-crdt-folders.md`.
   4: //!
   5: //! The plan's Phase C item #4 calls for CRDT shared folders replacing the
   6: //! existing vector-clock manifest in `One_link/src/one_link/foldersync.py`.
   7: //! This crate ships the four lattice types the folder model needs:
   8: //!
   9: //! - `VectorClock` for causal ordering across replicas.
  10: //! - `OrSet` for collaboratively edited file lists (add/remove that don't
  11: //!   resurrect tombstones).
  12: //! - `LwwRegister` for last-writer-wins scalar attributes.
  13: //! - `Folder`: composes the three to model a one-folder-per-replica state.
  14: //!
  15: //! All three sub-lattices satisfy the lattice merge laws (commutativity,
  16: //! associativity, idempotency). The acceptance gate
  17: //! (`tests/lattice_laws.rs`) property-tests this across ≥1M random states.
  18: 
  19: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  20: #![allow(missing_docs)]
  21:

  23: mod folder;
  24: mod lww;
  25: mod or_set;
  26: mod vector_clock;

  29: pub use folder::{FileEntry, FileId, Folder};
  30: pub use lww::LwwRegister;
  31: pub use or_set::OrSet;
  32: pub use vector_clock::{ReplicaId, VectorClock};
  33: 
  34: /// Lattice element trait: every CRDT type used in a folder must implement
  35: /// commutative + associative + idempotent merge.
  36: pub trait Lattice: Clone {
  37:     fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self);
  38: }

   1: //! Last-Writer-Wins register.
   2: //!
   3: //! Holds a value plus a (timestamp, replica id) pair. Merge picks the
   4: //! pair with the larger timestamp; ties break on a BLAKE3 keyed hash
   5: //! of `(replica || value-debug || timestamp)` so the merge is
   6: //! deterministic across all replicas AND an adversary can't grind
   7: //! a high replica id to win every concurrent edit (audit L10 May
   8: //! 2026 — previously `other.replica.0 > self.replica.0` let an
   9: //! attacker generate pubkeys until the BLAKE3 fingerprint started
  10: //! with high bytes ≈ 2^32 work for a leading `0xFFFF_FFFF`).
  11: //!
  12: //! Tie-breaker hash inputs:
  13: //! - The replica id (32 bytes)
  14: //! - The Debug repr of the value (so the hash differs per concurrent
  15: //!   edit; an attacker can't precompute a "always-high" replica id
  16: //!   that wins regardless of value)
  17: //! - The timestamp (8 bytes)
  18: //!
  19: //! Domain-tagged via BLAKE3 derive_key so this hash can't be confused
  20: //! with any other in the workspace.
  21: 
  22: use crate::vector_clock::ReplicaId;
  23: use crate::Lattice;
  24: 
  25: /// BLAKE3 derive_key context for the LWW tie-break hash. Bumping
  26: /// this is a wire-incompatible change to the merge function — only
  27: /// safe at a fresh-folder boundary.
  28: const LWW_TIEBREAK_CONTEXT: &str = "ol-crdt-lww-tiebreak-v1";
  29: 
  30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  31: pub struct LwwRegister<V: Clone + PartialEq + Eq + core::fmt::Debug> {
  32:     pub value: V,
  33:     pub timestamp: u64,
  34:     pub replica: ReplicaId,
  35: }
  36: 
  37: impl<V: Clone + PartialEq + Eq + core::fmt::Debug> LwwRegister<V> {
  38:     pub fn new(value: V, timestamp: u64, replica: ReplicaId) -> Self {
  39:         Self {
  40:             value,
  41:             timestamp,
  42:             replica,
  43:         }
  44:     }
  45: 
  46:     /// Audit L10 May 2026 — compute the tie-break hash. Combines
  47:     /// the replica id with a value-derived component so an attacker
  48:     /// can't grind a single high replica id that wins concurrent
  49:     /// edits across all values. The value's Debug repr is the
  50:     /// portable "value bytes" surface across generic V types.
  51:     fn tiebreak_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
  52:         let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(32 + 64);
  53:         buf.extend_from_slice(&self.replica.0);
  54:         // Hash the value's Debug repr — for the typical V types
  55:         // we use (strings, ids) this captures the content. The
  56:         // attacker can't precompute a winning replica id without
  57:         // knowing the eventual value.
  58:         let value_repr = format!("{:?}", self.value);
  59:         buf.extend_from_slice(value_repr.as_bytes());
  60:         buf.extend_from_slice(&self.timestamp.to_be_bytes());
  61:         blake3::derive_key(LWW_TIEBREAK_CONTEXT, &buf)
  62:     }
  63: 
  64:     /// Returns true iff `other` should overwrite self.
  65:     fn dominates(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  66:         match other.timestamp.cmp(&self.timestamp) {
  67:             std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => true,
  68:             std::cmp::Ordering::Less => false,
  69:             std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
  70:                 // L10 tie-break — hash-derived rather than raw
  71:                 // replica.0 comparison.
  72:                 other.tiebreak_hash() > self.tiebreak_hash()
  73:             }
  74:         }
  75:     }
  76: }
  77: 
  78: impl<V: Clone + PartialEq + Eq + core::fmt::Debug> Lattice for LwwRegister<V> {
  79:     fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) {
  80:         if self.dominates(other) {
  81:             *self = other.clone();
  82:         }
  83:     }
  84: }
  85: 
  86: #[cfg(test)]
  87: mod tests {
  88:     use super::*;
  89: 
  90:     fn rid(b: u8) -> ReplicaId {
  91:         ReplicaId([b; 32])
  92:     }
  93: 
  94:     #[test]
  95:     fn higher_timestamp_wins() {
  96:         let mut a = LwwRegister::new("v1", 1, rid(1));
  97:         let b = LwwRegister::new("v2", 2, rid(2));
  98:         a.merge(&b);
  99:         assert_eq!(a.value, "v2");
 100:     }

 102:     #[test]
 103:     fn tie_break_is_deterministic_and_commutative() {
 104:         // L10 May 2026 — tie-break is now hash-derived, so the
 105:         // exact winner depends on (replica, value, timestamp) all
 106:         // mixed in. The contract we test: BOTH orderings of the
 107:         // same merge inputs converge to the SAME value
 108:         // (commutativity).
 109:         let mut a = LwwRegister::new("v1", 5, rid(1));
 110:         let b = LwwRegister::new("v2", 5, rid(2));
 111:         a.merge(&b);
 112:         let forward_winner = a.value;
 113: 
 114:         let mut b2 = LwwRegister::new("v2", 5, rid(2));
 115:         let a2 = LwwRegister::new("v1", 5, rid(1));
 116:         b2.merge(&a2);
 117:         let reverse_winner = b2.value;
 118:

 120:     }

 122:     #[test]

 128:         // wins regardless of value.
 129:         // Find a value where low_replica wins over high_replica

 135:             high.merge(&low);
 136:             if high.replica == rid(0x01) {
 137:                 found_inversion = true;
 138:                 break;
 139:             }
 140:         }
 141:         assert!(
 142:             found_inversion,
 143:             "high-replica should not win every tie-break — \
 144:              grind-defeats-the-CRDT vector still open"
 145:         );
 146:     }

 151:         let snap = a.clone();
 152:         a.merge(&snap);

 154:     }

   1: //! Observed-Remove Set (OR-set).
   2: //!
   3: //! Each add stamps the element with a unique tag (here: a 16-byte
   4: //! BLAKE3-derived id keyed on the replica + counter). Remove tombstones
   5: //! the *tags currently observed*. Concurrent (add, remove) of the same
   6: //! element resolves as add-wins: the concurrent add has a fresh tag that
   7: //! the remove never saw.
   8: //!
   9: //! Bounded-storage variant: we keep the set of tombstoned tags. For long-
  10: //! lived folders a periodic `prune_synced(vc)` pass garbage-collects
  11: //! tombstones causally dominated by every replica's clock. This crate
  12: //! doesn't enforce sync state — callers wire pruning to their gossip
  13: //! layer.
  14: 
  15: use std::collections::BTreeSet;
  16: 
  17: use crate::Lattice;
  18: 
  19: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
  20: pub struct Tag(pub [u8; 16]);
  21: 
  22: /// Generic OR-set keyed on any orderable element type.
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  24: pub struct OrSet<E: Ord + Clone> {
  25:     /// (element, tag) tuples that have been added.
  26:     pub(crate) added: BTreeSet<(E, Tag)>,
  27:     /// Tags whose add has been remove-tombstoned.
  28:     pub(crate) removed: BTreeSet<Tag>,
  29: }
  30: 
  31: impl<E: Ord + Clone> Default for OrSet<E> {
  32:     fn default() -> Self {
  33:         Self {
  34:             added: BTreeSet::new(),
  35:             removed: BTreeSet::new(),
  36:         }
  37:     }
  38: }
  39: 
  40: impl<E: Ord + Clone> OrSet<E> {
  41:     pub fn new() -> Self {
  42:         Self::default()
  43:     }
  44: 
  45:     /// Add `element` with the caller-supplied tag. Tags must be unique
  46:     /// per add — callers derive them from (replica id || vector clock
  47:     /// counter) hashed via BLAKE3, truncated to 16 bytes.
  48:     pub fn add(&mut self, element: E, tag: Tag) {
  49:         self.added.insert((element, tag));
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     /// Remove every currently-observed (element, tag) pair for this
  53:     /// element value. Future adds with a fresh tag survive — the
  54:     /// add-wins property.
  55:     pub fn remove(&mut self, element: &E) {
  56:         for (e, tag) in self.added.iter() {
  57:             if e == element && !self.removed.contains(tag) {
  58:                 self.removed.insert(tag.clone());
  59:             }
  60:         }
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// True if `element` is currently in the set (has at least one
  64:     /// non-tombstoned tag).
  65:     pub fn contains(&self, element: &E) -> bool {
  66:         self.added
  67:             .iter()
  68:             .any(|(e, tag)| e == element && !self.removed.contains(tag))
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &E> {
  72:         let mut emitted: BTreeSet<&E> = BTreeSet::new();
  73:         for (e, tag) in &self.added {
  74:             if !self.removed.contains(tag) {
  75:                 emitted.insert(e);
  76:             }
  77:         }
  78:         emitted.into_iter()
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
  82:         self.iter().count()
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  86:         self.len() == 0
  87:     }

  89:     /// Iterate the underlying (element, tag) add log in deterministic

  92:     pub fn iter_added(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &(E, Tag)> {
  93:         self.added.iter()
  94:     }
  95: 
  96:     /// Iterate the tombstone set in deterministic order.
  97:     pub fn iter_removed(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Tag> {
  98:         self.removed.iter()
  99:     }
 100: }

   1: //! Vector clocks for causal ordering between replicas.
   2: 
   3: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
   4: 
   5: use crate::Lattice;
   6: 
   7: /// Stable identifier for a replica. The folder model uses 32-byte
   8: /// BLAKE3 fingerprints of the device public key; here we keep it
   9: /// generic so callers control the namespace.
  10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)]
  11: pub struct ReplicaId(pub [u8; 32]);
  12: 
  13: /// Vector clock: per-replica monotonic counter, sparse map.
  14: ///
  15: /// Merge takes pointwise max; comparison is the standard partial order
  16: /// (a ≤ b iff every coordinate of a is ≤ b's, with strictness somewhere).
  17: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
  18: pub struct VectorClock {
  19:     pub(crate) counters: BTreeMap<ReplicaId, u64>,
  20: }
  21: 
  22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  23: pub enum ClockOrder {
  24:     Before,
  25:     After,
  26:     Equal,
  27:     Concurrent,
  28: }
  29: 
  30: impl VectorClock {
  31:     pub fn new() -> Self {
  32:         Self::default()
  33:     }
  34: 
  35:     /// Tick this replica's counter by one and return the new value.
  36:     pub fn tick(&mut self, replica: &ReplicaId) -> u64 {
  37:         let entry = self.counters.entry(replica.clone()).or_insert(0);
  38:         *entry += 1;
  39:         *entry
  40:     }
  41: 
  42:     pub fn get(&self, replica: &ReplicaId) -> u64 {
  43:         self.counters.get(replica).copied().unwrap_or(0)
  44:     }
  45: 
  46:     /// Iterate (replica, counter) pairs in deterministic order. Used by
  47:     /// the structural-hash function in the lattice-law acceptance gate.
  48:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&ReplicaId, &u64)> {
  49:         self.counters.iter()
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     /// Causal comparison. Returns `Concurrent` if neither dominates.
  53:     pub fn compare(&self, other: &Self) -> ClockOrder {
  54:         let mut self_dominates = false;
  55:         let mut other_dominates = false;
  56: 
  57:         let mut all_keys: std::collections::BTreeSet<&ReplicaId> = self.counters.keys().collect();
  58:         all_keys.extend(other.counters.keys());
  59: 
  60:         for k in all_keys {
  61:             let a = self.get(k);
  62:             let b = other.get(k);
  63:             if a > b {
  64:                 self_dominates = true;
  65:             } else if b > a {
  66:                 other_dominates = true;
  67:             }
  68:             if self_dominates && other_dominates {
  69:                 return ClockOrder::Concurrent;
  70:             }
  71:         }
  72:         match (self_dominates, other_dominates) {
  73:             (false, false) => ClockOrder::Equal,
  74:             (true, false) => ClockOrder::After,
  75:             (false, true) => ClockOrder::Before,
  76:             (true, true) => unreachable!("dominance flags exclusive above"),
  77:         }
  78:     }
  79: }
  80: 
  81: impl Lattice for VectorClock {
  82:     /// Pointwise max — the canonical CRDT merge for a vector clock.
  83:     fn merge(&mut self, other: &Self) {
  84:         for (rid, &v) in &other.counters {
  85:             let entry = self.counters.entry(rid.clone()).or_insert(0);
  86:             if v > *entry {
  87:                 *entry = v;
  88:             }
  89:         }
  90:     }
  91: }
  92:

   1: //! Phase C acceptance gate for `ol_crdt` (FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md line 289):
   2: //!
   3: //!     "lattice merge laws" property tests.
   4: //!
   5: //! Property-tests commutativity, associativity, and idempotency of
   6: //! `Folder::merge` across ≥1M random (a, b, c) triples. The randomized
   7: //! folder generator covers four state-shape buckets:
   8: //!
   9: //! 1. Pure adds.
  10: //! 2. Adds + removes.
  11: //! 3. Adds + concurrent re-adds (add-wins regression coverage).
  12: //! 4. LWW-attribute battles (concurrent renames of the same FileId).
  13: //!
  14: //! Iteration count is configurable via `OL_CRDT_GATE_ITERS` env var
  15: //! (default: 10_000 for CI; the acceptance gate run sets it to 1_000_000).
  16: //! At default iter count this test runs in ≤500 ms; at gate count it
  17: //! runs in ≤45 s on a tuned x86 host.
  18: 
  19: use std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher;
  20: use std::hash::Hasher;
  21: 
  22: use ol_crdt::{FileEntry, Folder, Lattice, LwwRegister, ReplicaId};
  23: 
  24: fn next_rng(state: &mut u64) -> u64 {
  25:     // SplitMix64. Tiny, fast, deterministic — we want reproducibility,
  26:     // not cryptographic quality.
  27:     *state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  28:     let mut z = *state;
  29:     z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  30:     z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  31:     z ^ (z >> 31)
  32: }
  33: 
  34: fn random_id(state: &mut u64, namespace: u8) -> [u8; 32] {
  35:     let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
  36:     for chunk in bytes.chunks_mut(8) {
  37:         let v = next_rng(state).to_le_bytes();
  38:         chunk.copy_from_slice(&v);
  39:     }
  40:     bytes[0] = namespace;
  41:     bytes
  42: }
  43: 
  44: fn random_folder(state: &mut u64, bucket: u8) -> Folder {
  45:     let mut f = Folder::new();
  46:     let replicas: Vec<ReplicaId> = (0..3)
  47:         .map(|i| ReplicaId(random_id(state, i as u8)))
  48:         .collect();
  49:     let file_ids: Vec<[u8; 32]> = (0..6).map(|i| random_id(state, 0x80 | i as u8)).collect();
  50: 
  51:     let n_ops = (next_rng(state) % 8) + 1;
  52:     for _ in 0..n_ops {
  53:         let r = &replicas[(next_rng(state) as usize) % replicas.len()];
  54:         let fid = file_ids[(next_rng(state) as usize) % file_ids.len()];
  55:         let action = match bucket {
  56:             0 => 0,                   // pure adds
  57:             1 => next_rng(state) % 2, // add or remove
  58:             2 => next_rng(state) % 3, // add / remove / re-add
  59:             _ => next_rng(state) % 4, // also rename battles
  60:         };
  61:         match action {
  62:             0 | 2 => {
  63:                 let name = format!("file_{}.bin", next_rng(state) % 100);
  64:                 let size = next_rng(state) % 65536;
  65:                 let mtime = next_rng(state) % 1_000_000;
  66:                 f.add_file(r, fid, name, size, mtime);
  67:             }
  68:             1 => {
  69:                 f.remove_file(r, &fid);
  70:             }
  71:             _ => {
  72:                 // Direct LWW attribute battle: overwrite display_name via
  73:                 // a freshly-stamped entry.
  74:                 let counter = f.clock.tick(r);
  75:                 let entry = FileEntry {
  76:                     display_name: LwwRegister::new(
  77:                         format!("rename_{}.bin", next_rng(state) % 100),
  78:                         counter,
  79:                         r.clone(),
  80:                     ),
  81:                     size_bytes: LwwRegister::new(0, counter, r.clone()),
  82:                     last_modified_ms: LwwRegister::new(counter, counter, r.clone()),
  83:                 };
  84:                 if let Some(existing) = f.entries.get_mut(&fid) {
  85:                     existing.merge(&entry);
  86:                 } else {
  87:                     f.entries.insert(fid, entry);
  88:                 }
  89:             }
  90:         }
  91:     }
  92:     f
  93: }
  94: 
  95: fn folder_hash(f: &Folder) -> u64 {
  96:     // Stable structural hash: hash the deterministic serialization of
  97:     // sub-lattices. Used to compare merge outputs across paths.
  98:     let mut h = DefaultHasher::new();
  99:     // Vector clock
 100:     for (rid, c) in f.clock.iter() {
 101:         h.write(&rid.0);
 102:         h.write_u64(*c);
 103:     }
 104:     h.write(b"|");
 105:     // OR-set added
 106:     for (e, tag) in f.files.iter_added() {
 107:         h.write(e);
 108:         h.write(&tag.0);
 109:     }
 110:     h.write(b"|");
 111:     // OR-set removed
 112:     for tag in f.files.iter_removed() {
 113:         h.write(&tag.0);
 114:     }
 115:     h.write(b"|");
 116:     // Entry map
 117:     for (fid, entry) in &f.entries {
 118:         h.write(fid);
 119:         h.write(entry.display_name.value.as_bytes());
 120:         h.write_u64(entry.display_name.timestamp);
 121:         h.write(&entry.display_name.replica.0);
 122:         h.write_u64(entry.size_bytes.value);
 123:         h.write_u64(entry.size_bytes.timestamp);
 124:         h.write(&entry.size_bytes.replica.0);
 125:         h.write_u64(entry.last_modified_ms.value);
 126:         h.write_u64(entry.last_modified_ms.timestamp);
 127:         h.write(&entry.last_modified_ms.replica.0);
 128:     }
 129:     h.finish()
 130: }
 131: 
 132: #[test]
 133: fn folder_merge_laws() {
 134:     let iters: u64 = std::env::var("OL_CRDT_GATE_ITERS")
 135:         .ok()
 136:         .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
 137:         .unwrap_or(10_000);
 138: 
 139:     let mut state: u64 = 0xCAFE_F00D_DEAD_BEEF;
 140:     let mut comm_fail = 0u64;
 141:     let mut assoc_fail = 0u64;
 142:     let mut idem_fail = 0u64;
 143: 
 144:     for i in 0..iters {
 145:         let bucket = (i % 4) as u8;
 146:         let a = random_folder(&mut state, bucket);
 147:         let b = random_folder(&mut state, bucket);
 148:         let c = random_folder(&mut state, bucket);
 149: 
 150:         // Commutativity: a ⊔ b == b ⊔ a
 151:         let mut ab = a.clone();
 152:         ab.merge(&b);
 153:         let mut ba = b.clone();
 154:         ba.merge(&a);
 155:         if folder_hash(&ab) != folder_hash(&ba) {
 156:             comm_fail += 1;
 157:         }
 158: 
 159:         // Associativity: (a ⊔ b) ⊔ c == a ⊔ (b ⊔ c)
 160:         let mut left = ab.clone();
 161:         left.merge(&c);
 162:         let mut bc = b.clone();
 163:         bc.merge(&c);
 164:         let mut right = a.clone();
 165:         right.merge(&bc);
 166:         if folder_hash(&left) != folder_hash(&right) {
 167:             assoc_fail += 1;
 168:         }
 169: 
 170:         // Idempotency: a ⊔ a == a
 171:         let mut aa = a.clone();
 172:         aa.merge(&a);
 173:         if folder_hash(&aa) != folder_hash(&a) {
 174:             idem_fail += 1;
 175:         }
 176:     }
 177: 
 178:     assert_eq!(
 179:         comm_fail, 0,
 180:         "commutativity violations across {iters} iters"
 181:     );
 182:     assert_eq!(
 183:         assoc_fail, 0,
 184:         "associativity violations across {iters} iters"
 185:     );
 186:     assert_eq!(idem_fail, 0, "idempotency violations across {iters} iters");
 187: }

  90: | `device_mesh::dfs_repair_plan_64_chunks_4_devices`     | 9.55 µs  | least-loaded planner over 64 chunks         |
  91: 
  92: ## Layer 3 — mesh state
  93: 
  94: | Benchmark                                              | Time     | Notes                                       |
  95: |---                                                     |---       |---                                          |
  96: | `device_mesh::mesh_state_auth_op_sign`                 | 318 µs   | subkey signs canonical transcript           |
  97: | `device_mesh::mesh_state_auth_op_verify`               | 53.2 µs  | hybrid signature verify                     |
  98: | `device_mesh::mesh_state_root_16_subtrees_8_keys`      | 8.45 µs  | BLAKE3 over 16 subtrees × 8 entries each    |
  99: | `device_mesh::mesh_state_ingest_single_op`             | 330 µs   | verify + apply + log + state-root update    |
 100: 
 101: ## Layer 2 — quorum
 102: 
 103: | Benchmark                                       | Time     | Notes                            |
 104: |---                                              |---       |---                               |
 105: | `device_mesh::quorum_mint_policy_3_of_5`        | 267 µs   | master signs policy transcript   |
 106: | `device_mesh::quorum_sign_approval`             | 330 µs   | approver signs proposal_id       |
 107: | `device_mesh::quorum_propose_operation`         | 538 µs   | issuer signs full proposal       |
 108: | `device_mesh::quorum_certificate_verify_2_of_3` | 559 µs   | end-to-end cert verify           |
 109: 
 110: ## What this means for the daemon
 111: 
 112: - **Subkey derivation is free**: 221 ns. Re-deriving any historical
 113:   day on the master takes microseconds for a 365-day chain.
 114: - **Field binding costs ~130 ns extra**: the OTP mask is one BLAKE3
 115:   XOF expansion, then byte-XOR. Negligible.
 116: - **Ratchet step is free**: 238 ns. The daemon advances at midnight
 117:   local time; runtime cost is well under any scheduling jitter.
 118: - **Master pin handle is fast enough for UI**: 1.6 µs. The friend's
 119:   app can re-derive the pin handle on every render without it being
 120:   measurable.
 121: - **Hardware-wrap round-trip is ~330 ns per direction**: cold-storage
 122:   + load happens once per device boot. Even a daemon that boots 100
 123:   times a day pays only microseconds total.
 124: - **Mint + attestation is ~430 µs**: this is the master signing a
 125:   fresh subkey. Once per device pair, period.
 126: - **Liveness verify is ~53 µs**: same cost as a single PQ-hybrid
 127:   signature verify (row 1). At a 60-second heartbeat across 10
 128:   siblings, total verify cost is ~530 µs per minute.
 129: - **Liveness issue is ~688 µs**: dominated by the ML-DSA sign cost,
 130:   same as row 1's `pqsig::sign`. Each device pays this once per
 131:   heartbeat interval.
 132: - **Quorum cert verify is ~559 µs**: one master-signed-policy verify
 133:   + one master-signed-attestation verify per signer + one subkey
 134:   verify per signer. For 2-of-3, that's ~6 hybrid-verify calls,
 135:   bounded by ML-DSA verify (~50 µs) + book-keeping. Sublinear in
 136:   K for the bounded MAX_APPROVALS=64.
 137: - **Mint a policy in ~267 µs**: one master sign over a small
 138:   transcript. The master pays this once per policy version.
 139: 
 140: ## Repro
 141: 
 142: ```text
 143: cargo bench -p ol_device_mesh --bench device_mesh_bench
 144: ```

 443: fn bench_fan_out_plan(c: &mut Criterion) {
 444:     let policy = ErasurePolicy::new(10, 4, 1).unwrap();
 445:     let n_stripes = 8usize;
 446:     let stripe = policy.total_shards() as usize;
 447:     let chunks: Vec<ChunkHash> = (0..(n_stripes * stripe))
 448:         .map(|i| {
 449:             let mut h = [0u8; 32];
 450:             h[..2].copy_from_slice(&(i as u16).to_be_bytes());
 451:             h
 452:         })
 453:         .collect();
 454:     let m = FileManifest {
 455:         file_size: chunks.len() as u64,
 456:         chunk_size: 8192,
 457:         chunks: chunks.clone(),
 458:         mime: b"x".to_vec(),
 459:         created_unix: 0,
 460:         policy,
 461:     };
 462:     let placements: Vec<ChunkPlacement> = chunks
 463:         .iter()
 464:         .map(|c| {
 465:             let mut p = ChunkPlacement::empty(*c);
 466:             for i in 1u8..=4 {
 467:                 p.add_holder([i; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 1);
 468:             }
 469:             p
 470:         })
 471:         .collect();
 472:     let sources: Vec<SourceCapacity> = (1u8..=4)
 473:         .map(|i| SourceCapacity {
 474:             device_id: [i; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 475:             estimated_bps: 100_000_000 * u64::from(i),
 476:             current_load_bytes: 0,
 477:         })

 559: fn bench_self_routing_pick_best_route(c: &mut Criterion) {
 560:     use ol_device_mesh::self_routing::{
 561:         pick_best_route, sign_route_announcement, PeerLink, RouteTable,
 562:     };
 563:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
 564:     let mut ids = Vec::new();
 565:     let mut sks = Vec::new();
 566:     let mut atts = Vec::new();
 567:     for i in 1u8..=6 {
 568:         let id = [i; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 569:         let (sk, a) =
 570:             mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 0, 365).unwrap();
 571:         ids.push(id);
 572:         sks.push(sk);
 573:         atts.push(a);
 574:     }
 575:     let mut table = RouteTable::empty();
 576:     for i in 0..ids.len() {
 577:         let links: Vec<PeerLink> = (0..ids.len())
 578:             .filter(|j| *j != i)
 579:             .map(|j| PeerLink {
 580:                 peer_device_id: ids[j],
 581:                 tau_score: (((i + j) as u32) * 13) % 200 + 1,
 582:                 last_seen_unix: 1,
 583:                 direct: true,
 584:             })
 585:             .collect();
 586:         let ann = sign_route_announcement(&sks[i], 1, links).unwrap();
 587:         let vk = HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&atts[i].subkey_vk_bytes).unwrap();
 588:         table.ingest(ann, &vk).unwrap();
 589:     }
 590:     let src = ids[0];
 591:     let dst = ids[ids.len() - 1];
 592:     c.bench_function("device_mesh::self_routing_pick_best_route_6_node_clique", |b| {
 593:         b.iter(|| {
 594:             let r = pick_best_route(black_box(&table), black_box(&src), black_box(&dst));
 595:             black_box(r);
 596:         });
 597:     });
 598: }

   1: //! Cohort-prior cold-start.
   2: //!
   3: //! When a fresh user mints a fresh master, the routing history is
   4: //! empty. Picking purely-uniformly across devices works but is
   5: //! slow to converge. A cohort prior lets the daemon pre-seed the
   6: //! posterior with "typical-user" values per device class so the
   7: //! picker starts with a reasonable bias.
   8: 
   9: use crate::device_class::DeviceClass;
  10: 
  11: /// Default `α` for the cohort prior (uniform Beta(1, 1)).
  12: pub const COHORT_DEFAULT_ALPHA: u32 = 1;
  13: 
  14: /// Default `β` for the cohort prior.
  15: pub const COHORT_DEFAULT_BETA: u32 = 1;
  16: 
  17: /// Cold-start prior. Defaults to uniform Beta(1, 1); callers can
  18: /// adjust per-class to bias toward "people usually act on phone
  19: /// for DMs" / "people usually act on laptop for work files" /
  20: /// etc.
  21: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  22: pub struct CohortPrior {
  23:     /// Default α applied to every (context, device) pair.
  24:     pub default_alpha: u32,
  25:     /// Default β applied to every (context, device) pair.
  26:     pub default_beta: u32,
  27:     /// Extra α applied when the device is a Phone.
  28:     pub phone_alpha_bonus: u32,
  29:     /// Extra α applied when the device is a Laptop.
  30:     pub laptop_alpha_bonus: u32,
  31:     /// Extra α applied when the device is a Desktop.
  32:     pub desktop_alpha_bonus: u32,
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl CohortPrior {
  36:     /// Uniform prior (no class-specific bias). Slow to converge
  37:     /// but unbiased.
  38:     #[must_use]
  39:     pub const fn uniform() -> Self {
  40:         Self {
  41:             default_alpha: COHORT_DEFAULT_ALPHA,
  42:             default_beta: COHORT_DEFAULT_BETA,
  43:             phone_alpha_bonus: 0,
  44:             laptop_alpha_bonus: 0,
  45:             desktop_alpha_bonus: 0,
  46:         }
  47:     }
  48: 
  49:     /// Conservative bias: phone gets a small boost (most messages
  50:     /// land there first); laptop gets a moderate boost for work
  51:     /// stuff; desktop gets a small boost. Daemon-tunable.
  52:     #[must_use]
  53:     pub const fn typical_user() -> Self {
  54:         Self {
  55:             default_alpha: COHORT_DEFAULT_ALPHA,
  56:             default_beta: COHORT_DEFAULT_BETA,
  57:             phone_alpha_bonus: 3,
  58:             laptop_alpha_bonus: 2,
  59:             desktop_alpha_bonus: 1,
  60:         }
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// `(α, β)` for `class`. Sums the default + class-specific
  64:     /// bonus.
  65:     #[must_use]
  66:     pub const fn for_class(&self, class: DeviceClass) -> (u32, u32) {
  67:         let bonus = match class {
  68:             DeviceClass::Phone => self.phone_alpha_bonus,
  69:             DeviceClass::Laptop => self.laptop_alpha_bonus,
  70:             DeviceClass::Desktop => self.desktop_alpha_bonus,
  71:             _ => 0,
  72:         };
  73:         (self.default_alpha.saturating_add(bonus), self.default_beta)
  74:     }
  75: }
  76: 
  77: impl Default for CohortPrior {
  78:     fn default() -> Self {
  79:         Self::uniform()
  80:     }
  81: }
  82: 
  83: #[cfg(test)]
  84: mod tests {
  85:     use super::*;
  86: 
  87:     #[test]
  88:     fn uniform_no_bias() {
  89:         let p = CohortPrior::uniform();
  90:         for c in [
  91:             DeviceClass::Phone,
  92:             DeviceClass::Laptop,
  93:             DeviceClass::Desktop,
  94:             DeviceClass::Generic,
  95:         ] {
  96:             assert_eq!(p.for_class(c), (1, 1));
  97:         }
  98:     }

 109:         assert!(desktop_a > generic_a);
 110:     }

   1: //! Routing context: who / when / what the message is.
   2: //!
   3: //! The context is hashed into a 32-byte key that indexes the
   4: //! posterior table. The hash captures the discrete-bucketed
   5: //! features (hour-of-day, day-of-week, message class) plus the
   6: //! 32-byte contact pin so different contacts get separate
   7: //! posteriors.
   8: 
   9: use blake3::Hasher;
  10: 
  11: /// Domain-separation tag for the routing-context hash.
  12: pub const ROUTING_CONTEXT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-routing-context-v1";
  13: 
  14: /// One discrete routing context.
  15: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
  16: pub struct RoutingContext {
  17:     /// 32-byte BLAKE3 pin of the contact's master verifying key
  18:     /// (the friend the message is from). Zero bytes for system
  19:     /// messages with no contact.
  20:     pub contact_pin: [u8; 32],
  21:     /// Hour-of-day bucket (0..23).
  22:     pub hour_bucket: u8,
  23:     /// Day-of-week bucket (0..6, Monday = 0).
  24:     pub day_of_week: u8,
  25:     /// 4-byte message-class tag (e.g. `b"DM  "`, `b"FILE"`,
  26:     /// `b"CALL"`). Anything the daemon wants to bucket on.
  27:     pub message_class: [u8; 4],
  28:     /// Urgency bucket (0..3, higher = more urgent).
  29:     pub urgency: u8,
  30: }
  31: 
  32: impl RoutingContext {
  33:     /// Compute the 32-byte canonical hash that indexes the
  34:     /// posterior table.
  35:     #[must_use]
  36:     pub fn canonical_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
  37:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
  38:         h.update(ROUTING_CONTEXT_DOMAIN);
  39:         h.update(&self.contact_pin);
  40:         h.update(&[self.hour_bucket, self.day_of_week]);
  41:         h.update(&self.message_class);
  42:         h.update(&[self.urgency]);
  43:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
  44:     }
  45: }

  18: impl RoutingHistory {
  19:     /// Empty history.
  20:     #[must_use]
  21:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
  22:         Self::default()
  23:     }
  24: 
  25:     /// Observe an action. Creates a fresh record (with the supplied
  26:     /// prior `α / β`) if one doesn't exist; otherwise updates the
  27:     /// existing record's posterior.
  28:     pub fn observe(
  29:         &mut self,
  30:         context_hash: [u8; 32],
  31:         device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  32:         acted: bool,
  33:         now_unix: u64,
  34:         prior_alpha: u32,
  35:         prior_beta: u32,
  36:     ) {
  37:         let key = (context_hash, device_id);
  38:         let rec = self.records.entry(key).or_insert_with(|| {
  39:             DeviceActionRecord {
  40:                 context_hash,
  41:                 device_id,
  42:                 alpha: prior_alpha.max(1),
  43:                 beta: prior_beta.max(1),
  44:                 last_updated_unix: now_unix,
  45:             }
  46:         });
  47:         rec.observe(acted, now_unix);
  48:     }
  49: 
  50:     /// Look up the record for `(context_hash, device_id)`. Returns
  51:     /// `None` if we've never observed this pair.
  52:     #[must_use]
  53:     pub fn record(
  54:         &self,
  55:         context_hash: &[u8; 32],
  56:         device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  57:     ) -> Option<&DeviceActionRecord> {
  58:         self.records.get(&(*context_hash, *device_id))
  59:     }
  60: 
  61:     /// Total record count.
  62:     #[must_use]
  63:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
  64:         self.records.len()
  65:     }
  66: 
  67:     /// True iff no records.
  68:     #[must_use]
  69:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  70:         self.records.is_empty()
  71:     }
  72: 
  73:     /// Apply a global half-life decay sweep at `now_unix`. Daemon
  74:     /// runs this periodically (e.g., once per day).
  75:     pub fn decay_all(&mut self, now_unix: u64, half_life_secs: u64) {
  76:         for r in self.records.values_mut() {
  77:             r.decay(now_unix, half_life_secs);
  78:         }
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     /// Iterate `(context_hash, device_id, record)` in deterministic
  82:     /// order.
  83:     pub fn iter(
  84:         &self,
  85:     ) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&[u8; 32], &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], &DeviceActionRecord)>
  86:     {
  87:         self.records.iter().map(|((ctx, dev), rec)| (ctx, dev, rec))
  88:     }
  89: }

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 9 — active-inference device routing.
   2: //!
   3: //! Learns which device the user actually acts on for each kind of
   4: //! incoming message, in each time-of-day context, and routes
   5: //! accordingly. "Message from Alice on a Wednesday afternoon →
   6: //! laptop, because that's where Alex always reads Alice's
   7: //! messages." Outperforms the simple "wake whichever device is
   8: //! online" heuristic.
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Algorithm
  11: //!
  12: //! Per (`context`, `device`) pair we maintain a `Beta(α, β)`
  13: //! posterior over the probability that the user will ACT on a
  14: //! message routed to that device in that context. We update on
  15: //! every observed action (`act` → α += 1; `dismiss` → β += 1).
  16: //!
  17: //! Picking a device uses **Thompson sampling**: for each candidate
  18: //! we sample `p ~ Beta(α, β)` and pick the device with the largest
  19: //! sample. This naturally trades exploitation (high posterior mean)
  20: //! against exploration (high posterior variance) without any
  21: //! manual ε-greedy hack — and it converges to the optimal device
  22: //! at log(N) regret.
  23: //!
  24: //! Cold-start: when we have no personal history for `(context,
  25: //! device)`, the posterior starts at `Beta(α_cohort, β_cohort)`
  26: //! seeded from the cohort prior. Cohort prior can be a flat
  27: //! Beta(1, 1) (uniform) or per-device-class derived from typical-
  28: //! user data.
  29: //!
  30: //! ## Composition with the lower layers
  31: //!
  32: //! - **Layer 1**: device identities + master attestation.
  33: //! - **Layer 5 / Layer 6**: candidate device set comes from
  34: //!   wherever the daemon enumerates "online + reachable" devices.
  35: //! - **Phase D `ol_prefetch` / `ol_bandit`** (shipped): this layer
  36: //!   is the daemon-side glue that wraps the bandit into the
  37: //!   personal-device-mesh routing question.
  38: //!
  39: //! ## What this layer ships
  40: //!
  41: //! - [`RoutingContext`] — canonical structure for "who / when /
  42: //!   what" that conditions the routing decision.
  43: //! - [`DeviceActionRecord`] — Beta-posterior counters (α, β) per
  44: //!   `(context_hash, device_id)`.
  45: //! - [`RoutingHistory`] — observation table.
  46: //! - [`CohortPrior`] — cold-start prior.
  47: //! - [`pick_device_for_context`] — Thompson-sampling picker.
  48: //! - [`RoutingPolicy`] — daemon-side knobs.
  49: //!
  50: //! ## What this layer doesn't ship
  51: //!
  52: //! - The actual "did the user act on this" detector — daemon
  53: //!   surface; we just consume the boolean.
  54: //! - History replication across the mesh — Layer-3 CRDT mirror
  55: //!   pattern handles it; the daemon owns the wiring.
  56: 
  57: pub mod context;
  58: pub mod cohort;
  59: pub mod history;
  60: pub mod picker;
  61: pub mod policy;
  62: pub mod record;
  63: 
  64: pub use cohort::{CohortPrior, COHORT_DEFAULT_ALPHA, COHORT_DEFAULT_BETA};
  65: pub use context::{RoutingContext, ROUTING_CONTEXT_DOMAIN};
  66: pub use history::RoutingHistory;
  67: pub use picker::{pick_device_for_context, MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_PICK};
  68: pub use policy::{RoutingPolicy, ROUTING_HISTORY_DECAY_DEFAULT_SECS};
  69: pub use record::{DeviceActionRecord, MAX_POSTERIOR_COUNT};
<<<CONTENT_END>>>
