<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Repair planner — assign under-replicated chunks to fresh devices.
   2: //!
   3: //! Given a set of [`super::ChunkPlacement`] records and a set of
   4: //! mesh-member device ids, produce a list of [`RepairAssignment`]s
   5: //! that brings every chunk up to `policy.min_devices_per_shard`.
   6: //!
   7: //! The planner picks the LEAST-LOADED eligible device (smallest
   8: //! current chunk count) at each step, then bumps that device's
   9: //! virtual load before picking the next assignment so the work
  10: //! spreads evenly across the mesh.
  11: 
  12: use std::collections::BTreeSet;
  13: 
  14: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  15: 
  16: use super::manifest::ChunkHash;
  17: use super::placement::{device_load_map, ChunkPlacement};
  18: use super::policy::ErasurePolicy;
  19: 
  20: /// One repair assignment: device `assigned_to` should fetch + start
  21: /// holding chunk `chunk_hash`. Higher layers turn this into a
  22: /// fetch over Phase A2 QUIC (once shipped).
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  24: pub struct RepairAssignment {
  25:     /// Chunk needing additional replicas.
  26:     pub chunk_hash: ChunkHash,
  27:     /// Device picked to receive a copy.
  28:     pub assigned_to: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  29: }
  30: 
  31: /// Compute a repair plan.
  32: ///
  33: /// - `placements` are the current per-chunk placement records.
  34: /// - `mesh_devices` is the full mesh roster (every device id that
  35: ///   could legally receive a chunk; typically all devices in the
  36: ///   master's policy).
  37: /// - `policy` is the durability policy applied to under-replication
  38: ///   detection.
  39: ///
  40: /// Returns an assignment list in deterministic order (chunk hash
  41: /// ascending; for each chunk, devices that already-hold are
  42: /// excluded, and the remaining are picked least-loaded-first).
  43: #[must_use]
  44: pub fn repair_plan<'a, I>(
  45:     placements: I,
  46:     mesh_devices: &BTreeSet<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
  47:     policy: &ErasurePolicy,
  48: ) -> Vec<RepairAssignment>
  49: where
  50:     I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a ChunkPlacement>,
  51: {
  52:     // Snapshot the placements into a Vec so we can iterate twice.
  53:     let placements: Vec<&ChunkPlacement> = placements.into_iter().collect();
  54:     let mut load = device_load_map(placements.iter().copied());
  55:     // Ensure every mesh device has an entry (even if currently 0).
  56:     for d in mesh_devices {
  57:         load.entry(*d).or_insert(0);
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     let mut out = Vec::new();
  61:     // Iterate placements in deterministic order (BTreeMap-style:
  62:     // we sort by chunk hash before consuming).
  63:     let mut sorted: Vec<&ChunkPlacement> = placements;
  64:     sorted.sort_by_key(|p| p.chunk_hash);
  65:     for p in sorted {
  66:         let need = policy.needed_for_durability(p.holder_count());
  67:         for _ in 0..need {
  68:             // Pick the least-loaded eligible device that isn't
  69:             // already in the placement and isn't already-assigned
  70:             // this round.
  71:             let already_assigned: BTreeSet<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> = out
  72:                 .iter()
  73:                 .filter(|a: &&RepairAssignment| a.chunk_hash == p.chunk_hash)
  74:                 .map(|a| a.assigned_to)
  75:                 .collect();
  76:             let candidate = mesh_devices
  77:                 .iter()
  78:                 .filter(|d| !p.device_ids.contains(*d))
  79:                 .filter(|d| !already_assigned.contains(*d))
  80:                 .min_by_key(|d| (load.get(*d).copied().unwrap_or(0), **d));
  81:             let Some(&pick) = candidate else {
  82:                 break; // not enough eligible devices for this chunk
  83:             };
  84:             *load.entry(pick).or_insert(0) += 1;
  85:             out.push(RepairAssignment {
  86:                 chunk_hash: p.chunk_hash,
  87:                 assigned_to: pick,
  88:             });
  89:         }
  90:     }
  91:     out
  92: }
  93:

   1: //! Signed "I'm under duress" broadcast.
   2: //!
   3: //! When a [`super::DuressEnvelope::unlock`] returns
   4: //! [`super::UnlockOutcome::Decoy`], the daemon SILENTLY signs a
   5: //! [`DuressAlert`] using the seized device's subkey and emits it to
   6: //! every sibling. Siblings validate the signature under the
   7: //! master-attested subkey VK and escalate to a Layer-2 quorum
   8: //! revocation. The seized device continues running in decoy mode so
   9: //! the captor doesn't notice.
  10: 
  11: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
  12: 
  13: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  14: use crate::subkey::{DeviceSubkey, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  15: 
  16: /// Domain-separation tag for duress-alert signing.
  17: pub const DUR_ALERT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-duress-alert-v1";
  18: 
  19: /// One signed duress alert.
  20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  21: pub struct DuressAlert {
  22:     /// The seized device.
  23:     pub triggered_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  24:     /// Subkey day-index at sign time.
  25:     pub triggered_day_index: u64,
  26:     /// Wall-clock seconds the alert was issued.
  27:     pub triggered_unix: u64,
  28:     /// 16-byte random nonce so replays are detectable per
  29:     /// proposal_id-style dedup at receivers.
  30:     pub nonce: [u8; 16],
  31:     /// Subkey signature over the canonical transcript.
  32:     pub subkey_sig: Vec<u8>,
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl DuressAlert {
  36:     /// Canonical bytes the subkey signs over.
  37:     #[must_use] 
  38:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  39:         triggered_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  40:         triggered_day_index: u64,
  41:         triggered_unix: u64,
  42:         nonce: &[u8; 16],
  43:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  44:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  45:             DUR_ALERT_DOMAIN.len() + DEVICE_ID_LEN + 8 + 8 + 16,
  46:         );
  47:         out.extend_from_slice(DUR_ALERT_DOMAIN);
  48:         out.extend_from_slice(triggered_device_id);
  49:         out.extend_from_slice(&triggered_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  50:         out.extend_from_slice(&triggered_unix.to_be_bytes());
  51:         out.extend_from_slice(nonce);
  52:         out
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// Verify under the seized device's subkey VK (which receivers
  56:     /// have via the Layer-1 `SubkeyAttestation` cache).
  57:     pub fn verify(&self, subkey_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  58:         if self.subkey_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
  59:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
  60:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
  61:                 got: self.subkey_sig.len(),
  62:             });
  63:         }
  64:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
  65:             &self.triggered_device_id,
  66:             self.triggered_day_index,
  67:             self.triggered_unix,
  68:             &self.nonce,
  69:         );
  70:         subkey_vk
  71:             .verify(&transcript, &self.subkey_sig)
  72:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::DuressAlertVerifyFail)
  73:     }
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Sign a duress alert using the seized device's subkey.
  77: pub fn sign_duress_alert(
  78:     subkey: &DeviceSubkey,
  79:     triggered_unix: u64,
  80:     nonce: [u8; 16],
  81: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<DuressAlert> {
  82:     let transcript = DuressAlert::canonical_transcript(
  83:         subkey.device_id(),
  84:         subkey.day_index(),
  85:         triggered_unix,
  86:         &nonce,
  87:     );
  88:     let sig = subkey.sign(&transcript)?;
  89:     Ok(DuressAlert {
  90:         triggered_device_id: *subkey.device_id(),
  91:         triggered_day_index: subkey.day_index(),
  92:         triggered_unix,
  93:         nonce,
  94:         subkey_sig: sig.to_vec(),
  95:     })
  96: }

   1: //! Argon2id-derived duress key.
   2: //!
   3: //! User types a short code (e.g., a 6-digit number or a 4-word
   4: //! passphrase) under stress. We need a serious work factor to defeat
   5: //! offline brute force on a captured envelope; Argon2id with
   6: //! memory-hard parameters is the standard tool.
   7: //!
   8: //! `m_cost = 19,456 KiB` and `t_cost = 2` are the OWASP-recommended
   9: //! "balanced" Argon2id defaults that complete in about 50 ms on a
  10: //! 2025 mobile `SoC`. The CPU+memory cost for an attacker is ~25 ×
  11: //! that on commodity hardware — sufficient given that a 6-digit
  12: //! duress code has only 1 M possibilities anyway (the user picks
  13: //! something memorable). Daemons SHOULD enforce a minimum code
  14: //! length + entropy at the entry surface.
  15: 
  16: use argon2::{Algorithm, Argon2, Params, Version};
  17: use zeroize::ZeroizeOnDrop;
  18: 
  19: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  20: 
  21: /// Length of the derived key bytes.
  22: pub const DURESS_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  23: 
  24: /// Memory cost for Argon2id (KiB).
  25: pub const ARGON2_M_COST_KIB: u32 = 19_456;
  26: 
  27: /// Time cost (iterations).
  28: pub const ARGON2_T_COST: u32 = 2;
  29: 
  30: /// Parallelism.
  31: pub const ARGON2_P_COST: u32 = 1;
  32: 
  33: /// A 32-byte symmetric key derived from a duress code.
  34: #[derive(ZeroizeOnDrop)]
  35: pub struct DuressCode {
  36:     key: [u8; DURESS_KEY_LEN],
  37: }
  38: 
  39: impl DuressCode {
  40:     /// Borrow the raw key bytes for AEAD use. Do NOT log.
  41:     #[must_use]
  42:     pub const fn key_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; DURESS_KEY_LEN] {
  43:         &self.key
  44:     }
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl std::fmt::Debug for DuressCode {
  48:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  49:         f.debug_struct("DuressCode").finish_non_exhaustive()
  50:     }
  51: }
  52: 
  53: /// Derive a [`DuressCode`] from the user-entered bytes + a per-
  54: /// envelope salt via Argon2id.
  55: pub fn derive_duress_key(
  56:     user_code: &[u8],
  57:     salt: &[u8],
  58: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<DuressCode> {
  59:     if user_code.is_empty() {
  60:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::DuressCodeEmpty);
  61:     }
  62:     let params = Params::new(
  63:         ARGON2_M_COST_KIB,
  64:         ARGON2_T_COST,
  65:         ARGON2_P_COST,
  66:         Some(DURESS_KEY_LEN),
  67:     )
  68:     .map_err(|e| DeviceMeshError::DuressArgon2Failed(format!("{e}")))?;
  69:     let argon = Argon2::new(Algorithm::Argon2id, Version::V0x13, params);
  70:     let mut key = [0u8; DURESS_KEY_LEN];
  71:     argon
  72:         .hash_password_into(user_code, salt, &mut key)
  73:         .map_err(|e| DeviceMeshError::DuressArgon2Failed(format!("{e}")))?;
  74:     Ok(DuressCode { key })
  75: }
  76:

  78: mod tests {

   1: //! Plausibly-deniable duress envelope.
   2: //!
   3: //! On disk, [`DuressEnvelope`] holds two ChaCha20-Poly1305
   4: //! ciphertexts (`real_ct` + `decoy_ct`) that are structurally
   5: //! identical to the captor. Each carries a fresh random salt + a
   6: //! 12-byte AEAD nonce. The two AEAD keys are derived from two
   7: //! different user codes via Argon2id:
   8: //!
   9: //! - `decoy_key  = Argon2id(decoy_code, decoy_salt)`
  10: //! - `real_key   = Argon2id(real_code,  real_salt) XOR field_witness_otp`
  11: //!
  12: //! The captor entering EITHER code can only unwrap whichever
  13: //! ciphertext that key opens. The user's real code, ABSENT the
  14: //! field witness, also fails to open `real_ct` — the XOR mask
  15: //! makes the derived key unusable. With the field witness in hand,
  16: //! `real_key` is reconstructed + `real_ct` decrypts.
  17: //!
  18: //! Structural indistinguishability: both ciphertexts have the same
  19: //! shape on disk — same headers, same overhead. An attacker who
  20: //! captures the disk image and tries every plausible code can at
  21: //! most recover the decoy; nothing on disk reveals that another
  22: //! ciphertext lurks.
  23: 
  24: use blake3::Hasher;
  25: use chacha20poly1305::aead::{Aead, KeyInit};
  26: use chacha20poly1305::{ChaCha20Poly1305, Key, Nonce};
  27: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  28: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  29: 
  30: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  31: 
  32: use super::code::{derive_duress_key, DURESS_KEY_LEN};
  33: 
  34: /// Length of the per-ciphertext random salt.
  35: pub const DUR_SALT_LEN: usize = 32;
  36: 
  37: /// Length of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce.
  38: pub const DUR_NONCE_LEN: usize = 12;
  39: 
  40: /// Domain-separation tag for the envelope canonical-bytes form.
  41: pub const DUR_ENVELOPE_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-duress-envelope-v1";
  42: 
  43: /// Maximum plaintext size accepted by the envelope (16 MiB).
  44: pub const DUR_MAX_PLAINTEXT_LEN: usize = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
  45: 
  46: /// On-disk envelope. The two ciphertexts are STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL.
  47: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  48: pub struct DuressEnvelope {
  49:     /// Salt for Argon2id-deriving the real-ciphertext key.
  50:     pub real_salt: [u8; DUR_SALT_LEN],
  51:     /// Salt for the decoy-ciphertext key.
  52:     pub decoy_salt: [u8; DUR_SALT_LEN],
  53:     /// AEAD nonce for the real ciphertext.
  54:     pub real_nonce: [u8; DUR_NONCE_LEN],
  55:     /// AEAD nonce for the decoy ciphertext.
  56:     pub decoy_nonce: [u8; DUR_NONCE_LEN],
  57:     /// AEAD ciphertext of the real plaintext (field-bound).
  58:     pub real_ct: Vec<u8>,
  59:     /// AEAD ciphertext of the decoy plaintext.
  60:     pub decoy_ct: Vec<u8>,
  61: }
  62: 
  63: /// Outcome of an unlock attempt.
  64: #[derive(Debug)]
  65: pub enum UnlockOutcome {
  66:     /// User's REAL code + correct field witness — return the real
  67:     /// plaintext. Daemon proceeds normally.
  68:     Real(Vec<u8>),
  69:     /// User's DUR code (or real code without the field witness) —
  70:     /// return the decoy plaintext. Daemon SILENTLY emits a
  71:     /// [`super::DuressAlert`] to siblings + locks the device into
  72:     /// decoy-only mode per the [`super::DuressPolicy`].
  73:     Decoy(Vec<u8>),
  74:     /// Neither code matched. Don't reveal whether the code was wrong
  75:     /// or just the wrong one — the daemon's UI presents a unified
  76:     /// "wrong code" response.
  77:     WrongCode,
  78: }
  79: 
  80: /// Build an envelope. Generates fresh random salts + nonces and
  81: /// produces the two ciphertexts.
  82: ///
  83: /// `field_witness` is the 32-byte secret needed to reconstruct the
  84: /// real key on unlock. Higher layers can re-derive it from the
  85: /// Phase E coherence-field state at mint time (or use any 32-byte
  86: /// shared secret).
  87: pub fn create_duress_envelope<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
  88:     real_plaintext: &[u8],
  89:     decoy_plaintext: &[u8],
  90:     real_code: &[u8],
  91:     decoy_code: &[u8],
  92:     field_witness: &[u8; 32],
  93:     rng: &mut R,
  94: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<DuressEnvelope> {
  95:     if real_plaintext.is_empty() || decoy_plaintext.is_empty() {
  96:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::DuressEnvelopePlaintextEmpty);
  97:     }
  98:     if real_plaintext.len() > DUR_MAX_PLAINTEXT_LEN
  99:         || decoy_plaintext.len() > DUR_MAX_PLAINTEXT_LEN
 100:     {
 101:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::DuressEnvelopePlaintextTooLong {
 102:             max: DUR_MAX_PLAINTEXT_LEN,
 103:         });
 104:     }
 105:     if real_code == decoy_code {
 106:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::DuressCodesIdentical);
 107:     }
 108: 
 109:     let mut real_salt = [0u8; DUR_SALT_LEN];
 110:     let mut decoy_salt = [0u8; DUR_SALT_LEN];
 111:     let mut real_nonce = [0u8; DUR_NONCE_LEN];
 112:     let mut decoy_nonce = [0u8; DUR_NONCE_LEN];
 113:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut real_salt);
 114:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut decoy_salt);
 115:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut real_nonce);
 116:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut decoy_nonce);
 117: 
 118:     let real_key = make_real_key(real_code, &real_salt, field_witness)?;
 119:     let decoy_key = derive_duress_key(decoy_code, &decoy_salt)?;
 120: 
 121:     let real_ct = aead_encrypt(real_key.as_slice(), &real_nonce, real_plaintext)?;
 122:     let decoy_ct = aead_encrypt(decoy_key.key_bytes(), &decoy_nonce, decoy_plaintext)?;
 123: 
 124:     let mut rk_bytes = real_key;
 125:     rk_bytes.zeroize();
 126: 
 127:     Ok(DuressEnvelope {
 128:         real_salt,
 129:         decoy_salt,
 130:         real_nonce,
 131:         decoy_nonce,
 132:         real_ct,
 133:         decoy_ct,
 134:     })
 135: }
 136: 
 137: /// Unlock attempt. Tries the supplied `user_code` against:
 138: ///   1. The real-ciphertext key (with field witness if supplied).
 139: ///   2. The decoy-ciphertext key.
 140: ///
 141: /// Returns the first match, or `WrongCode` if neither succeeds.
 142: ///
 143: /// Constant-time-ish: both attempts ALWAYS run regardless of the
 144: /// first result. The branch on the final outcome leaks at most a
 145: /// single bit (which ciphertext matched), but the captor learns
 146: /// only "this code returned plaintext" — exactly the property we
 147: /// want when the captor types the decoy code.
 148: pub fn unlock_duress_envelope(
 149:     env: &DuressEnvelope,
 150:     user_code: &[u8],
 151:     field_witness: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 152: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<UnlockOutcome> {
 153:     // Decoy path always runs.
 154:     let decoy_key = derive_duress_key(user_code, &env.decoy_salt)?;
 155:     let decoy_attempt =
 156:         aead_decrypt(decoy_key.key_bytes(), &env.decoy_nonce, &env.decoy_ct);
 157: 
 158:     // Real path always runs (when a witness is supplied).
 159:     let real_attempt = if let Some(witness) = field_witness {
 160:         let real_key = make_real_key(user_code, &env.real_salt, witness).ok();
 161:         real_key.and_then(|k| {
 162:             aead_decrypt(&k, &env.real_nonce, &env.real_ct).ok()
 163:         })
 164:     } else {
 165:         None
 166:     };
 167: 
 168:     // Real takes precedence if both unwrap (impossible in practice
 169:     // because the keys are independently random — but defensive).
 170:     if let Some(real) = real_attempt {
 171:         return Ok(UnlockOutcome::Real(real));
 172:     }
 173:     if let Ok(decoy) = decoy_attempt {
 174:         return Ok(UnlockOutcome::Decoy(decoy));
 175:     }
 176:     Ok(UnlockOutcome::WrongCode)
 177: }
 178: 
 179: fn make_real_key(
 180:     user_code: &[u8],
 181:     salt: &[u8; DUR_SALT_LEN],
 182:     field_witness: &[u8; 32],
 183: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<[u8; DURESS_KEY_LEN]> {
 184:     let argon_key = derive_duress_key(user_code, salt)?;
 185:     // Mix the field witness in via BLAKE3 keyed hash so a different
 186:     // witness gives a different key. NOT a simple XOR — using a
 187:     // keyed hash defeats algebraic attacks where the attacker
 188:     // learns the witness from disk + recomputes.
 189:     let mut h = Hasher::new_keyed(argon_key.key_bytes());
 190:     h.update(b"OL-mesh-duress-real-key-mix-v1");
 191:     h.update(field_witness);
 192:     let mut out = [0u8; DURESS_KEY_LEN];
 193:     out.copy_from_slice(h.finalize().as_bytes());
 194:     Ok(out)
 195: }
 196: 
 197: fn aead_encrypt(
 198:     key: &[u8],
 199:     nonce: &[u8; DUR_NONCE_LEN],
 200:     plaintext: &[u8],
 201: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<Vec<u8>> {
 202:     let cipher = ChaCha20Poly1305::new(Key::from_slice(key));
 203:     cipher
 204:         .encrypt(Nonce::from_slice(nonce), plaintext)
 205:         .map_err(|e| DeviceMeshError::DuressAeadFailed(format!("encrypt: {e}")))
 206: }
 207: 
 208: fn aead_decrypt(
 209:     key: &[u8],
 210:     nonce: &[u8; DUR_NONCE_LEN],
 211:     ciphertext: &[u8],
 212: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<Vec<u8>> {
 213:     let cipher = ChaCha20Poly1305::new(Key::from_slice(key));
 214:     cipher
 215:         .decrypt(Nonce::from_slice(nonce), ciphertext)
 216:         .map_err(|e| DeviceMeshError::DuressAeadFailed(format!("decrypt: {e}")))
 217: }

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 10 — adversary-grade privacy tier: duress mode +
   2: //! plausibly-deniable second persona + steganographic pairing.
   3: //!
   4: //! The dramatic finisher. Three properties:
   5: //!
   6: //! 1. **Duress mode**: a device gets seized (border crossing,
   7: //!    coercion, mugging). The user types a *duress code* instead
   8: //!    of the real unlock. The device:
   9: //!    - Presents a complete, plausible DECOY mesh state to the
  10: //!      captor (decoy contacts, decoy files, decoy messages).
  11: //!    - Silently emits a signed [`DuressAlert`] to siblings so
  12: //!      Layer-2 quorum revocation kicks in.
  13: //!    - The real state remains encrypted; the captor cannot tell
  14: //!      from the disk image alone that it exists.
  15: //!
  16: //! 2. **Plausibly deniable second persona**: every [`DuressEnvelope`]
  17: //!    on disk has two ciphertexts (real + decoy) that are
  18: //!    structurally identical. Without the field witness, even
  19: //!    knowing the user's password recovers AT MOST the decoy.
  20: //!    The real ciphertext is XOR-bound to a coherence-field
  21: //!    witness (the row-9 mechanism reused at Layer 1).
  22: //!
  23: //! 3. **Steganographic pairing**: pairing a new device commits over
  24: //!    THREE channels (QR + sub-perceptible audio chirp +
  25: //!    accelerometer-pattern). The pair completes only when all
  26: //!    three commit to the same secret within a time window. A
  27: //!    remote attacker who photographs the QR from across the room
  28: //!    cannot reproduce the audio + motion, so the pairing fails.
  29: //!
  30: //! ## What this layer ships
  31: //!
  32: //! - [`DuressCode`] — Argon2id-derived 32-byte key from a short
  33: //!   user-entered code.
  34: //! - [`DuressEnvelope`] — two ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD ciphertexts
  35: //!   (`real_ct` + `decoy_ct`) plus the salts. Structurally
  36: //!   indistinguishable from the outside.
  37: //! - [`UnlockOutcome`] — `Real(_)`, `Decoy(_)`, or `WrongCode`.
  38: //!   The daemon flips the duress flag on `Decoy`.
  39: //! - [`DuressAlert`] — signed broadcast "I'm under duress as of T."
  40: //! - [`PairingCommitment`] + [`verify_pairing_cross_channel`] —
  41: //!   the cross-channel pair verifier.
  42: //! - [`DuressPolicy`] — daemon-side policy (whether to emit a
  43: //!   silent alert immediately on decoy unlock; how long to keep
  44: //!   the device in decoy-only mode after a duress unlock; etc.).
  45: //!
  46: //! ## Field-binding
  47: //!
  48: //! `DuressEnvelope::create` requires a 32-byte `field_witness` for
  49: //! the REAL ciphertext. The witness derives from the Phase E
  50: //! coherence-field state at mint time (or any 32-byte secret the
  51: //! user holds out-of-band). Without it, no password recovers the
  52: //! real ciphertext — the attacker can only see the decoy.
  53: //!
  54: //! ## Composition with the lower layers
  55: //!
  56: //! - **Layer 1**: every [`DuressAlert`] is signed by the seized
  57: //!   device's subkey.
  58: //! - **Layer 2**: receiving siblings escalate the alert into a
  59: //!   K-of-N [`crate::quorum::QuorumCertificate`] to formally
  60: //!   revoke the seized device's subkey.
  61: //! - **Layer 9 field-witness machinery** (`ol_threshold_recovery`):
  62: //!   reused as the witness binding mechanism for the real
  63: //!   ciphertext.
  64: //! - **F2 pair-by-QR**: the cross-channel commit extends the
  65: //!   shipped QR-pair primitive with the audio + motion channels.
  66: 
  67: pub mod alert;
  68: pub mod code;
  69: pub mod envelope;
  70: pub mod pair;
  71: pub mod policy;
  72: 
  73: pub use alert::{
  74:     sign_duress_alert, DuressAlert, DUR_ALERT_DOMAIN,
  75: };
  76: pub use code::{derive_duress_key, DuressCode, ARGON2_M_COST_KIB, ARGON2_T_COST};
  77: pub use envelope::{
  78:     create_duress_envelope, unlock_duress_envelope, DuressEnvelope, UnlockOutcome,

  83:     PAIR_COMMITMENT_DOMAIN, REQUIRED_PAIR_CHANNELS,
  84: };
  85: pub use policy::{DuressPolicy, DURESS_DEFAULT_QUARANTINE_SECS};

   1: //! Steganographic cross-channel pairing.
   2: //!
   3: //! When pairing a new device, the pairing secret is committed
   4: //! across THREE channels:
   5: //!
   6: //! - QR — visual code on the existing-device screen, scanned by the
   7: //!   new device.
   8: //! - Audio — sub-perceptible chirp / modulation in normal audio
   9: //!   played by the existing device, picked up by the new device's
  10: //!   microphone.
  11: //! - Motion — accelerometer pattern observed when the user
  12: //!   physically touches the two devices together for a moment.
  13: //!
  14: //! Each channel produces a [`PairingCommitment`]: a BLAKE3
  15: //! commitment over `(channel_tag, pairing_secret, channel_nonce)`.
  16: //! The receiver collects commitments from all three channels and
  17: //! checks that they ALL commit to the same secret within a time
  18: //! window. A remote attacker who photographs the QR from across the
  19: //! room can't reproduce the audio + motion → the pairing fails.
  20: 
  21: use blake3::Hasher;
  22: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  23: 
  24: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  25: 
  26: /// Domain-separation tag for pairing commitments.
  27: pub const PAIR_COMMITMENT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-pair-commitment-v1";
  28: 
  29: /// Number of channels that must agree.
  30: pub const REQUIRED_PAIR_CHANNELS: usize = 3;
  31: 
  32: /// The three channels.
  33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
  34: pub enum PairingChannel {
  35:     /// Visual QR code.
  36:     Qr,
  37:     /// Sub-perceptible audio chirp.
  38:     Audio,
  39:     /// Accelerometer / motion pattern.
  40:     Motion,
  41: }
  42: 
  43: impl PairingChannel {
  44:     /// Canonical 8-byte tag mixed into the commitment.
  45:     #[must_use]
  46:     pub const fn tag(self) -> [u8; 8] {
  47:         match self {
  48:             Self::Qr => *b"OL-PR-QR",
  49:             Self::Audio => *b"OL-PR-AU",
  50:             Self::Motion => *b"OL-PR-MO",
  51:         }
  52:     }
  53: }
  54: 
  55: /// One channel's commitment over the pairing secret.
  56: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  57: pub struct PairingCommitment {
  58:     /// Which channel produced this commitment.
  59:     pub channel: PairingChannel,
  60:     /// BLAKE3 of `(domain || channel.tag() || pairing_secret || nonce)`.
  61:     pub commitment: [u8; 32],
  62:     /// Per-channel nonce that the verifier learns out-of-band
  63:     /// (e.g., transmitted alongside the commitment over the same
  64:     /// channel).
  65:     pub nonce: [u8; 16],
  66:     /// Wall-clock-millis when this commitment was emitted.
  67:     pub timestamp_ms: u64,
  68: }
  69: 
  70: impl PairingCommitment {
  71:     /// Build a commitment for `channel` over `pairing_secret`.
  72:     #[must_use]
  73:     pub fn build(
  74:         channel: PairingChannel,
  75:         pairing_secret: &[u8],
  76:         nonce: [u8; 16],
  77:         timestamp_ms: u64,
  78:     ) -> Self {
  79:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
  80:         h.update(PAIR_COMMITMENT_DOMAIN);
  81:         h.update(&channel.tag());
  82:         h.update(pairing_secret);
  83:         h.update(&nonce);
  84:         let digest = h.finalize();
  85:         let mut commitment = [0u8; 32];
  86:         commitment.copy_from_slice(digest.as_bytes());
  87:         Self {
  88:             channel,
  89:             commitment,
  90:             nonce,
  91:             timestamp_ms,
  92:         }
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     /// Constant-time check that this commitment matches an expected
  96:     /// `pairing_secret`.
  97:     #[must_use]
  98:     pub fn matches(&self, pairing_secret: &[u8]) -> bool {
  99:         let expected = Self::build(
 100:             self.channel,
 101:             pairing_secret,
 102:             self.nonce,
 103:             self.timestamp_ms,
 104:         );
 105:         bool::from(expected.commitment.ct_eq(&self.commitment))
 106:     }
 107: }
 108: 
 109: /// Verify that the supplied commitments cross-confirm
 110: /// `pairing_secret` across all three required channels within
 111: /// `window_ms` of each other.
 112: ///
 113: /// Returns `Ok(())` if and only if:
 114: ///   - the QR, Audio, AND Motion channels are ALL present
 115: ///   - each commitment matches the secret
 116: ///   - the gap between earliest and latest commitment is ≤ `window_ms`
 117: pub fn verify_pairing_cross_channel(
 118:     commitments: &[PairingCommitment],
 119:     pairing_secret: &[u8],
 120:     window_ms: u64,
 121: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 122:     let mut have_qr = false;
 123:     let mut have_audio = false;
 124:     let mut have_motion = false;
 125:     let mut min_ts: Option<u64> = None;
 126:     let mut max_ts: Option<u64> = None;
 127:     for c in commitments {
 128:         if !c.matches(pairing_secret) {
 129:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PairChannelCommitmentMismatch {
 130:                 channel: c.channel,
 131:             });
 132:         }
 133:         match c.channel {
 134:             PairingChannel::Qr => have_qr = true,
 135:             PairingChannel::Audio => have_audio = true,
 136:             PairingChannel::Motion => have_motion = true,
 137:         }
 138:         min_ts = Some(min_ts.map_or(c.timestamp_ms, |x| x.min(c.timestamp_ms)));
 139:         max_ts = Some(max_ts.map_or(c.timestamp_ms, |x| x.max(c.timestamp_ms)));
 140:     }
 141:     if !(have_qr && have_audio && have_motion) {
 142:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::PairChannelMissing {
 143:             qr: have_qr,
 144:             audio: have_audio,
 145:             motion: have_motion,
 146:         });
 147:     }
 148:     let span = max_ts.unwrap_or(0).saturating_sub(min_ts.unwrap_or(0));
 149:     if span > window_ms {
 150:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::PairChannelOutOfWindow {
 151:             span_ms: span,
 152:             window_ms,
 153:         });
 154:     }
 155:     Ok(())
 156: }

   1: //! Duress-mode policy.
   2: 
   3: /// Default time the daemon keeps the device in decoy-only mode
   4: /// after a duress unlock. 24 hours. During this window:
   5: ///   - The real ciphertext is NEVER touched.
   6: ///   - Sibling-emitted commands targeting the seized device are
   7: ///     queued but not executed.
   8: ///   - The user's "I'm safe now" out-of-band signal lifts the
   9: ///     quarantine + re-enables the real state.
  10: pub const DURESS_DEFAULT_QUARANTINE_SECS: u64 = 24 * 3600;
  11: 
  12: /// Duress policy controlling daemon behaviour after a decoy unlock.
  13: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  14: pub struct DuressPolicy {
  15:     /// `true` if the daemon should silently emit a [`super::DuressAlert`]
  16:     /// the moment a decoy unlock succeeds.
  17:     pub emit_alert_on_decoy_unlock: bool,
  18:     /// Quarantine window in seconds.
  19:     pub quarantine_secs: u64,
  20:     /// `true` if siblings should automatically initiate a Layer-2
  21:     /// quorum revocation once `min_alerts_for_revoke` alerts are
  22:     /// received within `alert_dedup_window_secs`.
  23:     pub auto_revoke_on_alert: bool,
  24:     /// Minimum number of distinct alerts (with distinct nonces) the
  25:     /// siblings need to see before escalating to revocation. 1 is
  26:     /// the minimum; higher values reduce false-positive escalations
  27:     /// from a flapping device.
  28:     pub min_alerts_for_revoke: u8,
  29:     /// Window over which `min_alerts_for_revoke` is counted.
  30:     pub alert_dedup_window_secs: u64,
  31: }
  32: 
  33: impl DuressPolicy {
  34:     /// Conservative default: alert immediately, quarantine for 24h,
  35:     /// auto-revoke after 1 alert, 1h dedup window.
  36:     #[must_use]
  37:     pub const fn conservative() -> Self {
  38:         Self {
  39:             emit_alert_on_decoy_unlock: true,
  40:             quarantine_secs: DURESS_DEFAULT_QUARANTINE_SECS,
  41:             auto_revoke_on_alert: true,
  42:             min_alerts_for_revoke: 1,
  43:             alert_dedup_window_secs: 3_600,
  44:         }
  45:     }
  46: 
  47:     /// Hardened preset for journalist / activist / dissident use:
  48:     /// alert immediately, quarantine for 7 days, auto-revoke after
  49:     /// 1 alert, 24h dedup window. Decoy-only mode persists across
  50:     /// power cycles until the user explicitly clears it via the
  51:     /// out-of-band recovery path.
  52:     #[must_use]
  53:     pub const fn hardened() -> Self {
  54:         Self {
  55:             emit_alert_on_decoy_unlock: true,
  56:             quarantine_secs: 7 * DURESS_DEFAULT_QUARANTINE_SECS,
  57:             auto_revoke_on_alert: true,
  58:             min_alerts_for_revoke: 1,
  59:             alert_dedup_window_secs: 24 * 3600,
  60:         }
  61:     }
  62: }
  63: 
  64: impl Default for DuressPolicy {
  65:     fn default() -> Self {
  66:         Self::conservative()
  67:     }
  68: }
  69: 
  70: #[cfg(test)]
  71: mod tests {
  72:     use super::*;
  73: 
  74:     #[test]
  75:     fn conservative_emits_and_auto_revokes() {
  76:         let p = DuressPolicy::conservative();
  77:         assert!(p.emit_alert_on_decoy_unlock);
  78:         assert!(p.auto_revoke_on_alert);
  79:         assert_eq!(p.quarantine_secs, DURESS_DEFAULT_QUARANTINE_SECS);
  80:     }
  81: 
  82:     #[test]
  83:     fn hardened_quarantine_is_seven_days() {
  84:         let p = DuressPolicy::hardened();
  85:         assert_eq!(p.quarantine_secs, 7 * 24 * 3600);
  86:     }
  87: }

   1: //! Source-signed delivery receipt.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each successful chunk delivery is acknowledged by the SOURCE
   4: //! signing a [`ChunkAck`] over `(file_id, chunk_hash, receiver_id,
   5: //! delivered_unix, byte_offset)`. The receiver can persist these
   6: //! as proof "I, source S, delivered chunk C to receiver R at T."
   7: //! Useful for the bandit estimator (Phase D) and for the
   8: //! anti-fan-out-abuse rate-limiter at a higher layer.
   9: 
  10: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
  11: 
  12: use crate::distributed_fs::{ChunkHash, FileId, CHUNK_HASH_LEN, FILE_ID_LEN};
  13: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  14: use crate::subkey::{DeviceSubkey, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  15: 
  16: /// Domain-separation tag for ack signing.
  17: pub const ACK_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-chunk-ack-v1";
  18: 
  19: /// Source-signed delivery receipt for one chunk.
  20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  21: pub struct ChunkAck {
  22:     /// File the chunk belongs to.
  23:     pub file_id: FileId,
  24:     /// The chunk just delivered.
  25:     pub chunk_hash: ChunkHash,
  26:     /// Source device id.
  27:     pub source_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  28:     /// Receiver device id (who got the chunk).
  29:     pub receiver_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  30:     /// Source's subkey day-index at sign time.
  31:     pub source_day_index: u64,
  32:     /// Wall-clock seconds the delivery completed.
  33:     pub delivered_unix: u64,
  34:     /// Size in bytes of the chunk delivered.
  35:     pub byte_size: u32,
  36:     /// Source's subkey signature.
  37:     pub source_sig: Vec<u8>,
  38: }
  39: 
  40: impl ChunkAck {
  41:     /// Canonical bytes the source's subkey signs over.
  42:     #[must_use] 
  43:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  44:         file_id: &FileId,
  45:         chunk_hash: &ChunkHash,
  46:         source_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  47:         receiver_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  48:         source_day_index: u64,
  49:         delivered_unix: u64,
  50:         byte_size: u32,
  51:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  52:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  53:             ACK_DOMAIN.len()
  54:                 + FILE_ID_LEN
  55:                 + CHUNK_HASH_LEN
  56:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  57:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  58:                 + 8
  59:                 + 8
  60:                 + 4,
  61:         );
  62:         out.extend_from_slice(ACK_DOMAIN);
  63:         out.extend_from_slice(file_id);
  64:         out.extend_from_slice(chunk_hash);
  65:         out.extend_from_slice(source_device_id);
  66:         out.extend_from_slice(receiver_device_id);
  67:         out.extend_from_slice(&source_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  68:         out.extend_from_slice(&delivered_unix.to_be_bytes());
  69:         out.extend_from_slice(&byte_size.to_be_bytes());
  70:         out
  71:     }
  72: 
  73:     /// Verify the source's signature.
  74:     pub fn verify(&self, source_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  75:         if self.source_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
  76:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
  77:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
  78:                 got: self.source_sig.len(),
  79:             });
  80:         }
  81:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
  82:             &self.file_id,
  83:             &self.chunk_hash,
  84:             &self.source_device_id,
  85:             &self.receiver_device_id,
  86:             self.source_day_index,
  87:             self.delivered_unix,
  88:             self.byte_size,
  89:         );
  90:         source_vk
  91:             .verify(&transcript, &self.source_sig)
  92:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::ChunkAckVerifyFail)
  93:     }
  94: }
  95: 
  96: /// Sign a chunk-ack as the SOURCE.
  97: pub fn sign_chunk_ack(
  98:     source: &DeviceSubkey,
  99:     file_id: FileId,
 100:     chunk_hash: ChunkHash,
 101:     receiver_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 102:     delivered_unix: u64,
 103:     byte_size: u32,
 104: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<ChunkAck> {
 105:     let transcript = ChunkAck::canonical_transcript(
 106:         &file_id,
 107:         &chunk_hash,
 108:         source.device_id(),
 109:         &receiver_device_id,
 110:         source.day_index(),
 111:         delivered_unix,
 112:         byte_size,
 113:     );
 114:     let sig = source.sign(&transcript)?;
 115:     Ok(ChunkAck {
 116:         file_id,
 117:         chunk_hash,
 118:         source_device_id: *source.device_id(),
 119:         receiver_device_id,
 120:         source_day_index: source.day_index(),
 121:         delivered_unix,
 122:         byte_size,
 123:         source_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 124:     })
 125: }

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 5 — multi-device fan-out for big transfers.
   2: //!
   3: //! When a receiver wants a large file, fan-out lets multiple source
   4: //! devices in the same personal mesh stream chunks in parallel.
   5: //! Phone in TX requests "the 50GB project folder" → laptop +
   6: //! desktop + tablet each carry a fraction → phone reassembles via
   7: //! Phase B fountain codes (any K of K+M shards suffice).
   8: //!
   9: //! ## Composition with the lower layers
  10: //!
  11: //! - **Layer 1 (subkeys)**: every [`FetchRequest`] is signed by the
  12: //!   receiver's per-device subkey; every [`ChunkAck`] is signed by
  13: //!   the source's subkey. The other party verifies under the
  14: //!   master-attested subkey VK from Layer 1.
  15: //! - **Layer 4 (placement)**: the planner reads the per-chunk
  16: //!   placement map to know which sources hold which chunks.
  17: //! - **Layer 6 (`τ_c` routing, future)**: per-source capacity scores
  18: //!   are populated by the daemon's bandit + tau-field measurement;
  19: //!   the planner is policy-agnostic about how they're computed.
  20: //! - **Phase B fountain codes (shipped)**: the planner over-requests
  21: //!   slightly so the receiver completes as soon as ANY `k` shards
  22: //!   arrive, even if some sources are slow.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## What this layer does
  25: //!
  26: //! - [`fan_out_plan`] assigns each chunk in a fetch set to one
  27: //!   source device, weighted by source capacity, while respecting
  28: //!   "only holders can serve" and "spread load."
  29: //! - [`replan_after_source_failure`] redistributes the chunks
  30: //!   assigned to a dropped source across the remaining sources.
  31: //! - [`TransferProgress`] tracks per-chunk arrival state and signals
  32: //!   completion when `≥ k` shards have arrived.
  33: //!
  34: //! ## What this layer doesn't ship
  35: //!
  36: //! - The actual wire transport (Phase A2 QUIC + Layer 6 self-mesh
  37: //!   routing once shipped).
  38: //! - The fountain-code encode / decode (Phase B `ol_fountain`,
  39: //!   shipped). The planner counts shards; the decoder runs upstream
  40: //!   when chunks arrive.
  41: //! - The capacity estimator (Phase D bandit, shipped).
  42: //!
  43: //! ## Example
  44: //!
  45: //! ```no_run
  46: //! // Doctest is `no_run` because ML-DSA key material is ~2 KB —
  47: //! // signing operations push doctest stacks past their default
  48: //! // size on Windows. Compile-time validation is preserved.
  49: //! use ol_device_mesh::distributed_fs::{ChunkHash, ChunkPlacement, ErasurePolicy, FileManifest};
  50: //! use ol_device_mesh::fan_out::{fan_out_plan, SourceCapacity};
  51: //! use ol_device_mesh::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  52: //!
  53: //! // 3 chunks across 3 sources of varying capacity.
  54: //! let chunks: Vec<ChunkHash> = vec![[0x11; 32], [0x22; 32], [0x33; 32]];
  55: //! let policy = ErasurePolicy::new(2, 1, 1).unwrap();
  56: //! let manifest = FileManifest {
  57: //!     file_size: 1_000_000,
  58: //!     chunk_size: 8192,
  59: //!     chunks: chunks.clone(),
  60: //!     mime: b"x".to_vec(),
  61: //!     created_unix: 0,
  62: //!     policy,
  63: //! };
  64: //! let placements: Vec<ChunkPlacement> = chunks
  65: //!     .iter()
  66: //!     .map(|c| {
  67: //!         let mut p = ChunkPlacement::empty(*c);
  68: //!         p.add_holder([1; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 1);
  69: //!         p.add_holder([2; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 1);
  70: //!         p.add_holder([3; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 1);
  71: //!         p
  72: //!     })
  73: //!     .collect();
  74: //! let sources = vec![
  75: //!     SourceCapacity { device_id: [1; DEVICE_ID_LEN], estimated_bps: 100_000_000, current_load_bytes: 0 },
  76: //!     SourceCapacity { device_id: [2; DEVICE_ID_LEN], estimated_bps:  50_000_000, current_load_bytes: 0 },
  77: //!     SourceCapacity { device_id: [3; DEVICE_ID_LEN], estimated_bps:  10_000_000, current_load_bytes: 0 },
  78: //! ];
  79: //! let plan = fan_out_plan(&manifest, &placements, &sources, 1.0).unwrap();
  80: //! // Every assigned chunk has exactly one source.
  81: //! let total_chunks: usize = plan.assignments.iter().map(|a| a.chunk_hashes.len()).sum();
  82: //! assert_eq!(total_chunks, 3);
  83: //! ```
  84: 
  85: pub mod ack;
  86: pub mod plan;
  87: pub mod progress;
  88: pub mod request;
  89:

  92:     fan_out_plan, replan_after_source_failure, FanOutAssignment, FanOutPlan,

  97:     sign_fetch_request, FetchRequest, FetchNonce, FETCH_NONCE_LEN, FETCH_REQUEST_DOMAIN,
  98:     MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FETCH,
  99: };

   1: //! Fan-out planner.
   2: //!
   3: //! Given a file manifest, the per-chunk placement map, and a set of
   4: //! per-source capacity profiles, compute an assignment of chunks to
   5: //! sources that:
   6: //!
   7: //! 1. Respects "only holders can serve" (the placement is the
   8: //!    source of truth for who owns what).
   9: //! 2. Spreads load across sources weighted by capacity (faster
  10: //!    sources carry more chunks).
  11: //! 3. Is deterministic: same input → same output, so any device
  12: //!    in the mesh can re-derive the plan locally without a fresh
  13: //!    coordination round.
  14: //! 4. Optionally over-requests: ask for `ceil(k * overrequest_factor)`
  15: //!    shards even though `k` suffice, so the receiver completes
  16: //!    when ANY `k` arrive — masking slow sources without
  17: //!    re-planning.
  18: 
  19: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  20: 
  21: use crate::distributed_fs::{ChunkHash, ChunkPlacement, FileManifest};
  22: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  23: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  24: 
  25: /// One source's capacity profile, as the receiver estimates it.
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  27: pub struct SourceCapacity {
  28:     /// Source device id.
  29:     pub device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  30:     /// Estimated bytes-per-second the source can deliver to this
  31:     /// receiver. Typically a Phase D bandit estimate. Higher = more
  32:     /// chunks assigned.
  33:     pub estimated_bps: u64,
  34:     /// Current in-flight bytes already-assigned to this source from
  35:     /// other plans. The planner adds the new assignment on top so
  36:     /// load tracking stays accurate across overlapping fan-outs.
  37:     pub current_load_bytes: u64,
  38: }
  39: 
  40: /// Per-source assignment in a fan-out plan.
  41: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  42: pub struct FanOutAssignment {
  43:     /// Which source serves these chunks.
  44:     pub source_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  45:     /// Chunk hashes assigned to this source (sorted ascending).
  46:     pub chunk_hashes: Vec<ChunkHash>,
  47:     /// Estimated bytes the source will deliver (= chunks ×
  48:     /// `manifest.chunk_size`).
  49:     pub estimated_bytes: u64,
  50: }
  51: 
  52: /// The full plan: per-source assignments + over-request factor.
  53: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  54: pub struct FanOutPlan {
  55:     /// File the plan targets.
  56:     pub file_id: crate::distributed_fs::FileId,
  57:     /// Per-source assignment list. Order is by `source_device_id`
  58:     /// ascending so the plan hashes deterministically.
  59:     pub assignments: Vec<FanOutAssignment>,
  60:     /// Number of distinct chunk hashes asked for across all sources.
  61:     /// May exceed `manifest.policy.k` when `overrequest_factor > 1`.
  62:     pub total_chunks: usize,
  63: }
  64: 
  65: /// Compute a fan-out plan.
  66: ///
  67: /// Algorithm: for each chunk in the manifest (in canonical order),
  68: /// pick the eligible source — a device that (a) holds the chunk and
  69: /// (b) has the smallest projected `current_load + assigned_so_far /
  70: /// estimated_bps`. Tie-break on lex device id.
  71: ///
  72: /// `overrequest_factor` ≥ 1.0; values like 1.2 trade ~20 % extra
  73: /// bandwidth for resilience against straggling sources. Set to 1.0
  74: /// for the strict-shards mode.
  75: pub fn fan_out_plan(
  76:     manifest: &FileManifest,
  77:     placements: &[ChunkPlacement],
  78:     sources: &[SourceCapacity],
  79:     overrequest_factor: f64,
  80: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<FanOutPlan> {
  81:     manifest.shape_check()?;
  82:     if sources.is_empty() {
  83:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FanOutNoSources);
  84:     }
  85:     if overrequest_factor < 1.0 || !overrequest_factor.is_finite() {
  86:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FanOutBadOverrequestFactor {
  87:             got_bits: overrequest_factor.to_bits(),
  88:         });
  89:     }
  90:     // Build a lookup: chunk_hash → set of holder device ids (from
  91:     // the placement records). Chunks not in any placement get an
  92:     // empty holder set, which causes the planner to skip them.
  93:     let mut holders: BTreeMap<ChunkHash, Vec<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>> =
  94:         BTreeMap::new();
  95:     for p in placements {
  96:         holders.insert(p.chunk_hash, p.device_ids.iter().copied().collect());
  97:     }
  98:     // Mutable per-source projected load (current + accumulated).
  99:     let mut load: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u128> = sources
 100:         .iter()
 101:         .map(|s| (s.device_id, s.current_load_bytes as u128))
 102:         .collect();
 103:     let cap: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u64> = sources
 104:         .iter()
 105:         .map(|s| (s.device_id, s.estimated_bps.max(1)))
 106:         .collect();
 107:     // Determine how many of the manifest's chunks to actually fetch.
 108:     // Manifest has `chunks.len()` shards total (= k*stripes + m*stripes).
 109:     // `k_total` is the number of data shards across all stripes.
 110:     let stripe = manifest.policy.total_shards() as usize;
 111:     let n_stripes = manifest.chunks.len() / stripe;
 112:     let k_total = n_stripes * (manifest.policy.k as usize);
 113:     // k_total ≤ chunks.len() ≤ MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FILE = 2^20, well
 114:     // within f64's 53-bit mantissa.
 115:     #[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss, clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]
 116:     let target = ((k_total as f64) * overrequest_factor).ceil() as usize;
 117:     let target = target.min(manifest.chunks.len());
 118:     // Per-source bucket of assigned chunks.
 119:     let mut bucket: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], Vec<ChunkHash>> = sources
 120:         .iter()
 121:         .map(|s| (s.device_id, Vec::new()))
 122:         .collect();
 123:     let mut assigned = 0usize;
 124:     for chunk in &manifest.chunks {
 125:         if assigned >= target {
 126:             break;
 127:         }
 128:         let Some(holder_list) = holders.get(chunk) else {
 129:             continue;
 130:         };
 131:         // Among holders that are ALSO known sources, pick the
 132:         // smallest projected `(load + chunk_size) / bps`. Tie-break
 133:         // on lex device id.
 134:         let chunk_bytes = manifest.chunk_size as u128;
 135:         let pick = holder_list
 136:             .iter()
 137:             .filter(|h| cap.contains_key(*h))
 138:             .min_by(|a, b| {
 139:                 let la = load.get(*a).copied().unwrap_or(0) + chunk_bytes;
 140:                 let lb = load.get(*b).copied().unwrap_or(0) + chunk_bytes;
 141:                 let ca = *cap.get(*a).unwrap_or(&1) as u128;
 142:                 let cb = *cap.get(*b).unwrap_or(&1) as u128;
 143:                 // Compare la / ca vs lb / cb without floats:
 144:                 //   la * cb  vs  lb * ca.
 145:                 let lhs = la.saturating_mul(cb);
 146:                 let rhs = lb.saturating_mul(ca);
 147:                 match lhs.cmp(&rhs) {
 148:                     std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => a.cmp(b),
 149:                     other => other,
 150:                 }
 151:             });
 152:         let Some(&pick) = pick else {
 153:             // No eligible source for this chunk; skip it. The
 154:             // receiver may still recover if it gets enough other
 155:             // shards via fountain decoding.
 156:             continue;
 157:         };
 158:         let bucket_entry = bucket.entry(pick).or_default();
 159:         bucket_entry.push(*chunk);
 160:         *load.entry(pick).or_insert(0) += chunk_bytes;
 161:         assigned += 1;
 162:     }
 163:     // Build the assignment list — deterministic order.
 164:     let mut assignments: Vec<FanOutAssignment> = bucket
 165:         .into_iter()
 166:         .filter(|(_, chunks)| !chunks.is_empty())
 167:         .map(|(device_id, mut chunks)| {
 168:             chunks.sort_unstable();
 169:             let estimated_bytes =
 170:                 (chunks.len() as u64).saturating_mul(manifest.chunk_size as u64);
 171:             FanOutAssignment {
 172:                 source_device_id: device_id,
 173:                 chunk_hashes: chunks,
 174:                 estimated_bytes,
 175:             }
 176:         })
 177:         .collect();
 178:     assignments.sort_by_key(|a| a.source_device_id);
 179:     Ok(FanOutPlan {
 180:         file_id: manifest.file_id(),
 181:         assignments,
 182:         total_chunks: assigned,
 183:     })
 184: }
 185: 
 186: /// Replan after a source fails mid-transfer.
 187: ///
 188: /// `still_needed_chunks` is the list of chunks that haven't yet
 189: /// arrived (the receiver's pending+in-flight set). `failed_source`
 190: /// is the source id to drop from the eligible pool. The function
 191: /// returns a fresh plan covering the unmet chunks via the surviving
 192: /// sources.
 193: pub fn replan_after_source_failure(
 194:     manifest: &FileManifest,
 195:     placements: &[ChunkPlacement],
 196:     sources: &[SourceCapacity],
 197:     failed_source: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 198:     still_needed_chunks: &[ChunkHash],
 199:     overrequest_factor: f64,
 200: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<FanOutPlan> {
 201:     // Synthesize a sub-manifest containing ONLY the still-needed
 202:     // chunks. The planner is policy-agnostic so this is sound; it
 203:     // just needs the chunk list + chunk_size to compute load.
 204:     if still_needed_chunks.is_empty() {
 205:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FanOutNothingToReplan);
 206:     }
 207:     let surviving_sources: Vec<SourceCapacity> = sources
 208:         .iter()
 209:         .filter(|s| s.device_id != failed_source)
 210:         .copied()
 211:         .collect();
 212:     if surviving_sources.is_empty() {
 213:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FanOutNoSources);
 214:     }
 215:     // Build a sub-manifest. We use the original manifest's policy
 216:     // so total_shards / k math stays consistent. The chunks list
 217:     // is rounded up to the next stripe-multiple by padding with
 218:     // copies of the last needed chunk; the planner skips chunks
 219:     // it can't place (no holder in surviving_sources), so padding
 220:     // is harmless.
 221:     let stripe = manifest.policy.total_shards() as usize;
 222:     let mut chunks = still_needed_chunks.to_vec();
 223:     // Sort + dedup so the planner's lookup hits.
 224:     chunks.sort_unstable();
 225:     chunks.dedup();
 226:     // Pad to stripe multiple.
 227:     while !chunks.len().is_multiple_of(stripe) {
 228:         chunks.push(*chunks.last().expect("non-empty"));
 229:     }
 230:     let sub_manifest = FileManifest {
 231:         file_size: manifest.file_size,
 232:         chunk_size: manifest.chunk_size,
 233:         chunks,
 234:         mime: manifest.mime.clone(),
 235:         created_unix: manifest.created_unix,
 236:         policy: manifest.policy,
 237:     };
 238:     fan_out_plan(&sub_manifest, placements, &surviving_sources, overrequest_factor)
 239: }

 262:         }
 263:         p
 264:     }

   1: //! Receiver-side transfer progress tracker.
   2: //!
   3: //! Holds the state of an in-progress fan-out fetch:
   4: //! - which chunks have completed,
   5: //! - which are currently in-flight from each source,
   6: //! - which are still pending.
   7: //!
   8: //! Signals completion as soon as `≥ k_total` distinct shards have
   9: //! arrived (where `k_total = n_stripes * policy.k`), so a fast
  10: //! subset of sources can finish the transfer without waiting on
  11: //! slow ones — the fountain-code property.
  12: 
  13: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
  14: 
  15: use crate::distributed_fs::{ChunkHash, FileManifest};
  16: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  17: 
  18: use super::plan::FanOutPlan;
  19: 
  20: /// Per-transfer tracker.
  21: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  22: pub struct TransferProgress {
  23:     /// File the transfer targets.
  24:     pub file_id: crate::distributed_fs::FileId,
  25:     /// Plan currently being executed.
  26:     pub plan: FanOutPlan,
  27:     /// Chunks already received successfully.
  28:     pub completed_chunks: BTreeSet<ChunkHash>,
  29:     /// Chunks currently in-flight, with the source we're waiting on.
  30:     pub in_flight_chunks: BTreeMap<ChunkHash, [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
  31:     /// Sources that have failed (dropped, timed out, lost connection).
  32:     pub failed_sources: BTreeSet<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
  33:     /// Number of distinct shards needed to reconstruct
  34:     /// (= `n_stripes` * policy.k from the manifest).
  35:     pub completion_threshold: usize,
  36: }
  37: 
  38: impl TransferProgress {
  39:     /// Initialize a fresh tracker for a plan + manifest.
  40:     #[must_use]
  41:     pub fn new(plan: FanOutPlan, manifest: &FileManifest) -> Self {
  42:         let stripe = manifest.policy.total_shards() as usize;
  43:         let n_stripes = manifest.chunks.len() / stripe.max(1);
  44:         let completion_threshold = n_stripes * (manifest.policy.k as usize);
  45:         Self {
  46:             file_id: plan.file_id,
  47:             plan,
  48:             completed_chunks: BTreeSet::new(),
  49:             in_flight_chunks: BTreeMap::new(),
  50:             failed_sources: BTreeSet::new(),
  51:             completion_threshold,
  52:         }
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// Begin tracking a chunk as in-flight from `source`.
  56:     pub fn mark_in_flight(
  57:         &mut self,
  58:         chunk: ChunkHash,
  59:         source: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  60:     ) {
  61:         if !self.completed_chunks.contains(&chunk) {
  62:             self.in_flight_chunks.insert(chunk, source);
  63:         }
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     /// Mark a chunk completed. Returns `true` iff this completion
  67:     /// brought us to or past the threshold for the first time.
  68:     pub fn complete_chunk(&mut self, chunk: ChunkHash) -> bool {
  69:         let was_at_threshold = self.completed_chunks.len() >= self.completion_threshold;
  70:         self.in_flight_chunks.remove(&chunk);
  71:         self.completed_chunks.insert(chunk);
  72:         let now_at_threshold = self.completed_chunks.len() >= self.completion_threshold;
  73:         now_at_threshold && !was_at_threshold
  74:     }
  75: 
  76:     /// Mark a source as failed. Returns the list of in-flight chunks
  77:     /// previously assigned to it, which the higher layer should
  78:     /// `replan_after_source_failure` against the surviving sources.
  79:     pub fn mark_source_failed(
  80:         &mut self,
  81:         source: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  82:     ) -> Vec<ChunkHash> {
  83:         self.failed_sources.insert(source);
  84:         let mut released = Vec::new();
  85:         let still_in_flight: BTreeMap<ChunkHash, [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> = self
  86:             .in_flight_chunks
  87:             .iter()
  88:             .filter_map(|(chunk, src)| {
  89:                 if *src == source {
  90:                     released.push(*chunk);
  91:                     None
  92:                 } else {
  93:                     Some((*chunk, *src))
  94:                 }
  95:             })
  96:             .collect();
  97:         self.in_flight_chunks = still_in_flight;
  98:         released
  99:     }
 100: 
 101:     /// Have we collected enough distinct shards?
 102:     #[must_use]
 103:     pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {
 104:         self.completed_chunks.len() >= self.completion_threshold
 105:     }
 106: 
 107:     /// Chunks the plan assigned that haven't completed and aren't
 108:     /// currently in-flight.
 109:     #[must_use]
 110:     pub fn pending(&self) -> Vec<ChunkHash> {
 111:         let mut out = Vec::new();
 112:         for a in &self.plan.assignments {
 113:             if self.failed_sources.contains(&a.source_device_id) {
 114:                 continue;
 115:             }
 116:             for c in &a.chunk_hashes {
 117:                 if !self.completed_chunks.contains(c) && !self.in_flight_chunks.contains_key(c) {
 118:                     out.push(*c);
 119:                 }
 120:             }
 121:         }
 122:         out
 123:     }
 124: }

 181:     #[test]
 182:     fn complete_chunk_threshold_signal() {
 183:         let mut t = TransferProgress::new(plan(), &manifest());
 184:         assert!(!t.complete_chunk([1; 32]));
 185:         assert!(!t.complete_chunk([2; 32]));
 186:         assert!(!t.complete_chunk([3; 32]));
 187:         // Fourth completion brings us to threshold for the first time.
 188:         assert!(t.complete_chunk([4; 32]));
 189:         // Another completion doesn't re-fire the signal.
 190:         assert!(!t.complete_chunk([5; 32]));
 191:     }

   1: //! Receiver-side signed fetch request.
   2: //!
   3: //! A [`FetchRequest`] is "I, device R, want chunks `X` from you,
   4: //! device S, for `FileId` `F`, by deadline `D`." The receiver's subkey
   5: //! signs the canonical bytes; sources verify under the master-
   6: //! attested subkey VK before serving.
   7: 
   8: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
   9: 
  10: use crate::distributed_fs::{ChunkHash, FileId, CHUNK_HASH_LEN, FILE_ID_LEN};
  11: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  12: use crate::subkey::{DeviceSubkey, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  13: 
  14: /// Length of the per-request nonce.
  15: pub const FETCH_NONCE_LEN: usize = 16;
  16: /// Per-request nonce.
  17: pub type FetchNonce = [u8; FETCH_NONCE_LEN];
  18: 
  19: /// Max chunks one request can name. Bounds wire size + verify cost.
  20: pub const MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FETCH: usize = 8192;
  21: 
  22: /// Domain-separation tag for fetch-request signing.
  23: pub const FETCH_REQUEST_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-fetch-request-v1";
  24: 
  25: /// Receiver's signed fetch request.
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  27: pub struct FetchRequest {
  28:     /// File the receiver is reassembling.
  29:     pub file_id: FileId,
  30:     /// The device asking for chunks (receiver).
  31:     pub receiver_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  32:     /// The device being asked to serve (source).
  33:     pub source_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  34:     /// Sorted, de-duplicated list of chunk hashes the receiver wants.
  35:     /// Sources MUST serve only the listed hashes.
  36:     pub chunk_hashes: Vec<ChunkHash>,
  37:     /// Receiver-supplied upper bound on bytes the source may deliver
  38:     /// in response. Sources stop once they've delivered this much.
  39:     pub max_byte_budget: u64,
  40:     /// Wall-clock seconds after which the source must drop the request.
  41:     pub deadline_unix: u64,
  42:     /// Per-request nonce. Sources track recently-seen nonces to drop
  43:     /// duplicate requests.
  44:     pub nonce: FetchNonce,
  45:     /// Receiver subkey day-index at sign time.
  46:     pub receiver_day_index: u64,
  47:     /// Wall-clock seconds at sign time.
  48:     pub issued_unix: u64,
  49:     /// Receiver's subkey signature over the canonical transcript.
  50:     pub receiver_sig: Vec<u8>,
  51: }
  52: 
  53: impl FetchRequest {
  54:     /// Canonical bytes the receiver's subkey signs over.
  55:     ///
  56:     /// 9 args reflects the wire-format binding; structural, not
  57:     /// a logical bundle.
  58:     #[must_use]
  59:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  60:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  61:         file_id: &FileId,
  62:         receiver_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  63:         source_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  64:         chunk_hashes: &[ChunkHash],
  65:         max_byte_budget: u64,
  66:         deadline_unix: u64,
  67:         nonce: &FetchNonce,
  68:         receiver_day_index: u64,
  69:         issued_unix: u64,
  70:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  71:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  72:             FETCH_REQUEST_DOMAIN.len()
  73:                 + FILE_ID_LEN
  74:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  75:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  76:                 + 4
  77:                 + chunk_hashes.len() * CHUNK_HASH_LEN
  78:                 + 8
  79:                 + 8
  80:                 + FETCH_NONCE_LEN
  81:                 + 8
  82:                 + 8,
  83:         );
  84:         out.extend_from_slice(FETCH_REQUEST_DOMAIN);
  85:         out.extend_from_slice(file_id);
  86:         out.extend_from_slice(receiver_device_id);
  87:         out.extend_from_slice(source_device_id);
  88:         let count = u32::try_from(chunk_hashes.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
  89:         out.extend_from_slice(&count.to_be_bytes());
  90:         for c in chunk_hashes {
  91:             out.extend_from_slice(c);
  92:         }
  93:         out.extend_from_slice(&max_byte_budget.to_be_bytes());
  94:         out.extend_from_slice(&deadline_unix.to_be_bytes());
  95:         out.extend_from_slice(nonce);
  96:         out.extend_from_slice(&receiver_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  97:         out.extend_from_slice(&issued_unix.to_be_bytes());
  98:         out
  99:     }
 100: 
 101:     /// Validate the request's shape.
 102:     pub fn shape_check(&self) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 103:         if self.chunk_hashes.is_empty() {
 104:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestEmpty);
 105:         }
 106:         if self.chunk_hashes.len() > MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FETCH {
 107:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestTooManyChunks {
 108:                 got: self.chunk_hashes.len(),
 109:                 max: MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FETCH,
 110:             });
 111:         }
 112:         let mut prev: Option<&ChunkHash> = None;
 113:         for c in &self.chunk_hashes {
 114:             if let Some(p) = prev {
 115:                 if c <= p {
 116:                     return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestChunksNotSorted);
 117:                 }
 118:             }
 119:             prev = Some(c);
 120:         }
 121:         if self.deadline_unix <= self.issued_unix {
 122:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestDeadlineNotAfterIssue {
 123:                 issued_unix: self.issued_unix,
 124:                 deadline_unix: self.deadline_unix,
 125:             });
 126:         }
 127:         if self.receiver_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 128:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 129:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
 130:                 got: self.receiver_sig.len(),
 131:             });
 132:         }
 133:         Ok(())
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     /// Verify the receiver's signature.
 137:     pub fn verify(&self, receiver_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 138:         self.shape_check()?;
 139:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 140:             &self.file_id,
 141:             &self.receiver_device_id,
 142:             &self.source_device_id,
 143:             &self.chunk_hashes,
 144:             self.max_byte_budget,
 145:             self.deadline_unix,
 146:             &self.nonce,
 147:             self.receiver_day_index,
 148:             self.issued_unix,
 149:         );
 150:         receiver_vk
 151:             .verify(&transcript, &self.receiver_sig)
 152:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestVerifyFail)
 153:     }
 154: }
 155: 
 156: /// Sign a fetch request. Chunk hashes are sorted + de-duplicated at
 157: /// sign time so two receivers asking for the same set produce
 158: /// identical transcripts (caches benefit).
 159: ///
 160: /// 8 args reflects the protocol's signed-field surface.
 161: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 162: pub fn sign_fetch_request(
 163:     receiver: &DeviceSubkey,
 164:     source_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 165:     file_id: FileId,
 166:     mut chunk_hashes: Vec<ChunkHash>,
 167:     max_byte_budget: u64,
 168:     issued_unix: u64,
 169:     deadline_unix: u64,
 170:     nonce: FetchNonce,
 171: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<FetchRequest> {
 172:     if deadline_unix <= issued_unix {
 173:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestDeadlineNotAfterIssue {
 174:             issued_unix,
 175:             deadline_unix,
 176:         });
 177:     }
 178:     chunk_hashes.sort_unstable();
 179:     chunk_hashes.dedup();
 180:     if chunk_hashes.is_empty() {
 181:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestEmpty);
 182:     }
 183:     if chunk_hashes.len() > MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FETCH {
 184:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::FetchRequestTooManyChunks {
 185:             got: chunk_hashes.len(),
 186:             max: MAX_CHUNKS_PER_FETCH,
 187:         });
 188:     }
 189:     let transcript = FetchRequest::canonical_transcript(
 190:         &file_id,
 191:         receiver.device_id(),
 192:         &source_device_id,
 193:         &chunk_hashes,
 194:         max_byte_budget,
 195:         deadline_unix,
 196:         &nonce,
 197:         receiver.day_index(),
 198:         issued_unix,
 199:     );
 200:     let sig = receiver.sign(&transcript)?;
 201:     Ok(FetchRequest {
 202:         file_id,
 203:         receiver_device_id: *receiver.device_id(),
 204:         source_device_id,
 205:         chunk_hashes,
 206:         max_byte_budget,
 207:         deadline_unix,
 208:         nonce,
 209:         receiver_day_index: receiver.day_index(),
 210:         issued_unix,
 211:         receiver_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 212:     })
 213: }

   1: //! Hardware-bound subkey wrapping.
   2: //!
   3: //! At rest, the per-device subkey seed should be wrapped under the
   4: //! platform's hardware key store: Apple Secure Enclave on iOS/macOS,
   5: //! Android `StrongBox` on modern Android, Windows TPM2 on PC, ARM
   6: //! `TrustZone` on embedded. Loss of the device's RAM (cold-boot,
   7: //! sleep with display lock, etc.) means the wrapped seed sits in
   8: //! cold storage; unwrapping requires the hardware key.
   9: //!
  10: //! This module defines the *trait* the daemon programs against, plus
  11: //! a [`SoftwareWrapper`] reference implementation that uses
  12: //! BLAKE3-keyed AEAD-style XOR + MAC (NOT for production — it's a
  13: //! testing fixture). Per-platform backends (Secure Enclave / TPM /
  14: //! `StrongBox` / `TrustZone`) implement the same trait against their
  15: //! respective KEKs.
  16: //!
  17: //! ## Sovereignty contract
  18: //!
  19: //! Hardware-bound is TOFU-degrading: if no hardware backend is
  20: //! available the daemon falls back to a software-encrypted seed file
  21: //! on disk. Vendor attestation chains (Apple, Google, Microsoft) are
  22: //! OPTIONAL — they harden the binding but the system functions
  23: //! without them.
  24: 
  25: use blake3::Hasher;
  26: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  27: use zeroize::ZeroizeOnDrop;
  28: 
  29: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  30: 
  31: /// Number of bytes of overhead the [`SoftwareWrapper`] adds to each
  32: /// wrapped seed (nonce + MAC).
  33: pub const WRAPPED_KEY_OVERHEAD: usize = 12 + 32;
  34: 
  35: /// Wrap / unwrap the raw subkey seed using a hardware-bound key.
  36: ///
  37: /// The trait is intentionally minimal: callers hand in plaintext
  38: /// bytes, get out ciphertext bytes, and vice versa. The KEK never
  39: /// leaves the platform's secure store.
  40: pub trait HardwareWrapper: std::fmt::Debug + Send + Sync {
  41:     /// Wrap a raw seed for at-rest storage. The returned ciphertext
  42:     /// is what the daemon writes to disk.
  43:     fn wrap(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> DeviceMeshResult<Vec<u8>>;
  44: 
  45:     /// Unwrap ciphertext back to the raw seed. Returns
  46:     /// [`DeviceMeshError::HardwareUnwrapFail`] on integrity failure.
  47:     fn unwrap(&self, ciphertext: &[u8]) -> DeviceMeshResult<Vec<u8>>;
  48: }
  49: 
  50: /// Reference / test implementation: a single in-memory 32-byte KEK
  51: /// XOR'd with a BLAKE3-derived keystream + 32-byte BLAKE3-keyed MAC.
  52: ///
  53: /// ## NOT FOR PRODUCTION
  54: ///
  55: /// The KEK lives in process memory, so it offers NO hardware
  56: /// protection. Suitable for tests + the daemon's "no hardware
  57: /// available" fallback when paired with an OS-keyring-stored KEK
  58: /// outside this crate. Production binds to platform hardware via a
  59: /// per-platform impl.
  60: #[derive(ZeroizeOnDrop)]
  61: pub struct SoftwareWrapper {
  62:     kek: [u8; 32],
  63: }
  64: 
  65: impl std::fmt::Debug for SoftwareWrapper {
  66:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  67:         f.debug_struct("SoftwareWrapper").finish_non_exhaustive()
  68:     }
  69: }
  70: 
  71: impl SoftwareWrapper {
  72:     /// Construct from a raw 32-byte KEK.
  73:     #[must_use] 
  74:     pub const fn new(kek: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
  75:         Self { kek }
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     fn keystream(&self, nonce: &[u8; 12], len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
  79:         let mut h = Hasher::new_keyed(&self.kek);
  80:         h.update(b"OL-device-mesh-hw-stream-v1");
  81:         h.update(nonce);
  82:         let mut reader = h.finalize_xof();
  83:         let mut out = vec![0u8; len];
  84:         reader.fill(&mut out);
  85:         out
  86:     }
  87: 
  88:     fn mac(&self, nonce: &[u8; 12], ciphertext: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
  89:         let mut h = Hasher::new_keyed(&self.kek);
  90:         h.update(b"OL-device-mesh-hw-mac-v1");
  91:         h.update(nonce);
  92:         h.update(ciphertext);
  93:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
  94:     }
  95: }
  96: 
  97: impl HardwareWrapper for SoftwareWrapper {
  98:     fn wrap(&self, plaintext: &[u8]) -> DeviceMeshResult<Vec<u8>> {
  99:         // Deterministic nonce from BLAKE3(kek || plaintext). This is
 100:         // safe under the assumption that each plaintext seed is
 101:         // unique (which is true — they're 64-byte hybrid seeds). For
 102:         // a generic AEAD that's not safe; this is a CONFINED test
 103:         // fixture and we accept the constraint.
 104:         let mut nh = Hasher::new_keyed(&self.kek);
 105:         nh.update(b"OL-device-mesh-hw-nonce-v1");
 106:         nh.update(plaintext);
 107:         let nd = nh.finalize();
 108:         let mut nonce = [0u8; 12];
 109:         nonce.copy_from_slice(&nd.as_bytes()[..12]);
 110: 
 111:         let ks = self.keystream(&nonce, plaintext.len());
 112:         let mut ct = vec![0u8; plaintext.len()];
 113:         for i in 0..plaintext.len() {
 114:             ct[i] = plaintext[i] ^ ks[i];
 115:         }
 116:         let mac = self.mac(&nonce, &ct);
 117:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(12 + ct.len() + 32);
 118:         out.extend_from_slice(&nonce);
 119:         out.extend_from_slice(&ct);
 120:         out.extend_from_slice(&mac);
 121:         Ok(out)
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     fn unwrap(&self, ciphertext: &[u8]) -> DeviceMeshResult<Vec<u8>> {
 125:         if ciphertext.len() < WRAPPED_KEY_OVERHEAD {
 126:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 127:                 expected: WRAPPED_KEY_OVERHEAD,
 128:                 got: ciphertext.len(),
 129:             });
 130:         }
 131:         let pt_len = ciphertext.len() - WRAPPED_KEY_OVERHEAD;
 132:         let mut nonce = [0u8; 12];
 133:         nonce.copy_from_slice(&ciphertext[..12]);
 134:         let ct = &ciphertext[12..12 + pt_len];
 135:         let supplied_mac = &ciphertext[12 + pt_len..];
 136: 
 137:         let expected_mac = self.mac(&nonce, ct);
 138:         if !bool::from(expected_mac.ct_eq(supplied_mac)) {
 139:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::HardwareUnwrapFail);
 140:         }
 141:         let ks = self.keystream(&nonce, pt_len);
 142:         let mut pt = vec![0u8; pt_len];
 143:         for i in 0..pt_len {
 144:             pt[i] = ct[i] ^ ks[i];
 145:         }
 146:         Ok(pt)
 147:     }
 148: }
