   1: //! Coherence Mesh Row 8 — Personal Device Mesh identity layer (Layer 1).
   2: //!
   3: //! Builds the cryptographic foundation that lets one logical identity
   4: //! own many devices without revealing the device count to friends and
   5: //! without sacrificing per-device forward secrecy.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## What this crate provides
   8: //!
   9: //! - `MasterIdentity`: a [`ol_pqsig::HybridSigningKey`] anchored to a
  10: //!   32-byte master seed. Generated once per human. Friends pin the
  11: //!   master verifying key.
  12: //! - `DeviceClass`: phone / laptop / tablet / desktop / server /
  13: //!   wearable / appliance — drives device-policy decisions in higher
  14: //!   layers (battery, network, allowed-caps) and is bound into the
  15: //!   subkey-derivation transcript so two devices of the same class but
  16: //!   different `device_id` never collide.
  17: //! - `DeviceSubkey`: a per-device hybrid signing key deterministically
  18: //!   derived from `(master_seed, device_class, device_id, day_index)`
  19: //!   via BLAKE3-keyed HKDF.  Friends never see subkey verifying keys
  20: //!   directly; everything is signed under the master pubkey via a
  21: //!   cross-sign attestation (see `SubkeyAttestation`).
  22: //! - **Daily ratchet**: each subkey has an underlying *chain root* and
  23: //!   a current *day index*. `step_one_day()` advances the chain via
  24: //!   `S_{n+1} = HKDF(S_n, "ratchet")` and zeroizes `S_n`.  A stolen
  25: //!   device whose subkey is captured today cannot decrypt any prior
  26: //!   day's traffic, even with the master pubkey, because the prior
  27: //!   subkeys are not recoverable without the master *seed*.
  28: //! - **Field-binding hook**: subkey derivation optionally consumes a
  29: //!   [`ol_threshold_recovery::FieldWitness`] so a captured raw seed is
  30: //!   useless without reproducing the coherence-field state at mint.
  31: //! - **Cross-witness attestation**: each device periodically signs a
  32: //!   `LivenessProof` over its own state + the wall-clock epoch.  A
  33: //!   sibling device that fails to produce a fresh proof gets flagged
  34: //!   for auto-revocation by quorum at Layer 2.
  35: //! - **`HardwareWrapper` trait**: opaque interface for wrapping the raw
  36: //!   subkey bytes under platform key storage (Secure Enclave / TPM /
  37: //!   `StrongBox` / `TrustZone`).  A software-only reference impl is
  38: //!   provided; production builds wire platform backends via the trait.
  39: //!
  40: //! ## Layer-1 acceptance gate
  41: //!
  42: //! - Subkey derivation is deterministic on `(master_seed, device_class,
  43: //!   device_id, day_index)` and byte-stable across builds.
  44: //! - Daily ratchet advances forward only; old seeds zeroize on step.
  45: //! - Subkey attestations are cross-signed by the master and verify
  46: //!   under the master's `HybridVerifyingKey`.
  47: //! - `LivenessProof` timing variance under the ct-gate ≤ 15 %.
  48: //! - 1M iters of property-testing on the subkey/ratchet/attestation
  49: //!   surface pass with no panics.
  50: //!
  51: //! ## Layer status
  52: //!
  53: //! - **Layer 1** (this crate): identity stack — what's documented
  54: //!   above.  Pure Rust; no daemon wiring yet.
  55: //! - **Layer 2** (separate ship): threshold device quorum on top of
  56: //!   row 9 Shamir.
  57: //! - **Layer 3+** (separate ships): CRDT state mirror, distributed
  58: //!   filesystem, multi-device fan-out, τ_c-routed self-mesh, etc.
  59: //!
  60: //! ## Worked example
  61: //!
  62: //! ```no_run
  63: //! // Doctest is `no_run` because ML-DSA-65 key material is ~2 KB
  64: //! // and signing operations push doctest stacks past their default
  65: //! // size on Windows. Compile-time validation is preserved.
  66: //! use ol_device_mesh::{
  67: //!     mint_subkey, sibling_witness, state_root, verify_liveness,
  68: //!     DeviceClass, LivenessProof, MasterIdentity,
  69: //!     DEFAULT_LIVENESS_SKEW_SECS,
  70: //! };
  71: //! use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  72: //!
  73: //! // Generate the master identity once per human; friends pin its VK.
  74: //! let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  75: //! let pinned_vk = master.verifying_key();
  76: //!
  77: //! // Mint a per-device subkey for the phone, valid for one year.
  78: //! let phone_id = [0x42u8; 16];
  79: //! let (phone_subkey, phone_attestation) =
  80: //!     mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, phone_id, 0, 365).unwrap();
  81: //!
  82: //! // Friends only ever check attestations under the pinned master VK.
  83: //! phone_attestation.verify(&pinned_vk).unwrap();
  84: //!
  85: //! // The phone issues a liveness proof every N minutes so siblings
  86: //! // can confirm it's alive + not seized.
  87: //! let now_unix = 1_700_000_000u64;
  88: //! let proof = LivenessProof::issue(
  89: //!     &phone_subkey,
  90: //!     now_unix,
  91: //!     state_root(b"current crdt state hash"),
  92: //! ).unwrap();
  93: //!
  94: //! // A sibling device verifies the proof under the phone's subkey VK
  95: //! // (obtained from the attestation it cached) and the wall clock.
  96: //! let witness = sibling_witness(phone_subkey.verifying_key(), DEFAULT_LIVENESS_SKEW_SECS);
  97: //! verify_liveness(&proof, &witness, now_unix).unwrap();
  98: //! ```

   1: //! Master identity — the 32-byte seed everything else derives from.
   2: //!
   3: //! `MasterIdentity` wraps a `HybridSigningKey` plus the raw seed used
   4: //! to deterministically derive per-device subkeys. The seed never
   5: //! leaves the device that holds the master role; everywhere else
   6: //! works with the `HybridVerifyingKey` (the friends-side pin).
   7: //!
   8: //! Threat model for the seed:
   9: //!
  10: //! - At rest: stored under hardware wrapping (Layer-1 [`crate::HardwareWrapper`])
  11: //!   or under threshold-recovery sharding (`ol_threshold_recovery`).
  12: //! - In memory: zeroized on `Drop`.
  13: //! - Recovery: lost master seed reconstitutes from any K of N
  14: //!   threshold-recovery shares.
  15: 
  16: use ol_pqsig::{HybridSigningKey, HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SK_LEN};
  17: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  18: use zeroize::ZeroizeOnDrop;
  19: 
  20: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  21: 
  22: /// Length of the canonical master seed in bytes.
  23: pub const MASTER_SEED_LEN: usize = HYBRID_SK_LEN;
  24: 
  25: /// The master identity that owns the device mesh. Friends pin this
  26: /// identity's `HybridVerifyingKey`; per-device subkeys are derived
  27: /// from `seed` via `derivation::derive_subkey_seed`.
  28: #[derive(ZeroizeOnDrop)]
  29: pub struct MasterIdentity {
  30:     /// Canonical seed: 32-byte Ed25519 seed || 32-byte ML-DSA seed.
  31:     seed: [u8; MASTER_SEED_LEN],
  32: }
  33: 
  34: impl MasterIdentity {
  35:     /// Generate a fresh master identity from a cryptographically
  36:     /// secure RNG. Use exactly once per human.
  37:     pub fn generate<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> Self {
  38:         let mut seed = [0u8; MASTER_SEED_LEN];
  39:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut seed);
  40:         Self { seed }
  41:     }
  42: 
  43:     /// Construct from an existing seed. Use this on a paired device
  44:     /// recovering from threshold-recovery shares.
  45:     #[must_use] 
  46:     pub const fn from_seed(seed: [u8; MASTER_SEED_LEN]) -> Self {
  47:         Self { seed }
  48:     }
  49: 
  50:     /// Parse from wire bytes (length-checked).
  51:     pub const fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> DeviceMeshResult<Self> {
  52:         if bytes.len() != MASTER_SEED_LEN {
  53:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
  54:                 expected: MASTER_SEED_LEN,
  55:                 got: bytes.len(),
  56:             });
  57:         }
  58:         let mut seed = [0u8; MASTER_SEED_LEN];
  59:         seed.copy_from_slice(bytes);
  60:         Ok(Self { seed })
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// Borrow the raw seed. Callers who hold this for any non-trivial
  64:     /// duration MUST zeroize it themselves.
  65:     #[must_use] 
  66:     pub const fn seed(&self) -> &[u8; MASTER_SEED_LEN] {
  67:         &self.seed
  68:     }
  69: 
  70:     /// Materialize the underlying [`HybridSigningKey`]. Called rarely
  71:     /// (only when the master itself signs an attestation); per-device
  72:     /// signing always goes through `DeviceSubkey`.
  73:     #[must_use] 
  74:     pub fn signing_key(&self) -> HybridSigningKey {
  75:         HybridSigningKey::from_bytes(&self.seed)
  76:             .expect("master seed length is invariant-checked")
  77:     }
  78: 
  79:     /// Borrow the public verifying key — the byte string friends pin.
  80:     #[must_use] 
  81:     pub fn verifying_key(&self) -> HybridVerifyingKey {
  82:         self.signing_key().verifying_key()
  83:     }
  84: }
  85: 
  86: impl std::fmt::Debug for MasterIdentity {
  87:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  88:         f.debug_struct("MasterIdentity").finish_non_exhaustive()
  89:     }
  90: }

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 3 — full-state CRDT mirror across the device mesh.
   2: //!
   3: //! Every device replica holds the same logical app state: contacts,
   4: //! capability ledger, clipboard, settings, file manifests, anything
   5: //! the higher layers want to keep in sync across phone / laptop /
   6: //! tablet / desktop.
   7: //!
   8: //! ## Composition with Layers 1 and 2
   9: //!
  10: //! - Every state change ([`AuthenticatedOp`]) is signed by the
  11: //!   emitting device's Layer-1 subkey. Replicas verify the signature
  12: //!   under the master-attested subkey VK before merging.
  13: //! - High-stakes subtrees (capability ledger, master settings, the
  14: //!   device roster itself) are flagged in the [`SubtreePolicy`] as
  15: //!   requiring a Layer-2 [`crate::quorum::QuorumCertificate`].
  16: //!   Replicas refuse to merge an op against a quorum-gated subtree
  17: //!   unless a valid certificate is attached.
  18: //! - The Layer-1 [`crate::LivenessProof`]'s `state_root` field IS
  19: //!   the [`MeshState::root`] of this layer. A sibling failing to
  20: //!   converge to the same root within the heartbeat window gets
  21: //!   flagged for Layer-2 quorum revocation.
  22: //!
  23: //! ## Subtree taxonomy
  24: //!
  25: //! - [`Subtree::LwwRegister`] — single-value last-writer-wins.
  26: //! - [`Subtree::OrSet`] — observed-remove set with tombstones.
  27: //! - [`Subtree::PnCounter`] — per-device positive/negative counter.
  28: //! - [`Subtree::LwwMap`] — Map<bytes, lww-bytes>; tombstones on
  29: //!   delete.
  30: //!
  31: //! These four primitives compose into 95 % of real app state: chat
  32: //! drafts are LWW-Register, contact lists are OR-Set, send-counts
  33: //! are PN-Counter, settings are LWW-Map, etc.
  34: //!
  35: //! ## Sync protocol
  36: //!
  37: //! Each device keeps a [`SyncState`] tracking the highest sequence
  38: //! number it has seen per peer device. To converge, two devices
  39: //! exchange [`SyncSummary`] records and reply with the ops the peer
  40: //! is missing. Anti-entropy is bounded by the gap between summaries;
  41: //! a freshly-paired device gets a one-shot catch-up.
  42: //!
  43: //! ## Replay protection
  44: //!
  45: //! Every op carries a strictly-increasing per-device sequence
  46: //! number. Replicas drop ops where `seq <= last_seen_seq[device]`,
  47: //! so an attacker who captures a signed op cannot replay it after
  48: //! the sender has issued a newer op for the same device. The
  49: //! per-op wall-clock timestamp + LWW ordering preserve eventual
  50: //! consistency even if replay is attempted concurrently with new
  51: //! ops.
  52: //!
  53: //! ## What this layer doesn't ship
  54: //!
  55: //! - Sequence CRDTs (Yjs / RGA / Logoot). Out of scope for the
  56: //!   first ship; LWW-Map covers the immediate need.
  57: //! - Compaction / snapshot encoding for cold-start sync. The
  58: //!   `SyncState` exposes an op-log iterator; persistence is a
  59: //!   higher-layer concern.
  60: //! - Sub-second pairwise sync. Anti-entropy is bandwidth-bounded
  61: //!   and assumes minute-scale convergence.
  62: //!
  63: //! ## Example: two replicas converge
  64: //!
  65: //! ```no_run
  66: //! // Doctest is `no_run` because ML-DSA key material is ~2 KB —
  67: //! // signing operations push doctest stacks past their default
  68: //! // size on Windows. Compile-time validation is preserved.
  69: //! use ol_device_mesh::mesh_state::{
  70: //!     AuthenticatedOp, Delta, MeshState, SubtreePolicyKind, SyncState,
  71: //! };
  72: //! use ol_device_mesh::{
  73: //!     mint_subkey, DeviceClass, MasterIdentity, DeviceMeshResult,
  74: //! };
  75: //! use ol_pqsig::HybridVerifyingKey;
  76: //! use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  77: //!
  78: //! let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  79: //! let (phone_sk, phone_att) =
  80: //!     mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, [0xAA; 16], 0, 365).unwrap();
  81: //! let phone_vk = HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&phone_att.subkey_vk_bytes).unwrap();
  82: //!
  83: //! // Replica A: tracks one LWW-Map subtree.
  84: //! let mut state_a = MeshState::empty();
  85: //! state_a.ensure_subtree(b"contacts".to_vec(), SubtreePolicyKind::LwwMap).unwrap();
  86: //! let mut sync_a = SyncState::empty();
  87: //!
  88: //! // Phone signs an op and ingests it locally.
  89: //! let op = AuthenticatedOp::sign(
  90: //!     &phone_sk,
  91: //!     b"contacts".to_vec(),
  92: //!     Delta::MapPut { key: b"alice".to_vec(), value: b"alice@example".to_vec(), ts: 1 },

  94: //!     1_700_000_000,

   2: //!

  28:     /// Write `(value, ts)` to a [`crate::mesh_state::LwwRegister`].

  30:         /// Value bytes.
  31:         value: Vec<u8>,
  32:         /// LWW timestamp.

  43:     /// Tagged remove from an [`crate::mesh_state::OrSet`].

  45:         /// Element bytes.

  53:         device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],

  56:         delta: i64,

  58:     /// Put `(value, ts)` into an [`crate::mesh_state::LwwMap`].
  59:     MapPut {
  60:         /// Map key.

  66:     },
  67:     /// Tombstone an [`crate::mesh_state::LwwMap`] entry.
  68:     MapDelete {
  69:         /// Map key.
  70:         key: Vec<u8>,
  71:         /// LWW timestamp.
  72:         ts: u64,

  77:     /// One-byte discriminant used in the canonical transcript.
  78:     #[must_use]
  79:     pub const fn kind_tag(&self) -> u8 {
  80:         match self {
  81:             Self::LwwSet { .. } => 1,
  82:             Self::OrAdd { .. } => 2,
  83:             Self::OrRemove { .. } => 3,
  84:             Self::Counter { .. } => 4,
  85:             Self::MapPut { .. } => 5,
  86:             Self::MapDelete { .. } => 6,
  87:         }
  88:     }
  89:     /// True iff this delta requires the subtree to be of the kind
  90:     /// implied by `kind_tag`. Used by upstream policy checks.
  91:     pub const fn validate_size(&self) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  92:         match self {
  93:             Self::LwwSet { value, .. } | Self::MapPut { value, .. }
  94:                 if value.len() > MAX_DELTA_VALUE_LEN => {
  95:                     return Err(DeviceMeshError::DeltaValueTooLong {
  96:                         got: value.len(),
  97:                         max: MAX_DELTA_VALUE_LEN,
  98:                     });
  99:                 }
 100:             _ => {}
 101:         }
 102:         Ok(())
 103:     }
 104:     fn canonical_into(&self, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
 105:         out.push(self.kind_tag());
 106:         match self {
 107:             Self::LwwSet { value, ts } => {
 108:                 push_bytes(out, value);
 109:                 out.extend_from_slice(&ts.to_be_bytes());
 110:             }
 111:             Self::OrAdd { element, tag } | Self::OrRemove { element, tag } => {
 112:                 push_bytes(out, element);
 113:                 out.extend_from_slice(tag);
 114:             }
 115:             Self::Counter { device_id, delta } => {
 116:                 out.extend_from_slice(device_id);
 117:                 out.extend_from_slice(&delta.to_be_bytes());
 118:             }
 119:             Self::MapPut { key, value, ts } => {
 120:                 push_bytes(out, key);
 121:                 push_bytes(out, value);
 122:                 out.extend_from_slice(&ts.to_be_bytes());
 123:             }
 124:             Self::MapDelete { key, ts } => {
 125:                 push_bytes(out, key);
 126:                 out.extend_from_slice(&ts.to_be_bytes());
 127:             }
 128:         }
 129:     }
 130: }
 131: 
 132: fn push_bytes(out: &mut Vec<u8>, b: &[u8]) {
 133:     let len = u32::try_from(b.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 134:     out.extend_from_slice(&len.to_be_bytes());
 135:     out.extend_from_slice(&b[..len as usize]);
 136: }
 137: 
 138: /// An op signed by the emitter's subkey, ready for sibling replicas
 139: /// to verify + merge.
 140: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 141: pub struct AuthenticatedOp {
 142:     /// Target subtree label.
 143:     pub subtree: Vec<u8>,
 144:     /// The CRDT delta.
 145:     pub delta: Delta,
 146:     /// Emitter device id.
 147:     pub device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 148:     /// Emitter's subkey day-index.
 149:     pub day_index: u64,
 150:     /// Per-device monotonic sequence number. Replicas drop ops where
 151:     /// `seq <= last_seen[device_id]` to defeat replay.
 152:     pub seq: u64,
 153:     /// Wall-clock seconds at issue time. Layer 3 doesn't enforce a
 154:     /// skew window; higher layers may.
 155:     pub wall_unix: u64,
 156:     /// Subkey signature over the canonical transcript.
 157:     pub subkey_sig: Vec<u8>,
 158: }
 159: 
 160: impl AuthenticatedOp {
 161:     /// Canonical bytes the subkey signs over.
 162:     #[must_use] 
 163:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
 164:         subtree: &[u8],
 165:         delta: &Delta,
 166:         device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 167:         day_index: u64,
 168:         seq: u64,
 169:         wall_unix: u64,
 170:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
 171:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
 172:             AUTH_OP_DOMAIN.len() + 4 + subtree.len() + 1 + 64 + DEVICE_ID_LEN + 8 + 8 + 8,
 173:         );
 174:         out.extend_from_slice(AUTH_OP_DOMAIN);
 175:         push_bytes(&mut out, subtree);
 176:         delta.canonical_into(&mut out);
 177:         out.extend_from_slice(device_id);
 178:         out.extend_from_slice(&day_index.to_be_bytes());
 179:         out.extend_from_slice(&seq.to_be_bytes());
 180:         out.extend_from_slice(&wall_unix.to_be_bytes());
 181:         out
 182:     }
 183:     /// Sign a delta into an [`AuthenticatedOp`].
 184:     pub fn sign(
 185:         subkey: &DeviceSubkey,
 186:         subtree: Vec<u8>,
 187:         delta: Delta,
 188:         seq: u64,
 189:         wall_unix: u64,
 190:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<Self> {
 191:         if subtree.len() > MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN {
 192:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::SubtreeLabelTooLong {
 193:                 got: subtree.len(),
 194:                 max: MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN,
 195:             });
 196:         }
 197:         delta.validate_size()?;
 198:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 199:             &subtree,
 200:             &delta,
 201:             subkey.device_id(),
 202:             subkey.day_index(),
 203:             seq,
 204:             wall_unix,
 205:         );
 206:         let sig = subkey.sign(&transcript)?;
 207:         Ok(Self {
 208:             subtree,
 209:             delta,
 210:             device_id: *subkey.device_id(),
 211:             day_index: subkey.day_index(),
 212:             seq,
 213:             wall_unix,
 214:             subkey_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 215:         })
 216:     }
 217:     /// Verify the signature under the supplied subkey VK. Caller is
 218:     /// responsible for proving the VK is the emitter's (via a
 219:     /// master-signed [`crate::SubkeyAttestation`]).
 220:     pub fn verify(&self, subkey_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 221:         if self.subkey_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 222:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 223:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
 224:                 got: self.subkey_sig.len(),
 225:             });
 226:         }
 227:         if self.subtree.len() > MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN {
 228:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::SubtreeLabelTooLong {
 229:                 got: self.subtree.len(),
 230:                 max: MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN,
 231:             });
 232:         }
 233:         self.delta.validate_size()?;
 234:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 235:             &self.subtree,
 236:             &self.delta,
 237:             &self.device_id,
 238:             self.day_index,
 239:             self.seq,
 240:             self.wall_unix,
 241:         );
 242:         subkey_vk
 243:             .verify(&transcript, &self.subkey_sig)
 244:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::AuthOpVerifyFail)
 245:     }
 246: }

   1: //! Subtree-level policy: which CRDT kind a label uses, and whether
   2: //! mutations to that subtree require a Layer-2 quorum certificate.
   3: 
   4: use super::state::Subtree;
   5: 
   6: /// CRDT kind for a subtree. Bound at first-write time and immutable
   7: /// afterwards.
   8: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   9: pub enum SubtreePolicyKind {
  10:     /// `LwwRegister` — single LWW value.
  11:     LwwRegister,
  12:     /// `OrSet` — observed-remove set.
  13:     OrSet,
  14:     /// `PnCounter` — per-device positive/negative counter.
  15:     PnCounter,
  16:     /// `LwwMap` — Map<bytes, LWW bytes> with tombstones.
  17:     LwwMap,
  18: }
  19: 
  20: /// Higher-layer policy for a subtree: kind + whether ops require a
  21: /// quorum certificate. The mesh-state engine reads this at op-apply
  22: /// time; the daemon owns the policy table.
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  24: pub struct SubtreePolicy {
  25:     /// CRDT kind for this subtree.
  26:     pub kind: SubtreePolicyKind,
  27:     /// `true` if any op against this subtree requires a Layer-2
  28:     /// [`crate::quorum::QuorumCertificate`].
  29:     pub quorum_gated: bool,
  30: }
  31: 
  32: impl SubtreePolicy {
  33:     /// A plain (non-quorum-gated) policy of the given kind.
  34:     #[must_use]
  35:     pub const fn plain(kind: SubtreePolicyKind) -> Self {
  36:         Self { kind, quorum_gated: false }
  37:     }
  38:     /// A quorum-gated policy of the given kind.
  39:     #[must_use]
  40:     pub const fn quorum_gated(kind: SubtreePolicyKind) -> Self {
  41:         Self { kind, quorum_gated: true }
  42:     }
  43: }
  44: 
  45: /// What kind is the given subtree?
  46: #[must_use]
  47: pub const fn subtree_kind(subtree: &Subtree) -> SubtreePolicyKind {
  48:     match subtree {
  49:         Subtree::LwwRegister(_) => SubtreePolicyKind::LwwRegister,
  50:         Subtree::OrSet(_) => SubtreePolicyKind::OrSet,
  51:         Subtree::PnCounter(_) => SubtreePolicyKind::PnCounter,
  52:         Subtree::LwwMap(_) => SubtreePolicyKind::LwwMap,
  53:     }
  54: }

   1: //! CRDT lattice types + the canonical [`MeshState`] container.
   2: 
   3: use blake3::Hasher;
   4: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
   5: 
   6: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
   7: 
   8: use super::ops::{Delta, MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN};
   9: 
  10: /// Label that names a subtree within the mesh state. Bounded so
  11: /// canonical hashing has predictable cost.
  12: pub type SubtreeLabel = Vec<u8>;
  13: 
  14: /// Per-subtree root: BLAKE3 over the subtree's canonical encoding.
  15: pub type SubtreeRoot = [u8; 32];
  16: 
  17: /// Global state root: BLAKE3 over the sorted list of
  18: /// `(label, subtree_root)` pairs.
  19: pub type StateRoot = [u8; 32];
  20: 
  21: /// Tag bound to each OR-Set element so concurrent adds/removes can
  22: /// be reconciled. Typically derived from `(device_id, seq)` by the
  23: /// emitter.
  24: pub type OrSetTag = [u8; 16];
  25: 
  26: /// One subtree of the mesh state. Each variant is a CRDT lattice.
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  28: pub enum Subtree {
  29:     /// Last-writer-wins single value. Ties broken by lexicographic
  30:     /// device-id comparison so two concurrent writes resolve
  31:     /// deterministically.
  32:     LwwRegister(LwwRegister),
  33:     /// Observed-remove set: tagged adds, tagged removes; remove
  34:     /// only erases adds whose tags appear in the remove set.
  35:     OrSet(OrSet),
  36:     /// Per-device positive/negative counter.
  37:     PnCounter(PnCounter),
  38:     /// Map<key, lww-bytes> with tombstones on delete.
  39:     LwwMap(LwwMap),
  40: }
  41: 
  42: impl Subtree {
  43:     /// Empty subtree of the supplied kind.
  44:     #[must_use]
  45:     pub fn empty_of_kind(kind: super::policy::SubtreePolicyKind) -> Self {
  46:         use super::policy::SubtreePolicyKind as K;
  47:         match kind {
  48:             K::LwwRegister => Self::LwwRegister(LwwRegister::empty()),
  49:             K::OrSet => Self::OrSet(OrSet::empty()),
  50:             K::PnCounter => Self::PnCounter(PnCounter::empty()),
  51:             K::LwwMap => Self::LwwMap(LwwMap::empty()),
  52:         }
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// BLAKE3 commitment of this subtree's canonical encoding.
  56:     #[must_use]
  57:     pub fn root(&self) -> SubtreeRoot {
  58:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
  59:         match self {
  60:             Self::LwwRegister(r) => {
  61:                 h.update(b"OL-mesh-subtree-lww-register-v1");
  62:                 r.canonical_into(&mut h);
  63:             }
  64:             Self::OrSet(s) => {
  65:                 h.update(b"OL-mesh-subtree-or-set-v1");
  66:                 s.canonical_into(&mut h);
  67:             }
  68:             Self::PnCounter(c) => {
  69:                 h.update(b"OL-mesh-subtree-pn-counter-v1");
  70:                 c.canonical_into(&mut h);
  71:             }
  72:             Self::LwwMap(m) => {
  73:                 h.update(b"OL-mesh-subtree-lww-map-v1");
  74:                 m.canonical_into(&mut h);
  75:             }
  76:         }
  77:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
  78:     }
  79: 
  80:     /// Apply a delta to this subtree. Returns
  81:     /// [`DeviceMeshError::DeltaKindMismatch`] if the delta isn't
  82:     /// applicable to this variant.
  83:     pub fn apply(
  84:         &mut self,
  85:         delta: &Delta,
  86:         emitter_device_id: &[u8; 16],
  87:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  88:         match (self, delta) {
  89:             (Self::LwwRegister(r), Delta::LwwSet { value, ts }) => {
  90:                 r.set(value.clone(), *ts, emitter_device_id);
  91:                 Ok(())
  92:             }
  93:             (Self::OrSet(s), Delta::OrAdd { element, tag }) => {
  94:                 s.add(element.clone(), *tag);
  95:                 Ok(())
  96:             }
  97:             (Self::OrSet(s), Delta::OrRemove { element, tag }) => {
  98:                 s.remove(element, tag);
  99:                 Ok(())
 100:             }
 101:             (Self::PnCounter(c), Delta::Counter { device_id, delta }) => {
 102:                 c.adjust(*device_id, *delta);
 103:                 Ok(())
 104:             }
 105:             (Self::LwwMap(m), Delta::MapPut { key, value, ts }) => {
 106:                 m.put(key.clone(), value.clone(), *ts, emitter_device_id);
 107:                 Ok(())
 108:             }
 109:             (Self::LwwMap(m), Delta::MapDelete { key, ts }) => {
 110:                 m.delete(key, *ts, emitter_device_id);
 111:                 Ok(())
 112:             }
 113:             _ => Err(DeviceMeshError::DeltaKindMismatch),
 114:         }
 115:     }
 116: }
 117: 
 118: // ── LwwRegister ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 119: 
 120: /// Last-writer-wins register. Ties on `ts` are broken by
 121: /// lexicographic comparison of the writer's device id so two
 122: /// concurrent writes from different devices converge deterministically.
 123: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 124: pub struct LwwRegister {
 125:     value: Option<Vec<u8>>,
 126:     ts: u64,
 127:     last_writer: [u8; 16],
 128: }
 129: 
 130: impl LwwRegister {
 131:     /// Empty register (no value yet).
 132:     #[must_use]
 133:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
 134:         Self::default()
 135:     }
 136:     /// Current value (or `None` if no write has ever happened).
 137:     #[must_use]
 138:     pub fn value(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
 139:         self.value.as_deref()
 140:     }
 141:     /// Current write timestamp.
 142:     #[must_use]
 143:     pub const fn ts(&self) -> u64 {
 144:         self.ts
 145:     }
 146:     /// Apply a write at `(ts, writer)`. Deterministic under arbitrary
 147:     /// delivery order: ties on `ts` break to the larger writer id;
 148:     /// ties on `(ts, writer)` break to the lexicographically larger
 149:     /// value bytes (so two concurrent same-source writes converge).
 150:     pub fn set(&mut self, value: Vec<u8>, ts: u64, writer: &[u8; 16]) {
 151:         if self.is_dominated_by(ts, writer, Some(&value)) {
 152:             self.value = Some(value);
 153:             self.ts = ts;
 154:             self.last_writer = *writer;
 155:         }
 156:     }
 157:     fn is_dominated_by(
 158:         &self,
 159:         ts: u64,
 160:         writer: &[u8; 16],
 161:         value: Option<&[u8]>,
 162:     ) -> bool {
 163:         match ts.cmp(&self.ts) {
 164:             std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => true,
 165:             std::cmp::Ordering::Less => false,
 166:             std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => match writer.cmp(&self.last_writer) {
 167:                 std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => true,
 168:                 std::cmp::Ordering::Less => false,
 169:                 // Same (ts, writer): tertiary tie-break on value bytes.
 170:                 // None (delete) is treated as MAX so a delete dominates a
 171:                 // same-(ts,writer) put.
 172:                 std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => match (value, self.value.as_deref()) {
 173:                     (None, Some(_)) => true,
 174:                     (None | Some(_), None) => false,
 175:                     (Some(v_new), Some(v_old)) => v_new > v_old,
 176:                 },
 177:             },
 178:         }
 179:     }
 180:     fn canonical_into(&self, h: &mut Hasher) {
 181:         h.update(&self.ts.to_be_bytes());
 182:         h.update(&self.last_writer);
 183:         match &self.value {
 184:             None => {
 185:                 h.update(&[0u8]);
 186:             }
 187:             Some(v) => {
 188:                 h.update(&[1u8]);
 189:                 let len = u32::try_from(v.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 190:                 h.update(&len.to_be_bytes());
 191:                 h.update(&v[..len as usize]);
 192:             }
 193:         }
 194:     }
 195: }
 196: 
 197: // ── OrSet ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 198: 
 199: /// Observed-remove set: each add carries a unique tag. A remove
 200: /// erases all adds whose `(element, tag)` pair appears in the remove
 201: /// set. Replays of the same `(element, tag)` are idempotent.
 202: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 203: pub struct OrSet {
 204:     adds: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, BTreeSet<OrSetTag>>,
 205:     removes: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, BTreeSet<OrSetTag>>,
 206: }
 207: 
 208: impl OrSet {
 209:     /// Empty set.
 210:     #[must_use]
 211:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
 212:         Self::default()
 213:     }
 214:     /// All currently-visible elements.
 215:     #[must_use]
 216:     pub fn members(&self) -> Vec<&[u8]> {
 217:         let mut out = Vec::new();
 218:         for (elem, adds) in &self.adds {
 219:             let tomb = self.removes.get(elem);
 220:             let visible = adds
 221:                 .iter()
 222:                 .any(|t| tomb.is_none_or(|r| !r.contains(t)));
 223:             if visible {
 224:                 out.push(elem.as_slice());
 225:             }
 226:         }
 227:         out
 228:     }
 229:     /// True iff `element` is currently in the set.
 230:     #[must_use]
 231:     pub fn contains(&self, element: &[u8]) -> bool {
 232:         match self.adds.get(element) {
 233:             None => false,
 234:             Some(adds) => {
 235:                 let tomb = self.removes.get(element);
 236:                 adds.iter()
 237:                     .any(|t| tomb.is_none_or(|r| !r.contains(t)))
 238:             }
 239:         }
 240:     }
 241:     /// Tagged add. Replays are idempotent.
 242:     pub fn add(&mut self, element: Vec<u8>, tag: OrSetTag) {
 243:         self.adds.entry(element).or_default().insert(tag);
 244:     }
 245:     /// Tagged remove. Idempotent.
 246:     pub fn remove(&mut self, element: &[u8], tag: &OrSetTag) {
 247:         self.removes
 248:             .entry(element.to_vec())
 249:             .or_default()
 250:             .insert(*tag);
 251:     }
 252:     fn canonical_into(&self, h: &mut Hasher) {
 253:         let n_adds = u32::try_from(self.adds.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 254:         h.update(&n_adds.to_be_bytes());
 255:         for (k, v) in &self.adds {
 256:             let kl = u32::try_from(k.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 257:             h.update(&kl.to_be_bytes());
 258:             h.update(&k[..kl as usize]);
 259:             let nl = u32::try_from(v.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 260:             h.update(&nl.to_be_bytes());
 261:             for tag in v {
 262:                 h.update(tag);
 263:             }
 264:         }
 265:         let n_rem = u32::try_from(self.removes.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 266:         h.update(&n_rem.to_be_bytes());
 267:         for (k, v) in &self.removes {
 268:             let kl = u32::try_from(k.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 269:             h.update(&kl.to_be_bytes());
 270:             h.update(&k[..kl as usize]);
 271:             let nl = u32::try_from(v.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 272:             h.update(&nl.to_be_bytes());
 273:             for tag in v {
 274:                 h.update(tag);
 275:             }
 276:         }
 277:     }
 278: }
 279: 
 280: // ── PnCounter ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 281: 
 282: /// Per-device positive/negative counter. Each device tracks its own
 283: /// `(positive, negative)` totals; the global value is the sum.
 284: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 285: pub struct PnCounter {
 286:     pos: BTreeMap<[u8; 16], u128>,
 287:     neg: BTreeMap<[u8; 16], u128>,
 288: }
 289: 
 290: impl PnCounter {
 291:     /// Empty counter.
 292:     #[must_use]
 293:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
 294:         Self::default()
 295:     }
 296:     /// Current value (positive sum minus negative sum), as i128 to
 297:     /// allow negative results.
 298:     #[must_use]
 299:     pub fn value(&self) -> i128 {
 300:         let p: u128 = self.pos.values().sum();
 301:         let n: u128 = self.neg.values().sum();
 302:         (p as i128) - (n as i128)
 303:     }
 304:     /// Adjust this device's slot. `delta > 0` accumulates into
 305:     /// the positive bucket; `delta < 0` into the negative bucket.
 306:     /// Replays at the SAME (device, value) are idempotent because
 307:     /// the underlying values are CRDT-style absolute accumulators.
 308:     pub fn adjust(&mut self, device_id: [u8; 16], delta: i64) {
 309:         if delta == 0 {
 310:             return;
 311:         }
 312:         if delta > 0 {
 313:             let entry = self.pos.entry(device_id).or_insert(0);
 314:             *entry = entry.saturating_add(delta as u128);
 315:         } else {
 316:             let entry = self.neg.entry(device_id).or_insert(0);
 317:             *entry = entry.saturating_add((-delta) as u128);
 318:         }
 319:     }
 320:     fn canonical_into(&self, h: &mut Hasher) {
 321:         let n = u32::try_from(self.pos.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 322:         h.update(&n.to_be_bytes());
 323:         for (k, v) in &self.pos {
 324:             h.update(k);
 325:             h.update(&v.to_be_bytes());
 326:         }
 327:         let n = u32::try_from(self.neg.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 328:         h.update(&n.to_be_bytes());
 329:         for (k, v) in &self.neg {
 330:             h.update(k);
 331:             h.update(&v.to_be_bytes());
 332:         }
 333:     }
 334: }
 335: 
 336: // ── LwwMap ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 337: 
 338: /// Map<key, lww-bytes> with tombstone semantics on delete.
 339: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 340: pub struct LwwMap {
 341:     entries: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, LwwRegister>,
 342: }
 343: 
 344: impl LwwMap {
 345:     /// Empty map.
 346:     #[must_use]
 347:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
 348:         Self::default()
 349:     }
 350:     /// Borrow the value for `key` (or `None` if absent / tombstoned).
 351:     #[must_use]
 352:     pub fn get(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]> {
 353:         self.entries.get(key).and_then(|r| r.value())
 354:     }
 355:     /// Number of currently-visible (non-tombstoned) entries.
 356:     #[must_use]
 357:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 358:         self.entries.values().filter(|r| r.value().is_some()).count()
 359:     }
 360:     /// True iff no entries are currently visible.
 361:     #[must_use]
 362:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 363:         self.len() == 0
 364:     }
 365:     /// Put a value at `(key, ts)` from `writer`.
 366:     pub fn put(&mut self, key: Vec<u8>, value: Vec<u8>, ts: u64, writer: &[u8; 16]) {
 367:         let entry = self.entries.entry(key).or_insert_with(LwwRegister::empty);
 368:         entry.set(value, ts, writer);
 369:     }
 370:     /// Delete `key` at `(ts, writer)`. Implemented as a LWW
 371:     /// tombstone (value = None). A delete dominates a same-
 372:     /// `(ts, writer)` put under our tie-break rule, so concurrent
 373:     /// put-vs-delete from the same writer at the same timestamp
 374:     /// converges to delete.
 375:     pub fn delete(&mut self, key: &[u8], ts: u64, writer: &[u8; 16]) {
 376:         let entry = self.entries.entry(key.to_vec()).or_insert_with(LwwRegister::empty);
 377:         if entry.is_dominated_by(ts, writer, None) {
 378:             entry.value = None;
 379:             entry.ts = ts;
 380:             entry.last_writer = *writer;
 381:         }
 382:     }
 383:     fn canonical_into(&self, h: &mut Hasher) {
 384:         let n = u32::try_from(self.entries.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 385:         h.update(&n.to_be_bytes());
 386:         for (k, v) in &self.entries {
 387:             let kl = u32::try_from(k.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 388:             h.update(&kl.to_be_bytes());
 389:             h.update(&k[..kl as usize]);
 390:             v.canonical_into(h);
 391:         }
 392:     }
 393: }
 394: 
 395: // ── MeshState ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 396: 
 397: /// The complete mesh-replicated state — a map of named subtrees.
 398: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 399: pub struct MeshState {
 400:     subtrees: BTreeMap<SubtreeLabel, Subtree>,
 401: }
 402: 
 403: impl MeshState {
 404:     /// Empty state.
 405:     #[must_use]
 406:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
 407:         Self::default()
 408:     }
 409:     /// Borrow a subtree by label.
 410:     #[must_use]
 411:     pub fn subtree(&self, label: &[u8]) -> Option<&Subtree> {
 412:         self.subtrees.get(label)
 413:     }
 414:     /// Number of subtrees currently tracked.
 415:     #[must_use]
 416:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 417:         self.subtrees.len()
 418:     }
 419:     /// True iff no subtrees.
 420:     #[must_use]
 421:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 422:         self.subtrees.is_empty()
 423:     }
 424:     /// Iterate `(label, subtree)` pairs in deterministic order.
 425:     pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&[u8], &Subtree)> {
 426:         self.subtrees.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_slice(), v))
 427:     }
 428:     /// Ensure `label` exists with a subtree of `kind`. Errors if the
 429:     /// label is too long or the subtree exists with a different kind.
 430:     pub fn ensure_subtree(
 431:         &mut self,
 432:         label: SubtreeLabel,
 433:         kind: super::policy::SubtreePolicyKind,
 434:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 435:         if label.len() > MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN {
 436:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::SubtreeLabelTooLong {
 437:                 got: label.len(),
 438:                 max: MAX_SUBTREE_LABEL_LEN,
 439:             });
 440:         }
 441:         let entry = self.subtrees.entry(label);
 442:         match entry {
 443:             std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Vacant(v) => {
 444:                 v.insert(Subtree::empty_of_kind(kind));
 445:                 Ok(())
 446:             }
 447:             std::collections::btree_map::Entry::Occupied(o) => {
 448:                 if super::policy::subtree_kind(o.get()) == kind {
 449:                     Ok(())
 450:                 } else {
 451:                     Err(DeviceMeshError::SubtreeKindCollision)
 452:                 }
 453:             }
 454:         }
 455:     }
 456:     /// Apply a [`Delta`] to the named subtree. Caller is responsible
 457:     /// for verifying the op's signature + subtree policy upstream;
 458:     /// this function is the pure-state-machine half.
 459:     pub fn apply_delta(
 460:         &mut self,
 461:         label: &[u8],
 462:         delta: &Delta,
 463:         emitter_device_id: &[u8; 16],
 464:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 465:         let st = self
 466:             .subtrees
 467:             .get_mut(label)
 468:             .ok_or(DeviceMeshError::SubtreeMissing)?;
 469:         st.apply(delta, emitter_device_id)
 470:     }
 471:     /// Compute the canonical state root. BLAKE3 over the sorted
 472:     /// `(label, subtree_root)` list.
 473:     #[must_use]
 474:     pub fn root(&self) -> StateRoot {
 475:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 476:         h.update(b"OL-mesh-state-root-v1");
 477:         let n = u32::try_from(self.subtrees.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 478:         h.update(&n.to_be_bytes());
 479:         for (label, sub) in &self.subtrees {
 480:             let ll = u32::try_from(label.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 481:             h.update(&ll.to_be_bytes());
 482:             h.update(&label[..ll as usize]);
 483:             h.update(&sub.root());
 484:         }
 485:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 486:     }
 487: }

   1: //! Pairwise sync session + anti-entropy.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each replica keeps a [`SyncState`]: the highest sequence number
   4: //! it has observed per peer device, plus a chronological op log.
   5: //! Two replicas converge by:
   6: //!
   7: //! 1. Exchanging [`SyncSummary`] records (a compact `device_id ->
   8: //!    highest_seq` map).
   9: //! 2. Each side replies with the ops the peer is missing, up to
  10: //!    [`MAX_OPS_PER_SYNC`] per round.
  11: //! 3. Each side ingests the peer's ops via [`SyncState::ingest`],
  12: //!    which drops replays (seq ≤ `last_seen`) and signature failures.
  13: //!
  14: //! The protocol is monotonic: a peer that has fallen behind by N ops
  15: //! catches up in `ceil(N / MAX_OPS_PER_SYNC)` rounds. There is no
  16: //! "rejected-because-out-of-order" path; CRDTs converge under any
  17: //! delivery order.
  18: 
  19: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
  20: 
  21: use ol_pqsig::HybridVerifyingKey;
  22: 
  23: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  24: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  25: 
  26: use super::ops::AuthenticatedOp;
  27: use super::state::MeshState;
  28: 
  29: /// Maximum number of ops a replica returns in one sync reply.
  30: pub const MAX_OPS_PER_SYNC: usize = 1024;
  31: 
  32: /// Sync state for one replica.
  33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  34: pub struct SyncState {
  35:     /// Sparse set of `(device_id, seq)` pairs already observed.
  36:     /// Used for ingest-time dedup; CRDT idempotence handles the
  37:     /// actual state-merge correctness.
  38:     seen: BTreeSet<([u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u64)>,
  39:     /// Highest seq observed per device. Used by [`SyncSummary`]
  40:     /// + by [`Self::record_local_emit`] for monotonicity.
  41:     last_seen_seq: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u64>,
  42:     /// Chronological log of ops we hold, in ingest order. Used to
  43:     /// reply to peer summaries.
  44:     op_log: Vec<AuthenticatedOp>,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl SyncState {
  48:     /// Fresh sync state with no peers observed.
  49:     #[must_use]
  50:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
  51:         Self::default()
  52:     }
  53: 
  54:     /// Borrow the op log in chronological-emit order.
  55:     #[must_use] 
  56:     pub fn op_log(&self) -> &[AuthenticatedOp] {
  57:         &self.op_log
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     /// Highest seq seen from `device_id` (0 if never seen).
  61:     #[must_use]
  62:     pub fn last_seen(&self, device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]) -> u64 {
  63:         self.last_seen_seq.get(device_id).copied().unwrap_or(0)
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     /// Summary of what we've seen — what we send to a peer when
  67:     /// initiating sync.
  68:     #[must_use]
  69:     pub fn summary(&self) -> SyncSummary {
  70:         SyncSummary {
  71:             last_seen_seq: self.last_seen_seq.clone(),
  72:         }
  73:     }
  74: 
  75:     /// Ingest an op from a peer. Returns `Ok(true)` if the op is
  76:     /// newly applied; `Ok(false)` if it was a replay (already seen).
  77:     /// Returns the underlying [`DeviceMeshError`] if signature verify
  78:     /// fails, the subkey VK can't be resolved, the subtree is
  79:     /// missing, or the delta kind mismatches the subtree.
  80:     ///
  81:     /// `vk_lookup` resolves a `(device_id, day_index)` pair to the
  82:     /// emitter's hybrid verifying key. Callers typically wrap their
  83:     /// Layer-1 `SubkeyAttestation` cache here.
  84:     pub fn ingest<F>(
  85:         &mut self,
  86:         op: AuthenticatedOp,
  87:         state: &mut MeshState,
  88:         vk_lookup: F,
  89:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<bool>
  90:     where
  91:         F: Fn(&[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u64) -> DeviceMeshResult<HybridVerifyingKey>,
  92:     {
  93:         // Replay check via the seen-set, NOT a max-seen comparator.
  94:         // CRDTs are idempotent under replay, so applying twice is
  95:         // safe; the seen-set just skips redundant verify + apply
  96:         // work. Crucially this allows out-of-order delivery for the
  97:         // same device (seq 3 arriving after seq 5 from the same
  98:         // emitter), which the gossip / anti-entropy protocol relies
  99:         // on for partial-network healing.
 100:         if self.seen.contains(&(op.device_id, op.seq)) {
 101:             return Ok(false);
 102:         }
 103:         // Resolve VK + verify signature.
 104:         let vk = vk_lookup(&op.device_id, op.day_index)?;
 105:         op.verify(&vk)?;
 106:         // Apply to state. The subtree must already exist (created
 107:         // by `MeshState::ensure_subtree` at higher-layer setup).
 108:         state.apply_delta(&op.subtree, &op.delta, &op.device_id)?;
 109:         // Record sequence + append to log.
 110:         self.seen.insert((op.device_id, op.seq));
 111:         let entry = self.last_seen_seq.entry(op.device_id).or_insert(0);
 112:         if op.seq > *entry {
 113:             *entry = op.seq;
 114:         }
 115:         self.op_log.push(op);
 116:         Ok(true)
 117:     }
 118: 
 119:     /// Return up to [`MAX_OPS_PER_SYNC`] ops the peer is missing.
 120:     /// "Missing" = ops in our log whose `seq > peer.last_seen[device_id]`.
 121:     #[must_use]
 122:     pub fn diff_for_peer(&self, peer: &SyncSummary) -> Vec<AuthenticatedOp> {
 123:         let mut out = Vec::new();
 124:         for op in &self.op_log {
 125:             let peer_seen = peer.last_seen_seq.get(&op.device_id).copied().unwrap_or(0);
 126:             if op.seq > peer_seen {
 127:                 out.push(op.clone());
 128:                 if out.len() >= MAX_OPS_PER_SYNC {
 129:                     break;
 130:                 }
 131:             }
 132:         }
 133:         out
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     /// Emit (sign + record + append to log) the next op for this
 137:     /// device. Caller supplies the next `seq`; bookkeeping enforces
 138:     /// strict monotonicity per device.
 139:     pub fn record_local_emit(
 140:         &mut self,
 141:         op: AuthenticatedOp,
 142:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 143:         let prior = self.last_seen(&op.device_id);
 144:         if op.seq <= prior {
 145:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::OpSeqNotMonotonic {
 146:                 device_id: op.device_id,
 147:                 got: op.seq,
 148:                 last_seen: prior,
 149:             });
 150:         }
 151:         self.seen.insert((op.device_id, op.seq));
 152:         self.last_seen_seq.insert(op.device_id, op.seq);
 153:         self.op_log.push(op);
 154:         Ok(())
 155:     }
 156: }
 157: 
 158: /// Compact summary of one replica's progress — exchanged at sync
 159: /// start so each side can compute the diff.
 160: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
 161: pub struct SyncSummary {
 162:     /// Highest sequence number seen from each peer device id.
 163:     pub last_seen_seq: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u64>,
 164: }
 165: 
 166: #[cfg(test)]
 167: mod tests {
 168:     use super::*;
 169:     use crate::master::MasterIdentity;
 170:     use crate::mesh_state::ops::Delta;
 171:     use crate::mesh_state::policy::SubtreePolicyKind;
 172:     use crate::subkey::{fresh_device_id, mint_subkey, SubkeyAttestation};
 173:     use crate::DeviceClass;
 174:     use ol_pqsig::HYBRID_VK_LEN;
 175:     use rand::rngs::OsRng;
 176: 
 177:     fn vk_from_attestation(att: &SubkeyAttestation) -> HybridVerifyingKey {
 178:         assert_eq!(att.subkey_vk_bytes.len(), HYBRID_VK_LEN);
 179:         HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&att.subkey_vk_bytes).unwrap()
 180:     }
 181: 
 182:     #[test]
 183:     fn ingest_round_trips_then_replays_no_op() {
 184:         let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
 185:         let id = fresh_device_id(&mut OsRng);
 186:         let (sk, att) =
 187:             mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 0, 365).unwrap();
 188:         let mut state = MeshState::empty();
 189:         state
 190:             .ensure_subtree(b"x".to_vec(), SubtreePolicyKind::LwwRegister)
 191:             .unwrap();
 192:         let mut sync = SyncState::empty();
 193: 
 194:         let op = AuthenticatedOp::sign(
 195:             &sk,
 196:             b"x".to_vec(),
 197:             Delta::LwwSet { value: b"v".to_vec(), ts: 1 },
 198:             1,
 199:             1_700_000_000,
 200:         )
 201:         .unwrap();
 202: 
 203:         let vk = vk_from_attestation(&att);
 204:         let applied = sync
 205:             .ingest(op.clone(), &mut state, |_, _| Ok(vk.clone()))
 206:             .unwrap();
 207:         assert!(applied);
 208:         // Replay is a no-op.
 209:         let applied = sync.ingest(op, &mut state, |_, _| Ok(vk.clone())).unwrap();
 210:         assert!(!applied);

 267:     #[test]
 268:     fn two_replicas_converge() {
 269:         // Two devices, each emits an op; after a full pair-sync,
 270:         // both have identical state.
 271:         let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
 272:         let id_a = fresh_device_id(&mut OsRng);
 273:         let id_b = fresh_device_id(&mut OsRng);
 274:         let (sk_a, att_a) =
 275:             mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id_a, 0, 365).unwrap();
 276:         let (sk_b, att_b) =
 277:             mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Laptop, id_b, 0, 365).unwrap();
 278:         let vk_a = vk_from_attestation(&att_a);
 279:         let vk_b = vk_from_attestation(&att_b);
 280:         let lookup = |id: &[u8; 16], _day: u64| -> DeviceMeshResult<HybridVerifyingKey> {
 281:             if id == &id_a {
 282:                 Ok(vk_a.clone())
 283:             } else if id == &id_b {
 284:                 Ok(vk_b.clone())
 285:             } else {
 286:                 Err(DeviceMeshError::AttestationMissing {
 287:                     device_id: *id,
 288:                     day_index: 0,
 289:                 })
 290:             }
 291:         };
 292: 
 293:         let mut sa = SyncState::empty();
 294:         let mut sb = SyncState::empty();
 295:         let mut state_a = MeshState::empty();
 296:         let mut state_b = MeshState::empty();
 297:         state_a
 298:             .ensure_subtree(b"x".to_vec(), SubtreePolicyKind::LwwMap)
 299:             .unwrap();
 300:         state_b
 301:             .ensure_subtree(b"x".to_vec(), SubtreePolicyKind::LwwMap)
 302:             .unwrap();
 303: 
 304:         let op_a = AuthenticatedOp::sign(
 305:             &sk_a,
 306:             b"x".to_vec(),
 307:             Delta::MapPut { key: b"k1".to_vec(), value: b"a".to_vec(), ts: 1 },
 308:             1,
 309:             1,
 310:         )
 311:         .unwrap();
 312:         sa.ingest(op_a, &mut state_a, &lookup).unwrap();
 313:         let op_b = AuthenticatedOp::sign(
 314:             &sk_b,
 315:             b"x".to_vec(),
 316:             Delta::MapPut { key: b"k2".to_vec(), value: b"b".to_vec(), ts: 2 },
 317:             1,
 318:             2,
 319:         )
 320:         .unwrap();
 321:         sb.ingest(op_b, &mut state_b, &lookup).unwrap();
 322: 
 323:         // Each side computes its diff for the other; ingests.
 324:         let diff_for_b = sa.diff_for_peer(&sb.summary());
 325:         for op in diff_for_b {
 326:             sb.ingest(op, &mut state_b, &lookup).unwrap();
 327:         }
 328:         let diff_for_a = sb.diff_for_peer(&sa.summary());
 329:         for op in diff_for_a {
 330:             sa.ingest(op, &mut state_a, &lookup).unwrap();
 331:         }
 332:         assert_eq!(state_a.root(), state_b.root());
 333:     }

   1: //! Per-device approval records.
   2: //!
   3: //! An [`QuorumApproval`] is "I, device X, approve proposal P at
   4: //! wall-clock T." The approver's subkey signs the canonical bytes;
   5: //! the `proposal_id` binds the approval to one specific proposal so
   6: //! it can't be replayed against a different operation.
   7: 
   8: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
   9: 
  10: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  11: use crate::subkey::{DeviceSubkey, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  12: 
  13: use super::proposal::{ProposalId, QuorumProposal};
  14: 
  15: /// Domain-separation tag for approval-signing.
  16: pub const APPROVAL_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-device-mesh-approval-v1";
  17: 
  18: /// One sibling-device approval.
  19: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  20: pub struct QuorumApproval {
  21:     /// Which proposal is being approved (BLAKE3 over canonical bytes).
  22:     pub proposal_id: ProposalId,
  23:     /// Approving device's id.
  24:     pub approver_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  25:     /// Approver's subkey day-index at approval time.
  26:     pub approver_day_index: u64,
  27:     /// Wall-clock seconds at approval time.
  28:     pub approved_unix: u64,
  29:     /// Approver's subkey signature over the canonical bytes.
  30:     pub approver_sig: Vec<u8>,
  31: }
  32: 
  33: impl QuorumApproval {
  34:     /// Canonical bytes the approver signs over.
  35:     #[must_use] 
  36:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  37:         proposal_id: &ProposalId,
  38:         approver_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  39:         approver_day_index: u64,
  40:         approved_unix: u64,
  41:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  42:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  43:             APPROVAL_DOMAIN.len() + 32 + DEVICE_ID_LEN + 8 + 8,
  44:         );
  45:         out.extend_from_slice(APPROVAL_DOMAIN);
  46:         out.extend_from_slice(proposal_id);
  47:         out.extend_from_slice(approver_device_id);
  48:         out.extend_from_slice(&approver_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  49:         out.extend_from_slice(&approved_unix.to_be_bytes());
  50:         out
  51:     }
  52: 
  53:     /// Verify the approver's signature against the supplied subkey
  54:     /// VK. Caller proves the VK is the approver's via the master-
  55:     /// signed [`crate::SubkeyAttestation`] cache.
  56:     pub fn verify(&self, approver_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  57:         if self.approver_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
  58:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
  59:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
  60:                 got: self.approver_sig.len(),
  61:             });
  62:         }
  63:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
  64:             &self.proposal_id,
  65:             &self.approver_device_id,
  66:             self.approver_day_index,
  67:             self.approved_unix,
  68:         );
  69:         approver_vk
  70:             .verify(&transcript, &self.approver_sig)
  71:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::ApprovalVerifyFail)
  72:     }
  73: }
  74: 
  75: /// Sign an approval on `proposal` using `approver`'s subkey.
  76: pub fn sign_approval(
  77:     approver: &DeviceSubkey,
  78:     proposal: &QuorumProposal,
  79:     approved_unix: u64,
  80: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<QuorumApproval> {
  81:     if approved_unix > proposal.deadline_unix {
  82:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::ApprovalPastDeadline {
  83:             approved_unix,
  84:             deadline_unix: proposal.deadline_unix,
  85:         });
  86:     }
  87:     let proposal_id = proposal.proposal_id();
  88:     let transcript = QuorumApproval::canonical_transcript(
  89:         &proposal_id,
  90:         approver.device_id(),
  91:         approver.day_index(),
  92:         approved_unix,
  93:     );
  94:     let sig = approver.sign(&transcript)?;
  95:     Ok(QuorumApproval {
  96:         proposal_id,
  97:         approver_device_id: *approver.device_id(),
  98:         approver_day_index: approver.day_index(),
  99:         approved_unix,
 100:         approver_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 101:     })
 102: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_device_mesh/src/quorum/certificate.rs", "bytes": 13429, "sha256": "ba9f722802141c1f44cd7d934988a42b54be2ec74863b312132d9fa85be56577", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-14T01:34:28.767837+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Quorum certificate: end-to-end verifiable record of K-of-N approval.
   2: //!
   3: //! The certificate carries everything a verifier needs to confirm
   4: //! "the master, whose VK is X, has authorized this operation through
   5: //! a K-of-N quorum of its device mesh."
   6: 
   7: use std::collections::HashSet;
   8: 
   9: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_VK_LEN};
  10: 
  11: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  12: use crate::subkey::{SubkeyAttestation, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  13: 
  14: use super::approval::QuorumApproval;
  15: use super::policy::QuorumPolicy;
  16: use super::proposal::QuorumProposal;
  17: 
  18: /// Maximum allowed approvals in one certificate. Bounded to keep
  19: /// verification cost predictable and reject amplification.
  20: pub const MAX_APPROVALS: usize = 64;
  21: 
  22: /// Maximum size of a policy's eligible-devices roster.
  23: pub const MAX_ELIGIBLE_DEVICES: usize = 64;
  24: 
  25: /// A fully-formed quorum certificate.
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  27: pub struct QuorumCertificate {
  28:     /// The proposal being authorised.
  29:     pub proposal: QuorumProposal,
  30:     /// At least `proposal.policy.k` approvals from distinct
  31:     /// eligible devices.
  32:     pub approvals: Vec<QuorumApproval>,
  33:     /// The policy that governs this proposal (master-signed).
  34:     pub policy: QuorumPolicy,
  35:     /// `SubkeyAttestation` cache for every signer (issuer + approvers).
  36:     /// Verifier looks up each signer's VK here instead of going off-
  37:     /// network. Order is irrelevant; lookup is by device id.
  38:     pub subkey_attestations: Vec<SubkeyAttestation>,
  39: }
  40: 
  41: impl QuorumCertificate {
  42:     /// End-to-end verify this certificate under `master_vk`.
  43:     ///
  44:     /// `now_unix` is the verifier's current wall-clock. The proposal
  45:     /// must not yet be past its `deadline_unix`.
  46:     pub fn verify(
  47:         &self,
  48:         master_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey,
  49:         now_unix: u64,
  50:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  51:         // (0) Shape: bounded approvals + bounded roster.
  52:         if self.approvals.len() > MAX_APPROVALS {
  53:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::CertTooManyApprovals {
  54:                 got: self.approvals.len(),
  55:                 max: MAX_APPROVALS,
  56:             });
  57:         }
  58:         if self.policy.eligible_devices.len() > MAX_ELIGIBLE_DEVICES {
  59:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PolicyRosterTooLarge {
  60:                 got: self.policy.eligible_devices.len(),
  61:                 max: MAX_ELIGIBLE_DEVICES,
  62:             });
  63:         }
  64: 
  65:         // (1) Policy signed by master.
  66:         self.policy.verify(master_vk)?;
  67: 
  68:         // (2) Every subkey attestation signed by master.
  69:         for att in &self.subkey_attestations {
  70:             att.verify(master_vk)?;
  71:         }
  72: 
  73:         // (3) Proposal binds to this policy.
  74:         if self.proposal.policy_id != self.policy.policy_id {
  75:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::CertProposalPolicyMismatch);
  76:         }
  77: 
  78:         // (4) Proposal hasn't expired vs verifier wall clock.
  79:         if now_unix > self.proposal.deadline_unix {
  80:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::CertProposalExpired {
  81:                 deadline_unix: self.proposal.deadline_unix,
  82:                 now_unix,
  83:             });
  84:         }
  85: 
  86:         // (5) Issuer is eligible.
  87:         if !self.policy.is_eligible(&self.proposal.issuer_device_id) {
  88:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::IssuerNotEligible {
  89:                 device_id: self.proposal.issuer_device_id,
  90:             });
  91:         }
  92: 
  93:         // (6) Issuer signature verifies under its attested subkey VK.
  94:         let issuer_vk = self.subkey_vk_for(
  95:             &self.proposal.issuer_device_id,
  96:             self.proposal.issuer_day_index,
  97:         )?;
  98:         self.proposal.verify_issuer(&issuer_vk)?;
  99: 
 100:         // (7) Each approval is signed by its approver's attested VK,
 101:         // commits to THIS proposal's id, is from an eligible device,
 102:         // is within the deadline, and the approver-set is distinct.
 103:         let proposal_id = self.proposal.proposal_id();
 104:         let mut seen: HashSet<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> = HashSet::new();
 105:         for a in &self.approvals {
 106:             if a.proposal_id != proposal_id {
 107:                 return Err(DeviceMeshError::ApprovalForOtherProposal);
 108:             }
 109:             if a.approved_unix > self.proposal.deadline_unix {
 110:                 return Err(DeviceMeshError::ApprovalPastDeadline {
 111:                     approved_unix: a.approved_unix,
 112:                     deadline_unix: self.proposal.deadline_unix,
 113:                 });
 114:             }
 115:             if !self.policy.is_eligible(&a.approver_device_id) {
 116:                 return Err(DeviceMeshError::ApproverNotEligible {
 117:                     device_id: a.approver_device_id,
 118:                 });
 119:             }
 120:             if !seen.insert(a.approver_device_id) {
 121:                 return Err(DeviceMeshError::DuplicateApprover {
 122:                     device_id: a.approver_device_id,
 123:                 });
 124:             }
 125:             let approver_vk =
 126:                 self.subkey_vk_for(&a.approver_device_id, a.approver_day_index)?;
 127:             a.verify(&approver_vk)?;
 128:         }
 129: 
 130:         // (8) Distinct-approver count meets the threshold.
 131:         if seen.len() < (self.policy.k as usize) {
 132:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::CertBelowThreshold {
 133:                 got: seen.len(),
 134:                 needed: self.policy.k,
 135:             });
 136:         }
 137: 
 138:         Ok(())
 139:     }
 140: 
 141:     /// Look up a signer's hybrid verifying key from the attestation
 142:     /// cache. The attestation must already verify under the master
 143:     /// (caller is responsible — `verify` checks this in step (2)
 144:     /// before any lookup in step (6)+).
 145:     fn subkey_vk_for(
 146:         &self,
 147:         device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 148:         day_index: u64,
 149:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<HybridVerifyingKey> {
 150:         for att in &self.subkey_attestations {
 151:             if &att.device_id == device_id && att.covers_day(day_index) {
 152:                 if att.subkey_vk_bytes.len() != HYBRID_VK_LEN {
 153:                     return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 154:                         expected: HYBRID_VK_LEN,
 155:                         got: att.subkey_vk_bytes.len(),
 156:                     });
 157:                 }
 158:                 return HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&att.subkey_vk_bytes)
 159:                     .map_err(DeviceMeshError::from);
 160:             }
 161:         }
 162:         Err(DeviceMeshError::AttestationMissing {
 163:             device_id: *device_id,
 164:             day_index,
 165:         })
 166:     }
 167: }
 168:

 170: mod tests {

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 2 — threshold device quorum.
   2: //!
   3: //! High-stakes operations require K-of-N device approval. Examples
   4: //! the upper layers will tag through Layer 2:
   5: //!
   6: //! - granting a new capability to a friend or app,
   7: //! - sending to a first-time contact,
   8: //! - transferring more than a configurable byte budget,
   9: //! - revoking a sibling device,
  10: //! - rotating the master identity,
  11: //! - factor-resetting the mesh.
  12: //!
  13: //! ## Composition
  14: //!
  15: //! ```text
  16: //! QuorumPolicy        master signs (label, k, eligible_device_ids)
  17: //!     │
  18: //!     │   pinned by every device in the mesh
  19: //!     ▼
  20: //! QuorumProposal      issuer device proposes an operation, signs it
  21: //!     │
  22: //!     │   broadcast to siblings
  23: //!     ▼
  24: //! QuorumApproval(s)   each eligible sibling co-signs the proposal_id
  25: //!     │
  26: //!     │   collected by the issuer (or any device)
  27: //!     ▼
  28: //! QuorumCertificate   proposal + ≥K approvals + subkey attestations
  29: //!     │
  30: //!     │   produced once, persisted, verified by anyone with the
  31: //!     │   master verifying key.
  32: //!     ▼
  33: //!  authorised operation executes
  34: //! ```
  35: //!
  36: //! ## Verification rule
  37: //!
  38: //! [`QuorumCertificate::verify`] checks ALL of the following:
  39: //!
  40: //! 1. The [`QuorumPolicy`] is signed by the master.
  41: //! 2. Every subkey attestation in the cert is signed by the master.
  42: //! 3. The [`QuorumProposal`] is signed by the issuer's subkey AND
  43: //!    the issuer is in the policy's eligible list.
  44: //! 4. Each [`QuorumApproval`] is signed by its claimed approver's
  45: //!    subkey AND the approver is in the policy's eligible list.
  46: //! 5. The certificate carries at least `policy.k` DISTINCT approvers
  47: //!    (the policy author counts as one approval if they signed both
  48: //!    the proposal and an approval — Layer 2 doesn't fold the
  49: //!    proposal signature into the K count; callers must include an
  50: //!    explicit approval if they want the issuer to count).
  51: //! 6. No approval's `approved_unix` is past the proposal's
  52: //!    `deadline_unix`.
  53: //! 7. The proposal's `deadline_unix` itself is not yet past
  54: //!    `now_unix` (verifier checks this; we don't bake the verifier's
  55: //!    clock into the certificate).
  56: //!
  57: //! ## Anti-replay
  58: //!
  59: //! Every proposal carries a 16-byte nonce + the issuer's device id +
  60: //! a wall-clock timestamp. The `proposal_id` is BLAKE3 over the
  61: //! canonical proposal bytes, so two proposals with the same nonce
  62: //! but different issuers / deadlines / operation digests yield
  63: //! distinct ids. Approvals bind to the proposal id, never to the
  64: //! raw operation. Higher layers track seen `proposal_id`s to drop
  65: //! duplicates.
  66: //!
  67: //! ## What this layer doesn't do
  68: //!
  69: //! - Negative votes (a "refuse" record that kills the proposal).
  70: //!   Skipped intentionally; Layer 2 is the positive-quorum path.
  71: //!   Higher layers can build refusal-by-time-out from the deadline.
  72: //! - BLS / FROST threshold signatures. Each device signs
  73: //!   independently and the verifier checks K independent signatures.
  74: //!   That's how Bitcoin multi-sig works; it's simpler, audits
  75: //!   cleanly, and avoids dragging in a new curve.
  76: //! - Per-policy approval rate limits. Higher layers add those.
  77: //!
  78: //! ## Example
  79: //!
  80: //! ```no_run
  81: //! use ol_device_mesh::quorum::{
  82: //!     mint_policy, propose_operation, sign_approval, QuorumCertificate,
  83: //! };
  84: //! use ol_device_mesh::{
  85: //!     mint_subkey, DeviceClass, MasterIdentity,
  86: //! };
  87: //! use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  88: //!
  89: //! let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  90: //!
  91: //! // Three devices on the mesh.
  92: //! let phone_id = [0xAA; 16];
  93: //! let laptop_id = [0xBB; 16];
  94: //! let desktop_id = [0xCC; 16];
  95: //! let (phone_sk, phone_att) =
  96: //!     mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, phone_id, 0, 365).unwrap();
  97: //! let (laptop_sk, laptop_att) =
  98: //!     mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Laptop, laptop_id, 0, 365).unwrap();
  99: //! let (desktop_sk, desktop_att) =
 100: //!     mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Desktop, desktop_id, 0, 365).unwrap();
 101: //!
 102: //! // The master signs a policy: "high-stakes ops require 2 of {phone,
 103: //! // laptop, desktop}."
 104: //! let policy = mint_policy(
 105: //!     &master,
 106: //!     [0x01; 16],
 107: //!     b"high-stakes",
 108: //!     2,
 109: //!     vec![phone_id, laptop_id, desktop_id],
 110: //! ).unwrap();
 111: //!
 112: //! // Phone proposes an operation.
 113: //! let op_digest = [0xEE; 32];
 114: //! let now = 1_700_000_000u64;
 115: //! let proposal = propose_operation(
 116: //!     &phone_sk,
 117: //!     &policy,
 118: //!     op_digest,
 119: //!     [0xDA; 16],
 120: //!     now,
 121: //!     now + 3600,
 122: //! ).unwrap();
 123: //!
 124: //! // Laptop and desktop sign approvals.
 125: //! let a1 = sign_approval(&laptop_sk, &proposal, now + 60).unwrap();
 126: //! let a2 = sign_approval(&desktop_sk, &proposal, now + 120).unwrap();
 127: //!
 128: //! // Build the certificate (anyone can do this).
 129: //! let cert = QuorumCertificate {
 130: //!     proposal,
 131: //!     approvals: vec![a1, a2],
 132: //!     policy: policy.clone(),
 133: //!     subkey_attestations: vec![phone_att, laptop_att, desktop_att],
 134: //! };
 135: //!
 136: //! // Anyone with the master VK can verify the whole thing.
 137: //! cert.verify(&master.verifying_key(), now + 200).unwrap();
 138: //! ```
