   1: //! Master-signed quorum policy.
   2: //!
   3: //! A policy describes WHICH devices count for a class of operations
   4: //! and HOW MANY of them must approve. Master signs it; every device
   5: //! pins the policy bytes.
   6: 
   7: use blake3::Hasher;
   8: use ol_pqsig::{HybridSigningKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
   9: 
  10: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  11: use crate::master::MasterIdentity;
  12: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  13: 
  14: /// Length of the canonical policy identifier (random 16 bytes —
  15: /// chosen by master at mint, treated as opaque by everyone else).
  16: pub const POLICY_ID_LEN: usize = 16;
  17: 
  18: /// Length of a [`QuorumPolicyId`].
  19: pub type QuorumPolicyId = [u8; POLICY_ID_LEN];
  20: 
  21: /// Maximum allowed length of a policy's human-readable label.
  22: pub const POLICY_LABEL_MAX: usize = 64;
  23: 
  24: /// Domain-separation tag for the policy-signing transcript.
  25: pub const POLICY_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-device-mesh-policy-v1";
  26: 
  27: /// A master-signed quorum policy.
  28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  29: pub struct QuorumPolicy {
  30:     /// Stable identifier for this policy. Chosen by the master at
  31:     /// mint; higher layers reference it by id.
  32:     pub policy_id: QuorumPolicyId,
  33:     /// Human-readable label (e.g. `b"high-stakes-cap-grant"`).
  34:     /// Length-bounded; signed into the transcript.
  35:     pub label: Vec<u8>,
  36:     /// Threshold: how many approvals are required. MUST be ≥ 1 and
  37:     /// ≤ `eligible_devices.len()`.
  38:     pub k: u8,
  39:     /// Devices that count for approving this policy's operations.
  40:     /// Stable per master signature; revoking a device requires
  41:     /// re-signing a new policy.
  42:     pub eligible_devices: Vec<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
  43:     /// Master's hybrid signature over the canonical transcript.
  44:     pub master_sig: Vec<u8>,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl QuorumPolicy {
  48:     /// Canonical bytes the master signs over.
  49:     #[must_use] 
  50:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  51:         policy_id: &QuorumPolicyId,
  52:         label: &[u8],
  53:         k: u8,
  54:         eligible_devices: &[[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]],
  55:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  56:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  57:             POLICY_DOMAIN.len()
  58:                 + POLICY_ID_LEN
  59:                 + 2
  60:                 + label.len()
  61:                 + 1
  62:                 + 2
  63:                 + eligible_devices.len() * DEVICE_ID_LEN,
  64:         );
  65:         out.extend_from_slice(POLICY_DOMAIN);
  66:         out.extend_from_slice(policy_id);
  67:         let label_len = u16::try_from(label.len()).unwrap_or(u16::MAX);
  68:         out.extend_from_slice(&label_len.to_be_bytes());
  69:         out.extend_from_slice(label);
  70:         out.push(k);
  71:         let n = u16::try_from(eligible_devices.len()).unwrap_or(u16::MAX);
  72:         out.extend_from_slice(&n.to_be_bytes());
  73:         for id in eligible_devices {
  74:             out.extend_from_slice(id);
  75:         }
  76:         out
  77:     }
  78: 
  79:     /// Verify the master signature on this policy.
  80:     pub fn verify(&self, master_vk: &ol_pqsig::HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  81:         self.shape_check()?;
  82:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
  83:             &self.policy_id,
  84:             &self.label,
  85:             self.k,
  86:             &self.eligible_devices,
  87:         );
  88:         master_vk
  89:             .verify(&transcript, &self.master_sig)
  90:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::PolicyVerifyFail)
  91:     }
  92: 
  93:     /// Return whether `device_id` is in the eligible list.
  94:     #[must_use]
  95:     pub fn is_eligible(&self, device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]) -> bool {
  96:         self.eligible_devices.iter().any(|d| d == device_id)
  97:     }
  98: 
  99:     /// BLAKE3 commitment of the canonical transcript. Higher layers
 100:     /// use this as the policy's content-addressed handle.
 101:     #[must_use]
 102:     pub fn handle(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
 103:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 104:             &self.policy_id,
 105:             &self.label,
 106:             self.k,
 107:             &self.eligible_devices,
 108:         );
 109:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 110:         h.update(b"OL-device-mesh-policy-handle-v1");
 111:         h.update(&transcript);
 112:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     fn shape_check(&self) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 116:         if self.label.len() > POLICY_LABEL_MAX {
 117:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PolicyLabelTooLong {
 118:                 got: self.label.len(),
 119:                 max: POLICY_LABEL_MAX,
 120:             });
 121:         }
 122:         if self.eligible_devices.is_empty() {
 123:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PolicyEmptyRoster);
 124:         }
 125:         if self.eligible_devices.len() > super::certificate::MAX_ELIGIBLE_DEVICES {
 126:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PolicyRosterTooLarge {
 127:                 got: self.eligible_devices.len(),
 128:                 max: super::certificate::MAX_ELIGIBLE_DEVICES,
 129:             });
 130:         }
 131:         if self.k == 0 || (self.k as usize) > self.eligible_devices.len() {
 132:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PolicyBadThreshold {
 133:                 k: self.k,
 134:                 n: self.eligible_devices.len(),
 135:             });
 136:         }
 137:         // Reject duplicate device IDs in the roster — otherwise a
 138:         // duplicate could be used to inflate the apparent K.
 139:         let mut sorted = self.eligible_devices.clone();
 140:         sorted.sort_unstable();
 141:         let dedup_len = {
 142:             let mut s = sorted.clone();
 143:             s.dedup();
 144:             s.len()
 145:         };
 146:         if dedup_len != sorted.len() {
 147:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::PolicyDuplicateRoster);
 148:         }
 149:         if self.master_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 150:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 151:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
 152:                 got: self.master_sig.len(),
 153:             });
 154:         }
 155:         Ok(())
 156:     }
 157: }
 158: 
 159: /// Mint a fresh quorum policy: master signs the canonical transcript
 160: /// and returns the populated struct.
 161: pub fn mint_policy(
 162:     master: &MasterIdentity,
 163:     policy_id: QuorumPolicyId,
 164:     label: &[u8],
 165:     k: u8,
 166:     eligible_devices: Vec<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
 167: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<QuorumPolicy> {
 168:     let policy_unsigned = QuorumPolicy {
 169:         policy_id,
 170:         label: label.to_vec(),
 171:         k,
 172:         eligible_devices,
 173:         master_sig: vec![0u8; HYBRID_SIG_LEN], // placeholder for shape_check
 174:     };
 175:     policy_unsigned.shape_check()?;
 176:     let transcript = QuorumPolicy::canonical_transcript(
 177:         &policy_unsigned.policy_id,
 178:         &policy_unsigned.label,
 179:         policy_unsigned.k,
 180:         &policy_unsigned.eligible_devices,
 181:     );
 182:     let master_signing: HybridSigningKey = master.signing_key();
 183:     let sig = master_signing.sign(&transcript)?;
 184:     Ok(QuorumPolicy {
 185:         policy_id: policy_unsigned.policy_id,
 186:         label: policy_unsigned.label,
 187:         k: policy_unsigned.k,
 188:         eligible_devices: policy_unsigned.eligible_devices,
 189:         master_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 190:     })
 191: }

 212:     #[test]

   1: //! Quorum proposals.
   2: //!
   3: //! A proposal is "I, device X, propose that operation O be approved
   4: //! under policy P by the deadline D." The issuer's subkey signs the
   5: //! canonical bytes; the BLAKE3 digest of the canonical bytes is the
   6: //! [`ProposalId`] that approvals bind to.
   7: 
   8: use blake3::Hasher;
   9: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
  10: 
  11: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  12: use crate::subkey::{DeviceSubkey, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  13: 
  14: use super::policy::{QuorumPolicy, QuorumPolicyId, POLICY_ID_LEN};
  15: 
  16: /// Length of the per-proposal nonce.
  17: pub const PROPOSAL_NONCE_LEN: usize = 16;
  18: 
  19: /// Per-proposal nonce; uniformly random per proposal.
  20: pub type ProposalNonce = [u8; PROPOSAL_NONCE_LEN];
  21: 
  22: /// Length of the BLAKE3 digest committing to the operation payload.
  23: pub const OPERATION_DIGEST_LEN: usize = 32;
  24: 
  25: /// Domain-separation tag for proposal-signing.
  26: pub const PROPOSAL_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-device-mesh-proposal-v1";
  27: 
  28: /// BLAKE3 digest of the canonical proposal transcript; what
  29: /// approvals bind to.
  30: pub type ProposalId = [u8; 32];
  31: 
  32: /// One issued proposal.
  33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  34: pub struct QuorumProposal {
  35:     /// Which policy governs this proposal.
  36:     pub policy_id: QuorumPolicyId,
  37:     /// 32-byte digest of the actual operation payload. Layer 2
  38:     /// doesn't interpret these bytes; higher layers commit to the
  39:     /// operation via BLAKE3.
  40:     pub operation_digest: [u8; OPERATION_DIGEST_LEN],
  41:     /// Per-proposal nonce.
  42:     pub nonce: ProposalNonce,
  43:     /// Wall-clock seconds at issue time.
  44:     pub issued_unix: u64,
  45:     /// Wall-clock seconds the proposal expires.
  46:     pub deadline_unix: u64,
  47:     /// Issuer's device id.
  48:     pub issuer_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  49:     /// Issuer's subkey day-index at issue time. Verifier cross-
  50:     /// checks against the subkey-attestation cache.
  51:     pub issuer_day_index: u64,
  52:     /// Issuer's subkey signature over the canonical bytes.
  53:     pub issuer_sig: Vec<u8>,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl QuorumProposal {
  57:     /// Canonical bytes the issuer signs over.
  58:     #[must_use] 
  59:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  60:         policy_id: &QuorumPolicyId,
  61:         operation_digest: &[u8; OPERATION_DIGEST_LEN],
  62:         nonce: &ProposalNonce,
  63:         issued_unix: u64,
  64:         deadline_unix: u64,
  65:         issuer_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  66:         issuer_day_index: u64,
  67:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  68:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  69:             PROPOSAL_DOMAIN.len()
  70:                 + POLICY_ID_LEN
  71:                 + OPERATION_DIGEST_LEN
  72:                 + PROPOSAL_NONCE_LEN
  73:                 + 8
  74:                 + 8
  75:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  76:                 + 8,
  77:         );
  78:         out.extend_from_slice(PROPOSAL_DOMAIN);
  79:         out.extend_from_slice(policy_id);
  80:         out.extend_from_slice(operation_digest);
  81:         out.extend_from_slice(nonce);
  82:         out.extend_from_slice(&issued_unix.to_be_bytes());
  83:         out.extend_from_slice(&deadline_unix.to_be_bytes());
  84:         out.extend_from_slice(issuer_device_id);
  85:         out.extend_from_slice(&issuer_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  86:         out
  87:     }
  88: 
  89:     /// Compute the [`ProposalId`] (BLAKE3 over the canonical transcript).
  90:     #[must_use] 
  91:     pub fn proposal_id(&self) -> ProposalId {
  92:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
  93:             &self.policy_id,
  94:             &self.operation_digest,
  95:             &self.nonce,
  96:             self.issued_unix,
  97:             self.deadline_unix,
  98:             &self.issuer_device_id,
  99:             self.issuer_day_index,
 100:         );
 101:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 102:         h.update(b"OL-device-mesh-proposal-id-v1");
 103:         h.update(&transcript);
 104:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 105:     }
 106: 
 107:     /// Verify the issuer's signature against the supplied subkey VK.
 108:     /// Caller is responsible for proving that VK is the issuer's
 109:     /// (typically via a [`crate::SubkeyAttestation`] under the master).
 110:     pub fn verify_issuer(&self, issuer_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 111:         if self.issuer_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 112:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 113:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
 114:                 got: self.issuer_sig.len(),
 115:             });
 116:         }
 117:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 118:             &self.policy_id,
 119:             &self.operation_digest,
 120:             &self.nonce,
 121:             self.issued_unix,
 122:             self.deadline_unix,
 123:             &self.issuer_device_id,
 124:             self.issuer_day_index,
 125:         );
 126:         issuer_vk
 127:             .verify(&transcript, &self.issuer_sig)
 128:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::ProposalIssuerVerifyFail)
 129:     }
 130: }
 131: 
 132: /// Propose an operation. The issuer's subkey signs the canonical
 133: /// transcript; the resulting [`QuorumProposal`] is broadcast to the
 134: /// sibling devices that will sign approvals.
 135: pub fn propose_operation(
 136:     issuer: &DeviceSubkey,
 137:     policy: &QuorumPolicy,
 138:     operation_digest: [u8; OPERATION_DIGEST_LEN],
 139:     nonce: ProposalNonce,
 140:     issued_unix: u64,
 141:     deadline_unix: u64,
 142: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<QuorumProposal> {
 143:     if !policy.is_eligible(issuer.device_id()) {
 144:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::IssuerNotEligible {
 145:             device_id: *issuer.device_id(),
 146:         });
 147:     }
 148:     if deadline_unix <= issued_unix {
 149:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::ProposalDeadlineNotAfterIssue {
 150:             issued_unix,
 151:             deadline_unix,
 152:         });
 153:     }
 154:     let transcript = QuorumProposal::canonical_transcript(
 155:         &policy.policy_id,
 156:         &operation_digest,
 157:         &nonce,
 158:         issued_unix,
 159:         deadline_unix,
 160:         issuer.device_id(),
 161:         issuer.day_index(),
 162:     );
 163:     let sig = issuer.sign(&transcript)?;
 164:     Ok(QuorumProposal {
 165:         policy_id: policy.policy_id,
 166:         operation_digest,
 167:         nonce,
 168:         issued_unix,
 169:         deadline_unix,
 170:         issuer_device_id: *issuer.device_id(),
 171:         issuer_day_index: issuer.day_index(),
 172:         issuer_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 173:     })
 174: }

   1: //! Daily ratchet for per-device subkey forward secrecy.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each device's subkey chain is rooted at `day_index = 0` and
   4: //! advances forward one day at a time. The chain is one-way: the
   5: //! transition `S_n → S_{n+1}` is a BLAKE3-keyed HKDF call that can't
   6: //! be inverted, and the device zeroizes `S_n` as soon as it has
   7: //! `S_{n+1}` in hand.
   8: //!
   9: //! Crucially, the master *seed* can re-derive ANY day in the chain
  10: //! via `derive_subkey_seed(master_seed, class, id, day)`, so loss of
  11: //! a device's current subkey doesn't lose history if the master is
  12: //! recoverable.  But an attacker who captures only the device's
  13: //! present-day subkey cannot decrypt any prior day's traffic — the
  14: //! prior subkeys are gone from RAM and inaccessible without the
  15: //! master.
  16: //!
  17: //! ## Threat-coverage matrix
  18: //!
  19: //! | Attacker has              | Can recover prior days?            |
  20: //! |---                        |---                                 |
  21: //! | Today's device subkey     | NO — chain is one-way              |
  22: //! | Master seed               | YES — derive any day deterministically |
  23: //! | Today's device + master   | YES                                |
  24: //! | Yesterday's device subkey | YES, only via THAT device's RAM    |
  25: 
  26: use crate::derivation::SUBKEY_SEED_LEN;
  27: use blake3::Hasher;
  28: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  29: 
  30: /// Domain-separation tag for the daily-ratchet HKDF.
  31: pub const RATCHET_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-device-mesh-ratchet-v1";
  32: 
  33: /// Step a subkey seed forward by one day.
  34: ///
  35: /// `prev` is zeroized in place after the new seed is computed —
  36: /// callers should NEVER keep a copy of `prev` alive past this call.
  37: ///
  38: /// Returns the new seed (which the caller stores in place of `prev`).
  39: pub fn ratchet_one_day(prev: &mut [u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN]) -> [u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN] {
  40:     let mut out = [0u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
  41:     // Ed25519 half — distinct sub-context from ML-DSA half so the
  42:     // two halves remain independent under ratcheting.
  43:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  44:     h.update(RATCHET_DOMAIN);
  45:     h.update(b"-ed25519");
  46:     h.update(prev);
  47:     out[..32].copy_from_slice(h.finalize().as_bytes());
  48: 
  49:     let mut h2 = Hasher::new();
  50:     h2.update(RATCHET_DOMAIN);
  51:     h2.update(b"-mldsa");
  52:     h2.update(prev);
  53:     out[32..].copy_from_slice(h2.finalize().as_bytes());
  54: 
  55:     // Zeroize the previous seed in place — that's the forward-secrecy
  56:     // contract for this call.
  57:     prev.zeroize();
  58:     out
  59: }
  60: 
  61: #[cfg(test)]
  62: mod tests {
  63:     use super::*;
  64: 
  65:     #[test]
  66:     fn ratchet_advances_seed() {
  67:         let mut s = [0x42u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
  68:         let next = ratchet_one_day(&mut s);
  69:         // Previous seed zeroized.
  70:         assert_eq!(s, [0u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN]);
  71:         // Next seed is non-zero (with overwhelming probability).
  72:         assert_ne!(next, [0u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN]);
  73:         // Both halves changed.
  74:         assert_ne!(&next[..32], &[0u8; 32][..]);
  75:         assert_ne!(&next[32..], &[0u8; 32][..]);
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     #[test]
  79:     fn ratchet_is_deterministic_on_input() {
  80:         let mut a = [0x55u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
  81:         let mut b = [0x55u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
  82:         let next_a = ratchet_one_day(&mut a);
  83:         let next_b = ratchet_one_day(&mut b);
  84:         assert_eq!(next_a, next_b);
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     #[test]
  88:     fn ratchet_is_one_way_under_distinct_inputs() {
  89:         // Two distinct prev seeds produce distinct next seeds (with
  90:         // overwhelming probability).
  91:         let mut a = [0x11u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
  92:         let mut b = [0x22u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
  93:         let next_a = ratchet_one_day(&mut a);
  94:         let next_b = ratchet_one_day(&mut b);
  95:         assert_ne!(next_a, next_b);
  96:     }
  97: 
  98:     #[test]
  99:     fn ratchet_chain_diverges_over_days() {
 100:         // Step the same seed N times and confirm each step yields a
 101:         // fresh value (the chain doesn't cycle within N).
 102:         let mut s = [0x77u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
 103:         let mut history = vec![s];
 104:         for _ in 0..32 {
 105:             s = ratchet_one_day(&mut s);
 106:             assert!(!history.contains(&s), "ratchet cycle detected");
 107:             history.push(s);
 108:         }
 109:     }
 110: }

   1: //! Master-signed onion-pubkey attestation.
   2: //!
   3: //! Binds a `device_id → ristretto_pubkey` mapping under the master's
   4: //! hybrid signing key. Replicas pin the master VK once + use the
   5: //! attestation to validate every onion hop they hear about.
   6: 
   7: use ol_pqsig::{HybridSigningKey, HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
   8: 
   9: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  10: use crate::master::MasterIdentity;
  11: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  12: 
  13: use super::identity::ONION_PUBKEY_LEN;
  14: 
  15: /// Domain-separation tag for the onion-attestation signing transcript.
  16: pub const ONION_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-onion-attestation-v1";
  17: 
  18: /// Master-signed onion attestation.
  19: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  20: pub struct OnionAttestation {
  21:     /// Device the attestation binds.
  22:     pub device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  23:     /// Compressed Ristretto255 onion public key.
  24:     pub onion_pubkey: [u8; ONION_PUBKEY_LEN],
  25:     /// First day the binding is valid for (matching the Layer-1
  26:     /// `SubkeyAttestation` shape so revocations work uniformly).
  27:     pub mint_day_index: u64,
  28:     /// Last day the binding is valid for.
  29:     pub expiry_day_index: u64,
  30:     /// Master hybrid signature over the canonical transcript.
  31:     pub master_sig: Vec<u8>,
  32: }
  33: 
  34: impl OnionAttestation {
  35:     /// Canonical bytes the master signs.
  36:     #[must_use] 
  37:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  38:         device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  39:         onion_pubkey: &[u8; ONION_PUBKEY_LEN],
  40:         mint_day_index: u64,
  41:         expiry_day_index: u64,
  42:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  43:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  44:             ONION_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN.len()
  45:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  46:                 + ONION_PUBKEY_LEN
  47:                 + 8
  48:                 + 8,
  49:         );
  50:         out.extend_from_slice(ONION_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN);
  51:         out.extend_from_slice(device_id);
  52:         out.extend_from_slice(onion_pubkey);
  53:         out.extend_from_slice(&mint_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  54:         out.extend_from_slice(&expiry_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  55:         out
  56:     }
  57: 
  58:     /// Verify the master signature.
  59:     pub fn verify(&self, master_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  60:         if self.master_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
  61:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
  62:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
  63:                 got: self.master_sig.len(),
  64:             });
  65:         }
  66:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
  67:             &self.device_id,
  68:             &self.onion_pubkey,
  69:             self.mint_day_index,
  70:             self.expiry_day_index,
  71:         );
  72:         master_vk
  73:             .verify(&transcript, &self.master_sig)
  74:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::OnionAttestationVerifyFail)
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     /// Is `day` within the validity window?
  78:     #[must_use]
  79:     pub const fn covers_day(&self, day: u64) -> bool {
  80:         day >= self.mint_day_index && day <= self.expiry_day_index
  81:     }
  82: }
  83: 
  84: /// Mint an onion attestation under the master.
  85: pub fn sign_onion_attestation(
  86:     master: &MasterIdentity,
  87:     device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  88:     onion_pubkey: [u8; ONION_PUBKEY_LEN],
  89:     mint_day_index: u64,
  90:     expiry_day_index: u64,
  91: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<OnionAttestation> {
  92:     if expiry_day_index < mint_day_index {
  93:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::OnionAttestationBadValidityWindow {
  94:             mint: mint_day_index,
  95:             expiry: expiry_day_index,
  96:         });
  97:     }
  98:     let transcript = OnionAttestation::canonical_transcript(
  99:         &device_id,
 100:         &onion_pubkey,
 101:         mint_day_index,
 102:         expiry_day_index,
 103:     );
 104:     let signing: HybridSigningKey = master.signing_key();
 105:     let sig = signing.sign(&transcript)?;
 106:     Ok(OnionAttestation {
 107:         device_id,
 108:         onion_pubkey,
 109:         mint_day_index,
 110:         expiry_day_index,
 111:         master_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 112:     })
 113: }

   1: //! Self-mesh circuit builder + peeler.
   2: //!
   3: //! Composes a Layer-6 [`crate::self_routing::Route`] with the
   4: //! shipped F3 [`ol_onion::sphinx`] Sphinx Coherence primitive to
   5: //! produce a fully-built [`ol_onion::sphinx::SphinxPacket`] aimed at
   6: //! the destination device. The peeler wraps the shipped Sphinx
   7: //! peel call so callers can drive the personal-mesh circuit without
   8: //! re-deriving Ristretto scalars themselves.
   9: 
  10: use curve25519_dalek::ristretto::CompressedRistretto;
  11: use ol_onion::sphinx::core::{
  12:     build_sphinx_onion, generate_static_keypair, peel_sphinx_layer, SphinxHop,
  13:     SphinxPacket, SphinxPeelOutcome, SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD,
  14: };
  15: use ol_onion::HopId;
  16: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  17: 
  18: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  19: use crate::self_routing::Route;
  20: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  21: 
  22: use super::identity::OnionIdentity;
  23: use super::registry::OnionKeyRegistry;
  24: 
  25: /// Domain-separation prefix the sender prepends to the payload
  26: /// before handing it to Sphinx. The destination strips it on
  27: /// receive; foreign packets that don't carry the prefix are dropped.
  28: pub const SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-self-onion-v1\0";
  29: 
  30: /// Peel outcome from a self-onion layer. Wraps the underlying
  31: /// Sphinx outcome with self-mesh-specific semantics.
  32: ///
  33: /// `SphinxPacket` is ~1.3 KiB, so the `Forward` payload is boxed —
  34: /// the enum stays cheap on the stack (matches against this enum live
  35: /// in the per-hop forwarding hot loop).
  36: #[derive(Debug)]
  37: pub enum SelfOnionPeelOutcome {
  38:     /// Forward the packet onward to `next_hop_device_id`.
  39:     Forward {
  40:         /// Device id of the next hop (decoded from the Sphinx
  41:         /// header).
  42:         next_hop_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  43:         /// The packet to forward (with one layer removed).
  44:         next_packet: Box<SphinxPacket>,
  45:     },
  46:     /// This device is the destination; here's the payload.
  47:     Deliver {
  48:         /// User payload bytes (with the self-onion domain prefix
  49:         /// stripped).
  50:         payload: Vec<u8>,
  51:     },
  52:     /// The packet's outer payload didn't carry the self-onion
  53:     /// domain prefix — it's not a self-mesh packet. The daemon
  54:     /// drops it.
  55:     NotSelfOnion,
  56: }
  57: 
  58: /// Build a self-onion circuit for `route` carrying `payload`.
  59: ///
  60: /// `route` is the output of [`crate::self_routing::pick_best_route`].
  61: /// `registry` provides each hop's master-attested Ristretto255
  62: /// pubkey. `day_index` selects the validity window in the registry
  63: /// (typically the receiver's `subkey.day_index()`).
  64: pub fn build_self_onion_circuit<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
  65:     route: &Route,
  66:     registry: &OnionKeyRegistry,
  67:     day_index: u64,
  68:     payload: &[u8],
  69:     rng: &mut R,
  70: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<SphinxPacket> {
  71:     if route.hops.len() < 2 {
  72:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::SelfOnionRouteTooShort {
  73:             got: route.hops.len(),
  74:         });
  75:     }
  76:     // The destination is the LAST hop. The first hop is `src` — we
  77:     // don't include it in the Sphinx circuit (Sphinx walks
  78:     // intermediate + final; the source's job is just to send the
  79:     // built packet to the first intermediate, which is `hops[1]`).
  80:     let sphinx_targets: &[[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]] = &route.hops[1..];
  81: 
  82:     let mut sphinx_circuit: Vec<SphinxHop> = Vec::with_capacity(sphinx_targets.len());
  83:     for device_id in sphinx_targets {
  84:         let pk_bytes = registry.pubkey_for(device_id, day_index)?;
  85:         // Pad device_id to SLOT_ID_LEN (32 bytes) by prefixing with
  86:         // zeros — the Sphinx hop id is opaque to the protocol, we
  87:         // just need it to be unique + recoverable.
  88:         let mut slot_id = [0u8; 32];
  89:         slot_id[16..].copy_from_slice(device_id);
  90:         let hop = SphinxHop::new(slot_id, pk_bytes)
  91:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::SelfOnionBadHopPubkey {
  92:                 device_id: *device_id,
  93:             })?;
  94:         sphinx_circuit.push(hop);
  95:     }
  96: 
  97:     // Domain-prefix the payload.
  98:     let mut wrapped = Vec::with_capacity(SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD.len() + payload.len());
  99:     wrapped.extend_from_slice(SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD);
 100:     wrapped.extend_from_slice(payload);
 101:     if wrapped.len() > SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD {
 102:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::SelfOnionPayloadOversize {
 103:             got: payload.len(),
 104:             max: SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD.saturating_sub(SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD.len()),
 105:         });
 106:     }
 107: 
 108:     let (eph_sk, _eph_pk) = generate_static_keypair(rng);
 109:     let packet =
 110:         build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &sphinx_circuit, &wrapped, rng).map_err(|e| {
 111:             DeviceMeshError::SelfOnionSphinxBuildFailed(format!("{e}"))
 112:         })?;
 113:     Ok(packet)
 114: }
 115: 
 116: /// Peel one layer of a self-onion packet using the local device's
 117: /// onion identity. Returns the next hop or the delivered payload.
 118: pub fn peel_self_onion_layer(
 119:     local_identity: &OnionIdentity,
 120:     packet: &SphinxPacket,
 121: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<SelfOnionPeelOutcome> {
 122:     let scalar = local_identity.peel_scalar();
 123:     let outcome = peel_sphinx_layer(&scalar, packet)
 124:         .map_err(|e| DeviceMeshError::SelfOnionSphinxPeelFailed(format!("{e}")))?;
 125:     match outcome {
 126:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_hop, next_packet } => {
 127:             // The Sphinx hop id is the SLOT_ID_LEN-padded device id.
 128:             // Recover the trailing DEVICE_ID_LEN bytes.
 129:             let slot_bytes = *next_hop.as_bytes();
 130:             let mut device_id = [0u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 131:             device_id.copy_from_slice(&slot_bytes[16..]);
 132:             Ok(SelfOnionPeelOutcome::Forward {
 133:                 next_hop_device_id: device_id,
 134:                 next_packet: Box::new(next_packet),
 135:             })
 136:         }
 137:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => {
 138:             // Strip the self-onion domain prefix.
 139:             if payload.len() < SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD.len()
 140:                 || &payload[..SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD.len()] != SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD
 141:             {
 142:                 return Ok(SelfOnionPeelOutcome::NotSelfOnion);
 143:             }
 144:             let body = payload[SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD.len()..].to_vec();
 145:             Ok(SelfOnionPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload: body })
 146:         }
 147:         // Audit M4: a Sphinx-level authenticated cover packet that
 148:         // happened to be addressed to this device. Self-onion sees
 149:         // it as "not a self-onion delivery" so the dispatcher drops
 150:         // it without surfacing a payload.
 151:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => Ok(SelfOnionPeelOutcome::NotSelfOnion),
 152:     }
 153: }

   1: //! Per-device Ristretto255 onion identity.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each device gets a Ristretto255 keypair derived deterministically
   4: //! from the master seed plus the device id and a domain string.
   5: //! The secret half lives in the device's memory (and the platform
   6: //! hardware wrapper at rest, via Layer-1 [`crate::HardwareWrapper`]);
   7: //! the public half is master-attested and broadcast to siblings via
   8: //! [`super::OnionAttestation`].
   9: //!
  10: //! Deterministic derivation means the master can re-mint the onion
  11: //! identity on a new pairing (analogous to the Layer-1
  12: //! [`crate::redrive_subkey_at_day`] path).
  13: 
  14: use blake3::Hasher;
  15: use curve25519_dalek::constants::RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
  16: use curve25519_dalek::ristretto::RistrettoPoint;
  17: use curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar;
  18: use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop};
  19: 
  20: use crate::master::MasterIdentity;
  21: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  22: 
  23: /// Length of the secret scalar's wire form (`Scalar::to_bytes` is
  24: /// canonically 32 bytes; we keep the bytes for at-rest storage).
  25: pub const ONION_SECRET_LEN: usize = 32;
  26: 
  27: /// Length of the Ristretto255 public point's compressed form.
  28: pub const ONION_PUBKEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  29: 
  30: /// Domain-separation tag for onion-identity derivation.
  31: pub const ONION_DERIVATION_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-onion-identity-v1";
  32: 
  33: /// One device's Ristretto255 onion identity.
  34: #[derive(ZeroizeOnDrop)]
  35: pub struct OnionIdentity {
  36:     secret_bytes: [u8; ONION_SECRET_LEN],
  37: }
  38: 
  39: impl OnionIdentity {
  40:     /// Construct from raw scalar bytes (e.g., after at-rest load).
  41:     #[must_use] 
  42:     pub const fn from_secret_bytes(secret_bytes: [u8; ONION_SECRET_LEN]) -> Self {
  43:         Self { secret_bytes }
  44:     }
  45: 
  46:     /// Borrow the raw secret bytes. DANGEROUS — only for at-rest
  47:     /// serialization via the hardware wrapper.
  48:     #[must_use] 
  49:     pub const fn secret_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; ONION_SECRET_LEN] {
  50:         &self.secret_bytes
  51:     }
  52: 
  53:     /// Materialize the scalar.
  54:     fn scalar(&self) -> Scalar {
  55:         let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
  56:         wide[..32].copy_from_slice(&self.secret_bytes);
  57:         Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide)
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     /// Compute the public point.
  61:     #[must_use] 
  62:     pub fn public_point(&self) -> RistrettoPoint {
  63:         let s = self.scalar();
  64:         &s * RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE
  65:     }
  66: 
  67:     /// Compressed public-point bytes (32-byte Ristretto255 encoding).
  68:     #[must_use] 
  69:     pub fn public_bytes(&self) -> [u8; ONION_PUBKEY_LEN] {
  70:         self.public_point().compress().to_bytes()
  71:     }
  72: 
  73:     /// Borrow the secret scalar for the Sphinx peel path. The
  74:     /// caller must NOT log or persist the result.
  75:     #[must_use] 
  76:     pub fn peel_scalar(&self) -> Scalar {
  77:         self.scalar()
  78:     }
  79: }
  80: 
  81: impl std::fmt::Debug for OnionIdentity {
  82:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  83:         f.debug_struct("OnionIdentity").finish_non_exhaustive()
  84:     }
  85: }
  86: 
  87: /// Derive the device's onion identity deterministically from the
  88: /// master seed + device id.
  89: ///
  90: /// HKDF chain: `BLAKE3-XOF(ONION_DERIVATION_DOMAIN || master_seed ||
  91: /// device_id)` expanded to 64 bytes, then folded into a Scalar via
  92: /// `from_bytes_mod_order_wide` for unbiased sampling.
  93: #[must_use]
  94: pub fn derive_onion_identity(
  95:     master: &MasterIdentity,
  96:     device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  97: ) -> OnionIdentity {
  98:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  99:     h.update(ONION_DERIVATION_DOMAIN);
 100:     h.update(master.seed());
 101:     h.update(device_id);
 102:     let mut reader = h.finalize_xof();
 103:     let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
 104:     reader.fill(&mut wide);
 105:     let scalar = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide);
 106:     // Encode the scalar back to canonical 32-byte form. This is
 107:     // bit-exact under from_bytes_mod_order_wide for any later
 108:     // reload (`from_secret_bytes` → `from_bytes_mod_order_wide`
 109:     // with zero-padded high half).
 110:     let mut secret_bytes = [0u8; ONION_SECRET_LEN];
 111:     secret_bytes.copy_from_slice(&scalar.to_bytes());
 112:     wide.zeroize();
 113:     OnionIdentity { secret_bytes }
 114: }

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 7 — self-onion routing through your own devices when
   2: //! the underlying network is hostile.
   3: //!
   4: //! When you're on an untrusted Wi-Fi (airport, coffee shop, hostile
   5: //! border crossing), direct device-to-device traffic leaks who you
   6: //! talk to even if every packet is encrypted: the destination IP
   7: //! addresses are visible to the on-path observer. Self-onion routing
   8: //! wraps the traffic in a Sphinx Coherence onion (the F3 layer
   9: //! already shipped) where each hop is one of YOUR OWN devices, so
  10: //! the observer sees only an opaque relay sequence among devices
  11: //! they can't link to you.
  12: //!
  13: //! ## What this layer ships
  14: //!
  15: //! - [`OnionIdentity`] — a per-device Ristretto255 keypair, derived
  16: //!   deterministically from the master seed so the master can
  17: //!   re-mint it on any new pairing. The PUBKEY half is the
  18: //!   Sphinx static-pk for that device's hop.
  19: //! - [`OnionAttestation`] — master-signed binding of
  20: //!   `device_id → ristretto_pubkey`. Replicas verify under the
  21: //!   master VK before trusting any device as a hop.
  22: //! - [`OnionKeyRegistry`] — aggregated attestation table; what the
  23: //!   sender consults to materialise [`ol_onion::sphinx::SphinxHop`]
  24: //!   structs for a circuit.
  25: //! - [`build_self_onion_circuit`] — given a Layer-6 route + the
  26: //!   registry + a payload, produce a fully-built
  27: //!   [`ol_onion::sphinx::SphinxPacket`] aimed at the destination
  28: //!   device.
  29: //! - [`peel_self_onion_layer`] — wrapper around the Sphinx peel
  30: //!   that takes a [`OnionIdentity`] and dispatches the result.
  31: //! - [`SelfOnionContext`] — policy: min hop count, hostile-network
  32: //!   flag, cover-traffic rate. Daemons consult this to decide
  33: //!   "direct or self-onion."
  34: //!
  35: //! ## Composition with the lower layers
  36: //!
  37: //! - **Layer 1**: every [`OnionAttestation`] is signed by the
  38: //!   master's hybrid signing key (the same root every other
  39: //!   personal-mesh primitive trusts).
  40: //! - **Layer 3 (CRDT mirror)**: the registry can be stored as a
  41: //!   Layer-3 LWW-Map subtree keyed by `device_id` so every device
  42: //!   sees the same onion-key view.
  43: //! - **Layer 6 (self-routing)**: hop selection consumes a
  44: //!   [`crate::self_routing::Route`] — the routing layer's max-min-τ
  45: //!   picker chooses the path; this layer turns it into a Sphinx
  46: //!   circuit.
  47: //! - **F3 `ol_onion::sphinx`**: the Sphinx machinery itself.
  48: //!   Layer 7 doesn't reimplement Sphinx; it composes the shipped
  49: //!   primitive with personal-mesh identities.
  50: //!
  51: //! ## What this layer doesn't ship
  52: //!
  53: //! - The Sphinx Coherence primitive itself (already shipped as
  54: //!   `ol_onion::sphinx`).
  55: //! - Hostile-network detection (daemon-level concern — Wi-Fi SSID
  56: //!   trust list, captive-portal heuristics, etc.).
  57: //! - Cover-traffic emission (Phase B `ol_onion::sphinx::cover`
  58: //!   shipped; this layer just references the rate policy).
  59: 
  60: pub mod attestation;
  61: pub mod circuit;
  62: pub mod identity;
  63: pub mod policy;
  64: pub mod registry;
  65: 
  66: pub use attestation::{
  67:     sign_onion_attestation, OnionAttestation, ONION_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN,
  68: };
  69: pub use circuit::{
  70:     build_self_onion_circuit, peel_self_onion_layer, SelfOnionPeelOutcome,
  71:     SELF_ONION_DOMAIN_PAYLOAD,
  72: };
  73: pub use identity::{
  74:     derive_onion_identity, OnionIdentity, ONION_DERIVATION_DOMAIN, ONION_SECRET_LEN,
  75:     ONION_PUBKEY_LEN,
  76: };
  77: pub use policy::{SelfOnionContext, DEFAULT_MIN_HOPS};
  78: pub use registry::OnionKeyRegistry;

   1: //! Self-onion routing policy.
   2: //!
   3: //! Tells the daemon WHEN to switch from direct device-to-device
   4: //! traffic to a self-onion circuit. The daemon owns the actual
   5: //! hostile-network detection; this layer just expresses the
   6: //! resulting decision.
   7: 
   8: /// Default minimum hop count for self-onion circuits. At 2 hops
   9: /// (one intermediate device), the on-path observer can't link
  10: /// `src → dst`; one peeling hop is enough to break the trivial
  11: /// "same destination IP every connection" inference.
  12: pub const DEFAULT_MIN_HOPS: usize = 2;
  13: 
  14: /// Policy controlling self-onion behaviour.
  15: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  16: pub struct SelfOnionContext {
  17:     /// Minimum number of intermediate devices in a circuit. 2+
  18:     /// gives meaningful obscuring; 3+ for actively-monitored
  19:     /// networks.
  20:     pub min_hops: usize,
  21:     /// `true` when the daemon believes the local network is
  22:     /// untrusted. Higher layers populate this from Wi-Fi-SSID
  23:     /// allow-lists, captive-portal detection, geolocation, etc.
  24:     pub network_is_hostile: bool,
  25:     /// Bytes-per-second of cover traffic the daemon SHOULD inject
  26:     /// while in hostile mode. Zero means "no cover." See Phase B
  27:     /// `ol_onion::sphinx::cover` for the actual emission primitive.
  28:     pub cover_traffic_bps: u64,
  29: }
  30: 
  31: impl SelfOnionContext {
  32:     /// Sensible defaults for "trusted home network" — no self-onion,
  33:     /// no cover.
  34:     #[must_use]
  35:     pub const fn trusted_home() -> Self {
  36:         Self {
  37:             min_hops: DEFAULT_MIN_HOPS,
  38:             network_is_hostile: false,
  39:             cover_traffic_bps: 0,
  40:         }
  41:     }
  42: 
  43:     /// "Hostile network" preset: 3-hop minimum + 100 KB/s cover.
  44:     #[must_use]
  45:     pub const fn hostile_network() -> Self {
  46:         Self {
  47:             min_hops: 3,
  48:             network_is_hostile: true,
  49:             cover_traffic_bps: 100_000,
  50:         }
  51:     }
  52: 
  53:     /// `true` if the current policy says "use self-onion."
  54:     #[must_use]
  55:     pub const fn requires_self_onion(&self) -> bool {
  56:         self.network_is_hostile
  57:     }
  58: }
  59: 
  60: impl Default for SelfOnionContext {
  61:     fn default() -> Self {
  62:         Self::trusted_home()
  63:     }
  64: }

   1: //! Aggregated onion-key registry.
   2: //!
   3: //! Pins one [`OnionAttestation`] per device. Replicas verify each
   4: //! attestation under the pinned master VK on ingest; lookups
   5: //! materialise the bound pubkey for sender-side circuit construction.
   6: 
   7: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
   8: 
   9: use ol_pqsig::HybridVerifyingKey;
  10: 
  11: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  12: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  13: 
  14: use super::attestation::OnionAttestation;
  15: use super::identity::ONION_PUBKEY_LEN;
  16: 
  17: /// Registry of master-attested onion-pubkey mappings.
  18: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  19: pub struct OnionKeyRegistry {
  20:     entries: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], OnionAttestation>,
  21: }
  22: 
  23: impl OnionKeyRegistry {
  24:     /// Empty registry.
  25:     #[must_use]
  26:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
  27:         Self::default()
  28:     }
  29: 
  30:     /// Ingest an attestation. Verifies it under `master_vk` and
  31:     /// replaces any prior entry for the same device id.
  32:     pub fn ingest(
  33:         &mut self,
  34:         att: OnionAttestation,
  35:         master_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey,
  36:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  37:         att.verify(master_vk)?;
  38:         self.entries.insert(att.device_id, att);
  39:         Ok(())
  40:     }
  41: 
  42:     /// Look up the onion pubkey bound to `device_id` at `day`.
  43:     pub fn pubkey_for(
  44:         &self,
  45:         device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  46:         day: u64,
  47:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<[u8; ONION_PUBKEY_LEN]> {
  48:         let att = self.entries.get(device_id).ok_or(
  49:             DeviceMeshError::OnionRegistryDeviceMissing { device_id: *device_id },
  50:         )?;
  51:         if !att.covers_day(day) {
  52:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::OnionRegistryDayOutOfWindow {
  53:                 device_id: *device_id,
  54:                 day,
  55:                 mint: att.mint_day_index,
  56:                 expiry: att.expiry_day_index,
  57:             });
  58:         }
  59:         Ok(att.onion_pubkey)
  60:     }
  61: 
  62:     /// Iterator over `(device_id, attestation)` pairs in deterministic order.
  63:     pub fn entries(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], &OnionAttestation)> {
  64:         self.entries.iter()
  65:     }
  66: 
  67:     /// Number of attestations held.
  68:     #[must_use]
  69:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
  70:         self.entries.len()
  71:     }
  72: 
  73:     /// True iff no attestations.
  74:     #[must_use]
  75:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  76:         self.entries.is_empty()
  77:     }
  78: }

   1: //! Signed route announcement.
   2: //!
   3: //! A [`RouteAnnouncement`] is "I, device A, can reach these peers
   4: //! with these `τ_c` scores as of time T." Devices sign their own
   5: //! announcements; replicas verify under the master-attested subkey
   6: //! VK before merging into the route table.
   7: 
   8: use ol_pqsig::{HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
   9: 
  10: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  11: use crate::subkey::{DeviceSubkey, DEVICE_ID_LEN};
  12: 
  13: use super::route::TauScore;
  14: 
  15: /// Max links one announcement can carry. Bounds wire size + verify
  16: /// cost. At 32 devices per personal mesh, this is plenty.
  17: pub const MAX_LINKS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT: usize = 64;
  18: 
  19: /// Domain-separation tag for route-announcement signing.
  20: pub const ROUTE_ANNOUNCEMENT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-mesh-route-announcement-v1";
  21: 
  22: /// One reachability claim within an announcement.
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  24: pub struct PeerLink {
  25:     /// The peer device.
  26:     pub peer_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  27:     /// `τ_c` score the announcer estimates for this peer. Higher =
  28:     /// better. See [`super::route::TauScore`].
  29:     pub tau_score: TauScore,
  30:     /// Wall-clock seconds when the announcer last actually observed
  31:     /// the peer (last successful probe / packet exchange).
  32:     pub last_seen_unix: u64,
  33:     /// `true` iff the announcer is offering itself as a direct relay
  34:     /// for this peer. `false` means "I observed the peer but won't
  35:     /// forward traffic" (used by passive presence reports).
  36:     pub direct: bool,
  37: }
  38: 
  39: /// Signed claim covering every link the announcer is willing to
  40: /// vouch for at this moment.
  41: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  42: pub struct RouteAnnouncement {
  43:     /// Which device authored the announcement.
  44:     pub announcer_device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  45:     /// Announcer subkey's day-index at sign time.
  46:     pub announcer_day_index: u64,
  47:     /// Wall-clock seconds at sign time.
  48:     pub announced_at_unix: u64,
  49:     /// Reachability claims. Sorted ascending by `peer_device_id` so
  50:     /// canonical bytes are deterministic.
  51:     pub links: Vec<PeerLink>,
  52:     /// Announcer's subkey signature over the canonical transcript.
  53:     pub announcer_sig: Vec<u8>,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl RouteAnnouncement {
  57:     /// Canonical bytes the announcer's subkey signs.
  58:     #[must_use] 
  59:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
  60:         announcer_device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  61:         announcer_day_index: u64,
  62:         announced_at_unix: u64,
  63:         links: &[PeerLink],
  64:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
  65:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
  66:             ROUTE_ANNOUNCEMENT_DOMAIN.len()
  67:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
  68:                 + 8
  69:                 + 8
  70:                 + 4
  71:                 + links.len() * (DEVICE_ID_LEN + 4 + 8 + 1),
  72:         );
  73:         out.extend_from_slice(ROUTE_ANNOUNCEMENT_DOMAIN);
  74:         out.extend_from_slice(announcer_device_id);
  75:         out.extend_from_slice(&announcer_day_index.to_be_bytes());
  76:         out.extend_from_slice(&announced_at_unix.to_be_bytes());
  77:         let count = u32::try_from(links.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
  78:         out.extend_from_slice(&count.to_be_bytes());
  79:         for l in links {
  80:             out.extend_from_slice(&l.peer_device_id);
  81:             out.extend_from_slice(&l.tau_score.to_be_bytes());
  82:             out.extend_from_slice(&l.last_seen_unix.to_be_bytes());
  83:             out.push(u8::from(l.direct));
  84:         }
  85:         out
  86:     }
  87: 
  88:     /// Validate the shape (sorted links, no duplicates, bounded).
  89:     pub fn shape_check(&self) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
  90:         if self.links.len() > MAX_LINKS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT {
  91:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::RouteAnnouncementTooManyLinks {
  92:                 got: self.links.len(),
  93:                 max: MAX_LINKS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT,
  94:             });
  95:         }
  96:         let mut prev: Option<&[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> = None;
  97:         for l in &self.links {
  98:             if let Some(p) = prev {
  99:                 if &l.peer_device_id <= p {
 100:                     return Err(DeviceMeshError::RouteAnnouncementLinksNotSorted);
 101:                 }
 102:             }
 103:             // No device should announce itself as its own peer.
 104:             if l.peer_device_id == self.announcer_device_id {
 105:                 return Err(DeviceMeshError::RouteAnnouncementSelfLoop);
 106:             }
 107:             prev = Some(&l.peer_device_id);
 108:         }
 109:         if self.announcer_sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 110:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 111:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
 112:                 got: self.announcer_sig.len(),
 113:             });
 114:         }
 115:         Ok(())
 116:     }
 117: 
 118:     /// Verify the announcer's signature against the supplied subkey VK.
 119:     pub fn verify(&self, vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 120:         self.shape_check()?;
 121:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 122:             &self.announcer_device_id,
 123:             self.announcer_day_index,
 124:             self.announced_at_unix,
 125:             &self.links,
 126:         );
 127:         vk.verify(&transcript, &self.announcer_sig)
 128:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::RouteAnnouncementVerifyFail)
 129:     }
 130: }
 131: 
 132: /// Sign an announcement. The `links` list is sorted + de-duplicated
 133: /// at sign time so two devices announcing the same set of peers
 134: /// produce identical transcripts (caches benefit).
 135: pub fn sign_route_announcement(
 136:     announcer: &DeviceSubkey,
 137:     announced_at_unix: u64,
 138:     mut links: Vec<PeerLink>,
 139: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<RouteAnnouncement> {
 140:     if links.len() > MAX_LINKS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT {
 141:         return Err(DeviceMeshError::RouteAnnouncementTooManyLinks {
 142:             got: links.len(),
 143:             max: MAX_LINKS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT,
 144:         });
 145:     }
 146:     // Sort + dedup by peer_device_id. We keep the highest-tau entry
 147:     // when duplicates are supplied (so a slightly-stale lower-tau
 148:     // sample doesn't override a fresher higher-tau one).
 149:     links.sort_by_key(|l| (l.peer_device_id, std::cmp::Reverse(l.tau_score)));
 150:     links.dedup_by_key(|l| l.peer_device_id);
 151:     // Drop any self-loop entries.
 152:     links.retain(|l| l.peer_device_id != *announcer.device_id());
 153:     let transcript = RouteAnnouncement::canonical_transcript(
 154:         announcer.device_id(),
 155:         announcer.day_index(),
 156:         announced_at_unix,
 157:         &links,
 158:     );
 159:     let sig = announcer.sign(&transcript)?;
 160:     Ok(RouteAnnouncement {
 161:         announcer_device_id: *announcer.device_id(),
 162:         announcer_day_index: announcer.day_index(),
 163:         announced_at_unix,
 164:         links,
 165:         announcer_sig: sig.to_vec(),
 166:     })
 167: }

   1: //! DTN (delay-tolerant networking) courier detection.
   2: //!
   3: //! When two devices (`src`, `dst`) can't reach each other directly
   4: //! OR through any currently-online intermediate, a "courier" device
   5: //! may still carry state between them — picture a tablet that
   6: //! visits home (sees the desktop) then flies elsewhere (sees the
   7: //! phone) and acts as a physical sneakernet between the two.
   8: //!
   9: //! [`dtn_couriers`] returns devices that have been seen reachable
  10: //! to BOTH endpoints within the configured time window, even if
  11: //! they aren't currently online at both at the same time.
  12: 
  13: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  14: 
  15: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  16: 
  17: use super::table::RouteTable;
  18: 
  19: /// One per-courier observation record.
  20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  21: pub struct CourierObservation {
  22:     /// Courier device id.
  23:     pub device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  24:     /// Last time the courier was seen reachable to `src`.
  25:     pub src_seen_unix: u64,
  26:     /// Last time the courier was seen reachable to `dst`.
  27:     pub dst_seen_unix: u64,
  28: }
  29: 
  30: impl CourierObservation {
  31:     /// Time gap between the two reachability sightings. Smaller is
  32:     /// better (less latency in the courier's round trip).
  33:     #[must_use]
  34:     pub const fn gap_secs(&self) -> u64 {
  35:         self.src_seen_unix.abs_diff(self.dst_seen_unix)
  36:     }
  37: }
  38: 
  39: /// Return devices that have been reachable to both `src` and `dst`
  40: /// within `max_gap_secs` of each other.
  41: ///
  42: /// A device `D` qualifies as a courier iff:
  43: /// 1. Some announcement reports `D` reaching `src`.
  44: /// 2. Some announcement reports `D` reaching `dst`.
  45: /// 3. The two `last_seen_unix` values are within `max_gap_secs`.
  46: ///
  47: /// The two sightings may come from `D`'s own announcement (`D`
  48: /// claims it reached `src` and `dst`) or from announcements by `src`
  49: /// and `dst` themselves (each said it saw `D`).
  50: ///
  51: /// Returns observations sorted by smallest `gap_secs` first.
  52: #[must_use]
  53: pub fn dtn_couriers(
  54:     table: &RouteTable,
  55:     src: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  56:     dst: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  57:     max_gap_secs: u64,
  58: ) -> Vec<CourierObservation> {
  59:     // Map: courier_device → (best src_seen, best dst_seen).
  60:     let mut sightings: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], (u64, u64)> = BTreeMap::new();
  61: 
  62:     // For each announcement A authored by D:
  63:     //   - A.links contains an entry for `src` → D saw src at time T.
  64:     //   - A.links contains an entry for `dst` → D saw dst at time T.
  65:     // For each announcement A authored by src:
  66:     //   - A.links has D → src saw D at T (so D is reachable to src then).
  67:     // For each announcement A authored by dst:
  68:     //   - A.links has D → dst saw D at T.
  69:     for announcer in table.announcers() {
  70:         let Some(ann) = table.announcement_for(announcer) else { continue };
  71:         for link in &ann.links {
  72:             // src's announcement of D → D was reachable to src at link.last_seen_unix.
  73:             if announcer == src && link.peer_device_id != *src && link.peer_device_id != *dst {
  74:                 let entry = sightings.entry(link.peer_device_id).or_insert((0, 0));
  75:                 if link.last_seen_unix > entry.0 {
  76:                     entry.0 = link.last_seen_unix;
  77:                 }
  78:             }
  79:             // dst's announcement of D.
  80:             if announcer == dst && link.peer_device_id != *src && link.peer_device_id != *dst {
  81:                 let entry = sightings.entry(link.peer_device_id).or_insert((0, 0));
  82:                 if link.last_seen_unix > entry.1 {
  83:                     entry.1 = link.last_seen_unix;
  84:                 }
  85:             }
  86:             // D's announcement of src or dst.
  87:             if announcer != src && announcer != dst {
  88:                 if link.peer_device_id == *src {
  89:                     let entry = sightings.entry(*announcer).or_insert((0, 0));
  90:                     if link.last_seen_unix > entry.0 {
  91:                         entry.0 = link.last_seen_unix;
  92:                     }
  93:                 } else if link.peer_device_id == *dst {
  94:                     let entry = sightings.entry(*announcer).or_insert((0, 0));
  95:                     if link.last_seen_unix > entry.1 {
  96:                         entry.1 = link.last_seen_unix;
  97:                     }
  98:                 }
  99:             }
 100:         }
 101:     }
 102: 
 103:     let mut out: Vec<CourierObservation> = sightings
 104:         .into_iter()
 105:         .filter_map(|(device_id, (a, b))| {
 106:             if a > 0 && b > 0 {
 107:                 let obs = CourierObservation {
 108:                     device_id,
 109:                     src_seen_unix: a,
 110:                     dst_seen_unix: b,
 111:                 };
 112:                 if obs.gap_secs() <= max_gap_secs {
 113:                     Some(obs)
 114:                 } else {
 115:                     None
 116:                 }
 117:             } else {
 118:                 None
 119:             }
 120:         })
 121:         .collect();
 122:     out.sort_by(|a, b| a.gap_secs().cmp(&b.gap_secs()).then(a.device_id.cmp(&b.device_id)));
 123:     out
 124: }
 125:

   1: //! Row 8 Layer 6 — τ_c-routed self-mesh + DTN courier.
   2: //!
   3: //! Personal-mesh routing: given a source and destination among your
   4: //! OWN devices, pick the highest-coherence (`τ_c`) path. The path may
   5: //! be direct (`src → dst` over LAN / cellular / Wi-Fi) or multi-hop
   6: //! through another device in the mesh (e.g., phone → desktop →
   7: //! laptop because the phone can't directly reach the laptop on the
   8: //! current Wi-Fi network).
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Self-mesh vs friend-mesh
  11: //!
  12: //! Friend-mesh routing (the Phase D `ol_routing` `τ_c` PDE) optimises
  13: //! a public swarm graph. Self-mesh routing optimises a small graph
  14: //! of YOUR devices — phone, laptop, tablet, desktop, server — and
  15: //! has tighter trust assumptions:
  16: //!
  17: //! - Every node in the graph is signed by the master via a Layer-1
  18: //!   `SubkeyAttestation`. There are no untrusted intermediates.
  19: //! - Cover traffic + onion routing are SKIPPED on self-traffic (you
  20: //!   talking to yourself; no metadata to hide).
  21: //! - Multi-path racing for critical messages is cheap because the
  22: //!   max fan-out is bounded by your device count.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## Composition with the lower layers
  25: //!
  26: //! - **Layer 1**: every [`RouteAnnouncement`] is signed by the
  27: //!   announcing device's subkey.
  28: //! - **Layer 3 (CRDT mirror)**: route announcements can be stored
  29: //!   as a Layer-3 LWW-Map subtree keyed by announcer device id, so
  30: //!   every device sees the same route view.
  31: //! - **Layer 5 (fan-out)**: the fan-out planner picks sources via
  32: //!   [`RouteTable::pick_best_route`]; multi-source races use
  33: //!   [`RouteTable::multi_path_plan`].
  34: //!
  35: //! ## What this layer ships
  36: //!
  37: //! - [`RouteAnnouncement`] — signed claim "I (announcer) can reach
  38: //!   peers {P → `τ_score`, `last_seen_unix`} as of `announced_at_unix`."
  39: //!   Includes a `direct` flag per link so the receiver knows
  40: //!   whether the announcer is offering itself as a relay or just
  41: //!   reporting another device's reachability.
  42: //! - [`RouteTable`] — receiver's aggregated view across all
  43: //!   ingested announcements. Stale announcements get evicted via
  44: //!   the deterministic LWW rule on `announced_at_unix`.
  45: //! - [`pick_best_route`] — max-min-τ_c path finder. Dijkstra-style
  46: //!   variant where the "distance" to a node is the WORST τ on the
  47: //!   path so far; we maximise this floor (equivalent to widest-
  48: //!   path / bottleneck routing).
  49: //! - [`multi_path_plan`] — the K highest-τ_c paths, edge-disjoint
  50: //!   when possible so the receiver can race Wi-Fi vs cellular
  51: //!   vs Ethernet legs.
  52: //! - [`dtn_couriers`] — physical-courier detection: devices that
  53: //!   have been seen near both endpoints within a configurable
  54: //!   time window, even if they're not currently online at the
  55: //!   same time. Sufficient for "tablet flies home and syncs
  56: //!   between desktop and phone."
  57: //!
  58: //! ## What this layer doesn't ship
  59: //!
  60: //! - The actual wire transport (Phase A2 QUIC + the OS networking
  61: //!   stack underneath).
  62: //! - The `τ_c` estimator (Phase D `ol_routing` + Phase E
  63: //!   `ol_coherence_field` provide it; this layer just consumes the
  64: //!   scalar score).
  65: //! - The reachability prober (it's a daemon-level concern; this
  66: //!   layer accepts whatever the prober reports).
  67: 
  68: pub mod announcement;
  69: pub mod dtn;
  70: pub mod route;
  71: pub mod table;
  72: 
  73: pub use announcement::{
  74:     sign_route_announcement, PeerLink, RouteAnnouncement,
  75:     ROUTE_ANNOUNCEMENT_DOMAIN, MAX_LINKS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT,
  76: };
  77: pub use dtn::{dtn_couriers, CourierObservation};
  78: pub use route::{pick_best_route, Route, TauScore};
  79: pub use table::{multi_path_plan, RouteTable};

   1: //! Route + `τ_c` score types.
   2: 
   3: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
   4: 
   5: use super::table::RouteTable;
   6: 
   7: /// Discrete `τ_c` estimate. Higher = better (lower loss + lower
   8: /// latency). Stored as a u32 so the canonical wire format is
   9: /// deterministic and ordering is total.
  10: pub type TauScore = u32;
  11: 
  12: /// Worst-case "no edge known" sentinel — distinct from `TauScore = 0`
  13: /// which means "we know about this edge but it's degraded."
  14: pub const TAU_UNKNOWN: TauScore = 0;
  15: 
  16: /// A resolved route from src to dst.
  17: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  18: pub struct Route {
  19:     /// Hops in order: `hops[0] == src`, `hops.last() == dst`. For a
  20:     /// direct route, `hops == [src, dst]` (length 2).
  21:     pub hops: Vec<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
  22:     /// The minimum `τ_c` across all hops on this path — the
  23:     /// bottleneck score. Higher = better.
  24:     pub bottleneck_tau: TauScore,
  25:     /// Latest of the per-edge `last_seen_unix` values along the
  26:     /// path. Receivers use this to age out stale routes.
  27:     pub min_last_seen_unix: u64,
  28: }
  29: 
  30: impl Route {
  31:     /// Number of hops minus one (the path length).
  32:     #[must_use]
  33:     pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
  34:         self.hops.len().saturating_sub(1)
  35:     }
  36:     /// `true` iff this is a direct `src → dst` route.
  37:     #[must_use]
  38:     pub fn is_direct(&self) -> bool {
  39:         self.length() == 1
  40:     }
  41: }
  42: 
  43: /// Find the maximum-bottleneck-τ path from `src` to `dst` in the
  44: /// given route table.
  45: ///
  46: /// Algorithm: variant of Dijkstra where "distance" is replaced with
  47: /// "smallest τ on the path so far," and we MAXIMIZE that quantity.
  48: /// Equivalent to the widest-path / bottleneck-routing problem,
  49: /// runs in `O((V + E) log V)`.
  50: ///
  51: /// Returns `None` if no path exists.
  52: #[must_use]
  53: pub fn pick_best_route(
  54:     table: &RouteTable,
  55:     src: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  56:     dst: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  57: ) -> Option<Route> {
  58:     use std::collections::{BinaryHeap, BTreeMap};
  59: 
  60:     if src == dst {
  61:         return Some(Route {
  62:             hops: vec![*src],
  63:             bottleneck_tau: TauScore::MAX,
  64:             min_last_seen_unix: u64::MAX,
  65:         });
  66:     }
  67: 
  68:     // best_tau[v] = highest bottleneck-tau seen reaching v.
  69:     let mut best_tau: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], TauScore> = BTreeMap::new();
  70:     let mut best_seen: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u64> = BTreeMap::new();
  71:     let mut prev: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> = BTreeMap::new();
  72: 
  73:     // Max-heap by bottleneck-tau; tie-break on freshness; final
  74:     // tie-break on lex device id so the algorithm is deterministic.
  75:     let mut heap: BinaryHeap<(TauScore, u64, [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN])> = BinaryHeap::new();
  76:     best_tau.insert(*src, TauScore::MAX);
  77:     best_seen.insert(*src, u64::MAX);
  78:     heap.push((TauScore::MAX, u64::MAX, *src));
  79: 
  80:     while let Some((cur_tau, cur_seen, node)) = heap.pop() {
  81:         if cur_tau < *best_tau.get(&node).unwrap_or(&TAU_UNKNOWN) {
  82:             continue;
  83:         }
  84:         if node == *dst {
  85:             break;
  86:         }
  87:         // Find all announcements that mention `node` as the
  88:         // announcer; their links describe `node`'s view of its
  89:         // peers.
  90:         let Some(ann) = table.announcement_for(&node) else {
  91:             continue;
  92:         };
  93:         for link in &ann.links {
  94:             if !link.direct {
  95:                 continue;
  96:             }
  97:             let edge_tau = link.tau_score;
  98:             let edge_seen = link.last_seen_unix;
  99:             let new_bottleneck = cur_tau.min(edge_tau);
 100:             let new_seen = cur_seen.min(edge_seen);
 101:             let prior = best_tau.get(&link.peer_device_id).copied().unwrap_or(TAU_UNKNOWN);
 102:             let prior_seen = best_seen.get(&link.peer_device_id).copied().unwrap_or(0);
 103:             let dominates = new_bottleneck > prior
 104:                 || (new_bottleneck == prior && new_seen > prior_seen);
 105:             if dominates {
 106:                 best_tau.insert(link.peer_device_id, new_bottleneck);
 107:                 best_seen.insert(link.peer_device_id, new_seen);
 108:                 prev.insert(link.peer_device_id, node);
 109:                 heap.push((new_bottleneck, new_seen, link.peer_device_id));
 110:             }
 111:         }
 112:     }
 113: 
 114:     let final_tau = best_tau.get(dst).copied()?;
 115:     let final_seen = best_seen.get(dst).copied().unwrap_or(0);
 116:     let mut hops = vec![*dst];
 117:     let mut cursor = *dst;
 118:     while let Some(p) = prev.get(&cursor) {
 119:         hops.push(*p);
 120:         cursor = *p;
 121:         if cursor == *src {
 122:             break;
 123:         }
 124:     }
 125:     if cursor != *src {
 126:         return None;
 127:     }
 128:     hops.reverse();
 129:     Some(Route {
 130:         hops,
 131:         bottleneck_tau: final_tau,
 132:         min_last_seen_unix: final_seen,
 133:     })
 134: }

 216:         // src → dst direct (tau 30)
 217:         // Best: through `a` with bottleneck 100.
 218:         let (ids, sks, atts, _m) = setup(4);
 219:         let src = ids[0];
 220:         let dst = ids[1];
 221:         let via_a = ids[2];
 222:         let via_b = ids[3];

 224:         // src reaches a (100), b (50), dst direct (30).

 234:             )

 247:         .unwrap();
 248:         // b reaches dst (50).
 249:         table.ingest(

 253:             .unwrap(),
 254:             &vk(&atts[3]),
 255:         )
 256:         .unwrap();
 257:         // dst announces its own reachability.
 258:         table.ingest(
 259:             sign_route_announcement(

 264:         )
 265:         .unwrap();
 266:         let r = pick_best_route(&table, &src, &dst).unwrap();
 267:         // Bottleneck on path src → a → dst is min(100, 100) = 100.

   1: //! Aggregated route table.
   2: //!
   3: //! A [`RouteTable`] is the receiver's view across every ingested
   4: //! [`RouteAnnouncement`]. New announcements from the same announcer
   5: //! REPLACE the prior one when their `announced_at_unix` is strictly
   6: //! greater (LWW); ties on timestamp break to the announcement with
   7: //! the higher `announcer_day_index` so the newer subkey wins.
   8: 
   9: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
  10: 
  11: use ol_pqsig::HybridVerifyingKey;
  12: 
  13: use crate::errors::DeviceMeshResult;
  14: use crate::subkey::DEVICE_ID_LEN;
  15: 
  16: use super::announcement::RouteAnnouncement;
  17: use super::route::{pick_best_route, Route, TauScore, TAU_UNKNOWN};
  18: 
  19: /// Aggregated route view.
  20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  21: pub struct RouteTable {
  22:     announcements: BTreeMap<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], RouteAnnouncement>,
  23: }
  24: 
  25: impl RouteTable {
  26:     /// Empty table.
  27:     #[must_use]
  28:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
  29:         Self::default()
  30:     }
  31: 
  32:     /// Number of announcers we've heard from.
  33:     #[must_use]
  34:     pub fn announcer_count(&self) -> usize {
  35:         self.announcements.len()
  36:     }
  37: 
  38:     /// Borrow the latest announcement for a given announcer.
  39:     #[must_use]
  40:     pub fn announcement_for(
  41:         &self,
  42:         announcer: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  43:     ) -> Option<&RouteAnnouncement> {
  44:         self.announcements.get(announcer)
  45:     }
  46: 
  47:     /// All announcers we've heard from, in deterministic order.
  48:     pub fn announcers(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> {
  49:         self.announcements.keys()
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     /// Ingest a fresh announcement. Verifies the announcer's
  53:     /// signature under the supplied subkey VK; if the announcement
  54:     /// dominates the prior one (newer `announced_at_unix`, or same
  55:     /// timestamp + newer `announcer_day_index`), it replaces it.
  56:     /// Otherwise the call is a no-op.
  57:     ///
  58:     /// Returns `Ok(true)` if the table actually changed.
  59:     pub fn ingest(
  60:         &mut self,
  61:         ann: RouteAnnouncement,
  62:         announcer_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey,
  63:     ) -> DeviceMeshResult<bool> {
  64:         ann.verify(announcer_vk)?;
  65:         let prior = self.announcements.get(&ann.announcer_device_id);
  66:         let dominates = match prior {
  67:             None => true,
  68:             Some(old) => match ann.announced_at_unix.cmp(&old.announced_at_unix) {
  69:                 std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => true,
  70:                 std::cmp::Ordering::Less => false,
  71:                 std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
  72:                     ann.announcer_day_index > old.announcer_day_index
  73:                 }
  74:             },
  75:         };
  76:         if !dominates {
  77:             return Ok(false);
  78:         }
  79:         self.announcements.insert(ann.announcer_device_id, ann);
  80:         Ok(true)
  81:     }
  82: 
  83:     /// Drop announcements older than `max_age_secs` relative to
  84:     /// `now_unix`. Returns the number of entries evicted.
  85:     pub fn prune_stale(&mut self, now_unix: u64, max_age_secs: u64) -> usize {
  86:         let threshold = now_unix.saturating_sub(max_age_secs);
  87:         let before = self.announcements.len();
  88:         self.announcements
  89:             .retain(|_, a| a.announced_at_unix >= threshold);
  90:         before - self.announcements.len()
  91:     }
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /// Find up to `k` highest-bottleneck-τ paths between `src` and
  95: /// `dst`. The first path is the maximum-bottleneck one; subsequent
  96: /// paths are found by removing the bottleneck edge of the prior
  97: /// best path and re-running the picker. Returns fewer than `k`
  98: /// paths if the topology can't supply more disjoint options.
  99: ///
 100: /// Useful for the daemon's "race over Wi-Fi + cellular" mode where
 101: /// the receiver wants distinct physical legs.
 102: #[must_use]
 103: pub fn multi_path_plan(
 104:     table: &RouteTable,
 105:     src: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 106:     dst: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 107:     k: usize,
 108: ) -> Vec<Route> {
 109:     if k == 0 {
 110:         return Vec::new();
 111:     }
 112:     let mut working = table.clone();
 113:     let mut paths = Vec::with_capacity(k);
 114:     for _ in 0..k {
 115:         let Some(r) = pick_best_route(&working, src, dst) else {
 116:             break;
 117:         };
 118:         // Find the bottleneck edge along the path and patch the
 119:         // working table to drop it.
 120:         let bottleneck_edge = find_bottleneck_edge(&r, &working);
 121:         paths.push(r);
 122:         if let Some((u, v)) = bottleneck_edge {
 123:             redact_edge(&mut working, &u, &v);
 124:         } else {
 125:             break; // no edge to remove → no more disjoint paths
 126:         }
 127:     }
 128:     paths
 129: }
 130: 
 131: fn find_bottleneck_edge(
 132:     r: &Route,
 133:     table: &RouteTable,
 134: ) -> Option<([u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN])> {
 135:     if r.hops.len() < 2 {
 136:         return None;
 137:     }
 138:     let mut worst: Option<(TauScore, [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN])> = None;
 139:     for w in r.hops.windows(2) {
 140:         let u = w[0];
 141:         let v = w[1];
 142:         let edge_tau = table
 143:             .announcement_for(&u)
 144:             .map_or(TAU_UNKNOWN, |a| {
 145:                 a.links
 146:                     .iter()
 147:                     .find(|l| l.peer_device_id == v && l.direct)
 148:                     .map_or(TAU_UNKNOWN, |l| l.tau_score)
 149:             });
 150:         match worst {
 151:             None => worst = Some((edge_tau, u, v)),
 152:             Some((cur, _, _)) if edge_tau < cur => worst = Some((edge_tau, u, v)),
 153:             _ => {}
 154:         }
 155:     }
 156:     worst.map(|(_, u, v)| (u, v))
 157: }
 158: 
 159: fn redact_edge(
 160:     table: &mut RouteTable,
 161:     u: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 162:     v: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 163: ) {
 164:     // Remove the (u→v) edge from u's announcement. The bidirectional
 165:     // counterpart (v→u) stays; this just blocks the chosen edge in
 166:     // the FORWARD direction for subsequent multi-path picks.
 167:     if let Some(a) = table.announcements.get_mut(u) {
 168:         a.links
 169:             .retain(|l| !(l.peer_device_id == *v && l.direct));
 170:     }
 171: }

 228:     fn ingest_older_is_no_op() {

   1: //! Per-device subkey and master-signed attestation.
   2: //!
   3: //! A [`DeviceSubkey`] is the working signing key on one physical
   4: //! device. It's a [`ol_pqsig::HybridSigningKey`] derived
   5: //! deterministically from the master seed plus a transcript of
   6: //! `(device_class, device_id, day_index)` — see
   7: //! [`crate::derivation`].
   8: //!
   9: //! Devices NEVER advertise their subkey verifying key directly.
  10: //! Instead the master mints a [`SubkeyAttestation`] that binds:
  11: //! - the subkey's verifying-key bytes,
  12: //! - the device class + ID,
  13: //! - the day index at mint,
  14: //! - an expiry day index (the chain horizon),
  15: //!
  16: //! and signs the whole transcript under the master's hybrid signing
  17: //! key. Friends pin the master pubkey and verify each subkey via the
  18: //! master's signature on the attestation. From a friend's POV there
  19: //! is still ONE identity.
  20: 
  21: use blake3::Hasher;
  22: use ol_pqsig::{HybridSigningKey, HybridVerifyingKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN, HYBRID_VK_LEN};
  23: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  24: use zeroize::ZeroizeOnDrop;
  25: 
  26: use crate::derivation::{
  27:     derive_field_bound_subkey_seed, derive_subkey_seed, SUBKEY_SEED_LEN,
  28: };
  29: use crate::device_class::{DeviceClass, DEVICE_CLASS_TAG_LEN};
  30: use crate::errors::{DeviceMeshError, DeviceMeshResult};
  31: use crate::master::MasterIdentity;
  32: 
  33: /// Length of the per-device identifier.
  34: pub const DEVICE_ID_LEN: usize = 16;
  35: 
  36: /// Domain-separation tag for the subkey-attestation signing transcript.
  37: pub const SUBKEY_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-device-mesh-attestation-v1";
  38: 
  39: /// One device's working signing key. Sized exactly like the master
  40: /// but lives in a single device's RAM and ratchets daily.
  41: #[derive(ZeroizeOnDrop)]
  42: pub struct DeviceSubkey {
  43:     seed: [u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN],
  44:     class: DeviceClass,
  45:     device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  46:     /// Current day index — incremented monotonically by the ratchet.
  47:     day_index: u64,
  48: }
  49: 
  50: impl DeviceSubkey {
  51:     /// Construct directly from a derived seed. Caller is responsible
  52:     /// for using one of the [`mint_subkey`] / [`mint_subkey_field_bound`]
  53:     /// entry points; this is mostly useful in tests + recovery flows.
  54:     #[must_use] 
  55:     pub const fn from_seed(
  56:         seed: [u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN],
  57:         class: DeviceClass,
  58:         device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
  59:         day_index: u64,
  60:     ) -> Self {
  61:         Self {
  62:             seed,
  63:             class,
  64:             device_id,
  65:             day_index,
  66:         }
  67:     }
  68: 
  69:     /// Borrow the device class.
  70:     #[must_use]
  71:     pub const fn class(&self) -> DeviceClass {
  72:         self.class
  73:     }
  74: 
  75:     /// Borrow the device ID.
  76:     #[must_use]
  77:     pub const fn device_id(&self) -> &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN] {
  78:         &self.device_id
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     /// Current day index.
  82:     #[must_use]
  83:     pub const fn day_index(&self) -> u64 {
  84:         self.day_index
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     /// Materialize the underlying signing key (and zeroize the
  88:     /// scratch buffer on drop).
  89:     #[must_use] 
  90:     pub fn signing_key(&self) -> HybridSigningKey {
  91:         HybridSigningKey::from_bytes(&self.seed)
  92:             .expect("subkey seed length is invariant-checked")
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     /// Subkey's verifying key — what the attestation binds.
  96:     #[must_use] 
  97:     pub fn verifying_key(&self) -> HybridVerifyingKey {
  98:         self.signing_key().verifying_key()
  99:     }
 100: 
 101:     /// Sign a message under this subkey.
 102:     pub fn sign(&self, message: &[u8]) -> DeviceMeshResult<[u8; HYBRID_SIG_LEN]> {
 103:         Ok(self.signing_key().sign(message)?)
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     /// Advance the ratchet one day. Zeroizes the prior seed.
 107:     pub fn step_one_day(&mut self) {
 108:         let new_seed = crate::ratchet::ratchet_one_day(&mut self.seed);
 109:         self.seed = new_seed;
 110:         self.day_index = self.day_index.saturating_add(1);
 111:     }
 112: 
 113:     /// Borrow the raw seed (DANGEROUS — only for serialization to
 114:     /// the hardware wrapper).
 115:     #[must_use] 
 116:     pub const fn raw_seed(&self) -> &[u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN] {
 117:         &self.seed
 118:     }
 119: }
