 121: impl std::fmt::Debug for DeviceSubkey {
 122:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 123:         f.debug_struct("DeviceSubkey")
 124:             .field("class", &self.class)
 125:             .field("day_index", &self.day_index)
 126:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 127:     }

 130: /// Master-signed attestation that binds a device subkey's verifying
 131: /// key to the master pubkey. Friends verify each attestation under
 132: /// the master's `HybridVerifyingKey`; the subkey verifying key never
 133: /// needs to be pinned separately.
 134: ///
 135: /// Layout (canonical-bytes form, signed):
 136: ///
 137: /// ```text
 138: /// SUBKEY_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN (29 bytes ASCII)
 139: /// device_class.tag()         (8 bytes)
 140: /// device_id                  (16 bytes)
 141: /// mint_day_index             (8 bytes, big-endian u64)
 142: /// expiry_day_index           (8 bytes, big-endian u64)
 143: /// subkey_vk_bytes            (HYBRID_VK_LEN bytes)
 144: /// ```
 145: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 146: pub struct SubkeyAttestation {
 147:     /// Class of the attested device.
 148:     pub class: DeviceClass,
 149:     /// Device ID.
 150:     pub device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 151:     /// First day the subkey is valid for.
 152:     pub mint_day_index: u64,
 153:     /// Last day the subkey is valid for (chain horizon).
 154:     pub expiry_day_index: u64,
 155:     /// Subkey's hybrid verifying key bytes.
 156:     pub subkey_vk_bytes: Vec<u8>,
 157:     /// Master's hybrid signature over the canonical transcript.
 158:     pub master_sig: Vec<u8>,
 159: }
 160: 
 161: impl SubkeyAttestation {
 162:     /// Canonical bytes the master signs over.
 163:     #[must_use]
 164:     pub fn canonical_transcript(
 165:         class: DeviceClass,
 166:         device_id: &[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 167:         mint_day_index: u64,
 168:         expiry_day_index: u64,
 169:         subkey_vk_bytes: &[u8],
 170:     ) -> Vec<u8> {
 171:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(
 172:             SUBKEY_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN.len()
 173:                 + DEVICE_CLASS_TAG_LEN
 174:                 + DEVICE_ID_LEN
 175:                 + 8
 176:                 + 8
 177:                 + subkey_vk_bytes.len(),
 178:         );
 179:         out.extend_from_slice(SUBKEY_ATTESTATION_DOMAIN);
 180:         out.extend_from_slice(&class.tag());
 181:         out.extend_from_slice(device_id);
 182:         out.extend_from_slice(&mint_day_index.to_be_bytes());
 183:         out.extend_from_slice(&expiry_day_index.to_be_bytes());
 184:         out.extend_from_slice(subkey_vk_bytes);
 185:         out
 186:     }
 187: 
 188:     /// Verify the attestation under the master's verifying key.
 189:     pub fn verify(&self, master_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> DeviceMeshResult<()> {
 190:         if self.subkey_vk_bytes.len() != HYBRID_VK_LEN {
 191:             return Err(DeviceMeshError::BadLength {
 192:                 expected: HYBRID_VK_LEN,
 193:                 got: self.subkey_vk_bytes.len(),
 194:             });
 195:         }
 196:         let transcript = Self::canonical_transcript(
 197:             self.class,
 198:             &self.device_id,
 199:             self.mint_day_index,
 200:             self.expiry_day_index,
 201:             &self.subkey_vk_bytes,
 202:         );
 203:         master_vk
 204:             .verify(&transcript, &self.master_sig)
 205:             .map_err(|_| DeviceMeshError::AttestationVerifyFail)
 206:     }
 207: 
 208:     /// Returns true if `day` falls within the attestation's validity
 209:     /// window.
 210:     #[must_use]
 211:     pub const fn covers_day(&self, day: u64) -> bool {
 212:         day >= self.mint_day_index && day <= self.expiry_day_index
 213:     }
 214: }
 215: 
 216: /// Mint a fresh subkey for `(class, device_id)` at `mint_day_index`
 217: /// and produce the master-signed attestation. The attestation is
 218: /// valid through `expiry_day_index` inclusive.
 219: pub fn mint_subkey(
 220:     master: &MasterIdentity,
 221:     class: DeviceClass,
 222:     device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 223:     mint_day_index: u64,
 224:     expiry_day_index: u64,
 225: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<(DeviceSubkey, SubkeyAttestation)> {
 226:     let seed = derive_subkey_seed(master.seed(), class, &device_id, mint_day_index);
 227:     let subkey = DeviceSubkey::from_seed(seed, class, device_id, mint_day_index);
 228:     let attestation = build_attestation(master, &subkey, mint_day_index, expiry_day_index)?;
 229:     Ok((subkey, attestation))
 230: }
 231: 
 232: /// Mint a field-bound subkey. The subkey's underlying seed is XOR-
 233: /// masked by a BLAKE3 keystream keyed on `field_seed`, so a captured
 234: /// raw subkey is useless without reproducing the field witness.
 235: pub fn mint_subkey_field_bound(
 236:     master: &MasterIdentity,
 237:     class: DeviceClass,
 238:     device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 239:     mint_day_index: u64,
 240:     expiry_day_index: u64,
 241:     field_seed: &[u8; 32],
 242: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<(DeviceSubkey, SubkeyAttestation)> {
 243:     let seed = derive_field_bound_subkey_seed(
 244:         master.seed(),
 245:         class,
 246:         &device_id,
 247:         mint_day_index,
 248:         field_seed,
 249:     );
 250:     let subkey = DeviceSubkey::from_seed(seed, class, device_id, mint_day_index);
 251:     let attestation = build_attestation(master, &subkey, mint_day_index, expiry_day_index)?;
 252:     Ok((subkey, attestation))
 253: }
 254: 
 255: fn build_attestation(
 256:     master: &MasterIdentity,
 257:     subkey: &DeviceSubkey,
 258:     mint_day_index: u64,
 259:     expiry_day_index: u64,
 260: ) -> DeviceMeshResult<SubkeyAttestation> {
 261:     let subkey_vk_bytes = subkey.verifying_key().to_bytes().to_vec();
 262:     let transcript = SubkeyAttestation::canonical_transcript(
 263:         subkey.class,
 264:         subkey.device_id(),
 265:         mint_day_index,
 266:         expiry_day_index,
 267:         &subkey_vk_bytes,
 268:     );
 269:     let master_signing = master.signing_key();
 270:     let master_sig = master_signing.sign(&transcript)?.to_vec();
 271:     Ok(SubkeyAttestation {
 272:         class: subkey.class,
 273:         device_id: *subkey.device_id(),
 274:         mint_day_index,
 275:         expiry_day_index,
 276:         subkey_vk_bytes,
 277:         master_sig,
 278:     })
 279: }
 280: 
 281: /// Re-derive a subkey for an arbitrary day directly from the master.
 282: /// Used in two flows:
 283: ///   1. New device pairing: master fast-forwards to the current day.
 284: ///   2. Forensic recovery: replay a specific day's traffic in support.
 285: ///
 286: /// This is the master-only path; ordinary device operation uses
 287: /// `step_one_day` to advance forward.
 288: #[must_use] 
 289: pub fn redrive_subkey_at_day(
 290:     master: &MasterIdentity,
 291:     class: DeviceClass,
 292:     device_id: [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 293:     day_index: u64,
 294: ) -> DeviceSubkey {
 295:     let seed = derive_subkey_seed(master.seed(), class, &device_id, day_index);
 296:     DeviceSubkey::from_seed(seed, class, device_id, day_index)
 297: }
 298: 
 299: /// RNG-helper: fresh 16-byte device ID.
 300: pub fn fresh_device_id<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> [u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN] {
 301:     let mut id = [0u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 302:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut id);
 303:     id
 304: }
 305: 
 306: /// Convenience: BLAKE3 of the master verifying key (used as the
 307: /// friend-side identity-pin handle).
 308: #[must_use]
 309: pub fn master_pin_handle(master_vk: &HybridVerifyingKey) -> [u8; 32] {
 310:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 311:     h.update(b"OL-device-mesh-master-pin-v1");
 312:     h.update(&master_vk.to_bytes());
 313:     *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 314: }

 172: // ── Field-binding attacks ─────────────────────────────────────────
 173: 
 174: #[test]
 175: fn adversarial_field_bound_seed_unrecoverable_without_witness() {
 176:     // The plain-derivation seed and the field-bound seed must differ
 177:     // for any non-trivial witness, AND the field-bound seed must not
 178:     // appear in plaintext-recoverable form. (We check the strict
 179:     // property: knowing the master + transcript + plain raw seed does
 180:     // NOT reveal the field-bound seed without the witness.)
 181:     let master = [0x42; MASTER_SEED_LEN];
 182:     let id = [0x55; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 183:     let plain = derive_subkey_seed(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, &id, 0);
 184:     let bound = derive_field_bound_subkey_seed(
 185:         &master,
 186:         DeviceClass::Phone,
 187:         &id,
 188:         0,
 189:         &[0xCC; 32],
 190:     );
 191:     assert_ne!(plain, bound);
 192:     // Bonus: bounding under TWO different witnesses yields two distinct
 193:     // bound seeds, both differing from plain.
 194:     let bound_b = derive_field_bound_subkey_seed(
 195:         &master,
 196:         DeviceClass::Phone,
 197:         &id,
 198:         0,
 199:         &[0xDD; 32],
 200:     );
 201:     assert_ne!(bound, bound_b);
 202:     assert_ne!(bound_b, plain);
 203: }
 204: 
 205: // ── Ratchet attacks ───────────────────────────────────────────────
 206: 
 207: #[test]
 208: fn adversarial_ratchet_cannot_recover_prior_day() {
 209:     // Take a subkey at day=5, advance to day=6, confirm day-5 seed
 210:     // is not recoverable from day-6 alone (one-way property).
 211:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
 212:     let id = [0x88; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 213:     let (mut sk, _att) =
 214:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 5, 365).unwrap();
 215:     let day5_seed = *sk.raw_seed();
 216:     sk.step_one_day();
 217:     assert_ne!(sk.raw_seed(), &day5_seed);
 218:     // Master CAN re-derive day 5 (it has the master seed):
 219:     let re_day5 = redrive_subkey_at_day(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 5);
 220:     assert_eq!(re_day5.raw_seed(), &day5_seed);
 221: }

 223: // ── Domain-separation / cross-protocol attacks ────────────────────
 224: 
 225: #[test]
 226: fn adversarial_subkey_seed_independent_of_other_blake3_uses() {
 227:     // Sanity: the subkey-derivation output is bound to its domain
 228:     // string. Two callers that BLAKE3-hash the same transcript but
 229:     // with DIFFERENT domain strings must produce different bytes.
 230:     let master = [0x42; MASTER_SEED_LEN];
 231:     let id = [0x55; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 232:     let real = derive_subkey_seed(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, &id, 0);
 233: 
 234:     // Hand-computed BLAKE3 over the SAME transcript bytes but without
 235:     // the domain tag — must not match.
 236:     let mut h = blake3::Hasher::new();
 237:     h.update(&master);
 238:     h.update(&DeviceClass::Phone.tag());
 239:     h.update(&id);
 240:     h.update(&0u64.to_be_bytes());
 241:     let mut naive = [0u8; SUBKEY_SEED_LEN];
 242:     naive[..32].copy_from_slice(h.finalize().as_bytes());
 243:     naive[32..].copy_from_slice(h.finalize().as_bytes());
 244:     assert_ne!(real, naive);
 245: }

 138: #[test]
 139: fn adversarial_record_history_drift_under_intermittent_decay() {
 140:     // Bias toward laptop, then sweep decay, then bias toward phone.
 141:     // The picker should track the most recent signal.
 142:     let mut h = RoutingHistory::empty();
 143:     let ctx_hash = ctx().canonical_hash();
 144:     // Phase 1: laptop wins.
 145:     for _ in 0..200 {
 146:         h.observe(ctx_hash, [0x02; DEVICE_ID_LEN], true, 100, 1, 1);
 147:         h.observe(ctx_hash, [0x01; DEVICE_ID_LEN], false, 100, 1, 1);
 148:     }
 149:     // Aggressive decay (one half-life).
 150:     h.decay_all(160, 60);
 151:     // Phase 2: phone wins.
 152:     for _ in 0..200 {
 153:         h.observe(ctx_hash, [0x01; DEVICE_ID_LEN], true, 200, 1, 1);
 154:         h.observe(ctx_hash, [0x02; DEVICE_ID_LEN], false, 200, 1, 1);
 155:     }
 156:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0x77; 32]);
 157:     let candidates = vec![
 158:         ([0x01u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Phone),
 159:         ([0x02u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Laptop),
 160:     ];
 161:     let mut phone_picks = 0;
 162:     let trials = 200;
 163:     for _ in 0..trials {
 164:         if let Some(p) = pick_device_for_context(
 165:             &ctx(),
 166:             &candidates,
 167:             &h,
 168:             &CohortPrior::uniform(),
 169:             &mut rng,
 170:         ) {
 171:             if p == [0x01; DEVICE_ID_LEN] {
 172:                 phone_picks += 1;
 173:             }
 174:         }
 175:     }
 176:     // After decay + phase 2, phone should dominate.
 177:     assert!(
 178:         phone_picks > trials * 6 / 10,
 179:         "phone {phone_picks}/{trials} — decay didn't track drift"
 180:     );
 181: }

 150: #[test]
 151: fn adversarial_repair_plan_load_balanced() {
 152:     // 4 chunks needing 2 new holders each across a 4-device mesh.
 153:     // Total assignments = 8 across 4 devices = 2 each (load-balanced).
 154:     let policy = ErasurePolicy::new(2, 1, 2).unwrap();
 155:     let mesh: BTreeSet<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]> =
 156:         (1u8..=4).map(|i| [i; DEVICE_ID_LEN]).collect();
 157:     let placements: Vec<ChunkPlacement> = (0u8..4)
 158:         .map(|i| ChunkPlacement::empty([i; 32]))
 159:         .collect();
 160:     let plan = repair_plan(placements.iter(), &mesh, &policy);
 161:     assert_eq!(plan.len(), 8);
 162:     let mut device_counts = std::collections::BTreeMap::<[u8; 16], usize>::new();
 163:     for a in &plan {
 164:         *device_counts.entry(a.assigned_to).or_default() += 1;
 165:     }
 166:     // Each of the 4 mesh devices got 2 assignments.
 167:     for d in &mesh {
 168:         assert_eq!(*device_counts.get(d).unwrap_or(&0), 2);
 169:     }
 170: }

  15: #[test]
  16: fn adversarial_captor_with_disk_image_only_unlocks_decoy() {
  17:     // The captor has the envelope bytes + types the user's REAL
  18:     // code (because they coerced it out of the user). WITHOUT the
  19:     // field witness, they still only recover the decoy at best —
  20:     // and probably nothing.
  21:     let witness = [0x42; 32];
  22:     let env = create_duress_envelope(
  23:         b"REAL secrets the captor must not see",
  24:         b"decoy fake plausible state",
  25:         b"real-pass",
  26:         b"duress-code",
  27:         &witness,
  28:         &mut OsRng,
  29:     )
  30:     .unwrap();
  31:     // Captor types the real code WITHOUT the witness.
  32:     let outcome = unlock_duress_envelope(&env, b"real-pass", None).unwrap();
  33:     assert!(matches!(outcome, UnlockOutcome::WrongCode));
  34: }

 259: #[test]
 260: fn adversarial_progress_source_failure_releases_in_flight() {
 261:     use ol_device_mesh::fan_out::plan::{FanOutAssignment, FanOutPlan};
 262:     let chunks: Vec<ChunkHash> = (1u8..=6).map(|i| [i; 32]).collect();
 263:     let m = manifest_for(chunks);
 264:     let plan = FanOutPlan {
 265:         file_id: [0xAA; FILE_ID_LEN],
 266:         assignments: vec![
 267:             FanOutAssignment {
 268:                 source_device_id: [1; 16],
 269:                 chunk_hashes: vec![[1; 32], [2; 32], [3; 32]],
 270:                 estimated_bytes: 3,
 271:             },
 272:             FanOutAssignment {
 273:                 source_device_id: [2; 16],
 274:                 chunk_hashes: vec![[4; 32], [5; 32], [6; 32]],
 275:                 estimated_bytes: 3,
 276:             },
 277:         ],
 278:         total_chunks: 6,
 279:     };
 280:     let mut prog = TransferProgress::new(plan, &m);
 281:     prog.mark_in_flight([1; 32], [1; 16]);
 282:     prog.mark_in_flight([2; 32], [1; 16]);
 283:     prog.mark_in_flight([4; 32], [2; 16]);
 284:     let released = prog.mark_source_failed([1; 16]);
 285:     assert_eq!(released.len(), 2);
 286:     // Chunks from source 2 remain in flight.
 287:     assert!(prog.in_flight_chunks.contains_key(&[4; 32]));
 288:     // After failure, source 1's chunks count as pending again (but
 289:     // they were already removed from in_flight). pending() excludes
 290:     // the failed-source assignments entirely.
 291:     let pending = prog.pending();
 292:     for c in &pending {
 293:         assert!(c[0] >= 4);
 294:     }
 295: }

 165: #[test]
 166: fn adversarial_attestation_substitution_rejected() {
 167:     // Two masters mint subkeys for the same device_id; attacker
 168:     // substitutes their master's attestation into a certificate
 169:     // signed under the real master's policy.
 170:     let real_master = make_master();
 171:     let fake_master = make_master();
 172:     let id1 = [0x11; 16];
 173:     let id2 = [0x22; 16];
 174:     let id3 = [0x33; 16];
 175:     let (sk1, _a1_real) =
 176:         mint_subkey(&real_master, DeviceClass::Phone, id1, 0, 365).unwrap();
 177:     let (_sk1_fake, a1_fake) =
 178:         mint_subkey(&fake_master, DeviceClass::Phone, id1, 0, 365).unwrap();
 179:     let (sk2, a2) =
 180:         mint_subkey(&real_master, DeviceClass::Laptop, id2, 0, 365).unwrap();
 181:     let (sk3, a3) =
 182:         mint_subkey(&real_master, DeviceClass::Desktop, id3, 0, 365).unwrap();
 183:     let policy =
 184:         mint_policy(&real_master, [0xAA; 16], b"p", 2, vec![id1, id2, id3]).unwrap();
 185:     let now: u64 = 1_700_000_000;
 186:     let proposal = propose_operation(
 187:         &sk1, &policy, [0xEE; 32], [0xDA; 16], now, now + 3600,
 188:     )
 189:     .unwrap();
 190:     let ap2 = sign_approval(&sk2, &proposal, now + 1).unwrap();
 191:     let ap3 = sign_approval(&sk3, &proposal, now + 2).unwrap();
 192:     let cert = QuorumCertificate {
 193:         proposal,
 194:         approvals: vec![ap2, ap3],
 195:         policy,
 196:         // Use the FAKE master's attestation for device id1.
 197:         subkey_attestations: vec![a1_fake, a2, a3],
 198:     };
 199:     let err = cert
 200:         .verify(&real_master.verifying_key(), now + 100)
 201:         .unwrap_err();
 202:     // Fake attestation fails master verification first.
 203:     assert!(matches!(err, DeviceMeshError::AttestationVerifyFail));
 204: }

 239: fn adversarial_cross_policy_certificate_rejected() {
 240:     // Build TWO policies under the same master; attacker stuffs the
 241:     // wrong policy into the certificate.

 247:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id1, 0, 365).unwrap();
 248:     let (sk2, a2) =
 249:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Laptop, id2, 0, 365).unwrap();
 250:     let (_sk3, a3) =
 251:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Desktop, id3, 0, 365).unwrap();
 252:     let policy_a =
 253:         mint_policy(&master, [0xAA; 16], b"a", 1, vec![id1, id2, id3]).unwrap();
 254:     let policy_b =

 273: #[test]
 274: fn adversarial_revoked_device_rotated_attestation_still_required() {
 275:     // Sibling key gets rotated. An OLD attestation for a previous
 276:     // day shouldn't cover an approval the device signed at a NEW
 277:     // day index.
 278:     let master = make_master();
 279:     let id1 = [0x11; 16];
 280:     let id2 = [0x22; 16];
 281:     let (sk1, a1) =
 282:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id1, 0, 365).unwrap();
 283:     let (mut sk2, a2_initial) =
 284:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Laptop, id2, 0, 0).unwrap();
 285:     // Day-0 attestation only covers day 0. sk2 advances to day 1.
 286:     sk2.step_one_day();
 287:     assert_eq!(sk2.day_index(), 1);
 288:     let policy =
 289:         mint_policy(&master, [0xAA; 16], b"p", 1, vec![id1, id2]).unwrap();
 290:     let now: u64 = 1_700_000_000;
 291:     let proposal = propose_operation(
 292:         &sk1, &policy, [0xEE; 32], [0xDA; 16], now, now + 3600,
 293:     )
 294:     .unwrap();
 295:     let approval = sign_approval(&sk2, &proposal, now + 1).unwrap();
 296:     let cert = QuorumCertificate {
 297:         proposal,
 298:         approvals: vec![approval],
 299:         policy,
 300:         subkey_attestations: vec![a1, a2_initial], // only covers day 0
 301:     };
 302:     let err = cert.verify(&master.verifying_key(), now + 100).unwrap_err();
 303:     assert!(matches!(err, DeviceMeshError::AttestationMissing { .. }));
 304: }

  12: fn registry_for(n: usize) -> (
  13:     MasterIdentity,
  14:     Vec<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
  15:     Vec<OnionIdentity>,
  16:     OnionKeyRegistry,
  17: ) {
  18:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  19:     let mut ids = Vec::new();
  20:     let mut identities = Vec::new();
  21:     let mut reg = OnionKeyRegistry::empty();
  22:     for i in 1u8..=(n as u8) {
  23:         let id = [i; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
  24:         let identity = derive_onion_identity(&master, &id);
  25:         let att = sign_onion_attestation(
  26:             &master, id, identity.public_bytes(), 0, 365,
  27:         )
  28:         .unwrap();
  29:         reg.ingest(att, &master.verifying_key()).unwrap();
  30:         ids.push(id);
  31:         identities.push(identity);
  32:     }
  33:     (master, ids, identities, reg)
  34: }

 174: fn adversarial_packet_carrying_non_self_onion_payload_dropped() {

 176:     // carry the OL-mesh-self-onion-v1 prefix. peel_self_onion_layer

 208: fn make_three() -> (
 209:     Vec<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>,
 210:     Vec<ol_device_mesh::DeviceSubkey>,
 211:     Vec<HybridVerifyingKey>,
 212: ) {
 213:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
 214:     let mut ids = Vec::new();

 220:         let vk = HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&att.subkey_vk_bytes).unwrap();
 221:         ids.push(id);
 222:         sks.push(sk);
 223:         vks.push(vk);
 224:     }
 225:     (ids, sks, vks)
 226: }

  36: #[test]
  37: fn adversarial_v2_attestation_with_mint_day_equal_expiry_rejected() {
  38:     // A 1-day attestation is theoretically valid (mint == expiry
  39:     // means valid only on `mint_day_index`). But mint_day_index > 0
  40:     // with the same expiry day should NOT cover later days — the
  41:     // covers_day check must be strict.
  42:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  43:     let id = fresh_device_id(&mut OsRng);
  44:     let (_sk, att) = mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 10, 10).unwrap();
  45:     assert!(att.covers_day(10));
  46:     assert!(!att.covers_day(11));
  47:     assert!(!att.covers_day(9));
  48: }
  49: 
  50: #[test]
  51: fn adversarial_v2_subkey_minted_for_future_day() {
  52:     // Mint a subkey for a far-future day (clock skew or attacker
  53:     // future-dating). The attestation should still verify (day
  54:     // index is just an integer), but covers_day(today) is false.
  55:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  56:     let id = fresh_device_id(&mut OsRng);
  57:     let (_sk, att) =
  58:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 100_000, 100_365).unwrap();
  59:     att.verify(&master.verifying_key()).unwrap();
  60:     assert!(!att.covers_day(0));
  61:     assert!(att.covers_day(100_000));
  62: }

   1: //! Constant-time validation for the liveness-proof verify path.
   2: //!
   3: //! `verify_liveness` does:
   4: //!   1. signature verify under the witness subkey VK (ol_pqsig, uniform
   5: //!      across tamper position — see row 1's own ct gate)
   6: //!   2. clock-skew check (after the signature so the timing branch
   7: //!      never reaches a forged proof)
   8: //!
   9: //! This gate measures total wall-clock variance across 5 tamper
  10: //! positions in the subkey signature. Gate at 30% relative stddev —
  11: //! the residual baseline comes from ML-DSA-internal data-dependent
  12: //! verify variance (a property of the upstream `ml-dsa` crate, not
  13: //! our layer). If upstream tightens to strict CT verify later, this
  14: //! gate tightens too.
  15: 
  16: use std::time::Instant;
  17: 
  18: use ol_device_mesh::{
  19:     mint_subkey, sibling_witness, state_root, verify_liveness, DeviceClass,
  20:     LivenessProof, MasterIdentity, DEFAULT_LIVENESS_SKEW_SECS,
  21: };
  22: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  23: 
  24: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 200;
  25: 
  26: fn relative_stddev(samples: &[f64]) -> f64 {
  27:     let mean: f64 = samples.iter().sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  28:     let variance: f64 =
  29:         samples.iter().map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  30:     variance.sqrt() / mean
  31: }
  32: 
  33: fn measure<F: FnMut()>(mut work: F, iters: usize) -> u128 {
  34:     let start = Instant::now();
  35:     for _ in 0..iters {
  36:         work();
  37:     }
  38:     start.elapsed().as_nanos()
  39: }
  40: 
  41: #[test]
  42: fn liveness_verify_constant_time_across_tamper_positions() {
  43:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  44:     let id = [0x55u8; 16];
  45:     let (sk, _att) =
  46:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 0, 365).unwrap();
  47:     let witness = sibling_witness(sk.verifying_key(), DEFAULT_LIVENESS_SKEW_SECS);
  48:     let now = 1_700_000_000u64;
  49:     let real = LivenessProof::issue(&sk, now, state_root(b"state")).unwrap();
  50:     let sig_len = real.subkey_sig.len();
  51: 
  52:     // Tamper positions across the signature: early Ed25519, mid
  53:     // Ed25519, last Ed25519, early ML-DSA, last ML-DSA.
  54:     let positions = [
  55:         0usize,
  56:         32,
  57:         63,
  58:         64,
  59:         sig_len - 1,
  60:     ];
  61: 
  62:     let mut tampered: Vec<LivenessProof> = positions
  63:         .iter()
  64:         .map(|&pos| {
  65:             let mut p = real.clone();
  66:             p.subkey_sig[pos] ^= 0x01;
  67:             p
  68:         })
  69:         .collect();
  70: 
  71:     // Warm-up.
  72:     for proof in &tampered {
  73:         let _ = measure(|| {
  74:             let _ = verify_liveness(proof, &witness, now);
  75:         }, 5);
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(tampered.len());
  79:     for proof in &mut tampered {
  80:         let ns = measure(
  81:             || {
  82:                 let _ = std::hint::black_box(verify_liveness(
  83:                     std::hint::black_box(proof),
  84:                     std::hint::black_box(&witness),
  85:                     now,
  86:                 ));
  87:             },
  88:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  89:         ) as f64;
  90:         totals.push(ns);
  91:     }
  92:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
  93:     eprintln!(
  94:         "liveness-verify timing totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}"
  95:     );
  96:     // 30% gate matches row 1's pqsig::verify ct-gate (this verify
  97:     // delegates to it).
  98:     assert!(
  99:         rel < 0.30,
 100:         "liveness verify relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 30% gate — \
 101:          likely a short-circuit regression in verify_liveness"
 102:     );
 103: }

  35: #[test]
  36: fn quorum_certificate_verify_constant_time_across_approval_tamper() {
  37:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  38:     let id1 = [0x11u8; 16];
  39:     let id2 = [0x22u8; 16];
  40:     let id3 = [0x33u8; 16];
  41:     let (sk1, a1) =
  42:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id1, 0, 365).unwrap();
  43:     let (sk2, a2) =
  44:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Laptop, id2, 0, 365).unwrap();
  45:     let (sk3, a3) =
  46:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Desktop, id3, 0, 365).unwrap();
  47:     let policy =
  48:         mint_policy(&master, [0xAA; 16], b"p", 2, vec![id1, id2, id3]).unwrap();
  49:     let now: u64 = 1_700_000_000;
  50:     let proposal = propose_operation(
  51:         &sk1, &policy, [0xEE; 32], [0xDA; 16], now, now + 3600,
  52:     )
  53:     .unwrap();
  54:     let ap2 = sign_approval(&sk2, &proposal, now + 60).unwrap();
  55:     let ap3 = sign_approval(&sk3, &proposal, now + 120).unwrap();

  58:         proposal,
  59:         approvals: vec![ap2, ap3],
  60:         policy,
  61:         subkey_attestations: vec![a1, a2, a3],
  62:     };
  63: 
  64:     // Five tamper positions in the first approval's signature.
  65:     let sig_len = base_cert.approvals[0].approver_sig.len();
  66:     let positions = [0usize, 32, 63, 64, sig_len - 1];
  67: 
  68:     let mut variants: Vec<QuorumCertificate> = positions
  69:         .iter()
  70:         .map(|&pos| {
  71:             let mut c = base_cert.clone();
  72:             c.approvals[0].approver_sig[pos] ^= 0x01;
  73:             c
  74:         })
  75:         .collect();
  76: 
  77:     // Warm-up.
  78:     for cert in &variants {
  79:         let _ = measure(
  80:             || {
  81:                 let _ = cert.verify(&master.verifying_key(), now + 200);
  82:             },
  83:             5,
  84:         );
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(variants.len());
  88:     for cert in &mut variants {

  90:             || {
  91:                 let _ = std::hint::black_box(cert.verify(
  92:                     std::hint::black_box(&master.verifying_key()),
  93:                     now + 200,
  94:                 ));
  95:             },
  96:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  97:         ) as f64;
  98:         totals.push(ns);

   1: //! Cross-layer integration tests for Row 8.

   3: //! Each test exercises 3+ layers together to flush out
   4: //! layer-interaction bugs (wrong byte alignments, wrong key

   7: //! catch ~95% of bugs; cross-layer tests catch the rest.

  40: /// 3-device mesh fixture: master + phone + laptop + desktop
  41: /// subkeys, all attested.
  42: struct ThreeDeviceMesh {
  43:     master: MasterIdentity,
  44:     device_ids: [[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]; 3],
  45:     subkeys: Vec<ol_device_mesh::subkey::DeviceSubkey>,
  46:     attestations: Vec<SubkeyAttestation>,
  47: }
  48: 
  49: impl ThreeDeviceMesh {
  50:     fn new() -> Self {
  51:         let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  52:         let mut device_ids = [[0u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]; 3];
  53:         let mut subkeys = Vec::new();
  54:         let mut attestations = Vec::new();
  55:         let classes = [DeviceClass::Phone, DeviceClass::Laptop, DeviceClass::Desktop];
  56:         for (i, class) in classes.into_iter().enumerate() {
  57:             let id = fresh_device_id(&mut OsRng);
  58:             device_ids[i] = id;
  59:             let (sk, att) = mint_subkey(&master, class, id, 0, 365).unwrap();
  60:             subkeys.push(sk);
  61:             attestations.push(att);
  62:         }
  63:         Self {
  64:             master,
  65:             device_ids,
  66:             subkeys,
  67:             attestations,
  68:         }
  69:     }
  70:     fn vk_for(&self, idx: usize) -> HybridVerifyingKey {
  71:         assert_eq!(self.attestations[idx].subkey_vk_bytes.len(), HYBRID_VK_LEN);
  72:         HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&self.attestations[idx].subkey_vk_bytes).unwrap()
  73:     }
  74: }

  77: fn layer1_to_layer2_quorum_certificate_round_trips() {
  78:     // Layer 1 mints 3 device subkeys.
  79:     // Layer 2 builds a 2-of-3 quorum cert that verifies end-to-end
  80:     // under the original master.
  81:     let mesh = ThreeDeviceMesh::new();
  82:     let policy = mint_policy(
  83:         &mesh.master,
  84:         [0x11; 16],
  85:         b"shared-folder-policy",
  86:         2,
  87:         mesh.device_ids.to_vec(),
  88:     )
  89:     .unwrap();
  90:     let proposal = propose_operation(
  91:         &mesh.subkeys[0],
  92:         &policy,
  93:         [0xAA; 32],
  94:         [0x33; 16],
  95:         100,
  96:         2000,
  97:     )
  98:     .unwrap();
  99:     let approval_b = sign_approval(&mesh.subkeys[1], &proposal, 110).unwrap();
 100:     let approval_c = sign_approval(&mesh.subkeys[2], &proposal, 120).unwrap();
 101:     let cert = QuorumCertificate {
 102:         policy,
 103:         proposal,
 104:         approvals: vec![approval_b, approval_c],
 105:         subkey_attestations: mesh.attestations.clone(),
 106:     };
 107:     cert.verify(&mesh.master.verifying_key(), 150).unwrap();
 108: }

 110: #[test]
 111: fn layer3_mesh_state_ingest_with_layer1_subkey() {
 112:     // Layer 1: mint a phone subkey.
 113:     // Layer 3: ingest a signed LWW write into MeshState; confirm the
 114:     // verify-by-subkey path resolves correctly.
 115:     let mesh = ThreeDeviceMesh::new();
 116:     let mut state = MeshState::empty();
 117:     state
 118:         .ensure_subtree(b"folder.alpha".to_vec(), SubtreePolicyKind::LwwRegister)
 119:         .unwrap();
 120:     let mut sync = SyncState::empty();
 121:     let op = AuthenticatedOp::sign(
 122:         &mesh.subkeys[0],
 123:         b"folder.alpha".to_vec(),
 124:         Delta::LwwSet {
 125:             value: b"hello mesh".to_vec(),
 126:             ts: 100,
 127:         },
 128:         1,
 129:         1,
 130:     )
 131:     .unwrap();
 132:     let phone_vk = mesh.vk_for(0);
 133:     let phone_id = mesh.device_ids[0];
 134:     let phone_vk_for_lookup = phone_vk.clone();
 135:     let applied = sync
 136:         .ingest(op, &mut state, |id, _day| {
 137:             assert_eq!(id, &phone_id, "ingest should resolve VK for emitter id");
 138:             Ok(phone_vk_for_lookup.clone())
 139:         })
 140:         .unwrap();
 141:     assert!(applied);
 142:     // Verify the value landed in the subtree.
 143:     let subtree = state.subtree(b"folder.alpha").unwrap();
 144:     let bytes = subtree.root();
 145:     assert!(bytes.iter().any(|b| *b != 0));
 146: }

 148: #[test]
 149: fn layer4_to_layer5_manifest_drives_fan_out_plan() {
 150:     // Layer 4: build a 6-chunk manifest with 2+1 erasure (3 shards
 151:     // per stripe → 6 chunks total covers 2 stripes).
 152:     // Layer 5: fan-out plan distributes chunks across 2 source devices.
 153:     let mesh = ThreeDeviceMesh::new();
 154:     let policy = ErasurePolicy::new(2, 1, 1).unwrap();
 155:     let chunks: Vec<ChunkHash> = (0..6u8).map(|i| [i; 32]).collect();
 156:     let manifest = FileManifest {
 157:         file_size: 6 * 1024,
 158:         chunk_size: 1024,
 159:         chunks: chunks.clone(),
 160:         mime: b"text/plain".to_vec(),
 161:         created_unix: 1_700_000_000,
 162:         policy,
 163:     };
 164:     manifest.shape_check().unwrap();
 165:     let file_id = manifest.file_id();
 166:     assert_eq!(file_id.len(), FILE_ID_LEN);
 167: 
 168:     let placements: Vec<ChunkPlacement> = chunks
 169:         .iter()
 170:         .map(|c| {
 171:             let mut set = BTreeSet::new();
 172:             set.insert(mesh.device_ids[0]);
 173:             set.insert(mesh.device_ids[1]);
 174:             ChunkPlacement {
 175:                 chunk_hash: *c,
 176:                 device_ids: set,
 177:                 last_attest_unix: 100,
 178:             }
 179:         })
 180:         .collect();
 181: 
 182:     let sources = vec![
 183:         SourceCapacity {
 184:             device_id: mesh.device_ids[0],
 185:             estimated_bps: 5_000_000,
 186:             current_load_bytes: 0,
 187:         },
 188:         SourceCapacity {
 189:             device_id: mesh.device_ids[1],
 190:             estimated_bps: 5_000_000,
 191:             current_load_bytes: 0,
 192:         },
 193:     ];
 194:     let plan = fan_out_plan(&manifest, &placements, &sources, 1.0).unwrap();
 195:     let counts: BTreeMap<_, _> = plan
 196:         .assignments
 197:         .iter()
 198:         .map(|a| (a.source_device_id, a.chunk_hashes.len()))
 199:         .collect();
 200:     // Two stripes of (k=2, m=1) = 3 shards each; only k=2 per stripe
 201:     // needs fetching → 4 chunks total assigned across the 2 sources.
 202:     let total: usize = counts.values().sum();
 203:     assert_eq!(total, 4, "expected 4 (k=2 per stripe × 2 stripes), got {total}");
 204:     // Both sources should get some work given equal capacity.
 205:     assert!(
 206:         counts.values().all(|&n| n > 0),
 207:         "expected both sources assigned chunks: {counts:?}"
 208:     );
 209: }

 232: #[test]
 233: fn layer6_self_routing_then_layer9_records_observation() {
 234:     // Layer 1 mints 3 subkeys → Layer 6 device A announces a 2-link
 235:     // table → Layer 9 records routing observations under a context
 236:     // and picks via Beta-posterior Thompson sampling.
 237:     let mesh = ThreeDeviceMesh::new();
 238:     let a = &mesh.subkeys[0];
 239:     let a_id = mesh.device_ids[0];
 240:     let b_id = mesh.device_ids[1];
 241:     let c_id = mesh.device_ids[2];
 242: 
 243:     // A announces direct links A→B (τ=50) and A→C (τ=100).
 244:     let ann = sign_route_announcement(
 245:         a,
 246:         100,
 247:         vec![
 248:             PeerLink {
 249:                 peer_device_id: b_id,
 250:                 tau_score: 50,
 251:                 last_seen_unix: 100,
 252:                 direct: true,
 253:             },
 254:             PeerLink {
 255:                 peer_device_id: c_id,
 256:                 tau_score: 100,
 257:                 last_seen_unix: 100,
 258:                 direct: true,
 259:             },
 260:         ],
 261:     )
 262:     .unwrap();
 263:     let a_vk = mesh.vk_for(0);
 264:     let mut table = RouteTable::empty();
 265:     table.ingest(ann, &a_vk).unwrap();
 266:     let route = pick_best_route(&table, &a_id, &c_id).unwrap();
 267:     assert_eq!(route.hops, vec![a_id, c_id]);
 268: 
 269:     // Layer 9 observation + picker.
 270:     let ctx = RoutingContext {
 271:         contact_pin: [1; 32],
 272:         hour_bucket: 9,
 273:         day_of_week: 2,
 274:         message_class: *b"DM  ",
 275:         urgency: 1,
 276:     };
 277:     let ctx_hash = ctx.canonical_hash();
 278:     let mut history = RoutingHistory::empty();
 279:     for _ in 0..40 {
 280:         history.observe(ctx_hash, c_id, true, 1, 1, 1);
 281:     }
 282:     let candidates = vec![
 283:         (b_id, DeviceClass::Laptop),
 284:         (c_id, DeviceClass::Desktop),
 285:     ];
 286:     let cohort = CohortPrior::uniform();
 287:     let mut c_count = 0;
 288:     for _ in 0..200 {
 289:         if let Some(pick) =
 290:             pick_device_for_context(&ctx, &candidates, &history, &cohort, &mut OsRng)
 291:         {
 292:             if pick == c_id {
 293:                 c_count += 1;
 294:             }
 295:         }
 296:     }
 297:     assert!(c_count >= 150, "C won only {c_count}/200; expected ≥150");
 298: }

 329:         .unwrap(),

   1: //! Proptest-driven stress harness mirroring the cargo-fuzz targets.
   2: //!
   3: //! The shipped `fuzz_device_mesh_*` targets under `native/fuzz/` need
   4: //! cargo-fuzz + nightly + a permission-unrestricted machine. Windows
   5: //! Smart App Control blocks the cargo-fuzz binary on consumer
   6: //! installs, so on those hosts we drive the same fuzz-target bodies
   7: //! through proptest at high iteration counts inside the normal
   8: //! `cargo test` harness.
   9: //!
  10: //! This is not a replacement for libfuzzer (no coverage-guided
  11: //! mutation, no SanitizerCoverage hits, no corpus minimization), but
  12: //! it does exercise the same surface with structured random bytes,
  13: //! which catches the bulk of "must never panic on arbitrary input"
  14: //! issues. CI runs the real libfuzzer harness on Linux.
  15: 
  16: use proptest::prelude::*;
  17: use rand::SeedableRng;
  18: use rand_chacha::ChaCha20Rng;
  19: 
  20: use ol_device_mesh::active_routing::{
  21:     pick_device_for_context, CohortPrior, DeviceActionRecord, RoutingContext,
  22:     RoutingHistory,
  23: };
  24: use ol_device_mesh::compute::{
  25:     pick_executor, sign_capability_attestation, CapabilityRegistry, DeviceCapability,
  26: };
  27: use ol_device_mesh::distributed_fs::{
  28:     sign_storage_attestation, ChunkHash, ErasurePolicy, FileManifest, FILE_ID_LEN,
  29: };
  30: use ol_device_mesh::duress::{
  31:     sign_duress_alert, verify_pairing_cross_channel, PairingChannel, PairingCommitment,
  32: };
  33: use ol_device_mesh::fan_out::{
  34:     fan_out_plan, sign_fetch_request, SourceCapacity, FETCH_NONCE_LEN,
  35: };
  36: use ol_device_mesh::mesh_state::{AuthenticatedOp, Delta, MeshState, SyncState};
  37: use ol_device_mesh::quorum::{
  38:     mint_policy, propose_operation, sign_approval, QuorumCertificate,
  39: };
  40: use ol_device_mesh::self_onion::{
  41:     build_self_onion_circuit, derive_onion_identity, peel_self_onion_layer,

  52: fn stress_cases() -> u32 {
  53:     if std::env::var("ONE_LINK_F1_GATE").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
  54:         500_000
  55:     } else {
  56:         100_000
  57:     }
  58: }

  60: // ── Attestation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  61: 
  62: fn fuzz_attestation_body(data: &[u8]) {
  63:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA1u8; 32]);
  64:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
  65:     let (_sk, mut att) =
  66:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, [0x55; 16], 0, 365).unwrap();
  67:     if !data.is_empty() {
  68:         let pick = data[0] % 5;
  69:         let body = &data[1..];
  70:         match pick {
  71:             0 => {
  72:                 let n = body.len().min(att.master_sig.len());
  73:                 att.master_sig[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
  74:             }
  75:             1 => {
  76:                 let n = body.len().min(att.subkey_vk_bytes.len());
  77:                 att.subkey_vk_bytes[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
  78:             }
  79:             2 if body.len() >= 8 => {
  80:                 let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
  81:                 buf.copy_from_slice(&body[..8]);
  82:                 att.mint_day_index = u64::from_be_bytes(buf);
  83:             }
  84:             3 if body.len() >= 8 => {
  85:                 let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
  86:                 buf.copy_from_slice(&body[..8]);
  87:                 att.expiry_day_index = u64::from_be_bytes(buf);
  88:             }
  89:             _ if !body.is_empty() => {
  90:                 let n = body.len().min(att.device_id.len());
  91:                 att.device_id[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
  92:             }
  93:             _ => {}
  94:         }
  95:     }
  96:     let _ = att.verify(&master.verifying_key());
  97: }
  98: 
  99: // ── Quorum ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 100: 
 101: fn fuzz_quorum_body(data: &[u8]) {
 102:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA2u8; 32]);
 103:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 104:     let id1 = [0x11u8; 16];
 105:     let id2 = [0x22u8; 16];
 106:     let id3 = [0x33u8; 16];
 107:     let (sk1, a1) =
 108:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id1, 0, 365).unwrap();
 109:     let (sk2, a2) =
 110:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Laptop, id2, 0, 365).unwrap();
 111:     let (sk3, a3) =
 112:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Desktop, id3, 0, 365).unwrap();
 113:     let policy =
 114:         mint_policy(&master, [0x42; 16], b"fuzz", 2, vec![id1, id2, id3]).unwrap();
 115:     let now: u64 = 1_700_000_000;
 116:     let proposal = propose_operation(
 117:         &sk1, &policy, [0xEE; 32], [0xDA; 16], now, now + 3600,
 118:     )
 119:     .unwrap();
 120:     let ap2 = sign_approval(&sk2, &proposal, now + 1).unwrap();
 121:     let ap3 = sign_approval(&sk3, &proposal, now + 2).unwrap();
 122:     let mut cert = QuorumCertificate {
 123:         proposal,
 124:         approvals: vec![ap2, ap3],
 125:         policy,
 126:         subkey_attestations: vec![a1, a2, a3],
 127:     };
 128:     if !data.is_empty() {
 129:         let pick = data[0] % 5;
 130:         let body = &data[1..];
 131:         match pick {
 132:             0 if !body.is_empty() => {
 133:                 let n = body.len().min(cert.proposal.issuer_sig.len());
 134:                 cert.proposal.issuer_sig[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
 135:             }
 136:             1 if !body.is_empty() && !cert.approvals.is_empty() => {
 137:                 let n = body.len().min(cert.approvals[0].approver_sig.len());
 138:                 cert.approvals[0].approver_sig[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
 139:             }
 140:             2 if !body.is_empty() => {
 141:                 let n = body.len().min(cert.policy.master_sig.len());
 142:                 cert.policy.master_sig[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
 143:             }
 144:             3 if body.len() >= 8 => {
 145:                 let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
 146:                 buf.copy_from_slice(&body[..8]);
 147:                 cert.proposal.deadline_unix = u64::from_be_bytes(buf);
 148:             }
 149:             4 if !cert.approvals.is_empty() => {
 150:                 cert.approvals.push(cert.approvals[0].clone());
 151:             }
 152:             _ => {}
 153:         }
 154:     }
 155:     let _ = cert.verify(&master.verifying_key(), now + 100);
 156: }
 157: 
 158: // ── Mesh state ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 159: 
 160: fn fuzz_state_body(data: &[u8]) {
 161:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA3u8; 32]);
 162:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 163:     let id = [0xAB; 16];
 164:     let (sk, att) =
 165:         mint_subkey(&master, DeviceClass::Phone, id, 0, 365).unwrap();
 166:     let vk = HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(&att.subkey_vk_bytes).unwrap();
 167:     let mut op = AuthenticatedOp::sign(
 168:         &sk,
 169:         b"x".to_vec(),
 170:         Delta::LwwSet { value: b"baseline".to_vec(), ts: 1 },
 171:         1,
 172:         1,
 173:     )
 174:     .unwrap();
 175:     if !data.is_empty() {
 176:         let pick = data[0] % 5;
 177:         let body = &data[1..];
 178:         match pick {
 179:             0 if !body.is_empty() => {
 180:                 let n = body.len().min(op.subkey_sig.len());
 181:                 op.subkey_sig[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
 182:             }
 183:             1 if !body.is_empty() => {
 184:                 let n = body.len().min(op.subtree.len());
 185:                 op.subtree[..n].copy_from_slice(&body[..n]);
 186:             }
 187:             2 if body.len() >= 8 => {
 188:                 let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
 189:                 buf.copy_from_slice(&body[..8]);
 190:                 op.seq = u64::from_be_bytes(buf);
 191:             }
 192:             3 if body.len() >= 8 => {
 193:                 let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
 194:                 buf.copy_from_slice(&body[..8]);
 195:                 op.wall_unix = u64::from_be_bytes(buf);
 196:             }
 197:             _ if !body.is_empty() => {
 198:                 op.device_id[0] = body[0];
 199:             }
 200:             _ => {}
 201:         }
 202:     }
 203:     let _ = op.verify(&vk);
 204: }

 206: // ── Distributed FS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 207: 
 208: fn fuzz_dfs_body(data: &[u8]) {
 209:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA4u8; 32]);
 210:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 211:     let (sk, _att) = mint_subkey(
 212:         &master, DeviceClass::Phone, [0x77; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 0, 365,
 213:     )
 214:     .unwrap();
 215:     let n_chunks = (data.len() / 32).clamp(1, 8) * 3; // multiple of (k=2,m=1)
 216:     let mut chunks: Vec<ChunkHash> = Vec::with_capacity(n_chunks);
 217:     for i in 0..n_chunks {
 218:         let mut h = [0u8; 32];
 219:         for (j, b) in data.iter().take(32).enumerate() {
 220:             h[j] = b.wrapping_add(i as u8);
 221:         }
 222:         chunks.push(h);
 223:     }
 224:     let policy = ErasurePolicy::new(2, 1, 1).unwrap();
 225:     let manifest = FileManifest {
 226:         file_size: (n_chunks as u64) * 1024,
 227:         chunk_size: 1024,
 228:         chunks: chunks.clone(),
 229:         mime: b"application/octet-stream".to_vec(),
 230:         created_unix: 1_700_000_000,
 231:         policy,
 232:     };
 233:     let _ = manifest.shape_check();
 234:     let _ = manifest.file_id();
 235:     let _ = sign_storage_attestation(&sk, 1_700_000_000, chunks);
 236: }

 238: // ── Fan-out ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 239: 
 240: fn fuzz_fan_out_body(data: &[u8]) {
 241:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA5u8; 32]);
 242:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 243:     let (sk, _att) = mint_subkey(
 244:         &master, DeviceClass::Phone, fresh_device_id(&mut rng), 0, 365,
 245:     )
 246:     .unwrap();
 247:     let mut nonce = [0u8; FETCH_NONCE_LEN];
 248:     for (i, b) in data.iter().take(FETCH_NONCE_LEN).enumerate() {
 249:         nonce[i] = *b;
 250:     }
 251:     let chunks: Vec<ChunkHash> = (0..(data.len() / 32).clamp(1, 4))
 252:         .map(|i| {
 253:             let mut h = [0u8; 32];
 254:             for (j, b) in data.iter().take(32).enumerate() {
 255:                 h[j] = b.wrapping_add(i as u8);
 256:             }
 257:             h
 258:         })
 259:         .collect();
 260:     let _ = sign_fetch_request(
 261:         &sk,
 262:         [0x99; DEVICE_ID_LEN],
 263:         [0xFE; FILE_ID_LEN],
 264:         chunks,
 265:         1_000_000,
 266:         100,
 267:         2_000,
 268:         nonce,
 269:     );
 270: }

 274: fn fuzz_self_routing_body(data: &[u8]) {
 275:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA6u8; 32]);
 276:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 277:     let (sk, _att) = mint_subkey(
 278:         &master, DeviceClass::Phone, [0x88; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 0, 365,

 281:     let links: Vec<PeerLink> = (0..(data.len() / 4).min(8))

 284:             tau_score: u32::from(data.get(i + 1).copied().unwrap_or(1)),
 285:             last_seen_unix: u64::from(data.get(i + 2).copied().unwrap_or(1)),
 286:             direct: data.get(i + 3).copied().unwrap_or(0) & 1 == 1,
 287:         })

 292: // ── Self-onion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 293: 
 294: fn fuzz_self_onion_body(data: &[u8]) {
 295:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA7u8; 32]);
 296:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 297:     let phone_id = [0xCC; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 298:     let identity = derive_onion_identity(&master, &phone_id);
 299:     let att = sign_onion_attestation(&master, phone_id, identity.public_bytes(), 0, 365).unwrap();
 300:     let mut reg = OnionKeyRegistry::empty();
 301:     reg.ingest(att, &master.verifying_key()).unwrap();
 302:     // Body is the payload we'd onion-encrypt.
 303:     let _ = data; // payload-driven self-onion is exercised by property_self_onion.
 304: }

 306: // ── Compute ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 307: 
 308: fn fuzz_compute_body(data: &[u8]) {
 309:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA8u8; 32]);
 310:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 311:     let id1 = [0xD1; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 312:     let id2 = [0xD2; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 313:     let id3 = [0xD3; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
 314:     let mut reg = CapabilityRegistry::empty();
 315:     let master_vk = master.verifying_key();
 316:     reg.ingest(
 317:         sign_capability_attestation(
 318:             &master, id1,
 319:             vec![DeviceCapability::Microphone, DeviceCapability::Camera],
 320:             0, 365,
 321:         )
 322:         .unwrap(),
 323:         &master_vk,
 324:     )
 325:     .unwrap();
 326:     reg.ingest(
 327:         sign_capability_attestation(
 328:             &master, id2,
 329:             vec![DeviceCapability::Gpu, DeviceCapability::CpuHeavy],
 330:             0, 365,
 331:         )
 332:         .unwrap(),
 333:         &master_vk,
 334:     )
 335:     .unwrap();
 336:     reg.ingest(
 337:         sign_capability_attestation(
 338:             &master, id3,
 339:             vec![DeviceCapability::LargeDisk, DeviceCapability::AlwaysOn],
 340:             0, 365,
 341:         )
 342:         .unwrap(),
 343:         &master_vk,
 344:     )
 345:     .unwrap();
 346:     let caps: Vec<SourceCapacity> = [id1, id2, id3]
 347:         .iter()
 348:         .enumerate()
 349:         .map(|(i, id)| SourceCapacity {
 350:             device_id: *id,
 351:             estimated_bps: u64::from(data.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(1)) * 1_000,
 352:             current_load_bytes: u64::from(data.get(i + 3).copied().unwrap_or(0)),
 353:         })
 354:         .collect();
 355:     let _ = pick_executor(&[DeviceCapability::Gpu], &reg, &caps, 100);
 356:     let _ = pick_executor(&[DeviceCapability::Microphone], &reg, &caps, 100);
 357: }

 359: // ── Active routing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
 360: 
 361: fn fuzz_active_routing_body(data: &[u8]) {
 362:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xA9u8; 32]);
 363:     let mut contact = [0u8; 32];
 364:     for (i, b) in data.iter().take(32).enumerate() {
 365:         contact[i] = *b;
 366:     }
 367:     let ctx = RoutingContext {
 368:         contact_pin: contact,
 369:         hour_bucket: data.get(32).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 370:         day_of_week: data.get(33).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 371:         message_class: [
 372:             data.get(34).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 373:             data.get(35).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 374:             data.get(36).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 375:             data.get(37).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 376:         ],
 377:         urgency: data.get(38).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 378:     };
 379:     let mut history = RoutingHistory::empty();
 380:     let ctx_hash = ctx.canonical_hash();
 381:     for &b in data.iter().take(16) {
 382:         history.observe(ctx_hash, [b; DEVICE_ID_LEN], (b & 1) == 1, u64::from(b), 1, 1);
 383:     }
 384:     let candidates: Vec<([u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass)> = data
 385:         .iter()
 386:         .take(8)
 387:         .map(|b| ([*b; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Phone))
 388:         .collect();
 389:     let _ = pick_device_for_context(
 390:         &ctx, &candidates, &history, &CohortPrior::uniform(), &mut rng,
 391:     );
 392: }

 394: // ── Duress (alert + commitment only — full envelope is too slow) ───
 395: 
 396: fn fuzz_duress_body(data: &[u8]) {
 397:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xAAu8; 32]);
 398:     let secret_bytes: Vec<u8> = data.iter().take(16).copied().collect();
 399:     if !secret_bytes.is_empty() {
 400:         let qr = PairingCommitment::build(
 401:             PairingChannel::Qr,
 402:             &secret_bytes,
 403:             [data.get(16).copied().unwrap_or(0); 16],
 404:             u64::from(data.get(17).copied().unwrap_or(0)),
 405:         );
 406:         let audio = PairingCommitment::build(
 407:             PairingChannel::Audio,
 408:             &secret_bytes,
 409:             [data.get(18).copied().unwrap_or(0); 16],
 410:             u64::from(data.get(19).copied().unwrap_or(0)),
 411:         );
 412:         let motion = PairingCommitment::build(
 413:             PairingChannel::Motion,
 414:             &secret_bytes,
 415:             [data.get(20).copied().unwrap_or(0); 16],
 416:             u64::from(data.get(21).copied().unwrap_or(0)),
 417:         );
 418:         let _ =
 419:             verify_pairing_cross_channel(&[qr, audio, motion], &secret_bytes, 1_000_000);
 420:     }
 421:     let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut rng);
 422:     let (sk, _) = mint_subkey(
 423:         &master, DeviceClass::Phone, [0xAA; DEVICE_ID_LEN], 0, 365,
 424:     )
 425:     .unwrap();
 426:     let mut nonce = [0u8; 16];
 427:     for (i, b) in data.iter().take(16).enumerate() {
 428:         nonce[i] = *b;
 429:     }
 430:     if let Ok(mut alert) = sign_duress_alert(&sk, 1, nonce) {
 431:         if let Some(&b) = data.first() {
 432:             if !alert.subkey_sig.is_empty() {
 433:                 alert.subkey_sig[0] ^= b;
 434:             }
 435:         }
 436:         let _ = alert.verify(&sk.verifying_key());
 437:     }
 438: }

  76:         alpha in 1u32..500u32,

  80:             context_hash: [0; 32],

  87:         let mut after_act = base;
  88:         after_act.observe(true, 1);
  89:         let mut after_dis = base;
  90:         after_dis.observe(false, 1);
  91:         prop_assert!(after_act.posterior_mean() >= mean_before - 1e-12);

  96: // ── Thompson-sampling convergence (deterministic seed) ────────────

  98: #[test]
  99: fn picker_convergence_to_majority_winner() {
 100:     // Seeded RNG so the test is deterministic.
 101:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xAA; 32]);
 102:     let ctx = RoutingContext {
 103:         contact_pin: [1; 32],
 104:         hour_bucket: 9,
 105:         day_of_week: 1,
 106:         message_class: *b"DM  ",
 107:         urgency: 1,
 108:     };
 109:     let candidates = vec![
 110:         ([0x01u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Phone),
 111:         ([0x02u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Laptop),
 112:     ];
 113:     let mut history = RoutingHistory::empty();
 114:     let ctx_hash = ctx.canonical_hash();
 115:     // Strong evidence: phone gets 50 acts; laptop gets 50 dismisses.
 116:     for _ in 0..50 {
 117:         history.observe(ctx_hash, [0x01; DEVICE_ID_LEN], true, 1, 1, 1);
 118:         history.observe(ctx_hash, [0x02; DEVICE_ID_LEN], false, 1, 1, 1);
 119:     }
 120:     let cohort = CohortPrior::uniform();
 121:     let mut phone_picks = 0;
 122:     let trials = 500;
 123:     for _ in 0..trials {
 124:         if let Some(p) =
 125:             pick_device_for_context(&ctx, &candidates, &history, &cohort, &mut rng)
 126:         {
 127:             if p == [0x01; DEVICE_ID_LEN] {
 128:                 phone_picks += 1;
 129:             }
 130:         }
 131:     }
 132:     // Posterior on phone is ~51/52 ≈ 0.98; on laptop ~1/52 ≈ 0.019.
 133:     // Phone should sweep the vast majority.
 134:     assert!(
 135:         phone_picks >= 450,
 136:         "phone won only {phone_picks}/{trials}; expected >=450"
 137:     );
 138: }

 140: #[test]
 141: fn picker_explores_when_uninformed() {
 142:     // No history → Thompson sampling on Beta(1,1) gives uniform-ish
 143:     // picks. Empirically, each of 3 candidates should win ~1/3.
 144:     let mut rng = ChaCha20Rng::from_seed([0xBB; 32]);
 145:     let ctx = RoutingContext {
 146:         contact_pin: [1; 32],
 147:         hour_bucket: 9,
 148:         day_of_week: 1,
 149:         message_class: *b"DM  ",
 150:         urgency: 1,
 151:     };
 152:     let candidates = vec![
 153:         ([0x01u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Phone),
 154:         ([0x02u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Laptop),
 155:         ([0x03u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], DeviceClass::Desktop),
 156:     ];
 157:     let history = RoutingHistory::empty();
 158:     let cohort = CohortPrior::uniform();
 159:     let mut counts = std::collections::HashMap::<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN], u32>::new();
 160:     let trials = 600;
 161:     for _ in 0..trials {
 162:         if let Some(p) =
 163:             pick_device_for_context(&ctx, &candidates, &history, &cohort, &mut rng)
 164:         {
 165:             *counts.entry(p).or_default() += 1;
 166:         }
 167:     }
 168:     // No candidate should sweep > 60% in the uninformed regime.
 169:     for (_, c) in &counts {
 170:         assert!(*c < (trials * 6 / 10));
 171:     }
 172: }

  65:         let count = ((chunk_count / stripe.max(1)) * stripe.max(1)).max(stripe);

  79:             policy,
  80:         };
  81:         prop_assert!(m.shape_check().is_ok());
  82:         prop_assert_eq!(m.file_id(), m.file_id());

 206:     /// Liveness proof issued at time T with skew K verifies at any
 207:     /// verifier-time within [T-K, T+K] and rejects outside.
 208:     #[test]
 209:     fn liveness_skew_window_property(
 210:         master_seed in any::<[u8; MASTER_SEED_LEN]>(),
 211:         class in class_strategy(),
 212:         id in any::<[u8; DEVICE_ID_LEN]>(),
 213:         issued_at in 1_000_000u64..2_000_000u64,
 214:         skew in 1u64..10_000u64,
 215:         verifier_offset in -20_000i64..20_000i64,
 216:     ) {
 217:         let master = MasterIdentity::from_seed(master_seed);
 218:         let (sk, _att) = mint_subkey(&master, class, id, 0, 365).unwrap();
 219:         let proof = LivenessProof::issue(&sk, issued_at, state_root(b"s")).unwrap();
 220:         let witness = sibling_witness(sk.verifying_key(), skew);
 221:         let verifier_now = if verifier_offset >= 0 {
 222:             issued_at.saturating_add(verifier_offset as u64)
 223:         } else {
 224:             issued_at.saturating_sub((-verifier_offset) as u64)
 225:         };
 226:         let actual_diff = if verifier_now > issued_at {
 227:             verifier_now - issued_at
 228:         } else {
 229:             issued_at - verifier_now
 230:         };
 231:         let r = verify_liveness(&proof, &witness, verifier_now);
 232:         if actual_diff <= skew {
 233:             prop_assert!(r.is_ok());
 234:         } else {
 235:             prop_assert!(r.is_err());
 236:         }
 237:     }

  88:     /// Two-hop round-trip: build at src, peel at dst, payload survives.
  89:     #[test]

  91:         payload in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..256),
  92:     ) {
  93:         let master = MasterIdentity::generate(&mut OsRng);
  94:         let src_id = [0x11; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
  95:         let dst_id = [0x22; DEVICE_ID_LEN];
  96:         let dst_identity = derive_onion_identity(&master, &dst_id);
  97:         let mut reg = OnionKeyRegistry::empty();
  98:         for id in &[src_id, dst_id] {
  99:             let ident = derive_onion_identity(&master, id);
 100:             let att = sign_onion_attestation(
 101:                 &master, *id, ident.public_bytes(), 0, 365,
 102:             ).unwrap();
 103:             reg.ingest(att, &master.verifying_key()).unwrap();
 104:         }

 106:             hops: vec![src_id, dst_id],
 107:             bottleneck_tau: 100,
 108:             min_last_seen_unix: 1,

 111:             &route, &reg, 0, &payload, &mut OsRng,
 112:         ).unwrap();
 113:         let outcome = peel_self_onion_layer(&dst_identity, &packet).unwrap();
 114:         match outcome {
 115:             SelfOnionPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload: got } => {
 116:                 prop_assert_eq!(got, payload);
 117:             }
 118:             other => prop_assert!(
 119:                 false,

   1: # ol_discovery microbenchmark results
   2: 
   3: Captured against `0.21.0-alpha.0` on Windows 11 Intel host, release
   4: profile (`cargo bench -p ol_discovery`). Median of Criterion samples
   5: after warm-up.
   6: 
   7: ## Final numbers
   8: 
   9: | Benchmark                              | Time      | Notes                          |
  10: |---                                     |---        |---                             |
  11: | `node_id::distance`                    | ~ns       | 32-byte XOR + copy             |
  12: | `record::canonical_bytes` (2 endpoints)| 32.9 ns   | length-prefixed encoder        |
  13: | `routing::insert_into_empty`           | 39.1 ns   | first peer in a bucket         |
  14: | `routing::insert_into_populated_100`   | 28.3 ns   | replace-or-bump hot path       |
  15: | `routing::synthetic_id_for_bucket(128)`|  7.0 ns   | bucket-refresh hot path        |
  16: | `routing::stale_buckets_n_512`         |  140 ns   | maintenance scan, 512 entries  |
  17: | `routing::closest_to_n_16`             |  344 ns   | sort over 16-peer table        |
  18: | `routing::closest_to_n_64`             | 1.54 µs   | 64-peer table                  |
  19: | `routing::closest_to_n_256`            | 2.64 µs   | 256-peer table                 |
  20: | `routing::closest_to_n_1024`           | 3.80 µs   | 1024-peer table                |
  21: | `record::sign`                         | 11.7 µs   | Ed25519 sign                   |
  22: | `record::verify`                       | 26.1 µs   | Ed25519 verify                 |
  23: 
  24: ## What this lets the daemon do
  25: 
  26: The hot maintenance path (`tick_maintenance` on a 1-minute timer):
  27: - `stale_buckets(now, max_age)` scans the table in ~140 ns per 512-bucket
  28:   pass; for 256 fully-populated buckets the scan is microseconds, not
  29:   milliseconds.
  30: - Each issued refresh lookup picks a `synthetic_id_for_bucket(i)` in
  31:   7 ns. Even refreshing all 256 buckets in one tick is < 2 µs of
  32:   CPU before any network I/O.
  33: - Republishing one record costs one Ed25519 sign (~12 µs) plus the
  34:   STORE network send. Republishing the full TTL window of records is
  35:   CPU-bound on the network, not on the crypto.
  36: 
  37: ## Why `synthetic_id_for_bucket` exists at all
  38: 
  39: After the May-2026 `synthetic_id_for_bucket` correctness fix (it was
  40: flipping the LSB-numbered bit instead of the MSB-numbered bit), the
  41: function now actually lands the synthetic ID in the requested bucket.
  42: Caught by the `synthetic_id_round_trip` proptest. Without the fix,
  43: `refresh_stale_buckets` was issuing FIND_NODE refresh lookups against
  44: the wrong bucket — silently degrading the maintenance loop's value.
  45: 
  46: ## Repro
  47: 
  48: ```text
  49: cargo bench -p ol_discovery --bench discovery_bench
  50: ```
