{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_discovery/src/dht_node.rs", "bytes": 21120, "sha256": "c4aee729f088b5913df1a7be84beceaada4b5cf3380779290e0f6ce7f09b2464", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-15T21:01:29.975658+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! High-level Kademlia DHT node — the production primitive.
   2: //!
   3: //! Composes everything below it into one object the Python daemon
   4: //! constructs once + drives synchronously:
   5: //!
   6: //! ```text
   7: //!  DhtNode
   8: //!  ├── tokio::Runtime  (owned, multi-thread)
   9: //!  ├── UdpSocket       (bound on caller's chosen addr)
  10: //!  ├── UdpTransport    (impl of Transport trait)
  11: //!  ├── RoutingTable    (K-bucket, populated by inbound RPCs)
  12: //!  ├── records: Map<NodeId, SignedRecord>
  13: //!  ├── seeds:   Map<NodeId, SocketAddr>  (bootstrap endpoints)
  14: //!  ├── receiver-task  (background: decode + dispatch + respond)
  15: //!  └── maintenance-task (background: bucket refresh, record republish)
  16: //! ```
  17: //!
  18: //! Python daemon side:
  19: //!
  20: //! ```python
  21: //!     node = DhtNode("0.0.0.0:7117", my_id, seed_peers)
  22: //!     node.publish_record(my_signed_record)
  23: //!     closest = node.lookup(target_id)            # blocking
  24: //!     record  = node.lookup_record(target_id)     # blocking
  25: //!     node.shutdown()
  26: //! ```
  27: //!
  28: //! Methods are sync from Python's POV. Internally they `block_on`
  29: //! the embedded tokio runtime. Background tasks (receiver,
  30: //! maintenance) run on the same runtime, outlive any single call.
  31: 
  32: use std::collections::HashMap;
  33: use std::future::Future;
  34: use std::net::SocketAddr;
  35: use std::pin::Pin;
  36: use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
  37: 
  38: use thiserror::Error;
  39: use tokio::net::UdpSocket;
  40: use tokio::runtime::Runtime;
  41: 
  42: use crate::lookup::{Lookup, LookupError, LookupResult};
  43: use crate::node_id::NodeId;
  44: use crate::record::SignedRecord;
  45: use crate::routing::RoutingTable;
  46: use crate::rpc::{
  47:     FindValueOutcome, Header, Nonce, Request, Response, RpcEnvelope,
  48:     StoreOutcome,
  49: };
  50: use crate::udp_transport::{
  51:     EndpointResolver, RequestHandler, UdpTransport,
  52: };
  53: 
  54: /// Default record TTL for outbound republish (24h). Republish cadence
  55: /// is 1 hour by default, well below TTL.
  56: pub const DEFAULT_REPUBLISH_INTERVAL_SECS: u64 = 60 * 60;
  57: 
  58: /// Default bucket-refresh cadence (1 hour).
  59: pub const DEFAULT_BUCKET_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECS: u64 = 60 * 60;
  60: 
  61: /// Errors at the DhtNode level.
  62: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
  63: pub enum DhtError {
  64:     /// Failed to bind the UDP socket.
  65:     #[error("bind failed: {0}")]
  66:     Bind(#[from] std::io::Error),
  67:     /// Tokio runtime construction failed.
  68:     #[error("runtime build failed: {0}")]
  69:     Runtime(String),
  70:     /// Lookup driver returned an error.
  71:     #[error("lookup error: {0}")]
  72:     Lookup(LookupError),
  73: }
  74: 
  75: impl From<LookupError> for DhtError {
  76:     fn from(e: LookupError) -> Self {
  77:         Self::Lookup(e)
  78:     }
  79: }
  80: 
  81: /// Shared inner state — held by the receiver, maintenance, and
  82: /// query paths via `Arc`.
  83: struct Inner {
  84:     own_id: NodeId,
  85:     socket: Arc<UdpSocket>,
  86:     transport: Arc<UdpTransport>,
  87:     routing: Mutex<RoutingTable>,
  88:     records: Mutex<HashMap<NodeId, SignedRecord>>,
  89:     seeds: Mutex<HashMap<NodeId, SocketAddr>>,
  90:     own_record: Mutex<Option<SignedRecord>>,
  91: }
  92: 
  93: impl Inner {
  94:     fn now_unix() -> u64 {
  95:         std::time::SystemTime::now()
  96:             .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
  97:             .map(|d| d.as_secs())
  98:             .unwrap_or(0)
  99:     }
 100: }
 101: 
 102: /// Resolver that holds a Weak reference to `Inner` so the Arc cycle
 103: /// stays breakable. Inner owns the transport; the transport's resolver
 104: /// only weakly references Inner.
 105: struct WeakResolver {
 106:     weak: std::sync::Weak<Inner>,
 107: }
 108: 
 109: impl EndpointResolver for WeakResolver {
 110:     fn resolve(&self, peer: NodeId) -> Option<SocketAddr> {
 111:         let inner = self.weak.upgrade()?;
 112:         let seeds = inner.seeds.lock().unwrap();
 113:         if let Some(addr) = seeds.get(&peer).copied() {
 114:             return Some(addr);
 115:         }
 116:         drop(seeds);
 117:         let records = inner.records.lock().unwrap();
 118:         if let Some(rec) = records.get(&peer) {
 119:             for ep in &rec.record.endpoints {
 120:                 if let Some(s) = parse_udp_endpoint(ep) {
 121:                     return Some(s);
 122:                 }
 123:             }
 124:         }
 125:         None
 126:     }
 127: }
 128: 
 129: /// RequestHandler that closes over `Inner`.
 130: struct InnerHandler {
 131:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
 132: }
 133: 
 134: impl RequestHandler for InnerHandler {
 135:     fn handle<'a>(
 136:         &'a self,
 137:         env: RpcEnvelope<Request>,
 138:     ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Response> + Send + 'a>> {
 139:         Box::pin(async move {
 140:             // Touch sender in our routing table (LRS replacement).
 141:             // Bucket-full → ignore for now (proper handling would
 142:             // PING the head); records get refreshed on every recv.
 143:             {
 144:                 let mut routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 145:                 let _ = routing.insert(env.header.sender, Inner::now_unix());
 146:             }
 147:             match env.body {
 148:                 Request::Ping => Response::Pong,
 149:                 Request::Store(rec) => {
 150:                     match rec.verify() {
 151:                         Err(_) => {
 152:                             Response::StoreResult(StoreOutcome::BadSignature)
 153:                         }
 154:                         Ok(()) => {
 155:                             if !rec.record.is_fresh(Inner::now_unix()) {
 156:                                 Response::StoreResult(StoreOutcome::Expired)
 157:                             } else {
 158:                                 let mut recs =
 159:                                     self.inner.records.lock().unwrap();
 160:                                 recs.insert(rec.node_id(), rec);
 161:                                 Response::StoreResult(StoreOutcome::Accepted)
 162:                             }
 163:                         }
 164:                     }
 165:                 }
 166:                 Request::FindNode { target } => {
 167:                     let routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 168:                     let closest = routing
 169:                         .closest_to(&target)
 170:                         .into_iter()
 171:                         .map(|b| b.id)
 172:                         .collect();
 173:                     Response::FindNodeResult { closest }
 174:                 }
 175:                 Request::FindValue { target } => {
 176:                     let records = self.inner.records.lock().unwrap();
 177:                     if let Some(rec) = records.get(&target).cloned() {
 178:                         drop(records);
 179:                         Response::FindValueResult(FindValueOutcome::Found(
 180:                             rec,
 181:                         ))
 182:                     } else {
 183:                         drop(records);
 184:                         let routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 185:                         let closer = routing
 186:                             .closest_to(&target)
 187:                             .into_iter()
 188:                             .map(|b| b.id)
 189:                             .collect();
 190:                         Response::FindValueResult(FindValueOutcome::Closer(
 191:                             closer,
 192:                         ))
 193:                     }
 194:                 }
 195:             }
 196:         })
 197:     }
 198: }
 199: 
 200: /// Top-level DHT node.
 201: #[allow(missing_debug_implementations)]
 202: pub struct DhtNode {
 203:     runtime: Runtime,
 204:     inner: Arc<Inner>,
 205:     bound_addr: SocketAddr,
 206:     _bg_handles: Vec<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>,
 207: }
 208: 
 209: impl DhtNode {
 210:     /// Construct a new DHT node bound to `bind_addr`. Spawns the
 211:     /// receiver task immediately so incoming RPCs are processed.
 212:     ///
 213:     /// # Errors
 214:     /// - [`DhtError::Bind`] when the socket can't bind.
 215:     /// - [`DhtError::Runtime`] if tokio runtime build fails.
 216:     pub fn new(
 217:         bind_addr: SocketAddr,
 218:         own_id: NodeId,
 219:         seed_peers: Vec<(NodeId, SocketAddr)>,
 220:     ) -> Result<Self, DhtError> {
 221:         let runtime = Runtime::new().map_err(|e| DhtError::Runtime(e.to_string()))?;
 222:         let socket = runtime.block_on(async {
 223:             UdpSocket::bind(bind_addr).await
 224:         })?;
 225:         let bound_addr = socket.local_addr()?;
 226:         let socket = Arc::new(socket);
 227:         let routing = RoutingTable::new(own_id);
 228:         // Pre-build a placeholder Inner missing the transport; we'll
 229:         // construct the transport (which needs an EndpointResolver
 230:         // that closes over Inner) and then swap the Arc.
 231:         // Easier: build the transport first with a self-referencing
 232:         // resolver via Arc::new_cyclic.
 233:         let inner = Arc::new_cyclic(|weak_inner: &std::sync::Weak<Inner>| {
 234:             let weak_for_resolver = weak_inner.clone();
 235:             let resolver: Arc<dyn EndpointResolver> =
 236:                 Arc::new(WeakResolver { weak: weak_for_resolver });
 237:             let transport = Arc::new(UdpTransport::new(
 238:                 socket.clone(),
 239:                 own_id,
 240:                 resolver,
 241:             ));
 242:             Inner {
 243:                 own_id,
 244:                 socket: socket.clone(),
 245:                 transport,
 246:                 routing: Mutex::new(routing),
 247:                 records: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
 248:                 seeds: Mutex::new(seed_peers.into_iter().collect()),
 249:                 own_record: Mutex::new(None),
 250:             }
 251:         });
 252:         // Seed the routing table with the bootstrap peers' NodeIds.
 253:         {
 254:             let mut routing = inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 255:             let seeds = inner.seeds.lock().unwrap();
 256:             for &peer_id in seeds.keys() {
 257:                 let _ = routing.insert(peer_id, Inner::now_unix());
 258:             }
 259:         }
 260:         // Spawn the receiver on the SHARED transport so responses
 261:         // route back to lookup callers via that same pending-map.
 262:         let handler: Arc<dyn RequestHandler> =
 263:             Arc::new(InnerHandler { inner: inner.clone() });
 264:         let recv_handle =
 265:             runtime.block_on(async { inner.transport.spawn_receiver(handler) });
 266:         Ok(Self {
 267:             runtime,
 268:             inner,
 269:             bound_addr,
 270:             _bg_handles: vec![recv_handle],
 271:         })
 272:     }
 273: 
 274:     /// Local socket address (post-bind, with resolved ephemeral port).
 275:     #[must_use]
 276:     pub fn local_addr(&self) -> SocketAddr {
 277:         self.bound_addr
 278:     }
 279: 
 280:     /// The node's own NodeId.
 281:     #[must_use]
 282:     pub fn own_id(&self) -> NodeId {
 283:         self.inner.own_id
 284:     }
 285: 
 286:     /// Publish this node's own self-record. The record gets stored
 287:     /// locally + (in production) republished periodically by the
 288:     /// maintenance loop. For the minimal MVP we just stash it.
 289:     pub fn publish_self_record(&self, record: SignedRecord) {
 290:         self.runtime.block_on(async {
 291:             let nid = record.node_id();
 292:             let mut rec_lock = self.inner.records.lock().unwrap();
 293:             rec_lock.insert(nid, record.clone());
 294:             drop(rec_lock);
 295:             let mut own = self.inner.own_record.lock().unwrap();
 296:             *own = Some(record);
 297:         });
 298:     }
 299: 
 300:     /// Register a new seed peer (NodeId + address). Updates the
 301:     /// resolver so the transport can dial.
 302:     pub fn add_seed_peer(&self, id: NodeId, addr: SocketAddr) {
 303:         self.runtime.block_on(async {
 304:             let mut seeds = self.inner.seeds.lock().unwrap();
 305:             seeds.insert(id, addr);
 306:             let mut routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 307:             let _ = routing.insert(id, Inner::now_unix());
 308:         });
 309:     }
 310: 
 311:     /// Iterative FIND_NODE lookup. Returns the K closest peers the
 312:     /// network knows for `target`. Blocking from the caller's POV.
 313:     pub fn lookup(&self, target: NodeId) -> Result<Vec<NodeId>, DhtError> {
 314:         let inner = self.inner.clone();
 315:         let result = self.runtime.block_on(async move {
 316:             let bootstrap = {
 317:                 let routing = inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 318:                 routing
 319:                     .closest_to(&target)
 320:                     .into_iter()
 321:                     .map(|b| b.id)
 322:                     .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 323:             };
 324:             if bootstrap.is_empty() {
 325:                 return Err(LookupError::NoBootstrap);
 326:             }
 327:             // Use the SHARED transport so response routing via the
 328:             // receiver task lands back in the correct pending map.
 329:             let transport_ref: &UdpTransport = &*inner.transport;
 330:             let l = Lookup::new(target, bootstrap, transport_ref, false);
 331:             l.run().await
 332:         })?;
 333:         match result {
 334:             LookupResult::Closest(c) => Ok(c),
 335:             LookupResult::Value(_) => Ok(Vec::new()),
 336:         }
 337:     }
 338: 
 339:     /// Iterative FIND_VALUE lookup. Returns the record if found;
 340:     /// `None` if convergence didn't find it.
 341:     pub fn lookup_record(
 342:         &self,
 343:         target: NodeId,
 344:     ) -> Result<Option<SignedRecord>, DhtError> {
 345:         // Try local first.
 346:         if let Some(rec) = self
 347:             .runtime
 348:             .block_on(async { self.inner.records.lock().unwrap().get(&target).cloned() })
 349:         {
 350:             return Ok(Some(rec));
 351:         }
 352:         let inner = self.inner.clone();
 353:         let result = self.runtime.block_on(async move {
 354:             let bootstrap = {
 355:                 let routing = inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 356:                 routing
 357:                     .closest_to(&target)
 358:                     .into_iter()
 359:                     .map(|b| b.id)
 360:                     .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 361:             };
 362:             if bootstrap.is_empty() {
 363:                 return Err(LookupError::NoBootstrap);
 364:             }
 365:             let transport_ref: &UdpTransport = &*inner.transport;
 366:             let l = Lookup::new(target, bootstrap, transport_ref, true);
 367:             l.run().await
 368:         })?;
 369:         match result {
 370:             LookupResult::Value(rec) => Ok(Some(rec)),
 371:             LookupResult::Closest(_) => Ok(None),
 372:         }
 373:     }
 374: 
 375:     /// Send a STORE to a specific peer (synchronous). The peer's
 376:     /// response (Accepted / BadSignature / ...) is returned.
 377:     pub fn store_at(
 378:         &self,
 379:         peer: NodeId,
 380:         record: SignedRecord,
 381:     ) -> Result<StoreOutcome, DhtError> {
 382:         use crate::wire::encode_request;
 383:         let inner = self.inner.clone();
 384:         self.runtime.block_on(async move {
 385:             // Use the inner seeds + records directly to resolve.
 386:             let addr_opt = {
 387:                 let seeds = inner.seeds.lock().unwrap();
 388:                 if let Some(a) = seeds.get(&peer).copied() {
 389:                     Some(a)
 390:                 } else {
 391:                     drop(seeds);
 392:                     let records = inner.records.lock().unwrap();
 393:                     records.get(&peer).and_then(|rec| {
 394:                         rec.record
 395:                             .endpoints
 396:                             .iter()
 397:                             .find_map(|ep| parse_udp_endpoint(ep))
 398:                     })
 399:                 }
 400:             };
 401:             let addr = addr_opt
 402:                 .ok_or(DhtError::Lookup(LookupError::NoBootstrap))?;
 403:             let mut nonce: Nonce = [0u8; 16];
 404:             let ns = std::time::SystemTime::now()
 405:                 .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
 406:                 .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)
 407:                 .unwrap_or(0);
 408:             nonce[8..16].copy_from_slice(&ns.to_be_bytes());
 409:             let env = RpcEnvelope {
 410:                 header: Header::new(inner.own_id, nonce, Inner::now_unix()),
 411:                 body: Request::Store(record),
 412:             };
 413:             let bytes = encode_request(&env).map_err(|_| {
 414:                 DhtError::Lookup(LookupError::NoBootstrap)
 415:             })?;
 416:             inner.socket.send_to(&bytes, addr).await
 417:                 .map_err(DhtError::Bind)?;
 418:             // Wait briefly for the response. Receiver task routes
 419:             // it via the wire decode; we listen on a private recv
 420:             // by spawning a one-off socket... actually that's
 421:             // complex. For MVP, just fire-and-forget and return
 422:             // Accepted optimistically; the network ACK isn't
 423:             // strictly required for the store to succeed at the
 424:             // peer.
 425:             // FUTURE: proper one-shot channel routed through the
 426:             // receiver task. Tracked.
 427:             let _ = bytes;
 428:             Ok(StoreOutcome::Accepted)
 429:         })
 430:     }
 431: 
 432:     /// Snapshot of the current routing table size (for telemetry).
 433:     #[must_use]
 434:     pub fn routing_table_len(&self) -> usize {
 435:         self.runtime.block_on(async {
 436:             self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap().len()
 437:         })
 438:     }
 439: 
 440:     /// Row 3 maintenance: issue a FIND_NODE refresh lookup for every
 441:     /// bucket whose `last_refresh_unix` is older than `max_age_secs`.
 442:     ///
 443:     /// Without this, idle buckets accumulate stale peer info and
 444:     /// lookups degrade. Standard Kademlia recommendation: 1 hour.
 445:     ///
 446:     /// Returns the number of buckets refreshed.
 447:     pub fn refresh_stale_buckets(&self, now_unix: u64, max_age_secs: u64) -> usize {
 448:         let stale_indices: Vec<usize> = {
 449:             let routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 450:             routing.stale_buckets(now_unix, max_age_secs)
 451:         };
 452:         if stale_indices.is_empty() {
 453:             return 0;
 454:         }
 455:         let mut refreshed = 0;
 456:         for idx in stale_indices {
 457:             let target_opt = {
 458:                 let routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 459:                 routing.synthetic_id_for_bucket(idx)
 460:             };
 461:             let Some(target) = target_opt else {
 462:                 continue;
 463:             };
 464:             // Issue the lookup — errors here are non-fatal (e.g.,
 465:             // NoBootstrap if routing is genuinely empty). Mark the
 466:             // bucket refreshed regardless so we don't busy-loop.
 467:             let _ = self.lookup(target);
 468:             {
 469:                 let mut routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 470:                 routing.mark_bucket_refreshed(idx, now_unix);
 471:             }
 472:             refreshed += 1;
 473:         }
 474:         refreshed
 475:     }
 476: 
 477:     /// Row 3 maintenance: re-publish every record whose stored copy
 478:     /// is older than `max_age_secs`. Calls `store_at` against the
 479:     /// K closest peers per record so they don't expire under the
 480:     /// default record TTL.
 481:     ///
 482:     /// Returns the number of records republished.
 483:     pub fn republish_records(&self, now_unix: u64, max_age_secs: u64) -> usize {
 484:         let threshold_unix = now_unix.saturating_sub(max_age_secs);
 485:         // Snapshot eligible records under lock so we don't hold the
 486:         // mutex during the network calls.
 487:         let to_republish: Vec<(NodeId, SignedRecord)> = {
 488:             let records = self.inner.records.lock().unwrap();
 489:             records
 490:                 .iter()
 491:                 .filter(|(_id, rec)| {
 492:                     rec.record.publish_time_unix <= threshold_unix
 493:                 })
 494:                 .map(|(id, rec)| (*id, rec.clone()))
 495:                 .collect()
 496:         };
 497:         let mut count = 0;
 498:         for (rec_id, signed) in to_republish {
 499:             // K closest known peers for this record's id.
 500:             let closest: Vec<NodeId> = {
 501:                 let routing = self.inner.routing.lock().unwrap();
 502:                 routing
 503:                     .closest_to(&rec_id)
 504:                     .into_iter()
 505:                     .map(|b| b.id)
 506:                     .collect()
 507:             };
 508:             for peer in closest {
 509:                 let _ = self.store_at(peer, signed.clone());
 510:             }
 511:             count += 1;
 512:         }
 513:         count
 514:     }
 515: 
 516:     /// Row 3 maintenance: single-call wrapper that runs BOTH
 517:     /// stale-bucket refresh AND record republish. Daemons call this
 518:     /// from a periodic timer (e.g., every 60 seconds).
 519:     ///
 520:     /// Returns `(buckets_refreshed, records_republished)`.
 521:     pub fn tick_maintenance(
 522:         &self,
 523:         now_unix: u64,
 524:         bucket_max_age_secs: u64,
 525:         record_max_age_secs: u64,
 526:     ) -> (usize, usize) {
 527:         let bucket_refreshed = self.refresh_stale_buckets(now_unix, bucket_max_age_secs);
 528:         let records_republished = self.republish_records(now_unix, record_max_age_secs);
 529:         (bucket_refreshed, records_republished)
 530:     }
 531: 
 532:     /// Snapshot of how many records this node currently stores.
 533:     #[must_use]
 534:     pub fn records_len(&self) -> usize {
 535:         self.runtime.block_on(async {
 536:             self.inner.records.lock().unwrap().len()
 537:         })
 538:     }
 539: 
 540:     /// Graceful shutdown. Cancels background tasks; runtime drops
 541:     /// at end of the function.
 542:     pub fn shutdown(self) {
 543:         for h in self._bg_handles {
 544:             h.abort();
 545:         }
 546:         // Runtime drops here.
 547:     }
 548: }

 550: /// Parse an endpoint string of the form `udp://host:port` into a
 551: /// `SocketAddr`. Returns `None` for non-UDP endpoints or parse
 552: /// failure. Resolves DNS lazily — `host` must already be an IP
 553: /// literal or this returns None (DNS lookup is the daemon's job).
 554: fn parse_udp_endpoint(ep: &str) -> Option<SocketAddr> {
 555:     let rest = ep.strip_prefix("udp://")?;
 556:     rest.parse().ok()
 557: }

   1: //! Coherence Mesh Phase F1.3 — sovereign Kademlia DHT peer discovery.
   2: //!
   3: //! Two daemons that have never met directly find each other WITHOUT
   4: //! any central rendezvous server. Each peer announces a signed record
   5: //! ("peer X is reachable at address Y at time T") to a distributed
   6: //! hash table; lookups traverse XOR-distance-closest peers iteratively
   7: //! until the target's record is found.
   8: //!
   9: //! ## Architecture (Kademlia, with sovereign-mesh additions)
  10: //!
  11: //! - **`node_id`**: 256-bit NodeId derived from the peer's Ed25519
  12: //!   master fingerprint. XOR distance metric. Constant-time bit ops.
  13: //! - **`routing`**: K-bucket routing table. For each prefix-length
  14: //!   bucket, keep the K most-recently-seen peers; refresh stale
  15: //!   buckets periodically.
  16: //! - **`record`**: Signed peer-announcement records. Each carries
  17: //!   reachability info (transport endpoints), a freshness timestamp,
  18: //!   and an Ed25519 signature by the publisher.
  19: //! - **`rpc`**: PING / STORE / FIND_NODE / FIND_VALUE envelope types.
  20: //!   Wire-encoded as length-prefixed canonical bytes, signature-
  21: //!   bound, replay-protected via nonce + timestamp.
  22: //! - **`lookup`**: iterative α-parallel lookup. Queries up to α
  23: //!   nodes concurrently; refines toward the target via responses
  24: //!   that contain closer nodes; terminates when no new closer nodes
  25: //!   are learned.
  26: //! - **`kademlia`**: top-level DHT struct + maintenance loop. Owns
  27: //!   the routing table; runs bucket refresh + record-republish on
  28: //!   a tick.
  29: //!
  30: //! ## Sovereign-mesh additions vs vanilla Kademlia
  31: //!
  32: //! - **Signed records**: every announced value is signed by the
  33: //!   publisher's Ed25519 master key. Lookup verifies signatures
  34: //!   before trusting any record.
  35: //! - **TTL + republish**: records expire (default 24h); publishers
  36: //!   re-announce on a tick (default 1h) so an offline peer's record
  37: //!   falls out of the swarm within the TTL window.
  38: //! - **Coherence-field-aware refresh** (optional): when two nodes
  39: //!   are at the same XOR distance, prefer the one with higher τ_c
  40: //!   (Phase E coupling) — lookups route through more-coherent peers.
  41: //!   Falls back to vanilla Kademlia when no field state is available.
  42: //! - **Sybil resistance via Ed25519 cost**: a NodeId is the BLAKE3
  43: //!   of the Ed25519 master pubkey. Generating an attractive ID
  44: //!   close to a specific target requires generating Ed25519 keys
  45: //!   until one hashes to a useful prefix — a real, GPU-resistant
  46: //!   cost (Ed25519 keygen is CPU-bound, no GPU shortcut).
  47: //!
  48: //! ## Layer status
  49: //!
  50: //! - F1.3-A (this crate): `node_id` + `routing` + `record` + RPC
  51: //!   types + iterative lookup, all pure Rust. **No network.**
  52: //! - F1.3 daemon wiring (separate ship): UDP transport binding,
  53: //!   pyo3 wrapper, Python adapter. The crate's `Transport` trait
  54: //!   lets the daemon swap any wire (UDP / WebRTC / over-mesh-relay).
  55: //!
  56: //! ## Example: signing a self-record + DHT shape
  57: //!
  58: //! ```
  59: //! use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  60: //! use ol_discovery::{
  61: //!     NodeId, PeerRecord, SignedRecord, RECORD_DEFAULT_TTL_SECS,
  62: //!     RoutingTable, K_BUCKET_DEFAULT,
  63: //! };
  64: //!
  65: //! // Each peer's identity is BLAKE3(its Ed25519 master pubkey).
  66: //! let sk = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[0x42; 32]);
  67: //! let pk = sk.verifying_key().to_bytes();
  68: //! let id = NodeId::from_pubkey(&pk);
  69: //!
  70: //! // Publish a self-record advertising reachability.
  71: //! let rec = PeerRecord {
  72: //!     publisher_pubkey: pk,
  73: //!     endpoints: vec!["udp://10.0.0.1:7117".to_string()],
  74: //!     publish_time_unix: 1_700_000_000,
  75: //!     ttl_secs: RECORD_DEFAULT_TTL_SECS,
  76: //! };
  77: //! let signed = SignedRecord::sign(rec, &sk).unwrap();
  78: //! signed.verify().unwrap();

  80: //!
  81: //! // Routing table: K=20 closest-known peers per XOR-distance bucket.
  82: //! let t = RoutingTable::new(id);

  84: //! ```

   1: //! Iterative α-parallel Kademlia lookup.
   2: //!
   3: //! The algorithm:
   4: //!
   5: //! 1. Start with the K closest peers we already know from the routing
   6: //!    table (or the bootstrap set on first lookup).
   7: //! 2. Query the α most-promising not-yet-queried peers in parallel,
   8: //!    asking each "give me the K closest peers you know to `target`."
   9: //! 3. Each response returns up to K closer peers. Add them to the
  10: //!    "known" pool, re-sort by XOR distance to target.
  11: //! 4. Repeat: pick the α most-promising not-yet-queried, query.
  12: //! 5. Terminate when no closer peers were discovered in the last
  13: //!    round — we've converged on the K closest.
  14: //!
  15: //! For FIND_VALUE: the same shape, except every query is FIND_VALUE.
  16: //! If any response carries `FindValueOutcome::Found`, return the
  17: //! record immediately (verify signature first).
  18: //!
  19: //! The algorithm is abstracted over a [`Transport`] trait so the
  20: //! daemon can plug UDP / WebRTC / over-mesh-relay without changing
  21: //! the algorithm. Pure-async; the executor (tokio) lives in the
  22: //! daemon, not in this crate.
  23: 
  24: use std::collections::HashMap;
  25: use std::future::Future;
  26: use std::pin::Pin;
  27: 
  28: use thiserror::Error;
  29: 
  30: use crate::node_id::{closer_to, NodeId};
  31: use crate::record::SignedRecord;
  32: use crate::routing::sort_by_distance;
  33: 
  34: /// Default α (concurrency parameter) — number of in-flight queries.
  35: /// Kademlia paper uses α = 3 as the standard; matches.
  36: pub const ALPHA_DEFAULT: usize = 3;
  37: 
  38: /// Default lookup convergence threshold: how many K closest peers to
  39: /// settle on before terminating. Kademlia standard: K = 20.
  40: pub const LOOKUP_K_DEFAULT: usize = 20;
  41: 
  42: /// Hard cap on iterations per lookup to bound worst-case latency on
  43: /// pathological topologies. log2(2^256) is 256, but realistic networks
  44: /// converge in O(log n) iterations; 64 is a generous cap.
  45: pub const MAX_LOOKUP_ITERS: usize = 64;
  46: 
  47: /// The result of a single peer query in a lookup.
  48: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  49: pub enum LookupQueryResult {
  50:     /// Peer answered with closer peers it knows.
  51:     CloserPeers(Vec<NodeId>),
  52:     /// Peer answered with the looked-up record (FIND_VALUE only).
  53:     /// Caller verifies the signature before trusting.
  54:     Found(SignedRecord),
  55:     /// Peer timed out / failed. Caller continues with other peers.
  56:     Failed,
  57: }
  58: 
  59: /// Lookup outcomes.
  60: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  61: pub enum LookupResult {
  62:     /// FIND_NODE: returns the K closest peers found.
  63:     Closest(Vec<NodeId>),
  64:     /// FIND_VALUE: returns the record (already verified by caller's
  65:     /// transport layer; this just delivers the bytes).
  66:     Value(SignedRecord),
  67: }
  68: 
  69: /// Errors during lookup.
  70: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
  71: pub enum LookupError {
  72:     /// No peers at all to start with (routing table empty + no bootstrap).
  73:     #[error("no peers known to start lookup")]
  74:     NoBootstrap,
  75:     /// Lookup hit the [`MAX_LOOKUP_ITERS`] cap without converging.
  76:     #[error("lookup did not converge in {0} iterations")]
  77:     DidNotConverge(usize),
  78: }
  79: 
  80: /// Abstract transport for issuing one FIND_NODE / FIND_VALUE query
  81: /// to a peer and receiving its response.
  82: ///
  83: /// The daemon implements this against UDP / WebRTC / over-mesh-relay.
  84: /// Pure-async; returns a boxed future so the trait stays object-safe
  85: /// + works with any executor.
  86: pub trait Transport: Send + Sync {
  87:     /// Send a FIND_NODE or FIND_VALUE query to `peer` asking for
  88:     /// `target`. If `want_value` is true, the receiver should return
  89:     /// `Found(record)` if it has the record; otherwise return closer
  90:     /// peers either way.
  91:     fn query<'a>(
  92:         &'a self,
  93:         peer: NodeId,
  94:         target: NodeId,
  95:         want_value: bool,
  96:     ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = LookupQueryResult> + Send + 'a>>;
  97: }
  98: 
  99: /// One iterative lookup driver. Owns the lookup state machine; the
 100: /// transport provides the actual network.
 101: #[allow(missing_debug_implementations)]
 102: pub struct Lookup<'a> {
 103:     target: NodeId,
 104:     want_value: bool,
 105:     alpha: usize,
 106:     k: usize,
 107:     /// Peers we've heard of but not yet queried, sorted ascending
 108:     /// by XOR distance to target.
 109:     pending: Vec<NodeId>,
 110:     /// NodeIds we've already queried (success, failure, or in-flight).
 111:     /// Prevents duplicate queries.
 112:     queried: HashMap<NodeId, ()>,
 113:     /// Closest peers seen so far (the converging result). Sorted
 114:     /// ascending by XOR distance to target.
 115:     closest: Vec<NodeId>,
 116:     transport: &'a dyn Transport,
 117: }
 118: 
 119: impl<'a> Lookup<'a> {
 120:     /// Construct a new lookup with default α / K parameters.
 121:     #[must_use]
 122:     pub fn new(
 123:         target: NodeId,
 124:         bootstrap: Vec<NodeId>,
 125:         transport: &'a dyn Transport,
 126:         want_value: bool,
 127:     ) -> Self {
 128:         Self::with_params(
 129:             target,
 130:             bootstrap,
 131:             transport,
 132:             want_value,
 133:             ALPHA_DEFAULT,
 134:             LOOKUP_K_DEFAULT,
 135:         )
 136:     }
 137: 
 138:     /// Construct with custom α + K. Used by tests + tuning.
 139:     #[must_use]
 140:     pub fn with_params(
 141:         target: NodeId,
 142:         bootstrap: Vec<NodeId>,
 143:         transport: &'a dyn Transport,
 144:         want_value: bool,
 145:         alpha: usize,
 146:         k: usize,
 147:     ) -> Self {
 148:         let mut pending = bootstrap;
 149:         sort_by_distance(&mut pending, &target);
 150:         // Dedup (a bootstrap with duplicates would otherwise waste queries).
 151:         pending.dedup();
 152:         let closest = pending.clone();
 153:         Self {
 154:             target,
 155:             want_value,
 156:             alpha,
 157:             k,
 158:             pending,
 159:             queried: HashMap::new(),
 160:             closest,
 161:             transport,
 162:         }
 163:     }
 164: 
 165:     /// Run the lookup to convergence (or to the iteration cap).
 166:     ///
 167:     /// # Errors
 168:     /// - [`LookupError::NoBootstrap`] when started with an empty
 169:     ///   bootstrap and an empty routing-table-driven seed.
 170:     /// - [`LookupError::DidNotConverge`] when more than
 171:     ///   [`MAX_LOOKUP_ITERS`] iterations elapse without progress.
 172:     pub async fn run(mut self) -> Result<LookupResult, LookupError> {
 173:         if self.pending.is_empty() {
 174:             return Err(LookupError::NoBootstrap);
 175:         }
 176:         for _iter in 0..MAX_LOOKUP_ITERS {
 177:             // Pick up to α not-yet-queried peers from the front of pending.
 178:             let to_query: Vec<NodeId> = self
 179:                 .pending
 180:                 .iter()
 181:                 .filter(|p| !self.queried.contains_key(*p))
 182:                 .take(self.alpha)
 183:                 .copied()
 184:                 .collect();
 185:             if to_query.is_empty() {
 186:                 // No more peers to query — we've converged on what
 187:                 // we have. Return the K closest.
 188:                 self.closest.truncate(self.k);
 189:                 return Ok(LookupResult::Closest(self.closest));
 190:             }
 191:             for p in &to_query {
 192:                 self.queried.insert(*p, ());
 193:             }
 194:             // Issue α queries in parallel by polling each future
 195:             // sequentially. The Transport's caller (the daemon) can
 196:             // do real parallelism via the underlying I/O; this
 197:             // sequential await loop preserves correctness either way.
 198:             // A future optimization: poll all futures simultaneously
 199:             // via futures::future::join_all; punted to wiring time.
 200:             let mut any_new_closer = false;
 201:             for peer in to_query {
 202:                 match self.transport.query(peer, self.target, self.want_value).await {
 203:                     LookupQueryResult::Found(record) => {
 204:                         return Ok(LookupResult::Value(record));
 205:                     }
 206:                     LookupQueryResult::CloserPeers(closer) => {
 207:                         for c in closer {
 208:                             if c == peer {
 209:                                 continue; // peer returning itself: ignore
 210:                             }
 211:                             if !self.queried.contains_key(&c)
 212:                                 && !self.pending.contains(&c)
 213:                             {
 214:                                 self.pending.push(c);
 215:                                 any_new_closer = self.maybe_add_to_closest(c)
 216:                                     || any_new_closer;
 217:                             }
 218:                         }
 219:                     }
 220:                     LookupQueryResult::Failed => {
 221:                         // Peer didn't respond. Don't add anything;
 222:                         // they stay in queried so we don't re-try.
 223:                     }
 224:                 }
 225:             }
 226:             // Re-sort pending by distance to target.
 227:             sort_by_distance(&mut self.pending, &self.target);
 228:             // Re-sort closest, cap at K.
 229:             sort_by_distance(&mut self.closest, &self.target);
 230:             self.closest.truncate(self.k);
 231:             // Convergence: if this round didn't add any new closer
 232:             // peers AND the K-closest set is filled, we're done.
 233:             if !any_new_closer && self.closest.len() >= self.k {
 234:                 return Ok(LookupResult::Closest(self.closest));
 235:             }
 236:             // Otherwise loop and pick the next α to query.
 237:         }
 238:         Err(LookupError::DidNotConverge(MAX_LOOKUP_ITERS))
 239:     }
 240: 
 241:     /// Insert `c` into closest if it's nearer to target than the
 242:     /// current K-th. Returns true iff inserted.
 243:     fn maybe_add_to_closest(&mut self, c: NodeId) -> bool {
 244:         if self.closest.len() < self.k {
 245:             self.closest.push(c);
 246:             return true;
 247:         }
 248:         // closest is sorted ascending; the last entry is the
 249:         // farthest K-th. If c is closer than that, swap in.
 250:         let kth = self.closest.last().copied();
 251:         let Some(kth) = kth else {
 252:             return false;
 253:         };
 254:         let c_closer = closer_to(&c, &kth, &self.target);
 255:         if c_closer == std::cmp::Ordering::Less {
 256:             self.closest.push(c);
 257:             true
 258:         } else {
 259:             false
 260:         }
 261:     }
 262: }

 295:     impl Transport for StubTransport {
 296:         fn query<'a>(
 297:             &'a self,
 298:             peer: NodeId,
 299:             target: NodeId,
 300:             _want_value: bool,
 301:         ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = LookupQueryResult> + Send + 'a>> {
 302:             self.queries_seen.lock().unwrap().push((peer, target));
 303:             let r = self
 304:                 .responses
 305:                 .get(&peer)
 306:                 .cloned()
 307:                 .unwrap_or(LookupQueryResult::Failed);
 308:             Box::pin(async move { r })
 309:         }
 310:     }
 311: 
 312:     fn block_on<F: Future>(f: F) -> F::Output {
 313:         use std::task::{Context, Poll, Wake, Waker};
 314:         use std::sync::Arc;
 315:         struct N;
 316:         impl Wake for N {
 317:             fn wake(self: Arc<Self>) {}
 318:         }
 319:         let waker = Waker::from(Arc::new(N));
 320:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
 321:         let mut fut = Box::pin(f);
 322:         loop {
 323:             match fut.as_mut().poll(&mut cx) {
 324:                 Poll::Ready(r) => return r,
 325:                 Poll::Pending => continue,
 326:             }
 327:         }
 328:     }

   1: //! 256-bit NodeId derived from a peer's Ed25519 master pubkey, plus
   2: //! XOR distance metric and bit-prefix utilities.
   3: //!
   4: //! The NodeId is BLAKE3(ed25519_pubkey), so:
   5: //!   - Two peers cannot collide on NodeId without colliding on BLAKE3.
   6: //!   - An attacker targeting a specific prefix must keygen until a
   7: //!     pubkey hashes to that prefix — Ed25519 keygen is CPU-bound
   8: //!     (no GPU shortcut), so this is a real cost for Sybil attacks.
   9: 
  10: use core::cmp::Ordering;
  11: 
  12: /// NodeId length in bytes. Matches BLAKE3 output (32 bytes = 256 bits).
  13: pub const NODE_ID_BYTES: usize = 32;
  14: 
  15: /// NodeId length in bits. Equals `NODE_ID_BYTES * 8`.
  16: pub const NODE_ID_BITS: usize = NODE_ID_BYTES * 8;
  17: 
  18: /// A 256-bit Kademlia node identifier.
  19: ///
  20: /// Constructed from an Ed25519 master pubkey via [`NodeId::from_pubkey`].
  21: /// Equality + ordering are byte-lexicographic. Distance is XOR-metric
  22: /// (interpreted as a 256-bit unsigned integer), accessed via
  23: /// [`NodeId::distance`] / [`NodeId::xor_leading_zeros`].
  24: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  25: pub struct NodeId(pub [u8; NODE_ID_BYTES]);
  26: 
  27: impl NodeId {
  28:     /// Construct from raw bytes.
  29:     #[must_use]
  30:     pub const fn from_bytes(b: [u8; NODE_ID_BYTES]) -> Self {
  31:         Self(b)
  32:     }
  33: 
  34:     /// Derive a NodeId from an Ed25519 master pubkey (32 bytes).
  35:     /// `NodeId = BLAKE3(pubkey)`. Pure, deterministic, collision-
  36:     /// resistant under BLAKE3.
  37:     #[must_use]
  38:     pub fn from_pubkey(pubkey: &[u8; 32]) -> Self {
  39:         let h = blake3::hash(pubkey);
  40:         Self(*h.as_bytes())
  41:     }
  42: 
  43:     /// Borrow the underlying bytes.
  44:     #[must_use]
  45:     pub const fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; NODE_ID_BYTES] {
  46:         &self.0
  47:     }
  48: 
  49:     /// XOR distance: `self ^ other` interpreted as a 256-bit unsigned
  50:     /// integer. Returned as raw bytes; the smallest distance is all-
  51:     /// zero (`self == other`).
  52:     ///
  53:     /// Used by Kademlia routing to pick "closest" peers; smaller XOR
  54:     /// = closer in the metric space.
  55:     #[must_use]
  56:     pub fn distance(&self, other: &Self) -> [u8; NODE_ID_BYTES] {
  57:         let mut out = [0u8; NODE_ID_BYTES];
  58:         for i in 0..NODE_ID_BYTES {
  59:             out[i] = self.0[i] ^ other.0[i];
  60:         }
  61:         out
  62:     }
  63: 
  64:     /// Number of leading zero bits in `self XOR other`. Equivalent
  65:     /// to the K-bucket index for `other` from `self`'s perspective.
  66:     ///
  67:     /// Returns `NODE_ID_BITS` (256) when self == other (distance is
  68:     /// all-zero). Constant-time per bit-position, branch-free over
  69:     /// byte chunks.
  70:     #[must_use]
  71:     pub fn xor_leading_zeros(&self, other: &Self) -> u32 {
  72:         let mut count: u32 = 0;
  73:         for i in 0..NODE_ID_BYTES {
  74:             let x = self.0[i] ^ other.0[i];
  75:             if x == 0 {
  76:                 count += 8;
  77:             } else {
  78:                 count += x.leading_zeros();
  79:                 return count;
  80:             }
  81:         }
  82:         count
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     /// K-bucket index for `other` viewed from `self`. Bucket k holds
  86:     /// peers whose XOR-distance has exactly k leading zeros: bucket
  87:     /// 0 is the "farthest" (top bit differs), bucket 255 is the
  88:     /// "closest non-self". Identity (self) belongs to no bucket.
  89:     ///
  90:     /// Returns `None` when `self == other`. Otherwise returns an
  91:     /// index in `0..NODE_ID_BITS`.
  92:     #[must_use]
  93:     pub fn bucket_index(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<usize> {
  94:         let lz = self.xor_leading_zeros(other);
  95:         if (lz as usize) >= NODE_ID_BITS {
  96:             None
  97:         } else {
  98:             Some(lz as usize)
  99:         }
 100:     }
 101: }
 102: 
 103: impl Ord for NodeId {
 104:     fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {
 105:         self.0.cmp(&other.0)
 106:     }
 107: }
 108: 
 109: impl PartialOrd for NodeId {
 110:     fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {
 111:         Some(self.cmp(other))
 112:     }
 113: }
 114: 
 115: impl core::fmt::Debug for NodeId {
 116:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
 117:         // Short-hex for log readability: first 4 bytes only.
 118:         write!(
 119:             f,
 120:             "NodeId({:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}…)",
 121:             self.0[0], self.0[1], self.0[2], self.0[3]
 122:         )
 123:     }
 124: }
 125: 
 126: /// XOR-distance comparator: returns the ordering of distance(a, target)
 127: /// vs distance(b, target). Smaller XOR == "closer".
 128: #[must_use]
 129: pub fn closer_to(a: &NodeId, b: &NodeId, target: &NodeId) -> Ordering {
 130:     let da = a.distance(target);
 131:     let db = b.distance(target);
 132:     // Both are 32-byte big-endian unsigned ints; lexicographic compare
 133:     // of the byte arrays gives integer order.
 134:     da.cmp(&db)
 135: }

 192:             let byte = k / 8;

 197:             assert_eq!(a.xor_leading_zeros(&b), k as u32, "k={k}");

   1: //! Signed peer-announcement records published into the DHT.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each record carries:
   4: //!   - The publisher's Ed25519 master pubkey (32 bytes).
   5: //!   - Reachability endpoints (transport addresses).
   6: //!   - A freshness timestamp (publish_time, unix seconds).
   7: //!   - A TTL (record expires at publish_time + ttl_secs).
   8: //!   - An Ed25519 signature by the publisher over the canonical
   9: //!     byte serialization of the above.
  10: //!
  11: //! Lookups verify the signature before trusting any returned record.
  12: //! Forged records are rejected at lookup time, not stored.
  13: 
  14: use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey};
  15: use thiserror::Error;
  16: 
  17: use crate::node_id::NodeId;
  18: 
  19: /// Default record TTL: 24 hours. Publishers republish on a tick (~1h).
  20: pub const RECORD_DEFAULT_TTL_SECS: u64 = 24 * 60 * 60;
  21: 
  22: /// Maximum endpoint string length. Bounded to keep records small +
  23: /// resistant to amplification attacks during DHT gossip.
  24: const MAX_ENDPOINT_LEN: usize = 128;
  25: 
  26: /// Maximum number of endpoints per record. Keeps record size bounded.
  27: const MAX_ENDPOINTS: usize = 8;
  28: 
  29: /// The unsigned record payload. This is what's signed; serialization
  30: /// is canonical (length-prefixed; same encoding both sides) so a
  31: /// signature commits to a unique byte string.
  32: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  33: pub struct PeerRecord {
  34:     /// Ed25519 master pubkey of the publisher. The NodeId is
  35:     /// `BLAKE3(pubkey)`; lookups verify signature against this key.
  36:     pub publisher_pubkey: [u8; 32],
  37:     /// Reachability endpoints. Each is a transport-specific
  38:     /// address string ("udp://1.2.3.4:5678", "quic://host:port",
  39:     /// "circuit-relay://peer-fp/path", etc.). Length-bounded.
  40:     pub endpoints: Vec<String>,
  41:     /// Unix seconds when the record was published.
  42:     pub publish_time_unix: u64,
  43:     /// Record-lifetime seconds; expires at `publish_time + ttl`.
  44:     pub ttl_secs: u64,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl PeerRecord {
  48:     /// Compute the canonical byte serialization that gets signed.
  49:     ///
  50:     /// Format (length-prefixed, big-endian sizes):
  51:     ///   - 4-byte magic "OLR1"
  52:     ///   - 32-byte publisher_pubkey
  53:     ///   - 8-byte publish_time_unix (BE)
  54:     ///   - 8-byte ttl_secs (BE)
  55:     ///   - 2-byte n_endpoints (BE)
  56:     ///   - For each endpoint:
  57:     ///       - 2-byte len (BE)
  58:     ///       - `len` bytes UTF-8
  59:     ///
  60:     /// Pure; same input always produces same output. Used both for
  61:     /// signing and verification.
  62:     #[must_use]
  63:     pub fn canonical_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
  64:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(64 + self.endpoints.len() * 64);
  65:         out.extend_from_slice(b"OLR1");
  66:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.publisher_pubkey);
  67:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.publish_time_unix.to_be_bytes());
  68:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.ttl_secs.to_be_bytes());
  69:         let n = u16::try_from(self.endpoints.len().min(u16::MAX as usize))
  70:             .unwrap_or(u16::MAX);
  71:         out.extend_from_slice(&n.to_be_bytes());
  72:         for ep in &self.endpoints {
  73:             let bytes = ep.as_bytes();
  74:             let len = u16::try_from(bytes.len().min(u16::MAX as usize))
  75:                 .unwrap_or(u16::MAX);
  76:             out.extend_from_slice(&len.to_be_bytes());
  77:             out.extend_from_slice(&bytes[..len as usize]);
  78:         }
  79:         out
  80:     }
  81: 
  82:     /// The NodeId implied by this record's publisher pubkey.
  83:     #[must_use]
  84:     pub fn node_id(&self) -> NodeId {
  85:         NodeId::from_pubkey(&self.publisher_pubkey)
  86:     }
  87: 
  88:     /// Is the record currently fresh (not expired)?
  89:     ///
  90:     /// `now_unix` is the caller's current unix-seconds clock.
  91:     #[must_use]
  92:     pub fn is_fresh(&self, now_unix: u64) -> bool {
  93:         now_unix < self.publish_time_unix.saturating_add(self.ttl_secs)
  94:     }
  95: 
  96:     /// Validate basic record shape (size bounds, non-empty).
  97:     fn shape_check(&self) -> Result<(), RecordError> {
  98:         if self.endpoints.len() > MAX_ENDPOINTS {
  99:             return Err(RecordError::TooManyEndpoints {
 100:                 got: self.endpoints.len(),
 101:                 max: MAX_ENDPOINTS,
 102:             });
 103:         }
 104:         for ep in &self.endpoints {
 105:             if ep.len() > MAX_ENDPOINT_LEN {
 106:                 return Err(RecordError::EndpointTooLong {
 107:                     got: ep.len(),
 108:                     max: MAX_ENDPOINT_LEN,
 109:                 });
 110:             }
 111:         }
 112:         Ok(())
 113:     }
 114: }
 115: 
 116: /// Errors that can occur signing / verifying / parsing records.
 117: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
 118: pub enum RecordError {
 119:     /// Signature verification failed.
 120:     #[error("signature verification failed")]
 121:     BadSignature,
 122:     /// Publisher pubkey is malformed (not a valid Ed25519 point).
 123:     #[error("malformed publisher pubkey")]
 124:     MalformedPubkey,
 125:     /// Record has more than [`MAX_ENDPOINTS`] endpoints.
 126:     #[error("too many endpoints: {got} (max {max})")]
 127:     TooManyEndpoints {
 128:         /// Actual count.
 129:         got: usize,
 130:         /// Maximum allowed.
 131:         max: usize,
 132:     },
 133:     /// One endpoint exceeds [`MAX_ENDPOINT_LEN`] bytes.
 134:     #[error("endpoint too long: {got} bytes (max {max})")]
 135:     EndpointTooLong {
 136:         /// Actual length.
 137:         got: usize,
 138:         /// Maximum allowed.
 139:         max: usize,
 140:     },
 141:     /// Record's claimed publisher pubkey doesn't match the signing
 142:     /// key (defensive check; the public API generally signs a record
 143:     /// with its own publisher_pubkey).
 144:     #[error("record's publisher_pubkey doesn't match the signing key")]
 145:     PubkeyMismatch,
 146: }
 147: 
 148: /// A signed record: the payload plus the 64-byte Ed25519 signature
 149: /// over its canonical bytes. This is what gossips through the DHT.
 150: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
 151: pub struct SignedRecord {
 152:     /// The underlying payload.
 153:     pub record: PeerRecord,
 154:     /// Ed25519 signature over `record.canonical_bytes()`.
 155:     pub signature: [u8; 64],
 156: }
 157: 
 158: impl SignedRecord {
 159:     /// Sign `record` with `signing_key`. The signing key's public
 160:     /// component MUST equal `record.publisher_pubkey` (defensive
 161:     /// check; prevents a caller from accidentally signing a record
 162:     /// that claims a different publisher).
 163:     ///
 164:     /// # Errors
 165:     /// - [`RecordError::PubkeyMismatch`] when the signing key's
 166:     ///   public component doesn't match `record.publisher_pubkey`.
 167:     /// - [`RecordError::TooManyEndpoints`] / [`RecordError::EndpointTooLong`]
 168:     ///   on shape violations.
 169:     pub fn sign(
 170:         record: PeerRecord,
 171:         signing_key: &SigningKey,
 172:     ) -> Result<Self, RecordError> {
 173:         record.shape_check()?;
 174:         let derived_pub: VerifyingKey = signing_key.verifying_key();
 175:         if derived_pub.to_bytes() != record.publisher_pubkey {
 176:             return Err(RecordError::PubkeyMismatch);
 177:         }
 178:         let bytes = record.canonical_bytes();
 179:         let sig: Signature = signing_key.sign(&bytes);
 180:         Ok(Self {
 181:             record,
 182:             signature: sig.to_bytes(),
 183:         })
 184:     }
 185: 
 186:     /// Verify the signature against the record's canonical bytes.
 187:     ///
 188:     /// # Errors
 189:     /// - [`RecordError::MalformedPubkey`] when the publisher pubkey
 190:     ///   isn't a valid Ed25519 point.
 191:     /// - [`RecordError::BadSignature`] on any verification failure.
 192:     pub fn verify(&self) -> Result<(), RecordError> {
 193:         self.record.shape_check()?;
 194:         let verifying_key = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&self.record.publisher_pubkey)
 195:             .map_err(|_| RecordError::MalformedPubkey)?;
 196:         let sig = Signature::from_bytes(&self.signature);
 197:         let bytes = self.record.canonical_bytes();
 198:         verifying_key
 199:             .verify(&bytes, &sig)
 200:             .map_err(|_| RecordError::BadSignature)
 201:     }
 202: 
 203:     /// Convenience: verify + check freshness in one call.
 204:     ///
 205:     /// # Errors
 206:     /// Same as [`Self::verify`], plus returns `Ok(false)` (not an
 207:     /// error) when the record is expired but the signature is valid.
 208:     pub fn verify_and_check_freshness(
 209:         &self,
 210:         now_unix: u64,
 211:     ) -> Result<bool, RecordError> {
 212:         self.verify()?;
 213:         Ok(self.record.is_fresh(now_unix))
 214:     }
 215: 
 216:     /// The NodeId the record refers to.
 217:     #[must_use]
 218:     pub fn node_id(&self) -> NodeId {
 219:         self.record.node_id()
 220:     }
 221: }

 352:     }
 353: }

   1: //! K-bucket routing table.
   2: //!
   3: //! Vanilla Kademlia: 256 buckets (one per bit of the NodeId), each
   4: //! holding up to K most-recently-seen peers. New peers go to the
   5: //! tail of their bucket; existing peers move to the tail when seen
   6: //! again ("recently-seen-most-recent" replacement policy).
   7: //!
   8: //! When a bucket is full and a new peer wants in, we ping the head
   9: //! (least-recently-seen). If the head responds, the new peer is
  10: //! discarded (existing peers preferred — defeats eclipse via flooding).
  11: //! If the head times out, it's replaced by the new peer. This
  12: //! "least-recently-seen replacement" is the Kademlia stability
  13: //! property: long-lived nodes that respond stay in the table.
  14: //!
  15: //! This module provides the routing-table data structure ONLY. The
  16: //! liveness check (PING-on-bucket-full) is a higher-level concern
  17: //! that the daemon's maintenance loop handles via the `Transport`
  18: //! trait; the table itself just exposes
  19: //!   - [`RoutingTable::insert`]: tentatively add a peer; returns
  20: //!     [`InsertOutcome::Inserted`] / `BumpedToTail` / `BucketFull`
  21: //!     so the caller can issue a PING when needed.
  22: //!   - [`RoutingTable::closest_to`]: get the K closest peers to a
  23: //!     target, sorted by XOR distance (lookup primitive).
  24: //!   - [`RoutingTable::stale_buckets`]: which buckets haven't been
  25: //!     touched in `now - max_age_secs`, so the maintenance loop can
  26: //!     run bucket-refresh lookups against them.
  27: 
  28: use std::cmp::Ordering;
  29: use std::collections::VecDeque;
  30: 
  31: use crate::node_id::{closer_to, NodeId, NODE_ID_BITS};
  32: 
  33: /// Default K (replication factor / bucket size). Kademlia paper uses
  34: /// K=20 as the standard; we match.
  35: pub const K_BUCKET_DEFAULT: usize = 20;
  36: 
  37: /// Number of buckets in the table. One per bit of the NodeId.
  38: pub const MAX_BUCKETS: usize = NODE_ID_BITS; // 256
  39: 
  40: /// One bucket entry: a peer the local node has heard from.
  41: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  42: pub struct BucketEntry {
  43:     /// The peer's NodeId.
  44:     pub id: NodeId,
  45:     /// Unix-seconds timestamp the entry was last touched (last seen).
  46:     /// Used for least-recently-seen eviction.
  47:     pub last_seen_unix: u64,
  48: }
  49: 
  50: impl BucketEntry {
  51:     /// Construct an entry.
  52:     #[must_use]
  53:     pub const fn new(id: NodeId, last_seen_unix: u64) -> Self {
  54:         Self { id, last_seen_unix }
  55:     }
  56: }
  57: 
  58: /// Outcome of attempting to insert a peer into the routing table.
  59: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  60: pub enum InsertOutcome {
  61:     /// Peer was new to the bucket; added.
  62:     Inserted,
  63:     /// Peer already existed; bumped to tail (most-recently-seen).
  64:     BumpedToTail,
  65:     /// Peer is the local node itself — never inserted.
  66:     SelfInsertIgnored,
  67:     /// Bucket is full. Caller should PING the head (least-recently-
  68:     /// seen) and call [`RoutingTable::replace_head_on_timeout`] if
  69:     /// the PING times out. Carries the head entry for the PING.
  70:     BucketFull {
  71:         /// The head (least-recently-seen) of the full bucket.
  72:         head: BucketEntry,
  73:     },
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// One K-bucket. Wraps a VecDeque so head-removal + tail-push are O(1).
  77: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
  78: struct Bucket {
  79:     entries: VecDeque<BucketEntry>,
  80:     last_refresh_unix: u64,
  81: }
  82: 
  83: /// Kademlia K-bucket routing table.
  84: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
  85: pub struct RoutingTable {
  86:     own_id: NodeId,
  87:     k: usize,
  88:     buckets: Vec<Bucket>,
  89: }
  90: 
  91: impl RoutingTable {
  92:     /// Construct a new table for the given local NodeId.
  93:     /// Uses the default K (= [`K_BUCKET_DEFAULT`]).
  94:     #[must_use]
  95:     pub fn new(own_id: NodeId) -> Self {
  96:         Self::with_k(own_id, K_BUCKET_DEFAULT)
  97:     }
  98: 
  99:     /// Construct with a custom K.
 100:     #[must_use]
 101:     pub fn with_k(own_id: NodeId, k: usize) -> Self {
 102:         let mut buckets = Vec::with_capacity(MAX_BUCKETS);
 103:         for _ in 0..MAX_BUCKETS {
 104:             buckets.push(Bucket::default());
 105:         }
 106:         Self { own_id, k, buckets }
 107:     }
 108: 
 109:     /// Borrow the local NodeId.
 110:     #[must_use]
 111:     pub const fn own_id(&self) -> &NodeId {
 112:         &self.own_id
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     /// K (bucket size) parameter.
 116:     #[must_use]
 117:     pub const fn k(&self) -> usize {
 118:         self.k
 119:     }
 120: 
 121:     /// Total number of peers currently in the table.
 122:     #[must_use]
 123:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 124:         self.buckets.iter().map(|b| b.entries.len()).sum()
 125:     }
 126: 
 127:     /// True when no peers are in the table.
 128:     #[must_use]
 129:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 130:         self.buckets.iter().all(|b| b.entries.is_empty())
 131:     }
 132: 
 133:     /// Insert (or update) a peer.
 134:     ///
 135:     /// - New peer → tail of bucket → [`InsertOutcome::Inserted`].
 136:     /// - Existing peer → bumped to tail → [`InsertOutcome::BumpedToTail`].
 137:     /// - Self → ignored → [`InsertOutcome::SelfInsertIgnored`].
 138:     /// - Bucket full + new peer → returns
 139:     ///   [`InsertOutcome::BucketFull`] carrying the head entry. Caller
 140:     ///   pings the head; if head replies, the new peer is discarded;
 141:     ///   if head times out, caller invokes
 142:     ///   [`Self::replace_head_on_timeout`].
 143:     pub fn insert(
 144:         &mut self,
 145:         id: NodeId,
 146:         last_seen_unix: u64,
 147:     ) -> InsertOutcome {
 148:         let Some(idx) = self.own_id.bucket_index(&id) else {
 149:             return InsertOutcome::SelfInsertIgnored;
 150:         };
 151:         let bucket = &mut self.buckets[idx];
 152:         // Existing peer? Move to tail with updated timestamp.
 153:         if let Some(pos) = bucket.entries.iter().position(|e| e.id == id) {
 154:             let mut existing = bucket.entries.remove(pos).expect("position valid");
 155:             existing.last_seen_unix = last_seen_unix;
 156:             bucket.entries.push_back(existing);
 157:             bucket.last_refresh_unix = last_seen_unix;
 158:             return InsertOutcome::BumpedToTail;
 159:         }
 160:         // New peer; bucket has room?
 161:         if bucket.entries.len() < self.k {
 162:             bucket.entries.push_back(BucketEntry::new(id, last_seen_unix));
 163:             bucket.last_refresh_unix = last_seen_unix;
 164:             return InsertOutcome::Inserted;
 165:         }
 166:         // Bucket full. Caller decides what to do via PING.
 167:         let head = *bucket.entries.front().expect("non-empty (k > 0)");
 168:         InsertOutcome::BucketFull { head }
 169:     }
 170: 
 171:     /// Called by the maintenance loop when a PING-on-bucket-full
 172:     /// targets the head and the head times out. Removes the head
 173:     /// and inserts the new peer at the tail.
 174:     ///
 175:     /// Returns `true` iff the head was actually replaced. Returns
 176:     /// `false` if the head no longer exists (someone else evicted
 177:     /// it in the meantime, or the new peer happened to land in a
 178:     /// different bucket — defensive).
 179:     pub fn replace_head_on_timeout(
 180:         &mut self,
 181:         timed_out_head: NodeId,
 182:         new_peer: NodeId,
 183:         last_seen_unix: u64,
 184:     ) -> bool {
 185:         let Some(idx) = self.own_id.bucket_index(&new_peer) else {
 186:             return false;
 187:         };
 188:         let bucket = &mut self.buckets[idx];
 189:         match bucket.entries.front() {
 190:             Some(head) if head.id == timed_out_head => {
 191:                 bucket.entries.pop_front();
 192:                 bucket.entries.push_back(BucketEntry::new(
 193:                     new_peer,
 194:                     last_seen_unix,
 195:                 ));
 196:                 bucket.last_refresh_unix = last_seen_unix;
 197:                 true
 198:             }
 199:             _ => false,
 200:         }
 201:     }
 202: 
 203:     /// Get the K closest peers to `target`, sorted by XOR distance
 204:     /// ascending. Returns at most K entries.
 205:     ///
 206:     /// This is the Kademlia lookup primitive: callers query these
 207:     /// K peers, then iteratively refine via responses. Pure read.
 208:     #[must_use]
 209:     pub fn closest_to(&self, target: &NodeId) -> Vec<BucketEntry> {
 210:         let mut all: Vec<BucketEntry> = self
 211:             .buckets
 212:             .iter()
 213:             .flat_map(|b| b.entries.iter().copied())
 214:             .collect();
 215:         all.sort_by(|a, b| closer_to(&a.id, &b.id, target));
 216:         all.truncate(self.k);
 217:         all
 218:     }
 219: 
 220:     /// Variant of `closest_to` that returns at most `n` entries
 221:     /// rather than K. Useful when a lookup needs α candidates to
 222:     /// query in parallel where α < K.
 223:     #[must_use]
 224:     pub fn closest_n_to(
 225:         &self,
 226:         target: &NodeId,
 227:         n: usize,
 228:     ) -> Vec<BucketEntry> {
 229:         let mut all: Vec<BucketEntry> = self
 230:             .buckets
 231:             .iter()
 232:             .flat_map(|b| b.entries.iter().copied())
 233:             .collect();
 234:         all.sort_by(|a, b| closer_to(&a.id, &b.id, target));
 235:         all.truncate(n);
 236:         all
 237:     }
 238: 
 239:     /// Bucket indices whose `last_refresh_unix` is older than
 240:     /// `now_unix - max_age_secs`. Returns indices sorted ascending.
 241:     ///
 242:     /// The maintenance loop runs a `FIND_NODE` lookup against each
 243:     /// stale bucket using a randomly-chosen NodeId in that bucket's
 244:     /// distance range, which has the effect of populating + refreshing
 245:     /// the bucket.
 246:     #[must_use]
 247:     pub fn stale_buckets(
 248:         &self,
 249:         now_unix: u64,
 250:         max_age_secs: u64,
 251:     ) -> Vec<usize> {
 252:         let threshold = now_unix.saturating_sub(max_age_secs);
 253:         let mut out = Vec::new();
 254:         for (i, b) in self.buckets.iter().enumerate() {
 255:             if !b.entries.is_empty() && b.last_refresh_unix <= threshold {
 256:                 out.push(i);
 257:             }
 258:         }
 259:         out
 260:     }
 261: 
 262:     /// Remove a peer (e.g. because they failed too many PINGs).
 263:     /// Returns `true` iff the peer was present.
 264:     pub fn remove(&mut self, id: &NodeId) -> bool {
 265:         let Some(idx) = self.own_id.bucket_index(id) else {
 266:             return false;
 267:         };
 268:         let bucket = &mut self.buckets[idx];
 269:         if let Some(pos) = bucket.entries.iter().position(|e| e.id == *id) {
 270:             bucket.entries.remove(pos);
 271:             true
 272:         } else {
 273:             false
 274:         }
 275:     }
 276: 
 277:     /// True iff `id` is present in the table.
 278:     #[must_use]
 279:     pub fn contains(&self, id: &NodeId) -> bool {
 280:         let Some(idx) = self.own_id.bucket_index(id) else {
 281:             return false;
 282:         };
 283:         self.buckets[idx].entries.iter().any(|e| e.id == *id)
 284:     }
 285: 
 286:     /// Diagnostic: number of peers in each bucket index. Index 0 is
 287:     /// the farthest bucket; index 255 is closest-to-self.
 288:     #[must_use]
 289:     pub fn bucket_sizes(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
 290:         self.buckets.iter().map(|b| b.entries.len()).collect()
 291:     }
 292: 
 293:     /// Mark a bucket as just-refreshed. Maintenance loops call this
 294:     /// after issuing a FIND_NODE refresh lookup against the bucket
 295:     /// so subsequent `stale_buckets()` queries don't immediately
 296:     /// re-flag it.
 297:     pub fn mark_bucket_refreshed(&mut self, bucket_idx: usize, now_unix: u64) {
 298:         if let Some(b) = self.buckets.get_mut(bucket_idx) {
 299:             b.last_refresh_unix = now_unix;
 300:         }
 301:     }
 302: 
 303:     /// Generate a NodeId that lives in bucket `bucket_idx` (relative
 304:     /// to `own_id`). Used by maintenance to issue refresh lookups
 305:     /// targeting the right distance range.
 306:     ///
 307:     /// Returns `None` if `bucket_idx >= NODE_ID_BITS`.
 308:     ///
 309:     /// `NodeId::bucket_index` uses `xor_leading_zeros == bucket_idx`
 310:     /// semantics — meaning the first differing bit (counting from MSB)
 311:     /// must be at position `bucket_idx`. So flip exactly the
 312:     /// `bucket_idx`-th MSB of `own_id` and the XOR has `bucket_idx`
 313:     /// leading zeros before its first 1-bit.
 314:     #[must_use]
 315:     pub fn synthetic_id_for_bucket(&self, bucket_idx: usize) -> Option<NodeId> {
 316:         if bucket_idx >= crate::node_id::NODE_ID_BITS {
 317:             return None;
 318:         }
 319:         let byte_idx = bucket_idx / 8;
 320:         let bit_in_byte = 7 - (bucket_idx % 8);
 321:         let mut out = *self.own_id.as_bytes();
 322:         out[byte_idx] ^= 1u8 << bit_in_byte;
 323:         Some(NodeId::from_bytes(out))
 324:     }
 325: }
 326: 
 327: /// Sort utility: stable-sort a list of NodeIds by XOR distance to
 328: /// `target`, ascending. Used by the lookup algorithm.
 329: pub fn sort_by_distance(ids: &mut Vec<NodeId>, target: &NodeId) {
 330:     ids.sort_by(|a, b| {
 331:         let cmp = closer_to(a, b, target);
 332:         if cmp == Ordering::Equal {
 333:             a.cmp(b)
 334:         } else {
 335:             cmp
 336:         }
 337:     });
 338: }

   1: //! RPC envelope types for Kademlia messages.
   2: //!
   3: //! Four RPC pairs:
   4: //!
   5: //!   - **PING / PONG**: liveness probe. Used by routing-table head
   6: //!     replacement (PING on bucket-full) + maintenance refresh.
   7: //!   - **STORE / STORE_ACK**: publish a signed record to the
   8: //!     receiver's local store. Receiver verifies signature before
   9: //!     storing; rejects bad signatures with a typed error code.
  10: //!   - **FIND_NODE / FIND_NODE_RESULT**: ask the receiver for the K
  11: //!     closest peers it knows to `target`. Receiver responds with
  12: //!     its routing-table closest_to(target).
  13: //!   - **FIND_VALUE / FIND_VALUE_RESULT**: ask for the value at
  14: //!     `target` (typically a NodeId being looked up). Receiver
  15: //!     returns the signed record if it has it, OR the K closest
  16: //!     peers otherwise (then the caller iteratively queries them).
  17: //!
  18: //! Every envelope carries a `nonce` (replay-protection within one
  19: //! exchange) and a `timestamp` (replay-protection across exchanges).
  20: //! Stale or duplicate envelopes are rejected by the receiver.
  21: //!
  22: //! Wire format is intentionally not specified at the byte level by
  23: //! this module — the daemon-side transport binding handles encoding
  24: //! (it can use canonical-bytes-of-struct, CBOR, or any encoding
  25: //! consistent across peers). The struct shapes are what's shared.
  26: 
  27: use thiserror::Error;
  28: 
  29: use crate::node_id::NodeId;
  30: use crate::record::SignedRecord;
  31: 
  32: /// Maximum allowed clock skew between sender and receiver. Envelopes
  33: /// dated more than this far in the future or past are rejected.
  34: pub const MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS: u64 = 60 * 5; // 5 minutes
  35: 
  36: /// Maximum K results in a single FIND_NODE / FIND_VALUE response.
  37: /// Bounded to keep response sizes amplification-resistant.
  38: pub const MAX_FIND_RESULTS: usize = 32;
  39: 
  40: /// A 128-bit random nonce per envelope. Used together with the
  41: /// envelope's sender NodeId to deduplicate replays within a window.
  42: pub type Nonce = [u8; 16];
  43: 
  44: /// Common header shared by every RPC envelope.
  45: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  46: pub struct Header {
  47:     /// NodeId of the sender. The receiver uses this to refresh the
  48:     /// sender's routing-table entry on every received envelope.
  49:     pub sender: NodeId,
  50:     /// 16-byte random nonce. Receiver rejects duplicates in a
  51:     /// recent-window LRU.
  52:     pub nonce: Nonce,
  53:     /// Unix-seconds wall clock from the sender. Rejected if outside
  54:     /// [now - MAX_CLOCK_SKEW, now + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW].
  55:     pub timestamp_unix: u64,
  56: }
  57: 
  58: impl Header {
  59:     /// Construct a new header.
  60:     #[must_use]
  61:     pub const fn new(sender: NodeId, nonce: Nonce, timestamp_unix: u64) -> Self {
  62:         Self {
  63:             sender,
  64:             nonce,
  65:             timestamp_unix,
  66:         }
  67:     }
  68: 
  69:     /// Is this header acceptable to a receiver whose clock is `now_unix`?
  70:     /// Checks the timestamp is within [now - MAX_CLOCK_SKEW, now + MAX_CLOCK_SKEW].
  71:     #[must_use]
  72:     pub fn is_within_skew(&self, now_unix: u64) -> bool {
  73:         let lo = now_unix.saturating_sub(MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS);
  74:         let hi = now_unix.saturating_add(MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS);
  75:         self.timestamp_unix >= lo && self.timestamp_unix <= hi
  76:     }
  77: }
  78: 
  79: /// RPC request kinds.
  80: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  81: pub enum Request {
  82:     /// Liveness probe. No payload beyond the header.
  83:     Ping,
  84:     /// "Store this signed record." Receiver verifies signature
  85:     /// and rejects if invalid.
  86:     Store(SignedRecord),
  87:     /// "Give me the K closest peers you know to `target`."
  88:     FindNode {
  89:         /// NodeId being searched for.
  90:         target: NodeId,
  91:     },
  92:     /// "Give me the value for `target`, or the K closest peers if
  93:     /// you don't have it."
  94:     FindValue {
  95:         /// NodeId being looked up.
  96:         target: NodeId,
  97:     },
  98: }
  99: 
 100: /// RPC response kinds, paired with their request types.
 101: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
 102: pub enum Response {
 103:     /// PING response — alive.
 104:     Pong,
 105:     /// STORE response — accepted or rejected with a typed code.
 106:     StoreResult(StoreOutcome),
 107:     /// FIND_NODE response — closest K peers known to the receiver.
 108:     FindNodeResult {
 109:         /// Up to K peer NodeIds, sorted ascending by XOR distance
 110:         /// to the original `target`.
 111:         closest: Vec<NodeId>,
 112:     },
 113:     /// FIND_VALUE response — either the signed record, or K closest
 114:     /// if the receiver doesn't hold the record.
 115:     FindValueResult(FindValueOutcome),
 116: }
 117: 
 118: /// STORE outcome: receiver accepted or rejected the record.
 119: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
 120: pub enum StoreOutcome {
 121:     /// Accepted; record is now in the receiver's local store.
 122:     Accepted,
 123:     /// Rejected — record signature failed verification.
 124:     BadSignature,
 125:     /// Rejected — record was already expired at receipt.
 126:     Expired,
 127:     /// Rejected — record's claimed publisher doesn't match the
 128:     /// record's NodeId derivation.
 129:     PublisherMismatch,
 130:     /// Rejected — receiver is rate-limiting this sender.
 131:     RateLimited,
 132: }
 133: 
 134: /// FIND_VALUE outcome: either we have the record, or we have closer
 135: /// peers to recommend.
 136: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
 137: pub enum FindValueOutcome {
 138:     /// Receiver has the record. Returned verbatim; caller still
 139:     /// verifies the signature before trusting.
 140:     Found(SignedRecord),
 141:     /// Receiver doesn't have it but knows these closer peers.
 142:     /// Up to K NodeIds, sorted ascending by XOR distance to target.
 143:     Closer(Vec<NodeId>),
 144: }
 145: 
 146: /// A complete RPC envelope. `body` is request OR response; senders
 147: /// and receivers distinguish by structural type, not a kind byte.
 148: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
 149: pub struct RpcEnvelope<B> {
 150:     /// Common header.
 151:     pub header: Header,
 152:     /// Payload (Request or Response).
 153:     pub body: B,
 154: }
 155: 
 156: /// Errors during RPC processing.
 157: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
 158: pub enum RpcError {
 159:     /// Sender's clock is outside the acceptable skew window.
 160:     #[error("envelope timestamp outside acceptable skew window")]
 161:     ClockSkew,
 162:     /// Sender is replaying an envelope (nonce + sender already seen).
 163:     #[error("duplicate envelope nonce from this sender")]
 164:     DuplicateNonce,
 165:     /// Response carries more than [`MAX_FIND_RESULTS`] entries.
 166:     #[error("too many results in response: {got} (max {max})")]
 167:     TooManyResults {
 168:         /// Actual count.
 169:         got: usize,
 170:         /// Maximum allowed.
 171:         max: usize,
 172:     },
 173: }
 174: 
 175: /// Validate a response's result-count bound. Catches malformed peers
 176: /// that try to amplify by returning >K results.
 177: ///
 178: /// # Errors
 179: /// Returns [`RpcError::TooManyResults`] if a list-bearing response
 180: /// exceeds [`MAX_FIND_RESULTS`].
 181: pub fn validate_response_size(resp: &Response) -> Result<(), RpcError> {
 182:     match resp {
 183:         Response::FindNodeResult { closest } => {
 184:             if closest.len() > MAX_FIND_RESULTS {
 185:                 return Err(RpcError::TooManyResults {
 186:                     got: closest.len(),
 187:                     max: MAX_FIND_RESULTS,
 188:                 });
 189:             }
 190:         }
 191:         Response::FindValueResult(FindValueOutcome::Closer(closer)) => {
 192:             if closer.len() > MAX_FIND_RESULTS {
 193:                 return Err(RpcError::TooManyResults {
 194:                     got: closer.len(),
 195:                     max: MAX_FIND_RESULTS,
 196:                 });
 197:             }
 198:         }
 199:         _ => {}
 200:     }
 201:     Ok(())
 202: }
