{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_erasure/src/stripe.rs", "bytes": 11982, "sha256": "c38b3f1f770d35bf17940257d92d2525f79fabffe641d4174f2b8dec58aa2534", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:48.021666+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Stripe encode + decode operating on whole chunks.
   2: 
   3: use ol_fec::Codec;
   4: 
   5: use crate::error::ErasureError;
   6: 
   7: /// Per-shard role within a stripe. Mirrors `ol_chunk_store::StripeRole`
   8: /// but is local to this crate (we don't want a runtime dep on
   9: /// chunk_store; the daemon glues the two when it stores shards on
  10: /// disk).
  11: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  12: pub enum ShardRole {
  13:     /// One of `k` data shards.
  14:     Data,
  15:     /// One of `m` parity shards.
  16:     Parity,
  17: }
  18: 
  19: /// Stripe identity: 32-byte BLAKE3 of the **canonical stripe context**
  20: /// (plaintext length || k || m || plaintext-content-id). Two senders
  21: /// of the same plaintext at the same (k, m) produce the same StripeId
  22: /// — that's the cross-sender dedup property for data shards.
  23: pub type StripeId = [u8; 32];
  24: 
  25: /// Stripe configuration. `k` data shards + `m` parity shards, all
  26: /// equal length. The total `k + m` must be ≤ 255 (ADR-0016).
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
  28: pub struct StripeParams {
  29:     /// Number of data shards.
  30:     pub k: usize,
  31:     /// Number of parity shards.
  32:     pub m: usize,
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl StripeParams {
  36:     /// Standard durability config: 10 data + 4 parity = 14 shards,
  37:     /// any 10 recover. ~1.4× storage overhead.
  38:     pub const STANDARD: Self = Self { k: 10, m: 4 };
  39: 
  40:     /// Archival config: 6 data + 6 parity = 12 shards, any 6 recover.
  41:     /// ~2.0× storage; tolerates losing half the cohort.
  42:     pub const ARCHIVAL: Self = Self { k: 6, m: 6 };
  43: 
  44:     /// Ephemeral config: 9 data + 1 parity = 10 shards, any 9 recover.
  45:     /// ~1.11× storage; tolerates one device loss only.
  46:     pub const EPHEMERAL: Self = Self { k: 9, m: 1 };
  47: }
  48: 
  49: /// One shard of a stripe — bytes + role + position. The daemon wraps
  50: /// this in a `ChunkRecord` with the matching `StripeDescriptor` when
  51: /// it persists to disk.
  52: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  53: pub struct Shard {
  54:     /// Raw shard bytes. Same length across all shards in a stripe.
  55:     pub bytes: Vec<u8>,
  56:     /// Data or Parity.
  57:     pub role: ShardRole,
  58:     /// Position within its role (`0..k` for Data, `0..m` for Parity).
  59:     pub index: u8,
  60:     /// Length of the ORIGINAL plaintext, before padding to a multiple
  61:     /// of `k`. Carried in every shard so the decoder knows how much
  62:     /// to trim from the reassembled buffer.
  63:     pub plaintext_len: u64,
  64:     /// Identity of the stripe this shard belongs to.
  65:     pub stripe_id: StripeId,
  66: }
  67: 
  68: /// BLAKE3 derive_key context for stripe IDs. Domain-separated against
  69: /// other BLAKE3 derivations on the same plaintext (ADR-0006 registry).
  70: const STRIPE_ID_CONTEXT: &str = "ol-erasure-stripe-id-v1";
  71: 
  72: /// Compute the canonical [`StripeId`] for a (plaintext, k, m) tuple.
  73: ///
  74: /// Same plaintext + same params → same StripeId. Different params →
  75: /// different StripeId (so RS(10,4) and RS(6,6) stripes of the same
  76: /// plaintext do NOT collide).
  77: #[must_use]
  78: pub fn stripe_id_of(plaintext: &[u8], params: StripeParams) -> StripeId {
  79:     // BLAKE3 derive_key over a length-prefixed canonical concatenation:
  80:     //   [u64 plaintext_len][u8 k][u8 m][plaintext bytes]
  81:     let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(plaintext.len() + 10);
  82:     input.extend_from_slice(&(plaintext.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
  83:     input.push(params.k as u8);
  84:     input.push(params.m as u8);
  85:     input.extend_from_slice(plaintext);
  86:     blake3::derive_key(STRIPE_ID_CONTEXT, &input)
  87: }
  88: 
  89: /// Encode `plaintext` into a stripe of `k + m` shards.
  90: ///
  91: /// Padding: if `plaintext.len()` is not a multiple of `k`, the last
  92: /// data shard is zero-padded. The decoder trims back to the original
  93: /// length using the `plaintext_len` field carried in every shard.
  94: ///
  95: /// # Errors
  96: ///
  97: /// - [`ErasureError::InvalidParameters`] if the underlying `ol_fec`
  98: ///   codec rejects `(k, m)`.
  99: /// - [`ErasureError::EmptyPlaintext`] if `plaintext.is_empty()`.
 100: pub fn encode_stripe(plaintext: &[u8], params: StripeParams) -> Result<Vec<Shard>, ErasureError> {
 101:     if plaintext.is_empty() {
 102:         return Err(ErasureError::EmptyPlaintext);
 103:     }
 104:     let codec = Codec::new(params.k, params.m)?;
 105:     let stripe_id = stripe_id_of(plaintext, params);
 106:     let plaintext_len = plaintext.len() as u64;
 107: 
 108:     // Pad to a multiple of k, then split into k equal-sized shards.
 109:     let shard_len = plaintext.len().div_ceil(params.k);
 110:     let mut padded = vec![0u8; shard_len * params.k];
 111:     padded[..plaintext.len()].copy_from_slice(plaintext);
 112:     let mut data_shards: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..params.k)
 113:         .map(|i| padded[i * shard_len..(i + 1) * shard_len].to_vec())
 114:         .collect();
 115: 
 116:     // Encode parity.
 117:     let data_refs: Vec<&[u8]> = data_shards.iter().map(|d| d.as_slice()).collect();
 118:     let parity_shards = codec.encode(&data_refs)?;
 119: 
 120:     // Build typed Shard values.
 121:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(params.k + params.m);
 122:     for (i, bytes) in data_shards.drain(..).enumerate() {
 123:         out.push(Shard {
 124:             bytes,
 125:             role: ShardRole::Data,
 126:             index: i as u8,
 127:             plaintext_len,
 128:             stripe_id,
 129:         });
 130:     }
 131:     for (i, bytes) in parity_shards.into_iter().enumerate() {
 132:         out.push(Shard {
 133:             bytes,
 134:             role: ShardRole::Parity,
 135:             index: i as u8,
 136:             plaintext_len,
 137:             stripe_id,
 138:         });
 139:     }
 140:     Ok(out)
 141: }
 142: 
 143: /// Decode a stripe back to its original plaintext given any `k` of
 144: /// the `k + m` shards.
 145: ///
 146: /// `present` is indexed as: positions `0..k` for data shards
 147: /// 0..k, positions `k..k+m` for parity shards 0..m. Caller MUST
 148: /// supply the shards in the canonical position layout; the function
 149: /// verifies role + index match each slot.
 150: ///
 151: /// # Errors
 152: ///
 153: /// - [`ErasureError::PresentSlotCount`] on length mismatch.
 154: /// - [`ErasureError::ShardDescriptorMismatch`] if a shard at slot
 155: ///   `i` reports the wrong role/index.
 156: /// - [`ErasureError::InvalidParameters`] if the codec fails.
 157: pub fn decode_stripe(
 158:     params: StripeParams,
 159:     present: &[Option<&Shard>],
 160: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ErasureError> {
 161:     let total = params.k + params.m;
 162:     if present.len() != total {
 163:         return Err(ErasureError::PresentSlotCount {
 164:             expected: total,
 165:             got: present.len(),
 166:         });
 167:     }
 168:     // Sanity-check role + index per slot.
 169:     for (pos, slot) in present.iter().enumerate() {
 170:         let Some(shard) = slot else {
 171:             continue;
 172:         };
 173:         let (expected_role, expected_index) = if pos < params.k {
 174:             (ShardRole::Data, pos as u8)
 175:         } else {
 176:             (ShardRole::Parity, (pos - params.k) as u8)
 177:         };
 178:         if shard.role != expected_role || shard.index != expected_index {
 179:             return Err(ErasureError::ShardDescriptorMismatch {
 180:                 pos,
 181:                 role: shard.role,
 182:                 index: shard.index,
 183:                 expected_role,
 184:                 expected_index,
 185:             });
 186:         }
 187:     }
 188: 
 189:     let codec = Codec::new(params.k, params.m)?;
 190:     let raw_present: Vec<Option<&[u8]>> = present
 191:         .iter()
 192:         .map(|s| s.as_ref().map(|shard| shard.bytes.as_slice()))
 193:         .collect();
 194:     let data_shards = codec.decode(&raw_present)?;
 195: 
 196:     // Determine plaintext_len from any present shard.
 197:     let plaintext_len = present
 198:         .iter()
 199:         .find_map(|s| s.as_ref().map(|shard| shard.plaintext_len as usize))
 200:         .expect("at least one present shard ensures we have plaintext_len");
 201: 
 202:     let mut plaintext = Vec::with_capacity(plaintext_len);
 203:     for shard in &data_shards {
 204:         plaintext.extend_from_slice(shard);
 205:     }
 206:     plaintext.truncate(plaintext_len);
 207:     Ok(plaintext)
 208: }

   1: //! Throughput benchmarks for `ol_fec`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per ADR-0016: targets ≥500 MiB/s/core scalar on RS(10,4) at 64 KiB
   4: //! shards. Phase D upgrades (SIMD) will push past 5 GiB/s/core.

  12:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed);
  13:     (0..k)

  15:         .collect()
  16: }

  21:         (4, 2, 16 * 1024),  // small RS(4,2), 16 KiB shards

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_fec/src/cauchy.rs", "bytes": 8743, "sha256": "1f8c712e499960e3fc0b054a8c8b57a2421a43c8e273942b82a2bac26029485d", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:48.028665+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Cauchy matrix construction over GF(2^8).
   2: //!
   3: //! Per ADR-0016: any submatrix of a Cauchy matrix over GF(2^8) is
   4: //! invertible. That's the defining property — every `(k, m)`
   5: //! configuration we instantiate has the **always-decodable** guarantee
   6: //! for any `k`-shard subset of the `k+m` produced shards.
   7: //!
   8: //! ## Construction
   9: //!
  10: //! Pick two disjoint sets of GF(2^8) elements `X = {x_0..x_{m-1}}` and
  11: //! `Y = {y_0..y_{k-1}}` with all `x_i + y_j != 0` (since `+` is XOR in
  12: //! GF(2^8), this means `x_i != y_j`).
  13: //!
  14: //! The Cauchy matrix entry at row `i`, column `j` is
  15: //! `C[i][j] = 1 / (x_i + y_j) = 1 / (x_i ^ y_j)`.
  16: //!
  17: //! For our systematic encoder we then prepend the `k × k` identity to
  18: //! get the full `(k+m) × k` generator matrix `G`:
  19: //!
  20: //! ```text
  21: //! G = [ I_k       ]   ← rows 0..k:   data shards (identity)
  22: //!     [ C_(m,k)   ]   ← rows k..k+m: parity shards
  23: //! ```
  24: //!
  25: //! ## Choice of x_i, y_j
  26: //!
  27: //! We use the disjoint sets `Y = {0, 1, 2, ..., k-1}` and
  28: //! `X = {k, k+1, ..., k+m-1}`. With `k + m ≤ 255` (per ADR-0016
  29: //! limit), these sets fit in the field and are pairwise distinct.
  30: 
  31: use crate::error::FecError;
  32: use crate::gf256::{div, mul};
  33: 
  34: /// A pre-built systematic generator matrix: `(k + m) × k` over GF(2^8).
  35: ///
  36: /// Rows 0..k are the identity (data shards copy through unchanged).
  37: /// Rows k..(k+m) are the Cauchy matrix `C` that produces the parity
  38: /// shards. We store only the parity rows; the identity is implicit.
  39: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  40: pub struct CauchyMatrix {
  41:     k: usize,
  42:     m: usize,
  43:     /// `m × k` parity coefficients. `parity[i][j]` = coefficient of
  44:     /// data shard `j` contributing to parity shard `i`.
  45:     parity: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
  46: }
  47: 
  48: impl CauchyMatrix {
  49:     /// Build a systematic Cauchy matrix for `(k, m)`.
  50:     ///
  51:     /// # Errors
  52:     ///
  53:     /// - [`FecError::InvalidParameters`] if `k == 0` or `m == 0` or
  54:     ///   `k + m > 255`.
  55:     pub fn new(k: usize, m: usize) -> Result<Self, FecError> {
  56:         if k == 0 || m == 0 || k + m > 255 {
  57:             return Err(FecError::InvalidParameters { k, m });
  58:         }
  59:         let mut parity = Vec::with_capacity(m);
  60:         for i in 0..m {
  61:             let mut row = Vec::with_capacity(k);
  62:             for j in 0..k {
  63:                 // x_i = k + i; y_j = j. Both fit in u8.
  64:                 let x_i = (k + i) as u8;
  65:                 let y_j = j as u8;
  66:                 // x_i + y_j = x_i ^ y_j (GF(2^8)). Guaranteed non-zero
  67:                 // because x_i != y_j (disjoint sets).
  68:                 let denom = x_i ^ y_j;
  69:                 debug_assert!(denom != 0);
  70:                 row.push(div(1, denom));
  71:             }
  72:             parity.push(row);
  73:         }
  74:         Ok(Self { k, m, parity })
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     /// Number of data shards.
  78:     #[inline]
  79:     #[must_use]
  80:     pub fn k(&self) -> usize {
  81:         self.k
  82:     }
  83: 
  84:     /// Number of parity shards.
  85:     #[inline]
  86:     #[must_use]
  87:     pub fn m(&self) -> usize {
  88:         self.m
  89:     }
  90: 
  91:     /// Total shards = `k + m`.
  92:     #[inline]
  93:     #[must_use]
  94:     pub fn total(&self) -> usize {
  95:         self.k + self.m
  96:     }
  97: 
  98:     /// Borrow the parity coefficient row for parity shard `i`. Length
  99:     /// is `k`. Panics if `i >= m`.
 100:     #[inline]
 101:     #[must_use]
 102:     pub fn parity_row(&self, i: usize) -> &[u8] {
 103:         &self.parity[i]
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     /// Build the full systematic generator matrix as a flat `(k+m) × k`
 107:     /// `Vec<Vec<u8>>`. Used by the decoder to pick the row subset
 108:     /// matching the received shard indices.
 109:     #[must_use]
 110:     pub fn generator(&self) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {
 111:         let mut g = Vec::with_capacity(self.total());
 112:         // Identity rows.
 113:         for j in 0..self.k {
 114:             let mut row = vec![0u8; self.k];
 115:             row[j] = 1;
 116:             g.push(row);
 117:         }
 118:         // Parity rows.
 119:         for row in &self.parity {
 120:             g.push(row.clone());
 121:         }
 122:         g
 123:     }
 124: }
 125: 
 126: /// Invert a `k × k` matrix over GF(2^8) via Gauss-Jordan elimination.
 127: ///
 128: /// Used by [`crate::decoder`] to solve for the original data when given
 129: /// any `k` of the `k + m` shards.
 130: ///
 131: /// Returns the inverse matrix. The input is consumed in place to save
 132: /// the allocation; caller passes a freshly-built copy.
 133: ///
 134: /// # Errors
 135: ///
 136: /// Returns `None` if the matrix is singular (cannot be inverted). For
 137: /// matrices drawn from a Cauchy generator, this case is impossible by
 138: /// construction — every `k × k` submatrix is invertible.
 139: #[must_use]
 140: pub fn invert(mut m: Vec<Vec<u8>>) -> Option<Vec<Vec<u8>>> {
 141:     let n = m.len();
 142:     if n == 0 || m.iter().any(|r| r.len() != n) {
 143:         return None;
 144:     }
 145:     // Augment with identity.
 146:     for i in 0..n {
 147:         let mut id = vec![0u8; n];
 148:         id[i] = 1;
 149:         m[i].extend_from_slice(&id);
 150:     }
 151:     // Forward elimination + back substitution in one Gauss-Jordan pass.
 152:     for col in 0..n {
 153:         // Find a pivot row in `col..n`.
 154:         let mut pivot = None;
 155:         for r in col..n {
 156:             if m[r][col] != 0 {
 157:                 pivot = Some(r);
 158:                 break;
 159:             }
 160:         }
 161:         let pivot = pivot?;
 162:         m.swap(col, pivot);
 163:         // Normalize pivot row so `m[col][col] = 1`.
 164:         let pivot_val = m[col][col];
 165:         let pivot_inv = crate::gf256::inv(pivot_val);
 166:         for v in &mut m[col] {
 167:             *v = mul(*v, pivot_inv);
 168:         }
 169:         // Eliminate other rows.
 170:         for r in 0..n {
 171:             if r == col {
 172:                 continue;
 173:             }
 174:             let factor = m[r][col];
 175:             if factor == 0 {
 176:                 continue;
 177:             }
 178:             // Subtract `factor * m[col]` from m[r]; subtraction = XOR.
 179:             for c in 0..2 * n {
 180:                 let v = mul(factor, m[col][c]);
 181:                 m[r][c] ^= v;
 182:             }
 183:         }
 184:     }
 185:     // Strip the original-left half; return the right half = inverse.
 186:     let mut inv = Vec::with_capacity(n);
 187:     for row in m {
 188:         inv.push(row[n..].to_vec());
 189:     }
 190:     Some(inv)
 191: }

 241:     #[test]
 242:     fn cauchy_submatrix_always_invertible() {
 243:         // For k=10, m=4: pick any 10 of the 14 rows and confirm the
 244:         // resulting 10x10 submatrix is invertible.
 245:         let c = CauchyMatrix::new(10, 4).unwrap();
 246:         let gen = c.generator();
 247:         // 14 choose 10 = 1001 subsets; enumerate via bitmask.
 248:         let n = 14;
 249:         let k = 10;
 250:         let mut bits: u64 = (1 << k) - 1;
 251:         let limit = 1u64 << n;
 252:         let mut tested = 0;
 253:         while bits < limit {
 254:             // Build the submatrix of `gen` for the rows whose bit is set.
 255:             let mut sub: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(k);
 256:             for r in 0..n {
 257:                 if (bits >> r) & 1 == 1 {
 258:                     sub.push(gen[r].clone());
 259:                 }
 260:             }
 261:             assert_eq!(sub.len(), k);
 262:             assert!(
 263:                 invert(sub).is_some(),
 264:                 "submatrix bits={bits:b} not invertible"
 265:             );
 266:             tested += 1;
 267:             // Gosper's hack: next bitmask with same popcount.
 268:             let c2 = bits & bits.wrapping_neg();
 269:             let r2 = bits + c2;
 270:             bits = (((r2 ^ bits) >> 2) / c2) | r2;
 271:         }
 272:         assert_eq!(tested, 1001, "expected 1001 subsets, tested {tested}");
 273:     }
 274: }

   1: //! Reed-Solomon codec: systematic encode + erasure decode.
   2: 
   3: use crate::cauchy::{invert, CauchyMatrix};
   4: use crate::error::FecError;
   5: use crate::gf256::fma_into;
   6: 
   7: /// Reed-Solomon Codec over GF(2^8) using a Cauchy systematic matrix.
   8: ///
   9: /// One codec instance is built per `(k, m)` configuration and reused
  10: /// across many encode/decode calls — the matrix is precomputed.
  11: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  12: pub struct Codec {
  13:     cauchy: CauchyMatrix,
  14: }
  15: 
  16: impl Codec {
  17:     /// Build a codec for `(k, m)`: `k` data shards plus `m` parity
  18:     /// shards, recoverable from any `k` of the `k + m`.
  19:     ///
  20:     /// # Errors
  21:     ///
  22:     /// [`FecError::InvalidParameters`] if `k == 0`, `m == 0`, or
  23:     /// `k + m > 255`.
  24:     pub fn new(k: usize, m: usize) -> Result<Self, FecError> {
  25:         Ok(Self {
  26:             cauchy: CauchyMatrix::new(k, m)?,
  27:         })
  28:     }
  29: 
  30:     /// Data-shard count.
  31:     #[inline]
  32:     #[must_use]
  33:     pub fn k(&self) -> usize {
  34:         self.cauchy.k()
  35:     }
  36: 
  37:     /// Parity-shard count.
  38:     #[inline]
  39:     #[must_use]
  40:     pub fn m(&self) -> usize {
  41:         self.cauchy.m()
  42:     }
  43: 
  44:     /// Total-shard count = `k + m`.
  45:     #[inline]
  46:     #[must_use]
  47:     pub fn total_shards(&self) -> usize {
  48:         self.cauchy.total()
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     /// Encode `data` (k equal-length shards) into the m parity shards.
  52:     /// The data shards themselves are the FIRST k of the (k + m) total
  53:     /// shards (systematic), so callers don't need to copy them here.
  54:     ///
  55:     /// # Errors
  56:     ///
  57:     /// - [`FecError::DataShardCount`] if `data.len() != k`.
  58:     /// - [`FecError::InconsistentShardLen`] if shards aren't equal length.
  59:     pub fn encode(&self, data: &[&[u8]]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, FecError> {
  60:         if data.len() != self.k() {
  61:             return Err(FecError::DataShardCount {
  62:                 expected: self.k(),
  63:                 got: data.len(),
  64:             });
  65:         }
  66:         let shard_len = data[0].len();
  67:         for (i, d) in data.iter().enumerate() {
  68:             if d.len() != shard_len {
  69:                 return Err(FecError::InconsistentShardLen {
  70:                     expected: shard_len,
  71:                     len: d.len(),
  72:                 });
  73:             }
  74:             let _ = i;
  75:         }
  76:         let mut parity: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..self.m()).map(|_| vec![0u8; shard_len]).collect();
  77:         for (i, parity_shard) in parity.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  78:             let row = self.cauchy.parity_row(i);
  79:             for (j, &coeff) in row.iter().enumerate() {
  80:                 fma_into(parity_shard, data[j], coeff);
  81:             }
  82:         }
  83:         Ok(parity)
  84:     }
  85: 
  86:     /// Decode the original `k` data shards from any `k` of the
  87:     /// `k + m` shards.
  88:     ///
  89:     /// `present` has length `k + m`; `present[i]` is `Some(&[u8])` if
  90:     /// shard `i` was received, `None` if it's missing. At least `k`
  91:     /// entries must be `Some`. All present shards must be equal length.
  92:     ///
  93:     /// # Errors
  94:     ///
  95:     /// - [`FecError::PresentSlotCount`] if `present.len() != k + m`.
  96:     /// - [`FecError::InsufficientShards`] if fewer than `k` shards
  97:     ///   are present.
  98:     /// - [`FecError::InconsistentShardLen`] if present shards aren't
  99:     ///   all the same length.
 100:     pub fn decode(&self, present: &[Option<&[u8]>]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, FecError> {
 101:         let total = self.total_shards();
 102:         if present.len() != total {
 103:             return Err(FecError::PresentSlotCount {
 104:                 expected: total,
 105:                 got: present.len(),
 106:             });
 107:         }
 108:         // Collect indices of present shards.
 109:         let mut indices = Vec::with_capacity(total);
 110:         let mut shard_len: Option<usize> = None;
 111:         for (i, slot) in present.iter().enumerate() {
 112:             if let Some(s) = slot {
 113:                 match shard_len {
 114:                     None => shard_len = Some(s.len()),
 115:                     Some(len) if len == s.len() => {}
 116:                     Some(len) => {
 117:                         return Err(FecError::InconsistentShardLen {
 118:                             expected: len,
 119:                             len: s.len(),
 120:                         });
 121:                     }
 122:                 }
 123:                 indices.push(i);
 124:             }
 125:         }
 126:         if indices.len() < self.k() {
 127:             return Err(FecError::InsufficientShards {
 128:                 needed: self.k(),
 129:                 got: indices.len(),
 130:             });
 131:         }
 132:         // Use the first k present shards.
 133:         indices.truncate(self.k());
 134:         let shard_len = shard_len.expect("at least one present shard");
 135: 
 136:         // Fast path: all k data shards (indices 0..k) are present —
 137:         // no recovery needed.
 138:         if indices.iter().enumerate().all(|(i, &idx)| idx == i) {
 139:             return Ok((0..self.k())
 140:                 .map(|i| present[i].expect("present").to_vec())
 141:                 .collect());
 142:         }
 143: 
 144:         // Build the k × k submatrix of the generator matrix
 145:         // corresponding to the chosen indices.
 146:         let gen = self.cauchy.generator();
 147:         let sub: Vec<Vec<u8>> = indices.iter().map(|&i| gen[i].clone()).collect();
 148:         let inv = invert(sub).expect("Cauchy submatrices are always invertible");
 149: 
 150:         // Decode: data = inv * recv_data (matrix-vector across shards).
 151:         let mut data: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..self.k()).map(|_| vec![0u8; shard_len]).collect();
 152:         for (out_row, inv_row) in data.iter_mut().zip(inv.iter()) {
 153:             for (j, &coeff) in inv_row.iter().enumerate() {
 154:                 fma_into(
 155:                     out_row,
 156:                     present[indices[j]].expect("indexed present"),
 157:                     coeff,
 158:                 );
 159:             }
 160:         }
 161:         Ok(data)
 162:     }
 163: }

   1: //! GF(2^8) arithmetic — the Rijndael / AES field.
   2: //!
   3: //! Elements are bytes; addition is XOR. Multiplication is polynomial
   4: //! multiplication modulo the irreducible polynomial
   5: //! `x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1` (0x11B). We precompute log/exp tables
   6: //! using the primitive root `g = 0x03`:
   7: //!
   8: //! - [`LOG`]: `LOG[a] = i` iff `g^i = a` (defined for `a != 0`).
   9: //! - [`EXP`]: `EXP[i] = g^i`, extended to 510 entries so wraparound
  10: //!   `(log_a + log_b) % 255` can be avoided with a single index.
  11: //!
  12: //! Per-op cost: ~3 scalar cycles (two table loads + one add). Fast
  13: //! enough that the engine's RS encode is bandwidth-bound on the XOR
  14: //! pass, not the multiply.
  15: 
  16: /// Number of elements in GF(2^8).
  17: pub const FIELD_SIZE: usize = 256;
  18: 
  19: /// Multiplicative order of GF(2^8) — the field minus the additive
  20: /// identity. `LOG[a]` is in `0..255` for `a != 0`.
  21: pub const FIELD_ORDER: usize = 255;
  22: 
  23: /// Primitive root used to build the log/exp tables. `0x03` is the
  24: /// smallest primitive root for the Rijndael irreducible polynomial.
  25: pub const PRIMITIVE_ROOT: u8 = 0x03;
  26: 
  27: /// Irreducible polynomial of GF(2^8) used by AES + this codec:
  28: /// `x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1`. Reduction is done lazily via the
  29: /// precomputed `EXP` table.
  30: pub const IRREDUCIBLE_POLY: u16 = 0x11B;
  31: 
  32: /// Discrete-log table: `LOG[a] = i` such that `g^i = a` for `a in 1..256`.
  33: /// `LOG[0]` is unused (logarithm of zero is undefined).
  34: pub static LOG: [u8; FIELD_SIZE] = {
  35:     let mut log = [0u8; FIELD_SIZE];
  36:     let mut x: u16 = 1;
  37:     let mut i: usize = 0;
  38:     while i < FIELD_ORDER {
  39:         // SAFETY: x ∈ 1..256, indexing is in bounds.
  40:         log[x as usize] = i as u8;
  41:         x = mul_no_table(x, PRIMITIVE_ROOT as u16);
  42:         i += 1;
  43:     }
  44:     log
  45: };
  46: 
  47: /// Exponentiation table, double-sized so multiplication doesn't need
  48: /// `% 255`. `EXP[i] = g^(i % 255)` for `i in 0..510`.
  49: pub static EXP: [u8; 2 * FIELD_ORDER] = {
  50:     let mut exp = [0u8; 2 * FIELD_ORDER];
  51:     let mut x: u16 = 1;
  52:     let mut i: usize = 0;
  53:     while i < FIELD_ORDER {
  54:         exp[i] = x as u8;
  55:         exp[i + FIELD_ORDER] = x as u8;
  56:         x = mul_no_table(x, PRIMITIVE_ROOT as u16);
  57:         i += 1;
  58:     }
  59:     exp
  60: };
  61: 
  62: /// Polynomial multiplication mod [`IRREDUCIBLE_POLY`]. Used at
  63: /// compile-time to build [`LOG`] and [`EXP`]; not on the hot path.
  64: const fn mul_no_table(a: u16, b: u16) -> u16 {
  65:     let mut result: u16 = 0;
  66:     let mut aa = a;
  67:     let mut bb = b;
  68:     let mut i = 0;
  69:     while i < 8 {
  70:         if (bb & 1) != 0 {
  71:             result ^= aa;
  72:         }
  73:         let high_bit = aa & 0x80;
  74:         aa <<= 1;
  75:         if high_bit != 0 {
  76:             aa ^= IRREDUCIBLE_POLY;
  77:         }
  78:         bb >>= 1;
  79:         i += 1;
  80:     }
  81:     result & 0xFF
  82: }
  83: 
  84: /// GF(2^8) multiplication via table lookup. ~3 cycles scalar.
  85: #[inline]
  86: #[must_use]
  87: pub fn mul(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
  88:     if a == 0 || b == 0 {
  89:         return 0;
  90:     }
  91:     let la = LOG[a as usize] as usize;
  92:     let lb = LOG[b as usize] as usize;
  93:     // Safe because la + lb ≤ 254 + 254 = 508 < 510.
  94:     EXP[la + lb]
  95: }
  96: 
  97: /// GF(2^8) addition is XOR. Inline for clarity at call sites.
  98: #[inline]
  99: #[must_use]
 100: pub const fn add(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
 101:     a ^ b
 102: }
 103: 
 104: /// Multiplicative inverse: `inv(a) * a = 1`. Panics for `a == 0`.
 105: #[inline]
 106: #[must_use]
 107: pub fn inv(a: u8) -> u8 {
 108:     assert!(a != 0, "GF(2^8) zero has no multiplicative inverse");
 109:     let la = LOG[a as usize] as usize;
 110:     // 255 - la is in 1..=254, well-defined index.
 111:     EXP[FIELD_ORDER - la]
 112: }
 113: 
 114: /// Division: `a / b = a * inv(b)`. Panics for `b == 0`.
 115: #[inline]
 116: #[must_use]
 117: pub fn div(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
 118:     if a == 0 {
 119:         return 0;
 120:     }
 121:     assert!(b != 0, "GF(2^8) division by zero");
 122:     let la = LOG[a as usize] as usize;
 123:     let lb = LOG[b as usize] as usize;
 124:     // la in 0..255, lb in 0..255; la + 255 - lb in 0..509.
 125:     EXP[la + FIELD_ORDER - lb]
 126: }
 127: 
 128: /// In-place fused multiply-add over a byte slice:
 129: /// `dest[i] = dest[i] + coeff * src[i]` for `i in 0..src.len()`.
 130: ///
 131: /// This is the hot inner loop of Reed-Solomon encoding and decoding.
 132: /// Dispatches to a SIMD-accelerated path when available; falls back
 133: /// to the scalar table-lookup path otherwise. Both paths are
 134: /// **byte-identical** in output (property-tested).
 135: ///
 136: /// **x86_64 SSSE3 path**: uses PSHUFB to do 16 GF(2^8) multiplications
 137: /// per instruction via the 4-bit-by-4-bit decomposition
 138: /// (Plank-Greenan-Miller 2013). Two 16-entry tables (high-nibble +
 139: /// low-nibble of the multiplication result) are precomputed per
 140: /// coefficient and held in SSE registers. ~5-7× faster than scalar.
 141: ///
 142: /// **Scalar fallback**: per-coefficient 256-entry multiplication table
 143: /// (the "Klauspost trick"). Amortizes log/exp lookups across the shard.
 144: #[inline]
 145: pub fn fma_into(dest: &mut [u8], src: &[u8], coeff: u8) {
 146:     debug_assert_eq!(dest.len(), src.len());
 147:     if coeff == 0 {
 148:         return;
 149:     }
 150:     if coeff == 1 {
 151:         // Fast path: addition (XOR) only, no multiply. Uses the same
 152:         // word-wide XOR helper as ol_fountain when available; for now
 153:         // a tight byte loop is what the autovectorizer handles well.
 154:         for (d, s) in dest.iter_mut().zip(src.iter()) {
 155:             *d ^= *s;
 156:         }
 157:         return;
 158:     }
 159: 
 160:     // Runtime SIMD dispatch.
 161:     #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
 162:     {
 163:         if std::is_x86_feature_detected!("ssse3") {
 164:             // SAFETY: feature-detected at runtime.
 165:             unsafe {
 166:                 fma_into_ssse3(dest, src, coeff);
 167:             }
 168:             return;
 169:         }
 170:     }
 171:     fma_into_scalar(dest, src, coeff);
 172: }
 173: 
 174: /// Scalar fallback: per-coefficient 256-entry table lookup.
 175: #[inline]
 176: pub fn fma_into_scalar(dest: &mut [u8], src: &[u8], coeff: u8) {
 177:     debug_assert_eq!(dest.len(), src.len());
 178:     if coeff == 0 {
 179:         return;
 180:     }
 181:     if coeff == 1 {
 182:         for (d, s) in dest.iter_mut().zip(src.iter()) {
 183:             *d ^= *s;
 184:         }
 185:         return;
 186:     }
 187:     let mut mul_table = [0u8; FIELD_SIZE];
 188:     let lc = LOG[coeff as usize] as usize;
 189:     mul_table[0] = 0;
 190:     for x in 1..FIELD_SIZE {
 191:         let lx = LOG[x] as usize;
 192:         mul_table[x] = EXP[lc + lx];
 193:     }
 194:     for (d, s) in dest.iter_mut().zip(src.iter()) {
 195:         *d ^= mul_table[*s as usize];
 196:     }
 197: }
 198: 
 199: /// SSSE3 PSHUFB path. Splits each source byte into high + low nibbles,
 200: /// precomputes the two 16-byte multiplication tables for `coeff`, and
 201: /// processes 16 bytes per iteration via `_mm_shuffle_epi8`.
 202: ///
 203: /// # Safety
 204: ///
 205: /// Caller must verify SSSE3 is available before calling (we check via
 206: /// `is_x86_feature_detected!("ssse3")` in `fma_into`).
 207: #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]
 208: #[target_feature(enable = "ssse3")]
 209: unsafe fn fma_into_ssse3(dest: &mut [u8], src: &[u8], coeff: u8) {
 210:     use std::arch::x86_64::*;
 211: 
 212:     debug_assert_eq!(dest.len(), src.len());
 213: 
 214:     // Precompute two 16-byte tables: low_table[i] = coeff * i,
 215:     // high_table[i] = coeff * (i << 4). Together they let us compute
 216:     // coeff * b = low_table[b & 0x0F] ^ high_table[b >> 4] for any
 217:     // byte b, vectorized 16-wide via PSHUFB.
 218:     let mut low_table = [0u8; 16];
 219:     let mut high_table = [0u8; 16];
 220:     for i in 0..16usize {
 221:         low_table[i] = mul(coeff, i as u8);
 222:         high_table[i] = mul(coeff, (i as u8) << 4);
 223:     }
 224: 
 225:     // SAFETY: all SSSE3 intrinsics + pointer arithmetic below are
 226:     // guarded by:
 227:     //  - This function's `target_feature = "ssse3"` (caller verified).
 228:     //  - Loop bound `n16 = n & !15` keeps loads + stores within
 229:     //    `[src.as_ptr()..src.as_ptr() + n)` and the mirrored dest range.
 230:     //  - The tail loop does byte-wise scalar access.
 231:     unsafe {
 232:         let low_v = _mm_loadu_si128(low_table.as_ptr().cast::<__m128i>());
 233:         let high_v = _mm_loadu_si128(high_table.as_ptr().cast::<__m128i>());
 234:         let mask_nibble = _mm_set1_epi8(0x0F);
 235: 
 236:         let n = src.len();
 237:         let n16 = n & !15;
 238:         let mut i = 0usize;
 239:         while i < n16 {
 240:             let s = _mm_loadu_si128(src.as_ptr().add(i).cast::<__m128i>());
 241:             let low_nibbles = _mm_and_si128(s, mask_nibble);
 242:             // Right-shift each byte 4 bits to get high nibbles.
 243:             // `_mm_srli_epi64` shifts the *whole 64-bit lane*, so bytes
 244:             // leak across boundaries; we mask off the leakage with
 245:             // `& 0x0F` again.
 246:             let high_nibbles = _mm_and_si128(_mm_srli_epi64(s, 4), mask_nibble);
 247:             let low_result = _mm_shuffle_epi8(low_v, low_nibbles);
 248:             let high_result = _mm_shuffle_epi8(high_v, high_nibbles);
 249:             let product = _mm_xor_si128(low_result, high_result);
 250:             let d = _mm_loadu_si128(dest.as_ptr().add(i).cast::<__m128i>());
 251:             let d_xor = _mm_xor_si128(d, product);
 252:             _mm_storeu_si128(dest.as_mut_ptr().add(i).cast::<__m128i>(), d_xor);
 253:             i += 16;
 254:         }
 255:         // Scalar tail for the last 0..15 bytes.
 256:         while i < n {
 257:             let s_byte = src[i];
 258:             let low = low_table[(s_byte & 0x0F) as usize];
 259:             let high = high_table[((s_byte >> 4) & 0x0F) as usize];
 260:             dest[i] ^= low ^ high;
 261:             i += 1;
 262:         }
 263:     }
 264: }

   1: //! `ol_fec` — Reed-Solomon FEC over GF(2^8) using a Cauchy systematic
   2: //! matrix per [ADR-0016](../../../docs/decisions/0016-reed-solomon-fec.md).
   3: //!
   4: //! Phase C item #1 (erasure-recovery codec) and substrate for item #2
   5: //! (erasure-coded durability via `ol_erasure`).
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Surface
   8: //!
   9: //! - [`Codec`] — pre-built `(k, m)` Reed-Solomon codec.
  10: //! - [`gf256`] — GF(2^8) primitive operations + log/exp tables.
  11: //! - [`cauchy::CauchyMatrix`] — the always-invertible generator matrix
  12: //!   structure underlying the codec.
  13: //!
  14: //! ## Why custom, not `reed-solomon-erasure`?
  15: //!
  16: //! Per ADR-0016: sovereignty + always-invertible recovery (Cauchy
  17: //! submatrices, unlike Vandermonde, are invertible for ANY erasure
  18: //! pattern). Speed is ~500 MiB/s/core scalar; SIMD acceleration is a
  19: //! Phase D upgrade.
  20: 
  21: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_fec/0.21.0")]
  22: 
  23: pub mod cauchy;
  24: pub mod codec;
  25: pub mod error;
  26: pub mod gf256;
  27: 
  28: pub use cauchy::CauchyMatrix;
  29: pub use codec::Codec;
  30: pub use error::FecError;

   1: //! Phase C acceptance gate for ADR-0016:
   2: //!
   3: //!   > Reed-Solomon (10,4) survives any 4-shard erasure with 100%
   4: //!   > recovery across ≥10,000 seeds.
   5: //!
   6: //! For each seed:
   7: //! 1. Build 10 random 1 KiB data shards.
   8: //! 2. Encode → 4 parity shards (14 total).
   9: //! 3. Pick 4 random shard indices (out of 14) to drop. Per Cauchy
  10: //!    submatrix theory, ANY 4-erasure pattern is decodable.
  11: //! 4. Decode from the remaining 10 shards.
  12: //! 5. Assert byte-exact recovery of the original 10 data shards.
  13: //!
  14: //! Anything less than 100% across 10K seeds = ADR-0016 doesn't ship.
  15: 
  16: use ol_fec::Codec;
  17: use rand::rngs::StdRng;
  18: use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
  19: use rand::{Rng, SeedableRng};
  20: 
  21: const K: usize = 10;
  22: const M: usize = 4;
  23: const N: usize = K + M; // 14
  24: const SHARD_LEN: usize = 1024;
  25: const SEEDS: u64 = 10_000;
  26: 
  27: #[test]
  28: fn adr0016_rs_10_4_survives_any_4_erasure_across_10k_seeds() {
  29:     let codec = Codec::new(K, M).expect("RS(10,4) constructs");
  30:     let mut failures = 0usize;
  31:     for seed in 0..SEEDS {
  32:         let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed);
  33:         let data: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..K)
  34:             .map(|_| (0..SHARD_LEN).map(|_| rng.random::<u8>()).collect())
  35:             .collect();
  36:         let data_refs: Vec<&[u8]> = data.iter().map(|d| d.as_slice()).collect();
  37:         let parity = codec.encode(&data_refs).expect("encode");
  38: 
  39:         // Pick 4 of 14 indices to drop, uniformly at random.
  40:         let mut indices: Vec<usize> = (0..N).collect();
  41:         indices.shuffle(&mut rng);
  42:         let dropped: Vec<usize> = indices.into_iter().take(M).collect();
  43: 
  44:         // Assemble the `present` vector.
  45:         let mut present: Vec<Option<&[u8]>> = Vec::with_capacity(N);
  46:         for i in 0..K {
  47:             if dropped.contains(&i) {
  48:                 present.push(None);
  49:             } else {
  50:                 present.push(Some(data[i].as_slice()));
  51:             }
  52:         }
  53:         for i in 0..M {
  54:             let shard_index = K + i;
  55:             if dropped.contains(&shard_index) {
  56:                 present.push(None);
  57:             } else {
  58:                 present.push(Some(parity[i].as_slice()));
  59:             }
  60:         }
  61:         let present_count = present.iter().filter(|o| o.is_some()).count();
  62:         assert_eq!(
  63:             present_count, K,
  64:             "exactly K shards must be present after dropping M"
  65:         );
  66: 
  67:         let decoded = codec.decode(&present).expect("decode");
  68:         if decoded != data {
  69:             failures += 1;
  70:             eprintln!("seed {seed}: dropped={:?}, decoded mismatch", dropped);
  71:         }
  72:     }
  73:     assert_eq!(failures, 0, "Phase C gate: failed {failures}/{SEEDS}");
  74:     eprintln!(
  75:         "ADR-0016 acceptance: PASSED {SEEDS}/{SEEDS} RS(10,4) decodes with random 4-erasure patterns"
  76:     );
  77: }
  78: 
  79: /// Additional gate: 100% recovery when ANY combination of `m` shards is
  80: /// dropped — not just random sampling. We enumerate enough seeds to
  81: /// cover every (K+M choose M) = (14 choose 4) = 1001 erasure pattern at
  82: /// least once with high probability.
  83: #[test]
  84: fn adr0016_rs_10_4_recovers_from_every_4_erasure_pattern() {
  85:     let codec = Codec::new(K, M).expect("RS(10,4) constructs");
  86:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(0xCAFE_BABE);

  88:         .map(|_| (0..SHARD_LEN).map(|_| rng.random::<u8>()).collect())
  89:         .collect();
  90:     let data_refs: Vec<&[u8]> = data.iter().map(|d| d.as_slice()).collect();
  91:     let parity = codec.encode(&data_refs).expect("encode");
  92: 
  93:     // Enumerate all C(14, 4) = 1001 ways to drop 4 shards.
  94:     let mut tested = 0usize;
  95:     for a in 0..N {
  96:         for b in (a + 1)..N {
  97:             for c in (b + 1)..N {
  98:                 for d in (c + 1)..N {
  99:                     let dropped = [a, b, c, d];
 100:                     let mut present: Vec<Option<&[u8]>> = Vec::with_capacity(N);
 101:                     for i in 0..K {
 102:                         if dropped.contains(&i) {
 103:                             present.push(None);
 104:                         } else {
 105:                             present.push(Some(data[i].as_slice()));
 106:                         }
 107:                     }
 108:                     for i in 0..M {
 109:                         let shard_index = K + i;
 110:                         if dropped.contains(&shard_index) {
 111:                             present.push(None);
 112:                         } else {
 113:                             present.push(Some(parity[i].as_slice()));
 114:                         }
 115:                     }
 116:                     let decoded = codec.decode(&present).expect("decode");
 117:                     assert_eq!(decoded, data, "erasure pattern {dropped:?} failed");
 118:                     tested += 1;
 119:                 }
 120:             }
 121:         }
 122:     }
 123:     assert_eq!(tested, 1001, "expected to enumerate 1001 patterns");
 124: }

   1: //! Cross-platform determinism vectors for `ol_fec`.
   2: //!
   3: //! The Reed-Solomon parity bytes for a fixed `(plaintext, k, m)` MUST
   4: //! be byte-identical across x86_64 / aarch64 / RISC-V — peers
   5: //! interoperate by comparing bytes, not by re-deriving parity from
   6: //! local state. Both the scalar path AND the SSSE3 SIMD path MUST
   7: //! produce identical bytes (the SIMD-matches-scalar property test in
   8: //! `gf256.rs` covers this exhaustively).
   9: //!
  10: //! This file pins the parity output for a specific RS(10, 4) encode of
  11: //! 10×64-byte data shards. A platform that diverges fails this test
  12: //! loudly.
  13: 
  14: use ol_fec::Codec;
  15: 
  16: fn hex_encode_lower(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
  17:     const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
  18:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
  19:     for &b in bytes {
  20:         out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
  21:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);
  22:     }
  23:     out
  24: }
  25: 
  26: /// Deterministic 64-byte data shard for index `i`. The byte pattern is
  27: /// `(i + j) as u8` for `j in 0..64`, with a final 0xCD marker so any
  28: /// off-by-one in indexing is immediately visible.
  29: fn data_shard(i: u8) -> Vec<u8> {
  30:     let mut out = vec![0u8; 64];
  31:     for j in 0..63 {
  32:         out[j] = i.wrapping_add(j as u8);
  33:     }
  34:     out[63] = 0xCD;
  35:     out
  36: }
  37: 
  38: #[test]
  39: fn cross_platform_rs_10_4_parity_pinned() {
  40:     let codec = Codec::new(10, 4).unwrap();
  41:     let data: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0u8..10).map(data_shard).collect();
  42:     let data_refs: Vec<&[u8]> = data.iter().map(|d| d.as_slice()).collect();
  43:     let parity = codec.encode(&data_refs).unwrap();
  44: 
  45:     assert_eq!(parity.len(), 4);
  46:     for p in &parity {
  47:         assert_eq!(p.len(), 64);
  48:     }
  49: 
  50:     // Pin each of the 4 parity shards by hex. Any divergence in the
  51:     // GF(2^8) operations, Cauchy matrix construction, or SIMD path
  52:     // failure mode immediately surfaces here.
  53:     let p_hex: [String; 4] = [
  54:         hex_encode_lower(&parity[0]),
  55:         hex_encode_lower(&parity[1]),
  56:         hex_encode_lower(&parity[2]),
  57:         hex_encode_lower(&parity[3]),
  58:     ];
  59: 
  60:     let expected = pinned_parity_hex();
  61:     let mut diverged = Vec::new();
  62:     for i in 0..4 {
  63:         if p_hex[i] != expected[i] {
  64:             diverged.push((i, p_hex[i].clone(), expected[i]));
  65:         }
  66:     }
  67:     if !diverged.is_empty() {
  68:         // Print all four so the new vector is easy to copy in.
  69:         eprintln!("=== ol_fec determinism: divergence detected ===");
  70:         for (i, actual, expected) in &diverged {
  71:             eprintln!("shard {i}: ACTUAL   = {actual}");
  72:             eprintln!("           EXPECTED = {expected}");
  73:         }
  74:         eprintln!("=== current platform's parity (paste into PINNED_P{{0..3}}): ===");
  75:         for (i, hex) in p_hex.iter().enumerate() {
  76:             eprintln!("PINNED_P{i} = \"{hex}\"");
  77:         }
  78:         panic!(
  79:             "ol_fec parity diverged from the pinned vector ({} shards). \
  80:              If you changed the GF(2^8) primitives or Cauchy matrix \
  81:              construction, update the test vector AND bump the \
  82:              wire-format version per ADR-0016.",
  83:             diverged.len()
  84:         );
  85:     }
  86: }
  87: 
  88: /// Pinned parity bytes for the RS(10, 4) encode of the 10 data shards
  89: /// produced by [`data_shard`].
  90: ///
  91: /// Recompute via:
  92: /// ```ignore
  93: /// for p in &parity { println!("{}", hex_encode_lower(p)); }
  94: /// ```
  95: fn pinned_parity_hex() -> [&'static str; 4] {
  96:     PINNED_PARITY_HEX
  97: }
  98:

   1: //! Throughput benchmarks for `ol_fountain`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Targets the ADR-0015 hot paths:
   4: //!
   5: //! - LT encode: one symbol at a time, K source symbols of 1 KiB.
   6: //! - LT decode: ingest stream until reconstructed.
   7: //! - Packet encode/decode: wire-format header serialization.
   8: 
   9: use criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, BenchmarkId, Criterion, Throughput};
  10: use ol_fountain::{FountainPacket, LtDecoder, LtEncoder};
  11: 
  12: fn make_source(seed: u64, len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
  13:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(len);
  14:     let mut state = seed.wrapping_add(0xC0FFEE);
  15:     while out.len() < len {
  16:         // SplitMix-style PRNG for fast deterministic fill.
  17:         state = state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  18:         let mut z = state;
  19:         z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  20:         z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  21:         let z = z ^ (z >> 31);
  22:         out.extend_from_slice(&z.to_le_bytes());
  23:     }
  24:     out.truncate(len);
  25:     out
  26: }
  27: 
  28: const SYMBOL_LEN: usize = 1024;
  29: 
  30: fn bench_encode_one_symbol(c: &mut Criterion) {
  31:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("fountain_encode_symbol");
  32:     for &k in &[8u32, 64, 256] {
  33:         let source = make_source(0xDEAD_BEEF, (k as usize) * SYMBOL_LEN);
  34:         let enc = LtEncoder::new(&source, SYMBOL_LEN).unwrap();
  35:         group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes(SYMBOL_LEN as u64));
  36:         group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(k), &k, |b, _| {
  37:             let mut sid = 0u32;
  38:             b.iter(|| {
  39:                 let payload = enc.encode_symbol(black_box(sid));
  40:                 sid = sid.wrapping_add(1);
  41:                 black_box(payload);
  42:             });
  43:         });
  44:     }
  45:     group.finish();
  46: }
  47: 
  48: fn bench_decode_full_chunk(c: &mut Criterion) {
  49:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("fountain_decode_chunk");
  50:     for &k in &[8u32, 64, 256] {
  51:         let source = make_source(0xCAFE_BABE, (k as usize) * SYMBOL_LEN);
  52:         let enc = LtEncoder::new(&source, SYMBOL_LEN).unwrap();
  53:         // Pre-compute enough symbols to guarantee decode succeeds.
  54:         let max_symbols = (k * 3).max(64);
  55:         let symbols: Vec<_> = (0u32..max_symbols)
  56:             .map(|sid| (sid, enc.encode_symbol(sid)))
  57:             .collect();
  58:         group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes((k as u64) * (SYMBOL_LEN as u64)));
  59:         group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::from_parameter(k), &k, |b, _| {
  60:             b.iter(|| {
  61:                 let mut dec = LtDecoder::new(k, SYMBOL_LEN, source.len()).unwrap();
  62:                 for (sid, payload) in &symbols {
  63:                     if dec.ingest(*sid, payload).unwrap() {
  64:                         break;
  65:                     }
  66:                 }
  67:                 let result = dec.finish().unwrap();

  69:             });
  70:         });
  71:     }
  72:     group.finish();
  73: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_fountain/src/decoder.rs", "bytes": 14183, "sha256": "681e645424abb40ddbfc276f56640ac47c65fb24dc1bc2a98ecfea0ce6605d80", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T18:02:46.579545+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}

   1: //! LT decoder: belief-propagation reconstruction of source symbols from
   2: //! a stream of encoded packets.
   3: //!
   4: //! Algorithm (standard LT decoding):
   5: //!
   6: //! 1. Each incoming encoded symbol is stored with its (deterministic)
   7: //!    neighbor set computed from `(k, symbol_id)`.
   8: //! 2. If any encoded symbol has exactly one *unresolved* neighbor, that
   9: //!    neighbor is recovered: source[n] = encoded XOR XOR(all-other-resolved-neighbors).
  10: //! 3. Once a source is resolved, every encoded symbol whose neighbor
  11: //!    set includes it XORs it out + drops it from its neighbor set.
  12: //! 4. Repeat until no degree-1 encoded symbols exist or all sources
  13: //!    are resolved.
  14: //!
  15: //! This is O((K + N) × d_avg) per ingest in the worst case, where N is
  16: //! the number of encoded symbols held. For K ≤ 256 and d_avg ≈ 4, this
  17: //! is microseconds per ingest.
  18: 
  19: use std::collections::{HashMap, VecDeque};
  20: 
  21: use crate::distribution::{robust_soliton_cdf, sample_degree, sample_neighbors};
  22: use crate::error::FountainError;
  23: use crate::rng::SplitMix64;
  24: use crate::xor::xor_into;
  25: 
  26: /// Maximum encoded-symbol count the decoder will hold per chunk. Caps
  27: /// memory at symbol_len * MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK bytes ≈ 2 MiB for
  28: /// symbol_len=1024. Sized to give K=1024 source symbols a 2× headroom
  29: /// over loss (Phase B acceptance gate: K=1024 at 5% loss across ≥1000
  30: /// random seeds — needs ~1.25K received, this gives 2K).
  31: pub const MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK: u32 = 2048;
  32: 
  33: /// Per-packet state inside the decoder: payload + remaining-unresolved
  34: /// neighbors. As neighbors are recovered they get XORed out of `payload`
  35: /// and removed from `neighbors`.
  36: struct PendingPacket {
  37:     payload: Vec<u8>,
  38:     neighbors: Vec<u32>,
  39: }
  40: 
  41: /// LT decoder for a single chunk.
  42: pub struct LtDecoder {
  43:     k: u32,
  44:     symbol_len: usize,
  45:     source_len: usize,
  46:     /// Resolved source symbols. `None` until decoded.
  47:     sources: Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>>,
  48:     /// Pending encoded packets keyed by symbol_id (so duplicates are
  49:     /// dropped silently).
  50:     pending: HashMap<u32, PendingPacket>,
  51:     /// Reverse index: source-symbol index → set of symbol_ids whose
  52:     /// neighbor sets currently include it. Used for fast propagation.
  53:     inverse: HashMap<u32, std::collections::BTreeSet<u32>>,
  54:     /// Queue of packets currently at degree-1, ready to resolve. We
  55:     /// push to the back on ingest / cascade and pop from the front in
  56:     /// propagate. This converts the O(pending) linear scan in the
  57:     /// classical decoder to O(1) amortized per resolution.
  58:     degree1_queue: VecDeque<u32>,
  59:     /// Number of source symbols resolved so far.
  60:     resolved: u32,
  61:     /// Degree CDF cached.
  62:     cdf: Vec<f64>,
  63: }
  64: 
  65: impl std::fmt::Debug for LtDecoder {
  66:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  67:         f.debug_struct("LtDecoder")
  68:             .field("k", &self.k)
  69:             .field("resolved", &self.resolved)
  70:             .field("pending", &self.pending.len())
  71:             .finish()
  72:     }
  73: }
  74: 
  75: impl LtDecoder {
  76:     /// Build a decoder for a chunk with `k` source symbols, each of
  77:     /// length `symbol_len`, encoding an original source of `source_len`
  78:     /// bytes (≤ `k * symbol_len`).
  79:     ///
  80:     /// # Errors
  81:     ///
  82:     /// [`FountainError::InvalidSymbolLen`] if `symbol_len == 0`.
  83:     pub fn new(k: u32, symbol_len: usize, source_len: usize) -> Result<Self, FountainError> {
  84:         if symbol_len == 0 {
  85:             return Err(FountainError::InvalidSymbolLen("must be > 0"));
  86:         }
  87:         if source_len > (k as usize) * symbol_len {
  88:             return Err(FountainError::InvalidSymbolLen(
  89:                 "source_len > k * symbol_len",
  90:             ));
  91:         }
  92:         Ok(Self {
  93:             k,
  94:             symbol_len,
  95:             source_len,
  96:             sources: vec![None; k as usize],
  97:             pending: HashMap::new(),
  98:             inverse: HashMap::new(),
  99:             degree1_queue: VecDeque::new(),
 100:             resolved: 0,
 101:             cdf: robust_soliton_cdf(k),
 102:         })
 103:     }
 104: 
 105:     /// K (source-symbol count).
 106:     #[inline]
 107:     #[must_use]
 108:     pub fn k(&self) -> u32 {
 109:         self.k
 110:     }
 111: 
 112:     /// Symbol length in bytes.
 113:     #[inline]
 114:     #[must_use]
 115:     pub fn symbol_len(&self) -> usize {
 116:         self.symbol_len
 117:     }
 118: 
 119:     /// Number of source symbols resolved so far.
 120:     #[inline]
 121:     #[must_use]
 122:     pub fn resolved_count(&self) -> u32 {
 123:         self.resolved
 124:     }
 125: 
 126:     /// True iff all K source symbols are resolved.
 127:     #[inline]
 128:     #[must_use]
 129:     pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {
 130:         self.resolved == self.k
 131:     }
 132: 
 133:     /// Ingest one encoded packet. Returns `Ok(true)` when this packet
 134:     /// completed the decode; `Ok(false)` otherwise.
 135:     ///
 136:     /// # Errors
 137:     ///
 138:     /// - [`FountainError::SymbolLenMismatch`] if `payload.len() !=
 139:     ///   symbol_len`.
 140:     /// - [`FountainError::SymbolIdOverflow`] if `symbol_id >=
 141:     ///   MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK`.
 142:     pub fn ingest(&mut self, symbol_id: u32, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<bool, FountainError> {
 143:         if self.is_complete() {
 144:             return Ok(true);
 145:         }
 146:         if payload.len() != self.symbol_len {
 147:             return Err(FountainError::SymbolLenMismatch {
 148:                 expected: self.symbol_len,
 149:                 got: payload.len(),
 150:             });
 151:         }
 152:         if symbol_id >= MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK {
 153:             return Err(FountainError::SymbolIdOverflow {
 154:                 got: symbol_id,
 155:                 max: MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK,
 156:             });
 157:         }
 158:         if self.pending.contains_key(&symbol_id) {
 159:             // Duplicate; drop.
 160:             return Ok(self.is_complete());
 161:         }
 162: 
 163:         let mut rng = SplitMix64::for_symbol(self.k, symbol_id);
 164:         let d = sample_degree(&self.cdf, &mut rng);
 165:         let neighbors = sample_neighbors(self.k, d, &mut rng);
 166: 
 167:         // Pre-XOR any already-resolved neighbors out of the payload.
 168:         let mut working_payload = payload.to_vec();
 169:         let mut unresolved = Vec::with_capacity(neighbors.len());
 170:         for n in &neighbors {
 171:             if let Some(src) = &self.sources[*n as usize] {
 172:                 xor_into(&mut working_payload, src);
 173:             } else {
 174:                 unresolved.push(*n);
 175:             }
 176:         }
 177: 
 178:         // If after pre-resolution the packet has 0 unresolved neighbors,
 179:         // it's redundant; drop it.
 180:         if unresolved.is_empty() {
 181:             return Ok(self.is_complete());
 182:         }
 183: 
 184:         // Insert pending + update reverse index.
 185:         for n in &unresolved {
 186:             self.inverse
 187:                 .entry(*n)
 188:                 .or_insert_with(std::collections::BTreeSet::new)
 189:                 .insert(symbol_id);
 190:         }
 191:         let neighbor_count = unresolved.len();
 192:         self.pending.insert(
 193:             symbol_id,
 194:             PendingPacket {
 195:                 payload: working_payload,
 196:                 neighbors: unresolved,
 197:             },
 198:         );
 199:         if neighbor_count == 1 {
 200:             self.degree1_queue.push_back(symbol_id);
 201:         }
 202: 
 203:         // Propagate any degree-1 packets.
 204:         self.propagate();
 205:         Ok(self.is_complete())
 206:     }
 207: 
 208:     /// Belief-propagation pass: drain the degree-1 queue, resolving the
 209:     /// referenced source for each and cascading into dependents. New
 210:     /// degree-1 packets discovered during cascade are pushed to the
 211:     /// queue and picked up in the same drain.
 212:     ///
 213:     /// Complexity: O(N_resolved × d_avg × symbol_len) where N_resolved
 214:     /// is at most K. The previous implementation scanned all pending
 215:     /// packets per resolution (O(K × pending)) — this version is
 216:     /// O(K × d_avg).
 217:     fn propagate(&mut self) {
 218:         while let Some(sid) = self.degree1_queue.pop_front() {
 219:             // Stale entry — the packet may have been resolved (and
 220:             // removed) via cascade since it was queued, or its degree
 221:             // may no longer be 1 (a cascade XOR'd in extra neighbors,
 222:             // which never happens in LT codes, but be defensive).
 223:             let pkt = match self.pending.remove(&sid) {
 224:                 Some(p) if p.neighbors.len() == 1 => p,
 225:                 Some(p) => {
 226:                     self.pending.insert(sid, p);
 227:                     continue;
 228:                 }
 229:                 None => continue,
 230:             };
 231:             let target = pkt.neighbors[0];
 232:             // pkt.payload IS source[target]. Cascade BEFORE we move the
 233:             // payload into self.sources, so the inner XOR borrows
 234:             // pkt.payload as `&[u8]` (cheap) instead of indexing into
 235:             // self.sources (which would conflict with the &mut on
 236:             // self.pending). After the cascade, move the payload Vec
 237:             // directly into the resolved-sources slot — no clone.
 238:             let dependents = self.inverse.remove(&target).unwrap_or_default();
 239:             for dep_sid in dependents {
 240:                 if dep_sid == sid {
 241:                     continue;
 242:                 }
 243:                 if let Some(dep) = self.pending.get_mut(&dep_sid) {
 244:                     if let Some(pos) = dep.neighbors.iter().position(|n| *n == target) {
 245:                         dep.neighbors.remove(pos);
 246:                         xor_into(&mut dep.payload, &pkt.payload);
 247:                         if dep.neighbors.len() == 1 {
 248:                             self.degree1_queue.push_back(dep_sid);
 249:                         }
 250:                     }
 251:                 }
 252:             }
 253:             self.sources[target as usize] = Some(pkt.payload);
 254:             self.resolved += 1;
 255:             if self.is_complete() {
 256:                 self.degree1_queue.clear();
 257:                 break;
 258:             }
 259:         }
 260:     }
 261: 
 262:     /// Consume the decoder + return the reconstructed source bytes.
 263:     ///
 264:     /// # Errors
 265:     ///
 266:     /// [`FountainError::IncompleteDecode`] if not all K sources have
 267:     /// been resolved.
 268:     pub fn finish(self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FountainError> {
 269:         if !self.is_complete() {
 270:             return Err(FountainError::IncompleteDecode {
 271:                 resolved: self.resolved,
 272:                 k: self.k,
 273:             });
 274:         }
 275:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(self.source_len);
 276:         for i in 0..self.k as usize {
 277:             let s = self.sources[i].as_ref().expect("resolved");
 278:             out.extend_from_slice(s);
 279:         }
 280:         out.truncate(self.source_len);
 281:         Ok(out)
 282:     }
 283: }

   1: //! Robust Soliton Distribution (Luby 2002) for LT codes.
   2: //!
   3: //! Computes Ω(d) — the probability of selecting degree d when encoding
   4: //! a single LT symbol — as a function of:
   5: //!
   6: //! - **K**: source-symbol count
   7: //! - **c**: free knob, typically 0.03-0.2; smaller = lower overhead at
   8: //!   the cost of failure rate. We use **c = 0.03**.
   9: //! - **δ**: target decoding failure probability. We use **δ = 0.05**.
  10: //!
  11: //! Both `c` and `δ` are fixed for Phase B v1 per ADR-0015 to keep the
  12: //! wire format simple — the receiver re-derives the same CDF from K.
  13: //!
  14: //! ## Reference
  15: //!
  16: //! Luby, "LT Codes," FOCS 2002. The classic K-dependent distribution.
  17: 
  18: use crate::rng::SplitMix64;
  19: 
  20: /// Phase B v1 LT codes free knob (Luby's `c`).
  21: pub const C: f64 = 0.03;
  22: 
  23: /// Phase B v1 LT codes target failure probability (Luby's `δ`).
  24: pub const DELTA: f64 = 0.05;
  25: 
  26: /// Compute the Robust Soliton CDF for K source symbols. Returns a
  27: /// `Vec<f64>` of length K, where `cdf[d-1]` is the cumulative probability
  28: /// up to and including degree `d`.
  29: #[must_use]
  30: pub fn robust_soliton_cdf(k: u32) -> Vec<f64> {
  31:     let k_f = f64::from(k);
  32:     // R = c * ln(K/δ) * sqrt(K)
  33:     let r = C * (k_f / DELTA).ln() * k_f.sqrt();
  34:     let r_int = r.round().max(1.0) as u32;
  35:     let r_int = r_int.min(k); // cap
  36: 
  37:     // Compute (ρ + τ) per degree, then normalize.
  38:     let mut weights = vec![0.0f64; k as usize];
  39:     for d in 1..=k {
  40:         let i = (d - 1) as usize;
  41:         // ρ(d)
  42:         let rho = if d == 1 {
  43:             1.0 / k_f
  44:         } else {
  45:             1.0 / (f64::from(d) * f64::from(d - 1))
  46:         };
  47:         // τ(d)
  48:         let tau = if d < r_int {
  49:             r / (f64::from(d) * k_f)
  50:         } else if d == r_int {
  51:             r * (r / DELTA).ln() / k_f
  52:         } else {
  53:             0.0
  54:         };
  55:         weights[i] = rho + tau;
  56:     }
  57:     // Normalize.
  58:     let z: f64 = weights.iter().sum();
  59:     for w in &mut weights {
  60:         *w /= z;
  61:     }
  62:     // Convert to CDF.
  63:     let mut cdf = vec![0.0f64; k as usize];
  64:     let mut acc = 0.0f64;
  65:     for (i, w) in weights.iter().enumerate() {
  66:         acc += *w;
  67:         cdf[i] = acc;
  68:     }
  69:     // Clamp the last entry to 1.0 to absorb float rounding.
  70:     if let Some(last) = cdf.last_mut() {
  71:         *last = 1.0;
  72:     }
  73:     cdf
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Sample a degree from the Robust Soliton CDF using `rng`.
  77: #[must_use]
  78: pub fn sample_degree(cdf: &[f64], rng: &mut SplitMix64) -> u32 {
  79:     let u = rng.next_f64_01();
  80:     // Linear scan — K is small (≤ 256) so binary search is overkill.
  81:     for (i, &c) in cdf.iter().enumerate() {
  82:         if u <= c {
  83:             return (i + 1) as u32;
  84:         }
  85:     }
  86:     // Float overflow safety: return max degree.
  87:     cdf.len() as u32
  88: }
  89: 
  90: /// Sample `d` distinct source-symbol indices in `[0, k)` using `rng`.
  91: ///
  92: /// For `d` close to `k`, uses reservoir-style sampling without replacement
  93: /// to avoid quadratic retry. For `d` small, uses Floyd's algorithm with
  94: /// a small `HashSet`.
  95: #[must_use]
  96: pub fn sample_neighbors(k: u32, d: u32, rng: &mut SplitMix64) -> Vec<u32> {
  97:     let d = d.min(k);
  98:     let mut chosen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
  99:     // Floyd's algorithm: O(d) draws even when d ≈ k.
 100:     for j in (k - d)..k {
 101:         let r = rng.next_u32_below(j + 1);
 102:         if chosen.contains(&r) {
 103:             chosen.insert(j);
 104:         } else {
 105:             chosen.insert(r);
 106:         }
 107:     }
 108:     chosen.into_iter().collect()
 109: }
 110:

   1: //! LT encoder: takes a source buffer + symbol_len; produces one encoded
   2: //! symbol per call.
   3: 
   4: use crate::distribution::{robust_soliton_cdf, sample_degree, sample_neighbors};
   5: use crate::error::FountainError;
   6: use crate::rng::SplitMix64;
   7: use crate::xor::xor_into;
   8: 
   9: /// LT encoder over a fixed source buffer.
  10: ///
  11: /// Constructed once per chunk; `encode_symbol(symbol_id)` returns one
  12: /// XORed payload of length `symbol_len`. Senders typically call this
  13: /// in a monotonic loop until the receiver signals decode complete.
  14: pub struct LtEncoder<'a> {
  15:     source: &'a [u8],
  16:     k: u32,
  17:     symbol_len: usize,
  18:     cdf: Vec<f64>,
  19:     /// Padding for the last source symbol when `source.len() % symbol_len != 0`.
  20:     /// Owned so `encode_symbol` can return a slice into either `source`
  21:     /// or this padding buffer.
  22:     last_padded: Option<Vec<u8>>,
  23: }
  24: 
  25: impl<'a> std::fmt::Debug for LtEncoder<'a> {
  26:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  27:         f.debug_struct("LtEncoder")
  28:             .field("k", &self.k)
  29:             .field("symbol_len", &self.symbol_len)
  30:             .field("source_len", &self.source.len())
  31:             .finish()
  32:     }
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl<'a> LtEncoder<'a> {
  36:     /// Build an encoder over `source` with `symbol_len`-byte symbols.
  37:     ///
  38:     /// `k` is derived as `ceil(source.len() / symbol_len)`. The last
  39:     /// source symbol is zero-padded if `source.len() % symbol_len != 0`.
  40:     ///
  41:     /// # Errors
  42:     ///
  43:     /// - [`FountainError::InvalidSymbolLen`] if `symbol_len == 0`.
  44:     /// - [`FountainError::EmptySource`] if `source` is empty.
  45:     pub fn new(source: &'a [u8], symbol_len: usize) -> Result<Self, FountainError> {
  46:         if symbol_len == 0 {
  47:             return Err(FountainError::InvalidSymbolLen("must be > 0"));
  48:         }
  49:         if source.is_empty() {
  50:             return Err(FountainError::EmptySource);
  51:         }
  52:         let k = ((source.len() + symbol_len - 1) / symbol_len) as u32;
  53:         let last_padded = if source.len() % symbol_len != 0 {
  54:             let mut buf = vec![0u8; symbol_len];
  55:             let tail_start = (k as usize - 1) * symbol_len;
  56:             let tail_len = source.len() - tail_start;
  57:             buf[..tail_len].copy_from_slice(&source[tail_start..]);
  58:             Some(buf)
  59:         } else {
  60:             None
  61:         };
  62:         let cdf = robust_soliton_cdf(k);
  63:         Ok(Self {
  64:             source,
  65:             k,
  66:             symbol_len,
  67:             cdf,
  68:             last_padded,
  69:         })
  70:     }
  71: 
  72:     /// Source-symbol count.
  73:     #[inline]
  74:     #[must_use]
  75:     pub fn k(&self) -> u32 {
  76:         self.k
  77:     }
  78: 
  79:     /// Symbol length in bytes.
  80:     #[inline]
  81:     #[must_use]
  82:     pub fn symbol_len(&self) -> usize {
  83:         self.symbol_len
  84:     }
  85: 
  86:     /// Original source length in bytes (pre-padding).
  87:     #[inline]
  88:     #[must_use]
  89:     pub fn source_len(&self) -> usize {
  90:         self.source.len()
  91:     }
  92: 
  93:     /// Borrow source symbol `i`. Returns the padded slice for the last
  94:     /// symbol if the source isn't an exact multiple of `symbol_len`.
  95:     fn source_symbol(&self, i: u32) -> &[u8] {
  96:         let i_us = i as usize;
  97:         let last = (self.k - 1) as usize;
  98:         if i_us == last {
  99:             if let Some(buf) = &self.last_padded {
 100:                 return buf.as_slice();
 101:             }
 102:         }
 103:         let start = i_us * self.symbol_len;
 104:         &self.source[start..start + self.symbol_len]
 105:     }
 106: 
 107:     /// Encode one symbol with the given `symbol_id`. Returns the XORed
 108:     /// payload of length `symbol_len`.
 109:     #[must_use]
 110:     pub fn encode_symbol(&self, symbol_id: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
 111:         let mut rng = SplitMix64::for_symbol(self.k, symbol_id);
 112:         let d = sample_degree(&self.cdf, &mut rng);
 113:         let neighbors = sample_neighbors(self.k, d, &mut rng);
 114:         // First neighbor: clone directly into the output buffer (skips
 115:         // a zero-fill + first XOR-against-zero, which is the dominant
 116:         // cost at degree=1 under Robust Soliton).
 117:         let mut iter = neighbors.iter();
 118:         let first = *iter.next().expect("sample_neighbors yields ≥ 1");
 119:         let mut out = self.source_symbol(first).to_vec();
 120:         // Remaining neighbors: word-wide XOR into `out`.
 121:         for n in iter {
 122:             xor_into(&mut out, self.source_symbol(*n));
 123:         }
 124:         out
 125:     }
 126: 
 127:     /// Convenience: re-derive the neighbor set for a given symbol_id
 128:     /// without producing the payload. Useful for tests / diagnostics.
 129:     #[must_use]
 130:     pub fn neighbors_for(&self, symbol_id: u32) -> Vec<u32> {
 131:         let mut rng = SplitMix64::for_symbol(self.k, symbol_id);
 132:         let d = sample_degree(&self.cdf, &mut rng);
 133:         sample_neighbors(self.k, d, &mut rng)
 134:     }
 135: }
 136:

   1: //! `ol_fountain` — LT fountain codes for One Link's swarm transfer
   2: //! layer per [ADR-0015](../../../docs/decisions/0015-fountain-codes.md).
   3: //!
   4: //! ## What this gives you
   5: //!
   6: //! - [`LtEncoder`] — encodes a chunk plaintext into a stream of LT
   7: //!   symbols, deterministically seeded by `symbol_id`.
   8: //! - [`LtDecoder`] — reconstructs the chunk plaintext from any
   9: //!   sufficient subset of encoded symbols via belief propagation.
  10: //! - [`FountainPacket`] — on-wire encode/decode of a single fountain
  11: //!   packet (chunk_id + k + symbol_id + source_length + payload).
  12: //! - [`Distribution`](distribution) — Robust Soliton degree distribution
  13: //!   with Phase B-fixed (`c=0.03`, `δ=0.05`) parameters.
  14: //!
  15: //! ## What this crate does NOT do
  16: //!
  17: //! - It does not wire fountain packets through the QUIC frame layer;
  18: //!   that's `ol_transfer`'s job (will land in Phase B-1.5 once a
  19: //!   `FountainBurst` frame kind ships).
  20: //! - It does not verify chunk integrity. The caller is expected to
  21: //!   compute `BLAKE3(decoded_plaintext)` and compare to the chunk_id
  22: //!   before storing.
  23: 
  24: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_fountain/0.21.0")]
  25: 
  26: pub mod decoder;
  27: pub mod distribution;
  28: pub mod encoder;
  29: pub mod error;
  30: pub mod packet;
  31: pub mod rng;
  32: mod xor;

   1: //! On-wire packet format for LT fountain transfer per ADR-0015.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wire shape:
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //! +----------+----------+---------+-------------+
   7: //! | chunk_id | k        | symbol  | source      | encoded_payload
   8: //! | 32B      | u32 LE   | u32 LE  | u32 LE      | (symbol_len B)
   9: //! +----------+----------+---------+-------------+
  10: //!   0..32      32..36     36..40    40..44        44..
  11: //! ```
  12: //!
  13: //! 44-byte header + `symbol_len` byte payload. `source_length` is the
  14: //! original chunk plaintext length (`length_plaintext` in ADR-0003).
  15: 
  16: use crate::error::FountainError;
  17: 
  18: /// Length of a fountain packet header on the wire.
  19: pub const PACKET_HEADER_LEN: usize = 44;
  20: 
  21: /// A parsed fountain packet ready to feed into an [`crate::decoder::LtDecoder`].
  22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  23: pub struct FountainPacket {
  24:     /// 32-byte chunk_id this packet belongs to.
  25:     pub chunk_id: [u8; 32],
  26:     /// K = source-symbol count for the chunk.
  27:     pub k: u32,
  28:     /// Monotonically-increasing symbol_id from the sender.
  29:     pub symbol_id: u32,
  30:     /// Original chunk plaintext length (so the decoder can trim padding).
  31:     pub source_length: u32,
  32:     /// LT-encoded payload bytes.
  33:     pub payload: Vec<u8>,
  34: }
  35: 
  36: impl FountainPacket {
  37:     /// Construct a new packet.
  38:     #[must_use]
  39:     pub fn new(
  40:         chunk_id: [u8; 32],
  41:         k: u32,
  42:         symbol_id: u32,
  43:         source_length: u32,
  44:         payload: Vec<u8>,
  45:     ) -> Self {
  46:         Self {
  47:             chunk_id,
  48:             k,
  49:             symbol_id,
  50:             source_length,
  51:             payload,
  52:         }
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// Encode to wire bytes.
  56:     #[must_use]
  57:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
  58:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(PACKET_HEADER_LEN + self.payload.len());
  59:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.chunk_id);
  60:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.k.to_le_bytes());
  61:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.symbol_id.to_le_bytes());
  62:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.source_length.to_le_bytes());
  63:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.payload);
  64:         out
  65:     }
  66: 
  67:     /// Decode from wire bytes.
  68:     ///
  69:     /// # Errors
  70:     ///
  71:     /// [`FountainError::MalformedPacket`] if the buffer is shorter than
  72:     /// the header.
  73:     pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, FountainError> {
  74:         if bytes.len() < PACKET_HEADER_LEN {
  75:             return Err(FountainError::MalformedPacket("packet shorter than header"));
  76:         }
  77:         let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
  78:         chunk_id.copy_from_slice(&bytes[0..32]);
  79:         let k = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[32..36].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
  80:         let symbol_id = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[36..40].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
  81:         let source_length = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[40..44].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
  82:         if k == 0 {
  83:             return Err(FountainError::MalformedPacket("k must be > 0"));
  84:         }
  85:         let payload = bytes[PACKET_HEADER_LEN..].to_vec();
  86:         if payload.is_empty() {
  87:             return Err(FountainError::MalformedPacket("empty payload"));
  88:         }
  89:         Ok(Self {
  90:             chunk_id,
  91:             k,
  92:             symbol_id,
  93:             source_length,
  94:             payload,
  95:         })
  96:     }
  97: }
  98:

   1: //! Deterministic seeded PRNG used by the LT encoder + decoder.
   2: //!
   3: //! For wire interoperability between sender and receiver, both sides
   4: //! MUST agree on:
   5: //!
   6: //! 1. The degree sampled for a given `symbol_id`.
   7: //! 2. The set of source-symbol indices sampled for a given `symbol_id`.
   8: //!
   9: //! We derive a per-`symbol_id` seed via BLAKE3 keyed hash, then run a
  10: //! tiny SplitMix64-compatible PRNG over it. SplitMix64 is exact,
  11: //! deterministic, and 1 multiply + 1 shift per 64-bit draw — fast
  12: //! enough that encoding never bottlenecks on RNG.
  13: 
  14: const SEED_CONTEXT: &str = "ol-fountain-lt-v1";
  15: 
  16: /// Derive a 64-bit seed for `(k, symbol_id)`.
  17: ///
  18: /// Uses BLAKE3.derive_key with [`SEED_CONTEXT`] and the 8-byte key
  19: /// `[k_le; 4][symbol_id_le; 4]` → take the first 8 bytes of the output.
  20: #[inline]
  21: #[must_use]
  22: pub fn seed_for(k: u32, symbol_id: u32) -> u64 {
  23:     let mut input = [0u8; 8];
  24:     input[0..4].copy_from_slice(&k.to_le_bytes());
  25:     input[4..8].copy_from_slice(&symbol_id.to_le_bytes());
  26:     let key = blake3::derive_key(SEED_CONTEXT, &input);
  27:     u64::from_le_bytes(key[..8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"))
  28: }
  29: 
  30: /// SplitMix64 deterministic PRNG. See https://prng.di.unimi.it/splitmix64.c
  31: ///
  32: /// One `next` call is 1 multiply + 1 add + 1 xor; ~2 cycles on x86.
  33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  34: pub struct SplitMix64 {
  35:     state: u64,
  36: }
  37: 
  38: impl SplitMix64 {
  39:     /// Construct from a seed.
  40:     #[inline]
  41:     #[must_use]
  42:     pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
  43:         Self { state: seed }
  44:     }
  45: 
  46:     /// Construct from `(k, symbol_id)` via [`seed_for`].
  47:     #[inline]
  48:     #[must_use]
  49:     pub fn for_symbol(k: u32, symbol_id: u32) -> Self {
  50:         Self::new(seed_for(k, symbol_id))
  51:     }
  52: 
  53:     /// Draw the next 64-bit value.
  54:     #[inline]
  55:     pub fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
  56:         self.state = self.state.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  57:         let mut z = self.state;
  58:         z = (z ^ (z >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  59:         z = (z ^ (z >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  60:         z ^ (z >> 31)
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// Draw a uniform `[0, range)` u32. Uses Lemire's nearly-divisionless
  64:     /// method; bias is statistically undetectable for our K ≤ 65536.
  65:     #[inline]
  66:     pub fn next_u32_below(&mut self, range: u32) -> u32 {
  67:         debug_assert!(range > 0);
  68:         let r = u64::from(range);
  69:         let x = (self.next_u64() >> 32) as u64; // u32 reduced
  70:         ((x.wrapping_mul(r)) >> 32) as u32
  71:     }
  72: 
  73:     /// Draw a uniform `[0, 1)` float. Used by the degree CDF sampler.
  74:     #[inline]
  75:     pub fn next_f64_01(&mut self) -> f64 {
  76:         // 53-bit mantissa.
  77:         let bits = self.next_u64() >> 11;
  78:         bits as f64 * (1.0 / ((1u64 << 53) as f64))
  79:     }
  80: }
  81:
