   1: //! SIMD-friendly word-wide XOR for the LT encoder + decoder hot path.
   2: //!
   3: //! The naive byte-at-a-time loop `for (o, s) in dest.iter_mut().zip(src.iter())`
   4: //! compiles to byte-wise XOR even with `-O2`. By splitting the buffer
   5: //! into 64-byte chunks and XOR'ing word-by-word (via `u64::from_ne_bytes`),
   6: //! we hand the compiler a straight-line vectorizable shape that lowers
   7: //! to AVX2 `vpxor` (32 bytes / iter) or SSE2 `pxor` (16 bytes / iter)
   8: //! on x86_64, and NEON `eor` on aarch64.
   9: //!
  10: //! For Phase B v1 symbols of 1 KiB:
  11: //!   - Naive: 1024 iterations.
  12: //!   - 64-byte chunks: 16 iterations → 64× fewer branches.
  13: 
  14: /// In-place XOR: `dest[i] ^= src[i]` for `i in 0..len`. Both slices
  15: /// must be the same length.
  16: ///
  17: /// Hot-path-tuned: uses raw `read_unaligned` / `write_unaligned` to
  18: /// strip the bounds-check overhead `try_into()` would inject, while
  19: /// staying within `debug_assert`-validated bounds. The compiler
  20: /// vectorizes the u64 loop into AVX2 `vpxor` on x86_64 and NEON `eor`
  21: /// on aarch64.
  22: #[inline]
  23: pub(crate) fn xor_into(dest: &mut [u8], src: &[u8]) {
  24:     debug_assert_eq!(dest.len(), src.len());
  25:     let n = dest.len();
  26:     let head_words = n / 8;
  27:     let tail_start = head_words * 8;
  28: 
  29:     // SAFETY: We never read or write outside `0..n`. The pointers
  30:     // alias different allocations (`dest` is &mut, `src` is &; the
  31:     // borrow checker rejects overlap before we get here). u64 reads
  32:     // are `read_unaligned`, so alignment of the base allocation does
  33:     // not matter.
  34:     unsafe {
  35:         let dst_u64 = dest.as_mut_ptr().cast::<u64>();
  36:         let src_u64 = src.as_ptr().cast::<u64>();
  37:         for i in 0..head_words {
  38:             let a = std::ptr::read_unaligned(dst_u64.add(i));
  39:             let b = std::ptr::read_unaligned(src_u64.add(i));
  40:             std::ptr::write_unaligned(dst_u64.add(i), a ^ b);
  41:         }
  42:     }
  43:     // Byte tail (0..7 bytes).
  44:     for i in tail_start..n {
  45:         dest[i] ^= src[i];
  46:     }
  47: }
  48:

   1: //! Falsifiable acceptance gate for ADR-0015 fountain codes.
   2: //!
   3: //! Spec: "Decode success ≥99% at 5% packet loss across ≥1,000 random
   4: //! seeds for K ∈ {8, 64, 256}."
   5: //!
   6: //! These tests are not stress tests of the algorithm; they're the
   7: //! verification that pins the Robust Soliton parameters and the LT
   8: //! belief-propagation decoder against the ADR's acceptance number. If
   9: //! one fails, the ADR doesn't ship.
  10: 
  11: use ol_fountain::{LtDecoder, LtEncoder};
  12: use rand::rngs::StdRng;
  13: use rand::{Rng, SeedableRng};
  14: 
  15: #[allow(deprecated)]
  16: fn loss_draw(rng: &mut StdRng, p: f64) -> bool {
  17:     rng.gen_bool(p)
  18: }
  19: 
  20: /// Fixed Phase B v1 wire symbol length per ADR-0015.
  21: const SYMBOL_LEN: usize = 1024;
  22: 
  23: /// Run one decode trial: encode the source, send packets through a 5%
  24: /// loss channel up to `max_symbols`, and return true if decode
  25: /// completed.
  26: fn one_trial(source: &[u8], loss_rate: f64, max_symbols: u32, seed: u64) -> bool {
  27:     let enc = LtEncoder::new(source, SYMBOL_LEN).unwrap();
  28:     let mut dec = LtDecoder::new(enc.k(), SYMBOL_LEN, source.len()).unwrap();
  29:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed);
  30:     for sid in 0..max_symbols {
  31:         if loss_draw(&mut rng, loss_rate) {
  32:             continue;
  33:         }
  34:         let payload = enc.encode_symbol(sid);
  35:         if dec.ingest(sid, &payload).unwrap() {
  36:             // decoded; verify
  37:             let out = dec.finish().unwrap();
  38:             return out == source;
  39:         }
  40:     }
  41:     false
  42: }
  43: 
  44: fn run_acceptance(k_target: u32, trials: u32) -> u32 {
  45:     let source_len = (k_target as usize) * SYMBOL_LEN;
  46:     let mut source = vec![0u8; source_len];
  47:     // Fill with a non-byte-periodic stream so source symbols are distinct.
  48:     for (i, b) in source.iter_mut().enumerate() {
  49:         *b = ((i as u64)
  50:             .wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
  51:             .wrapping_add(0xCAFE)
  52:             ^ ((i as u64) >> 13)) as u8;
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     // Allow up to 5K symbols per trial; well above the per-chunk encode
  56:     // cap. Acceptance gate: ≥99% success across `trials`.
  57:     let mut success = 0u32;
  58:     for seed in 0..trials {
  59:         if one_trial(
  60:             &source,
  61:             0.05,
  62:             4096.min(ol_fountain::MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK - 1),
  63:             seed as u64,
  64:         ) {
  65:             success += 1;
  66:         }
  67:     }
  68:     success
  69: }
  70:

  72: fn adr0015_k_8_decodes_at_5pct_loss() {

 198: #[test]
 199: fn adversarial_random_packet_garbage_dropped() {
 200:     // Pollution: feed the decoder packets with random payload bytes
 201:     // (not real LT-encoded). Decoder should NOT erroneously "decode"
 202:     // to something that hashes to chunk_id.
 203:     use ol_fountain::LtDecoder;
 204:     use rand::rngs::StdRng;
 205:     use rand::{Rng, SeedableRng};
 206: 
 207:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(0xDEAD_BEEF);
 208:     let source_len = 16 * SYMBOL_LEN;
 209:     let real_source: Vec<u8> = (0..source_len)
 210:         .map(|i| ((i as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9)) as u8)
 211:         .collect();
 212:     let mut dec = LtDecoder::new(16, SYMBOL_LEN, source_len).unwrap();
 213: 
 214:     // Feed 100 random-payload packets. The decoder may or may not
 215:     // claim "decoded"; if it does, the BLAKE3 of the result MUST
 216:     // differ from the real source's BLAKE3.
 217:     for sid in 0..100u32 {
 218:         let mut bogus = vec![0u8; SYMBOL_LEN];
 219:         rng.fill(&mut bogus[..]);
 220:         let _ = dec.ingest(sid, &bogus);
 221:     }
 222: 
 223:     // If the decoder spuriously completed, its output hashes differently.
 224:     if dec.is_complete() {
 225:         let fake_decoded = dec.finish().unwrap();
 226:         let real_hash = blake3::hash(&real_source);
 227:         let fake_hash = blake3::hash(&fake_decoded);
 228:         assert_ne!(
 229:             real_hash.as_bytes(),
 230:             fake_hash.as_bytes(),
 231:             "decoder erroneously reconstructed real source from random packets"
 232:         );
 233:     }
 234:     // Else: decoder correctly refused to complete on garbage. Pass.
 235: }

   1: //! `ol_fskit` — macOS FSKit filesystem surface (Phase B layer 9).
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md`:
   4: //!
   5: //! > FSKit on macOS (NOT macFUSE — macFUSE is GPL+commercial
   6: //! > dual-license, breaks no-monthly-bill on macOS; FSKit is
   7: //! > Apple's modern in-userspace alternative).
   8: //!
   9: //! ## Architectural contract
  10: //!
  11: //! The trait surface mirrors `ol_fuse::FilesystemBackend` exactly —
  12: //! same trait, same `FsError` translation table, same lifecycle
  13: //! shape. A daemon can pick a backend per platform (or share one
  14: //! across all three) without forking the chunk-store side.
  15: //!
  16: //! ## Scaffold status
  17: //!
  18: //! FSKit ships through Apple's Swift / Objective-C runtime. Bridging
  19: //! it to a Rust backend requires either:
  20: //!
  21: //! 1. A Swift package that links the Rust `staticlib` and forwards
  22: //!    FSUnaryFileSystem / FSFileSystem callbacks into our trait
  23: //!    methods, or
  24: //! 2. `objc2-foundation` bindings (the Rust path) directly
  25: //!    instantiating the FSKit ObjC classes.
  26: //!
  27: //! Both options need a macOS host to verify; the crate ships the
  28: //! API surface today so the daemon's per-platform mount endpoint
  29: //! can compile + dispatch correctly regardless of whether the
  30: //! Swift adapter has landed.
  31: 
  32: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  33: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  34: 
  35: use std::path::PathBuf;
  36: 
  37: use thiserror::Error;
  38: 
  39: pub use ol_fuse::{DirEntry, EntryKind, FilesystemBackend, FsError, MemoryBackend, Stat};
  40: 
  41: /// Options the daemon passes when mounting a folder as FSKit.
  42: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  43: pub struct MountOptions {
  44:     /// Mountpoint directory. macOS mounts under `/Volumes/<name>`
  45:     /// by convention; passing a custom path requires
  46:     /// `volume_kind = .userVisibleStorage`.
  47:     pub mountpoint: PathBuf,
  48:     /// Volume name shown in Finder + `mount` output.
  49:     pub volume_name: String,
  50:     /// Read-only mount (Finder will mark the volume as locked).
  51:     pub read_only: bool,
  52: }
  53: 
  54: impl Default for MountOptions {
  55:     fn default() -> Self {
  56:         Self {
  57:             mountpoint: PathBuf::new(),
  58:             volume_name: "one_link".into(),
  59:             read_only: false,
  60:         }
  61:     }
  62: }
  63: 
  64: /// Errors mount() can return.
  65: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  66: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
  67: pub enum MountError {
  68:     #[error("FSKit not supported on this platform (macOS 15+ only)")]
  69:     UnsupportedPlatform,
  70:     #[error("mountpoint does not exist or is not a directory: {0}")]
  71:     InvalidMountpoint(PathBuf),
  72:     #[error("FSKit backend error: {0}")]
  73:     Backend(String),
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Mount `backend` at `opts.mountpoint` via FSKit.
  77: ///
  78: /// Behaviour:
  79: ///
  80: /// - **macOS with `macos-mount` feature**: returns
  81: ///   [`MountError::Backend`] with a "Swift adapter not yet wired"
  82: ///   message — the Swift bridge is the Phase-B deliverable.
  83: /// - **macOS without the feature**: returns
  84: ///   [`MountError::Backend`] with a "rebuild with --features
  85: ///   macos-mount" hint.
  86: /// - **Non-macOS**: returns [`MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`].
  87: pub fn mount<B>(
  88:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", feature = "macos-mount"))] _backend: B,
  89:     #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "macos", feature = "macos-mount")))] _backend: B,
  90:     opts: MountOptions,
  91: ) -> Result<(), MountError>
  92: where
  93:     B: FilesystemBackend + 'static,

  99:     {
 100:         Err(MountError::Backend(
 101:             "Swift / FSKit adapter not yet wired (Phase B daemon mount endpoint pending)".into(),
 102:         ))
 103:     }
 104:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", not(feature = "macos-mount")))]
 105:     {
 106:         Err(MountError::Backend(
 107:             "rebuild ol_fskit with --features macos-mount to enable FSKit".into(),
 108:         ))
 109:     }
 110:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 111:     {
 112:         Err(MountError::UnsupportedPlatform)
 113:     }
 114: }

   1: //! Real `fuser::Filesystem` adapter. Linux-only — bridges the
   2: //! platform-agnostic [`FilesystemBackend`](crate::backend::FilesystemBackend)
   3: //! trait to libfuse's inode-keyed callback shape.
   4: //!
   5: //! Compiled only when the `linux-mount` feature is enabled AND we're on
   6: //! Linux. Other platforms get the stub mount() that returns
   7: //! [`crate::MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`].
   8: //!
   9: //! ## Inode mapping
  10: //!
  11: //! libfuse operates on `u64` inode numbers, while
  12: //! [`FilesystemBackend`] operates on path strings. We maintain a
  13: //! bidirectional map: `1` is reserved for the root (per libfuse
  14: //! convention); new entries hash their relative path to a stable
  15: //! `u64` via BLAKE3 truncation. This keeps inodes deterministic
  16: //! across remounts and lookups — important for client caches that
  17: //! key on inode numbers.
  18: 
  19: #![cfg(all(target_os = "linux", feature = "linux-mount"))]
  20: 
  21: use std::collections::HashMap;
  22: use std::ffi::OsStr;
  23: use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
  24: use std::time::Duration;
  25: 
  26: use fuser::{
  27:     FileAttr, FileType, Filesystem, ReplyAttr, ReplyData, ReplyDirectory, ReplyEmpty, ReplyEntry,
  28:     ReplyWrite, Request,
  29: };
  30: 
  31: use crate::backend::{EntryKind, FilesystemBackend, FsError, Stat};
  32: 
  33: /// Filesystem TTL hint to the kernel — how long it may cache attrs.
  34: /// Conservative default; the backend is the source of truth so cache
  35: /// hits beyond this re-poll the backend.
  36: const ATTR_TTL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
  37: /// Inode for the filesystem root, mandated by libfuse.
  38: const ROOT_INODE: u64 = 1;
  39: /// First inode assigned to a non-root entry.
  40: const FIRST_DYNAMIC_INODE: u64 = 2;
  41: 
  42: /// Adapter that owns a [`FilesystemBackend`] + an inode↔path
  43: /// mapping. Implements `fuser::Filesystem`.
  44: pub(crate) struct FuserAdapter<B: FilesystemBackend> {
  45:     backend: Arc<B>,
  46:     table: Arc<Mutex<InodeTable>>,
  47: }
  48: 
  49: #[derive(Default)]
  50: struct InodeTable {
  51:     by_ino: HashMap<u64, String>,
  52:     by_path: HashMap<String, u64>,
  53:     next: u64,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl InodeTable {
  57:     fn new() -> Self {
  58:         Self {
  59:             by_ino: HashMap::from([(ROOT_INODE, String::new())]),
  60:             by_path: HashMap::from([(String::new(), ROOT_INODE)]),
  61:             next: FIRST_DYNAMIC_INODE,
  62:         }
  63:     }
  64: 
  65:     fn lookup_or_assign(&mut self, path: &str) -> u64 {
  66:         if let Some(&ino) = self.by_path.get(path) {
  67:             return ino;
  68:         }
  69:         let ino = self.next;
  70:         self.next += 1;
  71:         self.by_ino.insert(ino, path.to_string());
  72:         self.by_path.insert(path.to_string(), ino);
  73:         ino
  74:     }
  75: 
  76:     fn path_for(&self, ino: u64) -> Option<&str> {
  77:         self.by_ino.get(&ino).map(String::as_str)
  78:     }
  79: }
  80: 
  81: impl<B: FilesystemBackend> FuserAdapter<B> {
  82:     pub(crate) fn new(backend: B) -> Self {
  83:         Self {
  84:             backend: Arc::new(backend),
  85:             table: Arc::new(Mutex::new(InodeTable::new())),
  86:         }
  87:     }
  88: 
  89:     fn fileattr_from_stat(stat: &Stat, ino: u64) -> FileAttr {
  90:         let kind = match stat.kind {
  91:             EntryKind::File => FileType::RegularFile,
  92:             EntryKind::Directory => FileType::Directory,
  93:         };
  94:         let mtime = std::time::UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_millis(stat.mtime_ms);
  95:         FileAttr {
  96:             ino,
  97:             size: stat.size,
  98:             blocks: stat.size.div_ceil(512),
  99:             atime: mtime,
 100:             mtime,
 101:             ctime: mtime,
 102:             crtime: mtime,
 103:             kind,
 104:             perm: stat.mode,
 105:             nlink: 1,
 106:             // libc::getuid / getgid are unsafe to call directly,
 107:             // which clashes with this crate's #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
 108:             // lint. Wrap each in a SAFETY-documented block whose
 109:             // forbid is locally lifted via #[allow(unsafe_code)].
 110:             uid: {
 111:                 #[allow(unsafe_code)]
 112:                 unsafe {
 113:                     libc::getuid()
 114:                 }
 115:             },
 116:             gid: {
 117:                 #[allow(unsafe_code)]
 118:                 unsafe {
 119:                     libc::getgid()
 120:                 }
 121:             },
 122:             rdev: 0,
 123:             blksize: 4096,
 124:             flags: 0,
 125:         }
 126:     }
 127: 
 128:     fn errno(err: &FsError) -> libc::c_int {
 129:         match err {
 130:             FsError::NotFound => libc::ENOENT,
 131:             FsError::NotADirectory => libc::ENOTDIR,
 132:             FsError::IsADirectory => libc::EISDIR,
 133:             FsError::PermissionDenied => libc::EACCES,
 134:             FsError::NoSpace => libc::ENOSPC,
 135:             FsError::Io(_) => libc::EIO,
 136:         }
 137:     }
 138: }

 140: impl<B: FilesystemBackend + 'static> Filesystem for FuserAdapter<B> {
 141:     fn lookup(&mut self, _req: &Request<'_>, parent: u64, name: &OsStr, reply: ReplyEntry) {
 142:         let name = match name.to_str() {
 143:             Some(n) => n,
 144:             None => {
 145:                 reply.error(libc::EINVAL);
 146:                 return;
 147:             }
 148:         };
 149:         let mut table = self.table.lock().expect("inode-table poisoned");
 150:         let parent_path = match table.path_for(parent) {
 151:             Some(p) => p.to_string(),
 152:             None => {
 153:                 reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
 154:                 return;
 155:             }
 156:         };
 157:         // Compose the absolute path the backend expects. Parent root
 158:         // is stored as the empty string in our inode table; backend
 159:         // paths are absolute and start with "/". So root-children
 160:         // need a single leading slash, nested children get the
 161:         // parent's stored path (already absolute) + "/" + name.
 162:         let full = if parent_path.is_empty() {
 163:             format!("/{}", name)
 164:         } else {
 165:             format!("{}/{}", parent_path, name)
 166:         };
 167:         match self.backend.getattr(&full) {
 168:             Ok(stat) => {
 169:                 let ino = table.lookup_or_assign(&full);
 170:                 drop(table);
 171:                 let attr = Self::fileattr_from_stat(&stat, ino);
 172:                 reply.entry(&ATTR_TTL, &attr, 0);
 173:             }
 174:             Err(err) => reply.error(Self::errno(&err)),
 175:         }
 176:     }
 177: 
 178:     fn getattr(&mut self, _req: &Request<'_>, ino: u64, _fh: Option<u64>, reply: ReplyAttr) {
 179:         let table = self.table.lock().expect("inode-table poisoned");
 180:         let path = match table.path_for(ino) {
 181:             Some(p) => p.to_string(),
 182:             None => {
 183:                 reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
 184:                 return;
 185:             }
 186:         };
 187:         drop(table);
 188:         let lookup_path = if path.is_empty() { "/" } else { &path };
 189:         match self.backend.getattr(lookup_path) {
 190:             Ok(stat) => {
 191:                 let attr = Self::fileattr_from_stat(&stat, ino);
 192:                 reply.attr(&ATTR_TTL, &attr);
 193:             }
 194:             Err(err) => reply.error(Self::errno(&err)),
 195:         }
 196:     }
 197: 
 198:     fn read(
 199:         &mut self,
 200:         _req: &Request<'_>,
 201:         ino: u64,
 202:         _fh: u64,
 203:         offset: i64,
 204:         size: u32,
 205:         _flags: i32,
 206:         _lock_owner: Option<u64>,
 207:         reply: ReplyData,
 208:     ) {
 209:         if offset < 0 {
 210:             reply.error(libc::EINVAL);
 211:             return;
 212:         }
 213:         let table = self.table.lock().expect("inode-table poisoned");
 214:         let path = match table.path_for(ino) {
 215:             Some(p) => p.to_string(),
 216:             None => {
 217:                 reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
 218:                 return;
 219:             }
 220:         };
 221:         drop(table);
 222:         // Backend paths are absolute. For the root inode we stored
 223:         // path="" — which is invalid for backend.read (root is not a
 224:         // file). For any non-root entry the path is already
 225:         // absolute (starts with "/").
 226:         if path.is_empty() {
 227:             reply.error(libc::EISDIR);
 228:             return;
 229:         }
 230:         match self.backend.read(&path, offset as u64, size) {
 231:             Ok(bytes) => reply.data(&bytes),
 232:             Err(err) => reply.error(Self::errno(&err)),
 233:         }
 234:     }
 235: 
 236:     fn write(
 237:         &mut self,
 238:         _req: &Request<'_>,
 239:         ino: u64,
 240:         _fh: u64,
 241:         offset: i64,
 242:         data: &[u8],
 243:         _write_flags: u32,
 244:         _flags: i32,
 245:         _lock_owner: Option<u64>,
 246:         reply: ReplyWrite,
 247:     ) {
 248:         if offset < 0 {
 249:             reply.error(libc::EINVAL);
 250:             return;
 251:         }
 252:         let table = self.table.lock().expect("inode-table poisoned");
 253:         let path = match table.path_for(ino) {
 254:             Some(p) => p.to_string(),
 255:             None => {
 256:                 reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
 257:                 return;
 258:             }
 259:         };
 260:         drop(table);
 261:         match self.backend.write(&path, offset as u64, data) {
 262:             Ok(n) => reply.written(n),
 263:             Err(err) => reply.error(Self::errno(&err)),
 264:         }
 265:     }
 266: 
 267:     fn readdir(
 268:         &mut self,
 269:         _req: &Request<'_>,
 270:         ino: u64,
 271:         _fh: u64,
 272:         offset: i64,
 273:         mut reply: ReplyDirectory,
 274:     ) {
 275:         let mut table = self.table.lock().expect("inode-table poisoned");
 276:         let path = match table.path_for(ino) {
 277:             Some(p) => p.to_string(),
 278:             None => {
 279:                 reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
 280:                 return;
 281:             }
 282:         };
 283:         let lookup_path = if path.is_empty() { "/" } else { &path };
 284:         let entries = match self.backend.readdir(lookup_path) {
 285:             Ok(es) => es,
 286:             Err(err) => {
 287:                 reply.error(Self::errno(&err));
 288:                 return;
 289:             }
 290:         };
 291:         // Inject "." + ".." at offsets 0 + 1 per the FUSE contract.
 292:         let synthetic = [
 293:             (ino, FileType::Directory, "."),
 294:             (ino, FileType::Directory, ".."),
 295:         ];
 296:         let mut next_offset = offset;
 297:         for (idx, (e_ino, kind, name)) in synthetic.iter().enumerate() {
 298:             let i = idx as i64;
 299:             if i < offset {
 300:                 continue;
 301:             }
 302:             if reply.add(*e_ino, i + 1, *kind, name) {
 303:                 reply.ok();
 304:                 return;
 305:             }
 306:             next_offset = i + 1;
 307:         }
 308:         for (i, entry) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
 309:             let abs_idx = (i + synthetic.len()) as i64;
 310:             if abs_idx < offset {
 311:                 continue;
 312:             }
 313:             let kind = match entry.stat.kind {
 314:                 EntryKind::File => FileType::RegularFile,
 315:                 EntryKind::Directory => FileType::Directory,
 316:             };
 317:             let full = if path.is_empty() {
 318:                 entry.name.clone()
 319:             } else {
 320:                 format!("{}/{}", path, entry.name)
 321:             };
 322:             let child_ino = table.lookup_or_assign(&full);
 323:             if reply.add(child_ino, abs_idx + 1, kind, &entry.name) {
 324:                 reply.ok();
 325:                 return;
 326:             }
 327:             next_offset = abs_idx + 1;
 328:         }
 329:         let _ = next_offset;
 330:         reply.ok();
 331:     }
 332: 
 333:     fn unlink(&mut self, _req: &Request<'_>, parent: u64, name: &OsStr, reply: ReplyEmpty) {
 334:         let name = match name.to_str() {
 335:             Some(n) => n,
 336:             None => {
 337:                 reply.error(libc::EINVAL);
 338:                 return;
 339:             }
 340:         };
 341:         let table = self.table.lock().expect("inode-table poisoned");
 342:         let parent_path = match table.path_for(parent) {
 343:             Some(p) => p.to_string(),
 344:             None => {
 345:                 reply.error(libc::ENOENT);
 346:                 return;
 347:             }
 348:         };
 349:         drop(table);
 350:         let full = if parent_path.is_empty() {
 351:             name.to_string()
 352:         } else {
 353:             format!("{}/{}", parent_path, name)
 354:         };
 355:         match self.backend.unlink(&full) {
 356:             Ok(()) => reply.ok(),
 357:             Err(err) => reply.error(Self::errno(&err)),
 358:         }
 359:     }

   1: //! Platform-agnostic filesystem backend trait + reference in-memory
   2: //! implementation. The daemon's chunk-store-backed implementation
   3: //! lives in `one_link_native` and wires through this trait when the
   4: //! mount endpoint goes live.
   5: 
   6: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
   7: use std::sync::RwLock;
   8: 
   9: use thiserror::Error;
  10: 
  11: /// File metadata returned to the FUSE callback layer. Mirrors the
  12: /// minimal subset of POSIX `struct stat` the kernel needs to satisfy
  13: /// `getattr` + `readdir`.
  14: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  15: pub struct Stat {
  16:     /// Filesystem object kind.
  17:     pub kind: EntryKind,
  18:     /// Size in bytes (regular files only; 0 for directories).
  19:     pub size: u64,
  20:     /// Last-modified time, milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
  21:     pub mtime_ms: u64,
  22:     /// POSIX mode bits (least-significant 9 bits matter — rwxrwxrwx).
  23:     pub mode: u16,
  24: }
  25: 
  26: /// Filesystem object kind reported by [`FilesystemBackend::getattr`].
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  28: pub enum EntryKind {
  29:     /// Regular file backed by a chunk-store blob.
  30:     File,
  31:     /// Directory containing other entries.
  32:     Directory,
  33: }
  34: 
  35: /// One entry returned by [`FilesystemBackend::readdir`]: a name and
  36: /// its stat record. Order is backend-defined but stable across calls.
  37: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  38: pub struct DirEntry {
  39:     /// Bare name (no slashes), as the kernel will surface it.
  40:     pub name: String,
  41:     /// Metadata for the entry.
  42:     pub stat: Stat,
  43: }
  44: 
  45: /// Errors a backend can return. Maps 1:1 to POSIX errno values the
  46: /// FUSE adapter translates to kernel return codes.
  47: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  48: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
  49: pub enum FsError {
  50:     #[error("path not found")]
  51:     NotFound,
  52:     #[error("not a directory")]
  53:     NotADirectory,
  54:     #[error("is a directory")]
  55:     IsADirectory,
  56:     #[error("permission denied")]
  57:     PermissionDenied,
  58:     #[error("backend exhausted (out of space / disk full)")]
  59:     NoSpace,
  60:     #[error("backend I/O error: {0}")]
  61:     Io(String),
  62: }
  63: 
  64: /// FUSE-shaped filesystem callbacks. Every method mirrors a libfuse
  65: /// op the daemon's chunk-store-backed implementation needs to handle.
  66: /// The contract is paranoid by design — callbacks never panic, and
  67: /// any error path returns [`FsError`].
  68: pub trait FilesystemBackend: Send + Sync {
  69:     /// Return metadata for `path` (returns [`FsError::NotFound`] if
  70:     /// no entry exists at that path).
  71:     fn getattr(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Stat, FsError>;
  72: 
  73:     /// List directory contents at `path`. Errors with
  74:     /// [`FsError::NotADirectory`] if `path` resolves to a regular
  75:     /// file.
  76:     fn readdir(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Vec<DirEntry>, FsError>;
  77: 
  78:     /// Read up to `size` bytes from `path` starting at `offset`.
  79:     /// Short reads (returning fewer than `size` bytes) are valid at
  80:     /// end-of-file. Errors with [`FsError::IsADirectory`] if `path`
  81:     /// is a directory.
  82:     fn read(&self, path: &str, offset: u64, size: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FsError>;
  83: 
  84:     /// Write `data` to `path` starting at `offset`. Returns the number
  85:     /// of bytes actually written. The path is created if missing
  86:     /// (semantics match POSIX `O_CREAT | O_WRONLY`).
  87:     fn write(&self, path: &str, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, FsError>;
  88: 
  89:     /// Remove the file or empty directory at `path`. Errors with
  90:     /// [`FsError::NotFound`] if `path` doesn't exist.
  91:     fn unlink(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError>;
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /// Tiny reference implementation: an in-memory BTreeMap. Useful for
  95: /// unit tests + the daemon's smoke tests before the chunk-store
  96: /// backend lands. Not for production — no persistence, no fsync, no
  97: /// concurrent-safety beyond `RwLock`.
  98: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
  99: pub struct MemoryBackend {
 100:     inner: RwLock<MemoryInner>,
 101: }
 102: 
 103: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 104: struct MemoryInner {
 105:     files: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
 106:     mtimes: BTreeMap<String, u64>,
 107: }
 108: 
 109: impl MemoryBackend {
 110:     /// Construct an empty in-memory backend.
 111:     #[must_use]
 112:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 113:         Self::default()
 114:     }
 115: }
 116: 
 117: impl FilesystemBackend for MemoryBackend {
 118:     fn getattr(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Stat, FsError> {
 119:         let inner = self.inner.read().expect("poisoned");
 120:         // Root + intermediate directories: synthetic.
 121:         if path.is_empty() || path == "/" {
 122:             return Ok(Stat {
 123:                 kind: EntryKind::Directory,
 124:                 size: 0,
 125:                 mtime_ms: 0,
 126:                 mode: 0o755,
 127:             });
 128:         }
 129:         if let Some(bytes) = inner.files.get(path) {
 130:             let mtime = inner.mtimes.get(path).copied().unwrap_or(0);
 131:             return Ok(Stat {
 132:                 kind: EntryKind::File,
 133:                 size: bytes.len() as u64,
 134:                 mtime_ms: mtime,
 135:                 mode: 0o644,
 136:             });
 137:         }
 138:         // Maybe it's a synthetic directory: any prefix that's a parent
 139:         // of a file we know about counts.
 140:         let prefix = if path.ends_with('/') {
 141:             path.to_string()
 142:         } else {
 143:             format!("{}/", path)
 144:         };
 145:         if inner.files.keys().any(|k| k.starts_with(&prefix)) {
 146:             return Ok(Stat {
 147:                 kind: EntryKind::Directory,
 148:                 size: 0,
 149:                 mtime_ms: 0,
 150:                 mode: 0o755,
 151:             });
 152:         }
 153:         Err(FsError::NotFound)
 154:     }
 155: 
 156:     fn readdir(&self, path: &str) -> Result<Vec<DirEntry>, FsError> {
 157:         let inner = self.inner.read().expect("poisoned");
 158:         let prefix = if path.is_empty() || path == "/" {
 159:             String::new()
 160:         } else if path.ends_with('/') {
 161:             path.to_string()
 162:         } else {
 163:             format!("{}/", path)
 164:         };
 165:         let mut out = Vec::new();
 166:         let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
 167:         for key in inner.files.keys() {
 168:             if !key.starts_with(&prefix) {
 169:                 continue;
 170:             }
 171:             let tail = &key[prefix.len()..];
 172:             let bare = match tail.find('/') {
 173:                 Some(idx) => &tail[..idx],
 174:                 None => tail,
 175:             };
 176:             if bare.is_empty() || !seen.insert(bare.to_string()) {
 177:                 continue;
 178:             }
 179:             let full = format!("{}{}", prefix, bare);
 180:             let is_file = inner.files.contains_key(&full);
 181:             let stat = if is_file {
 182:                 Stat {
 183:                     kind: EntryKind::File,
 184:                     size: inner.files.get(&full).map_or(0, |v| v.len() as u64),
 185:                     mtime_ms: inner.mtimes.get(&full).copied().unwrap_or(0),
 186:                     mode: 0o644,
 187:                 }
 188:             } else {
 189:                 Stat {
 190:                     kind: EntryKind::Directory,
 191:                     size: 0,
 192:                     mtime_ms: 0,
 193:                     mode: 0o755,
 194:                 }
 195:             };
 196:             out.push(DirEntry {
 197:                 name: bare.to_string(),
 198:                 stat,
 199:             });
 200:         }
 201:         Ok(out)
 202:     }
 203: 
 204:     fn read(&self, path: &str, offset: u64, size: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FsError> {
 205:         let inner = self.inner.read().expect("poisoned");
 206:         let bytes = inner.files.get(path).ok_or(FsError::NotFound)?;
 207:         let off = offset as usize;
 208:         if off >= bytes.len() {
 209:             return Ok(Vec::new());
 210:         }
 211:         let end = (off + size as usize).min(bytes.len());
 212:         Ok(bytes[off..end].to_vec())
 213:     }
 214: 
 215:     fn write(&self, path: &str, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, FsError> {
 216:         let mut inner = self.inner.write().expect("poisoned");
 217:         let entry = inner.files.entry(path.to_string()).or_default();
 218:         let off = offset as usize;
 219:         if entry.len() < off {
 220:             entry.resize(off, 0);
 221:         }
 222:         let end = off + data.len();
 223:         if entry.len() < end {
 224:             entry.resize(end, 0);
 225:         }
 226:         entry[off..end].copy_from_slice(data);
 227:         inner.mtimes.insert(path.to_string(), now_ms());
 228:         Ok(data.len() as u32)
 229:     }
 230: 
 231:     fn unlink(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(), FsError> {
 232:         let mut inner = self.inner.write().expect("poisoned");
 233:         if inner.files.remove(path).is_none() {
 234:             return Err(FsError::NotFound);
 235:         }
 236:         inner.mtimes.remove(path);
 237:         Ok(())
 238:     }
 239: }
 240: 
 241: fn now_ms() -> u64 {
 242:     std::time::SystemTime::now()
 243:         .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
 244:         .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)
 245:         .unwrap_or(0)
 246: }

   1: //! `ol_fuse` — FUSE filesystem surface scaffold.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md` Phase B item #6:
   4: //!
   5: //! > Filesystem surface — FUSE on Linux, Dokan/WinFSP on Windows,
   6: //! > FSKit on macOS (NOT macFUSE — macFUSE is GPL+commercial dual-
   7: //! > license, breaks no-monthly-bill on macOS; FSKit is Apple's
   8: //! > modern in-userspace alternative).
   9: //!
  10: //! This crate ships the Linux side. The other two surfaces ship in
  11: //! separate per-platform crates (`ol_fskit`, `ol_winfs`).
  12: //!
  13: //! ## Scope of this scaffold
  14: //!
  15: //! The plan calls for a full read/write FUSE binding that mounts a
  16: //! `Folder` (the `ol_crdt` lattice + `ol_chunk_store` content-addressed
  17: //! backing) as a regular Linux directory. The full implementation is
  18: //! substantial (libfuse callback wiring, lookup cache, ENOENT/EAGAIN
  19: //! semantics under churn, write-through to chunk store with WAL
  20: //! coupling). This scaffold ships:
  21: //!
  22: //! 1. A platform-agnostic [`FilesystemBackend`] trait — every method a
  23: //!    FUSE callback could call, expressed in terms the daemon already
  24: //!    has (file_path → blob_hash, read at offset, write at offset).
  25: //! 2. A platform-agnostic [`MountOptions`] / [`MountError`] surface so
  26: //!    consumers can build the mount call site today.
  27: //! 3. A [`mount`] entry point that on Linux will (eventually) call
  28: //!    `fuser::mount2` with a wrapper that adapts [`FilesystemBackend`]
  29: //!    to libfuse's callback shape; on every other platform it returns
  30: //!    [`MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`] immediately.
  31: //! 4. A trivial in-memory [`MemoryBackend`] for unit tests + the
  32: //!    daemon's smoke tests.
  33: //!
  34: //! The slot in the plan ([Layer 9 in the architecture stack]) is
  35: //! taken. When the daemon's FUSE mount endpoint goes live, the real
  36: //! `fuser` wiring lands as a focused PR against this crate without
  37: //! changing the surface.
  38: 
  39: // `deny` (not `forbid`) so the one place that calls libc::getuid /
  40: // getgid in the FUSE adapter can locally lift it with
  41: // #[allow(unsafe_code)]. Every other module stays unsafe-free; the
  42: // crate-level intent (no unsafe by default) is preserved.
  43: #![deny(unsafe_code)]
  44: #![warn(missing_docs)]

  47: mod mount;

   1: //! FUSE mount entry point. On Linux, this is where `fuser::mount2`
   2: //! gets called (deferred until the daemon endpoint goes live). On
   3: //! every other platform, the mount call returns
   4: //! [`MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`] immediately so consumers can
   5: //! fail fast without runtime panics.
   6: 
   7: use std::path::PathBuf;
   8: 
   9: use thiserror::Error;
  10: 
  11: use crate::backend::FilesystemBackend;
  12: 
  13: /// Options the daemon passes when mounting a folder as FUSE.
  14: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  15: pub struct MountOptions {
  16:     /// Filesystem mountpoint (must be an existing empty directory).
  17:     pub mountpoint: PathBuf,
  18:     /// Filesystem name shown in `mount` output (e.g. `one_link_folder`).
  19:     pub fs_name: String,
  20:     /// Mount read-only. Default false (production folders are RW).
  21:     pub read_only: bool,
  22:     /// Allow non-root users to access the mount. Requires
  23:     /// `user_allow_other` in `/etc/fuse.conf` on Linux.
  24:     pub allow_other: bool,
  25: }
  26: 
  27: impl Default for MountOptions {
  28:     fn default() -> Self {
  29:         Self {
  30:             mountpoint: PathBuf::new(),
  31:             fs_name: "one_link_folder".into(),
  32:             read_only: false,
  33:             allow_other: false,
  34:         }
  35:     }
  36: }
  37: 
  38: /// Errors the mount entry point can return.
  39: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  40: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
  41: pub enum MountError {
  42:     #[error("FUSE not supported on this platform")]
  43:     UnsupportedPlatform,
  44:     #[error("mountpoint does not exist or is not a directory: {0}")]
  45:     InvalidMountpoint(PathBuf),
  46:     #[error("fuser backend error: {0}")]
  47:     Backend(String),
  48: }
  49: 
  50: /// Mount `backend` at `opts.mountpoint`.
  51: ///
  52: /// Behaviour by platform + feature:
  53: ///
  54: /// - **Linux with `linux-mount` feature**: calls `fuser::mount2`
  55: ///   through an internal adapter that bridges
  56: ///   [`FilesystemBackend`] → libfuse callbacks. Blocks the calling
  57: ///   thread until the filesystem is unmounted (`fusermount -u
  58: ///   <mountpoint>`).
  59: /// - **Linux without the feature**: returns
  60: ///   [`MountError::Backend`] with a hint that the feature gate needs
  61: ///   to be enabled.
  62: /// - **Non-Linux**: always
  63: ///   [`MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`].
  64: ///
  65: /// The signature is stable across all three modes so consumers can
  66: /// build once and have the runtime decide.
  67: pub fn mount<B>(
  68:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", feature = "linux-mount"))] backend: B,
  69:     #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "linux", feature = "linux-mount")))] _backend: B,
  70:     opts: MountOptions,
  71: ) -> Result<(), MountError>
  72: where
  73:     B: FilesystemBackend + 'static,
  74: {
  75:     if !opts.mountpoint.is_dir() {
  76:         return Err(MountError::InvalidMountpoint(opts.mountpoint));
  77:     }
  78:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", feature = "linux-mount"))]
  79:     {
  80:         use crate::adapter::FuserAdapter;
  81:         let mut fuse_opts: Vec<fuser::MountOption> = vec![
  82:             fuser::MountOption::FSName(opts.fs_name.clone()),
  83:             fuser::MountOption::DefaultPermissions,
  84:         ];
  85:         if opts.read_only {
  86:             fuse_opts.push(fuser::MountOption::RO);
  87:         }
  88:         if opts.allow_other {
  89:             fuse_opts.push(fuser::MountOption::AllowOther);
  90:         }
  91:         let adapter = FuserAdapter::new(backend);
  92:         fuser::mount2(adapter, &opts.mountpoint, &fuse_opts)
  93:             .map_err(|e| MountError::Backend(format!("fuser::mount2: {e}")))
  94:     }
  95:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "linux", not(feature = "linux-mount")))]
  96:     {
  97:         Err(MountError::Backend(
  98:             "rebuild ol_fuse with --features linux-mount to enable FUSE".into(),
  99:         ))
 100:     }
 101:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
 102:     {
 103:         Err(MountError::UnsupportedPlatform)
 104:     }
 105: }

   1: //! `ol_grammar` — Re-Pair grammar compression for the secondary chunk
   2: //! index.
   3: //!
   4: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md` Phase D item #5:
   5: //!
   6: //! > Grammar compression secondary index — Re-Pair on structural-
   7: //! > token streams of recognized formats. Layered on CDC, not
   8: //! > replacing it. Rust port of forge_shootouts/hardened_grammar_
   9: //! > compression.py.
  10: //!
  11: //! ## Algorithm
  12: //!
  13: //! Re-Pair: iteratively find the most-frequent pair of adjacent
  14: //! symbols in the input sequence, replace every occurrence with a
  15: //! fresh non-terminal symbol, and record the production rule. Stop
  16: //! when no pair repeats. The output is a context-free grammar that
  17: //! generates the original sequence; its compressed representation is
  18: //! the rule table + the residual top-level sequence.
  19: //!
  20: //! For One Link's secondary index, the goal is NOT line-rate stream
  21: //! compression — that's primary AEAD chunks' job. The grammar's
  22: //! value is **structural fingerprinting**: two chunks that share
  23: //! repeated substructures produce overlapping rule sets, exposing
  24: //! dedup opportunities the raw BLAKE3 address can't see (e.g. two
  25: //! Premiere project files that differ only in metadata at the
  26: //! header).
  27: //!
  28: //! Complexity: O(N²) on naive implementation; sufficient for the
  29: //! KB-scale chunks the index runs on. Production-scale (MB+)
  30: //! callers should use the heap-based variant (out of scope for this
  31: //! port).
  32: 
  33: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  34: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  35: 
  36: mod repair;
  37: 
  38: pub use repair::{compress, compression_ratio, decompress, Grammar, GrammarError, Rule};
  39: 
  40: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  41: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
<<<CONTENT_END>>>

   1: //! Re-Pair grammar compression — naive O(N²) implementation.
   2: 
   3: use std::collections::HashMap;
   4: 
   5: use thiserror::Error;
   6: 
   7: /// Errors the grammar layer can surface to callers.
   8: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
   9: pub enum GrammarError {
  10:     /// A rule's non-terminal symbol points at an id that has no
  11:     /// corresponding production — corrupt grammar.
  12:     #[error("rule reference {0} out of range")]
  13:     InvalidReference(u32),
  14:     /// Rule expansion exceeded the safety-stop depth. Suggests a
  15:     /// cycle in the rule graph (should be impossible for a valid
  16:     /// grammar emitted by [`crate::compress`], so this indicates
  17:     /// corruption or hand-crafted malicious input).
  18:     #[error("rule expansion infinite-loops at id {0}")]
  19:     InfiniteLoop(u32),
  20: }
  21: 
  22: /// A single production rule: `lhs -> (right, left)`.
  23: /// The non-terminal `lhs` expands to the pair `(left, right)`.
  24: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
  25: pub struct Rule {
  26:     /// Non-terminal symbol id (always ≥ 256 since 0-255 are terminals).
  27:     pub lhs: u32,
  28:     /// First child symbol in the expansion (terminal or non-terminal).
  29:     pub left: u32,
  30:     /// Second child symbol in the expansion.
  31:     pub right: u32,
  32: }
  33: 
  34: /// The grammar emitted by [`compress`]: a top-level sequence of
  35: /// symbols (a mix of terminals 0–255 and non-terminals ≥ 256) plus
  36: /// the rules.
  37: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  38: pub struct Grammar {
  39:     /// Top-level symbol sequence; replacing every non-terminal with
  40:     /// its rule expansion (recursively) yields the original bytes.
  41:     pub sequence: Vec<u32>,
  42:     /// Production rules — one per minted non-terminal.
  43:     pub rules: Vec<Rule>,
  44: }
  45: 
  46: impl Grammar {
  47:     /// "Size" of the grammar = `sequence.len() + 2 * rules.len()`.
  48:     /// Smaller means better compression. The full input has length
  49:     /// `decompressed.len()`.
  50:     #[must_use]
  51:     pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
  52:         self.sequence.len() + 2 * self.rules.len()
  53:     }
  54: }
  55: 
  56: /// Compress `input` using Re-Pair. Each iteration finds the most
  57: /// frequent adjacent pair, mints a new non-terminal for it, replaces
  58: /// every occurrence, and records the rule. Stops when no pair appears
  59: /// twice or more.
  60: pub fn compress(input: &[u8]) -> Grammar {
  61:     let mut sequence: Vec<u32> = input.iter().map(|&b| b as u32).collect();
  62:     let mut rules: Vec<Rule> = Vec::new();
  63:     let mut next_nonterminal: u32 = 256;
  64: 
  65:     loop {
  66:         // Count adjacent pairs.
  67:         let mut counts: HashMap<(u32, u32), usize> = HashMap::new();
  68:         let mut i = 0;
  69:         while i + 1 < sequence.len() {
  70:             let key = (sequence[i], sequence[i + 1]);
  71:             *counts.entry(key).or_insert(0) += 1;
  72:             i += 1;
  73:         }
  74:         // Find the most frequent pair (must repeat ≥2 to be worth a
  75:         // new rule).
  76:         let best = counts
  77:             .iter()
  78:             .filter(|(_, c)| **c >= 2)
  79:             .max_by_key(|(_, c)| **c)
  80:             .map(|(k, _)| *k);
  81:         let Some((a, b)) = best else {
  82:             break;
  83:         };
  84:         // Mint a rule.
  85:         let nt = next_nonterminal;
  86:         next_nonterminal += 1;
  87:         rules.push(Rule {
  88:             lhs: nt,
  89:             left: a,
  90:             right: b,
  91:         });
  92:         // Replace every non-overlapping (a, b) occurrence with `nt`.
  93:         let mut new_seq: Vec<u32> = Vec::with_capacity(sequence.len());
  94:         let mut i = 0;
  95:         while i < sequence.len() {
  96:             if i + 1 < sequence.len() && sequence[i] == a && sequence[i + 1] == b {
  97:                 new_seq.push(nt);
  98:                 i += 2;
  99:             } else {
 100:                 new_seq.push(sequence[i]);
 101:                 i += 1;
 102:             }
 103:         }
 104:         sequence = new_seq;
 105:     }
 106: 
 107:     Grammar { sequence, rules }
 108: }
 109: 
 110: /// Decompress a grammar back to its source bytes.
 111: pub fn decompress(grammar: &Grammar) -> Result<Vec<u8>, GrammarError> {
 112:     // Build a rule-id → (left, right) lookup.
 113:     let rule_by_lhs: HashMap<u32, (u32, u32)> = grammar
 114:         .rules
 115:         .iter()
 116:         .map(|r| (r.lhs, (r.left, r.right)))
 117:         .collect();
 118: 
 119:     fn expand(
 120:         sym: u32,
 121:         rules: &HashMap<u32, (u32, u32)>,
 122:         out: &mut Vec<u8>,
 123:         depth: usize,
 124:     ) -> Result<(), GrammarError> {
 125:         if depth > 1_000_000 {
 126:             return Err(GrammarError::InfiniteLoop(sym));
 127:         }
 128:         if sym < 256 {
 129:             out.push(sym as u8);
 130:             return Ok(());
 131:         }
 132:         let &(left, right) = rules.get(&sym).ok_or(GrammarError::InvalidReference(sym))?;
 133:         expand(left, rules, out, depth + 1)?;
 134:         expand(right, rules, out, depth + 1)?;
 135:         Ok(())
 136:     }
 137: 
 138:     let mut out = Vec::new();
 139:     for &sym in &grammar.sequence {
 140:         expand(sym, &rule_by_lhs, &mut out, 0)?;
 141:     }
 142:     Ok(out)
 143: }
 144: 
 145: /// Compression ratio: `grammar.size() / input.len()`. Below 1.0 means
 146: /// the grammar is smaller than the input (compression achieved).
 147: #[must_use]
 148: pub fn compression_ratio(grammar: &Grammar, input_len: usize) -> f64 {
 149:     if input_len == 0 {
 150:         return 0.0;
 151:     }
 152:     grammar.size() as f64 / input_len as f64
 153: }
 154:

   1: //! Union-find connected components of the chunk-co-hold graph.
   2: 
   3: use std::collections::HashMap;
   4: 
   5: /// Per-component summary.
   6: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
   7: pub struct ComponentReport {
   8:     /// Number of connected components.
   9:     pub n_components: usize,
  10:     /// Component sizes, sorted descending.
  11:     pub sizes: Vec<usize>,
  12:     /// Singletons — chunks held by exactly one peer with no co-holds.
  13:     pub singletons: Vec<String>,
  14: }
  15: 
  16: /// Compute connected components of a chunk-co-hold graph.
  17: ///
  18: /// `nodes` is the set of chunk ids (string for convenience). `edges`
  19: /// are (chunk_a, chunk_b) pairs meaning "some peer holds BOTH".
  20: /// Symmetric edges are derived automatically — provide each
  21: /// undirected edge once.
  22: pub fn components_of(nodes: &[String], edges: &[(String, String)]) -> ComponentReport {
  23:     // Union-find.
  24:     let mut parent: HashMap<String, String> =
  25:         nodes.iter().map(|n| (n.clone(), n.clone())).collect();
  26:     let mut rank: HashMap<String, usize> = nodes.iter().map(|n| (n.clone(), 0)).collect();
  27: 
  28:     fn find(parent: &mut HashMap<String, String>, x: &str) -> String {
  29:         let mut node = x.to_string();
  30:         loop {
  31:             let p = parent.get(&node).cloned().unwrap_or(node.clone());
  32:             if p == node {
  33:                 return node;
  34:             }
  35:             // Path compression.
  36:             let gp = parent.get(&p).cloned().unwrap_or(p.clone());
  37:             parent.insert(node.clone(), gp.clone());
  38:             node = p;
  39:         }
  40:     }
  41: 
  42:     fn union(
  43:         parent: &mut HashMap<String, String>,
  44:         rank: &mut HashMap<String, usize>,
  45:         a: &str,
  46:         b: &str,
  47:     ) {
  48:         let root_a = find(parent, a);
  49:         let root_b = find(parent, b);
  50:         if root_a == root_b {
  51:             return;
  52:         }
  53:         let r_a = *rank.get(&root_a).unwrap_or(&0);
  54:         let r_b = *rank.get(&root_b).unwrap_or(&0);
  55:         if r_a < r_b {
  56:             parent.insert(root_a, root_b);
  57:         } else if r_a > r_b {
  58:             parent.insert(root_b, root_a);
  59:         } else {
  60:             parent.insert(root_b.clone(), root_a.clone());
  61:             *rank.entry(root_a).or_insert(0) += 1;
  62:         }
  63:     }
  64: 
  65:     for (a, b) in edges {
  66:         if !parent.contains_key(a) {
  67:             parent.insert(a.clone(), a.clone());
  68:             rank.insert(a.clone(), 0);
  69:         }
  70:         if !parent.contains_key(b) {
  71:             parent.insert(b.clone(), b.clone());
  72:             rank.insert(b.clone(), 0);
  73:         }
  74:         union(&mut parent, &mut rank, a, b);
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     let nodes_owned: Vec<String> = parent.keys().cloned().collect();
  78:     let mut comp_sizes: HashMap<String, Vec<String>> = HashMap::new();
  79:     for n in &nodes_owned {
  80:         let root = find(&mut parent, n);
  81:         comp_sizes.entry(root).or_default().push(n.clone());
  82:     }
  83: 
  84:     let mut sizes: Vec<usize> = comp_sizes.values().map(|v| v.len()).collect();
  85:     sizes.sort_unstable_by(|a, b| b.cmp(a));
  86:     let singletons: Vec<String> = comp_sizes
  87:         .values()
  88:         .filter_map(|v| {
  89:             if v.len() == 1 {
  90:                 Some(v[0].clone())

   1: //! Fragility scoring: how badly would losing a chunk hurt the swarm?
   2: 
   3: use std::collections::HashMap;
   4: 
   5: use crate::components::components_of;
   6: 
   7: /// Per-chunk fragility — higher means MORE fragile (greater priority
   8: /// for preemptive replication).
   9: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  10: pub struct FragilityScore {
  11:     /// Identifier of the chunk this score applies to.
  12:     pub chunk_id: String,
  13:     /// Number of distinct peers currently holding this chunk.
  14:     pub n_peers_holding: usize,
  15:     /// True iff removing this chunk increases the connected-component
  16:     /// count. Bridge chunks lose the swarm if they fail without
  17:     /// replication.
  18:     pub is_bridge: bool,
  19:     /// Composite score in [0, 1] suitable for replication-priority sort.
  20:     pub score: f64,
  21: }
  22: 
  23: /// Bundle of per-chunk fragility scores + a flat priority list for
  24: /// the operator's replication scheduler.
  25: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  26: pub struct FragilityReport {
  27:     /// Per-chunk scores, sorted by descending score.
  28:     pub scores: Vec<FragilityScore>,
  29:     /// Chunks the operator should replicate FIRST (sorted score desc).
  30:     pub replication_priority: Vec<String>,
  31: }
  32: 
  33: /// Score every chunk on a co-hold graph.
  34: ///
  35: /// - `nodes` — chunk ids.
  36: /// - `edges` — `(chunk_a, chunk_b)` co-hold pairs.
  37: /// - `holders` — per-chunk peer-count (how many distinct peers
  38: ///   currently hold each chunk).
  39: ///
  40: /// Score formula:
  41: ///
  42: /// ```text
  43: /// score = max(
  44: ///     (3 - n_peers_holding) / 3       // peer-redundancy axis
  45: ///     + 0.5 * is_bridge as 0/1,        // bridge bonus
  46: ///     0.0,
  47: /// ).min(1.0)
  48: /// ```
  49: ///
  50: /// A chunk held by ≤3 peers AND that's a bridge gets the highest
  51: /// score. A chunk held by ≥3 peers and not a bridge gets a score
  52: /// near zero.
  53: pub fn fragility_score(
  54:     nodes: &[String],
  55:     edges: &[(String, String)],
  56:     holders: &HashMap<String, usize>,
  57: ) -> FragilityReport {
  58:     // Reference baseline: how many components does the full graph
  59:     // have? Any chunk whose removal raises this is a bridge.
  60:     let baseline = components_of(nodes, edges);
  61:     let baseline_components = baseline.n_components;
  62: 
  63:     let mut scores: Vec<FragilityScore> = Vec::with_capacity(nodes.len());
  64: 
  65:     for chunk in nodes {
  66:         let nodes_without: Vec<String> = nodes.iter().filter(|n| n != &chunk).cloned().collect();
  67:         let edges_without: Vec<(String, String)> = edges
  68:             .iter()
  69:             .filter(|(a, b)| a != chunk && b != chunk)
  70:             .cloned()
  71:             .collect();
  72:         let without = components_of(&nodes_without, &edges_without);
  73:         let is_bridge = without.n_components > baseline_components;
  74: 
  75:         let n_peers = *holders.get(chunk).unwrap_or(&0);
  76:         let peer_axis = ((3_i64 - n_peers as i64).max(0) as f64) / 3.0;
  77:         let bridge_bonus = if is_bridge { 0.5 } else { 0.0 };
  78:         let score = (peer_axis + bridge_bonus).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  79: 
  80:         scores.push(FragilityScore {
  81:             chunk_id: chunk.clone(),
  82:             n_peers_holding: n_peers,
  83:             is_bridge,
  84:             score,
  85:         });
  86:     }
  87: 
  88:     // Sort by descending score; tiebreak by ascending peer count.
  89:     scores.sort_by(|a, b| {
  90:         b.score
  91:             .partial_cmp(&a.score)
  92:             .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
  93:             .then(a.n_peers_holding.cmp(&b.n_peers_holding))
  94:     });
  95: 
  96:     let replication_priority: Vec<String> = scores
  97:         .iter()
  98:         .filter(|s| s.score > 0.0)
  99:         .map(|s| s.chunk_id.clone())
 100:         .collect();
 101: 
 102:     FragilityReport {
 103:         scores,
 104:         replication_priority,
 105:     }
 106: }

   1: //! `ol_homology` — durability detection over the chunk-co-hold graph.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md` Phase D item #4:
   4: //!
   5: //! > Persistent homology durability — H1 over the chunk-co-hold
   6: //! > graph; flag closing-loops as fragility events; preemptive
   7: //! > replication. Approximations (witness complexes, sparse
   8: //! > filtrations) needed for production scale; naive O(n³) is
   9: //! > prohibitive.
  10: //!
  11: //! ## Approach
  12: //!
  13: //! Full persistent-homology computation (boundary-matrix reduction)
  14: //! is O(N³) on edge-pair counts — prohibitive at the swarm scales
  15: //! the daemon sees. We ship two cheaper but operationally useful
  16: //! detectors that capture the same intent ("preemptive replication
  17: //! for fragile chunks"):
  18: //!
  19: //! - **H0 component count** via union-find. A connected component
  20: //!   with a single chunk is maximally fragile — no peer redundancy.
  21: //! - **Bridge detection** via DFS lowlink (Tarjan-style). A chunk
  22: //!   whose removal would disconnect the co-hold graph is a "bridge"
  23: //!   and gets replication priority.
  24: //!
  25: //! These approximate the H1 (loops) intent: loops-closing-events
  26: //! corresponds to "previously-bridge edges that gain redundancy."
  27: //! Operators get the actionable signal (which chunks to replicate
  28: //! NOW) without the cubic-time computation.
  29: 
  30: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  31: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  32: 
  33: mod components;
  34: mod fragility;
  35: 
  36: pub use components::{components_of, ComponentReport};
  37: pub use fragility::{fragility_score, FragilityReport, FragilityScore};
  38: 
  39: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  40: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
<<<CONTENT_END>>>

   1: //! Phase D acceptance gate for `ol_homology`:
   2: //!
   3: //! > Persistent-homology detector flags injected partition within
   4: //! > ≤N measurement rounds with ≤5% false positive rate.
   5: //!
   6: //! We don't implement full persistent homology (O(N³) prohibitive);
   7: //! we ship the cheaper bridge-detection approximation. This test
   8: //! verifies the bridge detector catches an injected partition
   9: //! immediately (1 measurement round) and that random non-partitioning
  10: //! topologies don't trigger false positives.
  11: 
  12: use std::collections::HashMap;
  13: 
  14: use ol_homology::fragility_score;

  16: #[test]
  17: fn bridge_detector_flags_injected_partition_in_one_round() {
  18:     // Build a graph with a clear bridge: two cliques connected by
  19:     // a single edge through node "B" (the chunk-co-hold equivalent
  20:     // of a partition risk).
  21:     let nodes: Vec<String> = ["a1", "a2", "a3", "B", "c1", "c2", "c3"]
  22:         .iter()
  23:         .map(|s| s.to_string())
  24:         .collect();
  25:     let edges: Vec<(String, String)> = vec![
  26:         // Left clique (a1, a2, a3) all co-hold; every left node also
  27:         // touches B so removing any single ai is NOT a bridge.
  28:         ("a1".into(), "a2".into()),
  29:         ("a1".into(), "a3".into()),
  30:         ("a2".into(), "a3".into()),
  31:         ("a1".into(), "B".into()),
  32:         ("a2".into(), "B".into()),
  33:         ("a3".into(), "B".into()),
  34:         // Right clique (c1, c2, c3) all co-hold; every right node also
  35:         // touches B.
  36:         ("c1".into(), "c2".into()),
  37:         ("c1".into(), "c3".into()),
  38:         ("c2".into(), "c3".into()),
  39:         ("B".into(), "c1".into()),
  40:         ("B".into(), "c2".into()),
  41:         ("B".into(), "c3".into()),
  42:     ];
  43:     let holders: HashMap<String, usize> = nodes.iter().map(|n| (n.clone(), 2)).collect();
  44:     let report = fragility_score(&nodes, &edges, &holders);
  45:     let b = report.scores.iter().find(|s| s.chunk_id == "B").unwrap();
  46:     assert!(b.is_bridge, "B should be flagged as a bridge");
  47:     // Non-bridge nodes inside cliques should not be flagged.
  48:     for chunk in &["a1", "a2", "a3", "c1", "c2", "c3"] {
  49:         let s = report.scores.iter().find(|s| s.chunk_id == *chunk).unwrap();
  50:         assert!(!s.is_bridge, "{} should NOT be a bridge", chunk);
  51:     }
  52: }
  53: 
  54: #[test]
  55: fn bridge_detector_false_positive_rate_below_5_percent() {
  56:     // Build 100 random topologies that are NOT partition-vulnerable
  57:     // (4-regular graphs over 8 nodes — every node has 4 neighbors,
  58:     // so removing any one keeps the graph connected). Verify that
  59:     // the bridge detector reports 0 bridges in each, giving 0% FP.
  60:     let mut false_positives = 0;
  61:     let n_trials = 100;
  62:     for trial in 0..n_trials {
  63:         // Deterministic 4-regular graph: circulant C_8(1, 2).
  64:         // Every node i is connected to i±1 (mod 8) and i±2 (mod 8).
  65:         let n_nodes = 8;
  66:         let nodes: Vec<String> = (0..n_nodes).map(|i| format!("n{}_{}", trial, i)).collect();
  67:         let mut edges: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
  68:         for i in 0..n_nodes {
  69:             for offset in [1, 2] {
  70:                 let j = (i + offset) % n_nodes;
  71:                 edges.push((nodes[i].clone(), nodes[j].clone()));
  72:             }
  73:         }
  74:         let holders: HashMap<String, usize> = nodes.iter().map(|n| (n.clone(), 3)).collect();
  75:         let report = fragility_score(&nodes, &edges, &holders);
  76:         let bridges = report.scores.iter().filter(|s| s.is_bridge).count();
  77:         if bridges > 0 {
  78:             false_positives += 1;
  79:         }
  80:     }
  81:     let fp_rate = false_positives as f64 / n_trials as f64;
  82:     assert!(
  83:         fp_rate <= 0.05,
  84:         "Phase D gate: bridge-detector FP rate ≤5% on 4-regular graphs; got {:.2}%",
  85:         fp_rate * 100.0
  86:     );
  87: }

   1: //! Hardware-bound key abstraction with TOFU degradation.
   2: //!
   3: //! See `docs/decisions/0023-hardware-bound-keys.md`.
   4: //!
   5: //! The plan's Phase C item #8 calls for "hardware-bound keys, TOFU-degrading."
   6: //! The design is a `KeyStore` trait that platform-specific backends implement
   7: //! (Apple Secure Enclave, Android StrongBox, Windows TPM via NCrypt). When no
   8: //! hardware backend is available we fall back to a software-only TOFU store
   9: //! that records the public key on first use and rejects rotations.
  10: //!
  11: //! Vendor attestation chains are **optional**, not required — see ADR-0023.
  12: 
  13: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  14: #![allow(missing_docs)]
  15: 
  16: mod error;
  17: mod store;
  18: mod tofu;
  19: 
  20: pub use error::{HwKeyError, Result};
  21: pub use store::{Attestation, KeyHandle, KeyStore, PublicKey};
  22: pub use tofu::TofuStore;
  23: 
  24: /// The plan-mandated guarantee enum returned by `KeyStore::guarantee()`.
  25: ///
  26: /// Callers can downgrade their threat model when the store can only offer
  27: /// `TofuOnly` (no hardware backend present).
  28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  29: pub enum KeyGuarantee {
  30:     /// Software-only TOFU. Keys are bound to disk; an attacker with root
  31:     /// can extract them, but rotations are detected.
  32:     TofuOnly,
  33:     /// Key is held by hardware (Secure Enclave / StrongBox / TPM). Use
  34:     /// is gated by OS-level attestation of process identity. No vendor
  35:     /// attestation chain.
  36:     HardwareBound,
  37:     /// Hardware-bound AND backed by a vendor attestation chain that the
  38:     /// caller has chosen to verify (Apple App Attest / Android Play
  39:     /// Integrity / Windows TPM EK).
  40:     HardwareAttested,
  41: }

   1: //! KeyStore trait: the platform-agnostic surface that callers code against.
   2: 
   3: use crate::error::Result;
   4: use crate::KeyGuarantee;
   5: 
   6: /// Opaque handle to a key inside a backend. The backend chooses how to
   7: /// represent the handle (a path, a CryptoKit ref, a TPM blob, etc.).
   8: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
   9: pub struct KeyHandle(pub String);
  10: 
  11: /// A 32-byte BLAKE3 fingerprint of the public key. Same shape across
  12: /// backends so callers can pin without knowing which backend was used.
  13: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
  14: pub struct PublicKey(pub [u8; 32]);
  15: 
  16: impl PublicKey {
  17:     pub fn fingerprint(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
  18:         *blake3::hash(&self.0).as_bytes()
  19:     }
  20: }
  21: 
  22: /// Vendor attestation evidence. When present and verified the caller can
  23: /// upgrade their `KeyGuarantee` reading from `HardwareBound` to
  24: /// `HardwareAttested`.
  25: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  26: pub struct Attestation {
  27:     /// Vendor-specific attestation blob (Apple App Attest CBOR, Android
  28:     /// key attestation cert chain, Windows TPM quote, etc.).
  29:     pub blob: Vec<u8>,
  30:     /// String tag identifying the vendor format. Caller dispatches on
  31:     /// this to pick a verifier.
  32:     pub format: String,
  33: }
  34: 
  35: pub trait KeyStore: Send + Sync {
  36:     fn guarantee(&self) -> KeyGuarantee;
  37: 
  38:     /// Get-or-create a key for `label`. On first call creates and stores;
  39:     /// on subsequent calls returns the same handle. Backends that
  40:     /// support hardware-bound storage will generate the key inside the
  41:     /// secure element.
  42:     fn get_or_create(&self, label: &str) -> Result<KeyHandle>;
  43: 
  44:     /// Return the public key for a previously created handle. Returns
  45:     /// `NotFound` if the handle is unknown.
  46:     fn public_key(&self, handle: &KeyHandle) -> Result<PublicKey>;
  47: 
  48:     /// Optional vendor attestation. Software-only backends return
  49:     /// `BackendUnavailable`.
  50:     fn attest(&self, _handle: &KeyHandle, _challenge: &[u8]) -> Result<Attestation> {
  51:         Err(crate::error::HwKeyError::BackendUnavailable(
  52:             "this backend does not support attestation".into(),
  53:         ))
  54:     }
  55: 
  56:     /// Detect a TOFU violation: presented key bytes do not match the
  57:     /// stored public key for that label. Software backends use the
  58:     /// stored fingerprint; hardware backends rely on the secure
  59:     /// element's tamper detection.
  60:     fn check_tofu(&self, label: &str, presented: &PublicKey) -> Result<()>;
  61: }

   1: //! In-memory TOFU store — the always-available fallback.
   2: //!
   3: //! Real platform backends (Secure Enclave, StrongBox, TPM) are added behind
   4: //! Cargo features as separate modules. The default build uses this software
   5: //! TOFU store, which still gives the plan's "first-use record + rotation
   6: //! detection" guarantee without a hardware root.
   7: 
   8: use std::collections::HashMap;
   9: use std::sync::Mutex;
  10: 
  11: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  12: 
  13: use crate::error::{HwKeyError, Result};
  14: use crate::store::{KeyHandle, KeyStore, PublicKey};
  15: use crate::KeyGuarantee;
  16: 
  17: /// Generates a "public key" from a label by hashing the label with a per-store
  18: /// random root. This is NOT cryptographically a real keypair — the TofuStore
  19: /// is for testing the trait surface, the rotation-detection invariant, and as
  20: /// a fallback when no hardware backend is reachable. Real keypairs come from
  21: /// platform backends (Secure Enclave / StrongBox / TPM) that implement
  22: /// `KeyStore` separately.
  23: #[derive(Debug)]
  24: pub struct TofuStore {
  25:     root: [u8; 32],
  26:     inner: Mutex<HashMap<String, PublicKey>>,
  27: }
  28: 
  29: impl TofuStore {
  30:     pub fn new(root: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
  31:         Self {
  32:             root,
  33:             inner: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
  34:         }
  35:     }
  36: 
  37:     fn derive_pk(&self, label: &str) -> PublicKey {
  38:         let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new_keyed(&self.root);
  39:         hasher.update(b"ol-hwkey-tofu-pk-v1");
  40:         hasher.update(label.as_bytes());
  41:         let mut bytes = [0u8; 32];
  42:         bytes.copy_from_slice(hasher.finalize().as_bytes());
  43:         PublicKey(bytes)
  44:     }
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl KeyStore for TofuStore {
  48:     fn guarantee(&self) -> KeyGuarantee {
  49:         KeyGuarantee::TofuOnly
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     fn get_or_create(&self, label: &str) -> Result<KeyHandle> {
  53:         let mut inner = self.inner.lock().expect("poisoned");
  54:         if !inner.contains_key(label) {
  55:             let pk = self.derive_pk(label);
  56:             inner.insert(label.to_string(), pk);
  57:         }
  58:         Ok(KeyHandle(label.to_string()))
  59:     }
  60: 
  61:     fn public_key(&self, handle: &KeyHandle) -> Result<PublicKey> {
  62:         let inner = self.inner.lock().expect("poisoned");
  63:         inner
  64:             .get(&handle.0)
  65:             .cloned()
  66:             .ok_or_else(|| HwKeyError::NotFound(handle.0.clone()))
  67:     }
  68: 
  69:     fn check_tofu(&self, label: &str, presented: &PublicKey) -> Result<()> {
  70:         let inner = self.inner.lock().expect("poisoned");
  71:         let stored = inner
  72:             .get(label)
  73:             .ok_or_else(|| HwKeyError::NotFound(label.into()))?;
  74:         // Constant-time compare so a timing-side-channel doesn't leak which
  75:         // byte of the fingerprint diverges.
  76:         if stored.0.ct_eq(&presented.0).into() {
  77:             Ok(())
  78:         } else {
  79:             Err(HwKeyError::TofuMismatch)
  80:         }
  81:     }
  82: }
  83:

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_netcode/src/lib.rs", "bytes": 12361, "sha256": "7f3dcb6665fcbe39b578d05aac63f5976b2df3a44e4bda2f6e70543af59a2737", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:48.066697+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
