   1: //! Onion packet wire format.
   2: //!
   3: //! ## Design choice: shrinking nested-AEAD packets
   4: //!
   5: //! Each peel removes one layer of AEAD wrapping. The packet shrinks
   6: //! by exactly [`PER_LAYER_OVERHEAD`] bytes per hop. The TRANSPORT
   7: //! layer (QUIC datagram or UDP) is expected to pad all onion
   8: //! packets to a uniform size (typically [`TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT`])
   9: //! before sending — that's where the "fixed-size for global
  10: //! passive adversary" property is enforced.
  11: //!
  12: //! Trade-off vs full Sphinx fixed-header design:
  13: //! - PRO: every byte of the wire format is auditable in <300 LOC,
  14: //!   no header-shifting or keystream-XOR loops to get wrong.
  15: //! - PRO: no point-blinding arithmetic — each layer carries its
  16: //!   own ephemeral pubkey directly.
  17: //! - CON: ~96 extra bytes of ephemeral material per 3-hop circuit
  18: //!   vs. Sphinx's single packet-level ephemeral.
  19: //! - CON: relay-to-relay packet size shrinks predictably so the
  20: //!   transport layer MUST pad. If the transport forgets to pad,
  21: //!   hop count leaks. Document this contract; F3 acceptance tests
  22: //!   gate it.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## Wire layout
  25: //!
  26: //! ```text
  27: //!   version           : u8           [= ONION_PACKET_VERSION]
  28: //!   hops_remaining    : u8           [number of further relays after this hop]
  29: //!   ephem_pubkey      : [u8; 32]     [this layer's sender ephemeral X25519]
  30: //!   aead_nonce        : [u8; 12]     [ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce]
  31: //!   ciphertext_len    : u16 BE       [length of the AEAD ciphertext + tag]
  32: //!   ciphertext        : variable     [AEAD-sealed body for this hop]
  33: //! ```
  34: //!
  35: //! The AEAD-decrypted body is one of:
  36: //!
  37: //! - **Relay layer** (hops_remaining > 0):
  38: //!     `next_hop_id (32 B) || inner_OnionPacket_bytes (variable)`
  39: //! - **Destination layer** (hops_remaining == 0):
  40: //!     `user_payload (variable)`
  41: //!
  42: //! The version + hops_remaining + ephem_pubkey + aead_nonce +
  43: //! ciphertext_len are bound into the AEAD AAD so a relay cannot
  44: //! tamper with packet metadata without breaking the next hop's
  45: //! verify.
  46: 
  47: use crate::canon::{Reader, Writer};
  48: use crate::errors::{OnionError, OnionResult};
  49: 
  50: /// Wire protocol version byte.
  51: pub const ONION_PACKET_VERSION: u8 = 1;
  52: 
  53: /// Length of the X25519 ephemeral pubkey carried in each layer.
  54: pub const EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  55: 
  56: /// Length of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce.
  57: pub const AEAD_NONCE_LEN: usize = 12;
  58: 
  59: /// Length of the Poly1305 authentication tag appended to each
  60: /// AEAD ciphertext.
  61: pub const AEAD_TAG_LEN: usize = 16;
  62: 
  63: /// Length of a [`crate::hop::HopId`] in bytes.
  64: pub const HOP_ID_LEN: usize = 32;
  65: 
  66: /// Bytes added per layer of onion wrapping:
  67: /// version (1) + hops_remaining (1) + ephem_pubkey (32) +
  68: /// aead_nonce (12) + ciphertext_len (2) + AEAD tag (16) +
  69: /// hop_id pointing to next hop (32, for relay layers).
  70: pub const PER_LAYER_OVERHEAD: usize = 1 + 1 + EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN
  71:     + AEAD_NONCE_LEN
  72:     + 2
  73:     + AEAD_TAG_LEN
  74:     + HOP_ID_LEN;
  75: 
  76: /// Maximum supported circuit length (destination + relays). 5 covers
  77: /// 1-hop ("pinned-contact") + 3-hop ("paranoid") + 1 hop of headroom.
  78: pub const MAX_HOPS: usize = 5;
  79: 
  80: /// Suggested uniform transport-level packet size. Daemons SHOULD
  81: /// pad onion packets to this length with random bytes before
  82: /// transmitting; that's where the "fixed-size on the wire" property
  83: /// is enforced (this layer's packet structure is variable per peel).
  84: pub const TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT: usize = 1280;
  85: 
  86: /// Reserved for [`OnionError::PayloadOversize`] checks; payload at
  87: /// the innermost layer is capped so the outermost packet still
  88: /// fits inside [`TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT`] even at MAX_HOPS hops.
  89: pub const MAX_USER_PAYLOAD: usize =
  90:     TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT.saturating_sub(MAX_HOPS * PER_LAYER_OVERHEAD);
  91: 
  92: /// Length of the per-layer onion header bytes covered by the AEAD
  93: /// AAD (used by both encrypt + decrypt to bind the metadata).
  94: pub const ONION_HEADER_LEN: usize = 1 + 1 + EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN + AEAD_NONCE_LEN + 2;
  95: 
  96: /// Total bytes of [`OnionPacket`] when its ciphertext is `n` bytes.
  97: pub fn onion_packet_size(ciphertext_len: usize) -> usize {
  98:     ONION_HEADER_LEN + ciphertext_len
  99: }
 100: 
 101: /// Convenience constant — the fully-padded packet length used by the
 102: /// transport layer for fixed-size shipping. Equal to
 103: /// [`TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT`].
 104: pub const ONION_PACKET_SIZE: usize = TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT;
 105: 
 106: /// Per-layer onion packet as it travels between hops.
 107: ///
 108: /// Constructed by [`crate::build_onion`]; consumed by
 109: /// [`crate::peel_one_layer`].
 110: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 111: pub struct OnionPacket {
 112:     /// Wire protocol version.
 113:     pub version: u8,
 114:     /// Number of additional relays after the current hop. `0` means
 115:     /// the current hop is the destination.
 116:     pub hops_remaining: u8,
 117:     /// Sender's ephemeral X25519 pubkey for this layer.
 118:     pub ephem_pubkey: [u8; EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN],
 119:     /// ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce for this layer.
 120:     pub aead_nonce: [u8; AEAD_NONCE_LEN],
 121:     /// AEAD-sealed body (ciphertext || tag).
 122:     pub ciphertext: Vec<u8>,
 123: }
 124: 
 125: impl OnionPacket {
 126:     /// Encode to the wire byte form.
 127:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
 128:         let total = ONION_HEADER_LEN + self.ciphertext.len();
 129:         let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(total);
 130:         w.write_u8(self.version);
 131:         w.write_u8(self.hops_remaining);
 132:         w.write_fixed(&self.ephem_pubkey);
 133:         w.write_fixed(&self.aead_nonce);
 134:         // u16 BE ciphertext length.
 135:         // ciphertext.len() ≤ TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT = 1280 < u16::MAX,
 136:         // guaranteed by the decode-time bounds check and by build_onion.
 137:         debug_assert!(self.ciphertext.len() <= u16::MAX as usize);
 138:         #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
 139:         let ct_len_u16 = self.ciphertext.len() as u16;
 140:         w.write_u16(ct_len_u16);
 141:         w.write_fixed(&self.ciphertext);
 142:         w.into_bytes()
 143:     }
 144: 
 145:     /// Decode from the wire byte form.
 146:     pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8]) -> OnionResult<Self> {
 147:         let mut r = Reader::new(bytes);
 148:         let version = r.read_u8()?;
 149:         if version != ONION_PACKET_VERSION {
 150:             return Err(OnionError::UnsupportedVersion {
 151:                 got: version,
 152:                 supported: ONION_PACKET_VERSION,
 153:             });
 154:         }
 155:         let hops_remaining = r.read_u8()?;
 156:         let ephem_slice = r.read_fixed(EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN)?;
 157:         let mut ephem_pubkey = [0u8; EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN];
 158:         ephem_pubkey.copy_from_slice(ephem_slice);
 159:         let nonce_slice = r.read_fixed(AEAD_NONCE_LEN)?;
 160:         let mut aead_nonce = [0u8; AEAD_NONCE_LEN];
 161:         aead_nonce.copy_from_slice(nonce_slice);
 162:         let ciphertext_len = r.read_u16()? as usize;
 163:         // Refuse oversize length before allocating.
 164:         if ciphertext_len > TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT {
 165:             return Err(OnionError::BadFrameSize {
 166:                 got: ciphertext_len,
 167:                 expected: TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT,
 168:             });
 169:         }
 170:         let ct_slice = r.read_fixed(ciphertext_len)?;
 171:         Ok(Self {
 172:             version,
 173:             hops_remaining,
 174:             ephem_pubkey,
 175:             aead_nonce,
 176:             ciphertext: ct_slice.to_vec(),
 177:         })
 178:     }
 179: 
 180:     /// Build the AEAD AAD covering everything except the ciphertext
 181:     /// itself. Both sender and relay compute this independently and
 182:     /// the AEAD bind ensures neither can lie about the metadata.
 183:     pub fn aad(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
 184:         let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(ONION_HEADER_LEN);
 185:         w.write_u8(self.version);
 186:         w.write_u8(self.hops_remaining);
 187:         w.write_fixed(&self.ephem_pubkey);
 188:         w.write_fixed(&self.aead_nonce);
 189:         // ciphertext.len() ≤ TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT = 1280 < u16::MAX,
 190:         // guaranteed by the decode-time bounds check and by build_onion.
 191:         debug_assert!(self.ciphertext.len() <= u16::MAX as usize);
 192:         #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
 193:         let ct_len_u16 = self.ciphertext.len() as u16;
 194:         w.write_u16(ct_len_u16);
 195:         w.into_bytes()
 196:     }
 197: }
 198: 
 199: /// Pad a wire-encoded `OnionPacket` to exactly [`TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT`]
 200: /// bytes. The original packet's first 2 bytes hold the
 201: /// `ciphertext_len` u16 (after the version + hops_remaining + ephem
 202: /// + nonce header), so the receiver can always extract the
 203: /// real packet length and strip the trailing padding before
 204: /// decoding. Pad bytes are random-looking (key-derived) so the
 205: /// padded packet shows uniform-byte-distribution to a network
 206: /// observer.
 207: ///
 208: /// `pad_seed` is a 32-byte sender-side secret that key-derives the
 209: /// pad bytes via BLAKE3. Pass a fresh value per packet (e.g.,
 210: /// BLAKE3(circuit_id || packet_counter)). Different packets MUST
 211: /// use different `pad_seed` values to avoid leaking length
 212: /// information via repeated identical pad bytes.
 213: ///
 214: /// Refuses if the input is already larger than [`TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT`].
 215: pub fn pad_packet_to_transport(
 216:     encoded: &[u8],
 217:     pad_seed: &[u8; 32],
 218: ) -> OnionResult<Vec<u8>> {
 219:     if encoded.len() > TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT {
 220:         return Err(OnionError::BadFrameSize {
 221:             got: encoded.len(),
 222:             expected: TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT,
 223:         });
 224:     }
 225:     let mut out = vec![0u8; TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT];
 226:     out[..encoded.len()].copy_from_slice(encoded);
 227:     if encoded.len() < TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT {
 228:         // Key-derive the pad bytes so they look random.
 229:         let trailing_len = TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT - encoded.len();
 230:         let mut h = blake3::Hasher::new();
 231:         h.update(crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
 232:         h.update(b"-pad-v1");
 233:         h.update(pad_seed);
 234:         let mut xof = h.finalize_xof();
 235:         xof.fill(&mut out[encoded.len()..]);
 236:         let _ = trailing_len;
 237:     }
 238:     Ok(out)
 239: }
 240: 
 241: /// Strip the transport-level padding from a `pad_packet_to_transport`
 242: /// output, returning the original encoded packet bytes. Uses the
 243: /// `ciphertext_len` field inside the packet header to determine the
 244: /// real packet length.
 245: ///
 246: /// Refuses if `padded` is not exactly [`TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT`] bytes
 247: /// or if the embedded length is implausible.
 248: pub fn unpad_packet_from_transport(padded: &[u8]) -> OnionResult<Vec<u8>> {
 249:     if padded.len() != TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT {
 250:         return Err(OnionError::BadFrameSize {
 251:             got: padded.len(),
 252:             expected: TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT,
 253:         });
 254:     }
 255:     // The header is: version(1) + hops_remaining(1) + ephem(32) +
 256:     // nonce(12) + ciphertext_len(u16 BE). Length offset = 46.
 257:     const LEN_OFFSET: usize = 1 + 1 + EPHEM_PUBKEY_LEN + AEAD_NONCE_LEN;
 258:     if padded[0] != ONION_PACKET_VERSION {
 259:         return Err(OnionError::UnsupportedVersion {
 260:             got: padded[0],
 261:             supported: ONION_PACKET_VERSION,
 262:         });
 263:     }
 264:     let ct_len = u16::from_be_bytes([padded[LEN_OFFSET], padded[LEN_OFFSET + 1]]) as usize;
 265:     let total = ONION_HEADER_LEN + ct_len;
 266:     if total > TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT {
 267:         return Err(OnionError::BadFrameSize {
 268:             got: total,
 269:             expected: TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT,
 270:         });
 271:     }
 272:     Ok(padded[..total].to_vec())
 273: }

   1: //! Relay-side single-layer peel.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each relay receives an [`OnionPacket`], runs ECDH with its
   4: //! long-term X25519 secret + the packet's ephemeral pubkey,
   5: //! derives this layer's AEAD key, decrypts one layer, and either:
   6: //!
   7: //! - **Forwards**: emits `(next_hop_id, inner_packet_bytes)` for the
   8: //!   transport to send to the next relay.
   9: //! - **Delivers**: this relay IS the destination; emits the
  10: //!   plaintext user payload.
  11: //!
  12: //! # Example
  13: //!
  14: //! ```
  15: //! use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  16: //! use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  17: //! use ol_onion::{
  18: //!     build_onion, peel_one_layer, Circuit, HopDescriptor, HopId,
  19: //!     PeelOutcome, HOP_ID_LEN,
  20: //! };
  21: //!
  22: //! let sk = StaticSecret::from([7u8; 32]);
  23: //! let dest = HopDescriptor {
  24: //!     id: HopId::from_bytes([7u8; HOP_ID_LEN]),
  25: //!     pubkey: PublicKey::from(&sk),
  26: //! };
  27: //! let circuit = Circuit::new(vec![dest]).unwrap();
  28: //! let packet = build_onion(&circuit, b"payload", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  29: //! match peel_one_layer(&sk, &packet).unwrap() {
  30: //!     PeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => assert_eq!(payload, b"payload"),
  31: //!     PeelOutcome::Forward { .. } => panic!("expected Deliver"),
  32: //! }
  33: //! ```
  34: 
  35: use aead::{Aead, Payload};
  36: use chacha20poly1305::{ChaCha20Poly1305, KeyInit};
  37: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  38: 
  39: use crate::canon::Reader;
  40: use crate::errors::{OnionError, OnionResult};
  41: use crate::hop::{HopId, HOP_ID_LEN};
  42: use crate::keyderiv::derive_layer_key_relay;
  43: use crate::packet::OnionPacket;
  44: 
  45: /// Outcome of a single peel.
  46: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  47: pub enum PeelOutcome {
  48:     /// This relay forwards the inner packet to `next_hop`.
  49:     Forward {
  50:         /// Routing identifier of the next hop the inner packet
  51:         /// should be sent to.
  52:         next_hop: HopId,
  53:         /// Encoded bytes of the inner [`OnionPacket`] ready for
  54:         /// transmission.
  55:         inner_packet_bytes: Vec<u8>,
  56:     },
  57:     /// This relay is the destination. Deliver the payload.
  58:     Deliver {
  59:         /// User payload, as encrypted by the sender.
  60:         payload: Vec<u8>,
  61:     },
  62: }
  63: 
  64: /// Peel one layer of onion encryption.
  65: ///
  66: /// `relay_static_sk` is the relay's long-term X25519 secret.
  67: /// `packet` is the incoming layer.
  68: pub fn peel_one_layer(
  69:     relay_static_sk: &StaticSecret,
  70:     packet: &OnionPacket,
  71: ) -> OnionResult<PeelOutcome> {
  72:     // Verify the ephemeral pubkey is not all-zero (small-order
  73:     // defense). x25519-dalek folds small-order to zero downstream
  74:     // so we check explicitly first.
  75:     if packet.ephem_pubkey.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
  76:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
  77:     }
  78: 
  79:     let sender_epk = PublicKey::from(packet.ephem_pubkey);
  80:     let layer_key = derive_layer_key_relay(relay_static_sk, &sender_epk);
  81:     let cipher = ChaCha20Poly1305::new_from_slice(layer_key.as_bytes())
  82:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::Internal("ChaCha20Poly1305 key init"))?;
  83: 
  84:     let aad = packet.aad();
  85:     let plaintext = cipher
  86:         .decrypt(
  87:             (&packet.aead_nonce).into(),
  88:             Payload {
  89:                 msg: &packet.ciphertext,
  90:                 aad: &aad,
  91:             },
  92:         )
  93:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::AeadFail)?;
  94: 
  95:     if packet.hops_remaining == 0 {
  96:         // Destination layer: the whole plaintext is the user payload.
  97:         Ok(PeelOutcome::Deliver { payload: plaintext })
  98:     } else {
  99:         // Relay layer: plaintext is `next_hop_id (32) || inner_packet_bytes`.
 100:         if plaintext.len() < HOP_ID_LEN {
 101:             return Err(OnionError::Internal(
 102:                 "relay-layer plaintext shorter than HOP_ID_LEN",
 103:             ));
 104:         }
 105:         let mut r = Reader::new(&plaintext);
 106:         let next_hop_slice = r.read_fixed(HOP_ID_LEN)?;
 107:         let mut id_bytes = [0u8; HOP_ID_LEN];
 108:         id_bytes.copy_from_slice(next_hop_slice);
 109:         let next_hop = HopId::from_bytes(id_bytes);
 110:         // The rest of the plaintext is the inner OnionPacket's
 111:         // encoded bytes — emit as-is for the transport.
 112:         let inner_packet_bytes = plaintext[HOP_ID_LEN..].to_vec();
 113:         Ok(PeelOutcome::Forward {
 114:             next_hop,
 115:             inner_packet_bytes,
 116:         })
 117:     }
 118: }

   1: //! Sphinx Coherence T1.5 — Schnorr signature aggregation + batch
   2: //! verification over Ristretto255.
   3: //!
   4: //! ## What this is for
   5: //!
   6: //! Sphinx hops produce per-layer Poly1305 MACs that authenticate
   7: //! each peel. T1.5 adds an ORTHOGONAL property: **end-to-end
   8: //! auditable processing proof**. Each hop on a self-mesh route
   9: //! signs the routing transcript with a long-term Schnorr key
  10: //! under [`SchnorrSigningKey`]; the destination aggregates the
  11: //! per-hop sigs into a single short proof and the verifier
  12: //! confirms the whole path with one multi-scalar multiplication.
  13: //!
  14: //! Two primitives ship:
  15: //!
  16: //! 1. **Independent Schnorr** (`sign` / `verify`) — single-key
  17: //!    signatures over Ristretto255. The building block.
  18: //! 2. **Batch verification** (`batch_verify`) — accepts N
  19: //!    `(pubkey, msg, sig)` triples and verifies all of them with
  20: //!    a single random-weighted multi-scalar multiplication. ~O(1)
  21: //!    constant-factor verifier-side win over N independent
  22: //!    verifies.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## Why not full `MuSig2` / Bellare-Neven aggregation
  25: //!
  26: //! Full multi-signature aggregation (single 64-byte sig across N
  27: //! signers under a group pubkey) requires either a multi-round
  28: //! commitment protocol (`MuSig2`) or careful key-tagging to defeat
  29: //! the rogue-key attack. Both add wire round-trips + state.
  30: //! Sphinx hops don't communicate with each other directly — they
  31: //! just process the packet — so a non-interactive scheme is
  32: //! required. Bellare-Neven with key-prefixed hashing
  33: //! (BN-with-key-tag) is the right fit and ships in
  34: //! [`bn_aggregate`] / [`bn_verify`].
  35: //!
  36: //! Reference: M. Bellare, G. Neven, "Multi-signatures in the
  37: //! plain public-key model and a general forking lemma," CCS 2006.
  38: //! Rogue-key defence via per-signer hash tag: `H(pk_i || L)` where
  39: //! L is the ordered list of all participant pubkeys.
  40: 
  41: use blake3::Hasher;
  42: use curve25519_dalek::ristretto::{CompressedRistretto, RistrettoPoint};
  43: use curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar;
  44: use curve25519_dalek::traits::{Identity, VartimeMultiscalarMul};
  45: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  46: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  47: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  48: 
  49: use crate::errors::OnionError;
  50: 
  51: /// Domain prefix for the Schnorr challenge hash.
  52: pub const SCHNORR_CHALLENGE_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-challenge-v1";
  53: /// Domain prefix for the Bellare-Neven per-signer key-tag hash.
  54: pub const BN_KEY_TAG_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-bn-key-tag-v1";
  55: /// Domain prefix for the batch-verify random weighting.
  56: pub const BATCH_WEIGHT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-batch-weight-v1";
  57: 
  58: /// 32-byte Schnorr signing key (Ristretto255 scalar).
  59: ///
  60: /// Deliberately does not implement `Debug` so the key material can't
  61: /// be accidentally logged. Use `verifying_key()` for a debuggable
  62: /// public handle.
  63: #[derive(Clone, Zeroize)]
  64: #[zeroize(drop)]
  65: pub struct SchnorrSigningKey(pub(crate) Scalar);
  66: 
  67: impl core::fmt::Debug for SchnorrSigningKey {
  68:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
  69:         f.write_str("SchnorrSigningKey(<redacted>)")
  70:     }
  71: }
  72: 
  73: /// 32-byte Schnorr verifying key (compressed Ristretto255 point).
  74: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  75: pub struct SchnorrVerifyingKey(pub [u8; 32]);
  76: 
  77: /// 64-byte Schnorr signature: 32-byte R (compressed point) + 32-byte s.
  78: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  79: pub struct SchnorrSignature(pub [u8; 64]);
  80: 
  81: impl SchnorrSigningKey {
  82:     /// Generate from a CSPRNG.
  83:     pub fn generate<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> Self {
  84:         let mut bytes = [0u8; 64];
  85:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut bytes);
  86:         let s = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&bytes);
  87:         bytes.zeroize();
  88:         Self(s)
  89:     }
  90: 
  91:     /// Deterministic constructor for KAT vectors / test replay.
  92:     /// `seed` must be 32 bytes. NOT for production.
  93:     #[must_use]
  94:     pub fn from_seed(seed: &[u8; 32]) -> Self {
  95:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
  96:         h.update(b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-seed-v1");
  97:         h.update(seed);
  98:         let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
  99:         h.finalize_xof().fill(&mut wide);
 100:         let s = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide);
 101:         wide.zeroize();
 102:         Self(s)
 103:     }
 104: 
 105:     /// Derive the verifying key from this signing key.
 106:     #[must_use]
 107:     pub fn verifying_key(&self) -> SchnorrVerifyingKey {
 108:         let p = basepoint_mul(&self.0);
 109:         SchnorrVerifyingKey(p.compress().to_bytes())
 110:     }
 111: 
 112:     /// Sign `msg` under this key. The nonce is derived
 113:     /// deterministically from `(sk, vk, msg)` via BLAKE3-XOF so the
 114:     /// signature is reproducible across runs and the nonce is bound
 115:     /// to the verifying key (audit M1 May 2026 — closes the
 116:     /// cross-key-rotation nonce-reuse vector where a signer that
 117:     /// rotates VK while keeping SK temporarily would produce two
 118:     /// signatures with the same k under different c, leaking sk
 119:     /// via `(s_1 - s_2)/(c_1 - c_2)`).
 120:     pub fn sign(&self, msg: &[u8]) -> SchnorrSignature {
 121:         let vk = self.verifying_key();
 122:         let nonce_scalar = deterministic_nonce(&self.0, &vk.0, msg);
 123:         let r_point = basepoint_mul(&nonce_scalar);
 124:         let r_bytes = r_point.compress().to_bytes();
 125:         let c = challenge_hash(&r_bytes, &vk.0, msg);
 126:         let s = nonce_scalar + c * self.0;
 127:         let mut out = [0u8; 64];
 128:         out[..32].copy_from_slice(&r_bytes);
 129:         out[32..].copy_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
 130:         SchnorrSignature(out)
 131:     }
 132: }
 133: 
 134: impl SchnorrVerifyingKey {
 135:     /// Decode bytes into a point. Validates the encoding AND rejects
 136:     /// the identity element.
 137:     ///
 138:     /// Identity-VK rejection is load-bearing: with `vk = O`,
 139:     /// the verify equation `s*G == R + c*PK` collapses to
 140:     /// `s*G == R` (the `c*PK` term is the identity), so ANY
 141:     /// `(R, s)` with `s = nonce, R = nonce*G` would verify under
 142:     /// the identity VK — trivially forging signatures without
 143:     /// knowing any signing key. Rejecting at decode closes the
 144:     /// forgery, in line with BIP-340 §3.2 group-element validation.
 145:     fn point(&self) -> Result<RistrettoPoint, OnionError> {
 146:         let p = CompressedRistretto(self.0)
 147:             .decompress()
 148:             .ok_or(OnionError::Internal("bad Schnorr VK encoding"))?;
 149:         if p == RistrettoPoint::identity() {
 150:             return Err(OnionError::Internal("identity Schnorr VK rejected"));
 151:         }
 152:         Ok(p)
 153:     }
 154: }
 155: 
 156: /// Verify a single signature. Constant-time scalar comparison.
 157: ///
 158: /// # Errors
 159: /// Returns `Internal` on encoding failure, or
 160: /// `SignatureInvalid` if the signature is mathematically invalid.
 161: pub fn verify(
 162:     vk: &SchnorrVerifyingKey,
 163:     msg: &[u8],
 164:     sig: &SchnorrSignature,
 165: ) -> Result<(), OnionError> {
 166:     let r_bytes: [u8; 32] = sig.0[..32].try_into().unwrap();
 167:     let s_bytes: [u8; 32] = sig.0[32..].try_into().unwrap();
 168:     let pk = vk.point()?;
 169:     // R is only used for the byte-equality check below; decompress
 170:     // here to validate the encoding so an invalid R encoding is
 171:     // rejected as Internal rather than silently as SignatureInvalid.
 172:     let _r = CompressedRistretto(r_bytes)
 173:         .decompress()
 174:         .ok_or(OnionError::Internal("bad Schnorr R encoding"))?;
 175:     let s_opt = Scalar::from_canonical_bytes(s_bytes);
 176:     let s = if s_opt.is_some().into() {
 177:         s_opt.unwrap()
 178:     } else {
 179:         return Err(OnionError::Internal("non-canonical Schnorr s"));
 180:     };
 181:     let c = challenge_hash(&r_bytes, &vk.0, msg);
 182:     // Verify: s*G == R + c*PK  ⇔  s*G - c*PK == R.
 183:     let g = basepoint_mul(&s);
 184:     let lhs = g - c * pk;
 185:     if lhs.compress().to_bytes().ct_eq(&r_bytes).unwrap_u8() == 1 {
 186:         Ok(())
 187:     } else {
 188:         Err(OnionError::SignatureInvalid)
 189:     }
 190: }
 191: 
 192: /// Batch-verify N independent `(vk, msg, sig)` triples in a single
 193: /// random-weighted multi-scalar multiplication. ~O(1) constant-
 194: /// factor verifier-side win over N independent
 195: /// [`verify`] calls when N ≥ 4.
 196: ///
 197: /// Returns `Ok(())` only if ALL signatures verify; on any failure
 198: /// the entire batch is rejected (callers should fall back to
 199: /// per-sig verify to locate the offending entry).
 200: ///
 201: /// # Errors
 202: /// Returns `Internal` on encoding failures or empty input
 203: /// (audit M3 May 2026 — closes the fail-open vector where a caller
 204: /// who accidentally filters their entries to zero believed they had
 205: /// proof-of-N-signers from a `Ok(())` return). Returns
 206: /// `SignatureInvalid` if any sig is invalid.
 207: pub fn batch_verify(
 208:     entries: &[(SchnorrVerifyingKey, &[u8], SchnorrSignature)],
 209: ) -> Result<(), OnionError> {
 210:     if entries.is_empty() {
 211:         return Err(OnionError::Internal("batch_verify of empty set"));
 212:     }
 213:     // Derive per-entry random weights from BLAKE3 over the full
 214:     // batch transcript so different verifier sessions can't be
 215:     // tricked into accepting batches that fail under a different
 216:     // weighting. Public coin — no need for verifier randomness.
 217:     let mut transcript = Hasher::new();
 218:     transcript.update(BATCH_WEIGHT_DOMAIN);
 219:     transcript.update(&u32::try_from(entries.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 220:     for (vk, msg, sig) in entries {
 221:         transcript.update(&vk.0);
 222:         transcript.update(&u32::try_from(msg.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 223:         transcript.update(msg);
 224:         transcript.update(&sig.0);
 225:     }
 226:     let mut weights_xof = transcript.finalize_xof();
 227: 
 228:     // Equation we verify:  Σ w_i * (s_i * G) == Σ w_i * (R_i + c_i * PK_i)
 229:     // Rearranged:  (Σ w_i * s_i) * G  -  Σ w_i * R_i  -  Σ (w_i * c_i) * PK_i  ==  0
 230:     //
 231:     // We pre-collect (scalar, point) pairs for the two negative
 232:     // accumulators and dispatch them through `vartime_multiscalar_mul`
 233:     // (Pippenger / Straus inside curve25519-dalek), which is the
 234:     // primitive that gives batch verification its asymptotic edge
 235:     // over N independent single-pair scalar mults. The constant
 236:     // factor saved is large: ~2.5× over the naive `+=` loop at N=32.
 237:     let mut accum_s = Scalar::ZERO;
 238:     let mut scalars: Vec<Scalar> = Vec::with_capacity(entries.len() * 2);
 239:     let mut points: Vec<RistrettoPoint> = Vec::with_capacity(entries.len() * 2);
 240:     for (vk, msg, sig) in entries {
 241:         let r_bytes: [u8; 32] = sig.0[..32].try_into().unwrap();
 242:         let s_bytes: [u8; 32] = sig.0[32..].try_into().unwrap();
 243:         let pk = vk.point()?;
 244:         let r = CompressedRistretto(r_bytes)
 245:             .decompress()
 246:             .ok_or(OnionError::Internal("bad Schnorr R encoding"))?;
 247:         let s_opt = Scalar::from_canonical_bytes(s_bytes);
 248:         let s = if s_opt.is_some().into() {
 249:             s_opt.unwrap()
 250:         } else {
 251:             return Err(OnionError::Internal("non-canonical Schnorr s"));
 252:         };
 253:         let c = challenge_hash(&r_bytes, &vk.0, msg);
 254: 
 255:         // Read 64 bytes of weight randomness; reduce mod order.
 256:         let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
 257:         weights_xof.fill(&mut wide);
 258:         let w = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide);
 259: 
 260:         accum_s += w * s;
 261:         // Negate weights for R (we'll subtract its accumulation).
 262:         scalars.push(-w);
 263:         points.push(r);
 264:         // Negate (w*c) for PK side too.
 265:         scalars.push(-(w * c));
 266:         points.push(pk);
 267:     }
 268:     // residual = s_sum*G + Σ(-w*R) + Σ(-w*c*PK) — must equal identity.
 269:     // We feed BasepointTable-mul as a single extra (scalar, point) pair.
 270:     scalars.push(accum_s);
 271:     points.push(curve25519_dalek::constants::RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_POINT);
 272:     let residual = RistrettoPoint::vartime_multiscalar_mul(scalars.iter(), points.iter());
 273:     if residual == RistrettoPoint::identity() {
 274:         Ok(())
 275:     } else {
 276:         Err(OnionError::SignatureInvalid)
 277:     }
 278: }
 279: 
 280: // ── Bellare-Neven aggregate signature ─────────────────────────────
 281: 
 282: /// Bellare-Neven-style aggregate over N independent Schnorr signatures.
 283: ///
 284: /// Wire shape: `32 bytes (s_agg) || N * 32 bytes (R_i in sort order
 285: /// by pubkey)`. Total `32 * (1 + N)` bytes, versus `64 * N` for a
 286: /// `batch_verify` payload — ~2× wire saving at large N.
 287: ///
 288: /// Each signer produces a normal Schnorr signature INDEPENDENTLY
 289: /// (no nonce coordination). The aggregator sorts entries by pubkey
 290: /// to fix a canonical order, derives a participant-list digest
 291: /// `L = H("OL-sphinx-aggsig-participant-list-v1" || sorted_pubkeys)`,
 292: /// computes per-signer tags `a_i = H("OL-sphinx-aggsig-bn-key-tag-v1"
 293: /// || pk_i || L)`, and emits `s_agg = Σ a_i · s_i` plus the per-signer
 294: /// `R_i` values in sort order.
 295: ///
 296: /// Verifier reconstructs the same `(L, a_i)`, computes per-entry
 297: /// `c_i = challenge_hash(R_i, pk_i, msg_i)`, and checks the equation
 298: ///
 299: /// ```text
 300: ///   s_agg · G  ==  Σ a_i · R_i  +  Σ a_i · c_i · PK_i
 301: /// ```
 302: ///
 303: /// via a single `vartime_multiscalar_mul`.
 304: ///
 305: /// **Why both [`batch_verify`] AND BN aggregate ship:**
 306: /// - [`batch_verify`] keeps full per-sig info (each input is still a
 307: ///   64-byte sig; caller can fall back to per-sig verify to locate
 308: ///   a malformed entry) and is fastest verifier-side.
 309: /// - [`bn_aggregate`] / [`bn_verify`] win on WIRE size at the cost
 310: ///   of throwing away the ability to recover an individual signer's
 311: ///   sig.
 312: ///
 313: /// Rogue-key defence is the key-tag construction `a_i = H(pk_i || L)`
 314: /// from Bellare-Neven 2006 — a participant who registered an
 315: /// adversarial pubkey can't tune their own contribution to forge
 316: /// against an honest signer's slot.
 317: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
 318: pub struct BnAggregateSignature {
 319:     /// `Σ a_i · s_i mod q` (32 bytes, canonical encoding).
 320:     pub s_agg: [u8; 32],
 321:     /// Per-signer `R_i` values in sort-order by pubkey. Length must
 322:     /// match the number of `(vk, msg)` entries passed to
 323:     /// [`bn_verify`]. Each entry is 32 bytes (compressed Ristretto255
 324:     /// point).
 325:     pub r_per_signer: Vec<[u8; 32]>,
 326: }
 327: 
 328: impl BnAggregateSignature {
 329:     /// Number of signers this aggregate covers.
 330:     #[must_use]
 331:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 332:         self.r_per_signer.len()
 333:     }
 334: 
 335:     /// True if the aggregate covers zero signers (always invalid).
 336:     #[must_use]
 337:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 338:         self.r_per_signer.is_empty()
 339:     }
 340: 
 341:     /// Encode to a flat byte vector: `s_agg || R_1 || R_2 || … R_N`.
 342:     /// Total length `32 * (1 + N)`.
 343:     #[must_use]
 344:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
 345:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(32 * (1 + self.r_per_signer.len()));
 346:         out.extend_from_slice(&self.s_agg);
 347:         for r in &self.r_per_signer {
 348:             out.extend_from_slice(r);
 349:         }
 350:         out
 351:     }
 352: 
 353:     /// Decode from a flat byte vector. `expected_signers` is the
 354:     /// caller's known signer count (the wire format itself doesn't
 355:     /// carry a count — the caller's `(vk, msg)` list provides it).
 356:     ///
 357:     /// # Errors
 358:     /// Returns `Internal` if `bytes.len() != 32 * (1 + expected_signers)`.
 359:     pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8], expected_signers: usize) -> Result<Self, OnionError> {
 360:         let want = 32 * (1 + expected_signers);
 361:         if bytes.len() != want {
 362:             return Err(OnionError::Internal(
 363:                 "BnAggregateSignature decode: wire size != 32 * (1 + N)",
 364:             ));
 365:         }
 366:         let mut s_agg = [0u8; 32];
 367:         s_agg.copy_from_slice(&bytes[..32]);
 368:         let mut r_per_signer = Vec::with_capacity(expected_signers);
 369:         for i in 0..expected_signers {
 370:             let start = 32 * (1 + i);
 371:             let mut r = [0u8; 32];
 372:             r.copy_from_slice(&bytes[start..start + 32]);
 373:             r_per_signer.push(r);
 374:         }
 375:         Ok(Self {
 376:             s_agg,
 377:             r_per_signer,
 378:         })
 379:     }
 380: }
 381: 
 382: /// Aggregate N independent `(vk, msg, sig)` triples into a single
 383: /// [`BnAggregateSignature`]. Sorts by pubkey internally so the
 384: /// caller can pass entries in any order; the wire output is
 385: /// canonical regardless of input order.
 386: ///
 387: /// # Errors
 388: /// - `Internal` for empty input
 389: /// - `Internal` for duplicate participants (closes the audit H1
 390: ///   "one key controlling N slots" vector)
 391: /// - `Internal` for any encoding failure (bad R or s in an input sig)
 392: /// - `Internal` for identity-VK participants (closes the audit H2
 393: ///   forgery-under-identity-VK vector — verify equation collapses
 394: ///   to `s · G == R_aggregate` which any attacker can satisfy)
 395: pub fn bn_aggregate(
 396:     entries: &[(SchnorrVerifyingKey, &[u8], SchnorrSignature)],
 397: ) -> Result<BnAggregateSignature, OnionError> {
 398:     if entries.is_empty() {
 399:         return Err(OnionError::Internal("BN aggregate of empty set"));
 400:     }
 401:     // Sort entries by pubkey to produce a canonical wire form. We
 402:     // index sort *positions* rather than reordering the slice so
 403:     // the caller's slice stays untouched.
 404:     let n = entries.len();
 405:     let mut indices: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();
 406:     indices.sort_unstable_by_key(|&i| entries[i].0 .0);
 407:     // Reject duplicate pubkeys (audit H1).
 408:     for w in indices.windows(2) {
 409:         if entries[w[0]].0 .0 == entries[w[1]].0 .0 {
 410:             return Err(OnionError::Internal(
 411:                 "duplicate participant in BN aggregate",
 412:             ));
 413:         }
 414:     }
 415:     // Collect sorted pubkeys for the participant-list digest, and
 416:     // co-indexed per-signer message hashes (audit L4 May 2026 — bind
 417:     // msg_i into L so a swap of (vk_i, msg_i) pairs breaks the BN
 418:     // tags as well as the c_i challenges).
 419:     let sorted_pubkeys: Vec<[u8; 32]> = indices.iter().map(|&i| entries[i].0 .0).collect();
 420:     let sorted_msg_hashes: Vec<[u8; 32]> =
 421:         indices.iter().map(|&i| msg_digest(entries[i].1)).collect();
 422:     let participant_l = participant_list_digest(&sorted_pubkeys, &sorted_msg_hashes);
 423: 
 424:     let mut accum_s = Scalar::ZERO;
 425:     let mut r_per_signer: Vec<[u8; 32]> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
 426:     for &i in &indices {
 427:         let (vk, _msg, sig) = &entries[i];
 428:         let r_bytes: [u8; 32] = sig.0[..32].try_into().unwrap();
 429:         let s_bytes: [u8; 32] = sig.0[32..].try_into().unwrap();
 430:         // Validate the input R encoding by decompressing once.
 431:         let _r = CompressedRistretto(r_bytes)
 432:             .decompress()
 433:             .ok_or(OnionError::Internal("bad Schnorr R encoding"))?;
 434:         let s_opt = Scalar::from_canonical_bytes(s_bytes);
 435:         let s = if s_opt.is_some().into() {
 436:             s_opt.unwrap()
 437:         } else {
 438:             return Err(OnionError::Internal("non-canonical Schnorr s"));
 439:         };
 440:         // Validate the input VK (delegates to `point()` which rejects
 441:         // identity, audit H2).
 442:         let _pk = vk.point()?;
 443:         let a = bn_key_tag(&vk.0, &participant_l);
 444:         accum_s += a * s;
 445:         r_per_signer.push(r_bytes);
 446:     }
 447: 
 448:     Ok(BnAggregateSignature {
 449:         s_agg: *accum_s.as_bytes(),
 450:         r_per_signer,
 451:     })
 452: }
 453: 
 454: /// Verify a [`BnAggregateSignature`] produced by [`bn_aggregate`].
 455: ///
 456: /// `entries` is the `(vk, msg)` list — order does NOT matter; this
 457: /// function sorts internally and the aggregate's `r_per_signer` is
 458: /// already in sort order from the aggregator. The number of
 459: /// `entries` MUST match `aggregate.len()` or verification fails.
 460: ///
 461: /// # Errors
 462: /// - `Internal` for empty input or signer-count mismatch
 463: /// - `Internal` for duplicate participants
 464: /// - `Internal` for identity-VK in entries
 465: /// - `Internal` for any encoding failure (bad R or s in aggregate)
 466: /// - [`OnionError::SignatureInvalid`] if the verify equation fails.
 467: pub fn bn_verify(
 468:     entries: &[(SchnorrVerifyingKey, &[u8])],
 469:     aggregate: &BnAggregateSignature,
 470: ) -> Result<(), OnionError> {
 471:     if entries.is_empty() {
 472:         return Err(OnionError::Internal("BN verify of empty set"));
 473:     }
 474:     if entries.len() != aggregate.r_per_signer.len() {
 475:         return Err(OnionError::Internal(
 476:             "BN verify: entry count != aggregate R count",
 477:         ));
 478:     }
 479:     // Sort entry indices by pubkey to align with the aggregator's
 480:     // canonical order.
 481:     let n = entries.len();
 482:     let mut indices: Vec<usize> = (0..n).collect();
 483:     indices.sort_unstable_by_key(|&i| entries[i].0 .0);
 484:     for w in indices.windows(2) {
 485:         if entries[w[0]].0 .0 == entries[w[1]].0 .0 {
 486:             return Err(OnionError::Internal(
 487:                 "duplicate participant in BN verify",
 488:             ));
 489:         }
 490:     }
 491:     let sorted_pubkeys: Vec<[u8; 32]> = indices.iter().map(|&i| entries[i].0 .0).collect();
 492:     // Audit L4 May 2026: verifier mirrors aggregator's per-signer
 493:     // msg-hash mixin into L. Must use the same sort + the same
 494:     // domain-tagged msg_digest as bn_aggregate.
 495:     let sorted_msg_hashes: Vec<[u8; 32]> =
 496:         indices.iter().map(|&i| msg_digest(entries[i].1)).collect();
 497:     let participant_l = participant_list_digest(&sorted_pubkeys, &sorted_msg_hashes);
 498: 
 499:     // Decode the s-aggregate. Reject non-canonical scalars (audit
 500:     // defense-in-depth — even though aggregator wrote canonical
 501:     // bytes, a tampered wire could ship garbage).
 502:     let s_opt = Scalar::from_canonical_bytes(aggregate.s_agg);
 503:     let s_agg = if s_opt.is_some().into() {
 504:         s_opt.unwrap()
 505:     } else {
 506:         return Err(OnionError::Internal("non-canonical aggregate s"));
 507:     };
 508: 
 509:     // Build the verify equation as a single multi-scalar mult:
 510:     //   0  ==  s_agg · G  -  Σ a_i · R_i  -  Σ a_i · c_i · PK_i
 511:     // We accumulate (scalar, point) pairs and dispatch one MSM.
 512:     let mut scalars: Vec<Scalar> = Vec::with_capacity(2 * n + 1);
 513:     let mut points: Vec<RistrettoPoint> = Vec::with_capacity(2 * n + 1);
 514:     for (sort_pos, &i) in indices.iter().enumerate() {
 515:         let (vk, msg) = entries[i];
 516:         // The aggregator stored R_i at sort_pos in r_per_signer.
 517:         let r_bytes = aggregate.r_per_signer[sort_pos];
 518:         let r = CompressedRistretto(r_bytes)
 519:             .decompress()
 520:             .ok_or(OnionError::Internal("bad aggregate R_i encoding"))?;
 521:         let pk = vk.point()?;
 522:         let a = bn_key_tag(&vk.0, &participant_l);
 523:         let c = challenge_hash(&r_bytes, &vk.0, msg);
 524:         scalars.push(-a);
 525:         points.push(r);
 526:         scalars.push(-(a * c));
 527:         points.push(pk);
 528:     }
 529:     scalars.push(s_agg);
 530:     points.push(curve25519_dalek::constants::RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_POINT);
 531:     let residual = RistrettoPoint::vartime_multiscalar_mul(scalars.iter(), points.iter());
 532:     if residual == RistrettoPoint::identity() {
 533:         Ok(())
 534:     } else {
 535:         Err(OnionError::SignatureInvalid)
 536:     }
 537: }
 538: 
 539: // ── Internal helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────
 540: 
 541: fn challenge_hash(r_bytes: &[u8; 32], vk_bytes: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8]) -> Scalar {
 542:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 543:     h.update(SCHNORR_CHALLENGE_DOMAIN);
 544:     h.update(r_bytes);
 545:     h.update(vk_bytes);
 546:     h.update(&u32::try_from(msg.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 547:     h.update(msg);
 548:     let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
 549:     h.finalize_xof().fill(&mut wide);
 550:     Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide)
 551: }
 552: 
 553: fn deterministic_nonce(sk: &Scalar, vk_bytes: &[u8; 32], msg: &[u8]) -> Scalar {
 554:     // Audit M1 May 2026: domain bumped `-v1` → `-v2` because the
 555:     // input shape changed (vk is now mixed in). Old `-v1` signers
 556:     // and `-v2` signers under the same key produce DIFFERENT
 557:     // signatures over the same message — but verifiers don't see
 558:     // the nonce directly so the only observable change is the
 559:     // KAT vectors regenerated for `-v2`.
 560:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 561:     h.update(b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-nonce-v2");
 562:     h.update(sk.as_bytes());
 563:     h.update(vk_bytes);
 564:     h.update(&u32::try_from(msg.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 565:     h.update(msg);
 566:     let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
 567:     h.finalize_xof().fill(&mut wide);
 568:     let s = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide);
 569:     wide.zeroize();
 570:     s
 571: }
 572: 
 573: fn participant_list_digest(
 574:     pubkeys: &[[u8; 32]],
 575:     msg_hashes: &[[u8; 32]],
 576: ) -> [u8; 32] {
 577:     // Audit L4 May 2026 — additionally bind per-entry message
 578:     // digests into the participant list. Without this, two BN
 579:     // aggregates with the SAME signer set but DIFFERENT per-signer
 580:     // messages share the same `a_i = H(pk_i || L)` tags; the
 581:     // sig-binding via `c_i = challenge_hash(R_i, vk_i, msg_i)`
 582:     // still rejects a swap, but binding messages into L is
 583:     // defense-in-depth (a future protocol mistake that loses
 584:     // `msg_i` in `c_i` derivation still gets caught).
 585:     //
 586:     // Domain bumped `-v1` -> `-v2`. BN multi-sig only shipped
 587:     // working `bn_verify` in e5f58f7 (May 14 2026) so no aggregates
 588:     // have made it past the dev tree under `-v1`.
 589:     debug_assert_eq!(
 590:         pubkeys.len(),
 591:         msg_hashes.len(),
 592:         "participant_list_digest invariant: pubkeys and msg_hashes co-indexed",
 593:     );
 594:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 595:     h.update(b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-participant-list-v2");
 596:     h.update(&u32::try_from(pubkeys.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 597:     for (pk, mh) in pubkeys.iter().zip(msg_hashes.iter()) {
 598:         h.update(pk);
 599:         h.update(mh);
 600:     }
 601:     *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 602: }
 603: 
 604: fn msg_digest(msg: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
 605:     // Domain-tagged BLAKE3 digest of a single per-entry message. Used
 606:     // to bind per-signer messages into participant_list_digest (L4).
 607:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 608:     h.update(b"OL-sphinx-aggsig-msg-digest-v1");
 609:     h.update(&u32::try_from(msg.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX).to_be_bytes());
 610:     h.update(msg);
 611:     *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 612: }
 613: 
 614: fn bn_key_tag(pk: &[u8; 32], participant_l: &[u8; 32]) -> Scalar {
 615:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 616:     h.update(BN_KEY_TAG_DOMAIN);
 617:     h.update(pk);
 618:     h.update(participant_l);
 619:     let mut wide = [0u8; 64];
 620:     h.finalize_xof().fill(&mut wide);
 621:     Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&wide)
 622: }
 623: 
 624: // ── Helpers for the basepoint table ──────────────────────────────
 625: //
 626: // curve25519-dalek 4.x does basepoint multiplication via the
 627: // `Mul` impl on `&RistrettoBasepointTable`. Wrap it in a tiny
 628: // helper so call sites read naturally.
 629: 
 630: use curve25519_dalek::constants::RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
 631: 
 632: #[inline]
 633: fn basepoint_mul(k: &Scalar) -> RistrettoPoint {
 634:     RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE * k
 635: }

 744:     fn batch_verify_rejects_swapped_msgs() {
 745:         // Two signers, but verifier passes the SWAPPED messages.
 746:         // Each individual sig is valid for its OWN msg, but the
 747:         // (vk, msg) pairing is wrong → batch must reject.
 748:         let sk_a = SchnorrSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
 749:         let sk_b = SchnorrSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
 750:         let sig_a = sk_a.sign(b"alpha");
 751:         let sig_b = sk_b.sign(b"beta");
 752:         let entries = vec![
 753:             (sk_a.verifying_key(), b"beta".as_slice(), sig_a),
 754:             (sk_b.verifying_key(), b"alpha".as_slice(), sig_b),
 755:         ];
 756:         assert!(batch_verify(&entries).is_err());
 757:     }
 758: 
 759:     // ── Bellare-Neven multi-sig round trip ──────────────────────
 760: 
 761:     fn bn_setup(
 762:         n: usize,
 763:     ) -> (
 764:         Vec<SchnorrSigningKey>,
 765:         Vec<Vec<u8>>,
 766:         Vec<(SchnorrVerifyingKey, Vec<u8>, SchnorrSignature)>,
 767:     ) {
 768:         let sks: Vec<SchnorrSigningKey> = (0..n)
 769:             .map(|_| SchnorrSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng))
 770:             .collect();
 771:         let msgs: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (0..n)
 772:             .map(|i| {
 773:                 let mut v = b"BN-msg-".to_vec();
 774:                 v.push(i as u8);
 775:                 v
 776:             })
 777:             .collect();
 778:         let owned: Vec<(SchnorrVerifyingKey, Vec<u8>, SchnorrSignature)> = sks
 779:             .iter()
 780:             .zip(msgs.iter())
 781:             .map(|(sk, m)| (sk.verifying_key(), m.clone(), sk.sign(m)))
 782:             .collect();
 783:         (sks, msgs, owned)
 784:     }
 785: 
 786:     fn bn_borrow(
 787:         owned: &[(SchnorrVerifyingKey, Vec<u8>, SchnorrSignature)],
 788:     ) -> Vec<(SchnorrVerifyingKey, &[u8], SchnorrSignature)> {
 789:         owned.iter().map(|(vk, m, s)| (*vk, m.as_slice(), *s)).collect()
 790:     }
 791: 
 792:     fn bn_borrow_verify(
 793:         owned: &[(SchnorrVerifyingKey, Vec<u8>, SchnorrSignature)],
 794:     ) -> Vec<(SchnorrVerifyingKey, &[u8])> {
 795:         owned.iter().map(|(vk, m, _)| (*vk, m.as_slice())).collect()
 796:     }

   1: //! Sphinx Coherence core — packet build + peel with Ristretto255
   2: //! alpha blinding.
   3: //!
   4: //! Ties together [`primitives`] (key derivation, filler, ChaCha20)
   5: //! and [`header`] (slot construction + shift) with the Ristretto255
   6: //! group operations. Each hop's `alpha` is blinded so a global
   7: //! passive adversary sees uncorrelated random group elements at
   8: //! every relay.
   9: 
  10: use curve25519_dalek::constants::RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
  11: use curve25519_dalek::ristretto::{CompressedRistretto, RistrettoPoint};
  12: use curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar;
  13: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  14: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  15: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  16: 
  17: use crate::errors::{OnionError, OnionResult};
  18: use crate::hop::HopId;
  19: use crate::sphinx::header::{
  20:     build_header, peel_header, HeaderPeelOutcome, DESTINATION_MARKER,
  21: };
  22: use crate::sphinx::primitives::{
  23:     chacha20_xor_in_place, derive_hop_keys, HopKeys, HEADER_LEN, MAX_HOPS, PAYLOAD_LEN, SLOT_ID_LEN,
  24:     SLOT_LEN, SLOT_MAC_LEN,
  25: };
  26: 
  27: /// Sphinx wire protocol version.
  28: pub const SPHINX_VERSION: u8 = 3;
  29: 
  30: /// Length of a Ristretto255 compressed point.
  31: pub const RISTRETTO_POINT_LEN: usize = 32;
  32: 
  33: /// Total fixed packet size:
  34: /// version(1) + alpha(32) + mac(16) + header(HEADER_LEN) + payload(PAYLOAD_LEN).
  35: pub const SPHINX_PACKET_LEN: usize = 1 + RISTRETTO_POINT_LEN + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN + PAYLOAD_LEN;
  36: 
  37: /// Maximum user payload length. Two bytes reserved for length prefix.
  38: pub const SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD: usize = PAYLOAD_LEN - 2;
  39: 
  40: /// Hop descriptor for Sphinx Coherence circuits.
  41: ///
  42: /// Each hop has:
  43: /// - a [`HopId`] used by upstream relays to forward the packet.
  44: /// - a Ristretto255 static public key used for ECDH key agreement.
  45: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  46: pub struct SphinxHop {
  47:     pub id: HopId,
  48:     pub static_pk: RistrettoPoint,
  49: }
  50: 
  51: impl SphinxHop {
  52:     /// Construct from raw bytes. Refuses invalid Ristretto255 encodings.
  53:     pub fn new(id: [u8; SLOT_ID_LEN], static_pk_bytes: [u8; 32]) -> OnionResult<Self> {
  54:         let pk = CompressedRistretto::from_slice(&static_pk_bytes)
  55:             .map_err(|_| OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?
  56:             .decompress()
  57:             .ok_or(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?;
  58:         Ok(Self {
  59:             id: HopId::from_bytes(id),
  60:             static_pk: pk,
  61:         })
  62:     }
  63: 
  64:     /// Compress the static pubkey to wire bytes.
  65:     pub fn pubkey_bytes(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
  66:         self.static_pk.compress().to_bytes()
  67:     }
  68: }
  69: 
  70: /// Generate a fresh Sphinx static secret + corresponding public key.
  71: ///
  72: /// Audit I1 May 2026 (defense-in-depth): rejects the scalar-zero
  73: /// case so the returned pubkey is never the Ristretto255 identity
  74: /// point. Probability of hitting this naturally is ~2^-252 — an
  75: /// adversary cannot grind it — but the trivial early-exit costs
  76: /// nothing and removes the "identity scalar leaks every shared
  77: /// secret as zero" footgun. Re-rolls on the astronomically rare
  78: /// hit; bounded retry count keeps the function total.
  79: pub fn generate_static_keypair<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> (Scalar, RistrettoPoint) {
  80:     // 64 retries gives 2^-(252*64) probability of failure — beyond
  81:     // any thermodynamic bound. The loop is purely structural.
  82:     for _ in 0..64 {
  83:         let mut bytes = [0u8; 64];
  84:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut bytes);
  85:         let scalar = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&bytes);
  86:         if scalar == Scalar::ZERO {
  87:             continue;
  88:         }
  89:         let point = &scalar * RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
  90:         return (scalar, point);
  91:     }
  92:     // Unreachable in any universe with a working RNG. If the RNG is
  93:     // broken (all-zeros), the daemon should fail loudly rather than
  94:     // silently return a zero-scalar keypair — panic preserves the
  95:     // invariant that callers never observe a zero scalar.
  96:     panic!("generate_static_keypair: RNG returned 64 consecutive zero scalars (broken RNG)")
  97: }
  98: 
  99: /// Sphinx Coherence wire packet (fixed [`SPHINX_PACKET_LEN`] bytes).
 100: #[derive(Clone)]
 101: pub struct SphinxPacket {
 102:     bytes: [u8; SPHINX_PACKET_LEN],
 103: }
 104: 
 105: impl SphinxPacket {
 106:     /// Wrap raw wire bytes after validating length + version.
 107:     pub fn from_bytes(b: &[u8]) -> OnionResult<Self> {
 108:         if b.len() != SPHINX_PACKET_LEN {
 109:             return Err(OnionError::BadFrameSize {
 110:                 got: b.len(),
 111:                 expected: SPHINX_PACKET_LEN,
 112:             });
 113:         }
 114:         if b[0] != SPHINX_VERSION {
 115:             return Err(OnionError::UnsupportedVersion {
 116:                 got: b[0],
 117:                 supported: SPHINX_VERSION,
 118:             });
 119:         }
 120:         let mut bytes = [0u8; SPHINX_PACKET_LEN];
 121:         bytes.copy_from_slice(b);
 122:         Ok(Self { bytes })
 123:     }
 124: 
 125:     /// View the wire bytes.
 126:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; SPHINX_PACKET_LEN] {
 127:         &self.bytes
 128:     }
 129: 
 130:     fn alpha(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
 131:         let mut a = [0u8; 32];
 132:         a.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[1..33]);
 133:         a
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     fn mac(&self) -> [u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN] {
 137:         let mut m = [0u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN];
 138:         m.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[33..33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN]);
 139:         m
 140:     }
 141: 
 142:     fn header(&self) -> &[u8] {
 143:         let start = 33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN;
 144:         &self.bytes[start..start + HEADER_LEN]
 145:     }
 146: 
 147:     fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] {
 148:         let start = 33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN;
 149:         &self.bytes[start..start + PAYLOAD_LEN]
 150:     }
 151: }

 155:         f.debug_struct("SphinxPacket")
 156:             .field("version", &self.bytes[0])
 157:             .field("len", &self.bytes.len())
 158:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 159:     }
 160: }

 165:     }

 169: /// Outcome of [`peel_sphinx_layer`].
 170: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 171: pub enum SphinxPeelOutcome {
 172:     /// Forward to the next hop with the new packet.
 173:     Forward {
 174:         next_hop: HopId,
 175:         next_packet: SphinxPacket,
 176:     },
 177:     /// This relay is the destination — deliver the payload.
 178:     Deliver { payload: Vec<u8> },
 179:     /// Audit M4: authenticated cover-traffic packet. The destination's
 180:     /// cryptographic check matched the per-circuit cover-trailer MAC,
 181:     /// so this is a Row-6 cover packet — drop silently without
 182:     /// surfacing the payload to the application.
 183:     ///
 184:     /// Replaces the pre-M4 plaintext-sentinel detection, which was
 185:     /// forgeable: a network attacker could bit-flip the first 8 bytes
 186:     /// of any real payload to look like the sentinel and cause the
 187:     /// destination to drop a legitimate packet. The MAC binding makes
 188:     /// the cover claim unforgeable without the per-hop shared key.
 189:     Cover,
 190: }
 191: 
 192: /// Build a Sphinx Coherence onion packet for delivery along the
 193: /// chosen circuit.
 194: ///
 195: /// - `sender_eph_sk`: a fresh per-circuit ephemeral Ristretto255 secret
 196: ///   (generated via [`generate_static_keypair`] then discarded after build).
 197: /// - `circuit`: ordered hops, last is the destination.
 198: /// - `payload`: user payload bytes (up to [`SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD`]).
 199: /// - `rng`: source of random pad bytes for the destination header.
 200: pub fn build_sphinx_onion<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 201:     sender_eph_sk: &Scalar,
 202:     circuit: &[SphinxHop],
 203:     payload: &[u8],
 204:     rng: &mut R,
 205: ) -> OnionResult<SphinxPacket> {
 206:     if circuit.is_empty() {
 207:         return Err(OnionError::EmptyCircuit);
 208:     }
 209:     if circuit.len() > MAX_HOPS {
 210:         return Err(OnionError::TooManyHops {
 211:             got: circuit.len(),
 212:             max: MAX_HOPS,
 213:         });
 214:     }
 215:     if payload.len() > SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD {
 216:         return Err(OnionError::PayloadOversize {
 217:             got: payload.len(),
 218:             max: SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD,
 219:         });
 220:     }
 221: 
 222:     // ── Step 1: precompute the alpha chain + shared secrets + hop keys.
 223:     let n = circuit.len();
 224:     let alpha_0 = sender_eph_sk * RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
 225:     let mut cumulative_blind = Scalar::ONE;
 226:     let mut hop_keys: Vec<HopKeys> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
 227:     let mut alpha_i = alpha_0;
 228: 
 229:     for hop in circuit.iter() {
 230:         let alpha_bytes = alpha_i.compress().to_bytes();
 231:         // Shared secret: sender_eph_sk * cumulative_blind * hop.pk.
 232:         let shared_point = (sender_eph_sk * cumulative_blind) * hop.static_pk;
 233:         let shared_bytes = shared_point.compress().to_bytes();
 234:         if shared_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 235:             return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 236:         }
 237:         let keys = derive_hop_keys(&shared_bytes, &alpha_bytes);
 238:         // Compute blinding scalar for next hop. Audit L1 May 2026:
 239:         // wide reduction from 64-byte seed → bias-free scalar.
 240:         let b_i = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&keys.blinding_seed);
 241:         hop_keys.push(keys);
 242:         // Update for next iter.
 243:         cumulative_blind *= b_i;
 244:         alpha_i = b_i * alpha_i;
 245:     }
 246:     // alpha_i is now the alpha that the destination's "next" hop
 247:     // would receive — unused (no next hop after destination).
 248: 
 249:     // ── Step 2: build the routing-info header.
 250:     let mut next_hop_ids: Vec<[u8; SLOT_ID_LEN]> = circuit
 251:         .iter()
 252:         .skip(1)
 253:         .map(|h| *h.id.as_bytes())
 254:         .collect();
 255:     next_hop_ids.push(DESTINATION_MARKER);
 256:     debug_assert_eq!(next_hop_ids.len(), n);
 257: 
 258:     let n_relays = n - 1;
 259:     let filler_len = n_relays * SLOT_LEN;
 260:     let pad_len = HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN - filler_len;
 261:     let mut random_pad = vec![0u8; pad_len];
 262:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut random_pad);
 263: 
 264:     let built = build_header(&hop_keys, &next_hop_ids, &random_pad);
 265: 
 266:     // ── Step 3: build the encrypted payload (right-to-left).
 267:     let mut payload_buf = [0u8; PAYLOAD_LEN];
 268:     // Length prefix (2 bytes) + payload. The length is bounded above by
 269:     // SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD (= PAYLOAD_LEN - 2 ≤ u16::MAX), enforced
 270:     // by the early-return check above, so the cast is invariant-safe.
 271:     #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
 272:     let plen_u16 = payload.len() as u16;
 273:     payload_buf[..2].copy_from_slice(&plen_u16.to_be_bytes());
 274:     payload_buf[2..2 + payload.len()].copy_from_slice(payload);
 275:     // Encrypt in-place with each hop's payload stream, innermost first.
 276:     // No per-hop Vec allocation — chacha20 XORs directly into payload_buf.
 277:     for keys in hop_keys.iter().rev() {
 278:         chacha20_xor_in_place(&keys.payload_stream, &mut payload_buf);
 279:     }
 280: 
 281:     // ── Step 4: assemble outermost packet.
 282:     let mut bytes = [0u8; SPHINX_PACKET_LEN];
 283:     bytes[0] = SPHINX_VERSION;
 284:     bytes[1..33].copy_from_slice(&alpha_0.compress().to_bytes());
 285:     bytes[33..33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN].copy_from_slice(&built.mac);
 286:     bytes[33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN..33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN].copy_from_slice(&built.header);
 287:     bytes[33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&payload_buf);
 288: 
 289:     // Zeroize hop keys explicitly (they zeroize on drop, but be defensive).
 290:     for mut k in hop_keys {
 291:         k.header_stream.zeroize();
 292:         k.payload_stream.zeroize();
 293:         k.mac_key.zeroize();
 294:         k.blinding_seed.zeroize();
 295:     }
 296:     payload_buf.zeroize();
 297: 
 298:     Ok(SphinxPacket { bytes })
 299: }
 300: 
 301: /// Walk the Sphinx blinding chain to compute the FINAL-HOP shared
 302: /// secret without building the full packet.
 303: ///
 304: /// Used by the cover-traffic builder (audit M4) to derive the
 305: /// destination's per-circuit shared key, which seeds the
 306: /// authenticated cover trailer that replaces the pre-M4 plaintext
 307: /// sentinel. Returning only the final-hop key (not the intermediates)
 308: /// keeps callers from accidentally accessing a relay's session
 309: /// material — they only see what the destination would derive itself.
 310: pub fn compute_final_hop_shared_key(
 311:     sender_eph_sk: &Scalar,
 312:     circuit: &[SphinxHop],
 313: ) -> OnionResult<[u8; 32]> {
 314:     if circuit.is_empty() {
 315:         return Err(OnionError::EmptyCircuit);
 316:     }
 317:     if circuit.len() > MAX_HOPS {
 318:         return Err(OnionError::TooManyHops {
 319:             got: circuit.len(),
 320:             max: MAX_HOPS,
 321:         });
 322:     }
 323:     let mut cumulative_blind = Scalar::ONE;
 324:     let mut alpha_i = sender_eph_sk * RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
 325:     let last_idx = circuit.len() - 1;
 326:     for (idx, hop) in circuit.iter().enumerate() {
 327:         let alpha_bytes = alpha_i.compress().to_bytes();
 328:         let shared_point = (sender_eph_sk * cumulative_blind) * hop.static_pk;
 329:         let shared_bytes = shared_point.compress().to_bytes();
 330:         if shared_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 331:             return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 332:         }
 333:         if idx == last_idx {
 334:             return Ok(shared_bytes);
 335:         }
 336:         let keys = derive_hop_keys(&shared_bytes, &alpha_bytes);
 337:         // Wide reduction (audit L1) — must match build_sphinx_onion.
 338:         let b_i = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&keys.blinding_seed);
 339:         cumulative_blind *= b_i;
 340:         alpha_i = b_i * alpha_i;
 341:     }
 342:     // Unreachable: empty-circuit caught above; last_idx always reached.
 343:     Err(OnionError::Internal("compute_final_hop_shared_key: chain walk did not terminate"))
 344: }
 345: 
 346: /// Peel one layer of a Sphinx Coherence packet at this relay.
 347: ///
 348: /// # Replay defense (audit L2 May 2026)
 349: ///
 350: /// **This function does NOT provide replay protection by itself.**
 351: /// A passive observer who captured an old packet can re-inject it
 352: /// here, and `peel_sphinx_layer` will happily process it again and
 353: /// produce the same `SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward` (or `Deliver`)
 354: /// result. This is standard Sphinx behavior — replay detection is
 355: /// the daemon's responsibility, not the packet primitive's.
 356: ///
 357: /// Daemons that route this primitive MUST maintain a recently-seen
 358: /// bloom filter (or set) keyed on the per-packet `shared_secret`
 359: /// digest (or equivalently the encrypted MAC field) and drop any
 360: /// packet whose digest is already in the filter. Tor and Loopix
 361: /// both apply this same defense at the relay level.
 362: ///
 363: /// A practical recipe:
 364: /// 1. Compute `tag = BLAKE3("ol-sphinx-replay-tag-v1" || shared_secret)`
 365: ///    after the relay decapsulates `alpha`.
 366: /// 2. Check `tag` against a circular bloom filter sized for the
 367: ///    relay's expected packets-per-window (e.g. 1M slots, 1% FPR,
 368: ///    rotate every 10 min).
 369: /// 3. If tag is present → drop the packet, return without
 370: ///    forwarding. Otherwise → insert `tag` and proceed.
 371: ///
 372: /// The relay's drop on replay is silent — replaying a known-good
 373: /// packet does not yield any usable oracle signal because the bloom
 374: /// check happens before any wire-visible side-effect.
 375: pub fn peel_sphinx_layer(
 376:     relay_sk: &Scalar,
 377:     packet: &SphinxPacket,
 378: ) -> OnionResult<SphinxPeelOutcome> {
 379:     let alpha_bytes = packet.alpha();
 380:     if alpha_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 381:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 382:     }
 383:     let alpha_point = CompressedRistretto::from_slice(&alpha_bytes)
 384:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?
 385:         .decompress()
 386:         .ok_or(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?;
 387:     let shared_point = relay_sk * alpha_point;
 388:     let shared_bytes = shared_point.compress().to_bytes();
 389:     if shared_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 390:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 391:     }
 392:     let keys = derive_hop_keys(&shared_bytes, &alpha_bytes);
 393: 
 394:     // Verify + peel header.
 395:     let mac = packet.mac();
 396:     let outcome = peel_header(&keys, packet.header(), &mac).map_err(|_| OnionError::AeadFail)?;
 397: 
 398:     // Decrypt one payload layer in-place — no separate keystream Vec.
 399:     let mut payload = vec![0u8; PAYLOAD_LEN];
 400:     payload.copy_from_slice(packet.payload());
 401:     chacha20_xor_in_place(&keys.payload_stream, &mut payload);
 402: 
 403:     match outcome {
 404:         HeaderPeelOutcome::Deliver => {
 405:             // Extract user payload via length prefix.
 406:             let plen = u16::from_be_bytes([payload[0], payload[1]]) as usize;
 407:             if plen > SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD {
 408:                 return Err(OnionError::Internal("destination payload length oversize"));
 409:             }
 410:             let user_payload = &payload[2..2 + plen];
 411:             // Audit M4: authenticated cover-traffic detection. The
 412:             // sender, knowing its own ephemeral key and this hop's
 413:             // static key, can derive the same shared_bytes we just
 414:             // derived above — and only the sender can produce the
 415:             // matching MAC trailer. A network attacker bit-flipping
 416:             // the payload to forge cover status can't compute a valid
 417:             // tag without the shared key, so a forged "cover" status
 418:             // is rejected at probability 1 - 2^-128.
 419:             if crate::sphinx::cover::is_cover_payload_authenticated(
 420:                 &shared_bytes,
 421:                 user_payload,
 422:             ) {
 423:                 return Ok(SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover);
 424:             }
 425:             let mut user_payload_owned = vec![0u8; plen];
 426:             user_payload_owned.copy_from_slice(user_payload);
 427:             Ok(SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver {
 428:                 payload: user_payload_owned,
 429:             })
 430:         }
 431:         HeaderPeelOutcome::Forward {
 432:             next_hop_id,
 433:             next_header,
 434:             next_mac,
 435:         } => {
 436:             // Blind alpha for the next hop. Audit L1: wide reduction.
 437:             let b_scalar = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&keys.blinding_seed);
 438:             let next_alpha = b_scalar * alpha_point;
 439:             let next_alpha_bytes = next_alpha.compress().to_bytes();
 440: 
 441:             // Assemble next packet.
 442:             let mut bytes = [0u8; SPHINX_PACKET_LEN];
 443:             bytes[0] = SPHINX_VERSION;
 444:             bytes[1..33].copy_from_slice(&next_alpha_bytes);
 445:             bytes[33..33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN].copy_from_slice(&next_mac);
 446:             bytes[33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN..33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN].copy_from_slice(&next_header);
 447:             bytes[33 + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&payload);
 448: 
 449:             Ok(SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward {
 450:                 next_hop: HopId::from_bytes(next_hop_id),
 451:                 next_packet: SphinxPacket { bytes },
 452:             })
 453:         }
 454:     }
 455: }

 561:         let mut packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &circuit, b"max-hops", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
