   1: //! Row 6 — cover traffic primitive for Sphinx Coherence.
   2: //!
   3: //! Sphinx alone defeats SPATIAL correlation across relays (alpha
   4: //! blinding makes same-circuit packets pairwise indistinguishable
   5: //! at every hop). It does NOT defeat TEMPORAL correlation: a global
   6: //! passive adversary watching every relay's timeline can correlate
   7: //! "packet ingress at R1 at time T" with "packet egress from R2 at
   8: //! T+δ" for the same circuit.
   9: //!
  10: //! Cover traffic closes this gap. Each daemon emits "cover" Sphinx
  11: //! packets at random intervals along random circuits. On the wire,
  12: //! cover packets are indistinguishable from real packets (same
  13: //! size, same encryption, same structure). An observer cannot tell
  14: //! which packets carry real user data and which are cover.
  15: //!
  16: //! ## Design
  17: //!
  18: //! - **Cover-packet builder**: builds a valid Sphinx packet bound
  19: //!   for a "self-mesh" destination (the sender's own pubkey) or a
  20: //!   trusted-relay pool. The destination decrypts to discover the
  21: //!   payload is the cover sentinel + drops it.
  22: //! - **Poisson scheduler**: the daemon emits cover packets according
  23: //!   to a Poisson process with configurable rate λ. The
  24: //!   exponentially-distributed inter-arrival times make the cover
  25: //!   traffic indistinguishable from "burst-then-idle" patterns of
  26: //!   real traffic.
  27: //! - **Cover sentinel**: a fixed magic prefix (8 bytes) in the
  28: //!   payload tells the destination "this is cover, discard." The
  29: //!   sentinel is encrypted inside the onion so observers can't
  30: //!   distinguish cover from real on the wire.
  31: //!
  32: //! ## What this layer is NOT
  33: //!
  34: //! This is the PRIMITIVE for cover traffic, not the full mixnet.
  35: //! It provides:
  36: //! - A way to build cover packets.
  37: //! - A scheduler that yields wait-times.
  38: //!
  39: //! It does NOT provide:
  40: //! - Active-inference cover (Tier 2 item 6) — adaptive rate that
  41: //!   maximizes observer entropy. That's a future polish.
  42: //! - Loop circuits + reply-block (SURB) integration — separate ship.
  43: //! - Daemon-level wiring (the actual "emit a packet now" call).
  44: //!
  45: //! ## References
  46: //!
  47: //! - Loopix (Piotrowska et al. 2017): the canonical mixnet cover
  48: //!   traffic design using Poisson padding.
  49: //! - Tor's "Padding Spec" (PROP254): a simpler client-relay cover
  50: //!   scheme without true mix semantics.
  51: //!
  52: //! ## Example: equalized-rate cover scheduling
  53: //!
  54: //! ```
  55: //! use ol_onion::sphinx::cover::{CoverScheduler, RateEqualizer};
  56: //!
  57: //! // Aim for 5 packets/sec on the wire regardless of real traffic.
  58: //! let mut eq = RateEqualizer::new(5.0);
  59: //! eq.observe_real_emission(1_000);
  60: //! eq.observe_real_emission(1_500);
  61: //! eq.observe_real_emission(2_000);
  62: //! // Real ≈ 2 Hz, so cover fills ≈ 3 Hz of the budget.
  63: //! let cover_rate = eq.current_cover_rate();
  64: //! assert!(cover_rate > 0.0 && cover_rate <= 5.0);
  65: //!
  66: //! // Schedule the next cover packet using an Exp(λ) sample.
  67: //! let mut sched = CoverScheduler::new(cover_rate.max(0.001), [0x42; 32]);
  68: //! let wait_ms = sched.next_wait_ms();
  69: //! assert!(wait_ms < 60_000, "wait sample bounded under normal rates");
  70: //! ```
  71: 
  72: use blake3::Hasher;
  73: use curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar;
  74: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  75: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  76: 
  77: use crate::errors::{OnionError, OnionResult};
  78: use crate::sphinx::core::{
  79:     build_sphinx_onion, compute_final_hop_shared_key, SphinxHop, SphinxPacket,
  80: };
  81: 
  82: /// Cover-packet sentinel prefix. Provides a fast-path filter on
  83: /// receive so the BLAKE3 verification only runs on packets that
  84: /// could plausibly be cover (probability 2^-64 of a random payload
  85: /// passing the prefix gate). The sentinel is INSIDE the encrypted
  86: /// Sphinx onion, so a network observer cannot detect it; only the
  87: /// final destination sees the cleartext payload.
  88: ///
  89: /// **Audit M4 hardening note:** the sentinel alone is NOT
  90: /// sufficient to authenticate cover status — a network attacker
  91: /// who can bit-flip the encrypted payload at any relay could
  92: /// transform a real packet's first 8 bytes to look like the
  93: /// sentinel and cause the destination to drop a legitimate packet.
  94: /// The authenticated trailer ([`COVER_TRAILER_LEN`] bytes) appended
  95: /// after the random body cryptographically binds cover status to
  96: /// the per-hop shared key — unforgeable without that key.
  97: pub const COVER_SENTINEL: &[u8; 8] = b"OL-COVER";
  98: 
  99: /// Length of the authenticated cover-trailer MAC. 128 bits gives
 100: /// 2^-128 forgery probability — way below practical concern. Audit M4.
 101: pub const COVER_TRAILER_LEN: usize = 16;
 102: 
 103: /// Minimum payload size for cover packets (after the sentinel
 104: /// prefix). Cover packets pad up to a configurable size so they
 105: /// match the size distribution of real traffic.
 106: pub const COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN: usize = 64;
 107: 
 108: /// Default Poisson rate λ for the cover-traffic scheduler, in
 109: /// packets per second. Higher = more cover, more bandwidth cost.
 110: /// Loopix paper suggests λ_loop ≈ 1 pkt/sec; daemon can tune up or
 111: /// down based on bandwidth budget.
 112: pub const COVER_DEFAULT_RATE_HZ: f64 = 1.0;
 113: 
 114: /// BLAKE3 domain separator for the cover-trailer MAC derivation.
 115: /// Bumping the suffix invalidates all pre-existing cover packets
 116: /// in flight — useful if the spec changes.
 117: const COVER_TRAILER_DOMAIN: &str = "ol-sphinx-cover-trailer-v1";
 118: 
 119: /// Compute the authenticated cover trailer over `cover_body` keyed
 120: /// by the destination's per-circuit shared key. Audit M4.
 121: ///
 122: /// Implementation: BLAKE3 `derive_key(domain, shared_key)` produces
 123: /// a context-bound MAC key, fed into a keyed BLAKE3 hash over the
 124: /// body. Truncated to 16 bytes — sufficient since BLAKE3 outputs are
 125: /// pseudorandom and the trailer's role is unforgeability-of-status,
 126: /// not collision resistance over an enumerable space.
 127: pub(crate) fn compute_cover_trailer(
 128:     shared_key: &[u8; 32],
 129:     cover_body: &[u8],
 130: ) -> [u8; COVER_TRAILER_LEN] {
 131:     let mac_key = blake3::derive_key(COVER_TRAILER_DOMAIN, shared_key);
 132:     let mut h = Hasher::new_keyed(&mac_key);
 133:     h.update(cover_body);
 134:     let digest = h.finalize();
 135:     let mut tag = [0u8; COVER_TRAILER_LEN];
 136:     tag.copy_from_slice(&digest.as_bytes()[..COVER_TRAILER_LEN]);
 137:     tag
 138: }
 139: 
 140: /// Constant-time test: does `payload` carry a valid authenticated
 141: /// cover trailer keyed by `shared_key`? Audit M4.
 142: ///
 143: /// Returns true iff:
 144: ///   1. `payload.len() >= COVER_SENTINEL.len() + COVER_TRAILER_LEN`,
 145: ///   2. `payload[..COVER_SENTINEL.len()] == COVER_SENTINEL`,
 146: ///   3. The trailing 16 bytes equal the BLAKE3-keyed MAC over
 147: ///      `payload[..len - COVER_TRAILER_LEN]`.
 148: ///
 149: /// The body fed to the MAC INCLUDES the sentinel — binding the
 150: /// sentinel prefix into the tag so an attacker can't append a
 151: /// pre-computed valid trailer onto a random payload that happens
 152: /// to start with a forged sentinel.
 153: ///
 154: /// The prefix check is non-constant-time (sentinel is public), but
 155: /// the trailer compare uses `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` so leaking
 156: /// fine-grained body content via tag comparison timing is not
 157: /// possible.
 158: pub fn is_cover_payload_authenticated(
 159:     shared_key: &[u8; 32],
 160:     payload: &[u8],
 161: ) -> bool {
 162:     if payload.len() < COVER_SENTINEL.len() + COVER_TRAILER_LEN {
 163:         return false;
 164:     }
 165:     if &payload[..COVER_SENTINEL.len()] != COVER_SENTINEL {
 166:         return false;
 167:     }
 168:     let body_end = payload.len() - COVER_TRAILER_LEN;
 169:     let body = &payload[..body_end];
 170:     let actual_tag = &payload[body_end..];
 171:     let expected = compute_cover_trailer(shared_key, body);
 172:     bool::from(expected.ct_eq(actual_tag))
 173: }
 174: 
 175: /// Identify whether a delivered payload carries the COVER_SENTINEL
 176: /// prefix (FAST PATH; does NOT authenticate).
 177: ///
 178: /// **Pre-M4 callers using this for cover detection are insecure** —
 179: /// the sentinel-alone gate is forgeable by a network attacker who
 180: /// bit-flips a real payload's first 8 bytes. Use
 181: /// [`is_cover_payload_authenticated`] instead, which the Sphinx
 182: /// peel layer now invokes internally before returning
 183: /// [`crate::sphinx::core::SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover`].
 184: ///
 185: /// Retained ONLY as a quick-rejection helper for benchmarks +
 186: /// fast-path tests. Production receive paths MUST go through
 187: /// the authenticated check.
 188: #[deprecated(
 189:     since = "0.21.0-alpha",
 190:     note = "audit M4 — use is_cover_payload_authenticated; the plaintext-prefix check is forgeable"
 191: )]
 192: pub fn is_cover_payload(payload: &[u8]) -> bool {
 193:     payload.len() >= COVER_SENTINEL.len()
 194:         && &payload[..COVER_SENTINEL.len()] == COVER_SENTINEL
 195: }
 196: 
 197: /// Build a cover Sphinx packet bound for `circuit` (typically a
 198: /// self-mesh destination — the sender's own pubkey — or a trusted
 199: /// cover-pool relay).
 200: ///
 201: /// Audit M4 wire format:
 202: ///
 203: /// ```text
 204: ///   payload = COVER_SENTINEL (8 bytes)
 205: ///           || random body  (cover_size bytes, ≥ COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN)
 206: ///           || MAC trailer  (COVER_TRAILER_LEN bytes, BLAKE3-keyed
 207: ///                            by the destination's per-circuit shared key)
 208: /// ```
 209: ///
 210: /// The destination derives the same shared key from its own static
 211: /// secret + the incoming alpha, recomputes the MAC, and
 212: /// constant-time-compares against the trailer. Only a packet from a
 213: /// sender who knows the destination's static pubkey (and chose this
 214: /// circuit) can produce a valid trailer — the MAC binds cover
 215: /// status to the circuit's secret session material.
 216: pub fn build_cover_packet<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 217:     sender_eph_sk: &Scalar,
 218:     circuit: &[SphinxHop],
 219:     cover_size: usize,
 220:     rng: &mut R,
 221: ) -> OnionResult<SphinxPacket> {
 222:     if cover_size < COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN {
 223:         return Err(OnionError::Internal(
 224:             "cover payload below minimum size",
 225:         ));
 226:     }
 227:     if circuit.is_empty() {
 228:         return Err(OnionError::EmptyCircuit);
 229:     }
 230:     // Walk the blinding chain to derive what the destination will
 231:     // see as its shared key. Failing here surfaces small-order or
 232:     // empty-circuit errors before we spend cycles on the packet build.
 233:     let dest_shared_key = compute_final_hop_shared_key(sender_eph_sk, circuit)?;
 234:     // Layout: sentinel (8) || random body (cover_size) || MAC (16).
 235:     let total_len = COVER_SENTINEL.len() + cover_size + COVER_TRAILER_LEN;
 236:     let mut payload = vec![0u8; total_len];
 237:     payload[..COVER_SENTINEL.len()].copy_from_slice(COVER_SENTINEL);
 238:     let body_start = COVER_SENTINEL.len();
 239:     let body_end = body_start + cover_size;
 240:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut payload[body_start..body_end]);
 241:     let trailer = compute_cover_trailer(&dest_shared_key, &payload[..body_end]);
 242:     payload[body_end..].copy_from_slice(&trailer);
 243:     build_sphinx_onion(sender_eph_sk, circuit, &payload, rng)
 244: }
 245: 
 246: /// Poisson-process scheduler for cover-packet emission times.
 247: ///
 248: /// Maintains a current λ (rate) and a deterministic-on-seed RNG so
 249: /// emission timing can be audited without exposing future emission
 250: /// times to anyone but the daemon.
 251: ///
 252: /// ## Usage
 253: ///
 254: /// ```ignore
 255: /// let mut sched = CoverScheduler::new(rate_hz, seed);
 256: /// loop {
 257: ///     let wait_ms = sched.next_wait_ms();
 258: ///     sleep(wait_ms);
 259: ///     emit_cover_packet();
 260: /// }
 261: /// ```
 262: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 263: pub struct CoverScheduler {
 264:     rate_hz: f64,
 265:     /// Internal RNG state (seeded BLAKE3 keystream). Survives clone
 266:     /// for replay, but each `next_wait_ms` advances it.
 267:     counter: u64,
 268:     seed: [u8; 32],
 269: }
 270: 
 271: impl CoverScheduler {
 272:     /// New scheduler with rate `rate_hz` (packets per second) seeded
 273:     /// by `seed`. Different seeds give independent emission patterns.
 274:     pub fn new(rate_hz: f64, seed: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
 275:         assert!(rate_hz > 0.0, "rate must be positive");
 276:         Self {
 277:             rate_hz,
 278:             counter: 0,
 279:             seed,
 280:         }
 281:     }
 282: 
 283:     /// Construct with the default rate ([`COVER_DEFAULT_RATE_HZ`]).
 284:     pub fn with_default_rate(seed: [u8; 32]) -> Self {
 285:         Self::new(COVER_DEFAULT_RATE_HZ, seed)
 286:     }
 287: 
 288:     /// Sample the next inter-arrival time in milliseconds from the
 289:     /// exponential distribution Exp(λ).
 290:     ///
 291:     /// For a Poisson process with rate λ packets/sec, inter-arrival
 292:     /// times are exponentially distributed with mean 1/λ.
 293:     pub fn next_wait_ms(&mut self) -> u64 {
 294:         // Sample a uniform u in (0, 1] from the BLAKE3 keystream.
 295:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 296:         h.update(b"OL-cover-scheduler-v1");
 297:         h.update(&self.seed);
 298:         h.update(&self.counter.to_le_bytes());
 299:         let digest = h.finalize();
 300:         let bytes = digest.as_bytes();
 301:         // First 8 bytes → u64 → scale to (0, 1].
 302:         let raw = u64::from_le_bytes([
 303:             bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3], bytes[4], bytes[5], bytes[6], bytes[7],
 304:         ]);
 305:         // Avoid raw == 0 to keep u > 0.
 306:         let raw_nonzero = raw.max(1);
 307:         let u = (raw_nonzero as f64) / (u64::MAX as f64);
 308:         // Exponential sample: -ln(u) / λ in seconds. u ∈ (0, 1] →
 309:         // ln(u) ≤ 0 → wait_sec ≥ 0 by construction, so sign-loss
 310:         // is impossible. Clamp to u64::MAX as defense-in-depth.
 311:         let wait_sec = -(u.ln()) / self.rate_hz;
 312:         let wait_ms_f = (wait_sec * 1000.0).clamp(0.0, u64::MAX as f64);
 313:         #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_sign_loss)]
 314:         let wait_ms = wait_ms_f as u64;
 315:         self.counter = self.counter.wrapping_add(1);
 316:         wait_ms
 317:     }
 318: 
 319:     /// Current configured rate.
 320:     pub fn rate_hz(&self) -> f64 {
 321:         self.rate_hz
 322:     }
 323: 
 324:     /// Update the rate. Useful for adaptive-rate control (e.g.
 325:     /// throttle during low-bandwidth conditions). Future polish:
 326:     /// Tier 2 active-inference will set this from observer-entropy
 327:     /// minimization.
 328:     pub fn set_rate_hz(&mut self, rate_hz: f64) {
 329:         assert!(rate_hz > 0.0, "rate must be positive");
 330:         self.rate_hz = rate_hz;
 331:     }
 332: }
 333: 
 334: /// Adaptive rate equalizer for cover traffic.
 335: ///
 336: /// Maintains a CONSTANT total emission rate (cover + real) regardless
 337: /// of the real-traffic load. When real traffic spikes, cover rate
 338: /// drops; when real traffic is idle, cover rate rises to fill the
 339: /// gap. An observer sees a uniform-rate output stream and cannot
 340: /// infer "is there real traffic now?" from packet timing alone.
 341: ///
 342: /// ## How it differs from plain Poisson cover
 343: ///
 344: /// - Plain Poisson: cover at fixed λ. Total observed rate = real_rate + λ.
 345: ///   An observer can subtract λ to estimate real_rate.
 346: /// - Equalized: cover_rate = max(0, target_total - real_rate). Total
 347: ///   observed rate = target_total constant. Observer sees no signal.
 348: ///
 349: /// ## Usage
 350: ///
 351: /// ```ignore
 352: /// let mut eq = RateEqualizer::new(target_total_hz=5.0);
 353: /// // Daemon updates observed real rate every time it emits a real packet.
 354: /// eq.observe_real_emission(now_ms);
 355: /// // Daemon queries current cover rate when scheduling next cover packet.
 356: /// let cover_rate = eq.current_cover_rate();
 357: /// scheduler.set_rate_hz(cover_rate.max(0.001)); // floor to avoid stall
 358: /// ```
 359: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 360: pub struct RateEqualizer {
 361:     target_total_hz: f64,
 362:     /// Sliding-window observed real rate (Hz). Exponentially weighted.
 363:     observed_real_rate: f64,
 364:     /// EWMA half-life in seconds. Determines how quickly the equalizer
 365:     /// reacts to bursts vs steady state.
 366:     half_life_sec: f64,
 367:     /// Wall-clock ms of last observed real emission.
 368:     last_emit_ms: u64,
 369: }
 370: 
 371: /// Default EWMA half-life: 30 seconds. Bursts of real traffic
 372: /// pull cover rate down for ~30 sec, then it recovers.
 373: pub const RATE_EQ_DEFAULT_HALF_LIFE_SEC: f64 = 30.0;
 374: 
 375: impl RateEqualizer {
 376:     /// Construct an equalizer targeting `target_total_hz` packets per
 377:     /// second on the wire. Cover fills whatever real doesn't supply.
 378:     pub fn new(target_total_hz: f64) -> Self {
 379:         assert!(target_total_hz > 0.0, "target rate must be positive");
 380:         Self {
 381:             target_total_hz,
 382:             observed_real_rate: 0.0,
 383:             half_life_sec: RATE_EQ_DEFAULT_HALF_LIFE_SEC,
 384:             last_emit_ms: 0,
 385:         }
 386:     }
 387: 
 388:     /// Set the EWMA half-life. Smaller = react faster to bursts;
 389:     /// larger = smoother but slower to adapt.
 390:     pub fn set_half_life_sec(&mut self, half_life_sec: f64) {
 391:         assert!(half_life_sec > 0.0, "half_life must be positive");
 392:         self.half_life_sec = half_life_sec;
 393:     }
 394: 
 395:     /// Notify the equalizer that a real packet was emitted at
 396:     /// `now_ms` wall-clock milliseconds. Updates the EWMA.
 397:     pub fn observe_real_emission(&mut self, now_ms: u64) {
 398:         if self.last_emit_ms == 0 {
 399:             // First observation; seed with target rate as initial guess.
 400:             self.observed_real_rate = 1.0;
 401:             self.last_emit_ms = now_ms;
 402:             return;
 403:         }
 404:         let dt_sec = (now_ms.saturating_sub(self.last_emit_ms)) as f64 / 1000.0;
 405:         if dt_sec <= 0.0 {
 406:             return;
 407:         }
 408:         // Instantaneous rate from this gap.
 409:         let instant_rate = 1.0 / dt_sec;
 410:         // EWMA weight from half-life: alpha = 1 - 0.5^(dt / half_life)
 411:         let alpha = 1.0 - 0.5f64.powf(dt_sec / self.half_life_sec);
 412:         let alpha = alpha.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 413:         self.observed_real_rate =
 414:             (1.0 - alpha) * self.observed_real_rate + alpha * instant_rate;
 415:         self.last_emit_ms = now_ms;
 416:     }
 417: 
 418:     /// Notify that wall-clock time has advanced even without real
 419:     /// emissions. Used to DECAY the observed_real_rate toward zero
 420:     /// during idle periods so cover rate rises to fill the gap.
 421:     pub fn observe_idle_tick(&mut self, now_ms: u64) {
 422:         if self.last_emit_ms == 0 {
 423:             self.last_emit_ms = now_ms;
 424:             return;
 425:         }
 426:         let dt_sec = (now_ms.saturating_sub(self.last_emit_ms)) as f64 / 1000.0;
 427:         if dt_sec <= 0.0 {
 428:             return;
 429:         }
 430:         // Decay observed rate toward zero with the same half-life.
 431:         let decay = 0.5f64.powf(dt_sec / self.half_life_sec);
 432:         self.observed_real_rate *= decay;
 433:         self.last_emit_ms = now_ms;
 434:     }
 435: 
 436:     /// Current cover rate λ that would maintain target total emission.
 437:     /// Floored at zero so we never get negative rates when real traffic
 438:     /// exceeds target.
 439:     pub fn current_cover_rate(&self) -> f64 {
 440:         (self.target_total_hz - self.observed_real_rate).max(0.0)
 441:     }
 442: 
 443:     /// Read the EWMA-smoothed observed real rate. For diagnostics.
 444:     pub fn observed_real_rate(&self) -> f64 {
 445:         self.observed_real_rate
 446:     }
 447: 
 448:     /// Read the target total emission rate.
 449:     pub fn target_total_hz(&self) -> f64 {
 450:         self.target_total_hz
 451:     }
 452: }

 462:     fn make_relay() -> (Scalar, SphinxHop) {
 463:         let (sk, pk) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 464:         let mut id = [0u8; 32];
 465:         OsRng.fill(&mut id);
 466:         (
 467:             sk,
 468:             SphinxHop {
 469:                 id: HopId::from_bytes(id),
 470:                 static_pk: pk,
 471:             },
 472:         )
 473:     }
 474: 
 475:     #[test]
 476:     fn cover_trailer_authenticated_check() {
 477:         // Two distinct shared-keys produce distinct, non-matching
 478:         // trailers for the same body — replay/swap is detectable.
 479:         let k1 = [0x11u8; 32];
 480:         let k2 = [0x22u8; 32];
 481:         let body = [0xAAu8; 32];
 482:         let t1 = compute_cover_trailer(&k1, &body);
 483:         let t2 = compute_cover_trailer(&k2, &body);
 484:         assert_ne!(t1, t2);
 485: 
 486:         // Build a synthetic cover payload and check the verify path.
 487:         let mut payload = COVER_SENTINEL.to_vec();
 488:         payload.extend_from_slice(&body);
 489:         let trailer = compute_cover_trailer(&k1, &payload);
 490:         payload.extend_from_slice(&trailer);
 491:         assert!(is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k1, &payload));
 492:         // Wrong key fails.
 493:         assert!(!is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k2, &payload));
 494:         // Bit-flip in body invalidates the trailer.
 495:         let mut tampered = payload.clone();
 496:         tampered[20] ^= 1;
 497:         assert!(!is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k1, &tampered));
 498:         // Bit-flip in trailer invalidates.
 499:         let mut bad_tag = payload.clone();
 500:         let last = bad_tag.len() - 1;
 501:         bad_tag[last] ^= 1;
 502:         assert!(!is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k1, &bad_tag));
 503:         // Real-looking payloads (no sentinel) reject immediately.
 504:         assert!(!is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k1, b"hello world"));
 505:         assert!(!is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k1, &[]));
 506:         // A payload that's mostly cover-shaped but with a flipped
 507:         // sentinel byte fails the prefix gate.
 508:         let mut wrong_prefix = payload.clone();
 509:         wrong_prefix[0] ^= 1;
 510:         assert!(!is_cover_payload_authenticated(&k1, &wrong_prefix));
 511:     }
 512: 
 513:     #[test]
 514:     fn build_cover_packet_round_trip() {
 515:         let (dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
 516:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 517:         let packet =
 518:             build_cover_packet(&eph_sk, &[dest.clone()], 128, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 519:         let outcome = peel_sphinx_layer(&dest_sk, &packet).unwrap();
 520:         // Audit M4: peel returns the authenticated Cover variant for
 521:         // a packet built via the cover-traffic path. The payload is
 522:         // not surfaced to the caller (no plaintext leak via
 523:         // mis-classified delivery).
 524:         assert!(matches!(outcome, SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover));
 525:     }

 527:     #[test]
 528:     fn build_cover_packet_three_hop() {
 529:         let (r1_sk, r1) = make_relay();
 530:         let (r2_sk, r2) = make_relay();
 531:         let (dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
 532:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 533:         let mut packet =
 534:             build_cover_packet(&eph_sk, &[r1, r2, dest], 256, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 535: 
 536:         // Cover packets are indistinguishable from real packets at
 537:         // every relay (same size, same blinding, Forward at intermediates).
 538:         // The destination's peel returns Cover (audit M4).
 539:         for sk in [&r1_sk, &r2_sk, &dest_sk] {
 540:             match peel_sphinx_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap() {
 541:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => packet = next_packet,
 542:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => return,
 543:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { .. } => {
 544:                     panic!("cover packet leaked as Deliver — MAC binding broken");
 545:                 }
 546:             }
 547:         }
 548:     }
 549: 
 550:     #[test]
 551:     fn real_payload_doesnt_mis_classify_as_cover() {
 552:         use crate::sphinx::core::build_sphinx_onion;
 553:         // A real payload starting with the SENTINEL bytes but with a
 554:         // random tail (no authenticated trailer) must NOT classify
 555:         // as cover. This is the audit-M4 protection: a network
 556:         // attacker can't forge cover status by flipping bytes.
 557:         let (dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
 558:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 559:         let mut fake_cover = COVER_SENTINEL.to_vec();
 560:         fake_cover.extend_from_slice(&[0xCCu8; 128]); // body
 561:         fake_cover.extend_from_slice(&[0xDDu8; COVER_TRAILER_LEN]); // bogus tag
 562:         let packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[dest], &fake_cover, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 563:         match peel_sphinx_layer(&dest_sk, &packet).unwrap() {
 564:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => {
 565:                 assert_eq!(payload, fake_cover);
 566:             }
 567:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => {
 568:                 panic!("forged cover status accepted — MAC binding broken!");
 569:             }
 570:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { .. } => panic!("expected Deliver"),
 571:         }
 572:     }

 574:     #[test]
 575:     fn build_cover_packet_rejects_below_min() {
 576:         let (_, dest) = make_relay();
 577:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 578:         let err =

   1: //! T1.3 — field-bound blinding for Sphinx Coherence.
   2: //!
   3: //! Each hop's blinding factor derivation takes an additional 32-byte
   4: //! `field_witness` input. The witness is the digest of the relay's
   5: //! coherence-field PDE state (Phase E `ol_coherence_field`) at the
   6: //! tick the sender observed.
   7: //!
   8: //! ```text
   9: //!   key_input = BLAKE3("field-bound" || shared || alpha || witness)
  10: //! ```
  11: //!
  12: //! Daemon-side responsibility:
  13: //! - At build time: fetch each relay's most recently published
  14: //!   field witness via the discovery layer (`ol_discovery`).
  15: //! - At peel time: provide the relay's CURRENT (or recent-window)
  16: //!   witness. If it doesn't match the sender's bake, MAC fails.
  17: //!
  18: //! This Sphinx layer only plumbs the bytes through. The actual field
  19: //! sampling + freshness window are the daemon's concern.
  20: //!
  21: //! ## Why this matters
  22: //!
  23: //! Standard Sphinx + PQ-hybrid still relies entirely on cryptographic
  24: //! key material to prevent decryption. A future cryptanalytic break
  25: //! (post-quantum compute + ML-KEM weakness) could decrypt historical
  26: //! traffic given a recording.
  27: //!
  28: //! Field-bound blinding adds a physical-environment requirement:
  29: //! the adversary must ALSO have observed the relay's coherence-
  30: //! field state at construction time. The state is environmental
  31: //! (RF + topology) and not reconstructable from network captures.
  32: //! Recording-attack defense becomes physics-bound, not just
  33: //! cryptography-bound.
  34: 
  35: use crate::sphinx::primitives::{derive_hop_keys, HopKeys};
  36: 
  37: /// Length of a field witness in bytes (matches BLAKE3 output).
  38: pub const FIELD_WITNESS_LEN: usize = 32;
  39: 
  40: /// Sentinel for "no field witness" — when a hop opts out of field-
  41: /// binding, pass this value. Both sides must agree to use it.
  42: pub const NO_WITNESS: [u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN] = [0u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN];
  43: 
  44: /// Derive per-hop keys with a field witness mixed in.
  45: ///
  46: /// When `witness == NO_WITNESS`, this is bytewise-equivalent to
  47: /// [`derive_hop_keys`] (the BLAKE3 input space is partitioned by
  48: /// the domain-separation tag, so a zero-witness still produces a
  49: /// distinct key from the non-field-bound version).
  50: pub fn derive_hop_keys_with_witness(
  51:     shared: &[u8; 32],
  52:     alpha: &[u8; 32],
  53:     witness: &[u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN],
  54: ) -> HopKeys {
  55:     use blake3::Hasher;
  56:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  57:     h.update(crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
  58:     h.update(b"-sphinx-field-bound-v1");
  59:     h.update(shared);
  60:     h.update(alpha);
  61:     h.update(witness);
  62:     let d = h.finalize();
  63:     let mut combined_shared = [0u8; 32];
  64:     combined_shared.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
  65:     derive_hop_keys(&combined_shared, alpha)
  66: }
  67:

  69: mod tests {

  76:         let shared = [0x11; 32];
  77:         let alpha = [0x22; 32];

  79:         let k_field = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &NO_WITNESS);

   1: //! Sphinx header build + peel.
   2: //!
   3: //! Pure-byte algorithm — no elliptic curves. The header is the
   4: //! load-bearing part of Sphinx: a fixed-size structure that each
   5: //! relay decrypts + shifts + appends-keystream-tail without
   6: //! changing total size, and which the destination's MAC verifies
   7: //! against the cumulative output of all upstream relays.
   8: //!
   9: //! ## Header layout (HEADER_LEN bytes per hop)
  10: //!
  11: //! Each relay's view after decrypt:
  12: //! ```text
  13: //!   slot[0]               : (next_hop_id || next_mac)        [48 bytes]
  14: //!   slot[1..n_remaining]  : encrypted inner-layer bytes      [decrypted-or-filler]
  15: //! ```
  16: //!
  17: //! ## Build algorithm
  18: //!
  19: //! ```text
  20: //! 1. Compute filler from upstream relays' header_stream keys.
  21: //! 2. Destination's pre-encryption header:
  22: //!    bytes[..SLOT_LEN]              = [0u8; SLOT_LEN]  (destination marker)
  23: //!    bytes[SLOT_LEN..HEADER_LEN-FL] = random pad (FL = filler.len())
  24: //!    bytes[HEADER_LEN-FL..]         = filler            (the "raw" trailing portion)
  25: //! 3. ChaCha20-encrypt ONLY bytes[..HEADER_LEN-FL] with destination's stream key.
  26: //!    Trailing FL bytes (which are filler) stay raw.
  27: //!    Compute destination's MAC over the resulting encrypted+raw bytes.
  28: //! 4. For each preceding relay (right-to-left in the circuit):
  29: //!    pre = (next_hop_id || prev_mac || prev_header[..HEADER_LEN-SLOT_LEN])
  30: //!    encrypted = pre XOR chacha20(this_hop.header_stream, HEADER_LEN bytes)
  31: //!    new_mac = HMAC(this_hop.mac_key, encrypted)
  32: //! 5. The outermost-layer's (encrypted, mac) is what the sender hands
  33: //!    to the first relay.
  34: //! ```
  35: //!
  36: //! ## Peel algorithm
  37: //!
  38: //! ```text
  39: //! 1. Verify packet.mac == HMAC(my_mac_key, packet.header). Drop on miss.
  40: //! 2. Generate keystream of length HEADER_LEN + SLOT_LEN.
  41: //! 3. Decrypt: decrypted = packet.header XOR keystream[..HEADER_LEN].
  42: //! 4. Read slot 0: (next_hop_id, next_mac).
  43: //! 5. If next_hop_id == [0u8; SLOT_ID_LEN]: destination — deliver.
  44: //! 6. Else (relay):
  45: //!    forwarded[..HEADER_LEN-SLOT_LEN] = decrypted[SLOT_LEN..]
  46: //!    forwarded[HEADER_LEN-SLOT_LEN..] = keystream[HEADER_LEN..HEADER_LEN+SLOT_LEN]
  47: //!    forward (forwarded, next_mac) to next_hop_id.
  48: //! ```
  49: 
  50: use crate::sphinx::primitives::{
  51:     build_filler, chacha20_keystream_into, chacha20_xor_in_place, header_mac, verify_header_mac,
  52:     HopKeys, HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN, HEADER_LEN, SLOT_ID_LEN, SLOT_LEN, SLOT_MAC_LEN,
  53: };
  54: 
  55: /// Special destination marker: a slot whose hop_id is all zero
  56: /// signals "this hop is the destination, deliver the payload."
  57: pub const DESTINATION_MARKER: [u8; SLOT_ID_LEN] = [0u8; SLOT_ID_LEN];
  58: 
  59: /// Per-hop routing slot the sender embeds in the header.
  60: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  61: pub struct RoutingSlot {
  62:     /// Hop-id of the next hop (or `DESTINATION_MARKER` for the
  63:     /// destination's slot).
  64:     pub next_hop_id: [u8; SLOT_ID_LEN],
  65: }
  66: 
  67: /// Output of [`build_header`]: the encrypted outermost header + its
  68: /// MAC, ready to ship to the first relay.
  69: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  70: pub struct BuiltHeader {
  71:     /// The encrypted header bytes (length [`HEADER_LEN`]).
  72:     pub header: Vec<u8>,
  73:     /// The MAC the FIRST relay verifies.
  74:     pub mac: [u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN],
  75: }
  76: 
  77: /// Build the Sphinx onion header right-to-left.
  78: ///
  79: /// `hop_keys[i]` is the per-hop key material for the i-th hop in
  80: /// the circuit (0 = first relay, last = destination).
  81: /// `next_hop_ids[i]` is the routing identifier the i-th relay uses
  82: /// to forward the packet to the (i+1)-th hop. The LAST hop is the
  83: /// destination, so `next_hop_ids[n-1]` is unused at the destination
  84: /// (it's the marker that triggers Deliver).
  85: ///
  86: /// `random_pad` is a slice of random bytes used to fill the
  87: /// destination's "middle" header bytes (between the marker slot
  88: /// and the filler). Length must equal `HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN - (n-1) * SLOT_LEN`.
  89: pub fn build_header(
  90:     hop_keys: &[HopKeys],
  91:     next_hop_ids: &[[u8; SLOT_ID_LEN]],
  92:     random_pad: &[u8],
  93: ) -> BuiltHeader {
  94:     assert!(!hop_keys.is_empty(), "circuit must have at least one hop");
  95:     assert_eq!(
  96:         hop_keys.len(),
  97:         next_hop_ids.len(),
  98:         "hop_keys + next_hop_ids must have equal length"
  99:     );
 100:     let n = hop_keys.len();
 101:     let n_relays = n - 1;
 102:     let filler_len = n_relays * SLOT_LEN;
 103:     let pad_len = HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN - filler_len;
 104:     assert_eq!(
 105:         random_pad.len(),
 106:         pad_len,
 107:         "random_pad must be exactly {pad_len} bytes for n={n} hops"
 108:     );
 109: 
 110:     // ── Step 1: build cumulative filler from upstream-relay streams.
 111:     let relay_streams: Vec<[u8; 32]> = hop_keys
 112:         .iter()
 113:         .take(n_relays)
 114:         .map(|k| k.header_stream)
 115:         .collect();
 116:     let filler = build_filler(&relay_streams);
 117:     debug_assert_eq!(filler.len(), filler_len);
 118: 
 119:     // ── Step 2: destination's encrypted header.
 120:     let dest_keys = hop_keys.last().expect("non-empty");
 121:     // Stack-array header buffer (HEADER_LEN = 240 bytes).
 122:     let mut header = [0u8; HEADER_LEN];
 123:     // Marker slot (first SLOT_LEN bytes: all zero hop_id || zero mac).
 124:     // Already zero.
 125:     // Random pad (next pad_len bytes).
 126:     header[SLOT_LEN..SLOT_LEN + pad_len].copy_from_slice(random_pad);
 127:     // Filler (last filler_len bytes). Set raw (NOT XOR'd later).
 128:     header[HEADER_LEN - filler_len..].copy_from_slice(&filler);
 129:     // ChaCha20-encrypt ONLY the first (HEADER_LEN - filler_len) bytes
 130:     // with destination's stream key. The trailing filler stays raw.
 131:     let visible_end = HEADER_LEN - filler_len;
 132:     chacha20_xor_in_place(&dest_keys.header_stream, &mut header[..visible_end]);
 133:     let mut prev_mac = header_mac(&dest_keys.mac_key, &header);
 134: 
 135:     // ── Step 3: wrap upstream relays right-to-left.
 136:     let mut pre = [0u8; HEADER_LEN];
 137:     for i in (0..n_relays).rev() {
 138:         let keys = &hop_keys[i];
 139:         let next_hop_id = &next_hop_ids[i];
 140:         // Build pre-encryption header in the stack buffer:
 141:         //   pre[..SLOT_ID_LEN]       = next_hop_id
 142:         //   pre[SLOT_ID_LEN..SLOT_LEN] = prev_mac
 143:         //   pre[SLOT_LEN..]          = header[..HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN]
 144:         pre[..SLOT_ID_LEN].copy_from_slice(next_hop_id);
 145:         pre[SLOT_ID_LEN..SLOT_LEN].copy_from_slice(&prev_mac);
 146:         pre[SLOT_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&header[..HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN]);
 147:         // ChaCha20-encrypt the full HEADER_LEN bytes with this hop's stream.
 148:         chacha20_xor_in_place(&keys.header_stream, &mut pre);
 149:         // Swap pre into header for the next iteration.
 150:         header.copy_from_slice(&pre);
 151:         prev_mac = header_mac(&keys.mac_key, &header);
 152:     }
 153: 
 154:     BuiltHeader {
 155:         header: header.to_vec(),
 156:         mac: prev_mac,
 157:     }
 158: }
 159: 
 160: /// Outcome of a single peel.
 161: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 162: pub enum HeaderPeelOutcome {
 163:     /// Forward to `next_hop_id` with the new header + MAC.
 164:     Forward {
 165:         /// Routing id of the next hop.
 166:         next_hop_id: [u8; SLOT_ID_LEN],
 167:         /// Encrypted header bytes for the next hop.
 168:         next_header: Vec<u8>,
 169:         /// MAC the next hop verifies.
 170:         next_mac: [u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN],
 171:     },
 172:     /// This relay is the destination — deliver the user payload.
 173:     Deliver,
 174: }
 175: 
 176: /// Peel one layer of a Sphinx header.
 177: ///
 178: /// Returns Err if MAC verification fails.
 179: pub fn peel_header(
 180:     keys: &HopKeys,
 181:     received_header: &[u8],
 182:     received_mac: &[u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN],
 183: ) -> Result<HeaderPeelOutcome, ()> {
 184:     if received_header.len() != HEADER_LEN {
 185:         return Err(());
 186:     }
 187:     // 1. Verify MAC.
 188:     if !verify_header_mac(&keys.mac_key, received_header, received_mac) {
 189:         return Err(());
 190:     }
 191:     // 2. Generate extended keystream into a stack buffer.
 192:     let mut keystream = [0u8; HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN];
 193:     chacha20_keystream_into(&keys.header_stream, &mut keystream);
 194:     // 3. Decrypt into a stack buffer.
 195:     let mut decrypted = [0u8; HEADER_LEN];
 196:     decrypted.copy_from_slice(received_header);
 197:     for i in 0..HEADER_LEN {
 198:         decrypted[i] ^= keystream[i];
 199:     }
 200:     // 4. Read slot 0.
 201:     let mut next_hop_id = [0u8; SLOT_ID_LEN];
 202:     next_hop_id.copy_from_slice(&decrypted[..SLOT_ID_LEN]);
 203:     let mut next_mac = [0u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN];
 204:     next_mac.copy_from_slice(&decrypted[SLOT_ID_LEN..SLOT_LEN]);
 205: 
 206:     // 5. Destination check.
 207:     if next_hop_id == DESTINATION_MARKER {
 208:         return Ok(HeaderPeelOutcome::Deliver);
 209:     }
 210: 
 211:     // 6. Build forwarded header — only allocates the final Vec at
 212:     // return time, no intermediate Vecs.
 213:     let mut forwarded = vec![0u8; HEADER_LEN];
 214:     forwarded[..HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN].copy_from_slice(&decrypted[SLOT_LEN..]);
 215:     forwarded[HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN..]
 216:         .copy_from_slice(&keystream[HEADER_LEN..HEADER_LEN + SLOT_LEN]);
 217: 
 218:     Ok(HeaderPeelOutcome::Forward {
 219:         next_hop_id,
 220:         next_header: forwarded,
 221:         next_mac,
 222:     })
 223: }

 236:     fn random_pad_for(n_hops: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
 237:         let pad_len = HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN - (n_hops - 1) * SLOT_LEN;
 238:         (0..pad_len).map(|i| (i as u8).wrapping_mul(31)).collect()
 239:     }

   1: //! T1.2 — PQ-hybrid blinding for Sphinx Coherence.
   2: //!
   3: //! The first relay in the circuit has an ML-KEM-768 long-term key
   4: //! pair alongside its Ristretto255 key. The sender encapsulates to
   5: //! the entry relay's PQ pubkey and mixes the resulting shared
   6: //! secret into hop 0's BLAKE3 key derivation:
   7: //!
   8: //! ```text
   9: //!   classical_shared = (eph_sk * cumulative_blind) * relay_x_pk
  10: //!   pq_shared        = ML-KEM-768.Encap(relay_pq_pk).shared
  11: //!   hybrid_shared    = BLAKE3("hybrid" || classical_shared || pq_shared || alpha)
  12: //! ```
  13: //!
  14: //! The hybrid binding flows down the chain via cumulative_blind:
  15: //! every subsequent alpha_i is `b_0 * b_1 * ... * b_{i-1} * alpha_0`
  16: //! where `b_0` is derived from `hybrid_shared`. So a quantum
  17: //! adversary cannot reproduce alpha_1+ without first breaking
  18: //! ML-KEM-768 (to recover b_0).
  19: //!
  20: //! ## Wire format addition
  21: //!
  22: //! The PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet inserts an 1088-byte ML-KEM ciphertext
  23: //! between alpha and header_mac. Total packet size:
  24: //!
  25: //! ```text
  26: //!   1 + 32 + 1088 + 16 + 240 + 1024 = 2401 bytes
  27: //! ```
  28: //!
  29: //! ## Relay modes
  30: //!
  31: //! - **Entry relay**: holds an ML-KEM decapsulation key. Decapsulates
  32: //!   the carried ciphertext and uses hybrid derivation.
  33: //! - **Intermediate relay**: ignores the carried ciphertext (it was
  34: //!   encapsulated for the entry relay only). Uses classical
  35: //!   Ristretto255-only derivation.
  36: //!
  37: //! The daemon's transport layer knows whether the packet arrived
  38: //! directly from the sender (entry mode) or via a forwarded peel
  39: //! (intermediate mode), so it calls the appropriate peel function.
  40:

  44: use curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar;
  45: use hybrid_array::Array;
  46: use ml_kem::kem::{Decapsulate, Encapsulate};
  47: use ml_kem::{KemCore, MlKem768};
  48: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  49: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  50: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  51: 
  52: use crate::errors::{OnionError, OnionResult};
  53: use crate::hop::HopId;
  54: use crate::sphinx::core::RISTRETTO_POINT_LEN;

  58:     build_header, peel_header, HeaderPeelOutcome, DESTINATION_MARKER,
  59: };

  66: /// ML-KEM-768 ciphertext length (FIPS 203 §6.3.1).
  67: pub const ML_KEM_CT_LEN: usize = 1088;
  68: 
  69: /// ML-KEM-768 encapsulation-key length.
  70: pub const ML_KEM_EK_LEN: usize = 1184;
  71: 
  72: /// PQ Sphinx wire protocol version. Distinct from classical SPHINX_VERSION.
  73: pub const PQ_SPHINX_VERSION: u8 = 4;
  74: 
  75: /// Total fixed PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet size:
  76: /// version(1) + alpha(32) + pq_ct(1088) + mac(16) + header(240) + payload(1024).
  77: pub const PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN: usize =
  78:     1 + RISTRETTO_POINT_LEN + ML_KEM_CT_LEN + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN + PAYLOAD_LEN;
  79: 
  80: /// Type alias for the ML-KEM-768 encapsulation key.
  81: type MlKemEk = <MlKem768 as KemCore>::EncapsulationKey;
  82: /// Type alias for the ML-KEM-768 decapsulation key.
  83: type MlKemDk = <MlKem768 as KemCore>::DecapsulationKey;
  84: type MlKemCtSize = <MlKem768 as KemCore>::CiphertextSize;
  85: 
  86: /// PQ-hybrid Sphinx hop: classical Ristretto255 + ML-KEM-768 pubkey.
  87: #[derive(Clone)]
  88: pub struct PqSphinxHop {
  89:     pub id: HopId,
  90:     pub static_x_pk: RistrettoPoint,
  91:     /// ML-KEM-768 encapsulation key. Only the ENTRY hop needs to
  92:     /// carry one; intermediate hops use empty bytes (skip PQ).
  93:     /// `None` means classical-only (intermediate hops).
  94:     pub static_pq_pk: Option<MlKemEk>,
  95: }
  96: 
  97: impl std::fmt::Debug for PqSphinxHop {
  98:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  99:         f.debug_struct("PqSphinxHop")
 100:             .field("id", &self.id)
 101:             .field("has_pq_pk", &self.static_pq_pk.is_some())
 102:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 103:     }
 104: }

 106: /// Generate a fresh ML-KEM-768 keypair.
 107: pub fn generate_pq_keypair<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> (MlKemDk, MlKemEk) {
 108:     MlKem768::generate(rng)
 109: }

 111: /// Combine classical X25519/Ristretto ECDH output with an ML-KEM-768
 112: /// shared secret via BLAKE3 to produce a hybrid shared secret.
 113: ///
 114: /// `classical_shared`: 32-byte Ristretto255 ECDH output.
 115: /// `pq_shared`: 32-byte ML-KEM-768 shared key.
 116: /// `alpha`: 32-byte hop ephemeral pubkey (binds the derivation to
 117: /// this specific packet).
 118: pub fn combine_hybrid_shared(
 119:     classical_shared: &[u8; 32],
 120:     pq_shared: &[u8; 32],
 121:     alpha: &[u8; 32],
 122: ) -> [u8; 32] {
 123:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 124:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
 125:     h.update(b"-sphinx-pq-hybrid-v1");
 126:     h.update(classical_shared);
 127:     h.update(pq_shared);
 128:     h.update(alpha);
 129:     let d = h.finalize();
 130:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
 131:     out.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
 132:     out
 133: }

 135: /// PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet.
 136: #[derive(Clone)]
 137: pub struct PqSphinxPacket {
 138:     bytes: Vec<u8>,
 139: }
 140: 
 141: impl PqSphinxPacket {
 142:     /// Wrap raw wire bytes.
 143:     pub fn from_bytes(b: &[u8]) -> OnionResult<Self> {
 144:         if b.len() != PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN {
 145:             return Err(OnionError::BadFrameSize {
 146:                 got: b.len(),
 147:                 expected: PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN,
 148:             });
 149:         }
 150:         if b[0] != PQ_SPHINX_VERSION {
 151:             return Err(OnionError::UnsupportedVersion {
 152:                 got: b[0],
 153:                 supported: PQ_SPHINX_VERSION,
 154:             });
 155:         }
 156:         Ok(Self { bytes: b.to_vec() })
 157:     }
 158: 
 159:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
 160:         &self.bytes
 161:     }
 162: 
 163:     fn alpha(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
 164:         let mut a = [0u8; 32];
 165:         a.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[1..33]);
 166:         a
 167:     }
 168: 
 169:     fn pq_ct(&self) -> &[u8] {
 170:         &self.bytes[33..33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN]
 171:     }
 172: 
 173:     fn mac(&self) -> [u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN] {
 174:         let start = 33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN;
 175:         let mut m = [0u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN];
 176:         m.copy_from_slice(&self.bytes[start..start + SLOT_MAC_LEN]);
 177:         m
 178:     }
 179: 
 180:     fn header(&self) -> &[u8] {
 181:         let start = 33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN + SLOT_MAC_LEN;
 182:         &self.bytes[start..start + HEADER_LEN]
 183:     }
 184: 
 185:     fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] {
 186:         let start = 33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN + SLOT_MAC_LEN + HEADER_LEN;
 187:         &self.bytes[start..start + PAYLOAD_LEN]
 188:     }
 189: }

 192:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 193:         f.debug_struct("PqSphinxPacket")
 194:             .field("len", &self.bytes.len())
 195:             .field("version", &self.bytes.first().copied().unwrap_or(0))
 196:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 197:     }

 203:     }

 207: /// Outcome of a PQ-hybrid Sphinx peel.
 208: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 209: pub enum PqSphinxPeelOutcome {
 210:     Forward {
 211:         next_hop: HopId,
 212:         next_packet: PqSphinxPacket,
 213:     },
 214:     Deliver {
 215:         payload: Vec<u8>,
 216:     },
 217: }
 218: 
 219: /// Build a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet.
 220: ///
 221: /// `circuit[0]` MUST have `static_pq_pk = Some(_)` (the entry hop).
 222: /// Subsequent hops MAY have `None` — the PQ binding propagates via
 223: /// cumulative blinding.
 224: pub fn build_pq_sphinx_onion<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 225:     sender_eph_sk: &Scalar,
 226:     circuit: &[PqSphinxHop],
 227:     payload: &[u8],
 228:     rng: &mut R,
 229: ) -> OnionResult<PqSphinxPacket> {
 230:     if circuit.is_empty() {
 231:         return Err(OnionError::EmptyCircuit);
 232:     }
 233:     if circuit.len() > MAX_HOPS {
 234:         return Err(OnionError::TooManyHops {
 235:             got: circuit.len(),
 236:             max: MAX_HOPS,
 237:         });
 238:     }
 239:     if payload.len() > PAYLOAD_LEN - 2 {
 240:         return Err(OnionError::PayloadOversize {
 241:             got: payload.len(),
 242:             max: PAYLOAD_LEN - 2,
 243:         });
 244:     }
 245:     // Entry hop must have a PQ pubkey.
 246:     let entry_pq_pk = circuit[0]
 247:         .static_pq_pk
 248:         .as_ref()
 249:         .ok_or(OnionError::Internal(
 250:             "first hop must have an ML-KEM pubkey",
 251:         ))?;
 252: 
 253:     // ── Step 1: ML-KEM encapsulation to entry hop.
 254:     let (pq_ct, pq_shared) = entry_pq_pk
 255:         .encapsulate(rng)
 256:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::Internal("ML-KEM encapsulation failed"))?;
 257:     let pq_ct_bytes: &Array<u8, MlKemCtSize> = &pq_ct;
 258:     let pq_shared_bytes: [u8; 32] = {
 259:         let mut s = [0u8; 32];
 260:         s.copy_from_slice(&pq_shared);
 261:         s
 262:     };
 263: 
 264:     // ── Step 2: precompute alpha chain + shared secrets + hop keys.
 265:     let n = circuit.len();
 266:     let alpha_0 = sender_eph_sk * RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
 267:     let mut cumulative_blind = Scalar::ONE;
 268:     let mut hop_keys: Vec<HopKeys> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
 269:     let mut alpha_i = alpha_0;
 270: 
 271:     for (i, hop) in circuit.iter().enumerate() {
 272:         let alpha_bytes = alpha_i.compress().to_bytes();
 273:         let classical_shared_point =
 274:             (sender_eph_sk * cumulative_blind) * hop.static_x_pk;
 275:         let classical_shared = classical_shared_point.compress().to_bytes();
 276:         if classical_shared.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 277:             return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 278:         }
 279:         let derive_input = if i == 0 {
 280:             // Entry hop: hybrid derivation.
 281:             combine_hybrid_shared(&classical_shared, &pq_shared_bytes, &alpha_bytes)
 282:         } else {
 283:             classical_shared
 284:         };
 285:         let keys = derive_hop_keys(&derive_input, &alpha_bytes);
 286:         // Audit L1 May 2026: wide reduction from 64-byte seed.
 287:         let b_i = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&keys.blinding_seed);
 288:         hop_keys.push(keys);
 289:         cumulative_blind *= b_i;
 290:         alpha_i = b_i * alpha_i;
 291:     }
 292: 
 293:     // ── Step 3: build header.
 294:     let mut next_hop_ids: Vec<[u8; SLOT_ID_LEN]> = circuit
 295:         .iter()
 296:         .skip(1)
 297:         .map(|h| *h.id.as_bytes())
 298:         .collect();
 299:     next_hop_ids.push(DESTINATION_MARKER);
 300: 
 301:     let n_relays = n - 1;
 302:     let filler_len = n_relays * SLOT_LEN;
 303:     let pad_len = HEADER_LEN - SLOT_LEN - filler_len;
 304:     let mut random_pad = vec![0u8; pad_len];
 305:     rng.fill_bytes(&mut random_pad);
 306: 
 307:     let built = build_header(&hop_keys, &next_hop_ids, &random_pad);
 308: 
 309:     // ── Step 4: build encrypted payload — in-place, no per-hop Vec.
 310:     let mut payload_buf = [0u8; PAYLOAD_LEN];
 311:     // Payload length is bounded above by SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD
 312:     // (≤ u16::MAX) — enforced by the entry-time check. Cast is safe.
 313:     #[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
 314:     let plen_u16 = payload.len() as u16;
 315:     payload_buf[..2].copy_from_slice(&plen_u16.to_be_bytes());
 316:     payload_buf[2..2 + payload.len()].copy_from_slice(payload);
 317:     for keys in hop_keys.iter().rev() {
 318:         chacha20_xor_in_place(&keys.payload_stream, &mut payload_buf);
 319:     }
 320: 
 321:     // ── Step 5: assemble outer packet.
 322:     let mut bytes = vec![0u8; PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN];
 323:     bytes[0] = PQ_SPHINX_VERSION;
 324:     bytes[1..33].copy_from_slice(&alpha_0.compress().to_bytes());
 325:     bytes[33..33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN].copy_from_slice(pq_ct_bytes);
 326:     let mac_start = 33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN;
 327:     bytes[mac_start..mac_start + SLOT_MAC_LEN].copy_from_slice(&built.mac);
 328:     let hdr_start = mac_start + SLOT_MAC_LEN;
 329:     bytes[hdr_start..hdr_start + HEADER_LEN].copy_from_slice(&built.header);
 330:     bytes[hdr_start + HEADER_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&payload_buf);
 331: 
 332:     // Zeroize sensitive material.
 333:     for mut k in hop_keys {
 334:         k.header_stream.zeroize();
 335:         k.payload_stream.zeroize();
 336:         k.mac_key.zeroize();
 337:         k.blinding_seed.zeroize();
 338:     }
 339:     payload_buf.zeroize();
 340: 
 341:     Ok(PqSphinxPacket { bytes })
 342: }
 343: 
 344: /// Peel one layer of a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet at the ENTRY relay.
 345: ///
 346: /// Decapsulates the carried ML-KEM ciphertext with the entry relay's
 347: /// PQ decapsulation key, then derives the hybrid shared secret +
 348: /// peels the header + payload.
 349: ///
 350: /// After this peel, the OUTPUT packet still carries the original
 351: /// ML-KEM ciphertext for wire-format uniformity, but downstream
 352: /// relays will use `peel_pq_sphinx_intermediate` which ignores it.
 353: pub fn peel_pq_sphinx_entry(
 354:     relay_x_sk: &Scalar,
 355:     relay_pq_sk: &MlKemDk,
 356:     packet: &PqSphinxPacket,
 357: ) -> OnionResult<PqSphinxPeelOutcome> {
 358:     let alpha_bytes = packet.alpha();
 359:     if alpha_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 360:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 361:     }
 362:     let alpha_point = CompressedRistretto::from_slice(&alpha_bytes)
 363:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?
 364:         .decompress()
 365:         .ok_or(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?;
 366: 
 367:     // Classical ECDH.
 368:     let classical_shared = (relay_x_sk * alpha_point).compress().to_bytes();
 369:     if classical_shared.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 370:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 371:     }
 372:     // PQ decapsulation.
 373:     let pq_ct_slice = packet.pq_ct();
 374:     let ct_arr: Array<u8, MlKemCtSize> = Array::try_from(pq_ct_slice)
 375:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::Internal("ML-KEM ciphertext size"))?;
 376:     let pq_shared = relay_pq_sk
 377:         .decapsulate(&ct_arr)
 378:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::AeadFail)?;
 379:     let pq_shared_bytes: [u8; 32] = {
 380:         let mut s = [0u8; 32];
 381:         s.copy_from_slice(&pq_shared);
 382:         s
 383:     };
 384: 
 385:     // Hybrid combine.
 386:     let hybrid_shared = combine_hybrid_shared(&classical_shared, &pq_shared_bytes, &alpha_bytes);
 387:     let keys = derive_hop_keys(&hybrid_shared, &alpha_bytes);
 388: 
 389:     finish_peel(&keys, packet, alpha_point)
 390: }
 391: 
 392: /// Peel one layer of a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet at an INTERMEDIATE
 393: /// relay (downstream of the entry hop). Uses classical Ristretto255-
 394: /// only derivation. The PQ binding still flows through alpha via
 395: /// cumulative blinding.
 396: pub fn peel_pq_sphinx_intermediate(
 397:     relay_x_sk: &Scalar,
 398:     packet: &PqSphinxPacket,
 399: ) -> OnionResult<PqSphinxPeelOutcome> {
 400:     let alpha_bytes = packet.alpha();
 401:     if alpha_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 402:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 403:     }
 404:     let alpha_point = CompressedRistretto::from_slice(&alpha_bytes)
 405:         .map_err(|_| OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?
 406:         .decompress()
 407:         .ok_or(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey)?;
 408:     let classical_shared = (relay_x_sk * alpha_point).compress().to_bytes();
 409:     if classical_shared.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 410:         return Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 411:     }
 412:     let keys = derive_hop_keys(&classical_shared, &alpha_bytes);
 413:     finish_peel(&keys, packet, alpha_point)
 414: }
 415: 
 416: fn finish_peel(
 417:     keys: &HopKeys,
 418:     packet: &PqSphinxPacket,
 419:     alpha_point: RistrettoPoint,
 420: ) -> OnionResult<PqSphinxPeelOutcome> {
 421:     let mac = packet.mac();
 422:     let outcome = peel_header(keys, packet.header(), &mac).map_err(|_| OnionError::AeadFail)?;
 423: 
 424:     let mut payload = vec![0u8; PAYLOAD_LEN];
 425:     payload.copy_from_slice(packet.payload());
 426:     chacha20_xor_in_place(&keys.payload_stream, &mut payload);
 427: 
 428:     match outcome {
 429:         HeaderPeelOutcome::Deliver => {
 430:             let plen = u16::from_be_bytes([payload[0], payload[1]]) as usize;
 431:             if plen > PAYLOAD_LEN - 2 {
 432:                 return Err(OnionError::Internal("destination payload length oversize"));
 433:             }
 434:             let mut user_payload = vec![0u8; plen];
 435:             user_payload.copy_from_slice(&payload[2..2 + plen]);
 436:             Ok(PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver {
 437:                 payload: user_payload,
 438:             })
 439:         }
 440:         HeaderPeelOutcome::Forward {
 441:             next_hop_id,
 442:             next_header,
 443:             next_mac,
 444:         } => {
 445:             // Audit L1 May 2026: wide reduction.
 446:             let b_scalar = Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide(&keys.blinding_seed);
 447:             let next_alpha = b_scalar * alpha_point;
 448:             let next_alpha_bytes = next_alpha.compress().to_bytes();
 449: 
 450:             // Assemble next packet — keep the ORIGINAL pq_ct field
 451:             // intact for wire-format uniformity (intermediate peel
 452:             // ignores it).
 453:             let mut bytes = vec![0u8; PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN];
 454:             bytes[0] = PQ_SPHINX_VERSION;
 455:             bytes[1..33].copy_from_slice(&next_alpha_bytes);
 456:             bytes[33..33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN].copy_from_slice(packet.pq_ct());
 457:             let mac_start = 33 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN;
 458:             bytes[mac_start..mac_start + SLOT_MAC_LEN].copy_from_slice(&next_mac);
 459:             let hdr_start = mac_start + SLOT_MAC_LEN;
 460:             bytes[hdr_start..hdr_start + HEADER_LEN].copy_from_slice(&next_header);
 461:             bytes[hdr_start + HEADER_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&payload);
 462: 
 463:             Ok(PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Forward {
 464:                 next_hop: HopId::from_bytes(next_hop_id),
 465:                 next_packet: PqSphinxPacket { bytes },
 466:             })
 467:         }
 468:     }
 469: }

   1: //! Sphinx primitives: constants, key derivation, MAC, stream
   2: //! cipher, and the filler-byte construction.
   3: //!
   4: //! Everything in this module is pure-byte math — no elliptic curve
   5: //! operations. This makes the filler-byte algorithm directly
   6: //! testable in isolation, which is the part the previous F3 attempt
   7: //! got wrong.
   8: 
   9: use blake3::Hasher;
  10: use chacha20::cipher::{KeyIvInit, StreamCipher};
  11: use chacha20::ChaCha20;
  12: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  13: 
  14: use crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN;
  15: 
  16: // ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  17: 
  18: /// Length of a routing-information slot: 32-byte hop_id +
  19: /// 16-byte MAC = 48 bytes per relay slot.
  20: pub const SLOT_LEN: usize = 48;
  21: 
  22: /// Bytes for the hop_id portion of a slot.
  23: pub const SLOT_ID_LEN: usize = 32;
  24: 
  25: /// Bytes for the MAC portion of a slot.
  26: pub const SLOT_MAC_LEN: usize = 16;
  27: 
  28: /// Maximum supported circuit length (relays + destination).
  29: pub const MAX_HOPS: usize = 5;
  30: 
  31: /// Total fixed header length: one slot per hop.
  32: pub const HEADER_LEN: usize = MAX_HOPS * SLOT_LEN;
  33: 
  34: /// Fixed payload length.
  35: pub const PAYLOAD_LEN: usize = 1024;
  36: 
  37: /// Length of the per-layer ChaCha20 keystream we generate. We need
  38: /// HEADER_LEN bytes for the visible header XOR + SLOT_LEN bytes
  39: /// past the end for the trailing-slot padding after shift.
  40: pub const HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN: usize = HEADER_LEN + SLOT_LEN;
  41: 
  42: /// Length of the BLAKE3-derived per-hop AEAD key.
  43: pub const LAYER_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  44: 
  45: // ── Per-hop derived keys ─────────────────────────────────────────
  46: 
  47: /// Key material derived for one hop in the circuit.
  48: ///
  49: /// The sender derives this from `(shared_secret, alpha_i)` at build
  50: /// time. The relay derives the same value from
  51: /// `(my_shared_secret, alpha_received)` at peel time.
  52: #[derive(Clone)]
  53: pub struct HopKeys {
  54:     /// 32-byte ChaCha20 key for the header stream cipher.
  55:     pub header_stream: [u8; 32],
  56:     /// 32-byte ChaCha20 key for the payload stream cipher.
  57:     pub payload_stream: [u8; 32],
  58:     /// 32-byte BLAKE3-keyed-MAC key for the per-hop header MAC.
  59:     pub mac_key: [u8; 32],
  60:     /// 64-byte raw bytes used as the per-hop blinding scalar for the
  61:     /// next alpha derivation. The Ristretto255 layer reduces these
  62:     /// 64 bytes via `Scalar::from_bytes_mod_order_wide` to eliminate
  63:     /// the ~2^-124 modular bias that the legacy 32-byte
  64:     /// `from_bytes_mod_order` reduction carries (audit L1 May 2026).
  65:     pub blinding_seed: [u8; 64],
  66: }
  67: 
  68: impl std::fmt::Debug for HopKeys {
  69:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  70:         // Never leak key bytes in debug formatting.
  71:         f.debug_struct("HopKeys").finish_non_exhaustive()
  72:     }
  73: }
  74: 
  75: /// Derive the 4 per-hop sub-keys from a shared secret + alpha pair.
  76: ///
  77: /// `shared` is the X25519 / Ristretto255 ECDH output (32 bytes).
  78: /// `alpha` is the per-hop ephemeral pubkey carried in the packet.
  79: pub fn derive_hop_keys(shared: &[u8; 32], alpha: &[u8; 32]) -> HopKeys {
  80:     HopKeys {
  81:         header_stream: derive_subkey(shared, alpha, b"sphinx-header-stream-v1"),
  82:         payload_stream: derive_subkey(shared, alpha, b"sphinx-payload-stream-v1"),
  83:         mac_key: derive_subkey(shared, alpha, b"sphinx-mac-v1"),
  84:         // Audit L1 May 2026: domain bumped `-v1` → `-v2` since the
  85:         // output width grew 32 → 64 bytes. The new XOF-based
  86:         // derivation feeds 64 bytes into `from_bytes_mod_order_wide`
  87:         // at the call site, eliminating the ~2^-124 modular bias
  88:         // the legacy 32-byte reduction carried.
  89:         blinding_seed: derive_subkey_wide(shared, alpha, b"sphinx-blind-v2"),
  90:     }
  91: }
  92: 
  93: fn derive_subkey(shared: &[u8; 32], alpha: &[u8; 32], tag: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
  94:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  95:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
  96:     h.update(b"-");
  97:     h.update(tag);
  98:     h.update(shared);
  99:     h.update(alpha);
 100:     let d = h.finalize();
 101:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
 102:     out.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
 103:     out
 104: }
 105: 
 106: fn derive_subkey_wide(shared: &[u8; 32], alpha: &[u8; 32], tag: &[u8]) -> [u8; 64] {
 107:     // Audit L1 May 2026: 64-byte XOF output for unbiased scalar
 108:     // reduction via `from_bytes_mod_order_wide`. Same input shape
 109:     // as `derive_subkey` so the rest of the protocol stays
 110:     // structurally identical — only the output width differs.
 111:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 112:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
 113:     h.update(b"-");
 114:     h.update(tag);
 115:     h.update(shared);
 116:     h.update(alpha);
 117:     let mut out = [0u8; 64];
 118:     h.finalize_xof().fill(&mut out);
 119:     out
 120: }
 121: 
 122: // ── BLAKE3-keyed MAC over the header ─────────────────────────────
 123: 
 124: /// Compute the per-hop header MAC. Truncates BLAKE3-keyed output to
 125: /// [`SLOT_MAC_LEN`].
 126: pub fn header_mac(key: &[u8; 32], header: &[u8]) -> [u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN] {
 127:     let mut h = Hasher::new_keyed(key);
 128:     h.update(header);
 129:     let d = h.finalize();
 130:     let mut out = [0u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN];
 131:     out.copy_from_slice(&d.as_bytes()[..SLOT_MAC_LEN]);
 132:     out
 133: }
 134: 
 135: /// Constant-time MAC comparison.
 136: pub fn verify_header_mac(
 137:     key: &[u8; 32],
 138:     header: &[u8],
 139:     expected: &[u8; SLOT_MAC_LEN],
 140: ) -> bool {
 141:     let actual = header_mac(key, header);
 142:     bool::from(actual.ct_eq(expected))
 143: }
 144: 
 145: // ── ChaCha20 stream cipher helpers ───────────────────────────────
 146: 
 147: /// Generate `len` bytes of ChaCha20 keystream with the given key.
 148: /// Uses an all-zero nonce — safe because each hop has a unique
 149: /// stream key per circuit.
 150: ///
 151: /// Prefer [`chacha20_keystream_into`] on hot paths to avoid the
 152: /// per-call Vec allocation; this function is kept for callers that
 153: /// can't pre-size their buffer (and tests).
 154: pub fn chacha20_keystream(key: &[u8; 32], len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
 155:     let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
 156:     chacha20_keystream_into(key, &mut buf);
 157:     buf
 158: }
 159: 
 160: /// Generate ChaCha20 keystream directly into a caller-provided
 161: /// buffer. The buffer MUST start at all zeros — `apply_keystream`
 162: /// XORs into the buffer, so a zero buffer yields pure keystream.
 163: /// Hot-path helper used by [`build_filler`] and
 164: /// [`crate::sphinx::core::build_sphinx_onion`].
 165: ///
 166: /// # SAFETY — zero-nonce key reuse (audit L3 May 2026)
 167: ///
 168: /// The all-zero nonce is SOUND ONLY because each `key` passed in
 169: /// here is unique-per-circuit-and-direction: it's a `derive_subkey`
 170: /// output keyed on `(shared_secret, alpha, role_tag)`. Different
 171: /// circuits produce different `shared_secret` values; different
 172: /// alphas inside the same circuit produce different per-hop keys;
 173: /// and the role tags (`sphinx-header-stream-v1` etc.) prevent role
 174: /// confusion within the same hop. So no two `apply_keystream` calls
 175: /// on this codepath ever share BOTH key and nonce.
 176: ///
 177: /// **Do NOT reuse this primitive for SURB reply blocks, multi-pass
 178: /// re-encryption, or any context where the SAME key encrypts more
 179: /// than one (key, nonce, message) tuple.** A future SURB or
 180: /// reply-block design MUST introduce a per-direction nonce
 181: /// (e.g. `[0u8; 11] || direction_byte`) before calling this.
 182: #[inline]
 183: pub fn chacha20_keystream_into(key: &[u8; 32], out: &mut [u8]) {
 184:     let nonce = [0u8; 12];
 185:     let mut cipher = ChaCha20::new(key.into(), (&nonce).into());
 186:     cipher.apply_keystream(out);
 187: }
 188: 
 189: /// ChaCha20 XOR-decrypt / encrypt into the buffer in place (no
 190: /// pre-zero step). Same key + zero nonce semantics as
 191: /// [`chacha20_keystream`].
 192: ///
 193: /// # SAFETY — zero-nonce key reuse (audit L3 May 2026)
 194: ///
 195: /// Same invariant as [`chacha20_keystream_into`]: the all-zero
 196: /// nonce is sound only because `key` is unique-per-(circuit,
 197: /// alpha, role). See that function's SAFETY section for the
 198: /// detailed argument and the future-work caveat about SURB
 199: /// reply blocks.
 200: #[inline]
 201: pub fn chacha20_xor_in_place(key: &[u8; 32], buf: &mut [u8]) {
 202:     let nonce = [0u8; 12];
 203:     let mut cipher = ChaCha20::new(key.into(), (&nonce).into());
 204:     cipher.apply_keystream(buf);
 205: }
 206: 
 207: /// XOR `keystream` into `buf` in place. Lengths must match.
 208: pub fn xor_in_place(buf: &mut [u8], keystream: &[u8]) {
 209:     debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), keystream.len());
 210:     for (b, k) in buf.iter_mut().zip(keystream.iter()) {
 211:         *b ^= *k;
 212:     }
 213: }
 214: 
 215: // ── Filler-byte construction (the load-bearing algorithm) ────────
 216: //
 217: // The filler `phi` has length `n_relays * SLOT_LEN` where
 218: // `n_relays = circuit.len() - 1` (the relays that come BEFORE the
 219: // destination — destination doesn't contribute to filler).
 220: //
 221: // Iterative construction:
 222: //
 223: //     phi[0] = empty
 224: //     for i in 0..n_relays:
 225: //         # Generate hop_i's extended keystream (HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN bytes).
 226: //         # Extend filler by SLOT_LEN zero bytes.
 227: //         # XOR the new (i+1)*SLOT_LEN-byte filler with the LAST
 228: //         # (i+1)*SLOT_LEN bytes of the keystream.
 229: //
 230: // The filler ends up at the trailing portion of the destination's
 231: // pre-encryption header. When upstream relays peel + shift, their
 232: // keystream tails reconstruct the destination's expected trailing
 233: // bytes byte-for-byte, so the MAC verifies all the way through.
 234: 
 235: /// Build the cumulative filler for `n_relays` upstream hops.
 236: ///
 237: /// `relay_header_streams[i]` is the header-stream ChaCha20 key for
 238: /// the `i`-th relay in the circuit (the relays *before* the
 239: /// destination).
 240: pub fn build_filler(relay_header_streams: &[[u8; 32]]) -> Vec<u8> {
 241:     let n = relay_header_streams.len();
 242:     if n == 0 {
 243:         return Vec::new();
 244:     }
 245:     // Allocate ONCE at max final size. We XOR-shift in place rather
 246:     // than allocating per-iteration. Stack-allocate the keystream
 247:     // buffer (HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN = 288 bytes for SLOT_LEN=48,
 248:     // MAX_HOPS=5; well under 1 KiB).
 249:     let final_len = n * SLOT_LEN;
 250:     let mut filler = vec![0u8; final_len];
 251:     let mut keystream = [0u8; HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN];
 252:     let mut current_len = 0;
 253:     for (i, key) in relay_header_streams.iter().enumerate() {
 254:         let new_len = (i + 1) * SLOT_LEN;
 255:         // Zero keystream buffer (apply_keystream XORs into existing
 256:         // bytes, so a zero buffer is needed for pure keystream).
 257:         for b in keystream.iter_mut() {
 258:             *b = 0;
 259:         }
 260:         chacha20_keystream_into(key, &mut keystream);
 261:         let tail_start = HEADER_KEYSTREAM_LEN - new_len;
 262:         for j in 0..new_len {
 263:             filler[j] ^= keystream[tail_start + j];
 264:         }
 265:         current_len = new_len;
 266:     }
 267:     debug_assert_eq!(current_len, final_len);
 268:     filler
 269: }

   1: //! obfs4-style handshake — ECDH + bridge-identity HMAC binding.
   2: //!
   3: //! Threat model:
   4: //!
   5: //! - **Passive DPI** observes wire bytes. Both handshake messages
   6: //!   look uniformly random; ChaCha20 obfuscation under the
   7: //!   handshake-derived key kicks in for the bulk data.
   8: //! - **Active probe attacker** tries to detect bridges by sending
   9: //!   random / well-known protocol bytes to candidate IPs and seeing
  10: //!   if anything responds in a bridge-shaped way. Defeated by the
  11: //!   bridge-identity HMAC: a valid first message requires
  12: //!   `HMAC(bridge_id || epoch_hour, client_ephem_pk)`. Without
  13: //!   `bridge_id` the attacker can't forge it. The bridge silently
  14: //!   drops invalid handshakes; a probe attacker sees nothing.
  15: //! - **Replay** within the current epoch is possible — the client's
  16: //!   ephemeral pubkey + HMAC are valid for ~1 hour. After the
  17: //!   epoch rolls over, the same handshake is rejected. Combined
  18: //!   with the bulk-cipher's per-conn nonce, replay yields no useful
  19: //!   plaintext-side oracle.
  20: //! - **Time-skew tolerance**: server accepts HMACs computed against
  21: //!   the current OR previous epoch, so clients off by < 1 hour
  22: //!   still succeed.
  23: //!
  24: //! ## Wire format
  25: //!
  26: //! ```text
  27: //!   Client → Server:
  28: //!     client_ephem_pubkey  : [u8; 32]    (X25519 ephemeral)
  29: //!     hmac_tag             : [u8; 16]    (BLAKE3-keyed tag)
  30: //!     pad                  : variable    (random; daemon picks size)
  31: //!
  32: //!   Server → Client:
  33: //!     server_ephem_pubkey  : [u8; 32]
  34: //!     auth_tag             : [u8; 16]    (BLAKE3-keyed over transcript)
  35: //!     pad                  : variable
  36: //! ```
  37: //!
  38: //! The 48 fixed bytes of each handshake message are wrapped in the
  39: //! `primitive` obfuscator using a session-derived key (or a pre-
  40: //! shared bridge "obfs key" for the very first message — for
  41: //! simplicity here we emit the bytes raw + rely on the HMAC for
  42: //! authenticity; the daemon can layer the byte obfuscator on top if
  43: //! it wants extra DPI resistance for the handshake itself).
  44: 
  45: use blake3::Hasher;
  46: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  47: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  48: use thiserror::Error;
  49: use x25519_dalek::{EphemeralSecret, PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  50: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  51: 
  52: use crate::transport_obfs::primitive::OBFS_KEY_LEN;
  53: use crate::transport_obfs::session::Session;
  54: 
  55: /// Length of the bridge identity handle (a public 32-byte tag the
  56: /// client knows out-of-band). This is bound into the HMAC so probe
  57: /// attackers without it can't forge a valid handshake.
  58: pub const BRIDGE_ID_LEN: usize = 32;
  59: 
  60: /// Length of the bridge's long-term X25519 public key.
  61: pub const BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  62: 
  63: /// Length of the bridge's long-term X25519 secret key.
  64: pub const BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN: usize = 32;
  65: 
  66: /// Length of the per-message handshake MAC.
  67: pub const HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN: usize = 16;
  68: 
  69: /// Length of the fixed-portion handshake message (ephem_pk + mac).
  70: pub const HANDSHAKE_LEN: usize = 32 + HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN;
  71: 
  72: /// Epoch window for the HMAC binding (seconds). 1 hour = 3600.
  73: /// Clients with skew < this value still authenticate.
  74: pub const HANDSHAKE_EPOCH_SECS: u64 = 3600;
  75: 
  76: /// Domain-separation tag for the handshake HMAC.
  77: const HMAC_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-obfs-handshake-v1";
  78: 
  79: /// Domain-separation tag for the per-direction session key derivation.
  80: const KDF_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-obfs-session-kdf-v1";
  81: 
  82: /// Typed error surface.
  83: #[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  84: pub enum HandshakeError {
  85:     /// Wrong byte length for a key, MAC, or handshake message.
  86:     #[error("wrong length: expected {expected}, got {got}")]
  87:     BadLength {
  88:         /// Required length.
  89:         expected: usize,
  90:         /// Actual length.
  91:         got: usize,
  92:     },
  93:     /// HMAC verification failed. Either the bridge_id is wrong, the
  94:     /// epoch is too far skewed, or the message was tampered.
  95:     #[error("handshake MAC did not verify")]
  96:     BadMac,
  97:     /// ECDH yielded a small-order shared secret (all-zero bytes).
  98:     #[error("ECDH produced small-order shared secret")]
  99:     SmallOrderPubkey,
 100: }
 101: 
 102: /// Result alias.
 103: pub type HandshakeResult<T> = Result<T, HandshakeError>;
 104: 
 105: /// Bridge keypair = long-term X25519 keys + a 32-byte public id tag.
 106: /// The id tag identifies which bridge a client is targeting + binds
 107: /// the HMAC. Clients learn `(bridge_pk, bridge_id)` out-of-band
 108: /// (e.g., via F2 pair-by-QR or an existing trusted channel).
 109: #[derive(Clone)]
 110: pub struct BridgeKeypair {
 111:     /// Long-term static X25519 secret. Drop zeroizes via x25519-dalek.
 112:     pub secret: StaticSecret,
 113:     /// Long-term static X25519 public.
 114:     pub public: PublicKey,
 115:     /// 32-byte public id tag. Bound into HMAC; not secret itself.
 116:     pub id: [u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 117: }
 118: 
 119: impl BridgeKeypair {
 120:     /// Generate a fresh keypair from a CSPRNG.
 121:     pub fn generate<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> Self {
 122:         let secret = StaticSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
 123:         let public = PublicKey::from(&secret);
 124:         let mut id = [0u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN];
 125:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut id);
 126:         Self { secret, public, id }
 127:     }
 128: 
 129:     /// Construct from raw seed + id bytes. The secret is the X25519
 130:     /// seed; clamping happens at use.
 131:     pub fn from_parts(
 132:         secret_seed: [u8; BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN],
 133:         id: [u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 134:     ) -> Self {
 135:         let secret = StaticSecret::from(secret_seed);
 136:         let public = PublicKey::from(&secret);
 137:         Self { secret, public, id }
 138:     }
 139: 
 140:     /// Serialize the SECRET half to wire bytes. Store encrypted at
 141:     /// rest; loss = bridge identity lost.
 142:     pub fn secret_bytes(&self) -> [u8; BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN] {
 143:         self.secret.to_bytes()
 144:     }
 145: 
 146:     /// Public X25519 key bytes (shareable; clients pin this).
 147:     pub fn public_bytes(&self) -> [u8; BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN] {
 148:         *self.public.as_bytes()
 149:     }
 150: 
 151:     /// Public id tag bytes (shareable; bound into HMACs).
 152:     pub fn id_bytes(&self) -> [u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN] {
 153:         self.id
 154:     }
 155: }
 156: 
 157: impl std::fmt::Debug for BridgeKeypair {
 158:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 159:         f.debug_struct("BridgeKeypair").finish_non_exhaustive()
 160:     }
 161: }
