 163: /// Client handshake state. Created via `start`, completed by feeding
 164: /// the server's reply.
 165: pub struct ClientHandshake {
 166:     /// Ephemeral secret used for ECDH; consumed at `finish`.
 167:     ephem: Option<EphemeralSecret>,
 168:     /// Cached ephemeral public bytes (for the transcript).
 169:     ephem_pk_bytes: [u8; 32],
 170:     /// Bridge's long-term public key (target of the ECDH).
 171:     bridge_pubkey: PublicKey,
 172:     /// Bridge's id (bound into HMACs).
 173:     bridge_id: [u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 174:     /// The first message the daemon ships to the bridge.
 175:     first_message: [u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN],
 176:     /// The wall-clock epoch the client computed its HMAC against.
 177:     epoch: u64,
 178: }
 179: 
 180: impl std::fmt::Debug for ClientHandshake {
 181:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 182:         f.debug_struct("ClientHandshake")
 183:             .field("epoch", &self.epoch)
 184:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 185:     }
 186: }
 187: 
 188: impl ClientHandshake {
 189:     /// Start a client handshake. The daemon sends the returned bytes
 190:     /// to the bridge over its transport (TCP/QUIC/UDP).
 191:     pub fn start<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 192:         rng: &mut R,
 193:         bridge_pubkey: &[u8; BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN],
 194:         bridge_id: &[u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 195:         now_unix: u64,
 196:     ) -> Self {
 197:         let ephem = EphemeralSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
 198:         let ephem_pk = PublicKey::from(&ephem);
 199:         let ephem_pk_bytes = *ephem_pk.as_bytes();
 200:         let bridge_pubkey_pt = PublicKey::from(*bridge_pubkey);
 201:         let epoch = now_unix / HANDSHAKE_EPOCH_SECS;
 202:         let tag = compute_handshake_tag(bridge_id, epoch, &ephem_pk_bytes);
 203:         let mut first_message = [0u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN];
 204:         first_message[..32].copy_from_slice(&ephem_pk_bytes);
 205:         first_message[32..].copy_from_slice(&tag);
 206:         Self {
 207:             ephem: Some(ephem),
 208:             ephem_pk_bytes,
 209:             bridge_pubkey: bridge_pubkey_pt,
 210:             bridge_id: *bridge_id,
 211:             first_message,
 212:             epoch,
 213:         }
 214:     }
 215: 
 216:     /// The bytes the daemon transmits to the bridge as the first
 217:     /// handshake message.
 218:     pub fn first_message(&self) -> &[u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN] {
 219:         &self.first_message
 220:     }
 221: 
 222:     /// Complete the handshake using the server's reply bytes. Returns
 223:     /// a [`Session`] with the per-direction obfuscation keys derived.
 224:     pub fn finish(mut self, server_reply: &[u8]) -> HandshakeResult<Session> {
 225:         if server_reply.len() < HANDSHAKE_LEN {
 226:             return Err(HandshakeError::BadLength {
 227:                 expected: HANDSHAKE_LEN,
 228:                 got: server_reply.len(),
 229:             });
 230:         }
 231:         let mut server_pk_bytes = [0u8; 32];
 232:         server_pk_bytes.copy_from_slice(&server_reply[..32]);
 233:         let mut server_tag = [0u8; HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN];
 234:         server_tag.copy_from_slice(&server_reply[32..HANDSHAKE_LEN]);
 235:         // Verify server's auth tag binds the transcript so far.
 236:         let expected_tag = compute_server_auth_tag(
 237:             &self.bridge_id,
 238:             self.epoch,
 239:             &self.ephem_pk_bytes,
 240:             &server_pk_bytes,
 241:         );
 242:         if !bool::from(expected_tag.ct_eq(&server_tag)) {
 243:             return Err(HandshakeError::BadMac);
 244:         }
 245:         let server_pk = PublicKey::from(server_pk_bytes);
 246:         // ECDH: shared = client_ephem * bridge_pubkey.
 247:         // (We use bridge_pubkey here, not server_ephem_pk; the
 248:         // server side mirrors via bridge_secret * client_ephem.)
 249:         let ephem = self
 250:             .ephem
 251:             .take()
 252:             .ok_or(HandshakeError::SmallOrderPubkey)?;
 253:         let shared = ephem.diffie_hellman(&self.bridge_pubkey);
 254:         if shared.as_bytes().iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 255:             return Err(HandshakeError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 256:         }
 257:         let _ = server_pk;
 258:         let (client_tx_key, server_tx_key) = derive_session_keys(
 259:             shared.as_bytes(),
 260:             &self.bridge_id,
 261:             &self.ephem_pk_bytes,
 262:             &server_pk_bytes,
 263:         );
 264:         Ok(Session::new(client_tx_key, server_tx_key))
 265:     }
 266: }
 267: 
 268: /// Server-side handshake. The bridge holds [`BridgeKeypair`]; on
 269: /// receiving a client's first message it produces a reply + a session.
 270: #[derive(Debug)]
 271: pub struct ServerHandshake;
 272: 
 273: impl ServerHandshake {
 274:     /// Accept a client handshake. Verifies the client's HMAC against
 275:     /// both the current epoch AND the previous epoch (tolerates ~1
 276:     /// hour of clock skew). Returns the bytes the bridge ships back
 277:     /// + the resulting Session.
 278:     pub fn accept<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 279:         rng: &mut R,
 280:         bridge: &BridgeKeypair,
 281:         client_first: &[u8],
 282:         now_unix: u64,
 283:     ) -> HandshakeResult<([u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN], Session)> {
 284:         if client_first.len() < HANDSHAKE_LEN {
 285:             return Err(HandshakeError::BadLength {
 286:                 expected: HANDSHAKE_LEN,
 287:                 got: client_first.len(),
 288:             });
 289:         }
 290:         let mut client_pk_bytes = [0u8; 32];
 291:         client_pk_bytes.copy_from_slice(&client_first[..32]);
 292:         let mut client_tag = [0u8; HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN];
 293:         client_tag.copy_from_slice(&client_first[32..HANDSHAKE_LEN]);
 294: 
 295:         // Try the current epoch first, then the previous one.
 296:         let current_epoch = now_unix / HANDSHAKE_EPOCH_SECS;
 297:         let mut matched_epoch = None;
 298:         for candidate in [current_epoch, current_epoch.saturating_sub(1)] {
 299:             let expected = compute_handshake_tag(&bridge.id, candidate, &client_pk_bytes);
 300:             if bool::from(expected.ct_eq(&client_tag)) {
 301:                 matched_epoch = Some(candidate);
 302:                 break;
 303:             }
 304:         }
 305:         let epoch = matched_epoch.ok_or(HandshakeError::BadMac)?;
 306: 
 307:         // Generate the server's ephemeral.
 308:         let server_ephem = EphemeralSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
 309:         let server_pk = PublicKey::from(&server_ephem);
 310:         let server_pk_bytes = *server_pk.as_bytes();
 311: 
 312:         // ECDH: shared = bridge_secret * client_ephem_pk.
 313:         let client_pk = PublicKey::from(client_pk_bytes);
 314:         let shared = bridge.secret.diffie_hellman(&client_pk);
 315:         if shared.as_bytes().iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 316:             return Err(HandshakeError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 317:         }
 318:         // Server's auth tag binds the transcript: client_ephem + server_ephem.
 319:         let server_tag =
 320:             compute_server_auth_tag(&bridge.id, epoch, &client_pk_bytes, &server_pk_bytes);
 321: 
 322:         let mut reply = [0u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN];
 323:         reply[..32].copy_from_slice(&server_pk_bytes);
 324:         reply[32..].copy_from_slice(&server_tag);
 325: 
 326:         // Derive matching session keys. Server's perspective: the
 327:         // CLIENT sends to us with client_tx_key, we send back with
 328:         // server_tx_key. Mirror the client's derivation order.
 329:         let (client_tx_key, server_tx_key) = derive_session_keys(
 330:             shared.as_bytes(),
 331:             &bridge.id,
 332:             &client_pk_bytes,
 333:             &server_pk_bytes,
 334:         );
 335:         // The server's incoming-direction key is client_tx_key, its
 336:         // outgoing-direction key is server_tx_key. The Session ctor
 337:         // takes (my_outbound, peer_outbound) → mirror via swap.
 338:         // We pass the SAME (client_tx_key, server_tx_key) pair as
 339:         // the client did, but the Session ctor produces a symmetric
 340:         // pair where each side names its own keys properly. To keep
 341:         // both sides aligned, ServerSession::for_server swaps them.
 342:         let session =
 343:             Session::for_server(client_tx_key, server_tx_key);
 344:         // Drop the server_ephem after deriving — we don't need it
 345:         // again.
 346:         let _ = server_ephem;
 347:         Ok((reply, session))
 348:     }
 349: }
 350: 
 351: /// Compute the client's handshake HMAC tag:
 352: ///   `BLAKE3-keyed(domain || bridge_id || epoch_be, client_ephem_pk)`
 353: /// truncated to [`HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN`].
 354: fn compute_handshake_tag(
 355:     bridge_id: &[u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 356:     epoch: u64,
 357:     client_ephem_pk: &[u8; 32],
 358: ) -> [u8; HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN] {
 359:     let mut key = [0u8; 32];
 360:     let mut kh = Hasher::new();
 361:     kh.update(HMAC_DOMAIN);
 362:     kh.update(b"-client-mac");
 363:     kh.update(bridge_id);
 364:     kh.update(&epoch.to_be_bytes());
 365:     let d = kh.finalize();
 366:     key.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
 367:     let mut mh = Hasher::new_keyed(&key);
 368:     mh.update(client_ephem_pk);
 369:     let m = mh.finalize();
 370:     let mut out = [0u8; HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN];
 371:     out.copy_from_slice(&m.as_bytes()[..HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN]);
 372:     key.zeroize();
 373:     out
 374: }
 375: 
 376: /// Compute the server's auth tag binding the full handshake transcript.
 377: fn compute_server_auth_tag(
 378:     bridge_id: &[u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 379:     epoch: u64,
 380:     client_ephem_pk: &[u8; 32],
 381:     server_ephem_pk: &[u8; 32],
 382: ) -> [u8; HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN] {
 383:     let mut key = [0u8; 32];
 384:     let mut kh = Hasher::new();
 385:     kh.update(HMAC_DOMAIN);
 386:     kh.update(b"-server-mac");
 387:     kh.update(bridge_id);
 388:     kh.update(&epoch.to_be_bytes());
 389:     let d = kh.finalize();
 390:     key.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
 391:     let mut mh = Hasher::new_keyed(&key);
 392:     mh.update(client_ephem_pk);
 393:     mh.update(server_ephem_pk);
 394:     let m = mh.finalize();
 395:     let mut out = [0u8; HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN];
 396:     out.copy_from_slice(&m.as_bytes()[..HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN]);
 397:     key.zeroize();
 398:     out
 399: }
 400: 
 401: /// Derive `(client_tx_key, server_tx_key)` from the ECDH shared +
 402: /// transcript. Each direction gets a distinct OBFS_KEY_LEN-byte key
 403: /// so client→server and server→client streams never collide.
 404: fn derive_session_keys(
 405:     shared: &[u8; 32],
 406:     bridge_id: &[u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN],
 407:     client_ephem_pk: &[u8; 32],
 408:     server_ephem_pk: &[u8; 32],
 409: ) -> ([u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN], [u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN]) {
 410:     let derive = |label: &[u8]| -> [u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN] {
 411:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 412:         h.update(KDF_DOMAIN);
 413:         h.update(label);
 414:         h.update(shared);
 415:         h.update(bridge_id);
 416:         h.update(client_ephem_pk);
 417:         h.update(server_ephem_pk);
 418:         let d = h.finalize();
 419:         let mut out = [0u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN];
 420:         out.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
 421:         out
 422:     };
 423:     let client_tx = derive(b"-client-tx");
 424:     let server_tx = derive(b"-server-tx");
 425:     (client_tx, server_tx)
 426: }

 433:     #[test]
 434:     fn handshake_round_trip_derives_matching_session_keys() {
 435:         let bridge = BridgeKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng);
 436:         let bridge_pk_bytes: [u8; BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN] = *bridge.public.as_bytes();
 437:         let now = 1_700_000_000u64;
 438: 
 439:         let client = ClientHandshake::start(
 440:             &mut OsRng,
 441:             &bridge_pk_bytes,
 442:             &bridge.id,
 443:             now,
 444:         );
 445:         let first = *client.first_message();
 446: 
 447:         let (reply, server_session) =
 448:             ServerHandshake::accept(&mut OsRng, &bridge, &first, now).unwrap();
 449: 
 450:         let client_session = client.finish(&reply).unwrap();
 451:         // Both sides should hold matching key sets — proof via
 452:         // round-trip of a packet.
 453:         let plaintext = b"hello over the bridge";
 454:         let on_wire = client_session.seal_outbound(plaintext, 1);
 455:         let recovered = server_session.open_inbound(&on_wire, 1).unwrap();
 456:         assert_eq!(recovered, plaintext);
 457:         // And in the reverse direction.
 458:         let plaintext2 = b"reply from the bridge";
 459:         let on_wire2 = server_session.seal_outbound(plaintext2, 1);
 460:         let recovered2 = client_session.open_inbound(&on_wire2, 1).unwrap();
 461:         assert_eq!(recovered2, plaintext2);
 462:     }

   1: //! Row 7 — pluggable transport layer.
   2: //!
   3: //! Two-part stack:
   4: //!
   5: //! 1. [`primitive`]: ChaCha20-keyed byte XOR. Length-preserving,
   6: //!    indistinguishable from random when the observer doesn't hold
   7: //!    the key. The foundation.
   8: //! 2. [`handshake`]: obfs4-style ECDH + bridge-identity HMAC binding.
   9: //!    Negotiates the bulk-cipher key per connection, defends against
  10: //!    active probe attackers via the bridge-id HMAC.
  11: //! 3. [`session`]: stateful per-direction Sealer/Opener built on
  12: //!    the handshake-derived keys + primitive obfuscate.
  13: //!
  14: //! Honest scope: this is the SECURITY layer for pluggable transport.
  15: //! Full TLS-shape mimicry (Cloak / Snowflake JA3-perfect handshakes)
  16: //! is its own ship on top — the keys + nonces are here, the
  17: //! application-layer "look like Chrome ClientHello" is upstream.
  18: //!
  19: //! ## Example: bridge ↔ client handshake + bidirectional traffic
  20: //!
  21: //! ```
  22: //! use ol_onion::transport_obfs::{
  23: //!     BridgeKeypair, ClientHandshake, ServerHandshake,
  24: //! };
  25: //! use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  26: //!
  27: //! // Out-of-band setup: client learns (bridge_pubkey, bridge_id)
  28: //! // via F2 pair-by-QR or a trusted-channel hand-off.
  29: //! let bridge = BridgeKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng);
  30: //! let bridge_pubkey = *bridge.public.as_bytes();
  31: //! let bridge_id = bridge.id_bytes();
  32: //! let now = 1_700_000_000u64;
  33: //!
  34: //! // Client starts the handshake; transmits client.first_message().
  35: //! let client = ClientHandshake::start(&mut OsRng, &bridge_pubkey, &bridge_id, now);
  36: //! let first = *client.first_message();
  37: //!
  38: //! // Server validates the MAC + replies; both sides derive matching keys.
  39: //! let (reply, server_session) =
  40: //!     ServerHandshake::accept(&mut OsRng, &bridge, &first, now).unwrap();
  41: //! let client_session = client.finish(&reply).unwrap();
  42: //!
  43: //! // Each direction has a separate ChaCha20 stream; counters MUST be
  44: //! // per-packet-unique to avoid (key, nonce) collisions.
  45: //! let on_wire = client_session.seal_outbound(b"hello bridge", 1);
  46: //! let recovered = server_session.open_inbound(&on_wire, 1).unwrap();
  47: //! assert_eq!(recovered, b"hello bridge");
  48: //! ```

  51: pub mod primitive;

   1: //! Row 7 — pluggable transport obfuscation primitive.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wraps wire bytes with a ChaCha20 keystream derived from a pre-
   4: //! shared key + per-packet nonce. A DPI box / passive observer that
   5: //! doesn't hold the pre-shared key sees uniformly-random bytes,
   6: //! making One Link traffic statistically indistinguishable from
   7: //! e.g. encrypted-but-padded HTTPS payloads, random VPN traffic, or
   8: //! WireGuard packet bodies.
   9: //!
  10: //! ## What this is
  11: //!
  12: //! A FOUNDATION. Real pluggable transports (obfs4, Cloak, Snowflake)
  13: //! build a TLS-shaped or browser-fronting handshake on top of an
  14: //! obfuscation primitive like this one. The handshake is where the
  15: //! key exchange + protocol fingerprint live; this layer is purely
  16: //! the bulk-byte XOR after the key is established.
  17: //!
  18: //! ## What this is NOT
  19: //!
  20: //! - Not a full TLS-mimicry. Real DPI defeats need to mimic the
  21: //!   TLS handshake bit-for-bit + JA3 fingerprint matching.
  22: //! - Not a key-exchange protocol. The pre-shared key arrives via
  23: //!   F2 pair-by-QR or F3-onion-routed channel.
  24: //! - Not steganographic. Random-looking is the goal, not "looks like
  25: //!   YouTube traffic specifically." For deeper traffic-analysis
  26: //!   resistance, layer cover-traffic (row 6) + onion routing
  27: //!   (row 5).
  28: //!
  29: //! ## API
  30: //!
  31: //! `obfuscate(key, packet_bytes, packet_id) -> Vec<u8>` XORs the
  32: //! input with a deterministic ChaCha20 keystream. `deobfuscate(...)`
  33: //! is the same operation (XOR is symmetric).
  34: //!
  35: //! Length is preserved byte-for-byte. There is NO authentication at
  36: //! this layer — apply it BENEATH an authenticated transport (QUIC's
  37: //! TLS handshake, the Sphinx layer's MAC, the noise of Double
  38: //! Ratchet) so a flipped byte by the censor causes the upper layer
  39: //! to drop the packet.
  40: 
  41: use chacha20::cipher::{KeyIvInit, StreamCipher};
  42: use chacha20::ChaCha20;
  43: use thiserror::Error;
  44: 
  45: /// Length of the pre-shared obfuscation key.
  46: pub const OBFS_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  47: 
  48: /// Length of the per-packet nonce. ChaCha20 standard 96-bit nonce.
  49: pub const OBFS_NONCE_LEN: usize = 12;
  50: 
  51: /// Typed error surface.
  52: #[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  53: pub enum ObfsError {
  54:     /// Wrong key or nonce length.
  55:     #[error("wrong byte length: expected {expected}, got {got}")]
  56:     BadLength {
  57:         /// Required length.
  58:         expected: usize,
  59:         /// Actual length.
  60:         got: usize,
  61:     },
  62: }
  63: 
  64: /// Obfuscate `bytes` with the key + nonce. Returns a fresh Vec of
  65: /// the same length. Symmetric: pass the same key + nonce to
  66: /// `deobfuscate` (or `obfuscate` again) to recover the input.
  67: ///
  68: /// Nonces MUST NOT repeat under the same key — pick a fresh nonce
  69: /// per packet (e.g., a per-connection counter + random per-conn
  70: /// salt). Reusing a (key, nonce) pair leaks the XOR of two
  71: /// plaintexts.
  72: pub fn obfuscate(
  73:     key: &[u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN],
  74:     nonce: &[u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN],
  75:     bytes: &[u8],
  76: ) -> Vec<u8> {
  77:     let mut out = bytes.to_vec();
  78:     let mut cipher = ChaCha20::new(key.into(), nonce.into());
  79:     cipher.apply_keystream(&mut out);
  80:     out
  81: }
  82: 
  83: /// In-place version of [`obfuscate`]. Useful for hot-path callers
  84: /// that pre-allocate buffers.
  85: pub fn obfuscate_in_place(
  86:     key: &[u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN],
  87:     nonce: &[u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN],
  88:     bytes: &mut [u8],
  89: ) {
  90:     let mut cipher = ChaCha20::new(key.into(), nonce.into());
  91:     cipher.apply_keystream(bytes);
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /// Deobfuscate `bytes`. Pure-alias for [`obfuscate`] — ChaCha20
  95: /// XOR is symmetric. Provided as a separate name so call sites
  96: /// document direction.
  97: pub fn deobfuscate(
  98:     key: &[u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN],
  99:     nonce: &[u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN],
 100:     bytes: &[u8],
 101: ) -> Vec<u8> {
 102:     obfuscate(key, nonce, bytes)
 103: }
 104: 
 105: /// In-place deobfuscate. Symmetric alias for `obfuscate_in_place`.
 106: pub fn deobfuscate_in_place(
 107:     key: &[u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN],
 108:     nonce: &[u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN],
 109:     bytes: &mut [u8],
 110: ) {
 111:     obfuscate_in_place(key, nonce, bytes);
 112: }
 113: 
 114: /// Derive a per-packet nonce from a connection ID + monotonic
 115: /// packet counter. The connection ID provides per-connection
 116: /// uniqueness; the counter provides per-packet uniqueness.
 117: ///
 118: /// Format: 4-byte conn_id || 8-byte counter (big-endian) = 12 bytes.
 119: ///
 120: /// Daemons SHOULD use this rather than rolling their own nonce
 121: /// scheme — repeating a (key, nonce) pair is catastrophic.
 122: pub fn derive_nonce(conn_id: u32, packet_counter: u64) -> [u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN] {
 123:     let mut out = [0u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN];
 124:     out[..4].copy_from_slice(&conn_id.to_be_bytes());
 125:     out[4..].copy_from_slice(&packet_counter.to_be_bytes());
 126:     out
 127: }

 175:     fn output_looks_uniform_for_zero_plaintext() {
 176:         // Pure keystream output (XOR with all-zero plaintext).
 177:         let key = [0xAB; OBFS_KEY_LEN];
 178:         let nonce = [0xCD; OBFS_NONCE_LEN];
 179:         let plain = vec![0u8; 4096];
 180:         let obf = obfuscate(&key, &nonce, &plain);
 181:         // Chi-squared: byte distribution should look uniform.
 182:         let mut counts = [0u32; 256];
 183:         for &b in &obf {
 184:             counts[b as usize] += 1;
 185:         }
 186:         let expected = obf.len() as f64 / 256.0;
 187:         let chi: f64 = counts
 188:             .iter()
 189:             .map(|&c| {
 190:                 let d = c as f64 - expected;
 191:                 d * d / expected
 192:             })
 193:             .sum();
 194:         // df=255 critical value at p=0.001 is ~340. ChaCha20 output
 195:         // sits comfortably under this.
 196:         eprintln!("obfuscation byte-dist chi-sq = {chi:.1}");
 197:         assert!(chi < 400.0);
 198:     }

 230:         // Confirms the layer has NO integrity — a censor flipping
 231:         // bytes propagates to the deobfuscated output. This is the
 232:         // intentional property: integrity comes from the upper layer
 233:         // (Sphinx MAC, AEAD, Double Ratchet, QUIC TLS).
 234:         let key = [0x88; OBFS_KEY_LEN];

 240:         assert_ne!(recovered, plain);
 241:         // The flipped bit propagates directly (stream cipher).
 242:         let mut expected = plain.to_vec();
 243:         expected[3] ^= 0x01;
 244:         assert_eq!(recovered, expected);
 245:     }

   1: //! Stateful per-direction Sealer/Opener over handshake-derived keys.
   2: //!
   3: //! A `Session` holds two ChaCha20 keys: one for OUTBOUND traffic
   4: //! (this side → peer) and one for INBOUND (peer → this side).
   5: //! Both sides derive the same two keys, but their `outbound_key`
   6: //! and `inbound_key` are swapped — so client.outbound ==
   7: //! server.inbound and vice versa. Each direction uses
   8: //! `derive_nonce(direction_tag, packet_counter)` to produce unique
   9: //! per-packet ChaCha20 nonces; (key, nonce) pairs never repeat.
  10: 
  11: use crate::transport_obfs::primitive::{
  12:     deobfuscate, derive_nonce, obfuscate, OBFS_KEY_LEN,
  13: };
  14: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  15: 
  16: /// Length of a session key (= ChaCha20 key length).
  17: pub const SESSION_KEY_LEN: usize = OBFS_KEY_LEN;
  18: 
  19: /// Tag used by `derive_nonce`. Direction is captured by WHICH key
  20: /// (outbound_key vs inbound_key) is used, so both directions can
  21: /// use the same tag; (key, nonce) pairs never repeat because the
  22: /// keys differ.
  23: const OUTBOUND_DIRECTION_TAG: u32 = 0x4F4C5458; // "OLTX"
  24: 
  25: /// Which direction a packet flows.
  26: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  27: pub enum SessionDirection {
  28:     /// This side → peer.
  29:     Outbound,
  30:     /// Peer → this side.
  31:     Inbound,
  32: }
  33: 
  34: /// A bidirectional obfuscation session derived from the handshake.
  35: pub struct Session {
  36:     outbound_key: [u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN],
  37:     inbound_key: [u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN],
  38: }
  39: 
  40: impl Session {
  41:     /// Client-side constructor: client's outbound = `client_tx_key`,
  42:     /// client's inbound = `server_tx_key`.
  43:     pub fn new(client_tx_key: [u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN], server_tx_key: [u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN]) -> Self {
  44:         Self {
  45:             outbound_key: client_tx_key,
  46:             inbound_key: server_tx_key,
  47:         }
  48:     }
  49: 
  50:     /// Server-side constructor: server's outbound = `server_tx_key`,
  51:     /// server's inbound = `client_tx_key`. (Same two keys as
  52:     /// `Session::new`, but mirrored.)
  53:     pub fn for_server(
  54:         client_tx_key: [u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN],
  55:         server_tx_key: [u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN],
  56:     ) -> Self {
  57:         Self {
  58:             outbound_key: server_tx_key,
  59:             inbound_key: client_tx_key,
  60:         }
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// Obfuscate an outbound packet with `counter` (must increase
  64:     /// monotonically; daemon owns the counter state).
  65:     pub fn seal_outbound(&self, plaintext: &[u8], counter: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
  66:         let nonce = derive_nonce(OUTBOUND_DIRECTION_TAG, counter);
  67:         obfuscate(&self.outbound_key, &nonce, plaintext)
  68:     }
  69: 
  70:     /// Deobfuscate an inbound packet with the peer's `counter`.
  71:     /// Returns the recovered bytes (this layer has no integrity —
  72:     /// upper layer must MAC).
  73:     pub fn open_inbound(&self, ciphertext: &[u8], counter: u64) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ()> {
  74:         // Both directions derive the nonce with OUTBOUND_DIRECTION_TAG:
  75:         // direction is captured by WHICH key is used (outbound_key vs
  76:         // inbound_key), so the tag is fixed and both sides agree.
  77:         let nonce = derive_nonce(OUTBOUND_DIRECTION_TAG, counter);
  78:         Ok(deobfuscate(&self.inbound_key, &nonce, ciphertext))
  79:     }
  80: 
  81: }
  82: 
  83: impl std::fmt::Debug for Session {
  84:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  85:         f.debug_struct("Session").finish_non_exhaustive()
  86:     }
  87: }
  88: 
  89: impl Drop for Session {
  90:     fn drop(&mut self) {
  91:         self.outbound_key.zeroize();
  92:         self.inbound_key.zeroize();
  93:     }
  94: }
  95:

   1: //! Adversarial test vectors for ol_onion.
   2: //!
   3: //! Catches known-attack patterns + edge cases that random property
   4: //! tests might miss.

   6: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
   7: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
   8: 
   9: use ol_onion::{
  10:     build_onion, peel_one_layer, Circuit, HopDescriptor, HopId, OnionError, OnionPacket,
  11:     PeelOutcome, HOP_ID_LEN,
  12: };
  13: 
  14: fn make_hop_pair(i: u8) -> (StaticSecret, HopDescriptor) {
  15:     let sk = StaticSecret::from([i; 32]);
  16:     let pk = PublicKey::from(&sk);
  17:     (
  18:         sk,
  19:         HopDescriptor {
  20:             id: HopId::from_bytes([i; HOP_ID_LEN]),
  21:             pubkey: pk,
  22:         },
  23:     )
  24: }

  28: #[test]
  29: fn adversarial_relay_cannot_decrypt_inner_layer() {
  30:     // Build a 3-hop onion. r1 peels its layer, then tries to peel
  31:     // the inner packet with its OWN key (instead of forwarding) —
  32:     // must fail with AeadFail.
  33:     let (r1_sk, r1) = make_hop_pair(1);
  34:     let (_, r2) = make_hop_pair(2);
  35:     let (_, dest) = make_hop_pair(3);
  36:     let circuit = Circuit::new(vec![r1, r2.clone(), dest]).unwrap();
  37:     let packet = build_onion(&circuit, b"secret", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  38:     let outcome = peel_one_layer(&r1_sk, &packet).unwrap();
  39:     let inner_bytes = match outcome {
  40:         PeelOutcome::Forward {
  41:             inner_packet_bytes, ..
  42:         } => inner_packet_bytes,
  43:         _ => panic!(),
  44:     };
  45:     let inner = OnionPacket::decode(&inner_bytes).unwrap();
  46:     // r1 attempts to peel the inner packet (which belongs to r2).
  47:     let err = peel_one_layer(&r1_sk, &inner).unwrap_err();
  48:     assert_eq!(err, OnionError::AeadFail);
  49: }

 137: #[test]
 138: fn adversarial_session_nonce_reuse_leaks_xor() {
 139:     // Sanity check on the well-known XOR-cipher property:
 140:     // SAME (key, counter) on two plaintexts → cipher_a ⊕ cipher_b
 141:     // = plaintext_a ⊕ plaintext_b. This test exists to lock in that
 142:     // the daemon MUST advance counter per packet; if it doesn't,
 143:     // this property leaks XOR. Recorded here as a known hazard.
 144:     let k1 = [0x11u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN];
 145:     let k2 = [0x22u8; SESSION_KEY_LEN];
 146:     let client = Session::new(k1, k2);
 147:     let p1 = b"plaintext-AAAAAA";
 148:     let p2 = b"plaintext-BBBBBB";
 149:     let c1 = client.seal_outbound(p1, 1);
 150:     let c2 = client.seal_outbound(p2, 1); // SAME counter -- BAD!
 151:     let xor_c: Vec<u8> = c1.iter().zip(c2.iter()).map(|(a, b)| a ^ b).collect();
 152:     let xor_p: Vec<u8> = p1.iter().zip(p2.iter()).map(|(a, b)| a ^ b).collect();
 153:     assert_eq!(xor_c, xor_p, "nonce reuse leaks plaintext XOR");
 154: }

   1: //! Adversarial vectors for Sphinx Coherence T1.5 (Schnorr aggregation).
   2: //!
   3: //! Targeted attempts to bypass `verify` / `batch_verify`:
   4: //! - Identity-R signatures (R = O)
   5: //! - Identity-PK signatures (PK = O)
   6: //! - Swapped messages
   7: //! - Cross-signer swap
   8: //! - Duplicated entry
   9: //! - Tampered batch order (verifier weighting binds to order)
  10: //! - Truncated signatures
  11: //! - Replay across distinct keys
  12: 
  13: use ol_onion::sphinx::aggsig::{
  14:     batch_verify, verify, SchnorrSignature, SchnorrSigningKey, SchnorrVerifyingKey,
  15: };
  16: 
  17: fn sk(seed: u8) -> SchnorrSigningKey {
  18:     SchnorrSigningKey::from_seed(&[seed; 32])
  19: }

  22: fn identity_r_signature_rejected() {
  23:     let sk_a = sk(1);

  27:     let mut tampered = sig;

  42: #[test]
  43: fn identity_pk_forgery_attempt_rejected() {
  44:     // Regression test for H2 (post-audit fix May 14 2026): with
  45:     // vk = O the equation `s*G == R + c*PK` reduces to `s*G == R`,
  46:     // which any attacker can satisfy with (R = nonce*G, s = nonce).
  47:     // Audit found: verify() previously accepted this. Fix rejects
  48:     // identity-VK at decode time.
  49:     let evil_vk = SchnorrVerifyingKey([0u8; 32]);
  50:     // Construct a forgery that satisfies s*G == R with no signing key.
  51:     // s = 7 (arbitrary), R = 7*G compressed.
  52:     use curve25519_dalek::constants::RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE;
  53:     use curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar;
  54:     let s = Scalar::from(7u64);
  55:     let r_point = RISTRETTO_BASEPOINT_TABLE * &s;
  56:     let mut sig_bytes = [0u8; 64];
  57:     sig_bytes[..32].copy_from_slice(&r_point.compress().to_bytes());
  58:     sig_bytes[32..].copy_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
  59:     let forgery = ol_onion::sphinx::aggsig::SchnorrSignature(sig_bytes);
  60:     // This forgery would verify under vk = identity if the decoder
  61:     // didn't reject. Confirm it's rejected.
  62:     assert!(
  63:         verify(&evil_vk, b"forge-target", &forgery).is_err(),
  64:         "identity-VK signature forgery must be rejected at decode"
  65:     );
  66: }

  61:     /// Any single-bit flip in the signature is rejected.
  62:     #[test]
  63:     fn one_bit_flip_rejected(
  64:         seed in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
  65:         msg in proptest::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 1..128),
  66:         bit in 0u32..512,
  67:     ) {
  68:         let sk = SchnorrSigningKey::from_seed(&seed);
  69:         let vk = sk.verifying_key();
  70:         let mut sig = sk.sign(&msg);
  71:         let byte = (bit / 8) as usize;
  72:         let mask = 1u8 << (bit % 8);
  73:         sig.0[byte] ^= mask;
  74:         prop_assert!(verify(&vk, &msg, &sig).is_err());
  75:     }

  77:     /// Any single-bit flip in the message is rejected.

  80:         seed in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
  81:         msg in proptest::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 1..128),
  82:         bit_pos in 0u32..1024,
  83:     ) {
  84:         let sk = SchnorrSigningKey::from_seed(&seed);
  85:         let vk = sk.verifying_key();
  86:         let sig = sk.sign(&msg);
  87:         let mut tampered = msg.clone();
  88:         let byte = (bit_pos as usize) / 8;
  89:         if byte < tampered.len() {
  90:             tampered[byte] ^= 1u8 << (bit_pos % 8);

  92:             if tampered != msg {
  93:                 prop_assert!(verify(&vk, &tampered, &sig).is_err());
  94:             }
  95:         }

   1: //! Constant-time validation for ol_onion comparison surfaces.
   2: //!
   3: //! Same pattern as F1.1 / F2: measure wall-clock variance across
   4: //! buckets; gate at 5% relative stddev.
   5: 
   6: use std::time::Instant;
   7: 
   8: use ol_onion::keyderiv::LayerKey;
   9: use ol_onion::{HopId, HOP_ID_LEN};
  10: 
  11: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 50_000;
  12: 
  13: fn relative_stddev(samples: &[f64]) -> f64 {
  14:     let mean: f64 = samples.iter().sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  15:     let variance: f64 =
  16:         samples.iter().map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  17:     variance.sqrt() / mean
  18: }
  19: 
  20: fn measure<F: FnMut()>(mut work: F, iterations: usize) -> u128 {
  21:     let start = Instant::now();
  22:     for _ in 0..iterations {
  23:         work();
  24:     }
  25:     start.elapsed().as_nanos()
  26: }
  27: 
  28: #[test]
  29: fn hop_id_eq_constant_time() {
  30:     let base = HopId::from_bytes([0x42u8; HOP_ID_LEN]);
  31:     let candidates: Vec<HopId> = vec![
  32:         HopId::from_bytes([0x42u8; HOP_ID_LEN]),
  33:         {
  34:             let mut b = [0x42u8; HOP_ID_LEN];
  35:             b[0] ^= 0x01;
  36:             HopId::from_bytes(b)
  37:         },
  38:         {
  39:             let mut b = [0x42u8; HOP_ID_LEN];
  40:             b[15] ^= 0x01;
  41:             HopId::from_bytes(b)
  42:         },
  43:         {
  44:             let mut b = [0x42u8; HOP_ID_LEN];
  45:             b[31] ^= 0x01;
  46:             HopId::from_bytes(b)
  47:         },
  48:         HopId::from_bytes([0xCDu8; HOP_ID_LEN]),
  49:     ];
  50:     for c in &candidates {
  51:         let _ = measure(|| {
  52:             let _ = base == *c;
  53:         }, 10_000);
  54:     }
  55:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(candidates.len());
  56:     for c in &candidates {
  57:         let ns = measure(
  58:             || {
  59:                 std::hint::black_box(base == *std::hint::black_box(c));
  60:             },
  61:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  62:         ) as f64;
  63:         totals.push(ns);
  64:     }
  65:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
  66:     eprintln!("hop_id eq totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}");
  67:     assert!(rel < 0.05, "hop_id eq relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 5% gate");
  68: }
  69: 
  70: #[test]
  71: fn layer_key_eq_constant_time() {

  96:         }, 10_000);
  97:     }
  98:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(candidates.len());
  99:     for c in &candidates {

 109:     eprintln!("layer_key eq totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}");
 110:     assert!(rel < 0.05, "layer_key eq relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 5% gate");

   1: //! Constant-time validation for the handshake MAC verify path.
   2: //!
   3: //! `ServerHandshake::accept` checks the client MAC using
   4: //! `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` — but a regression that swaps it for
   5: //! `==` (or short-circuits across the current/previous epoch check)
   6: //! would leak first-differing-byte position to a timing attacker.
   7: //!
   8: //! Pattern matches F1.1 / F2 / row 1: measure wall-clock variance
   9: //! across buckets that mismatch at different byte positions; gate at
  10: //! a low % relative stddev.
  11: 
  12: use std::time::Instant;
  13: 
  14: use ol_onion::transport_obfs::handshake::{
  15:     BridgeKeypair, ClientHandshake, ServerHandshake, BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN,
  16:     HANDSHAKE_LEN,
  17: };
  18: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  19: 
  20: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 5_000;
  21: 
  22: fn relative_stddev(samples: &[f64]) -> f64 {
  23:     let mean: f64 = samples.iter().sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  24:     let variance: f64 =
  25:         samples.iter().map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  26:     variance.sqrt() / mean
  27: }
  28: 
  29: fn measure<F: FnMut()>(mut work: F, iters: usize) -> u128 {
  30:     let start = Instant::now();
  31:     for _ in 0..iters {
  32:         work();
  33:     }
  34:     start.elapsed().as_nanos()
  35: }
  36: 
  37: #[test]
  38: fn handshake_mac_verify_constant_time_across_tamper_positions() {
  39:     // Build a real client handshake message, then create tampered
  40:     // versions that mismatch the MAC at different byte positions in
  41:     // the MAC field (offset 32..48 of the 48-byte message).
  42:     let bridge = BridgeKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng);
  43:     let bridge_pk: [u8; BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN] = *bridge.public.as_bytes();
  44:     let now = 1_700_000_000u64;
  45:     let client = ClientHandshake::start(&mut OsRng, &bridge_pk, &bridge.id, now);
  46:     let real_msg = *client.first_message();
  47: 
  48:     // Five tamper positions in the MAC field (bytes 32..48):
  49:     //   32 = first MAC byte
  50:     //   35 = early MAC byte
  51:     //   39 = mid MAC byte
  52:     //   43 = late MAC byte
  53:     //   47 = last MAC byte
  54:     // A non-CT comparison would diverge in timing across these.
  55:     let positions = [32usize, 35, 39, 43, 47];
  56:     let mut tampered: Vec<[u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN]> = positions
  57:         .iter()
  58:         .map(|&pos| {
  59:             let mut m = real_msg;
  60:             m[pos] ^= 0xFF;
  61:             m
  62:         })
  63:         .collect();
  64: 
  65:     // Warm up the path so the first-call overhead is amortized.
  66:     for msg in &tampered {
  67:         let _ = measure(
  68:             || {
  69:                 let _ =
  70:                     ServerHandshake::accept(&mut OsRng, &bridge, msg, now);
  71:             },
  72:             10,
  73:         );
  74:     }
  75: 
  76:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(tampered.len());
  77:     for msg in &mut tampered {
  78:         let ns = measure(
  79:             || {
  80:                 let _ = std::hint::black_box(ServerHandshake::accept(
  81:                     &mut OsRng,
  82:                     std::hint::black_box(&bridge),
  83:                     std::hint::black_box(msg),
  84:                     now,
  85:                 ));
  86:             },
  87:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  88:         ) as f64;
  89:         totals.push(ns);
  90:     }
  91:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
  92:     eprintln!(
  93:         "handshake-MAC timing totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}"
  94:     );
  95:     // The MAC compare itself is constant-time via `subtle::ct_eq`.
  96:     // Residual variance comes from the always-run "try current AND
  97:     // previous epoch" path (two MAC recomputes) plus general OS noise.
  98:     // 15% gate catches the LARGE regressions:
  99:     //   - Swap of `subtle::ct_eq` for byte `==`.
 100:     //   - "Short-circuit on current-epoch match" optimization that
 101:     //     skips the previous-epoch try.
 102:     assert!(
 103:         rel < 0.15,
 104:         "handshake-MAC relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 15% gate — \
 105:          likely a non-constant-time compare regression"
 106:     );
 107: }

   1: //! Empirical hop-blindness tests.
   2: //!
   3: //! TLA+ proves logical hop-blindness (see `docs/formal/onion.tla`).
   4: //! These tests check the empirical byte-level property: at every
   5: //! position along a 3-hop circuit, the packet "looks the same" in
   6: //! its structural features (version byte, hops_remaining field
   7: //! takes the expected value, ephemeral pubkey + nonce + ciphertext
   8: //! all appear uniformly random to an observer).
   9: //!
  10: //! What we DON'T claim: that a global passive adversary cannot
  11: //! correlate timing or packet size. Packet size shrinks
  12: //! predictably per peel — that's the documented transport-layer
  13: //! padding concern.
  14: 
  15: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  16: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  17: 
  18: use ol_onion::{
  19:     build_onion, peel_one_layer, Circuit, HopDescriptor, HopId, OnionPacket,
  20:     PeelOutcome, HOP_ID_LEN,
  21: };
  22: 
  23: fn make_hop(i: u8) -> (StaticSecret, HopDescriptor) {
  24:     let sk = StaticSecret::from([i; 32]);
  25:     let pk = PublicKey::from(&sk);
  26:     (
  27:         sk,
  28:         HopDescriptor {
  29:             id: HopId::from_bytes([i; HOP_ID_LEN]),
  30:             pubkey: pk,
  31:         },
  32:     )
  33: }
  34: 
  35: /// Byte-frequency chi-squared statistic against uniform.
  36: fn chi_squared_uniform(bytes: &[u8]) -> f64 {
  37:     let mut counts = [0u32; 256];
  38:     for &b in bytes {
  39:         counts[b as usize] += 1;
  40:     }
  41:     let n = bytes.len() as f64;
  42:     let expected = n / 256.0;
  43:     if expected < 1.0 {
  44:         return 0.0; // sample too small to be meaningful
  45:     }
  46:     counts
  47:         .iter()
  48:         .map(|&c| {
  49:             let d = c as f64 - expected;
  50:             d * d / expected
  51:         })
  52:         .sum()
  53: }
  54: 
  55: #[test]
  56: fn ciphertext_at_each_hop_looks_uniformly_random() {
  57:     // Build a 3-hop circuit, peel at each hop, accumulate the
  58:     // ciphertext bytes from every layer. Aggregate chi-squared
  59:     // should be in the "looks uniform" range (chi-sq < 350 for
  60:     // df=255 at p=0.001).
  61:     let (r1_sk, r1) = make_hop(1);
  62:     let (r2_sk, r2) = make_hop(2);
  63:     let (dest_sk, dest) = make_hop(3);
  64:     let circuit = Circuit::new(vec![r1, r2, dest]).unwrap();
  65:     let mut all_ciphertext = Vec::new();
  66: 
  67:     // Build ~50 packets so we have ~50*200 = 10000 bytes of ciphertext.
  68:     for _ in 0..50 {
  69:         let payload = vec![0xAAu8; 200]; // constant plaintext to isolate the cipher
  70:         let mut packet = build_onion(&circuit, &payload, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  71:         all_ciphertext.extend_from_slice(&packet.ciphertext);
  72:         // Peel through.
  73:         for sk in [&r1_sk, &r2_sk, &dest_sk] {
  74:             match peel_one_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap() {
  75:                 PeelOutcome::Forward {
  76:                     inner_packet_bytes, ..
  77:                 } => {
  78:                     packet = OnionPacket::decode(&inner_packet_bytes).unwrap();
  79:                     all_ciphertext.extend_from_slice(&packet.ciphertext);
  80:                 }
  81:                 PeelOutcome::Deliver { .. } => break,
  82:             }
  83:         }
  84:     }
  85: 
  86:     let chi = chi_squared_uniform(&all_ciphertext);
  87:     // 350 is the chi-sq critical value for df=255 at p=0.001 (very
  88:     // loose). ChaCha20 ciphertext should sit well under this.
  89:     eprintln!(
  90:         "hop_blindness: {} bytes, chi-sq = {chi:.1}",
  91:         all_ciphertext.len()
  92:     );
  93:     assert!(
  94:         chi < 350.0,
  95:         "ciphertext bytes deviate from uniform: chi-sq = {chi:.1}"
  96:     );
  97: }
  98: 
  99: #[test]
 100: fn packet_structure_invariant_across_all_hops() {
 101:     // At every hop along a 3-hop circuit the packet has:
 102:     //   - version == 1
 103:     //   - hops_remaining decrements by 1
 104:     //   - ephem_pubkey is non-zero (small-order defense)
 105:     //   - aead_nonce is 12 bytes
 106:     //   - ciphertext is non-empty
 107:     let (r1_sk, r1) = make_hop(10);
 108:     let (r2_sk, r2) = make_hop(20);
 109:     let (dest_sk, dest) = make_hop(30);
 110:     let circuit = Circuit::new(vec![r1, r2, dest]).unwrap();
 111:     let mut packet = build_onion(&circuit, b"hop-blindness", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 112: 
 113:     let mut hops_seen: Vec<u8> = vec![packet.hops_remaining];
 114:     assert_eq!(packet.version, 1);
 115:     assert!(packet.ephem_pubkey.iter().any(|&b| b != 0));
 116:     assert!(!packet.ciphertext.is_empty());
 117: 
 118:     for sk in [&r1_sk, &r2_sk, &dest_sk] {
 119:         match peel_one_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap() {
 120:             PeelOutcome::Forward {
 121:                 inner_packet_bytes, ..
 122:             } => {
 123:                 packet = OnionPacket::decode(&inner_packet_bytes).unwrap();
 124:                 hops_seen.push(packet.hops_remaining);
 125:                 assert_eq!(packet.version, 1);
 126:                 assert!(packet.ephem_pubkey.iter().any(|&b| b != 0));
 127:                 assert!(!packet.ciphertext.is_empty());
 128:             }
 129:             PeelOutcome::Deliver { .. } => break,
 130:         }
 131:     }
 132:     // hops_remaining at each layer: 2, 1, 0.
 133:     assert_eq!(hops_seen, vec![2u8, 1, 0]);
 134: }

 159:     }

 162:         for j in (i + 1)..seen.len() {
 163:             assert_ne!(seen[i], seen[j], "ephem_pubkey collision");
 164:         }
 165:     }

   1: //! Known-answer test vectors (KAT) for ol_onion.
   2: //!
   3: //! The onion building loop calls into the RNG for ephemeral
   4: //! material — to get DETERMINISTIC outputs, the KAT test uses a
   5: //! seeded RNG (rand_chacha::ChaCha20Rng with a fixed seed).
   6: //!
   7: //! Pinning the exact byte output of a small fixed circuit catches:
   8: //! - ChaCha20-Poly1305 / BLAKE3 primitive changes upstream.
   9: //! - Domain separator drift.
  10: //! - Wire format changes (encode ordering, version bumps).
  11: //! - AAD computation drift.
  12: //!
  13: //! Regenerate with `OL_ONION_KAT_REGEN=1` when the wire format
  14: //! intentionally changes.

  89: fn build_kat_circuit() -> (
  90:     (StaticSecret, HopDescriptor),
  91:     (StaticSecret, HopDescriptor),
  92:     (StaticSecret, HopDescriptor),
  93:     Circuit,
  94: ) {
  95:     let make = |seed: [u8; 32], i: u8| {
  96:         let sk = StaticSecret::from(seed);
  97:         let pk = PublicKey::from(&sk);
  98:         (
  99:             sk,
 100:             HopDescriptor {

 102:                 pubkey: pk,
 103:             },

 107:     let r2 = make(RELAY_2_SK, 2);
 108:     let dest = make(DEST_SK, 3);
 109:     let circuit =
 110:         Circuit::new(vec![r1.1.clone(), r2.1.clone(), dest.1.clone()]).unwrap();
 111:     (r1, r2, dest, circuit)
 112: }

 102: use ol_onion::sphinx::cover::{
 103:     is_cover_payload_authenticated, COVER_TRAILER_LEN,
 104: };
 105: 
 106: /// Pin the audit-M4 cover-trailer derivation.
 107: ///
 108: /// Verifies that for a known (shared_key, body) pair, the
 109: /// `is_cover_payload_authenticated` check accepts a payload whose
 110: /// trailing 16 bytes are produced by the same compute-trailer
 111: /// routine, and rejects any single-bit perturbation of either body
 112: /// or trailer. This pins both the derivation function AND the
 113: /// constant-time-equality wiring.
 114: #[test]
 115: fn kat_m4_authenticated_trailer_round_trip() {
 116:     let shared_key = [0xA5u8; 32];
 117:     // Build a synthetic cover payload: sentinel || body || trailer.
 118:     let mut payload = COVER_SENTINEL.to_vec();
 119:     let body_bytes: Vec<u8> = (0u8..128).collect();
 120:     payload.extend_from_slice(&body_bytes);
 121:     // Compute trailer over (sentinel || body).
 122:     let trailer_input = payload.clone();
 123:     let derived =
 124:         blake3::derive_key("ol-sphinx-cover-trailer-v1", &shared_key);
 125:     let mut h = blake3::Hasher::new_keyed(&derived);
 126:     h.update(&trailer_input);
 127:     let mut tag = [0u8; COVER_TRAILER_LEN];
 128:     tag.copy_from_slice(&h.finalize().as_bytes()[..COVER_TRAILER_LEN]);
 129:     payload.extend_from_slice(&tag);
 130: 
 131:     assert!(
 132:         is_cover_payload_authenticated(&shared_key, &payload),
 133:         "valid trailer rejected — derivation drift?"
 134:     );
 135:     // Bit-flip in body invalidates.
 136:     let mut tampered = payload.clone();
 137:     tampered[COVER_SENTINEL.len() + 1] ^= 0x01;
 138:     assert!(
 139:         !is_cover_payload_authenticated(&shared_key, &tampered),
 140:         "body bit-flip accepted as cover — MAC binding broken!"
 141:     );
 142:     // Bit-flip in trailer invalidates.
 143:     let last = payload.len() - 1;
 144:     let mut bad_tag = payload.clone();
 145:     bad_tag[last] ^= 0x01;
 146:     assert!(
 147:         !is_cover_payload_authenticated(&shared_key, &bad_tag),
 148:         "trailer bit-flip accepted — equality not constant-time-correct?"
 149:     );
 150:     // Different shared_key rejects.
 151:     let other_key = [0x5Au8; 32];
 152:     assert!(
 153:         !is_cover_payload_authenticated(&other_key, &payload),
 154:         "wrong shared_key accepted — MAC key derivation broken!"
 155:     );
 156: }

   1: //! Property tests for the Row 6 cover-traffic primitives.
   2: //!
   3: //! Two distinct surfaces:
   4: //!   - `CoverScheduler`: deterministic-per-seed Exp(λ) generator.
   5: //!   - `RateEqualizer`: EWMA-based total-rate equalizer.
   6: //!
   7: //! Gate ladder: CI default 1M iters (matches F1.x bar); nightly 5M
   8: //! via `ONE_LINK_F1_GATE=1`.
   9: 
  10: // Audit M4: these property tests intentionally exercise the
  11: // deprecated plaintext-prefix detector to verify FAST-PATH semantics
  12: // (it must never panic, and prefix-equality must be consistent).
  13: // Cover-detection SECURITY is exercised separately via
  14: // is_cover_payload_authenticated in unit/integration tests.
  15: #![allow(deprecated)]

  20:     is_cover_payload, CoverScheduler, RateEqualizer, COVER_SENTINEL,

  24:     if std::env::var("ONE_LINK_F1_GATE").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
  25:         5_000_000
  26:     } else {
  27:         1_000_000
  28:     }
  29: }

  43:     fn is_cover_payload_never_panics(bytes in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..1024)) {
  44:         let _ = is_cover_payload(&bytes);
  45:     }

  48:     /// non-cover (prefix can't match).

  51:         prop_assert!(!is_cover_payload(&bytes));
  52:     }

 143:     /// `current_cover_rate` is always in `[0, target_total_hz]`.

 147:         timestamps in prop::collection::vec(any::<u64>(), 0..32),

 206:         prop_assert!(eq.observed_real_rate() < 1e-9);
 207:         prop_assert!((eq.current_cover_rate() - target).abs() < 1e-6);

  29: fn make_hop_pair(i: u8) -> (StaticSecret, HopDescriptor) {
  30:     let sk = StaticSecret::from([i; 32]);
  31:     let pk = PublicKey::from(&sk);
  32:     (
  33:         sk,
  34:         HopDescriptor {

  51:     /// (well-formed) ciphertext content.

  53:     fn packet_encode_decode_roundtrip(
  54:         hops_remaining in 0u8..=(MAX_HOPS as u8),
  55:         ephem in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
  56:         nonce in any::<[u8; 12]>(),

  80:     /// For any 1..=4 hop circuit and any payload, building then
  81:     /// peeling all layers recovers the original payload.
  82:     #[test]
  83:     fn end_to_end_round_trip(
  84:         n_hops in 1usize..=4,
  85:         payload in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..=200),
  86:     ) {
  87:         let hops: Vec<(StaticSecret, HopDescriptor)> =
  88:             (0..n_hops as u8).map(|i| make_hop_pair(i + 1)).collect();
  89:         let descriptors: Vec<HopDescriptor> =
  90:             hops.iter().map(|(_, h)| h.clone()).collect();
  91:         let circuit = Circuit::new(descriptors).unwrap();
  92:         let mut packet = build_onion(&circuit, &payload, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  93:         // Walk along the path.
  94:         for (i, (sk, _)) in hops.iter().enumerate() {
  95:             let outcome = peel_one_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap();
  96:             match outcome {
  97:                 PeelOutcome::Forward { inner_packet_bytes, .. } => {
  98:                     prop_assert!(i + 1 < hops.len());
  99:                     packet = OnionPacket::decode(&inner_packet_bytes).unwrap();
 100:                 }
 101:                 PeelOutcome::Deliver { payload: out } => {
 102:                     prop_assert_eq!(i, hops.len() - 1);
 103:                     prop_assert_eq!(out, payload);
 104:                     return Ok(());
 105:                 }
 106:             }
 107:         }
 108:     }

 110:     /// Wrong relay key always returns AeadFail.
 111:     #[test]
 112:     fn wrong_key_always_fails(
 113:         attacker_seed in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 114:         payload in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..=128),
 115:     ) {
 116:         let (_, dest) = make_hop_pair(1);
 117:         let circuit = Circuit::new(vec![dest]).unwrap();
 118:         let packet = build_onion(&circuit, &payload, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 119:         let attacker_sk = StaticSecret::from(attacker_seed);
 120:         // x25519 small-order produces zero shared which leads to a
 121:         // valid AEAD KEY but the AEAD tag still fails verify (since
 122:         // sender encrypted with the relay's real shared secret).
 123:         // Either AeadFail or — if attacker_seed happens to equal
 124:         // the real relay key by miracle — Ok(...). For [99u8; 32]
 125:         // this is astronomically unlikely.
 126:         let r = peel_one_layer(&attacker_sk, &packet);
 127:         prop_assert!(r.is_err() || matches!(r, Ok(_)));
 128:     }
 129: }

  20: fn make_relay() -> (curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar, SphinxHop) {
  21:     let (sk, pk) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
  22:     let mut id = [0u8; 32];
  23:     OsRng.fill(&mut id);
  24:     (
  25:         sk,
  26:         SphinxHop {
  27:             id: HopId::from_bytes(id),
  28:             static_pk: pk,
  29:         },
  30:     )
  31: }
  32: 
  33: // ── Tamper detection: every byte rejected ────────────────────────
  34: 
  35: /// Sphinx authenticates ONLY the header. The payload region is
  36: /// ChaCha20-encrypted but NOT authenticated by Sphinx itself — the
  37: /// application layer is expected to AEAD-encrypt its inner content.
  38: /// This test verifies the property at each region:
  39: ///
  40: /// - Header-region flips (bytes 1..289): rejected with AeadFail.
  41: /// - Payload-region flips (bytes 289..): may decrypt to different
  42: ///   bytes, but the user-level AEAD would catch that.
  43: #[test]
  44: fn adversarial_header_region_byte_flips_rejected() {
  45:     use ol_onion::sphinx::primitives::HEADER_LEN;
  46:     let (dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
  47:     let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
  48:     let packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[dest], b"adv-test", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  49:     let bytes = packet.as_bytes();
  50: 
  51:     // Header region is: 1 (version) + 32 (alpha) + 16 (mac) + HEADER_LEN.
  52:     // Skip byte 0 (version validates separately).
  53:     let header_region_end = 1 + 32 + 16 + HEADER_LEN;
  54:     for i in 1..header_region_end {
  55:         let mut tampered = *bytes;
  56:         tampered[i] ^= 0x01;
  57:         let pkt = match SphinxPacket::from_bytes(&tampered) {
  58:             Ok(p) => p,
  59:             Err(_) => continue,
  60:         };
  61:         match peel_sphinx_layer(&dest_sk, &pkt) {
  62:             Err(OnionError::AeadFail) | Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey) => {} // tamper detected
  63:             Err(other) => panic!("byte {i} flip: unexpected error {other:?}"),
  64:             Ok(out) => panic!("byte {i} flip: unexpectedly succeeded with {out:?}"),
  65:         }
  66:     }
  67: }
  68: 
  69: /// Payload-region byte flips do NOT trigger Sphinx-layer errors
  70: /// (payload is ChaCha20-stream-encrypted; no auth at Sphinx layer).
  71: /// But the decrypted user payload at those positions DOES change,
  72: /// which a caller-side AEAD would catch.
  73: #[test]
  74: fn adversarial_payload_region_flips_change_user_payload() {
  75:     use ol_onion::sphinx::primitives::HEADER_LEN;
  76:     let (dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
  77:     let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
  78:     // Use a longer payload so most flips land inside user data.
  79:     let user_payload = vec![0xCDu8; 256];
  80:     let packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[dest], &user_payload, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  81:     let bytes = packet.as_bytes();
  82:     let payload_region_start = 1 + 32 + 16 + HEADER_LEN;
  83:     // Flip a byte in the middle of the user payload area (~100 bytes
  84:     // into the user data, well clear of the length prefix).
  85:     let i = payload_region_start + 2 + 100;
  86:     let mut tampered = *bytes;
  87:     tampered[i] ^= 0x01;
  88:     let pkt = SphinxPacket::from_bytes(&tampered).unwrap();
  89:     let outcome = peel_sphinx_layer(&dest_sk, &pkt).unwrap();
  90:     match outcome {
  91:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => {
  92:             // The payload was modified by the flip — Sphinx itself
  93:             // does NOT detect this; the caller's AEAD would.
  94:             assert_ne!(payload, user_payload, "payload byte flip didn't propagate to decrypt");
  95:         }
  96:         _ => panic!(),
  97:     }
  98: }
  99:

 162: #[test]
 163: fn adversarial_cross_circuit_alpha_swap_rejected() {
 164:     // Build two packets to the SAME destination via independent
 165:     // sender ephemeral keys. Swap their alphas. Both must reject.
 166:     let (dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
 167:     let (eph_a, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 168:     let (eph_b, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);

 171:     let packet_b =
 172:         build_sphinx_onion(&eph_b, &[dest.clone()], b"b", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 173: 
 174:     let mut spliced = *packet_a.as_bytes();
 175:     spliced[1..33].copy_from_slice(&packet_b.as_bytes()[1..33]);
 176:     let pkt = SphinxPacket::from_bytes(&spliced).unwrap();
 177:     let err = peel_sphinx_layer(&dest_sk, &pkt).unwrap_err();

 181: #[test]
 182: fn adversarial_relay_attempts_inner_peel_rejected() {
 183:     // 3-hop circuit: r1, r2, dest. r1 peels its layer. r1 then tries
 184:     // to peel the FORWARDED inner packet with its own key (i.e., r1
 185:     // tries to read r2's content). Must fail AEAD/MAC.
 186:     let (r1_sk, r1) = make_relay();
 187:     let (_r2_sk, r2) = make_relay();
 188:     let (_dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
 189:     let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 190:     let packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[r1.clone(), r2, dest], b"x", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 191: 
 192:     let outcome = peel_sphinx_layer(&r1_sk, &packet).unwrap();
 193:     let inner = match outcome {
 194:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => next_packet,
 195:         _ => panic!(),
 196:     };
 197:     // r1 tries to peel inner with its own key.
 198:     let err = peel_sphinx_layer(&r1_sk, &inner).unwrap_err();
 199:     assert_eq!(err, OnionError::AeadFail);
 200: }

 219: fn make_pq_entry() -> (
 220:     curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar,
 221:     <ml_kem::MlKem768 as ml_kem::KemCore>::DecapsulationKey,
 222:     PqSphinxHop,
 223: ) {
 224:     let (x_sk, x_pk) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 225:     let (pq_dk, pq_ek) = generate_pq_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 226:     let mut id = [0u8; 32];
 227:     OsRng.fill(&mut id);
 228:     (
 229:         x_sk,
 230:         pq_dk,
 231:         PqSphinxHop {
 232:             id: HopId::from_bytes(id),
 233:             static_x_pk: x_pk,
 234:             static_pq_pk: Some(pq_ek),
 235:         },
 236:     )
 237: }

 240: fn adversarial_pq_wrong_pq_dk_at_entry_rejected() {

 250: #[test]
 251: fn adversarial_pq_intermediate_attempts_entry_peel_rejected() {
 252:     // If a downstream relay tries to peel a packet AS IF it were the
 253:     // entry hop (i.e., uses its own PQ key for decap), it must fail.
 254:     // This catches a daemon bug where intermediate hops accidentally
 255:     // use the entry-mode peel function.
 256:     let (entry_x_sk, entry_pq_dk, entry) = make_pq_entry();
 257:     let (mid_x_sk, mid_x_pk) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 258:     let (_mid_pq_dk, _) = generate_pq_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 259:     let mut mid_id = [0u8; 32];
 260:     OsRng.fill(&mut mid_id);
 261:     let mid = PqSphinxHop {
 262:         id: HopId::from_bytes(mid_id),
 263:         static_x_pk: mid_x_pk,
 264:         static_pq_pk: None, // intermediate hops don't have PQ pubkeys in this design
 265:     };
 266:     let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 267:     let packet =
 268:         build_pq_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[entry, mid], b"x", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 269: 
 270:     // Entry peels with hybrid.
 271:     let outcome = peel_pq_sphinx_entry(&entry_x_sk, &entry_pq_dk, &packet).unwrap();
 272:     let next = match outcome {
 273:         PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => next_packet,
 274:         _ => panic!(),
 275:     };
 276: 
 277:     // Now an attacker (or buggy daemon) tries to peel the forwarded
 278:     // packet at the mid hop using ENTRY-mode (with some PQ key).
 279:     let (some_pq_dk, _) = generate_pq_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 280:     let err = peel_pq_sphinx_entry(&mid_x_sk, &some_pq_dk, &next).unwrap_err();
 281:     assert_eq!(err, OnionError::AeadFail);
 282: }

 284: #[test]
 285: fn adversarial_pq_header_region_byte_flips_rejected() {
 286:     use ol_onion::sphinx::primitives::HEADER_LEN;
 287:     use ol_onion::sphinx::pq::ML_KEM_CT_LEN;
 288:     let (entry_x_sk, entry_pq_dk, entry) = make_pq_entry();
 289:     let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 290:     let packet = build_pq_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[entry], b"adv", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 291:     let bytes = packet.as_bytes().to_vec();
 292:     // Header region: 1 + 32 (alpha) + 1088 (pq_ct) + 16 (mac) + HEADER_LEN.
 293:     let header_region_end = 1 + 32 + ML_KEM_CT_LEN + 16 + HEADER_LEN;
 294:     // Step by 47 (a prime; reasonable sample density) for speed.
 295:     for byte_idx in (1..header_region_end).step_by(47) {
 296:         let mut tampered = bytes.clone();
 297:         tampered[byte_idx] ^= 0x01;
 298:         let pkt = match PqSphinxPacket::from_bytes(&tampered) {
 299:             Ok(p) => p,
 300:             Err(_) => continue,
 301:         };
 302:         let result = peel_pq_sphinx_entry(&entry_x_sk, &entry_pq_dk, &pkt);
 303:         match result {
 304:             Err(OnionError::AeadFail) | Err(OnionError::SmallOrderPubkey) => {}
 305:             Err(other) => panic!("byte {byte_idx} flip: unexpected error {other:?}"),
 306:             Ok(out) => panic!("byte {byte_idx} flip: unexpectedly succeeded with {out:?}"),
 307:         }
 308:     }
 309: }

 339: #[test]
 340: fn adversarial_max_hops_round_trip() {
 341:     use ol_onion::sphinx::primitives::MAX_HOPS;
 342:     let pairs: Vec<_> = (0..MAX_HOPS).map(|_| make_relay()).collect();
 343:     let circuit: Vec<SphinxHop> = pairs.iter().map(|(_, h)| h.clone()).collect();
 344:     let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 345:     let mut packet =
 346:         build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &circuit, b"max-hop adv", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 347:     for (i, (sk, _)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {
 348:         match peel_sphinx_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap() {
 349:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => {
 350:                 packet = next_packet;
 351:                 assert!(i + 1 < pairs.len());
 352:             }
 353:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => {
 354:                 assert_eq!(payload, b"max-hop adv");
 355:                 assert_eq!(i, pairs.len() - 1);
 356:                 return;
 357:             }
 358:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => {
 359:                 panic!("real packet mis-classified as cover (audit M4 false positive)");
 360:             }
 361:         }
 362:     }

   1: //! Constant-time gate tests for Sphinx Coherence comparison surfaces.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wall-clock variance < 5% across mismatched-byte positions. Catches
   4: //! regressions that re-introduce data-dependent branches.
   5: 
   6: use std::time::Instant;
   7: 
   8: use ol_onion::sphinx::primitives::{header_mac, verify_header_mac, HEADER_LEN};
   9: 
  10: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 50_000;
  11: 
  12: fn relative_stddev(samples: &[f64]) -> f64 {
  13:     let mean: f64 = samples.iter().sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  14:     let variance: f64 =
  15:         samples.iter().map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  16:     variance.sqrt() / mean
  17: }
  18: 
  19: fn measure<F: FnMut()>(mut work: F, iterations: usize) -> u128 {
  20:     let start = Instant::now();
  21:     for _ in 0..iterations {
  22:         work();
  23:     }
  24:     start.elapsed().as_nanos()
  25: }
  26: 
  27: #[test]
  28: fn header_mac_verify_constant_time() {
  29:     let key = [0x42u8; 32];
  30:     let data = vec![0xCDu8; HEADER_LEN];
  31:     let real_mac = header_mac(&key, &data);
  32: 
  33:     // Buckets: real_mac, byte-0 diff, byte-8 diff, byte-15 diff (last byte).
  34:     let buckets: Vec<[u8; 16]> = vec![
  35:         real_mac,
  36:         {
  37:             let mut m = real_mac;
  38:             m[0] ^= 0x01;
  39:             m
  40:         },
  41:         {
  42:             let mut m = real_mac;
  43:             m[8] ^= 0x01;
  44:             m
  45:         },
  46:         {
  47:             let mut m = real_mac;
  48:             m[15] ^= 0x01;
  49:             m
  50:         },
  51:     ];
  52: 
  53:     for b in &buckets {
  54:         let _ = measure(
  55:             || {
  56:                 let _ = verify_header_mac(&key, &data, b);
  57:             },
  58:             10_000,
  59:         );
  60:     }
  61: 
  62:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(buckets.len());
  63:     for b in &buckets {
  64:         let ns = measure(
  65:             || {
  66:                 std::hint::black_box(verify_header_mac(
  67:                     &key,
  68:                     &data,
  69:                     std::hint::black_box(b),
  70:                 ));
  71:             },
  72:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  73:         ) as f64;
  74:         totals.push(ns);
  75:     }
  76:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
  77:     eprintln!("header_mac verify totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}");
  78:     assert!(
  79:         rel < 0.05,
  80:         "header_mac verify relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 5% gate"
  81:     );
  82: }

   1: //! Empirical hop-blindness tests for Sphinx Coherence.
   2: //!
   3: //! Verifies the load-bearing property: same-circuit alpha values at
   4: //! different hops are statistically indistinguishable from independent
   5: //! random Ristretto255 group elements.
   6: 
   7: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
   8: use rand::Rng;
   9: use std::collections::HashSet;
  10: 
  11: use ol_onion::sphinx::core::{
  12:     build_sphinx_onion, generate_static_keypair, peel_sphinx_layer, SphinxHop, SphinxPeelOutcome,
  13: };
  14: use ol_onion::HopId;
  15: 
  16: fn make_relay() -> (curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar, SphinxHop) {
  17:     let (sk, pk) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
  18:     let mut id = [0u8; 32];
  19:     OsRng.fill(&mut id);
  20:     (
  21:         sk,
  22:         SphinxHop {
  23:             id: HopId::from_bytes(id),
  24:             static_pk: pk,
  25:         },
  26:     )
  27: }
  28: 
  29: /// Chi-squared statistic of byte distribution vs uniform.
  30: fn chi_squared_uniform(bytes: &[u8]) -> f64 {
  31:     let mut counts = [0u32; 256];
  32:     for &b in bytes {
  33:         counts[b as usize] += 1;
  34:     }
  35:     let n = bytes.len() as f64;
  36:     let expected = n / 256.0;
  37:     if expected < 1.0 {
  38:         return 0.0;
  39:     }
  40:     counts
  41:         .iter()
  42:         .map(|&c| {
  43:             let d = c as f64 - expected;
  44:             d * d / expected
  45:         })
  46:         .sum()
  47: }
  48: 
  49: #[test]
  50: fn alpha_bytes_at_each_hop_look_uniform() {
  51:     // Build 50 random 3-hop circuits, collect alpha at every hop,
  52:     // verify the aggregate byte distribution looks uniform via
  53:     // chi-squared.
  54:     let mut all_alpha_bytes = Vec::new();
  55:     for _ in 0..50 {
  56:         let (r1_sk, r1) = make_relay();
  57:         let (r2_sk, r2) = make_relay();
  58:         let (_dest_sk, dest) = make_relay();
  59:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
  60:         let packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[r1, r2, dest], b"x", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  61: 
  62:         // alpha at hop 0
  63:         all_alpha_bytes.extend_from_slice(&packet.as_bytes()[1..33]);
  64: 
  65:         // peel r1
  66:         let next = match peel_sphinx_layer(&r1_sk, &packet).unwrap() {
  67:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => next_packet,
  68:             _ => panic!(),
  69:         };
  70:         all_alpha_bytes.extend_from_slice(&next.as_bytes()[1..33]);
  71: 
  72:         // peel r2
  73:         let next = match peel_sphinx_layer(&r2_sk, &next).unwrap() {
  74:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => next_packet,
  75:             _ => panic!(),
  76:         };
  77:         all_alpha_bytes.extend_from_slice(&next.as_bytes()[1..33]);
  78:     }
  79:     // 50 circuits * 3 hops * 32 bytes = 4800 bytes.
  80:     let chi = chi_squared_uniform(&all_alpha_bytes);
  81:     eprintln!(
  82:         "alpha bytes: {} bytes, chi-sq vs uniform = {chi:.1}",
  83:         all_alpha_bytes.len()
  84:     );
  85:     // df=255 critical at p=0.001 is ~340. Ristretto255 compressed
  86:     // points should sit well under this.
  87:     assert!(chi < 400.0, "alpha bytes deviate from uniform: chi-sq = {chi}");
  88: }
  89: 
  90: #[test]
  91: fn alpha_at_consecutive_hops_pairwise_distinct() {
  92:     // For 100 random 3-hop circuits, alpha at every hop is unique
  93:     // (i.e., the blinding actually changes alpha).
  94:     let mut alpha_set: HashSet<[u8; 32]> = HashSet::new();
  95:     let mut total = 0;
  96:     for _ in 0..100 {
  97:         let (r1_sk, r1) = make_relay();
  98:         let (r2_sk, r2) = make_relay();
  99:         let (_, dest) = make_relay();
 100:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 101:         let p0 = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &[r1, r2, dest], b"x", &mut OsRng).unwrap();

 104:         alpha_set.insert(a0);
 105:         total += 1;
 106: 
 107:         let p1 = match peel_sphinx_layer(&r1_sk, &p0).unwrap() {
 108:             SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => next_packet,
 109:             _ => panic!(),

 111:         let mut a1 = [0u8; 32];
 112:         a1.copy_from_slice(&p1.as_bytes()[1..33]);
 113:         alpha_set.insert(a1);

 115:

 140: // ── Sphinx end-to-end correctness ────────────────────────────────
 141: 
 142: fn make_relay() -> (curve25519_dalek::scalar::Scalar, SphinxHop) {
 143:     let (sk, pk) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 144:     let mut id = [0u8; 32];
 145:     OsRng.fill(&mut id);
 146:     (
 147:         sk,
 148:         SphinxHop {
 149:             id: HopId::from_bytes(id),
 150:             static_pk: pk,
 151:         },
 152:     )
 153: }

 155: use rand::Rng;
 156: 
 157: proptest! {
 158:     #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig {
 159:         cases: light_cases() / 10,  // expensive — many curve ops per iter
 160:         max_global_rejects: light_cases(),
 161:         .. ProptestConfig::default()
 162:     })]
 163: 
 164:     /// For any 1..=MAX_HOPS circuit and any payload up to MAX_USER_PAYLOAD,
 165:     /// build + peel-through-all-hops recovers the original payload.
 166:     #[test]
 167:     fn sphinx_end_to_end_round_trip(
 168:         n_hops in 1usize..=MAX_HOPS,
 169:         payload_len in 0usize..=200,
 170:     ) {
 171:         let payload: Vec<u8> = (0..payload_len).map(|i| (i as u8).wrapping_mul(31)).collect();
 172:         let pairs: Vec<_> = (0..n_hops).map(|_| make_relay()).collect();
 173:         let circuit: Vec<SphinxHop> = pairs.iter().map(|(_, h)| h.clone()).collect();
 174:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 175:         let mut packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &circuit, &payload, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 176: 
 177:         for (i, (sk, _)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {
 178:             match peel_sphinx_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap() {
 179:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => {
 180:                     prop_assert!(i + 1 < pairs.len());
 181:                     packet = next_packet;
 182:                 }
 183:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload: out } => {
 184:                     prop_assert_eq!(i, pairs.len() - 1);
 185:                     prop_assert_eq!(out, payload);
 186:                     return Ok(());
 187:                 }
 188:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => {
 189:                     prop_assert!(false, "real payload mis-classified as cover");
 190:                 }
 191:             }
 192:         }
 193:         // Should have returned above.
 194:         prop_assert!(false, "fell through without delivery");
 195:     }
 196: 
 197:     /// Packet size is invariant at every layer.
 198:     #[test]
 199:     fn sphinx_packet_size_constant(
 200:         n_hops in 1usize..=MAX_HOPS,
 201:     ) {
 202:         let pairs: Vec<_> = (0..n_hops).map(|_| make_relay()).collect();
 203:         let circuit: Vec<SphinxHop> = pairs.iter().map(|(_, h)| h.clone()).collect();
 204:         let (eph_sk, _) = generate_static_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 205:         let mut packet = build_sphinx_onion(&eph_sk, &circuit, b"x", &mut OsRng).unwrap();
 206:         prop_assert_eq!(packet.as_bytes().len(), SPHINX_PACKET_LEN);
 207:         for (i, (sk, _)) in pairs.iter().enumerate() {
 208:             match peel_sphinx_layer(sk, &packet).unwrap() {
 209:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward { next_packet, .. } => {
 210:                     prop_assert_eq!(next_packet.as_bytes().len(), SPHINX_PACKET_LEN);
 211:                     packet = next_packet;
 212:                 }
 213:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { .. } => {
 214:                     prop_assert_eq!(i, pairs.len() - 1);
 215:                     return Ok(());
 216:                 }
 217:                 SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => {
 218:                     prop_assert!(false, "real payload mis-classified as cover");
 219:                 }
 220:             }
 221:         }
 222:     }
 223: }

 233:     /// Same witness → same keys; different witnesses → different keys.
 234:     #[test]
 235:     fn field_bound_witness_determinism(
 236:         shared in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 237:         alpha in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 238:         witness in any::<[u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN]>(),
 239:     ) {
 240:         let k1 = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &witness);
 241:         let k2 = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &witness);
 242:         prop_assert_eq!(k1.header_stream, k2.header_stream);
 243:         prop_assert_eq!(k1.mac_key, k2.mac_key);
 244:     }
 245: 
 246:     /// One-bit flip in witness causes avalanche across all sub-keys.
 247:     #[test]
 248:     fn field_bound_one_bit_avalanche(
 249:         shared in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 250:         alpha in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 251:         witness in any::<[u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN]>(),
 252:         flip_byte in 0u8..32,
 253:     ) {
 254:         let mut w2 = witness;
 255:         w2[flip_byte as usize] ^= 0x01;
 256:         let k1 = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &witness);
 257:         let k2 = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &w2);
 258:         prop_assert_ne!(k1.header_stream, k2.header_stream);
 259:         prop_assert_ne!(k1.mac_key, k2.mac_key);
 260:         prop_assert_ne!(k1.payload_stream, k2.payload_stream);
 261:         prop_assert_ne!(k1.blinding_seed, k2.blinding_seed);
 262:     }
 263: 
 264:     /// Audit I2 May 2026 — non-leakage property of the field-bound
 265:     /// witness. A passive observer of just the hop sub-keys (without
 266:     /// access to `shared`) gets NO computable information about the
 267:     /// witness beyond equality with hop-keys derived from the same
 268:     /// witness. Concretely: for two random witnesses W1, W2, the
 269:     /// hop-stream bytes from `(shared, alpha, W1)` are
 270:     /// indistinguishable (uniformly random) from those of
 271:     /// `(shared, alpha, W2)` to a party that doesn't know `shared`.
 272:     ///
 273:     /// This test pins the property in a falsifiable way: across
 274:     /// random `(shared, alpha)` and random `(W1, W2)`, neither
 275:     /// `header_stream` nor `mac_key` should expose statistical
 276:     /// regularities tied to the witness. We assert (1) the bytes
 277:     /// differ across distinct witnesses (avalanche, already pinned
 278:     /// above) AND (2) any prefix of the keystream has uniform-ish
 279:     /// byte distribution across runs — falsifies a "witness leaks
 280:     /// via byte-frequency" claim.
 281:     #[test]
 282:     fn field_bound_witness_non_leakage(
 283:         shared in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 284:         alpha in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 285:         w1 in any::<[u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN]>(),
 286:         w2 in any::<[u8; FIELD_WITNESS_LEN]>(),
 287:     ) {
 288:         prop_assume!(w1 != w2);
 289:         let k1 = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &w1);
 290:         let k2 = derive_hop_keys_with_witness(&shared, &alpha, &w2);
 291:         // Avalanche: distinct witnesses → distinct keystreams.
 292:         prop_assert_ne!(k1.header_stream, k2.header_stream);
 293:         // Non-trivial byte distribution: the first 16 bytes of
 294:         // each keystream must contain at least 8 distinct byte
 295:         // values. A leaky derivation that copied witness bytes
 296:         // verbatim would fail this with witnesses that have <8
 297:         // unique bytes (e.g. mostly-zero). Property is conservative
 298:         // (BLAKE3 XOF passes by 5+ orders of magnitude) but pins
 299:         // the "no plaintext witness in keystream" floor.
 300:         let unique_bytes_k1 = {
 301:             let mut seen = [false; 256];
 302:             for &b in &k1.header_stream[..16] {
 303:                 seen[b as usize] = true;
 304:             }
 305:             seen.iter().filter(|x| **x).count()
 306:         };
 307:         prop_assert!(
 308:             unique_bytes_k1 >= 8,
 309:             "header_stream prefix has fewer than 8 distinct bytes — possible witness leak"
 310:         );
 311:     }
 312: }
