   1: # ol_onion::transport_obfs (Row 7) microbenchmark results
   2: 
   3: Captured against `0.21.0-alpha.0` on Windows 11 Intel host, release
   4: profile (`cargo bench -p ol_onion --bench transport_obfs_bench`).
   5: 
   6: ## Final numbers
   7: 
   8: | Benchmark                              | Time      | Throughput            |
   9: |---                                     |---        |---                    |
  10: | `obfs::derive_nonce`                   | 1.3 ns    | ~770 M nonces / sec   |
  11: | `obfs::obfuscate_64`                   | 105 ns    | ~600 MB/s             |
  12: | `obfs::obfuscate_512`                  | 184 ns    | ~2.8 GB/s             |
  13: | `obfs::obfuscate_1500`                 | 635 ns    | ~2.4 GB/s             |
  14: | `obfs::obfuscate_65536`                | 19.1 µs   | ~3.4 GB/s             |
  15: | `obfs::deobfuscate_1500`               | 635 ns    | ~2.4 GB/s             |
  16: | `obfs::session_seal_outbound_1500`     | 635 ns    | ~2.4 GB/s             |
  17: | `obfs::handshake_client_start`         | 10.8 µs   | ~92 K starts / sec    |
  18: | `obfs::handshake_server_accept`        | 45.0 µs   | ~22 K accepts / sec   |
  19: | `obfs::handshake_full_round_trip`      | 92.2 µs   | ~11 K conns / sec     |
  20: 
  21: ## What this means for the daemon
  22: 
  23: - **Bulk-cipher throughput**: 2.4 GB/s on 1500-byte MTU packets, rising
  24:   to 3.4 GB/s on 64K writes. Saturates any practical network link.
  25: - **Per-packet cost is bounded**: 635 ns for a 1500-byte packet means
  26:   ~1.5M packets/sec/core before the obfs layer becomes a bottleneck.
  27: - **Handshake is the slow part** (as expected — X25519 + BLAKE3 + KDF):
  28:   ~92 µs for a full client-start → server-accept → client-finish.
  29:   ~11K connections/sec/core; a daemon doing 1 handshake/sec/peer can
  30:   support thousands of concurrent bridge peers.
  31: - **Nonce derivation is free**: 1.3 ns — fits in the L1 hot loop.
  32: 
  33: ## Why the handshake costs ~90 µs
  34: 
  35: Both `start` and `finish` do one X25519 scalarmul (~20-30 µs each).
  36: Accept does two X25519 scalarmuls (one ephemeral generation, one
  37: DH). The remainder is BLAKE3 keyed hashes for the MAC and KDF (each
  38: ~hundreds of ns).
  39: 
  40: ## Repro
  41: 
  42: ```text
  43: cargo bench -p ol_onion --bench transport_obfs_bench
  44: ```

   2: 
   3: Captured against `0.21.0-alpha.0` on Windows 11, Intel host, release
   4: profile (`cargo bench -p ol_pair_qr`). Numbers are median of 100

   7: Reproduce: `cargo bench -p ol_pair_qr`. CI gate considers a >15%

   9: automated).
  10: 
  11: | Benchmark                  | Time         | Throughput           |
  12: |---                         |---           |---                   |
  13: | `pair_full_roundtrip`      | 222.03 µs    | ~4,500 pairs / sec   |
  14: | `invite_decode_and_verify` |  25.46 µs    | ~39,000 decodes/sec  |
  15: | `sas_derive`               |  62.30 ns    | ~16,000,000 SAS/sec  |
  16: 
  17: ## Breakdown — `pair_full_roundtrip` (222 µs total)
  18: 
  19: The full roundtrip performs, per pair:
  20: 
  21: - 3 × `ed25519::Signer::sign`              (~3 × 15 µs ≈ 45 µs)
  22: - 3 × `ed25519::Verifier::verify`          (~3 × 25 µs ≈ 75 µs)
  23: - 2 × X25519 ECDH `diffie_hellman`         (~2 × 30 µs ≈ 60 µs)
  24: - 2 × `BLAKE3` hash (transcript + chain key) (~5 µs)
  25: - Canon encode / decode of 3 frames        (~1 µs)
  26: - SAS derive                                 (~0.06 µs)
  27: - Total accounted for                        ≈ 186 µs
  28: - Residual (allocator, rand, drop)           ≈ 36 µs
  29: 
  30: Ed25519 verify dominates. Acceptable for the pair-by-QR use case
  31: (cold path, called once per new contact). No batch-verification
  32: optimisation has been applied; the cold-path nature means it
  33: wouldn't help in practice.
  34: 
  35: ## Anchor budget
  36: 
  37: The pair-by-QR flow has a human-in-the-loop SAS-compare step that
  38: takes 3–5 seconds. The Rust crypto path adds ~222 µs to that — five
  39: orders of magnitude below the wall-clock budget. Optimization is
  40: NOT a priority for this layer.

   1: //! Strict length-prefixed canonical encoding for pair-by-QR frames.
   2: //!
   3: //! Why a dedicated encoder instead of [`ol_canon`]:
   4: //!
   5: //! - QR codes have a tight byte budget. A self-describing type-tag
   6: //!   per field would inflate the payload by 25-40%. Pair-QR frames
   7: //!   have a known fixed shape — we can write a strict positional
   8: //!   encoder and save every byte.
   9: //! - The transcript hash is the trust anchor. Any encoder ambiguity
  10: //!   = a downgrade attack vector. A small audit-able encoder beats
  11: //!   a feature-rich one for this surface.
  12: //!
  13: //! ## Wire shape
  14: //!
  15: //! Every top-level struct begins with:
  16: //!
  17: //! ```text
  18: //!     +-------+------+
  19: //!     | ver   | tag  |
  20: //!     | u8    | u8   |
  21: //!     +-------+------+
  22: //! ```
  23: //!
  24: //! followed by positional fields. Variable-length fields use a
  25: //! `u16` big-endian length prefix; fixed-length fields are written
  26: //! raw. Integers are big-endian, fixed-width. No varints — fixed
  27: //! width is unambiguous and trivially constant-time.
  28: //!
  29: //! The decoder refuses any field length beyond [`MAX_FIELD_BYTES`]
  30: //! before allocating, preventing memory-amplification by a hostile
  31: //! frame.
  32: 
  33: use crate::errors::{PairError, PairResult};
  34: 
  35: /// Hard cap on any single variable-length field. Generous enough
  36: /// for caps-scope payloads, small enough that a malicious 64 KiB
  37: /// length prefix is rejected immediately.
  38: pub const MAX_FIELD_BYTES: usize = 4096;
  39: 
  40: /// Reader cursor with bounds-checked primitive helpers.
  41: #[derive(Debug)]
  42: pub struct Reader<'a> {
  43:     buf: &'a [u8],
  44:     pos: usize,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl<'a> Reader<'a> {
  48:     /// Wrap a byte slice for sequential decoding.
  49:     pub fn new(buf: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
  50:         Self { buf, pos: 0 }
  51:     }
  52: 
  53:     /// Number of bytes remaining after the cursor.
  54:     pub fn remaining(&self) -> usize {
  55:         self.buf.len().saturating_sub(self.pos)
  56:     }
  57: 
  58:     /// True if the cursor is at end-of-stream.
  59:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
  60:         self.remaining() == 0
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// Total cursor position from the start of the buffer.
  64:     pub fn position(&self) -> usize {
  65:         self.pos
  66:     }
  67: 
  68:     /// Read one byte; advance cursor.
  69:     pub fn read_u8(&mut self) -> PairResult<u8> {
  70:         self.need(1)?;
  71:         let b = self.buf[self.pos];
  72:         self.pos += 1;
  73:         Ok(b)
  74:     }
  75: 
  76:     /// Read a big-endian u16; advance cursor.
  77:     pub fn read_u16(&mut self) -> PairResult<u16> {
  78:         self.need(2)?;
  79:         let v = u16::from_be_bytes([self.buf[self.pos], self.buf[self.pos + 1]]);
  80:         self.pos += 2;
  81:         Ok(v)
  82:     }
  83: 
  84:     /// Read a big-endian u32; advance cursor.
  85:     pub fn read_u32(&mut self) -> PairResult<u32> {
  86:         self.need(4)?;
  87:         let mut a = [0u8; 4];
  88:         a.copy_from_slice(&self.buf[self.pos..self.pos + 4]);
  89:         self.pos += 4;
  90:         Ok(u32::from_be_bytes(a))
  91:     }
  92: 
  93:     /// Read a big-endian u64; advance cursor.
  94:     pub fn read_u64(&mut self) -> PairResult<u64> {
  95:         self.need(8)?;
  96:         let mut a = [0u8; 8];
  97:         a.copy_from_slice(&self.buf[self.pos..self.pos + 8]);
  98:         self.pos += 8;
  99:         Ok(u64::from_be_bytes(a))
 100:     }
 101: 
 102:     /// Read `n` raw bytes; advance cursor.
 103:     pub fn read_fixed(&mut self, n: usize) -> PairResult<&'a [u8]> {
 104:         self.need(n)?;
 105:         let s = &self.buf[self.pos..self.pos + n];
 106:         self.pos += n;
 107:         Ok(s)
 108:     }
 109: 
 110:     /// Read a `u16 BE`-prefixed variable-length field. Length is
 111:     /// bounds-checked against [`MAX_FIELD_BYTES`] BEFORE the slice
 112:     /// is materialized.
 113:     pub fn read_var(&mut self) -> PairResult<&'a [u8]> {
 114:         let len = self.read_u16()? as usize;
 115:         if len > MAX_FIELD_BYTES {
 116:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 117:                 got: len,
 118:                 cap: MAX_FIELD_BYTES,
 119:             });
 120:         }
 121:         self.read_fixed(len)
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     /// Refuse if the buffer doesn't have `n` more bytes.
 125:     fn need(&self, n: usize) -> PairResult<()> {
 126:         if self.remaining() < n {
 127:             Err(PairError::Truncated {
 128:                 needed: n,
 129:                 got: self.remaining(),
 130:             })
 131:         } else {
 132:             Ok(())
 133:         }
 134:     }
 135: }
 136: 
 137: /// Write-side helper with strict length-prefixed fields. Owns its
 138: /// growable byte buffer.
 139: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
 140: pub struct Writer {
 141:     buf: Vec<u8>,
 142: }
 143: 
 144: impl Writer {
 145:     /// New empty writer.
 146:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 147:         Self::default()
 148:     }
 149: 
 150:     /// New writer pre-sized for a known target capacity (hint only).
 151:     pub fn with_capacity(cap: usize) -> Self {
 152:         Self {
 153:             buf: Vec::with_capacity(cap),
 154:         }
 155:     }
 156: 
 157:     /// Append one byte.
 158:     pub fn write_u8(&mut self, v: u8) {
 159:         self.buf.push(v);
 160:     }
 161: 
 162:     /// Append a big-endian u16.
 163:     pub fn write_u16(&mut self, v: u16) {
 164:         self.buf.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
 165:     }
 166: 
 167:     /// Append a big-endian u32.
 168:     pub fn write_u32(&mut self, v: u32) {
 169:         self.buf.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
 170:     }
 171: 
 172:     /// Append a big-endian u64.
 173:     pub fn write_u64(&mut self, v: u64) {
 174:         self.buf.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());
 175:     }
 176: 
 177:     /// Append `n` raw bytes (no length prefix).
 178:     pub fn write_fixed(&mut self, b: &[u8]) {
 179:         self.buf.extend_from_slice(b);
 180:     }
 181: 
 182:     /// Append a u16-length-prefixed variable-length field.
 183:     ///
 184:     /// Panics in debug builds if the slice exceeds [`MAX_FIELD_BYTES`]
 185:     /// (caller bug — every caller is internal, and an oversize
 186:     /// emission is always a programming error, never user-controlled).
 187:     /// Release builds clamp the slice silently. The caller-facing
 188:     /// invariant is that no producer in this crate constructs a
 189:     /// frame that needs more than ~512 bytes per field.
 190:     pub fn write_var(&mut self, b: &[u8]) {
 191:         debug_assert!(
 192:             b.len() <= MAX_FIELD_BYTES,
 193:             "ol_pair_qr: write_var slice exceeds cap"
 194:         );
 195:         let len = b.len().min(MAX_FIELD_BYTES) as u16;
 196:         self.write_u16(len);
 197:         self.buf.extend_from_slice(&b[..len as usize]);
 198:     }
 199: 
 200:     /// Consume the writer, returning the produced bytes.
 201:     pub fn into_bytes(self) -> Vec<u8> {
 202:         self.buf
 203:     }
 204: 
 205:     /// Borrow the produced bytes without consuming.
 206:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
 207:         &self.buf
 208:     }
 209: 
 210:     /// Current byte length of the produced output.
 211:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 212:         self.buf.len()
 213:     }
 214: 
 215:     /// True iff nothing has been written yet.
 216:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 217:         self.buf.is_empty()
 218:     }
 219: }

   1: //! Final shared chain-key derivation.
   2: //!
   3: //! After both sides verify the transcript hash + the SAS check
   4: //! passes, the chain key is derived deterministically from:
   5: //!
   6: //! - The transcript hash (binds the entire conversation).
   7: //! - The X25519 ECDH shared secret between the two ephemeral keys.
   8: //! - A domain-separation tag.
   9: //!
  10: //! ```text
  11: //!   chain_key = BLAKE3.derive_key("OL-pair-qr-v1-chain-key", transcript || x25519_ss)
  12: //! ```
  13: //!
  14: //! Optional Factor-2: if both sides also ran channel-reciprocity
  15: //! (see [`crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN`] + `ol_proximity_pair`), the
  16: //! privacy-amplified Factor-2 key is mixed in via
  17: //! [`mix_factor2_recip`] producing a new chain key that requires
  18: //! BOTH the in-person QR scan AND physical co-presence to derive.
  19: //! Remote-relay attackers without RF access cannot reproduce it.
  20: 
  21: use blake3::Hasher;
  22: use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop};
  23: 
  24: use crate::transcript::TranscriptHash;
  25: use crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN;
  26: 
  27: /// Length of the chain key in bytes.
  28: pub const CHAIN_KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  29: 
  30: /// Strongly-typed chain key. Zeroized on drop.
  31: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
  32: pub struct ChainKey {
  33:     inner: [u8; CHAIN_KEY_LEN],
  34: }
  35: 
  36: impl ChainKey {
  37:     /// Wrap raw bytes.
  38:     pub fn from_bytes(b: [u8; CHAIN_KEY_LEN]) -> Self {
  39:         Self { inner: b }
  40:     }
  41: 
  42:     /// View the raw 32 bytes. Callers MUST keep this short-lived;
  43:     /// the chain key is the seed material for the Double Ratchet
  44:     /// session and zeroizes itself on drop.
  45:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; CHAIN_KEY_LEN] {
  46:         &self.inner
  47:     }
  48: }
  49: 
  50: impl PartialEq for ChainKey {
  51:     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  52:         use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  53:         self.inner.ct_eq(&other.inner).into()
  54:     }
  55: }
  56: impl Eq for ChainKey {}
  57: 
  58: /// Derive the chain key from the transcript and the 32-byte X25519
  59: /// ECDH shared secret. Both sides compute the same value.
  60: pub fn derive_chain_key(
  61:     transcript: &TranscriptHash,
  62:     x25519_ss: &[u8; 32],
  63: ) -> ChainKey {
  64:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  65:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
  66:     h.update(b"-chain-key-v1");
  67:     h.update(transcript.as_bytes());
  68:     h.update(x25519_ss);
  69:     let digest = h.finalize();
  70:     let mut k = [0u8; CHAIN_KEY_LEN];
  71:     k.copy_from_slice(digest.as_bytes());
  72:     ChainKey { inner: k }
  73: }
  74: 
  75: /// Mix a Factor-2 channel-reciprocity-derived key into the chain
  76: /// key. The output requires possession of BOTH factor secrets to
  77: /// reproduce. Use this when both peers also ran
  78: /// `ol_proximity_pair`'s quantize→reconcile→amplify pipeline.
  79: ///
  80: /// `factor2_key` should be the 32-byte output of
  81: /// `ol_proximity_pair::privacy_amplify`.
  82: pub fn mix_factor2_recip(
  83:     chain_key: &ChainKey,
  84:     factor2_key: &[u8; 32],
  85: ) -> ChainKey {
  86:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  87:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
  88:     h.update(b"-chain-key-f2-mix-v1");
  89:     h.update(chain_key.as_bytes());
  90:     h.update(factor2_key);
  91:     let digest = h.finalize();
  92:     let mut k = [0u8; CHAIN_KEY_LEN];
  93:     k.copy_from_slice(digest.as_bytes());
  94:     ChainKey { inner: k }
  95: }
  96: 
  97: #[cfg(test)]
  98: mod tests {

   1: //! [`PairConfirm`] — the inviter's final commit to the transcript.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wire layout (after the 2-byte header):
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //!   u8   version    (= CONFIRM_VERSION)
   7: //!   u8   type tag   (= TAG_CONFIRM)
   8: //!   [32] id_pubkey  Ed25519 verifying key of the inviter's identity
   9: //!   [32] transcript transcript hash bytes
  10: //!   [64] signature  Ed25519(id_pubkey).sign("OL-pair-qr-v1-confirm" || transcript)
  11: //! ```
  12: //!
  13: //! Receipt of a valid `PairConfirm` is what flips the scanner from
  14: //! "pending" to "trusted." Both sides MUST also compare the
  15: //! human-readable SAS out of band — the signature alone proves the
  16: //! inviter possesses the master key, not that the user actually
  17: //! intended to pair this particular scanner.
  18: 
  19: use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey, PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH, SIGNATURE_LENGTH};
  20: 
  21: use crate::canon::{Reader, Writer};
  22: use crate::errors::{PairError, PairResult};
  23: use crate::transcript::{TranscriptHash, TRANSCRIPT_LEN};
  24: 
  25: /// Pair-by-QR confirm version on the wire.
  26: pub const CONFIRM_VERSION: u8 = 1;
  27: 
  28: /// Type-tag byte distinguishing a `PairConfirm` frame.
  29: pub const TAG_CONFIRM: u8 = 0x03;
  30: 
  31: /// Maximum encoded byte length for a `PairConfirm`.
  32: pub const CONFIRM_MAX_BYTES: usize = 200;
  33: 
  34: /// Domain-separation tag for the confirm signature.
  35: pub const CONFIRM_SIG_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-pair-qr-v1-confirm";
  36: 
  37: /// Pair-by-QR confirm frame.
  38: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  39: pub struct PairConfirm {
  40:     /// Inviter's master identity verifying key.
  41:     pub id_pubkey: [u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH],
  42:     /// Transcript hash being committed to.
  43:     pub transcript: TranscriptHash,
  44:     /// Ed25519 signature over `CONFIRM_SIG_DOMAIN || transcript`.
  45:     pub signature: [u8; SIGNATURE_LENGTH],
  46: }
  47: 
  48: impl PairConfirm {
  49:     /// Sign a confirm from the inviter side.
  50:     pub fn sign(signer: &SigningKey, transcript: TranscriptHash) -> Self {
  51:         let id_pubkey = signer.verifying_key().to_bytes();
  52:         let sig = signer.sign(&signing_payload(&transcript));
  53:         Self {
  54:             id_pubkey,
  55:             transcript,
  56:             signature: sig.to_bytes(),
  57:         }
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     /// Encode to canon bytes.
  61:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
  62:         let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(CONFIRM_MAX_BYTES);
  63:         w.write_u8(CONFIRM_VERSION);
  64:         w.write_u8(TAG_CONFIRM);
  65:         w.write_fixed(&self.id_pubkey);
  66:         w.write_fixed(self.transcript.as_bytes());
  67:         w.write_fixed(&self.signature);
  68:         w.into_bytes()
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     /// Decode and verify the confirm in one step.
  72:     ///
  73:     /// `expected_inviter_pubkey` is the inviter pubkey the scanner
  74:     /// already pinned from the QR; this method refuses any confirm
  75:     /// signed by a different key (defeats key-substitution).
  76:     /// `expected_transcript` is the transcript the scanner computed
  77:     /// locally; this method refuses any confirm committed to a
  78:     /// different transcript (defeats MITM swap).
  79:     ///
  80:     /// Both checks use `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` so a timing oracle
  81:     /// cannot leak which byte mismatched. Symmetry with the
  82:     /// transcript check + protection-in-depth (pubkey is public, but
  83:     /// keeping the verification surface uniformly constant-time is
  84:     /// the auditable property).
  85:     pub fn decode_and_verify(
  86:         bytes: &[u8],
  87:         expected_inviter_pubkey: &[u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH],
  88:         expected_transcript: &TranscriptHash,
  89:     ) -> PairResult<Self> {
  90:         use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  91:         let conf = Self::decode_raw(bytes)?;
  92:         if !bool::from(conf.id_pubkey.ct_eq(expected_inviter_pubkey)) {
  93:             return Err(PairError::BadSignature);
  94:         }
  95:         if !conf.transcript.ct_eq(expected_transcript) {
  96:             return Err(PairError::TranscriptMismatch);
  97:         }
  98:         let vk = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&conf.id_pubkey)
  99:             .map_err(|_| PairError::BadSignature)?;
 100:         let sig = Signature::from_bytes(&conf.signature);
 101:         vk.verify(&signing_payload(&conf.transcript), &sig)
 102:             .map_err(|_| PairError::BadSignature)?;
 103:         Ok(conf)
 104:     }
 105: 
 106:     /// Raw decode without verification. Fuzz harnesses only.
 107:     pub fn decode_raw(bytes: &[u8]) -> PairResult<Self> {
 108:         if bytes.len() > CONFIRM_MAX_BYTES {
 109:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 110:                 got: bytes.len(),
 111:                 cap: CONFIRM_MAX_BYTES,
 112:             });
 113:         }
 114:         let mut r = Reader::new(bytes);
 115:         let ver = r.read_u8()?;
 116:         if ver != CONFIRM_VERSION {
 117:             return Err(PairError::UnsupportedVersion {
 118:                 got: ver,
 119:                 supported: CONFIRM_VERSION,
 120:             });
 121:         }
 122:         let tag = r.read_u8()?;
 123:         if tag != TAG_CONFIRM {
 124:             return Err(PairError::BadTag {
 125:                 expected: TAG_CONFIRM,
 126:                 got: tag,
 127:             });
 128:         }
 129:         let id_slice = r.read_fixed(PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH)?;
 130:         let mut id_pubkey = [0u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH];
 131:         id_pubkey.copy_from_slice(id_slice);
 132: 
 133:         let tslice = r.read_fixed(TRANSCRIPT_LEN)?;
 134:         let mut tbytes = [0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
 135:         tbytes.copy_from_slice(tslice);
 136:         let transcript = TranscriptHash::from_bytes(tbytes);
 137: 
 138:         let sig_slice = r.read_fixed(SIGNATURE_LENGTH)?;
 139:         let mut signature = [0u8; SIGNATURE_LENGTH];
 140:         signature.copy_from_slice(sig_slice);
 141: 
 142:         if !r.is_empty() {
 143:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 144:                 got: bytes.len(),
 145:                 cap: r.position(),
 146:             });
 147:         }
 148:         Ok(Self {
 149:             id_pubkey,
 150:             transcript,
 151:             signature,
 152:         })
 153:     }
 154: }
 155: 
 156: fn signing_payload(transcript: &TranscriptHash) -> Vec<u8> {
 157:     let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(CONFIRM_SIG_DOMAIN.len() + TRANSCRIPT_LEN);
 158:     w.write_fixed(CONFIRM_SIG_DOMAIN);
 159:     w.write_fixed(transcript.as_bytes());
 160:     w.into_bytes()
 161: }

   1: //! Typed errors for the pair-by-QR protocol.
   2: 
   3: use thiserror::Error;
   4: 
   5: /// Top-level error type for every public operation in `ol_pair_qr`.
   6: ///
   7: /// Variants are deliberately granular — the daemon layer needs to
   8: /// distinguish "the QR was malformed" (user re-scans) from "signature
   9: /// mismatch" (active attacker; abort) from "invite expired" (user
  10: /// re-generates a new invite).
  11: #[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  12: pub enum PairError {
  13:     /// The encoded byte slice is too short for the expected struct.
  14:     #[error("truncated frame: needed {needed} bytes, got {got}")]
  15:     Truncated {
  16:         /// Bytes the decoder still needed.
  17:         needed: usize,
  18:         /// Bytes actually available.
  19:         got: usize,
  20:     },
  21: 
  22:     /// The wire frame exceeded the per-struct cap. Refused before
  23:     /// any allocation to avoid resource amplification.
  24:     #[error("frame oversize: {got} > cap {cap}")]
  25:     Oversize {
  26:         /// Declared length on the wire.
  27:         got: usize,
  28:         /// Per-struct cap enforced by the decoder.
  29:         cap: usize,
  30:     },
  31: 
  32:     /// The version byte didn't match what this build supports.
  33:     #[error("unsupported protocol version: got {got}, supported {supported}")]
  34:     UnsupportedVersion {
  35:         /// Version byte read off the wire.
  36:         got: u8,
  37:         /// Version this build accepts.
  38:         supported: u8,
  39:     },
  40: 
  41:     /// A required tag byte was wrong (e.g. PairResponse parsed as Invite).
  42:     #[error("type tag mismatch: expected 0x{expected:02x}, got 0x{got:02x}")]
  43:     BadTag {
  44:         /// Tag the decoder expected.
  45:         expected: u8,
  46:         /// Tag actually on the wire.
  47:         got: u8,
  48:     },
  49: 
  50:     /// An Ed25519 signature failed to verify. Treated as a hard error
  51:     /// — abort the pairing flow.
  52:     #[error("signature verification failed")]
  53:     BadSignature,
  54: 
  55:     /// The transcript hash the responder committed to does not match
  56:     /// what the inviter computed locally. Indicates active tampering.
  57:     #[error("transcript hash mismatch — possible MITM")]
  58:     TranscriptMismatch,
  59: 
  60:     /// The invite's wall-clock expiry has passed.
  61:     #[error("invite expired: now_unix={now}, expiry_unix={expiry}")]
  62:     Expired {
  63:         /// Caller-supplied current wall-clock time, unix seconds.
  64:         now: u64,
  65:         /// Expiry baked into the invite, unix seconds.
  66:         expiry: u64,
  67:     },
  68: 
  69:     /// A nonce was the wrong length on the wire.
  70:     #[error("nonce length wrong: expected {expected}, got {got}")]
  71:     BadNonceLen {
  72:         /// Required nonce length in bytes.
  73:         expected: usize,
  74:         /// Length actually decoded.
  75:         got: usize,
  76:     },
  77: 
  78:     /// The state machine was advanced from the wrong state (e.g.
  79:     /// `Inviter::receive_response` called before `Inviter::new`).
  80:     #[error("state machine called from wrong state")]
  81:     WrongState,
  82: 
  83:     /// A public-key byte slice was the wrong length.
  84:     #[error("bad pubkey length: expected {expected}, got {got}")]
  85:     BadPubkeyLen {
  86:         /// Required pubkey length in bytes.
  87:         expected: usize,
  88:         /// Length actually decoded.
  89:         got: usize,
  90:     },
  91: 
  92:     /// The ephemeral X25519 pubkey decoded to an all-zero / small-order
  93:     /// point. Rejected to prevent confined-subgroup attacks.
  94:     #[error("ephemeral X25519 public key is small-order")]
  95:     SmallOrderPubkey,
  96: 
  97:     /// Internal invariant failed. Indicates a bug, not an attack.
  98:     #[error("internal invariant violated: {0}")]
  99:     Internal(&'static str),
 100: }
 101: 
 102: /// Result alias for crate operations.
 103: pub type PairResult<T> = Result<T, PairError>;

   1: //! [`Invite`] — the QR payload + Ed25519 signature.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wire layout (after the 2-byte header):
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //!   u8   version             (= INVITE_VERSION)
   7: //!   u8   type tag            (= TAG_INVITE)
   8: //!   [32] id_pubkey           Ed25519 verifying key of the inviter's master identity
   9: //!   [32] ephemeral_x25519_pk inviter's one-time X25519 public
  10: //!   [32] nonce               INVITE_NONCE_LEN bytes of cryptographic randomness
  11: //!   u64  expiry_unix         wall-clock expiry, unix seconds
  12: //!   u16  scope.len()
  13: //!   [..] scope.bytes         caller-defined capability scope (see CapabilityScope)
  14: //!   [64] signature           Ed25519(id_pubkey).sign(body)
  15: //! ```
  16: //!
  17: //! `body` is every byte from `version` through `scope.bytes`
  18: //! inclusive — i.e. everything EXCEPT the trailing signature. The
  19: //! signature is verified before any field is trusted.
  20: 
  21: use blake3::Hasher;
  22: use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey, PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH, SIGNATURE_LENGTH};
  23: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  24: 
  25: use crate::canon::{Reader, Writer, MAX_FIELD_BYTES};
  26: use crate::errors::{PairError, PairResult};
  27: 
  28: /// Pair-by-QR protocol version on the wire. Bump in lockstep with
  29: /// any incompatible canon-encoding change.
  30: pub const INVITE_VERSION: u8 = 1;
  31: 
  32: /// Type-tag byte distinguishing an `Invite` from other frames.
  33: pub const TAG_INVITE: u8 = 0x01;
  34: 
  35: /// Length of the cryptographic nonce baked into the invite.
  36: pub const INVITE_NONCE_LEN: usize = 32;
  37: 
  38: /// Length of an X25519 raw public key.
  39: pub const X25519_PUBKEY_LEN: usize = 32;
  40: 
  41: /// Maximum encoded byte length for an `Invite` (well within QR-code
  42: /// Version-15 alphanumeric capacity even at error-correction level
  43: /// `H`, leaving generous headroom for base32 encoding overhead).
  44: pub const INVITE_MAX_BYTES: usize = 512;
  45: 
  46: /// Capability scope the inviter is granting to the scanner. The
  47: /// daemon layer encodes its own semantics here; this crate treats it
  48: /// as an opaque byte string but transcript-binds it so neither side
  49: /// can be tricked into agreeing on a different scope than the other.
  50: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  51: pub struct CapabilityScope(pub Vec<u8>);
  52: 
  53: impl CapabilityScope {
  54:     /// Construct from raw bytes. Returns [`PairError::Oversize`] if
  55:     /// the caller passes more than [`MAX_FIELD_BYTES`].
  56:     pub fn from_bytes(b: &[u8]) -> PairResult<Self> {
  57:         if b.len() > MAX_FIELD_BYTES {
  58:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
  59:                 got: b.len(),
  60:                 cap: MAX_FIELD_BYTES,
  61:             });
  62:         }
  63:         Ok(Self(b.to_vec()))
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     /// View as a byte slice.
  67:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
  68:         &self.0
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     /// Convenience: an empty scope (most narrow contact-only invite).
  72:     pub fn empty() -> Self {
  73:         Self(Vec::new())
  74:     }
  75: }
  76: 
  77: /// The pair-by-QR invite — what the inviter encodes into the QR code.
  78: ///
  79: /// Created via [`Invite::sign`]; verified + decoded via
  80: /// [`Invite::decode_and_verify`]. The raw constructor (`new_unsigned`)
  81: /// exists only to support test vectors and adversarial fuzzing.
  82: ///
  83: /// ## Example
  84: ///
  85: /// ```
  86: /// use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  87: /// use rand_core::OsRng;
  88: /// use ol_pair_qr::invite::{CapabilityScope, Invite, INVITE_NONCE_LEN};
  89: /// use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  90: ///
  91: /// let sk = SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
  92: /// let esk = StaticSecret::random_from_rng(OsRng);
  93: /// let epk = PublicKey::from(&esk).to_bytes();
  94: /// let mut nonce = [0u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN];
  95: /// rand_core::RngCore::fill_bytes(&mut OsRng, &mut nonce);
  96: ///
  97: /// let invite = Invite::sign(
  98: ///     &sk, epk, nonce, 1_900_000_000,
  99: ///     CapabilityScope::from_bytes(b"contact").unwrap(),
 100: /// );
 101: /// let encoded = invite.encode();
 102: /// let decoded = Invite::decode_and_verify(&encoded).unwrap();
 103: /// assert_eq!(decoded, invite);
 104: /// ```
 105: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 106: pub struct Invite {
 107:     /// Master identity public key of the inviter.
 108:     pub id_pubkey: [u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH],
 109:     /// Ephemeral X25519 public key bound to this single invite.
 110:     pub ephemeral_x25519_pk: [u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN],
 111:     /// Cryptographic nonce baked into the invite (never reused).
 112:     pub nonce: [u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN],
 113:     /// Wall-clock expiry, unix seconds.
 114:     pub expiry_unix: u64,
 115:     /// Capability scope (opaque to this crate).
 116:     pub scope: CapabilityScope,
 117:     /// Ed25519 signature over the canon-encoded body.
 118:     pub signature: [u8; SIGNATURE_LENGTH],
 119: }
 120: 
 121: impl Invite {
 122:     /// Sign an invite. The signing key MUST be the secret half of
 123:     /// `id_pubkey`. Returns the fully-signed [`Invite`] ready to
 124:     /// encode into a QR code.
 125:     pub fn sign(
 126:         signer: &SigningKey,
 127:         ephemeral_x25519_pk: [u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN],
 128:         nonce: [u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN],
 129:         expiry_unix: u64,
 130:         scope: CapabilityScope,
 131:     ) -> Self {
 132:         let id_pubkey = signer.verifying_key().to_bytes();
 133:         let body = encode_body(
 134:             &id_pubkey,
 135:             &ephemeral_x25519_pk,
 136:             &nonce,
 137:             expiry_unix,
 138:             &scope,
 139:         );
 140:         let sig: Signature = signer.sign(&body);
 141:         Self {
 142:             id_pubkey,
 143:             ephemeral_x25519_pk,
 144:             nonce,
 145:             expiry_unix,
 146:             scope,
 147:             signature: sig.to_bytes(),
 148:         }
 149:     }
 150: 
 151:     /// Encode the signed invite to its canon byte representation.
 152:     ///
 153:     /// Use this for QR-encoding. The returned `Vec<u8>` is the raw
 154:     /// payload; the QR layer (base32 + level-M ECC) is upstream.
 155:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
 156:         let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(INVITE_MAX_BYTES);
 157:         w.write_u8(INVITE_VERSION);
 158:         w.write_u8(TAG_INVITE);
 159:         w.write_fixed(&self.id_pubkey);
 160:         w.write_fixed(&self.ephemeral_x25519_pk);
 161:         w.write_fixed(&self.nonce);
 162:         w.write_u64(self.expiry_unix);
 163:         w.write_var(self.scope.as_bytes());
 164:         w.write_fixed(&self.signature);
 165:         w.into_bytes()
 166:     }
 167: 
 168:     /// Decode the byte representation **and** verify the Ed25519
 169:     /// signature in one step. Returns [`PairError::BadSignature`]
 170:     /// if the signature doesn't verify.
 171:     ///
 172:     /// This is the only safe decode path — `decode_raw` exists for
 173:     /// fuzz harnesses and explicitly does NOT verify.
 174:     pub fn decode_and_verify(bytes: &[u8]) -> PairResult<Self> {
 175:         let inv = Self::decode_raw(bytes)?;
 176:         let body = encode_body(
 177:             &inv.id_pubkey,
 178:             &inv.ephemeral_x25519_pk,
 179:             &inv.nonce,
 180:             inv.expiry_unix,
 181:             &inv.scope,
 182:         );
 183:         let vk = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&inv.id_pubkey)
 184:             .map_err(|_| PairError::BadSignature)?;
 185:         let sig = Signature::from_bytes(&inv.signature);
 186:         vk.verify(&body, &sig).map_err(|_| PairError::BadSignature)?;
 187:         Ok(inv)
 188:     }
 189: 
 190:     /// Raw decode WITHOUT signature verification. Fuzz harnesses use
 191:     /// this to exercise pure parsing paths. Daemon code must NEVER
 192:     /// call this — use [`Invite::decode_and_verify`] instead.
 193:     pub fn decode_raw(bytes: &[u8]) -> PairResult<Self> {
 194:         if bytes.len() > INVITE_MAX_BYTES {
 195:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 196:                 got: bytes.len(),
 197:                 cap: INVITE_MAX_BYTES,
 198:             });
 199:         }
 200:         let mut r = Reader::new(bytes);
 201:         let ver = r.read_u8()?;
 202:         if ver != INVITE_VERSION {
 203:             return Err(PairError::UnsupportedVersion {
 204:                 got: ver,
 205:                 supported: INVITE_VERSION,
 206:             });
 207:         }
 208:         let tag = r.read_u8()?;
 209:         if tag != TAG_INVITE {
 210:             return Err(PairError::BadTag {
 211:                 expected: TAG_INVITE,
 212:                 got: tag,
 213:             });
 214:         }
 215:         let id_pubkey_slice = r.read_fixed(PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH)?;
 216:         let mut id_pubkey = [0u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH];
 217:         id_pubkey.copy_from_slice(id_pubkey_slice);
 218: 
 219:         let ephemeral_slice = r.read_fixed(X25519_PUBKEY_LEN)?;
 220:         let mut ephemeral_x25519_pk = [0u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN];
 221:         ephemeral_x25519_pk.copy_from_slice(ephemeral_slice);
 222: 
 223:         let nonce_slice = r.read_fixed(INVITE_NONCE_LEN)?;
 224:         let mut nonce = [0u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN];
 225:         nonce.copy_from_slice(nonce_slice);
 226: 
 227:         let expiry_unix = r.read_u64()?;
 228:         let scope_bytes = r.read_var()?;
 229:         let scope = CapabilityScope(scope_bytes.to_vec());
 230: 
 231:         let sig_slice = r.read_fixed(SIGNATURE_LENGTH)?;
 232:         let mut signature = [0u8; SIGNATURE_LENGTH];
 233:         signature.copy_from_slice(sig_slice);
 234: 
 235:         // Refuse trailing garbage — strict frame.
 236:         if !r.is_empty() {
 237:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 238:                 got: bytes.len(),
 239:                 cap: r.position(),
 240:             });
 241:         }
 242: 
 243:         Ok(Invite {
 244:             id_pubkey,
 245:             ephemeral_x25519_pk,
 246:             nonce,
 247:             expiry_unix,
 248:             scope,
 249:             signature,
 250:         })
 251:     }
 252: 
 253:     /// Return the canon-encoded body (everything except the
 254:     /// signature) — used by the transcript hash + by tests.
 255:     pub fn body_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
 256:         encode_body(
 257:             &self.id_pubkey,
 258:             &self.ephemeral_x25519_pk,
 259:             &self.nonce,
 260:             self.expiry_unix,
 261:             &self.scope,
 262:         )
 263:     }
 264: 
 265:     /// BLAKE3 fingerprint of this invite. Used as a short identifier
 266:     /// for log records; not a transcript anchor.
 267:     pub fn fingerprint(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
 268:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
 269:         h.update(b"OL-pair-qr-v1-invite-fp");
 270:         h.update(&self.encode());
 271:         *h.finalize().as_bytes()
 272:     }
 273: 
 274:     /// Refuse if the invite's `expiry_unix` is at or before
 275:     /// `now_unix`. Returns [`PairError::Expired`] on miss.
 276:     pub fn check_not_expired(&self, now_unix: u64) -> PairResult<()> {
 277:         if now_unix >= self.expiry_unix {
 278:             return Err(PairError::Expired {
 279:                 now: now_unix,
 280:                 expiry: self.expiry_unix,
 281:             });
 282:         }
 283:         Ok(())
 284:     }
 285: }
 286: 
 287: fn encode_body(
 288:     id_pubkey: &[u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH],
 289:     ephemeral_x25519_pk: &[u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN],
 290:     nonce: &[u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN],
 291:     expiry_unix: u64,
 292:     scope: &CapabilityScope,
 293: ) -> Vec<u8> {
 294:     let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(INVITE_MAX_BYTES);
 295:     w.write_u8(INVITE_VERSION);
 296:     w.write_u8(TAG_INVITE);
 297:     w.write_fixed(id_pubkey);
 298:     w.write_fixed(ephemeral_x25519_pk);
 299:     w.write_fixed(nonce);
 300:     w.write_u64(expiry_unix);
 301:     w.write_var(scope.as_bytes());
 302:     w.into_bytes()
 303: }
 304: 
 305: impl Drop for Invite {
 306:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 307:         // Nonce isn't sensitive after the protocol completes, but
 308:         // zeroizing on drop is cheap and keeps the value out of
 309:         // freed-allocation residue.
 310:         self.nonce.zeroize();
 311:     }
 312: }

   1: //! Inviter state machine.
   2: //!
   3: //! The inviter is the device generating the QR code. Lifecycle:
   4: //!
   5: //! 1. [`Inviter::new`] — generate ephemeral X25519 keypair, build
   6: //!    + sign the [`Invite`], emit the bytes that go into the QR.
   7: //! 2. [`Inviter::receive_response`] — accept the scanner's
   8: //!    [`PairResponse`], verify the signature, compute the
   9: //!    transcript hash + SAS for the user to compare.
  10: //! 3. [`Inviter::confirm`] — after the user confirms the SAS
  11: //!    matches, sign the [`PairConfirm`] and derive the final
  12: //!    [`ChainKey`].
  13: 
  14: use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  15: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  16: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  17: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  18: 
  19: use crate::chain_key::{derive_chain_key, ChainKey};
  20: use crate::confirm::PairConfirm;
  21: use crate::errors::{PairError, PairResult};
  22: use crate::invite::{CapabilityScope, Invite, INVITE_NONCE_LEN};
  23: use crate::response::PairResponse;
  24: use crate::sas::Sas;
  25: use crate::transcript::{transcript_hash, TranscriptHash};
  26: 
  27: /// State enum for the inviter machine.
  28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  29: pub enum InviterState {
  30:     /// Invite generated; waiting for scanner's response.
  31:     AwaitingResponse,
  32:     /// Response received + verified; waiting for user to confirm SAS.
  33:     AwaitingUserConfirm,
  34:     /// User confirmed; chain key derived; pairing complete.
  35:     Done,
  36:     /// Pairing was aborted (e.g. user said SAS mismatch).
  37:     Aborted,
  38: }
  39: 
  40: /// Inviter side of the pair-by-QR protocol.
  41: ///
  42: /// The state machine refuses out-of-order transitions and returns
  43: /// [`PairError::WrongState`] when a call doesn't match the current
  44: /// stage.
  45: pub struct Inviter {
  46:     id_signing: SigningKey,
  47:     ephemeral_secret: Option<StaticSecret>,
  48:     invite: Invite,
  49:     state: InviterState,
  50: 
  51:     // Populated after receive_response:
  52:     response: Option<PairResponse>,
  53:     transcript: Option<TranscriptHash>,
  54:     sas: Option<Sas>,
  55:     pending_chain_key: Option<ChainKey>,
  56: }
  57: 
  58: impl Inviter {
  59:     /// Construct a new inviter and produce the QR-encodable invite
  60:     /// bytes. The caller passes their identity signing key + an RNG
  61:     /// for the ephemeral material.
  62:     pub fn new<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
  63:         id_signing: SigningKey,
  64:         rng: &mut R,
  65:         expiry_unix: u64,
  66:         scope: CapabilityScope,
  67:     ) -> Self {
  68:         let ephemeral_secret = StaticSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
  69:         let ephemeral_pk = PublicKey::from(&ephemeral_secret).to_bytes();
  70:         let mut nonce = [0u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN];
  71:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut nonce);
  72:         let invite = Invite::sign(&id_signing, ephemeral_pk, nonce, expiry_unix, scope);
  73:         Self {
  74:             id_signing,
  75:             ephemeral_secret: Some(ephemeral_secret),
  76:             invite,
  77:             state: InviterState::AwaitingResponse,
  78:             response: None,
  79:             transcript: None,
  80:             sas: None,
  81:             pending_chain_key: None,
  82:         }
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     /// Read-only view of the invite the QR layer should encode.
  86:     pub fn invite(&self) -> &Invite {
  87:         &self.invite
  88:     }
  89: 
  90:     /// Encoded invite bytes ready for QR encoding.
  91:     pub fn invite_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
  92:         self.invite.encode()
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     /// Current state.
  96:     pub fn state(&self) -> InviterState {
  97:         self.state
  98:     }
  99: 
 100:     /// Accept the scanner's response. Verifies the signature,
 101:     /// computes the transcript hash + SAS, and advances state.
 102:     pub fn receive_response(&mut self, response_bytes: &[u8]) -> PairResult<&Sas> {
 103:         if self.state != InviterState::AwaitingResponse {
 104:             return Err(PairError::WrongState);
 105:         }
 106:         let bind = self.invite.body_bytes();
 107:         let response = PairResponse::decode_and_verify(response_bytes, &bind)?;
 108: 
 109:         let esk = self
 110:             .ephemeral_secret
 111:             .as_ref()
 112:             .ok_or(PairError::Internal("ephemeral_secret missing"))?;
 113:         let peer_pk = PublicKey::from(response.ephemeral_x25519_pk);
 114:         let ss = esk.diffie_hellman(&peer_pk);
 115:         let ss_bytes: [u8; 32] = ss.to_bytes();
 116: 
 117:         // Reject all-zero / small-order shared secret. x25519-dalek
 118:         // already returns an all-zero SS for small-order pubkeys.
 119:         if ss_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
 120:             return Err(PairError::SmallOrderPubkey);
 121:         }
 122: 
 123:         let t = transcript_hash(&self.invite, &response);
 124:         let sas = Sas::derive(&t);
 125:         let chain_key = derive_chain_key(&t, &ss_bytes);
 126: 
 127:         self.response = Some(response);
 128:         self.transcript = Some(t);
 129:         self.sas = Some(sas);
 130:         self.pending_chain_key = Some(chain_key);
 131:         self.state = InviterState::AwaitingUserConfirm;
 132:         Ok(self.sas.as_ref().expect("just set"))
 133:     }
 134: 
 135:     /// View the SAS without advancing state (e.g. for re-displaying
 136:     /// in the UI). Returns `None` until [`Inviter::receive_response`]
 137:     /// has been called.
 138:     pub fn sas(&self) -> Option<&Sas> {
 139:         self.sas.as_ref()
 140:     }
 141: 
 142:     /// User confirmed the SAS matches. Sign the [`PairConfirm`] and
 143:     /// finalize the chain key. Returns `(confirm_bytes, chain_key)`.
 144:     pub fn confirm(&mut self) -> PairResult<(Vec<u8>, ChainKey)> {
 145:         self.confirm_inner(None)
 146:     }
 147: 
 148:     /// Like [`Inviter::confirm`] but mixes in a Factor-2
 149:     /// channel-reciprocity key (output of `ol_proximity_pair::privacy_amplify`).
 150:     /// Both peers MUST supply the same factor-2 key; otherwise the
 151:     /// chain keys diverge and the first ciphertext fails to decrypt.
 152:     pub fn confirm_with_factor2(
 153:         &mut self,
 154:         factor2_key: &[u8; 32],
 155:     ) -> PairResult<(Vec<u8>, ChainKey)> {
 156:         self.confirm_inner(Some(factor2_key))
 157:     }
 158: 
 159:     fn confirm_inner(
 160:         &mut self,
 161:         factor2_key: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 162:     ) -> PairResult<(Vec<u8>, ChainKey)> {
 163:         if self.state != InviterState::AwaitingUserConfirm {
 164:             return Err(PairError::WrongState);
 165:         }
 166:         let t = self
 167:             .transcript
 168:             .ok_or(PairError::Internal("transcript missing"))?;
 169:         let chain_key = self
 170:             .pending_chain_key
 171:             .take()
 172:             .ok_or(PairError::Internal("chain_key missing"))?;
 173:         let final_chain_key = match factor2_key {
 174:             Some(f2) => crate::chain_key::mix_factor2_recip(&chain_key, f2),
 175:             None => chain_key,
 176:         };
 177:         let confirm = PairConfirm::sign(&self.id_signing, t);
 178:         let bytes = confirm.encode();
 179:         self.state = InviterState::Done;
 180:         // Zeroize ephemeral material now that pairing is done.
 181:         if let Some(esk) = self.ephemeral_secret.take() {
 182:             drop(esk);
 183:         }
 184:         Ok((bytes, final_chain_key))
 185:     }
 186: 
 187:     /// User rejected the SAS comparison. Mark the machine aborted
 188:     /// and zeroize secret material.
 189:     pub fn abort(&mut self) {
 190:         self.state = InviterState::Aborted;
 191:         self.ephemeral_secret = None;
 192:         self.pending_chain_key = None;
 193:     }
 194: }
 195: 
 196: impl Drop for Inviter {
 197:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 198:         if let Some(esk) = self.ephemeral_secret.take() {
 199:             drop(esk);
 200:         }
 201:         let mut sig_bytes = self.invite.signature;
 202:         sig_bytes.zeroize();
 203:     }
 204: }
 205: 
 206: impl std::fmt::Debug for Inviter {
 207:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 208:         f.debug_struct("Inviter")
 209:             .field("state", &self.state)
 210:             .field("invite_id_pubkey_prefix", &&self.invite.id_pubkey[..4])
 211:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 212:     }
 213: }

   1: //! `ol_pair_qr` — pair-by-QR Factor-1 trust establishment.
   2: //!
   3: //! Phase F2 of the Coherence Mesh plan. Two devices that have never
   4: //! met derive a shared chain-key in person, with no third-party
   5: //! infrastructure trusted at any point in the protocol.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Threat model
   8: //!
   9: //! - **Network attacker (active MITM)**: can drop, modify, inject,
  10: //!   replay anything on the wire. Cannot break Ed25519 or X25519.
  11: //! - **Optical attacker (telephoto / digital relay of the QR)**:
  12: //!   can photograph or live-stream the QR code from a distance, or
  13: //!   relay it to a remote confederate.
  14: //! - **Hardware attacker**: out of scope (covered by hwkey + duress
  15: //!   layers).
  16: //!
  17: //! Defenses provided **without** relying on the network:
  18: //!
  19: //! 1. The QR carries an Ed25519-signed `Invite` whose body binds:
  20: //!    the inviter's identity pubkey, an ephemeral X25519 pubkey, a
  21: //!    one-time nonce, an expiry, and the capability scope being
  22: //!    granted. A network attacker cannot tamper with the bytes the
  23: //!    scanner sees.
  24: //! 2. The scanner replies with its own signed
  25: //!    [`PairResponse`](response::PairResponse) committed to the full
  26: //!    transcript hash; the inviter verifies the transcript before
  27: //!    completing.
  28: //! 3. Both sides derive a [`Sas`](sas::Sas) — a short authentication
  29: //!    string — from the transcript. Users compare the SAS out-of-band
  30: //!    (verbally / visually) to detect any MITM, telephoto, or relay
  31: //!    attack on the network channel.
  32: //! 4. Optional **Factor-2 channel reciprocity** via
  33: //!    [`ol_proximity_pair`] mixes a quantized-channel-bits secret
  34: //!    into the final chain key, defeating remote-relay attacks even
  35: //!    if the SAS check were skipped.
  36: //!
  37: //! ## Determinism
  38: //!
  39: //! Every wire frame is encoded via the strict length-prefixed
  40: //! [`canon`] module. Same struct → same bytes, every platform,
  41: //! every build. Required because the transcript hash is the trust
  42: //! anchor and any encoder ambiguity = security hole.
  43: //!
  44: //! ## End-to-end example
  45: //!
  46: //! ```
  47: //! use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  48: //! use rand_core::OsRng;
  49: //!
  50: //! use ol_pair_qr::invite::CapabilityScope;
  51: //! use ol_pair_qr::{Inviter, Scanner};
  52: //!
  53: //! // Inviter generates a QR-encodable invite.
  54: //! let mut inviter = Inviter::new(
  55: //!     SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng),
  56: //!     &mut OsRng,
  57: //!     1_900_000_000, // expiry_unix (year 2030+)
  58: //!     CapabilityScope::from_bytes(b"contact:alice").unwrap(),
  59: //! );
  60: //! let qr_bytes = inviter.invite_bytes();
  61: //!
  62: //! // Scanner reads the QR, verifies, builds a response.
  63: //! let scanner_sk = SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
  64: //! let now_unix = 100; // current wall clock
  65: //! let (mut scanner, response_bytes) =
  66: //!     Scanner::scan(scanner_sk, &qr_bytes, now_unix, &mut OsRng).unwrap();
  67: //!
  68: //! // Inviter receives the response, computes SAS for user comparison.
  69: //! let sas_inviter = inviter.receive_response(&response_bytes).unwrap();
  70: //! let sas_scanner = scanner.sas();
  71: //! assert_eq!(sas_inviter, sas_scanner); // identical 5-word string
  72: //!
  73: //! // Users compare SAS verbally. On match, inviter confirms.
  74: //! let (confirm_bytes, chain_key_inviter) = inviter.confirm().unwrap();
  75: //! let chain_key_scanner = scanner.receive_confirm(&confirm_bytes).unwrap();
  76: //!
  77: //! // Both sides derive byte-identical 32-byte chain keys.
  78: //! assert_eq!(chain_key_inviter, chain_key_scanner);
  79: //! ```
  80:

   1: //! [`PairResponse`] — the scanner's reply to the inviter.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wire layout (after the 2-byte header):
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //!   u8   version         (= RESPONSE_VERSION)
   7: //!   u8   type tag        (= TAG_RESPONSE)
   8: //!   [32] id_pubkey       Ed25519 verifying key of the scanner's identity
   9: //!   [32] ephem_x25519_pk scanner's one-time X25519 public
  10: //!   [32] nonce           RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN bytes of cryptographic randomness
  11: //!   [64] signature       Ed25519(id_pubkey).sign("OL-pair-qr-v1-response" || transcript_bind)
  12: //! ```
  13: //!
  14: //! `transcript_bind` is the scanner's local view of the invite's
  15: //! body bytes — see [`PairResponse::sign_for_transcript`]. The
  16: //! signature binds the scanner's reply to the exact invite they
  17: //! scanned, so a network attacker cannot pair the scanner's reply
  18: //! with a different invite (cross-protocol replay).
  19: 
  20: use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey, PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH, SIGNATURE_LENGTH};
  21: use zeroize::Zeroize;
  22: 
  23: use crate::canon::{Reader, Writer};
  24: use crate::errors::{PairError, PairResult};
  25: use crate::invite::{X25519_PUBKEY_LEN, INVITE_MAX_BYTES};
  26: 
  27: /// Pair-by-QR response version on the wire.
  28: pub const RESPONSE_VERSION: u8 = 1;
  29: 
  30: /// Type-tag byte distinguishing a `PairResponse` frame.
  31: pub const TAG_RESPONSE: u8 = 0x02;
  32: 
  33: /// Length of the cryptographic nonce baked into the response.
  34: pub const RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN: usize = 32;
  35: 
  36: /// Maximum encoded byte length for a `PairResponse`.
  37: pub const RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES: usize = 256;
  38: 
  39: /// Domain-separation tag for the response signature. Prepended to
  40: /// `transcript_bind` so a response signature can never be replayed
  41: /// as some other Ed25519-signed message.
  42: pub const RESPONSE_SIG_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-pair-qr-v1-response";
  43: 
  44: /// The pair-by-QR response — what the scanner sends back to the
  45: /// inviter over the freshly-discovered network channel.
  46: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  47: pub struct PairResponse {
  48:     /// Master identity public key of the scanner.
  49:     pub id_pubkey: [u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH],
  50:     /// Ephemeral X25519 public key bound to this single response.
  51:     pub ephemeral_x25519_pk: [u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN],
  52:     /// Cryptographic nonce baked into the response.
  53:     pub nonce: [u8; RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN],
  54:     /// Ed25519 signature over `RESPONSE_SIG_DOMAIN || transcript_bind`.
  55:     pub signature: [u8; SIGNATURE_LENGTH],
  56: }
  57: 
  58: impl PairResponse {
  59:     /// Sign a response. `transcript_bind` MUST be the body bytes of
  60:     /// the invite the scanner just scanned (i.e. `invite.body_bytes()`).
  61:     /// This binding is what defeats invite-substitution attacks.
  62:     pub fn sign_for_transcript(
  63:         signer: &SigningKey,
  64:         ephemeral_x25519_pk: [u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN],
  65:         nonce: [u8; RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN],
  66:         transcript_bind: &[u8],
  67:     ) -> Self {
  68:         let id_pubkey = signer.verifying_key().to_bytes();
  69:         let sig = signer.sign(&signing_payload(transcript_bind, &nonce, &ephemeral_x25519_pk));
  70:         Self {
  71:             id_pubkey,
  72:             ephemeral_x25519_pk,
  73:             nonce,
  74:             signature: sig.to_bytes(),
  75:         }
  76:     }
  77: 
  78:     /// Encode the signed response to its canon byte representation.
  79:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Vec<u8> {
  80:         let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES);
  81:         w.write_u8(RESPONSE_VERSION);
  82:         w.write_u8(TAG_RESPONSE);
  83:         w.write_fixed(&self.id_pubkey);
  84:         w.write_fixed(&self.ephemeral_x25519_pk);
  85:         w.write_fixed(&self.nonce);
  86:         w.write_fixed(&self.signature);
  87:         w.into_bytes()
  88:     }
  89: 
  90:     /// Decode the byte representation AND verify the Ed25519
  91:     /// signature against the locally-computed `transcript_bind`.
  92:     /// This is the only safe decode path for production code.
  93:     pub fn decode_and_verify(bytes: &[u8], transcript_bind: &[u8]) -> PairResult<Self> {
  94:         if transcript_bind.len() > INVITE_MAX_BYTES {
  95:             // Defensive: a hostile inviter-side bug could pass an
  96:             // unreasonable bind. Refuse before signature work.
  97:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
  98:                 got: transcript_bind.len(),
  99:                 cap: INVITE_MAX_BYTES,
 100:             });
 101:         }
 102:         let resp = Self::decode_raw(bytes)?;
 103:         let vk = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&resp.id_pubkey)
 104:             .map_err(|_| PairError::BadSignature)?;
 105:         let sig = Signature::from_bytes(&resp.signature);
 106:         vk.verify(
 107:             &signing_payload(transcript_bind, &resp.nonce, &resp.ephemeral_x25519_pk),
 108:             &sig,
 109:         )
 110:         .map_err(|_| PairError::BadSignature)?;
 111:         Ok(resp)
 112:     }
 113: 
 114:     /// Raw decode WITHOUT signature verification. Fuzz harnesses
 115:     /// only.
 116:     pub fn decode_raw(bytes: &[u8]) -> PairResult<Self> {
 117:         if bytes.len() > RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES {
 118:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 119:                 got: bytes.len(),
 120:                 cap: RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES,
 121:             });
 122:         }
 123:         let mut r = Reader::new(bytes);
 124:         let ver = r.read_u8()?;
 125:         if ver != RESPONSE_VERSION {
 126:             return Err(PairError::UnsupportedVersion {
 127:                 got: ver,
 128:                 supported: RESPONSE_VERSION,
 129:             });
 130:         }
 131:         let tag = r.read_u8()?;
 132:         if tag != TAG_RESPONSE {
 133:             return Err(PairError::BadTag {
 134:                 expected: TAG_RESPONSE,
 135:                 got: tag,
 136:             });
 137:         }
 138:         let id_slice = r.read_fixed(PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH)?;
 139:         let mut id_pubkey = [0u8; PUBLIC_KEY_LENGTH];
 140:         id_pubkey.copy_from_slice(id_slice);
 141: 
 142:         let ephem_slice = r.read_fixed(X25519_PUBKEY_LEN)?;
 143:         let mut ephemeral_x25519_pk = [0u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN];
 144:         ephemeral_x25519_pk.copy_from_slice(ephem_slice);
 145: 
 146:         let nonce_slice = r.read_fixed(RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN)?;
 147:         let mut nonce = [0u8; RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN];
 148:         nonce.copy_from_slice(nonce_slice);
 149: 
 150:         let sig_slice = r.read_fixed(SIGNATURE_LENGTH)?;
 151:         let mut signature = [0u8; SIGNATURE_LENGTH];
 152:         signature.copy_from_slice(sig_slice);
 153: 
 154:         if !r.is_empty() {
 155:             return Err(PairError::Oversize {
 156:                 got: bytes.len(),
 157:                 cap: r.position(),
 158:             });
 159:         }
 160:         Ok(PairResponse {
 161:             id_pubkey,
 162:             ephemeral_x25519_pk,
 163:             nonce,
 164:             signature,
 165:         })
 166:     }
 167: }
 168: 
 169: fn signing_payload(
 170:     transcript_bind: &[u8],
 171:     nonce: &[u8; RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN],
 172:     ephem_pk: &[u8; X25519_PUBKEY_LEN],
 173: ) -> Vec<u8> {
 174:     // Domain-tag || u32 len-prefix(transcript_bind) || transcript_bind
 175:     //            || nonce || ephem_pk
 176:     let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(RESPONSE_SIG_DOMAIN.len() + transcript_bind.len() + 96);
 177:     w.write_fixed(RESPONSE_SIG_DOMAIN);
 178:     w.write_u32(transcript_bind.len() as u32);
 179:     w.write_fixed(transcript_bind);
 180:     w.write_fixed(nonce);
 181:     w.write_fixed(ephem_pk);
 182:     w.into_bytes()
 183: }
 184: 
 185: impl Drop for PairResponse {
 186:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 187:         self.nonce.zeroize();
 188:     }
 189: }

   1: //! SAS — short authentication string derivation.
   2: //!
   3: //! 30 bits of entropy encoded as 5 words from a 64-word dictionary.
   4: //! Each word represents 6 bits; we use 5 words = 30 bits ≈ 10⁹
   5: //! distinct SAS values.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Why 30 bits?
   8: //!
   9: //! The user compares the SAS once, out-of-band. An active MITM
  10: //! attacker has to guess the user's SAS value BEFORE the user
  11: //! reads it. With 30 bits, the attack success probability is
  12: //! 2⁻³⁰ ≈ 1 in 10⁹ per pairing attempt — solid for a one-shot
  13: //! in-person comparison.
  14: //!
  15: //! ## Why words (not numbers or emoji)?
  16: //!
  17: //! Words are easier to read aloud, easier to confirm at a glance,
  18: //! and survive screen-reader / accessibility paths. Numbers are
  19: //! more error-prone for the user; emoji rendering varies across
  20: //! devices and can collide ambiguously.
  21: //!
  22: //! ## Example
  23: //!
  24: //! ```
  25: //! use ol_pair_qr::sas::Sas;
  26: //! use ol_pair_qr::transcript::TranscriptHash;
  27: //!
  28: //! let t = TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0x42u8; 32]);
  29: //! let sas = Sas::derive(&t);
  30: //! // Five words, space-joined, all from the 64-word dictionary.
  31: //! assert_eq!(sas.display().split(' ').count(), 5);
  32: //! // Determinism: same transcript → same SAS.
  33: //! assert_eq!(sas, Sas::derive(&t));
  34: //! ```
  35: 
  36: use blake3::Hasher;
  37: 
  38: use crate::sas_words::SAS_WORDS;
  39: use crate::transcript::TranscriptHash;
  40: use crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN;
  41: 
  42: /// Number of bits represented by the SAS (5 words × 6 bits).
  43: pub const SAS_BITS: usize = 30;
  44: 
  45: /// Number of words displayed in the SAS.
  46: pub const SAS_WORD_COUNT: usize = 5;
  47: 
  48: /// Strongly-typed SAS value. Display this to the user; both sides
  49: /// compare verbally and confirm a match before completing the pair.
  50: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  51: pub struct Sas {
  52:     /// 5-tuple of word slices (each word from [`SAS_WORDS`]).
  53:     pub words: [&'static str; SAS_WORD_COUNT],
  54:     /// Raw 30 bits packed into the low bits of this u32.
  55:     pub raw_bits: u32,
  56: }
  57: 
  58: impl Sas {
  59:     /// Derive the SAS from the transcript hash deterministically.
  60:     /// Both sides compute the same SAS from the same transcript.
  61:     pub fn derive(transcript: &TranscriptHash) -> Self {
  62:         let mut h = Hasher::new();
  63:         h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
  64:         h.update(b"-sas-v1");
  65:         h.update(transcript.as_bytes());
  66:         let digest = h.finalize();
  67:         let bytes = digest.as_bytes();
  68:         // Take 30 bits from the first 4 bytes; mask to 30 bits.
  69:         let raw_bits = u32::from_be_bytes([bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])
  70:             & ((1u32 << SAS_BITS) - 1);
  71:         let mut words = [""; SAS_WORD_COUNT];
  72:         for i in 0..SAS_WORD_COUNT {
  73:             // Most significant 6 bits first → reads naturally
  74:             // left-to-right.
  75:             let shift = SAS_BITS - 6 * (i + 1);
  76:             let idx = ((raw_bits >> shift) & 0x3F) as usize;
  77:             words[i] = SAS_WORDS[idx];
  78:         }
  79:         Self { words, raw_bits }
  80:     }
  81: 
  82:     /// Human-readable space-joined rendering.
  83:     pub fn display(&self) -> String {
  84:         self.words.join(" ")
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     /// Constant-time word-by-word comparison. Use this when the
  88:     /// daemon receives the peer's SAS over the wire (which is NOT
  89:     /// the standard flow — usually users compare verbally — but
  90:     /// the option exists for accessibility tooling).
  91:     pub fn ct_eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  92:         use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  93:         let a = self.raw_bits.to_be_bytes();
  94:         let b = other.raw_bits.to_be_bytes();
  95:         a.ct_eq(&b).into()
  96:     }
  97: }
  98:

   2: //!
   3: //! Properties of this list:
   4: //!
   5: //! - Exactly 64 words (one per 6-bit nibble).
   6: //! - All distinct first letter+second letter prefix (anti-homophone).
   7: //! - All 4–7 ASCII letters (fast to read aloud, easy to type if needed).
   8: //! - Common-vocabulary English so users without specialized training
   9: //!   can repeat them on the first try.

  11: //! Bumping this list constitutes a wire-format change — bump

  14: /// 64 distinct English words for short-authentication-string display.
  15: ///
  16: /// Properties enforced by tests in this module:
  17: /// - All distinct (no duplicates).
  18: /// - Each is 4-7 lowercase ASCII letters.
  19: /// - All 2-letter prefixes distinct (anti-homophone read-aloud).
  20: /// - All pairs have Levenshtein distance ≥ 2 (anti-typo / anti-mishearing).
  21: /// - None on the minimal English-language deny list.
  22: /// - No triple-letter runs (easy to pronounce).
  23: pub const SAS_WORDS: [&str; 64] = [
  24:     "agile", "amuse", "apple", "basil", "blaze", "brick", "cargo", "cedar",
  25:     "chess", "climb", "copper", "crane", "daisy", "decoy", "drift", "eagle",

  67:         let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
  68:         for w in &SAS_WORDS {
  69:             let prefix: String = w.chars().take(2).collect();
  70:             assert!(seen.insert(prefix.clone()), "duplicate prefix: {prefix}");
  71:         }
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     /// Compute the Levenshtein edit distance between two ASCII
  75:     /// lowercase strings. Returns the minimum number of single-char
  76:     /// insertions, deletions, or substitutions needed to transform
  77:     /// `a` into `b`.
  78:     fn levenshtein(a: &str, b: &str) -> usize {
  79:         let a = a.as_bytes();
  80:         let b = b.as_bytes();
  81:         let (la, lb) = (a.len(), b.len());
  82:         if la == 0 {
  83:             return lb;
  84:         }
  85:         if lb == 0 {
  86:             return la;
  87:         }
  88:         let mut prev: Vec<usize> = (0..=lb).collect();
  89:         let mut curr: Vec<usize> = vec![0; lb + 1];
  90:         for i in 1..=la {
  91:             curr[0] = i;
  92:             for j in 1..=lb {
  93:                 let cost = if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] { 0 } else { 1 };
  94:                 curr[j] = (curr[j - 1] + 1)
  95:                     .min(prev[j] + 1)
  96:                     .min(prev[j - 1] + cost);
  97:             }
  98:             std::mem::swap(&mut prev, &mut curr);
  99:         }
 100:         prev[lb]
 101:     }
 102: 
 103:     /// Pair-trust-grade requirement: no two dictionary words may
 104:     /// differ by a single keystroke. A 1-character typo of "tiger"
 105:     /// must NOT collide with another dictionary word, otherwise a
 106:     /// user who slightly mishears the SAS could silently confirm
 107:     /// a different value.
 108:     #[test]
 109:     fn dictionary_levenshtein_distance_at_least_2() {
 110:         for (i, a) in SAS_WORDS.iter().enumerate() {
 111:             for b in SAS_WORDS.iter().skip(i + 1) {
 112:                 let d = levenshtein(a, b);
 113:                 assert!(
 114:                     d >= 2,
 115:                     "SAS dictionary has Levenshtein-1 collision: {a:?} ↔ {b:?}"
 116:                 );
 117:             }
 118:         }
 119:     }

   1: //! Scanner state machine.
   2: //!
   3: //! The scanner is the device reading the QR code. Lifecycle:
   4: //!
   5: //! 1. [`Scanner::scan`] — decode + verify the [`Invite`], check
   6: //!    expiry, generate the [`PairResponse`].
   7: //! 2. The scanner displays the SAS derived from the transcript
   8: //!    (built from the verified Invite + the scanner's own
   9: //!    response).
  10: //! 3. [`Scanner::receive_confirm`] — accept the inviter's
  11: //!    [`PairConfirm`], verify it commits to the same transcript
  12: //!    the scanner saw, and emit the final [`ChainKey`].
  13: 
  14: use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  15: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  16: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  17: 
  18: use crate::chain_key::{derive_chain_key, ChainKey};
  19: use crate::confirm::PairConfirm;
  20: use crate::errors::{PairError, PairResult};
  21: use crate::invite::Invite;
  22: use crate::response::{PairResponse, RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN};
  23: use crate::sas::Sas;
  24: use crate::transcript::{transcript_hash, TranscriptHash};
  25: 
  26: /// State enum for the scanner machine.
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  28: pub enum ScannerState {
  29:     /// Invite scanned + verified; response generated; waiting for
  30:     /// inviter's confirm.
  31:     AwaitingConfirm,
  32:     /// User confirmed SAS + inviter's confirm verified; chain key
  33:     /// derived; pairing complete.
  34:     Done,
  35:     /// Pairing was aborted (user said SAS mismatch, or confirm
  36:     /// signature invalid).
  37:     Aborted,
  38: }
  39: 
  40: /// Scanner side of the pair-by-QR protocol.
  41: pub struct Scanner {
  42:     #[allow(dead_code)] // retained so future revisions can re-sign confirm-acks
  43:     id_signing: SigningKey,
  44:     ephemeral_secret: Option<StaticSecret>,
  45:     invite: Invite,
  46:     response: PairResponse,
  47:     transcript: TranscriptHash,
  48:     sas: Sas,
  49:     pending_chain_key: Option<ChainKey>,
  50:     state: ScannerState,
  51: }
  52: 
  53: impl Scanner {
  54:     /// Scan + verify an invite, generate the response, and compute
  55:     /// the transcript + SAS for the user to compare.
  56:     ///
  57:     /// Returns the constructed scanner and the wire bytes of the
  58:     /// response that should be sent back to the inviter.
  59:     pub fn scan<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
  60:         id_signing: SigningKey,
  61:         invite_bytes: &[u8],
  62:         now_unix: u64,
  63:         rng: &mut R,
  64:     ) -> PairResult<(Self, Vec<u8>)> {
  65:         let invite = Invite::decode_and_verify(invite_bytes)?;
  66:         invite.check_not_expired(now_unix)?;
  67: 
  68:         let ephemeral_secret = StaticSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
  69:         let ephemeral_pk = PublicKey::from(&ephemeral_secret).to_bytes();
  70:         let mut nonce = [0u8; RESPONSE_NONCE_LEN];
  71:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut nonce);
  72: 
  73:         let response = PairResponse::sign_for_transcript(
  74:             &id_signing,
  75:             ephemeral_pk,
  76:             nonce,
  77:             &invite.body_bytes(),
  78:         );
  79:         let response_bytes = response.encode();
  80: 
  81:         // Compute transcript + SAS + ECDH for the chain key.
  82:         let t = transcript_hash(&invite, &response);
  83:         let sas = Sas::derive(&t);
  84: 
  85:         let inviter_pk = PublicKey::from(invite.ephemeral_x25519_pk);
  86:         let ss = ephemeral_secret.diffie_hellman(&inviter_pk);
  87:         let ss_bytes: [u8; 32] = ss.to_bytes();
  88:         if ss_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
  89:             return Err(PairError::SmallOrderPubkey);
  90:         }
  91:         let chain_key = derive_chain_key(&t, &ss_bytes);
  92: 
  93:         Ok((
  94:             Self {
  95:                 id_signing,
  96:                 ephemeral_secret: Some(ephemeral_secret),
  97:                 invite,
  98:                 response,
  99:                 transcript: t,
 100:                 sas,
 101:                 pending_chain_key: Some(chain_key),
 102:                 state: ScannerState::AwaitingConfirm,
 103:             },
 104:             response_bytes,
 105:         ))
 106:     }
 107: 
 108:     /// Read the SAS to display to the user.
 109:     pub fn sas(&self) -> &Sas {
 110:         &self.sas
 111:     }
 112: 
 113:     /// Read the inviter's identity pubkey for UI display
 114:     /// ("you are pairing with: <pubkey-fingerprint>").
 115:     pub fn inviter_pubkey(&self) -> &[u8; 32] {
 116:         &self.invite.id_pubkey
 117:     }
 118: 
 119:     /// Current state.
 120:     pub fn state(&self) -> ScannerState {
 121:         self.state
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     /// Accept the inviter's confirm. Verifies the signature + that
 125:     /// the transcript hash matches what we saw, then advances to
 126:     /// Done and returns the final chain key.
 127:     pub fn receive_confirm(&mut self, confirm_bytes: &[u8]) -> PairResult<ChainKey> {
 128:         self.receive_confirm_inner(confirm_bytes, None)
 129:     }
 130: 
 131:     /// Like [`Scanner::receive_confirm`] but mixes in a Factor-2
 132:     /// channel-reciprocity key. Both peers MUST supply the same
 133:     /// factor-2 key; otherwise the chain keys diverge.
 134:     pub fn receive_confirm_with_factor2(
 135:         &mut self,
 136:         confirm_bytes: &[u8],
 137:         factor2_key: &[u8; 32],
 138:     ) -> PairResult<ChainKey> {
 139:         self.receive_confirm_inner(confirm_bytes, Some(factor2_key))
 140:     }
 141: 
 142:     fn receive_confirm_inner(
 143:         &mut self,
 144:         confirm_bytes: &[u8],
 145:         factor2_key: Option<&[u8; 32]>,
 146:     ) -> PairResult<ChainKey> {
 147:         if self.state != ScannerState::AwaitingConfirm {
 148:             return Err(PairError::WrongState);
 149:         }
 150:         let _ = PairConfirm::decode_and_verify(
 151:             confirm_bytes,
 152:             &self.invite.id_pubkey,
 153:             &self.transcript,
 154:         )?;
 155:         let chain_key = self
 156:             .pending_chain_key
 157:             .take()
 158:             .ok_or(PairError::Internal("chain_key missing"))?;
 159:         let final_chain_key = match factor2_key {
 160:             Some(f2) => crate::chain_key::mix_factor2_recip(&chain_key, f2),
 161:             None => chain_key,
 162:         };
 163:         self.state = ScannerState::Done;
 164:         // Zeroize ephemeral material now that pairing is done.
 165:         if let Some(esk) = self.ephemeral_secret.take() {
 166:             drop(esk);
 167:         }
 168:         Ok(final_chain_key)
 169:     }
 170: 
 171:     /// User said the SAS doesn't match. Abort + zeroize secrets.
 172:     pub fn abort(&mut self) {
 173:         self.state = ScannerState::Aborted;
 174:         self.ephemeral_secret = None;
 175:         self.pending_chain_key = None;
 176:     }
 177: 
 178:     /// Read-only view of the scanned invite (for UI / audit).
 179:     pub fn invite(&self) -> &Invite {
 180:         &self.invite
 181:     }
 182: 
 183:     /// Read-only view of the response the scanner sent (for audit).
 184:     pub fn response(&self) -> &PairResponse {
 185:         &self.response
 186:     }
 187: }
 188: 
 189: impl Drop for Scanner {
 190:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 191:         if let Some(esk) = self.ephemeral_secret.take() {
 192:             drop(esk);
 193:         }
 194:     }
 195: }
 196: 
 197: impl std::fmt::Debug for Scanner {
 198:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 199:         f.debug_struct("Scanner")
 200:             .field("state", &self.state)
 201:             .field(
 202:                 "inviter_pubkey_prefix",
 203:                 &&self.invite.id_pubkey[..4],
 204:             )
 205:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 206:     }
 207: }

   1: //! Transcript hash — the single trust anchor for the pair flow.
   2: //!
   3: //! The transcript is the BLAKE3 hash of the canon-encoded
   4: //! concatenation of every message both parties have committed to so
   5: //! far, prefixed with a domain-separator. Both sides compute it
   6: //! independently from their own observed bytes; if they diverge by
   7: //! a single bit, the SAS derived from the transcript will differ
   8: //! and the user-visible compare step fails.
   9: 
  10: use blake3::Hasher;
  11: 
  12: use crate::canon::Writer;
  13: use crate::invite::Invite;
  14: use crate::response::PairResponse;
  15: use crate::PROTOCOL_DOMAIN;
  16: 
  17: /// Length of the transcript hash in bytes.
  18: pub const TRANSCRIPT_LEN: usize = 32;
  19: 
  20: /// Strongly-typed 32-byte transcript hash. Implements
  21: /// constant-time equality via `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`.
  22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
  23: pub struct TranscriptHash(pub [u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]);
  24: 
  25: impl TranscriptHash {
  26:     /// Wrap raw bytes.
  27:     pub fn from_bytes(b: [u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]) -> Self {
  28:         Self(b)
  29:     }
  30: 
  31:     /// View the raw 32 bytes.
  32:     pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN] {
  33:         &self.0
  34:     }
  35: 
  36:     /// Constant-time equality. Use this instead of `==` when
  37:     /// comparing against attacker-controlled values.
  38:     pub fn ct_eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  39:         use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  40:         self.0.ct_eq(&other.0).into()
  41:     }
  42: }
  43: 
  44: /// Build the transcript hash from the invite and response.
  45: ///
  46: /// The PairConfirm message commits to this exact value; if anything
  47: /// in either party's view of the invite/response diverges, the
  48: /// confirmation's signature fails to verify locally.
  49: pub fn transcript_hash(invite: &Invite, response: &PairResponse) -> TranscriptHash {
  50:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
  51:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
  52:     h.update(b"-transcript");
  53:     // Length-prefix each frame so they can never be ambiguously
  54:     // re-grouped. Frame lengths are well below `u32::MAX`.
  55:     let invite_bytes = invite.encode();
  56:     let response_bytes = response.encode();
  57:     let mut w = Writer::with_capacity(8 + invite_bytes.len() + response_bytes.len());
  58:     w.write_u32(invite_bytes.len() as u32);
  59:     w.write_fixed(&invite_bytes);
  60:     w.write_u32(response_bytes.len() as u32);
  61:     w.write_fixed(&response_bytes);
  62:     h.update(w.as_bytes());
  63:     let digest = h.finalize();
  64:     let mut out = [0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
  65:     out.copy_from_slice(digest.as_bytes());
  66:     TranscriptHash(out)
  67: }

 270: #[test]
 271: fn adversarial_sas_collision_resistance_smoke() {
 272:     // Generate 1000 distinct transcripts by BLAKE3-hashing the
 273:     // iteration counter (gives full 32-byte entropy each iter).
 274:     // The number of distinct SAS values observed should be ≥ 999
 275:     // because the SAS has 30 bits of entropy and the birthday bound
 276:     // at 1000 samples in 2³⁰ space is < 1 expected collision.
 277:     use ol_pair_qr::sas::Sas;
 278:     use std::collections::HashSet;
 279:     let mut seen = HashSet::new();
 280:     for i in 0u64..1000 {
 281:         let h = blake3::hash(&i.to_le_bytes());
 282:         let mut bytes = [0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
 283:         bytes.copy_from_slice(h.as_bytes());
 284:         let t = TranscriptHash::from_bytes(bytes);
 285:         seen.insert(Sas::derive(&t).raw_bits);
 286:     }
 287:     assert!(
 288:         seen.len() >= 999,
 289:         "SAS collision rate too high: {} distinct from 1000",
 290:         seen.len()
 291:     );
 292: }

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_pair_qr/tests/constant_time_gate.rs", "bytes": 8533, "sha256": "a627be32eabf63ce39ec076eb8ac8b52e56784de32c59d7978b5d9b657e622f8", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T23:25:45.796197+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
