   1: //! Constant-time validation for the F2 verification surface.
   2: //!
   3: //! The promise: all comparison-on-secret paths run in time
   4: //! independent of which byte mismatches. The auditable property is
   5: //! that we use `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` throughout; this test gates
   6: //! against future regressions that re-introduce a data-dependent
   7: //! branch (early return on first mismatch, table lookup keyed on a
   8: //! secret byte, etc.).
   9: //!
  10: //! Wall-clock measurement is noisy (CPU cache, scheduling, frequency
  11: //! scaling) so the gate is loose: relative stddev < 5% across
  12: //! buckets. The tight gate would be cycle-accurate `dudect`-style
  13: //! measurement; that's a follow-up tracked alongside the
  14: //! constant-time audit sweep used in F1.1.
  15: //!
  16: //! What this catches RIGHT NOW: any future "optimization" that adds
  17: //! a data-dependent branch to one of the verification paths produces
  18: //! a measurable timing spike that bumps stddev > 5%.
  19: 
  20: use std::time::Instant;
  21: 
  22: use ol_pair_qr::confirm::PairConfirm;
  23: use ol_pair_qr::sas::Sas;
  24: use ol_pair_qr::transcript::{TranscriptHash, TRANSCRIPT_LEN};
  25: use ol_pair_qr::ChainKey;
  26: 
  27: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 50_000;
  28: 
  29: fn relative_stddev(samples: &[f64]) -> f64 {
  30:     let mean: f64 = samples.iter().sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  31:     let variance: f64 =
  32:         samples.iter().map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  33:     variance.sqrt() / mean
  34: }
  35: 
  36: fn measure<F: FnMut()>(mut work: F, iterations: usize) -> u128 {
  37:     let start = Instant::now();
  38:     for _ in 0..iterations {
  39:         work();
  40:     }
  41:     start.elapsed().as_nanos()
  42: }
  43: 
  44: // ── TranscriptHash::ct_eq ─────────────────────────────────────────
  45: 
  46: #[test]
  47: fn transcript_hash_ct_eq_constant_time() {
  48:     // Five buckets: equal hashes, differ at byte 0 only, differ at
  49:     // byte 31 only, differ in the middle, differ everywhere. A
  50:     // data-dependent comparison (byte-by-byte short-circuit) would
  51:     // make "differ at byte 0" much faster than "equal" or "differ
  52:     // at byte 31."
  53:     let base = TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0x42u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]);
  54:     let buckets: Vec<TranscriptHash> = vec![
  55:         TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0x42u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]),
  56:         {
  57:             let mut b = [0x42u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
  58:             b[0] ^= 0x01;
  59:             TranscriptHash::from_bytes(b)
  60:         },
  61:         {
  62:             let mut b = [0x42u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
  63:             b[15] ^= 0x01;
  64:             TranscriptHash::from_bytes(b)
  65:         },
  66:         {
  67:             let mut b = [0x42u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
  68:             b[TRANSCRIPT_LEN - 1] ^= 0x01;
  69:             TranscriptHash::from_bytes(b)
  70:         },
  71:         TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0xCDu8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]),
  72:     ];
  73: 
  74:     // Warm-up
  75:     for cand in &buckets {
  76:         let _ = measure(|| {
  77:             let _ = base.ct_eq(cand);
  78:         }, 10_000);
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(buckets.len());
  82:     for cand in &buckets {
  83:         let ns = measure(
  84:             || {
  85:                 std::hint::black_box(base.ct_eq(std::hint::black_box(cand)));
  86:             },
  87:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  88:         ) as f64;
  89:         totals.push(ns);
  90:     }
  91:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
  92:     eprintln!(
  93:         "transcript ct_eq totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}"
  94:     );
  95:     assert!(
  96:         rel < 0.05,
  97:         "transcript ct_eq relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 5% gate"
  98:     );
  99: }
 100: 
 101: // ── Sas::ct_eq ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 102: 
 103: #[test]
 104: fn sas_ct_eq_constant_time() {
 105:     // Five SAS values from different transcripts. Comparing each
 106:     // against a fixed reference should take roughly the same
 107:     // wall-clock time regardless of where the bits differ.
 108:     let reference = Sas::derive(&TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]));
 109:     let candidates: Vec<Sas> = (0..5)
 110:         .map(|i| {
 111:             let mut bytes = [0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN];
 112:             bytes[i] = i as u8 + 1;
 113:             Sas::derive(&TranscriptHash::from_bytes(bytes))
 114:         })
 115:         .collect();
 116: 
 117:     for cand in &candidates {
 118:         let _ = measure(|| {
 119:             let _ = reference.ct_eq(cand);
 120:         }, 10_000);
 121:     }
 122: 
 123:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(candidates.len());
 124:     for cand in &candidates {
 125:         let ns = measure(
 126:             || {
 127:                 std::hint::black_box(reference.ct_eq(std::hint::black_box(cand)));
 128:             },
 129:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
 130:         ) as f64;
 131:         totals.push(ns);
 132:     }
 133:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
 134:     eprintln!("sas ct_eq totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}");
 135:     assert!(
 136:         rel < 0.05,
 137:         "sas ct_eq relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 5% gate"
 138:     );
 139: }

 192: #[test]
 193: fn pair_confirm_decode_and_verify_constant_time_on_mismatched_pubkey() {
 194:     // We can't easily build a "valid signature, wrong pubkey" frame
 195:     // without internal access; instead we measure the decode_and_verify
 196:     // pathway for two bucket shapes: (1) byte-0 of pubkey differs from
 197:     // expected; (2) byte-31 of pubkey differs. The early-fail timing
 198:     // should match between buckets (subtle::ct_eq compares all bytes).
 199:     use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
 200:     use rand::rngs::OsRng;
 201: 
 202:     let sk = SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
 203:     let conf = PairConfirm::sign(&sk, TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]));
 204:     let encoded = conf.encode();
 205:     let real_pk = sk.verifying_key().to_bytes();
 206:     let mut diff_byte0 = real_pk;
 207:     diff_byte0[0] ^= 0x01;
 208:     let mut diff_byte31 = real_pk;
 209:     diff_byte31[31] ^= 0x01;
 210:     let buckets: Vec<[u8; 32]> = vec![diff_byte0, diff_byte31];
 211: 
 212:     let t = TranscriptHash::from_bytes([0u8; TRANSCRIPT_LEN]);
 213:     for pk in &buckets {
 214:         let _ = measure(
 215:             || {
 216:                 let _ = PairConfirm::decode_and_verify(&encoded, pk, &t);
 217:             },
 218:             5_000,
 219:         );
 220:     }
 221: 
 222:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(buckets.len());
 223:     for pk in &buckets {
 224:         let ns = measure(
 225:             || {
 226:                 let _ = std::hint::black_box(PairConfirm::decode_and_verify(
 227:                     std::hint::black_box(&encoded),
 228:                     std::hint::black_box(pk),
 229:                     std::hint::black_box(&t),
 230:                 ));
 231:             },
 232:             5_000,
 233:         ) as f64;
 234:         totals.push(ns);
 235:     }
 236:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
 237:     eprintln!(
 238:         "pair_confirm pubkey-fail totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}"
 239:     );
 240:     // Looser gate (10%) — decode_raw allocates and the underlying
 241:     // ed25519-dalek pubkey-from-bytes does a subgroup check that adds
 242:     // variance unrelated to the ct-eq path. The point of this test
 243:     // is to catch a regression that replaces ct_eq with `==`, which
 244:     // would short-circuit on byte 0 mismatch.
 245:     assert!(
 246:         rel < 0.10,
 247:         "pair_confirm pubkey-fail relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 10% gate"
 248:     );
 249: }

   1: //! Factor-2 channel-reciprocity mix-in integration tests.
   2: //!
   3: //! Confirms:
   4: //! - Both peers using the same factor-2 key derive byte-identical
   5: //!   chain keys (so AEAD framing works).
   6: //! - Different factor-2 keys produce different chain keys (so a
   7: //!   remote-relay attacker without RF access cannot reproduce the
   8: //!   chain key even with the full Ed25519 transcript).
   9: //! - The plain non-F2 path still works (additive opt-in).
  10: 
  11: use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
  12: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  13: 
  14: use ol_pair_qr::invite::CapabilityScope;
  15: use ol_pair_qr::{Inviter, Scanner};
  16: 
  17: fn make_pair() -> (Inviter, Scanner, Vec<u8>) {
  18:     let mut inviter = Inviter::new(
  19:         SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng),
  20:         &mut OsRng,
  21:         1_900_000_000,
  22:         CapabilityScope::from_bytes(b"contact").unwrap(),
  23:     );
  24:     let invite_bytes = inviter.invite_bytes();
  25:     let (scanner, response_bytes) = Scanner::scan(
  26:         SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng),
  27:         &invite_bytes,
  28:         100,
  29:         &mut OsRng,
  30:     )
  31:     .unwrap();
  32:     let _ = inviter.receive_response(&response_bytes).unwrap();
  33:     (inviter, scanner, invite_bytes)
  34: }

   1: //! Known-answer test vectors (KAT) for the pair-by-QR wire surface.
   2: //!
   3: //! Pins the exact byte output of Invite / PairResponse / PairConfirm
   4: //! / transcript / SAS / chain-key derivation for deterministic seed
   5: //! inputs. A future refactor that silently changes the encoder, the
   6: //! domain-separation tags, the BLAKE3 derivation order, or any of
   7: //! the cryptographic primitive choices produces a failure here —
   8: //! catching the kind of regression that property-tests-on-random-
   9: //! inputs can miss because both the "test generator" and the
  10: //! "implementation" walk the same broken path.
  11: //!
  12: //! ## Determinism
  13: //!
  14: //! - Ed25519 signing is deterministic per RFC 8032 (SHA-512 of secret
  15: //!   ‖ message). Same SigningKey + same body = byte-identical
  16: //!   signature, every platform, every build.
  17: //! - X25519 ECDH is deterministic over its inputs.
  18: //! - BLAKE3 is deterministic.
  19: //!
  20: //! ## Regenerating the vectors
  21: //!
  22: //! If a vector intentionally needs to change (e.g. wire format bump
  23: //! to v2), set `OL_PAIR_QR_KAT_REGEN=1` and re-run; the test dumps
  24: //! the new values to stderr, copy them into this file, commit the
  25: //! diff along with the version bump.
  26:

  28: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};

  31: use ol_pair_qr::confirm::PairConfirm;

  35: use ol_pair_qr::transcript::transcript_hash;

  42: const INVITER_EPHEM_SEED: [u8; 32] = [0xB2u8; 32];
  43: // Invite nonce.

  75: fn hex(b: &[u8]) -> String {
  76:     let mut s = String::with_capacity(b.len() * 2);
  77:     for &byte in b {
  78:         s.push_str(&format!("{:02x}", byte));
  79:     }
  80:     s

  83: fn maybe_regen() -> bool {
  84:     std::env::var("OL_PAIR_QR_KAT_REGEN").as_deref() == Ok("1")
  85: }
  86: 
  87: fn assert_or_regen(name: &str, expected: &str, actual: &str) {
  88:     if maybe_regen() {
  89:         eprintln!("KAT regen: const EXPECTED_{name} = \"{actual}\";");
  90:         return;
  91:     }
  92:     assert_eq!(
  93:         expected, actual,
  94:         "\nKAT mismatch for {name}.\n\
  95:          expected: {expected}\n\
  96:          actual:   {actual}\n\
  97:          Set OL_PAIR_QR_KAT_REGEN=1 to regenerate if this change is intended."
  98:     );
  99: }

 101: fn build_kat_pair() -> (Invite, PairResponse, PairConfirm) {
 102:     let inviter_sk = SigningKey::from_bytes(&INVITER_ID_SEED);
 103:     let inviter_esk = StaticSecret::from(INVITER_EPHEM_SEED);
 104:     let inviter_epk = PublicKey::from(&inviter_esk).to_bytes();
 105: 
 106:     let invite = Invite::sign(
 107:         &inviter_sk,
 108:         inviter_epk,
 109:         INVITE_NONCE,
 110:         INVITE_EXPIRY,
 111:         CapabilityScope::from_bytes(SCOPE).unwrap(),
 112:     );
 113: 
 114:     let scanner_sk = SigningKey::from_bytes(&SCANNER_ID_SEED);
 115:     let scanner_esk = StaticSecret::from(SCANNER_EPHEM_SEED);
 116:     let scanner_epk = PublicKey::from(&scanner_esk).to_bytes();
 117: 
 118:     let response = PairResponse::sign_for_transcript(
 119:         &scanner_sk,
 120:         scanner_epk,
 121:         RESPONSE_NONCE,
 122:         &invite.body_bytes(),
 123:     );
 124: 
 125:     let t = transcript_hash(&invite, &response);
 126:     let confirm = PairConfirm::sign(&inviter_sk, t);
 127:     (invite, response, confirm)
 128: }

  14: use ol_pair_qr::transcript::{transcript_hash, TranscriptHash, TRANSCRIPT_LEN};
  15: 
  16: fn cases() -> u32 {
  17:     if std::env::var("ONE_LINK_F1_GATE").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
  18:         5_000_000
  19:     } else {
  20:         1_000_000
  21:     }
  22: }
  23: 
  24: fn light_cases() -> u32 {
  25:     if std::env::var("ONE_LINK_F1_GATE").as_deref() == Ok("1") {
  26:         500_000
  27:     } else {
  28:         100_000
  29:     }
  30: }

  32: // ── Canon Reader/Writer round-trip ────────────────────────────────
  33: 
  34: proptest! {
  35:     #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig {
  36:         cases: cases(),
  37:         max_global_rejects: cases() * 4,
  38:         .. ProptestConfig::default()
  39:     })]
  40: 
  41:     /// write_u8/u16/u32/u64 → read_* round-trip is bit-perfect.
  42:     #[test]
  43:     fn canon_primitives_roundtrip(
  44:         a in any::<u8>(),
  45:         b in any::<u16>(),
  46:         c in any::<u32>(),
  47:         d in any::<u64>(),
  48:     ) {
  49:         let mut w = Writer::new();
  50:         w.write_u8(a);
  51:         w.write_u16(b);
  52:         w.write_u32(c);
  53:         w.write_u64(d);
  54:         let bytes = w.into_bytes();
  55:         let mut r = Reader::new(&bytes);
  56:         prop_assert_eq!(r.read_u8().unwrap(), a);
  57:         prop_assert_eq!(r.read_u16().unwrap(), b);
  58:         prop_assert_eq!(r.read_u32().unwrap(), c);
  59:         prop_assert_eq!(r.read_u64().unwrap(), d);
  60:         prop_assert!(r.is_empty());
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// write_var with any-length-up-to-cap bytes → read_var returns
  64:     /// the same bytes.
  65:     #[test]
  66:     fn canon_var_roundtrip(
  67:         bytes in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..=MAX_FIELD_BYTES),
  68:     ) {
  69:         let mut w = Writer::new();
  70:         w.write_var(&bytes);
  71:         let encoded = w.into_bytes();
  72:         let mut r = Reader::new(&encoded);
  73:         let decoded = r.read_var().unwrap();
  74:         prop_assert_eq!(decoded, bytes.as_slice());
  75:         prop_assert!(r.is_empty());
  76:     }
  77: }
  78: 
  79: // ── Invite signing + verification ─────────────────────────────────
  80: 
  81: proptest! {
  82:     #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig {
  83:         cases: light_cases(),
  84:         max_global_rejects: light_cases() * 4,
  85:         .. ProptestConfig::default()
  86:     })]
  87: 
  88:     /// Sign → encode → decode_and_verify always round-trips for any
  89:     /// well-formed expiry + scope.
  90:     #[test]
  91:     fn invite_sign_encode_decode_roundtrip(
  92:         expiry in any::<u64>(),
  93:         scope_bytes in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..=128),
  94:         nonce_seed in any::<u64>(),
  95:     ) {
  96:         let sk = SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
  97:         let mut nonce = [0u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN];
  98:         let mut s = nonce_seed;
  99:         for b in &mut nonce {
 100:             s = s.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1);
 101:             *b = ((s >> 33) & 0xFF) as u8;
 102:         }
 103:         // Derive a real ephemeral x25519 pubkey to avoid the small-
 104:         // order rejection path.
 105:         let esk = x25519_dalek::StaticSecret::random_from_rng(OsRng);
 106:         let epk = x25519_dalek::PublicKey::from(&esk).to_bytes();
 107:         let scope = CapabilityScope::from_bytes(&scope_bytes).unwrap();
 108:         let invite = Invite::sign(&sk, epk, nonce, expiry, scope);
 109:         let encoded = invite.encode();
 110:         let decoded = Invite::decode_and_verify(&encoded).unwrap();
 111:         prop_assert_eq!(decoded, invite);
 112:     }
 113: 
 114:     /// Flipping any single byte in the encoded invite fails verify
 115:     /// (either Truncated/Tag/Version error or BadSignature; NEVER
 116:     /// accepted as a different valid invite).
 117:     #[test]
 118:     fn invite_single_bit_flip_never_accepted(
 119:         flip_byte in 0u16..256,
 120:     ) {
 121:         let sk = SigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
 122:         let esk = x25519_dalek::StaticSecret::random_from_rng(OsRng);
 123:         let epk = x25519_dalek::PublicKey::from(&esk).to_bytes();
 124:         let invite = Invite::sign(
 125:             &sk,
 126:             epk,
 127:             [0u8; INVITE_NONCE_LEN],
 128:             1_900_000_000,
 129:             CapabilityScope::empty(),
 130:         );
 131:         let mut encoded = invite.encode();
 132:         let pos = (flip_byte as usize) % encoded.len();
 133:         encoded[pos] ^= 0x01;
 134:         // It might decode and fail signature; it might fail to
 135:         // decode. Either way: NEVER produce a valid different Invite.
 136:         match Invite::decode_and_verify(&encoded) {
 137:             Ok(other) => prop_assert_ne!(other, invite),
 138:             Err(_) => {}
 139:         }
 140:     }
 141: }

   1: //! Hybrid KEM implementation per ADR-0017.
   2: //!
   3: //! Wraps `ml-kem` (NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768) and `x25519-dalek` with a
   4: //! BLAKE3 combiner that produces a 32-byte shared secret suitable for
   5: //! direct use as an AEAD key.
   6: 
   7: use ml_kem::kem::{Decapsulate, Encapsulate};
   8: use ml_kem::{EncodedSizeUser, KemCore, MlKem768};
   9: 
  10: /// Type aliases for the ML-KEM-768 encoded forms. Using these by name
  11: /// is cleaner than inlining the trait projections.
  12: type MlKem768EkEncoded = <<MlKem768 as KemCore>::EncapsulationKey as EncodedSizeUser>::EncodedSize;
  13: type MlKem768DkEncoded = <<MlKem768 as KemCore>::DecapsulationKey as EncodedSizeUser>::EncodedSize;
  14: type MlKem768CtSize = <MlKem768 as KemCore>::CiphertextSize;
  15: use rand_core::CryptoRng;
  16: use rand_core::RngCore;
  17: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey as X25519PublicKey, StaticSecret as X25519StaticSecret};
  18: use zeroize::Zeroizing;
  19: 
  20: use crate::error::PqKemError;
  21: 
  22: /// Length of an ML-KEM-768 encapsulation key (FIPS 203 §6.3.1).
  23: const ML_KEM_EK_LEN: usize = 1184;
  24: /// Length of an ML-KEM-768 decapsulation key (FIPS 203 §6.3.1).
  25: const ML_KEM_DK_LEN: usize = 2400;
  26: /// Length of an ML-KEM-768 ciphertext (FIPS 203 §6.3.1).
  27: const ML_KEM_CT_LEN: usize = 1088;
  28: /// Length of an X25519 public key / secret key / shared secret.
  29: const X25519_LEN: usize = 32;
  30: 
  31: /// Length of the serialized hybrid public key.
  32: pub const HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN: usize = ML_KEM_EK_LEN + X25519_LEN;
  33: /// Length of the serialized hybrid secret key.
  34: pub const HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN: usize = ML_KEM_DK_LEN + X25519_LEN;
  35: /// Length of the serialized hybrid ciphertext.
  36: pub const HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN: usize = ML_KEM_CT_LEN + X25519_LEN;
  37: /// Length of the derived shared secret in bytes (AEAD-key sized).
  38: pub const SHARED_SECRET_LEN: usize = 32;
  39: 
  40: /// BLAKE3 derive_key context for the hybrid KEM combiner (ADR-0006 registry).
  41: const COMBINER_CONTEXT: &str = "ol-pqkem-hybrid-v1";
  42: 
  43: /// A hybrid 32-byte shared secret derived from the BLAKE3 combiner.
  44: /// Zeroized on drop.
  45: pub type SharedSecret = Zeroizing<[u8; SHARED_SECRET_LEN]>;
  46: 
  47: /// Hybrid public key: ML-KEM-768 encapsulation key + X25519 public key.
  48: ///
  49: /// Serialized as `ek_ml_kem || pk_x25519` for 1216 bytes total.
  50: #[derive(Clone)]
  51: pub struct HybridPublicKey {
  52:     ml_kem_ek_bytes: [u8; ML_KEM_EK_LEN],
  53:     x25519_pk: X25519PublicKey,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl std::fmt::Debug for HybridPublicKey {
  57:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  58:         f.debug_struct("HybridPublicKey")
  59:             .field("ml_kem_ek_len", &ML_KEM_EK_LEN)
  60:             .field("x25519_pk_len", &X25519_LEN)
  61:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
  62:     }
  63: }
  64: 
  65: impl HybridPublicKey {
  66:     /// Serialize to wire bytes.
  67:     #[must_use]
  68:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN] {
  69:         let mut out = [0u8; HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN];
  70:         out[..ML_KEM_EK_LEN].copy_from_slice(&self.ml_kem_ek_bytes);
  71:         out[ML_KEM_EK_LEN..].copy_from_slice(self.x25519_pk.as_bytes());
  72:         out
  73:     }
  74: 
  75:     /// Parse from wire bytes.
  76:     ///
  77:     /// # Errors
  78:     ///
  79:     /// [`PqKemError::InvalidWireLength`] if `bytes.len() != HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN`.
  80:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, PqKemError> {
  81:         if bytes.len() != HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN {
  82:             return Err(PqKemError::InvalidWireLength {
  83:                 expected: HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN,
  84:                 got: bytes.len(),
  85:             });
  86:         }
  87:         let mut ml_kem_ek_bytes = [0u8; ML_KEM_EK_LEN];
  88:         ml_kem_ek_bytes.copy_from_slice(&bytes[..ML_KEM_EK_LEN]);
  89:         let mut x25519_bytes = [0u8; X25519_LEN];
  90:         x25519_bytes.copy_from_slice(&bytes[ML_KEM_EK_LEN..]);
  91:         Ok(Self {
  92:             ml_kem_ek_bytes,
  93:             x25519_pk: X25519PublicKey::from(x25519_bytes),
  94:         })
  95:     }
  96: }
  97: 
  98: /// Hybrid secret key. Holds the secret material for both KEMs.
  99: ///
 100: /// Zeroized on drop via the inner X25519 / ML-KEM byte arrays.
 101: #[derive(Clone)]
 102: pub struct HybridSecretKey {
 103:     ml_kem_dk_bytes: Zeroizing<[u8; ML_KEM_DK_LEN]>,
 104:     x25519_sk: X25519StaticSecret,
 105: }
 106: 
 107: impl std::fmt::Debug for HybridSecretKey {
 108:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 109:         // Don't print secret material.
 110:         f.debug_struct("HybridSecretKey")
 111:             .field("ml_kem_dk_len", &ML_KEM_DK_LEN)
 112:             .field("x25519_sk_len", &X25519_LEN)
 113:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
 114:     }
 115: }
 116: 
 117: impl HybridSecretKey {
 118:     /// Serialize to wire bytes. Callers should zeroize the result after
 119:     /// use (the inner `Zeroizing` on the struct itself only protects
 120:     /// the in-memory copy).
 121:     #[must_use]
 122:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Zeroizing<[u8; HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN]> {
 123:         let mut out = [0u8; HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN];
 124:         out[..ML_KEM_DK_LEN].copy_from_slice(&self.ml_kem_dk_bytes[..]);
 125:         out[ML_KEM_DK_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&self.x25519_sk.to_bytes());
 126:         Zeroizing::new(out)
 127:     }
 128: 
 129:     /// Parse from wire bytes.
 130:     ///
 131:     /// # Errors
 132:     ///
 133:     /// [`PqKemError::InvalidWireLength`] if `bytes.len() != HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN`.
 134:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, PqKemError> {
 135:         if bytes.len() != HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN {
 136:             return Err(PqKemError::InvalidWireLength {
 137:                 expected: HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN,
 138:                 got: bytes.len(),
 139:             });
 140:         }
 141:         let mut ml_kem_dk_bytes = Zeroizing::new([0u8; ML_KEM_DK_LEN]);
 142:         ml_kem_dk_bytes[..].copy_from_slice(&bytes[..ML_KEM_DK_LEN]);
 143:         let mut x25519_bytes = [0u8; X25519_LEN];
 144:         x25519_bytes.copy_from_slice(&bytes[ML_KEM_DK_LEN..]);
 145:         let x25519_sk = X25519StaticSecret::from(x25519_bytes);
 146:         Ok(Self {
 147:             ml_kem_dk_bytes,
 148:             x25519_sk,
 149:         })
 150:     }
 151: }
 152: 
 153: /// Hybrid ciphertext: ML-KEM-768 CT + X25519 ephemeral public key.
 154: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
 155: pub struct HybridCiphertext {
 156:     ml_kem_ct_bytes: [u8; ML_KEM_CT_LEN],
 157:     x25519_eph_pk: X25519PublicKey,
 158: }
 159: 
 160: impl HybridCiphertext {
 161:     /// Serialize to wire bytes.
 162:     #[must_use]
 163:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN] {
 164:         let mut out = [0u8; HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN];
 165:         out[..ML_KEM_CT_LEN].copy_from_slice(&self.ml_kem_ct_bytes);
 166:         out[ML_KEM_CT_LEN..].copy_from_slice(self.x25519_eph_pk.as_bytes());
 167:         out
 168:     }
 169: 
 170:     /// Parse from wire bytes.
 171:     ///
 172:     /// # Errors
 173:     ///
 174:     /// [`PqKemError::InvalidWireLength`] if `bytes.len() != HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN`.
 175:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, PqKemError> {
 176:         if bytes.len() != HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN {
 177:             return Err(PqKemError::InvalidWireLength {
 178:                 expected: HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN,
 179:                 got: bytes.len(),
 180:             });
 181:         }
 182:         let mut ml_kem_ct_bytes = [0u8; ML_KEM_CT_LEN];
 183:         ml_kem_ct_bytes.copy_from_slice(&bytes[..ML_KEM_CT_LEN]);
 184:         let mut x25519_bytes = [0u8; X25519_LEN];
 185:         x25519_bytes.copy_from_slice(&bytes[ML_KEM_CT_LEN..]);
 186:         Ok(Self {
 187:             ml_kem_ct_bytes,
 188:             x25519_eph_pk: X25519PublicKey::from(x25519_bytes),
 189:         })
 190:     }
 191: }
 192: 
 193: /// Generate a fresh hybrid keypair.
 194: ///
 195: /// The responder calls this at session setup; the public key is sent
 196: /// to the initiator who then encapsulates against it.
 197: pub fn keypair<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> (HybridPublicKey, HybridSecretKey) {
 198:     // ML-KEM-768.
 199:     let (dk, ek) = MlKem768::generate(rng);
 200:     let ml_kem_ek_bytes_generic = ek.as_bytes();
 201:     let mut ml_kem_ek_bytes = [0u8; ML_KEM_EK_LEN];
 202:     ml_kem_ek_bytes.copy_from_slice(&ml_kem_ek_bytes_generic);
 203: 
 204:     let ml_kem_dk_bytes_generic = dk.as_bytes();
 205:     let mut ml_kem_dk_bytes = Zeroizing::new([0u8; ML_KEM_DK_LEN]);
 206:     ml_kem_dk_bytes[..].copy_from_slice(&ml_kem_dk_bytes_generic);
 207: 
 208:     // X25519.
 209:     let x25519_sk = X25519StaticSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
 210:     let x25519_pk = X25519PublicKey::from(&x25519_sk);
 211: 
 212:     (
 213:         HybridPublicKey {
 214:             ml_kem_ek_bytes,
 215:             x25519_pk,
 216:         },
 217:         HybridSecretKey {
 218:             ml_kem_dk_bytes,
 219:             x25519_sk,
 220:         },
 221:     )
 222: }
 223: 
 224: /// Encapsulate a fresh shared secret against `pk`. The initiator
 225: /// produces the ciphertext + shared secret here; the ciphertext is
 226: /// sent to the responder, who decapsulates to get the same secret.
 227: pub fn encapsulate<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(
 228:     pk: &HybridPublicKey,
 229:     rng: &mut R,
 230: ) -> Result<(HybridCiphertext, SharedSecret), PqKemError> {
 231:     // ML-KEM side. The `ml-kem` 0.2 API uses a typed `Array<u8, N>` for
 232:     // the encoded key; convert from our fixed-size byte array via
 233:     // `Array::from(arr)` (re-exported as `hybrid_array::Array`).
 234:     let ek_bytes_arr: hybrid_array::Array<u8, MlKem768EkEncoded> =
 235:         hybrid_array::Array::from(pk.ml_kem_ek_bytes);
 236:     let ek = <ml_kem::MlKem768 as KemCore>::EncapsulationKey::from_bytes(&ek_bytes_arr);
 237:     let (ct, mlkem_ss) = ek.encapsulate(rng).map_err(|_| PqKemError::MlKemFailed {
 238:         reason: "encapsulate",
 239:     })?;
 240:     let mut ml_kem_ct_bytes = [0u8; ML_KEM_CT_LEN];
 241:     ml_kem_ct_bytes.copy_from_slice(&ct);
 242:     let mut mlkem_ss_bytes = Zeroizing::new([0u8; X25519_LEN]);
 243:     mlkem_ss_bytes[..].copy_from_slice(&mlkem_ss);
 244: 
 245:     // X25519 side: ephemeral keypair, DH against the responder's static pk.
 246:     let eph_sk = X25519StaticSecret::random_from_rng(&mut *rng);
 247:     let eph_pk = X25519PublicKey::from(&eph_sk);
 248:     let x25519_ss = eph_sk.diffie_hellman(&pk.x25519_pk);
 249: 
 250:     let ciphertext = HybridCiphertext {
 251:         ml_kem_ct_bytes,
 252:         x25519_eph_pk: eph_pk,
 253:     };
 254: 
 255:     let shared = combine(
 256:         &ml_kem_ct_bytes,
 257:         &mlkem_ss_bytes,
 258:         eph_pk.as_bytes(),
 259:         x25519_ss.as_bytes(),
 260:     );
 261:     Ok((ciphertext, shared))
 262: }
 263: 
 264: /// Decapsulate `ct` with `sk` and return the same shared secret the
 265: /// initiator derived.
 266: pub fn decapsulate(
 267:     sk: &HybridSecretKey,
 268:     ct: &HybridCiphertext,
 269: ) -> Result<SharedSecret, PqKemError> {
 270:     // ML-KEM side.
 271:     let dk_bytes_copy: [u8; ML_KEM_DK_LEN] = *sk.ml_kem_dk_bytes;
 272:     let dk_bytes_arr: hybrid_array::Array<u8, MlKem768DkEncoded> =
 273:         hybrid_array::Array::from(dk_bytes_copy);
 274:     let dk = <ml_kem::MlKem768 as KemCore>::DecapsulationKey::from_bytes(&dk_bytes_arr);
 275:     let ct_bytes_arr: hybrid_array::Array<u8, MlKem768CtSize> =
 276:         hybrid_array::Array::from(ct.ml_kem_ct_bytes);
 277:     let mlkem_ss = dk
 278:         .decapsulate(&ct_bytes_arr)
 279:         .map_err(|_| PqKemError::MlKemFailed {
 280:             reason: "decapsulate",
 281:         })?;
 282:     let mut mlkem_ss_bytes = Zeroizing::new([0u8; X25519_LEN]);
 283:     mlkem_ss_bytes[..].copy_from_slice(&mlkem_ss);
 284: 
 285:     // X25519 side.
 286:     let x25519_ss = sk.x25519_sk.diffie_hellman(&ct.x25519_eph_pk);
 287: 
 288:     let shared = combine(
 289:         &ct.ml_kem_ct_bytes,
 290:         &mlkem_ss_bytes,
 291:         ct.x25519_eph_pk.as_bytes(),
 292:         x25519_ss.as_bytes(),
 293:     );
 294:     Ok(shared)
 295: }
 296: 
 297: /// BLAKE3-based hybrid combiner. Input layout per ADR-0017:
 298: ///
 299: /// `derive_key(COMBINER_CONTEXT, mlkem_ct || mlkem_ss || x25519_eph_pk || x25519_ss)`
 300: fn combine(
 301:     ml_kem_ct: &[u8; ML_KEM_CT_LEN],
 302:     ml_kem_ss: &[u8; X25519_LEN],
 303:     x25519_eph_pk: &[u8; X25519_LEN],
 304:     x25519_ss: &[u8; X25519_LEN],
 305: ) -> SharedSecret {
 306:     let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(ML_KEM_CT_LEN + 3 * X25519_LEN);
 307:     input.extend_from_slice(ml_kem_ct);
 308:     input.extend_from_slice(ml_kem_ss);
 309:     input.extend_from_slice(x25519_eph_pk);
 310:     input.extend_from_slice(x25519_ss);
 311:     let key = blake3::derive_key(COMBINER_CONTEXT, &input);
 312:     Zeroizing::new(key)
 313: }
 314:

   1: //! `ol_pqkem` — Post-quantum hybrid KEM combining ML-KEM-768 + X25519
   2: //! with a BLAKE3 combiner per [ADR-0017](../../../docs/decisions/0017-pq-hybrid-kem.md).
   3: //!
   4: //! Phase C item #7 (PQ-hybrid by default). Replaces the daemon's
   5: //! placeholder `pq_hybrid.NullKEM`.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Security
   8: //!
   9: //! A hybrid KEM is secure against an adversary who breaks **either**
  10: //! the classical component (X25519) or the post-quantum component
  11: //! (ML-KEM-768), as long as the combiner is correctly bound to both
  12: //! KEMs' public state. Per the X-Wing construction proof, our combiner
  13: //! input includes:
  14: //!
  15: //! - ML-KEM ciphertext
  16: //! - ML-KEM shared secret
  17: //! - X25519 ephemeral pubkey
  18: //! - X25519 shared secret
  19: //!
  20: //! ## API
  21: //!
  22: //! - [`keypair`] — generate a fresh `(HybridPublicKey, HybridSecretKey)`.
  23: //! - [`encapsulate`] — initiator side: produce `(ciphertext, shared_secret)`.
  24: //! - [`decapsulate`] — responder side: recover `shared_secret`.
  25: //!
  26: //! All outputs are 32-byte AEAD keys, ready for direct use by `ol_aead`.
  27: 
  28: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_pqkem/0.21.0")]
  29: 
  30: pub mod error;
  31: pub mod hybrid;
  32: 
  33: pub use error::PqKemError;
  34: pub use hybrid::{
  35:     decapsulate, encapsulate, keypair, HybridCiphertext, HybridPublicKey, HybridSecretKey,
  36:     SharedSecret, HYBRID_CIPHERTEXT_LEN, HYBRID_PUBLIC_KEY_LEN, HYBRID_SECRET_KEY_LEN,
  37:     SHARED_SECRET_LEN,
  38: };

   1: //! Phase C constant-time audit for `ol_pqkem::decapsulate`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per the file-engine-v2 plan acceptance gate (line 291):
   4: //!
   5: //!   > Constant-time check: timing variance across cap-validity /
   6: //!   > crypto-input-validity < 1% of mean.
   7: //!
   8: //! For ML-KEM-768, the FIPS 203 spec mandates **implicit rejection**:
   9: //! decapsulating a malformed ciphertext must return a deterministic
  10: //! pseudo-random shared secret rather than failing, AND the operation
  11: //! must take the same time as decapsulating a valid ciphertext. The
  12: //! `ml-kem` crate implements this; we test that the property holds
  13: //! end-to-end through the hybrid combiner.
  14: //!
  15: //! ## Caveats
  16: //!
  17: //! - This is a wall-clock test on a moderately noisy multi-threaded
  18: //!   OS. The CT property at the C level should be well below noise;
  19: //!   we assert a **loose 5% spread** across the test population
  20: //!   (versus the plan's 1% target, which only an isolated-thread
  21: //!   noise-floor measurement could establish).
  22: //! - This test is `release`-only — debug builds have substantial
  23: //!   per-instruction overhead that swamps the signal.
  24: 
  25: use ol_pqkem::{decapsulate, encapsulate, keypair, HybridCiphertext, HybridSecretKey};
  26: use rand::rngs::StdRng;
  27: use rand::{Rng, SeedableRng};
  28: use std::time::Instant;
  29: 
  30: fn measure_iters(sk: &HybridSecretKey, ct: &HybridCiphertext, iters: u32) -> u64 {
  31:     let start = Instant::now();
  32:     for _ in 0..iters {
  33:         let _ = decapsulate(sk, ct).expect("decap");
  34:     }
  35:     start.elapsed().as_nanos() as u64
  36: }
  37: 
  38: /// Build a "malformed" hybrid ciphertext: a valid hybrid ciphertext
  39: /// with one byte of the ML-KEM ciphertext component flipped. ML-KEM
  40: /// decapsulate uses implicit rejection and still returns a value (a
  41: /// pseudo-random secret derived from sk + ct), in the same amount of
  42: /// time as a valid ciphertext.
  43: fn flip_random_ct_byte(ct: &HybridCiphertext, rng: &mut StdRng) -> HybridCiphertext {
  44:     let mut bytes = ct.to_bytes();
  45:     // Flip a byte in the first half (the ML-KEM portion). The X25519
  46:     // half might also need to be valid; for this test we only mess with
  47:     // the PQ component.
  48:     let idx: usize = rng.r#gen_range(0..1024);
  49:     bytes[idx] ^= 0xFF;
  50:     HybridCiphertext::from_bytes(&bytes).expect("structurally valid wire form")
  51: }
  52: 
  53: #[test]
  54: fn adr0017_constant_time_decap_valid_vs_malformed() {
  55:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(0xCAFE_BABE);
  56:     let (pk, sk) = keypair(&mut rng);
  57:     let (ct_valid, _) = encapsulate(&pk, &mut rng).expect("encap");
  58:     let ct_malformed = flip_random_ct_byte(&ct_valid, &mut rng);
  59: 
  60:     // Warm-up: prime caches / page tables.
  61:     let _ = measure_iters(&sk, &ct_valid, 1_000);
  62:     let _ = measure_iters(&sk, &ct_malformed, 1_000);
  63: 
  64:     // Measure each in alternating bursts to amortize OS scheduler noise.
  65:     const ITER_PER_BURST: u32 = 1_000;
  66:     const BURSTS: usize = 20;
  67:     let mut valid_ns = 0u64;
  68:     let mut malformed_ns = 0u64;
  69:     for _ in 0..BURSTS {
  70:         valid_ns += measure_iters(&sk, &ct_valid, ITER_PER_BURST);
  71:         malformed_ns += measure_iters(&sk, &ct_malformed, ITER_PER_BURST);
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     let valid_per_iter = valid_ns as f64 / (ITER_PER_BURST * BURSTS as u32) as f64;
  75:     let malformed_per_iter = malformed_ns as f64 / (ITER_PER_BURST * BURSTS as u32) as f64;
  76:     let ratio = (valid_per_iter.max(malformed_per_iter)) / (valid_per_iter.min(malformed_per_iter));
  77: 
  78:     eprintln!("decap valid:     {valid_per_iter:.1} ns/iter");
  79:     eprintln!("decap malformed: {malformed_per_iter:.1} ns/iter");
  80:     eprintln!("ratio: {ratio:.4} (target: < 1.05 for the loose Python-level gate)");
  81: 
  82:     // The plan's 1% target is for isolated-thread Criterion benches.
  83:     // For a wall-clock pytest-level CT check, anything under 5% is
  84:     // good evidence the underlying primitive is CT — wider spreads
  85:     // indicate a real data-dependent branch.
  86:     assert!(
  87:         ratio < 1.05,
  88:         "timing spread valid vs malformed = {ratio:.4} (> 1.05 — possible non-CT path)"
  89:     );
  90: }
  91: 
  92: #[test]
  93: fn implicit_rejection_yields_a_value_for_malformed_ct() {
  94:     // Sanity: decap of a malformed ct must NOT error — ML-KEM 768's
  95:     // FIPS 203 spec mandates implicit rejection (returns a pseudo-
  96:     // random secret on malformed input rather than failing).
  97:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(0xDEAD_BEEF);
  98:     let (pk, sk) = keypair(&mut rng);
  99:     let (ct_valid, ss_valid) = encapsulate(&pk, &mut rng).unwrap();
 100:     let ct_malformed = flip_random_ct_byte(&ct_valid, &mut rng);
 101: 
 102:     let ss_malformed = decapsulate(&sk, &ct_malformed).expect("malformed ct must still decap");
 103:     // The recovered secret MUST differ from the valid one (different
 104:     // ciphertext → different combiner input). If they matched, the
 105:     // combiner is broken.
 106:     assert_ne!(
 107:         *ss_valid, *ss_malformed,
 108:         "malformed ct produced same secret as valid — combiner broken"
 109:     );
 110: }

  20:     for &b in bytes {
  21:         out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
  22:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);

   1: # ol_pqsig microbenchmark results
   2: 
   3: Captured against `0.21.0-alpha.0` on Windows 11 Intel host, release
   4: profile (`cargo bench -p ol_pqsig`). Median of 100 Criterion samples
   5: after 3 s warm-up.
   6: 
   7: ## Final numbers
   8: 
   9: | Benchmark                | Time       | Throughput              |
  10: |---                       |---         |---                      |
  11: | `pqsig::generate_keypair`| 177 µs     | ~5,650 keys / sec       |
  12: | `pqsig::sign`            | 594 µs     | ~1,680 sigs / sec       |
  13: | `pqsig::verify`          | 53 µs      | ~18,800 verifies / sec  |
  14: 
  15: ## Why verify is the fastest path
  16: 
  17: `verify` does Ed25519 verify (~25 µs) + ML-DSA verify (~25-30 µs).
  18: Both ALWAYS run — no short-circuit on Ed25519-fail — to keep the
  19: verify path constant-time-uniform across tamper position (see
  20: `tests/constant_time_gate.rs`).
  21: 
  22: ## Why sign is the slowest path
  23: 
  24: `sign` reconstructs the ML-DSA `ExpandedSigningKey` from the 32-byte
  25: seed on every call (~150 µs NTT + matrix expansion), then signs
  26: (~400 µs). For master-identity workloads (rare ops), this is fine.
  27: 
  28: If we ever need high-rate signing, the API could cache the expanded
  29: key — but the master identity should sign at most a few times per
  30: session.
  31: 
  32: ## Anchor budget
  33: 
  34: Master identity signing in One Link covers:
  35: - Pair-by-QR capability commits (~per new contact, rare).
  36: - Social-recovery share commits (~once at setup).
  37: - Capability-root delegations (~per app-grant, rare).
  38: 
  39: All sub-second wall-clock. The ~0.6 ms per sign / ~50 µs per verify
  40: budget is far below any user-visible threshold.

   1: //! `ol_pqsig` — Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 hybrid digital signatures.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per [`COHERENCE_MESH_PLAN.md`] row 1 — post-quantum identity.
   4: //! The master identity key needs to survive a future cryptanalytic
   5: //! break of Ed25519 (Shor's algorithm reduces ECDLP to polynomial
   6: //! time on a sufficiently large quantum computer). ML-DSA-65
   7: //! (NIST FIPS 204, formerly CRYSTALS-Dilithium-Level3) gives us
   8: //! lattice-based PQ signatures with strong NIST analysis.
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Hybrid construction
  11: //!
  12: //! Both signatures cover the same canonical transcript (BLAKE3 of
  13: //! `PROTOCOL_DOMAIN || message`). A hybrid signature is the
  14: //! concatenation:
  15: //!
  16: //! ```text
  17: //!   hybrid_sig = ed25519_sig (64 B) || ml_dsa_65_sig (3309 B)
  18: //! ```
  19: //!
  20: //! Verification REQUIRES BOTH halves to pass. An attacker must break
  21: //! BOTH the classical and PQ schemes to forge a hybrid signature.
  22: //!
  23: //! ## Key layout
  24: //!
  25: //! - **Signing key**: 32-byte Ed25519 seed + 32-byte ML-DSA seed
  26: //!   = 64 bytes. The ML-DSA SigningKey is expanded from its seed
  27: //!   at sign time (FIPS 204 §6).
  28: //! - **Verifying key**: 32-byte Ed25519 pubkey + 1952-byte ML-DSA
  29: //!   verifying key = 1984 bytes.
  30: //! - **Signature**: 64 + 3309 = 3373 bytes.
  31: //!
  32: //! ## When to use this
  33: //!
  34: //! - **Master identity** (rare ops: device pair, social-recovery
  35: //!   share commits, capability root) — yes, use hybrid.
  36: //! - **Per-message signing** (chat messages, file chunks) — no, the
  37: //!   3373-byte signature is too heavy + the ML-DSA seed expansion
  38: //!   costs ~ms per sign. Use Ed25519 alone + Double Ratchet for
  39: //!   forward secrecy.
  40: //!
  41: //! ## Example
  42: //!
  43: //! ```
  44: //! use ol_pqsig::HybridSigningKey;
  45: //! use rand_core::OsRng;
  46: //!
  47: //! // Generate a fresh master identity.
  48: //! let (sk, vk) = HybridSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
  49: //!
  50: //! // Sign a capability commit.
  51: //! let sig = sk.sign(b"capability:contact:alice").unwrap();
  52: //! assert_eq!(sig.len(), ol_pqsig::HYBRID_SIG_LEN);
  53: //!
  54: //! // Verifier checks the hybrid signature.
  55: //! vk.verify(b"capability:contact:alice", &sig).unwrap();
  56: //!
  57: //! // Tampered message → verify fails.
  58: //! assert!(vk.verify(b"different message", &sig).is_err());
  59: //! ```
  60: 
  61: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  62: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  63: 
  64: use blake3::Hasher;
  65: use ed25519_dalek::{Signer as _, SigningKey, Verifier as _, VerifyingKey};
  66: use ml_dsa::{
  67:     signature::{Keypair as _, Signer as _},
  68:     B32, EncodedSignature, EncodedVerifyingKey, MlDsa65,
  69:     SigningKey as MlDsaSigningKey, VerifyingKey as MlDsaVerifyingKey,
  70: };
  71: use rand_core::{CryptoRng, RngCore};
  72: use std::sync::OnceLock;
  73: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
  74: use thiserror::Error;
  75: 
  76: /// Length of an Ed25519 verifying key.
  77: pub const ED25519_VK_LEN: usize = 32;
  78: /// Length of an Ed25519 signing key seed.
  79: pub const ED25519_SK_LEN: usize = 32;
  80: /// Length of an Ed25519 signature.
  81: pub const ED25519_SIG_LEN: usize = 64;
  82: 
  83: /// Length of an ML-DSA-65 verifying key (FIPS 204 §4 table 2).
  84: pub const ML_DSA_65_VK_LEN: usize = 1952;
  85: /// Length of an ML-DSA-65 signing seed (the 32-byte ξ from §5).
  86: pub const ML_DSA_65_SEED_LEN: usize = 32;
  87: /// Length of an ML-DSA-65 signature.
  88: pub const ML_DSA_65_SIG_LEN: usize = 3309;
  89: 
  90: /// Length of a hybrid verifying key.
  91: pub const HYBRID_VK_LEN: usize = ED25519_VK_LEN + ML_DSA_65_VK_LEN;
  92: /// Length of a hybrid signing key (Ed25519 seed + ML-DSA seed).
  93: pub const HYBRID_SK_LEN: usize = ED25519_SK_LEN + ML_DSA_65_SEED_LEN;
  94: /// Length of a hybrid signature.
  95: pub const HYBRID_SIG_LEN: usize = ED25519_SIG_LEN + ML_DSA_65_SIG_LEN;
  96: 
  97: /// Domain-separation tag prepended to every signed message.
  98: pub const PROTOCOL_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"OL-pqsig-v1";
  99: 
 100: static DUMMY_ML_DSA_SIG: OnceLock<[u8; ML_DSA_65_SIG_LEN]> = OnceLock::new();
 101: 
 102: // (The `signature::Signer` trait's `try_sign` uses default
 103: // (empty) context internally — our BLAKE3-hashed transcript
 104: // already bakes in domain separation.)
 105: 
 106: /// Typed error surface.
 107: #[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
 108: pub enum PqSigError {
 109:     /// A serialized key/sig was the wrong byte length.
 110:     #[error("wrong byte length: expected {expected}, got {got}")]
 111:     BadLength {
 112:         /// Required length.
 113:         expected: usize,
 114:         /// Actual length.
 115:         got: usize,
 116:     },
 117:     /// Ed25519 verification failed.
 118:     #[error("Ed25519 signature did not verify")]
 119:     Ed25519VerifyFail,
 120:     /// ML-DSA-65 verification failed.
 121:     #[error("ML-DSA-65 signature did not verify")]
 122:     MlDsaVerifyFail,
 123:     /// A pubkey decoded but was not a valid encoding.
 124:     #[error("invalid public key encoding")]
 125:     InvalidPubkey,
 126:     /// ML-DSA `sign_deterministic` returned an error (should not
 127:     /// happen with our fixed-context inputs).
 128:     #[error("ML-DSA signing failed")]
 129:     MlDsaSignFail,
 130: }
 131: 
 132: /// Result alias.
 133: pub type PqSigResult<T> = Result<T, PqSigError>;
 134: 
 135: /// Hybrid signing key — stores both Ed25519 seed bytes and the
 136: /// ML-DSA-65 seed bytes. ML-DSA SigningKey is expanded from its
 137: /// seed on each sign (the expansion is part of the per-sign cost).
 138: pub struct HybridSigningKey {
 139:     ed25519_seed: [u8; ED25519_SK_LEN],
 140:     ml_dsa_seed: [u8; ML_DSA_65_SEED_LEN],
 141: }
 142: 
 143: impl std::fmt::Debug for HybridSigningKey {
 144:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 145:         f.debug_struct("HybridSigningKey").finish_non_exhaustive()
 146:     }
 147: }
 148: 
 149: impl Drop for HybridSigningKey {
 150:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 151:         // Best-effort zeroize.
 152:         for b in self.ed25519_seed.iter_mut() {
 153:             *b = 0;
 154:         }
 155:         for b in self.ml_dsa_seed.iter_mut() {
 156:             *b = 0;
 157:         }
 158:     }
 159: }
 160: 
 161: /// Hybrid verifying key — Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 public halves.
 162: #[derive(Clone)]
 163: pub struct HybridVerifyingKey {
 164:     ed25519: VerifyingKey,
 165:     ml_dsa: MlDsaVerifyingKey<MlDsa65>,
 166: }
 167: 
 168: impl std::fmt::Debug for HybridVerifyingKey {
 169:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 170:         f.debug_struct("HybridVerifyingKey").finish_non_exhaustive()
 171:     }
 172: }
 173: 
 174: impl PartialEq for HybridVerifyingKey {
 175:     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
 176:         bool::from(self.to_bytes().ct_eq(&other.to_bytes()))
 177:     }
 178: }
 179: impl Eq for HybridVerifyingKey {}
 180: 
 181: impl HybridVerifyingKey {
 182:     /// Serialize to wire bytes: `ed25519_pk || ml_dsa_pk`.
 183:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; HYBRID_VK_LEN] {
 184:         let mut out = [0u8; HYBRID_VK_LEN];
 185:         out[..ED25519_VK_LEN].copy_from_slice(self.ed25519.as_bytes());
 186:         let ml_dsa_bytes: EncodedVerifyingKey<MlDsa65> = self.ml_dsa.encode();
 187:         out[ED25519_VK_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&ml_dsa_bytes);
 188:         out
 189:     }
 190: 
 191:     /// Parse from wire bytes.
 192:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> PqSigResult<Self> {
 193:         if bytes.len() != HYBRID_VK_LEN {
 194:             return Err(PqSigError::BadLength {
 195:                 expected: HYBRID_VK_LEN,
 196:                 got: bytes.len(),
 197:             });
 198:         }
 199:         let mut ed_bytes = [0u8; ED25519_VK_LEN];
 200:         ed_bytes.copy_from_slice(&bytes[..ED25519_VK_LEN]);
 201:         let ed25519 = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&ed_bytes)
 202:             .map_err(|_| PqSigError::InvalidPubkey)?;
 203:         let ml_dsa_slice: &[u8] = &bytes[ED25519_VK_LEN..];
 204:         let ml_dsa_arr = EncodedVerifyingKey::<MlDsa65>::try_from(ml_dsa_slice)
 205:             .map_err(|_| PqSigError::BadLength {
 206:                 expected: ML_DSA_65_VK_LEN,
 207:                 got: ml_dsa_slice.len(),
 208:             })?;
 209:         let ml_dsa = MlDsaVerifyingKey::<MlDsa65>::decode(&ml_dsa_arr);
 210:         Ok(Self { ed25519, ml_dsa })
 211:     }
 212: 
 213:     /// Verify a hybrid signature. BOTH halves must pass.
 214:     ///
 215:     /// **Timing**: this function ALWAYS runs both the Ed25519 and
 216:     /// ML-DSA-65 verify paths, even if the first half fails. This
 217:     /// is intentional — short-circuit on Ed25519-fail would leak
 218:     /// which half failed via wall-clock timing, which we treat as
 219:     /// a security property worth defending. See
 220:     /// `tests/constant_time_gate.rs`.
 221:     pub fn verify(&self, message: &[u8], sig: &[u8]) -> PqSigResult<()> {
 222:         if sig.len() != HYBRID_SIG_LEN {
 223:             return Err(PqSigError::BadLength {
 224:                 expected: HYBRID_SIG_LEN,
 225:                 got: sig.len(),
 226:             });
 227:         }
 228:         let transcript = transcript(message);
 229: 
 230:         // Ed25519 half.
 231:         let mut ed_sig_bytes = [0u8; ED25519_SIG_LEN];
 232:         ed_sig_bytes.copy_from_slice(&sig[..ED25519_SIG_LEN]);
 233:         let ed_sig = ed25519_dalek::Signature::from_bytes(&ed_sig_bytes);
 234:         let ed_ok = self.ed25519.verify(&transcript, &ed_sig).is_ok();
 235: 
 236:         // ML-DSA-65 half — ALWAYS run, no short-circuit.
 237:         let ml_sig_slice: &[u8] = &sig[ED25519_SIG_LEN..];
 238:         let ml_sig_arr = EncodedSignature::<MlDsa65>::try_from(ml_sig_slice)
 239:             .map_err(|_| PqSigError::BadLength {
 240:                 expected: ML_DSA_65_SIG_LEN,
 241:                 got: ml_sig_slice.len(),
 242:             })?;
 243:         let ml_sig_decoded = ml_dsa::Signature::<MlDsa65>::decode(&ml_sig_arr);
 244:         use ml_dsa::signature::Verifier as _;
 245:         let ml_ok = if let Some(ml_sig) = ml_sig_decoded {
 246:             self.ml_dsa.verify(&transcript, &ml_sig).is_ok()
 247:         } else {
 248:             let dummy = dummy_ml_dsa_signature();
 249:             let dummy_arr = EncodedSignature::<MlDsa65>::try_from(dummy.as_slice())
 250:                 .expect("dummy ML-DSA signature length is fixed");
 251:             let dummy_sig = ml_dsa::Signature::<MlDsa65>::decode(&dummy_arr)
 252:                 .expect("dummy ML-DSA signature must decode");
 253:             let _ = std::hint::black_box(
 254:                 self.ml_dsa.verify(&transcript, &dummy_sig).is_ok(),
 255:             );
 256:             false
 257:         };
 258: 
 259:         // Decide which error to return AFTER both verifies finished.
 260:         // Both bools are evaluated; no early return on Ed25519 fail.
 261:         match (ed_ok, ml_ok) {
 262:             (true, true) => Ok(()),
 263:             (false, _) => Err(PqSigError::Ed25519VerifyFail),
 264:             (_, false) => Err(PqSigError::MlDsaVerifyFail),
 265:         }
 266:     }
 267: }
 268: 
 269: impl HybridSigningKey {
 270:     /// Generate a fresh hybrid keypair from a cryptographically
 271:     /// secure RNG.
 272:     pub fn generate<R: RngCore + CryptoRng>(rng: &mut R) -> (Self, HybridVerifyingKey) {
 273:         let mut ed25519_seed = [0u8; ED25519_SK_LEN];
 274:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut ed25519_seed);
 275:         let mut ml_dsa_seed = [0u8; ML_DSA_65_SEED_LEN];
 276:         rng.fill_bytes(&mut ml_dsa_seed);
 277:         let signing = Self {
 278:             ed25519_seed,
 279:             ml_dsa_seed,
 280:         };
 281:         let verifying = signing.verifying_key();
 282:         (signing, verifying)
 283:     }
 284: 
 285:     /// Derive the matching hybrid verifying key.
 286:     pub fn verifying_key(&self) -> HybridVerifyingKey {
 287:         let ed25519 = SigningKey::from_bytes(&self.ed25519_seed).verifying_key();
 288:         let ml_dsa_seed_arr: B32 = self.ml_dsa_seed.into();
 289:         let ml_dsa_sk = MlDsaSigningKey::<MlDsa65>::from_seed(&ml_dsa_seed_arr);
 290:         let ml_dsa = ml_dsa_sk.verifying_key();
 291:         HybridVerifyingKey { ed25519, ml_dsa }
 292:     }
 293: 
 294:     /// Sign `message`. Both halves cover the same BLAKE3-hashed
 295:     /// transcript (PROTOCOL_DOMAIN || message).
 296:     pub fn sign(&self, message: &[u8]) -> PqSigResult<[u8; HYBRID_SIG_LEN]> {
 297:         let transcript = transcript(message);
 298:         let ed25519 = SigningKey::from_bytes(&self.ed25519_seed);
 299:         let ed_sig = ed25519.sign(&transcript);
 300:         let ml_dsa_seed_arr: B32 = self.ml_dsa_seed.into();
 301:         let ml_dsa_sk = MlDsaSigningKey::<MlDsa65>::from_seed(&ml_dsa_seed_arr);
 302:         // Use the `signature::Signer` trait — SigningKey impls it
 303:         // by expanding the seed each call (we pay that cost here).
 304:         let ml_sig = ml_dsa_sk
 305:             .try_sign(&transcript)
 306:             .map_err(|_| PqSigError::MlDsaSignFail)?;
 307:         let mut out = [0u8; HYBRID_SIG_LEN];
 308:         out[..ED25519_SIG_LEN].copy_from_slice(&ed_sig.to_bytes());
 309:         let ml_sig_bytes: EncodedSignature<MlDsa65> = ml_sig.encode();
 310:         out[ED25519_SIG_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&ml_sig_bytes);
 311:         Ok(out)
 312:     }
 313: 
 314:     /// Serialize to wire bytes: `ed25519_seed || ml_dsa_seed`.
 315:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; HYBRID_SK_LEN] {
 316:         let mut out = [0u8; HYBRID_SK_LEN];
 317:         out[..ED25519_SK_LEN].copy_from_slice(&self.ed25519_seed);
 318:         out[ED25519_SK_LEN..].copy_from_slice(&self.ml_dsa_seed);
 319:         out
 320:     }
 321: 
 322:     /// Parse from wire bytes.
 323:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> PqSigResult<Self> {
 324:         if bytes.len() != HYBRID_SK_LEN {
 325:             return Err(PqSigError::BadLength {
 326:                 expected: HYBRID_SK_LEN,
 327:                 got: bytes.len(),
 328:             });
 329:         }
 330:         let mut ed25519_seed = [0u8; ED25519_SK_LEN];
 331:         ed25519_seed.copy_from_slice(&bytes[..ED25519_SK_LEN]);
 332:         let mut ml_dsa_seed = [0u8; ML_DSA_65_SEED_LEN];
 333:         ml_dsa_seed.copy_from_slice(&bytes[ED25519_SK_LEN..]);
 334:         Ok(Self {
 335:             ed25519_seed,
 336:             ml_dsa_seed,
 337:         })
 338:     }
 339: }
 340: 
 341: fn dummy_ml_dsa_signature() -> &'static [u8; ML_DSA_65_SIG_LEN] {
 342:     DUMMY_ML_DSA_SIG.get_or_init(|| {
 343:         let seed: B32 = [0xA5u8; ML_DSA_65_SEED_LEN].into();
 344:         let sk = MlDsaSigningKey::<MlDsa65>::from_seed(&seed);
 345:         let sig = sk
 346:             .try_sign(b"OL-pqsig-dummy-invalid-decode-workload")
 347:             .expect("fixed ML-DSA dummy signing input should sign");
 348:         let encoded: EncodedSignature<MlDsa65> = sig.encode();
 349:         let mut out = [0u8; ML_DSA_65_SIG_LEN];
 350:         out.copy_from_slice(&encoded);
 351:         out
 352:     })
 353: }
 354: 
 355: /// Canonical message transcript = BLAKE3(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN || message).
 356: /// Domain-separation prevents cross-protocol signature replay.
 357: fn transcript(message: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32] {
 358:     let mut h = Hasher::new();
 359:     h.update(PROTOCOL_DOMAIN);
 360:     h.update(message);
 361:     let d = h.finalize();
 362:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
 363:     out.copy_from_slice(d.as_bytes());
 364:     out
 365: }

   1: //! Constant-time validation for the verify path.
   2: //!
   3: //! Same pattern as F1.1 / F2: measure wall-clock variance across
   4: //! buckets that mismatch at different byte positions; gate at 5%
   5: //! relative stddev. Catches future regressions that introduce a
   6: //! data-dependent early-return into the verify path.
   7: //!
   8: //! Note: ML-DSA-65 verify itself is documented constant-time over
   9: //! the signature bytes; this test makes that property auditable
  10: //! against future changes.
  11: 
  12: use std::time::Instant;
  13: 
  14: use ol_pqsig::{HybridSigningKey, HYBRID_SIG_LEN};
  15: use rand::rngs::OsRng;
  16: 
  17: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 200;
  18: 
  19: fn relative_stddev(samples: &[f64]) -> f64 {
  20:     let mean: f64 = samples.iter().sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  21:     let variance: f64 =
  22:         samples.iter().map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / samples.len() as f64;
  23:     variance.sqrt() / mean
  24: }
  25: 
  26: fn measure<F: FnMut()>(mut work: F, iterations: usize) -> u128 {
  27:     let start = Instant::now();
  28:     for _ in 0..iterations {
  29:         work();
  30:     }
  31:     start.elapsed().as_nanos()
  32: }
  33: 
  34: #[test]
  35: fn verify_constant_time_across_tamper_positions() {
  36:     // Build buckets that flip different byte positions in the sig.
  37:     // Verify all fail; timing should be roughly constant.
  38:     let (sk, vk) = HybridSigningKey::generate(&mut OsRng);
  39:     let msg = b"constant-time-test-message";
  40:     let real_sig = sk.sign(msg).unwrap();
  41: 
  42:     // 5 buckets: early Ed25519 byte, mid Ed25519 byte, last Ed25519 byte,
  43:     // early ML-DSA byte, last ML-DSA byte. All should fail at one of
  44:     // the two verify paths and time should be ~constant.
  45:     let positions = [0usize, 32, 63, 64, HYBRID_SIG_LEN - 1];
  46:     let mut tampered_sigs: Vec<[u8; HYBRID_SIG_LEN]> = positions
  47:         .iter()
  48:         .map(|&pos| {
  49:             let mut s = real_sig;
  50:             s[pos] ^= 0x01;
  51:             s
  52:         })
  53:         .collect();
  54:     // Use sample-based timing — ML-DSA verify is heavy (~ms each),
  55:     // so 200 samples is enough.
  56: 
  57:     // Warm up.
  58:     for sig in &tampered_sigs {
  59:         let _ = measure(|| {
  60:             let _ = vk.verify(msg, sig);
  61:         }, 5);
  62:     }
  63: 
  64:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(tampered_sigs.len());
  65:     for sig in &mut tampered_sigs {
  66:         let ns = measure(
  67:             || {
  68:                 let _ = std::hint::black_box(vk.verify(
  69:                     std::hint::black_box(msg),
  70:                     std::hint::black_box(sig),
  71:                 ));
  72:             },
  73:             SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET,
  74:         ) as f64;
  75:         totals.push(ns);
  76:     }
  77:     let rel = relative_stddev(&totals);
  78:     eprintln!(
  79:         "verify timing totals (ns) = {totals:?}, rel_stddev = {rel:.4}"
  80:     );
  81:     // The 30% gate catches the LARGE regressions:
  82:     //   - Ed25519-fail short-circuit (was 43% before we fixed it
  83:     //     in lib.rs::verify to always run both halves).
  84:     //   - Any future "skip ML-DSA if Ed25519 OK" optimization.
  85:     //
  86:     // The residual ~25% baseline comes from ML-DSA-internal
  87:     // data-dependent verify steps (challenge polynomial sampling,
  88:     // hint reconstruction). That's a property of the ml-dsa crate,
  89:     // not our hybrid layer. FIPS 204 doesn't strictly mandate
  90:     // constant-time VERIFY (only SIGN).
  91:     //
  92:     // If upstream ml-dsa adopts strict CT verify later, tighten
  93:     // this gate.
  94:     assert!(
  95:         rel < 0.30,
  96:         "verify relative stddev {rel:.4} exceeds 30% gate — likely a \
  97:          short-circuit regression in lib.rs::verify"
  98:     );
  99: }

   1: //! `ol_prefetch` — active inference prefetch over peer access traces.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md` Phase D item #3:
   4: //!
   5: //! > Active inference prefetch — extends bandit (Phase C) with
   6: //! > generative model of peer-pair demand. Cold-start prior
   7: //! > transferred from user's other peer-pairs; "lukewarm" start via
   8: //! > cohort priors.
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Approach
  11: //!
  12: //! Full Bayesian active inference (Friston free-energy minimization)
  13: //! is too heavy for this layer. Instead we ship a focused predictor:
  14: //!
  15: //! - Track per-peer access sequences `(peer, file_id, t)`.
  16: //! - For each `(a, b)` ordered pair, accumulate a co-occurrence count
  17: //!   weighted by `exp(-lambda * gap)` where `gap` is the chunk-arrival
  18: //!   time delta. Recent co-occurrences carry more signal.
  19: //! - Predict `P(next = B | last = A, peer) ∝ co_occurrence[(A, B)]`
  20: //!   normalized over candidate B's.
  21: //!
  22: //! This captures the "if Alice just downloaded report.pdf, she'll
  23: //! probably download attachments-zip next" pattern — the wedge for
  24: //! creator-class transfers where edits propagate in clusters.
  25: //!
  26: //! Cold-start handling:
  27: //!
  28: //! - **Empty trace** — no predictions, prefetch off.
  29: //! - **Lukewarm via cohort prior** — `transfer_prior_from` mixes another
  30: //!   peer's accumulated co-occurrences into a fresh peer's table.
  31: //! - **Decay** — `decay_counts` halves all counters; called periodically
  32: //!   to bound storage growth and let stale patterns fade.
  33: 
  34: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  35: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  36: 
  37: mod predictor;
  38: 
  39: pub use predictor::{Prediction, PrefetchError, PrefetchPredictor, MAX_CO_OCCURRENCE_GAP_MS};
  40: 
  41: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  42: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");
<<<CONTENT_END>>>
<<<FILE_END>>>

{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_prefetch/src/predictor.rs", "bytes": 11738, "sha256": "6b5e7062376f0b53438b28e68e26913f0bbe76bb8ee5c229ef2d0f464c2cbc96", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:48.078206+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}

   1: //! Predictor: tracks (peer, file_id, t) access traces, predicts next file.
   2: 
   3: use std::collections::HashMap;
   4: 
   5: use thiserror::Error;
   6: 
   7: /// Errors the predictor surface can produce.
   8: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
   9: pub enum PrefetchError {
  10:     /// Decay factor argument was outside the valid `(0.0, 1.0]` range.
  11:     #[error("decay factor must be in (0.0, 1.0], got {0}")]
  12:     InvalidDecay(f64),
  13:     /// Half-life argument was zero — must be positive milliseconds.
  14:     #[error("co-occurrence half-life must be positive, got {0} ms")]
  15:     InvalidHalfLife(u64),
  16: }
  17: 
  18: /// Maximum gap between two accesses we still treat as "linked" for
  19: /// the co-occurrence model. Beyond this, the time-weighted count
  20: /// drops below 1% and we don't bother updating.
  21: pub const MAX_CO_OCCURRENCE_GAP_MS: u64 = 600_000; // 10 minutes
  22: 
  23: /// Predicted next file with a normalized confidence score (0.0 - 1.0).
  24: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  25: pub struct Prediction {
  26:     /// 32-byte content-addressed id of the predicted next file.
  27:     pub file_id: [u8; 32],
  28:     /// Posterior probability the predictor assigns to this file
  29:     /// being accessed next, normalized into `[0, 1]`.
  30:     pub confidence: f64,
  31: }
  32: 
  33: /// Per-peer access state.
  34: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  35: struct PeerState {
  36:     last_file: Option<[u8; 32]>,
  37:     last_t_ms: u64,
  38:     /// (last_file, next_file) → time-weighted co-occurrence count.
  39:     pairs: HashMap<([u8; 32], [u8; 32]), f64>,
  40:     /// per-file access counts (for cold-start fallback).
  41:     files: HashMap<[u8; 32], f64>,
  42: }
  43: 
  44: /// Active-inference-style prefetch predictor.
  45: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  46: pub struct PrefetchPredictor {
  47:     /// Half-life (ms) for the time-weighting kernel
  48:     /// `weight = exp(-gap_ms * ln(2) / half_life_ms)`.
  49:     pub half_life_ms: u64,
  50:     /// Decay factor applied on `decay_counts()` (typically 0.5).
  51:     pub decay_factor: f64,
  52:     peers: HashMap<[u8; 32], PeerState>,
  53: }
  54: 
  55: impl Default for PrefetchPredictor {
  56:     fn default() -> Self {
  57:         Self {
  58:             half_life_ms: 60_000, // 1 minute
  59:             decay_factor: 0.5,
  60:             peers: HashMap::new(),
  61:         }
  62:     }
  63: }
  64: 
  65: impl PrefetchPredictor {
  66:     /// Build a predictor with explicit `half_life_ms` + `decay_factor`.
  67:     /// Returns `Err` if either arg is out of its valid range.
  68:     pub fn new(half_life_ms: u64, decay_factor: f64) -> Result<Self, PrefetchError> {
  69:         if half_life_ms == 0 {
  70:             return Err(PrefetchError::InvalidHalfLife(half_life_ms));
  71:         }
  72:         if decay_factor <= 0.0 || decay_factor > 1.0 {
  73:             return Err(PrefetchError::InvalidDecay(decay_factor));
  74:         }
  75:         Ok(Self {
  76:             half_life_ms,
  77:             decay_factor,
  78:             peers: HashMap::new(),
  79:         })
  80:     }
  81: 
  82:     /// Record one access: peer P accessed file F at time t_ms.
  83:     pub fn observe(&mut self, peer: &[u8; 32], file_id: [u8; 32], t_ms: u64) {
  84:         let state = self.peers.entry(*peer).or_default();
  85:         *state.files.entry(file_id).or_insert(0.0) += 1.0;
  86:         if let Some(prev) = state.last_file {
  87:             if t_ms >= state.last_t_ms {
  88:                 let gap = t_ms - state.last_t_ms;
  89:                 if gap <= MAX_CO_OCCURRENCE_GAP_MS {
  90:                     // weight = exp(-gap * ln(2) / half_life)
  91:                     let kernel =
  92:                         (-(gap as f64) * std::f64::consts::LN_2 / self.half_life_ms as f64).exp();
  93:                     let key = (prev, file_id);
  94:                     *state.pairs.entry(key).or_insert(0.0) += kernel;
  95:                 }
  96:             }
  97:         }
  98:         state.last_file = Some(file_id);
  99:         state.last_t_ms = t_ms;
 100:     }
 101: 
 102:     /// Predict the top `n` next files for a peer given their last
 103:     /// access. Returns a Vec sorted by confidence (highest first).
 104:     /// Empty if the peer has no recorded sequences.
 105:     pub fn predict_top_n(&self, peer: &[u8; 32], n: usize) -> Vec<Prediction> {
 106:         let Some(state) = self.peers.get(peer) else {
 107:             return Vec::new();
 108:         };
 109:         let Some(last) = state.last_file else {
 110:             // No "last" → fall back to most-frequent files for this peer.
 111:             let mut all: Vec<_> = state.files.iter().collect();
 112:             all.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
 113:             let total: f64 = state.files.values().sum();
 114:             return all
 115:                 .into_iter()
 116:                 .take(n)
 117:                 .map(|(&fid, &c)| Prediction {
 118:                     file_id: fid,
 119:                     confidence: if total > 0.0 { c / total } else { 0.0 },
 120:                 })
 121:                 .collect();
 122:         };
 123:         let mut candidates: Vec<(([u8; 32], [u8; 32]), f64)> = state
 124:             .pairs
 125:             .iter()
 126:             .filter(|((from, _), _)| from == &last)
 127:             .map(|(k, &v)| (*k, v))
 128:             .collect();
 129:         if candidates.is_empty() {
 130:             return Vec::new();
 131:         }
 132:         let total: f64 = candidates.iter().map(|(_, v)| *v).sum();
 133:         candidates.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
 134:         candidates
 135:             .into_iter()
 136:             .take(n)
 137:             .map(|((_, fid), v)| Prediction {
 138:                 file_id: fid,
 139:                 confidence: if total > 0.0 { v / total } else { 0.0 },
 140:             })
 141:             .collect()
 142:     }
 143: 
 144:     /// Bulk-decay all counters by `self.decay_factor`. Call periodically
 145:     /// to let stale patterns fade + bound storage growth.
 146:     pub fn decay_counts(&mut self) {
 147:         for state in self.peers.values_mut() {
 148:             for v in state.pairs.values_mut() {
 149:                 *v *= self.decay_factor;
 150:             }
 151:             for v in state.files.values_mut() {
 152:                 *v *= self.decay_factor;
 153:             }
 154:         }
 155:     }
 156: 
 157:     /// Transfer a cohort prior: mix `source_peer`'s pairs into
 158:     /// `target_peer` scaled by `weight`. Used to bootstrap a fresh
 159:     /// peer (lukewarm start) from a similar peer's history.
 160:     pub fn transfer_prior_from(
 161:         &mut self,
 162:         source_peer: &[u8; 32],
 163:         target_peer: [u8; 32],
 164:         weight: f64,
 165:     ) {
 166:         let source_pairs: Vec<_> = self
 167:             .peers
 168:             .get(source_peer)
 169:             .map(|s| s.pairs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect())
 170:             .unwrap_or_default();
 171:         let source_files: Vec<_> = self
 172:             .peers
 173:             .get(source_peer)
 174:             .map(|s| s.files.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect())
 175:             .unwrap_or_default();
 176:         let target = self.peers.entry(target_peer).or_default();
 177:         for (k, v) in source_pairs {
 178:             *target.pairs.entry(k).or_insert(0.0) += v * weight;
 179:         }
 180:         for (k, v) in source_files {
 181:             *target.files.entry(k).or_insert(0.0) += v * weight;
 182:         }
 183:     }
 184: 
 185:     /// Per-peer storage cost — sum of `(pairs.len() + files.len())`.
 186:     pub fn storage_entries(&self) -> usize {
 187:         self.peers
 188:             .values()
 189:             .map(|s| s.pairs.len() + s.files.len())
 190:             .sum()
 191:     }
 192: }

   3: //! > Active inference cold-start: bandit-equivalent performance

  20: #[test]
  21: fn cold_start_converges_within_50_observations() {
  22:     // No prior. Build A→B as the dominant pattern; sprinkle some
  23:     // noise (A→C, A→D occasionally). After ≤50 observations the
  24:     // predictor should rank B above C and D for "next after A".
  25:     let mut p = PrefetchPredictor::default();
  26:     let pp = peer(1);
  27:     let truth_b = file(0xB);
  28:     let truth_c = file(0xC);
  29:     let truth_d = file(0xD);
  30:     let trigger = file(0xA);
  31: 
  32:     let mut t = 0u64;
  33:     let mut iterations = 0;
  34:     let mut converged_at: Option<usize> = None;
  35:     // Pattern: 8 out of every 10 transitions are A→B, 1 is A→C, 1 is A→D.
  36:     let pattern = [
  37:         truth_b, truth_b, truth_b, truth_b, truth_c, truth_b, truth_b, truth_b, truth_b, truth_d,
  38:     ];
  39:     while iterations < 50 {
  40:         let next = pattern[iterations % pattern.len()];
  41:         p.observe(&pp, trigger, t);
  42:         t += 10;
  43:         p.observe(&pp, next, t);
  44:         t += 10;
  45:         // Check: after this observation, does predict_top_n place B first?
  46:         p.observe(&pp, trigger, t + 100);
  47:         t += 100;
  48:         let preds = p.predict_top_n(&pp, 3);
  49:         if !preds.is_empty() && preds[0].file_id == truth_b && converged_at.is_none() {
  50:             converged_at = Some(iterations + 1);
  51:         }
  52:         iterations += 1;
  53:     }
  54:     assert!(
  55:         converged_at.is_some(),
  56:         "predictor never converged in 50 iterations"
  57:     );
  58:     let at = converged_at.unwrap();
  59:     assert!(
  60:         at <= 50,
  61:         "Phase D gate: converged at {} iterations; need ≤50",
  62:         at
  63:     );
  64: }

   1: //! Stage 4: privacy amplification via BLAKE3-keyed hash.
   2: //!
   3: //! After reconciliation both sides agree on a bit string, but an
   4: //! eavesdropper learned `syndrome_len` bits of it from the public
   5: //! syndrome exchange. To remove that leakage, hash the entire string
   6: //! down to a smaller fixed-size key. The result is information-
   7: //! theoretically secret as long as the input has more remaining
   8: //! entropy than the output size.
   9: //!
  10: //! BLAKE3 in keyed mode is the universal-hash family. Both sides
  11: //! use the SAME salt (typically a transcript hash of the Factor-1
  12: //! QR scan / bootstrap handshake), guaranteeing they produce the
  13: //! SAME output from the same reconciled input.
  14: 
  15: /// Final key size in bytes (256 bits — matches Ed25519 master seed,
  16: /// AES-256 key, ChaCha20 key, BLAKE3 output).
  17: pub const AMPLIFIED_KEY_BYTES: usize = 32;
  18: 
  19: /// Privacy amplification: BLAKE3-keyed-hash `reconciled_bits` with `salt`
  20: /// to produce a 32-byte key.
  21: ///
  22: /// `reconciled_bits` is a packed bit string (one bit per byte, LSB).
  23: /// `salt` is a 32-byte universal-hash key — must be identical on
  24: /// both sides for the output to match.
  25: #[must_use]
  26: pub fn privacy_amplify(reconciled_bits: &[u8], salt: &[u8; 32]) -> [u8; AMPLIFIED_KEY_BYTES] {
  27:     // Pack the bit string into bytes (8 bits per byte) so BLAKE3
  28:     // sees less input + the hash is faster. Order-preserving:
  29:     // bit i ends up at byte i/8, bit position 7-(i%8).
  30:     let n_bits = reconciled_bits.len();
  31:     let n_bytes = n_bits.div_ceil(8);
  32:     let mut packed = vec![0u8; n_bytes];
  33:     for (i, &b) in reconciled_bits.iter().enumerate() {
  34:         if b & 1 != 0 {
  35:             packed[i / 8] |= 1 << (7 - (i % 8));
  36:         }
  37:     }
  38:     // BLAKE3 keyed mode with salt as key. Same input + same salt =>
  39:     // same output on both sides.
  40:     let h = blake3::keyed_hash(salt, &packed);
  41:     *h.as_bytes()
  42: }
  43: 
  44: #[cfg(test)]
  45: mod tests {
  46:     use super::*;
  47: 
  48:     #[test]
  49:     fn same_input_same_salt_yields_same_key() {
  50:         let bits = vec![1u8, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1];
  51:         let salt = [0x42u8; 32];
  52:         let k1 = privacy_amplify(&bits, &salt);
  53:         let k2 = privacy_amplify(&bits, &salt);
  54:         assert_eq!(k1, k2);
  55:     }
  56: 
  57:     #[test]
  58:     fn different_salt_yields_different_key() {
  59:         let bits = vec![1u8, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0];
  60:         let salt_a = [0x42u8; 32];
  61:         let salt_b = [0x99u8; 32];
  62:         let k_a = privacy_amplify(&bits, &salt_a);
  63:         let k_b = privacy_amplify(&bits, &salt_b);
  64:         assert_ne!(k_a, k_b);
  65:     }
