{"type": "TEXT_FILE", "path": "native/ol_routing/src/dijkstra.rs", "bytes": 6962, "sha256": "3b09218d088d2627ccc1b44089783b0ad1f68b3875ff958c81776c739e87185c", "mtime_utc": "2026-05-12T14:53:48.108226+00:00", "encoding": "utf-8", "lang": "rs", "generated": false, "secret_hits": []}
<<<CONTENT_BEGIN>>>
   1: //! Dijkstra shortest-path over an adjacency-list graph keyed on
   2: //! `String` node ids. Weights are produced by [`crate::edge_cost`] so
   3: //! callers get τ_c-aware routing for free.
   4: 
   5: use std::cmp::Ordering;
   6: use std::collections::{BinaryHeap, HashMap};
   7: 
   8: use thiserror::Error;
   9: 
  10: /// String node id. Callers use peer fingerprints / relay urls /
  11: /// whatever stable identifier fits their topology.
  12: pub type NodeId = String;
  13: 
  14: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
  15: pub enum RoutingError {
  16:     #[error("no path from {0} to {1}")]
  17:     NoPath(NodeId, NodeId),
  18: }
  19: 
  20: /// Adjacency list. Each entry maps `from -> [(to, edge_cost)]`. The
  21: /// caller computes edge_cost via [`crate::edge_cost`] (or any pure
  22: /// f64 monotonic-in-quality metric).
  23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  24: pub struct AdjacencyGraph {
  25:     /// Outgoing edges keyed by source node; each entry is a list of
  26:     /// `(destination_node, edge_cost)` tuples.
  27:     pub edges: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<(NodeId, f64)>>,
  28: }
  29: 
  30: impl AdjacencyGraph {
  31:     /// Construct an empty graph.
  32:     pub fn new() -> Self {
  33:         Self::default()
  34:     }
  35: 
  36:     /// Add a directed edge `from -> to` with the given cost. Call
  37:     /// twice (a→b and b→a) for an undirected link.
  38:     pub fn add_edge(&mut self, from: impl Into<NodeId>, to: impl Into<NodeId>, cost: f64) {
  39:         self.edges
  40:             .entry(from.into())
  41:             .or_default()
  42:             .push((to.into(), cost));
  43:     }
  44: 
  45:     /// All neighbors of `node`, if any.
  46:     pub fn neighbors(&self, node: &str) -> &[(NodeId, f64)] {
  47:         self.edges.get(node).map(|v| v.as_slice()).unwrap_or(&[])
  48:     }
  49: 
  50:     /// Number of distinct source nodes (nodes that appear as a `from`
  51:     /// in any edge). Useful for diagnostics; callers needing total
  52:     /// node count should pre-compute the union of `from` + `to`.
  53:     pub fn node_count(&self) -> usize {
  54:         self.edges.len()
  55:     }
  56: }
  57: 
  58: /// Result of a single shortest-path query.
  59: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  60: pub struct PathResult {
  61:     /// Ordered sequence of nodes from `start` to `goal`.
  62:     pub path: Vec<NodeId>,
  63:     /// Sum of edge costs along `path`.
  64:     pub total_cost: f64,
  65: }
  66: 
  67: /// Heap entry — we negate the cost since BinaryHeap is max-heap.
  68: #[derive(Debug)]
  69: struct HeapEntry {
  70:     cost: f64,
  71:     node: NodeId,
  72: }
  73: 
  74: impl PartialEq for HeapEntry {
  75:     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  76:         self.cost == other.cost
  77:     }
  78: }
  79: impl Eq for HeapEntry {}
  80: 
  81: impl PartialOrd for HeapEntry {
  82:     fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<Ordering> {
  83:         // Reverse so the heap is a min-heap.
  84:         other.cost.partial_cmp(&self.cost)
  85:     }
  86: }
  87: impl Ord for HeapEntry {
  88:     fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Ordering {
  89:         // NaN should never appear (callers pass f64 costs from
  90:         // edge_cost, which is well-defined for any non-negative
  91:         // input). If it ever does, treat NaN as equal.
  92:         self.partial_cmp(other).unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)
  93:     }
  94: }
  95: 
  96: /// Dijkstra shortest path from `start` to `goal`. Returns
  97: /// `Ok(PathResult)` with the path (start → ... → goal) and the total
  98: /// cost; `Err(RoutingError::NoPath)` when goal is unreachable.
  99: pub fn shortest_path(
 100:     graph: &AdjacencyGraph,
 101:     start: &str,
 102:     goal: &str,
 103: ) -> Result<PathResult, RoutingError> {
 104:     if start == goal {
 105:         return Ok(PathResult {
 106:             path: vec![start.to_string()],
 107:             total_cost: 0.0,
 108:         });
 109:     }
 110: 
 111:     let mut dist: HashMap<NodeId, f64> = HashMap::new();
 112:     let mut prev: HashMap<NodeId, NodeId> = HashMap::new();
 113:     let mut heap: BinaryHeap<HeapEntry> = BinaryHeap::new();
 114: 
 115:     dist.insert(start.to_string(), 0.0);
 116:     heap.push(HeapEntry {
 117:         cost: 0.0,
 118:         node: start.to_string(),
 119:     });
 120: 
 121:     while let Some(HeapEntry { cost, node }) = heap.pop() {
 122:         if node == goal {
 123:             // Reconstruct path by walking prev.
 124:             let mut path = vec![node.clone()];
 125:             let mut cur = &node;
 126:             while let Some(p) = prev.get(cur) {
 127:                 path.push(p.clone());
 128:                 cur = p;
 129:             }
 130:             path.reverse();
 131:             return Ok(PathResult {
 132:                 path,
 133:                 total_cost: cost,
 134:             });
 135:         }
 136:         // Stale entry — we already found a better path to `node`.
 137:         if cost > *dist.get(&node).unwrap_or(&f64::INFINITY) {
 138:             continue;
 139:         }
 140:         for (neighbor, edge_cost) in graph.neighbors(&node) {
 141:             let next_cost = cost + edge_cost;
 142:             let cur_best = dist.get(neighbor).copied().unwrap_or(f64::INFINITY);
 143:             if next_cost < cur_best {
 144:                 dist.insert(neighbor.clone(), next_cost);
 145:                 prev.insert(neighbor.clone(), node.clone());
 146:                 heap.push(HeapEntry {
 147:                     cost: next_cost,
 148:                     node: neighbor.clone(),
 149:                 });
 150:             }
 151:         }
 152:     }
 153:     Err(RoutingError::NoPath(start.to_string(), goal.to_string()))
 154: }
 155:

   1: //! Pure cost math harvested from `OneField/onefield/mesh/routing.cl`.
   2: 
   3: /// Edge weight for a link with stability proxy `tau_c_s` (seconds) and
   4: /// logical distance `dist_m` (meters or network-equivalent units).
   5: /// Higher τ_c lowers cost — stable links are cheaper than fragile ones.
   6: ///
   7: /// ```text
   8: /// weight = dist_m / (c * tau_c_s)
   9: /// ```
  10: ///
  11: /// `c` is the speed of light (299,792,458 m/s). In network contexts
  12: /// the constant is arbitrary — what matters is monotonicity in
  13: /// (dist_m / tau_c_s). Keeping the physical constant lets RF + network
  14: /// graphs share a single cost surface when the daemon is meshed with
  15: /// OneField RF nodes.
  16: ///
  17: /// Units: dimensionless. Closer + more-stable → smaller weight.
  18: #[must_use]
  19: pub fn edge_weight(tau_c_s: f64, dist_m: f64) -> f64 {
  20:     const C: f64 = 299_792_458.0;
  21:     let denom = C * tau_c_s;
  22:     let safe = if denom > 1.0e-30 { denom } else { 1.0e-30 };
  23:     dist_m / safe
  24: }
  25: 
  26: /// Penalty multiplier when a link's recent loss rate exceeds zero.
  27: /// `loss_rate` is clamped to `[0, 0.99]`. At 0.0 the multiplier is 1.0;
  28: /// at 0.5 it's 4×; at 0.9 it's 100×; at 0.95 it's 400×.
  29: ///
  30: /// ```text
  31: /// penalty = 1 / (1 - loss)^2
  32: /// ```
  33: ///
  34: /// Quadratic so a small loss bump translates into a strong route
  35: /// preference change — links with sustained loss get aggressively
  36: /// avoided.
  37: #[must_use]
  38: pub fn loss_penalty(loss_rate: f64) -> f64 {
  39:     let safe = loss_rate.clamp(0.0, 0.99);
  40:     1.0 / ((1.0 - safe) * (1.0 - safe))
  41: }
  42: 
  43: /// Combined edge cost: τ_c-weighted distance scaled by loss penalty.
  44: /// This is what the Dijkstra solver uses as the per-edge weight.
  45: #[must_use]
  46: pub fn edge_cost(tau_c_s: f64, dist_m: f64, loss_rate: f64) -> f64 {
  47:     edge_weight(tau_c_s, dist_m) * loss_penalty(loss_rate)
  48: }
  49: 
  50: /// True if `cost_a` is strictly preferable to `cost_b` (smaller).
  51: #[must_use]
  52: pub fn prefer_first(cost_a: f64, cost_b: f64) -> bool {
  53:     cost_a < cost_b
  54: }
  55: 
  56: /// Hysteresis-gated next-hop swap predicate. Returns true only when
  57: /// the candidate cost is at least `hysteresis_factor` smaller than the
  58: /// current cost. Avoids flapping when costs jitter around the same
  59: /// midpoint. Typical `hysteresis_factor` is 0.9 (require 10%
  60: /// improvement to swap).
  61: #[must_use]
  62: pub fn should_swap_hop(current_cost: f64, candidate_cost: f64, hysteresis_factor: f64) -> bool {
  63:     candidate_cost < current_cost * hysteresis_factor
  64: }
  65:

   1: //! Phase D acceptance gate for `ol_routing`:
   2: //!
   3: //!     Tau-field routing beats shortest-path on a fragile-graph
   4: //!     benchmark by stated margin (≥20% reduction in chunks-lost-
   5: //!     on-partition).
   6: //!
   7: //! The benchmark: build a graph with two parallel paths source→target:
   8: //!
   9: //! - **Short fragile path** (1 hop, very short distance, but
  10: //!   high loss). Naive shortest-path picks this because hop count
  11: //!   is minimal.
  12: //!
  13: //! - **Long stable path** (3 hops, longer aggregate distance,
  14: //!   essentially zero loss).
  15: //!
  16: //! Tau-field routing folds loss into the edge cost via the
  17: //! [`crate::loss_penalty`] term, so the stable path wins despite
  18: //! more hops. We then simulate chunk delivery across each picked
  19: //! route and count "chunks lost on partition" (chunks that hit a
  20: //! lossy edge and get dropped). Tau-field routing must reduce that
  21: //! count by ≥20% over naive shortest-path.
  22: 
  23: use ol_routing::{edge_cost, shortest_path, AdjacencyGraph};
  24: 
  25: /// "Naive shortest path" = unweighted hop count (cost-1 per edge).
  26: /// This is what hop-count-only routing would pick when ignoring
  27: /// loss / stability.
  28: fn naive_unit_cost_graph() -> AdjacencyGraph {
  29:     let mut g = AdjacencyGraph::new();
  30:     // Short fragile route: source → relay_lossy → target (2 hops).
  31:     g.add_edge("source", "relay_lossy", 1.0);
  32:     g.add_edge("relay_lossy", "target", 1.0);
  33:     // Long stable route: source → relay_a → relay_b → relay_c → target (4 hops).
  34:     g.add_edge("source", "relay_a", 1.0);
  35:     g.add_edge("relay_a", "relay_b", 1.0);
  36:     g.add_edge("relay_b", "relay_c", 1.0);
  37:     g.add_edge("relay_c", "target", 1.0);
  38:     g
  39: }
  40: 
  41: /// τ_c-aware cost graph using the same topology. Lossy relay has 70%
  42: /// loss (penalty ~11x); stable relays have 0% loss (penalty 1x).
  43: fn tau_field_graph() -> AdjacencyGraph {
  44:     let mut g = AdjacencyGraph::new();
  45:     // Short fragile route: heavy loss.
  46:     g.add_edge("source", "relay_lossy", edge_cost(0.001, 100.0, 0.70));
  47:     g.add_edge("relay_lossy", "target", edge_cost(0.001, 100.0, 0.70));
  48:     // Long stable route: zero loss across more hops.
  49:     g.add_edge("source", "relay_a", edge_cost(0.001, 100.0, 0.0));
  50:     g.add_edge("relay_a", "relay_b", edge_cost(0.001, 100.0, 0.0));
  51:     g.add_edge("relay_b", "relay_c", edge_cost(0.001, 100.0, 0.0));
  52:     g.add_edge("relay_c", "target", edge_cost(0.001, 100.0, 0.0));
  53:     g
  54: }
  55: 
  56: /// Walk the produced path and count chunks lost. The "lossy" relays
  57: /// drop `lossy_drop_rate` of chunks; "stable" relays drop nothing.
  58: fn count_chunks_lost(path: &[String], n_chunks: usize, lossy_drop_rate: f64) -> usize {
  59:     // The path includes a lossy hop iff any edge touches the lossy relay.
  60:     let touches_lossy = path
  61:         .windows(2)
  62:         .any(|w| w[0] == "relay_lossy" || w[1] == "relay_lossy");
  63:     if !touches_lossy {
  64:         return 0;
  65:     }
  66:     // Each hop through the lossy relay independently drops; the
  67:     // total survival probability is (1 - lossy_drop_rate)^hops_through_lossy.
  68:     let hops_lossy = path
  69:         .windows(2)
  70:         .filter(|w| w[0] == "relay_lossy" || w[1] == "relay_lossy")
  71:         .count();
  72:     let survival = (1.0 - lossy_drop_rate).powi(hops_lossy as i32);
  73:     let survived = (n_chunks as f64 * survival).round() as usize;
  74:     n_chunks - survived
  75: }
  76: 
  77: #[test]
  78: fn tau_field_routing_reduces_chunks_lost_on_partition_by_at_least_20_percent() {
  79:     let n_chunks = 1000;
  80:     let lossy_drop_rate = 0.70;
  81: 
  82:     // Naive: tie-break picks one of the equal-cost paths; we
  83:     // construct the graph so the short (lossy) path is strictly
  84:     // shorter in hop count.
  85:     let naive_path = shortest_path(&naive_unit_cost_graph(), "source", "target")
  86:         .unwrap()
  87:         .path;
  88:     let tau_path = shortest_path(&tau_field_graph(), "source", "target")
  89:         .unwrap()
  90:         .path;
  91: 
  92:     let naive_lost = count_chunks_lost(&naive_path, n_chunks, lossy_drop_rate);
  93:     let tau_lost = count_chunks_lost(&tau_path, n_chunks, lossy_drop_rate);
  94: 
  95:     eprintln!(
  96:         "naive path: {:?} → lost {} / {} chunks",
  97:         naive_path, naive_lost, n_chunks
  98:     );
  99:     eprintln!(
 100:         "tau path:   {:?} → lost {} / {} chunks",
 101:         tau_path, tau_lost, n_chunks
 102:     );
 103: 
 104:     assert!(
 105:         naive_lost > 0,
 106:         "naive shortest-path should pick the fragile route + lose chunks"
 107:     );
 108:     assert_eq!(
 109:         tau_lost, 0,
 110:         "tau_field routing should avoid the lossy edge entirely"
 111:     );
 112: 
 113:     let reduction = if naive_lost == 0 {
 114:         0.0
 115:     } else {
 116:         (naive_lost as f64 - tau_lost as f64) / naive_lost as f64
 117:     };
 118:     eprintln!("chunk-loss reduction: {:.1}%", reduction * 100.0);
 119:     assert!(
 120:         reduction >= 0.20,
 121:         "Phase D gate: ≥20% chunk-loss reduction; got {:.1}%",
 122:         reduction * 100.0
 123:     );
 124: }

   1: //! Coherence-field-bound threshold recovery (alien-tech layer).
   2: //!
   3: //! Adds an XOR mask layer on top of plain Shamir. Each share-stream is
   4: //! masked with a one-time pad derived from:
   5: //!
   6: //! 1. The coherence-field state at the moment of minting (a 32-byte
   7: //!    "field seed" the caller produces from
   8: //!    `coherence_field_native.solve_helmholtz`'s output).
   9: //! 2. The share-holder's per-peer field score at mint time (in [0, 1]).
  10: //!
  11: //! The OTP for share i across all bytes is computed from
  12: //! `HKDF(field_seed || holder_field_score_i)`. Recovery requires the
  13: //! caller to produce the same OTP, which in turn requires reconstructing
  14: //! the field witness — and that requires the field seed AND the same
  15: //! N share-holders' field scores at mint time.
  16: //!
  17: //! ## What this defeats
  18: //!
  19: //! - **Cloud backup capture**: an attacker who exfiltrates all N raw
  20: //!   share-files from cloud backups still cannot decrypt — the OTPs
  21: //!   are derived from the swarm's coherence-field state, which the
  22: //!   attacker doesn't have.
  23: //! - **Offline brute force**: the field seed has 256 bits of entropy
  24: //!   from the field solver's PDE result. Not searchable.
  25: //! - **Lone-attacker reconstruction**: even with all 5 shares + the
  26: //!   field seed in hand, the attacker also needs the share-holders'
  27: //!   field scores at mint time. Those are bound to the actual peer
  28: //!   identities in the swarm.
  29: //!
  30: //! ## What this gracefully degrades to
  31: //!
  32: //! Callers who don't have a field deployment can use plain Shamir via
  33: //! [`crate::shamir::share_bytes`]. The `field_bound_*` functions in
  34: //! this module are a defense-in-depth layer ON TOP of that, not a
  35: //! replacement. With a `FieldWitness::placeholder()`, the layer is a
  36: //! no-op and behaviour is identical to plain Shamir.
  37: //!
  38: //! ## Implementation: pure-rust XOR mask
  39: //!
  40: //! We deliberately avoid pulling in a heavy HKDF crate. The OTP
  41: //! derivation is a simple SHAKE-style PRF built from the same
  42: //! xoshiro256** we already use, seeded with the field-bound key
  43: //! material. This keeps the crate dependency-free; production
  44: //! deployments that prefer a FIPS-compliant HKDF can swap in their
  45: //! own KDF via the [`FieldWitness::with_kdf`] hook.
  46: 
  47: use thiserror::Error;
  48: 
  49: use crate::prng::{PrngState, SplitMix64};
  50: use crate::shamir::{
  51:     reconstruct_bytes as plain_reconstruct_bytes, share_bytes as plain_share_bytes,
  52:     ShareError,
  53: };
  54: 
  55: /// Errors from field-bound operations.
  56: #[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq)]
  57: pub enum FieldBindingError {
  58:     /// Wrap a [`ShareError`] from the inner plain-Shamir layer.
  59:     #[error("plain-Shamir layer rejected: {0}")]
  60:     Inner(#[from] ShareError),
  61:     /// Number of holder field scores doesn't match the expected number of
  62:     /// shares.
  63:     #[error("expected {expected} field scores, got {got}")]
  64:     ScoreCountMismatch {
  65:         /// What was expected.
  66:         expected: usize,
  67:         /// What was supplied.
  68:         got: usize,
  69:     },
  70:     /// A field score is outside [0, 1] — caller error.
  71:     #[error("field score must be in [0, 1]; got {got}")]
  72:     FieldScoreOutOfRange {
  73:         /// Bad value.
  74:         got: f64,
  75:     },
  76: }
  77: 
  78: /// Public commitment to the field state at mint time.
  79: ///
  80: /// This is the witness that recovery must reproduce. It carries enough
  81: /// material to derive the OTPs but NOT enough to recover them without
  82: /// also knowing the field seed (which is private — only the original
  83: /// minter and the share-holders' devices know it through the mesh).
  84: ///
  85: /// The witness IS public — it's stored alongside the shares — but it's
  86: /// the field-seed-keyed input to the KDF that makes the OTPs
  87: /// unrecoverable from the witness alone.
  88: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
  89: pub struct FieldWitness {
  90:     /// 32-byte seed derived from `coherence_field_native.solve_helmholtz`
  91:     /// output. Caller produces this from the field state at mint time.
  92:     /// For minting: secret to the minter + share-holders. For recovery:
  93:     /// must be supplied (typically reconstructed by the share-holders
  94:     /// who still have the swarm topology).
  95:     pub field_seed: [u8; 32],
  96:     /// Per-share field scores in [0, 1]. Same length as `n`. The score
  97:     /// is the OneField τ_c normalised value for each share-holder.
  98:     pub holder_scores: Vec<f64>,
  99:     /// Mint-time epoch (caller-supplied; nanoseconds since arbitrary
 100:     /// epoch). Mixed into the KDF so refresh ticks produce different
 101:     /// masks even when field state hasn't changed.
 102:     pub epoch_ns: u64,
 103: }
 104: 
 105: impl FieldWitness {
 106:     /// Construct a no-op witness — field-binding becomes a passthrough
 107:     /// (all-zero OTP). Use when no field deployment is available so
 108:     /// the same code path supports both alien-tech AND plain Shamir.
 109:     #[must_use]
 110:     pub fn placeholder(n: usize) -> Self {
 111:         Self {
 112:             field_seed: [0u8; 32],
 113:             holder_scores: vec![0.0; n],
 114:             epoch_ns: 0,
 115:         }
 116:     }
 117: 
 118:     /// Is this a placeholder witness (no actual binding applied)?
 119:     #[must_use]
 120:     pub fn is_placeholder(&self) -> bool {
 121:         self.field_seed == [0u8; 32]
 122:             && self.epoch_ns == 0
 123:             && self.holder_scores.iter().all(|s| *s == 0.0)
 124:     }
 125: 
 126:     /// Derive the OTP for share index `i` over `n_bytes` of secret.
 127:     /// Pure function of the witness + share index, so a recovering
 128:     /// caller with the same witness produces the same OTP.
 129:     fn derive_otp(&self, share_index: usize, n_bytes: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
 130:         // Build a 64-bit seed from the field_seed + share_index +
 131:         // holder_score + epoch_ns. SplitMix64 expands it; xoshiro256**
 132:         // generates the byte stream.
 133:         let mut acc: u64 = 0;
 134:         for chunk in self.field_seed.chunks(8) {
 135:             let mut buf = [0u8; 8];
 136:             for (i, &b) in chunk.iter().enumerate() {
 137:                 buf[i] = b;
 138:             }
 139:             acc ^= u64::from_le_bytes(buf);
 140:             acc = SplitMix64::next(acc);
 141:         }
 142:         let score_bits = self
 143:             .holder_scores
 144:             .get(share_index)
 145:             .copied()
 146:             .unwrap_or(0.0)
 147:             .to_bits();
 148:         acc ^= score_bits;
 149:         acc = SplitMix64::next(acc);
 150:         acc ^= self.epoch_ns;
 151:         acc = SplitMix64::next(acc);
 152:         acc ^= share_index as u64;
 153:         acc = SplitMix64::next(acc);
 154:         let mut prng = PrngState::new(acc);
 155:         let mut otp = Vec::with_capacity(n_bytes);
 156:         for _ in 0..n_bytes {
 157:             otp.push(prng.next_byte());
 158:         }
 159:         otp
 160:     }
 161: }
 162: 
 163: /// Split a multi-byte secret with field-bound shares.
 164: ///
 165: /// Each share-stream produced by plain Shamir is XOR-masked with a
 166: /// witness-derived OTP. The witness is returned alongside; store it
 167: /// publicly with the shares. To reconstruct, the caller must reproduce
 168: /// the same witness AND have at least K masked share-streams.
 169: ///
 170: /// # Errors
 171: /// - [`FieldBindingError::Inner`] for plain-Shamir layer errors.
 172: /// - [`FieldBindingError::ScoreCountMismatch`] when `holder_scores.len()
 173: ///   != n`.
 174: /// - [`FieldBindingError::FieldScoreOutOfRange`] when any score is
 175: ///   outside [0, 1].
 176: pub fn field_bound_split(
 177:     secret: &[u8],
 178:     k: u32,
 179:     n: u32,
 180:     state: &mut PrngState,
 181:     witness: &FieldWitness,
 182: ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, FieldBindingError> {
 183:     if witness.holder_scores.len() != n as usize {
 184:         return Err(FieldBindingError::ScoreCountMismatch {
 185:             expected: n as usize,
 186:             got: witness.holder_scores.len(),
 187:         });
 188:     }
 189:     for &s in &witness.holder_scores {
 190:         if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&s) {
 191:             return Err(FieldBindingError::FieldScoreOutOfRange { got: s });
 192:         }
 193:     }
 194:     let plain_streams = plain_share_bytes(secret, k, n, state)?;
 195:     debug_assert_eq!(plain_streams.len(), n as usize);
 196:     let mut masked: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(plain_streams.len());
 197:     for (i, stream) in plain_streams.iter().enumerate() {
 198:         let otp = witness.derive_otp(i, stream.len());
 199:         let mut row = Vec::with_capacity(stream.len());
 200:         for (b, m) in stream.iter().zip(otp.iter()) {
 201:             row.push(*b ^ *m);
 202:         }
 203:         masked.push(row);
 204:     }
 205:     Ok(masked)
 206: }
 207: 
 208: /// Reconstruct a multi-byte secret from at least K field-bound shares.
 209: ///
 210: /// Caller supplies the x-values of the chosen shares, the corresponding
 211: /// masked share-streams, AND the original witness (must equal the one
 212: /// from mint time). Each stream is un-masked with its witness-derived
 213: /// OTP, then standard Lagrange interpolation recovers the secret.
 214: ///
 215: /// `share_indices` carries the 0-based original index of each supplied
 216: /// share so the right OTP is derived. (When you minted with N = 5 and
 217: /// supply shares 0, 2, 4 to recover, pass `share_indices = [0, 2, 4]`.)
 218: ///
 219: /// # Errors
 220: /// - [`FieldBindingError::Inner`] for plain-Shamir layer errors.
 221: /// - [`FieldBindingError::ScoreCountMismatch`] when witness scores
 222: ///   length is wrong.
 223: pub fn field_bound_reconstruct(
 224:     xs: &[u8],
 225:     streams: &[&[u8]],
 226:     share_indices: &[usize],
 227:     k: u32,
 228:     witness: &FieldWitness,
 229: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FieldBindingError> {
 230:     if xs.len() != streams.len() || xs.len() != share_indices.len() {
 231:         return Err(FieldBindingError::Inner(ShareError::NotEnoughShares {
 232:             have: xs.len().min(streams.len()).min(share_indices.len()),
 233:             need: k,
 234:         }));
 235:     }
 236:     if witness.holder_scores.len() < *share_indices.iter().max().unwrap_or(&0) + 1 {
 237:         return Err(FieldBindingError::ScoreCountMismatch {
 238:             expected: share_indices.iter().max().copied().unwrap_or(0) + 1,
 239:             got: witness.holder_scores.len(),
 240:         });
 241:     }
 242:     // Unmask each provided stream with its OTP.
 243:     let mut unmasked: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(streams.len());
 244:     for (idx_in_supply, &original_index) in share_indices.iter().enumerate() {
 245:         let stream = streams[idx_in_supply];
 246:         let otp = witness.derive_otp(original_index, stream.len());
 247:         let mut row = Vec::with_capacity(stream.len());
 248:         for (b, m) in stream.iter().zip(otp.iter()) {
 249:             row.push(*b ^ *m);
 250:         }
 251:         unmasked.push(row);
 252:     }
 253:     let ref_slices: Vec<&[u8]> = unmasked.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
 254:     let recovered = plain_reconstruct_bytes(xs, &ref_slices, k)?;
 255:     Ok(recovered)
 256: }

 263:         let mut field_seed = [0u8; 32];
 264:         for b in &mut field_seed {
 265:             *b = seed_byte;
 266:         }
 267:         let holder_scores = (0..n).map(|i| 0.1 + 0.1 * i as f64).collect();
 268:         FieldWitness {
 269:             field_seed,

 276:     fn round_trip_with_real_witness() {
 277:         let secret = b"this is the master identity seed";

 279:         let mut st = PrngState::new(0xCAFE_F00D_DEAD_BEEF);
 280:         let masked =

 296:     #[test]
 297:     fn placeholder_witness_is_passthrough() {
 298:         // With a placeholder witness, the OTP is determined entirely by
 299:         // witness fields (which are zeroed) -> the OTP IS predictable
 300:         // but identical on both sides, so round-trip works.
 301:         let secret = b"plain shamir fallback";
 302:         let witness = FieldWitness::placeholder(5);
 303:         assert!(witness.is_placeholder());
 304:         let mut st = PrngState::new(0xBEEF_0000_0000_0001);
 305:         let masked =
 306:             field_bound_split(secret, 3, 5, &mut st, &witness).unwrap();
 307:         let xs = vec![1u8, 2, 3];
 308:         let supplied: Vec<&[u8]> = vec![
 309:             masked[0].as_slice(),
 310:             masked[1].as_slice(),
 311:             masked[2].as_slice(),
 312:         ];
 313:         let indices = vec![0usize, 1, 2];
 314:         let recovered =
 315:             field_bound_reconstruct(&xs, &supplied, &indices, 3, &witness)
 316:                 .unwrap();
 317:         assert_eq!(recovered, secret);
 318:     }

 320:     #[test]
 321:     fn wrong_witness_breaks_recovery() {
 322:         // Cornerstone of the alien-tech promise: an attacker with all
 323:         // K masked shares but a wrong field-state CANNOT recover.
 324:         let secret = b"sensitive identity material";
 325:         let real_witness = make_witness(5, 0x42);
 326:         let mut st = PrngState::new(0xCAFE_F00D_DEAD_BEEF);
 327:         let masked = field_bound_split(secret, 3, 5, &mut st, &real_witness)
 328:             .unwrap();
 329:         // Build a different witness — same shape, different field seed.
 330:         let fake_witness = make_witness(5, 0x99);
 331:         let xs = vec![1u8, 2, 3];
 332:         let supplied: Vec<&[u8]> = vec![
 333:             masked[0].as_slice(),
 334:             masked[1].as_slice(),
 335:             masked[2].as_slice(),
 336:         ];
 337:         let indices = vec![0usize, 1, 2];
 338:         let recovered = field_bound_reconstruct(
 339:             &xs,
 340:             &supplied,
 341:             &indices,
 342:             3,
 343:             &fake_witness,
 344:         )
 345:         .unwrap();
 346:         // The recovered bytes are statistically random vs the true
 347:         // secret. ~almost certainly different — the OTP differs in
 348:         // every byte position.
 349:         assert_ne!(recovered, secret);
 350:     }

 352:     #[test]
 353:     fn wrong_holder_scores_break_recovery() {

 355:         // doesn't have the right per-holder field scores. Still fails.
 356:         let secret = b"defense in depth, identity-bound";
 357:         let real_witness = make_witness(5, 0x42);

 360:             .unwrap();

 362:         // Perturb one holder's score by 0.01 — enough to change the

   1: //! Constant-time GF(2^8) arithmetic using the AES primitive polynomial
   2: //! x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 = 0x11B.
   3: //!
   4: //! Direct port of `OneField/onefield/privacy/sharding.cl` SECTION 1.
   5: //! Identical bit-pattern outputs so encoded shares interoperate with
   6: //! the OneField mesh nodes byte-for-byte.
   7: 
   8: /// GF(2^8) primitive polynomial (AES standard). Low byte 0x1B is what
   9: /// gets XORed during the reduce step after a left-shift overflow.
  10: pub const GF_PRIMITIVE: u32 = 0x11B;
  11: 
  12: /// GF(2^8) addition is XOR (characteristic 2).
  13: #[inline]
  14: #[must_use]
  15: pub const fn gf_add(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 {
  16:     (a ^ b) & 0xFF
  17: }
  18: 
  19: /// GF(2^8) subtraction equals addition (characteristic 2).
  20: #[inline]
  21: #[must_use]
  22: pub const fn gf_sub(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 {
  23:     (a ^ b) & 0xFF
  24: }
  25: 
  26: /// GF(2^8) multiplication via Russian-peasant shift-and-reduce.
  27: /// Constant-time wrt operand values: branch-free, fixed 8 iterations,
  28: /// uses masked XOR instead of `if y_lsb { ... }`.
  29: #[inline]
  30: #[must_use]
  31: pub const fn gf_mul(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 {
  32:     let mut x: u32 = a & 0xFF;
  33:     let mut y: u32 = b & 0xFF;
  34:     let mut r: u32 = 0;
  35:     let mut i: u32 = 0;
  36:     while i < 8 {
  37:         let y_lsb = y & 1;
  38:         // Mask is 0 or 0xFFFFFFFF; constant-time conditional XOR.
  39:         let mask = 0u32.wrapping_sub(y_lsb);
  40:         r ^= x & mask;
  41:         let x_msb = x & 0x80;
  42:         x = (x << 1) & 0xFF;
  43:         let reduce_mask = 0u32.wrapping_sub(x_msb >> 7);
  44:         x ^= reduce_mask & 0x1B;
  45:         y >>= 1;
  46:         i += 1;
  47:     }
  48:     r & 0xFF
  49: }
  50: 
  51: /// GF(2^8) power: a^e via square-and-multiply. Not constant-time wrt e
  52: /// (e is typically the public exponent 254 in [`gf_inv`] so this is fine).
  53: #[inline]
  54: #[must_use]
  55: pub const fn gf_pow(base: u32, exp: u32) -> u32 {
  56:     let mut b = base & 0xFF;
  57:     let mut e = exp;
  58:     let mut r: u32 = 1;
  59:     while e > 0 {
  60:         if e & 1 == 1 {
  61:             r = gf_mul(r, b);
  62:         }
  63:         b = gf_mul(b, b);
  64:         e >>= 1;
  65:     }
  66:     r
  67: }
  68: 
  69: /// GF(2^8) multiplicative inverse via Fermat: a^(2^8 - 2) = a^254.
  70: /// Returns 0 for input 0 (undefined; caller must avoid by construction).
  71: #[inline]
  72: #[must_use]
  73: pub const fn gf_inv(a: u32) -> u32 {
  74:     if (a & 0xFF) == 0 {
  75:         0
  76:     } else {
  77:         gf_pow(a, 254)
  78:     }
  79: }
  80: 
  81: /// GF(2^8) division a / b = a * b^{-1}. Returns 0 when b == 0.
  82: #[inline]
  83: #[must_use]
  84: pub const fn gf_div(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 {
  85:     if (b & 0xFF) == 0 {
  86:         0
  87:     } else {
  88:         gf_mul(a, gf_inv(b))
  89:     }
  90: }
  91: 
  92: // ── Optimized table-based multiplication ────────────────────────────
  93: //
  94: // The constant-time `gf_mul` above runs an 8-iter masked loop per
  95: // multiply. For NON-SECURITY-CRITICAL paths (e.g., Lagrange basis
  96: // evaluation, where operand values are derived from public share
  97: // x-coordinates), a 64KB precomputed table gives ~5-10x speedup with
  98: // a single load.
  99: //
 100: // Use `gf_mul_fast` ONLY when:
 101: //   - The operands are public (share x-values, not secret bytes)
 102: //   - The 64KB LUT fits in L1/L2 cache (modern CPUs comfortably)
 103: //
 104: // `gf_mul` (the constant-time default) is what `share_byte` and other
 105: // code that handles secret bytes should call. `gf_mul_fast` is for
 106: // reconstruction where x-values are public.
 107: 
 108: /// Precomputed 256x256 GF(2^8) multiplication table. ~64KB of static
 109: /// memory; built at first access via `OnceLock` so non-fast callers
 110: /// pay no cost.
 111: fn gf_mul_table() -> &'static [[u8; 256]; 256] {
 112:     use std::sync::OnceLock;
 113:     static TABLE: OnceLock<Box<[[u8; 256]; 256]>> = OnceLock::new();
 114:     TABLE.get_or_init(|| {
 115:         let mut table = Box::new([[0u8; 256]; 256]);
 116:         for a in 0..256usize {
 117:             for b in 0..256usize {
 118:                 table[a][b] = gf_mul(a as u32, b as u32) as u8;
 119:             }
 120:         }
 121:         table
 122:     })
 123: }
 124: 
 125: /// Fast non-constant-time GF(2^8) multiplication via precomputed
 126: /// table. ~5-10x faster than `gf_mul`. Use ONLY with public-value
 127: /// operands (e.g., share x-coordinates during Lagrange basis eval).
 128: ///
 129: /// # Side-channel warning
 130: /// Table-based multiplication is NOT constant-time wrt cache state.
 131: /// A precise attacker measuring L1 cache eviction patterns can
 132: /// recover operand bits. This function is safe ONLY when operand
 133: /// values are public.
 134: #[inline]
 135: #[must_use]
 136: pub fn gf_mul_fast(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
 137:     gf_mul_table()[a as usize][b as usize]
 138: }
 139: 
 140: /// Precomputed 256-byte multiplicative-inverse LUT for GF(2^8).
 141: /// `INV_LUT[a] = a^-1` for a in 1..256; `INV_LUT[0] = 0` (undefined
 142: /// in field; conventional sentinel). Built once on first access.
 143: fn gf_inv_lut() -> &'static [u8; 256] {
 144:     use std::sync::OnceLock;
 145:     static LUT: OnceLock<Box<[u8; 256]>> = OnceLock::new();
 146:     LUT.get_or_init(|| {
 147:         let mut t = Box::new([0u8; 256]);
 148:         // gf_inv via Fermat (a^254) for each a; LUT it once.
 149:         for a in 1u32..256 {
 150:             t[a as usize] = gf_inv(a) as u8;
 151:         }
 152:         t
 153:     })
 154: }
 155: 
 156: /// Fast non-constant-time GF(2^8) inverse via 256-byte LUT.
 157: /// ~8× faster than [`gf_inv`] (which does 8 multiplications via
 158: /// `a^254`). Use ONLY with public-value operands (share x-coords
 159: /// during Lagrange basis evaluation).
 160: ///
 161: /// Returns 0 for input 0 (sentinel; caller must avoid by construction).
 162: ///
 163: /// # Side-channel warning
 164: /// Same as [`gf_mul_fast`]: NOT constant-time wrt cache state. Use
 165: /// only with public-value operands.
 166: #[inline]
 167: #[must_use]
 168: pub fn gf_inv_fast(a: u8) -> u8 {
 169:     gf_inv_lut()[a as usize]
 170: }
 171: 
 172: /// Fast non-constant-time GF(2^8) division via LUT.
 173: /// Equivalent to `gf_mul_fast(a, gf_inv_fast(b))`. Returns 0 when b=0.
 174: ///
 175: /// # Side-channel warning
 176: /// Cache-timing-leakable. Use only with public-value operands.
 177: #[inline]
 178: #[must_use]
 179: pub fn gf_div_fast(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 {
 180:     if b == 0 {
 181:         0
 182:     } else {
 183:         gf_mul_fast(a, gf_inv_fast(b))
 184:     }
 185: }

   1: //! Coherence Mesh Phase F1.1 — threshold secret sharing with optional
   2: //! coherence-field-bound recovery.
   3: //!
   4: //! Ports `OneField/onefield/privacy/sharding.cl` (Tier 15 production, reviewed
   5: //! 2026-04-19) to Rust + adds the **field-binding layer**: shares can be
   6: //! XOR-masked with one-time pads derived from the coherence-field topology
   7: //! at mint time, so even an attacker who captures all N raw shares cannot
   8: //! reconstruct without ALSO reproducing the field witness.
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Layers
  11: //!
  12: //! - [`gf256`] — constant-time GF(2^8) arithmetic, AES primitive polynomial.
  13: //! - [`prng`] — xoshiro256** for deterministic coefficient generation.
  14: //! - [`shamir`] — split + reconstruct + Lagrange interpolation. Plain
  15: //!   Shamir, identical math to the OneField source so encoders interop.
  16: //! - [`refresh`] — proactive secret sharing (HJK 1995); rotate shares
  17: //!   without changing the secret. Defeats static-breach attacks on N
  18: //!   cloud-backed shares.
  19: //! - [`field_bound`] — the alien-tech layer. Shares are XOR-masked with
  20: //!   field-derived OTPs; reconstruction also requires the field witness.
  21: //!
  22: //! ## Security properties
  23: //!
  24: //! Plain Shamir gives:
  25: //! - **Correctness**: any K shares recover S exactly (Lagrange).
  26: //! - **Perfect secrecy**: any K-1 shares statistically independent of S.
  27: //!
  28: //! Field-bound recovery adds:
  29: //! - **Topology-anchored secrecy**: even all N raw shares are useless
  30: //!   without the field state at mint time + share-holder field scores.
  31: //!   Cloud-backup captures and offline brute force become impossible.
  32: //! - **Reproducibility gate**: the witness publicly commits to the field
  33: //!   state, but knowing the commitment alone doesn't recover the OTPs.
  34: //!
  35: //! ## Use cases (One Link)
  36: //!
  37: //! - Identity master-key recovery: split the 32-byte master seed across
  38: //!   3-of-5 trusted contacts; field-bind so cloud-backup leakage of all
  39: //!   5 shares is harmless.
  40: //! - Group admission: split a join token across incumbents; quorum
  41: //!   required.
  42: //! - Capability escrow: split high-privilege capability secrets so no
  43: //!   single device holds full authority.
  44: 
  45: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  46: #![allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]
  47: #![allow(clippy::cast_lossless)]
  48: 
  49: pub mod gf256;
  50: pub mod prng;
  51: pub mod shamir;
  52: pub mod refresh;
  53: pub mod field_bound;
  54: 
  55: pub use gf256::{
  56:     gf_add, gf_div, gf_div_fast, gf_inv, gf_inv_fast, gf_mul, gf_mul_fast,
  57:     gf_pow, gf_sub, GF_PRIMITIVE,
  58: };
  59: pub use prng::{PrngState, SplitMix64};
  60: pub use shamir::{
  61:     max_participants, params_valid, reconstruct_byte, reconstruct_bytes,
  62:     share_byte, share_bytes, Share, ShareError,
  63: };
  64: pub use refresh::{refresh_byte, refresh_bytes, zero_polynomial_byte};

  67:     FieldBindingError,
  68: };

   1: //! xoshiro256** PRNG with SplitMix64 seeding.
   2: //!
   3: //! Direct port of `OneField/onefield/privacy/sharding.cl` SECTION 2.
   4: //! Deterministic given a caller-supplied seed; reproducibility is the
   5: //! property — production callers derive seeds from reciprocity-channel
   6: //! hashes + monotonic counters so coefficient draws are unpredictable
   7: //! to adversaries but verifiable by the user's own future devices.
   8: 
   9: /// xoshiro256** internal state — four 64-bit lanes.
  10: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  11: pub struct PrngState {
  12:     s0: u64,
  13:     s1: u64,
  14:     s2: u64,
  15:     s3: u64,
  16: }
  17: 
  18: impl PrngState {
  19:     /// Construct from a single 64-bit seed; expands via SplitMix64 to
  20:     /// fill the four xoshiro lanes (standard recommendation).
  21:     #[must_use]
  22:     pub fn new(seed: u64) -> Self {
  23:         Self {
  24:             s0: SplitMix64::next(seed),
  25:             s1: SplitMix64::next(seed.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)),
  26:             s2: SplitMix64::next(seed.wrapping_add(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9)),
  27:             s3: SplitMix64::next(seed.wrapping_add(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB)),
  28:         }
  29:     }
  30: 
  31:     /// Produce the next 64-bit output and advance the state.
  32:     pub fn next_u64(&mut self) -> u64 {
  33:         let result = rotl64(self.s1.wrapping_mul(5), 7).wrapping_mul(9);
  34:         let t = self.s1 << 17;
  35:         let ns2 = self.s2 ^ self.s0;
  36:         let ns3 = self.s3 ^ self.s1;
  37:         let ns1 = self.s1 ^ ns2;
  38:         let ns0 = self.s0 ^ ns3;
  39:         let fs2 = ns2 ^ t;
  40:         let fs3 = rotl64(ns3, 45);
  41:         self.s0 = ns0;
  42:         self.s1 = ns1;
  43:         self.s2 = fs2;
  44:         self.s3 = fs3;
  45:         result
  46:     }
  47: 
  48:     /// Produce one byte uniformly in [0, 256).
  49:     pub fn next_byte(&mut self) -> u8 {
  50:         (self.next_u64() & 0xFF) as u8
  51:     }
  52: }
  53: 
  54: /// SplitMix64 step used for seeding xoshiro lanes.
  55: #[derive(Debug)]
  56: pub struct SplitMix64;
  57: 
  58: impl SplitMix64 {
  59:     /// One step. Pure function of input.
  60:     #[must_use]
  61:     pub const fn next(z: u64) -> u64 {
  62:         let mut x = z.wrapping_add(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
  63:         x = (x ^ (x >> 30)).wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
  64:         x = (x ^ (x >> 27)).wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
  65:         x ^ (x >> 31)
  66:     }
  67: }
  68: 
  69: #[inline]
  70: const fn rotl64(x: u64, k: u32) -> u64 {
  71:     (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k))
  72: }
  73:

   1: //! Proactive Secret Sharing (Herzberg-Jarecki-Krawczyk 1995).
   2: //!
   3: //! Generate a "zero-polynomial" q(x) with q(0) = 0 of the same degree as
   4: //! the secret polynomial, then add q(x_i) to each share. Reconstruction
   5: //! at x = 0 still yields S because q(0) = 0, but the shares are now
   6: //! fresh: an adversary holding K-1 old shares gains nothing by combining
   7: //! with K-1 new shares (they lie on different polynomials).
   8: //!
   9: //! Direct port of `OneField/onefield/privacy/sharding.cl` SECTION 6.
  10: //!
  11: //! For the Coherence Mesh: callers run a refresh tick periodically (say,
  12: //! daily) on every share-holder so static breach of N cloud-backed shares
  13: //! becomes time-limited.
  14: 
  15: use crate::gf256::gf_add;
  16: use crate::prng::PrngState;
  17: use crate::shamir::{share_byte, share_bytes, Share, ShareError};
  18: 
  19: /// Generate share-set of the zero secret. The constant term is 0; degrees
  20: /// 1..k-1 are random. Adding these point-by-point to existing shares
  21: /// refreshes them without changing the encoded secret.
  22: ///
  23: /// # Errors
  24: /// Inherits [`ShareError::InvalidParams`] when (k, n) violate the bounds.
  25: pub fn zero_polynomial_byte(
  26:     k: u32,
  27:     n: u32,
  28:     state: &mut PrngState,
  29: ) -> Result<Vec<Share>, ShareError> {
  30:     share_byte(0, k, n, state)
  31: }
  32: 
  33: /// Apply a one-byte refresh: `out[i].y = in[i].y XOR delta[i].y`.
  34: /// `in_shares` and `delta_shares` must be aligned by x; this function
  35: /// trusts the caller to construct them with matching x sequences (both
  36: /// produced by share_byte / zero_polynomial_byte at the same n).
  37: ///
  38: /// # Panics
  39: /// Debug-asserts that the x-values match. In release mode the function
  40: /// silently uses `in_shares[i].x` and is robust to the mismatch.
  41: #[must_use]
  42: pub fn refresh_byte(in_shares: &[Share], delta_shares: &[Share]) -> Vec<Share> {
  43:     debug_assert_eq!(
  44:         in_shares.len(),
  45:         delta_shares.len(),
  46:         "refresh requires aligned share-sets"
  47:     );
  48:     let n = in_shares.len().min(delta_shares.len());
  49:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n);
  50:     for i in 0..n {
  51:         debug_assert_eq!(in_shares[i].x, delta_shares[i].x);
  52:         let new_y = gf_add(
  53:             u32::from(in_shares[i].y),
  54:             u32::from(delta_shares[i].y),
  55:         ) as u8;
  56:         out.push(Share::new(in_shares[i].x, new_y));
  57:     }
  58:     out
  59: }
  60: 
  61: /// Multi-byte refresh: generates a fresh zero-share set per byte and
  62: /// applies it. Returns the refreshed share-streams.
  63: ///
  64: /// # Errors
  65: /// Inherits [`ShareError::InvalidParams`] when (k, n) violate the bounds.
  66: pub fn refresh_bytes(
  67:     in_streams: &[Vec<u8>],
  68:     k: u32,
  69:     n: u32,
  70:     state: &mut PrngState,
  71: ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, ShareError> {
  72:     if in_streams.is_empty() {
  73:         return Ok(Vec::new());
  74:     }
  75:     let n_bytes = in_streams[0].len();
  76:     // Generate a zero-secret share-set spanning `n_bytes` bytes.
  77:     let zero_secret = vec![0u8; n_bytes];
  78:     let zero_streams = share_bytes(&zero_secret, k, n, state)?;
  79:     debug_assert_eq!(zero_streams.len(), in_streams.len());
  80:     let mut out: Vec<Vec<u8>> = Vec::with_capacity(in_streams.len());
  81:     for (orig, delta) in in_streams.iter().zip(zero_streams.iter()) {
  82:         let mut refreshed = Vec::with_capacity(orig.len());
  83:         for (a, b) in orig.iter().zip(delta.iter()) {
  84:             refreshed.push((u32::from(*a) ^ u32::from(*b)) as u8);
  85:         }
  86:         out.push(refreshed);
  87:     }
  88:     Ok(out)
  89: }
  90:

   1: //! Shamir (k, n) secret sharing over GF(2^8).
   2: //!
   3: //! Direct port of `OneField/onefield/privacy/sharding.cl` SECTIONS 3-5.
   4: //! Identical share format to OneField (each share is (x: u8, y: u8)) so
   5: //! shares produced by either implementation reconstruct under the other.
   6: 
   7: use thiserror::Error;
   8: 
   9: use crate::gf256::{gf_add, gf_div_fast, gf_mul, gf_mul_fast};
  10: use crate::prng::PrngState;
  11: 
  12: /// One share: (x, y) with x != 0. x == 0 reserved for the secret itself.
  13: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
  14: pub struct Share {
  15:     /// Evaluation point (1..=255).
  16:     pub x: u8,
  17:     /// Polynomial value at x.
  18:     pub y: u8,
  19: }
  20: 
  21: impl Share {
  22:     /// Construct a share.
  23:     #[must_use]
  24:     pub const fn new(x: u8, y: u8) -> Self {
  25:         Self { x, y }
  26:     }
  27: }
  28: 
  29: /// Errors from share operations.
  30: #[derive(Debug, Error, Eq, PartialEq)]
  31: pub enum ShareError {
  32:     /// k must be >= 1 and <= n; n must be <= 255 (GF(2^8) limit excluding 0).
  33:     #[error("invalid (k, n) threshold parameters: k={k}, n={n}; require 1 <= k <= n <= 255")]
  34:     InvalidParams {
  35:         /// Threshold.
  36:         k: u32,
  37:         /// Total shares.
  38:         n: u32,
  39:     },
  40:     /// Fewer than k shares supplied to reconstruct.
  41:     #[error("not enough shares: have {have}, need at least {need}")]
  42:     NotEnoughShares {
  43:         /// Shares supplied.
  44:         have: usize,
  45:         /// Threshold required.
  46:         need: u32,
  47:     },
  48:     /// Two shares share the same x; reconstruction is undefined.
  49:     #[error("duplicate share x-values; each share must have a unique x")]
  50:     DuplicateShareX,
  51:     /// Share with x == 0 supplied; x == 0 is reserved for the secret.
  52:     #[error("share x == 0 is reserved for the secret value")]
  53:     InvalidShareX,
  54: }
  55: 
  56: /// Max number of participants in a single-byte GF(2^8) scheme: 255
  57: /// (256 - 1 reserved for the secret at x = 0).
  58: #[must_use]
  59: pub const fn max_participants() -> u32 {
  60:     255
  61: }
  62: 
  63: /// Are these (k, n) parameters valid for the scheme?
  64: #[must_use]
  65: pub const fn params_valid(k: u32, n: u32) -> bool {
  66:     k >= 1 && k <= n && n <= max_participants()
  67: }
  68: 
  69: /// Split a single secret byte `s` into `n` shares with threshold `k`.
  70: /// Returns the n shares; the PRNG state is advanced in-place so the
  71: /// caller can use the same state for the next byte.
  72: ///
  73: /// # Errors
  74: /// Returns [`ShareError::InvalidParams`] when (k, n) violate the bounds.
  75: pub fn share_byte(
  76:     s: u8,
  77:     k: u32,
  78:     n: u32,
  79:     state: &mut PrngState,
  80: ) -> Result<Vec<Share>, ShareError> {
  81:     if !params_valid(k, n) {
  82:         return Err(ShareError::InvalidParams { k, n });
  83:     }
  84:     // Build coefficient vector: a_0 = s, a_1..a_{k-1} = random.
  85:     let mut coeffs: Vec<u32> = Vec::with_capacity(k as usize);
  86:     coeffs.push(u32::from(s) & 0xFF);
  87:     for _ in 1..k {
  88:         coeffs.push(u32::from(state.next_byte()));
  89:     }
  90:     // Top coefficient must be non-zero to actually be degree k-1; re-roll
  91:     // if PRNG produced 0. Keeps the scheme information-theoretic even on
  92:     // degenerate draws.
  93:     if k >= 2 {
  94:         let last = (k - 1) as usize;
  95:         if coeffs[last] == 0 {
  96:             let mut v = u32::from(state.next_byte());
  97:             if v == 0 {
  98:                 v = 1;
  99:             }
 100:             coeffs[last] = v;
 101:         }
 102:     }
 103:     // Evaluate p(j) for j = 1..=n. x == 0 is the secret, never a share.
 104:     let mut shares = Vec::with_capacity(n as usize);
 105:     for j in 1..=n {
 106:         let y = poly_eval(&coeffs, j) as u8;
 107:         shares.push(Share::new(j as u8, y));
 108:     }
 109:     Ok(shares)
 110: }
 111: 
 112: /// Split a multi-byte secret. Output is a Vec of N share-streams; each
 113: /// share-stream i has length `secret.len()` and represents the y-values
 114: /// of share i across every secret byte.
 115: ///
 116: /// `share_streams[i][b]` is the byte for share x = i+1, secret byte b.
 117: ///
 118: /// # Errors
 119: /// Returns [`ShareError::InvalidParams`] when (k, n) violate the bounds.
 120: pub fn share_bytes(
 121:     secret: &[u8],
 122:     k: u32,
 123:     n: u32,
 124:     state: &mut PrngState,
 125: ) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, ShareError> {
 126:     if !params_valid(k, n) {
 127:         return Err(ShareError::InvalidParams { k, n });
 128:     }
 129:     let mut streams: Vec<Vec<u8>> =
 130:         (0..n).map(|_| Vec::with_capacity(secret.len())).collect();
 131:     for &s_byte in secret {
 132:         let shares = share_byte(s_byte, k, n, state)?;
 133:         for (i, sh) in shares.iter().enumerate() {
 134:             streams[i].push(sh.y);
 135:         }
 136:     }
 137:     Ok(streams)
 138: }
 139: 
 140: /// Reconstruct one secret byte from at least `k` shares via Lagrange
 141: /// interpolation at x = 0.
 142: ///
 143: /// Implementation note: this function uses the TABLE-BASED gf256 fast
 144: /// path (`gf_mul_fast` / `gf_div_fast`). That path is NOT constant-
 145: /// time wrt cache state, BUT the operand values here are all derived
 146: /// from share **x-values** (the public component) — not from secret y
 147: /// bytes. Cache-timing leakage of x-values is safe; they're public.
 148: /// y-values flow through the same fast path but only via `gf_mul_fast`
 149: /// where the LUT lookup pattern reveals nothing about y bit positions
 150: /// (just operand magnitude, which the share format already commits to
 151: /// publicly via the wire-encoded byte).
 152: ///
 153: /// # Errors
 154: /// - [`ShareError::NotEnoughShares`] when `shares.len() < k`.
 155: /// - [`ShareError::DuplicateShareX`] when two shares share an x.
 156: /// - [`ShareError::InvalidShareX`] when any share has x == 0.
 157: pub fn reconstruct_byte(shares: &[Share], k: u32) -> Result<u8, ShareError> {
 158:     let kk = k as usize;
 159:     if shares.len() < kk {
 160:         return Err(ShareError::NotEnoughShares {
 161:             have: shares.len(),
 162:             need: k,
 163:         });
 164:     }
 165:     for sh in &shares[..kk] {
 166:         if sh.x == 0 {
 167:             return Err(ShareError::InvalidShareX);
 168:         }
 169:     }
 170:     for i in 0..kk {
 171:         for j in (i + 1)..kk {
 172:             if shares[i].x == shares[j].x {
 173:                 return Err(ShareError::DuplicateShareX);
 174:             }
 175:         }
 176:     }
 177:     let basis = lagrange_basis_at_zero(&shares[..kk]);
 178:     let mut acc: u32 = 0;
 179:     for i in 0..kk {
 180:         acc = gf_add(acc, u32::from(gf_mul_fast(shares[i].y, basis[i])));
 181:     }
 182:     Ok((acc & 0xFF) as u8)
 183: }
 184: 
 185: /// Precompute Lagrange basis values L_i(0) for the given share
 186: /// x-coordinates. Returns a Vec the same length as `shares`. The
 187: /// caller then evaluates p(0) = sum_i y_i * basis[i] over GF(2^8).
 188: ///
 189: /// Key optimization: when reconstructing a multi-byte secret, this
 190: /// computation is done ONCE per share-set (not once per byte) — the
 191: /// basis depends only on the x-values, which are constant across
 192: /// every byte of the secret. This turns the per-byte reconstruction
 193: /// cost from O(K^2) gf multiplications down to O(K) (just the
 194: /// final inner-product step).
 195: ///
 196: /// Uses table-based fast path (public-value operands).
 197: fn lagrange_basis_at_zero(shares: &[Share]) -> Vec<u8> {
 198:     let kk = shares.len();
 199:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(kk);
 200:     for i in 0..kk {
 201:         let xi = shares[i].x;
 202:         let mut num: u8 = 1;
 203:         let mut den: u8 = 1;
 204:         for j in 0..kk {
 205:             if i == j {
 206:                 continue;
 207:             }
 208:             let xj = shares[j].x;
 209:             num = gf_mul_fast(num, xj);
 210:             // gf_sub == XOR in GF(2^8).
 211:             den = gf_mul_fast(den, xi ^ xj);
 212:         }
 213:         out.push(gf_div_fast(num, den));
 214:     }
 215:     out
 216: }
 217: 
 218: /// Reconstruct a multi-byte secret from `k` share-streams. Each stream is
 219: /// keyed by its x-value via the parallel `xs` vector — `xs[i]` is the x
 220: /// value for `streams[i]`. Streams must all have the same length.
 221: ///
 222: /// # Errors
 223: /// Same as [`reconstruct_byte`], plus length-mismatch errors.
 224: pub fn reconstruct_bytes(
 225:     xs: &[u8],
 226:     streams: &[&[u8]],
 227:     k: u32,
 228: ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, ShareError> {
 229:     if xs.len() != streams.len() {
 230:         return Err(ShareError::NotEnoughShares {
 231:             have: xs.len().min(streams.len()),
 232:             need: k,
 233:         });
 234:     }
 235:     if (xs.len() as u32) < k {
 236:         return Err(ShareError::NotEnoughShares {
 237:             have: xs.len(),
 238:             need: k,
 239:         });
 240:     }
 241:     let n_bytes = streams[0].len();
 242:     for s in streams {
 243:         if s.len() != n_bytes {
 244:             // Treat length mismatch as "not enough usable data".
 245:             return Err(ShareError::NotEnoughShares {
 246:                 have: s.len(),
 247:                 need: n_bytes as u32,
 248:             });
 249:         }
 250:     }
 251:     // Optimization: the Lagrange basis depends only on x-values,
 252:     // which are constant across every byte of the secret. Compute
 253:     // once, reuse for every byte. Turns the per-byte cost from
 254:     // O(K^2) GF muls down to O(K) muls — a big win for multi-byte
 255:     // secrets like the 32-byte identity master key (typical case).
 256:     let kk = k as usize;
 257:     // Reuse validation + basis-prep logic from the single-byte path.
 258:     let zero_b_shares: Vec<Share> =
 259:         xs[..kk].iter().map(|&x| Share::new(x, 0)).collect();
 260:     // Validate share x-values once.
 261:     for sh in &zero_b_shares {
 262:         if sh.x == 0 {
 263:             return Err(ShareError::InvalidShareX);
 264:         }
 265:     }
 266:     for i in 0..kk {
 267:         for j in (i + 1)..kk {
 268:             if zero_b_shares[i].x == zero_b_shares[j].x {
 269:                 return Err(ShareError::DuplicateShareX);
 270:             }
 271:         }
 272:     }
 273:     let basis = lagrange_basis_at_zero(&zero_b_shares);
 274:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(n_bytes);
 275:     for b in 0..n_bytes {
 276:         let mut acc: u32 = 0;
 277:         for i in 0..kk {
 278:             acc = gf_add(acc, u32::from(gf_mul_fast(streams[i][b], basis[i])));
 279:         }
 280:         out.push((acc & 0xFF) as u8);
 281:     }
 282:     Ok(out)
 283: }
 284: 
 285: 
 286: /// Horner's method polynomial evaluation in GF(2^8).
 287: /// `coeffs[0] + coeffs[1]*x + coeffs[2]*x^2 + ...`
 288: fn poly_eval(coeffs: &[u32], x: u32) -> u32 {
 289:     if coeffs.is_empty() {
 290:         return 0;
 291:     }
 292:     let mut acc = coeffs[coeffs.len() - 1] & 0xFF;
 293:     for i in (0..coeffs.len() - 1).rev() {
 294:         let c = coeffs[i] & 0xFF;
 295:         acc = gf_add(gf_mul(acc, x), c);
 296:     }
 297:     acc & 0xFF
 298: }

   1: //! Adversarial test vectors — known-attack inputs that any correct
   2: //! threshold-recovery implementation must handle gracefully.
   3: //!
   4: //! Catches regressions that random property-based testing might miss:
   5: //! degenerate parameter combinations, structurally-crafted shares,
   6: //! boundary-condition secret content.
   7: 
   8: use ol_threshold_recovery::field_bound::{
   9:     field_bound_reconstruct, field_bound_split, FieldBindingError, FieldWitness,
  10: };
  11: use ol_threshold_recovery::prng::PrngState;

  30: #[test]
  31: fn adversarial_all_zero_shares() {
  32:     // If an attacker supplies all-zero shares, reconstruct should
  33:     // not crash. Returns whatever Lagrange gives at x = 0 over a
  34:     // constant-0 polynomial (which is 0). Either way: no panic.
  35:     let s = vec![
  36:         Share::new(1, 0),
  37:         Share::new(2, 0),
  38:         Share::new(3, 0),
  39:     ];
  40:     let r = reconstruct_byte(&s, 3);
  41:     assert!(r.is_ok());
  42:     // Polynomial through (1,0), (2,0), (3,0) is identically 0.
  43:     // So p(0) = 0.
  44:     assert_eq!(r.unwrap(), 0);
  45: }

 143: #[test]
 144: fn adversarial_field_bound_attacker_swaps_witness_components() {
 145:     // Real witness, attacker supplies wrong (a) epoch (b) holder score
 146:     // (c) field seed. Each MUST fail recovery.
 147:     let secret = b"32-byte master Ed25519 seed!!!!\x00";
 148:     let real_seed = [0x42u8; 32];
 149:     let real_scores = vec![0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50];
 150:     let real_epoch = 1_700_000_000u64;
 151:     let real = FieldWitness {
 152:         field_seed: real_seed,
 153:         holder_scores: real_scores.clone(),
 154:         epoch_ns: real_epoch,
 155:     };
 156:     let mut st = PrngState::new(0xCAFE);
 157:     let masked = field_bound_split(secret, 3, 5, &mut st, &real).unwrap();
 158:     let xs = vec![1u8, 2, 3];
 159:     let supplied: Vec<&[u8]> = masked[..3].iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
 160:     let indices = vec![0usize, 1, 2];
 161: 
 162:     // (a) Wrong epoch.
 163:     let mut wrong_epoch = real.clone();
 164:     wrong_epoch.epoch_ns = real_epoch.wrapping_add(1);
 165:     let r = field_bound_reconstruct(&xs, &supplied, &indices, 3, &wrong_epoch).unwrap();
 166:     assert_ne!(r, secret);
 167: 
 168:     // (b) Wrong score (one byte changed in one float).
 169:     let mut wrong_scores = real.clone();
 170:     wrong_scores.holder_scores[0] += f64::EPSILON; // smallest perturbation
 171:     let r = field_bound_reconstruct(&xs, &supplied, &indices, 3, &wrong_scores).unwrap();
 172:     assert_ne!(r, secret);
 173: 
 174:     // (c) Wrong seed (single byte flip).
 175:     let mut wrong_seed = real.clone();
 176:     wrong_seed.field_seed[0] ^= 1;
 177:     let r = field_bound_reconstruct(&xs, &supplied, &indices, 3, &wrong_seed).unwrap();
 178:     assert_ne!(r, secret);
 179: }

   1: //! Cross-validation against canonical AES test vectors + exhaustive
   2: //! edge cases. Catches any drift in gf_mul / gf_inv / share format.
   3: 
   4: use ol_threshold_recovery::gf256::{gf_inv, gf_mul, gf_pow};

  11: // ── AES test vectors (FIPS 197 GF(2^8) multiplication) ────────────
  12: 
  13: #[test]
  14: fn aes_mul_classic_vectors() {
  15:     // FIPS 197 §4.2.1 — classic AES MixColumns test vector chain.
  16:     // 0x53 * 0xCA = 0x01 (canonical inverse pair in AES GF(2^8)).
  17:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0x53, 0xCA), 0x01);
  18:     // 0x57 * 0x83 = 0xC1 (AES standard test pair).
  19:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0x57, 0x83), 0xC1);
  20:     // 0xD4 * 0x02 = 0xB3 (xtime equivalent).
  21:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0xD4, 0x02), 0xB3);
  22:     // 0xBF * 0x03 = 0xDA (xtime + add).
  23:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0xBF, 0x03), 0xDA);
  24: }
  25: 
  26: #[test]
  27: fn aes_inverse_classic_pair() {
  28:     // 0x53 and 0xCA are multiplicative inverses in AES GF(2^8).
  29:     assert_eq!(gf_inv(0x53), 0xCA);
  30:     assert_eq!(gf_inv(0xCA), 0x53);
  31: }
  32: 
  33: #[test]
  34: fn aes_xtime_consistency() {
  35:     // xtime(x) in AES is x * 0x02. Walk a small chain:
  36:     // xtime(0x57) = 0xAE; xtime(0xAE) = 0x47 (since high bit set, XOR 0x1B).
  37:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0x57, 0x02), 0xAE);
  38:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0xAE, 0x02), 0x47);
  39:     // xtime(0x47) = 0x8E (no reduction needed).
  40:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0x47, 0x02), 0x8E);
  41:     // xtime(0x8E) = 0x07 (high bit set; 0x11C ^ 0x11B = 0x07).
  42:     assert_eq!(gf_mul(0x8E, 0x02), 0x07);
  43: }
  44: 
  45: #[test]
  46: fn inverse_canonical_pairs() {
  47:     // Spot-check well-known canonical AES inverse pairs.
  48:     // 0x53 ↔ 0xCA is the textbook AES S-box example pair.
  49:     // 0x01 is the self-inverse (1 * 1 = 1 in any field).
  50:     let canonical = [(0x01u32, 0x01u32), (0x53, 0xCA), (0xCA, 0x53)];
  51:     for (a, expected) in canonical {
  52:         assert_eq!(gf_inv(a), expected, "gf_inv(0x{a:02X})");
  53:     }
  54: }
  55: 
  56: #[test]
  57: fn inverse_property_all_nonzero() {
  58:     // Exhaustive: a * a^-1 == 1 for every nonzero a. This is the
  59:     // canonical correctness check — passing it means the inverse
  60:     // table is fully consistent regardless of which specific
  61:     // textbook table values we trust.
  62:     for a in 1u32..256 {
  63:         let inv = gf_inv(a);
  64:         assert_eq!(gf_mul(a, inv), 1, "a=0x{a:02X} inv=0x{inv:02X}");
  65:         // Inverse is its own inverse.
  66:         assert_eq!(gf_inv(inv), a, "double-inv mismatch for a=0x{a:02X}");
  67:     }
  68: }
  69: 
  70: #[test]
  71: fn pow_matches_repeated_mul() {
  72:     // gf_pow(a, e) == a * a * ... e times. Spot-check.
  73:     for a in [0x02u32, 0x57, 0xA5] {
  74:         let mut expected = 1u32;
  75:         for e in 0..32u32 {
  76:             assert_eq!(gf_pow(a, e), expected, "a=0x{a:02X} e={e}");
  77:             expected = gf_mul(expected, a);
  78:         }
  79:     }
  80: }

 154: #[test]
 155: fn k_equals_n_requires_all_shares() {
 156:     // K = N: any single missing share makes recovery impossible
 157:     // (mathematically: not enough points to interpolate degree-(K-1)
 158:     // polynomial). Reconstruction with fewer than K returns the
 159:     // not-enough-shares error.
 160:     let mut st = PrngState::new(0xDEAD_BEEF);
 161:     let shares = share_byte(0x42, 3, 3, &mut st).unwrap();
 162:     assert_eq!(reconstruct_byte(&shares, 3).unwrap(), 0x42);
 163:     // Only 2 shares: error.
 164:     let sub = vec![shares[0], shares[1]];
 165:     let err = reconstruct_byte(&sub, 3).unwrap_err();
 166:     assert!(matches!(
 167:         err,
 168:         ol_threshold_recovery::shamir::ShareError::NotEnoughShares { .. }
 169:     ));
 170: }

 199: fn duplicate_share_recovery_fails() {

 202:     // one constraint).

 204:     let shares = share_byte(0x42, 2, 3, &mut st).unwrap();
 205:     let dup = vec![shares[0], shares[0]];

 213: #[test]
 214: fn share_y_distribution_not_constant() {
 215:     // For K >= 2, share y-values should NOT all equal the secret —
 216:     // otherwise the polynomial is degree-0 and the scheme leaks the
 217:     // secret directly. Sanity-check across many seeds.
 218:     let secret = 0x42u8;
 219:     let mut differ_count = 0;
 220:     for seed in 0u64..32 {
 221:         let mut st = PrngState::new(seed);
 222:         let shares = share_byte(secret, 3, 5, &mut st).unwrap();
 223:         for sh in &shares {
 224:             if sh.y != secret {
 225:                 differ_count += 1;
 226:             }
 227:         }
 228:     }
 229:     // Across 32 seeds * 5 shares = 160 shares, at most a vanishing
 230:     // fraction should accidentally equal the secret.
 231:     assert!(
 232:         differ_count >= 150,
 233:         "share y == secret happened too often: {differ_count} / 160"
 234:     );
 235: }
 236: 
 237: #[test]
 238: fn share_round_trip_preserves_order() {
 239:     let mut st = PrngState::new(0xF00D);
 240:     let shares = share_byte(0x42, 2, 4, &mut st).unwrap();
 241:     // Reconstructing with shares in different orders gives the same
 242:     // secret (Lagrange is order-independent).
 243:     let s1 = vec![shares[0], shares[1]];
 244:     let s2 = vec![shares[1], shares[0]];
 245:     assert_eq!(
 246:         reconstruct_byte(&s1, 2).unwrap(),
 247:         reconstruct_byte(&s2, 2).unwrap()
 248:     );
 249: }

   1: //! Constant-time validation for `gf_mul`.
   2: //!
   3: //! The promise: `gf_mul(a, b)` runs in the same number of cycles
   4: //! regardless of `a` and `b` (no data-dependent branches; masked XOR
   5: //! instead of `if y_lsb { ... }`). This test measures wall-clock
   6: //! variance across operand distributions and gates at < 5% relative
   7: //! standard deviation.
   8: //!
   9: //! Wall-clock measurement is noisy — CPU cache, scheduling, frequency
  10: //! scaling all add variance — so the gate is loose (5% relative
  11: //! stddev). The TIGHT gate would be `dudect` or `cpucycles`-based
  12: //! cycle-accurate measurement; that's a follow-up for the
  13: //! constant-time audit sweep tracked in Phase C.
  14: //!
  15: //! What this catches RIGHT NOW: any future "optimization" that adds
  16: //! a data-dependent branch to gf_mul (e.g., "skip when y == 0")
  17: //! creates a measurable timing spike that bumps stddev > 5%.
  18: 
  19: use std::time::Instant;
  20: 
  21: use ol_threshold_recovery::gf256::gf_mul;
  22: 
  23: const SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET: usize = 50_000;
  24: const BUCKETS: usize = 16;
  25: 
  26: fn measure_ns(a: u32, b: u32, n: usize) -> u128 {
  27:     let start = Instant::now();
  28:     let mut acc: u32 = 0;
  29:     for _ in 0..n {
  30:         // Use the accumulator so the optimiser can't dead-code-eliminate.
  31:         acc = gf_mul(a.wrapping_add(acc & 0xFF), b);
  32:     }
  33:     let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_nanos();
  34:     // Black-box the accumulator.
  35:     std::hint::black_box(acc);
  36:     elapsed
  37: }
  38: 
  39: #[test]
  40: fn gf_mul_constant_time_across_operand_buckets() {
  41:     // 16 buckets of distinct (a, b) operand pairs spanning the full
  42:     // GF(2^8) range. Measure SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET multiplications per
  43:     // bucket; compute relative stddev across the 16 wall-clock totals.
  44:     let pairs: [(u32, u32); BUCKETS] = [
  45:         (0x00, 0x00),
  46:         (0x00, 0xFF),
  47:         (0xFF, 0x00),
  48:         (0xFF, 0xFF),
  49:         (0x01, 0x80),
  50:         (0x80, 0x01),
  51:         (0x55, 0xAA),
  52:         (0xAA, 0x55),
  53:         (0x57, 0x83),
  54:         (0x53, 0xCA),
  55:         (0x10, 0x20),
  56:         (0x42, 0x42),
  57:         (0x7F, 0x80),
  58:         (0xFE, 0x01),
  59:         (0x33, 0xCC),
  60:         (0x99, 0x66),
  61:     ];
  62: 
  63:     // Warm-up pass to stabilise CPU frequency scaling + caches.
  64:     for &(a, b) in &pairs {
  65:         let _ = measure_ns(a, b, 10_000);
  66:     }
  67: 
  68:     let mut totals: Vec<f64> = Vec::with_capacity(BUCKETS);
  69:     for &(a, b) in &pairs {
  70:         let ns = measure_ns(a, b, SAMPLES_PER_BUCKET) as f64;
  71:         totals.push(ns);
  72:     }
  73: 
  74:     let mean: f64 = totals.iter().sum::<f64>() / totals.len() as f64;
  75:     let variance: f64 = totals
  76:         .iter()
  77:         .map(|t| (t - mean).powi(2))
  78:         .sum::<f64>()
  79:         / totals.len() as f64;
  80:     let stddev = variance.sqrt();
  81:     let rel_stddev = stddev / mean;
  82: 
  83:     println!(
  84:         "gf_mul timing: mean={:.0}ns stddev={:.0}ns rel={:.2}%",
  85:         mean,
  86:         stddev,
  87:         rel_stddev * 100.0
  88:     );
  89:     // Gate: < 5% relative stddev. Loose because wall-clock noise on
  90:     // a dev workstation is real; tightening requires cycle-accurate
  91:     // measurement (dudect / cpucycles), tracked separately.
  92:     assert!(
  93:         rel_stddev < 0.05,
  94:         "gf_mul timing varies > 5% across operand buckets: rel_stddev={:.2}%",
  95:         rel_stddev * 100.0
  96:     );
  97: }

   1: //! Property tests for ol_threshold_recovery.
   2: //!
   3: //! Gate ladder (matches Phase C / D conventions):
   4: //!   - Default CI cadence: 100k plain-Shamir + 20k field-bound +
   5: //!     10k wrong-witness — ~few seconds wall time.
   6: //!   - Nightly gate: set `ONE_LINK_F1_GATE=1` to crank to 1M / 200k /
   7: //!     100k. Matches the Phase C macaroon "1M random delegation
   8: //!     chains" cadence.
   9: 
  10: use proptest::prelude::*;
  11: 
  12: use ol_threshold_recovery::field_bound::{
  13:     field_bound_reconstruct, field_bound_split, FieldWitness,
  14: };

  16: use ol_threshold_recovery::shamir::{
  17:     reconstruct_bytes, share_bytes,

  20: fn nightly_gate() -> bool {
  21:     std::env::var("ONE_LINK_F1_GATE")
  22:         .map(|v| v == "1" || v.to_lowercase() == "true")
  23:         .unwrap_or(false)
  24: }

  26: fn plain_cases() -> u32 {
  27:     // CI default 100k -> 1M to match Phase C macaroon 1M-delegation gate.
  28:     if nightly_gate() { 5_000_000 } else { 1_000_000 }
  29: }
  30:

  32:     // CI default 20k -> 200k (10x field_bound is more expensive per iter).
  33:     if nightly_gate() { 1_000_000 } else { 200_000 }
  34: }

  41: // Plain Shamir round-trip: split (K, N) on a random secret, reconstruct
  42: // from a random K-sized subset of the shares.
  43: proptest! {
  44:     #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig {
  45:         cases: plain_cases(),
  46:         max_global_rejects: plain_cases() * 4,
  47:         .. ProptestConfig::default()

  50:     #[test]
  51:     fn plain_shamir_roundtrip(
  52:         secret in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 1usize..=256),
  53:         seed in any::<u64>(),
  54:         kn in (1u32..=10, 1u32..=10),
  55:     ) {
  56:         let (k, n) = (kn.0.min(kn.1), kn.1);
  57:         // Skip degenerate params.
  58:         prop_assume!(k >= 1 && k <= n && n <= 255);
  59:         let mut st = PrngState::new(seed);
  60:         let streams = share_bytes(&secret, k, n, &mut st).unwrap();
  61:         // Pick K shares (the first K — they're all equivalent).
  62:         let xs: Vec<u8> = (1..=k as u8).collect();
  63:         let refs: Vec<&[u8]> = streams[..k as usize]
  64:             .iter()
  65:             .map(Vec::as_slice)
  66:             .collect();
  67:         let recovered = reconstruct_bytes(&xs, &refs, k).unwrap();
  68:         prop_assert_eq!(recovered, secret);
  69:     }
  70: }
  71: 
  72: // Field-bound round-trip: split + masked reconstruct with the same
  73: // witness. Smaller iter count because the OTP derivation per share is
  74: // extra work.
  75: proptest! {
  76:     #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig {
  77:         cases: field_cases(),
  78:         max_global_rejects: field_cases() * 4,
  79:         .. ProptestConfig::default()

  82:     #[test]
  83:     fn field_bound_roundtrip_random_witness(
  84:         secret in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 1usize..=128),
  85:         seed in any::<u64>(),
  86:         field_seed in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
  87:         epoch in any::<u64>(),
  88:         kn in (2u32..=8, 2u32..=8),
  89:         score_seed in any::<u64>(),
  90:     ) {
  91:         let (k, n) = (kn.0.min(kn.1), kn.1);
  92:         prop_assume!(k >= 2 && k <= n && n <= 32);
  93:         // Deterministically derive holder scores from score_seed so the
  94:         // proptest is reproducible per case.
  95:         let mut score_prng = PrngState::new(score_seed);
  96:         let holder_scores: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
  97:             .map(|_| score_prng.next_u64() as f64 / (u64::MAX as f64))
  98:             .collect();
  99:         let witness = FieldWitness {
 100:             field_seed,
 101:             holder_scores,
 102:             epoch_ns: epoch,
 103:         };
 104:         let mut st = PrngState::new(seed);
 105:         let masked = field_bound_split(&secret, k, n, &mut st, &witness)
 106:             .expect("split");
 107:         let xs: Vec<u8> = (1..=k as u8).collect();
 108:         let supplied: Vec<&[u8]> =
 109:             masked[..k as usize].iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
 110:         let indices: Vec<usize> = (0..k as usize).collect();
 111:         let recovered = field_bound_reconstruct(
 112:             &xs, &supplied, &indices, k, &witness,
 113:         )
 114:         .expect("reconstruct");
 115:         prop_assert_eq!(recovered, secret);
 116:     }
 117: }
 118: 
 119: // Wrong-witness must NOT reconstruct the secret with overwhelming
 120: // probability. This is the alien-tech security gate.
 121: proptest! {
 122:     #![proptest_config(ProptestConfig {
 123:         cases: wrong_witness_cases(),
 124:         .. ProptestConfig::default()
 125:     })]
 126: 
 127:     #[test]
 128:     fn wrong_witness_doesnt_recover(
 129:         secret in prop::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 16usize..=64),
 130:         seed in any::<u64>(),
 131:         real_field_seed in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 132:         fake_field_seed in any::<[u8; 32]>(),
 133:         epoch in any::<u64>(),
 134:     ) {
 135:         prop_assume!(real_field_seed != fake_field_seed);
 136:         let n = 5u32;
 137:         let k = 3u32;
 138:         let holder_scores = vec![0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.4, 0.8];
 139:         let real_witness = FieldWitness {
 140:             field_seed: real_field_seed,
 141:             holder_scores: holder_scores.clone(),
 142:             epoch_ns: epoch,
 143:         };
 144:         let fake_witness = FieldWitness {
 145:             field_seed: fake_field_seed,
 146:             holder_scores,
 147:             epoch_ns: epoch,
 148:         };
 149:         let mut st = PrngState::new(seed);
 150:         let masked = field_bound_split(&secret, k, n, &mut st, &real_witness)
 151:             .expect("split");
 152:         let xs = vec![1u8, 2, 3];
 153:         let supplied: Vec<&[u8]> = vec![
 154:             masked[0].as_slice(),
 155:             masked[1].as_slice(),
 156:             masked[2].as_slice(),
 157:         ];
 158:         let indices = vec![0usize, 1, 2];
 159:         let recovered = field_bound_reconstruct(
 160:             &xs, &supplied, &indices, k, &fake_witness,
 161:         )
 162:         .expect("reconstruct");
 163:         // With overwhelming probability the wrong witness produces
 164:         // gibberish — i.e. at least one byte differs from the true
 165:         // secret. (Probability all bytes coincidentally match is
 166:         // 2^{-8*n_bytes}, negligible at >= 16 bytes.)
 167:         prop_assert_ne!(recovered, secret);
 168:     }
 169: }

   1: # ol_threshold_recovery wired-path bench results
   2: 
   3: Captured against `0.21.0-alpha.0` on Windows 11 Intel host, Python 3.14.
   4: 
   5: `tests/unit/test_threshold_recovery_native_vs_python.py` enforces:
   6: 1. Round-trip correctness against parameter sweep (11 (secret_len, k, n)
   7:    triples × 20 random secrets each).
   8: 2. Cross-implementation interop (native split ↔ Python combine, and
   9:    vice versa).
  10: 3. Speedup gate: native path is ≥2× faster than pure-Python on a
  11:    32-byte secret at (k=3, n=5). Test fails CI if regression drops
  12:    the ratio below 2×.
  13: 
  14: ## Captured numbers
  15: 
  16: For a 32-byte master seed at (k=3, n=5), 100 iterations:
  17: 
  18: | Operation        | Native      | Pure-Python | Speedup        |
  19: |---               |---          |---          |---             |
  20: | `split_compat`   | 0.37 ms     | 4.33 ms     | **11.8 ×**     |
  21: | `combine_compat` | 0.19 ms     | 4.88 ms     | **25.5 ×**     |
  22: 
  23: ## What this means for the daemon
  24: 
  25: Social-recovery wrap-shares for the master seed costs ~4 µs per share
  26: in the native path vs ~43 µs per share in pure-Python. For a 3-of-5
  27: recovery (the default), that's:
  28: 
  29: - Native: ~2 µs split + ~2 µs combine = under 5 µs of crypto.
  30: - Pure-Python fallback: ~22 µs split + ~50 µs combine = ~70 µs.
  31: 
  32: Both are sub-millisecond — the wiring isn't load-bearing for latency.
  33: The speedup matters when many seeds get split (e.g., capability
  34: escrow at high fanout) and as a CI canary: if a future change drops
  35: the native path below 2×, something has regressed.
  36: 
  37: ## Repro
  38: 
  39: ```text
  40: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_threshold_recovery_native_vs_python.py -s
  41: ```

   1: //! Loopback latency benchmarks for `ol_transfer::TransferEngine`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Pins the Phase B baseline for the integrated chunk-fetch path:
   4: //!
   5: //! - `fetch_chunk_local` — the chunk is already in the receiver's store
   6: //!   (no transport round trip). Measures the read-local fast path.
   7: //! - `fetch_chunk_warm` — fresh fetch from a paired peer over a warm
   8: //!   cached connection. Measures the QUIC round-trip + chunk_store
   9: //!   append + flush cost.
  10: //! - `fetch_many_warm_serial` — 16 chunks fetched serially over a warm
  11: //!   connection. Measures throughput on a small batch.
  12: //! - `bloom_handshake_warm` — bloom round trip with a 1000-chunk

 158:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("transfer_fetch");
 159:     group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes(1024));
 160:     group.bench_function("fetch_chunk_warm_1KiB", |b| {
 161:         // Setup once outside the iter so we measure steady-state per-fetch latency.
 162:         let fx = rt.block_on(setup_pair(rt.handle(), 10_000, 1024));
 163:         let mut i = 0u32;
 164:         b.iter(|| {
 165:             let idx = (i as usize) % fx.chunk_ids.len();
 166:             rt.block_on(async {
 167:                 let _ = fx
 168:                     .bob_engine
 169:                     .fetch_chunk(&fx.alice_fp, &fx.chunk_ids[idx])
 170:                     .await
 171:                     .unwrap();
 172:             });
 173:             i = i.wrapping_add(1);
 174:         });
 175:     });
 176:     group.finish();
 177: }

 179: fn bench_bloom_handshake_warm(c: &mut Criterion) {
 180:     let rt = Runtime::new().unwrap();
