 182: 
 183:     // Bob has a subset of the same chunks (the first 500).

 199: /// Compare `fetch_chunk_fountain` vs `fetch_chunk` (single ChunkResponse)
 200: /// on loopback. On a no-loss link, fountain has wire overhead from the
 201: /// FountainPacket header (~4.4% per symbol) + extra symbols beyond K
 202: /// for decode safety. This bench tells us how much that costs.
 203: fn bench_fountain_vs_warm(c: &mut Criterion) {
 204:     let rt = Runtime::new().unwrap();
 205: 
 206:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("fountain_vs_warm");
 207:     // 16 KiB chunk = K=16 source symbols at 1 KiB. Big enough for the
 208:     // fountain overhead to be visible; small enough to keep the bench
 209:     // fast.
 210:     let chunk_bytes = 16 * 1024u32;
 211:     group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes(chunk_bytes as u64));
 212: 
 213:     group.bench_function("warm_chunk_response_16KiB", |b| {
 214:         let fx = rt.block_on(setup_pair(rt.handle(), 10_000, chunk_bytes));
 215:         let mut i = 0u32;
 216:         b.iter(|| {
 217:             let idx = (i as usize) % fx.chunk_ids.len();
 218:             rt.block_on(async {
 219:                 let _ = fx
 220:                     .bob_engine
 221:                     .fetch_chunk(&fx.alice_fp, &fx.chunk_ids[idx])
 222:                     .await
 223:                     .unwrap();
 224:             });
 225:             i = i.wrapping_add(1);
 226:         });
 227:     });
 228: 
 229:     group.bench_function("fountain_16KiB", |b| {
 230:         let fx = rt.block_on(setup_pair(rt.handle(), 10_000, chunk_bytes));
 231:         let mut i = 0u32;
 232:         b.iter(|| {

 242:         });
 243:     });

 248: /// Compare `bloom_handshake_scoped` vs `bloom_handshake` on a server
 249: /// with a large memtable (10K chunks) where the want_list is small
 250: /// (100 chunks). Scoped path should crush the full-scan path because
 251: /// it doesn't walk the server's 10K chunks.
 252: fn bench_scoped_vs_full_bloom(c: &mut Criterion) {
 253:     let rt = Runtime::new().unwrap();
 254:     let fx = rt.block_on(setup_pair(rt.handle(), 10_000, 1024));
 255: 
 256:     // Bob has a subset of 100 chunks; want_list is 200 chunks (50% missing).
 257:     let bob_have: Vec<[u8; 32]> = fx.chunk_ids.iter().take(100).copied().collect();
 258:     let want_list: Vec<[u8; 32]> = fx.chunk_ids.iter().take(200).copied().collect();
 259: 
 260:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("scoped_vs_full_bloom");
 261: 
 262:     group.bench_function("full_scan_10k_server", |b| {
 263:         b.iter(|| {
 264:             rt.block_on(async {
 265:                 let _missing = fx
 266:                     .bob_engine
 267:                     .bloom_handshake(&fx.alice_fp, &bob_have)
 268:                     .await
 269:                     .unwrap();
 270:             });
 271:         });
 272:     });
 273: 
 274:     group.bench_function("scoped_200_want_10k_server", |b| {
 275:         b.iter(|| {
 276:             rt.block_on(async {
 277:                 let _missing = fx
 278:                     .bob_engine
 279:                     .bloom_handshake_scoped(&fx.alice_fp, &bob_have, &want_list)
 280:                     .await
 281:                     .unwrap();
 282:             });
 283:         });
 284:     });
 285: 
 286:     group.finish();
 287: }
 288: 
 289: /// Group-commit win: 32 chunks via `fetch_many` (1 fsync) vs 32
 290: /// sequential `fetch_chunk` calls (32 fsyncs).
 291: fn bench_group_commit_win(c: &mut Criterion) {
 292:     let rt = Runtime::new().unwrap();
 293:     const BATCH: u32 = 32;
 294: 
 295:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("group_commit");
 296:     group.throughput(Throughput::Elements(BATCH as u64));
 297: 
 298:     group.bench_function("fetch_many_batched_x32", |b| {
 299:         // Fresh fixture per measurement so each iter has un-fetched chunks.
 300:         b.iter_with_setup(
 301:             || rt.block_on(setup_pair(rt.handle(), BATCH, 1024)),
 302:             |fx| {
 303:                 rt.block_on(async {
 304:                     let outcomes = fx
 305:                         .bob_engine
 306:                         .fetch_many(&fx.alice_fp, fx.chunk_ids.clone())
 307:                         .await
 308:                         .unwrap();
 309:                     assert_eq!(outcomes.len(), BATCH as usize);
 310:                 });
 311:             },
 312:         );
 313:     });
 314: 
 315:     group.bench_function("sequential_fetch_chunk_x32", |b| {
 316:         b.iter_with_setup(
 317:             || rt.block_on(setup_pair(rt.handle(), BATCH, 1024)),
 318:             |fx| {
 319:                 rt.block_on(async {
 320:                     for cid in &fx.chunk_ids {
 321:                         let _ = fx.bob_engine.fetch_chunk(&fx.alice_fp, cid).await.unwrap();
 322:                     }
 323:                 });
 324:             },
 325:         );
 326:     });
 327:     group.finish();
 328: }

   1: //! `TransferConfig` knobs for the engine.

   5: /// Configuration for [`crate::TransferEngine`].
   6: ///
   7: /// Defaults are chosen per [ADR-0013](../../../docs/decisions/0013-transfer-engine.md).
   8: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
   9: pub struct TransferConfig {

  11:     /// fetches wait via a semaphore. Default 32.

  13: 
  14:     /// How long to wait for a single chunk request before failing.

  16:     /// peer should reply within this).

  18:

  24:     /// reused. Default matches the QUIC endpoint's `idle_timeout_ms`.
  25:     pub connection_idle_ms: u64,
  26: 
  27:     /// Bloom filter target false-positive rate for `bloom_handshake`.
  28:     /// Default 0.01 (1%) per ADR-0011.
  29:     pub bloom_target_fp: f64,
  30: }

   1: //! The [`TransferEngine`] type — owner of chunk_store + QUIC endpoint +
   2: //! peer registry. Implements [ADR-0013](../../../docs/decisions/0013-transfer-engine.md).
   3: 
   4: use std::collections::HashMap;
   5: use std::net::SocketAddr;
   6: use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock as StdRwLock};
   7: use std::time::Duration;
   8: 
   9: use ol_bloom::Bloom;
  10: use ol_chunk_store::{ChunkRecord, ChunkStore};
  11: use ol_fountain::{FountainPacket, LtDecoder};
  12: use ol_quic::{
  13:     transport::{read_frame, write_frame},
  14:     Connection, Endpoint, Frame, FrameKind, PeerFingerprint,
  15: };
  16: use tokio::sync::RwLock;
  17: 
  18: use crate::config::TransferConfig;
  19: use crate::error::{hex_prefix_8, TransferError};
  20: use crate::outcome::FetchOutcome;
  21: use crate::peer::PeerEntry;
  22: use crate::wire;
  23: 
  24: /// The integrated transfer engine. One per daemon identity.
  25: ///
  26: /// `TransferEngine` is `Send + Sync`. Daemons typically hold an
  27: /// `Arc<TransferEngine>` and clone it freely between the inbound server
  28: /// task (started via [`TransferEngine::run_server`]) and the outbound
  29: /// fetch path.
  30: pub struct TransferEngine {
  31:     /// Local chunk store. `std::sync::Mutex` because all calls into the
  32:     /// store are sync I/O and we only hold the lock for short critical
  33:     /// sections — never across an `.await`.
  34:     pub(crate) store: Arc<StdRwLock<ChunkStore>>,
  35: 
  36:     /// QUIC endpoint. Either server+dialer (built via
  37:     /// `Endpoint::server_for_identity`) or dial-only.
  38:     pub(crate) endpoint: Arc<Endpoint>,
  39: 
  40:     /// Peer registry, keyed by fingerprint.
  41:     pub(crate) peers: RwLock<HashMap<PeerFingerprint, Arc<PeerEntry>>>,
  42: 
  43:     /// Engine config.
  44:     pub(crate) config: TransferConfig,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: impl std::fmt::Debug for TransferEngine {
  48:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  49:         f.debug_struct("TransferEngine")
  50:             .field("endpoint", &self.endpoint)
  51:             .field("config", &self.config)
  52:             .finish_non_exhaustive()
  53:     }
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl TransferEngine {
  57:     /// Open a new engine wrapping an existing chunk store + QUIC endpoint.
  58:     ///
  59:     /// Returns an `Arc<Self>` because the engine is designed to be shared
  60:     /// freely between the inbound server task and outbound fetch callers.
  61:     #[must_use]
  62:     pub fn new(
  63:         store: Arc<StdRwLock<ChunkStore>>,
  64:         endpoint: Arc<Endpoint>,
  65:         config: TransferConfig,
  66:     ) -> Arc<Self> {
  67:         Arc::new(Self {
  68:             store,
  69:             endpoint,
  70:             peers: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
  71:             config,
  72:         })
  73:     }
  74: 
  75:     /// Register a peer. Idempotent: re-registering with a different
  76:     /// address updates the address but preserves any cached connection.
  77:     ///
  78:     /// # Errors
  79:     ///
  80:     /// None at present; reserved for future validation.
  81:     pub async fn register_peer(
  82:         &self,
  83:         fingerprint: PeerFingerprint,
  84:         addr: SocketAddr,
  85:     ) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
  86:         let mut peers = self.peers.write().await;
  87:         if let Some(entry) = peers.get(&fingerprint) {
  88:             *entry.addr.lock().await = addr;
  89:         } else {
  90:             peers.insert(fingerprint, Arc::new(PeerEntry::new(addr, &self.config)));
  91:         }
  92:         Ok(())
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     /// Forget a peer. Closes any cached connection.
  96:     pub async fn forget_peer(&self, fingerprint: &PeerFingerprint) {
  97:         let entry = {
  98:             let mut peers = self.peers.write().await;
  99:             peers.remove(fingerprint)
 100:         };
 101:         if let Some(entry) = entry {
 102:             let mut conn = entry.connection.lock().await;
 103:             if let Some(c) = conn.take() {
 104:                 c.close(0, b"forget_peer");
 105:             }
 106:         }
 107:     }
 108: 
 109:     /// Snapshot of registered peer fingerprints. Diagnostic.
 110:     pub async fn known_peers(&self) -> Vec<PeerFingerprint> {
 111:         let peers = self.peers.read().await;
 112:         peers.keys().copied().collect()
 113:     }
 114: 
 115:     /// Snapshot of chunk-store stats (cheap; counters only).
 116:     #[must_use]
 117:     pub fn store_stats(&self) -> ol_chunk_store::StoreStats {
 118:         self.store.read().expect("store rwlock poisoned").stats()
 119:     }
 120: 
 121:     /// Snapshot of the engine's endpoint local address (diagnostic).
 122:     ///
 123:     /// # Errors
 124:     ///
 125:     /// Returns the underlying [`ol_quic::QuicError`] from the endpoint.
 126:     pub fn local_addr(&self) -> Result<SocketAddr, TransferError> {
 127:         Ok(self.endpoint.local_addr()?)
 128:     }
 129: 
 130:     /// Fetch a chunk from a peer if not already in the local store.
 131:     ///
 132:     /// Idempotent: if the chunk is already local, returns the cached
 133:     /// record without contacting the peer.
 134:     ///
 135:     /// # Errors
 136:     ///
 137:     /// - [`TransferError::PeerUnknown`] if the peer is not registered.
 138:     /// - [`TransferError::ChunkNotFound`] if the peer doesn't have the chunk.
 139:     /// - [`TransferError::Timeout`] if the request exceeds
 140:     ///   [`TransferConfig::chunk_request_timeout_ms`].
 141:     /// - [`TransferError::ProtocolViolation`] / [`TransferError::ChunkIdMismatch`]
 142:     ///   for a buggy or malicious peer.
 143:     /// - [`TransferError::Store`] / [`TransferError::Transport`] for the
 144:     ///   underlying I/O failures.
 145:     pub async fn fetch_chunk(
 146:         &self,
 147:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 148:         chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 149:     ) -> Result<ChunkRecord, TransferError> {
 150:         self.fetch_chunk_inner(peer, chunk_id, /* flush_on_write = */ true)
 151:             .await
 152:     }
 153: 
 154:     /// Variant of [`Self::fetch_chunk`] that defers the post-write
 155:     /// `flush` (fsync) for batched commit. The caller is responsible
 156:     /// for invoking [`Self::commit`] before treating the chunk as
 157:     /// durable. Used internally by [`Self::fetch_many`].
 158:     async fn fetch_chunk_no_flush(
 159:         &self,
 160:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 161:         chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 162:     ) -> Result<ChunkRecord, TransferError> {
 163:         self.fetch_chunk_inner(peer, chunk_id, /* flush_on_write = */ false)
 164:             .await
 165:     }
 166: 
 167:     async fn fetch_chunk_inner(
 168:         &self,
 169:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 170:         chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 171:         flush_on_write: bool,
 172:     ) -> Result<ChunkRecord, TransferError> {
 173:         if let Some(rec) = self.read_local(chunk_id) {
 174:             return Ok(rec);
 175:         }
 176: 
 177:         let entry = self.peer_entry(peer).await?;
 178:         let _permit = entry
 179:             .inflight
 180:             .clone()
 181:             .acquire_owned()
 182:             .await
 183:             .expect("semaphore not closed");
 184: 
 185:         let connection = self.connection_for(peer, &entry).await?;
 186: 
 187:         let request = Frame::new(
 188:             FrameKind::ChunkRequest,
 189:             wire::encode_chunk_request(chunk_id),
 190:         )?;
 191:         let reply = self
 192:             .send_request_with_timeout(&connection, request, self.config.chunk_request_timeout_ms)
 193:             .await?;
 194: 
 195:         match reply.kind {
 196:             FrameKind::ChunkResponse => {
 197:                 let (rec_kind, rec_flags, rec_payload) =
 198:                     wire::decode_chunk_response(&reply.payload)?;
 199:                 let record = ChunkRecord::decode(rec_kind, rec_flags, rec_payload)?;
 200:                 if &record.chunk_id != chunk_id {
 201:                     return Err(TransferError::ChunkIdMismatch {
 202:                         requested_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(chunk_id),
 203:                         got_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(&record.chunk_id),
 204:                     });
 205:                 }
 206:                 if flush_on_write {
 207:                     self.write_local(&record)?;
 208:                 } else {
 209:                     self.write_local_no_flush(&record)?;
 210:                 }
 211:                 Ok(record)
 212:             }
 213:             FrameKind::ChunkNotFound => {
 214:                 let got_id = wire::decode_chunk_not_found(&reply.payload)?;
 215:                 if &got_id != chunk_id {
 216:                     return Err(TransferError::ChunkIdMismatch {
 217:                         requested_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(chunk_id),
 218:                         got_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(&got_id),
 219:                     });
 220:                 }
 221:                 Err(TransferError::ChunkNotFound {
 222:                     chunk_id_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(chunk_id),
 223:                 })
 224:             }
 225:             other => Err(TransferError::ProtocolViolation {
 226:                 expected_kind: FrameKind::ChunkResponse,
 227:                 actual_kind: other,
 228:             }),
 229:         }
 230:     }
 231: 
 232:     /// Fetch many chunks from a peer with per-peer bounded concurrency.
 233:     ///
 234:     /// Returns one [`FetchOutcome`] per requested chunk_id, in the same
 235:     /// order as the input vector.
 236:     ///
 237:     /// Per-peer bandwidth is bounded by
 238:     /// [`TransferConfig::max_inflight_per_peer`].
 239:     ///
 240:     /// # Errors
 241:     ///
 242:     /// Returns early with [`TransferError::PeerUnknown`] if the peer
 243:     /// isn't registered. Individual chunk failures are surfaced via
 244:     /// [`FetchOutcome::Error`] in the result vector, not as a top-level
 245:     /// `Err`.
 246:     pub async fn fetch_many(
 247:         self: &Arc<Self>,
 248:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 249:         chunk_ids: Vec<[u8; 32]>,
 250:     ) -> Result<Vec<FetchOutcome>, TransferError> {
 251:         let entry = self.peer_entry(peer).await?;
 252:         // Eager connection setup so unreachable peers fail fast.
 253:         let _ = self.connection_for(peer, &entry).await?;
 254: 
 255:         let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(chunk_ids.len());
 256:         for cid in chunk_ids {
 257:             let engine = Arc::clone(self);
 258:             let peer_fp = *peer;
 259:             // Each task uses the no-flush write path; we batch-commit
 260:             // ONCE at the end. This amortizes the fsync across N chunks
 261:             // and is the primary cost of the wire-fetch hot path (per
 262:             // the bench baseline, a single fsync costs ~500 µs vs ~100
 263:             // µs for the QUIC round-trip itself).
 264:             let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
 265:                 match engine.fetch_chunk_no_flush(&peer_fp, &cid).await {
 266:                     Ok(rec) => FetchOutcome::Fetched {
 267:                         chunk_id: cid,
 268:                         length_plaintext: rec.length_plaintext,
 269:                     },
 270:                     Err(TransferError::ChunkNotFound { .. }) => {
 271:                         FetchOutcome::NotFound { chunk_id: cid }
 272:                     }
 273:                     Err(other) => FetchOutcome::Error {
 274:                         chunk_id: cid,
 275:                         err: other,
 276:                     },
 277:                 }
 278:             });
 279:             handles.push(handle);
 280:         }
 281: 
 282:         let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(handles.len());
 283:         for h in handles {
 284:             match h.await {
 285:                 Ok(outcome) => out.push(outcome),
 286:                 Err(join_err) => {
 287:                     return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
 288:                         kind: FrameKind::ChunkResponse,
 289:                         reason: if join_err.is_panic() {
 290:                             "fetch task panicked"
 291:                         } else {
 292:                             "fetch task cancelled"
 293:                         },
 294:                     });
 295:                 }
 296:             }
 297:         }
 298:         // Single batched fsync. After this returns, every Fetched
 299:         // outcome in `out` is durable.
 300:         if out
 301:             .iter()
 302:             .any(|o| matches!(o, FetchOutcome::Fetched { .. }))
 303:         {
 304:             self.commit()?;
 305:         }
 306:         Ok(out)
 307:     }
 308: 
 309:     /// Bloom-init handshake per ADR-0011 + ADR-0013.
 310:     ///
 311:     /// We build a Bloom filter from `local_chunk_ids` (the chunk_ids we
 312:     /// already have for the manifest scope), send it to the peer, and
 313:     /// receive back the list of chunk_ids the peer thinks we still need.
 314:     ///
 315:     /// # Errors
 316:     ///
 317:     /// - [`TransferError::PeerUnknown`]
 318:     /// - [`TransferError::Bloom`] on encode failure (filter too large).
 319:     /// - [`TransferError::ProtocolViolation`] if the peer doesn't reply
 320:     ///   with `MissingChunks`.
 321:     /// - [`TransferError::Timeout`] on
 322:     ///   [`TransferConfig::bloom_handshake_timeout_ms`].
 323:     pub async fn bloom_handshake(
 324:         &self,
 325:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 326:         local_chunk_ids: &[[u8; 32]],
 327:     ) -> Result<Vec<[u8; 32]>, TransferError> {
 328:         let entry = self.peer_entry(peer).await?;
 329:         let connection = self.connection_for(peer, &entry).await?;
 330: 
 331:         let mut bloom =
 332:             Bloom::with_target_fp(local_chunk_ids.len().max(1), self.config.bloom_target_fp);
 333:         for cid in local_chunk_ids {
 334:             bloom.insert(cid);
 335:         }
 336:         let encoded = bloom.encode()?;
 337:         let request = Frame::new(FrameKind::BloomFilter, encoded)?;
 338:         let reply = self
 339:             .send_request_with_timeout(&connection, request, self.config.bloom_handshake_timeout_ms)
 340:             .await?;
 341: 
 342:         match reply.kind {
 343:             FrameKind::MissingChunks => wire::decode_missing_chunks(&reply.payload),
 344:             other => Err(TransferError::ProtocolViolation {
 345:                 expected_kind: FrameKind::MissingChunks,
 346:                 actual_kind: other,
 347:             }),
 348:         }
 349:     }
 350: 
 351:     /// Fetch a chunk via LT-fountain delivery per ADR-0015.
 352:     ///
 353:     /// Opens a fresh bi-directional stream, sends a `FountainRequest`
 354:     /// frame carrying the chunk_id, then ingests the inbound stream of
 355:     /// `FountainBurst` frames until the LT decoder reconstructs the
 356:     /// chunk plaintext. Sends `FountainAck` to tell the sender to stop
 357:     /// emitting once decode succeeds.
 358:     ///
 359:     /// Use this in preference to [`Self::fetch_chunk`] on lossy or
 360:     /// many-receivers workloads where ARQ retransmission round-trips
 361:     /// would dominate latency.
 362:     ///
 363:     /// # Errors
 364:     ///
 365:     /// - [`TransferError::ChunkNotFound`] if the server has no such chunk.
 366:     /// - [`TransferError::ChunkIdMismatch`] if the decoded bytes hash to
 367:     ///   a different chunk_id than requested (catches buggy / malicious peer).
 368:     /// - [`TransferError::Timeout`] if the full decode exceeds the
 369:     ///   chunk request timeout.
 370:     /// - [`TransferError::Transport`] for QUIC stream errors.
 371:     pub async fn fetch_chunk_fountain(
 372:         &self,
 373:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 374:         chunk_id: &[u8; 32],
 375:     ) -> Result<ChunkRecord, TransferError> {
 376:         if let Some(rec) = self.read_local(chunk_id) {
 377:             return Ok(rec);
 378:         }
 379:         let entry = self.peer_entry(peer).await?;
 380:         let _permit = entry
 381:             .inflight
 382:             .clone()
 383:             .acquire_owned()
 384:             .await
 385:             .expect("semaphore not closed");
 386: 
 387:         let connection = self.connection_for(peer, &entry).await?;
 388:         let (mut send, mut recv) = connection
 389:             .open_bi_stream()
 390:             .await
 391:             .map_err(TransferError::Transport)?;
 392: 
 393:         // Request side.
 394:         let req = Frame::new(FrameKind::FountainRequest, chunk_id.to_vec())?;
 395:         write_frame(&mut send, &req)
 396:             .await
 397:             .map_err(TransferError::Transport)?;
 398: 
 399:         // Response loop with overall timeout.
 400:         let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now()
 401:             + Duration::from_millis(self.config.chunk_request_timeout_ms);
 402:         let mut decoder: Option<LtDecoder> = None;
 403:         let mut chunk_source_len: u32 = 0;
 404: 
 405:         loop {
 406:             let read_future = read_frame(&mut recv);
 407:             let frame = match tokio::time::timeout_at(deadline, read_future).await {
 408:                 Ok(Ok(f)) => f,
 409:                 Ok(Err(e)) => return Err(TransferError::Transport(e)),
 410:                 Err(_) => {
 411:                     return Err(TransferError::Timeout {
 412:                         timeout_ms: self.config.chunk_request_timeout_ms,
 413:                     });
 414:                 }
 415:             };
 416:             match frame.kind {
 417:                 FrameKind::FountainBurst => {
 418:                     let pkt = FountainPacket::decode(&frame.payload)?;
 419:                     if &pkt.chunk_id != chunk_id {
 420:                         return Err(TransferError::ChunkIdMismatch {
 421:                             requested_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(chunk_id),
 422:                             got_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(&pkt.chunk_id),
 423:                         });
 424:                     }
 425:                     let dec = decoder.get_or_insert_with(|| {
 426:                         chunk_source_len = pkt.source_length;
 427:                         LtDecoder::new(pkt.k, pkt.payload.len(), pkt.source_length as usize)
 428:                             .expect("packet parameters valid")
 429:                     });
 430:                     if dec.ingest(pkt.symbol_id, &pkt.payload)? {
 431:                         // Decode complete; tell sender to stop.
 432:                         let ack = Frame::new(FrameKind::FountainAck, chunk_id.to_vec())?;
 433:                         write_frame(&mut send, &ack)
 434:                             .await
 435:                             .map_err(TransferError::Transport)?;
 436:                         let _ = send.finish();
 437:                         break;
 438:                     }
 439:                 }
 440:                 FrameKind::ChunkNotFound => {
 441:                     return Err(TransferError::ChunkNotFound {
 442:                         chunk_id_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(chunk_id),
 443:                     });
 444:                 }
 445:                 other => {
 446:                     return Err(TransferError::ProtocolViolation {
 447:                         expected_kind: FrameKind::FountainBurst,
 448:                         actual_kind: other,
 449:                     });
 450:                 }
 451:             }
 452:         }
 453: 
 454:         let dec = decoder.expect("decoder created on first FountainBurst");
 455:         let source_bytes = dec.finish()?;
 456:         // Parse `(kind, flags, payload)` back into a ChunkRecord.
 457:         if source_bytes.len() < 2 {
 458:             return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
 459:                 kind: FrameKind::FountainBurst,
 460:                 reason: "decoded chunk source < 2 bytes",
 461:             });
 462:         }
 463:         let record = ChunkRecord::decode(source_bytes[0], source_bytes[1], &source_bytes[2..])?;
 464:         if &record.chunk_id != chunk_id {
 465:             return Err(TransferError::ChunkIdMismatch {
 466:                 requested_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(chunk_id),
 467:                 got_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(&record.chunk_id),
 468:             });
 469:         }
 470:         // Persist durably.
 471:         self.write_local(&record)?;
 472:         let _ = chunk_source_len; // silence unused-mut warning on early-decode path
 473:         Ok(record)
 474:     }
 475: 
 476:     /// Scoped bloom-init handshake per ADR-0011 v2.
 477:     ///
 478:     /// Sends both a Bloom of `already_have` AND an explicit `want_list`
 479:     /// of chunk_ids the client cares about. Server walks `want_list`
 480:     /// against the bloom and returns the missing subset — avoiding the
 481:     /// full memtable scan that [`Self::bloom_handshake`] triggers on
 482:     /// large servers.
 483:     ///
 484:     /// Use this when the client knows the manifest scope it's syncing
 485:     /// (the common case for shared folders). Fall back to
 486:     /// `bloom_handshake` only when the scope is "everything the server
 487:     /// has."
 488:     ///
 489:     /// # Errors
 490:     ///
 491:     /// - [`TransferError::PeerUnknown`]
 492:     /// - [`TransferError::Bloom`] on encode failure (filter too large).
 493:     /// - [`TransferError::ProtocolViolation`] if the peer doesn't reply
 494:     ///   with `MissingChunks`.
 495:     /// - [`TransferError::Timeout`] on
 496:     ///   [`TransferConfig::bloom_handshake_timeout_ms`].
 497:     pub async fn bloom_handshake_scoped(
 498:         &self,
 499:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 500:         already_have: &[[u8; 32]],
 501:         want_list: &[[u8; 32]],
 502:     ) -> Result<Vec<[u8; 32]>, TransferError> {
 503:         let entry = self.peer_entry(peer).await?;
 504:         let connection = self.connection_for(peer, &entry).await?;
 505: 
 506:         let mut bloom =
 507:             Bloom::with_target_fp(already_have.len().max(1), self.config.bloom_target_fp);
 508:         for cid in already_have {
 509:             bloom.insert(cid);
 510:         }
 511:         let bloom_bytes = bloom.encode()?;
 512:         let payload = wire::encode_scoped_bloom(want_list, &bloom_bytes);
 513:         let request = Frame::new(FrameKind::ScopedBloomFilter, payload)?;
 514:         let reply = self
 515:             .send_request_with_timeout(&connection, request, self.config.bloom_handshake_timeout_ms)
 516:             .await?;
 517: 
 518:         match reply.kind {
 519:             FrameKind::MissingChunks => wire::decode_missing_chunks(&reply.payload),
 520:             other => Err(TransferError::ProtocolViolation {
 521:                 expected_kind: FrameKind::MissingChunks,
 522:                 actual_kind: other,
 523:             }),
 524:         }
 525:     }
 526: 
 527:     /// Send a `Ping` frame and await `Pong`. Diagnostic / liveness.
 528:     ///
 529:     /// # Errors
 530:     ///
 531:     /// - [`TransferError::PeerUnknown`]
 532:     /// - [`TransferError::Timeout`]
 533:     /// - [`TransferError::ProtocolViolation`] if the reply isn't `Pong`.
 534:     pub async fn ping(
 535:         &self,
 536:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 537:         payload: Vec<u8>,
 538:     ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, TransferError> {
 539:         let entry = self.peer_entry(peer).await?;
 540:         let connection = self.connection_for(peer, &entry).await?;
 541:         let request = Frame::new(FrameKind::Ping, payload)?;
 542:         let reply = self
 543:             .send_request_with_timeout(&connection, request, self.config.chunk_request_timeout_ms)
 544:             .await?;
 545:         match reply.kind {
 546:             FrameKind::Pong => Ok(reply.payload),
 547:             other => Err(TransferError::ProtocolViolation {
 548:                 expected_kind: FrameKind::Pong,
 549:                 actual_kind: other,
 550:             }),
 551:         }
 552:     }
 553: 
 554:     // ─────────────────────────── internals ─────────────────────────────
 555: 
 556:     fn read_local(&self, chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Option<ChunkRecord> {
 557:         let store = self.store.read().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 558:         if !store.has_chunk(chunk_id) {
 559:             return None;
 560:         }
 561:         store.read_chunk(chunk_id).ok()
 562:     }
 563: 
 564:     /// Persist a received chunk record durably (append + flush). Used
 565:     /// by `fetch_chunk` for single-chunk fetches.
 566:     pub(crate) fn write_local(&self, record: &ChunkRecord) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
 567:         let mut store = self.store.write().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 568:         store.append_chunk(record)?;
 569:         store.flush()?;
 570:         Ok(())
 571:     }
 572: 
 573:     /// Append a chunk record WITHOUT flushing. Used by `fetch_many` and
 574:     /// other batch paths that amortize the fsync across many writes via
 575:     /// a single trailing [`TransferEngine::commit`] call.
 576:     ///
 577:     /// **Durability:** the record is in the kernel page cache after this
 578:     /// call but is **not** guaranteed to survive a crash. Caller MUST
 579:     /// invoke `commit()` before treating the chunk as durable.
 580:     pub(crate) fn write_local_no_flush(&self, record: &ChunkRecord) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
 581:         let mut store = self.store.write().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 582:         store.append_chunk(record)?;
 583:         Ok(())
 584:     }
 585: 
 586:     /// Flush both chunk_log and manifest_log to durable storage. After
 587:     /// this returns, all chunks previously appended via the
 588:     /// `write_local_no_flush` path are durable.
 589:     ///
 590:     /// # Errors
 591:     ///
 592:     /// Returns [`TransferError::Store`] on I/O failure during fsync.
 593:     pub fn commit(&self) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
 594:         let mut store = self.store.write().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 595:         store.flush()?;
 596:         Ok(())
 597:     }
 598: 
 599:     pub(crate) async fn peer_entry(
 600:         &self,
 601:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 602:     ) -> Result<Arc<PeerEntry>, TransferError> {
 603:         let peers = self.peers.read().await;
 604:         peers
 605:             .get(peer)
 606:             .cloned()
 607:             .ok_or_else(|| TransferError::PeerUnknown {
 608:                 fingerprint_hex_prefix: hex_prefix_8(peer),
 609:             })
 610:     }
 611: 
 612:     pub(crate) async fn connection_for(
 613:         &self,
 614:         peer: &PeerFingerprint,
 615:         entry: &Arc<PeerEntry>,
 616:     ) -> Result<Arc<Connection>, TransferError> {
 617:         let mut slot = entry.connection.lock().await;
 618:         if let Some(conn) = slot.as_ref() {
 619:             return Ok(conn.clone());
 620:         }
 621:         let addr = *entry.addr.lock().await;
 622:         let conn = self
 623:             .endpoint
 624:             .connect(addr, *peer)
 625:             .await
 626:             .map_err(TransferError::Transport)?;
 627:         let conn_arc = Arc::new(conn);
 628:         *slot = Some(conn_arc.clone());
 629:         Ok(conn_arc)
 630:     }
 631: 
 632:     /// Force-drop a cached connection (used when a request hits a
 633:     /// transport error and we don't want to reuse the broken pipe).
 634:     pub async fn drop_cached_connection(&self, peer: &PeerFingerprint) {
 635:         if let Ok(entry) = self.peer_entry(peer).await {
 636:             let mut slot = entry.connection.lock().await;
 637:             if let Some(c) = slot.take() {
 638:                 c.close(0, b"transport-error-reset");
 639:             }
 640:         }
 641:     }
 642: 
 643:     async fn send_request_with_timeout(
 644:         &self,
 645:         connection: &Connection,
 646:         request: Frame,
 647:         timeout_ms: u64,
 648:     ) -> Result<Frame, TransferError> {
 649:         let fut = connection.send_frame_request_response(request);
 650:         match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(timeout_ms), fut).await {
 651:             Ok(Ok(reply)) => Ok(reply),
 652:             Ok(Err(e)) => Err(TransferError::Transport(e)),
 653:             Err(_) => Err(TransferError::Timeout { timeout_ms }),
 654:         }
 655:     }
 656: }

  92: pub(crate) fn hex_prefix_8(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
  93:     const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
  94:     let n = bytes.len().min(8);

  96:     for &b in &bytes[..n] {

  98:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);

   1: //! `ol_transfer` — the integrating engine for One Link's file engine v2
   2: //! per [ADR-0013](../../../docs/decisions/0013-transfer-engine.md).
   3: //!
   4: //! Wires together:
   5: //!
   6: //! - [`ol_chunk_store::ChunkStore`] (Phase A1 storage)
   7: //! - [`ol_quic::Endpoint`] / [`ol_quic::Connection`] (Phase A2 transport)
   8: //! - [`ol_bloom::Bloom`] (Phase B Bloom-init handshake per ADR-0011)
   9: //!
  10: //! ## Surface
  11: //!
  12: //! - [`TransferEngine::new`] — construct (returns `Arc<Self>`).
  13: //! - [`TransferEngine::register_peer`] / [`TransferEngine::forget_peer`]
  14: //!   — peer registry management.
  15: //! - [`TransferEngine::fetch_chunk`] — single-chunk fetch (idempotent,
  16: //!   skips transport if chunk is already local).
  17: //! - [`TransferEngine::fetch_many`] — bounded-concurrency batch fetch.
  18: //! - [`TransferEngine::bloom_handshake`] — ADR-0011 Bloom-init exchange.
  19: //! - [`TransferEngine::ping`] — liveness probe.
  20: //! - [`TransferEngine::run_server`] — long-running inbound dispatcher
  21: //!   (spawn on a tokio task).
  22: //!
  23: //! ## Threading
  24: //!
  25: //! `TransferEngine` is `Send + Sync` and designed to be shared via
  26: //! `Arc<Self>`. The chunk store is held under a `std::sync::Mutex` so
  27: //! the engine can mutate it from any task; the lock is held only for
  28: //! short critical sections and never across `.await`.

  34: pub mod error;

   1: //! Per-chunk outcome enum surfaced by [`crate::TransferEngine::fetch_many`].

   5: /// Result of fetching a single chunk. `fetch_many` returns one of these
   6: /// per requested chunk_id.
   7: #[derive(Debug)]
   8: pub enum FetchOutcome {
   9:     /// Chunk was fetched from the peer and is now in the local store.
  10:     Fetched {
  11:         /// The chunk_id that was fetched.
  12:         chunk_id: [u8; 32],
  13:         /// Plaintext length recorded in the chunk_log header.
  14:         length_plaintext: u32,
  15:     },
  16:     /// Chunk was already in the local store; no transport round trip.
  17:     AlreadyLocal {
  18:         /// The chunk_id that was found locally.
  19:         chunk_id: [u8; 32],
  20:     },
  21:     /// Peer doesn't have the chunk.
  22:     NotFound {
  23:         /// The chunk_id the peer reported missing.
  24:         chunk_id: [u8; 32],
  25:     },
  26:     /// Fetch failed for some other reason. Carries the underlying error.
  27:     Error {
  28:         /// The chunk_id whose fetch failed.
  29:         chunk_id: [u8; 32],
  30:         /// Reason the fetch failed.
  31:         err: TransferError,
  32:     },
  33: }
  34: 
  35: impl FetchOutcome {
  36:     /// The chunk_id this outcome refers to.
  37:     #[must_use]
  38:     pub fn chunk_id(&self) -> &[u8; 32] {
  39:         match self {
  40:             Self::Fetched { chunk_id, .. }
  41:             | Self::AlreadyLocal { chunk_id }
  42:             | Self::NotFound { chunk_id }
  43:             | Self::Error { chunk_id, .. } => chunk_id,
  44:         }
  45:     }
  46: 
  47:     /// Convenience: did the outcome represent a successful fetch (either
  48:     /// over the wire or from local cache)?
  49:     #[must_use]
  50:     pub fn is_success(&self) -> bool {
  51:         matches!(self, Self::Fetched { .. } | Self::AlreadyLocal { .. })
  52:     }
  53: }

   1: //! Inbound frame dispatch for the [`crate::TransferEngine`].
   2: //!
   3: //! `run_server` is a long-running task that accepts incoming connections
   4: //! from the endpoint, then for each connection accepts inbound
   5: //! bidirectional streams in a loop. Each stream carries one frame
   6: //! round-trip: read request, dispatch, write reply, finish.
   7: 
   8: use std::sync::Arc;
   9: 
  10: use ol_bloom::Bloom;
  11: use ol_fountain::{FountainPacket, LtEncoder};
  12: use ol_quic::{
  13:     transport::{read_frame, write_frame},
  14:     Connection, Frame, FrameKind,
  15: };
  16: use tracing::{debug, trace, warn};
  17: 
  18: use crate::engine::TransferEngine;
  19: use crate::error::TransferError;
  20: use crate::wire;
  21: 
  22: /// Server-side LT-encode parameters per ADR-0015.
  23: const FOUNTAIN_SYMBOL_LEN: usize = 1024;
  24: 
  25: /// Hard cap on symbols a server will emit for one chunk before
  26: /// declaring the receiver unable to decode. Matches
  27: /// `ol_fountain::MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK`.
  28: const FOUNTAIN_MAX_SYMBOLS: u32 = ol_fountain::MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK - 1;
  29: 
  30: impl TransferEngine {
  31:     /// Accept incoming connections on this engine's endpoint and
  32:     /// dispatch each one to [`handle_connection`]. Runs until the
  33:     /// endpoint is closed.
  34:     ///
  35:     /// Typically the daemon spawns this on a dedicated tokio task:
  36:     ///
  37:     /// ```ignore
  38:     /// let engine = TransferEngine::new(store, endpoint, config);
  39:     /// let engine_clone = Arc::clone(&engine);
  40:     /// tokio::spawn(async move { engine_clone.run_server().await });
  41:     /// ```
  42:     ///
  43:     /// # Errors
  44:     ///
  45:     /// Returns the first non-transient error encountered while accepting
  46:     /// or handling a connection. Transient per-connection errors are
  47:     /// logged via `tracing` and do not stop the server loop.
  48:     pub async fn run_server(self: Arc<Self>) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
  49:         loop {
  50:             let next = self.endpoint.accept().await;
  51:             match next {
  52:                 None => {
  53:                     debug!("endpoint closed; run_server exiting");
  54:                     return Ok(());
  55:                 }
  56:                 Some(Err(e)) => {
  57:                     warn!(error = ?e, "endpoint accept error; continuing");
  58:                     continue;
  59:                 }
  60:                 Some(Ok(conn)) => {
  61:                     let engine = Arc::clone(&self);
  62:                     tokio::spawn(async move {
  63:                         if let Err(e) = engine.handle_connection(conn).await {
  64:                             warn!(error = ?e, "connection handler exited with error");
  65:                         }
  66:                     });
  67:                 }
  68:             }
  69:         }
  70:     }
  71: 
  72:     /// Handle one accepted connection: loop accepting bi-streams until
  73:     /// the connection closes or errors out.
  74:     async fn handle_connection(self: Arc<Self>, conn: Connection) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
  75:         debug!(remote = ?conn.remote_address(), "new inbound connection");
  76:         loop {
  77:             match conn.accept_bi_stream().await {
  78:                 Ok((mut send, mut recv)) => {
  79:                     let engine = Arc::clone(&self);
  80:                     tokio::spawn(async move {
  81:                         if let Err(e) = engine.handle_stream(&mut send, &mut recv).await {
  82:                             trace!(error = ?e, "stream handler exited with error");
  83:                         }
  84:                     });
  85:                 }
  86:                 Err(e) => {
  87:                     debug!(error = ?e, "connection closed; handler exiting");
  88:                     return Ok(());
  89:                 }
  90:             }
  91:         }
  92:     }
  93: 
  94:     /// Handle one inbound bi-stream: read a frame, dispatch, write reply.
  95:     async fn handle_stream(
  96:         self: Arc<Self>,
  97:         send: &mut quinn::SendStream,
  98:         recv: &mut quinn::RecvStream,
  99:     ) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
 100:         let request = read_frame(recv).await?;
 101:         // FountainRequest is special: it streams many response frames
 102:         // on the same bi-stream, then optionally reads back a
 103:         // FountainAck. Dispatch separately.
 104:         if request.kind == FrameKind::FountainRequest {
 105:             return self.handle_fountain_request(&request, send, recv).await;
 106:         }
 107:         let reply = match request.kind {
 108:             FrameKind::ChunkRequest => self.handle_chunk_request(&request).await?,
 109:             FrameKind::BloomFilter => self.handle_bloom_filter(&request, &[]).await?,
 110:             FrameKind::ScopedBloomFilter => self.handle_scoped_bloom_filter(&request).await?,
 111:             FrameKind::Ping => Frame::new(FrameKind::Pong, request.payload.clone())?,
 112:             FrameKind::Close => {
 113:                 debug!("peer requested stream close");
 114:                 return Ok(());
 115:             }
 116:             other => {
 117:                 let body = format!("unexpected frame kind on server side: {other:?}");
 118:                 Frame::new(FrameKind::ProtoError, body.into_bytes())?
 119:             }
 120:         };
 121:         write_frame(send, &reply).await?;
 122:         send.finish()
 123:             .map_err(|e| TransferError::Transport(e.into()))?;
 124:         Ok(())
 125:     }
 126: 
 127:     /// Server-side handler for `FountainRequest`. Looks up the chunk,
 128:     /// serializes its on-disk record bytes, and streams LT-fountain
 129:     /// symbols on the same bi-stream until either:
 130:     ///
 131:     /// 1. The receiver sends `FountainAck` (decode complete).
 132:     /// 2. We've emitted [`FOUNTAIN_MAX_SYMBOLS`] without an ack
 133:     ///    (receiver gave up; we close the stream).
 134:     /// 3. The peer closes the stream.
 135:     async fn handle_fountain_request(
 136:         self: Arc<Self>,
 137:         request: &Frame,
 138:         send: &mut quinn::SendStream,
 139:         recv: &mut quinn::RecvStream,
 140:     ) -> Result<(), TransferError> {
 141:         // Parse the chunk_id from the request payload.
 142:         if request.payload.len() != 32 {
 143:             let err = Frame::new(
 144:                 FrameKind::ProtoError,
 145:                 b"FountainRequest payload must be 32-byte chunk_id".to_vec(),
 146:             )?;
 147:             write_frame(send, &err).await?;
 148:             send.finish()
 149:                 .map_err(|e| TransferError::Transport(e.into()))?;
 150:             return Ok(());
 151:         }
 152:         let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
 153:         chunk_id.copy_from_slice(&request.payload);
 154: 
 155:         // Look up the chunk; serialize to "source bytes" = (kind, flags, payload).
 156:         let record_opt = {
 157:             let store = self.store.read().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 158:             if store.has_chunk(&chunk_id) {
 159:                 Some(store.read_chunk(&chunk_id)?)
 160:             } else {
 161:                 None
 162:             }
 163:         };
 164:         let Some(record) = record_opt else {
 165:             let reply = Frame::new(FrameKind::ChunkNotFound, chunk_id.to_vec())?;
 166:             write_frame(send, &reply).await?;
 167:             send.finish()
 168:                 .map_err(|e| TransferError::Transport(e.into()))?;
 169:             return Ok(());
 170:         };
 171:         let (kind_byte, flags_byte, body) = record.encode();
 172:         let mut source = Vec::with_capacity(2 + body.len());
 173:         source.push(kind_byte);
 174:         source.push(flags_byte);
 175:         source.extend_from_slice(&body);
 176: 
 177:         let encoder = LtEncoder::new(&source, FOUNTAIN_SYMBOL_LEN)?;
 178:         let k = encoder.k();
 179:         let source_len_u32 = u32::try_from(source.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 180: 
 181:         // Phase B-2 emission protocol:
 182:         //   Step 1: emit `initial_burst` = ceil(K * 1.25) symbols (the
 183:         //           "25% overhead" from ADR-0015's robust-soliton
 184:         //           targets ≥99.9% decode probability on loss-free links).
 185:         //   Step 2: await ACK with a bounded timeout. If ACK arrives,
 186:         //           stop. If timeout, emit another `top_up` = ceil(K * 0.25)
 187:         //           and repeat until ACK or `FOUNTAIN_MAX_SYMBOLS`.
 188:         //
 189:         // This avoids the broken pattern where we'd emit every symbol
 190:         // up to the cap because a 0-duration peek never observes the
 191:         // client's ACK in flight.
 192:         let initial_burst = k.saturating_add(k / 4).max(k + 4);
 193:         let top_up = (k / 4).max(2);
 194:         // 2ms ack wait: loopback ACKs arrive in tens of microseconds; on
 195:         // LAN/WAN the bound is sub-RTT. If the client genuinely needs
 196:         // more symbols (loss > overhead margin) we top up after this
 197:         // timeout, repeated until ACK or MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK.
 198:         let ack_wait = std::time::Duration::from_millis(2);
 199: 
 200:         let mut sid: u32 = 0;
 201:         // Step 1: initial burst.
 202:         while sid < initial_burst && sid < FOUNTAIN_MAX_SYMBOLS {
 203:             let symbol = encoder.encode_symbol(sid);
 204:             let packet = FountainPacket::new(chunk_id, k, sid, source_len_u32, symbol).encode();
 205:             let frame = Frame::new(FrameKind::FountainBurst, packet)?;
 206:             write_frame(send, &frame).await?;
 207:             sid += 1;
 208:         }
 209: 
 210:         // Step 2: wait-for-ACK + optional top-up loop.
 211:         loop {
 212:             match tokio::time::timeout(ack_wait, read_frame(recv)).await {
 213:                 Ok(Ok(ack)) if ack.kind == FrameKind::FountainAck => break,
 214:                 Ok(Ok(_)) => break,  // unexpected frame; bail
 215:                 Ok(Err(_)) => break, // stream error; bail
 216:                 Err(_) => {
 217:                     // Timeout: top up if there's headroom.
 218:                     if sid >= FOUNTAIN_MAX_SYMBOLS {
 219:                         break;
 220:                     }
 221:                     let limit = (sid + top_up).min(FOUNTAIN_MAX_SYMBOLS);
 222:                     while sid < limit {
 223:                         let symbol = encoder.encode_symbol(sid);
 224:                         let packet =
 225:                             FountainPacket::new(chunk_id, k, sid, source_len_u32, symbol).encode();
 226:                         let frame = Frame::new(FrameKind::FountainBurst, packet)?;
 227:                         write_frame(send, &frame).await?;
 228:                         sid += 1;
 229:                     }
 230:                 }
 231:             }
 232:         }
 233:         send.finish()
 234:             .map_err(|e| TransferError::Transport(e.into()))?;
 235:         Ok(())
 236:     }
 237: 
 238:     /// Server-side handler for `ChunkRequest`. Looks up the chunk and
 239:     /// either replies with `ChunkResponse` (full record bytes) or
 240:     /// `ChunkNotFound` echoing the requested id.
 241:     async fn handle_chunk_request(&self, request: &Frame) -> Result<Frame, TransferError> {
 242:         let chunk_id = wire::decode_chunk_request(&request.payload)?;
 243:         let record_opt = {
 244:             let store = self.store.read().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 245:             if store.has_chunk(&chunk_id) {
 246:                 Some(store.read_chunk(&chunk_id)?)
 247:             } else {
 248:                 None
 249:             }
 250:         };
 251:         match record_opt {
 252:             Some(record) => {
 253:                 let (kind, flags, payload) = record.encode();
 254:                 let payload = wire::encode_chunk_response(kind, flags, &payload);
 255:                 Ok(Frame::new(FrameKind::ChunkResponse, payload)?)
 256:             }
 257:             None => {
 258:                 let payload = wire::encode_chunk_not_found(&chunk_id);
 259:                 Ok(Frame::new(FrameKind::ChunkNotFound, payload)?)
 260:             }
 261:         }
 262:     }
 263: 
 264:     /// Server-side handler for `ScopedBloomFilter`. Parses the want_list
 265:     /// + bloom from the payload, walks the want_list against the bloom,
 266:     /// and returns the subset NOT in the bloom (i.e. chunks the peer
 267:     /// doesn't yet have).
 268:     ///
 269:     /// Crucially, this path does **not** scan the local memtable — the
 270:     /// scope is fully client-supplied. For large servers (≥ 1M chunks)
 271:     /// this is the difference between O(server_memtable) and
 272:     /// O(want_list) work per handshake.
 273:     async fn handle_scoped_bloom_filter(&self, request: &Frame) -> Result<Frame, TransferError> {
 274:         let (want_list, bloom_bytes) = wire::decode_scoped_bloom(&request.payload)?;
 275:         let bloom = Bloom::decode(bloom_bytes)?;
 276:         let missing: Vec<[u8; 32]> = want_list
 277:             .into_iter()
 278:             .filter(|cid| !bloom.contains(cid))
 279:             .collect();
 280:         let payload = wire::encode_missing_chunks(&missing);
 281:         Ok(Frame::new(FrameKind::MissingChunks, payload)?)
 282:     }
 283: 
 284:     /// Server-side handler for `BloomFilter`. Given a peer-supplied
 285:     /// Bloom filter `bloom`, computes the subset of `manifest_chunk_ids`
 286:     /// the peer does NOT have (those for which `!bloom.contains(cid)`),
 287:     /// and returns a `MissingChunks` frame.
 288:     ///
 289:     /// For the v1 wire protocol we expose the manifest set as a hint
 290:     /// from the caller; the server-side default uses `&[]` which means
 291:     /// "no manifest scope known" → empty `MissingChunks`. Callers that
 292:     /// want the meaningful behavior should pre-register a manifest hook
 293:     /// via [`TransferEngine::set_manifest_scope`] (future API; v1 uses
 294:     /// the local memtable's chunk_ids as the implicit scope).
 295:     async fn handle_bloom_filter(
 296:         &self,
 297:         request: &Frame,
 298:         _explicit_scope: &[[u8; 32]],
 299:     ) -> Result<Frame, TransferError> {
 300:         let bloom = Bloom::decode(&request.payload)?;
 301:         // v1 default: scope = entire local memtable. Phase B-2 may
 302:         // narrow this to a specific manifest's chunk set; for v1 we
 303:         // serve the engine's whole inventory.
 304:         let local_ids: Vec<[u8; 32]> = {
 305:             let store = self.store.read().expect("store rwlock poisoned");
 306:             store.collect_chunk_ids()
 307:         };
 308:         let missing: Vec<[u8; 32]> = local_ids
 309:             .into_iter()
 310:             .filter(|cid| !bloom.contains(cid))
 311:             .collect();
 312:         let payload = wire::encode_missing_chunks(&missing);
 313:         Ok(Frame::new(FrameKind::MissingChunks, payload)?)
 314:     }
 315: }

   1: //! Wire-protocol payload formats for `ol_transfer` frames.
   2: //!
   3: //! Frame headers (kind + length) are handled by [`ol_quic::proto`]. This
   4: //! module decodes / encodes the *payload* contents for each frame kind we
   5: //! care about:
   6: //!
   7: //! - `ChunkRequest (0x01)` payload = 32 bytes (the chunk_id).
   8: //! - `ChunkResponse (0x02)` payload = `[record_kind: u8][record_flags: u8][record_payload: N bytes]`
   9: //!   — the chunk_record encoded form, same as on-disk before WAL framing.
  10: //! - `ChunkNotFound (0x03)` payload = 32 bytes (the missing chunk_id).
  11: //! - `BloomFilter (0x20)` payload = `[ol_bloom encoded bytes]` per ADR-0011.
  12: //! - `MissingChunks (0x21)` payload = `[count: u32 LE][chunk_id_1..n: 32 bytes each]`.
  13: //! - `Ping (0xF0)` / `Pong (0xF1)` payload = opaque echo bytes (≤64 KiB).
  14: //! - `ProtoError (0xFE)` payload = ASCII reason (≤64 KiB).
  15: 
  16: use ol_quic::FrameKind;
  17: 
  18: use crate::error::TransferError;
  19: 
  20: /// Length of one chunk_id on the wire.
  21: pub const CHUNK_ID_LEN: usize = 32;
  22: 
  23: /// Encode a `ChunkRequest` payload from a chunk_id.
  24: #[inline]
  25: #[must_use]
  26: pub fn encode_chunk_request(chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<u8> {
  27:     chunk_id.to_vec()
  28: }
  29: 
  30: /// Decode a `ChunkRequest` payload into a chunk_id.
  31: ///
  32: /// # Errors
  33: ///
  34: /// [`TransferError::MalformedPayload`] if `payload` is not exactly 32 bytes.
  35: pub fn decode_chunk_request(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 32], TransferError> {
  36:     if payload.len() != CHUNK_ID_LEN {
  37:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
  38:             kind: FrameKind::ChunkRequest,
  39:             reason: "expected 32-byte chunk_id",
  40:         });
  41:     }
  42:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
  43:     out.copy_from_slice(payload);
  44:     Ok(out)
  45: }
  46: 
  47: /// Encode a `ChunkResponse` payload: prepends the record_kind + flags
  48: /// bytes before the record payload.
  49: #[inline]
  50: #[must_use]
  51: pub fn encode_chunk_response(record_kind: u8, record_flags: u8, record_payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
  52:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(2 + record_payload.len());
  53:     out.push(record_kind);
  54:     out.push(record_flags);
  55:     out.extend_from_slice(record_payload);
  56:     out
  57: }
  58: 
  59: /// Decode a `ChunkResponse` payload into (record_kind, record_flags,
  60: /// record_payload).
  61: ///
  62: /// # Errors
  63: ///
  64: /// [`TransferError::MalformedPayload`] if `payload` is shorter than the
  65: /// 2-byte kind+flags prefix.
  66: pub fn decode_chunk_response(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(u8, u8, &[u8]), TransferError> {
  67:     if payload.len() < 2 {
  68:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
  69:             kind: FrameKind::ChunkResponse,
  70:             reason: "chunk-response payload < 2 bytes",
  71:         });
  72:     }
  73:     Ok((payload[0], payload[1], &payload[2..]))
  74: }
  75: 
  76: /// Encode a `ChunkNotFound` payload.
  77: #[inline]
  78: #[must_use]
  79: pub fn encode_chunk_not_found(chunk_id: &[u8; 32]) -> Vec<u8> {
  80:     chunk_id.to_vec()
  81: }
  82: 
  83: /// Decode a `ChunkNotFound` payload.
  84: ///
  85: /// # Errors
  86: ///
  87: /// [`TransferError::MalformedPayload`] if `payload` is not exactly 32 bytes.
  88: pub fn decode_chunk_not_found(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 32], TransferError> {
  89:     if payload.len() != CHUNK_ID_LEN {
  90:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
  91:             kind: FrameKind::ChunkNotFound,
  92:             reason: "expected 32-byte chunk_id",
  93:         });
  94:     }
  95:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
  96:     out.copy_from_slice(payload);
  97:     Ok(out)
  98: }
  99: 
 100: /// Encode a `MissingChunks` payload from an iterator of chunk_ids.
 101: ///
 102: /// Format: `[count: u32 LE][chunk_id_1..n: 32 bytes each]`.
 103: #[must_use]
 104: pub fn encode_missing_chunks(ids: &[[u8; 32]]) -> Vec<u8> {
 105:     let count = u32::try_from(ids.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 106:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + ids.len() * CHUNK_ID_LEN);
 107:     out.extend_from_slice(&count.to_le_bytes());
 108:     for id in ids {
 109:         out.extend_from_slice(id);
 110:     }
 111:     out
 112: }
 113: 
 114: /// Encode a `ScopedBloomFilter` payload.
 115: ///
 116: /// Format: `[want_count: u32 LE][want_id_1..n: 32 bytes each][bloom_bytes]`.
 117: #[must_use]
 118: pub fn encode_scoped_bloom(want_list: &[[u8; 32]], bloom_bytes: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
 119:     let count = u32::try_from(want_list.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
 120:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(4 + want_list.len() * CHUNK_ID_LEN + bloom_bytes.len());
 121:     out.extend_from_slice(&count.to_le_bytes());
 122:     for id in want_list {
 123:         out.extend_from_slice(id);
 124:     }
 125:     out.extend_from_slice(bloom_bytes);
 126:     out
 127: }
 128: 
 129: /// Decode a `ScopedBloomFilter` payload into the want_list and the
 130: /// encoded bloom bytes (caller passes the bloom bytes to
 131: /// `Bloom::decode`).
 132: ///
 133: /// # Errors
 134: ///
 135: /// [`TransferError::MalformedPayload`] if the header is missing or
 136: /// the declared want_count overflows the available bytes.
 137: pub fn decode_scoped_bloom(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(Vec<[u8; 32]>, &[u8]), TransferError> {
 138:     if payload.len() < 4 {
 139:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
 140:             kind: FrameKind::ScopedBloomFilter,
 141:             reason: "scoped-bloom payload < 4 bytes",
 142:         });
 143:     }
 144:     let count = u32::from_le_bytes(payload[0..4].try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize;
 145:     let want_bytes_len = count * CHUNK_ID_LEN;
 146:     if payload.len() < 4 + want_bytes_len {
 147:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
 148:             kind: FrameKind::ScopedBloomFilter,
 149:             reason: "scoped-bloom want_list exceeds payload",
 150:         });
 151:     }
 152:     let mut want = Vec::with_capacity(count);
 153:     for i in 0..count {
 154:         let start = 4 + i * CHUNK_ID_LEN;
 155:         let mut cid = [0u8; 32];
 156:         cid.copy_from_slice(&payload[start..start + CHUNK_ID_LEN]);
 157:         want.push(cid);
 158:     }
 159:     let bloom_bytes = &payload[4 + want_bytes_len..];
 160:     Ok((want, bloom_bytes))
 161: }
 162: 
 163: /// Decode a `MissingChunks` payload into a vector of chunk_ids.
 164: ///
 165: /// # Errors
 166: ///
 167: /// [`TransferError::MalformedPayload`] if the count header is missing
 168: /// or the payload length doesn't match `count * 32 + 4`.
 169: pub fn decode_missing_chunks(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<[u8; 32]>, TransferError> {
 170:     if payload.len() < 4 {
 171:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
 172:             kind: FrameKind::MissingChunks,
 173:             reason: "missing-chunks payload < 4 bytes",
 174:         });
 175:     }
 176:     let count = u32::from_le_bytes(payload[0..4].try_into().expect("4 bytes")) as usize;
 177:     let expected_len = 4 + count * CHUNK_ID_LEN;
 178:     if payload.len() != expected_len {
 179:         return Err(TransferError::MalformedPayload {
 180:             kind: FrameKind::MissingChunks,
 181:             reason: "missing-chunks payload length doesn't match declared count",
 182:         });
 183:     }
 184:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count);
 185:     for i in 0..count {
 186:         let start = 4 + i * CHUNK_ID_LEN;
 187:         let mut cid = [0u8; 32];
 188:         cid.copy_from_slice(&payload[start..start + CHUNK_ID_LEN]);
 189:         out.push(cid);
 190:     }
 191:     Ok(out)
 192: }

   1: //! End-to-end integration tests for `ol_transfer::TransferEngine`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Validates the full chunk-store + QUIC + Bloom-init wiring per
   4: //! ADR-0013's verification gate:
   5: //!
   6: //! 1. End-to-end fetch — paired peers; B fetches X from A; X is on B's store.
   7: //! 2. Idempotence — repeated `fetch_chunk` returns cached, no transport.
   8: //! 3. Bloom-init delta — B sends bloom of its 1024 chunks; gets back ~missing.
   9: //! 4. Chunk-not-found — B asks for Y, A doesn't have it.
  10: //! 5. Protocol violation — server replies with wrong frame kind.
  11: //! 6. Cached connection reuse — N fetches reuse one connection.
  12: //! 7. Concurrent fetch backpressure — bounded by `max_inflight_per_peer`.
  13: 
  14: use std::net::SocketAddr;
  15: use std::sync::{Arc, RwLock as StdRwLock};
  16: 
  17: use ol_chunk_store::{
  18:     ChunkAddressKind, ChunkAeadKind, ChunkRecord, ChunkRecordKind, ChunkStore, StripeDescriptor,
  19: };
  20: use ol_quic::{Endpoint, EndpointConfig, Identity, PeerFingerprint, PeerRegistry};
  21: use ol_transfer::{FetchOutcome, TransferConfig, TransferEngine, TransferError};
  22: use tempfile::TempDir;
  23:

  31: impl PeerRegistry for PairedRegistry {
  32:     fn is_paired_peer(&self, fp: &PeerFingerprint) -> bool {
  33:         self.permitted.iter().any(|p| p == fp)
  34:     }
  35: }

  37: fn fast_config() -> EndpointConfig {
  38:     let mut c = EndpointConfig::default();
  39:     c.bind = "127.0.0.1:0".parse().expect("valid bind");
  40:     c.idle_timeout_ms = 30_000;
  41:     c.keepalive_interval_ms = 5_000;
  42:     c
  43: }

  45: fn mk_record_u32(seed: u32, plaintext_len: u32, ciphertext_len: usize) -> ChunkRecord {
  46:     let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
  47:     chunk_id[..4].copy_from_slice(&seed.to_le_bytes());
  48:     chunk_id[31] = 0xCD;
  49:     ChunkRecord {
  50:         kind: ChunkRecordKind::ChunkBlob,
  51:         address_kind: ChunkAddressKind::Raw,
  52:         aead_kind: ChunkAeadKind::AesGcm256,
  53:         compressed: false,
  54:         format_aware: false,
  55:         length_plaintext: plaintext_len,
  56:         chunk_id,
  57:         ratchet_key_id: [0x77u8; 16],
  58:         stripe_descriptor: StripeDescriptor::NONE,
  59:         ciphertext: vec![0xCDu8; ciphertext_len],
  60:     }
  61: }

  63: fn mk_record(id_byte: u8, plaintext_len: u32, ciphertext_len: usize) -> ChunkRecord {
  64:     let mut chunk_id = [0u8; 32];
  65:     chunk_id[0] = id_byte;
  66:     chunk_id[1] = 0xAA;
  67:     ChunkRecord {
  68:         kind: ChunkRecordKind::ChunkBlob,
  69:         address_kind: ChunkAddressKind::Raw,
  70:         aead_kind: ChunkAeadKind::AesGcm256,
  71:         compressed: false,
  72:         format_aware: false,
  73:         length_plaintext: plaintext_len,
  74:         chunk_id,
  75:         ratchet_key_id: [0x77u8; 16],
  76:         stripe_descriptor: StripeDescriptor::NONE,
  77:         ciphertext: vec![0xCDu8; ciphertext_len],
  78:     }

  81: struct Peer {
  82:     // `identity` is referenced through endpoint TLS plumbing during
  83:     // setup; it stays owned here so the Arc isn't dropped before the
  84:     // endpoint, but isn't read directly inside the test body — keep
  85:     // the field with a leading underscore so Rust knows we hold it
  86:     // deliberately.
  87:     _identity: Arc<Identity>,
  88:     fingerprint: PeerFingerprint,
  89:     _root: TempDir,
  90:     store: Arc<StdRwLock<ChunkStore>>,
  91:     endpoint: Arc<Endpoint>,
  92:     addr: SocketAddr,
  93: }
  94: 
  95: fn build_peer(permitted_partners: Vec<PeerFingerprint>) -> Peer {
  96:     let identity = Arc::new(Identity::generate().unwrap());
  97:     let fingerprint = identity.fingerprint();
  98:     let root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
  99:     let store = ChunkStore::open(root.path()).unwrap();
 100:     let store = Arc::new(StdRwLock::new(store));
 101:     let registry = Arc::new(PairedRegistry {
 102:         permitted: permitted_partners,
 103:     });
 104:     let endpoint =
 105:         Arc::new(Endpoint::server_for_identity(identity.clone(), registry, fast_config()).unwrap());
 106:     let addr = endpoint.local_addr().unwrap();
 107:     Peer {
 108:         _identity: identity,
 109:         fingerprint,
 110:         _root: root,
 111:         store,
 112:         endpoint,
 113:         addr,
 114:     }
 115: }
 116: 
 117: /// Build a paired (alice, bob) duo where each accepts connections from
 118: /// the other.
 119: fn pair() -> (Peer, Peer) {
 120:     let alice_id = Arc::new(Identity::generate().unwrap());
 121:     let bob_id = Arc::new(Identity::generate().unwrap());
 122:     let alice_fp = alice_id.fingerprint();
 123:     let bob_fp = bob_id.fingerprint();
 124: 
 125:     let alice_root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
 126:     let bob_root = TempDir::new().unwrap();
 127:     let alice_store = Arc::new(StdRwLock::new(ChunkStore::open(alice_root.path()).unwrap()));
 128:     let bob_store = Arc::new(StdRwLock::new(ChunkStore::open(bob_root.path()).unwrap()));
 129: 
 130:     let alice_registry = Arc::new(PairedRegistry {
 131:         permitted: vec![bob_fp],
 132:     });
 133:     let bob_registry = Arc::new(PairedRegistry {
 134:         permitted: vec![alice_fp],
 135:     });
 136: 
 137:     let alice_endpoint = Arc::new(
 138:         Endpoint::server_for_identity(alice_id.clone(), alice_registry, fast_config()).unwrap(),
 139:     );
 140:     let bob_endpoint = Arc::new(
 141:         Endpoint::server_for_identity(bob_id.clone(), bob_registry, fast_config()).unwrap(),
 142:     );
 143:     let alice_addr = alice_endpoint.local_addr().unwrap();
 144:     let bob_addr = bob_endpoint.local_addr().unwrap();
 145: 
 146:     let alice = Peer {
 147:         _identity: alice_id,
 148:         fingerprint: alice_fp,
 149:         _root: alice_root,
 150:         store: alice_store,
 151:         endpoint: alice_endpoint,
 152:         addr: alice_addr,
 153:     };
 154:     let bob = Peer {
 155:         _identity: bob_id,
 156:         fingerprint: bob_fp,
 157:         _root: bob_root,
 158:         store: bob_store,
 159:         endpoint: bob_endpoint,
 160:         addr: bob_addr,
 161:     };
 162:     (alice, bob)
 163: }

 167: #[tokio::test]
 168: async fn fetch_chunk_round_trip() {
 169:     let (alice, bob) = pair();
 170: 
 171:     // Alice has the chunk.
 172:     let record = mk_record(0x42, 1024, 1040);
 173:     let chunk_id = record.chunk_id;
 174:     {
 175:         let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 176:         s.append_chunk(&record).unwrap();
 177:         s.flush().unwrap();
 178:     }
 179: 
 180:     let alice_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 181:         alice.store.clone(),
 182:         alice.endpoint.clone(),
 183:         TransferConfig::default(),
 184:     );
 185:     let bob_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 186:         bob.store.clone(),
 187:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 188:         TransferConfig::default(),
 189:     );
 190: 
 191:     let alice_server = Arc::clone(&alice_engine);
 192:     tokio::spawn(async move {
 193:         let _ = alice_server.run_server().await;
 194:     });
 195: 
 196:     bob_engine
 197:         .register_peer(alice.fingerprint, alice.addr)
 198:         .await
 199:         .unwrap();
 200: 
 201:     let fetched = bob_engine
 202:         .fetch_chunk(&alice.fingerprint, &chunk_id)
 203:         .await
 204:         .unwrap();
 205:     assert_eq!(fetched.chunk_id, chunk_id);
 206:     assert_eq!(fetched.length_plaintext, 1024);
 207:     assert_eq!(fetched.ciphertext.len(), 1040);
 208: 
 209:     // Bob's store now has it.
 210:     {
 211:         let s = bob.store.read().unwrap();
 212:         assert!(s.has_chunk(&chunk_id));
 213:     }
 214: }

 217: async fn fetch_chunk_idempotent_returns_local() {
 218:     let (alice, bob) = pair();
 219:     let record = mk_record(0x55, 256, 272);
 220:     let chunk_id = record.chunk_id;
 221:     {
 222:         let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 223:         s.append_chunk(&record).unwrap();
 224:         s.flush().unwrap();
 225:     }
 226: 
 227:     let alice_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 228:         alice.store.clone(),
 229:         alice.endpoint.clone(),
 230:         TransferConfig::default(),
 231:     );
 232:     let bob_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 233:         bob.store.clone(),
 234:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 235:         TransferConfig::default(),
 236:     );
 237: 
 238:     let alice_server = Arc::clone(&alice_engine);
 239:     tokio::spawn(async move {
 240:         let _ = alice_server.run_server().await;
 241:     });
 242: 
 243:     bob_engine
 244:         .register_peer(alice.fingerprint, alice.addr)
 245:         .await
 246:         .unwrap();
 247: 
 248:     // First fetch: over the wire.
 249:     let first = bob_engine
 250:         .fetch_chunk(&alice.fingerprint, &chunk_id)
 251:         .await
 252:         .unwrap();
 253:     // Second fetch: must hit local store (no transport).
 254:     let second = bob_engine
 255:         .fetch_chunk(&alice.fingerprint, &chunk_id)
 256:         .await
 257:         .unwrap();
 258:     assert_eq!(first.chunk_id, second.chunk_id);
 259:     assert_eq!(first.ciphertext, second.ciphertext);
 260: 
 261:     // Even forgetting Alice and re-fetching the now-local chunk works.
 262:     bob_engine.forget_peer(&alice.fingerprint).await;
 263:     let third = bob_engine
 264:         .fetch_chunk(&alice.fingerprint, &chunk_id)
 265:         .await
 266:         .unwrap();
 267:     assert_eq!(third.chunk_id, chunk_id);
 268: }

 315: #[tokio::test]
 316: async fn bloom_handshake_returns_missing_chunks() {
 317:     let (alice, bob) = pair();
 318: 
 319:     // Alice has 100 chunks; Bob has the first 50.
 320:     let mut alice_ids = Vec::new();
 321:     for i in 0u8..100 {
 322:         let r = mk_record(i, 64, 80);
 323:         let id = r.chunk_id;
 324:         {
 325:             let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 326:             s.append_chunk(&r).unwrap();
 327:             s.flush().unwrap();
 328:         }
 329:         alice_ids.push(id);
 330:     }
 331:     let mut bob_local = Vec::new();
 332:     for i in 0u8..50 {
 333:         let r = mk_record(i, 64, 80);
 334:         let id = r.chunk_id;
 335:         {
 336:             let mut s = bob.store.write().unwrap();
 337:             s.append_chunk(&r).unwrap();
 338:             s.flush().unwrap();
 339:         }
 340:         bob_local.push(id);
 341:     }
 342: 
 343:     let alice_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 344:         alice.store.clone(),
 345:         alice.endpoint.clone(),
 346:         TransferConfig::default(),
 347:     );
 348:     let bob_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 349:         bob.store.clone(),
 350:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 351:         TransferConfig::default(),
 352:     );
 353: 
 354:     let alice_server = Arc::clone(&alice_engine);
 355:     tokio::spawn(async move {
 356:         let _ = alice_server.run_server().await;
 357:     });
 358: 
 359:     bob_engine
 360:         .register_peer(alice.fingerprint, alice.addr)
 361:         .await
 362:         .unwrap();
 363: 
 364:     // Bob sends bloom of its 50 chunks; the server-side (Alice) iterates
 365:     // its memtable (100 chunks) and returns the ones NOT in Bob's bloom.
 366:     // Expected: roughly 50 missing (the second half), ± FP-rate noise.
 367:     let missing = bob_engine
 368:         .bloom_handshake(&alice.fingerprint, &bob_local)
 369:         .await
 370:         .unwrap();
 371:     // Filter false-positive rate is 1%, so expect between 45 and 50 missing.
 372:     assert!(
 373:         missing.len() >= 45 && missing.len() <= 50,
 374:         "expected ~50 missing chunks, got {}",
 375:         missing.len()
 376:     );
 377:     // None of the returned ids should be in bob_local (true positives).
 378:     for cid in &missing {
 379:         assert!(!bob_local.contains(cid));
 380:     }
 381: }

 465:     let mut fetched = 0;
 466:     let mut not_found = 0;
 467:     for (i, o) in outcomes.iter().enumerate() {
 468:         if i < 10 {
 469:             match o {
 470:                 FetchOutcome::Fetched {
 471:                     length_plaintext, ..
 472:                 } => {
 473:                     assert_eq!(*length_plaintext, 32);
 474:                     fetched += 1;
 475:                 }
 476:                 FetchOutcome::AlreadyLocal { .. } => {
 477:                     // Acceptable: occasional re-entrancy on shared store.
 478:                     fetched += 1;
 479:                 }
 480:                 other => panic!("expected Fetched for index {i}, got {other:?}"),
 481:             }
 482:         } else {
 483:             assert!(
 484:                 matches!(o, FetchOutcome::NotFound { .. }),
 485:                 "expected NotFound for index {i}, got {o:?}"
 486:             );
 487:             not_found += 1;
 488:         }
 489:     }
 490:     assert_eq!(fetched, 10);
 491:     assert_eq!(not_found, 2);
 492: }

 512: #[tokio::test]
 513: async fn bloom_handshake_scoped_filters_to_want_list() {
 514:     // Server has 200 chunks. Client has 50 of them. Client's want_list
 515:     // is a 100-chunk subset of the server's chunks. The server should
 516:     // return exactly the 50 in want_list that the client doesn't have.
 517:     let (alice, bob) = pair();
 518:     let mut all_ids = Vec::new();
 519:     for i in 0u32..200 {
 520:         let r = mk_record_u32(i, 32, 48);
 521:         let id = r.chunk_id;
 522:         {
 523:             let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 524:             s.append_chunk(&r).unwrap();
 525:             s.flush().unwrap();
 526:         }
 527:         all_ids.push(id);
 528:     }
 529:     // Bob's existing: first 50.
 530:     let bob_have: Vec<[u8; 32]> = all_ids.iter().take(50).copied().collect();
 531:     // Want list: 100 ids spanning ids 25..125 (so 25 overlap with already_have, 75 are missing).
 532:     let want_list: Vec<[u8; 32]> = all_ids.iter().skip(25).take(100).copied().collect();
 533: 
 534:     let alice_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 535:         alice.store.clone(),
 536:         alice.endpoint.clone(),
 537:         TransferConfig::default(),
 538:     );
 539:     let bob_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 540:         bob.store.clone(),
 541:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 542:         TransferConfig::default(),
 543:     );
 544:     let alice_server = Arc::clone(&alice_engine);
 545:     tokio::spawn(async move {
 546:         let _ = alice_server.run_server().await;
 547:     });
 548:     bob_engine
 549:         .register_peer(alice.fingerprint, alice.addr)
 550:         .await
 551:         .unwrap();
 552: 
 553:     let missing = bob_engine
 554:         .bloom_handshake_scoped(&alice.fingerprint, &bob_have, &want_list)
 555:         .await
 556:         .unwrap();
 557:     // Expected count: roughly 75 (want_list minus bob_have intersection).
 558:     // Bloom FP rate 1% means we may see slightly fewer.
 559:     assert!(
 560:         missing.len() >= 70 && missing.len() <= 75,
 561:         "expected ~75 missing, got {}",
 562:         missing.len()
 563:     );
 564:     // None of the returned ids should be in bob_have.
 565:     for cid in &missing {
 566:         assert!(!bob_have.contains(cid));
 567:     }
 568:     // All returned ids should be in want_list.
 569:     for cid in &missing {
 570:         assert!(want_list.contains(cid));
 571:     }
 572: }

 583:     {
 584:         let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 585:         s.append_chunk(&record).unwrap();
 586:         s.flush().unwrap();

 588:

 591:         alice.endpoint.clone(),

 595:         bob.store.clone(),
 596:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 597:         TransferConfig::default(),

 651: #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4)]
 652: async fn concurrent_fetch_stress_200_parallel() {
 653:     // Stress: bob asks alice for 200 chunks in parallel via fetch_many.
 654:     // Confirms the RwLock + group commit + fetch task spawn pattern
 655:     // doesn't deadlock under concurrent load.
 656:     let (alice, bob) = pair();
 657:     let mut chunk_ids = Vec::with_capacity(200);
 658:     for i in 0u32..200 {
 659:         let r = mk_record_u32(i, 1024, 1040);
 660:         let id = r.chunk_id;
 661:         {
 662:             let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 663:             s.append_chunk(&r).unwrap();
 664:         }
 665:         chunk_ids.push(id);
 666:     }
 667:     {
 668:         let mut s = alice.store.write().unwrap();
 669:         s.flush().unwrap();
 670:     }
 671: 
 672:     let alice_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 673:         alice.store.clone(),
 674:         alice.endpoint.clone(),
 675:         TransferConfig::default(),
 676:     );
 677:     let bob_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 678:         bob.store.clone(),
 679:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 680:         TransferConfig::default(),
 681:     );
 682:     let alice_server = Arc::clone(&alice_engine);
 683:     tokio::spawn(async move {
 684:         let _ = alice_server.run_server().await;
 685:     });
 686:     bob_engine
 687:         .register_peer(alice.fingerprint, alice.addr)
 688:         .await
 689:         .unwrap();
 690: 
 691:     let start = std::time::Instant::now();
 692:     let outcomes = bob_engine
 693:         .fetch_many(&alice.fingerprint, chunk_ids.clone())
 694:         .await
 695:         .unwrap();
 696:     let elapsed = start.elapsed();
 697: 
 698:     assert_eq!(outcomes.len(), 200);
 699:     let success_count = outcomes.iter().filter(|o| o.is_success()).count();
 700:     assert_eq!(success_count, 200);
 701:     eprintln!("200 parallel fetches: {:?}", elapsed);
 702: 
 703:     // Bob now has all 200 chunks.
 704:     let s = bob.store.read().unwrap();
 705:     let mut found = 0;
 706:     for cid in &chunk_ids {
 707:         if s.has_chunk(cid) {
 708:             found += 1;
 709:         }
 710:     }
 711:     assert_eq!(found, 200);
 712: }

 715: async fn cached_connection_reused_across_fetches() {

 725:             s.append_chunk(&r).unwrap();
 726:             s.flush().unwrap();
 727:         }

 729:     }
