 732:         alice.store.clone(),
 733:         alice.endpoint.clone(),
 734:         TransferConfig::default(),
 735:     );
 736:     let bob_engine = TransferEngine::new(
 737:         bob.store.clone(),
 738:         bob.endpoint.clone(),
 739:         TransferConfig::default(),
 740:     );
 741: 
 742:     let alice_server = Arc::clone(&alice_engine);
 743:     tokio::spawn(async move {
 744:         let _ = alice_server.run_server().await;
 745:     });
 746: 
 747:     bob_engine
 748:         .register_peer(alice.fingerprint, alice.addr)
 749:         .await
 750:         .unwrap();
 751: 
 752:     // Each fetch reuses the cached connection. We can't directly assert
 753:     // "exactly one connection" from outside, but we CAN observe that all
 754:     // 5 fetches succeed in rapid succession (handshake cost ~100ms each
 755:     // would be ~500ms total; cached path should be <100ms total). On a
 756:     // loopback this is easily met; we just assert all succeed.
 757:     for id in &ids {
 758:         let _ = bob_engine
 759:             .fetch_chunk(&alice.fingerprint, id)
 760:             .await
 761:             .unwrap();
 762:     }
 763:     let stats = bob_engine.store_stats();
 764:     assert!(stats.indexed_chunks >= 5);
 765: }

   1: //! Throughput benchmarks for `ol_wal`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Measures group-commit throughput at varying batch sizes. The chunk
   4: //! store layers above sit on top of these numbers; group commit is what
   5: //! makes 10K+ logical writes/s/thread possible per ADR-0005.
   6: //!
   7: //! Run:
   8: //!   cargo bench -p ol_wal --bench wal_bench
   9: 
  10: use criterion::{black_box, criterion_group, criterion_main, BenchmarkId, Criterion, Throughput};
  11: use ol_wal::{LogKind, Record, Wal};
  12: use tempfile::tempdir;
  13: 
  14: fn rec(payload_len: usize) -> Record {
  15:     Record {
  16:         kind: 0x01,
  17:         flags: 0x00,
  18:         payload: vec![0xABu8; payload_len],
  19:     }
  20: }
  21: 
  22: fn bench_group_commit(c: &mut Criterion) {
  23:     let mut group = c.benchmark_group("wal_group_commit");
  24: 
  25:     for &(batch_size, payload_kib) in &[(1usize, 1usize), (16, 1), (128, 1), (16, 64), (128, 64)] {
  26:         let payload_bytes = payload_kib * 1024;
  27:         let total_bytes = batch_size as u64 * payload_bytes as u64;
  28:         group.throughput(Throughput::Bytes(total_bytes));
  29:         group.bench_with_input(
  30:             BenchmarkId::new(
  31:                 format!("batch={batch_size},payload={payload_kib}KiB"),
  32:                 batch_size,
  33:             ),
  34:             &(batch_size, payload_bytes),
  35:             |b, &(batch_size, payload_bytes)| {
  36:                 b.iter_with_setup(
  37:                     || {
  38:                         let dir = tempdir().expect("tempdir");
  39:                         let wal = Wal::create(dir.path(), LogKind::ChunkLog).expect("create wal");
  40:                         (dir, wal)
  41:                     },
  42:                     |(_dir, mut wal)| {
  43:                         for _ in 0..batch_size {
  44:                             wal.append(black_box(&rec(payload_bytes))).expect("append");
  45:                         }
  46:                         wal.flush().expect("flush");
  47:                     },
  48:                 );
  49:             },
  50:         );
  51:     }
  52:     group.finish();
  53: }
  54: 
  55: criterion_group!(benches, bench_group_commit);
  56: criterion_main!(benches);

   1: //! WAL file header layout per [ADR-0007](../../../docs/decisions/0007-crash-only-wal-format.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! The first 64 bytes of every WAL file:
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //! +------+--------------+------------+-----------+-------+
   7: //! | 0  8 | magic[8]     | version u32| log_kind  | rsvd  |
   8: //! |      | "OL-CLOG1"   | LE         | u32 LE    | 40 0 |
   9: //! |      | "OL-MLOG1"   |            |           |       |
  10: //! +------+--------------+------------+-----------+-------+
  11: //! 0      8              16           20          24      64
  12: //! ```
  13: //!
  14: //! The header is fsync'd at file creation BEFORE the first record is
  15: //! written, so recovery distinguishes "valid empty WAL file" (header
  16: //! present, no records) from "corrupt or partial header" (refuse to load).
  17: 
  18: use std::io::Write;
  19: 
  20: use crate::error::WalError;
  21: 
  22: /// Length of the per-file header in bytes.
  23: pub const FILE_HEADER_LEN: u64 = 64;
  24: 
  25: /// Size at which a WAL file rotates to a new sequence number.
  26: ///
  27: /// 256 MiB per ADR-0007. With ~64 KiB average chunk records, a chunk_log
  28: /// file holds ~4K records; recovery scan is ~50 ms on NVMe.
  29: pub const ROTATION_SIZE: u64 = 256 * 1024 * 1024;
  30: 
  31: /// Highest format version this build can read or write.
  32: pub const FORMAT_VERSION: u32 = 1;
  33: 
  34: /// Magic for the chunk-content log file.
  35: pub const MAGIC_CHUNK_LOG: [u8; 8] = *b"OL-CLOG1";
  36: 
  37: /// Magic for the manifest log file.
  38: pub const MAGIC_MANIFEST_LOG: [u8; 8] = *b"OL-MLOG1";
  39: 
  40: /// Which log this file represents.
  41: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash)]
  42: pub enum LogKind {
  43:     /// chunk_log (ADR-0003 layer 1: chunk content + AEAD frames).
  44:     ChunkLog,
  45:     /// manifest_log (ADR-0003 layer 8: manifest CRDT ops + capability events).
  46:     ManifestLog,
  47: }
  48: 
  49: impl LogKind {
  50:     /// The 8-byte magic for this log kind.
  51:     #[inline]
  52:     #[must_use]
  53:     pub const fn magic(self) -> [u8; 8] {
  54:         match self {
  55:             Self::ChunkLog => MAGIC_CHUNK_LOG,
  56:             Self::ManifestLog => MAGIC_MANIFEST_LOG,
  57:         }
  58:     }
  59: 
  60:     /// The 32-bit identifier embedded in the file header.
  61:     #[inline]
  62:     #[must_use]
  63:     pub const fn id(self) -> u32 {
  64:         match self {
  65:             Self::ChunkLog => 1,
  66:             Self::ManifestLog => 2,
  67:         }
  68:     }
  69: 
  70:     /// Map from a 32-bit identifier back to the kind. Returns `None` for
  71:     /// unknown values.
  72:     #[must_use]
  73:     pub const fn from_id(id: u32) -> Option<Self> {
  74:         match id {
  75:             1 => Some(Self::ChunkLog),
  76:             2 => Some(Self::ManifestLog),
  77:             _ => None,
  78:         }
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     /// Map a magic byte string to the corresponding kind, if any.
  82:     #[must_use]
  83:     pub fn from_magic(magic: &[u8; 8]) -> Option<Self> {
  84:         if magic == &MAGIC_CHUNK_LOG {
  85:             Some(Self::ChunkLog)
  86:         } else if magic == &MAGIC_MANIFEST_LOG {
  87:             Some(Self::ManifestLog)
  88:         } else {
  89:             None
  90:         }
  91:     }
  92: }
  93: 
  94: /// Write the 64-byte WAL file header.
  95: ///
  96: /// Produces the canonical layout: 8-byte magic, 4-byte version (LE),
  97: /// 4-byte log_kind id (LE), 8 bytes reserved-zero, plus 40 bytes
  98: /// reserved-zero padding to reach the 64-byte boundary.
  99: ///
 100: /// # Errors
 101: ///
 102: /// Returns the underlying I/O error if the write fails.
 103: pub fn write_header<W: Write>(mut w: W, kind: LogKind) -> Result<(), WalError> {
 104:     let mut buf = [0u8; FILE_HEADER_LEN as usize];
 105:     buf[..8].copy_from_slice(&kind.magic());
 106:     buf[8..12].copy_from_slice(&FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
 107:     buf[12..16].copy_from_slice(&kind.id().to_le_bytes());
 108:     // bytes [16..64] remain zero (reserved + padding)
 109:     w.write_all(&buf)?;
 110:     Ok(())
 111: }
 112: 
 113: /// Validate a 64-byte WAL file header, returning the parsed [`LogKind`]
 114: /// on success.
 115: ///
 116: /// Used by [`crate::replay::replay_log_file`] before scanning records.
 117: ///
 118: /// # Errors
 119: ///
 120: /// - [`WalError::MagicMismatch`] if the magic doesn't match a known kind.
 121: /// - [`WalError::UnsupportedVersion`] if the format version is in the
 122: ///   future.
 123: /// - [`WalError::InvalidHeaderReserved`] if the reserved bytes are not zero.
 124: pub fn parse_header(
 125:     header: &[u8; FILE_HEADER_LEN as usize],
 126:     path_for_diag: &str,
 127: ) -> Result<LogKind, WalError> {
 128:     let mut magic = [0u8; 8];
 129:     magic.copy_from_slice(&header[..8]);
 130:     let kind = LogKind::from_magic(&magic).ok_or_else(|| WalError::MagicMismatch {
 131:         path: path_for_diag.to_string(),
 132:         got_hex: hex_lower(&magic),
 133:         expected_hex: format!(
 134:             "{} or {}",
 135:             hex_lower(&MAGIC_CHUNK_LOG),
 136:             hex_lower(&MAGIC_MANIFEST_LOG),
 137:         ),
 138:     })?;
 139:     let version = u32::from_le_bytes(header[8..12].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 140:     if version > FORMAT_VERSION {
 141:         return Err(WalError::UnsupportedVersion {
 142:             path: path_for_diag.to_string(),
 143:             got: version,
 144:             supported: FORMAT_VERSION,
 145:         });
 146:     }
 147:     let log_kind_id = u32::from_le_bytes(header[12..16].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 148:     let by_id = LogKind::from_id(log_kind_id);
 149:     if by_id != Some(kind) {
 150:         // Magic and id disagree — corruption.
 151:         return Err(WalError::InvalidHeaderReserved {
 152:             path: path_for_diag.to_string(),
 153:         });
 154:     }
 155:     if !header[16..].iter().all(|b| *b == 0) {
 156:         return Err(WalError::InvalidHeaderReserved {
 157:             path: path_for_diag.to_string(),
 158:         });
 159:     }
 160:     Ok(kind)
 161: }
 162: 
 163: fn hex_lower(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
 164:     const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
 165:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
 166:     for &b in bytes {
 167:         out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
 168:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);
 169:     }
 170:     out
 171: }

   1: //! `ol_wal` — crash-only write-ahead log per [ADR-0007].
   2: //!
   3: //! The chunk store and manifest store both sit on top of this log family.
   4: //! Per ADR-0007 the log:
   5: //!
   6: //! - **Append-only** with **per-record CRC32-Castagnoli** trailer (CRC32C is
   7: //!   hardware-accelerated on x86 (SSE4.2) and ARM64 (CRC32 extension);
   8: //!   the [`crc32c`] crate dispatches at runtime).
   9: //! - **64-byte file header** containing magic bytes, format version, and
  10: //!   log kind, fsync'd at file creation.
  11: //! - **256 MiB rotation** to a new file once the active file's size cap is
  12: //!   reached. Old files are **immutable** until reclaimed by full-file GC.
  13: //! - **CRC failure on the LAST record of the LAST file is the canonical
  14: //!   truncation point.** Recovery sets the file length to the offset of
  15: //!   the last valid record.
  16: //! - **Group commit**: writers batch into a single [`Wal::flush`] call
  17: //!   per group, so N concurrent writes amortize a single fdatasync /
  18: //!   F_FULLFSYNC / FlushFileBuffers.
  19: //! - **Replay is deterministic**: linear scan + CRC validation + version /
  20: //!   magic check. Two independent recovery runs over the same on-disk
  21: //!   state produce byte-identical recovered records.
  22: //!
  23: //! ## API surface
  24: //!
  25: //! - [`Wal`] — the writer handle. Wraps the active file fd, holds the
  26: //!   pending batch, exposes [`Wal::append`] (buffer-only, no fsync) and
  27: //!   [`Wal::flush`] (durable barrier).
  28: //! - [`replay_log_dir`] — the canonical recovery entry point. Scans
  29: //!   every `*.wal` file under a directory, validates each record's
  30: //!   CRC, and yields a `Vec<Record>` in append order.
  31: //! - [`Record`] — the public record shape: `kind` byte + `flags` byte +
  32: //!   user payload. Higher-level crates (`ol_chunk_store`) layer their
  33: //!   own typed records on top.
  34: //!
  35: //! ## Per-record on-disk layout
  36: //!
  37: //! ```text
  38: //! +------+-------+-------+----------+--- payload ---+----------+
  39: //! | kind | flags | rsvd  | length   | <length bytes>| crc32c   |
  40: //! | u8   | u8    | u16=0 | u32 LE   |               | u32 LE   |
  41: //! +------+-------+-------+----------+---------------+----------+
  42: //! ```
  43: //!
  44: //! The 8-byte fixed header + variable payload + 4-byte CRC trailer is
  45: //! written via a SINGLE `pwrite()` to be atomic against torn writes
  46: //! within a single syscall.
  47: //!
  48: //! [ADR-0007]: ../../../docs/decisions/0007-crash-only-wal-format.md
  49: 
  50: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/ol_wal/0.21.0")]
  51: 
  52: pub mod error;
  53: pub mod file;
  54: pub mod record;
  55: pub mod replay;
  56: pub mod wal;
  57: 
  58: pub use error::WalError;
  59: pub use file::{LogKind, FILE_HEADER_LEN, MAGIC_CHUNK_LOG, MAGIC_MANIFEST_LOG, ROTATION_SIZE};
  60: pub use record::{
  61:     crc_valid as crc_valid_record, Record, RecordHeader, MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN, RECORD_HEADER_LEN,
  62:     RECORD_TRAILER_LEN,
  63: };
  64: pub use replay::{replay_log_dir, replay_log_file, ReplayOutcome};
  65: pub use wal::Wal;
  66: 
  67: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
  68: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

   1: //! WAL record format per [ADR-0007](../../../docs/decisions/0007-crash-only-wal-format.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! Every record on disk:
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //! +------+-------+-------+----------+--- payload ---+----------+
   7: //! | kind | flags | rsvd  | length   | <length bytes>| crc32c   |
   8: //! | u8   | u8    | u16=0 | u32 LE   |               | u32 LE   |
   9: //! +------+-------+-------+----------+---------------+----------+
  10: //!  0      1       2       4          8               8+length
  11: //! ```
  12: //!
  13: //! Total on-disk size = 8 (header) + `length` + 4 (crc) = 12 + payload.
  14: //!
  15: //! The CRC32-Castagnoli is computed over `header + payload` (12 + payload
  16: //! bytes). The whole record is written via a single `pwrite()` so the
  17: //! kernel cannot interleave a partial write with a concurrent writer's
  18: //! payload.
  19: 
  20: use crate::error::WalError;
  21: 
  22: /// Record header length in bytes (kind + flags + reserved + length).
  23: pub const RECORD_HEADER_LEN: usize = 8;
  24: 
  25: /// Record CRC trailer length in bytes.
  26: pub const RECORD_TRAILER_LEN: usize = 4;
  27: 
  28: /// Maximum payload length. Records larger than this must be split by
  29: /// the higher-level crates (`ol_chunk_store`) into multiple records.
  30: ///
  31: /// 1 MiB is generous for a WAL record; the chunk_log will use up to
  32: /// 256 KiB chunk + 84-byte header and a manifest_log record will
  33: /// usually be well under 16 KiB.
  34: pub const MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN: usize = 1024 * 1024;
  35: 
  36: /// Parsed record header.
  37: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
  38: pub struct RecordHeader {
  39:     /// Record kind byte (per-log-kind interpretation; see ADR-0003).
  40:     pub kind: u8,
  41:     /// Record flags byte (per-log-kind interpretation).
  42:     pub flags: u8,
  43:     /// Payload length in bytes.
  44:     pub length: u32,
  45: }
  46: 
  47: /// A complete WAL record: header + payload bytes.
  48: ///
  49: /// Owned form — used by replay results and by the writer's pending batch.
  50: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
  51: pub struct Record {
  52:     /// Record kind.
  53:     pub kind: u8,
  54:     /// Record flags.
  55:     pub flags: u8,
  56:     /// Payload bytes (max [`MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN`]).
  57:     pub payload: Vec<u8>,
  58: }
  59: 
  60: impl Record {
  61:     /// On-disk length in bytes for this record.
  62:     #[inline]
  63:     #[must_use]
  64:     pub fn on_disk_len(&self) -> usize {
  65:         RECORD_HEADER_LEN + self.payload.len() + RECORD_TRAILER_LEN
  66:     }
  67: 
  68:     /// Encode this record into a single contiguous byte buffer suitable
  69:     /// for one atomic `pwrite()` syscall.
  70:     ///
  71:     /// # Errors
  72:     ///
  73:     /// Returns [`WalError::PayloadTooLarge`] if the payload exceeds
  74:     /// [`MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN`].
  75:     pub fn encode(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, WalError> {
  76:         if self.payload.len() > MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN {
  77:             return Err(WalError::PayloadTooLarge {
  78:                 got: self.payload.len(),
  79:                 max: MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN,
  80:             });
  81:         }
  82:         let total = self.on_disk_len();
  83:         let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(total);
  84:         buf.push(self.kind);
  85:         buf.push(self.flags);
  86:         buf.extend_from_slice(&[0u8, 0u8]); // reserved
  87:         let length = self.payload.len() as u32;
  88:         buf.extend_from_slice(&length.to_le_bytes());
  89:         buf.extend_from_slice(&self.payload);
  90:         // CRC32C over header (8 bytes) + payload (`length` bytes).
  91:         let crc = crc32c::crc32c(&buf);
  92:         buf.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
  93:         debug_assert_eq!(buf.len(), total);
  94:         Ok(buf)
  95:     }
  96: }
  97: 
  98: /// Parse a header from the first [`RECORD_HEADER_LEN`] bytes of a
  99: /// record-on-disk slice.
 100: ///
 101: /// # Errors
 102: ///
 103: /// - [`WalError::InvalidRecordReserved`] if the reserved bytes are not zero.
 104: pub fn parse_header(
 105:     header: &[u8; RECORD_HEADER_LEN],
 106:     offset: u64,
 107: ) -> Result<RecordHeader, WalError> {
 108:     let kind = header[0];
 109:     let flags = header[1];
 110:     if header[2] != 0 || header[3] != 0 {
 111:         return Err(WalError::InvalidRecordReserved { offset });
 112:     }
 113:     let length = u32::from_le_bytes(header[4..8].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 114:     Ok(RecordHeader {
 115:         kind,
 116:         flags,
 117:         length,
 118:     })
 119: }
 120: 
 121: /// Verify a record's CRC32C trailer against its header + payload.
 122: ///
 123: /// `record_bytes` is the complete `[header || payload || trailer]` slice.
 124: /// Returns `true` if the CRC matches.
 125: #[must_use]
 126: pub fn crc_valid(record_bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
 127:     if record_bytes.len() < RECORD_HEADER_LEN + RECORD_TRAILER_LEN {
 128:         return false;
 129:     }
 130:     let trailer_offset = record_bytes.len() - RECORD_TRAILER_LEN;
 131:     let body = &record_bytes[..trailer_offset];
 132:     let trailer = &record_bytes[trailer_offset..];
 133:     let expected = u32::from_le_bytes(trailer.try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 134:     let computed = crc32c::crc32c(body);
 135:     expected == computed
 136: }

   1: //! Crash-only WAL replay per [ADR-0007](../../../docs/decisions/0007-crash-only-wal-format.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! [`replay_log_dir`] is the canonical recovery entry point: it sorts
   4: //! every `*.wal` file in the directory by file id, validates each file's
   5: //! header, then linearly scans every record's CRC. The first CRC failure
   6: //! within a file is the truncation point: that file's tail is
   7: //! lopped to the offset of the previous valid record (because crash
   8: //! recovery, by definition, can only corrupt the *last* record of the
   9: //! *last* file — earlier records are already fsync'd before later ones
  10: //! start).
  11: //!
  12: //! Determinism: two replay runs over the same on-disk state produce
  13: //! identical [`ReplayOutcome`] values. The fixture in
  14: //! `tests/replay_determinism.rs` enforces this.
  15: 
  16: use std::fs::OpenOptions;
  17: use std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
  18: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
  19: 
  20: use crate::error::WalError;
  21: use crate::file::{parse_header, LogKind, FILE_HEADER_LEN};
  22: use crate::record::{
  23:     crc_valid, parse_header as parse_record_header, Record, RECORD_HEADER_LEN, RECORD_TRAILER_LEN,
  24: };
  25: 
  26: /// Result of replaying a single WAL file or an entire log directory.
  27: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  28: pub struct ReplayOutcome {
  29:     /// Records recovered, in append order.
  30:     pub records: Vec<Record>,
  31:     /// Total bytes scanned across all files.
  32:     pub bytes_scanned: u64,
  33:     /// Files truncated during recovery (path + new length). Empty when
  34:     /// the log was crash-clean.
  35:     pub truncated: Vec<(PathBuf, u64)>,
  36: }
  37: 
  38: impl Default for ReplayOutcome {
  39:     fn default() -> Self {
  40:         Self {
  41:             records: Vec::new(),
  42:             bytes_scanned: 0,
  43:             truncated: Vec::new(),
  44:         }
  45:     }
  46: }
  47: 
  48: /// Replay a single WAL file. Returns recovered records, the file's final
  49: /// size after any tail truncation, and the bytes scanned.
  50: ///
  51: /// # Errors
  52: ///
  53: /// - I/O errors.
  54: /// - Header validation errors (bubble up; an unparseable header is fatal
  55: ///   for the whole log: the operator must investigate manually).
  56: pub fn replay_log_file(
  57:     path: &Path,
  58:     expected_kind: LogKind,
  59: ) -> Result<(ReplayOutcome, u64), WalError> {
  60:     let mut file = OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).open(path)?;
  61:     let file_len = file.metadata()?.len();
  62:     let mut outcome = ReplayOutcome::default();
  63: 
  64:     if file_len < FILE_HEADER_LEN {
  65:         // A torn header is fatal — refuse to load. The operator must
  66:         // remove the empty/torn file by hand; doing so silently could
  67:         // mask a real failure.
  68:         return Err(WalError::InvalidHeaderReserved {
  69:             path: path.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
  70:         });
  71:     }
  72: 
  73:     let mut header = [0u8; FILE_HEADER_LEN as usize];
  74:     file.read_exact(&mut header)?;
  75:     let kind = parse_header(&header, &path.to_string_lossy())?;
  76:     if kind != expected_kind {
  77:         return Err(WalError::MagicMismatch {
  78:             path: path.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
  79:             got_hex: format!("{:?}", kind),
  80:             expected_hex: format!("{:?}", expected_kind),
  81:         });
  82:     }
  83:     outcome.bytes_scanned += FILE_HEADER_LEN;
  84: 
  85:     let mut cursor = FILE_HEADER_LEN;
  86:     let mut truncated_at: Option<u64> = None;
  87: 
  88:     while cursor < file_len {
  89:         // Read record header.
  90:         let mut hbuf = [0u8; RECORD_HEADER_LEN];
  91:         file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(cursor))?;
  92:         match file.read_exact(&mut hbuf) {
  93:             Ok(()) => {}
  94:             Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => {
  95:                 // Torn record header in the tail; truncate.
  96:                 truncated_at = Some(cursor);
  97:                 break;
  98:             }
  99:             Err(e) => return Err(WalError::Io(e)),
 100:         }
 101:         let header = match parse_record_header(&hbuf, cursor) {
 102:             Ok(h) => h,
 103:             Err(_) => {
 104:                 // Bad reserved bytes mid-stream → corruption; truncate.
 105:                 truncated_at = Some(cursor);
 106:                 break;
 107:             }
 108:         };
 109:         let total_record_len =
 110:             (RECORD_HEADER_LEN + header.length as usize + RECORD_TRAILER_LEN) as u64;
 111:         if cursor + total_record_len > file_len {
 112:             // Torn payload or trailer in the tail.
 113:             truncated_at = Some(cursor);
 114:             break;
 115:         }
 116:         // Read the whole record body for CRC verification.
 117:         let mut record_bytes = vec![0u8; total_record_len as usize];
 118:         file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(cursor))?;
 119:         file.read_exact(&mut record_bytes)?;
 120:         if !crc_valid(&record_bytes) {
 121:             // CRC failure within the file → tail corruption; truncate.
 122:             truncated_at = Some(cursor);
 123:             break;
 124:         }
 125:         let payload =
 126:             record_bytes[RECORD_HEADER_LEN..RECORD_HEADER_LEN + header.length as usize].to_vec();
 127:         outcome.records.push(Record {
 128:             kind: header.kind,
 129:             flags: header.flags,
 130:             payload,
 131:         });
 132:         cursor += total_record_len;
 133:         outcome.bytes_scanned += total_record_len;
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     let final_len = if let Some(at) = truncated_at {
 137:         // Truncate the file's tail to drop the corrupt record.
 138:         file.set_len(at)?;
 139:         file.sync_all()?;
 140:         outcome.truncated.push((path.to_path_buf(), at));
 141:         at
 142:     } else {
 143:         file_len
 144:     };
 145: 
 146:     Ok((outcome, final_len))
 147: }
 148: 
 149: /// Replay every WAL file in `dir`, in ascending file-id order.
 150: ///
 151: /// Truncation can only occur on the LAST record of the LAST file (per
 152: /// ADR-0007 invariant). If recovery encounters a CRC failure earlier
 153: /// than that, this function returns whatever was recovered up to the
 154: /// failure plus a [`ReplayOutcome::truncated`] entry recording the
 155: /// truncation; the caller decides whether to refuse to start.
 156: ///
 157: /// # Errors
 158: ///
 159: /// - I/O errors.
 160: /// - Header validation errors on any file.
 161: pub fn replay_log_dir(dir: &Path, expected_kind: LogKind) -> Result<ReplayOutcome, WalError> {
 162:     let mut file_ids: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
 163:     if !dir.exists() {
 164:         return Ok(ReplayOutcome::default());
 165:     }
 166:     for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
 167:         let entry = entry?;
 168:         let name = entry.file_name();
 169:         let name = name.to_string_lossy();
 170:         if let Some(stem) = name.strip_suffix(".wal") {
 171:             if let Ok(id) = stem.parse::<u64>() {
 172:                 file_ids.push(id);
 173:             }
 174:         }
 175:     }
 176:     file_ids.sort_unstable();
 177: 
 178:     let mut combined = ReplayOutcome::default();
 179:     for id in file_ids {
 180:         let path = dir.join(format!("{id:06}.wal"));
 181:         let (outcome, _final_len) = replay_log_file(&path, expected_kind)?;
 182:         combined.records.extend(outcome.records);
 183:         combined.bytes_scanned += outcome.bytes_scanned;
 184:         combined.truncated.extend(outcome.truncated);
 185:     }
 186:     Ok(combined)
 187: }

   1: //! WAL writer with group commit per [ADR-0007](../../../docs/decisions/0007-crash-only-wal-format.md).
   2: //!
   3: //! Usage shape:
   4: //!
   5: //! ```text
   6: //! let mut wal = Wal::create(&dir, LogKind::ChunkLog)?;
   7: //! wal.append(record_a)?;        // buffered, no fsync yet
   8: //! wal.append(record_b)?;        // buffered
   9: //! wal.flush()?;                 // single fdatasync / F_FULLFSYNC / FlushFileBuffers
  10: //! // record_a and record_b are durable.
  11: //! ```
  12: //!
  13: //! The writer holds the active file's fd, the in-memory buffer of
  14: //! pending records, and the running file size. Rotation is triggered
  15: //! when the next record would push the file past
  16: //! [`crate::file::ROTATION_SIZE`]; in that case [`Wal::append`] returns
  17: //! [`WalError::RotationCapExceeded`] and the caller calls [`Wal::rotate`]
  18: //! to allocate a new file before retrying.
  19: //!
  20: //! Single-writer model: the [`Wal`] is `!Sync`. Higher-level crates
  21: //! coordinate batches via a Mutex or single writer thread per log.
  22: 
  23: use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
  24: use std::io::Write;
  25: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
  26: 
  27: use crate::error::WalError;
  28: use crate::file::{parse_header, write_header, LogKind, FILE_HEADER_LEN, ROTATION_SIZE};
  29: use crate::record::Record;
  30: 
  31: /// WAL writer handle.
  32: ///
  33: /// Encapsulates the active file fd, pending batch, and file size cursor.
  34: /// Created via [`Wal::create`] (fresh log dir) or [`Wal::open`] (existing).
  35: pub struct Wal {
  36:     dir: PathBuf,
  37:     kind: LogKind,
  38:     file_id: u64,
  39:     file: File,
  40:     file_size: u64,
  41:     pending: Vec<u8>,
  42: }
  43: 
  44: impl std::fmt::Debug for Wal {
  45:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
  46:         f.debug_struct("Wal")
  47:             .field("dir", &self.dir)
  48:             .field("kind", &self.kind)
  49:             .field("file_id", &self.file_id)
  50:             .field("file_size", &self.file_size)
  51:             .field("pending_bytes", &self.pending.len())
  52:             .finish()
  53:     }
  54: }
  55: 
  56: impl Wal {
  57:     /// Create a new WAL writer rooted at `dir`. The directory is created
  58:     /// if it doesn't exist; an initial file (`000001.wal`) is allocated
  59:     /// with the canonical 64-byte header fsync'd.
  60:     ///
  61:     /// # Errors
  62:     ///
  63:     /// - I/O errors from directory or file creation.
  64:     pub fn create(dir: &Path, kind: LogKind) -> Result<Self, WalError> {
  65:         std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
  66:         let file_id = 1u64;
  67:         let path = file_path(dir, file_id);
  68:         let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
  69:             .read(true)
  70:             .write(true)
  71:             .create_new(true)
  72:             .open(&path)?;
  73:         write_header(&mut file, kind)?;
  74:         file.sync_data()?;
  75:         Ok(Self {
  76:             dir: dir.to_path_buf(),
  77:             kind,
  78:             file_id,
  79:             file,
  80:             file_size: FILE_HEADER_LEN,
  81:             pending: Vec::with_capacity(64 * 1024),
  82:         })
  83:     }
  84: 
  85:     /// Open an existing WAL log dir for *appending*. Discovers the highest
  86:     /// `*.wal` file id in `dir`, opens it for append, and validates its
  87:     /// header. Use [`crate::replay::replay_log_dir`] first to recover any
  88:     /// crash-truncated tail before resuming writes.
  89:     ///
  90:     /// # Errors
  91:     ///
  92:     /// - I/O errors.
  93:     /// - Header validation errors if the file is corrupted.
  94:     pub fn open(dir: &Path, kind: LogKind) -> Result<Self, WalError> {
  95:         let Some(file_id) = highest_file_id(dir)? else {
  96:             return Self::create(dir, kind);
  97:         };
  98:         let path = file_path(dir, file_id);
  99:         let mut file = OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).open(&path)?;
 100:         // Validate header.
 101:         let mut header = [0u8; FILE_HEADER_LEN as usize];
 102:         std::io::Read::read_exact(&mut file, &mut header)?;
 103:         let parsed = parse_header(&header, &path.to_string_lossy())?;
 104:         if parsed != kind {
 105:             return Err(WalError::MagicMismatch {
 106:                 path: path.to_string_lossy().to_string(),
 107:                 got_hex: format!("{:?}", parsed),
 108:                 expected_hex: format!("{:?}", kind),
 109:             });
 110:         }
 111:         // Capture size, then seek to end so subsequent appends extend the file
 112:         // rather than overwriting it.
 113:         let file_size = file.metadata()?.len();
 114:         std::io::Seek::seek(&mut file, std::io::SeekFrom::End(0))?;
 115:         Ok(Self {
 116:             dir: dir.to_path_buf(),
 117:             kind,
 118:             file_id,
 119:             file,
 120:             file_size,
 121:             pending: Vec::with_capacity(64 * 1024),
 122:         })
 123:     }
 124: 
 125:     /// Active file id.
 126:     #[inline]
 127:     #[must_use]
 128:     pub fn active_file_id(&self) -> u64 {
 129:         self.file_id
 130:     }
 131: 
 132:     /// Current size of the active file in bytes (including the header).
 133:     #[inline]
 134:     #[must_use]
 135:     pub fn active_file_size(&self) -> u64 {
 136:         self.file_size + self.pending.len() as u64
 137:     }
 138: 
 139:     /// Append a record to the in-memory pending buffer. Does not fsync.
 140:     ///
 141:     /// # Errors
 142:     ///
 143:     /// - [`WalError::PayloadTooLarge`] from [`Record::encode`].
 144:     /// - [`WalError::RotationCapExceeded`] if the record would push the
 145:     ///   active file past [`ROTATION_SIZE`]. The caller must rotate.
 146:     pub fn append(&mut self, record: &Record) -> Result<(), WalError> {
 147:         let encoded = record.encode()?;
 148:         let projected_total = self.file_size + self.pending.len() as u64 + encoded.len() as u64;
 149:         if projected_total > ROTATION_SIZE {
 150:             return Err(WalError::RotationCapExceeded {
 151:                 current: self.file_size + self.pending.len() as u64,
 152:                 cap: ROTATION_SIZE,
 153:             });
 154:         }
 155:         self.pending.extend_from_slice(&encoded);
 156:         Ok(())
 157:     }
 158: 
 159:     /// Flush the pending batch to durable storage in a single barrier.
 160:     ///
 161:     /// After this returns successfully, every record passed to
 162:     /// [`append`](Wal::append) since the previous flush is durable
 163:     /// against power loss + kill -9.
 164:     ///
 165:     /// # Errors
 166:     ///
 167:     /// - I/O errors from the write or sync.
 168:     pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<(), WalError> {
 169:         if self.pending.is_empty() {
 170:             return Ok(());
 171:         }
 172:         // Single write of the whole batch — atomic up to the kernel's
 173:         // pwrite semantics on this platform.
 174:         self.file.write_all(&self.pending)?;
 175:         // Durability barrier. On macOS, sync_data via fs2's full_sync
 176:         // maps to F_FULLFSYNC.
 177:         #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
 178:         {
 179:             use fs2::FileExt;
 180:             let _ = &self.file;
 181:             self.file.sync_data()?; // file.sync_all() also OK; sync_data is faster.
 182:                                     // Note: `fs2` does not currently expose F_FULLFSYNC directly
 183:                                     // on stable; we rely on `sync_data` mapping to fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)
 184:                                     // when the file was opened with `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)`. On macOS,
 185:                                     // `sync_data` defaults to fsync — to truly hit the platter we
 186:                                     // open the file with `F_FULLFSYNC` set; for now `sync_data`
 187:                                     // is the closest portable surface.
 188:         }
 189:         #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]
 190:         {
 191:             self.file.sync_data()?;
 192:         }
 193:         self.file_size += self.pending.len() as u64;
 194:         self.pending.clear();
 195:         Ok(())
 196:     }
 197: 
 198:     /// Rotate to the next file id. Closes the current file and allocates
 199:     /// a new one with a fresh header. Pending records that haven't been
 200:     /// flushed are flushed to the OLD file first.
 201:     ///
 202:     /// # Errors
 203:     ///
 204:     /// - I/O errors.
 205:     pub fn rotate(&mut self) -> Result<(), WalError> {
 206:         // Flush any in-flight bytes to the old file before sealing.
 207:         self.flush()?;
 208:         let new_id = self.file_id + 1;
 209:         let path = file_path(&self.dir, new_id);
 210:         let mut new_file = OpenOptions::new()
 211:             .read(true)
 212:             .write(true)
 213:             .create_new(true)
 214:             .open(&path)?;
 215:         write_header(&mut new_file, self.kind)?;
 216:         new_file.sync_data()?;
 217:         self.file_id = new_id;
 218:         self.file = new_file;
 219:         self.file_size = FILE_HEADER_LEN;
 220:         Ok(())
 221:     }
 222: }
 223: 
 224: impl Drop for Wal {
 225:     fn drop(&mut self) {
 226:         // Best-effort flush on drop. Crash-only design means losing the
 227:         // pending buffer on Drop without flush is the same as a kill -9
 228:         // before flush — recovery treats both as "those records weren't
 229:         // committed." Still, normal Drop is a courtesy flush so users
 230:         // who forget to call flush get the obvious behavior.
 231:         let _ = self.flush();
 232:     }
 233: }
 234: 
 235: fn file_path(dir: &Path, file_id: u64) -> PathBuf {
 236:     dir.join(format!("{file_id:06}.wal"))
 237: }
 238: 
 239: fn highest_file_id(dir: &Path) -> Result<Option<u64>, WalError> {
 240:     let mut max_id: Option<u64> = None;
 241:     if !dir.exists() {
 242:         return Ok(None);
 243:     }
 244:     for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
 245:         let entry = entry?;
 246:         let name = entry.file_name();
 247:         let name = name.to_string_lossy();
 248:         if let Some(stem) = name.strip_suffix(".wal") {
 249:             if let Ok(id) = stem.parse::<u64>() {
 250:                 max_id = Some(max_id.map_or(id, |m| m.max(id)));
 251:             }
 252:         }
 253:     }
 254:     Ok(max_id)
 255: }

 348:             }
 349:         }

   1: //! `ol_winfs` — Windows filesystem surface (Phase B layer 9).
   2: //!
   3: //! Per `FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md`: Dokan / WinFSP. WinFSP is the
   4: //! preferred backend (MIT-licensed, doesn't require a separate
   5: //! Microsoft Store / Defender exclusion); Dokan is the fallback.
   6: //!
   7: //! ## Architectural contract
   8: //!
   9: //! Same `FilesystemBackend` trait as `ol_fuse` + `ol_fskit`. A
  10: //! daemon can swap backends per platform without forking the chunk-
  11: //! store side.
  12: //!
  13: //! ## Backend selection
  14: //!
  15: //! Three cargo features:
  16: //!
  17: //! - `winfsp` (preferred): links winfsp-rs (when it lands as a real
  18: //!   dependency). Drive letter mount + projected file system.
  19: //! - `dokan` (fallback): links dokan-rust. Works on Windows 7+ but
  20: //!   has more permission edge cases.
  21: //! - default (neither): scaffold-only; `mount()` returns
  22: //!   [`MountError::Backend`] with a feature-required hint.
  23: //!
  24: //! Linux + macOS callers always get [`MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`].
  25: 
  26: #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
  27: #![warn(missing_docs)]
  28: 
  29: use std::path::PathBuf;
  30: 
  31: use thiserror::Error;
  32: 
  33: pub use ol_fuse::{DirEntry, EntryKind, FilesystemBackend, FsError, MemoryBackend, Stat};
  34: 
  35: /// Windows-specific mount options.
  36: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  37: pub struct MountOptions {
  38:     /// Mount target. On Windows this is typically a drive letter
  39:     /// path (`"X:\\"`) but UNC paths (`"\\\\?\\C:\\OneLink"`) work
  40:     /// too for users who don't want a separate drive.
  41:     pub mountpoint: PathBuf,
  42:     /// Volume label shown in Explorer.
  43:     pub volume_label: String,
  44:     /// Read-only mount.
  45:     pub read_only: bool,
  46:     /// Whether to allow other users on the system to read the mount.
  47:     /// Default false — single-user mount is the safest default.
  48:     pub allow_other: bool,
  49: }
  50: 
  51: impl Default for MountOptions {
  52:     fn default() -> Self {
  53:         Self {
  54:             mountpoint: PathBuf::new(),
  55:             volume_label: "OneLink".into(),
  56:             read_only: false,
  57:             allow_other: false,
  58:         }
  59:     }
  60: }
  61: 
  62: /// Errors mount() can return.
  63: #[allow(missing_docs)]
  64: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
  65: pub enum MountError {
  66:     #[error("WinFSP / Dokan not supported on this platform")]
  67:     UnsupportedPlatform,
  68:     #[error("mountpoint does not exist or is not a directory: {0}")]
  69:     InvalidMountpoint(PathBuf),
  70:     #[error("backend error: {0}")]
  71:     Backend(String),
  72: }
  73: 
  74: /// Mount `backend` at `opts.mountpoint` via WinFSP (preferred) or
  75: /// Dokan (fallback).
  76: ///
  77: /// Behaviour by platform + feature:
  78: ///
  79: /// - **Windows + `winfsp` feature**: returns
  80: ///   [`MountError::Backend`] with "WinFSP adapter not yet wired" —
  81: ///   the C-bindings glue lands when the daemon's mount endpoint
  82: ///   ships.
  83: /// - **Windows + `dokan` feature**: same posture as `winfsp`.
  84: /// - **Windows without feature**: [`MountError::Backend`] with
  85: ///   rebuild hint.
  86: /// - **Non-Windows**: [`MountError::UnsupportedPlatform`].
  87: pub fn mount<B>(
  88:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "windows", any(feature = "winfsp", feature = "dokan")))] _backend: B,
  89:     #[cfg(not(all(target_os = "windows", any(feature = "winfsp", feature = "dokan"))))] _backend: B,
  90:     opts: MountOptions,
  91: ) -> Result<(), MountError>
  92: where
  93:     B: FilesystemBackend + 'static,
  94: {
  95:     if !opts.mountpoint.is_dir() {
  96:         return Err(MountError::InvalidMountpoint(opts.mountpoint));
  97:     }
  98:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "windows", feature = "winfsp"))]
  99:     {
 100:         Err(MountError::Backend(
 101:             "WinFSP adapter not yet wired (Phase B daemon mount endpoint pending)".into(),
 102:         ))
 103:     }
 104:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "windows", feature = "dokan", not(feature = "winfsp")))]
 105:     {
 106:         Err(MountError::Backend(
 107:             "Dokan adapter not yet wired (Phase B daemon mount endpoint pending)".into(),
 108:         ))
 109:     }
 110:     #[cfg(all(target_os = "windows", not(any(feature = "winfsp", feature = "dokan"))))]
 111:     {
 112:         Err(MountError::Backend(
 113:             "rebuild ol_winfs with --features winfsp (preferred) or --features dokan".into(),
 114:         ))
 115:     }
 116:     #[cfg(not(target_os = "windows"))]
 117:     {
 118:         Err(MountError::UnsupportedPlatform)
 119:     }
 120: }
 121: 
 122: /// Crate version embedded for diagnostics.
 123: pub const VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");

   1: //! `one_link_native.aead` — Python binding for the `ol_aead` Rust crate.
   2: //!
   3: //! Surfaces per-chunk AEAD encrypt / decrypt + per-frame random-access
   4: //! decrypt + the host-preferred AEAD selector. Per
   5: //! [ADR-0008](../../../docs/decisions/0008-ffi-contract.md):
   6: //!
   7: //! - GIL released for encrypt / decrypt of large chunks.
   8: //! - Buffer arguments take `bytes`/`bytearray`/`memoryview` (zero-copy
   9: //!   ingest where Python permits; we copy into owned Rust Vec for
  10: //!   safety because in-place AEAD mutates the buffer).
  11: //! - Errors map to `one_link_native.OlAeadError`.

  14:     cipher::{AeadCipher as RustAeadCipher, AeadKind},
  15:     decrypt_chunk as rust_decrypt_chunk, decrypt_frame as rust_decrypt_frame,
  16:     encrypt_chunk as rust_encrypt_chunk, encrypt_frame as rust_encrypt_frame,
  17:     key::{ChunkAeadKey, FRAME_KEY_LEN as RUST_FRAME_KEY_LEN},
  18:     AEAD_TAG_LEN as RUST_AEAD_TAG_LEN,
  19: };

  24: use pyo3::types::{PyBytes, PyTuple};

  28: /// Map a string AEAD kind to the underlying enum.
  29: fn parse_kind(s: &str) -> PyResult<AeadKind> {
  30:     match s {
  31:         "aes" | "AES" | "AES-GCM" | "aes-gcm" | "aes-256-gcm" | "AES-256-GCM" => {
  32:             Ok(AeadKind::AesGcm256)
  33:         }
  34:         "chacha" | "ChaCha20" | "chacha20" | "chacha20-poly1305" | "ChaCha20Poly1305" => {
  35:             Ok(AeadKind::ChaCha20Poly1305)
  36:         }
  37:         other => Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  38:             "unknown AEAD kind '{other}'; expected 'aes' or 'chacha'"
  39:         ))),
  40:     }
  41: }
  42: 
  43: fn kind_to_str(k: AeadKind) -> &'static str {
  44:     match k {
  45:         AeadKind::AesGcm256 => "aes",
  46:         AeadKind::ChaCha20Poly1305 => "chacha",
  47:     }
  48: }
  49: 
  50: fn copy_buffer(py: Python<'_>, buf: PyBuffer<u8>) -> PyResult<Vec<u8>> {
  51:     if !buf.is_c_contiguous() {
  52:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err("buffer must be C-contiguous"));
  53:     }
  54:     let mut owned = vec![0u8; buf.item_count()];
  55:     buf.copy_to_slice(py, &mut owned)
  56:         .map_err(|e| PyValueError::new_err(format!("buffer copy failed: {e}")))?;
  57:     Ok(owned)
  58: }
  59: 
  60: fn check_chunk_id(chunk_id: &[u8]) -> PyResult<[u8; 32]> {
  61:     if chunk_id.len() != 32 {
  62:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  63:             "chunk_id must be 32 bytes (BLAKE3-256), got {}",
  64:             chunk_id.len(),
  65:         )));
  66:     }
  67:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
  68:     out.copy_from_slice(chunk_id);
  69:     Ok(out)
  70: }
  71: 
  72: fn check_key(key: &[u8]) -> PyResult<ChunkAeadKey> {
  73:     if key.len() != RUST_FRAME_KEY_LEN {
  74:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  75:             "key must be {RUST_FRAME_KEY_LEN} bytes, got {}",
  76:             key.len(),
  77:         )));
  78:     }
  79:     let mut bytes = [0u8; RUST_FRAME_KEY_LEN];
  80:     bytes.copy_from_slice(key);
  81:     Ok(ChunkAeadKey::from_bytes(bytes))
  82: }
  83: 
  84: fn check_tag(tag: &[u8]) -> PyResult<[u8; RUST_AEAD_TAG_LEN]> {
  85:     if tag.len() != RUST_AEAD_TAG_LEN {
  86:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  87:             "tag must be {RUST_AEAD_TAG_LEN} bytes, got {}",
  88:             tag.len(),
  89:         )));
  90:     }
  91:     let mut out = [0u8; RUST_AEAD_TAG_LEN];
  92:     out.copy_from_slice(tag);
  93:     Ok(out)
  94: }

  96: /// AEAD cipher initialized with a 32-byte key.
  97: ///
  98: /// Construct via :func:`new_cipher` or :func:`default_cipher_for_host`.
  99: /// Reuse across many encrypt / decrypt calls; cipher state is the
 100: /// expanded round keys derived once at construction.
 101: ///
 102: /// Wraps the inner cipher in an Arc so the pyo3 binding can clone
 103: /// cheaply (refcount bump) for ``py.allow_threads`` closures that
 104: /// release the GIL. The ring-backed `AeadCipher` itself is not Clone
 105: /// because `ring::aead::LessSafeKey` doesn't expose its key bytes —
 106: /// the Arc sidesteps that without compromising key isolation.
 107: #[pyclass(
 108:     name = "AeadCipher",
 109:     module = "one_link_native.aead",
 110:     frozen,
 111:     unsendable
 112: )]
 113: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 114: pub struct PyAeadCipher {
 115:     inner: std::sync::Arc<RustAeadCipher>,
 116: }
 117: 
 118: #[pymethods]
 119: impl PyAeadCipher {
 120:     /// Which AEAD kind this cipher dispatches to (``"aes"`` or ``"chacha"``).
 121:     #[getter]
 122:     fn kind(&self) -> &'static str {
 123:         kind_to_str(self.inner.kind())
 124:     }
 125: 
 126:     /// Encrypt a complete chunk plaintext into the on-wire layout.
 127:     ///
 128:     /// :param chunk_id: 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address (used as AAD + nonce input).
 129:     /// :param plaintext: the chunk's plaintext bytes (≤ 256 KiB).
 130:     /// :return: ciphertext bytes = ``len(plaintext) + frame_count * 16``.
 131:     /// :raises OlAeadError: on encrypt failure.
 132:     fn encrypt_chunk<'py>(
 133:         &self,
 134:         py: Python<'py>,
 135:         chunk_id: &[u8],
 136:         plaintext: PyBuffer<u8>,
 137:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 138:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 139:         let pt = copy_buffer(py, plaintext)?;
 140:         let cipher = self.inner.clone();
 141:         let ct = py
 142:             .allow_threads(|| rust_encrypt_chunk(&cipher, &id, &pt))
 143:             .map_err(aead_error_to_pyerr)?;
 144:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &ct))
 145:     }
 146: 
 147:     /// Decrypt a complete chunk ciphertext.
 148:     ///
 149:     /// :param chunk_id: 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address (must match the
 150:     ///     value used at encrypt time).
 151:     /// :param plaintext_len: original plaintext length (used to drive
 152:     ///     frame layout reconstruction).
 153:     /// :param ciphertext: the on-wire ciphertext bytes.
 154:     /// :return: plaintext bytes.
 155:     /// :raises OlAeadError: on tag verification failure.
 156:     fn decrypt_chunk<'py>(
 157:         &self,
 158:         py: Python<'py>,
 159:         chunk_id: &[u8],
 160:         plaintext_len: usize,
 161:         ciphertext: PyBuffer<u8>,
 162:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 163:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 164:         let ct = copy_buffer(py, ciphertext)?;
 165:         let cipher = self.inner.clone();
 166:         let pt = py
 167:             .allow_threads(|| rust_decrypt_chunk(&cipher, &id, plaintext_len, &ct))
 168:             .map_err(aead_error_to_pyerr)?;
 169:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &pt))
 170:     }
 171: 
 172:     /// Encrypt a single frame (≤ 16 KiB plaintext). Returns
 173:     /// ``(ciphertext, tag)`` where ``len(tag) == 16``.
 174:     fn encrypt_frame<'py>(
 175:         &self,
 176:         py: Python<'py>,
 177:         chunk_id: &[u8],
 178:         frame_index: u64,
 179:         plaintext: PyBuffer<u8>,
 180:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyTuple>> {
 181:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 182:         let pt = copy_buffer(py, plaintext)?;
 183:         let cipher = self.inner.clone();
 184:         let (ct, tag) = py
 185:             .allow_threads(|| rust_encrypt_frame(&cipher, &id, frame_index, &pt))
 186:             .map_err(aead_error_to_pyerr)?;
 187:         let ct_py = PyBytes::new_bound(py, &ct);
 188:         let tag_py = PyBytes::new_bound(py, &tag);
 189:         Ok(PyTuple::new_bound(
 190:             py,
 191:             vec![ct_py.into_any(), tag_py.into_any()],
 192:         ))
 193:     }
 194: 
 195:     /// Decrypt a single frame.
 196:     ///
 197:     /// :param chunk_id: 32-byte BLAKE3 chunk address.
 198:     /// :param frame_index: zero-based frame index within the chunk.
 199:     /// :param ciphertext: frame ciphertext (≤ 16 KiB).
 200:     /// :param tag: 16-byte AEAD authentication tag.
 201:     /// :return: frame plaintext.
 202:     /// :raises OlAeadError: on tag verification failure.
 203:     fn decrypt_frame<'py>(
 204:         &self,
 205:         py: Python<'py>,
 206:         chunk_id: &[u8],
 207:         frame_index: u64,
 208:         ciphertext: PyBuffer<u8>,
 209:         tag: &[u8],
 210:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 211:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 212:         let ct = copy_buffer(py, ciphertext)?;
 213:         let tag_arr = check_tag(tag)?;
 214:         let cipher = self.inner.clone();
 215:         let pt = py
 216:             .allow_threads(|| rust_decrypt_frame(&cipher, &id, frame_index, &ct, &tag_arr))
 217:             .map_err(aead_error_to_pyerr)?;
 218:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &pt))
 219:     }
 220: 
 221:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
 222:         format!("AeadCipher(kind='{}')", self.kind())
 223:     }
 224: }
 225: 
 226: /// Construct an AeadCipher of the named kind (``"aes"`` or ``"chacha"``).
 227: #[pyfunction]
 228: fn new_cipher(key: &[u8], kind: &str) -> PyResult<PyAeadCipher> {
 229:     let key = check_key(key)?;
 230:     let kind = parse_kind(kind)?;
 231:     Ok(PyAeadCipher {
 232:         inner: std::sync::Arc::new(RustAeadCipher::with_kind(kind, &key)),
 233:     })
 234: }
 235: 
 236: /// Construct an AeadCipher with the host's preferred AEAD (AES-256-GCM
 237: /// when AES-NI / ARM crypto extensions are available; ChaCha20-Poly1305
 238: /// fallback otherwise).
 239: #[pyfunction]
 240: fn default_cipher_for_host(key: &[u8]) -> PyResult<PyAeadCipher> {
 241:     let key = check_key(key)?;
 242:     Ok(PyAeadCipher {
 243:         inner: std::sync::Arc::new(RustAeadCipher::default_for_host(&key)),
 244:     })
 245: }
 246: 
 247: /// Return the host's preferred AEAD kind without constructing a cipher.
 248: #[pyfunction]
 249: fn default_aead_kind() -> &'static str {
 250:     kind_to_str(AeadKind::default_for_host())
 251: }
 252: 
 253: /// Return whether the host has hardware AES (AES-NI / ARM crypto ext)
 254: /// detected at runtime.
 255: #[pyfunction]
 256: fn host_has_hardware_aes() -> bool {
 257:     ol_aead::cipher::has_hardware_aes()
 258: }
 259: 
 260: /// Register the aead submodule.
 261: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 262:     // Constants per ADR-0002.
 263:     m.add("FRAME_KEY_LEN", RUST_FRAME_KEY_LEN)?;
 264:     m.add("AEAD_TAG_LEN", RUST_AEAD_TAG_LEN)?;
 265:     m.add("AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN", RUST_AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN)?;
 266:     m.add(

 268:         ol_aead::frame::MAX_CHUNK_PLAINTEXT_LEN,
 269:     )?;
 270: 
 271:     // Types and functions.
 272:     m.add_class::<PyAeadCipher>()?;
 273:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(new_cipher, m)?)?;
 274:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(default_cipher_for_host, m)?)?;
 275:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(default_aead_kind, m)?)?;
 276:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(host_has_hardware_aes, m)?)?;
 277: 
 278:     Ok(())

   1: //! `one_link_native.bandit` — Python binding for `ol_bandit`.
   2: //!
   3: //! Exposes the Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling bandit per ADR-0019.
   4: //! The daemon's `transfer_brain.py` (currently using EMA route memory)
   5: //! replaces its arm-selection loop with calls into this binding.
   6: 
   7: use ol_bandit::{Bandit, BanditError, BanditSeed};
   8: use pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError;
   9: use pyo3::prelude::*;
  10: use pyo3::types::PyList;
  11: 
  12: /// Python-visible bandit.
  13: #[pyclass(name = "Bandit", module = "one_link_native.bandit")]
  14: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  15: pub struct PyBandit {
  16:     inner: Bandit,
  17:     rng: BanditSeed,
  18: }
  19: 
  20: #[pymethods]
  21: impl PyBandit {
  22:     /// Build a fresh bandit with `n_arms` arms (uniform Beta(1, 1) priors).
  23:     ///
  24:     /// `seed` defaults to a derived constant; pass a u64 for
  25:     /// deterministic test replays.
  26:     #[new]
  27:     #[pyo3(signature = (n_arms, seed = 0xBABE_F00D))]
  28:     fn new(n_arms: usize, seed: u64) -> PyResult<Self> {
  29:         let inner = Bandit::new(n_arms).map_err(bandit_err_to_py)?;
  30:         Ok(Self {
  31:             inner,
  32:             rng: BanditSeed::new(seed),
  33:         })
  34:     }
  35: 
  36:     /// Number of arms.
  37:     #[getter]
  38:     fn n_arms(&self) -> usize {
  39:         self.inner.n_arms()
  40:     }
  41: 
  42:     /// Thompson-sample an arm to play.
  43:     fn select(&mut self) -> usize {
  44:         self.inner.select(&mut self.rng)
  45:     }
  46: 
  47:     /// Update with the observed reward `r in [0, 1]` for `arm_idx`.
  48:     fn update(&mut self, arm_idx: usize, reward: f64) -> PyResult<()> {
  49:         self.inner.update(arm_idx, reward).map_err(bandit_err_to_py)
  50:     }
  51: 
  52:     /// The arm with the highest posterior mean.
  53:     fn best_arm(&self) -> usize {
  54:         self.inner.best_arm()
  55:     }
  56: 
  57:     /// Per-arm `(alpha, beta)` tuples for diagnostics.
  58:     fn arms<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyList>> {
  59:         let out = PyList::empty_bound(py);
  60:         for arm in self.inner.arms() {
  61:             out.append((arm.alpha, arm.beta))?;
  62:         }
  63:         Ok(out)
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     /// Reset the internal RNG to `seed` (test/replay use only).
  67:     fn reseed(&mut self, seed: u64) {
  68:         self.rng = BanditSeed::new(seed);
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
  72:         format!(
  73:             "Bandit(n_arms={}, best_arm={})",
  74:             self.inner.n_arms(),
  75:             self.inner.best_arm()
  76:         )
  77:     }
  78: }
  79: 
  80: fn bandit_err_to_py(err: BanditError) -> PyErr {
  81:     match err {
  82:         BanditError::InvalidReward { got } => {
  83:             PyValueError::new_err(format!("invalid reward: {got}"))
  84:         }
  85:         other => crate::errors::OlBanditError::new_err(other.to_string()),
  86:     }
  87: }

  91:     m.add("__version__", ol_bandit::VERSION)?;
  92:     m.add_class::<PyBandit>()?;
  93:     Ok(())
  94: }

   1: //! `one_link_native.bloom` — Python binding for the `ol_bloom` crate.
   2: //!
   3: //! Surfaces the content-addressed Bloom filter used by ADR-0011's

  12: use pyo3::types::PyBytes;
  13: 
  14: use crate::errors::bloom_error_to_pyerr;
  15: 
  16: /// Python-visible Bloom filter sized for a target false-positive rate.
  17: #[pyclass(name = "Bloom", module = "one_link_native.bloom")]
  18: #[derive(Debug)]
  19: pub struct PyBloom {
  20:     inner: Bloom,
  21: }
  22: 
  23: #[pymethods]
  24: impl PyBloom {
  25:     /// Build an empty Bloom filter sized for `n` chunk_ids at 1% FP rate.
  26:     #[new]
  27:     #[pyo3(signature = (n, target_fp = None))]
  28:     fn new(n: usize, target_fp: Option<f64>) -> Self {
  29:         let inner = match target_fp {
  30:             Some(p) => Bloom::with_target_fp(n, p),
  31:             None => Bloom::new(n),
  32:         };
  33:         Self { inner }
  34:     }
  35: 
  36:     /// Insert a 32-byte chunk_id.
  37:     fn insert(&mut self, py: Python<'_>, chunk_id: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<()> {
  38:         let id = chunk_id_from_buffer(py, chunk_id)?;
  39:         self.inner.insert(&id);
  40:         Ok(())
  41:     }
  42: 
  43:     /// Test whether a 32-byte chunk_id is (probably) present.
  44:     fn contains(&self, py: Python<'_>, chunk_id: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<bool> {
  45:         let id = chunk_id_from_buffer(py, chunk_id)?;
  46:         Ok(self.inner.contains(&id))
  47:     }
  48: 
  49:     /// Number of bits in the filter.
  50:     #[getter]
  51:     fn m_bits(&self) -> u32 {
  52:         self.inner.m_bits()
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// Number of hash functions.
  56:     #[getter]
  57:     fn k(&self) -> u32 {
  58:         self.inner.k()
  59:     }
  60: 
  61:     /// Number of bits currently set.
  62:     fn popcount(&self) -> u64 {
  63:         self.inner.popcount()
  64:     }
  65: 
  66:     /// On-wire byte length (header + bit array).
  67:     fn encoded_len(&self) -> usize {
  68:         self.inner.encoded_len()
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     /// Encode to wire bytes per ADR-0011.
  72:     fn encode<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
  73:         let bytes = self.inner.encode().map_err(bloom_error_to_pyerr)?;
  74:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &bytes))
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     /// Decode from wire bytes per ADR-0011.
  78:     #[staticmethod]
  79:     fn decode(py: Python<'_>, encoded: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<Self> {
  80:         let buf = PyBuffer::<u8>::get_bound(encoded)?;
  81:         if buf.len_bytes() > MAX_FILTER_BYTES {
  82:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  83:                 "encoded bloom exceeds {} byte cap",
  84:                 MAX_FILTER_BYTES
  85:             )));
  86:         }
  87:         let slice =
  88:             unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.buf_ptr() as *const u8, buf.len_bytes()) };
  89:         let inner = py
  90:             .allow_threads(|| Bloom::decode(slice))
  91:             .map_err(bloom_error_to_pyerr)?;
  92:         Ok(Self { inner })
  93:     }
  94: 
  95:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
  96:         format!(
  97:             "Bloom(m_bits={}, k={}, popcount={})",
  98:             self.inner.m_bits(),
  99:             self.inner.k(),
 100:             self.inner.popcount(),
 101:         )
 102:     }
 103: }
 104: 
 105: fn chunk_id_from_buffer(py: Python<'_>, obj: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<[u8; 32]> {
 106:     let buf = PyBuffer::<u8>::get_bound(obj)?;
 107:     if buf.len_bytes() != 32 {
 108:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 109:             "chunk_id must be exactly 32 bytes, got {}",
 110:             buf.len_bytes()
 111:         )));
 112:     }
 113:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
 114:     let _ = py; // GIL token not needed for this short copy
 115:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.buf_ptr() as *const u8, 32) };
 116:     out.copy_from_slice(slice);
 117:     Ok(out)
 118: }
 119: 
 120: /// Sizing helper: optimal `m_bits` for `n` elements + target FP rate.
 121: #[pyfunction]
 122: #[pyo3(signature = (n, target_fp = 0.01))]
 123: fn optimal_m_bits(n: usize, target_fp: f64) -> u32 {
 124:     ol_bloom::optimal_m_bits(n, target_fp)
 125: }
 126: 
 127: /// Sizing helper: optimal `k` (hash count) for `n` elements + `m_bits`.
 128: #[pyfunction]
 129: fn optimal_k(n: usize, m_bits: u32) -> u32 {
 130:     ol_bloom::optimal_k(n, m_bits)
 131: }
 132: 
 133: /// Default target false-positive rate (1%).
 134: #[pyfunction]
 135: fn default_target_fp_rate() -> f64 {
 136:     ol_bloom::target_fp_rate()
 137: }
 138: 
 139: /// Register the `bloom` submodule on the given `PyModule`.
 140: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 141:     m.add("__version__", ol_bloom::VERSION)?;
 142:     m.add("BLOOM_HEADER_LEN", ol_bloom::BLOOM_HEADER_LEN)?;
 143:     m.add("MAX_FILTER_BYTES", ol_bloom::MAX_FILTER_BYTES)?;
 144:     m.add_class::<PyBloom>()?;
 145:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(optimal_m_bits, m)?)?;
 146:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(optimal_k, m)?)?;
 147:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(default_target_fp_rate, m)?)?;
 148:     Ok(())
 149: }

   1: //! `one_link_native.chunk` — Python binding for the `ol_chunk` Rust crate.
   2: //!
   3: //! Surfaces FastCDC + BLAKE3 chunk addressing + domain-separated key
   4: //! derivation. Per [ADR-0008](../../../docs/decisions/0008-ffi-contract.md):
   5: //!
   6: //! - Long-running operations release the GIL via `py.allow_threads`.
   7: //! - Buffer arguments use the Python buffer protocol (`bytes`, `bytearray`,
   8: //!   `memoryview`) for zero-copy ingest.
   9: //! - Errors map to `one_link_native.OlChunkError` (subclass of `OlError`).
  10: 
  11: use ol_chunk::{
  12:     blake3_wrap, frame_count_for_plaintext, scan_to_vec_parallel, AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN,
  13:     AEAD_TAG_LEN,
  14: };

  18: use pyo3::types::PyBytes;

  20: /// Python-visible boundary record. Wraps `(start, end, blake3_hash)`.
  21: #[pyclass(name = "Boundary", frozen, module = "one_link_native.chunk")]
  22: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
  23: pub struct PyBoundary {
  24:     /// Inclusive start byte offset.
  25:     #[pyo3(get)]
  26:     start: usize,
  27:     /// Exclusive end byte offset.
  28:     #[pyo3(get)]
  29:     end: usize,
  30:     /// BLAKE3-256 raw chunk address (32 bytes).
  31:     raw_address: [u8; 32],
  32: }
  33: 
  34: #[pymethods]
  35: impl PyBoundary {
  36:     /// Length of the chunk in bytes.
  37:     #[getter]
  38:     fn length(&self) -> usize {
  39:         self.end - self.start
  40:     }
  41: 
  42:     /// Raw chunk address as a 32-byte `bytes` object.
  43:     #[getter]
  44:     fn raw_address<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
  45:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.raw_address)
  46:     }
  47:

  49:     fn raw_address_hex(&self) -> String {
  50:         hex_lower(&self.raw_address)
  51:     }

  53:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
  54:         format!(
  55:             "Boundary(start={}, end={}, length={}, raw={})",
  56:             self.start,

  59:             self.raw_address_hex(),
  60:         )
  61:     }
  62: }

  64: /// Chunk-content-defined-chunking iterator over a contiguous byte buffer.
  65: ///
  66: /// Yields :class:`Boundary` objects until the buffer is exhausted.
  67: /// Created via :func:`cdc_iter`.
  68: #[pyclass(
  69:     name = "BoundaryIterator",
  70:     module = "one_link_native.chunk",
  71:     unsendable
  72: )]
  73: pub struct PyBoundaryIterator {
  74:     /// Eagerly-collected boundaries. We collect once at construction time
  75:     /// so the underlying buffer's lifetime doesn't have to outlive the
  76:     /// iterator. Memory: 32 bytes hash + 32 bytes positional = 64 B per
  77:     /// boundary; a 1 GiB buffer with 64 KiB mean chunks → ~16K boundaries
  78:     /// → 1 MB. Acceptable.
  79:     boundaries: std::vec::IntoIter<PyBoundary>,
  80: }
  81: 
  82: #[pymethods]
  83: impl PyBoundaryIterator {
  84:     fn __iter__(slf: PyRef<'_, Self>) -> PyRef<'_, Self> {
  85:         slf
  86:     }
  87:     fn __next__(mut slf: PyRefMut<'_, Self>) -> Option<PyBoundary> {
  88:         slf.boundaries.next()
  89:     }
  90:     fn __len__(&self) -> usize {
  91:         self.boundaries.len()
  92:     }
  93: }
  94: 
  95: /// Scan a byte buffer with the default ADR-0001 CDC parameters (8 KiB
  96: /// min, 64 KiB avg, 256 KiB max) and return an iterator of
  97: /// :class:`Boundary` objects.
  98: ///
  99: /// **Zero-copy fast path.** Borrows the underlying Python buffer
 100: /// memory directly via the buffer protocol (no `Vec` allocation, no
 101: /// memcpy). This is sound because :class:`PyBuffer` keeps the
 102: /// underlying Python object alive (and the bytes pinned) for the
 103: /// duration of this function; the buffer's `Drop` releases the
 104: /// pin AFTER the scan completes. GIL release via `py.allow_threads`
 105: /// does not invalidate the pin — that's an explicit guarantee of
 106: /// the Python buffer protocol.
 107: ///
 108: /// Releases the GIL while scanning. The buffer must be a contiguous,
 109: /// readable Python object (``bytes``, ``bytearray``, ``memoryview``).
 110: ///
 111: /// :param buf: input buffer
 112: /// :return: an iterator over Boundary instances
 113: /// :raises OlChunkError: if the buffer cannot be read as a contiguous u8 slice
 114: #[pyfunction]
 115: pub fn cdc_iter(py: Python<'_>, buf: PyBuffer<u8>) -> PyResult<PyBoundaryIterator> {
 116:     if !buf.is_c_contiguous() {
 117:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(
 118:             "buffer must be C-contiguous (got fortran-order or non-contiguous)",
 119:         ));
 120:     }
 121:     let len = buf.item_count();
 122:     if len == 0 {
 123:         return Ok(PyBoundaryIterator {
 124:             boundaries: Vec::new().into_iter(),
 125:         });
 126:     }
 127:     // SAFETY: `buf` (a PyBuffer) holds the buffer-protocol lock on the
 128:     // underlying Python object for the duration of this function. The
 129:     // bytes are pinned in memory until `buf` drops, which happens after
 130:     // we return. `py.allow_threads` releases the GIL, but the buffer
 131:     // protocol's pin is independent of GIL state — the Python object
 132:     // cannot be deallocated while a buffer view is held. The slice we
 133:     // form here is valid for the entirety of the scan.
 134:     let bytes: &[u8] = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.buf_ptr().cast::<u8>(), len) };
 135: 
 136:     let boundaries: Vec<PyBoundary> = py.allow_threads(|| {
 137:         scan_to_vec_parallel(bytes)
 138:             .into_iter()
 139:             .map(|b| PyBoundary {
 140:                 start: b.start,
 141:                 end: b.end,
 142:                 raw_address: b.raw_address,
 143:             })
 144:             .collect()
 145:     });
 146:     Ok(PyBoundaryIterator {
 147:         boundaries: boundaries.into_iter(),
 148:     })
 149: }
 150: 
 151: /// Compute the raw BLAKE3-256 chunk address for a buffer.
 152: ///
 153: /// Equivalent to `blake3.hash(buf).digest()` but exposed via the engine's
 154: /// canonical entry point. Zero-copy; see [`cdc_iter`] safety note.
 155: #[pyfunction]
 156: pub fn chunk_address_raw<'py>(py: Python<'py>, buf: PyBuffer<u8>) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 157:     if !buf.is_c_contiguous() {
 158:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err("buffer must be C-contiguous"));
 159:     }
 160:     let len = buf.item_count();
 161:     // SAFETY: see cdc_iter — PyBuffer pin extends past allow_threads.
 162:     let bytes: &[u8] = if len == 0 {
 163:         &[]
 164:     } else {
 165:         unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.buf_ptr().cast::<u8>(), len) }
 166:     };
 167:     let addr = py.allow_threads(|| blake3_wrap::chunk_address_raw(bytes));
 168:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &addr))
 169: }
 170: 
 171: /// Compute the convergent BLAKE3-256 chunk address for a buffer.
 172: ///
 173: /// Same plaintext from any peer produces the same address. Domain-separated
 174: /// from `chunk_address_raw`. Zero-copy.
 175: #[pyfunction]
 176: pub fn chunk_address_convergent<'py>(
 177:     py: Python<'py>,
 178:     buf: PyBuffer<u8>,
 179: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 180:     if !buf.is_c_contiguous() {
 181:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err("buffer must be C-contiguous"));
 182:     }
 183:     let len = buf.item_count();
 184:     // SAFETY: see cdc_iter.
 185:     let bytes: &[u8] = if len == 0 {
 186:         &[]
 187:     } else {
 188:         unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.buf_ptr().cast::<u8>(), len) }
 189:     };
 190:     let addr = py.allow_threads(|| blake3_wrap::chunk_address_convergent(bytes));
 191:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &addr))
 192: }

 194: /// Derive a per-chunk AEAD key from a ratchet chain key + chunk address
 195: /// per [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 3.
 196: ///
 197: /// Both arguments must be exactly 32 bytes.
 198: #[pyfunction]
 199: pub fn derive_aead_key<'py>(
 200:     py: Python<'py>,
 201:     ratchet_chain_key: &[u8],
 202:     chunk_id_full: &[u8],
 203: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 204:     if ratchet_chain_key.len() != 32 {
 205:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 206:             "ratchet_chain_key must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 207:             ratchet_chain_key.len(),
 208:         )));
 209:     }
 210:     if chunk_id_full.len() != 32 {
 211:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 212:             "chunk_id_full must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 213:             chunk_id_full.len(),
 214:         )));
 215:     }
 216:     let chain: [u8; 32] = ratchet_chain_key.try_into().expect("checked above");
 217:     let chunk: [u8; 32] = chunk_id_full.try_into().expect("checked above");
 218:     let key = blake3_wrap::derive_aead_key(&chain, &chunk);
 219:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &key))
 220: }

 233:             ratchet_chain_key.len(),

 240:         )));
 241:     }
 242:     let chain: [u8; 32] = ratchet_chain_key.try_into().expect("checked above");
 243:     let chunk: [u8; 32] = chunk_id_full.try_into().expect("checked above");
 244:     let id = blake3_wrap::derive_ratchet_key_id(&chain, &chunk);
 245:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &id))
 246: }
 247: 
 248: /// Derive the stripe seed and within-stripe position for a chunk per
 249: /// [ADR-0004](../../../docs/decisions/0004-stripe-layout.md) and
 250: /// [ADR-0006](../../../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) Rule 5.
 251: ///
 252: /// Returns `(stripe_seed, position)` where `stripe_seed` has the low 6
 253: /// bits cleared and `position` is in `[0, stripe_k)`.
 254: #[pyfunction]
 255: pub fn derive_stripe_seed(chunk_id_full: &[u8], stripe_k: u8) -> PyResult<(u64, u8)> {
 256:     if chunk_id_full.len() != 32 {
 257:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 258:             "chunk_id_full must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 259:             chunk_id_full.len(),
 260:         )));
 261:     }
 262:     if stripe_k == 0 {
 263:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err("stripe_k must be ≥ 1"));
 264:     }
 265:     let chunk: [u8; 32] = chunk_id_full.try_into().expect("checked above");
 266:     Ok(blake3_wrap::derive_stripe_seed(&chunk, stripe_k))
 267: }

 269: /// Compute the number of AEAD frames a chunk plaintext needs.

 271: /// One frame per `AEAD_FRAME_PLAINTEXT_LEN` bytes (16 KiB), rounded up.
 272: #[pyfunction]
 273: pub fn frame_count(plaintext_len: usize) -> usize {
 274:     frame_count_for_plaintext(plaintext_len)
 275: }

 302: /// Local lowercase hex encoder. Avoid pulling the `hex` crate into the
 303: /// binding crate just for one display function.
 304: fn hex_lower(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
 305:     const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
 306:     let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
 307:     for &b in bytes {
 308:         out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
 309:         out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0F) as usize] as char);
 310:     }
 311:     out

   1: //! pyo3 wrapper for `ol_confidential` — Row 10 confidential-compute
   2: //! daemon (sealed-op surface + remote attestation).
   3: //!
   4: //! ## Surface
   5: //!
   6: //! - `SoftwareProvider` — software-baseline tier. Generate from
   7: //!   CSPRNG, seal a master seed, derive child seeds, sealed-sign
   8: //!   transcripts, derive verifying keys, issue attestation docs.
   9: //! - `AttestationDoc` — the wire envelope (provider tag, master

  11: //!   witness commitment, optional platform quote, master signature).
  12: //! - `verify_attestation` — peer-side validator with peer-nonce
  13: //!   binding, freshness window enforcement, and optional field-

  15: //! - `attestation_nonce` — fresh 32-byte peer nonce convenience.
  16: //! - `fresh_software_provider`, `software_provider_from_seed` —
  17: //!   construction helpers.
  18: //!
  19: //! All sealed-key blobs cross the FFI as opaque `bytes`. The daemon

  47:     }

  93:     fn tier_byte(&self) -> u8 {

  95:     }
