 101: 
 102:     /// Seal a 32-byte master seed. Returns the opaque sealed bytes
 103:     /// + the provider tag byte (so callers can round-trip via
 104:     /// `SealedKey`).
 105:     fn seal_master<'py>(
 106:         &self,
 107:         py: Python<'py>,
 108:         seed: &[u8],
 109:     ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, u8)> {
 110:         if seed.len() != 32 {
 111:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 112:                 "seed must be exactly 32 bytes, got {}",
 113:                 seed.len()
 114:             )));
 115:         }
 116:         // Zeroize the local copy of the master seed before returning.
 117:         // Without this, a core dump captured between this fn's return
 118:         // and the next stack write recovers the seed bytes verbatim
 119:         // (audit finding M5, May 14 2026).
 120:         let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
 121:         arr.copy_from_slice(seed);
 122:         let sealed_result = self.inner.seal_master(&arr);
 123:         arr.zeroize();
 124:         let sealed = sealed_result.map_err(map_err)?;
 125:         Ok((
 126:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &sealed.bytes),
 127:             sealed.provider_tag.as_u8(),
 128:         ))
 129:     }
 130: 
 131:     /// Derive a child SealedKey from a sealed master + context tag.
 132:     fn derive_child<'py>(
 133:         &self,
 134:         py: Python<'py>,
 135:         sealed_master_bytes: &[u8],
 136:         sealed_master_tag: u8,
 137:         context_tag: &[u8],
 138:     ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, u8)> {
 139:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_master_tag)?;
 140:         let sealed_master = SealedKey {
 141:             provider_tag: tag,
 142:             bytes: sealed_master_bytes.to_vec(),
 143:         };
 144:         let child = self
 145:             .inner
 146:             .derive_child(&sealed_master, context_tag)
 147:             .map_err(map_err)?;
 148:         Ok((
 149:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &child.bytes),
 150:             child.provider_tag.as_u8(),
 151:         ))
 152:     }
 153: 
 154:     /// Sign `transcript` under a sealed master. Returns the hybrid
 155:     /// signature bytes.
 156:     fn sealed_sign<'py>(
 157:         &self,
 158:         py: Python<'py>,
 159:         sealed_bytes: &[u8],
 160:         sealed_tag: u8,
 161:         transcript: &[u8],
 162:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 163:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_tag)?;
 164:         let sealed = SealedKey {
 165:             provider_tag: tag,
 166:             bytes: sealed_bytes.to_vec(),
 167:         };
 168:         let sig = self.inner.sealed_sign(&sealed, transcript).map_err(map_err)?;
 169:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &sig))
 170:     }
 171: 
 172:     /// Recover the verifying key for a sealed master. Returns the
 173:     /// 1984-byte hybrid VK bytes.
 174:     fn verifying_key<'py>(
 175:         &self,
 176:         py: Python<'py>,
 177:         sealed_bytes: &[u8],
 178:         sealed_tag: u8,
 179:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 180:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_tag)?;
 181:         let sealed = SealedKey {
 182:             provider_tag: tag,
 183:             bytes: sealed_bytes.to_vec(),
 184:         };
 185:         let vk = self.inner.verifying_key(&sealed).map_err(map_err)?;
 186:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &vk.to_bytes()))
 187:     }
 188: 
 189:     /// Issue an attestation doc. Returns the encoded fields as a
 190:     /// tuple `(provider_tag_u8, master_vk_bytes, peer_nonce,
 191:     /// issued_unix, deadline_unix, field_witness_commitment_or_none,
 192:     /// platform_quote_bytes, issuer_sdp_pubkey_bytes, master_sig_bytes)`
 193:     /// — the Python daemon reassembles into its own typed wrapper.
 194:     ///
 195:     /// `issuer_sdp_pubkey` is the 32-byte Ed25519 SDP-layer pubkey of
 196:     /// the issuer's channel identity (audit C1). The master signature
 197:     /// binds to it so a verifier rejects any doc whose embedded SDP
 198:     /// pubkey does not match the channel they're actually talking to.
 199:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 200:     #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
 201:     #[pyo3(signature = (
 202:         sealed_bytes,
 203:         sealed_tag,
 204:         peer_nonce,
 205:         issued_unix,
 206:         deadline_unix,
 207:         issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 208:         field_witness=None,
 209:     ))]
 210:     fn attest<'py>(
 211:         &self,
 212:         py: Python<'py>,
 213:         sealed_bytes: &[u8],
 214:         sealed_tag: u8,
 215:         peer_nonce: &[u8],
 216:         issued_unix: u64,
 217:         deadline_unix: u64,
 218:         issuer_sdp_pubkey: &[u8],
 219:         field_witness: Option<&[u8]>,
 220:     ) -> PyResult<(
 221:         u8,
 222:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 223:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 224:         u64,
 225:         u64,
 226:         Option<Bound<'py, PyBytes>>,
 227:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 228:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 229:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 230:     )> {
 231:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_tag)?;
 232:         let sealed = SealedKey {
 233:             provider_tag: tag,
 234:             bytes: sealed_bytes.to_vec(),
 235:         };
 236:         let nonce = nonce_from_bytes(peer_nonce)?;
 237:         let witness = field_witness_from_bytes(field_witness)?;
 238:         let sdp = issuer_sdp_pubkey_from_bytes(issuer_sdp_pubkey)?;
 239:         let doc = self
 240:             .inner
 241:             .attest(
 242:                 &sealed,
 243:                 nonce,
 244:                 issued_unix,
 245:                 deadline_unix,
 246:                 witness.as_ref(),
 247:                 sdp,
 248:             )
 249:             .map_err(map_err)?;
 250:         let cmt = doc.field_witness_commitment.map(|c| PyBytes::new_bound(py, &c));
 251:         Ok((
 252:             doc.provider_tag.as_u8(),
 253:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.master_vk.to_bytes()),
 254:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.peer_nonce),
 255:             doc.issued_unix,
 256:             doc.deadline_unix,
 257:             cmt,
 258:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.platform_quote),
 259:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.issuer_sdp_pubkey),
 260:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.master_sig),
 261:         ))
 262:     }
 263: }
 264: 
 265: // ── Free functions ────────────────────────────────────────────────

 267: /// Generate a fresh `SoftwareProvider` from the OS CSPRNG.
 268: #[pyfunction]
 269: fn fresh_software_provider() -> PySoftwareProvider {
 270:     PySoftwareProvider {
 271:         inner: SoftwareProvider::generate(&mut OsRng),
 272:     }
 273: }
 274: 
 275: /// Deterministic constructor for KAT vectors and incident-response
 276: /// replay — `seed` is a 32-byte hex-or-bytes value.
 277: ///
 278: /// **Audit M7 May 2026 — gated**: gated behind the
 279: /// `unstable-deterministic-provider` Cargo feature, which is OFF in
 280: /// the default `maturin develop --release` build. Production wheels
 281: /// raise a runtime error when callers reach this function. Test
 282: /// wheels (built with `--features unstable-deterministic-provider`)
 283: /// get the real constructor. The Python wrapper documents this in
 284: /// its docstring.
 285: #[pyfunction]
 286: fn software_provider_from_seed(_seed: &[u8]) -> PyResult<PySoftwareProvider> {
 287:     #[cfg(feature = "unstable-deterministic-provider")]
 288:     {
 289:         if _seed.len() != 32 {
 290:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 291:                 "provider seed must be exactly 32 bytes, got {}",
 292:                 _seed.len()
 293:             )));
 294:         }
 295:         // Zeroize the local seed copy after the provider has taken it
 296:         // (audit finding M5, May 14 2026).
 297:         let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
 298:         arr.copy_from_slice(_seed);
 299:         let provider = SoftwareProvider::from_seed(&arr);
 300:         arr.zeroize();
 301:         return Ok(PySoftwareProvider { inner: provider });
 302:     }
 303:     #[cfg(not(feature = "unstable-deterministic-provider"))]
 304:     {
 305:         Err(PyValueError::new_err(
 306:             "software_provider_from_seed is disabled in this build. \
 307:              It is a deterministic-seed constructor intended for \
 308:              KAT vectors only and is gated behind the \
 309:              `unstable-deterministic-provider` Cargo feature \
 310:              (audit M7 May 2026). Use fresh_software_provider for \
 311:              production callers.",
 312:         ))
 313:     }
 314: }
 315: 
 316: /// Generate a fresh 32-byte attestation nonce.
 317: #[pyfunction]
 318: fn attestation_nonce(py: Python<'_>) -> Bound<'_, PyBytes> {
 319:     let n = fresh_attestation_nonce(&mut OsRng);
 320:     PyBytes::new_bound(py, &n)
 321: }
 322: 
 323: /// Verify a (deconstructed) AttestationDoc. Pass the same field
 324: /// tuple shape as returned by `attest`, plus the verifier's expected
 325: /// channel-identity SDP pubkey (audit C1).
 326: ///
 327: /// `min_tier_byte` enforces the provider-tier floor (audit H4):
 328: /// `1` = Software (any tier accepted), `2` = HardwareBound, `3` =
 329: /// HardwareAttested.
 330: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 331: #[pyfunction]
 332: #[pyo3(signature = (
 333:     provider_tag,
 334:     master_vk,
 335:     peer_nonce,
 336:     issued_unix,
 337:     deadline_unix,
 338:     field_witness_commitment,
 339:     platform_quote,
 340:     issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 341:     master_sig,
 342:     expected_peer_nonce,
 343:     now_unix,
 344:     expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 345:     expected_field_witness=None,
 346:     min_tier_byte=1u8,
 347: ))]
 348: fn verify(
 349:     provider_tag: u8,
 350:     master_vk: &[u8],
 351:     peer_nonce: &[u8],
 352:     issued_unix: u64,
 353:     deadline_unix: u64,
 354:     field_witness_commitment: Option<&[u8]>,
 355:     platform_quote: &[u8],
 356:     issuer_sdp_pubkey: &[u8],
 357:     master_sig: &[u8],
 358:     expected_peer_nonce: &[u8],
 359:     now_unix: u64,
 360:     expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey: &[u8],
 361:     expected_field_witness: Option<&[u8]>,
 362:     min_tier_byte: u8,
 363: ) -> PyResult<()> {
 364:     let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(provider_tag)?;
 365:     let vk = HybridVerifyingKey::from_bytes(master_vk)
 366:         .map_err(|e| PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()))?;
 367:     let nonce = nonce_from_bytes(peer_nonce)?;
 368:     let expected_nonce = nonce_from_bytes(expected_peer_nonce)?;
 369:     let fwc = match field_witness_commitment {
 370:         None => None,
 371:         Some(b) => {
 372:             if b.len() != 32 {
 373:                 return Err(PyValueError::new_err(
 374:                     "field_witness_commitment must be 32 bytes",
 375:                 ));
 376:             }
 377:             let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
 378:             arr.copy_from_slice(b);
 379:             Some(arr)
 380:         }
 381:     };
 382:     let expected_fw = field_witness_from_bytes(expected_field_witness)?;
 383:     let doc_sdp = issuer_sdp_pubkey_from_bytes(issuer_sdp_pubkey)?;
 384:     let expected_sdp = issuer_sdp_pubkey_from_bytes(expected_issuer_sdp_pubkey)?;
 385:     let min_tier = match min_tier_byte {
 386:         1 => ConfidentialTier::Software,
 387:         2 => ConfidentialTier::HardwareBound,
 388:         3 => ConfidentialTier::HardwareAttested,
 389:         other => {
 390:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 391:                 "unknown ConfidentialTier byte: {other}"
 392:             )));
 393:         }
 394:     };
 395:     let doc = AttestationDoc {
 396:         provider_tag: tag,
 397:         master_vk: vk,
 398:         peer_nonce: nonce,
 399:         issued_unix,
 400:         deadline_unix,
 401:         field_witness_commitment: fwc,
 402:         platform_quote: platform_quote.to_vec(),
 403:         issuer_sdp_pubkey: doc_sdp,
 404:         master_sig: master_sig.to_vec(),
 405:     };
 406:     verify_attestation(
 407:         &doc,
 408:         &expected_nonce,
 409:         expected_fw.as_ref(),
 410:         now_unix,
 411:         min_tier,
 412:         &expected_sdp,
 413:     )
 414:     .map_err(map_err)
 415: }
 416: 
 417: // ── Audit M6: Windows TPM-hardened provider pyo3 surface ───────────
 418: //
 419: // The hardened provider operates IDENTICALLY to PySoftwareProvider
 420: // from the daemon's perspective — same `seal_master` / `derive_child`
 421: // / `sealed_sign` / `verifying_key` / `attest` shape — but with
 422: // `tier_byte()` reporting HardwareBound (= 2) and the returned
 423: // attestation doc carrying a TPM-signed `platform_quote`. The peer
 424: // verifier uses the same `verify()` free function with
 425: // `min_tier_byte=2` to enforce the upgrade.
 426: //
 427: // Gated behind the `windows-tpm` Cargo feature so non-Windows hosts
 428: // can build the rest of `one_link_native` without pulling in the
 429: // Microsoft `windows` crate. A runtime caller on a wheel that wasn't
 430: // built with the feature gets a friendly `PyValueError` from the
 431: // fallback `fresh_windows_hardened_provider` stub.
 432: 
 433: #[cfg(feature = "windows-tpm")]
 434: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.confidential")]
 435: struct PyWindowsHardenedProvider {
 436:     inner: ol_confidential::WindowsHardenedProvider,
 437: }
 438: 
 439: #[cfg(feature = "windows-tpm")]
 440: #[pymethods]
 441: impl PyWindowsHardenedProvider {
 442:     /// Tier code. `2` = HardwareBound.
 443:     fn tier_byte(&self) -> u8 {
 444:         self.inner.tier() as u8
 445:     }
 446: 
 447:     /// Wire tag byte. `4` = WindowsTpm.
 448:     fn tag_byte(&self) -> u8 {
 449:         self.inner.tag().as_u8()
 450:     }
 451: 
 452:     /// Seal a 32-byte master seed. Returns `(sealed_bytes, tag_byte)`
 453:     /// with tag = WindowsTpm so future round-trips bind to this
 454:     /// provider class.
 455:     fn seal_master<'py>(
 456:         &self,
 457:         py: Python<'py>,
 458:         seed: &[u8],
 459:     ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, u8)> {
 460:         if seed.len() != 32 {
 461:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 462:                 "seed must be exactly 32 bytes, got {}",
 463:                 seed.len()
 464:             )));
 465:         }
 466:         let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
 467:         arr.copy_from_slice(seed);
 468:         let sealed_result = self.inner.seal_master(&arr);
 469:         arr.zeroize();
 470:         let sealed = sealed_result.map_err(map_err)?;
 471:         Ok((
 472:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &sealed.bytes),
 473:             sealed.provider_tag.as_u8(),
 474:         ))
 475:     }
 476: 
 477:     fn derive_child<'py>(
 478:         &self,
 479:         py: Python<'py>,
 480:         sealed_master_bytes: &[u8],
 481:         sealed_master_tag: u8,
 482:         context_tag: &[u8],
 483:     ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, u8)> {
 484:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_master_tag)?;
 485:         let sealed_master = SealedKey {
 486:             provider_tag: tag,
 487:             bytes: sealed_master_bytes.to_vec(),
 488:         };
 489:         let child = self
 490:             .inner
 491:             .derive_child(&sealed_master, context_tag)
 492:             .map_err(map_err)?;
 493:         Ok((
 494:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &child.bytes),
 495:             child.provider_tag.as_u8(),
 496:         ))
 497:     }
 498: 
 499:     fn sealed_sign<'py>(
 500:         &self,
 501:         py: Python<'py>,
 502:         sealed_bytes: &[u8],
 503:         sealed_tag: u8,
 504:         transcript: &[u8],
 505:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 506:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_tag)?;
 507:         let sealed = SealedKey {
 508:             provider_tag: tag,
 509:             bytes: sealed_bytes.to_vec(),
 510:         };
 511:         let sig = self.inner.sealed_sign(&sealed, transcript).map_err(map_err)?;
 512:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &sig))
 513:     }
 514: 
 515:     fn verifying_key<'py>(
 516:         &self,
 517:         py: Python<'py>,
 518:         sealed_bytes: &[u8],
 519:         sealed_tag: u8,
 520:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 521:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_tag)?;
 522:         let sealed = SealedKey {
 523:             provider_tag: tag,
 524:             bytes: sealed_bytes.to_vec(),
 525:         };
 526:         let vk = self.inner.verifying_key(&sealed).map_err(map_err)?;
 527:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &vk.to_bytes()))
 528:     }
 529: 
 530:     /// Issue a TPM-rooted attestation doc. Same return tuple as
 531:     /// PySoftwareProvider.attest, but the `platform_quote` field
 532:     /// carries the ECDSA-P256 signature produced by the TPM-resident
 533:     /// attestation key.
 534:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 535:     #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
 536:     #[pyo3(signature = (
 537:         sealed_bytes,
 538:         sealed_tag,
 539:         peer_nonce,
 540:         issued_unix,
 541:         deadline_unix,
 542:         issuer_sdp_pubkey,
 543:         field_witness=None,
 544:     ))]
 545:     fn attest<'py>(
 546:         &self,
 547:         py: Python<'py>,
 548:         sealed_bytes: &[u8],
 549:         sealed_tag: u8,
 550:         peer_nonce: &[u8],
 551:         issued_unix: u64,
 552:         deadline_unix: u64,
 553:         issuer_sdp_pubkey: &[u8],
 554:         field_witness: Option<&[u8]>,
 555:     ) -> PyResult<(
 556:         u8,
 557:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 558:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 559:         u64,
 560:         u64,
 561:         Option<Bound<'py, PyBytes>>,
 562:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 563:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 564:         Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
 565:     )> {
 566:         let tag = provider_tag_from_u8(sealed_tag)?;
 567:         let sealed = SealedKey {
 568:             provider_tag: tag,
 569:             bytes: sealed_bytes.to_vec(),
 570:         };
 571:         let nonce = nonce_from_bytes(peer_nonce)?;
 572:         let witness = field_witness_from_bytes(field_witness)?;
 573:         let sdp = issuer_sdp_pubkey_from_bytes(issuer_sdp_pubkey)?;
 574:         let doc = self
 575:             .inner
 576:             .attest(
 577:                 &sealed,
 578:                 nonce,
 579:                 issued_unix,
 580:                 deadline_unix,
 581:                 witness.as_ref(),
 582:                 sdp,
 583:             )
 584:             .map_err(map_err)?;
 585:         let cmt = doc
 586:             .field_witness_commitment
 587:             .map(|c| PyBytes::new_bound(py, &c));
 588:         Ok((
 589:             doc.provider_tag.as_u8(),
 590:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.master_vk.to_bytes()),
 591:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.peer_nonce),
 592:             doc.issued_unix,
 593:             doc.deadline_unix,
 594:             cmt,
 595:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.platform_quote),
 596:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.issuer_sdp_pubkey),
 597:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &doc.master_sig),
 598:         ))
 599:     }
 600: }
 601: 
 602: /// Construct a fresh `WindowsHardenedProvider`. Generates a per-
 603: /// process software AEAD sealing key + acquires (or creates) the
 604: /// TPM-resident ECDSA-P256 attestation key under `tpm_key_name`.
 605: ///
 606: /// `tpm_key_name` is the NCrypt key handle name; daemons should use
 607: /// a stable per-install identifier (e.g. `"OL-confidential-attest-v1"`)
 608: /// so the same TPM key survives across daemon restarts.
 609: #[cfg(feature = "windows-tpm")]
 610: #[pyfunction]
 611: fn fresh_windows_hardened_provider(tpm_key_name: &str) -> PyResult<PyWindowsHardenedProvider> {
 612:     let provider =
 613:         ol_confidential::WindowsHardenedProvider::create(&mut OsRng, tpm_key_name)
 614:             .map_err(map_err)?;
 615:     Ok(PyWindowsHardenedProvider { inner: provider })
 616: }
 617: 
 618: /// Fallback when the wheel wasn't built with `--features windows-tpm`.
 619: /// Surfaces a friendly error rather than a NameError on import.
 620: #[cfg(not(feature = "windows-tpm"))]
 621: #[pyfunction]
 622: fn fresh_windows_hardened_provider(_tpm_key_name: &str) -> PyResult<PyObject> {
 623:     Err(PyValueError::new_err(
 624:         "WindowsHardenedProvider is disabled in this build. \
 625:          Build the native wheel with `--features windows-tpm` on a \
 626:          Windows host with TPM 2.0 (audit M6 May 2026).",
 627:     ))
 628: }
 629: 
 630: pub fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 631:     m.add_class::<PySoftwareProvider>()?;
 632:     #[cfg(feature = "windows-tpm")]
 633:     m.add_class::<PyWindowsHardenedProvider>()?;
 634:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(fresh_software_provider, m)?)?;
 635:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(software_provider_from_seed, m)?)?;
 636:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(fresh_windows_hardened_provider, m)?)?;
 637:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(attestation_nonce, m)?)?;
 638:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(verify, m)?)?;
 639:     // Surface the build-time feature gate so Python callers can
 640:     // check capability availability without trying-and-catching.
 641:     m.add("HAS_WINDOWS_TPM_PROVIDER", cfg!(feature = "windows-tpm"))?;
 642:     m.add("ATTESTATION_NONCE_LEN", ATTESTATION_NONCE_LEN)?;
 643:     m.add(
 644:         "ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS",
 645:         ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS,
 646:     )?;
 647:     // Provider tag wire bytes (for daemons that need to round-trip
 648:     // doc bytes through the network).
 649:     m.add("PROVIDER_TAG_SOFTWARE", ProviderTag::Software.as_u8())?;
 650:     m.add("PROVIDER_TAG_WINDOWS_TPM", ProviderTag::WindowsTpm.as_u8())?;
 651:     m.add(
 652:         "PROVIDER_TAG_APPLE_SE",
 653:         ProviderTag::AppleSecureEnclave.as_u8(),
 654:     )?;
 655:     m.add(
 656:         "PROVIDER_TAG_ANDROID_STRONGBOX",
 657:         ProviderTag::AndroidStrongBox.as_u8(),
 658:     )?;
 659:     m.add("PROVIDER_TAG_INTEL_SGX", ProviderTag::IntelSgx.as_u8())?;
 660:     m.add("PROVIDER_TAG_AMD_SEV_SNP", ProviderTag::AmdSevSnp.as_u8())?;
 661:     m.add("PROVIDER_TAG_ARM_TRUSTZONE", ProviderTag::ArmTrustZone.as_u8())?;
 662:     Ok(())
 663: }

  11: /// Python-visible Folder CRDT.
  12: #[pyclass(name = "Folder", module = "one_link_native.crdt")]
  13: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
  14: pub struct PyFolder {
  15:     inner: Folder,
  16: }
  17: 
  18: #[pymethods]
  19: impl PyFolder {
  20:     #[new]
  21:     fn new() -> Self {
  22:         Self {
  23:             inner: Folder::new(),
  24:         }
  25:     }
  26: 
  27:     /// Add a file. `replica` and `file_id` must be exactly 32 bytes.
  28:     fn add_file(
  29:         &mut self,
  30:         replica: &[u8],
  31:         file_id: &[u8],
  32:         display_name: String,
  33:         size_bytes: u64,
  34:         last_modified_ms: u64,
  35:     ) -> PyResult<()> {
  36:         let rid = ReplicaId(bytes_to_32(replica, "replica")?);
  37:         let fid = bytes_to_32(file_id, "file_id")?;
  38:         self.inner
  39:             .add_file(&rid, fid, display_name, size_bytes, last_modified_ms);
  40:         Ok(())
  41:     }
  42: 
  43:     /// Remove a file (add-wins OR-set: concurrent re-adds win).
  44:     fn remove_file(&mut self, replica: &[u8], file_id: &[u8]) -> PyResult<()> {
  45:         let rid = ReplicaId(bytes_to_32(replica, "replica")?);
  46:         let fid = bytes_to_32(file_id, "file_id")?;
  47:         self.inner.remove_file(&rid, &fid);
  48:         Ok(())
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     /// True iff `file_id` is currently in the folder.
  52:     fn contains(&self, file_id: &[u8]) -> PyResult<bool> {
  53:         let fid = bytes_to_32(file_id, "file_id")?;
  54:         Ok(self.inner.contains(&fid))
  55:     }
  56: 
  57:     /// Merge another folder into this one (commutative, associative, idempotent).
  58:     fn merge(&mut self, other: &PyFolder) {
  59:         self.inner.merge(&other.inner);
  60:     }
  61: 
  62:     /// Number of present files.
  63:     fn len(&self) -> usize {
  64:         self.inner.iter().count()
  65:     }
  66: 
  67:     /// List of currently-present (file_id, display_name, size, mtime) tuples.
  68:     fn entries<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyList>> {
  69:         let out = PyList::empty_bound(py);
  70:         for (fid, entry) in self.inner.iter() {
  71:             let item = (
  72:                 PyBytes::new_bound(py, fid),
  73:                 &entry.display_name.value,
  74:                 entry.size_bytes.value,
  75:                 entry.last_modified_ms.value,
  76:             );
  77:             out.append(item)?;
  78:         }
  79:         Ok(out)
  80:     }
  81: 
  82:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
  83:         format!("Folder(present_files={})", self.inner.iter().count())
  84:     }
  85: }
  86: 
  87: fn bytes_to_32(bytes: &[u8], field: &str) -> PyResult<[u8; 32]> {
  88:     if bytes.len() != 32 {
  89:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  90:             "{field} must be exactly 32 bytes, got {}",
  91:             bytes.len()
  92:         )));
  93:     }
  94:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
  95:     out.copy_from_slice(bytes);
  96:     Ok(out)
  97: }
  98: 
  99: /// Register the `crdt` submodule.
 100: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 101:     m.add_class::<PyFolder>()?;
 102:     Ok(())
 103: }

   1: //! pyo3 wrapper for [`ol_discovery`] — Coherence Mesh Phase F1.3.
   2: //!
   3: //! Exposes the SYNC pieces of the sovereign-discovery layer to the
   4: //! Python daemon: NodeId, SignedRecord, RoutingTable. The async
   5: //! iterative-lookup driver stays in pure Rust for now; the daemon
   6: //! orchestrates lookup at the Python level using these sync primitives
   7: //! + its own async I/O (asyncio + UDP socket). When we want to push
   8: //! lookup into Rust we'll add a pyo3-asyncio binding; not blocking
   9: //! for first production wiring.
  10: 
  11: use pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError;
  12: use pyo3::prelude::*;

  21:     RECORD_DEFAULT_TTL_SECS,

  28: // ── NodeId ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  29: 
  30: /// A 256-bit Kademlia NodeId (= BLAKE3 of an Ed25519 master pubkey).
  31: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.discovery", frozen, eq, ord, hash)]
  32: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Hash)]
  33: struct PyNodeId {
  34:     inner: InnerNodeId,
  35: }
  36: 
  37: #[pymethods]
  38: impl PyNodeId {
  39:     /// Construct from 32 raw bytes.
  40:     #[new]
  41:     fn new(raw: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Self> {
  42:         if raw.len() != NODE_ID_BYTES {
  43:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  44:                 "NodeId must be exactly {NODE_ID_BYTES} bytes, got {}",
  45:                 raw.len()
  46:             )));
  47:         }
  48:         let mut b = [0u8; NODE_ID_BYTES];
  49:         b.copy_from_slice(raw);
  50:         Ok(Self {
  51:             inner: InnerNodeId::from_bytes(b),
  52:         })
  53:     }
  54: 
  55:     /// Derive a NodeId from an Ed25519 master pubkey (32 bytes).
  56:     #[staticmethod]
  57:     fn from_pubkey(pubkey: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Self> {
  58:         if pubkey.len() != 32 {
  59:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  60:                 "pubkey must be 32 bytes, got {}",
  61:                 pubkey.len()
  62:             )));
  63:         }
  64:         let mut pk = [0u8; 32];
  65:         pk.copy_from_slice(pubkey);
  66:         Ok(Self {
  67:             inner: InnerNodeId::from_pubkey(&pk),
  68:         })
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     /// The underlying 32 bytes.
  72:     fn as_bytes<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
  73:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, self.inner.as_bytes())
  74:     }
  75: 
  76:     /// XOR distance to another NodeId, as 32 raw bytes.
  77:     fn distance<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>, other: &Self) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
  78:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.inner.distance(&other.inner))
  79:     }
  80: 
  81:     /// Number of leading zeros in XOR distance (= K-bucket index, or
  82:     /// NODE_ID_BITS=256 when self == other).
  83:     fn xor_leading_zeros(&self, other: &Self) -> u32 {
  84:         self.inner.xor_leading_zeros(&other.inner)
  85:     }
  86: 
  87:     /// K-bucket index for `other` from this NodeId's perspective.
  88:     /// Returns None for self.
  89:     fn bucket_index(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<usize> {
  90:         self.inner.bucket_index(&other.inner)
  91:     }
  92: 
  93:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
  94:         format!("{:?}", self.inner)
  95:     }
  96: }
  97: 
  98: // ── PeerRecord + SignedRecord ────────────────────────────────────

 100: /// Unsigned peer-announcement payload.
 101: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.discovery", frozen)]
 102: #[derive(Clone)]
 103: struct PyPeerRecord {
 104:     inner: InnerPeerRecord,
 105: }
 106: 
 107: #[pymethods]
 108: impl PyPeerRecord {
 109:     #[new]
 110:     #[pyo3(signature = (publisher_pubkey, endpoints, publish_time_unix, ttl_secs = RECORD_DEFAULT_TTL_SECS))]
 111:     fn new(
 112:         publisher_pubkey: &[u8],
 113:         endpoints: Vec<String>,
 114:         publish_time_unix: u64,
 115:         ttl_secs: u64,
 116:     ) -> PyResult<Self> {
 117:         if publisher_pubkey.len() != 32 {
 118:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 119:                 "publisher_pubkey must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 120:                 publisher_pubkey.len()
 121:             )));
 122:         }
 123:         let mut pk = [0u8; 32];
 124:         pk.copy_from_slice(publisher_pubkey);
 125:         Ok(Self {
 126:             inner: InnerPeerRecord {
 127:                 publisher_pubkey: pk,
 128:                 endpoints,
 129:                 publish_time_unix,
 130:                 ttl_secs,
 131:             },
 132:         })
 133:     }
 134: 
 135:     fn publisher_pubkey<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 136:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.inner.publisher_pubkey)
 137:     }
 138: 
 139:     fn endpoints(&self) -> Vec<String> {
 140:         self.inner.endpoints.clone()
 141:     }
 142: 
 143:     fn publish_time_unix(&self) -> u64 {
 144:         self.inner.publish_time_unix
 145:     }
 146: 
 147:     fn ttl_secs(&self) -> u64 {
 148:         self.inner.ttl_secs
 149:     }
 150: 
 151:     fn canonical_bytes<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 152:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.inner.canonical_bytes())
 153:     }
 154: 
 155:     fn is_fresh(&self, now_unix: u64) -> bool {
 156:         self.inner.is_fresh(now_unix)
 157:     }
 158: 
 159:     fn node_id(&self) -> PyNodeId {
 160:         PyNodeId {
 161:             inner: self.inner.node_id(),
 162:         }
 163:     }
 164: }

 166: /// A signed peer record (PeerRecord + Ed25519 signature).
 167: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.discovery", frozen)]
 168: #[derive(Clone)]
 169: struct PySignedRecord {
 170:     inner: InnerSignedRecord,
 171: }
 172: 
 173: #[pymethods]
 174: impl PySignedRecord {
 175:     /// Sign a record with a 32-byte Ed25519 signing-key seed. The
 176:     /// signing key's public component must match record.publisher_pubkey
 177:     /// (defensive; prevents accidentally signing for the wrong identity).
 178:     #[staticmethod]
 179:     fn sign(record: &PyPeerRecord, signing_key_seed: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Self> {
 180:         if signing_key_seed.len() != 32 {
 181:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 182:                 "signing_key_seed must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 183:                 signing_key_seed.len()
 184:             )));
 185:         }
 186:         let mut seed = [0u8; 32];
 187:         seed.copy_from_slice(signing_key_seed);
 188:         let sk = ed25519_dalek::SigningKey::from_bytes(&seed);
 189:         let signed = InnerSignedRecord::sign(record.inner.clone(), &sk).map_err(map_record_err)?;
 190:         Ok(Self { inner: signed })
 191:     }
 192: 
 193:     /// Construct from explicit components (e.g., received off the wire).
 194:     #[new]
 195:     fn from_parts(record: &PyPeerRecord, signature: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Self> {
 196:         if signature.len() != 64 {
 197:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 198:                 "signature must be 64 bytes, got {}",
 199:                 signature.len()
 200:             )));
 201:         }
 202:         let mut sig = [0u8; 64];
 203:         sig.copy_from_slice(signature);
 204:         Ok(Self {
 205:             inner: InnerSignedRecord {
 206:                 record: record.inner.clone(),
 207:                 signature: sig,
 208:             },
 209:         })
 210:     }
 211: 
 212:     fn record(&self) -> PyPeerRecord {
 213:         PyPeerRecord {
 214:             inner: self.inner.record.clone(),
 215:         }
 216:     }
 217: 
 218:     fn signature<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 219:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.inner.signature)
 220:     }
 221: 
 222:     /// Verify the Ed25519 signature against the record's canonical
 223:     /// bytes. Returns None on success; raises ValueError on failure.
 224:     fn verify(&self) -> PyResult<()> {
 225:         self.inner.verify().map_err(map_record_err)
 226:     }
 227: 
 228:     /// Verify + check freshness in one call. Returns True if signed
 229:     /// AND fresh; False if signed but expired; raises ValueError
 230:     /// on signature failure.
 231:     fn verify_and_check_freshness(&self, now_unix: u64) -> PyResult<bool> {
 232:         self.inner
 233:             .verify_and_check_freshness(now_unix)
 234:             .map_err(map_record_err)
 235:     }
 236: 
 237:     fn node_id(&self) -> PyNodeId {
 238:         PyNodeId {
 239:             inner: self.inner.node_id(),
 240:         }
 241:     }
 242: }

 244: // ── RoutingTable ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 245: 
 246: /// Kademlia K-bucket routing table.
 247: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.discovery")]
 248: struct PyRoutingTable {
 249:     inner: InnerRoutingTable,
 250: }
 251: 
 252: /// Insert-outcome enum value as a 0-arg tuple-style Python type.
 253: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.discovery", frozen, eq)]
 254: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]
 255: enum PyInsertOutcome {
 256:     Inserted,
 257:     BumpedToTail,
 258:     SelfInsertIgnored,
 259:     BucketFull,
 260: }
 261: 
 262: #[pymethods]
 263: impl PyRoutingTable {
 264:     #[new]
 265:     #[pyo3(signature = (own_id, k = K_BUCKET_DEFAULT))]
 266:     fn new(own_id: &PyNodeId, k: usize) -> Self {
 267:         Self {
 268:             inner: InnerRoutingTable::with_k(own_id.inner, k),
 269:         }
 270:     }
 271: 
 272:     fn own_id(&self) -> PyNodeId {
 273:         PyNodeId {
 274:             inner: *self.inner.own_id(),
 275:         }
 276:     }
 277: 
 278:     fn k(&self) -> usize {
 279:         self.inner.k()
 280:     }
 281: 
 282:     fn len(&self) -> usize {
 283:         self.inner.len()
 284:     }
 285: 
 286:     fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 287:         self.inner.is_empty()
 288:     }
 289: 
 290:     /// Insert (or update) a peer. Returns a tuple (outcome,
 291:     /// bucket_full_head). When outcome != BucketFull, the second
 292:     /// element is None; otherwise it's the head NodeId the caller
 293:     /// should PING to test for replacement eligibility.
 294:     fn insert(
 295:         &mut self,
 296:         id: &PyNodeId,
 297:         last_seen_unix: u64,
 298:     ) -> (PyInsertOutcome, Option<PyNodeId>) {
 299:         match self.inner.insert(id.inner, last_seen_unix) {
 300:             InnerInsertOutcome::Inserted => (PyInsertOutcome::Inserted, None),
 301:             InnerInsertOutcome::BumpedToTail => (PyInsertOutcome::BumpedToTail, None),
 302:             InnerInsertOutcome::SelfInsertIgnored => (PyInsertOutcome::SelfInsertIgnored, None),
 303:             InnerInsertOutcome::BucketFull { head } => (
 304:                 PyInsertOutcome::BucketFull,
 305:                 Some(PyNodeId { inner: head.id }),
 306:             ),
 307:         }
 308:     }
 309: 
 310:     fn replace_head_on_timeout(
 311:         &mut self,
 312:         timed_out_head: &PyNodeId,
 313:         new_peer: &PyNodeId,
 314:         last_seen_unix: u64,
 315:     ) -> bool {
 316:         self.inner
 317:             .replace_head_on_timeout(timed_out_head.inner, new_peer.inner, last_seen_unix)
 318:     }
 319: 
 320:     fn closest_to(&self, target: &PyNodeId) -> Vec<PyNodeId> {
 321:         self.inner
 322:             .closest_to(&target.inner)
 323:             .into_iter()
 324:             .map(|e: InnerBucketEntry| PyNodeId { inner: e.id })
 325:             .collect()
 326:     }
 327: 
 328:     fn closest_n_to(&self, target: &PyNodeId, n: usize) -> Vec<PyNodeId> {
 329:         self.inner
 330:             .closest_n_to(&target.inner, n)
 331:             .into_iter()
 332:             .map(|e: InnerBucketEntry| PyNodeId { inner: e.id })
 333:             .collect()
 334:     }
 335: 
 336:     fn stale_buckets(&self, now_unix: u64, max_age_secs: u64) -> Vec<usize> {
 337:         self.inner.stale_buckets(now_unix, max_age_secs)
 338:     }
 339: 
 340:     fn remove(&mut self, id: &PyNodeId) -> bool {
 341:         self.inner.remove(&id.inner)
 342:     }
 343: 
 344:     fn contains(&self, id: &PyNodeId) -> bool {
 345:         self.inner.contains(&id.inner)
 346:     }
 347: 
 348:     fn bucket_sizes(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
 349:         self.inner.bucket_sizes()
 350:     }
 351: }

 353: // ── DhtNode (production-deployable orchestrator) ─────────────────
 354: 
 355: /// High-level Kademlia DHT node. Owns the tokio runtime, UDP socket,
 356: /// routing table, record store, and background receiver task.
 357: ///
 358: /// Construct once, call `publish_self_record` + `add_seed_peer` to
 359: /// wire up bootstrap, then `lookup` / `lookup_record` to find peers
 360: /// over the real network.
 361: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.discovery", unsendable)]
 362: struct PyDhtNode {
 363:     inner: Option<InnerDhtNode>,
 364: }
 365: 
 366: #[pymethods]
 367: impl PyDhtNode {
 368:     /// Construct a new DhtNode.
 369:     ///
 370:     /// `bind_addr`: "host:port" (e.g. "0.0.0.0:7117" for the daemon's
 371:     /// UDP port, or "127.0.0.1:0" for an ephemeral test port).
 372:     /// `own_id`: this node's NodeId.
 373:     /// `seed_peers`: list of (NodeId, "host:port") tuples for
 374:     /// bootstrap. May be empty for the first node in a fresh swarm.
 375:     #[new]
 376:     #[pyo3(signature = (bind_addr, own_id, seed_peers))]
 377:     fn new(
 378:         bind_addr: &str,
 379:         own_id: &PyNodeId,
 380:         seed_peers: Vec<(PyNodeId, String)>,
 381:     ) -> PyResult<Self> {
 382:         let addr: SocketAddr = bind_addr
 383:             .parse()
 384:             .map_err(|e| PyValueError::new_err(format!("bad bind_addr {bind_addr:?}: {e}")))?;
 385:         let seeds: Result<Vec<(InnerNodeId, SocketAddr)>, _> = seed_peers
 386:             .into_iter()
 387:             .map(|(id, addr_s)| addr_s.parse::<SocketAddr>().map(|a| (id.inner, a)))
 388:             .collect();
 389:         let seeds = seeds.map_err(|e| PyValueError::new_err(format!("bad seed address: {e}")))?;
 390:         let node = InnerDhtNode::new(addr, own_id.inner, seeds).map_err(map_dht_err)?;
 391:         Ok(Self { inner: Some(node) })
 392:     }
 393: 
 394:     /// Local bound socket address as "host:port".
 395:     fn local_addr(&self) -> PyResult<String> {
 396:         let node = self.require()?;
 397:         Ok(node.local_addr().to_string())
 398:     }
 399: 
 400:     /// The node's own NodeId.
 401:     fn own_id(&self) -> PyResult<PyNodeId> {
 402:         let node = self.require()?;
 403:         Ok(PyNodeId {
 404:             inner: node.own_id(),
 405:         })
 406:     }
 407: 
 408:     /// Publish this node's own self-record.
 409:     fn publish_self_record(&self, record: &PySignedRecord) -> PyResult<()> {
 410:         let node = self.require()?;
 411:         node.publish_self_record(record.inner.clone());
 412:         Ok(())
 413:     }
 414: 
 415:     /// Add a seed peer (NodeId + "host:port" address) to the
 416:     /// resolver + routing table.
 417:     fn add_seed_peer(&self, id: &PyNodeId, addr: &str) -> PyResult<()> {
 418:         let node = self.require()?;
 419:         let addr: SocketAddr = addr
 420:             .parse()
 421:             .map_err(|e| PyValueError::new_err(format!("bad addr {addr:?}: {e}")))?;
 422:         node.add_seed_peer(id.inner, addr);
 423:         Ok(())
 424:     }
 425: 
 426:     /// Iterative FIND_NODE lookup. Returns the K closest NodeIds.
 427:     /// Blocking.
 428:     fn lookup(&self, target: &PyNodeId) -> PyResult<Vec<PyNodeId>> {
 429:         let node = self.require()?;
 430:         let ids = node.lookup(target.inner).map_err(map_dht_err)?;
 431:         Ok(ids.into_iter().map(|i| PyNodeId { inner: i }).collect())
 432:     }
 433: 
 434:     /// Iterative FIND_VALUE lookup. Returns the SignedRecord if the
 435:     /// target's record was found anywhere in the swarm; None if the
 436:     /// search converged without finding it.
 437:     fn lookup_record(&self, target: &PyNodeId) -> PyResult<Option<PySignedRecord>> {
 438:         let node = self.require()?;
 439:         let rec = node.lookup_record(target.inner).map_err(map_dht_err)?;
 440:         Ok(rec.map(|r| PySignedRecord { inner: r }))
 441:     }
 442: 
 443:     /// How many peers are currently in the routing table.
 444:     fn routing_table_len(&self) -> PyResult<usize> {
 445:         let node = self.require()?;
 446:         Ok(node.routing_table_len())
 447:     }
 448: 
 449:     /// How many records the node is currently storing.
 450:     fn records_len(&self) -> PyResult<usize> {
 451:         let node = self.require()?;
 452:         Ok(node.records_len())
 453:     }
 454: 
 455:     /// Row 3 maintenance: refresh buckets that haven't been touched
 456:     /// in `max_age_secs` seconds. Daemon-side scheduler calls this
 457:     /// periodically (e.g., every 60s). Returns count of buckets
 458:     /// refreshed.
 459:     fn refresh_stale_buckets(
 460:         &self,
 461:         now_unix: u64,
 462:         max_age_secs: u64,
 463:     ) -> PyResult<usize> {
 464:         let node = self.require()?;
 465:         Ok(node.refresh_stale_buckets(now_unix, max_age_secs))
 466:     }
 467: 
 468:     /// Row 3 maintenance: re-publish records older than
 469:     /// `max_age_secs`. Daemons call this periodically so K-closest
 470:     /// peers don't expire the records. Returns count of records
 471:     /// republished.
 472:     fn republish_records(
 473:         &self,
 474:         now_unix: u64,
 475:         max_age_secs: u64,
 476:     ) -> PyResult<usize> {
 477:         let node = self.require()?;
 478:         Ok(node.republish_records(now_unix, max_age_secs))
 479:     }
 480: 
 481:     /// Row 3 maintenance: single-call wrapper running BOTH bucket
 482:     /// refresh AND record republish. Returns
 483:     /// `(buckets_refreshed, records_republished)`.
 484:     fn tick_maintenance(
 485:         &self,
 486:         now_unix: u64,
 487:         bucket_max_age_secs: u64,
 488:         record_max_age_secs: u64,
 489:     ) -> PyResult<(usize, usize)> {
 490:         let node = self.require()?;
 491:         Ok(node.tick_maintenance(
 492:             now_unix,
 493:             bucket_max_age_secs,
 494:             record_max_age_secs,
 495:         ))
 496:     }
 497: 
 498:     /// Graceful shutdown. After this call the node is dead and any
 499:     /// further method call returns a RuntimeError.
 500:     fn shutdown(&mut self) {
 501:         if let Some(node) = self.inner.take() {
 502:             node.shutdown();
 503:         }
 504:     }
 505: }

 508:     fn require(&self) -> PyResult<&InnerDhtNode> {
 509:         self.inner
 510:             .as_ref()
 511:             .ok_or_else(|| pyo3::exceptions::PyRuntimeError::new_err("DhtNode is shut down"))
 512:     }
 513: }

  74: impl PyShard {
  75:     /// Reconstruct a [`Shard`] from its components — used by the
  76:     /// `one_link.durability` adapter to round-trip shards from
  77:     /// on-disk bytes back into `decode_stripe`-callable form.
  78:     ///
  79:     /// Required so a daemon can:
  80:     ///
  81:     /// 1. Encode → write shard bytes + manifest to disk.
  82:     /// 2. Forget the plaintext (the whole point of erasure storage).
  83:     /// 3. Read shard bytes back from disk later + reconstruct
  84:     ///    `Shard` objects via this constructor.
  85:     /// 4. Pass them to `decode_stripe` for recovery.
  86:     ///
  87:     /// Without this constructor, step 3 is impossible — `Shard` is
  88:     /// otherwise opaque to Python.
  89:     #[new]
  90:     #[pyo3(signature = (stripe_id, index, role, plaintext_len, bytes))]
  91:     fn new(
  92:         stripe_id: &[u8],
  93:         index: u8,
  94:         role: &str,
  95:         plaintext_len: u64,
  96:         bytes: &[u8],
  97:     ) -> PyResult<Self> {
  98:         if stripe_id.len() != 32 {
  99:             return Err(pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError::new_err(
 100:                 format!("stripe_id must be 32 bytes; got {}", stripe_id.len()),
 101:             ));
 102:         }
 103:         let mut sid = [0u8; 32];
 104:         sid.copy_from_slice(stripe_id);
 105:         let role = match role {
 106:             "data" => ShardRole::Data,
 107:             "parity" => ShardRole::Parity,
 108:             other => {
 109:                 return Err(pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError::new_err(
 110:                     format!("role must be 'data' or 'parity'; got {other:?}"),
 111:                 ))
 112:             }
 113:         };
 114:         Ok(Self {
 115:             inner: RustShard {
 116:                 bytes: bytes.to_vec(),
 117:                 role,
 118:                 index,
 119:                 plaintext_len,
 120:                 stripe_id: sid,
 121:             },
 122:         })
 123:     }
 124: 
 125:     #[getter]
 126:     fn bytes<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 127:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.inner.bytes)
 128:     }
 129: 
 130:     /// `"data"` or `"parity"`.

 133:         match self.inner.role {
 134:             ShardRole::Data => "data",
 135:             ShardRole::Parity => "parity",
 136:         }
 137:     }

 161:     }

 164: /// Encode `plaintext` into a stripe of `k + m` shards.
 165: #[pyfunction]
 166: fn encode_stripe<'py>(
 167:     py: Python<'py>,
 168:     plaintext: &[u8],
 169:     params: &PyStripeParams,
 170: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyList>> {
 171:     let shards = py
 172:         .allow_threads(|| rust_encode(plaintext, params.inner))
 173:         .map_err(erasure_err_to_py)?;
 174:     let out = PyList::empty_bound(py);
 175:     for shard in shards {
 176:         out.append(Py::new(py, PyShard { inner: shard })?)?;
 177:     }
 178:     Ok(out)
 179: }
 180: 
 181: /// Decode a stripe back to plaintext. `present` is a list of length
 182: /// `k + m`; entries may be `Shard` or `None`.
 183: #[pyfunction]
 184: fn decode_stripe<'py>(
 185:     py: Python<'py>,
 186:     params: &PyStripeParams,
 187:     present: &Bound<'py, PyList>,
 188: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 189:     let total = params.inner.k + params.inner.m;
 190:     if present.len() != total {
 191:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 192:             "expected {total} present slots, got {}",
 193:             present.len()
 194:         )));
 195:     }
 196:     // Extract owned PyShard refs to keep them alive across the call.
 197:     let mut owned: Vec<Option<PyShard>> = Vec::with_capacity(total);
 198:     for item in present.iter() {
 199:         if item.is_none() {
 200:             owned.push(None);
 201:         } else {
 202:             let shard: PyShard = item.extract()?;
 203:             owned.push(Some(shard));
 204:         }
 205:     }
 206:     let view: Vec<Option<&RustShard>> =
 207:         owned.iter().map(|o| o.as_ref().map(|s| &s.inner)).collect();
 208:     let plaintext = py
 209:         .allow_threads(|| rust_decode(params.inner, &view))
 210:         .map_err(erasure_err_to_py)?;
 211:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &plaintext))
 212: }
 213: 
 214: /// Compute the canonical StripeId for `(plaintext, params)`.
 215: #[pyfunction]
 216: fn stripe_id<'py>(
 217:     py: Python<'py>,
 218:     plaintext: &[u8],
 219:     params: &PyStripeParams,
 220: ) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 221:     let id = stripe_id_of(plaintext, params.inner);
 222:     PyBytes::new_bound(py, &id)
 223: }

 227: }

   1: //! `one_link_native.fec` — Python binding for the `ol_fec` Rust crate.
   2: //!
   3: //! Surfaces Reed-Solomon encode + decode for the durability layer per
   4: //! ADR-0016. Python callers build a `Codec(k, m)`, pass data shards
   5: //! (`list[bytes]`), and receive the parity shards (`list[bytes]`).
   6: //! Decoding takes the same `(k, m)` codec + a `list[bytes | None]` of
   7: //! `k + m` slots and returns the recovered data shards.
   8: 
   9: use ol_fec::{Codec, FecError};
  10: use pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError;
  11: use pyo3::prelude::*;
  12: use pyo3::types::{PyBytes, PyList};
  13: 
  14: /// Python-visible Reed-Solomon codec.
  15: #[pyclass(name = "Codec", module = "one_link_native.fec")]
  16: #[derive(Debug)]
  17: pub struct PyCodec {
  18:     inner: Codec,
  19: }
  20: 
  21: #[pymethods]
  22: impl PyCodec {
  23:     /// Build a codec for `(k, m)`.
  24:     #[new]
  25:     fn new(k: usize, m: usize) -> PyResult<Self> {
  26:         Codec::new(k, m)
  27:             .map(|inner| Self { inner })
  28:             .map_err(fec_err_to_py)
  29:     }
  30: 
  31:     /// Data-shard count.
  32:     #[getter]
  33:     fn k(&self) -> usize {
  34:         self.inner.k()
  35:     }
  36: 
  37:     /// Parity-shard count.
  38:     #[getter]
  39:     fn m(&self) -> usize {
  40:         self.inner.m()
  41:     }
  42: 
  43:     /// Total shards = k + m.
  44:     #[getter]
  45:     fn total_shards(&self) -> usize {
  46:         self.inner.total_shards()
  47:     }
  48: 
  49:     /// Encode `data_shards` (length-k list of equal-length `bytes`) into
  50:     /// m parity shards (returned as a `list[bytes]`).
  51:     fn encode<'py>(
  52:         &self,
  53:         py: Python<'py>,
  54:         data_shards: &Bound<'py, PyList>,
  55:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyList>> {
  56:         let shards: Vec<Vec<u8>> = data_shards
  57:             .iter()
  58:             .map(|item| item.extract::<Vec<u8>>())
  59:             .collect::<PyResult<_>>()?;
  60:         let refs: Vec<&[u8]> = shards.iter().map(|s| s.as_slice()).collect();
  61:         let parity = py
  62:             .allow_threads(|| self.inner.encode(&refs))
  63:             .map_err(fec_err_to_py)?;
  64:         let out = PyList::empty_bound(py);
  65:         for p in parity {
  66:             out.append(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &p))?;
  67:         }
  68:         Ok(out)
  69:     }
  70: 
  71:     /// Decode from a `list[bytes | None]` of length `k + m`. Returns
  72:     /// the recovered k data shards as `list[bytes]`.
  73:     fn decode<'py>(
  74:         &self,
  75:         py: Python<'py>,
  76:         present: &Bound<'py, PyList>,
  77:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyList>> {
  78:         let total = self.inner.total_shards();
  79:         if present.len() != total {
  80:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  81:                 "present must have exactly {total} slots, got {}",
  82:                 present.len()
  83:             )));
  84:         }
  85:         let mut owned: Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>> = Vec::with_capacity(total);
  86:         for item in present.iter() {
  87:             if item.is_none() {
  88:                 owned.push(None);
  89:             } else {
  90:                 owned.push(Some(item.extract::<Vec<u8>>()?));
  91:             }
  92:         }
  93:         let view: Vec<Option<&[u8]>> = owned
  94:             .iter()
  95:             .map(|o| o.as_ref().map(|v| v.as_slice()))
  96:             .collect();
  97:         let data = py
  98:             .allow_threads(|| self.inner.decode(&view))
  99:             .map_err(fec_err_to_py)?;
 100:         let out = PyList::empty_bound(py);
 101:         for d in data {
 102:             out.append(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &d))?;
 103:         }
 104:         Ok(out)
 105:     }
 106: 
 107:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
 108:         format!("Codec(k={}, m={})", self.inner.k(), self.inner.m())
 109:     }
 110: }
 111: 
 112: fn fec_err_to_py(err: FecError) -> PyErr {
 113:     crate::errors::OlFecError::new_err(err.to_string())
 114: }
 115: 
 116: /// Register the `fec` submodule.
 117: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 118:     m.add("__version__", ol_fec::VERSION)?;
 119:     m.add_class::<PyCodec>()?;
 120:     Ok(())
 121: }

   1: //! `one_link_native.fountain` — Python binding for the `ol_fountain` crate.
   2: //!
   3: //! Exposes the LT-codes encoder, decoder, and on-wire packet codec per
   4: //! ADR-0015. Python callers use the encoder to produce streams of
   5: //! deterministic encoded symbols and the decoder to reconstruct the
   6: //! original chunk plaintext from any sufficient subset.
   7: 
   8: use ol_fountain::{FountainPacket, LtDecoder, LtEncoder, MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK, PACKET_HEADER_LEN};
   9: use pyo3::buffer::PyBuffer;
  10: use pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError;
  11: use pyo3::prelude::*;
  12: use pyo3::types::PyBytes;
  13: 
  14: use crate::errors::fountain_error_to_pyerr;
  15: 
  16: /// Python LT encoder. Constructed once per chunk; `encode_symbol(symbol_id)`
  17: /// returns one XORed payload of length `symbol_len`.
  18: #[pyclass(name = "LtEncoder", module = "one_link_native.fountain")]
  19: #[derive(Debug)]
  20: pub struct PyLtEncoder {
  21:     /// We hold the source buffer in an owned `Vec<u8>` so the encoder
  22:     /// can borrow it for its lifetime.
  23:     source: Vec<u8>,
  24:     symbol_len: usize,
  25:     cdf: Vec<f64>,
  26:     k: u32,
  27: }
  28: 
  29: #[pymethods]
  30: impl PyLtEncoder {
  31:     /// Build an encoder over `source` with `symbol_len`-byte symbols.
  32:     #[new]
  33:     fn new(py: Python<'_>, source: &Bound<'_, PyAny>, symbol_len: usize) -> PyResult<Self> {
  34:         let source = bytes_from_buffer(py, source)?;
  35:         if source.is_empty() {
  36:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err("source buffer must be non-empty"));
  37:         }
  38:         if symbol_len == 0 {
  39:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err("symbol_len must be > 0"));
  40:         }
  41:         let k = ((source.len() + symbol_len - 1) / symbol_len) as u32;
  42:         let cdf = ol_fountain::robust_soliton_cdf(k);
  43:         Ok(Self {
  44:             source,
  45:             symbol_len,
  46:             cdf,
  47:             k,
  48:         })
  49:     }
  50: 
  51:     /// K (source-symbol count).
  52:     #[getter]
  53:     fn k(&self) -> u32 {
  54:         self.k
  55:     }
  56: 
  57:     /// Symbol length in bytes.
  58:     #[getter]
  59:     fn symbol_len(&self) -> usize {
  60:         self.symbol_len
  61:     }
  62: 
  63:     /// Original source length in bytes (pre-padding).
  64:     #[getter]
  65:     fn source_len(&self) -> usize {
  66:         self.source.len()
  67:     }
  68: 
  69:     /// Encode one symbol with the given `symbol_id`.
  70:     fn encode_symbol<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>, symbol_id: u32) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
  71:         let enc = LtEncoder::new(&self.source, self.symbol_len).map_err(fountain_error_to_pyerr)?;
  72:         let payload = py.allow_threads(|| enc.encode_symbol(symbol_id));
  73:         let _ = &self.cdf; // kept for API stability
  74:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &payload))
  75:     }
  76: 
  77:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
  78:         format!(
  79:             "LtEncoder(k={}, symbol_len={}, source_len={})",
  80:             self.k,
  81:             self.symbol_len,
  82:             self.source.len(),
  83:         )
  84:     }
  85: }
  86: 
  87: /// Python LT decoder.
  88: #[pyclass(name = "LtDecoder", module = "one_link_native.fountain")]
  89: #[derive(Debug)]
  90: pub struct PyLtDecoder {
  91:     inner: Option<LtDecoder>,
  92: }
  93: 
  94: #[pymethods]
  95: impl PyLtDecoder {
  96:     /// Construct a decoder for a chunk with `k` source symbols of
  97:     /// `symbol_len` bytes encoding an original of `source_length` bytes.
  98:     #[new]
  99:     fn new(k: u32, symbol_len: usize, source_length: usize) -> PyResult<Self> {
 100:         let inner =
 101:             LtDecoder::new(k, symbol_len, source_length).map_err(fountain_error_to_pyerr)?;
 102:         Ok(Self { inner: Some(inner) })
 103:     }
 104: 
 105:     /// Ingest one encoded packet. Returns `True` if this packet
 106:     /// completed the decode.
 107:     fn ingest(
 108:         &mut self,
 109:         py: Python<'_>,
 110:         symbol_id: u32,
 111:         payload: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
 112:     ) -> PyResult<bool> {
 113:         let bytes = bytes_from_buffer(py, payload)?;
 114:         let dec = self
 115:             .inner
 116:             .as_mut()
 117:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("decoder already consumed via finish()"))?;
 118:         let r = py
 119:             .allow_threads(|| dec.ingest(symbol_id, &bytes))
 120:             .map_err(fountain_error_to_pyerr)?;
 121:         Ok(r)
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     /// True iff all K source symbols are resolved.
 125:     fn is_complete(&self) -> bool {
 126:         self.inner.as_ref().is_some_and(LtDecoder::is_complete)
 127:     }
 128: 
 129:     /// Number of source symbols resolved so far.
 130:     #[getter]
 131:     fn resolved_count(&self) -> u32 {
 132:         self.inner.as_ref().map_or(0, LtDecoder::resolved_count)
 133:     }
 134: 
 135:     /// K (source-symbol count).
 136:     #[getter]
 137:     fn k(&self) -> u32 {
 138:         self.inner.as_ref().map_or(0, LtDecoder::k)
 139:     }
 140: 
 141:     /// Consume the decoder + return the reconstructed source bytes.
 142:     fn finish<'py>(&mut self, py: Python<'py>) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 143:         let dec = self
 144:             .inner
 145:             .take()
 146:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("decoder already consumed via finish()"))?;
 147:         let bytes = py
 148:             .allow_threads(|| dec.finish())
 149:             .map_err(fountain_error_to_pyerr)?;
 150:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &bytes))
 151:     }
 152: 
 153:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
 154:         match &self.inner {
 155:             Some(d) => format!(
 156:                 "LtDecoder(k={}, resolved={}/{}, complete={})",
 157:                 d.k(),
 158:                 d.resolved_count(),
 159:                 d.k(),
 160:                 d.is_complete()
 161:             ),
 162:             None => "LtDecoder(consumed)".to_string(),
 163:         }
 164:     }
 165: }
 166: 
 167: /// Encode a fountain packet to wire bytes.
 168: #[pyfunction]
 169: fn encode_packet<'py>(
 170:     py: Python<'py>,
 171:     chunk_id: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
 172:     k: u32,
 173:     symbol_id: u32,
 174:     source_length: u32,
 175:     payload: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
 176: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 177:     let chunk_id = chunk_id_32(py, chunk_id)?;
 178:     let payload = bytes_from_buffer(py, payload)?;
 179:     let p = FountainPacket::new(chunk_id, k, symbol_id, source_length, payload);
 180:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &p.encode()))
 181: }
 182: 
 183: /// Decode a fountain packet from wire bytes. Returns
 184: /// `(chunk_id, k, symbol_id, source_length, payload_bytes)`.
 185: #[pyfunction]
 186: fn decode_packet<'py>(
 187:     py: Python<'py>,
 188:     encoded: &Bound<'_, PyAny>,
 189: ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, u32, u32, u32, Bound<'py, PyBytes>)> {
 190:     let bytes = bytes_from_buffer(py, encoded)?;
 191:     let p = FountainPacket::decode(&bytes).map_err(fountain_error_to_pyerr)?;
 192:     Ok((
 193:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &p.chunk_id),
 194:         p.k,
 195:         p.symbol_id,
 196:         p.source_length,
 197:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &p.payload),
 198:     ))
 199: }
 200: 
 201: fn bytes_from_buffer(py: Python<'_>, obj: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<Vec<u8>> {
 202:     let _ = py;
 203:     let buf = PyBuffer::<u8>::get_bound(obj)?;
 204:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(buf.buf_ptr() as *const u8, buf.len_bytes()) };
 205:     Ok(slice.to_vec())
 206: }
 207: 
 208: fn chunk_id_32(py: Python<'_>, obj: &Bound<'_, PyAny>) -> PyResult<[u8; 32]> {
 209:     let v = bytes_from_buffer(py, obj)?;
 210:     if v.len() != 32 {
 211:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 212:             "chunk_id must be exactly 32 bytes, got {}",
 213:             v.len()
 214:         )));
 215:     }
 216:     let mut out = [0u8; 32];
 217:     out.copy_from_slice(&v);
 218:     Ok(out)
 219: }
 220: 
 221: /// Register the `fountain` submodule on the given `PyModule`.
 222: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 223:     m.add("__version__", ol_fountain::VERSION)?;
 224:     m.add("PACKET_HEADER_LEN", PACKET_HEADER_LEN)?;
 225:     m.add("MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK", MAX_ENCODED_PER_CHUNK)?;
 226:     m.add("C", ol_fountain::C)?;
 227:     m.add("DELTA", ol_fountain::DELTA)?;
 228:     m.add_class::<PyLtEncoder>()?;
 229:     m.add_class::<PyLtDecoder>()?;
 230:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(encode_packet, m)?)?;
 231:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(decode_packet, m)?)?;
 232:     Ok(())
 233: }

  21:     #[new]

  23:         if root.len() != 32 {
  24:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(

  39:             KeyGuarantee::TofuOnly => "TofuOnly",
  40:             KeyGuarantee::HardwareBound => "HardwareBound",
  41:             KeyGuarantee::HardwareAttested => "HardwareAttested",
  42:         }
  43:     }

   1: //! `one_link_native` — pyo3 binding crate for One Link's hot-path Rust crates.
   2: //!
   3: //! Per [ADR-0008](../../../docs/decisions/0008-ffi-contract.md), this is the
   4: //! single Python-facing surface. Pure-Rust crates in the workspace
   5: //! (`ol_chunk`, eventually `ol_aead`, `ol_chunk_store`, `ol_wal`, ...) are
   6: //! re-exported here as Python submodules:
   7: //!
   8: //! ```python
   9: //! import one_link_native
  10: //! from one_link_native import chunk
  11: //!
  12: //! for boundary in chunk.cdc_iter(buf):
  13: //!     start, end, blake3 = boundary
  14: //!     ...
  15: //! ```
  16: //!
  17: //! The Python daemon imports through this crate; downstream Rust tooling
  18: //! depends on the pure-Rust crates directly.
  19: 
  20: #![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/one_link_native/0.21.0")]
  21: // pyo3 macro expansion uses unsafe internals (`ref_from_ptr`,
  22: // `unwrap_required_argument`) that the workspace-level
  23: // `unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn = "deny"` would flag. The pyo3 maintainers have
  24: // audited those usages; they are sound by construction inside the macro.
  25: // Our hand-written code in this crate keeps the workspace deny semantics
  26: // via local `unsafe { ... }` blocks where actually needed.
  27: #![allow(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
  28: // pyo3 0.22 macros emit `#[cfg(feature = "gil-refs")]` arms which are not
  29: // reachable on our feature set; the unexpected_cfgs lint is therefore a
  30: // false positive. pyo3 0.23 cleans this up; until then we silence it
  31: // uniformly so the release build is warning-clean.
  32: #![allow(unexpected_cfgs)]
  33: // pyo3 wraps every #[pymethods] item in a private module, so explicit
  34: // `pub fn` declarations on those methods become "unreachable pub". This
  35: // is structural — there's no actual visibility leakage. Suppress for
  36: // the whole crate; the macro-generated code is the source.
  37: #![allow(unreachable_pub)]
  38: // pyo3-wrapped types (PyChunkStore, PyAeadCipher, ...) hold non-Debug
  39: // inner state (file handles, ring keys). Adding manual Debug impls
  40: // would leak implementation details into operator logs; instead we
  41: // suppress the missing_debug_implementations workspace lint locally.
  42: #![allow(missing_debug_implementations)]
  43:

   1: //! pyo3 wrapper for `ol_onion::transport_obfs` — row 7 pluggable
   2: //! transport. Exposes:
   3: //! - Primitive byte XOR (`obfuscate` / `deobfuscate` / `derive_nonce`).
   4: //! - Handshake (BridgeKeypair, ClientHandshake, ServerHandshake).
   5: //! - Session (per-direction seal/open with handshake-derived keys).
   6: 
   7: use pyo3::exceptions::{PyRuntimeError, PyValueError};
   8: use pyo3::prelude::*;
   9: use pyo3::types::PyBytes;
  10: 
  11: use rand_core_06::OsRng;
  12: 
  13: use ol_onion::transport_obfs::{
  14:     deobfuscate as core_deobfuscate, derive_nonce as core_derive_nonce,
  15:     obfuscate as core_obfuscate, BridgeKeypair, ClientHandshake as RustClientHandshake,
  16:     HandshakeError, ServerHandshake as RustServerHandshake, Session as RustSession,
  17:     BRIDGE_ID_LEN, BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN, BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN, HANDSHAKE_EPOCH_SECS, HANDSHAKE_LEN,
  18:     HANDSHAKE_MAC_LEN, OBFS_KEY_LEN, OBFS_NONCE_LEN, SESSION_KEY_LEN,
  19: };
  20: 
  21: fn check_key_nonce(key: &[u8], nonce: &[u8]) -> PyResult<()> {
  22:     if key.len() != OBFS_KEY_LEN {
  23:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  24:             "key must be {OBFS_KEY_LEN} bytes, got {}",
  25:             key.len()
  26:         )));
  27:     }
  28:     if nonce.len() != OBFS_NONCE_LEN {
  29:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  30:             "nonce must be {OBFS_NONCE_LEN} bytes, got {}",
  31:             nonce.len()
  32:         )));
  33:     }
  34:     Ok(())
  35: }
  36: 
  37: fn map_hs_err(e: HandshakeError) -> PyErr {
  38:     PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string())
  39: }

  43: #[pyfunction]
  44: fn obfuscate<'py>(
  45:     py: Python<'py>,
  46:     key: &[u8],
  47:     nonce: &[u8],
  48:     data: &[u8],
  49: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
  50:     check_key_nonce(key, nonce)?;
  51:     let mut key_arr = [0u8; OBFS_KEY_LEN];
  52:     key_arr.copy_from_slice(key);
  53:     let mut nonce_arr = [0u8; OBFS_NONCE_LEN];
  54:     nonce_arr.copy_from_slice(nonce);
  55:     let out = core_obfuscate(&key_arr, &nonce_arr, data);
  56:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &out))
  57: }
  58:

  68:     key_arr.copy_from_slice(key);

  87: /// Generate a fresh bridge keypair. Returns (secret_seed_32, public_32, id_32).
  88: #[pyfunction]
  89: fn generate_bridge_keypair<'py>(
  90:     py: Python<'py>,
  91: ) -> PyResult<(
  92:     Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
  93:     Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
  94:     Bound<'py, PyBytes>,
  95: )> {
  96:     let kp = BridgeKeypair::generate(&mut OsRng);
  97:     Ok((
  98:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &kp.secret_bytes()),
  99:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &kp.public_bytes()),
 100:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &kp.id_bytes()),
 101:     ))
 102: }
 103: 
 104: /// Bidirectional obfuscation session.
 105: #[pyclass(name = "Session")]
 106: pub struct PySession {
 107:     inner: Option<RustSession>,
 108: }
 109: 
 110: #[pymethods]
 111: impl PySession {
 112:     /// Seal outbound data with the given packet counter.
 113:     fn seal_outbound<'py>(
 114:         &self,
 115:         py: Python<'py>,
 116:         plaintext: &[u8],
 117:         counter: u64,
 118:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 119:         let session = self
 120:             .inner
 121:             .as_ref()
 122:             .ok_or_else(|| PyRuntimeError::new_err("session is closed"))?;
 123:         let out = session.seal_outbound(plaintext, counter);
 124:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &out))
 125:     }
 126: 
 127:     /// Open inbound data with the peer's packet counter.
 128:     fn open_inbound<'py>(
 129:         &self,
 130:         py: Python<'py>,
 131:         ciphertext: &[u8],
 132:         counter: u64,
 133:     ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 134:         let session = self
 135:             .inner
 136:             .as_ref()
 137:             .ok_or_else(|| PyRuntimeError::new_err("session is closed"))?;
 138:         let out = session
 139:             .open_inbound(ciphertext, counter)
 140:             .map_err(|_| PyValueError::new_err("session open failed"))?;
 141:         Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &out))
 142:     }
 143: 
 144:     /// Explicitly close the session, zeroizing the keys on drop.
 145:     fn close(&mut self) {
 146:         let _ = self.inner.take();
 147:     }
 148: 
 149:     /// True iff the session is still active.
 150:     fn is_open(&self) -> bool {
 151:         self.inner.is_some()
 152:     }
 153: }
 154: 
 155: /// Client handshake state held across the start → finish round trip.
 156: #[pyclass(name = "ClientHandshake")]
 157: pub struct PyClientHandshake {
 158:     inner: Option<RustClientHandshake>,
 159:     first_message: [u8; HANDSHAKE_LEN],
 160: }
 161: 
 162: #[pymethods]
 163: impl PyClientHandshake {
 164:     #[new]
 165:     fn new(bridge_public: &[u8], bridge_id: &[u8], now_unix: u64) -> PyResult<Self> {
 166:         if bridge_public.len() != BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN {
 167:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 168:                 "bridge_public must be {BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN} bytes"
 169:             )));
 170:         }
 171:         if bridge_id.len() != BRIDGE_ID_LEN {
 172:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 173:                 "bridge_id must be {BRIDGE_ID_LEN} bytes"
 174:             )));
 175:         }
 176:         let mut pk = [0u8; BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN];
 177:         pk.copy_from_slice(bridge_public);
 178:         let mut id = [0u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN];
 179:         id.copy_from_slice(bridge_id);
 180:         let inner = RustClientHandshake::start(&mut OsRng, &pk, &id, now_unix);
 181:         let first_message = *inner.first_message();
 182:         Ok(Self {
 183:             inner: Some(inner),
 184:             first_message,
 185:         })
 186:     }
 187: 
 188:     /// The bytes the daemon transmits to the bridge.
 189:     fn first_message<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 190:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.first_message)
 191:     }
 192: 
 193:     /// Complete the handshake using the bridge's reply. Consumes
 194:     /// the handshake state and returns a Session.
 195:     fn finish(&mut self, server_reply: &[u8]) -> PyResult<PySession> {
 196:         let inner = self
 197:             .inner
 198:             .take()
 199:             .ok_or_else(|| PyRuntimeError::new_err("handshake already finished"))?;
 200:         let session = inner.finish(server_reply).map_err(map_hs_err)?;
 201:         Ok(PySession {
 202:             inner: Some(session),
 203:         })
 204:     }
 205: }
 206: 
 207: /// Server-side accept: pure static fn.
 208: #[pyfunction]
 209: fn server_accept<'py>(
 210:     py: Python<'py>,
 211:     bridge_secret: &[u8],
 212:     bridge_id: &[u8],
 213:     client_first_message: &[u8],
 214:     now_unix: u64,
 215: ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, PySession)> {
 216:     if bridge_secret.len() != BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN {
 217:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 218:             "bridge_secret must be {BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN} bytes"
 219:         )));
 220:     }
 221:     if bridge_id.len() != BRIDGE_ID_LEN {
 222:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 223:             "bridge_id must be {BRIDGE_ID_LEN} bytes"
 224:         )));
 225:     }
 226:     let mut sk = [0u8; BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN];
 227:     sk.copy_from_slice(bridge_secret);
 228:     let mut id = [0u8; BRIDGE_ID_LEN];
 229:     id.copy_from_slice(bridge_id);
 230:     let bridge = BridgeKeypair::from_parts(sk, id);
 231:     let (reply, session) =
 232:         RustServerHandshake::accept(&mut OsRng, &bridge, client_first_message, now_unix)
 233:             .map_err(map_hs_err)?;
 234:     Ok((
 235:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &reply),
 236:         PySession {
 237:             inner: Some(session),
 238:         },
 239:     ))
 240: }
 241: 
 242: pub fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 243:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(obfuscate, m)?)?;
 244:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(deobfuscate, m)?)?;
 245:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(derive_nonce, m)?)?;
 246:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(generate_bridge_keypair, m)?)?;
 247:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(server_accept, m)?)?;
 248:     m.add_class::<PyClientHandshake>()?;
 249:     m.add_class::<PySession>()?;
 250:     m.add("OBFS_KEY_LEN", OBFS_KEY_LEN)?;
 251:     m.add("OBFS_NONCE_LEN", OBFS_NONCE_LEN)?;
 252:     m.add("BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN", BRIDGE_PUBKEY_LEN)?;
 253:     m.add("BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN", BRIDGE_SECRET_LEN)?;
 254:     m.add("BRIDGE_ID_LEN", BRIDGE_ID_LEN)?;
 255:     m.add("HANDSHAKE_LEN", HANDSHAKE_LEN)?;

   1: //! pyo3 wrapper for [`ol_onion`] — Coherence Mesh F3.
   2: //!
   3: //! Exposes the build + peel surface to the Python daemon so the
   4: //! daemon can construct onion-wrapped messages for multi-hop
   5: //! delivery and act as a relay for inbound onion packets.

   8: use pyo3::prelude::*;
   9: use pyo3::types::PyBytes;
  10: 
  11: use rand_core_06::OsRng;
  12: use x25519_dalek::{PublicKey, StaticSecret};
  13: 
  14: use ol_onion::{
  15:     build_onion as core_build_onion, pad_packet_to_transport,
  16:     peel_one_layer as core_peel_one_layer, unpad_packet_from_transport, Circuit, HopDescriptor,
  17:     OnionError, OnionPacket, PeelOutcome, HOP_ID_LEN, MAX_HOPS, MAX_USER_PAYLOAD,
  18:     TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT,

  21: fn map_err(e: OnionError) -> PyErr {
  22:     PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string())
  23: }
  24: 
  25: fn parse_hop(hop: (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)) -> PyResult<HopDescriptor> {
  26:     let (id_bytes, pk_bytes) = hop;
  27:     if id_bytes.len() != HOP_ID_LEN {
  28:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  29:             "hop id must be {HOP_ID_LEN} bytes, got {}",
  30:             id_bytes.len()
  31:         )));
  32:     }
  33:     if pk_bytes.len() != 32 {
  34:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  35:             "hop pubkey must be 32 bytes, got {}",
  36:             pk_bytes.len()
  37:         )));
  38:     }
  39:     let mut id_arr = [0u8; HOP_ID_LEN];
  40:     id_arr.copy_from_slice(&id_bytes);
  41:     let mut pk_arr = [0u8; 32];
  42:     pk_arr.copy_from_slice(&pk_bytes);
  43:     Ok(HopDescriptor::new(id_arr, pk_arr))
  44: }
  45: 
  46: /// Build an onion packet for a circuit. `circuit` is a list of
  47: /// (hop_id_32_bytes, hop_pubkey_32_bytes) tuples in order from
  48: /// first hop to destination.
  49: #[pyfunction]
  50: fn build_onion<'py>(
  51:     py: Python<'py>,
  52:     circuit: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>,
  53:     payload: &[u8],
  54: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
  55:     let hops: Result<Vec<HopDescriptor>, PyErr> = circuit.into_iter().map(parse_hop).collect();
  56:     let hops = hops?;
  57:     let c = Circuit::new(hops).map_err(map_err)?;
  58:     let packet = core_build_onion(&c, payload, &mut OsRng).map_err(map_err)?;
  59:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &packet.encode()))
  60: }
  61: 
  62: /// Peel one layer of an onion packet at this relay.
  63: ///
  64: /// Returns `("forward", next_hop_id_bytes, inner_packet_bytes)` if
  65: /// this relay should forward, or `("deliver", b"", payload_bytes)`
  66: /// if this relay is the destination.
  67: #[pyfunction]
  68: fn peel_one_layer<'py>(
  69:     py: Python<'py>,
  70:     relay_static_sk: &[u8],
  71:     packet_bytes: &[u8],
  72: ) -> PyResult<(String, Bound<'py, PyBytes>, Bound<'py, PyBytes>)> {
  73:     if relay_static_sk.len() != 32 {
  74:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  75:             "relay_static_sk must be 32 bytes, got {}",
  76:             relay_static_sk.len()
  77:         )));
  78:     }
  79:     let mut sk_bytes = [0u8; 32];
  80:     sk_bytes.copy_from_slice(relay_static_sk);
  81:     let sk = StaticSecret::from(sk_bytes);
  82:     let packet = OnionPacket::decode(packet_bytes).map_err(map_err)?;
  83:     let outcome = core_peel_one_layer(&sk, &packet).map_err(map_err)?;
  84:     match outcome {
  85:         PeelOutcome::Forward {
  86:             next_hop,
  87:             inner_packet_bytes,
  88:         } => Ok((
  89:             "forward".to_string(),
  90:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_hop.as_bytes()),
  91:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &inner_packet_bytes),
  92:         )),
  93:         PeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => Ok((
  94:             "deliver".to_string(),
  95:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &[]),
  96:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &payload),
  97:         )),
  98:     }
  99: }

 101: /// Compute the public X25519 key for a 32-byte static secret. Helper
 102: /// for daemons that need to publish their relay pubkey.
 103: #[pyfunction]
 104: fn derive_pubkey<'py>(py: Python<'py>, static_sk_bytes: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 105:     if static_sk_bytes.len() != 32 {
 106:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 107:             "static_sk must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 108:             static_sk_bytes.len()
 109:         )));
 110:     }
 111:     let mut sk_bytes = [0u8; 32];
 112:     sk_bytes.copy_from_slice(static_sk_bytes);
 113:     let sk = StaticSecret::from(sk_bytes);
 114:     let pk = PublicKey::from(&sk);
 115:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, pk.as_bytes()))
 116: }

 118: /// Pad a wire-encoded onion packet to TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT bytes.
 119: /// Trailing pad bytes are key-derived from `pad_seed` (must be 32
 120: /// bytes; pass a fresh value per packet).

 122: fn pad_to_transport<'py>(
 123:     py: Python<'py>,

 130:             pad_seed.len()
 131:         )));
 132:     }
 133:     let mut seed = [0u8; 32];
 134:     seed.copy_from_slice(pad_seed);
 135:     let out = pad_packet_to_transport(packet_bytes, &seed).map_err(map_err)?;
 136:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &out))
 137: }

 139: /// Strip transport padding from a TRANSPORT_PAD_HINT-byte input,

 143:     py: Python<'py>,
 144:     padded_bytes: &[u8],
 145: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 146:     let out = unpad_packet_from_transport(padded_bytes).map_err(map_err)?;
 147:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &out))
 148: }
