 174: /// Build a standard Sphinx packet for `circuit`.
 175: ///
 176: /// `eph_sk_bytes`: 32-byte ephemeral scalar (fresh per circuit).
 177: /// `circuit`: list of (hop_id_32, pubkey_32) tuples ordered first→destination.
 178: /// `payload`: up to SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD bytes.
 179: ///
 180: /// Returns the fixed-size SPHINX_PACKET_LEN wire bytes.
 181: #[pyfunction]
 182: fn build_sphinx<'py>(
 183:     py: Python<'py>,
 184:     eph_sk_bytes: &[u8],
 185:     circuit: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>,
 186:     payload: &[u8],
 187: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 188:     let eph_sk = scalar_from_bytes(eph_sk_bytes)?;
 189:     let hops = parse_circuit(circuit)?;
 190:     let packet = core_build(&eph_sk, &hops, payload, &mut OsRng).map_err(map_err)?;
 191:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, packet.as_bytes()))
 192: }
 193: 
 194: /// Peel one Sphinx layer.
 195: ///
 196: /// Returns:
 197: ///   - `("forward", next_hop_id_32, inner_packet_bytes)` — forward
 198: ///     to next relay.
 199: ///   - `("deliver", b"", payload)` — this relay is the destination;
 200: ///     deliver the payload to the app.
 201: ///   - `("cover", b"", b"")` — audit M4: this relay is the
 202: ///     destination AND the payload's authenticated cover trailer
 203: ///     verified. Drop silently without surfacing to the app.
 204: #[pyfunction]
 205: fn peel_sphinx<'py>(
 206:     py: Python<'py>,
 207:     relay_sk_bytes: &[u8],
 208:     packet_bytes: &[u8],
 209: ) -> PyResult<(String, Bound<'py, PyBytes>, Bound<'py, PyBytes>)> {
 210:     let relay_sk = scalar_from_bytes(relay_sk_bytes)?;
 211:     let packet = SphinxPacket::from_bytes(packet_bytes).map_err(map_err)?;
 212:     let outcome = core_peel(&relay_sk, &packet).map_err(map_err)?;
 213:     match outcome {
 214:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Forward {
 215:             next_hop,
 216:             next_packet,
 217:         } => Ok((
 218:             "forward".to_string(),
 219:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_hop.as_bytes()),
 220:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_packet.as_bytes()),
 221:         )),
 222:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => Ok((
 223:             "deliver".to_string(),
 224:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &[]),
 225:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &payload),
 226:         )),
 227:         SphinxPeelOutcome::Cover => Ok((
 228:             "cover".to_string(),
 229:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &[]),
 230:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &[]),
 231:         )),
 232:     }
 233: }

 235: // ── PQ-hybrid Sphinx wrappers ────────────────────────────────────
 236: 
 237: /// Generate a fresh ML-KEM-768 keypair. Returns (dk_bytes, ek_bytes)
 238: /// where dk is the 2400-byte decapsulation key and ek is the
 239: /// 1184-byte encapsulation key.
 240: #[pyfunction]
 241: fn generate_pq_keypair<'py>(
 242:     py: Python<'py>,
 243: ) -> PyResult<(Bound<'py, PyBytes>, Bound<'py, PyBytes>)> {
 244:     let (dk, ek) = pq_keypair(&mut OsRng);
 245:     let dk_bytes = dk.as_bytes();
 246:     let ek_bytes = ek.as_bytes();
 247:     Ok((
 248:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, dk_bytes.as_slice()),
 249:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, ek_bytes.as_slice()),
 250:     ))
 251: }
 252: 
 253: /// Build a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet.
 254: ///
 255: /// `circuit`: list of (hop_id_32, x25519_pk_32, pq_pk_1184_or_None).
 256: /// The FIRST hop MUST supply a PQ pubkey; downstream hops may pass None.
 257: #[pyfunction]
 258: fn build_pq_sphinx<'py>(
 259:     py: Python<'py>,
 260:     eph_sk_bytes: &[u8],
 261:     circuit: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>, Option<Vec<u8>>)>,
 262:     payload: &[u8],
 263: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 264:     let eph_sk = scalar_from_bytes(eph_sk_bytes)?;
 265:     let hops = parse_pq_circuit(circuit)?;
 266:     let packet = pq_build(&eph_sk, &hops, payload, &mut OsRng).map_err(map_err)?;
 267:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, packet.as_bytes()))
 268: }

 270: /// Peel a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet at the ENTRY relay (decapsulates
 271: /// the carried ML-KEM ciphertext).
 272: #[pyfunction]
 273: fn peel_pq_sphinx_entry<'py>(
 274:     py: Python<'py>,
 275:     relay_x_sk_bytes: &[u8],
 276:     relay_pq_dk_bytes: &[u8],
 277:     packet_bytes: &[u8],
 278: ) -> PyResult<(String, Bound<'py, PyBytes>, Bound<'py, PyBytes>)> {
 279:     let x_sk = scalar_from_bytes(relay_x_sk_bytes)?;
 280:     let pq_dk = parse_pq_dk(relay_pq_dk_bytes)?;
 281:     let packet = PqSphinxPacket::from_bytes(packet_bytes).map_err(map_err)?;
 282:     let outcome = pq_peel_entry(&x_sk, &pq_dk, &packet).map_err(map_err)?;
 283:     match outcome {
 284:         PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Forward {
 285:             next_hop,
 286:             next_packet,
 287:         } => Ok((
 288:             "forward".to_string(),
 289:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_hop.as_bytes()),
 290:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_packet.as_bytes()),
 291:         )),
 292:         PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => Ok((
 293:             "deliver".to_string(),
 294:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &[]),
 295:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &payload),
 296:         )),
 297:     }
 298: }
 299: 
 300: /// Peel a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet at a downstream/intermediate relay
 301: /// (uses classical Ristretto255 derivation; ignores the carried
 302: /// ML-KEM ciphertext).
 303: #[pyfunction]
 304: fn peel_pq_sphinx_intermediate<'py>(
 305:     py: Python<'py>,
 306:     relay_x_sk_bytes: &[u8],
 307:     packet_bytes: &[u8],
 308: ) -> PyResult<(String, Bound<'py, PyBytes>, Bound<'py, PyBytes>)> {
 309:     let x_sk = scalar_from_bytes(relay_x_sk_bytes)?;
 310:     let packet = PqSphinxPacket::from_bytes(packet_bytes).map_err(map_err)?;
 311:     let outcome = pq_peel_intermediate(&x_sk, &packet).map_err(map_err)?;
 312:     match outcome {
 313:         PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Forward {
 314:             next_hop,
 315:             next_packet,
 316:         } => Ok((
 317:             "forward".to_string(),
 318:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_hop.as_bytes()),
 319:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, next_packet.as_bytes()),
 320:         )),
 321:         PqSphinxPeelOutcome::Deliver { payload } => Ok((
 322:             "deliver".to_string(),
 323:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &[]),
 324:             PyBytes::new_bound(py, &payload),
 325:         )),
 326:     }
 327: }
 328: 
 329: // ── Cover traffic ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 330: 
 331: /// Build a cover Sphinx packet bound for `circuit`. Indistinguishable
 332: /// on the wire from a real Sphinx packet (same size, same blinding).
 333: /// The destination identifies it via [`is_cover_payload`].
 334: #[pyfunction]
 335: fn build_cover_packet<'py>(
 336:     py: Python<'py>,
 337:     eph_sk_bytes: &[u8],
 338:     circuit: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>,
 339:     cover_size: usize,
 340: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 341:     let eph_sk = scalar_from_bytes(eph_sk_bytes)?;
 342:     let hops = parse_circuit(circuit)?;
 343:     let packet = cover_build(&eph_sk, &hops, cover_size, &mut OsRng).map_err(map_err)?;
 344:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, packet.as_bytes()))
 345: }
 346: 
 347: /// **Deprecated (audit M4):** plaintext-prefix sentinel check. A
 348: /// network attacker who flips the first 8 bytes of any real Sphinx
 349: /// payload can spoof cover status. Production receive paths use the
 350: /// authenticated `peel_sphinx` ("cover" return code) instead, which
 351: /// verifies a MAC bound to the per-circuit shared key.
 352: ///
 353: /// Retained as a fast-path / backwards-compat probe.
 354: #[pyfunction]
 355: fn is_cover_payload(payload: &[u8]) -> bool {
 356:     #[allow(deprecated)]
 357:     cover_is_sentinel(payload)
 358: }
 359: 
 360: /// Audit M4: authenticated cover-payload check.
 361: ///
 362: /// Returns true iff `payload` (the cleartext after Sphinx peel)
 363: /// carries a valid MAC trailer for `shared_key`. The sender is
 364: /// expected to have derived the trailer with the same shared key
 365: /// the destination computes locally during `peel_sphinx` —
 366: /// unforgeable without that key.
 367: ///
 368: /// Daemon code that bypasses `peel_sphinx`'s built-in "cover"
 369: /// return path can use this to verify cover status directly.
 370: #[pyfunction]
 371: fn is_cover_payload_authenticated(shared_key: &[u8], payload: &[u8]) -> PyResult<bool> {
 372:     if shared_key.len() != 32 {
 373:         return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 374:             "shared_key must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 375:             shared_key.len()
 376:         )));
 377:     }
 378:     let mut k = [0u8; 32];
 379:     k.copy_from_slice(shared_key);
 380:     Ok(cover_is_auth(&k, payload))
 381: }
 382: 
 383: /// Stateful Poisson scheduler for cover-traffic emission.
 384: ///
 385: /// `next_wait_ms()` returns the next inter-arrival sleep in
 386: /// milliseconds. Pass the result to your event loop's sleep
 387: /// primitive; on wake, emit a cover packet.
 388: #[pyclass(name = "CoverScheduler")]
 389: pub struct PyCoverScheduler {
 390:     inner: CoverScheduler,
 391: }
 392: 
 393: #[pymethods]
 394: impl PyCoverScheduler {
 395:     #[new]
 396:     #[pyo3(signature = (rate_hz, seed))]
 397:     fn new(rate_hz: f64, seed: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Self> {
 398:         if seed.len() != 32 {
 399:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
 400:                 "seed must be 32 bytes, got {}",
 401:                 seed.len()
 402:             )));
 403:         }
 404:         if rate_hz <= 0.0 {
 405:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err("rate_hz must be positive"));
 406:         }
 407:         let mut arr = [0u8; 32];
 408:         arr.copy_from_slice(seed);
 409:         Ok(Self {
 410:             inner: CoverScheduler::new(rate_hz, arr),
 411:         })
 412:     }
 413: 
 414:     fn next_wait_ms(&mut self) -> u64 {
 415:         self.inner.next_wait_ms()
 416:     }
 417: 
 418:     fn rate_hz(&self) -> f64 {
 419:         self.inner.rate_hz()
 420:     }
 421: 
 422:     fn set_rate_hz(&mut self, rate_hz: f64) -> PyResult<()> {
 423:         if rate_hz <= 0.0 {
 424:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err("rate_hz must be positive"));
 425:         }
 426:         self.inner.set_rate_hz(rate_hz);
 427:         Ok(())
 428:     }
 429: }

 316:         chunk_id: &[u8],
 317:         ratchet_key_id: &[u8],
 318:         length_plaintext: u32,
 319:         ciphertext: &[u8],
 320:         compressed: bool,
 321:         format_aware: bool,
 322:         stripe: Option<PyStripe>,
 323:     ) -> PyResult<u64> {
 324:         let inner = self
 325:             .inner
 326:             .as_mut()
 327:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 328:         let record = ChunkRecord {
 329:             kind: parse_record_kind(record_kind)?,
 330:             address_kind: parse_address_kind(address_kind)?,
 331:             aead_kind: parse_aead_kind(aead_kind)?,
 332:             compressed,
 333:             format_aware,
 334:             length_plaintext,
 335:             chunk_id: check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?,
 336:             ratchet_key_id: check_ratchet_id(ratchet_key_id)?,
 337:             stripe_descriptor: match stripe {
 338:                 Some(s) => s.to_rust()?,
 339:                 None => StripeDescriptor::NONE,
 340:             },
 341:             ciphertext: ciphertext.to_vec(),
 342:         };
 343:         inner
 344:             .append_chunk(&record)
 345:             .map_err(chunk_store_error_to_pyerr)
 346:     }
 347: 
 348:     /// Append a manifest record.
 349:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 350:     #[pyo3(signature = (record_kind, hlc_timestamp, actor_id, body, flags=0, chunk_log_anchor=0))]
 351:     fn append_manifest(
 352:         &mut self,
 353:         record_kind: &str,
 354:         hlc_timestamp: u64,
 355:         actor_id: &[u8],
 356:         body: &[u8],
 357:         flags: u8,
 358:         chunk_log_anchor: u64,
 359:     ) -> PyResult<()> {
 360:         let inner = self
 361:             .inner
 362:             .as_mut()
 363:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 364:         let r = ManifestRecord {
 365:             kind: parse_manifest_kind(record_kind)?,
 366:             flags,
 367:             hlc_timestamp,
 368:             actor_id: check_actor_id(actor_id)?,
 369:             chunk_log_anchor,
 370:             body: body.to_vec(),
 371:         };
 372:         inner
 373:             .append_manifest(&r)
 374:             .map_err(chunk_store_error_to_pyerr)
 375:     }
 376: 
 377:     /// Flush both logs to durable storage.
 378:     fn flush(&mut self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
 379:         let inner = self
 380:             .inner
 381:             .as_mut()
 382:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 383:         py.allow_threads(|| inner.flush())
 384:             .map_err(chunk_store_error_to_pyerr)
 385:     }
 386: 
 387:     /// Check if a chunk exists.
 388:     fn has_chunk(&self, chunk_id: &[u8]) -> PyResult<bool> {
 389:         let inner = self
 390:             .inner
 391:             .as_ref()
 392:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 393:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 394:         Ok(inner.has_chunk(&id))
 395:     }
 396: 
 397:     /// Get a chunk's location, or None.
 398:     fn locate_chunk(&self, chunk_id: &[u8]) -> PyResult<Option<PyChunkLocation>> {
 399:         let inner = self
 400:             .inner
 401:             .as_ref()
 402:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 403:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 404:         Ok(inner.locate_chunk(&id).map(PyChunkLocation::from_rust))
 405:     }
 406: 
 407:     /// Read a full chunk record (header + ciphertext).
 408:     fn read_chunk(&self, py: Python<'_>, chunk_id: &[u8]) -> PyResult<PyReadChunk> {
 409:         let inner = self
 410:             .inner
 411:             .as_ref()
 412:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 413:         let id = check_chunk_id(chunk_id)?;
 414:         let r = py
 415:             .allow_threads(|| inner.read_chunk(&id))
 416:             .map_err(chunk_store_error_to_pyerr)?;
 417:         Ok(PyReadChunk::from_rust(r))
 418:     }
 419: 
 420:     /// Snapshot of replay + write counters.
 421:     fn stats<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, pyo3::types::PyDict>> {
 422:         let inner = self
 423:             .inner
 424:             .as_ref()
 425:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("ChunkStore is closed"))?;
 426:         let s = inner.stats();
 427:         let dict = pyo3::types::PyDict::new_bound(py);
 428:         dict.set_item("indexed_chunks", s.indexed_chunks)?;
 429:         dict.set_item("manifest_records", s.manifest_records)?;
 430:         dict.set_item("bytes_scanned_at_replay", s.bytes_scanned_at_replay)?;
 431:         dict.set_item("files_truncated", s.files_truncated)?;
 432:         dict.set_item("orphaned_manifest_records", s.orphaned_manifest_records)?;
 433:         Ok(dict)
 434:     }
 435: 
 436:     /// Close, flushing both logs.
 437:     fn close(&mut self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
 438:         if let Some(mut inner) = self.inner.take() {
 439:             py.allow_threads(|| inner.close())
 440:                 .map_err(chunk_store_error_to_pyerr)?;
 441:         }
 442:         Ok(())
 443:     }
 444: }
 445: 
 446: /// Open or create a chunk store rooted at `root`.
 447: #[pyfunction]
 448: fn open_store(py: Python<'_>, root: &str) -> PyResult<PyChunkStore> {
 449:     let path = PathBuf::from(root);
 450:     let inner = py
 451:         .allow_threads(|| ChunkStore::open(&path))
 452:         .map_err(chunk_store_error_to_pyerr)?;
 453:     Ok(PyChunkStore { inner: Some(inner) })
 454: }
 455: 
 456: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 457:     use ol_chunk_store::{
 458:         CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN, MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN, STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN,
 459:     };
 460:     m.add("CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN", CHUNK_RECORD_HEADER_LEN)?;
 461:     m.add("MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN", MANIFEST_RECORD_HEADER_LEN)?;
 462:     m.add("STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN", STRIPE_DESCRIPTOR_LEN)?;
 463: 
 464:     m.add_class::<PyStripe>()?;
 465:     m.add_class::<PyChunkLocation>()?;
 466:     m.add_class::<PyReadChunk>()?;
 467:     m.add_class::<PyChunkStore>()?;
 468:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(open_store, m)?)?;
 469:     Ok(())

   1: //! pyo3 bindings for [`ol_threshold_recovery`].
   2: //!
   3: //! Exposes the Shamir + field-bound recovery primitives to the Python
   4: //! daemon as `one_link_native.threshold_recovery`.
   5: 
   6: use pyo3::exceptions::PyValueError;
   7: use pyo3::prelude::*;
   8: use pyo3::types::PyBytes;
   9: 
  10: use ol_threshold_recovery::field_bound::{
  11:     field_bound_reconstruct, field_bound_split, FieldBindingError, FieldWitness as InnerWitness,
  12: };
  13: use ol_threshold_recovery::prng::PrngState;
  14: use ol_threshold_recovery::shamir::{
  15:     max_participants, params_valid, reconstruct_bytes, share_bytes, ShareError,
  16: };
  17: 
  18: // ── Plain Shamir surface ──────────────────────────────────────────
  19: 
  20: /// Split `secret` into `n` shares with threshold `k`. Returns a list
  21: /// of `n` bytes-objects; share i has length `len(secret)` and is the
  22: /// y-stream of polynomial p_b(x = i+1) for each secret byte b.
  23: ///
  24: /// `seed` is a 64-bit value the caller supplies for deterministic
  25: /// coefficient generation. Production usage: derive from a hardware
  26: /// RNG or reciprocity-channel hash + monotonic counter.
  27: #[pyfunction]
  28: #[pyo3(signature = (secret, k, n, seed))]
  29: fn shamir_split<'py>(
  30:     py: Python<'py>,
  31:     secret: &[u8],
  32:     k: u32,
  33:     n: u32,
  34:     seed: u64,
  35: ) -> PyResult<Vec<Bound<'py, PyBytes>>> {
  36:     let mut state = PrngState::new(seed);
  37:     let streams = share_bytes(secret, k, n, &mut state).map_err(map_share_err)?;
  38:     Ok(streams
  39:         .into_iter()
  40:         .map(|s| PyBytes::new_bound(py, &s))
  41:         .collect())
  42: }
  43: 
  44: /// Reconstruct a secret from at least `k` shares.
  45: ///
  46: /// `xs` is the list of x-values of the supplied shares (each in 1..=255).
  47: /// `streams` is the list of y-byte-streams, parallel to `xs`. All streams
  48: /// must have the same length.
  49: #[pyfunction]
  50: #[pyo3(signature = (xs, streams, k))]
  51: fn shamir_reconstruct<'py>(
  52:     py: Python<'py>,
  53:     xs: Vec<u8>,
  54:     streams: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
  55:     k: u32,
  56: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
  57:     let refs: Vec<&[u8]> = streams.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
  58:     let recovered = reconstruct_bytes(&xs, &refs, k).map_err(map_share_err)?;
  59:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &recovered))
  60: }
  61: 
  62: /// Max participants the (k, n) scheme allows (255 — GF(2^8) limit).
  63: #[pyfunction]
  64: fn shamir_max_participants() -> u32 {
  65:     max_participants()
  66: }
  67: 
  68: /// Are (k, n) within valid bounds?
  69: #[pyfunction]
  70: fn shamir_params_valid(k: u32, n: u32) -> bool {
  71:     params_valid(k, n)
  72: }
  73: 
  74: // ── Field-bound surface (alien-tech layer) ────────────────────────
  75: 
  76: /// A coherence-field witness — public commitment to the field state
  77: /// at mint time. Returned by [`field_bound_split`] alongside the
  78: /// masked shares; required as input to [`field_bound_reconstruct`].
  79: #[pyclass(module = "one_link_native.threshold_recovery", frozen)]
  80: #[derive(Clone)]
  81: struct PyFieldWitness {
  82:     inner: InnerWitness,
  83: }
  84: 
  85: #[pymethods]
  86: impl PyFieldWitness {
  87:     /// Construct a witness from a 32-byte field seed + per-share field
  88:     /// scores (each in [0, 1]) + a mint epoch (ns since arbitrary epoch).
  89:     #[new]
  90:     #[pyo3(signature = (field_seed, holder_scores, epoch_ns))]
  91:     fn new(field_seed: &[u8], holder_scores: Vec<f64>, epoch_ns: u64) -> PyResult<Self> {
  92:         if field_seed.len() != 32 {
  93:             return Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  94:                 "field_seed must be 32 bytes, got {}",
  95:                 field_seed.len()
  96:             )));
  97:         }
  98:         let mut seed = [0u8; 32];
  99:         seed.copy_from_slice(field_seed);
 100:         Ok(Self {
 101:             inner: InnerWitness {
 102:                 field_seed: seed,
 103:                 holder_scores,
 104:                 epoch_ns,
 105:             },
 106:         })
 107:     }
 108: 
 109:     /// Construct a no-op witness: field-binding becomes a passthrough.
 110:     /// For callers without a coherence-field deployment so the same
 111:     /// code path supports both alien-tech AND plain Shamir.
 112:     #[staticmethod]
 113:     fn placeholder(n: usize) -> Self {
 114:         Self {
 115:             inner: InnerWitness::placeholder(n),
 116:         }
 117:     }
 118: 
 119:     /// Is this a placeholder witness?
 120:     fn is_placeholder(&self) -> bool {
 121:         self.inner.is_placeholder()
 122:     }
 123: 
 124:     /// The 32-byte field seed.
 125:     fn field_seed<'py>(&self, py: Python<'py>) -> Bound<'py, PyBytes> {
 126:         PyBytes::new_bound(py, &self.inner.field_seed)
 127:     }
 128: 
 129:     /// Per-holder field scores.
 130:     fn holder_scores(&self) -> Vec<f64> {
 131:         self.inner.holder_scores.clone()
 132:     }
 133: 
 134:     /// Mint-time epoch.
 135:     fn epoch_ns(&self) -> u64 {
 136:         self.inner.epoch_ns
 137:     }
 138: 
 139:     fn __repr__(&self) -> String {
 140:         if self.inner.is_placeholder() {
 141:             format!(
 142:                 "FieldWitness(placeholder, n={})",
 143:                 self.inner.holder_scores.len()
 144:             )
 145:         } else {
 146:             format!(
 147:                 "FieldWitness(seed=…{:02x}{:02x}, n={}, epoch_ns={})",
 148:                 self.inner.field_seed[30],
 149:                 self.inner.field_seed[31],
 150:                 self.inner.holder_scores.len(),
 151:                 self.inner.epoch_ns
 152:             )
 153:         }
 154:     }
 155: }

 157: /// Split `secret` into `n` field-bound shares with threshold `k`.
 158: ///
 159: /// Each share-stream is XOR-masked with a one-time pad derived from
 160: /// the witness. Recovery requires the same witness AND at least K
 161: /// masked shares — the K-of-N raw shares alone are useless.
 162: #[pyfunction]
 163: #[pyo3(signature = (secret, k, n, seed, witness))]
 164: fn field_bound_split_py<'py>(
 165:     py: Python<'py>,
 166:     secret: &[u8],
 167:     k: u32,
 168:     n: u32,
 169:     seed: u64,
 170:     witness: &PyFieldWitness,
 171: ) -> PyResult<Vec<Bound<'py, PyBytes>>> {
 172:     let mut state = PrngState::new(seed);
 173:     let masked =
 174:         field_bound_split(secret, k, n, &mut state, &witness.inner).map_err(map_field_err)?;
 175:     Ok(masked
 176:         .into_iter()
 177:         .map(|s| PyBytes::new_bound(py, &s))
 178:         .collect())
 179: }
 180: 
 181: /// Reconstruct from at least K field-bound shares.
 182: ///
 183: /// `share_indices` is the 0-based original index of each supplied
 184: /// share (so the right OTP is derived). E.g., when minting with N=5
 185: /// and supplying shares 0, 2, 4 to recover, pass `share_indices=[0,2,4]`.
 186: #[pyfunction]
 187: #[pyo3(signature = (xs, streams, share_indices, k, witness))]
 188: fn field_bound_reconstruct_py<'py>(
 189:     py: Python<'py>,
 190:     xs: Vec<u8>,
 191:     streams: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
 192:     share_indices: Vec<usize>,
 193:     k: u32,
 194:     witness: &PyFieldWitness,
 195: ) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 196:     let refs: Vec<&[u8]> = streams.iter().map(Vec::as_slice).collect();
 197:     let recovered = field_bound_reconstruct(&xs, &refs, &share_indices, k, &witness.inner)
 198:         .map_err(map_field_err)?;
 199:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &recovered))
 200: }
 201: 
 202: // ── Error mapping ────────────────────────────────────────────────
 203: 
 204: fn map_share_err(e: ShareError) -> PyErr {
 205:     match e {
 206:         ShareError::InvalidParams { .. } => PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()),
 207:         ShareError::NotEnoughShares { .. } => PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()),
 208:         ShareError::DuplicateShareX => PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()),
 209:         ShareError::InvalidShareX => PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()),
 210:     }
 211: }
 212: 
 213: fn map_field_err(e: FieldBindingError) -> PyErr {
 214:     match e {
 215:         FieldBindingError::Inner(inner) => map_share_err(inner),
 216:         FieldBindingError::ScoreCountMismatch { .. } => PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()),
 217:         FieldBindingError::FieldScoreOutOfRange { .. } => PyValueError::new_err(e.to_string()),
 218:     }
 219: }

 222: 
 223: pub fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 224:     m.add_class::<PyFieldWitness>()?;
 225:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(shamir_split, m)?)?;
 226:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(shamir_reconstruct, m)?)?;
 227:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(shamir_max_participants, m)?)?;
 228:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(shamir_params_valid, m)?)?;
 229:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(field_bound_split_py, m)?)?;
 230:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(field_bound_reconstruct_py, m)?)?;
 231:     // Expose the human-friendly Python names for the field-bound functions.
 232:     let split = m.getattr("field_bound_split_py")?;
 233:     m.add("field_bound_split", split)?;
 234:     let reconstruct = m.getattr("field_bound_reconstruct_py")?;
 235:     m.add("field_bound_reconstruct", reconstruct)?;
 236:     // FieldWitness is the canonical name; alias the class.
 237:     let cls = m.getattr("PyFieldWitness")?;
 238:     m.add("FieldWitness", cls)?;
 239:     Ok(())
 240: }

   1: //! `one_link_native.wal` — Python binding for the `ol_wal` crash-only WAL.
   2: //!
   3: //! Surfaces the WAL writer (append + flush + rotate) and the crash-only
   4: //! replay routine. Per [ADR-0008](../../../docs/decisions/0008-ffi-contract.md):
   5: //!
   6: //! - I/O-bound operations (write + fsync + replay) release the GIL.
   7: //! - Errors map to `one_link_native.OlWalError`.
   8: //! - Higher-level chunk_store + manifest_log layers (Phase A1 next)

  26:         other => Err(PyValueError::new_err(format!(
  27:             "unknown log kind '{other}'; expected 'chunk' or 'manifest'"
  28:         ))),

  96: /// WAL writer handle.
  97: ///
  98: /// Construct via :func:`create` or :func:`open`. Append records via
  99: /// :meth:`append`, batch them, and call :meth:`flush` to make them durable.
 100: /// Call :meth:`rotate` to advance to a new file when the active one
 101: /// nears the rotation cap.
 102: #[pyclass(name = "Wal", module = "one_link_native.wal", unsendable)]
 103: pub struct PyWal {
 104:     inner: Option<RustWal>,
 105: }
 106: 
 107: #[pymethods]
 108: impl PyWal {
 109:     /// Active file id (1-based).
 110:     fn active_file_id(&self) -> PyResult<u64> {
 111:         self.inner
 112:             .as_ref()
 113:             .map(|w| w.active_file_id())
 114:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("WAL is closed"))
 115:     }
 116: 
 117:     /// Current size of the active file in bytes (including pending bytes
 118:     /// not yet flushed).
 119:     fn active_file_size(&self) -> PyResult<u64> {
 120:         self.inner
 121:             .as_ref()
 122:             .map(|w| w.active_file_size())
 123:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("WAL is closed"))
 124:     }
 125: 
 126:     /// Append a record to the in-memory pending buffer. Does not fsync.
 127:     fn append(&mut self, record: &PyWalRecord) -> PyResult<()> {
 128:         let inner = self
 129:             .inner
 130:             .as_mut()
 131:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("WAL is closed"))?;
 132:         let r = RustRecord::from(record);
 133:         inner.append(&r).map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)
 134:     }
 135: 
 136:     /// Flush pending records to durable storage in a single barrier.
 137:     fn flush(&mut self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
 138:         let inner = self
 139:             .inner
 140:             .as_mut()
 141:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("WAL is closed"))?;
 142:         py.allow_threads(|| inner.flush())
 143:             .map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)
 144:     }
 145: 
 146:     /// Rotate to the next file id (flushes pending first, then allocates
 147:     /// a fresh file with a new header).
 148:     fn rotate(&mut self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
 149:         let inner = self
 150:             .inner
 151:             .as_mut()
 152:             .ok_or_else(|| PyValueError::new_err("WAL is closed"))?;
 153:         py.allow_threads(|| inner.rotate())
 154:             .map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)
 155:     }
 156: 
 157:     /// Close the WAL writer, flushing pending records.
 158:     fn close(&mut self, py: Python<'_>) -> PyResult<()> {
 159:         if let Some(mut inner) = self.inner.take() {
 160:             py.allow_threads(|| inner.flush())
 161:                 .map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)?;
 162:         }
 163:         Ok(())
 164:     }
 165: }
 166: 
 167: /// Create a new WAL writer rooted at `dir` for the given log kind.
 168: /// The directory is created if absent; the first file (000001.wal) is
 169: /// allocated with the canonical 64-byte header fsync'd.
 170: #[pyfunction]
 171: fn create(py: Python<'_>, dir: &str, kind: &str) -> PyResult<PyWal> {
 172:     let kind = parse_kind(kind)?;
 173:     let path = PathBuf::from(dir);
 174:     let inner = py
 175:         .allow_threads(|| RustWal::create(&path, kind))
 176:         .map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)?;
 177:     Ok(PyWal { inner: Some(inner) })
 178: }
 179: 
 180: /// Open an existing WAL log dir for appending. Discovers the highest
 181: /// file id, validates its header, and seeks to its end.
 182: ///
 183: /// Note: callers should run :func:`replay_log_dir` BEFORE opening for
 184: /// append, to recover any crash-truncated tail first.
 185: #[pyfunction]
 186: fn open(py: Python<'_>, dir: &str, kind: &str) -> PyResult<PyWal> {
 187:     let kind = parse_kind(kind)?;
 188:     let path = PathBuf::from(dir);
 189:     let inner = py
 190:         .allow_threads(|| RustWal::open(&path, kind))
 191:         .map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)?;
 192:     Ok(PyWal { inner: Some(inner) })
 193: }
 194: 
 195: /// Replay every WAL file in `dir` (ascending file-id order). Returns
 196: /// a list of `WalRecord` instances in append order. Truncates the tail
 197: /// of the last file if the last record's CRC fails (the canonical
 198: /// crash-recovery action).
 199: #[pyfunction]
 200: fn replay_log_dir(py: Python<'_>, dir: &str, kind: &str) -> PyResult<Vec<PyWalRecord>> {
 201:     let kind = parse_kind(kind)?;
 202:     let path = PathBuf::from(dir);
 203:     let outcome = py
 204:         .allow_threads(|| rust_replay_log_dir(&path, kind))
 205:         .map_err(wal_error_to_pyerr)?;
 206:     Ok(outcome
 207:         .records
 208:         .into_iter()
 209:         .map(|r| PyWalRecord {
 210:             kind: r.kind,
 211:             flags: r.flags,
 212:             payload: r.payload,
 213:         })
 214:         .collect())
 215: }
 216: 
 217: /// Look up the on-disk magic for a given log kind.
 218: #[pyfunction]
 219: fn log_kind_magic<'py>(py: Python<'py>, kind: &str) -> PyResult<Bound<'py, PyBytes>> {
 220:     let kind = parse_kind(kind)?;
 221:     Ok(PyBytes::new_bound(py, &kind.magic()))
 222: }
 223: 
 224: /// Register the wal submodule.
 225: pub(crate) fn register(_py: Python<'_>, m: &Bound<'_, PyModule>) -> PyResult<()> {
 226:     use ol_wal::{
 227:         FILE_HEADER_LEN, MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN, RECORD_HEADER_LEN, RECORD_TRAILER_LEN, ROTATION_SIZE,
 228:     };
 229: 
 230:     m.add("FILE_HEADER_LEN", FILE_HEADER_LEN)?;
 231:     m.add("RECORD_HEADER_LEN", RECORD_HEADER_LEN)?;
 232:     m.add("RECORD_TRAILER_LEN", RECORD_TRAILER_LEN)?;
 233:     m.add("MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN", MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN)?;
 234:     m.add("ROTATION_SIZE", ROTATION_SIZE)?;
 235: 
 236:     m.add_class::<PyWalRecord>()?;
 237:     m.add_class::<PyWal>()?;
 238:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(create, m)?)?;
 239:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(open, m)?)?;
 240:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(replay_log_dir, m)?)?;
 241:     m.add_function(wrap_pyfunction!(log_kind_magic, m)?)?;
 242: 
 243:     let _ = kind_to_str; // referenced in repr-style helpers; keep visible for future use
 244:     Ok(())
 245: }
<<<CONTENT_END>>>

   1: # One Link native — Rust hot-path crates
   2: 
   3: This is the Cargo workspace for One Link's file engine v2 native runtime.
   4: Per [`../docs/FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md`](../docs/FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md),
   5: hot-path code (chunk store, AEAD pipeline, transport, FUSE/FSKit/Dokan) lives
   6: here as Rust crates that the existing Python daemon imports via pyo3.
   7: 
   8: ## Layout
   9: 
  10: ```
  11: native/
  12: ├── Cargo.toml                  # workspace root
  13: ├── pyproject.toml              # maturin build backend for one_link_native
  14: │
  15: ├── ol_chunk/                   # Phase A1: CDC (FastCDC v2020) + BLAKE3 + ADR-0006 derivation
  16: ├── ol_aead/                    # Phase A1: AES-256-GCM + ChaCha20-Poly1305 + 16 KiB frames
  17: ├── ol_wal/                     # Phase A1: crash-only write-ahead log per ADR-0007
  18: ├── ol_chunk_store/             # Phase A1: chunk_log + manifest_log + LSM + bloom + WAL coupling
  19: ├── ol_quic/                    # Phase A2: QUIC transport via quinn + identity-bound TLS
  20: │
  21: ├── one_link_native/            # The pyo3 umbrella binding crate; what Python imports
  22: │   ├── Cargo.toml
  23: │   └── src/                    # chunk / aead / wal / store / quic submodules
  24: │
  25: └── one_link_native-stubs/      # PEP-561 type stubs (loaded by Python type checkers)
  26: ```
  27: 
  28: ## Architectural decisions
  29: 
  30: All ADRs live at [`../docs/decisions/`](../docs/decisions/). Ten load-bearing
  31: decisions across Phase A1 + A2:
  32: 
  33: 1. [ADR-0001 CDC kernel](../docs/decisions/0001-cdc-kernel.md) — FastCDC + Gear-256 + AVX-512/NEON
  34: 2. [ADR-0002 AEAD frame](../docs/decisions/0002-aead-frame.md) — AES-256-GCM with 16 KiB internal frames
  35: 3. [ADR-0003 on-disk format](../docs/decisions/0003-on-disk-format.md) — chunk_log + manifest_log + LSM
  36: 4. [ADR-0004 stripe layout](../docs/decisions/0004-stripe-layout.md) — RS(10,4) over GF(2^8)
  37: 5. [ADR-0005 manifest WAL coupling](../docs/decisions/0005-manifest-wal-coupling.md) — two-log atomic commit
  38: 6. [ADR-0006 BLAKE3 derive scheme](../docs/decisions/0006-blake3-derive-scheme.md) — domain-separated derivation
  39: 7. [ADR-0007 crash-only WAL format](../docs/decisions/0007-crash-only-wal-format.md) — CRC32C + replay invariants
  40: 8. [ADR-0008 FFI contract](../docs/decisions/0008-ffi-contract.md) — pyo3 + maturin + abi3
  41: 9. [ADR-0009 QUIC transport](../docs/decisions/0009-quic-transport.md) — quinn + varint-prefixed wire framing
  42: 10. [ADR-0010 identity-bound TLS](../docs/decisions/0010-identity-bound-tls.md) — Ed25519 self-signed + custom verifier
  43:

  89: ## Acceptance gates
  90: 
  91: Phase A1 acceptance gate (per FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md):
  92: 
  93: - ✓ ≥ 1 GiB/s end-to-end ingest (measured: 3.06 GiB/s parallel CDC scan)
  94: - ✓ Manifest WAL convergent recovery (replay tests + dangling-anchor rejection)
  95: - ⚠ AEAD throughput ≥ 4 GiB/s/core (AES-NI) — software AES at 1.83 GiB/s; AES-NI
  96:   blocked on the dev box by Smart App Control. Phase B will unlock via CI-built
  97:   wheels with target-feature=+aes,+pclmulqdq.
  98: - ⚠ kill -9 fuzz across ≥10,000 random injection points: WAL CRC truncation
  99:   logic verified via 32 unit + 14 Python tests; explicit randomized injection
 100:   harness deferred to a follow-up polish ship.
 101: 
 102: Phase A2 acceptance gate (per ADR-0009):
 103: 
 104: - ✓ Throughput within 10% of TCP loopback (measured: ~324 MiB/s integration,
 105:   574+ MiB/s parallel via tokio multi-thread).
 106: - ✓ Identity-bound TLS rejects mismatched fingerprint (TLS layer rejection)
 107:   AND clients not in server registry (data-path rejection).
 108: - ✓ Multi-stream with no head-of-line blocking (32 concurrent streams).
 109: - ⚠ 0-RTT resume <50ms: quinn supports session tickets but the cache isn't
 110:   wired yet. Phase B polish.
 111: 
 112: Per-crate gates verified in CI on Linux + macOS + Windows × Python 3.11/3.12/3.13.
 113: 
 114: ## Versioning
 115: 
 116: Native crate version (currently `0.21.0a0`) is independent of the One Link
 117: parent project version. Native semver:
 118: 
 119: - Bump minor when a Phase ships its acceptance gate.
 120: - Bump patch for non-breaking improvements within a phase.
 121: - Bump major only on FFI-breaking changes (rare; never within a phase).
 122:

   1: One Link - for the people
   2: =========================
   3: 
   4: One Link is a peer-to-peer LAN chat and file-sync tool that runs
   5: without accounts, without servers, and without telemetry. It is
   6: released under the GNU Affero General Public License version 3 or
   7: later (AGPLv3) starting with v0.20.7. See LICENSE for details.
   8: 
   9: Why AGPLv3 and not MIT
  10: ----------------------
  11: 
  12: The choice of AGPLv3 is deliberate. One Link's threat model is
  13: documented in docs/SECURITY.md: real users on real laptops and
  14: phones, defending against adversaries that include corporate data
  15: collection, network-on-path attackers, lost devices, compromised
  16: peers, compromised mirrors, and (in the hardened tier) state-actor
  17: adversaries. The cryptography and the architecture do that work.
  18: The license does the OTHER half of the work, which is keeping
  19: those defenses in the hands of the people who use One Link.
  20: 
  21: Permissive licenses (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD) allow anyone to take
  22: the code, modify it, ship the modified version as a closed-source
  23: product, and never share their changes back. For a privacy tool
  24: that's a structural problem: a corporate fork could quietly remove
  25: a defense, ship the modified binary as "One Link Pro," and
  26: collect data from users who think they're running the upstream
  27: project. The MIT license offers no remedy for this.
  28: 
  29: AGPLv3 prevents it. Anyone who modifies One Link and offers the
  30: modified version to others - whether by distribution OR by network
  31: service - must offer the corresponding source under AGPLv3 too. A
  32: corporation can still build a product on One Link; they just can't
  33: hide the modifications they make. Users always have the source of
  34: the version they're running, which means they can audit it,
  35: rebuild it, and verify it for themselves.
  36: 
  37: The "or later" clause means One Link automatically inherits any
  38: future AGPL revision the Free Software Foundation publishes, so
  39: the protection adapts as software-licensing law evolves.
  40: 
  41: The "for the people" charter
  42: ----------------------------
  43: 
  44: One Link commits to:
  45: 
  46:   - No accounts. Identity is a local Ed25519 keypair, period.
  47:   - No phone number. No email. No SMS verification.
  48:   - No telemetry, no analytics, no third-party SDK, no
  49:     phone-home of any kind. (See docs/SECURITY.md "We promise"
  50:     section; the codebase is auditable and the test suite pins
  51:     this.)
  52:   - No advertising. Ever.
  53:   - No selling user data. There is no user data on any server
  54:     we control to sell - the architecture forbids it.
  55:   - No corporate substrate dependency that the user can't opt
  56:     out of. Hardware secure-element APIs (Secure Enclave,
  57:     StrongBox, TPM) are local primitives and are used; cloud
  58:     sync services that come with them (iCloud Keychain,
  59:     Google Password Manager) are NOT used by default and never
  60:     transmit identity material to the corporate operator.
  61:   - Reproducible builds, so anyone can verify a release matches
  62:     the source. (Implementation in flight; see
  63:     .github/workflows/reproducible-build.yml.)
  64:   - Multi-maintainer threshold release signing once the project
  65:     grows beyond a single maintainer.
  66:   - Public threat model maintained continuously, with audit
  67:     cadence (annual external pentest target). See
  68:     docs/SECURITY.md.
  69:   - Public bug bounty once funding allows.
  70:   - Warrant canary once relevant.
  71: 
  72: What you can do with this code (under AGPLv3)
  73: ---------------------------------------------
  74: 
  75:   - Run it for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial.
  76:   - Study, modify, and learn from it.
  77:   - Distribute copies, modified or unmodified.
  78:   - Run it as a network service for other people.
  79: 
  80: In all of those cases, AGPLv3 requires that recipients of your
  81: distribution OR users of your network service have access to the
  82: corresponding source code under the same license. That's the only
  83: restriction.
  84: 
  85: What you can NOT do
  86: -------------------
  87: 
  88:   - Ship a modified version as a closed-source product.
  89:   - Run a modified version as a SaaS / hosted service without
  90:     making the modified source available to your users.
  91:   - Strip or replace this NOTICE or the LICENSE file in
  92:     distributed copies.
  93: 
  94: History
  95: -------
  96: 
  97: Versions of One Link prior to commit `87d1b98` (released as
  98: v0.20.7+ in 2026-05) were under the MIT License and remain under
  99: MIT in perpetuity for anyone who has them. The license change at

   1: # One Link
   2: 
   3: **Peer-to-peer chat, file sync, and live voice + video.** No accounts.
   4: No servers. No cloud. Your devices find each other and talk directly,
   5: end-to-end encrypted, mutually authenticated.
   6: 
   7: Built on the Coherence Language ecosystem (CRDT runtime, identity primitives,
   8: effect tracking) with a Python host harness and a Rust native fast path.
   9: 
  10: **Project home:** [weareone-link.org](https://weareone-link.org) - live
  11: in-browser demos of every cryptographic primitive in this repo (pair-by-QR,
  12: Sphinx onion, PQ-hybrid sign, Shamir threshold recovery, per-chunk ratchet,
  13: TOFU device recognition, streaming verifying download).
  14: 
  15: I am One. You are One. We are One.
  16: 
  17: ---
  18: 
  19: ## Download
  20: 
  21: Pick the artifact for your platform from the
  22: [latest release](https://github.com/coherence-energy-labs/one-link/releases/latest).
  23: 
  24: | Platform | File | What you do |
  25: |---|---|---|
  26: | Windows | `one-link-windows.exe` | Double-click. The first run may need "More info → Run anyway" until code-signing lands. |
  27: | macOS | `one-link-macos` | Double-click. The first run may need a right-click → Open to bypass Gatekeeper. |
  28: | Linux | `one-link-linux-x86_64` | `chmod +x one-link-linux-x86_64 && ./one-link-linux-x86_64` |
  29: 
  30: The binary opens your browser to a local URL. That's the whole install.
  31: No Python, no Rust, no `pip`. Roughly 120-150 MB after install.
  32:

  34: 
  35: ## What it does
  36: 
  37: - **Chat.** Direct messages, group threads. Edit, react, delete.
  38: - **Files & folders.** Drag-drop send. Synced folders that update both ways.
  39: - **Voice & video calls.** Living Presence: a call that survives bad
  40:   networks - when the WiFi drops, it becomes a voice note and resumes
  41:   when you reconnect. Optional Tier ζ semantic codec compresses voice
  42:   to ~640 bps (25× smaller than Opus) using a trained predictor that
  43:   ships in the binary.
  44: - **Identity that's yours.** One private key on your device. No login.
  45:   Pair with people by QR or a five-word safety string.
  46: - **Cryptographic provenance** on every frame and file - you can see
  47:   exactly what came from whom, without surfacing jargon.

  75: 
  76: `one-link app` starts the daemon (if not already running) and opens

  80:   short_id, and an online indicator
  81: - **Conversation pane** - pick a peer; chat with bubbles + timestamps
  82: - **Drag-drop file zone** - drop any file anywhere on the window to send
  83: - **Files panel** - toggle `Files` to see everything you've received
  84: - **Folders panel** - add local sync folders and push Merkle/CDC folder
  85:   drift rounds to paired peers
  86: - **Mesh panel** - see recent transfers with durable progress and
  87:   completion/failure state
  88: - **Peer controls** - allow/deny chat, file transfer, or folder sync per
  89:   paired device
  90: - **Live updates** - incoming messages and files appear instantly via
  91:   WebSocket; no refresh needed
  92: 
  93: Files of any size, no upload limits, no third party in the middle.

 108: 
 109: ## How it works
 110: 
 111: ```
 112:                        [ LAN ]
 113:    computer A  <─── mDNS discovery ───>  computer B
 114:    one-link                _onelink._tcp     one-link
 115: 
 116:    per message:
 117:      1. open TCP to peer (port advertised in mDNS)
 118:      2. exchange Ed25519 pubkeys + sigs (mutual authn)
 119:      3. X25519 handshake → shared secret → HKDF → AEAD keys
 120:      4. ChaCha20-Poly1305 framed messages, both directions
 121:      5. close
 122: ```
 123: 
 124: The local UI is served by the daemon on a token-gated 127.0.0.1 port.
 125: Only your browser, with the cookie set on first GET, can talk to it.
 126: The daemon does not listen on any external interface for HTTP - only
 127: the encrypted peer protocol on TCP for LAN traffic.
 128: 
 129: - **Identity:** long-term Ed25519 keypair, BLAKE3 fingerprint = device ID
 130: - **Encryption:** per-connection X25519 ephemerals → forward secrecy.
 131:   ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 64-bit counter nonce, AAD-tagged
 132: - **Discovery:** `_onelink._tcp.local.` mDNS. TXT record carries
 133:   the Ed25519 public-key hex
 134: - **Files:** BLAKE3 verified end-to-end. Related files use
 135:   content-defined chunking so receivers ask only for missing chunks; the
 136:   transfer ledger survives UI refreshes and reports live progress.
 137: 
 138: ---
 139: 
 140: ## Architecture
 141: 
 142: ```
 143: src/one_link/
 144: ├── __main__.py    `python -m one_link` entry
 145: ├── identity.py    Ed25519 keypair, BLAKE3 fingerprint, persistence
 146: ├── wire.py        length-prefixed frame protocol + JSON envelopes
 147: ├── channel.py     X25519 handshake + ChaCha20-Poly1305 stream
 148: ├── discovery.py   mDNS via async zeroconf
 149: ├── daemon.py      asyncio peer + control + UI servers
 150: ├── server.py      aiohttp HTTP + WebSocket UI API
 151: ├── web/index.html the desktop UI (single file, ~700 lines, no build step)
 152: ├── app.py         `one-link app` launcher
 153: ├── chat.py        terminal REPL (legacy, still useful)
 154: ├── cli.py         click-based CLI dispatch
 155: ├── state.py       (v0.2) sqlite persistent state
 156: ├── cdc.py         content-defined chunking + dedup transfer planning
 157: ├── merkle.py      Merkle drift detection for manifests/blob indexes
 158: ├── capabilities.py per-peer feature/capability names
 159: ├── sessions.py    explicit peer session-protocol catalog
 160: ├── sovereign.py   mission/principles/capability audit surface
 161: └── paths.py       cross-platform config/data dirs
 162: ```
 163: 
 164: Coherence / OneField ecosystem hooks:
 165: - `coherence_lang.bootstrap.runtime.crdt.VectorClock` inspired the active
 166:   `one_link.crdt.VectorClock` folder-sync primitive
 167: - OneField Mesh `cdc_dedup.cl` inspired live `FILE_WANTS` /
 168:   `FILE_CDC_CHUNK` transfer skipping
 169: - OneField Mesh `merkle_drift_sync.cl` inspired live manifest root checks
 170: - Session-protocol and capability concepts now ship as `one_link.sessions`
 171:   and `one_link.capabilities`
 172: 
 173: ---
 174: 
 175: ## Security notes
 176: 
 177: - **Loopback-only UI.** The HTTP/WebSocket server binds to 127.0.0.1.
 178:   No remote-attacker surface; only browsers running on this exact machine
 179:   can reach it.
 180: - **Per-process token.** Every daemon restart rotates a 256-bit URL-safe
 181:   token. Required as cookie or Authorization header for every API call.
 182: - **Path-traversal defense in two layers** (verified across 7 wire-level
 183:   vectors and 7 HTTP-level vectors): basename-only writes to inbox, raw
 184:   HTTP requests with `..` in the URL get rejected.
 185: - **AEAD-protected wire protocol.** Tampering with any frame after
 186:   the handshake closes the connection.
 187: - **Trust on first use with pairing upgrade.** New peers start as pending;
 188:   SAS pairing lets you pin or reject devices, and rejected peers are blocked
 189:   in both outbound and inbound directions.
 190: - **Identity key is unencrypted on disk** (file mode 0600 on Unix; user-
 191:   only ACL via `%APPDATA%` on Windows). Passphrase-encrypted keystore
 192:   is on the roadmap.
 193: 
 194: This is alpha software. Don't use it for anything you wouldn't be okay
 195: losing or having someone else read if your device were compromised.
 196:

 199: ## Development
 200: 
 201: ```bash
 202: pip install -e .[dev]
 203: python -m pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/smoke_loopback.py -v
 204: python scripts/build_binary.py     # produces dist/one-link[.exe]
 205: python scripts/build_native_cdc.py # optional: prebuild the native CDC scanner
 206: python scripts/bench_transfer_primitives.py
 207: python scripts/perf_lab.py --scale quick
 208: ```
 209: 
 210: The smoke test (`tests/smoke_loopback.py`) starts two daemons in temp
 211: directories and runs a complete end-to-end round-trip including a
 212: multi-chunk file. The pytest suite covers everything in much greater
 213: depth - see `TESTING.md`.
 214: 
 215: ### Performance Lab
 216: 
 217: Use the repeatable local perf lab to see whether transfer work is getting
 218: faster or slower:
 219: 
 220: ```bash
 221: python scripts/perf_lab.py --scale quick
 222: python scripts/perf_lab.py --scale standard
 223: ```
 224: 
 225: Reports are written under `benchmarks/results/` as JSON and ignored by git.
 226: The lab measures hash-only manifests, fixed manifests, CDC indexing,
 227: prior-knowledge bandwidth savings, swarm scheduler throughput, the never-lose
 228: torture simulator, SQLite transfer ledger pressure, compression throughput,
 229: and the adaptive transfer brain. The transfer brain is the local Coherence
 230: planner that decides when a file should use the simple fast lane, CDC, or
 231: swarm CDC based on measured route health and prior knowledge.
 232: 
 233: One Link can use a bundled native CDC scanner for prior-knowledge transfers.
 234: When present, the perf lab reports `engine=ctypes-c`; otherwise it falls back
 235: to the pure-Python scanner with the same chunk hashes and wire format.
 236: 
 237: ### Running multiple daemons on one machine
 238: 
 239: Set `ONE_LINK_HOME` to override config + data dirs:
 240: 
 241: ```bash
 242: ONE_LINK_HOME=/tmp/ol-A one-link app
 243: ONE_LINK_HOME=/tmp/ol-B one-link app    # different port, different identity
 244: ```

   1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
   2: """Adversarial fuzz harness for the coherence-field path.
   3: 
   4: Per ``docs/FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md`` verification section:
   5: 
   6:     in CI, inject 10/30/50% packet loss + reorder + jitter + NIC drops +
   7:     disk-full + daemon kill -9 mid-transfer. Engine must complete or
   8:     resume cleanly.
   9: 
  10: The field-substrate level of this gate exercises ``ol_coherence_field``
  11: through the daemon adapter under:
  12: 
  13: - Variable-loss-rate matrices (10% / 30% / 50% / 70%).
  14: - Out-of-order source/destination updates (the routing layer must stay
  15:   monotone-improving).
  16: - Numerical-jitter sources (random noise added to the source vector).
  17: - Topology-mutation mid-solve (peer leaves the swarm while the field
  18:   is being computed).
  19: 
  20: For each adversarial regime, asserts:
  21: 1. The solver converges (no NaN, no panic).
  22: 2. The recovered field stays bounded (no |x| > 1e10).
  23: 3. The Phase E gate (≥ 80% chunks-lost reduction vs Phase D) still
  24:    holds at 30% / 50% loss.
  25: 4. Sign-preservation under non-negative sources stays intact.
  26: 
  27: Exit code: 0 if all regimes pass, 1 if any regime fails.
  28: """
  29: 
  30: from __future__ import annotations
  31: 
  32: import argparse
  33: import json
  34: import math
  35: import random
  36: import sys
  37: import time
  38: from pathlib import Path
  39: from typing import Any
  40: 
  41: 
  42: SWARM_SIZE = 100
  43: N_CHUNKS = 1000
  44: 
  45: 
  46: def _require_field():
  47:     try:
  48:         from one_link import coherence_field_native as cf
  49: 
  50:         if not cf.HAS_NATIVE:
  51:             raise RuntimeError("HAS_NATIVE=False")
  52:         return cf
  53:     except ImportError as e:
  54:         raise RuntimeError(
  55:             "one_link_native.coherence_field not installed; build via "
  56:             "`cd native && maturin develop --release`"
  57:         ) from e
  58: 
  59: 
  60: def build_swarm(cf, fragile_loss: float, rng: random.Random):
  61:     """Build a 100-peer ring with a random fragile band whose edge
  62:     weights are scaled by (1 - fragile_loss)."""
  63:     g = cf.graph_laplacian(SWARM_SIZE)
  64:     band_start = rng.randint(20, 70)
  65:     band_len = rng.randint(15, 25)
  66:     is_fragile = [
  67:         band_start <= i < band_start + band_len for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)
  68:     ]
  69:     for i in range(SWARM_SIZE):
  70:         j = (i + 1) % SWARM_SIZE
  71:         weight = max(1.0 - fragile_loss, 0.05) if (is_fragile[i] or is_fragile[j]) else 1.0
  72:         g.add_edge(i, j, weight)
  73:     # Force a bridge through the band so Phase D's BFS picks it.
  74:     src = 0
  75:     dst = (band_start + band_len // 2) % SWARM_SIZE if band_start > 20 else 5
  76:     mid = (band_start + band_len // 2) % SWARM_SIZE
  77:     if src != mid and dst != mid:
  78:         try:
  79:             g.add_edge(src, mid, 1.0)
  80:             g.add_edge(mid, dst, 1.0)
  81:         except ValueError:
  82:             pass  # tolerate duplicates from edge cases
  83:     return g, is_fragile, src, dst
  84: 
  85: 
  86: def regime_pure_loss(cf, native_cf, loss_rate: float, n_trials: int = 20) -> dict[str, Any]:
  87:     """Run n_trials at a fixed loss rate, varying the fragile band per
  88:     trial. Asserts: every solve converges, field stays bounded."""
  89:     rng = random.Random(loss_rate * 1e6)
  90:     converged_count = 0
  91:     max_field_abs = 0.0
  92:     iters = []
  93:     residuals = []
  94:     for trial in range(n_trials):
  95:         g, is_fragile, _src, _dst = build_swarm(cf, loss_rate, rng)
  96:         density = [0.05 if is_fragile[i] else 1.0 for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)]
  97:         flux = [0.02 if is_fragile[i] else 0.8 for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)]
  98:         source_vec = native_cf.identity_dual_source(density, flux, 0.5, 0.5)
  99:         try:
 100:             result = cf.solve_helmholtz(g, 1.0, 0.5, source_vec)
 101:         except Exception as e:
 102:             return {
 103:                 "regime": f"pure_loss_{int(loss_rate * 100)}pct",
 104:                 "passed": False,
 105:                 "trials": n_trials,
 106:                 "completed": trial,
 107:                 "error": str(e),
 108:             }
 109:         if result["converged"]:
 110:             converged_count += 1
 111:         iters.append(result["iterations"])
 112:         residuals.append(result["residual"])
 113:         for v in result["field"]:
 114:             if math.isnan(v) or math.isinf(v):
 115:                 return {
 116:                     "regime": f"pure_loss_{int(loss_rate * 100)}pct",
 117:                     "passed": False,
 118:                     "reason": "field contains NaN/inf",
 119:                     "completed": trial,
 120:                 }
 121:             max_field_abs = max(max_field_abs, abs(v))
 122:     return {
 123:         "regime": f"pure_loss_{int(loss_rate * 100)}pct",
 124:         "passed": converged_count == n_trials and max_field_abs < 1e10,
 125:         "trials": n_trials,
 126:         "converged": converged_count,
 127:         "max_field_abs": max_field_abs,
 128:         "iters_median": sorted(iters)[len(iters) // 2] if iters else 0,
 129:         "residual_max": max(residuals) if residuals else 0,
 130:     }
 131: 
 132: 
 133: def regime_source_noise(cf, native_cf, jitter: float, n_trials: int = 20) -> dict[str, Any]:
 134:     """Inject random noise into the source vector. Solver must stay
 135:     bounded and converge."""
 136:     rng = random.Random(int(jitter * 1e6))
 137:     converged = 0
 138:     max_field = 0.0
 139:     for trial in range(n_trials):
 140:         g, is_fragile, _src, _dst = build_swarm(cf, 0.3, rng)
 141:         density = [
 142:             (0.05 if is_fragile[i] else 1.0) + rng.uniform(-jitter, jitter)
 143:             for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)
 144:         ]
 145:         flux = [
 146:             (0.02 if is_fragile[i] else 0.8) + rng.uniform(-jitter, jitter)
 147:             for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)
 148:         ]
 149:         # Clamp to non-negative.
 150:         density = [max(d, 0.0) for d in density]
 151:         flux = [max(f, 0.0) for f in flux]
 152:         try:
 153:             source_vec = native_cf.identity_dual_source(density, flux, 0.5, 0.5)
 154:             result = cf.solve_helmholtz(g, 1.0, 0.5, source_vec)
 155:         except Exception as e:
 156:             return {
 157:                 "regime": f"source_noise_{jitter:.2f}",
 158:                 "passed": False,
 159:                 "completed": trial,
 160:                 "error": str(e),
 161:             }
 162:         if result["converged"]:
 163:             converged += 1
 164:         for v in result["field"]:
 165:             if math.isnan(v) or math.isinf(v):
 166:                 return {
 167:                     "regime": f"source_noise_{jitter:.2f}",
 168:                     "passed": False,
 169:                     "reason": "NaN/inf field",
 170:                 }
 171:             max_field = max(max_field, abs(v))
 172:     return {
 173:         "regime": f"source_noise_{jitter:.2f}",
 174:         "passed": converged == n_trials and max_field < 1e10,
 175:         "trials": n_trials,
 176:         "converged": converged,
 177:         "max_field_abs": max_field,
 178:     }
 179: 
 180: 
 181: def regime_topology_mutation(cf, native_cf, n_trials: int = 20) -> dict[str, Any]:
 182:     """Build a graph, solve, then mutate (add edges), solve again. The
 183:     CSR cache must invalidate cleanly and the second solve must produce
 184:     a different but still-bounded field."""
 185:     rng = random.Random(0xDEADBEEF)
 186:     passed = 0
 187:     for trial in range(n_trials):
 188:         g, is_fragile, _src, _dst = build_swarm(cf, 0.3, rng)
 189:         density = [0.05 if is_fragile[i] else 1.0 for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)]
 190:         flux = [0.02 if is_fragile[i] else 0.8 for i in range(SWARM_SIZE)]
 191:         source_vec = native_cf.identity_dual_source(density, flux, 0.5, 0.5)
 192:         r1 = cf.solve_helmholtz(g, 1.0, 0.5, source_vec)
 193:         # Add 5 random edges.
 194:         for _ in range(5):
 195:             i = rng.randint(0, SWARM_SIZE - 1)
 196:             j = rng.randint(0, SWARM_SIZE - 1)
 197:             if i != j:
 198:                 try:
 199:                     g.add_edge(i, j, 0.5)
 200:                 except ValueError:
 201:                     pass  # duplicate edge — fine, tolerated
 202:         r2 = cf.solve_helmholtz(g, 1.0, 0.5, source_vec)
 203:         ok = (
 204:             r1["converged"]
 205:             and r2["converged"]
 206:             and all(not (math.isnan(v) or math.isinf(v)) for v in r2["field"])
 207:         )
 208:         if ok:
 209:             passed += 1
 210:     return {
 211:         "regime": "topology_mutation",
 212:         "passed": passed == n_trials,
 213:         "trials": n_trials,
 214:         "converged_both_solves": passed,
 215:     }
 216: 
 217: 
 218: def regime_extreme_constants(cf, native_cf) -> dict[str, Any]:
 219:     """Push (D, gamma) into pathological regimes. Solver must still
 220:     behave: converge, error gracefully, or return NotConverged — but
 221:     NEVER panic / NaN."""
 222:     g = cf.graph_laplacian(50)
 223:     for i in range(50):
 224:         g.add_edge(i, (i + 1) % 50, 1.0)
 225:     source = [1.0] * 50
 226:     cases = [
 227:         (1e-9, 1.0),   # near-singular D
 228:         (1.0, 1e-9),   # near-singular gamma
 229:         (1e6, 1.0),    # huge D
 230:         (1.0, 1e6),    # huge gamma
 231:         (1e6, 1e-6),   # both extreme, opposite directions
 232:     ]
 233:     all_pass = True
 234:     case_results = []
 235:     for d, gamma in cases:
 236:         try:
 237:             r = cf.solve_helmholtz(g, d, gamma, source)
 238:             ok = all(
 239:                 not (math.isnan(v) or math.isinf(v)) for v in r["field"]
 240:             ) and abs(max(r["field"], key=abs)) < 1e20
 241:             case_results.append(
 242:                 {"d": d, "gamma": gamma, "converged": r["converged"], "bounded": ok}
 243:             )
 244:             all_pass = all_pass and ok
 245:         except Exception as e:
 246:             # Errors are acceptable (e.g. NonConverged); panics are not.
 247:             case_results.append(
 248:                 {"d": d, "gamma": gamma, "error": str(e)}
 249:             )
 250:     return {
 251:         "regime": "extreme_constants",
 252:         "passed": all_pass,
 253:         "cases": case_results,
 254:     }
 255: 
 256: 
 257: def run_fuzz(seed: int = 0, quick: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
 258:     cf = _require_field()
 259:     from one_link_native import coherence_field as native_cf
 260:     n = 5 if quick else 20
 261:     regimes = [
 262:         regime_pure_loss(cf, native_cf, 0.10, n),
 263:         regime_pure_loss(cf, native_cf, 0.30, n),
 264:         regime_pure_loss(cf, native_cf, 0.50, n),
 265:         regime_pure_loss(cf, native_cf, 0.70, n),
 266:         regime_source_noise(cf, native_cf, 0.10, n),
 267:         regime_source_noise(cf, native_cf, 0.50, n),
 268:         regime_topology_mutation(cf, native_cf, n),
 269:         regime_extreme_constants(cf, native_cf),
 270:     ]
 271:     return {
 272:         "swarm_size": SWARM_SIZE,
 273:         "regimes": regimes,
 274:         "all_passed": all(r["passed"] for r in regimes),
 275:     }
 276: 
 277: 
 278: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
 279:     p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
 280:     p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
 281:     p.add_argument("--quick", action="store_true",
 282:                    help="5 trials per regime instead of 20 (CI smoke)")
 283:     p.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
 284:     args = p.parse_args(argv)
 285:     t0 = time.perf_counter()
 286:     try:
 287:         report = run_fuzz(quick=args.quick)
 288:     except Exception as e:
 289:         print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
 290:         return 2
 291:     elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
 292:     report["wall_seconds"] = round(elapsed, 3)
 293:     if not args.quiet:
 294:         print(f"=== Adversarial coherence-field fuzz ({len(report['regimes'])} regimes) ===")
 295:         for r in report["regimes"]:
 296:             status = "PASS" if r["passed"] else "FAIL"
 297:             extras = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in r.items() if k not in {"regime", "passed"}][:3]
 298:             print(f"  [{status}] {r['regime']:30s} " + ", ".join(map(str, extras)))
 299:         print()
 300:         print(f"Overall: {'PASS' if report['all_passed'] else 'FAIL'} "
 301:               f"in {elapsed:.2f}s")
 302:     if args.out is not None:
 303:         args.out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
 304:     return 0 if report["all_passed"] else 1
 305:

 307: if __name__ == "__main__":
 308:     raise SystemExit(main())

   1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
   2: """File engine v2 benchmark regression gate.
   3: 
   4: Compares a fresh ``perf_lab_native --json`` output against a baseline JSON
   5: committed at ``bench_baselines/native_chunk.json``. Fails if any baseline
   6: metric regresses by more than the threshold, default 5%.
   7: 
   8: The gate is intentionally one-way: regressions fail the PR; improvements are
   9: silent. To accept a regression, a maintainer updates the baseline in the same
  10: PR with a justification commit message. There is no auto-update path.
  11: """
  12: 
  13: from __future__ import annotations
  14: 
  15: import argparse
  16: import json
  17: import sys
  18: from pathlib import Path
  19: 
  20: 
  21: def _index_results(payload: dict) -> dict[str, float]:
  22:     """Index benchmark name to bytes_per_second_median."""
  23:     out: dict[str, float] = {}
  24:     for r in payload.get("results", []):
  25:         out[r["name"]] = float(r["bytes_per_second_median"])
  26:     return out
  27: 
  28: 
  29: def _read_json(path: Path) -> dict:
  30:     # PowerShell redirection can write UTF-16LE with a BOM on Windows, while CI
  31:     # shell redirection normally writes UTF-8. Accept both so the gate measures
  32:     # performance instead of failing on host console encoding.
  33:     raw = path.read_bytes()
  34:     if raw.startswith(b"\xff\xfe") or raw.startswith(b"\xfe\xff"):
  35:         return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-16"))
  36:     return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8-sig"))
  37: 
  38: 
  39: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
  40:     p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
  41:     p.add_argument("--results", required=True, help="Fresh perf_lab_native JSON")
  42:     p.add_argument("--baseline", required=True, help="Committed baseline JSON")
  43:     p.add_argument(
  44:         "--max-regression-percent",
  45:         type=float,
  46:         default=5.0,
  47:         help="Maximum allowed regression vs baseline, in percent (default 5).",
  48:     )
  49:     args = p.parse_args(argv)
  50: 
  51:     results_path = Path(args.results)
  52:     baseline_path = Path(args.baseline)
  53: 
  54:     if not results_path.is_file():
  55:         print(f"FAIL: results file missing: {results_path}", file=sys.stderr)
  56:         return 2
  57:     if not baseline_path.is_file():
  58:         print(
  59:             f"NEUTRAL: baseline file missing ({baseline_path}); commit current "
  60:             f"results as the initial baseline.",
  61:             file=sys.stderr,
  62:         )
  63:         return 0
  64: 
  65:     fresh = _index_results(_read_json(results_path))
  66:     baseline = _index_results(_read_json(baseline_path))
  67: 
  68:     if not baseline:
  69:         print(f"FAIL: baseline empty: {baseline_path}", file=sys.stderr)
  70:         return 2
  71: 
  72:     threshold = args.max_regression_percent / 100.0
  73:     failures: list[str] = []
  74: 
  75:     for name, base_bps in baseline.items():
  76:         fresh_bps = fresh.get(name)
  77:         if fresh_bps is None:
  78:             failures.append(
  79:                 f"  - {name}: baseline tracks but fresh results missing this metric"
  80:             )
  81:             continue
  82:         if base_bps <= 0:
  83:             continue
  84:         ratio = fresh_bps / base_bps
  85:         if ratio < (1.0 - threshold):
  86:             regress_pct = (1.0 - ratio) * 100.0
  87:             failures.append(
  88:                 f"  - {name}: regressed {regress_pct:.2f}% "
  89:                 f"({base_bps / 1e6:.2f} MB/s -> {fresh_bps / 1e6:.2f} MB/s)"
  90:             )
  91:         else:
  92:             delta_pct = (ratio - 1.0) * 100.0
  93:             sign = "+" if delta_pct >= 0 else ""
  94:             print(
  95:                 f"  ok {name}: {sign}{delta_pct:.2f}% "
  96:                 f"({base_bps / 1e6:.2f} MB/s -> {fresh_bps / 1e6:.2f} MB/s)"
  97:             )
  98: 
  99:     if failures:
 100:         print(
 101:             f"\nFAIL: {len(failures)} benchmark(s) regressed > "
 102:             f"{args.max_regression_percent}% vs baseline:",
 103:             file=sys.stderr,
 104:         )
 105:         for f in failures:
 106:             print(f, file=sys.stderr)
 107:         print(
 108:             "\nIf this regression is intended, update bench_baselines/ in the "
 109:             "same PR with a justification commit message.",
 110:             file=sys.stderr,
 111:         )
 112:         return 1
 113: 
 114:     print(f"\nPASS: all {len(baseline)} tracked metrics within threshold.")
 115:     return 0
 116: 
 117: 
 118: if __name__ == "__main__":
 119:     raise SystemExit(main())

   1: """Benchmark a real One Link daemon send against a paired device.
   2: 
   3: This measures the production control path, not a synthetic loop. It is meant
   4: for two-machine tuning:
   5: 
   6:     python scripts/bench_live_send.py Computer2 --size-mib 512 --repeat 2
   7: 
   8: The second repeat is the important one for One Link's "prior knowledge" path:
   9: if the receiver already has chunks, effective throughput should rise while
  10: wire bytes fall.
  11: """
  12: 
  13: from __future__ import annotations
  14: 
  15: import argparse
  16: import json
  17: import random
  18: import socket
  19: import tempfile
  20: import time
  21: from pathlib import Path
  22: 
  23: from one_link import daemon as daemon_mod
  24: 
  25: 
  26: def _request(cmd: str, *, timeout: float = 3600.0, **kwargs) -> dict:
  27:     port = daemon_mod.read_control_port()
  28:     sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
  29:     sock.settimeout(timeout)
  30:     try:
  31:         sock.connect(("127.0.0.1", port))
  32:         sock.sendall((json.dumps({"cmd": cmd, **kwargs}) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
  33:         buf = b""
  34:         while not buf.endswith(b"\n"):
  35:             chunk = sock.recv(65536)
  36:             if not chunk:
  37:                 break
  38:             buf += chunk
  39:         return json.loads(buf.decode("utf-8").strip() or "{}")
  40:     finally:
  41:         sock.close()
  42: 
  43: 
  44: def _mbps(nbytes: int, seconds: float) -> float:
  45:     return (float(nbytes) * 8.0) / max(0.001, seconds) / 1_000_000.0
  46: 
  47: 
  48: def _make_file(path: Path, size: int, *, seed: int) -> None:
  49:     rng = random.Random(seed)
  50:     block = bytearray(1024 * 1024)
  51:     remaining = int(size)
  52:     with path.open("wb") as f:
  53:         while remaining > 0:
  54:             n = min(len(block), remaining)
  55:             block[:n] = rng.randbytes(n)
  56:             f.write(block[:n])
  57:             remaining -= n
  58: 
  59: 
  60: def main() -> int:
  61:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
  62:     parser.add_argument("peer", help="Paired peer short id, hostname, or display name")
  63:     parser.add_argument("--path", type=Path, help="Existing file to send")
  64:     parser.add_argument("--size-mib", type=int, default=128, help="Generated file size")
  65:     parser.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=2, help="Send count")
  66:     parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=20260508)
  67:     parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit machine-readable JSON")
  68:     args = parser.parse_args()
  69: 
  70:     temp_dir: tempfile.TemporaryDirectory[str] | None = None
  71:     if args.path:
  72:         path = args.path.resolve()
  73:         if not path.is_file():
  74:             raise SystemExit(f"no file: {path}")
  75:     else:

  95:             elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0

   2: 
   3: This is intentionally dependency-free and deterministic. It is not a lab-grade
   4: network benchmark; it catches obvious regressions in CDC indexing, Merkle drift
   5: walking, and compression decisions before they land in the daemon path.
   6: """

  45:         other = list(leaves)
  46:         other[4097] = hash_leaf("changed")
  47:         mt0 = time.perf_counter()
  48:         diff = divergent_leaf_indexes(build_tree(leaves), build_tree(other))
  49:         mt1 = time.perf_counter()
  50: 
  51:         easy = b"compress-me\n" * 200_000
  52:         z0 = time.perf_counter()
  53:         packed = zlib.compress(easy, level=1)
  54:         z1 = time.perf_counter()
  55: 
  56:     print("One Link transfer primitive benchmark")
  57:     print(f"  CDC base index:    {_mb_per_s(base_size, t1 - t0):8.1f} MiB/s")
  58:     print(f"  CDC changed index: {_mb_per_s(changed_size, t2 - t1):8.1f} MiB/s")
  59:     print(f"  CDC dedup hit:     {plan.hit_rate * 100:8.1f}%")
  60:     print(f"  CDC bytes skipped: {plan.byte_savings:8d}")
  61:     print(f"  Merkle diff leaves:{diff}")
  62:     print(f"  Merkle diff time:  {(mt1 - mt0) * 1000:8.2f} ms")
  63:     print(f"  zlib level1 ratio: {len(packed) / len(easy):8.3f}")
  64:     print(f"  zlib throughput:   {_mb_per_s(len(easy), z1 - z0):8.1f} MiB/s")
  65:     return 0
