   1: """Signed capability grants — fine-grained authority with auto-expiry.
   2: 
   3: Today's capability system (capabilities.py) is binary: either a
   4: peer is paired (full access to whatever capabilities both sides
   5: advertise) or not paired (denied). Three real-world flows aren't
   6: served by that:
   7: 
   8:   1. **One-shot delegation**: "let my colleague pull these files
   9:      for the next hour while I'm asleep, then auto-revoke."
  10: 
  11:   2. **Bounded scope**: "this peer can read folder /shared but
  12:      not /private, files under 100 MB, no chat."
  13: 
  14:   3. **Offline-resilient revocation**: a peer that's currently
  15:      offline can't issue a revoke. A grant that auto-expires
  16:      bounds the worst-case exposure window without needing the
  17:      granter to come online.
  18: 
  19: Bundle 44 ships a signed-capability-grant primitive. The granter
  20: mints a Ed25519-signed token bearing:
  21: 
  22:   - granter_pub        (32 bytes — who issued)
  23:   - subject_pub        (32 bytes — who is granted to)
  24:   - capabilities       (set of strings — what's allowed)
  25:   - resource_scope     (bytes — opaque scope, e.g. folder root_id)
  26:   - not_before_ms      (epoch when grant activates)
  27:   - not_after_ms       (epoch when grant auto-expires)
  28:   - nonce              (16 bytes — replay defense per grant)
  29: 
  30: The receiver verifies on every use:
  31:   - Signature is valid under granter_pub
  32:   - now ∈ [not_before_ms, not_after_ms]
  33:   - nonce hasn't been replayed (caller maintains a seen-set)
  34:   - subject_pub matches the presenting peer
  35: 
  36: Combined with the existing pair-flow + capability-policy code,
  37: this lets a granter say "this device is paired AND can do these
  38: specific actions until time T". After T, the grant is dead even
  39: if the granter is offline. After explicit revoke (a tombstone the
  40: granter pre-commits or broadcasts), it's also dead.
  41: 
  42: Wire format
  43: -----------
  44: 
  45:   [magic: b"OLCAP1"] (6 bytes)
  46:   [version: 1 byte]
  47:   [granter_pub: 32 bytes]
  48:   [subject_pub: 32 bytes]
  49:   [not_before_ms: 8 bytes BE]
  50:   [not_after_ms: 8 bytes BE]
  51:   [nonce: 16 bytes]
  52:   [u16 caps_len]
  53:   [caps: caps_len bytes — UTF-8 sorted comma-separated capability tags]
  54:   [u16 scope_len]
  55:   [scope: scope_len bytes — opaque caller-defined]
  56:   [signature: 64 bytes]
  57: 
  58: The signature covers everything from magic to scope (i.e. the
  59: whole record except the trailing 64 bytes).
  60: 
  61: Capability tag namespace:
  62:   - "files:read" / "files:write"
  63:   - "folder:read:<root_id_hex>" / "folder:write:<root_id_hex>"
  64:   - "chat:send" / "chat:read"
  65:   - "groups:join" / "groups:speak"
  66:   - "rdz:lookup"
  67: The tags are caller-defined; this module is opaque to the names.
  68: """
  69: from __future__ import annotations
  70: 
  71: import secrets
  72: import struct
  73: import time
  74: from dataclasses import dataclass
  75: from typing import Iterable
  76: 
  77: from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
  78: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
  79:     Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519PublicKey,
  80: )
  81: 
  82: 
  83: GRANT_MAGIC = b"OLCAP1"
  84: GRANT_VERSION = 1
  85: NONCE_LEN = 16
  86: SIG_LEN = 64
  87: ED_PUB_LEN = 32
  88: HEADER_FIXED_LEN = (
  89:     len(GRANT_MAGIC) + 1
  90:     + ED_PUB_LEN + ED_PUB_LEN
  91:     + 8 + 8 + NONCE_LEN
  92: )
  93: MAX_CAPS_LEN = 4096
  94: MAX_SCOPE_LEN = 4096
  95: 
  96: 
  97: def _normalize_caps(capabilities: Iterable[str]) -> bytes:
  98:     """Caps are stored sorted + comma-joined for canonical
  99:     serialization. A grant with caps {"a", "b"} encodes the same
 100:     bytes as one with {"b", "a"}, so the signature is stable."""
 101:     seen = set()
 102:     for c in capabilities:
 103:         if not isinstance(c, str):
 104:             raise TypeError(f"capability must be a string, got {type(c)}")
 105:         if not c:
 106:             raise ValueError("capability strings must not be empty")
 107:         if "," in c:
 108:             raise ValueError(
 109:                 f"capability {c!r} contains comma (delimiter); "
 110:                 "use a non-comma name"
 111:             )
 112:         seen.add(c)
 113:     encoded = ",".join(sorted(seen)).encode("utf-8")
 114:     if len(encoded) > MAX_CAPS_LEN:
 115:         raise ValueError(
 116:             f"caps too long: {len(encoded)} > {MAX_CAPS_LEN}"
 117:         )
 118:     return encoded
 119: 
 120: 
 121: def _decode_caps(encoded: bytes) -> set[str]:
 122:     if not encoded:
 123:         return set()
 124:     s = encoded.decode("utf-8")
 125:     return set(part for part in s.split(",") if part)
 126: 
 127: 
 128: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 129: class CapabilityGrant:
 130:     granter_pub: bytes
 131:     subject_pub: bytes
 132:     not_before_ms: int
 133:     not_after_ms: int
 134:     nonce: bytes
 135:     capabilities: frozenset[str]
 136:     scope: bytes
 137:     signature: bytes
 138:     encoded: bytes
 139: 
 140: 
 141: def encode_grant(
 142:     *,
 143:     granter_priv_seed: bytes,
 144:     granter_pub: bytes,
 145:     subject_pub: bytes,
 146:     capabilities: Iterable[str],
 147:     not_before_ms: int,
 148:     not_after_ms: int,
 149:     nonce: bytes | None = None,
 150:     scope: bytes = b"",
 151: ) -> bytes:
 152:     """Mint + sign a capability grant. ``not_before_ms`` and
 153:     ``not_after_ms`` are wall-clock epochs in milliseconds. Caller
 154:     is responsible for picking sensible values; we enforce only
 155:     that ``not_before <= not_after`` and both fit in u64."""
 156:     if len(granter_priv_seed) != 32:
 157:         raise ValueError("granter_priv_seed must be 32 bytes")
 158:     if len(granter_pub) != ED_PUB_LEN:
 159:         raise ValueError(f"granter_pub must be {ED_PUB_LEN} bytes")
 160:     if len(subject_pub) != ED_PUB_LEN:
 161:         raise ValueError(f"subject_pub must be {ED_PUB_LEN} bytes")
 162:     if not (0 <= not_before_ms <= 2**63 - 1):
 163:         raise ValueError("not_before_ms out of range")
 164:     if not (0 <= not_after_ms <= 2**63 - 1):
 165:         raise ValueError("not_after_ms out of range")
 166:     if not_before_ms > not_after_ms:
 167:         raise ValueError(
 168:             f"not_before_ms {not_before_ms} > not_after_ms {not_after_ms}"
 169:         )
 170:     if nonce is None:
 171:         nonce = secrets.token_bytes(NONCE_LEN)
 172:     elif len(nonce) != NONCE_LEN:
 173:         raise ValueError(f"nonce must be {NONCE_LEN} bytes")
 174:     if len(scope) > MAX_SCOPE_LEN:
 175:         raise ValueError(f"scope too long: {len(scope)} > {MAX_SCOPE_LEN}")
 176: 
 177:     caps_bytes = _normalize_caps(capabilities)
 178:     body = (
 179:         GRANT_MAGIC + bytes([GRANT_VERSION])
 180:         + granter_pub + subject_pub
 181:         + struct.pack(">QQ", not_before_ms, not_after_ms)
 182:         + nonce
 183:         + struct.pack(">H", len(caps_bytes)) + caps_bytes
 184:         + struct.pack(">H", len(scope)) + bytes(scope)
 185:     )
 186:     sig = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(granter_priv_seed).sign(body)
 187:     return body + sig
 188: 
 189: 
 190: def parse_grant(blob: bytes) -> CapabilityGrant:
 191:     if len(blob) < HEADER_FIXED_LEN + 2 + 2 + SIG_LEN:
 192:         raise ValueError(
 193:             f"grant too short ({len(blob)} bytes); minimum is "
 194:             f"{HEADER_FIXED_LEN + 2 + 2 + SIG_LEN}"
 195:         )
 196:     if blob[:6] != GRANT_MAGIC:
 197:         raise ValueError("not a One Link capability grant (bad magic)")
 198:     if blob[6] != GRANT_VERSION:
 199:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported grant version {blob[6]}")
 200:     off = 7
 201:     granter_pub = blob[off:off + ED_PUB_LEN]; off += ED_PUB_LEN
 202:     subject_pub = blob[off:off + ED_PUB_LEN]; off += ED_PUB_LEN
 203:     not_before_ms, not_after_ms = struct.unpack(">QQ", blob[off:off + 16])
 204:     off += 16
 205:     nonce = blob[off:off + NONCE_LEN]; off += NONCE_LEN
 206:     if off + 2 > len(blob):
 207:         raise ValueError("grant truncated at caps_len")
 208:     caps_len = struct.unpack(">H", blob[off:off + 2])[0]
 209:     off += 2
 210:     if caps_len > MAX_CAPS_LEN:
 211:         raise ValueError(f"caps_len exceeds cap: {caps_len}")
 212:     if off + caps_len > len(blob):
 213:         raise ValueError("grant truncated at caps body")
 214:     caps_bytes = blob[off:off + caps_len]
 215:     off += caps_len
 216:     if off + 2 > len(blob):
 217:         raise ValueError("grant truncated at scope_len")
 218:     scope_len = struct.unpack(">H", blob[off:off + 2])[0]
 219:     off += 2
 220:     if scope_len > MAX_SCOPE_LEN:
 221:         raise ValueError(f"scope_len exceeds cap: {scope_len}")
 222:     if off + scope_len + SIG_LEN != len(blob):
 223:         raise ValueError(
 224:             f"grant length mismatch: header says caps={caps_len} "
 225:             f"scope={scope_len} but blob is {len(blob)} bytes"
 226:         )
 227:     scope = blob[off:off + scope_len]
 228:     off += scope_len
 229:     signature = blob[off:off + SIG_LEN]
 230:     return CapabilityGrant(
 231:         granter_pub=granter_pub,
 232:         subject_pub=subject_pub,
 233:         not_before_ms=not_before_ms,
 234:         not_after_ms=not_after_ms,
 235:         nonce=nonce,
 236:         capabilities=frozenset(_decode_caps(caps_bytes)),
 237:         scope=scope,
 238:         signature=signature,
 239:         encoded=blob,
 240:     )
 241: 
 242: 
 243: def verify_grant(
 244:     blob: bytes,
 245:     *,
 246:     expected_granter_pub: bytes | None = None,
 247:     expected_subject_pub: bytes | None = None,
 248:     now_ms: int | None = None,
 249:     seen_nonces: set[bytes] | None = None,
 250: ) -> CapabilityGrant:
 251:     """Verify a grant's signature + temporal validity + (optional)
 252:     granter/subject identity binding + (optional) replay defense.
 253: 
 254:     Raises ValueError on any failure; returns the parsed grant on
 255:     success."""
 256:     parsed = parse_grant(blob)
 257:     body = blob[:-SIG_LEN]
 258:     try:
 259:         Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(parsed.granter_pub).verify(
 260:             parsed.signature, body,
 261:         )
 262:     except InvalidSignature:
 263:         raise ValueError("grant signature invalid") from None
 264:     if expected_granter_pub is not None:
 265:         if parsed.granter_pub != expected_granter_pub:
 266:             raise ValueError(
 267:                 f"grant granter_pub doesn't match expected "
 268:                 f"{expected_granter_pub.hex()[:16]}…"
 269:             )
 270:     if expected_subject_pub is not None:
 271:         if parsed.subject_pub != expected_subject_pub:
 272:             raise ValueError(
 273:                 f"grant subject_pub doesn't match presenter "
 274:                 f"{expected_subject_pub.hex()[:16]}…"
 275:             )
 276:     if now_ms is None:
 277:         now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
 278:     if now_ms < parsed.not_before_ms:
 279:         raise ValueError(
 280:             f"grant not yet valid: now_ms {now_ms} < "
 281:             f"not_before {parsed.not_before_ms}"
 282:         )
 283:     # Audit L9 May 2026: tightened to `>=` so a grant expires AT
 284:     # not_after_ms, not one ms past. Matches the ExpiresAt caveat
 285:     # semantics in ol_capability::Caveat::check.
 286:     if now_ms >= parsed.not_after_ms:
 287:         raise ValueError(
 288:             f"grant expired: now_ms {now_ms} >= "
 289:             f"not_after {parsed.not_after_ms}"
 290:         )
 291:     if seen_nonces is not None:
 292:         if parsed.nonce in seen_nonces:
 293:             raise ValueError(
 294:                 f"grant nonce replayed: {parsed.nonce.hex()[:16]}…"
 295:             )
 296:         # Audit M11 May 2026: CapStore upgraded `seen_nonces` from
 297:         # `set` to `OrderedDict` so eviction-on-overflow drops the
 298:         # OLDEST nonce, not a random one. Accept both container
 299:         # shapes — sets via .add(), OrderedDicts via __setitem__.
 300:         adder = getattr(seen_nonces, "add", None)
 301:         if adder is not None:
 302:             adder(parsed.nonce)
 303:         else:
 304:             seen_nonces[parsed.nonce] = None  # type: ignore[index]
 305:     return parsed

   1: """At-rest encryption for AsyncCapsule recordings — closes audit C5.
   2: 
   3: When a call converts to async (Tier δ headline demo), the captured
   4: voice-note is held as an :class:`AsyncCapsule` until the recipient
   5: plays it. Between capture and delivery the capsule typically sits
   6: on disk in the daemon's data directory.
   7: 
   8: Audit C5: chat/group recordings need at-rest encryption so a
   9: stolen device cannot replay captured calls. This module adds that
  10: layer on top of the existing AsyncCapsule serialization.
  11: 
  12: Design:
  13:   - Each capsule is encrypted with a fresh ChaCha20-Poly1305 key
  14:     derived from (a) the daemon's per-device master seed, plus (b)
  15:     the capsule's call_id + finalized_at_ms (so two captures from
  16:     the same call cannot reuse the same nonce).
  17:   - The encrypted file format is:
  18:         magic(8)  || version(1) || nonce(12) || ciphertext_len(8)
  19:         || ciphertext || tag(16)
  20:   - Decryption requires the device's master seed AND knowledge of
  21:     the call_id; a peer-leaked capsule cannot be decrypted on its
  22:     own.
  23:   - Stream the capsule via :func:`seal_to_path` / :func:`open_from_path`
  24:     so the daemon doesn't hold the whole audio blob in memory at once.
  25: 
  26: Pure module: no daemon imports. The daemon's capsule store calls
  27: :func:`seal_to_path` on finalization + :func:`open_from_path` on
  28: playback. Tests provide an in-memory master seed.
  29: 
  30: Companion: docs/LIVING_PRESENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md Part 14.1 (C5)
  31: """
  32: 
  33: from __future__ import annotations
  34: 
  35: import hashlib
  36: import os
  37: import secrets
  38: import struct
  39: from dataclasses import dataclass
  40: from pathlib import Path
  41: from typing import Optional
  42: 
  43: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import ChaCha20Poly1305
  44: 
  45: 
  46: # Wire-format constants
  47: MAGIC = b"OLCAP1\x00\x00"                # 8 bytes
  48: SEAL_VERSION = 1
  49: NONCE_LEN = 12
  50: TAG_LEN = 16
  51: KEY_LEN = 32
  52: 
  53: 
  54: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  55: # Key derivation
  56: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  57: 
  58: def derive_capsule_key(
  59:     *,
  60:     master_seed: bytes,
  61:     call_id: str,
  62:     finalized_at_ms: int,
  63: ) -> bytes:
  64:     """Derive a 32-byte ChaCha20-Poly1305 key from the device master
  65:     seed + per-capsule context.
  66: 
  67:     Uses HKDF-Extract over (call_id, finalized_at_ms) as info. The
  68:     master_seed is the secret root; the info is binding but not
  69:     secret — so a stolen capsule file cannot be re-decrypted with a
  70:     different (master, call_id) pair, AND two capsules from the same
  71:     call at different finalize-times yield different keys.
  72:     """
  73:     if not isinstance(master_seed, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(master_seed) < 32:
  74:         raise ValueError("master_seed must be >= 32 bytes")
  75:     if not isinstance(call_id, str) or not call_id:
  76:         raise ValueError("call_id required")
  77:     info = b"one-link-capsule-at-rest-v1|" + call_id.encode("utf-8") + b"|"
  78:     info += finalized_at_ms.to_bytes(8, "big", signed=False)
  79:     # Simple HKDF-Extract + first-block-Expand (RFC 5869). For 32 bytes
  80:     # of output one Expand block suffices.
  81:     salt = b"\x00" * 32
  82:     prk = _hmac_sha256(salt, bytes(master_seed))
  83:     okm = _hmac_sha256(prk, info + b"\x01")
  84:     return okm[:KEY_LEN]
  85: 
  86: 
  87: def _hmac_sha256(key: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
  88:     import hmac
  89:     return hmac.new(key, data, hashlib.sha256).digest()
  90: 
  91: 
  92: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  93: # Seal / open — file-level
  94: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  95: 
  96: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  97: class SealedHeader:
  98:     """Plaintext header preceding the ciphertext."""
  99: 
 100:     magic: bytes
 101:     version: int
 102:     nonce: bytes
 103:     ciphertext_len: int
 104: 
 105: 
 106: def seal_to_path(
 107:     *,
 108:     plaintext: bytes,
 109:     out_path: Path,
 110:     master_seed: bytes,
 111:     call_id: str,
 112:     finalized_at_ms: int,
 113:     nonce: Optional[bytes] = None,
 114: ) -> None:
 115:     """Encrypt ``plaintext`` and write the sealed blob to ``out_path``.
 116: 
 117:     The output file's directory must exist. The temporary file is
 118:     written first then atomically renamed to ``out_path`` so a crash
 119:     mid-write never leaves a half-sealed file.
 120:     """
 121:     if nonce is None:
 122:         nonce = secrets.token_bytes(NONCE_LEN)
 123:     elif len(nonce) != NONCE_LEN:
 124:         raise ValueError(f"nonce must be {NONCE_LEN} bytes")
 125:     key = derive_capsule_key(
 126:         master_seed=master_seed,
 127:         call_id=call_id,
 128:         finalized_at_ms=finalized_at_ms,
 129:     )
 130:     aead = ChaCha20Poly1305(key)
 131:     # AEAD associated-data: call_id + finalized_at_ms so swapping
 132:     # those after-the-fact invalidates the seal (defense-in-depth).
 133:     aad = call_id.encode("utf-8") + finalized_at_ms.to_bytes(8, "big")
 134:     ciphertext_with_tag = aead.encrypt(nonce, bytes(plaintext), aad)
 135:     # Layout: MAGIC || version || nonce || len(ct+tag) || ct+tag
 136:     header = (
 137:         MAGIC
 138:         + struct.pack("!B", SEAL_VERSION)
 139:         + nonce
 140:         + struct.pack("!Q", len(ciphertext_with_tag))
 141:     )
 142:     tmp = out_path.with_suffix(out_path.suffix + ".tmp")
 143:     out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 144:     with tmp.open("wb") as f:
 145:         f.write(header)
 146:         f.write(ciphertext_with_tag)
 147:     os.replace(tmp, out_path)
 148: 
 149: 
 150: def open_from_path(
 151:     *,
 152:     sealed_path: Path,
 153:     master_seed: bytes,
 154:     call_id: str,
 155:     finalized_at_ms: int,
 156: ) -> bytes:
 157:     """Decrypt the sealed capsule at ``sealed_path``. Raises on:
 158:       - magic mismatch (not a sealed capsule)
 159:       - version unknown
 160:       - AEAD tag verification failure (tampered or wrong key)
 161:     """
 162:     with sealed_path.open("rb") as f:
 163:         header_fixed = f.read(len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN + 8)
 164:         if len(header_fixed) < len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN + 8:
 165:             raise ValueError("sealed capsule truncated header")
 166:         if header_fixed[:len(MAGIC)] != MAGIC:
 167:             raise ValueError("not a sealed capsule (bad magic)")
 168:         version = header_fixed[len(MAGIC)]
 169:         if version != SEAL_VERSION:
 170:             raise ValueError(
 171:                 f"unsupported sealed capsule version {version}",
 172:             )
 173:         nonce = header_fixed[len(MAGIC) + 1: len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN]
 174:         (ciphertext_len,) = struct.unpack(
 175:             "!Q", header_fixed[len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN:],
 176:         )
 177:         ciphertext = f.read(ciphertext_len)
 178:         if len(ciphertext) != ciphertext_len:
 179:             raise ValueError("sealed capsule truncated body")
 180:     key = derive_capsule_key(
 181:         master_seed=master_seed,
 182:         call_id=call_id,
 183:         finalized_at_ms=finalized_at_ms,
 184:     )
 185:     aead = ChaCha20Poly1305(key)
 186:     aad = call_id.encode("utf-8") + finalized_at_ms.to_bytes(8, "big")
 187:     return aead.decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, aad)
 188: 
 189: 
 190: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 191: # Header inspection (no key required)
 192: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 193: 
 194: def inspect_header(sealed_path: Path) -> SealedHeader:
 195:     """Read the unencrypted header without attempting decryption.
 196:     Used by the daemon's capsule UI to display "sealed capsule"
 197:     metadata in the chat list."""
 198:     with sealed_path.open("rb") as f:
 199:         buf = f.read(len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN + 8)
 200:     if len(buf) < len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN + 8:
 201:         raise ValueError("truncated header")
 202:     if buf[:len(MAGIC)] != MAGIC:
 203:         raise ValueError("not a sealed capsule")
 204:     version = buf[len(MAGIC)]
 205:     nonce = buf[len(MAGIC) + 1: len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN]
 206:     (ciphertext_len,) = struct.unpack("!Q", buf[len(MAGIC) + 1 + NONCE_LEN:])
 207:     return SealedHeader(
 208:         magic=MAGIC, version=version,
 209:         nonce=nonce, ciphertext_len=ciphertext_len,
 210:     )

   1: """Capsule store — serialize, seal, persist, recover.
   2: 
   3: Wraps the at-rest encryption layer (:mod:`capsule_at_rest`) around
   4: the AsyncCapsule serializer. The daemon's CallManager finalizes a
   5: capsule on async-conversion; this module persists it to disk in
   6: sealed form. Playback re-opens it with the same key.
   7: 
   8: Wire format inside the seal:
   9:   - Header dict (JSON) with all the capsule scalar fields
  10:   - 4-byte length prefix
  11:   - Audio payload bytes
  12:   - 4-byte length prefix
  13:   - Provenance chain encoded as a JSON array of wire dicts
  14: 
  15: The whole sequence is fed to ``seal_to_path`` so an attacker with
  16: the device can't read header / audio / provenance without the key.
  17: 
  18: Pure module: no daemon imports. The daemon's call_manager bridge
  19: calls ``save_sealed_capsule`` on finalization + ``load_sealed_capsule``
  20: on playback.
  21:

  46: def serialize_capsule(capsule: AsyncCapsule) -> bytes:
  47:     """Pack an AsyncCapsule into its sealed-plaintext form. Inverse of
  48:     :func:`deserialize_capsule`."""
  49:     header = {
  50:         "capsule_id": capsule.capsule_id,
  51:         "call_id": capsule.call_id,
  52:         "kind": int(capsule.kind),
  53:         "sender_master_vk_hex": capsule.sender_master_vk_hex,
  54:         "recipient_master_vk_hex": capsule.recipient_master_vk_hex,
  55:         "started_at_ms": capsule.started_at_ms,
  56:         "finalized_at_ms": capsule.finalized_at_ms,
  57:         "duration_ms": capsule.duration_ms,
  58:         "audio_codec": capsule.audio_codec,
  59:         "sample_rate_hz": capsule.sample_rate_hz,
  60:         "recording_state_at_conversion": int(capsule.recording_state_at_conversion),
  61:         "resumable_until_ms": capsule.resumable_until_ms,
  62:         "payload_hash": capsule.payload_hash,
  63:     }
  64:     header_bytes = json.dumps(header, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
  65:     prov_list = [to_wire_dict(p) for p in capsule.provenance_chain]
  66:     prov_bytes = json.dumps(prov_list, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
  67:     return (
  68:         struct.pack("!I", len(header_bytes))
  69:         + header_bytes
  70:         + struct.pack("!I", len(capsule.audio_payload))
  71:         + capsule.audio_payload
  72:         + struct.pack("!I", len(prov_bytes))
  73:         + prov_bytes

  77: def deserialize_capsule(data: bytes) -> AsyncCapsule:
  78:     """Unpack a sealed-plaintext capsule blob back into the
  79:     dataclass. Raises ValueError on malformed input."""
  80:     pos = 0
  81:     if len(data) < 4:
  82:         raise ValueError("capsule blob truncated at header length")
  83:     (header_len,) = struct.unpack("!I", data[pos:pos + 4])
  84:     pos += 4
  85:     if pos + header_len > len(data):
  86:         raise ValueError("capsule blob truncated at header body")
  87:     header = json.loads(data[pos:pos + header_len].decode("utf-8"))
  88:     pos += header_len
  89: 
  90:     if pos + 4 > len(data):
  91:         raise ValueError("capsule blob truncated at audio length")
  92:     (audio_len,) = struct.unpack("!I", data[pos:pos + 4])
  93:     pos += 4
  94:     if pos + audio_len > len(data):
  95:         raise ValueError("capsule blob truncated at audio body")
  96:     audio = data[pos:pos + audio_len]
  97:     pos += audio_len
  98: 
  99:     if pos + 4 > len(data):
 100:         raise ValueError("capsule blob truncated at provenance length")
 101:     (prov_len,) = struct.unpack("!I", data[pos:pos + 4])
 102:     pos += 4
 103:     if pos + prov_len > len(data):
 104:         raise ValueError("capsule blob truncated at provenance body")
 105:     prov_list = json.loads(data[pos:pos + prov_len].decode("utf-8"))
 106:     pos += prov_len
 107: 
 108:     if pos != len(data):
 109:         raise ValueError(
 110:             f"capsule blob has {len(data) - pos} trailing bytes",
 111:         )
 112: 
 113:     from one_link.frame_provenance import RecordingState
 114:     return AsyncCapsule(
 115:         capsule_id=header["capsule_id"],

 120:         started_at_ms=header["started_at_ms"],
 121:         finalized_at_ms=header["finalized_at_ms"],
 122:         duration_ms=header["duration_ms"],
 123:         audio_payload=audio,
 124:         audio_codec=header["audio_codec"],
 125:         sample_rate_hz=header["sample_rate_hz"],
 126:         provenance_chain=tuple(from_wire_dict(d) for d in prov_list),
 127:         recording_state_at_conversion=RecordingState(
 128:             header["recording_state_at_conversion"]
 129:         ),
 130:         resumable_until_ms=header["resumable_until_ms"],
 131:         payload_hash=header["payload_hash"],
 132:     )

   1: """Capsule transport — deliver an :class:`AsyncCapsule` to the peer.
   2: 
   3: After :class:`CallLifecycle` transitions to RESUMABLE the daemon
   4: needs to actually deliver the capsule's bytes to the receiving
   5: peer. We piggyback on the existing file-transfer pipeline:
   6: 
   7:   1. Sender emits ``CAPSULE_OFFER`` (header-only).
   8:   2. The receiver's daemon, on receiving ``CAPSULE_OFFER``, marks
   9:      the capsule as expected and opens an inbound slot keyed on
  10:      ``capsule_id``.
  11:   3. The sender then transfers the payload bytes via a sequence of
  12:      ``CAPSULE_CHUNK`` messages.
  13:   4. Sender ends with ``CAPSULE_COMPLETE``; receiver verifies the
  14:      concatenated payload's BLAKE3 matches the offer's
  15:      ``payload_hash``, then verifies the chained FrameProvenance
  16:      before surfacing the capsule in the chat UI.
  17: 
  18: This module is the pure transport adapter. The daemon owns the
  19: actual ``await channel.send(...)`` calls — same separation as
  20: every other module in this codebase.
  21: 
  22: Companion: docs/LIVING_PRESENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §6.6 (capsule format)
  23:            docs/LIVING_PRESENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §6.7 (resume flow)
  24: """
  25: 
  26: from __future__ import annotations
  27: 
  28: import logging
  29: import threading
  30: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  31: from typing import Iterator, Optional
  32: 
  33: from one_link.async_capsule import (
  34:     CAPSULE_CHUNK,
  35:     CAPSULE_COMPLETE,
  36:     CAPSULE_OFFER,
  37:     AsyncCapsule,
  38:     capsule_to_offer_msg,
  39: )
  40: from one_link.frame_provenance import (
  41:     FrameProvenance,
  42:     from_wire_dict,
  43:     make_segment_hash,
  44:     to_wire_dict,
  45:     verify_provenance,
  46: )
  47: 
  48: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  49: 
  50: 
  51: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  52: # Outbound: stream a capsule to the peer
  53: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  54: 
  55: # Chunk size for capsule payload transfer. Matched to the existing
  56: # file pipeline's chunk size convention; opus voice payloads are
  57: # small (10s of KB for a 30s clip), so a single chunk often holds
  58: # the whole capsule.
  59: DEFAULT_CAPSULE_CHUNK_SIZE = 16 * 1024
  60: 
  61: 
  62: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  63: class OutboundCapsuleChunk:
  64:     """One wire message for the chunked transfer. The daemon
  65:     iterates the generator and ``channel.send(encode_msg(...))``s
  66:     each in order."""
  67: 
  68:     msg_type: str
  69:     payload: dict
  70: 
  71: 
  72: def stream_capsule_to_messages(
  73:     capsule: AsyncCapsule,
  74:     *,
  75:     sender_short_id: str,
  76:     chunk_size: int = DEFAULT_CAPSULE_CHUNK_SIZE,
  77: ) -> Iterator[dict]:
  78:     """Yield the JSON-envelope dicts the daemon should
  79:     ``encode_msg`` + ``channel.send`` to deliver this capsule.
  80: 
  81:     The provenance chain is carried in the OFFER header (one per
  82:     captured frame), independent of how the audio_payload is
  83:     chunked for transport. This decoupling is correct because
  84:     frame granularity (audio frame, e.g. 50 fps) differs from
  85:     transport granularity (16 KB blocks).
  86:     """
  87:     if chunk_size < 1:
  88:         raise ValueError(f"chunk_size must be ≥1, got {chunk_size}")
  89: 
  90:     # 1) Offer (header + provenance chain)
  91:     offer_msg = capsule_to_offer_msg(capsule, sender_short_id)
  92:     offer_msg["provenance_chain"] = [
  93:         to_wire_dict(p) for p in capsule.provenance_chain
  94:     ]
  95:     yield offer_msg
  96: 
  97:     # 2) Chunks (audio data only — provenance carried in offer)
  98:     payload = capsule.audio_payload
  99:     n_chunks = (len(payload) + chunk_size - 1) // chunk_size or 1
 100:     from one_link.wire import make_msg
 101:     import base64
 102:     for i in range(n_chunks):
 103:         start = i * chunk_size
 104:         end = start + chunk_size
 105:         chunk_bytes = payload[start:end]
 106:         chunk_msg = make_msg(
 107:             CAPSULE_CHUNK,
 108:             sender_short_id,
 109:             capsule_id=capsule.capsule_id,
 110:             seq=i,
 111:             total=n_chunks,
 112:             data_b64=base64.b64encode(chunk_bytes).decode("ascii"),
 113:         )
 114:         yield chunk_msg
 115: 
 116:     # 3) Complete
 117:     complete_msg = make_msg(
 118:         CAPSULE_COMPLETE,
 119:         sender_short_id,
 120:         capsule_id=capsule.capsule_id,
 121:         payload_hash=capsule.payload_hash,
 122:         n_chunks=n_chunks,
 123:     )
 124:     yield complete_msg
 125: 
 126: 
 127: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 128: # Inbound: assemble a streamed capsule on the receiver side
 129: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 130: 
 131: class InboundError(Exception):
 132:     """Sentinel raised when a streamed capsule is rejected.
 133:     The daemon's dispatch catches it and logs + drops silently
 134:     (doctrine §3.2.d: no error codes leak to the user)."""
 135: 
 136: 
 137: @dataclass
 138: class InboundCapsule:
 139:     """In-progress receive state. The daemon holds one of these
 140:     per active inbound transfer."""
 141: 
 142:     capsule_id: str
 143:     sender_master_vk_hex: str
 144:     expected_payload_hash: str
 145:     declared_size: int
 146:     declared_duration_ms: int
 147:     declared_recording_state: int
 148:     declared_resumable_until_ms: int
 149:     declared_kind: int
 150:     declared_codec: str
 151:     declared_sample_rate: int
 152:     # Provenance chain comes in the OFFER and is verified before
 153:     # finalization. Empty tuple means "no chain advertised."
 154:     provenance_chain: tuple[FrameProvenance, ...] = ()
 155: 
 156:     # Chunk accumulation
 157:     _chunks: dict[int, bytes] = field(default_factory=dict)
 158:     _expected_n_chunks: Optional[int] = None
 159:     _completed: bool = False
 160: 
 161:     def add_chunk(
 162:         self,
 163:         *,
 164:         seq: int,
 165:         data: bytes,
 166:         declared_total: Optional[int],
 167:     ) -> None:
 168:         """Buffer one chunk. Re-receiving the same seq overwrites
 169:         (idempotent on retransmit)."""
 170:         if seq < 0:
 171:             raise InboundError("seq must be non-negative")
 172:         if declared_total is not None:
 173:             if self._expected_n_chunks is None:
 174:                 self._expected_n_chunks = int(declared_total)
 175:             elif self._expected_n_chunks != int(declared_total):
 176:                 raise InboundError(
 177:                     f"declared chunk total flipped: was "
 178:                     f"{self._expected_n_chunks}, now {declared_total}"
 179:                 )
 180:         if (
 181:             self._expected_n_chunks is not None
 182:             and seq >= self._expected_n_chunks
 183:         ):
 184:             raise InboundError(
 185:                 f"seq {seq} ≥ declared total {self._expected_n_chunks}"
 186:             )
 187:         self._chunks[seq] = data
 188: 
 189:     def all_chunks_present(self) -> bool:
 190:         if self._expected_n_chunks is None:
 191:             return False
 192:         return len(self._chunks) == self._expected_n_chunks
 193: 
 194:     def assemble_payload(self) -> bytes:
 195:         if not self.all_chunks_present():
 196:             raise InboundError("missing chunks; cannot assemble")
 197:         ordered = sorted(self._chunks.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[0])
 198:         return b"".join(c for _, c in ordered)
 199: 
 200:     def verify_and_finalize(
 201:         self,
 202:         *,
 203:         sender_public_bytes: bytes,
 204:     ) -> AsyncCapsule:
 205:         """Verify the assembled payload + each provenance against
 206:         the sender's pinned key. Returns the final immutable
 207:         :class:`AsyncCapsule`. Raises :class:`InboundError` if
 208:         verification fails for any reason."""
 209:         if self._completed:
 210:             raise InboundError("already finalized")
 211:         if not self.all_chunks_present():
 212:             raise InboundError("not all chunks received")
 213: 
 214:         payload = self.assemble_payload()
 215:         actual_hash = make_segment_hash(payload).hex()
 216:         if actual_hash != self.expected_payload_hash:
 217:             raise InboundError(
 218:                 f"payload hash mismatch: expected "
 219:                 f"{self.expected_payload_hash}, got {actual_hash}"
 220:             )
 221: 
 222:         # Every provenance in the offer-carried chain must verify
 223:         # against the sender's pinned key.
 224:         for p in self.provenance_chain:
 225:             if not verify_provenance(p, sender_public_bytes):
 226:                 raise InboundError("provenance verification failed")
 227: 
 228:         from one_link.async_capsule import CapsuleKind
 229:         capsule = AsyncCapsule(
 230:             capsule_id=self.capsule_id,
 231:             call_id="",                # filled in by daemon if it knows
 232:             kind=CapsuleKind(self.declared_kind),
 233:             sender_master_vk_hex=self.sender_master_vk_hex,
 234:             recipient_master_vk_hex="",
 235:             started_at_ms=0,
 236:             finalized_at_ms=0,
 237:             duration_ms=self.declared_duration_ms,
 238:             audio_payload=payload,
 239:             audio_codec=self.declared_codec,
 240:             sample_rate_hz=self.declared_sample_rate,
 241:             provenance_chain=self.provenance_chain,
 242:             recording_state_at_conversion=self.declared_recording_state,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
 243:             resumable_until_ms=self.declared_resumable_until_ms,
 244:             payload_hash=self.expected_payload_hash,
 245:         )
 246:         self._completed = True
 247:         return capsule
 248: 
 249: 
 250: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 251: # Receiver-side registry
 252: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 253: 
 254: class InboundCapsuleRegistry:
 255:     """Thread-safe map of capsule_id → :class:`InboundCapsule`.
 256: 
 257:     The daemon holds one. On CAPSULE_OFFER it opens an entry; on
 258:     each CAPSULE_CHUNK it routes the chunk into the entry; on
 259:     CAPSULE_COMPLETE it verifies + finalises + closes the entry."""
 260: 
 261:     # Bound the number of concurrent inbound capsules so a peer
 262:     # can't exhaust memory by spamming offers.
 263:     DEFAULT_MAX_INFLIGHT = 64
 264: 
 265:     def __init__(self, *, max_inflight: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INFLIGHT) -> None:
 266:         self._max = int(max_inflight)
 267:         self._by_id: dict[str, InboundCapsule] = {}
 268:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
 269: 
 270:     def open_inbound(
 271:         self,
 272:         *,
 273:         capsule_id: str,
 274:         sender_master_vk_hex: str,
 275:         expected_payload_hash: str,
 276:         declared_size: int,
 277:         declared_duration_ms: int,
 278:         declared_recording_state: int,
 279:         declared_resumable_until_ms: int,
 280:         declared_kind: int,
 281:         declared_codec: str,
 282:         declared_sample_rate: int,
 283:         provenance_chain: tuple[FrameProvenance, ...] = (),
 284:     ) -> InboundCapsule:
 285:         with self._lock:
 286:             if capsule_id in self._by_id:
 287:                 return self._by_id[capsule_id]
 288:             if len(self._by_id) >= self._max:
 289:                 # FIFO eviction — drop the oldest inbound.
 290:                 oldest = next(iter(self._by_id))
 291:                 del self._by_id[oldest]
 292:             entry = InboundCapsule(
 293:                 capsule_id=capsule_id,
 294:                 sender_master_vk_hex=sender_master_vk_hex,
 295:                 expected_payload_hash=expected_payload_hash,
 296:                 declared_size=int(declared_size),
 297:                 declared_duration_ms=int(declared_duration_ms),
 298:                 declared_recording_state=int(declared_recording_state),
 299:                 declared_resumable_until_ms=int(declared_resumable_until_ms),
 300:                 declared_kind=int(declared_kind),
 301:                 declared_codec=str(declared_codec),
 302:                 declared_sample_rate=int(declared_sample_rate),
 303:                 provenance_chain=tuple(provenance_chain),
 304:             )
 305:             self._by_id[capsule_id] = entry
 306:             return entry
 307: 
 308:     def get(self, capsule_id: str) -> Optional[InboundCapsule]:
 309:         with self._lock:
 310:             return self._by_id.get(capsule_id)
 311: 
 312:     def close(self, capsule_id: str) -> None:
 313:         with self._lock:
 314:             self._by_id.pop(capsule_id, None)
 315: 
 316:     def __len__(self) -> int:
 317:         with self._lock:
 318:             return len(self._by_id)
 319:

 321: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 322: # Wire-message parsers (defensive — never raise on malformed input)
 323: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 324: 
 325: def parse_inbound_offer(msg: dict) -> dict:
 326:     """Validate a CAPSULE_OFFER message. Returns the structured
 327:     fields on success; raises :class:`InboundError` on malformed."""
 328:     if msg.get("t") != CAPSULE_OFFER:
 329:         raise InboundError(f"not a {CAPSULE_OFFER}: t={msg.get('t')!r}")
 330:     capsule_id = msg.get("capsule_id")
 331:     if not isinstance(capsule_id, str) or not capsule_id:
 332:         raise InboundError("missing capsule_id")
 333:     payload_hash = msg.get("payload_hash")
 334:     if not isinstance(payload_hash, str) or len(payload_hash) != 64:
 335:         raise InboundError("missing or invalid payload_hash")
 336:     try:
 337:         size = int(msg.get("size", 0))
 338:         duration_ms = int(msg.get("duration_ms", 0))
 339:         recording_state = int(msg.get("recording_state", 0))
 340:         resumable_until_ms = int(msg.get("resumable_until_ms", 0))
 341:         kind = int(msg.get("kind", 0))
 342:         sample_rate = int(msg.get("sample_rate", 48_000))
 343:     except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
 344:         raise InboundError(f"malformed numeric field: {exc}") from exc
 345:     codec = msg.get("codec", "opus")
 346:     if not isinstance(codec, str):
 347:         raise InboundError("codec must be string")
 348:     # Provenance chain — optional but typical. Each entry is the
 349:     # wire form of a FrameProvenance.
 350:     raw_chain = msg.get("provenance_chain")
 351:     chain: list[FrameProvenance] = []
 352:     if raw_chain is not None:
 353:         if not isinstance(raw_chain, list):
 354:             raise InboundError("provenance_chain must be a list")
 355:         for entry in raw_chain:
 356:             if not isinstance(entry, dict):
 357:                 raise InboundError("provenance_chain entry must be dict")
 358:             try:
 359:                 chain.append(from_wire_dict(entry))
 360:             except ValueError as exc:
 361:                 raise InboundError(
 362:                     f"provenance_chain entry malformed: {exc}"
 363:                 ) from exc
 364:     return {
 365:         "capsule_id": capsule_id,
 366:         "payload_hash": payload_hash,
 367:         "size": size,
 368:         "duration_ms": duration_ms,
 369:         "recording_state": recording_state,
 370:         "resumable_until_ms": resumable_until_ms,
 371:         "kind": kind,
 372:         "codec": codec,
 373:         "sample_rate": sample_rate,
 374:         "provenance_chain": tuple(chain),
 375:     }
 376: 
 377: 
 378: def parse_inbound_chunk(msg: dict) -> dict:
 379:     """Validate a CAPSULE_CHUNK message."""
 380:     import base64
 381:     if msg.get("t") != CAPSULE_CHUNK:
 382:         raise InboundError(f"not a {CAPSULE_CHUNK}: t={msg.get('t')!r}")
 383:     capsule_id = msg.get("capsule_id")
 384:     if not isinstance(capsule_id, str):
 385:         raise InboundError("missing capsule_id")
 386:     try:
 387:         seq = int(msg.get("seq", -1))
 388:         total = (
 389:             int(msg.get("total"))
 390:             if msg.get("total") is not None
 391:             else None
 392:         )
 393:     except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
 394:         raise InboundError(f"malformed seq/total: {exc}") from exc
 395:     if seq < 0:
 396:         raise InboundError("seq required")
 397:     data_b64 = msg.get("data_b64")
 398:     if not isinstance(data_b64, str):
 399:         raise InboundError("missing data_b64")
 400:     try:
 401:         data = base64.b64decode(data_b64.encode("ascii"))
 402:     except Exception as exc:
 403:         raise InboundError(f"data_b64 not valid base64: {exc}") from exc
 404:     return {
 405:         "capsule_id": capsule_id,
 406:         "seq": seq,
 407:         "total": total,
 408:         "data": data,
 409:     }
 410: 
 411: 
 412: def parse_inbound_complete(msg: dict) -> dict:
 413:     if msg.get("t") != CAPSULE_COMPLETE:
 414:         raise InboundError(f"not a {CAPSULE_COMPLETE}: t={msg.get('t')!r}")
 415:     capsule_id = msg.get("capsule_id")
 416:     if not isinstance(capsule_id, str):
 417:         raise InboundError("missing capsule_id")
 418:     payload_hash = msg.get("payload_hash")
 419:     if not isinstance(payload_hash, str):
 420:         raise InboundError("missing payload_hash")
 421:     return {
 422:         "capsule_id": capsule_id,
 423:         "payload_hash": payload_hash,
 424:     }

   1: """Content-defined chunking and dedup planning.
   2: 
   3: This is the One Link Python mirror of the OneField CDC-dedup transport
   4: kernel. It does not change the wire protocol by itself; it gives folder sync
   5: and future file transfer a deterministic way to split related files so peers
   6: can exchange "which chunks do you already have?" before sending bytes.
   7: """
   8: 
   9: from __future__ import annotations
  10: 
  11: from dataclasses import dataclass
  12: from pathlib import Path
  13: from typing import Iterable
  14: 
  15: import blake3
  16: 
  17: 
  18: MIN_CHUNK_BYTES = 16 * 1024
  19: AVG_CHUNK_BYTES = 64 * 1024
  20: MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 256 * 1024
  21: _MASK_64 = (1 << 64) - 1
  22: _BOUNDARY_MASK = AVG_CHUNK_BYTES - 1
  23: _GEAR = tuple(
  24:     int.from_bytes(blake3.blake3(bytes([i])).digest(length=8), "little")
  25:     for i in range(256)
  26: )
  27: 
  28: 
  29: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  30: class Chunk:
  31:     """A content-defined byte range and its BLAKE3 digest."""
  32: 
  33:     index: int
  34:     start: int
  35:     end: int
  36:     hash: str
  37: 
  38:     @property
  39:     def size(self) -> int:
  40:         return self.end - self.start
  41: 
  42: 
  43: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  44: class FileIndex:
  45:     """Whole-file BLAKE3 plus its CDC chunks."""
  46: 
  47:     blob_hash: str
  48:     size: int
  49:     chunks: tuple[Chunk, ...]
  50: 
  51: 
  52: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  53: class DedupPlan:
  54:     """Which chunks need to cross the wire for a receiver's known hash set."""
  55: 
  56:     total_chunks: int
  57:     missing_chunks: tuple[Chunk, ...]
  58:     total_bytes: int
  59:     bytes_to_send: int
  60: 
  61:     @property
  62:     def hit_rate(self) -> float:
  63:         if self.total_chunks == 0:
  64:             return 0.0
  65:         return 1.0 - (len(self.missing_chunks) / self.total_chunks)
  66: 
  67:     @property
  68:     def byte_savings(self) -> int:
  69:         return self.total_bytes - self.bytes_to_send
  70: 
  71: 
  72: def _should_cut(chunk_len: int, rolling_hash: int) -> bool:
  73:     if chunk_len < MIN_CHUNK_BYTES:
  74:         return False
  75:     if chunk_len >= MAX_CHUNK_BYTES:
  76:         return True
  77:     return (rolling_hash & _BOUNDARY_MASK) == 0
  78: 
  79: 
  80: def chunk_bytes(data: bytes) -> tuple[Chunk, ...]:
  81:     """Split bytes into deterministic content-defined chunks.
  82: 
  83:     Boundaries depend on content, not offset, so inserting bytes near the
  84:     front of a file only shifts nearby chunks instead of invalidating the
  85:     entire tail.
  86:     """
  87: 
  88:     native = _chunk_bytes_native(data)
  89:     if native is not None:
  90:         return native
  91: 
  92:     chunks: list[Chunk] = []
  93:     start = 0
  94:     rolling = 0
  95:     gear = _GEAR
  96:     mask = _MASK_64
  97: 
  98:     for pos, b in enumerate(data):
  99:         rolling = ((rolling << 1) + gear[b]) & mask
 100: 
 101:         end = pos + 1
 102:         if _should_cut(end - start, rolling):
 103:             chunks.append(_make_chunk(len(chunks), start, end, data))
 104:             start = end
 105:             rolling = 0
 106: 
 107:     if start < len(data) or not chunks:
 108:         chunks.append(_make_chunk(len(chunks), start, len(data), data))
 109:     return tuple(chunks)
 110: 
 111: 
 112: def index_path(path: Path, *, read_size: int = 1024 * 1024) -> FileIndex:
 113:     """Hash and CDC-index a file in one streaming pass.
 114: 
 115:     Memory stays bounded by MAX_CHUNK_BYTES plus the rolling window. This is
 116:     the path used by live transfer, so very large files do not need a full
 117:     in-memory copy just to build the dedup offer.
 118:     """
 119: 
 120:     native = _index_path_native(path, read_size=read_size)
 121:     if native is not None:
 122:         return native
 123: 
 124:     chunks: list[Chunk] = []
 125:     file_hasher = blake3.blake3()
 126:     chunk_buf = bytearray()
 127:     rolling = 0
 128:     gear = _GEAR
 129:     mask = _MASK_64
 130:     offset = 0
 131: 
 132:     with open(path, "rb") as f:
 133:         for part in iter(lambda: f.read(read_size), b""):
 134:             file_hasher.update(part)
 135:             for b in part:
 136:                 rolling = ((rolling << 1) + gear[b]) & mask
 137:                 chunk_buf.append(b)
 138:                 if _should_cut(len(chunk_buf), rolling):
 139:                     end = offset + len(chunk_buf)
 140:                     chunks.append(
 141:                         Chunk(
 142:                             index=len(chunks),
 143:                             start=offset,
 144:                             end=end,
 145:                             hash=blake3.blake3(chunk_buf).hexdigest(),
 146:                         )
 147:                     )
 148:                     offset = end
 149:                     chunk_buf = bytearray()
 150:                     rolling = 0
 151: 
 152:     if chunk_buf or not chunks:
 153:         end = offset + len(chunk_buf)
 154:         chunks.append(
 155:             Chunk(
 156:                 index=len(chunks),
 157:                 start=offset,
 158:                 end=end,
 159:                 hash=blake3.blake3(chunk_buf).hexdigest(),
 160:             )
 161:         )
 162:     return FileIndex(
 163:         blob_hash=file_hasher.hexdigest(),
 164:         size=path.stat().st_size,
 165:         chunks=tuple(chunks),
 166:     )
 167: 
 168: 
 169: def hash_path(path: Path, *, read_size: int = 4 * 1024 * 1024) -> str:
 170:     """Return the whole-file BLAKE3 hash without building a chunk index.
 171: 
 172:     This is the fast lane for peers that only support the baseline stream
 173:     protocol. We still need a content identity for the durable transfer
 174:     ledger, but we should not pay Python CDC's byte-by-byte rolling-hash cost
 175:     when the receiver cannot use CDC chunks.
 176:     """
 177: 
 178:     file_hasher = blake3.blake3()
 179:     with open(path, "rb") as f:
 180:         for part in iter(lambda: f.read(read_size), b""):
 181:             file_hasher.update(part)
 182:     return file_hasher.hexdigest()
 183: 
 184: 
 185: def fixed_index_path(
 186:     path: Path,
 187:     *,
 188:     chunk_size: int = MAX_CHUNK_BYTES,
 189:     read_size: int = 4 * 1024 * 1024,
 190: ) -> FileIndex:
 191:     """Hash a file into fixed-size chunks with bounded memory.
 192: 
 193:     Fixed manifests are not a replacement for CDC when a file has inserted or
 194:     deleted bytes, but they are dramatically cheaper for brand-new large media
 195:     sends and for peers that already share exact aligned blocks. This gives the
 196:     transfer planner a high-throughput lane while CDC remains available for
 197:     true prior-knowledge drift.
 198:     """
 199: 
 200:     if chunk_size <= 0:
 201:         raise ValueError("chunk_size must be positive")
 202:     if read_size <= 0:
 203:         raise ValueError("read_size must be positive")
 204: 
 205:     chunks: list[Chunk] = []
 206:     file_hasher = blake3.blake3()
 207:     chunk_buf = bytearray()
 208:     offset = 0
 209: 
 210:     def flush() -> None:
 211:         nonlocal chunk_buf, offset
 212:         if not chunk_buf and chunks:
 213:             return
 214:         end = offset + len(chunk_buf)
 215:         chunks.append(
 216:             Chunk(
 217:                 index=len(chunks),
 218:                 start=offset,
 219:                 end=end,
 220:                 hash=blake3.blake3(chunk_buf).hexdigest(),
 221:             )
 222:         )
 223:         offset = end
 224:         chunk_buf = bytearray()
 225: 
 226:     with open(path, "rb") as f:
 227:         for part in iter(lambda: f.read(read_size), b""):
 228:             file_hasher.update(part)
 229:             view = memoryview(part)
 230:             pos = 0
 231:             while pos < len(view):
 232:                 take = min(chunk_size - len(chunk_buf), len(view) - pos)
 233:                 chunk_buf.extend(view[pos: pos + take])
 234:                 pos += take
 235:                 if len(chunk_buf) == chunk_size:
 236:                     flush()
 237: 
 238:     if chunk_buf or not chunks:
 239:         flush()
 240:     return FileIndex(
 241:         blob_hash=file_hasher.hexdigest(),
 242:         size=path.stat().st_size,
 243:         chunks=tuple(chunks),
 244:     )
 245: 
 246: 
 247: def chunk_path(path: Path, *, read_size: int = 1024 * 1024) -> tuple[Chunk, ...]:
 248:     """Chunk a file from disk with bounded memory."""
 249: 
 250:     return index_path(path, read_size=read_size).chunks
 251: 
 252: 
 253: def build_dedup_plan(chunks: Iterable[Chunk], receiver_hashes: set[str]) -> DedupPlan:
 254:     materialized = tuple(chunks)
 255:     missing = tuple(c for c in materialized if c.hash not in receiver_hashes)
 256:     return DedupPlan(
 257:         total_chunks=len(materialized),
 258:         missing_chunks=missing,
 259:         total_bytes=sum(c.size for c in materialized),
 260:         bytes_to_send=sum(c.size for c in missing),
 261:     )
 262: 
 263: 
 264: def _make_chunk(index: int, start: int, end: int, data: bytes) -> Chunk:
 265:     return Chunk(
 266:         index=index,
 267:         start=start,
 268:         end=end,
 269:         hash=blake3.blake3(data[start:end]).hexdigest(),
 270:     )
 271: 
 272: 
 273: def _chunk_bytes_native(data: bytes) -> tuple[Chunk, ...] | None:
 274:     try:
 275:         from .native_cdc import get_native_cdc_scanner
 276: 
 277:         scanner = get_native_cdc_scanner()
 278:         if scanner is None:
 279:             return None
 280:         buf = bytearray(data)
 281:         cuts, rolling, chunk_len = scanner.scan(
 282:             buf,
 283:             length=len(buf),
 284:             initial_rolling=0,
 285:             initial_chunk_len=0,
 286:             min_chunk=MIN_CHUNK_BYTES,
 287:             max_chunk=MAX_CHUNK_BYTES,
 288:             boundary_mask=_BOUNDARY_MASK,
 289:         )
 290:         _ = rolling, chunk_len
 291:         chunks: list[Chunk] = []
 292:         start = 0
 293:         for cut in cuts:
 294:             chunks.append(_make_chunk(len(chunks), start, cut, data))
 295:             start = cut
 296:         if start < len(data) or not chunks:
 297:             chunks.append(_make_chunk(len(chunks), start, len(data), data))
 298:         return tuple(chunks)
 299:     except Exception:
 300:         return None
 301: 
 302: 
 303: def _index_path_native(path: Path, *, read_size: int) -> FileIndex | None:
 304:     try:
 305:         from .native_cdc import get_native_cdc_scanner
 306: 
 307:         scanner = get_native_cdc_scanner()
 308:         if scanner is None:
 309:             return None
 310:         if read_size <= 0:
 311:             return None
 312: 
 313:         chunks: list[Chunk] = []
 314:         file_hasher = blake3.blake3()
 315:         chunk_hasher = blake3.blake3()
 316:         buf = bytearray(read_size)
 317:         absolute = 0
 318:         chunk_start = 0
 319:         rolling = 0
 320:         chunk_len = 0
 321: 
 322:         with open(path, "rb") as f:
 323:             while True:
 324:                 n = f.readinto(buf)
 325:                 if not n:
 326:                     break
 327:                 view = memoryview(buf)[:n]
 328:                 file_hasher.update(view)
 329:                 cuts, rolling, chunk_len = scanner.scan(
 330:                     buf,
 331:                     length=n,
 332:                     initial_rolling=rolling,
 333:                     initial_chunk_len=chunk_len,
 334:                     min_chunk=MIN_CHUNK_BYTES,
 335:                     max_chunk=MAX_CHUNK_BYTES,
 336:                     boundary_mask=_BOUNDARY_MASK,
 337:                 )
 338: 
 339:                 segment_start = 0
 340:                 for cut in cuts:
 341:                     if cut < segment_start or cut > n:
 342:                         raise RuntimeError(f"native CDC returned invalid cut {cut}")
 343:                     chunk_hasher.update(view[segment_start:cut])
 344:                     end = absolute + cut
 345:                     chunks.append(
 346:                         Chunk(
 347:                             index=len(chunks),
 348:                             start=chunk_start,
 349:                             end=end,
 350:                             hash=chunk_hasher.hexdigest(),
 351:                         )
 352:                     )
 353:                     chunk_start = end
 354:                     chunk_hasher = blake3.blake3()
 355:                     segment_start = cut
 356:                 if segment_start < n:
 357:                     chunk_hasher.update(view[segment_start:n])
 358:                 absolute += n
 359: 
 360:         if chunk_len or not chunks:
 361:             chunks.append(
 362:                 Chunk(
 363:                     index=len(chunks),
 364:                     start=chunk_start,
 365:                     end=absolute,
 366:                     hash=chunk_hasher.hexdigest(),
 367:                 )
 368:             )
 369:         return FileIndex(
 370:             blob_hash=file_hasher.hexdigest(),
 371:             size=path.stat().st_size,
 372:             chunks=tuple(chunks),
 373:         )
 374:     except Exception:
 375:         return None
<<<CONTENT_END>>>

   1: """Encrypted bidirectional channel between two peers.
   2: 
   3: Handshake (Noise-IK-flavored, simplified):
   4:     1. Initiator -> Responder
   5:        HELLO = init_pub_ed25519 || init_pub_x25519 || nonce_init || sig_init
   6:        sig_init signs: "OL1|HELLO|" + init_pub_ed25519 + init_pub_x25519 + nonce_init
   7:     2. Responder -> Initiator
   8:        REPLY = resp_pub_ed25519 || resp_pub_x25519 || nonce_resp || sig_resp
   9:        sig_resp signs: "OL1|REPLY|" + nonce_init + resp_pub_ed25519 + resp_pub_x25519 + nonce_resp
  10: 
  11: After both sides verify the other's signature, they:
  12:     shared = X25519(my_x25519_priv, peer_x25519_pub)
  13:     salt   = nonce_init || nonce_resp
  14:     transcript = SHA256(HELLO || REPLY)
  15:     keys   = HKDF(shared, salt, info="OL1/keys|" + transcript, L=64)
  16:     tx_key = keys[0:32]   # initiator -> responder
  17:     rx_key = keys[32:64]  # responder -> initiator
  18: 
  19: Each side keeps a 64-bit send counter (starts at 0) used as the ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce
  20: (little-endian, padded to 12 bytes). AAD = "OL1/data|" + transcript.
  21: 
  22: v0.8.2 Double Ratchet activation
  23: ================================
  24: 
  25: The legacy mode above uses a STATIC tx/rx key pair for the lifetime
  26: of the channel. v0.7.2 shipped an audited Signal-style Double Ratchet
  27: primitive (one_link.double_ratchet); v0.8.2 wires it in.
  28: 
  29: Activation flow:
  30:   1. Handshake completes as before. Channel stashes the X25519 ephemeral
  31:      PRIVATE key and the peer's X25519 ephemeral PUBLIC key for ratchet
  32:      bootstrap (these were previously discarded after key derivation).
  33:   2. Both sides exchange CAPS frames (legacy-encrypted). Daemon notes
  34:      `note_caps_sent()` after sending CAPS and `note_caps_received(features)`
  35:      when CAPS arrives.
  36:   3. When BOTH flags are set AND both feature lists contain
  37:      DOUBLE_RATCHET_V1, `maybe_activate_ratchet(role)` initialises the
  38:      ratchet state from the handshake bootstrap — and from that point
  39:      forward every send/recv goes through the ratchet, providing forward
  40:      secrecy + post-compromise security.
  41: 
  42: Atomicity: activation flips BOTH directions at the same logical
  43: boundary. Sending side: switch happens after the local CAPS frame
  44: is written. Receiving side: switch happens after the peer's CAPS
  45: frame is parsed. Each side's recv loop is single-threaded so there
  46: is no in-flight frame between the CAPS frame and the next frame.
  47: 
  48: Wire-format on the ratchet path:
  49:     [length-prefix, unchanged] [42-byte Header.encode()] [ciphertext]
  50: 
  51: AAD = header.encode() || transcript_hash. Splicing a ratchet frame
  52: across channels fails AEAD (different transcript_hash).
  53: 
  54: Backward compatibility: peers that don't advertise DOUBLE_RATCHET_V1
  55: stay on legacy. The activation is symmetric — either both speak
  56: ratchet or both stay legacy.
  57: """

 164:     # ─── Phase C-3 native transfer integration (ADR-0025) ─────────────
 165:     def derive_native_transfer_secret(self) -> bytes:
 166:         """Derive a 32-byte session secret suitable for seeding a
 167:         :class:`one_link.native_transfer.NativeTransferSession`.

 172:         derive via HKDF with a fresh info tag so each domain has
 173:         its own derived material — leaking either the legacy
 174:         channel keys or the DR root doesn't compromise the native
 175:         transfer secret.

 178:         ``transcript_hash`` + the DR bootstrap shared secret), so
 179:         sender + receiver hold matching native sessions without
 180:         any wire-format change."""

 182:             raise RuntimeError(

 184:                 "bootstrap material missing (handshake incomplete)"
 185:             )

 187:             algorithm=hashes.SHA256(),
 188:             length=32,
 189:             salt=self.transcript_hash,
 190:             info=b"OL1/native-transfer/seed|v1",

 205:         if self._native_transfer_session is None:

 212:     def establish_native_transfer(

 214:         *,

 217:     ):

 220: 
 221:         The daemon's ``send_file`` / chunk-store transport call sites
 222:         invoke this once per channel and reuse the returned session
 223:         across all chunks of that channel. The session is matched on
 224:         both peers (same shared secret, deterministic derivation), so
 225:         the receiver's instance decrypts what the sender's produces.
 226:

 228:         BoringSSL); pass ``"native"`` for the ring-backed

 258:         self._caps_sent = True

 260:     def note_caps_received(self, features: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | set[str]) -> None:
 261:         """Daemon calls this immediately after parsing the peer's
 262:         CAPS frame. Records DR + native-transfer capabilities, marks
 263:         recv-side ready."""
 264:         if features is None:
 265:             features = []
 266:         # Normalize to a set once so membership checks are O(1).
 267:         feature_set = set(features)
 268:         self._peer_dr_capable = DR_CAP in feature_set
 269:         self._peer_native_transfer_capable = NATIVE_TRANSFER_CAP in feature_set
 270:         self._caps_received = True
