 9073:     def field_rank_holders(
 9074:         self,
 9075:         holders: list[str],
 9076:         *,
 9077:         requester_short_id: str | None = None,
 9078:     ) -> list[str]:
 9079:         """Phase E #2 — rank candidate chunk-holders by field-distance.
 9080: 
 9081:         Given a list of peer short-ids that could serve a chunk,
 9082:         returns the same list re-ordered so the highest-coherence
 9083:         holder (smallest field-distance to the local peer or the
 9084:         requester) comes first. Single-element / empty input is
 9085:         passed through unchanged.
 9086: 
 9087:         Falls back to the input order when:
 9088:         - No snapshot exists yet
 9089:         - None of the holders is in the current snapshot
 9090:         - ``ONE_LINK_FIELD_PREFETCH_DISABLE=1`` is set
 9091:         - The native crate isn't available
 9092: 
 9093:         Intended consumer: any future multi-holder fetch decision
 9094:         path. The helper is wired and available; the only thing
 9095:         missing is a code path that calls it with a non-trivial
 9096:         holder list. Once swarm fetch lands, the call site is here."""
 9097:         if not holders or len(holders) < 2:
 9098:             return list(holders)
 9099:         if os.environ.get("ONE_LINK_FIELD_PREFETCH_DISABLE", "").lower() in (
 9100:             "1", "true", "yes", "on",
 9101:         ):
 9102:             return list(holders)
 9103:         snap_mgr = getattr(self, "_field_snapshot", None)
 9104:         if snap_mgr is None:
 9105:             return list(holders)
 9106:         try:
 9107:             snap = snap_mgr.snapshot()
 9108:         except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
 9109:             return list(holders)
 9110:         if snap is None:
 9111:             return list(holders)
 9112:         # Score each holder by its field value; sort descending.
 9113:         scored: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
 9114:         for h in holders:
 9115:             try:
 9116:                 s = snap_mgr.field_score_for_peer(h)
 9117:             except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
 9118:                 s = None
 9119:             scored.append((s if s is not None else -1.0, h))
 9120:         # If NONE of the holders is in the snapshot, fall back.
 9121:         if all(score < 0 for score, _ in scored):
 9122:             return list(holders)
 9123:         scored.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))
 9124:         return [h for _, h in scored]
 9125: 
 9126:     async def _field_homology_feeder_loop(self) -> None:
 9127:         """Background loop that runs persistent-homology fragility
 9128:         detection over the chunk-cohold graph every 30s and pushes
 9129:         the resulting events to the FieldSnapshotManager so the field
 9130:         anticipates partitions before they actually open.
 9131: 
 9132:         Data flow:
 9133:             _observe_prefetch -> self._chunk_holders[blob_hex] += short_id
 9134:             self._chunk_holders -> cohold graph (chunks, edges, holders)
 9135:             homology.fragility_score(...) -> ranked fragile chunks
 9136:             top-N fragile chunks -> [(holder_short_ids, weight), ...]
 9137:             FieldSnapshotManager.update_fragility_events(events)
 9138: 
 9139:         Single-daemon view is sparse (only locally-observed FILE_DONE
 9140:         events) but the wiring is end-to-end correct; chunk-holder
 9141:         gossip enriches the graph automatically without code changes.
 9142: 
 9143:         Honors ``ONE_LINK_FIELD_HOMOLOGY_DISABLE=1`` as an operator
 9144:         escape hatch — when set, the loop still runs but skips the
 9145:         actual fragility computation."""
 9146:         try:
 9147:             while True:
 9148:                 await asyncio.sleep(30.0)
 9149:                 mgr = getattr(self, "_field_snapshot", None)
 9150:                 if mgr is None:
 9151:                     continue
 9152:                 if os.environ.get(
 9153:                     "ONE_LINK_FIELD_HOMOLOGY_DISABLE", ""
 9154:                 ).lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"):
 9155:                     continue
 9156:                 try:
 9157:                     self._tick_homology_feeder(mgr)
 9158:                 except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
 9159:                     log.debug("homology feeder tick failed: %s", exc)
 9160:         except asyncio.CancelledError:
 9161:             pass
 9162: 
 9163:     def _tick_homology_feeder(self, mgr) -> None:
 9164:         """Single tick of the homology feeder. Pure helper so the
 9165:         tick body is testable without spinning the asyncio loop."""
 9166:         try:
 9167:             from one_link import homology_native
 9168:         except ImportError:
 9169:             return
 9170:         if not homology_native.HAS_NATIVE:
 9171:             return
 9172:         # Snapshot the registry; release the daemon's reference
 9173:         # before doing graph work.
 9174:         cohold = {
 9175:             blob_hex: list(short_ids)
 9176:             for blob_hex, short_ids in self._chunk_holders.items()
 9177:             if short_ids
 9178:         }
 9179:         if len(cohold) < 2:
 9180:             # Too few chunks to compute meaningful cohomology.
 9181:             # Clear any stale events so the field re-equilibrates.
 9182:             mgr.update_fragility_events([])
 9183:             return
 9184:         nodes = list(cohold.keys())
 9185:         # Edges: chunk_a -- chunk_b when they share at least one holder.
 9186:         # O(N²) in chunk count; capped by self._chunk_holders_cap.
 9187:         node_set = set(nodes)
 9188:         edges: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
 9189:         for i, a in enumerate(nodes):
 9190:             holders_a = set(cohold[a])
 9191:             for b in nodes[i + 1:]:
 9192:                 if a == b:
 9193:                     continue
 9194:                 if holders_a & set(cohold[b]):
 9195:                     edges.append((a, b))
 9196:         # Native fragility_score wants {chunk_id -> holder_count}, not
 9197:         # {chunk_id -> [holder_ids]}. Map down before the call.
 9198:         holder_counts = {cid: len(cohold[cid]) for cid in nodes}
 9199:         try:
 9200:             scores, _replication_priority = homology_native.fragility_score(
 9201:                 nodes, edges, holder_counts,
 9202:             )
 9203:         except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
 9204:             return
 9205:         # Translate top-N most-fragile chunks into per-peer events.
 9206:         # Each event is (peer_short_ids, weight) — the holders of
 9207:         # that chunk get a negative spike in the field source.
 9208:         top_n = 8
 9209:         events: list[tuple[list[str], float]] = []
 9210:         # `scores` items have .chunk_id + .score attributes; defensive
 9211:         # fall-throughs for crate-version differences.
 9212:         score_list: list = []
 9213:         try:
 9214:             for s in scores:
 9215:                 cid = getattr(s, "chunk_id", None)
 9216:                 score_val = float(getattr(s, "score", 0.0))
 9217:                 if cid is None or cid not in node_set:
 9218:                     continue
 9219:                 score_list.append((score_val, cid))
 9220:         except (TypeError, ValueError):  # pragma: no cover
 9221:             return
 9222:         score_list.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
 9223:         for score_val, cid in score_list[:top_n]:
 9224:             if score_val <= 0:
 9225:                 continue
 9226:             holders_of_cid = list(cohold.get(cid, []))
 9227:             if not holders_of_cid:
 9228:                 continue
 9229:             events.append((holders_of_cid, score_val))
 9230:         mgr.update_fragility_events(events)
 9231: 
 9232:     def _pick_best_relay(self, available_relays: list) -> list:
 9233:         """Phase D #1 (ADR-0028) + Phase E (FILE_ENGINE_V2_PLAN.md) —
 9234:         sort relay candidates by τ_c-weighted cost when ol_routing is
 9235:         available + we have empirical RTT/loss metrics for the relay
 9236:         set. Falls back to the input order otherwise. Pure helper:
 9237:         never raises, never drops a relay (just reorders).
 9238: 
 9239:         The cost model uses per-relay τ_c = max(1ms, 1.0 / max(rtt_ms,
 9240:         1.0)) and loss_rate from the relay's recent ACK record. Without
 9241:         empirical metrics, every relay defaults to the same cost so
 9242:         the input order is preserved.
 9243: 
 9244:         Phase E upgrade: when ``ol_coherence_field`` is available the
 9245:         heuristic ``loss_penalty = 1/(1-loss)^2`` is replaced with the
 9246:         BE-RAR interpolation ``nu(y) = 1/(1 - exp(-sqrt(y)))``. α = 1/2
 9247:         is forced by Bose statistics rather than fit, and the same
 9248:         function drives galaxy rotation-curve fitting in the S_One
 9249:         canonical theorem stack — see ``coherence_field_native``."""
 9250:         if len(available_relays) <= 1:
 9251:             return list(available_relays)
 9252:         try:
 9253:             from one_link import routing_native as _rt
 9254: 
 9255:             if not _rt.HAS_NATIVE:
 9256:                 return list(available_relays)
 9257:         except ImportError:
 9258:             return list(available_relays)
 9259:         # Without per-relay RTT/loss telemetry in this daemon (yet),
 9260:         # the routing-aware sort is currently a no-op pass-through.
 9261:         # When peer_rtc / relay_client start recording per-relay
 9262:         # metrics, this picks them up via _relay_metrics_for(url).
 9263:         # Bind through the unbound class form so the helper works on
 9264:         # both real Daemon instances and lightweight stubs that supply
 9265:         # ``_relay_metrics`` directly without rebinding the method.
 9266:         metrics_for = getattr(
 9267:             self, "_relay_metrics_for", None
 9268:         ) or (lambda u: Daemon._relay_metrics_for(self, u))
 9269:         # Phase E upgrade: when ol_coherence_field is available, replace
 9270:         # the heuristic `loss_penalty = 1/(1-loss)^2` with the BE-RAR
 9271:         # interpolation `nu(y) = 1/(1 - exp(-sqrt(y)))` (alpha = 1/2
 9272:         # forced by Bose statistics — not a free knob). y = loss / (1 -
 9273:         # loss) is the loss-deficit ratio, the network analog of the
 9274:         # gravitational potential the BE-RAR was originally derived for.
 9275:         # When the crate isn't installed, fall back to the Phase D
 9276:         # routing-native cost.
 9277:         use_be_rar = False
 9278:         try:
 9279:             from one_link import coherence_field_native as _cf
 9280: 
 9281:             use_be_rar = _cf.HAS_NATIVE
 9282:         except ImportError:
 9283:             _cf = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
 9284:         scored: list[tuple[float, object]] = []
 9285:         for relay in available_relays:
 9286:             url = getattr(relay, "_rendezvous_url", str(relay))
 9287:             metrics = metrics_for(url)
 9288:             if metrics is None:
 9289:                 # No empirical metrics → arbitrary stable cost.
 9290:                 scored.append((1.0, relay))
 9291:                 continue
 9292:             rtt_ms = max(1.0, float(metrics.get("rtt_ms", 100.0)))
 9293:             loss = min(0.99, max(0.0, float(metrics.get("loss_rate", 0.0))))
 9294:             tau_c_s = max(1.0e-3, 1.0 / rtt_ms)
 9295:             if use_be_rar:
 9296:                 # BE-RAR-weighted edge cost: edge_weight × nu(y_quality).
 9297:                 #
 9298:                 # Cosmological BE-RAR shape: nu(y) is monotonically
 9299:                 # DECREASING from ∞ at y=0 to 1 at y=∞. In the galaxy
 9300:                 # mapping, y = a_bar²/a_0² (gravitational pull relative
 9301:                 # to anchor): outer regions (low y) have huge nu boost
 9302:                 # (deep MOND), inner regions (high y) have nu = 1
 9303:                 # (Newtonian).
 9304:                 #
 9305:                 # Network analog: define y = (1 - loss)/loss as the
 9306:                 # "quality ratio." At loss = 0 (perfect) → y = ∞ →
 9307:                 # nu = 1 (baseline cost, no penalty). At loss → 1 →
 9308:                 # y → 0 → nu → ∞ (huge penalty multiplier). This is
 9309:                 # the physically-correct mapping; the earlier wiring
 9310:                 # (y = loss/(1 - loss)) was inverted.
 9311:                 #
 9312:                 # alpha = 1/2 is forced by Bose statistics — not a
 9313:                 # free knob — and the same nu(y) drives galaxy
 9314:                 # rotation-curve fitting in the S_One canonical stack.
 9315:                 edge_w = _rt.edge_weight(tau_c_s, 100.0)
 9316:                 # Loss clamped to (1e-6, 1−1e-6) so y is finite and
 9317:                 # be_rar() gets a positive input.
 9318:                 clamped_loss = min(max(loss, 1e-6), 1.0 - 1e-6)
 9319:                 y_quality = (1.0 - clamped_loss) / clamped_loss
 9320:                 penalty = _cf.be_rar(y_quality)
 9321:                 cost = edge_w * penalty
 9322:             else:
 9323:                 cost = _rt.edge_cost(tau_c_s, 100.0, loss)
 9324:             scored.append((cost, relay))
 9325:         scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
 9326:         return [r for _, r in scored]
 9327: 
 9328:     def _relay_metrics_for(self, url: str) -> dict | None:
 9329:         """Per-relay empirical metrics (``rtt_ms``, ``loss_rate``).
 9330:         Returns ``None`` for relays we haven't observed yet so
 9331:         :meth:`_pick_best_relay` falls back to input order; otherwise
 9332:         returns the EWMA-smoothed dict recorded by
 9333:         :meth:`record_relay_observation`. Tolerates a missing
 9334:         ``_relay_metrics`` field (returns ``None``) so the helper is
 9335:         safe to call on stubs / partially-initialized daemons."""
 9336:         store = getattr(self, "_relay_metrics", None)
 9337:         if store is None:
 9338:             return None
 9339:         return store.get(url)
 9340: 
 9341:     def record_relay_observation(
 9342:         self, url: str, *, rtt_ms: float | None, success: bool
 9343:     ) -> None:
 9344:         """Record one relay dial outcome. EWMA-smooths rtt_ms with
 9345:         alpha=0.2; loss_rate is the fraction of failed attempts in a
 9346:         moving window via the same EWMA. Call from every
 9347:         :func:`open_relay_outbound` success/failure site so
 9348:         :meth:`_pick_best_relay` has fresh data to sort on.
 9349: 
 9350:         Idempotent + thread-safe: dict-level updates are atomic in
 9351:         CPython under the GIL; the EWMA math is read-modify-write of a
 9352:         single key. The metrics surface tolerates a benign race that
 9353:         loses one update — never crashes."""
 9354:         alpha = 0.2
 9355:         now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
 9356:         cur = self._relay_metrics.get(url) or {
 9357:             "rtt_ms": 100.0,
 9358:             "loss_rate": 0.0,
 9359:             "n_attempts": 0,
 9360:             "n_successes": 0,
 9361:             "last_observed_ms": now_ms,
 9362:         }
 9363:         cur["n_attempts"] = int(cur.get("n_attempts", 0)) + 1
 9364:         if success:
 9365:             cur["n_successes"] = int(cur.get("n_successes", 0)) + 1
 9366:             if rtt_ms is not None and rtt_ms > 0:
 9367:                 prev = float(cur.get("rtt_ms", rtt_ms))
 9368:                 cur["rtt_ms"] = (1.0 - alpha) * prev + alpha * float(rtt_ms)
 9369:         # Loss-rate EWMA: 0 for success, 1 for failure.
 9370:         prev_loss = float(cur.get("loss_rate", 0.0))
 9371:         obs_loss = 0.0 if success else 1.0
 9372:         cur["loss_rate"] = (1.0 - alpha) * prev_loss + alpha * obs_loss
 9373:         cur["last_observed_ms"] = now_ms
 9374:         self._relay_metrics[url] = cur
 9375: 
 9376:     def _abort_incoming_file(self, blob: str, f: IncomingFile) -> None:
 9377:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9378:             f.handle.close()
 9379:         self._incoming_files.pop(blob, None)
 9380:         with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
 9381:             f.out_path.unlink()
 9382:         self._update_transfer(f.transfer_id, status="failed")

 9384:     def _ack_batch_size_from_chunk(self, msg: dict) -> int:
 9385:         try:
 9386:             requested = int(msg.get("ack_batch") or 1)
 9387:         except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
 9388:             requested = 1
 9389:         return max(1, min(FILE_ACK_BATCH_MAX, requested))
 9390: 
 9391:     async def _flush_file_ack_batch(self, channel, f: IncomingFile) -> None:
 9392:         if not f.ack_batch_ids:
 9393:             return
 9394:         ids = [str(v) for v in f.ack_batch_ids if v]
 9395:         f.ack_batch_ids.clear()
 9396:         if not ids:
 9397:             return
 9398:         await channel.send(encode_msg(make_msg(
 9399:             "FILE_ACK_BATCH",
 9400:             self.me.short_id,
 9401:             blob=f.blob_hex,
 9402:             ofs=ids,
 9403:             count=len(ids),
 9404:         )))
 9405: 
 9406:     async def _ack_file_chunk(
 9407:         self,
 9408:         channel,
 9409:         msg: dict,
 9410:         f: IncomingFile,
 9411:         *,
 9412:         force_individual: bool = False,
 9413:     ) -> None:
 9414:         msg_id = str(msg.get("id") or "")
 9415:         if not msg_id:
 9416:             return
 9417:         batch_size = self._ack_batch_size_from_chunk(msg)
 9418:         if force_individual or batch_size <= 1:
 9419:             await self._flush_file_ack_batch(channel, f)
 9420:             await channel.send(encode_msg(make_msg(
 9421:                 "ACK",
 9422:                 self.me.short_id,
 9423:                 of=msg_id,
 9424:             )))
 9425:             return
 9426:         f.ack_batch_ids.append(msg_id)
 9427:         if len(f.ack_batch_ids) >= batch_size:
 9428:             await self._flush_file_ack_batch(channel, f)
 9429: 
 9430:     def _inbound_is_rejected(self, peer_fp: str) -> bool:
 9431:         """Returns True if the peer is on our local rejection list.
 9432: 
 9433:         The legacy name `_check_inbound_trust` was preserved as a thin alias
 9434:         for back-compat with any external callers; new code should use this
 9435:         explicitly-named version.
 9436:         """
 9437:         if self.state is None:
 9438:             return False
 9439:         rec = self.state.get_peer(peer_fp)
 9440:         return bool(rec and rec.trust == "rejected")
 9441: 
 9442:     # Back-compat alias. New call sites should use _inbound_is_rejected.
 9443:     _check_inbound_trust = _inbound_is_rejected
 9444: 
 9445:     def _verify_channel_peer(self, peer: Peer, channel: ch.Channel) -> str:
 9446:         actual_fp = fingerprint_of(channel.peer_ed_pub)
 9447:         if peer.ed_pub_hex:
 9448:             try:
 9449:                 expected_pub = bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex)
 9450:             except ValueError as e:
 9451:                 raise RuntimeError(f"peer {peer.short_id} advertised invalid pubkey") from e
 9452:             expected_fp = fingerprint_of(expected_pub)
 9453:             if channel.peer_ed_pub != expected_pub:
 9454:                 raise RuntimeError(
 9455:                     "peer identity mismatch: expected full fingerprint "
 9456:                     f"{expected_fp}, got {actual_fp}"
 9457:                 )
 9458:             return actual_fp
 9459:         if channel.peer_short_id != peer.short_id:
 9460:             raise RuntimeError(
 9461:                 f"peer fingerprint mismatch: expected short id {peer.short_id}, "
 9462:                 f"got {channel.peer_short_id}"
 9463:             )
 9464:         return actual_fp

 9466:     def _check_outbound_trust(self, peer: Peer) -> str | None:
 9467:         """Returns None if outbound is allowed; otherwise an error string."""
 9468:         if self.state is None:
 9469:             return None
 9470:         fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(peer)
 9471:         if not fp:
 9472:             return None
 9473:         rec = self.state.get_peer(fp)
 9474:         if rec and rec.trust == "rejected":
 9475:             return f"peer {peer.short_id} is marked as rejected; cannot send"
 9476:         return None

 9478:     def _capability_allowed(
 9479:         self,
 9480:         peer_fp: str,
 9481:         cap: str,
 9482:         scope: bytes = b"",
 9483:     ) -> bool:
 9484:         """Audit H12 May 2026 — `scope` parameter threads the
 9485:         per-resource constraint through to ``CapStore.has_capability``.
 9486: 
 9487:         Default ``scope=b""`` preserves legacy global-cap behavior
 9488:         for call sites that haven't yet adopted resource-bound caps.
 9489:         Folder-related callers (MANIFEST_*, BLOB_*, anything tied to
 9490:         a specific folder) pass the folder name so a grant minted
 9491:         for one folder can't authorize access to another. The
 9492:         strict exact-match rule lives in
 9493:         ``cap_store.has_capability``: a scoped grant is INVISIBLE
 9494:         to unscoped callers, and a global grant is INVISIBLE to
 9495:         scoped queries.
 9496:         """
 9497:         # Audit L12 May 2026 — refuse to honor capabilities when the
 9498:         # on-disk master seed has been replaced since boot. A brief-
 9499:         # FS-access attacker swapping the seed could otherwise have
 9500:         # the daemon ride a stale in-memory identity while issuing
 9501:         # new grants under a different pubkey. Logs once per process
 9502:         # to avoid log spam; subsequent calls fall through to the
 9503:         # standard deny.
 9504:         try:
 9505:             if self.detect_seed_file_tamper():
 9506:                 if not getattr(self, "_seed_tamper_logged", False):
 9507:                     log.warning(
 9508:                         "SECURITY ALERT — master seed file fingerprint "
 9509:                         "differs from boot; refusing all capability "
 9510:                         "operations. Restart the daemon to re-anchor "
 9511:                         "identity OR investigate the FS-tamper origin."
 9512:                     )
 9513:                     self._seed_tamper_logged = True
 9514:                 return False
 9515:         except Exception:
 9516:             pass
 9517:         # Bundle 56: a peer with a valid signed capability grant
 9518:         # (Bundle 44) for this exact (cap) is allowed regardless of
 9519:         # the binary pinned-policy state. Useful for one-shot
 9520:         # delegation flows (e.g. a colleague granted "files:read"
 9521:         # for the next hour) without forcing them through the full
 9522:         # SAS pair flow. The grant's signature attests authority;
 9523:         # CapStore enforces auto-expiry + replay.
 9524:         if getattr(self, "_cap_store", None) is not None and self.state is not None:
 9525:             try:
 9526:                 # Audit M12 May 2026: drop any grants whose
 9527:                 # not_after_ms has passed before consulting the
 9528:                 # store. Without this, expired grants for OTHER
 9529:                 # (granter, subject) pairs accumulate indefinitely
 9530:                 # — a memory-pressure DoS vector when combined with
 9531:                 # H15's caveat-size cap. has_capability's inline
 9532:                 # sweep ONLY fires for the queried key; the
 9533:                 # explicit prune here is whole-store.
 9534:                 self._cap_store.prune_expired()
 9535:                 peer_pub = self._peer_pub_for_fp(peer_fp)
 9536:                 # Audit L13 May 2026 — delegation-chain enforcement.
 9537:                 # Walks the cap_store from THIS daemon's identity as
 9538:                 # the chain root toward ``peer_pub``, hopping through
 9539:                 # paired peers who themselves hold the cap. Bounded
 9540:                 # to depth 2 so a chain can be at most:
 9541:                 #   self → delegator → peer
 9542:                 # which is the realistic delegation pattern (a paired
 9543:                 # colleague handing limited access to a co-worker)
 9544:                 # without opening unbounded transitive trust.
 9545:                 if peer_pub is not None and self._cap_authorized_via_chain(
 9546:                     root_granter_pub=self.me.public_bytes,
 9547:                     subject_pub=peer_pub,
 9548:                     capability=cap,
 9549:                     scope=scope,
 9550:                     max_depth=2,
 9551:                 ):
 9552:                     return True
 9553:             except Exception:
 9554:                 pass
 9555:         if self.state is None:
 9556:             return True
 9557:         policy = self.state.get_peer_capability_policy(peer_fp)
 9558:         return policy is None or cap in policy
 9559: 
 9560:     def _cap_authorized_via_chain(
 9561:         self,
 9562:         *,
 9563:         root_granter_pub: bytes,
 9564:         subject_pub: bytes,
 9565:         capability: str,
 9566:         scope: bytes = b"",
 9567:         max_depth: int = 2,
 9568:     ) -> bool:
 9569:         """Audit L13 May 2026 — walk delegation chains in the local
 9570:         cap_store from ``root_granter_pub`` toward ``subject_pub``.
 9571: 
 9572:         A grant authorizes ``subject_pub`` for ``capability`` under
 9573:         ``scope`` iff there exists a chain
 9574:         ``root → x_1 → x_2 → … → subject_pub`` of length ≤ ``max_depth``
 9575:         such that every link is a stored, non-expired grant matching
 9576:         the requested (cap, scope).
 9577: 
 9578:         Why this matters
 9579:         ----------------
 9580:         Before this method, ``_capability_allowed`` queried the store
 9581:         with the daemon's own pubkey as granter — so any sub-grant a
 9582:         paired peer issued was invisible, even though the peer holds
 9583:         legitimate authority. Real delegation flows (a colleague
 9584:         granted "files:read" delegates to a co-worker for an
 9585:         afternoon) require the daemon to honor sub-grants whose
 9586:         granter is itself authorized by us.
 9587: 
 9588:         Security
 9589:         --------
 9590:         - ``max_depth`` caps transitive trust. Default 2 keeps the
 9591:           realistic pattern (self → delegator → end-subject) and
 9592:           forbids deep chains that amplify a single compromise.
 9593:         - The ``visited`` set prevents cycles (no key may appear
 9594:           twice on the path).
 9595:         - Strict scope semantics inherited from
 9596:           :py:meth:`CapStore.has_capability` (audit H12): a grant
 9597:           minted for one scope is invisible to queries on another.
 9598:         - The walker only sees grants the daemon explicitly stored
 9599:           via the CAPABILITY_GRANT wire path (which is authenticated
 9600:           + replay-bounded), so an adversary can't seed arbitrary
 9601:           delegation edges.
 9602:         """
 9603:         if self._cap_store is None:
 9604:             return False
 9605: 
 9606:         def walk(
 9607:             target: bytes,
 9608:             edges_left: int,
 9609:             visited_intermediates: frozenset[bytes],
 9610:         ) -> bool:
 9611:             """Is there a chain from ``root_granter_pub`` to ``target``
 9612:             of ≤ ``edges_left`` edges? Each call consumes 1 edge for
 9613:             the inbound (intermediate → target) link; recursion
 9614:             handles the remaining root → intermediate prefix.
 9615: 
 9616:             ``visited_intermediates`` tracks the chain of hops we've
 9617:             already used to detect cycles. The root and final
 9618:             target are NOT in the visited set (they're the chain
 9619:             endpoints).
 9620:             """
 9621:             if edges_left < 1:
 9622:                 return False
 9623:             # Direct edge: root → target (single-edge chain).
 9624:             if self._cap_store.has_capability(
 9625:                 granter_pub=root_granter_pub,
 9626:                 subject_pub=target,
 9627:                 capability=capability,
 9628:                 scope=scope if scope else None,
 9629:             ):
 9630:                 return True
 9631:             # Need ≥ 2 edges to slot an intermediate in.
 9632:             if edges_left < 2:
 9633:                 return False
 9634:             try:
 9635:                 inbound = self._cap_store.list_grants_for(
 9636:                     subject_pub=target,
 9637:                 )
 9638:             except Exception:
 9639:                 return False
 9640:             for sub in inbound:
 9641:                 if capability not in sub.capabilities:
 9642:                     continue
 9643:                 # Exact-scope match (audit H12).
 9644:                 sub_scope = sub.scope or b""
 9645:                 if sub_scope != (scope or b""):
 9646:                     continue
 9647:                 intermediate = sub.granter_pub
 9648:                 # Skip the root (would have matched direct check
 9649:                 # above) and any peer already on this path (cycle).
 9650:                 if intermediate == root_granter_pub:
 9651:                     continue
 9652:                 if intermediate == target:
 9653:                     continue
 9654:                 if intermediate in visited_intermediates:
 9655:                     continue
 9656:                 # Recurse with one fewer edge available, looking for
 9657:                 # a root → … → intermediate prefix.
 9658:                 if walk(
 9659:                     intermediate,
 9660:                     edges_left - 1,
 9661:                     visited_intermediates | {intermediate},
 9662:                 ):
 9663:                     return True
 9664:             return False
 9665: 
 9666:         return walk(subject_pub, max_depth, frozenset())
 9667: 
 9668:     async def issue_capability_grant(
 9669:         self,
 9670:         peer_fp: str,
 9671:         *,
 9672:         capabilities: list[str],
 9673:         scope: bytes = b"",
 9674:         duration_ms: int = 60 * 60 * 1000,
 9675:     ) -> bytes:
 9676:         """Bundle 58: mint a signed capability grant authorizing the
 9677:         named peer to take ``capabilities`` against this daemon's
 9678:         resources, store the grant in our local cap_store (which
 9679:         ``_capability_allowed`` consults), and ship a notification
 9680:         to the peer over the established channel.
 9681: 
 9682:         Returns the grant blob. The peer's ACK (success / failure)
 9683:         is logged; failure to ship doesn't roll back our local
 9684:         store, since the grant is locally authoritative."""
 9685:         import time as _time
 9686: 
 9687:         from one_link import caps_grants as _caps_grants
 9688: 
 9689:         peer_pub = self._peer_pub_for_fp(peer_fp)
 9690:         if peer_pub is None:
 9691:             raise RuntimeError(
 9692:                 f"no pubkey on file for peer {peer_fp[:16]}; cannot grant"
 9693:             )
 9694:         now = int(_time.time() * 1000)
 9695:         priv_seed = self.me.private.private_bytes_raw()
 9696:         grant_blob = _caps_grants.encode_grant(
 9697:             granter_priv_seed=priv_seed,
 9698:             granter_pub=self.me.public_bytes,
 9699:             subject_pub=peer_pub,
 9700:             capabilities=capabilities,
 9701:             not_before_ms=now,
 9702:             not_after_ms=now + duration_ms,
 9703:             scope=scope,
 9704:         )
 9705:         # Phase C-3 daemon migration (ADR-0021): dual-issue a
 9706:         # macaroon-style capability alongside the legacy Ed25519 grant.
 9707:         # The legacy blob remains authoritative on the wire so old
 9708:         # peers stay compatible; the macaroon is stashed in the cap
 9709:         # store for clients that advertise the new path. When all
 9710:         # paired peers advertise macaroon support, the legacy issue
 9711:         # collapses to the macaroon-only branch in a follow-up
 9712:         # release.
 9713:         try:
 9714:             from one_link import cap_migration as _cap_migration
 9715: 
 9716:             # Audit M14 May 2026: the macaroon path consumes the
 9717:             # daemon's separate cap_root_key (minted at first boot
 9718:             # via cap_root_key.load_or_create_cap_root_key) so the
 9719:             # macaroon HMAC root never shares entropy with the
 9720:             # identity Ed25519 seed. Falls back to seed-derivation
 9721:             # only if cap_root_key load fails (legacy daemons
 9722:             # mid-migration).
 9723:             cap_root = getattr(self, "_cap_root_key", None)
 9724:             if cap_root is not None:
 9725:                 # New path: mint via cap_root_key.
 9726:                 macaroon = _cap_migration.mint_share_capability_from_root(
 9727:                     cap_root_key=cap_root,
 9728:                     granter_pub=self.me.public_bytes,
 9729:                     subject_pub=peer_pub,
 9730:                     capabilities=capabilities,
 9731:                     not_after_ms=now + duration_ms,
 9732:                     scope=scope if isinstance(scope, (bytes, bytearray))
 9733:                           else bytes(scope or b""),
 9734:                 )
 9735:             else:
 9736:                 # Legacy fallback (audit M14 mid-migration only).
 9737:                 macaroon = _cap_migration.mint_share_capability(
 9738:                     granter_priv_seed=priv_seed,
 9739:                     granter_pub=self.me.public_bytes,
 9740:                     subject_pub=peer_pub,
 9741:                     capabilities=capabilities,
 9742:                     not_after_ms=now + duration_ms,
 9743:                     scope=scope if isinstance(scope, (bytes, bytearray))
 9744:                           else bytes(scope or b""),
 9745:                 )
 9746:             self._last_minted_macaroon = macaroon.encode()
 9747:         except Exception as exc:  # native module missing or transient failure
 9748:             self._last_minted_macaroon = None
 9749:             log.debug("macaroon dual-issue skipped: %s", exc)
 9750:         # Local-authoritative: store in OUR cap_store first, so
 9751:         # _capability_allowed picks it up immediately even if the
 9752:         # wire ship fails.
 9753:         self._cap_store.accept(
 9754:             grant_blob,
 9755:             expected_subject_pub=peer_pub,
 9756:             expected_granter_pub=self.me.public_bytes,
 9757:         )
 9758:         # Ship to the peer for their UI / audit. Module-level base64
 9759:         # is already in scope; do NOT shadow it with a local import.
 9760:         peer = self._peer_from_fp(peer_fp)
 9761:         if peer is not None:
 9762:             grant_b64 = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(grant_blob).rstrip(
 9763:                 b"=",
 9764:             ).decode("ascii")
 9765:             # Phase C-3 (ADR-0027): if a macaroon was dual-issued
 9766:             # alongside this Ed25519 grant, advertise it on the
 9767:             # CAPABILITY_GRANT wire frame as `macaroon_b64`. Receivers
 9768:             # that understand the new format can verify the macaroon
 9769:             # path; legacy receivers ignore unknown keys. The wire
 9770:             # is forward-compatible: this field is purely additive.
 9771:             grant_fields = {"grant_b64": grant_b64}
 9772:             if self._last_minted_macaroon is not None:
 9773:                 try:
 9774:                     grant_fields["macaroon_b64"] = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(
 9775:                         self._last_minted_macaroon
 9776:                     ).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii")
 9777:                 except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
 9778:                     log.debug("macaroon advertisement skipped: %s", exc)
 9779:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9780:                 await self.send_to(peer, [make_msg(
 9781:                     "CAPABILITY_GRANT",
 9782:                     self.me.short_id,
 9783:                     **grant_fields,
 9784:                 )])
 9785:         return grant_blob
 9786: 
 9787:     def _peer_from_fp(self, peer_fp: str) -> Optional[Peer]:
 9788:         """Resolve a peer_fp to a discovery.Peer if present in
 9789:         the registry, else None."""
 9790:         if self.discovery is None or self.discovery.registry is None:
 9791:             return None
 9792:         for p in self.discovery.registry.list():
 9793:             if fingerprint_of(bytes.fromhex(p.ed_pub_hex)) == peer_fp:
 9794:                 return p
 9795:         return None
 9796: 
 9797:     def _peer_pub_for_fp(self, peer_fp: str) -> Optional[bytes]:
 9798:         """Resolve a hex fingerprint back to the 32-byte raw pubkey
 9799:         from the peer registry, when known. Used by Bundle 56's
 9800:         grant lookup; returns None if we don't have a pub on file
 9801:         (in which case grant-based authority is unavailable for
 9802:         this peer)."""
 9803:         if self.state is None:
 9804:             return None
 9805:         rec = self.state.get_peer(peer_fp)
 9806:         if rec is None or not rec.pubkey:
 9807:             return None
 9808:         return rec.pubkey
 9809: 
 9810:     def _apply_default_capability_policy(self, peer_fp: str) -> None:
 9811:         """v0.20.7 (security audit C3): at SAS-pair finalize, the per-peer
 9812:         policy default is driven by the `pair_default_allow_all` setting.
 9813: 
 9814:         One Link's user-facing default is trust-after-SAS: an unset
 9815:         pair_default_allow_all setting is treated as allow-all so a
 9816:         verified person/device can chat, send files, sync folders, and
 9817:         call without hidden prompts. Users who want strict per-capability
 9818:         grants can turn the setting off before pairing.
 9819: 
 9820:           - True or unset: leave policy = None.
 9821:             policy=None means legacy allow-all — every advertised
 9822:             capability flows. Aligns with the user mental model
 9823:             "I just SAS-verified this device, of course I trust it."
 9824:           - False: install [CHAT] only (the v0.7.2 audit-finding-A
 9825:             deny-by-default for files/folders/groups).
 9826: 
 9827:         Either way, the user can still flip individual caps in the
 9828:         per-device drawer — this only sets the initial state."""
 9829:         if self.state is None:
 9830:             return
 9831:         existing = self.state.get_peer_capability_policy(peer_fp)
 9832:         if existing is not None:
 9833:             return
 9834:         try:
 9835:             v = self.state.get_setting("pair_default_allow_all")
 9836:             # Match /api/settings: unset means allow-all. Only an
 9837:             # explicit false/off/no/0 switches pairing into strict mode.
 9838:             allow_all = (
 9839:                 v is None
 9840:                 or (isinstance(v, str) and v.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes"))
 9841:             )
 9842:         except Exception:
 9843:             allow_all = True
 9844:         if allow_all:
 9845:             return  # leave policy = None (legacy allow-all semantics)
 9846:         from one_link.capabilities import DEFAULT_ALLOW_AFTER_PAIRING
 9847:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9848:             self.state.set_peer_capability_policy(
 9849:                 peer_fp,
 9850:                 list(DEFAULT_ALLOW_AFTER_PAIRING),
 9851:                 actor="pairing",
 9852:                 note="deny-by-default on first pair",
 9853:             )
 9854: 
 9855:     def _emit_capability_request(
 9856:         self, peer_fp: str, peer_sid: str, cap: str,
 9857:     ) -> None:
 9858:         """v0.7.1: notify UI that a peer is asking for a capability
 9859:         the user hasn't granted. Rate-limited per (fp, cap) so a
 9860:         peer hammering offer-retries can't spam the UI. The user
 9861:         responds via POST /api/peers/{fp}/capabilities/grant."""
 9862:         if self.ui_server is None:
 9863:             return
 9864:         now = time.monotonic()
 9865:         key = (peer_fp, cap)
 9866:         last = self._capability_request_seen.get(key, 0.0)
 9867:         if now - last < CAPABILITY_REQUEST_DEDUP_S:
 9868:             return
 9869:         self._capability_request_seen[key] = now
 9870:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9871:             self.ui_server.broadcast({
 9872:                 "type": "capability_request",
 9873:                 "fingerprint": peer_fp,
 9874:                 "short_id": peer_sid,
 9875:                 "capability": cap,
 9876:                 "ts_ms": int(time.time() * 1000),
 9877:             })
 9878: 
 9879:     def _session_stats(self) -> dict:
 9880:         now = time.time()
 9881:         return {
 9882:             "open": len(self._outbound_sessions),
 9883:             "idle_timeout_s": OUTBOUND_SESSION_IDLE_S,
 9884:             "sessions": [
 9885:                 {
 9886:                     "peer": s.peer.short_id,
 9887:                     "peer_fp": s.peer_fp,
 9888:                     "idle_s": round(now - s.last_used, 3),
 9889:                     "messages_sent": s.messages_sent,
 9890:                 }
 9891:                 for s in self._outbound_sessions.values()
 9892:             ],
 9893:         }
 9894: 
 9895:     async def _drop_outbound_session(self, peer_fp: str) -> None:
 9896:         sess = self._outbound_sessions.pop(peer_fp, None)
 9897:         if sess is None:
 9898:             return
 9899:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9900:             await sess.channel.close()
 9901:         # Audit fix: if this was a relay-tunneled session, the inbound
 9902:         # pump task owns an aiohttp ClientSession that must flush+close
 9903:         # before the event loop tears down. Channel.close() triggers
 9904:         # the WS close cascade via _RelayStreamWriter._on_close, which
 9905:         # ends the pump's `async for msg in ws`. We give it a bounded
 9906:         # window to drain its finally block; if it doesn't, cancel.
 9907:         pump = sess.relay_pump_task
 9908:         if pump is not None and not pump.done():
 9909:             with contextlib.suppress(BaseException):
 9910:                 await asyncio.wait_for(pump, timeout=2.0)
 9911:             if not pump.done():
 9912:                 pump.cancel()
 9913:                 with contextlib.suppress(BaseException):
 9914:                     await asyncio.wait_for(pump, timeout=0.5)
 9915: 
 9916:     async def _probe_outbound_session(self, sess: OutboundSession) -> bool:
 9917:         """H4: send a PING and wait briefly for a PONG. Returns True if the
 9918:         session is still alive, False if it timed out or errored. Ignores
 9919:         any non-PONG frames that arrive in the meantime (e.g. CAPS), as the
 9920:         server may push them eagerly.
 9921: 
 9922:         v0.7.0: also stamps the round-trip latency into pair health so the
 9923:         UI can show "32ms" or whatever instead of guessing from regime."""
 9924:         try:
 9925:             async with sess.lock:
 9926:                 ping_at = time.monotonic()
 9927:                 # Route PING through the PeerTransport facade — the
 9928:                 # first message-type to migrate from raw channel.send.
 9929:                 # Pure facade path for WebRTC peers (no behavior change);
 9930:                 # routes through QuicTransport for peers on the QUIC
 9931:                 # track once that cap negotiates true. See
 9932:                 # PHASE_A2_QUIC_CUTOVER_PLAN.md.
 9933:                 ping_bytes = encode_msg(make_msg("PING", self.me.short_id))
 9934:                 await self._send_via_transport(
 9935:                     sess.peer_fp, sess.channel, ping_bytes
 9936:                 )
 9937:                 deadline = ping_at + OUTBOUND_SESSION_PING_DEADLINE_S
 9938:                 while True:
 9939:                     remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
 9940:                     if remaining <= 0:
 9941:                         return False
 9942:                     plaintext = await asyncio.wait_for(
 9943:                         sess.channel.recv(), timeout=remaining
 9944:                     )
 9945:                     reply = decode_msg(plaintext)
 9946:                     rt = reply.get("t")
 9947:                     if rt == "PONG":
 9948:                         sess.last_used = time.time()
 9949:                         latency_ms = (time.monotonic() - ping_at) * 1000.0
 9950:                         self._stamp_pair_health(
 9951:                             sess.peer_fp, latency_ms=latency_ms,
 9952:                         )
 9953:                         return True
 9954:                     if rt == "CAPS":
 9955:                         features = list(normalize_caps(reply.get("features", [])))
 9956:                         sess.channel.peer_caps = {
 9957:                             "protocol": reply.get("protocol", "?"),
 9958:                             "features": features,
 9959:                             "from": reply.get("from"),
 9960:                             "app_version": reply.get("app_version"),
 9961:                         }
 9962:                         # v0.8.2: ratchet activation on probe-time CAPS.
 9963:                         # In practice the session was already CAPS-
 9964:                         # exchanged at construction — this is a
 9965:                         # defence in depth for any session that
 9966:                         # somehow missed it.
 9967:                         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9968:                             sess.channel.note_caps_received(features)
 9969:                             sess.channel.maybe_activate_ratchet()
 9970:                         if self.state is not None:
 9971:                             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 9972:                                 self.state.set_peer_capabilities(sess.peer_fp, features)
 9973:                         continue
 9974:                     # Anything else mid-probe is unexpected for an idle
 9975:                     # session — treat as dead to be safe.
 9976:                     return False
 9977:         except (asyncio.TimeoutError, ConnectionError, OSError):
 9978:             return False
 9979:         except Exception:
 9980:             return False
 9981: 
 9982:     async def _get_outbound_session(
 9983:         self,
 9984:         peer: Peer,
 9985:         *,
 9986:         resume_pending: bool = True,
 9987:     ) -> OutboundSession:
 9988:         peer_fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(peer)
 9989:         if not peer_fp:
 9990:             raise RuntimeError("peer has no verifiable public key for persistent session")
 9991:         # v0.20.7+ (Bundle 55): serialize the check-or-create critical
 9992:         # section so N concurrent send_to() calls to the same peer
 9993:         # collapse onto a single fresh session. Without this, each
 9994:         # caller dials its own TCP connection while the others are
 9995:         # mid-handshake; the last to store wins and the rest race to
 9996:         # be torn down by the peer's per-fp cap.
 9997:         create_lock = self._outbound_session_create_locks.get(peer_fp)
 9998:         if create_lock is None:
 9999:             create_lock = asyncio.Lock()
10000:             self._outbound_session_create_locks[peer_fp] = create_lock
10001:         async with create_lock:
10002:             existing = self._outbound_sessions.get(peer_fp)
10003:             now = time.time()
10004:             if existing and now - existing.last_used <= OUTBOUND_SESSION_IDLE_S:
10005:                 idle = now - existing.last_used
10006:                 if idle <= OUTBOUND_SESSION_PING_AFTER_S:
10007:                     return existing
10008:                 if await self._probe_outbound_session(existing):
10009:                     return existing
10010:                 log.info(
10011:                     "outbound session probe failed for %s — reopening",
10012:                     peer.short_id,
10013:                 )
10014:             await self._drop_outbound_session(peer_fp)
10015:             return await self._create_outbound_session_locked(
10016:                 peer, peer_fp, resume_pending=resume_pending,
10017:             )
10018: 
10019:     async def _create_outbound_session_locked(
10020:         self,
10021:         peer: Peer,
10022:         peer_fp: str,
10023:         *,
10024:         resume_pending: bool = True,
10025:     ) -> OutboundSession:
10026:         """Caller holds ``self._outbound_session_create_locks[peer_fp]``.
10027:         Performs the dial + handshake + dict-store under the lock so a
10028:         racing caller arriving on the same peer_fp finds the session
10029:         already in the dict by the time it gets to the check."""
10030:         now = time.time()
10031: 
10032:         reader, writer, regime = await self._dial_peer_with_regime(peer)
10033:         # Audit fix: when the regime is "relay", _dial_peer_with_regime
10034:         # stashes the inbound-pump task on the writer for cleanup.
10035:         relay_pump = getattr(writer, "_relay_pump_task", None)
10036:         try:
10037:             try:
10038:                 # v0.20.7 (M1): bind expected responder pubkey into the
10039:                 # HELLO sig so an attacker re-routing our HELLO can't
10040:                 # silently land us at a different paired peer.
10041:                 channel = await asyncio.wait_for(
10042:                     ch.initiate(
10043:                         reader, writer, self.me,
10044:                         expected_responder_ed_pub=bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex),
10045:                     ),
10046:                     timeout=HANDSHAKE_DEADLINE_OUTBOUND_S,
10047:                 )
10048:             except asyncio.TimeoutError as e:
10049:                 raise RuntimeError(
10050:                     f"session open to {peer.short_id}: handshake timed out "
10051:                     f"after {HANDSHAKE_DEADLINE_OUTBOUND_S}s — peer not responsive"
10052:                 ) from e
10053:             actual_fp = self._verify_channel_peer(peer, channel)
10054:             if actual_fp != peer_fp:
10055:                 raise RuntimeError("peer fingerprint changed while opening session")
10056:             if self.state is not None:
10057:                 with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10058:                     self.state.upsert_peer(
10059:                         fingerprint=peer_fp,
10060:                         short_id=channel.peer_short_id,
10061:                         pubkey=channel.peer_ed_pub,
10062:                         hostname=peer.hostname,
10063:                         address=peer.address,
10064:                         port=peer.port,
10065:                     )
10066:                 winning_endpoint = getattr(writer, "_one_link_winning_endpoint", None)
10067:                 if winning_endpoint:
10068:                     host, port = winning_endpoint
10069:                     with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10070:                         self.state.observe_route_candidate(
10071:                             peer_fp=peer_fp,
10072:                             route=regime,
10073:                             transport="tcp",
10074:                             host=str(host),
10075:                             port=int(port),
10076:                             ok=True,
10077:                             source="session_open",
10078:                             verified=True,
10079:                             metadata={"short_id": peer.short_id},
10080:                         )
10081:             await channel.send(encode_msg(self._build_my_caps_for_channel(channel)))
10082:             # v0.8.2: half-step toward ratchet activation. The
10083:             # peer's CAPS will arrive on the first recv inside the
10084:             # session-using path (send_to / send_file / probe). At
10085:             # that point note_caps_received fires and the channel
10086:             # flips to ratchet mode for both directions.
10087:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10088:                 channel.note_caps_sent()
10089:                 channel.maybe_activate_ratchet()
10090:             sess = OutboundSession(
10091:                 peer_fp=peer_fp,
10092:                 peer=peer,
10093:                 channel=channel,
10094:                 lock=asyncio.Lock(),
10095:                 last_used=now,
10096:                 regime=regime,
10097:                 relay_pump_task=relay_pump,
10098:             )
10099:             self._outbound_sessions[peer_fp] = sess
10100:             # v0.7.1: a fresh session means the peer just came back
10101:             # online (or we just dialed them for the first time
10102:             # this session). Schedule any pending outbox messages
10103:             # for delivery in the background — the caller doesn't
10104:             # block on the flush.
10105:             self._schedule_outbox_flush(peer_fp)
10106:             # v0.7.4: same trigger for paused outbound transfers.
10107:             # The resume task acquires its own per-peer lock so two
10108:             # session-up events can't fire duplicate sends. Fresh
10109:             # send_file() calls disable this while their just-created
10110:             # "planning" row is still moving into offered/active; otherwise
10111:             # the resume worker can race and recursively resend the same row.
10112:             if resume_pending:
10113:                 self._schedule_resume_paused(peer_fp, force=True)
10114:             return sess
10115:         except Exception:
10116:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10117:                 writer.close()
10118:                 await writer.wait_closed()
10119:             raise
10120: 
10121:     async def send_to(self, peer: Peer, msgs: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
10122:         """Send chat/control messages over a reusable encrypted session."""
10123:         block = self._check_outbound_trust(peer)
10124:         if block:
10125:             raise RuntimeError(block)
10126:         peer_fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(peer)
10127:         if peer_fp and not self._capability_allowed(peer_fp, CHAT):
10128:             raise RuntimeError(f"chat capability disabled for peer {peer.short_id}")
10129:         sess = await self._get_outbound_session(peer)
10130:         try:
10131:             async with sess.lock:
10132:                 results: list[dict] = []
10133:                 for m in msgs:
10134:                     send_started = time.monotonic()
10135:                     # Phase A2: route through the PeerTransport facade
10136:                     # — the second message-type migration after PING.
10137:                     # send_to handles text + control messages, the
10138:                     # next-highest-traffic path after PING. WebRTC
10139:                     # behavior unchanged; QUIC peers (when capability
10140:                     # negotiation flips true) route through QuicTransport
10141:                     # via _send_via_transport.
10142:                     await self._send_via_transport(
10143:                         sess.peer_fp, sess.channel, encode_msg(m)
10144:                     )
10145:                     while True:
10146:                         ack = decode_msg(await sess.channel.recv())
10147:                         ack_type = str(ack.get("t") or "")
10148:                         if ack_type == "CAPS":
10149:                             features = list(normalize_caps(ack.get("features", [])))
10150:                             sess.channel.peer_caps = {
10151:                                 "protocol": ack.get("protocol", "?"),
10152:                                 "features": features,
10153:                                 "from": ack.get("from"),
10154:                                 "app_version": ack.get("app_version"),
10155:                             }
10156:                             # v0.8.2: half-step toward ratchet
10157:                             # activation. If we already sent CAPS
10158:                             # right after handshake, this completes
10159:                             # the negotiation and flips the channel.
10160:                             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10161:                                 sess.channel.note_caps_received(features)
10162:                                 if sess.channel.maybe_activate_ratchet():
10163:                                     log.info(
10164:                                         "ratchet activated on outbound "
10165:                                         "session for %s",
10166:                                         sess.peer_fp[:8],
10167:                                     )
10168:                             if self.state is not None:
10169:                                 with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10170:                                     self.state.set_peer_capabilities(sess.peer_fp, features)
10171:                             continue
10172:                         if ack_type != "ACK":
10173:                             try:
10174:                                 await self._on_peer_message(sess.channel, ack)
10175:                             except Exception as exc:
10176:                                 log.debug(
10177:                                     "out-of-band peer frame %s failed while "
10178:                                     "waiting for ACK from %s: %s",
10179:                                     ack_type, sess.peer_fp[:8], exc,
10180:                                 )
10181:                             continue
10182:                         break
10183:                     if ack.get("rejected"):
10184:                         raise RuntimeError(str(ack.get("rejected")))
10185:                     results.append(ack)
10186:                     sess.messages_sent += 1
10187:                     sess.last_used = time.time()
10188:                     self._stamp_pair_health(
10189:                         sess.peer_fp,
10190:                         latency_ms=(time.monotonic() - send_started) * 1000.0,
10191:                         best_route=sess.regime,
10192:                     )
10193:                     # v0.6.2: group-protocol frames (GROUP_*) are not chat
10194:                     # messages — they're transport-layer envelopes carrying
10195:                     # encrypted multi-recipient payloads. Skip the regular
10196:                     # message-log persist + UI broadcast so they don't
10197:                     # clutter the 1-on-1 chat history. The receiver-side
10198:                     # _handle_group_msg persists the decrypted plaintext
10199:                     # into the dedicated group_messages table.
10200:                     if not m.get("t", "").startswith("GROUP_"):
10201:                         ev = self._persist(
10202:                             msg=m, direction="out", peer_fp=sess.peer_fp,
10203:                             peer_short_id=peer.short_id,
10204:                         )
10205:                         self._broadcast_tail(ev)
10206:                 self._schedule_resume_paused(sess.peer_fp, force=True)
10207:                 return results
10208:         except Exception:
10209:             await self._drop_outbound_session(sess.peer_fp)
10210:             raise
10211: 
10212:     async def _send_control(self, peer: Peer, msg: dict) -> Optional[bytes]:
10213:         """Open a one-shot connection, send a single control msg, wait for
10214:         ACK, close cleanly. Waiting for the ACK forces the receiver to fully
10215:         process the message before our close — avoids Win10053 abort races.
10216: 
10217:         v0.20.7 (security audit H11): returns the channel's
10218:         transcript_hash so callers (notably the pair flow) can bind
10219:         per-session derivations to it. Returns None on dial / handshake
10220:         failure so existing callers that ignore the return value
10221:         continue to work unchanged.
10222:         """
10223:         reader, writer = await self._dial_peer(peer)
10224:         try:
10225:             # v0.20.7 (M1): bind expected responder pubkey to defeat UKS.
10226:             channel = await ch.initiate(
10227:                 reader, writer, self.me,
10228:                 expected_responder_ed_pub=bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex),
10229:             )
10230:             self._verify_channel_peer(peer, channel)
10231:             transcript = getattr(channel, "transcript_hash", None)
10232:             try:
10233:                 await channel.send(encode_msg(self._build_my_caps_for_channel(channel)))
10234:                 # v0.8.2: half-step. This is _send_control — a
10235:                 # short-lived dial that sends one msg + waits for
10236:                 # ACK. If the peer's CAPS arrives + we've already
10237:                 # sent ours, the recv loop below picks up the
10238:                 # peer's CAPS and the channel flips automatically.
10239:                 with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10240:                     channel.note_caps_sent()
10241:                     channel.maybe_activate_ratchet()
10242:             except Exception:
10243:                 pass
10244:             await channel.send(encode_msg(msg))
10245:             # Wait for ACK (skipping any peer-CAPS that arrives interleaved)
10246:             try:
10247:                 while True:
10248:                     ack = decode_msg(await asyncio.wait_for(channel.recv(), timeout=5.0))
10249:                     ack_type = str(ack.get("t") or "")
10250:                     if ack_type == "CAPS":
10251:                         features = list(normalize_caps(ack.get("features", [])))
10252:                         channel.peer_caps = {
10253:                             "protocol": ack.get("protocol", "?"),
10254:                             "features": features,
10255:                             "from": ack.get("from"),
10256:                             "app_version": ack.get("app_version"),
10257:                         }
10258:                         if self.state is not None:
10259:                             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10260:                                 fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(peer)
10261:                                 if fp:
10262:                                     self.state.set_peer_capabilities(fp, features)
10263:                         continue
10264:                     if ack_type == "ACK":
10265:                         break
10266:                     try:
10267:                         await self._on_peer_message(channel, ack)
10268:                     except Exception as exc:
10269:                         log.debug(
10270:                             "out-of-band peer frame %s failed while waiting "
10271:                             "for control ACK from %s: %s",
10272:                             ack_type, peer.short_id, exc,
10273:                         )
10274:                     continue
10275:             except (asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.IncompleteReadError):
10276:                 # Peer didn't ACK in time; the message was still transmitted
10277:                 # but the peer may have closed early. Acceptable for control.
10278:                 pass
10279:             await channel.close()
10280:             return transcript
10281:         except Exception:
10282:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10283:                 writer.close()
10284:                 await writer.wait_closed()
10285:             raise
10286: 
10287:     async def initiate_pair(self, peer: Peer) -> str:
10288:         """Start pairing with peer. Returns the SAS to display in our UI.
10289: 
10290:         v0.20.7 (security audit H11): the SAS is computed AFTER the
10291:         encrypted channel opens, so it can be bound to the channel's
10292:         transcript_hash. Without that binding, an attacker grinding
10293:         Ed25519 keypairs can pre-compute a colliding SAS offline.
10294:         With the transcript bound in, the attacker has to grind during
10295:         the live pair window against a fresh per-session value.
10296:         """
10297:         peer_fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(peer) or fingerprint_of(
10298:             bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex)
10299:         )
10300:         # Make sure the peer DB has a row so trust changes can attach later
10301:         # AND so we can read the previously-rejected flag below.
10302:         if self.state is not None:
10303:             self.state.upsert_peer(
10304:                 fingerprint=peer_fp,
10305:                 short_id=peer.short_id,
10306:                 pubkey=bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex),
10307:                 hostname=peer.hostname,
10308:                 address=peer.address,
10309:                 port=peer.port,
10310:             )
10311:         # v0.20.7 (security audit M20): surface previously-rejected
10312:         # state so the UI can show a "this peer was previously
10313:         # blocked" warning before the user clicks Match.
10314:         previously_rejected = False
10315:         if self.state is not None:
10316:             try:
10317:                 rec = self.state.get_peer(peer_fp)
10318:                 previously_rejected = bool(rec and rec.trust == "rejected")
10319:             except Exception:
10320:                 previously_rejected = False
10321:         # Send PAIR_REQUEST first so we have the channel's
10322:         # transcript_hash; SAS is bound to it.
10323:         transcript = await self._send_control(
10324:             peer, make_msg("PAIR_REQUEST", self.me.short_id),
10325:         )
10326:         sas = compute_sas(
10327:             self.me.public_bytes,
10328:             bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex),
10329:             transcript_hash=transcript,
10330:         )
10331:         existing = self.pairing.get(peer_fp)
10332:         if (
10333:             existing is None
10334:             or existing.state in (
10335:                 PairState.NONE, PairState.PAIRED, PairState.REJECTED,
10336:             )
10337:             or existing.is_expired()
10338:         ):
10339:             self.pairing.begin(
10340:                 peer_fp=peer_fp, sas=sas, incoming=False,
10341:                 previously_rejected=previously_rejected,
10342:             )
10343:         return sas
10344: 
10345:     async def confirm_pair(self, peer: Peer) -> dict:
10346:         """User confirms the SAS matched. Send PAIR_CONFIRM; if peer also
10347:         confirmed already, both sides become paired now."""
10348:         peer_fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(peer) or fingerprint_of(
10349:             bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex)
10350:         )
10351:         # Be defensive: ensure peer exists in state DB so set_peer_trust works.
10352:         if self.state is not None:
10353:             try:
10354:                 self.state.upsert_peer(
10355:                     fingerprint=peer_fp,
10356:                     short_id=peer.short_id,
10357:                     pubkey=bytes.fromhex(peer.ed_pub_hex),
10358:                     hostname=peer.hostname,
10359:                     address=peer.address,
10360:                     port=peer.port,
10361:                 )
10362:             except Exception:
10363:                 pass
10364: 
10365:         ctx = self.pairing.we_confirm(peer_fp)
10366:         if ctx is None or ctx.is_expired():
10367:             # v0.20.7 (security audit H12): no live ctx (or stale).
10368:             # Old behavior re-derived a v1 SAS from pubkeys-only and
10369:             # quietly continued; with v2 SAS that fallback would
10370:             # display a different code than what the peer sees and
10371:             # the user would (correctly) see a mismatch on the next
10372:             # exchange. Cleaner to refuse here and force a fresh
10373:             # ceremony from initiate_pair where the SAS gets bound
10374:             # to a real transcript.
10375:             log.warning(
10376:                 "confirm_pair refused: no live pair context for %s",
10377:                 peer.short_id,
10378:             )
10379:             return {
10380:                 "ok": False,
10381:                 "reason": "no_live_pair_context",
10382:                 "user_message": (
10383:                     "Pair session expired. Click Pair again to restart."
10384:                 ),
10385:             }
10386: 
10387:         await self._send_control(
10388:             peer, make_msg("PAIR_CONFIRM", self.me.short_id),
10389:         )
10390:         # Re-check after the await — they_confirmed might have flipped
10391:         # while _send_control was running and yielding to the event loop.
10392:         ctx = self.pairing.get(peer_fp) or ctx
10393:         if ctx and ctx.both_confirmed and self.state is not None:
10394:             self.state.set_peer_trust(peer_fp, "pinned", actor="pairing")
10395:             self._apply_default_capability_policy(peer_fp)
10396:             if self.ui_server is not None:
10397:                 self.ui_server.broadcast({
10398:                     "type": "peer_trust", "fingerprint": peer_fp, "trust": "pinned",
10399:                 })
10400:             log.info("paired with %s via confirm_pair", peer.short_id)
10401:         else:
10402:             log.info(
10403:                 "confirm_pair: still waiting for peer (we=%s they=%s)",
10404:                 ctx.we_confirmed if ctx else "?",
10405:                 ctx.they_confirmed if ctx else "?",
10406:             )
10407:         return {
10408:             "state": ctx.state.value if ctx else "unknown",
10409:             "both_confirmed": bool(ctx and ctx.both_confirmed),
10410:         }
10411: 
10412:     # ─── groups (v0.6.2) ───────────────────────────────────────────
10413: 
10414:     # ─── v0.7.0: Linked Mesh ──────────────────────────────────────
10415: 
10416:     MAX_ENDPOINTS_PER_ANNOUNCEMENT = 8
10417:     ENDPOINT_VERIFY_CONNECT_DEADLINE_S = 1.25
10418:     ENDPOINT_VERIFY_HANDSHAKE_DEADLINE_S = 2.0

10420:     def _stamp_pair_health(
10421:         self,
10422:         peer_fp: str,
10423:         *,
10424:         latency_ms: float | None = None,
10425:         bandwidth_bps: float | None = None,
10426:         reliability: float | None = None,
10427:         best_route: str | None = None,
10428:     ) -> None:
10429:         """v0.7.0: record liveness for this peer. Latency is EWMA'd
10430:         when provided (alpha=0.3 — fast enough to track real changes,
10431:         slow enough to ignore single-packet jitter)."""
10432:         if not peer_fp:
10433:             return
10434:         now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
10435:         h = self._pair_health.get(peer_fp)
10436:         if h is None:
10437:             h = {"last_alive_ms": now_ms, "latency_ewma_ms": float("nan")}
10438:             self._pair_health[peer_fp] = h
10439:         else:
10440:             h["last_alive_ms"] = now_ms
10441:         if latency_ms is not None:
10442:             prev = h.get("latency_ewma_ms")
10443:             if prev is None or prev != prev:  # NaN check
10444:                 h["latency_ewma_ms"] = float(latency_ms)
10445:             else:
10446:                 h["latency_ewma_ms"] = 0.7 * prev + 0.3 * float(latency_ms)
10447:         if bandwidth_bps is not None and bandwidth_bps > 0:
10448:             prev_bw = h.get("bandwidth_bps")
10449:             if prev_bw is None or prev_bw <= 0:
10450:                 h["bandwidth_bps"] = float(bandwidth_bps)
10451:             else:
10452:                 h["bandwidth_bps"] = 0.7 * prev_bw + 0.3 * float(bandwidth_bps)
10453:         if reliability is not None:
10454:             h["reliability"] = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(reliability)))
10455:         if best_route:
10456:             h["best_route"] = str(best_route)
10457: 
10458:     def _route_memory_for(self, peer_fp: str) -> RouteMemory:
10459:         mem = self._route_memory.get(peer_fp)
10460:         if mem is None:
10461:             mem = RouteMemory()
10462:             self._route_memory[peer_fp] = mem
10463:         return mem
10464: 
10465:     def _persist_route_memory(self, peer_fp: str, mem: RouteMemory) -> None:
10466:         if self.state is None or not peer_fp:
10467:             return
10468:         for c in mem.candidates():
10469:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
10470:                 self.state.upsert_route_memory(
10471:                     peer_fp=peer_fp,
10472:                     route=c.route,
10473:                     attempts=c.attempts,
10474:                     successes=c.successes,
10475:                     failures=c.failures,
10476:                     score=c.score,
10477:                     latency_ms=c.latency_ms,
10478:                     bandwidth_bps=c.bandwidth_bps,
10479:                     metadata={"source": "transfer_runtime"},
10480:                 )
10481: 
10482:     def _load_persisted_route_memory(self) -> None:
10483:         if self.state is None:
10484:             return
10485:         try:
10486:             rows = self.state.list_route_memory()
10487:         except Exception as e:
10488:             log.debug("route memory load skipped: %s", e)
10489:             return
10490:         rebuilt: dict[str, RouteMemory] = {}
10491:         now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
10492:         for row in rows:
10493:             peer_fp = str(row.get("peer_fp") or "")
10494:             route = str(row.get("route") or "")
10495:             if not peer_fp or not route:
10496:                 continue
10497:             mem = rebuilt.setdefault(peer_fp, RouteMemory())
10498:             successes = max(0, int(row.get("successes") or 0))
10499:             failures = max(0, int(row.get("failures") or 0))
10500:             latency_ms = row.get("latency_ms")
10501:             bandwidth_bps = row.get("bandwidth_bps")
10502:             for _ in range(successes):
10503:                 mem.observe(RouteObservation(
10504:                     route=route,
10505:                     ok=True,
10506:                     latency_ms=latency_ms,
10507:                     bandwidth_bps=bandwidth_bps,
10508:                     at_ms=now_ms,
10509:                 ))
10510:             for _ in range(failures):
10511:                 mem.observe(RouteObservation(
10512:                     route=route,
10513:                     ok=False,
10514:                     error_code="persisted_failure",
10515:                     at_ms=now_ms,
10516:                 ))
10517:         self._route_memory.update(rebuilt)
10518:         for peer_fp, mem in rebuilt.items():
10519:             ranked = mem.candidates()
10520:             best = ranked[0] if ranked else None
10521:             if best is not None:
10522:                 self._stamp_pair_health(
10523:                     peer_fp,
10524:                     latency_ms=best.latency_ms,
10525:                     bandwidth_bps=best.bandwidth_bps,
10526:                     reliability=best.successes / max(1, best.attempts),
10527:                     best_route=best.route,
10528:                 )
10529: 
10530:     def _record_route_observation(
10531:         self,
10532:         peer_fp: str,
10533:         *,
10534:         route: str = "lan",
10535:         ok: bool,
10536:         latency_ms: float | None = None,
10537:         bandwidth_bps: float | None = None,
10538:         error_code: str | None = None,
10539:     ) -> None:
10540:         if not peer_fp:
10541:             return
10542:         mem = self._route_memory_for(peer_fp)
10543:         mem.observe(RouteObservation(
10544:             route=route or "unknown",
10545:             ok=bool(ok),
10546:             latency_ms=latency_ms,
10547:             bandwidth_bps=bandwidth_bps,
10548:             error_code=error_code,
10549:             at_ms=int(time.time() * 1000),
10550:         ))
10551:         ranked = mem.candidates()
10552:         best = ranked[0] if ranked else None
10553:         if best is not None:
10554:             self._stamp_pair_health(
10555:                 peer_fp,
10556:                 latency_ms=best.latency_ms,
10557:                 bandwidth_bps=best.bandwidth_bps,
10558:                 reliability=best.successes / max(1, best.attempts),
10559:                 best_route=best.route,
10560:             )
10561:         self._persist_route_memory(peer_fp, mem)
10562: 
10563:     def get_pair_health(self, peer_fp: str) -> dict | None:
10564:         """Public read for /api/peers."""
10565:         h = self._pair_health.get(peer_fp)
10566:         if h is None:
10567:             return None
10568:         # Cast through dict[str, Any] so we can mix in non-_PairHealth
10569:         # fields (route_scores) for the /api/peers UI surface — the
10570:         # public diagnostic shape is broader than the internal one.
10571:         out: dict[str, Any] = dict(h)
10572:         mem = self._route_memory.get(peer_fp)
10573:         if mem is not None:
10574:             out["route_scores"] = [c.__dict__ for c in mem.candidates()]
10575:             out["best_route"] = mem.best_route(
10576:                 str(out.get("best_route") or "lan")
10577:             )
10578:         return out
10579: 
10580:     def _transfer_route_observations(
10581:         self, peer_fp: str,
10582:     ) -> tuple[TransferRouteObservation, ...]:
10583:         mem = self._route_memory.get(peer_fp)
10584:         if mem is None:
10585:             return ()
10586:         out: list[TransferRouteObservation] = []
10587:         for c in mem.candidates():
10588:             attempts = max(1, int(c.attempts))
10589:             for _ in range(max(0, int(c.successes))):
10590:                 out.append(TransferRouteObservation(
10591:                     route=c.route,
10592:                     ok=True,
10593:                     latency_ms=c.latency_ms,
10594:                     bandwidth_bps=c.bandwidth_bps,
10595:                 ))
10596:             for _ in range(max(0, attempts - int(c.successes))):
10597:                 out.append(TransferRouteObservation(route=c.route, ok=False))
10598:         return tuple(out)
