14523:     def _broadcast_tail(self, msg: dict) -> None:
14524:         # The control-socket tail-stream path multiplexes many event
14525:         # types over a single line-oriented socket, so it keeps the
14526:         # legacy {"event": "msg", "msg": ...} envelope. Subscribers
14527:         # there demultiplex on ``event``.
14528:         line = (json.dumps({"event": "msg", "msg": msg}) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
14529:         dead: list[asyncio.StreamWriter] = []
14530:         for w in list(self._tail_subs):
14531:             try:
14532:                 w.write(line)
14533:             except Exception:
14534:                 dead.append(w)
14535:         for w in dead:
14536:             self._tail_subs.discard(w)
14537:         # UI-WebSocket path. The browser dispatcher in index.html
14538:         # routes on m.type, so:
14539:         #   - Events that ALREADY have a "type" field (call_event,
14540:         #     frame_provenance, transfer, traces_cleared, etc.) are
14541:         #     sent through verbatim so their typed handlers fire.
14542:         #   - Events that don't (chat/file _persist outputs, which
14543:         #     carry "t":"TEXT"/"FILE_OFFER"/... with no "type") are
14544:         #     wrapped as {"type":"msg","msg":<inner>} so the
14545:         #     browser's m.type === "msg" branch picks them up. This
14546:         #     is the only way an incoming chat bubble live-renders
14547:         #     on the receiver without a manual refresh.
14548:         if self.ui_server is not None:
14549:             try:
14550:                 if "type" in msg:
14551:                     self.ui_server.broadcast(msg)
14552:                 else:
14553:                     self.ui_server.broadcast({"type": "msg", "msg": msg})
14554:             except Exception:
14555:                 pass
14556: 
14557: 
14558:     # ─── lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14559:     async def start(self) -> None:
14560:         self._acquire_instance_lock()
14561:         # Persistent state (sqlite) — created early so peer/handshake hooks
14562:         # can record into it.
14563:         try:
14564:             self.state = State()
14565:             # v0.20.7 (security audit H21 + M29 + partial C5):
14566:             # acquire a LockBox unconditionally so chain_keys and
14567:             # the UI token get AES-GCM-wrapped at rest. The lockbox
14568:             # picks the strongest key it can without prompting:
14569:             #   - ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE set ⇒ scrypt-derived key
14570:             #     (resists attackers with same-user OS access).
14571:             #   - Otherwise silent DRK from acquire_or_create_silent_drk:
14572:             #     DPAPI-wrapped per-user on Windows; raw 32 random
14573:             #     bytes with 0o600 perms on POSIX.
14574:             # The point: every install gets at-rest encryption by
14575:             # default, no UX friction. A user who steals the laptop
14576:             # without the login password cannot DPAPI-unwrap the
14577:             # DRK, so wrapped sqlite values stay opaque.
14578:             try:
14579:                 from one_link.lockbox import acquire_lockbox
14580:                 from one_link.paths import data_dir
14581:                 lb = acquire_lockbox(data_dir())
14582:                 self.state.set_lockbox(lb)
14583:                 log.info(
14584:                     "lockbox: at-rest wrap active for chain_keys + UI token"
14585:                 )
14586:             except Exception as e:
14587:                 log.warning(
14588:                     "lockbox: failed to initialize (%s); proceeding "
14589:                     "with cleartext at-rest storage",
14590:                     e,
14591:                 )
14592:             # v0.20.7 (security audit M30): attach the path-PII
14593:             # encryptor when the master seed is available. Same-path-
14594:             # → same-ciphertext (AES-SIV deterministic AEAD), so the
14595:             # chunk_sources / file_index_cache indexes still work; a
14596:             # T4 attacker sees opaque ciphertext instead of the user's
14597:             # full home-dir layout. Daemons without a master seed
14598:             # (legacy installs that haven't run `backup init`) keep
14599:             # cleartext paths — there's no recoverable secret to
14600:             # derive a key from anyway, so the gain would be illusory.
14601:             try:
14602:                 from one_link import master_seed as _ms
14603:                 from one_link.path_pii import PathPIIEncryptor
14604:                 from one_link.paths import data_dir as _data_dir
14605:                 _seed = _ms.load_seed(_data_dir())
14606:                 if _seed is not None:
14607:                     self.state.set_path_pii_encryptor(PathPIIEncryptor(_seed))
14608:                     log.info(
14609:                         "path-pii: AES-SIV deterministic encryption "
14610:                         "active for chunk_sources / file_index_cache "
14611:                         "path columns (audit M30)"
14612:                     )
14613:             except Exception as e:
14614:                 log.warning(
14615:                     "path-pii: failed to initialize (%s); paths in "
14616:                     "chunk_sources / file_index_cache stay cleartext",
14617:                     e,
14618:                 )
14619:             # Row 10: seal the master seed under a per-process
14620:             # SoftwareProvider so the plaintext seed only re-
14621:             # materialises for ~µs per sign / attest inside the Rust
14622:             # provider. Best-effort: if the native ext isn't built
14623:             # or no master seed exists yet, daemon proceeds without
14624:             # the sealed handle and code that wants it logs +
14625:             # falls back.
14626:             try:
14627:                 from one_link import master_seed as _ms
14628:                 from one_link.paths import data_dir as _data_dir
14629:                 _sealed = _ms.load_sealed_master(_data_dir())
14630:                 if _sealed is None:
14631:                     self.sealed_master = None
14632:                 elif _sealed is False:
14633:                     self.sealed_master = None
14634:                     log.info(
14635:                         "row-10: one_link_native.confidential not "
14636:                         "built; skipping sealed-master at runtime "
14637:                         "(daemon proceeds with legacy plaintext-in-"
14638:                         "memory derivation)."
14639:                     )
14640:                 else:
14641:                     self.sealed_master = _sealed
14642:                     log.info(
14643:                         "row-10: sealed-master under per-process "
14644:                         "SoftwareProvider active; master plaintext "
14645:                         "only materialises during sealed_sign / "
14646:                         "attest inside Rust provider."
14647:                     )
14648:                 # Audit L12 May 2026: record the on-disk seed file
14649:                 # fingerprint at boot so detect_seed_file_tamper()
14650:                 # can detect on-disk replacement (a brief-FS-access
14651:                 # attacker swapping the seed). Checked from
14652:                 # _capability_allowed on the hot path.
14653:                 self._seed_file_fingerprint_at_boot = _ms.seed_file_fingerprint(
14654:                     _data_dir()
14655:                 )
14656:                 # Audit M14 May 2026: load (or mint) the per-daemon
14657:                 # cap_root_key — a separate 32-byte secret used
14658:                 # exclusively for macaroon HMAC root derivation.
14659:                 # Without this, the macaroon root shared entropy
14660:                 # with the identity Ed25519 seed and a side-channel
14661:                 # on the macaroon HMAC could leak bits of the
14662:                 # identity seed.
14663:                 try:
14664:                     from one_link import cap_root_key as _crk
14665:                     self._cap_root_key, _created = (
14666:                         _crk.load_or_create_cap_root_key(_data_dir())
14667:                     )
14668:                     if _created:
14669:                         log.info(
14670:                             "row-3/audit-M14: minted fresh cap_root_key "
14671:                             "(macaroon HMAC root key, separate from "
14672:                             "identity seed entropy)"
14673:                         )
14674:                 except Exception as exc:
14675:                     self._cap_root_key = None
14676:                     log.warning(
14677:                         "audit-M14: failed to load/mint cap_root_key (%s); "
14678:                         "macaroons fall back to seed-derivation (legacy path)",

14689:             # Default 0.5 Hz (~one cover packet per 2 s). The emit
14690:             # callback runs the FULL Sphinx cover-packet pipeline

14692:             # keypair, 1-hop circuit to self, build_cover_packet,
14693:             # immediately peel + verify the cover sentinel. Real
14694:             # cryptography end-to-end — Ristretto255 ECDH,
14695:             # ChaCha20-Poly1305 per-layer encrypt, BLAKE3 MAC. No
14696:             # stubs: a regression in any Sphinx primitive stops
14697:             # the counter immediately because peel/sentinel asserts
14698:             # raise. Wire-level peer-to-peer cover emission needs
14699:             # the Row 7 daemon-side onion-key exchange and lands

14702:                 from one_link.cover_traffic import (

14714:                     _cover_payload_size = max(
14715:                         int(_native_sphinx.COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN), 512
14716:                     )
14717:                     # Audit H11 May 2026: capture the event loop so
14718:                     # the emit callback (which runs on the
14719:                     # CoverTrafficDaemon background thread) can
14720:                     # marshal aiortc DataChannel sends back onto it.
14721:                     # `aiortc.RTCDataChannel.send` is not documented
14722:                     # thread-safe; calling it from the cover thread

14724:                     # the peer list inside the emit prevents the
14725:                     # `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during

14730:                     def _emit_cover_real() -> None:
14731:                         # Fresh ephemeral keypair per packet — Sphinx
14732:                         # design requires this for forward secrecy.
14733:                         eph_sk, _eph_pk = _native_sphinx.generate_keypair()
14734:                         target_peer = None
14735:                         target_pk = None
14736:                         prtc = getattr(self, "peer_rtc", None)
14737:                         if prtc is not None:
14738:                             # H11: list() copy snapshots the dict
14739:                             # so a concurrent mutation in
14740:                             # register_peer / _close_peer doesn't
14741:                             # raise. We accept that the snapshot
14742:                             # may be stale by one tick — cover
14743:                             # traffic is best-effort.
14744:                             try:
14745:                                 peers_snapshot = list(
14746:                                     getattr(prtc, "_peers", {}).values()
14747:                                 )
14748:                             except Exception:
14749:                                 peers_snapshot = []
14750:                             for p in peers_snapshot:
14751:                                 pk = getattr(p, "onion_pubkey", None)
14752:                                 dc = getattr(p, "control_dc", None)
14753:                                 if pk and getattr(dc, "readyState", "") == "open":
14754:                                     target_peer = p
14755:                                     target_pk = pk
14756:                                     break
14757:                         if target_peer is not None and target_pk is not None:
14758:                             circuit = [(self._cover_self_hop_id, target_pk)]
14759:                             packet = _native_sphinx.build_cover_packet(
14760:                                 eph_sk, circuit, _cover_payload_size
14761:                             )
14762:                             try:
14763:                                 from one_link.peer_rtc import PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION
14764:                                 envelope = {
14765:                                     "v": PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
14766:                                     "t": "cover_packet",
14767:                                     "packet_b64": base64.b64encode(packet).decode("ascii"),
14768:                                 }
14769:                                 # H11: marshal the actual aiortc
14770:                                 # send_dc onto the event loop so
14771:                                 # aiortc only sees calls from its
14772:                                 # own thread. Background-thread
14773:                                 # call_soon_threadsafe is the
14774:                                 # supported bridge.
14775:                                 _cover_event_loop.call_soon_threadsafe(
14776:                                     prtc.send_dc, target_peer, "control", envelope,
14777:                                 )
14778:                                 # Audit L8 May 2026: serialize all
14779:                                 # telemetry mutations against the
14780:                                 # asyncio handlers via _telemetry_lock.
14781:                                 with self._telemetry_lock:
14782:                                     self._cover_emit_count += 1
14783:                                     self._cover_wire_sent_count = (
14784:                                         getattr(self, "_cover_wire_sent_count", 0) + 1
14785:                                     )
14786:                                 return
14787:                             except Exception:
14788:                                 pass
14789:                         circuit = [
14790:                             (
14791:                                 self._cover_self_hop_id,
14792:                                 self._cover_relay_pk,
14793:                             )
14794:                         ]
14795:                         packet = _native_sphinx.build_cover_packet(
14796:                             eph_sk, circuit, _cover_payload_size
14797:                         )
14798:                         kind, _next, _payload = _native_sphinx.peel_sphinx(
14799:                             self._cover_relay_sk, packet
14800:                         )
14801:                         # Audit M4 May 2026 — `peel_sphinx` now returns
14802:                         # kind == "cover" directly for cover packets
14803:                         # (the destination's per-circuit MAC over the
14804:                         # cover-trailer authenticates the cover bit
14805:                         # cryptographically; no plaintext sentinel
14806:                         # fallback). The previous code asserted
14807:                         # kind == "deliver" + checked the plaintext
14808:                         # sentinel, which was the M8 oracle vector.
14809:                         # That path is gone; cover packets now peel
14810:                         # as "cover".
14811:                         if kind != "cover":
14812:                             raise RuntimeError(
14813:                                 f"cover-traffic peel: expected "
14814:                                 f"cover, got {kind!r}"
14815:                             )
14816:                         # Audit L8: locked counter mutation.
14817:                         with self._telemetry_lock:
14818:                             self._cover_emit_count += 1
14819:                             self._cover_loopback_count = (
14820:                                 getattr(self, "_cover_loopback_count", 0) + 1
14821:                             )
14822: 
14823:                     ct = _CTD(rate_hz=0.5, emit_cover=_emit_cover_real)
14824:                     ct.start()

14826:                     log.info(
14827:                         "row-6: cover-traffic scheduler started "

14842:             # MAY 15 2026 — REMOVED self-pinning into the peers table.
14843:             #
14844:             # The previous code did `upsert_peer(fingerprint=self.me.fingerprint, ...)`
14845:             # at every boot. That caused a real user-visible bug: each time the
14846:             # daemon booted with a fresh seed (recovery, re-bootstrap, dev-loop
14847:             # restart), a NEW peer row got pinned. Old rows stayed in the DB
14848:             # because they had different fingerprints. Over many restarts the
14849:             # sidebar accumulated "WeareOne offline / WeareOne offline / …"
14850:             # ghost duplicates, all pinned, all stale.
14851:             #
14852:             # The daemon's own identity is already authoritative via `self.me`
14853:             # — every code path that previously read it from the peers table
14854:             # can read it from `self.me` instead. The peers table is for
14855:             # PEERS, not self. The API layer also filters self by
14856:             # fingerprint AND by pubkey at line 5764 / 5853 of server.py as
14857:             # belt-and-suspenders.
14858:             #
14859:             # If you find a code path that ASSUMES self appears in the peers
14860:             # table, the right fix is to update that code path to read from

15171:             # Write the bound port to data_dir/ui_port.txt so the CLI's
15172:             # auto-open-browser hook can target the right port even when
15173:             # the daemon is on a dynamic / fallback port.
15174:             try:
15175:                 from one_link.paths import data_dir as _dd
15176:                 (_dd() / "ui_port.txt").write_text(str(ui_port), encoding="utf-8")
15177:             except Exception:
15178:                 pass
15179:         except Exception as e:
15180:             log.warning("UI server failed to start: %s", e)
15181:             self.ui_server = None
15182:             ui_port = 0
15183: 
15184:         # v0.5.1: rendezvous client. Optional — only starts if URLs are
15185:         # configured. The daemon stays fully functional on LAN-only when
15186:         # rendezvous is disabled or unreachable.
15187:         await self._start_rendezvous(peer_port=peer_port)
15188: 
15189:         log.info(
15190:             "One Link daemon up — id=%s host=%s peer=:%d ctrl=:%d ui=:%d",
15191:             self.me.short_id,
15192:             self.me.hostname,

15194:             ctrl_port,

15198:     async def _on_local_folder_change(self, folder_name: str, entry) -> None:
15199:         """Called by the FolderEngine when a watched file is added / changed
15200:         / deleted. Notify the UI so the folder status indicator updates;
15201:         peer push happens on the next sync tick."""
15202:         if self.ui_server is not None:
15203:             try:
15204:                 self.ui_server.broadcast({
15205:                     "type": "folder_change",
15206:                     "folder": folder_name,
15207:                     "file": entry.file_path,
15208:                     "deleted": entry.blob_hash is None,
15209:                 })
15210:             except Exception:
15211:                 pass

15213:     async def _folder_sync_loop(self) -> None:
15214:         """Periodically push our manifest for each shared folder to every
15215:         pinned peer that's currently reachable. One-way per cycle; the
15216:         reverse direction happens when the peer initiates."""
15217:         # Initial settle delay so discovery + state are fully up.
15218:         try:
15219:             await asyncio.sleep(8.0)
15220:             while True:
15221:                 await self._run_one_folder_sync_cycle()
15222:                 await asyncio.sleep(30.0)
15223:         except asyncio.CancelledError:
15224:             pass
15225: 
15226:     async def _run_one_folder_sync_cycle(self) -> None:
15227:         if (
15228:             self.folder_engine is None
15229:             or self.state is None
15230:             or self.discovery is None
15231:         ):
15232:             return
15233:         folders = self.state.list_folders()
15234:         if not folders:
15235:             return
15236:         for folder in folders:
15237:             for peer_fp in folder["shared_with"]:
15238:                 if not self._is_pinned(peer_fp):
15239:                     continue
15240:                 # Find the peer in discovery.
15241:                 peer = None
15242:                 for p in self.discovery.registry.list():
15243:                     cand_fp = self._peer_fp_from_peer(p)
15244:                     if cand_fp == peer_fp:
15245:                         peer = p
15246:                         break
15247:                 if peer is None:
15248:                     continue
15249:                 try:
15250:                     await self.push_folder_to_peer(peer, folder["name"])
15251:                 except Exception as e:
15252:                     log.info("folder sync to %s failed: %s", peer.short_id, e)
15253: 
15254:     async def serve_forever(self) -> None:
15255:         assert self._peer_server and self._control_server
15256:         try:
15257:             await asyncio.gather(
15258:                 self._peer_server.serve_forever(),
15259:                 self._control_server.serve_forever(),
15260:             )
15261:         except RuntimeError as e:
15262:             if "is closed" not in str(e):
15263:                 raise
15264: 
15265:     async def stop(self) -> None:
15266:         # Row 6 — drain cover-traffic scheduler first so its worker
15267:         # thread doesn't try to emit through a half-torn-down state.
15268:         cover = getattr(self, "_cover_traffic", None)
15269:         if cover is not None and cover.is_running:
15270:             try:
15271:                 cover.stop(join_timeout=2.0)
15272:                 log.info(
15273:                     "row-6: cover-traffic scheduler stopped "
15274:                     "(emitted=%d errors=%d)",
15275:                     cover.emitted, cover.errors,
15276:                 )
15277:             except Exception as e:
15278:                 log.warning("row-6: cover-traffic stop raised: %s", e)
15279:             self._cover_traffic = None
15280:         # Phase E: stop the field-snapshot topology feeder + the
15281:         # snapshot manager itself. Feeder first so it doesn't observe
15282:         # a half-torn-down peer table mid-tick.
15283:         feeder = getattr(self, "_field_topology_feeder_task", None)
15284:         if feeder is not None and not feeder.done():
15285:             feeder.cancel()
15286:             try:
15287:                 await feeder
15288:             except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
15289:                 pass
15290:         homology_feeder = getattr(
15291:             self, "_field_homology_feeder_task", None,
15292:         )
15293:         if homology_feeder is not None and not homology_feeder.done():
15294:             homology_feeder.cancel()
15295:             try:
15296:                 await homology_feeder
15297:             except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
15298:                 pass
15299:         if self._field_snapshot is not None:
15300:             try:
15301:                 self._field_snapshot.stop(join_timeout=2.0)
15302:             except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
15303:                 pass
15304:         # Phase A2: close the local QUIC endpoint. Active QUIC peer
15305:         # connections close as part of their own session teardown.
15306:         quic_ep = getattr(self, "_quic_endpoint", None)
15307:         if quic_ep is not None:
15308:             try:
15309:                 quic_ep.close()
15310:             except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
15311:                 pass
15312:             self._quic_endpoint = None
15313:         # v0.5.1: revoke rendezvous registration first so peers learn
15314:         # we're going offline before we tear down anything else.
15315:         if self.rendezvous is not None:
15316:             try:
15317:                 await self.rendezvous.stop()
15318:             except Exception:
15319:                 pass
15320:             self.rendezvous = None
15321:         # v0.5.5: stop relay listeners.
15322:         for listener in list(self._relay_listener_clients):
15323:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
15324:                 await listener.stop()
15325:         self._relay_listener_clients.clear()
15326:         for peer_fp in list(self._outbound_sessions):
15327:             await self._drop_outbound_session(peer_fp)
15328:         if self._folder_sync_task and not self._folder_sync_task.done():
15329:             self._folder_sync_task.cancel()
15330:             try:
15331:                 await self._folder_sync_task
15332:             except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
15333:                 pass
15334:         if self.folder_engine is not None:
15335:             try:
15336:                 await self.folder_engine.stop()
15337:             except Exception:
15338:                 pass
15339:         if self._prune_task and not self._prune_task.done():
15340:             self._prune_task.cancel()
15341:             try:
15342:                 await self._prune_task
15343:             except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
15344:                 pass
15345:         if self._dm_reaper_task and not self._dm_reaper_task.done():
15346:             self._dm_reaper_task.cancel()
15347:             try:
15348:                 await self._dm_reaper_task
15349:             except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
15350:                 pass
15351:         if self._prior_index_task and not self._prior_index_task.done():
15352:             self._prior_index_task.cancel()
15353:             try:
15354:                 await self._prior_index_task
15355:             except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
15356:                 pass
15357:         if self.ui_server is not None:
15358:             try:
15359:                 await self.ui_server.stop()
15360:             except Exception:
15361:                 pass
15362:         if self.discovery:
15363:             await self.discovery.stop()
15364:         if self._peer_server:
15365:             self._peer_server.close()
15366:             await self._peer_server.wait_closed()
15367:         if self._control_server:
15368:             self._control_server.close()
15369:             await self._control_server.wait_closed()
15370:         if self.state is not None:
15371:             try:
15372:                 self.state.close()
15373:             except Exception:
15374:                 pass
15375:         self._release_instance_lock()

15378: async def run() -> None:
15379:     _install_asyncio_exception_handler(asyncio.get_running_loop())

15391: def read_control_port() -> int:
15392:     p = _control_port_path()
15393:     if not p.exists():
15394:         recovered = _recover_control_port_from_live_pid()
15395:         if recovered is not None:
15396:             return recovered
15397:         raise RuntimeError("daemon not running (no control.port file)")
15398:     try:
15399:         port = int(p.read_text().strip())
15400:     except Exception as e:
15401:         _clear_stale_runtime_files()
15402:         raise RuntimeError("daemon not running (bad control.port file)") from e
15403:     if is_daemon_alive(port):
15404:         return port
15405:     lock_pid = _read_lock_pid()
15406:     if lock_pid is None or not _pid_is_alive(lock_pid):
15407:         _clear_stale_runtime_files()
15408:     raise RuntimeError(f"daemon not running (stale control.port {port})")

15411: def query_control_status(port: int, *, timeout: float = 0.5) -> dict[str, Any]:
15412:     s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
15413:     s.settimeout(timeout)
15414:     try:
15415:         s.connect(("127.0.0.1", int(port)))
15416:         s.sendall(b'{"cmd":"status"}\n')
15417:         buf = b""
15418:         while not buf.endswith(b"\n") and len(buf) < 65536:
15419:             chunk = s.recv(65536)
15420:             if not chunk:
15421:                 break
15422:             buf += chunk
15423:         if not buf:
15424:             return {}
15425:         return json.loads(buf.decode("utf-8").strip() or "{}")
15426:     except Exception:
15427:         return {}
15428:     finally:
15429:         s.close()
15430: 
15431: 
15432: def is_daemon_alive(port: int, *, timeout: float = 0.5) -> bool:
15433:     """Return True only when the local One Link control protocol answers.
15434: 
15435:     A bare TCP connect is not enough: a stale port can be reused by an
15436:     unrelated process, and a wedged daemon can accept sockets without ever
15437:     replying. The launcher and CLI need the stronger signal.
15438:     """
15439:     msg = query_control_status(port, timeout=timeout)
15440:     return msg.get("ok") is True and bool(msg.get("pid"))

   1: """v0.8.1: developer-backend error log.
   2: 
   3: Captures every interesting failure inside the daemon — server
   4: exception paths, daemon-level raises, peer-frame rejections,
   5: capability denials, transfer pause/fail events — with structured
   6: context so the UI's Debug pane can show "what happened, why, and
   7: how to fix" without the user squinting at logs.
   8: 
   9: In-memory ring buffer (default 500 entries). No sqlite — failures
  10: shouldn't take a write lock or slow normal operation, and a daemon
  11: restart is a perfectly reasonable point to forget old errors.
  12: 
  13: Each entry is a dict with:
  14:   ts_ms      — wall clock
  15:   severity   — "info" | "warn" | "error"
  16:   source     — e.g. "send_file", "create_group", "channel.recv"
  17:   code       — machine-readable, e.g. "capability_disabled",
  18:                "peer_offline", "winerror_10053"
  19:   message    — human-readable, what happened
  20:   context    — dict of relevant ids (peer_fp, transfer_id,
  21:                group_id, etc.)
  22:   suggestion — what to try next, e.g. "Re-pair this device" or
  23:                "Restart One Link to pick up the new endpoints"
  24: """
  25: from __future__ import annotations
  26: 
  27: import logging
  28: import threading
  29: import time
  30: import traceback
  31: from collections import deque
  32: from typing import Any, Iterable, Optional
  33: 
  34: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  35: 
  36: # Capacity of the ring buffer. 500 entries × ~1KB each = ~500 KB
  37: # resident; small enough to be free, big enough to capture a busy
  38: # session's worth of failures.
  39: MAX_ENTRIES = 500
  40: 
  41: 
  42: class DebugLog:
  43:     """Process-wide debug log. Threadsafe."""
  44: 
  45:     def __init__(self, capacity: int = MAX_ENTRIES):
  46:         self._buf: deque[dict[str, Any]] = deque(maxlen=capacity)
  47:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
  48:         self._next_id = 1
  49:         # Optional WS broadcaster — set by UIServer at startup so
  50:         # new entries push live to the Debug pane without poll.
  51:         self._broadcast = None
  52: 
  53:     def attach_broadcast(self, fn) -> None:
  54:         """Wire a callable(dict) → broadcasts a `debug_event` WS
  55:         notification with the new entry. Optional."""
  56:         self._broadcast = fn
  57: 
  58:     def record(
  59:         self,
  60:         *,
  61:         severity: str = "error",
  62:         source: str,
  63:         code: str,
  64:         message: str,
  65:         context: Optional[dict] = None,
  66:         suggestion: Optional[str] = None,
  67:         traceback_str: Optional[str] = None,
  68:     ) -> dict:
  69:         """Append an entry. Returns the entry dict including a
  70:         monotonic id (1-indexed)."""
  71:         if severity not in ("info", "warn", "error"):
  72:             severity = "error"
  73:         entry = {
  74:             "id": self._next_id,
  75:             "ts_ms": int(time.time() * 1000),
  76:             "severity": severity,
  77:             "source": str(source)[:80],
  78:             "code": str(code)[:64],
  79:             "message": str(message)[:500],
  80:             "context": dict(context or {}),
  81:             "suggestion": str(suggestion)[:300] if suggestion else None,
  82:             "traceback": (str(traceback_str)[:2000] if traceback_str else None),
  83:         }
  84:         with self._lock:
  85:             self._next_id += 1
  86:             self._buf.append(entry)
  87:         # Mirror to the standard logger so server.log shows it too.
  88:         log_level = (
  89:             logging.ERROR if severity == "error"
  90:             else logging.WARNING if severity == "warn"
  91:             else logging.INFO
  92:         )
  93:         log.log(
  94:             log_level,
  95:             "[debug_log %s] %s: %s",
  96:             entry["source"], entry["code"], entry["message"],
  97:         )
  98:         # Live-push to UI subscribers if attached.
  99:         if self._broadcast is not None:
 100:             try:
 101:                 self._broadcast(entry)
 102:             except Exception:
 103:                 pass
 104:         return entry
 105: 
 106:     def record_exception(
 107:         self,
 108:         exc: BaseException,
 109:         *,
 110:         source: str,
 111:         code: Optional[str] = None,
 112:         suggestion: Optional[str] = None,
 113:         context: Optional[dict] = None,
 114:     ) -> dict:
 115:         """Convenience: record a Python exception with traceback."""
 116:         return self.record(
 117:             severity="error",
 118:             source=source,
 119:             code=code or type(exc).__name__,
 120:             message=str(exc) or type(exc).__name__,
 121:             context=context,
 122:             suggestion=suggestion or _default_suggestion(exc),
 123:             traceback_str="".join(
 124:                 traceback.format_exception(type(exc), exc, exc.__traceback__)
 125:             ),
 126:         )
 127: 
 128:     def tail(
 129:         self,
 130:         *,
 131:         limit: int = 200,
 132:         since_id: Optional[int] = None,
 133:         severity: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
 134:         sources: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
 135:     ) -> list[dict]:
 136:         """Most-recent-first list of entries. since_id limits to
 137:         entries strictly newer than the given id (for incremental
 138:         polling)."""
 139:         sev_set = set(severity) if severity else None
 140:         src_set = set(sources) if sources else None
 141:         with self._lock:
 142:             snapshot = list(self._buf)
 143:         # newest first
 144:         snapshot.reverse()
 145:         out = []
 146:         for entry in snapshot:
 147:             if since_id is not None and entry["id"] <= since_id:
 148:                 continue
 149:             if sev_set and entry["severity"] not in sev_set:
 150:                 continue
 151:             if src_set and entry["source"] not in src_set:
 152:                 continue
 153:             out.append(entry)
 154:             if len(out) >= limit:
 155:                 break
 156:         return out
 157: 
 158:     def clear(self) -> int:
 159:         """Drop all entries. Returns count removed."""
 160:         with self._lock:
 161:             n = len(self._buf)
 162:             self._buf.clear()
 163:         return n
 164: 
 165:     def __len__(self) -> int:
 166:         with self._lock:
 167:             return len(self._buf)
 168: 
 169: 
 170: # Process-wide singleton. Imported by daemon + server; tests can
 171: # call `_singleton.clear()` between cases.
 172: _singleton = DebugLog()
 173: 
 174: 
 175: def get_debug_log() -> DebugLog:
 176:     return _singleton
 177: 
 178: 
 179: def _default_suggestion(exc: BaseException) -> str:
 180:     """Map common exception shapes to a human-friendly next step."""
 181:     name = type(exc).__name__
 182:     msg = str(exc).lower()
 183:     if name == "TransferPausedError":
 184:         return (
 185:             "This transfer is paused; it will resume automatically the "
 186:             "next time the peer's daemon comes back online."
 187:         )
 188:     if "winerror 10053" in msg or "winerror 10054" in msg or "connection aborted" in msg:
 189:         return (
 190:             "The peer's TCP connection dropped mid-stream. Often caused "
 191:             "by Wi-Fi roam, antivirus, or a brief peer-side hiccup. "
 192:             "Transfers retry automatically; for chat, try sending again."
 193:         )
 194:     if "handshake timed out" in msg or "not responsive" in msg:
 195:         return (
 196:             "The peer's daemon isn't answering. Make sure One Link is "
 197:             "still running there, then try again."
 198:         )
 199:     if "capability" in msg and "disabled" in msg:
 200:         return (
 201:             "Your local policy doesn't allow this action for that peer. "
 202:             "Open the device drawer (gear next to the peer in the "
 203:             "sidebar) and toggle the relevant capability on."
 204:         )
 205:     if "rejected" in msg:
 206:         return (
 207:             "The peer is marked as blocked. Click 'Allow device' in the "
 208:             "conversation header to unblock, then re-pair if needed."
 209:         )
 210:     if (
 211:         "decrypt" in msg or "invalidtag" in msg
 212:         or "wire_version_mismatch" in msg
 213:         or "ratchet header version" in msg
 214:     ):
 215:         return (
 216:             "The secure session could not be opened on this path yet. "
 217:             "One Link will reconnect and use the best compatible route automatically."
 218:         )
 219:     if "peer offline" in msg or "no peer" in msg or "unreachable" in msg:
 220:         return (
 221:             "The peer isn't reachable right now. Outbound chat falls "
 222:             "back to the outbox automatically; files wait for reconnect."
 223:         )
 224:     if "404" in msg and ("api" in msg or "request failed" in msg):
 225:         return (
 226:             "This window is ahead of the local background service. "
 227:             "Close and reopen One Link if it does not refresh itself."
 228:         )
 229:     return ""
 230:

   1: """Provably-deletable messages — the cryptographic delete button.
   2: 
   3: When a user clicks "delete" in most chat apps, the platform hides
   4: the message from the UI but the bytes still exist: in backups, in
   5: caches, on the recipient's device, in the audit log, in the
   6: "Recently Deleted" folder. "Delete" is a soft-state contract.
   7: 
   8: We can do better. The Double Ratchet already gives forward secrecy
   9: on chain advance — the previous key is unrecoverable. What's
  10: missing is a **publicly-verifiable proof** that a party has
  11: deleted: a signed commitment that says "I have applied this
  12: specific HKDF advance, so K_n is gone from my state."
  13: 
  14: Bundle 42 ships that primitive. The model:
  15: 
  16:   - Each message is keyed by a 32-byte chain key K_n.
  17:   - After encrypting / decrypting, the holder advances:
  18:       K_{n+1} = HKDF(K_n, "OL-deletion-chain-advance|v1", 32)
  19:   - The holder MAY retain K_n in a bounded cache for resend /
  20:     retransmit. ``delete(n)`` drops K_n from the cache + emits
  21:     a signed deletion proof bound to the chain identity, the
  22:     deleted key index, the post-delete chain hash, and a
  23:     timestamp.
  24:   - Anyone with the chain's verification pubkey (typically the
  25:     holder's Ed25519 identity) can verify the proof. They can't
  26:     recover K_n; they CAN audit "this party did delete this
  27:     message at this time."
  28: 
  29: This combines well with the existing channel ratchet: the channel
  30: provides forward secrecy on receive; this primitive lets the
  31: sender + receiver MUTUALLY commit to deletion AND prove it to a
  32: third-party auditor (e.g. when a journalist source needs to prove
  33: the message has been destroyed).
  34: 
  35: Threat note
  36: -----------
  37: 
  38: This protects against post-deletion content recovery from the
  39: party's own chain state. It does NOT defend against:
  40: 
  41:   - An attacker who captured K_n WHILE it was active. The
  42:     ciphertext from that period remains decryptable to anyone
  43:     holding the key from before the delete.
  44:   - A party that lies about deleting — the proof says "I did the
  45:     advance," but the proof can't force the party to actually
  46:     forget K_n. (The proof is a commitment, not a coercion.)
  47:     Trust here is anchored in the public nature of the commitment:
  48:     a party that produces deletion proofs while secretly retaining
  49:     K_n is detectable if any retained K_n leaks later.
  50: 
  51: Wire format for a deletion proof
  52: --------------------------------
  53: 
  54:   [magic: b"OLDLP1"] (6 bytes)
  55:   [version: 1 byte]
  56:   [chain_id: 16 bytes]                # caller-chosen unique chain ID
  57:   [deleted_key_index: 8 bytes BE]     # which K_n was deleted
  58:   [post_delete_chain_hash: 32 bytes]  # SHA-256 of chain state after advance
  59:   [timestamp_ms: 8 bytes BE]
  60:   [signature: 64 bytes]               # Ed25519 over the above
  61: """
  62: from __future__ import annotations
  63: 
  64: import hashlib
  65: import struct
  66: import time
  67: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  68: from typing import Optional
  69: 
  70: from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidSignature
  71: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
  72:     Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519PublicKey,
  73: )
  74: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
  75: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.hkdf import HKDF
  76: 
  77: 
  78: CHAIN_KEY_LEN = 32
  79: CHAIN_ID_LEN = 16
  80: PROOF_MAGIC = b"OLDLP1"
  81: PROOF_VERSION = 1
  82: PROOF_LEN = (
  83:     len(PROOF_MAGIC) + 1
  84:     + CHAIN_ID_LEN + 8 + 32 + 8 + 64
  85: )
  86: HKDF_INFO_ADVANCE = b"OL-deletion-chain-advance|v1"
  87: HKDF_INFO_MSG_KEY = b"OL-deletion-chain-msg-key|v1"
  88: 
  89: 
  90: def _hkdf(material: bytes, info: bytes, length: int = 32) -> bytes:
  91:     return HKDF(
  92:         algorithm=hashes.SHA256(),
  93:         length=length,
  94:         salt=None,
  95:         info=info,
  96:     ).derive(material)
  97: 
  98: 
  99: def advance_chain(chain_key: bytes) -> bytes:
 100:     if len(chain_key) != CHAIN_KEY_LEN:
 101:         raise ValueError(f"chain_key must be {CHAIN_KEY_LEN} bytes")
 102:     return _hkdf(chain_key, HKDF_INFO_ADVANCE, CHAIN_KEY_LEN)
 103: 
 104: 
 105: def derive_msg_key(chain_key: bytes) -> bytes:
 106:     if len(chain_key) != CHAIN_KEY_LEN:
 107:         raise ValueError(f"chain_key must be {CHAIN_KEY_LEN} bytes")
 108:     return _hkdf(chain_key, HKDF_INFO_MSG_KEY, CHAIN_KEY_LEN)
 109: 
 110: 
 111: def chain_state_hash(chain_key: bytes, index: int) -> bytes:
 112:     """Public commitment to chain state. SHA-256 over the
 113:     chain key + index. The index is included so a party that
 114:     advances out of order can't claim it's at index N+1 with the
 115:     K_N key."""
 116:     if len(chain_key) != CHAIN_KEY_LEN:
 117:         raise ValueError("chain_key wrong length")
 118:     h = hashlib.sha256()
 119:     h.update(b"OL-chain-state|")
 120:     h.update(struct.pack(">Q", index))
 121:     h.update(chain_key)
 122:     return h.digest()
 123: 
 124: 
 125: # ── DeletionChain ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 126: 
 127: 
 128: @dataclass
 129: class DeletionChain:
 130:     """Holds the current chain state + a bounded cache of historical
 131:     keys for replay / retransmit. ``delete(idx)`` removes a specific
 132:     historical key + emits a signed deletion proof.
 133: 
 134:     Construction: pass an initial 32-byte chain key (typically
 135:     derived from the channel handshake's transcript_hash + an HKDF
 136:     domain tag) + the holder's Ed25519 identity for signing
 137:     deletion proofs."""
 138: 
 139:     chain_id: bytes
 140:     current_chain_key: bytes
 141:     next_index: int = 0
 142:     sign_priv: Optional[Ed25519PrivateKey] = None
 143:     sign_pub: Optional[bytes] = None
 144:     cache_window: int = 64
 145:     _cache: dict[int, bytes] = field(default_factory=dict)
 146: 
 147:     def __post_init__(self):
 148:         if len(self.chain_id) != CHAIN_ID_LEN:
 149:             raise ValueError(f"chain_id must be {CHAIN_ID_LEN} bytes")
 150:         if len(self.current_chain_key) != CHAIN_KEY_LEN:
 151:             raise ValueError(
 152:                 f"current_chain_key must be {CHAIN_KEY_LEN} bytes"
 153:             )
 154: 
 155:     def seal_msg_key(self) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
 156:         """Reserve the next message-key in the chain. Returns
 157:         ``(index, msg_key)``. Caller uses msg_key to encrypt the
 158:         message body via their AEAD of choice. The chain advances
 159:         AFTER reservation so the next call gets a fresh msg_key."""
 160:         idx = self.next_index
 161:         msg_key = derive_msg_key(self.current_chain_key)
 162:         # Cache the chain key at this index so a delete-proof
 163:         # later can attest to the specific state.
 164:         self._cache[idx] = self.current_chain_key
 165:         # Bound the cache: drop the oldest entry on overflow.
 166:         while len(self._cache) > self.cache_window:
 167:             oldest = min(self._cache)
 168:             self._cache.pop(oldest, None)
 169:         # Advance.
 170:         self.current_chain_key = advance_chain(self.current_chain_key)
 171:         self.next_index = idx + 1
 172:         return idx, msg_key
 173: 
 174:     def get_msg_key(self, idx: int) -> Optional[bytes]:
 175:         """Re-derive the message key at index ``idx`` if the
 176:         underlying chain key is still cached. Returns None if the
 177:         key has been deleted or evicted from the window."""
 178:         ck = self._cache.get(idx)
 179:         if ck is None:
 180:             return None
 181:         return derive_msg_key(ck)
 182: 
 183:     def delete(self, idx: int) -> bytes:
 184:         """Drop the cached chain key at ``idx`` + emit a signed
 185:         deletion proof.
 186: 
 187:         After this call, ``get_msg_key(idx)`` returns None
 188:         permanently — the key is gone from local state. The proof
 189:         can be shipped to the peer (or an auditor) to attest that
 190:         the deletion happened.
 191: 
 192:         Raises if no signing key is configured (deletion proofs
 193:         require a signature; an unsigned proof is meaningless)."""
 194:         if self.sign_priv is None or self.sign_pub is None:
 195:             raise ValueError(
 196:                 "DeletionChain has no signing key; can't emit deletion proof"
 197:             )
 198:         if idx not in self._cache:
 199:             # Already deleted or never existed. Still emit a proof
 200:             # so the peer learns of the (idempotent) deletion.
 201:             post_hash = chain_state_hash(self.current_chain_key, self.next_index)
 202:         else:
 203:             ck = self._cache.pop(idx)
 204:             # Best-effort overwrite of the local copy. (Python
 205:             # bytes are immutable so we can't truly overwrite the
 206:             # underlying memory; this is the standard caveat for
 207:             # any pure-Python crypto. A C-extension impl could
 208:             # explicit_bzero the buffer.)
 209:             del ck
 210:             post_hash = chain_state_hash(self.current_chain_key, self.next_index)
 211:         ts = int(time.time() * 1000)
 212:         body = (
 213:             PROOF_MAGIC + bytes([PROOF_VERSION])
 214:             + self.chain_id
 215:             + struct.pack(">Q", idx)
 216:             + post_hash
 217:             + struct.pack(">Q", ts)
 218:         )
 219:         signature = self.sign_priv.sign(body)
 220:         return body + signature
 221: 
 222: 
 223: # ── deletion-proof verification ────────────────────────────────────
 224: 
 225: 
 226: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 227: class DeletionProof:
 228:     chain_id: bytes
 229:     deleted_index: int
 230:     post_chain_hash: bytes
 231:     timestamp_ms: int
 232:     signature: bytes
 233:     encoded: bytes
 234: 
 235: 
 236: def parse_deletion_proof(blob: bytes) -> DeletionProof:
 237:     if len(blob) != PROOF_LEN:
 238:         raise ValueError(
 239:             f"deletion proof must be {PROOF_LEN} bytes, got {len(blob)}"
 240:         )
 241:     if blob[:6] != PROOF_MAGIC:
 242:         raise ValueError("not a One Link deletion proof (bad magic)")
 243:     if blob[6] != PROOF_VERSION:
 244:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported proof version {blob[6]}")
 245:     off = 7
 246:     chain_id = blob[off:off + CHAIN_ID_LEN]
 247:     off += CHAIN_ID_LEN
 248:     deleted_index = struct.unpack(">Q", blob[off:off + 8])[0]
 249:     off += 8
 250:     post_hash = blob[off:off + 32]
 251:     off += 32
 252:     ts = struct.unpack(">Q", blob[off:off + 8])[0]
 253:     off += 8
 254:     signature = blob[off:off + 64]
 255:     return DeletionProof(
 256:         chain_id=chain_id,
 257:         deleted_index=deleted_index,
 258:         post_chain_hash=post_hash,
 259:         timestamp_ms=ts,
 260:         signature=signature,
 261:         encoded=blob,
 262:     )
 263: 
 264: 
 265: def verify_deletion_proof(blob: bytes, signer_pub: bytes) -> DeletionProof:
 266:     """Verify a deletion proof's signature. Returns the parsed
 267:     DeletionProof on success. Raises ValueError on tamper / bad
 268:     signature / wrong signer."""
 269:     proof = parse_deletion_proof(blob)
 270:     body = blob[:PROOF_LEN - 64]
 271:     try:
 272:         Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(signer_pub).verify(
 273:             proof.signature, body,
 274:         )
 275:     except InvalidSignature:
 276:         raise ValueError("deletion-proof signature invalid") from None
 277:     return proof

   2: 
   3: Guardian is deliberately two-speed: fast reversible protection, slow
   4: destructive revocation. A single device may freeze another device quickly,
   5: but hard revoke needs stronger proof unless the device is already frozen.

  56: def canonical_policy_json(obj: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bytes:
  57:     return json.dumps(
  58:         obj,
  59:         sort_keys=True,
  60:         separators=(",", ":"),
  61:         ensure_ascii=False,
  62:     ).encode("utf-8")
  63:

  65: def event_hash(event: Mapping[str, Any], previous_hash: str = "") -> str:
  66:     h = hashlib.sha256()
  67:     h.update(b"OL/device-guardian/event/v1|")
  68:     h.update(str(previous_hash or "").encode("ascii", "ignore"))
  69:     h.update(b"|")
  70:     h.update(canonical_policy_json(event))

  74: @dataclass(frozen=True)

  80:     detail: str
  81:     required_proofs: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
  82:     effects: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
  83:     reversible: bool = True
  84:     cooldown_ms: int = 0
  85: 
  86:     def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
  87:         return {
  88:             "allowed": self.allowed,
  89:             "target_state": self.target_state,
  90:             "severity": self.severity,
  91:             "event": self.event,
  92:             "detail": self.detail,
  93:             "required_proofs": list(self.required_proofs),
  94:             "effects": list(self.effects),
  95:             "reversible": self.reversible,
  96:             "cooldown_ms": self.cooldown_ms,
  97:         }
  98: 
  99: 
 100: def normalize_safety_state(state: str | None) -> str:
 101:     value = str(state or "trusted").strip().lower().replace("-", "_")
 102:     if value not in SAFETY_STATES:
 103:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported device safety state {state!r}")
 104:     return value
 105: 
 106: 
 107: def normalize_proofs(proofs: Any) -> frozenset[str]:
 108:     if proofs is None:
 109:         return frozenset()
 110:     if isinstance(proofs, str):
 111:         raw = [proofs]
 112:     else:
 113:         raw = list(proofs)
 114:     return frozenset(str(p or "").strip().lower() for p in raw if str(p or "").strip())
 115: 
 116: 
 117: def decide_device_safety_transition(
 118:     current_state: str | None,
 119:     requested_state: str,
 120:     *,
 121:     proofs: Any = None,
 122:     actor_is_local: bool = True,
 123:     active_suspicion: bool = False,
 124:     now: int | None = None,
 125: ) -> GuardianDecision:
 126:     """Authorize a device safety-state transition.
 127: 
 128:     Freeze/maybe-lost are deliberately quick and reversible. Revocation is
 129:     destructive, so it requires a strong proof unless the device is already
 130:     frozen/quarantined or an explicit suspicious-behavior proof is present.
 131:     """
 132:     _ = now if now is not None else now_ms()
 133:     current = normalize_safety_state(current_state)
 134:     requested = normalize_safety_state(requested_state)
 135:     given = normalize_proofs(proofs)
 136: 
 137:     if current == "revoked" and requested != "revoked":
 138:         return GuardianDecision(
 139:             False,
 140:             current,
 141:             "bad",
 142:             "guardian_transition_denied",
 143:             "revoked devices must be re-enrolled instead of silently restored",
 144:             required_proofs=("re_enroll",),
 145:             effects=("no_state_change",),
 146:             reversible=False,
 147:         )
 148:     if requested == current:
 149:         return GuardianDecision(
 150:             True,
 151:             requested,
 152:             "info",
 153:             "guardian_state_unchanged",
 154:             f"device already {requested}",
 155:             effects=("audit_only",),
 156:             reversible=requested not in DESTRUCTIVE_STATES,
 157:         )
 158:     if requested not in REVERSIBLE_TRANSITIONS.get(current, set()):
 159:         return GuardianDecision(
 160:             False,
 161:             current,
 162:             "bad",
 163:             "guardian_transition_denied",
 164:             f"transition {current}->{requested} is not allowed",
 165:             effects=("no_state_change",),
 166:             reversible=current not in DESTRUCTIVE_STATES,
 167:         )
 168: 
 169:     if requested in {"suspicious", "maybe_lost"}:
 170:         return GuardianDecision(
 171:             True,
 172:             requested,
 173:             "warn",
 174:             f"guardian_{requested}",
 175:             "soft protection enabled; sensitive actions now require extra trust",
 176:             effects=(
 177:                 "remote_sensitive_actions_limited",
 178:                 "audit_visible",
 179:                 "reversible",
 180:             ),
 181:         )
 182: 
 183:     if requested == "frozen":
 184:         if not actor_is_local and PROOF_RECENT_UNLOCK not in given:
 185:             return GuardianDecision(
 186:                 False,
 187:                 current,
 188:                 "bad",
 189:                 "guardian_transition_denied",
 190:                 "remote freeze requires recent local unlock proof",
 191:                 required_proofs=(PROOF_RECENT_UNLOCK,),
 192:                 effects=("no_state_change",),
 193:             )
 194:         return GuardianDecision(
 195:             True,
 196:             requested,
 197:             "bad",
 198:             "guardian_frozen",
 199:             "device frozen; it cannot route, sync, pull files, or run remote commands",
 200:             effects=(
 201:                 "exclude_from_routing",
 202:                 "block_remote_instruct",
 203:                 "block_future_epoch_keys",
 204:                 "audit_visible",
 205:                 "reversible",
 206:             ),
 207:         )
 208: 
 209:     if requested == "revoked":
 210:         strong = bool(given & STRONG_PROOFS)
 211:         frozen_path = current in {"frozen", "quarantined"} and PROOF_ALREADY_FROZEN in given
 212:         suspicion_path = active_suspicion and PROOF_SUSPICIOUS_BEHAVIOR in given
 213:         if not (strong or frozen_path or suspicion_path):
 214:             return GuardianDecision(
 215:                 False,
 216:                 current,
 217:                 "bad",
 218:                 "guardian_revoke_pending",
 219:                 "hard revoke needs recovery, quorum, hardware-key, or already-frozen proof",
 220:                 required_proofs=tuple(sorted(STRONG_PROOFS | {PROOF_ALREADY_FROZEN})),
 221:                 effects=("no_state_change", "offer_freeze_first"),
 222:                 reversible=False,
 223:                 cooldown_ms=2 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
 224:             )
 225:         return GuardianDecision(
 226:             True,
 227:             requested,
 228:             "bad",
 229:             "guardian_revoked",
 230:             "device permanently removed from trust; re-enrollment is required to return",
 231:             effects=(
 232:                 "exclude_from_routing",
 233:                 "block_remote_instruct",
 234:                 "block_future_epoch_keys",
 235:                 "require_reenrollment",
 236:                 "audit_visible",
 237:             ),
 238:             reversible=False,
 239:         )
 240: 
 241:     if requested == "recovered":
 242:         return GuardianDecision(
 243:             True,
 244:             requested,
 245:             "good",
 246:             "guardian_recovered",
 247:             "device marked recovered; re-proof before returning to full trust",
 248:             effects=("remote_sensitive_actions_limited", "audit_visible"),
 249:         )
 250: 
 251:     if requested == "trusted":
 252:         if current in {"frozen", "quarantined", "maybe_lost"} and not (
 253:             given & {PROOF_RECENT_UNLOCK, PROOF_RECOVERY_SECRET, PROOF_HARDWARE_KEY}
 254:         ):
 255:             return GuardianDecision(
 256:                 False,
 257:                 current,
 258:                 "warn",
 259:                 "guardian_recovery_pending",
 260:                 "restoring trust requires recent unlock, recovery, or hardware-key proof",
 261:                 required_proofs=(PROOF_RECENT_UNLOCK, PROOF_RECOVERY_SECRET, PROOF_HARDWARE_KEY),
 262:                 effects=("no_state_change",),
 263:             )
 264:         return GuardianDecision(
 265:             True,
 266:             requested,
 267:             "good",
 268:             "guardian_trusted",
 269:             "device returned to trusted state",
 270:             effects=("routing_allowed", "remote_instruct_allowed", "audit_visible"),
 271:         )
 272: 
 273:     if requested == "quarantined":
 274:         return GuardianDecision(
 275:             True,
 276:             requested,
 277:             "bad",
 278:             "guardian_quarantined",
 279:             "device quarantined after suspicious behavior",
 280:             effects=("exclude_from_routing", "block_remote_instruct", "audit_visible"),
 281:         )
 282: 
 283:     raise ValueError(f"unhandled guardian transition {current}->{requested}")
 284: 
 285: 
 286: def safety_blocks_routing(state: str | None) -> bool:
 287:     return normalize_safety_state(state) in ROUTE_BLOCK_STATES
 288: 
 289: 
 290: def safety_blocks_remote_instruction(state: str | None) -> bool:
 291:     return normalize_safety_state(state) in REMOTE_BLOCK_STATES
 292: 
 293: 
 294: def safety_score_penalty(state: str | None) -> float:
 295:     value = normalize_safety_state(state)
 296:     if value in {"suspicious", "recovered"}:
 297:         return 80.0
 298:     return 0.0

   1: """Cross-platform device-type detection for One Link.
   2: 
   3: Each daemon advertises a stable, human-meaningful device kind in
   4: its mDNS TXT record (and richer detail in its CAPS frame), so the
   5: pair-a-new-device list can show "Alex's MacBook Pro" instead of
   6: "30f968ee · 192.168.1.142".
   7: 
   8: Detection is best-effort and never raises — every probe is wrapped
   9: so a missing tool / permission denial / quirky platform falls back
  10: to a sensible default. The output is a `DeviceInfo` dataclass with:
  11: 
  12:   os:        windows | macos | linux | bsd | ios | android | other
  13:   kind:      desktop | laptop | server | mobile | tablet | embedded | unknown
  14:   vendor:    e.g. "Apple", "Lenovo", "Dell" — empty if unknown
  15:   model:     e.g. "MacBookPro18,1", "ThinkPad X1" — empty if unknown
  16:   arch:      x86_64 | arm64 | armv7 | unknown
  17:   display:   pretty short label, e.g. "MacBook Pro" / "Windows laptop"
  18: 
  19: The compact form for the mDNS TXT record is `<os>-<kind>` (e.g.
  20: `macos-laptop`); the full DeviceInfo travels post-handshake in the
  21: CAPS frame so a peer can render the rich label.
  22: """
  23: from __future__ import annotations
  24: 
  25: import contextlib
  26: import os
  27: import platform
  28: import subprocess
  29: import sys
  30: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  31: from pathlib import Path
  32: from typing import Any
  33: 
  34: from one_link.platform_guard import install_windows_platform_fastpath
  35: 
  36: install_windows_platform_fastpath()
  37: 
  38: 
  39: @dataclass
  40: class DeviceInfo:
  41:     os: str = "other"            # windows | macos | linux | bsd | ios | android | other
  42:     kind: str = "unknown"        # desktop | laptop | server | mobile | tablet | embedded | unknown
  43:     vendor: str = ""
  44:     model: str = ""
  45:     arch: str = "unknown"
  46:     display: str = ""            # pretty short label
  47: 
  48:     def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, str]:
  49:         return {
  50:             "os": self.os,
  51:             "kind": self.kind,
  52:             "vendor": self.vendor,
  53:             "model": self.model,
  54:             "arch": self.arch,
  55:             "display": self.display,
  56:         }
  57: 
  58:     @classmethod
  59:     def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any] | None) -> "DeviceInfo":
  60:         if not d:
  61:             return cls()
  62:         return cls(
  63:             os=str(d.get("os", "other")),
  64:             kind=str(d.get("kind", "unknown")),
  65:             vendor=str(d.get("vendor", "")),
  66:             model=str(d.get("model", "")),
  67:             arch=str(d.get("arch", "unknown")),
  68:             display=str(d.get("display", "")),
  69:         )
  70: 
  71:     def compact(self) -> str:
  72:         """Compact `<os>-<kind>` for the mDNS TXT record. Bounded
  73:         length, no special chars — safe across mDNS implementations."""
  74:         return f"{self.os}-{self.kind}"
  75: 
  76: 
  77: # ─── platform-specific probes ──────────────────────────────────────
  78: 
  79: def _normalize_arch() -> str:
  80:     m = (platform.machine() or "").lower()
  81:     if m in ("amd64", "x86_64", "x64"):
  82:         return "x86_64"
  83:     if m in ("arm64", "aarch64"):
  84:         return "arm64"
  85:     if m.startswith("armv7") or m.startswith("armv6"):
  86:         return "armv7"
  87:     if m in ("i386", "i686", "x86"):
  88:         return "x86"
  89:     return m or "unknown"
  90: 
  91: 
  92: def _safe_run(cmd: list[str], *, timeout: float = 1.5) -> str:
  93:     """Run a small command, return stdout or empty string on any
  94:     error. Bounded; never blocks the daemon startup if a tool hangs.
  95: 
  96:     On Windows we pass CREATE_NO_WINDOW so the probe doesn't flash a
  97:     conhost window when the daemon shells out to wmic / powershell /
  98:     PnPUtil for system info."""
  99:     import os as _os
 100:     creationflags = 0x08000000 if _os.name == "nt" else 0
 101:     try:
 102:         out = subprocess.run(
 103:             cmd,
 104:             capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
 105:             timeout=timeout,
 106:             creationflags=creationflags,
 107:         )
 108:         return (out.stdout or "").strip()
 109:     except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError, OSError, Exception):
 110:         return ""
 111: 
 112: 
 113: # ─── Windows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 114: 
 115: # DMI / WMI Win32_ComputerSystem.PCSystemType:
 116: #   0 = Unspecified, 1 = Desktop, 2 = Mobile (laptop),
 117: #   3 = Workstation, 4 = Enterprise Server, 5 = SOHO Server,
 118: #   6 = Appliance PC, 7 = Performance Server, 8 = Maximum
 119: _WIN_PC_TYPE = {
 120:     1: "desktop",
 121:     2: "laptop",
 122:     3: "desktop",     # Workstation = beefy desktop
 123:     4: "server",
 124:     5: "server",
 125:     6: "embedded",
 126:     7: "server",
 127: }

 130: def _detect_windows() -> DeviceInfo:
 131:     info = DeviceInfo(os="windows", arch=_normalize_arch())
 132:     # Battery presence is the most reliable laptop signal on Windows
 133:     # without elevation. Try psutil first; fall back to powershell.
 134:     has_battery = False
 135:     try:
 136:         import psutil  # types-psutil stub package supplies the type info
 137:         b = psutil.sensors_battery()
 138:         has_battery = b is not None
 139:     except Exception:
 140:         # Fall back to a tiny powershell call.
 141:         out = _safe_run([
 142:             "powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command",
 143:             "(Get-CimInstance Win32_Battery).Status",
 144:         ])
 145:         has_battery = bool(out and out.lower() != "null")
 146:     info.kind = "laptop" if has_battery else "desktop"
 147: 
 148:     # Vendor / model / canonical PCSystemType.
 149:     out = _safe_run([
 150:         "powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command",
 151:         "(Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem"
 152:         " | Select-Object -Property Manufacturer,Model,PCSystemType"
 153:         " | ConvertTo-Csv -NoTypeInformation"
 154:         " | Select-Object -Skip 1)",
 155:     ])
 156:     if out:
 157:         # Single CSV row: "Manufacturer","Model","PCSystemType"
 158:         try:
 159:             import csv
 160:             import io
 161:             row = next(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))
 162:             if len(row) >= 1:
 163:                 info.vendor = row[0].strip()
 164:             if len(row) >= 2:
 165:                 info.model = row[1].strip()
 166:             if len(row) >= 3:
 167:                 try:
 168:                     pc_type = int(row[2].strip())
 169:                     info.kind = _WIN_PC_TYPE.get(pc_type, info.kind)
 170:                 except (ValueError, TypeError):
 171:                     pass
 172:         except Exception:
 173:             pass
 174: 
 175:     info.display = _windows_display_label(info)
 176:     return info
 177: 
 178: 
 179: def _windows_display_label(info: DeviceInfo) -> str:
 180:     if info.vendor and info.model:
 181:         return f"{info.vendor} {info.model}"
 182:     if info.model:
 183:         return info.model
 184:     return f"Windows {info.kind}".strip()
 185: 
 186: 
 187: # ─── macOS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 188: 
 189: # Apple model identifiers we care about. The full prefix uniquely
 190: # identifies the line. `iMacPro` is included separately because it
 191: # isn't a regular iMac for kind purposes.
 192: _MAC_LAPTOP_PREFIXES = ("MacBook",)
 193: _MAC_DESKTOP_PREFIXES = (
 194:     "iMac", "iMacPro", "Macmini", "MacPro", "Mac",
 195: )
 196: 
 197: _MAC_PRETTY = {
 198:     "MacBookPro": "MacBook Pro",
 199:     "MacBookAir": "MacBook Air",
 200:     "MacBook": "MacBook",
 201:     "iMacPro": "iMac Pro",
 202:     "iMac": "iMac",
 203:     "Macmini": "Mac mini",
 204:     "MacPro": "Mac Pro",
 205:     "Mac": "Mac",         # Apple silicon Studio shows as Mac<N>,<M>
 206: }
 207: 
 208: 
 209: def _detect_macos() -> DeviceInfo:
 210:     info = DeviceInfo(os="macos", vendor="Apple", arch=_normalize_arch())
 211:     raw = _safe_run(["sysctl", "-n", "hw.model"])
 212:     info.model = raw or ""
 213:     # Pretty prefix is the longest match — "MacBookPro18,1" should
 214:     # match "MacBookPro" before "MacBook".
 215:     pretty = "Mac"
 216:     for prefix in sorted(_MAC_PRETTY, key=len, reverse=True):
 217:         if raw.startswith(prefix):
 218:             pretty = _MAC_PRETTY[prefix]
 219:             break
 220:     if any(raw.startswith(p) for p in _MAC_LAPTOP_PREFIXES):
 221:         info.kind = "laptop"
 222:     elif any(raw.startswith(p) for p in _MAC_DESKTOP_PREFIXES):
 223:         info.kind = "desktop"
 224:     else:
 225:         # Apple silicon Mac Studio shows as Mac14,13 etc — desktop.
 226:         info.kind = "desktop" if raw.startswith("Mac") else "unknown"
 227:     info.display = pretty
 228:     return info
 229:

 231: # ─── Linux ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 232: 
 233: # DMI chassis_type codes per SMBIOS spec.
 234: #   3 Desktop, 4 Low-profile Desktop, 5 Pizza Box, 6 Mini Tower,
 235: #   7 Tower, 8 Portable, 9 Laptop, 10 Notebook, 11 Hand Held,
 236: #   12 Docking Station, 13 All-in-One, 14 Sub Notebook,
 237: #   15 Space-saving, 16 Lunch Box, 17 Main Server Chassis,
 238: #   18 Expansion Chassis, 19 SubChassis, 20 Bus Expansion,
 239: #   21 Peripheral, 22 RAID, 23 Rack Mount, 24 Sealed Case PC,
 240: #   30 Tablet, 31 Convertible, 32 Detachable
 241: _DMI_CHASSIS = {
 242:     3: "desktop", 4: "desktop", 5: "desktop", 6: "desktop", 7: "desktop",
 243:     8: "laptop", 9: "laptop", 10: "laptop", 14: "laptop",
 244:     11: "mobile",
 245:     13: "desktop",
 246:     17: "server", 23: "server",
 247:     30: "tablet", 31: "laptop", 32: "tablet",
 248:     24: "embedded",
 249: }
 250: 
 251: 
 252: def _read_dmi(name: str) -> str:
 253:     p = Path(f"/sys/class/dmi/id/{name}")
 254:     try:
 255:         return p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").strip()
 256:     except OSError:
 257:         return ""
 258: 
 259: 
 260: def _detect_linux() -> DeviceInfo:
 261:     info = DeviceInfo(os="linux", arch=_normalize_arch())
 262:     # Battery → laptop is a strong default before DMI.
 263:     bat_glob = list(Path("/sys/class/power_supply").glob("BAT*")) \
 264:         if Path("/sys/class/power_supply").is_dir() else []
 265:     info.kind = "laptop" if bat_glob else "desktop"
 266:     # DMI overrides if present + parseable.
 267:     chassis_raw = _read_dmi("chassis_type")
 268:     try:
 269:         chassis_int = int(chassis_raw)
 270:         kind = _DMI_CHASSIS.get(chassis_int)
 271:         if kind:
 272:             info.kind = kind
 273:     except (ValueError, TypeError):
 274:         pass
 275:     info.vendor = _read_dmi("sys_vendor") or _read_dmi("chassis_vendor")
 276:     product = _read_dmi("product_name") or _read_dmi("board_name")
 277:     info.model = product
 278:     # Heuristic: if hostname contains "server" or "rpi" / "raspi"
 279:     # signals; respect the DMI answer first, fall back to hostname.
 280:     hn = (platform.node() or "").lower()
 281:     if info.kind == "desktop" and ("server" in hn or "kube" in hn or "k8s" in hn):
 282:         info.kind = "server"
 283:     if "raspberrypi" in hn or "raspi" in hn or info.model.lower().startswith("raspberry"):
 284:         info.kind = "embedded"
 285:         info.vendor = info.vendor or "Raspberry Pi"
 286:     info.display = _linux_display_label(info)
 287:     return info
 288: 
 289: 
 290: def _linux_display_label(info: DeviceInfo) -> str:
 291:     if info.vendor and info.model:
 292:         return f"{info.vendor} {info.model}".strip()
 293:     if info.model:
 294:         return info.model
 295:     return f"Linux {info.kind}".strip()
 296: 
 297: 
 298: # ─── BSD / others (best-effort) ────────────────────────────────────
 299: 
 300: def _detect_bsd() -> DeviceInfo:
 301:     info = DeviceInfo(os="bsd", arch=_normalize_arch())
 302:     info.model = platform.platform() or ""
 303:     info.kind = "desktop"  # no easy laptop probe; user can override
 304:     info.display = info.model or "BSD"
 305:     return info
 306: 
 307: 
 308: def _detect_other() -> DeviceInfo:
 309:     return DeviceInfo(
 310:         os="other", arch=_normalize_arch(),
 311:         kind="unknown", display=platform.platform() or "Unknown device",
 312:     )
 313: 
 314: 
 315: # ─── public entry point ───────────────────────────────────────────
 316: 
 317: _CACHED: DeviceInfo | None = None
 318: 
 319: 
 320: def detect(*, force: bool = False) -> DeviceInfo:
 321:     """Return DeviceInfo for the local machine. Cached after first
 322:     call (detection probes are mildly expensive on Windows + Linux).
 323:     Pass `force=True` to re-probe."""
 324:     global _CACHED
 325:     if _CACHED is not None and not force:
 326:         return _CACHED
 327:     sys_name = (sys.platform or "").lower()
 328:     try:
 329:         if sys_name.startswith("win"):
 330:             info = _detect_windows()
 331:         elif sys_name == "darwin":
 332:             info = _detect_macos()
 333:         elif sys_name.startswith("linux"):
 334:             info = _detect_linux()
 335:         elif sys_name.endswith("bsd") or sys_name == "freebsd":
 336:             info = _detect_bsd()
 337:         else:
 338:             info = _detect_other()
 339:     except Exception:
 340:         info = DeviceInfo()
 341:     if not info.display:
 342:         info.display = f"{info.os} {info.kind}".strip()
 343:     _CACHED = info
 344:     return info
 345:
