 239: 
 240: @dataclass
 241: class BrowserPeer:
 242:     """Live state for a single browser-as-peer connection."""
 243:     fingerprint: str          # sha256:<hex>
 244:     pubkey_bytes: bytes       # 32 bytes raw
 245:     pc: Any = None            # aiortc.RTCPeerConnection
 246:     control_dc: Any = None    # aiortc.RTCDataChannel — the post-connect
 247:                               # control channel we receive from the
 248:                               # browser (or open ourselves if initiator)
 249:     bulk_dc: Any = None       # aiortc.RTCDataChannel
 250:     connected_ms: int = field(default_factory=_now_ms)
 251:     last_activity_ms: int = field(default_factory=_now_ms)
 252:     paired_ms: Optional[int] = None  # set once pairing token redeemed
 253:                                      # OR pubkey already in roster
 254:     closed: bool = False
 255:     # Row 10 — peer-handshake attestation state.
 256:     # `attestation_challenge`: 32-byte nonce we sent the peer.
 257:     #   Populated when we initiate; checked when their response arrives.
 258:     # `attested_ms`: monotonic timestamp when verification passed.
 259:     #   None until the peer's attest_response has verified.
 260:     # `peer_master_vk`: 1984-byte hybrid VK extracted from a verified
 261:     #   attestation doc. None until attested. Pin this to detect
 262:     #   master-key rotation across reconnects.
 263:     attestation_challenge: Optional[bytes] = None
 264:     # Audit M9 May 2026: bind the in-flight challenge to the
 265:     # specific control DC instance it was sent on (the `id()` of the
 266:     # DC object at issue time). A peer reconnecting mid-handshake
 267:     # creates a NEW DC instance; binding to it prevents the new DC
 268:     # from accidentally accepting a response signed against the old
 269:     # DC's challenge (cross-DC confusion).
 270:     attestation_challenge_dc_id: Optional[int] = None
 271:     attested_ms: Optional[int] = None
 272:     peer_master_vk: Optional[bytes] = None
 273:     # Wall-clock unix seconds when the accepted attestation doc
 274:     # expires. Stored so the gate can re-check freshness on every
 275:     # dispatched message — without this, an attacker who succeeds
 276:     # ONCE within the 30s window can ride that "attested" state
 277:     # indefinitely (audit H7 May 2026).
 278:     attestation_deadline_unix: Optional[int] = None
 279:     # Per-peer rate-limit state for expensive control-DC frames
 280:     # (audit H9 May 2026: attest_challenge invokes the hybrid
 281:     # signing path which holds a process-wide GIL/native lock; an
 282:     # unauthenticated peer flooding challenges can stall every
 283:     # legitimate sign). Tracks (window_start_sec, count_in_window).
 284:     _attest_challenge_window_start: int = 0
 285:     _attest_challenge_count: int = 0
 286:     # H8 May 2026: cover_packet handler runs Sphinx peel (~100µs
 287:     # per packet); flood-protect on the same model.
 288:     _cover_packet_window_start: int = 0
 289:     _cover_packet_count: int = 0
 290:     # Row 6/7 — peer's Sphinx onion public key (Ristretto255 32-byte
 291:     # compressed point). Each peer publishes theirs on DC-open via
 292:     # the `onion_pubkey` envelope; we record the other side's so
 293:     # cover-traffic emission can build real Sphinx packets bound
 294:     # for them (instead of looping back to self).
 295:     onion_pubkey: Optional[bytes] = None
 296:     onion_pubkey_received_ms: Optional[int] = None
 297:     # Audit L7 May 2026: timestamp (unix seconds) of the last
 298:     # protocol-skew log we emitted for this peer. Rate-limits log
 299:     # spam if a peer floods bad-version frames.
 300:     _last_protocol_skew_log_s: int = 0
 301: 
 302: 
 303: # ── manager ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 304: 
 305: 
 306: class BrowserPeerManager:
 307:     """Single-process registry of active browser-as-peer connections
 308:     + the pairing-token store. Wraps aiortc imports lazily so a daemon
 309:     that doesn't ship aiortc still imports `peer_rtc` for the constants
 310:     + helpers."""
 311: 
 312:     def __init__(self, daemon: Any):
 313:         self.daemon = daemon
 314:         self._peers: dict[str, BrowserPeer] = {}    # fingerprint → BrowserPeer
 315:         self._pending_pairings: dict[str, PendingPair] = {}
 316:         self._dc_listeners: list[
 317:             Callable[[BrowserPeer, str, str, dict], Awaitable[None]]
 318:         ] = []
 319:         # `_paired_pubkeys`: persistent set of fingerprints that have
 320:         # already redeemed a pairing token at any point. Tracks the
 321:         # "this browser has been paired before" identity. Persistence
 322:         # to disk is wired in v0.20.2 — for v0.20.0 we keep in-memory
 323:         # only.
 324:         self._paired_pubkeys: set[str] = set()
 325:         # Audit C1 defense-in-depth: track the DTLS-SRTP fingerprint
 326:         # extracted from each peer's most-recent SDP offer. The
 327:         # envelope signature already binds the SDP to the peer's
 328:         # Ed25519 pubkey, so any silent change here would itself
 329:         # carry the same Ed25519 sig. The check is belt-and-suspenders
 330:         # — log + record on first observation; warn (but don't refuse)
 331:         # on subsequent changes since legitimate cert rotations DO
 332:         # happen on browser restart. Hard rejection lives upstream
 333:         # at the envelope-signature + pubkey-roster gates.
 334:         self._dtls_fingerprints: dict[str, str] = {}
 335:         # Audit I4 May 2026 — explicit replay cache for accepted
 336:         # attestation docs. Keyed by BLAKE3(master_sig) — collisions
 337:         # are vanishingly unlikely (2^-256). Each entry stores the
 338:         # acceptance wall-clock-ms so the cache self-prunes against
 339:         # ``ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_TTL_MS``. Without this, the sole
 340:         # defense against in-flight replay was the per-peer
 341:         # `attestation_challenge = None` clear (peer_rtc.py:807) —
 342:         # if a future refactor forgot that line, the 30-second
 343:         # challenge window would re-open silently. The cache is
 344:         # belt-and-suspenders.
 345:         self._seen_doc_ids: "dict[bytes, int]" = {}
 346:         # Audit I6 May 2026 — per-master-vk monotonic-issued-unix
 347:         # fork detection. A legitimate single-daemon issuer's docs
 348:         # produce non-decreasing `issued_unix` (modulo small clock
 349:         # skew). Two daemons claiming the same master_vk (a fork or
 350:         # cloned identity) will eventually produce a doc with an
 351:         # `issued_unix` that regresses below what we've already
 352:         # observed for that vk. Rejecting on regression detects
 353:         # forks without a wire-format change. Tolerates up to
 354:         # MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECS (5s, matches the I3 issuer-skew
 355:         # bound) of natural NTP wobble before flagging.
 356:         self._master_vk_last_issued_unix: "dict[bytes, int]" = {}
 357: 
 358:     # Audit I4 May 2026 — replay-cache TTL (ms). Comfortably exceeds
 359:     # the 30s ATTESTATION_FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECS so the cache strictly
 360:     # outlives the validity window of any doc it remembers.
 361:     ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_TTL_MS: int = 5 * 60 * 1000
 362:     # Hard cap on cache size — flood-defense companion to the TTL
 363:     # sweep. Drops oldest-first when exceeded.
 364:     ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES: int = 16_384
 365:     # Audit I6 May 2026 — tolerance for natural NTP wobble in the
 366:     # monotonic-issued-unix fork-detection check. Matches the I3
 367:     # issuer-clock-skew bound exactly so the two checks share a
 368:     # consistent tolerance.
 369:     ATTESTATION_FORK_MAX_BACKWARDS_SECS: int = 5
 370: 
 371:     def _attestation_doc_id(self, master_sig: bytes) -> bytes:
 372:         """Audit I4 — SHA-256 over a domain-tagged copy of
 373:         ``master_sig``. Used purely as an internal map key; the
 374:         security property is collision-resistance (so distinct sigs
 375:         can't collide) + preimage-resistance (so cache contents
 376:         don't directly leak sigs). SHA-256 is stdlib so the cache
 377:         works even when the native module is absent."""
 378:         import hashlib
 379:         return hashlib.sha256(
 380:             b"ol-attest-replay-cache-v1" + master_sig
 381:         ).digest()
 382: 
 383:     def _attestation_replay_check_and_record(self, master_sig: bytes) -> bool:
 384:         """Returns True iff this doc has NOT been seen before.
 385: 
 386:         Side-effect: on a fresh doc, records the id with the current
 387:         wall-clock; on a repeat, leaves the cache untouched. Sweeps
 388:         expired entries opportunistically (no background timer)."""
 389:         doc_id = self._attestation_doc_id(master_sig)
 390:         now_ms = _now_ms()
 391:         # Sweep expired entries first (bounded work: at most one
 392:         # full traversal every ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_TTL_MS).
 393:         if self._seen_doc_ids:
 394:             cutoff = now_ms - self.ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_TTL_MS
 395:             dead = [k for k, t in self._seen_doc_ids.items() if t < cutoff]
 396:             for k in dead:
 397:                 self._seen_doc_ids.pop(k, None)
 398:         if doc_id in self._seen_doc_ids:
 399:             return False
 400:         # Bound the cache size with oldest-first eviction (matches
 401:         # the M11 OrderedDict pattern in cap_store; here we use a
 402:         # plain dict ordered by insertion since Python 3.7+ preserves
 403:         # it).
 404:         if len(self._seen_doc_ids) >= self.ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES:
 405:             drop_n = self.ATTESTATION_REPLAY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES // 10
 406:             for k in list(self._seen_doc_ids.keys())[:drop_n]:
 407:                 self._seen_doc_ids.pop(k, None)
 408:         self._seen_doc_ids[doc_id] = now_ms
 409:         return True
 410: 
 411:     # ── pairing tokens ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 412: 
 413:     def mint_pairing_token(self, fp_hint: Optional[str] = None) -> PendingPair:
 414:         """Mint a fresh single-use pairing token. The laptop UI
 415:         renders this into a QR for the user to scan with their phone."""
 416:         token = _b64u(secrets.token_bytes(PAIRING_TOKEN_BYTES))
 417:         pp = PendingPair(token=token, created_ms=_now_ms(), fp_hint=fp_hint)
 418:         self._pending_pairings[token] = pp
 419:         log.info("peer-rtc: minted pairing token (ttl=%dms)", pp.ttl_ms)
 420:         # Sweep expired tokens opportunistically — keeps memory bounded
 421:         # without a background sweeper task.
 422:         self._sweep_expired_pairings()
 423:         if len(self._pending_pairings) > MAX_PENDING_PAIRING_TOKENS:
 424:             oldest = sorted(
 425:                 self._pending_pairings.items(),
 426:                 key=lambda item: item[1].created_ms,
 427:             )
 428:             overflow = len(self._pending_pairings) - MAX_PENDING_PAIRING_TOKENS
 429:             for old_token, _old in oldest[:overflow]:
 430:                 self._pending_pairings.pop(old_token, None)
 431:         return pp
 432: 
 433:     def _sweep_expired_pairings(self) -> int:
 434:         now = _now_ms()
 435:         expired = [t for t, pp in self._pending_pairings.items() if pp.expired(now)]
 436:         for t in expired:
 437:             self._pending_pairings.pop(t, None)
 438:         return len(expired)
 439: 
 440:     def redeem_pairing_token(self, token: str) -> Optional[PendingPair]:
 441:         """Try to redeem a pairing token. Returns the PendingPair on
 442:         success (consuming it) or None if missing/expired."""
 443:         if not token:
 444:             return None
 445:         pp = self._pending_pairings.pop(token, None)
 446:         if pp is None:
 447:             return None
 448:         if pp.expired():
 449:             return None
 450:         return pp
 451: 
 452:     # ── peer registry ───────────────────────────────────────────────
 453: 
 454:     def register_peer(self, peer: BrowserPeer) -> None:
 455:         existing = self._peers.get(peer.fingerprint)
 456:         if existing is not None and existing is not peer:
 457:             # Newest connection wins. Tear down the old one.
 458:             log.info(
 459:                 "peer-rtc: replacing existing connection for %s",
 460:                 peer.fingerprint,
 461:             )
 462:             self._close_peer(existing)
 463:         self._peers[peer.fingerprint] = peer
 464: 
 465:     def is_paired(self, fingerprint: str) -> bool:
 466:         return fingerprint in self._paired_pubkeys
 467: 
 468:     def mark_paired(self, fingerprint: str) -> None:
 469:         self._paired_pubkeys.add(fingerprint)
 470: 
 471:     def get_peer(self, fingerprint: str) -> Optional[BrowserPeer]:
 472:         return self._peers.get(fingerprint)
 473: 
 474:     def list_peers(self) -> list[BrowserPeer]:
 475:         return list(self._peers.values())
 476: 
 477:     def _close_peer(self, peer: BrowserPeer) -> None:
 478:         if peer.closed:
 479:             return
 480:         peer.closed = True
 481:         pc = peer.pc
 482:         if pc is not None:
 483:             try:
 484:                 # aiortc's pc.close is async; schedule it.
 485:                 loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
 486:                 loop.create_task(pc.close())
 487:             except Exception as e:
 488:                 log.debug("peer-rtc: pc.close error for %s: %s", peer.fingerprint, e)
 489:         self._peers.pop(peer.fingerprint, None)
 490: 
 491:     # ── DataChannel listener registry ──────────────────────────────
 492: 
 493:     def add_dc_listener(
 494:         self,
 495:         cb: Callable[[BrowserPeer, str, str, dict], Awaitable[None]],
 496:     ) -> None:
 497:         """Register a callback invoked when a DataChannel message
 498:         arrives from any browser peer. Signature:
 499:             cb(peer, channel_kind, msg_t, payload_dict)
 500:         Channel kind is "control" or "bulk". Payload is the parsed
 501:         JSON envelope minus the version + type."""
 502:         self._dc_listeners.append(cb)
 503: 
 504:     # ── Gate helpers (audit H7/H8/H9 May 2026) ─────────────────────
 505: 
 506:     def _gate_app_or_attested(
 507:         self, peer: BrowserPeer, msg_t: str
 508:     ) -> bool:
 509:         """Audit H7 + the attestation gate. Returns True if the
 510:         message should be processed, False if it must be dropped.
 511: 
 512:         Two combined checks:
 513:         - If ``require_attested_peers=True`` and peer hasn't yet
 514:           attested, drop.
 515:         - If peer HAS attested but the stored
 516:           ``attestation_deadline_unix`` has passed, drop AND clear
 517:           the attested state so a fresh attestation is required.
 518: 
 519:         H7 closes the gap where a peer that attested once within
 520:         the 30 s freshness window could ride that "attested" state
 521:         forever. The 30 s window from the attestation doc is the
 522:         peer's freshness promise; treating it as a one-shot opens
 523:         a forever-impersonation window after a single capture of
 524:         an attestation round.
 525:         """
 526:         # H7 — even when require_attested_peers is OFF, expire stale
 527:         # attestation state so onion/cover-packet handlers don't
 528:         # ride a long-dead doc.
 529:         now_unix = int(time.time())
 530:         dl = peer.attestation_deadline_unix
 531:         if peer.attested_ms is not None and dl is not None and now_unix > dl:
 532:             log.info(
 533:                 "peer-rtc: attestation for %s expired (deadline=%d, "
 534:                 "now=%d); clearing attested state",
 535:                 peer.fingerprint, dl, now_unix,
 536:             )
 537:             peer.attested_ms = None
 538:             peer.attestation_deadline_unix = None
 539:             # peer_master_vk stays pinned (audit C2 TOFU); a
 540:             # re-attestation must match it.
 541:         if getattr(self.daemon, "require_attested_peers", False):
 542:             if peer.attested_ms is None:
 543:                 # Audit L8 May 2026: take the daemon's telemetry
 544:                 # lock to serialize the read-modify-write across
 545:                 # asyncio + cover background thread.
 546:                 lock = getattr(self.daemon, "_telemetry_lock", None)
 547:                 if lock is not None:
 548:                     with lock:
 549:                         cnt = getattr(self.daemon, "_gate_drop_count", 0)
 550:                         try:
 551:                             self.daemon._gate_drop_count = cnt + 1
 552:                         except Exception:
 553:                             pass
 554:                 else:
 555:                     cnt = getattr(self.daemon, "_gate_drop_count", 0)
 556:                     try:
 557:                         self.daemon._gate_drop_count = cnt + 1
 558:                     except Exception:
 559:                         pass
 560:                 log.info(
 561:                     "peer-rtc: dropped %r from un-attested peer %s "
 562:                     "(require_attested_peers=on, drops=%d)",
 563:                     msg_t, peer.fingerprint,
 564:                     getattr(self.daemon, "_gate_drop_count", 0),
 565:                 )
 566:                 return False
 567:         return True
 568: 
 569:     def _allow_attest_challenge(self, peer: BrowserPeer) -> bool:
 570:         """H9 May 2026: per-peer rate-limit on attest_challenge so a
 571:         flood can't pin the native signing lock."""
 572:         now = int(time.time())
 573:         if now - peer._attest_challenge_window_start >= ATTEST_CHALLENGE_WINDOW_SECS:
 574:             peer._attest_challenge_window_start = now
 575:             peer._attest_challenge_count = 0
 576:         peer._attest_challenge_count += 1
 577:         return peer._attest_challenge_count <= ATTEST_CHALLENGE_MAX_PER_WINDOW
 578: 
 579:     def _allow_cover_packet(self, peer: BrowserPeer) -> bool:
 580:         """H8 May 2026: per-peer rate-limit on cover_packet so a
 581:         flood can't saturate Sphinx-peel CPU."""
 582:         now = int(time.time())
 583:         if now - peer._cover_packet_window_start >= COVER_PACKET_WINDOW_SECS:
 584:             peer._cover_packet_window_start = now
 585:             peer._cover_packet_count = 0
 586:         peer._cover_packet_count += 1
 587:         return peer._cover_packet_count <= COVER_PACKET_MAX_PER_WINDOW
 588: 
 589:     async def _dispatch_dc(
 590:         self, peer: BrowserPeer, channel_kind: str, raw: Any
 591:     ) -> None:
 592:         try:
 593:             if isinstance(raw, bytes):
 594:                 raw = raw.decode("utf-8")
 595:             if isinstance(raw, str) and len(raw.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")) > MAX_DC_TEXT_BYTES:
 596:                 log.warning("peer-rtc: oversized DC frame from %s", peer.fingerprint)
 597:                 return
 598:             envelope = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else None
 599:         except Exception as e:
 600:             log.debug("peer-rtc: bad DC frame from %s: %s", peer.fingerprint, e)
 601:             return
 602:         if not isinstance(envelope, dict):
 603:             return
 604:         wire_v = envelope.get("v")
 605:         if wire_v != PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION:
 606:             # Audit L7 May 2026: surface protocol-skew rather than
 607:             # silently drop. A future-version peer (v=OL-PEER-2)
 608:             # otherwise vanishes from the operator's view. Per-peer
 609:             # rate-limited log so a hostile flood of bad-version
 610:             # frames can't flood the log either.
 611:             now = int(time.time())
 612:             last = getattr(peer, "_last_protocol_skew_log_s", 0)
 613:             if now - last >= 60:
 614:                 log.info(
 615:                     "peer-rtc: dropping DC frame from %s with "
 616:                     "unsupported protocol version %r (we speak %s); "
 617:                     "peer may need an upgrade or downgrade",
 618:                     peer.fingerprint, wire_v, PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
 619:                 )
 620:                 peer._last_protocol_skew_log_s = now
 621:             return
 622:         msg_t = str(envelope.get("t") or "")
 623:         if not msg_t:
 624:             return
 625:         peer.last_activity_ms = _now_ms()
 626:         # Built-in ping/pong. Always handled; tests for liveness.
 627:         if msg_t == "ping":
 628:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 629:                 self.send_dc(peer, "control", {
 630:                     "v": PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
 631:                     "t": "pong",
 632:                     "ts": _now_ms(),
 633:                     "echo_ts": envelope.get("ts"),
 634:                 })
 635:             return
 636:         # Row 10 — peer-handshake attestation.
 637:         # The other side sends `attest_challenge` (their nonce); we
 638:         # respond with `attest_response` (our doc bound to their
 639:         # nonce). They send `attest_response` for OUR nonce; we
 640:         # verify + mark them attested.
 641:         #
 642:         # H9 (audit May 2026): attest_challenge invokes the hybrid
 643:         # signing path (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65, ~1–5 ms wall) under a
 644:         # process-wide native lock. An unauthenticated peer flooding
 645:         # challenges stalls every legit signer in the daemon. Apply a
 646:         # per-peer token bucket: ATTEST_CHALLENGE_MAX_PER_WINDOW per
 647:         # ATTEST_CHALLENGE_WINDOW_SECS, drop the rest.
 648:         if msg_t == "attest_challenge":
 649:             if not self._allow_attest_challenge(peer):
 650:                 log.info(
 651:                     "peer-rtc: rate-limited attest_challenge from %s",
 652:                     peer.fingerprint,
 653:                 )
 654:                 return
 655:             await self._handle_attest_challenge(peer, envelope)
 656:             return
 657:         if msg_t == "attest_response":
 658:             await self._handle_attest_response(peer, envelope)
 659:             return
 660:         # H8 + H10 (audit May 2026): onion_pubkey + cover_packet are
 661:         # NOT control-plane bootstrap — they are part of the running
 662:         # mesh state. Require attestation before accepting either,
 663:         # AND rate-limit cover_packet (Sphinx peel is ~100 µs/packet,
 664:         # an unauthenticated flood saturates a core).
 665:         if msg_t == "onion_pubkey":
 666:             if not self._gate_app_or_attested(peer, msg_t):
 667:                 return
 668:             await self._handle_onion_pubkey(peer, envelope)
 669:             return
 670:         if msg_t == "cover_packet":
 671:             if not self._gate_app_or_attested(peer, msg_t):
 672:                 return
 673:             if not self._allow_cover_packet(peer):
 674:                 log.info(
 675:                     "peer-rtc: rate-limited cover_packet from %s",
 676:                     peer.fingerprint,
 677:                 )
 678:                 return
 679:             await self._handle_cover_packet(peer, envelope)
 680:             return
 681:         # Row 10 — attestation gate. When the daemon requires
 682:         # attested peers, app-layer messages from peers that haven't
 683:         # completed the handshake are dropped. Control-plane
 684:         # messages (ping/pong, attest_challenge, attest_response)
 685:         # already returned above so the gate only sees app traffic.
 686:         if not self._gate_app_or_attested(peer, msg_t):
 687:             return
 688:         # Fan out to registered listeners (chat, files, etc. wire in
 689:         # v0.20.2+).
 690:         for cb in list(self._dc_listeners):
 691:             try:
 692:                 await cb(peer, channel_kind, msg_t, envelope)
 693:             except Exception as e:
 694:                 log.warning("peer-rtc: dc listener raised: %s", e)
 695: 
 696:     # ── Row 10 attestation ───────────────────────────────────────────
 697: 
 698:     def init_attestation(self, peer: BrowserPeer) -> bool:
 699:         """Generate a fresh challenge nonce + send it to the peer.
 700:         Callers invoke this once the DC is open. Returns ``True`` if
 701:         the challenge was sent, ``False`` if the daemon can't attest
 702:         (no sealed master or native ext not built). Safe to call
 703:         multiple times — overwrites the previous challenge so a
 704:         stale one doesn't cause cross-flow confusion."""
 705:         try:
 706:             from one_link.handshake_attestation import fresh_challenge_for_peer
 707:             import base64
 708:         except ImportError:
 709:             return False
 710:         try:
 711:             nonce = fresh_challenge_for_peer()
 712:         except Exception as e:
 713:             log.info("peer-rtc: init_attestation skipped (%s)", e)
 714:             return False
 715:         peer.attestation_challenge = nonce
 716:         # Audit M9 May 2026: record which DC instance the challenge
 717:         # was issued on so a response on a NEW DC (e.g. after
 718:         # reconnect) is treated as cross-flow and rejected.
 719:         peer.attestation_challenge_dc_id = (
 720:             id(peer.control_dc) if peer.control_dc is not None else None
 721:         )
 722:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 723:             self.send_dc(peer, "control", {
 724:                 "v": PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
 725:                 "t": "attest_challenge",
 726:                 "ts": _now_ms(),
 727:                 "challenge_b64": base64.b64encode(nonce).decode("ascii"),
 728:             })
 729:         return True
 730: 
 731:     async def _handle_attest_challenge(
 732:         self, peer: BrowserPeer, envelope: dict
 733:     ) -> None:
 734:         """Peer sent us their challenge; we respond with our doc
 735:         bound to their nonce AND to our own SDP-layer Ed25519 pubkey
 736:         (audit C1)."""
 737:         try:
 738:             import base64
 739:             from one_link.handshake_attestation import (
 740:                 AttestationWire,
 741:                 issue_for_challenge,
 742:             )
 743:         except ImportError:
 744:             return
 745:         sealed = getattr(self.daemon, "sealed_master", None)
 746:         if sealed is None:
 747:             log.info(
 748:                 "peer-rtc: attest_challenge from %s but no sealed_master; "
 749:                 "skipping response",
 750:                 peer.fingerprint,
 751:             )
 752:             return
 753:         # Our SDP pubkey is the identity that signs the WebRTC offer/answer
 754:         # envelope on this channel. Peer pins this against our channel ID.
 755:         try:
 756:             my_sdp_pubkey = bytes(self.daemon.me.public_bytes)
 757:         except Exception:
 758:             log.info(
 759:                 "peer-rtc: attest_challenge from %s but daemon.me.public_bytes "
 760:                 "unavailable; skipping response",
 761:                 peer.fingerprint,
 762:             )
 763:             return
 764:         if len(my_sdp_pubkey) != 32:
 765:             log.warning(
 766:                 "peer-rtc: attest_challenge from %s — our SDP pubkey is %d bytes "
 767:                 "(expected 32); cannot bind attestation",
 768:                 peer.fingerprint, len(my_sdp_pubkey),
 769:             )
 770:             return
 771:         challenge_b64 = str(envelope.get("challenge_b64") or "")
 772:         try:
 773:             challenge = base64.b64decode(challenge_b64)
 774:         except Exception:
 775:             return
 776:         if len(challenge) != 32:
 777:             return
 778:         try:
 779:             doc = issue_for_challenge(sealed, challenge, my_sdp_pubkey)
 780:             wire = AttestationWire.from_doc(doc).to_wire_dict()
 781:         except Exception as e:
 782:             log.info("peer-rtc: issue attestation failed: %s", e)
 783:             return
 784:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 785:             self.send_dc(peer, "control", {
 786:                 "v": PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
 787:                 "t": "attest_response",
 788:                 "ts": _now_ms(),
 789:                 "doc": wire,
 790:             })
 791: 
 792:     async def _handle_attest_response(
 793:         self, peer: BrowserPeer, envelope: dict
 794:     ) -> None:
 795:         """Peer sent us their attestation doc bound to OUR challenge
 796:         and their SDP pubkey (audit C1). Verify and update peer state
 797:         on success. TOFU-pins peer.peer_master_vk on first attest;
 798:         rejects rotation on subsequent attests (audit C2)."""
 799:         try:
 800:             from one_link.handshake_attestation import (
 801:                 AttestationWire,
 802:                 verify_doc,
 803:             )
 804:         except ImportError:
 805:             return
 806:         challenge = peer.attestation_challenge
 807:         if challenge is None:
 808:             log.info(
 809:                 "peer-rtc: attest_response from %s without prior "
 810:                 "init_attestation; ignoring",
 811:                 peer.fingerprint,
 812:             )
 813:             return
 814:         # Audit M9 May 2026: reject the response if the DC the
 815:         # response arrived on is NOT the same DC instance the
 816:         # challenge was issued on. Covers the reconnect race where
 817:         # an old DC's response could be accepted on a fresh DC.
 818:         challenge_dc_id = getattr(peer, "attestation_challenge_dc_id", None)
 819:         current_dc_id = id(peer.control_dc) if peer.control_dc is not None else None
 820:         if challenge_dc_id is not None and challenge_dc_id != current_dc_id:
 821:             log.info(
 822:                 "peer-rtc: dropping attest_response from %s — challenge "
 823:                 "was issued on a different DC instance (reconnect race)",
 824:                 peer.fingerprint,
 825:             )
 826:             peer.attestation_challenge = None
 827:             peer.attestation_challenge_dc_id = None
 828:             return
 829:         # The peer's SDP-layer pubkey is the identity that signed the
 830:         # WebRTC offer envelope on this channel. The attestation doc
 831:         # MUST commit to this pubkey.
 832:         peer_sdp_pubkey = bytes(peer.pubkey_bytes)
 833:         if len(peer_sdp_pubkey) != 32:
 834:             log.warning(
 835:                 "peer-rtc: attest_response from %s — peer SDP pubkey is %d bytes "
 836:                 "(expected 32); rejecting",
 837:                 peer.fingerprint, len(peer_sdp_pubkey),
 838:             )
 839:             return
 840:         wire_d = envelope.get("doc")
 841:         if not isinstance(wire_d, dict):
 842:             return
 843:         try:
 844:             wire = AttestationWire.from_wire_dict(wire_d)
 845:             doc = wire.to_doc()
 846:             verify_doc(doc, challenge, peer_sdp_pubkey)
 847:         except Exception as e:
 848:             log.warning(
 849:                 "peer-rtc: attestation from %s failed verify: %s",
 850:                 peer.fingerprint, e,
 851:             )
 852:             return
 853:         # Audit I4 May 2026 — explicit replay-cache check. A doc that
 854:         # already passed verify in the recent past is rejected here
 855:         # before we update any peer state. The per-peer
 856:         # `attestation_challenge = None` clear (below) still removes
 857:         # the primary replay window; this is belt-and-suspenders so a
 858:         # future refactor that drops that clear doesn't open a 30s
 859:         # replay vector.
 860:         if not self._attestation_replay_check_and_record(doc.master_sig):
 861:             log.warning(
 862:                 "peer-rtc: attestation from %s rejected — doc replay "
 863:                 "(BLAKE3(master_sig) already seen in recent cache window)",
 864:                 peer.fingerprint,
 865:             )
 866:             return
 867:         # Audit I6 May 2026 — per-master-vk fork detection. If we've
 868:         # previously seen ANY doc from this master_vk (across any
 869:         # peer fingerprint), require the new doc's `issued_unix` to
 870:         # be NOT meaningfully earlier than the previous one. A
 871:         # cloned-identity attacker on a second host that produces an
 872:         # earlier-issued doc with the same master_vk gets caught
 873:         # here. Tolerates ATTESTATION_FORK_MAX_BACKWARDS_SECS of
 874:         # natural clock wobble before flagging.
 875:         prev_issued_unix = self._master_vk_last_issued_unix.get(doc.master_vk)
 876:         if (
 877:             prev_issued_unix is not None
 878:             and doc.issued_unix + self.ATTESTATION_FORK_MAX_BACKWARDS_SECS
 879:             < prev_issued_unix
 880:         ):
 881:             log.warning(
 882:                 "peer-rtc: SECURITY ALERT — peer %s presented attestation "
 883:                 "with master_vk=%s and issued_unix=%d, but previously "
 884:                 "observed issued_unix=%d for the same master_vk. Possible "
 885:                 "fork / cloned identity. Refusing.",
 886:                 peer.fingerprint,
 887:                 doc.master_vk[:8].hex(),
 888:                 doc.issued_unix,
 889:                 prev_issued_unix,
 890:             )
 891:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 892:                 self._close_peer(peer)
 893:             return
 894:         # Record the high-water-mark for this master_vk.
 895:         self._master_vk_last_issued_unix[doc.master_vk] = max(
 896:             prev_issued_unix if prev_issued_unix is not None else 0,
 897:             doc.issued_unix,
 898:         )
 899:         # Audit C2 (May 14 2026): TOFU-pin peer_master_vk. If we
 900:         # previously pinned a different master VK against this peer
 901:         # fingerprint, refuse the new doc and tear the peer down.
 902:         # An attacker who stole the SDP signing key but cannot
 903:         # recover the original master seed would silently roll
 904:         # forward to a fresh master without this check.
 905:         prior_vk = peer.peer_master_vk
 906:         if prior_vk is not None and prior_vk != doc.master_vk:
 907:             log.warning(
 908:                 "peer-rtc: SECURITY ALERT — peer %s presented master_vk "
 909:                 "%s but previously pinned %s. Refusing and tearing down.",
 910:                 peer.fingerprint,
 911:                 doc.master_vk[:8].hex(),
 912:                 prior_vk[:8].hex(),
 913:             )
 914:             peer.attestation_challenge = None
 915:             peer.attestation_challenge_dc_id = None
 916:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 917:                 self._close_peer(peer)
 918:             return
 919:         # Pin the peer's master VK + mark attested.
 920:         peer.peer_master_vk = doc.master_vk
 921:         peer.attested_ms = _now_ms()
 922:         # Record the doc's deadline so the gate can re-check freshness
 923:         # on every dispatched frame (audit H7 May 2026). Without this,
 924:         # a single successful 30 s round-trip grants the peer an
 925:         # indefinitely-attested state.
 926:         peer.attestation_deadline_unix = int(doc.deadline_unix)
 927:         # Clear the challenge so a stale response doesn't get accepted.
 928:         peer.attestation_challenge = None
 929:         peer.attestation_challenge_dc_id = None
 930:         log.info(
 931:             "peer-rtc: peer %s attested (provider_tag=%d, vk_len=%d, "
 932:             "deadline_unix=%d)",
 933:             peer.fingerprint, doc.provider_tag, len(doc.master_vk),
 934:             peer.attestation_deadline_unix,
 935:         )
 936: 
 937:     def init_onion_announce(self, peer: BrowserPeer) -> bool:
 938:         """Announce this daemon's Sphinx onion pubkey to a browser peer."""
 939:         pk = getattr(self.daemon, "_cover_relay_pk", None)
 940:         if not pk:
 941:             return False
 942:         try:
 943:             self.send_dc(peer, "control", {
 944:                 "v": PEER_DC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
 945:                 "t": "onion_pubkey",
 946:                 "ts": _now_ms(),
 947:                 "pubkey_b64": base64.b64encode(pk).decode("ascii"),
 948:             })
 949:             return True
 950:         except Exception as e:
 951:             log.info("peer-rtc: onion pubkey announce failed: %s", e)
 952:             return False

 954:     async def _handle_onion_pubkey(
 955:         self,
 956:         peer: BrowserPeer,
 957:         envelope: dict,
 958:     ) -> None:
 959:         try:
 960:             pk = base64.b64decode(
 961:                 str(envelope.get("pubkey_b64") or ""),
 962:                 validate=True,
 963:             )
 964:         except Exception:
 965:             return
 966:         if len(pk) != 32:
 967:             log.info(
 968:                 "peer-rtc: %s sent onion_pubkey of wrong length %d",
 969:                 peer.fingerprint, len(pk),
 970:             )
 971:             return
 972:         # Audit H10 May 2026 — TOFU pin onion_pubkey. Without this,
 973:         # a peer that has already announced K1 can later send K2 and
 974:         # silently redirect our cover-traffic emitter (which picks
 975:         # the first peer with onion_pubkey + open DC) to a key the
 976:         # attacker holds. The attacker would then have a free
 977:         # decryption oracle for our cover packets — including the
 978:         # COVER_SENTINEL plaintext as a known-plaintext crib against
 979:         # the channel.
 980:         if peer.onion_pubkey is not None and peer.onion_pubkey != pk:
 981:             log.warning(
 982:                 "peer-rtc: SECURITY ALERT — peer %s rotated onion_pubkey "
 983:                 "(prior=%s, new=%s); refusing.",
 984:                 peer.fingerprint,
 985:                 peer.onion_pubkey[:8].hex(),
 986:                 pk[:8].hex(),
 987:             )
 988:             return
 989:         peer.onion_pubkey = pk
 990:         peer.onion_pubkey_received_ms = _now_ms()
 991:         log.info("peer-rtc: recorded onion pubkey for %s", peer.fingerprint)
 992: 
 993:     async def _handle_cover_packet(
 994:         self,
 995:         peer: BrowserPeer,
 996:         envelope: dict,
 997:     ) -> None:
 998:         """Audit M8 May 2026 — constant-time response across the
 999:         success / failure split.
1000: 
1001:         The pre-M8 implementation emitted distinguishing debug log
1002:         lines for ``failed to peel`` vs ``non-deliver`` vs ``lacks
1003:         cover sentinel`` — three different code paths that an
1004:         adversary with DC access could probe (by varying the inbound
1005:         bytes and watching which log shape they produced indirectly
1006:         via timing or controlled log scrape). Combined with the M4
1007:         plaintext sentinel, this was a format-reverse-engineering
1008:         oracle.
1009: 
1010:         New shape:
1011:           - All non-success peel outcomes collapse to a single
1012:             silent-drop branch with NO log emission (debug or
1013:             otherwise).
1014:           - Success is identified by the M4 authenticated peel
1015:             returning kind=="cover" (the destination's per-circuit
1016:             shared key has verified the trailer MAC). Plaintext
1017:             sentinel inspection is no longer involved.
1018:           - The telemetry counter increment is the ONLY observable
1019:             side effect of success, and it lives in private daemon
1020:             state never echoed to any peer.
1021:         """
1022:         relay_sk = getattr(self.daemon, "_cover_relay_sk", None)
1023:         if relay_sk is None:
1024:             return
1025:         try:
1026:             from one_link_native import sphinx as _native_sphinx
1027:         except ImportError:
1028:             return
1029:         # Decode + peel are wrapped in a single try; any failure
1030:         # silently drops with NO log emission so adversarial probing
1031:         # cannot distinguish failure modes from outside.
1032:         try:
1033:             packet = base64.b64decode(
1034:                 str(envelope.get("packet_b64") or ""),
1035:                 validate=True,
1036:             )
1037:             kind, _next_hop, _payload = _native_sphinx.peel_sphinx(
1038:                 relay_sk,
1039:                 packet,
1040:             )
1041:         except Exception:
1042:             return
1043:         # Audit M4: the authenticated peel returns kind=="cover" iff
1044:         # the trailer MAC verifies under the destination's per-
1045:         # circuit shared key. We do NOT fall back to inspecting the
1046:         # plaintext sentinel — that path is forgeable and was the
1047:         # M8 oracle. kind=="deliver" with a cover-shaped payload but
1048:         # an invalid MAC is treated as a REAL packet (delivered
1049:         # normally elsewhere), not a cover-drop here.
1050:         if kind != "cover":
1051:             return
1052:         # Audit L8 May 2026: lock the read-modify-write so the cover
1053:         # background thread's increment of _cover_emit_count and this
1054:         # path's increment of _cover_recv_count don't tear under
1055:         # concurrent access.
1056:         lock = getattr(self.daemon, "_telemetry_lock", None)
1057:         try:
1058:             if lock is not None:
1059:                 with lock:
1060:                     self.daemon._cover_recv_count = (
1061:                         getattr(self.daemon, "_cover_recv_count", 0) + 1
1062:                     )
1063:             else:
1064:                 self.daemon._cover_recv_count = (
1065:                     getattr(self.daemon, "_cover_recv_count", 0) + 1
1066:                 )
1067:         except Exception:
1068:             pass
1069: 
1070:     def send_dc(
1071:         self, peer: BrowserPeer, channel_kind: str, envelope: dict
1072:     ) -> None:
1073:         """Send a JSON envelope down the peer's DataChannel. Non-async;
1074:         aiortc's send is synchronous (queues into the channel's send
1075:         buffer)."""
1076:         if peer.closed:
1077:             return
1078:         dc = peer.control_dc if channel_kind == "control" else peer.bulk_dc
1079:         if dc is None:
1080:             log.debug(
1081:                 "peer-rtc: no %s channel for %s", channel_kind, peer.fingerprint,
1082:             )
1083:             return
1084:         try:
1085:             dc.send(json.dumps(envelope))
1086:         except Exception as e:
1087:             log.warning(
1088:                 "peer-rtc: send on %s failed for %s: %s",
1089:                 channel_kind, peer.fingerprint, e,
1090:             )
1091: 
1092:     # ── envelope verification ──────────────────────────────────────
1093: 
1094:     @staticmethod
1095:     def verify_offer_envelope(envelope: dict) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
1096:         """Validate the signed offer envelope. Returns
1097:         (pubkey_bytes, fingerprint) on success; raises ValueError
1098:         on any failure. Drops timestamps outside the replay window."""
1099:         if not isinstance(envelope, dict):
1100:             raise ValueError("envelope must be an object")
1101:         if envelope.get("v") != PEER_RTC_PROTOCOL_VERSION:
1102:             raise ValueError(f"unsupported protocol version: {envelope.get('v')!r}")
1103:         if envelope.get("t") != "offer":
1104:             raise ValueError(f"unexpected envelope type: {envelope.get('t')!r}")
1105:         pubkey_b64u = envelope.get("pubkey_b64u")
1106:         if not isinstance(pubkey_b64u, str):
1107:             raise ValueError("pubkey_b64u required")
1108:         if len(pubkey_b64u) > 64:
1109:             raise ValueError("pubkey_b64u too large")
1110:         pubkey = _b64ud(pubkey_b64u)
1111:         if len(pubkey) != 32:
1112:             raise ValueError("pubkey must be 32 bytes")
1113:         fingerprint = envelope.get("fingerprint")
1114:         if not isinstance(fingerprint, str) or ":" not in fingerprint:
1115:             raise ValueError("fingerprint required (algo:hex)")
1116:         if len(fingerprint) > 128:
1117:             raise ValueError("fingerprint too large")
1118:         sig_b64u = envelope.get("signature")
1119:         if not isinstance(sig_b64u, str):
1120:             raise ValueError("signature required")
1121:         if len(sig_b64u) > 128:
1122:             raise ValueError("signature too large")
1123:         sig = _b64ud(sig_b64u)
1124:         if len(sig) != 64:
1125:             raise ValueError("signature must be 64 bytes")
1126:         sdp = envelope.get("sdp")
1127:         if not isinstance(sdp, str) or not sdp:
1128:             raise ValueError("sdp required")
1129:         if len(sdp.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")) > MAX_SDP_BYTES:
1130:             raise ValueError("sdp too large")
1131:         ts = envelope.get("ts")
1132:         if not isinstance(ts, int):
1133:             raise ValueError("ts required (int ms)")
1134:         now = _now_ms()
1135:         if abs(now - ts) > OFFER_REPLAY_WINDOW_MS:
1136:             raise ValueError("offer envelope timestamp out of replay window")
1137:         try:
1138:             Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(pubkey).verify(
1139:                 sig, _canonical(envelope),
1140:             )
1141:         except InvalidSignature as e:
1142:             raise ValueError("offer signature does not verify") from e
1143:         # Don't trust the browser's claimed fingerprint without
1144:         # checking it against a re-derivation. We re-derive the
1145:         # sha256-tagged form ourselves and require equality.
1146:         # (BLAKE3 fingerprints can come along when the browser
1147:         # vendors BLAKE3-WASM in a later ship; we accept whichever
1148:         # algorithm the browser tagged, as long as it derives
1149:         # correctly.)
1150:         algo, _, claimed_hex = fingerprint.partition(":")
1151:         if algo == "sha256":
1152:             import hashlib
1153:             expected = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(pubkey).hexdigest()
1154:             if expected != fingerprint:
1155:                 raise ValueError("fingerprint does not match pubkey (sha256)")
1156:         return pubkey, fingerprint
1157: 
1158:     # ── DTLS fingerprint cross-check (audit C1 defense-in-depth) ──
1159: 
1160:     def record_dtls_fingerprint(
1161:         self,
1162:         *,
1163:         pubkey: bytes,
1164:         sdp: str,
1165:     ) -> tuple[str, bool]:
1166:         """Extract the SDP's DTLS-SRTP fingerprint, store it against
1167:         this peer's Ed25519 pubkey, and check it against the
1168:         previously-observed value.
1169: 
1170:         Returns ``(current_dtls_fp, matches_or_first_seen)``.
1171:         - ``("", True)`` if the SDP has no a=fingerprint line (no
1172:           cross-check possible).
1173:         - ``(fp, True)`` on first observation or matching observation.
1174:         - ``(fp, False)`` if the fingerprint changed — recorded as a
1175:           structured WARNING in the daemon log. Not a hard reject;
1176:           the envelope-signature path already does that.
1177:         """
1178:         dtls_fp = _extract_dtls_fingerprint(sdp)
1179:         if not dtls_fp:
1180:             return "", True
1181:         pubkey_hex = pubkey.hex()
1182:         previous = self._dtls_fingerprints.get(pubkey_hex)
1183:         if previous is not None and previous != dtls_fp:
1184:             log.warning(
1185:                 "peer-rtc: DTLS fingerprint changed for browser peer "
1186:                 "(pubkey=%s...): %s -> %s",
1187:                 pubkey_hex[:16],
1188:                 previous[:24] + "...",
1189:                 dtls_fp[:24] + "...",
1190:             )
1191:             self._dtls_fingerprints[pubkey_hex] = dtls_fp
1192:             return dtls_fp, False
1193:         self._dtls_fingerprints[pubkey_hex] = dtls_fp
1194:         return dtls_fp, True
1195: 
1196:     def get_recorded_dtls_fingerprint(self, pubkey: bytes) -> Optional[str]:
1197:         """For tests + diagnostics: read the recorded DTLS
1198:         fingerprint for a pubkey (or None if never observed)."""
1199:         return self._dtls_fingerprints.get(pubkey.hex())

   1: """Peer-transport facade — unified interface for WebRTC and QUIC.
   2: 
   3: The daemon owns one ``PeerTransport`` per peer. The facade exposes a
   4: single ``send(payload: bytes)`` / ``recv(timeout_ms: int)`` surface;
   5: the underlying transport (WebRTC datachannel via ``peer_rtc`` or QUIC
   6: session via ``peer_quic``) is selected once at session-creation time
   7: based on capability negotiation, then never changes for the lifetime
   8: of the peer connection.
   9: 
  10: Why a facade rather than swap-in:
  11: 
  12: - The existing channel-layer code (``channel.send``,
  13:   ``channel.recv``) treats the underlying transport as a bag of bytes.
  14:   Adding QUIC alongside WebRTC means either (a) duplicating the
  15:   channel layer per transport or (b) putting a thin facade between
  16:   the channel and the wire. (b) is what this module is.
  17: - The facade preserves ALL existing behaviour. WebRTC stays the
  18:   default; v0.20.x peers never hit the QUIC code path; existing
  19:   tests pass unchanged.
  20: - Per-message routing is O(1): the facade caches the chosen transport
  21:   on construction.
  22: 
  23: When the QUIC datapath eventually fully replaces WebRTC for
  24: daemon↔daemon (per ``PHASE_A2_QUIC_CUTOVER_PLAN.md``), the facade's
  25: WebRTC implementation is what we delete — every call site already
  26: talks to the facade, so the migration is local.
  27: """
  28: 
  29: from __future__ import annotations
  30: 
  31: import logging
  32: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  33: from typing import Optional, Protocol
  34: 
  35: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  36: 
  37: 
  38: class TransportSendError(RuntimeError):
  39:     """Raised when the underlying transport cannot complete a send.
  40:     Callers translate to higher-level retry / reconnect / drop-peer
  41:     decisions."""
  42: 
  43: 
  44: class TransportRecvError(RuntimeError):
  45:     """Raised when recv() times out or the transport is closed by
  46:     the remote."""
  47: 
  48: 
  49: class PeerTransport(Protocol):
  50:     """Common shape every transport implementation honours.
  51: 
  52:     Implementations:
  53:     - ``WebRTCTransport`` wraps the existing peer_rtc datachannel.
  54:     - ``QuicTransport`` wraps a ``QuicPeerSession`` from peer_quic.
  55: 
  56:     Methods are NOT required to be thread-safe in absolute terms;
  57:     callers serialise per-peer at the daemon layer via existing
  58:     per-peer locks."""
  59: 
  60:     @property
  61:     def kind(self) -> str:
  62:         """Either ``"webrtc"`` or ``"quic"``. Reported in telemetry."""
  63:         ...
  64: 
  65:     def is_open(self) -> bool: ...
  66: 
  67:     def send_bytes(self, payload: bytes) -> None:
  68:         """Sync send. Implementations either fully synchronous (QUIC
  69:         wraps a blocking ``quinn`` call) or raise when the underlying
  70:         is async-only (WebRTC channel.send)."""
  71:         ...
  72: 
  73:     async def send_bytes_async(self, payload: bytes) -> None:
  74:         """Async send — production-path. WebRTC awaits the channel
  75:         coroutine directly; QUIC offloads the blocking call to a
  76:         thread-pool executor."""
  77:         ...

  86:     """Per-transport telemetry. Bumped by the facade as bytes flow;

  96: @dataclass
  97: class WebRTCTransport:
  98:     """Wraps the existing ``peer_rtc`` channel as a PeerTransport.
  99: 
 100:     The actual datachannel is owned by the daemon's existing channel
 101:     object; this adapter forwards bytes through it.
 102:     """
 103: 
 104:     channel: object
 105:     """The peer's :class:`one_link.channel.Channel` instance."""
 106: 
 107:     stats: TransportStats = field(default_factory=TransportStats)
 108: 
 109:     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
 110:         self.stats.transport_kind = "webrtc"
 111: 
 112:     @property
 113:     def kind(self) -> str:
 114:         return "webrtc"
 115: 
 116:     def is_open(self) -> bool:
 117:         if self.channel is None:
 118:             return False
 119:         # Channel objects expose `is_closed` semantics differently
 120:         # depending on transport state; treat absence of error as open.
 121:         closed = getattr(self.channel, "_closed", False)
 122:         return not closed
 123: 
 124:     def send_bytes(self, payload: bytes) -> None:
 125:         """Sync send (test-stub callers + fallback paths). Production
 126:         daemon code uses :meth:`send_bytes_async`."""
 127:         if not self.is_open():
 128:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 129:             raise TransportSendError("WebRTC channel closed")
 130:         import asyncio
 131: 
 132:         send_fn = getattr(self.channel, "send", None)
 133:         if send_fn is None:
 134:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 135:             raise TransportSendError("WebRTC channel has no send()")
 136:         try:
 137:             coro_or_none = send_fn(payload)
 138:             if asyncio.iscoroutine(coro_or_none):
 139:                 self.stats.send_failures += 1
 140:                 raise TransportSendError(
 141:                     "channel.send() returned a coroutine; await it at "
 142:                     "the daemon call site or use send_bytes_async()"
 143:                 )
 144:         except TransportSendError:
 145:             raise
 146:         except Exception as e:
 147:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 148:             raise TransportSendError(str(e)) from e
 149:         self._record_send(len(payload))
 150: 
 151:     async def send_bytes_async(self, payload: bytes) -> None:
 152:         """Async send — the production-path entry point. Channel's
 153:         send() in real daemons is a coroutine; awaiting it here keeps
 154:         the call-site contract clean."""
 155:         if not self.is_open():
 156:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 157:             raise TransportSendError("WebRTC channel closed")
 158:         import asyncio
 159: 
 160:         send_fn = getattr(self.channel, "send", None)
 161:         if send_fn is None:
 162:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 163:             raise TransportSendError("WebRTC channel has no send()")
 164:         try:
 165:             coro_or_none = send_fn(payload)
 166:             if asyncio.iscoroutine(coro_or_none):
 167:                 await coro_or_none
 168:         except Exception as e:
 169:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 170:             raise TransportSendError(str(e)) from e
 171:         self._record_send(len(payload))
 172: 
 173:     def _record_send(self, n_bytes: int) -> None:
 174:         self.stats.bytes_sent += n_bytes
 175:         self.stats.sends += 1
 176:         import time
 177: 
 178:         self.stats.last_send_ns = time.perf_counter_ns()
 179: 
 180:     def rtt_ms(self) -> Optional[float]:
 181:         # WebRTC ICE candidates expose RTT via stats; the channel
 182:         # surface doesn't currently propagate it. Returning None is
 183:         # the safe default — callers that need RTT fall back to
 184:         # daemon-level relay-metrics tracking.
 185:         rtt = getattr(self.channel, "rtt_ms", None)
 186:         if callable(rtt):
 187:             try:
 188:                 v = rtt()
 189:                 return float(v) if v is not None else None
 190:             except Exception:
 191:                 return None
 192:         if isinstance(rtt, (int, float)):
 193:             return float(rtt)
 194:         return None
 195: 
 196:     def close(self) -> None:
 197:         # WebRTC channels are owned by the daemon's session-tracker,
 198:         # not the facade. Closing the facade is a no-op; the daemon
 199:         # tears the channel down via its own lifecycle hooks.
 200:         pass
 201: 
 202: 
 203: @dataclass
 204: class QuicTransport:
 205:     """Wraps a :class:`one_link.peer_quic.QuicPeerSession`."""
 206: 
 207:     session: object
 208:     """A QuicPeerSession from peer_quic.open_outbound()."""
 209: 
 210:     stats: TransportStats = field(default_factory=TransportStats)
 211: 
 212:     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
 213:         self.stats.transport_kind = "quic"
 214: 
 215:     @property
 216:     def kind(self) -> str:
 217:         return "quic"
 218: 
 219:     def is_open(self) -> bool:
 220:         if self.session is None:
 221:             return False
 222:         is_conn = getattr(self.session, "is_connected", None)
 223:         return bool(is_conn()) if callable(is_conn) else False
 224: 
 225:     def send_bytes(self, payload: bytes) -> None:
 226:         """Sync send. QuicPeerSession.send_frame is blocking under
 227:         the hood (calls quinn's blocking API); safe to invoke from
 228:         sync code paths."""
 229:         if not self.is_open():
 230:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 231:             raise TransportSendError("QUIC session closed")
 232:         # The ol_quic frame type used for generic message-layer bytes
 233:         # — we encode an existing channel-layer message into a single
 234:         # QUIC frame so the channel's message format stays intact.
 235:         try:
 236:             from one_link import peer_quic
 237: 
 238:             frame_type = peer_quic.FRAME_CHUNK_REQUEST  # generic carrier
 239:             send_fn = getattr(self.session, "send_frame", None)
 240:             if send_fn is None:
 241:                 self.stats.send_failures += 1
 242:                 raise TransportSendError("QUIC session has no send_frame()")
 243:             send_fn(frame_type, payload)
 244:         except TransportSendError:
 245:             raise
 246:         except Exception as e:
 247:             self.stats.send_failures += 1
 248:             raise TransportSendError(str(e)) from e
 249:         self._record_send(len(payload))
 250: 
 251:     async def send_bytes_async(self, payload: bytes) -> None:
 252:         """Async-flavoured send. The underlying QUIC send is blocking;
 253:         we offload it to a thread pool so the asyncio loop doesn't
 254:         block on the I/O wait."""
 255:         import asyncio
 256: 
 257:         loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
 258:         await loop.run_in_executor(None, self.send_bytes, payload)
 259: 
 260:     def _record_send(self, n_bytes: int) -> None:
 261:         self.stats.bytes_sent += n_bytes
 262:         self.stats.sends += 1
 263:         import time
 264: 
 265:         self.stats.last_send_ns = time.perf_counter_ns()
 266: 
 267:     def rtt_ms(self) -> Optional[float]:
 268:         if not self.is_open():
 269:             return None
 270:         try:
 271:             rtt = self.session.rtt_ms()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
 272:             return float(rtt) if rtt is not None else None
 273:         except Exception:
 274:             return None
 275: 
 276:     def close(self) -> None:
 277:         if self.session is None:
 278:             return
 279:         try:
 280:             close_fn = getattr(self.session, "close", None)
 281:             if callable(close_fn):
 282:                 close_fn()
 283:         except Exception:
 284:             pass
 285: 
 286: 
 287: def make_transport_for_peer(
 288:     transport_kind: str,
 289:     *,
 290:     channel: Optional[object] = None,
 291:     quic_session: Optional[object] = None,
 292: ) -> PeerTransport:
 293:     """Build the facade for a given (kind, underlying) pair. Raises
 294:     ``ValueError`` if the required underlying is missing for the
 295:     requested kind."""
 296:     if transport_kind == "webrtc":
 297:         if channel is None:
 298:             raise ValueError(
 299:                 "WebRTC transport requires a channel object"
 300:             )
 301:         return WebRTCTransport(channel=channel)
 302:     if transport_kind == "quic":
 303:         if quic_session is None:
 304:             raise ValueError(
 305:                 "QUIC transport requires a QuicPeerSession"
 306:             )
 307:         return QuicTransport(session=quic_session)
 308:     raise ValueError(
 309:         f"unknown transport kind: {transport_kind!r} "
 310:         "(expected 'webrtc' or 'quic')"
 311:     )

   3: Benchmarks here are deterministic, local, and dependency-light. They are not a

  52: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  53: class BenchResult:
  54:     name: str
  55:     metrics: dict[str, float | int | str | bool]
  56:     seconds: float
  57:     notes: str = ""
  58: 
  59:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
  60:         return {
  61:             "name": self.name,
  62:             "seconds": round(self.seconds, 6),
  63:             "metrics": self.metrics,
  64:             "notes": self.notes,
  65:         }
  66: 
  67: 
  68: def _mb_per_s(nbytes: int, seconds: float) -> float:
  69:     return round((nbytes / MiB) / max(seconds, 1e-9), 3)
  70: 
  71: 
  72: def _time(fn: Callable[[], dict]) -> BenchResult:
  73:     t0 = time.perf_counter()
  74:     out = fn()
  75:     elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
  76:     return BenchResult(
  77:         name=str(out.pop("name")),
  78:         metrics=out,
  79:         seconds=elapsed,
  80:         notes=str(out.pop("notes", "")) if "notes" in out else "",
  81:     )

 150: def bench_prior_knowledge(*, size_mib: int, mutation_bytes: int, seed: int) -> BenchResult:
 151:     def run() -> dict:
 152:         rng = random.Random(seed)
 153:         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ol_perf_prior_") as td:
 154:             root = Path(td)
 155:             base = root / "base.bin"
 156:             changed = root / "changed.bin"
 157:             payload = rng.randbytes(size_mib * MiB)
 158:             base.write_bytes(payload)
 159:             insert = rng.randbytes(mutation_bytes)
 160:             changed.write_bytes(payload[: MiB] + insert + payload[MiB:])
 161:             base_idx = index_path(base)
 162:             changed_idx = index_path(changed)
 163:             t0 = time.perf_counter()
 164:             plan = build_dedup_plan(changed_idx.chunks, {c.hash for c in base_idx.chunks})
 165:             plan_seconds = time.perf_counter() - t0
 166:         return {
 167:             "name": "prior_knowledge_dedup",
 168:             "changed_size_bytes": changed_idx.size,
 169:             "chunks": changed_idx.chunk_count if hasattr(changed_idx, "chunk_count") else len(changed_idx.chunks),
 170:             "hit_rate": round(plan.hit_rate, 6),
 171:             "bytes_to_send": plan.bytes_to_send,
 172:             "bytes_saved": plan.byte_savings,
 173:             "bandwidth_reduction": round(plan.byte_savings / max(1, changed_idx.size), 6),
 174:             "plan_micros": round(plan_seconds * 1_000_000, 3),
 175:         }
 176: 
 177:     return _time(run)

 180: def bench_swarm_scheduler(*, chunks: int, sources: int, seed: int) -> BenchResult:
 181:     def run() -> dict:
 182:         manifest = synthetic_manifest(
 183:             name="scheduler.bin",
 184:             size=chunks * MiB,
 185:             chunk_size=MiB,
 186:         )
 187:         rng = random.Random(seed)
 188:         srcs = []
 189:         all_hashes = [c.hash for c in manifest.chunks]
 190:         for i in range(sources):
 191:             # Each source gets a deterministic overlapping subset.
 192:             claim = [
 193:                 h for j, h in enumerate(all_hashes)
 194:                 if (j + i) % max(2, min(7, sources)) == 0 or rng.random() < 0.08
 195:             ]
 196:             srcs.append(source_from_hashes(
 197:                 f"{i:064x}",
 198:                 claim,
 199:                 trust_score=1.0 + (i % 3) * 0.25,
 200:                 latency_ms=5.0 + i,
 201:                 bandwidth_bps=50_000_000 + (i * 5_000_000),
 202:                 reliability=0.90 + (i % 5) * 0.015,
 203:             ))
 204:         t0 = time.perf_counter()
 205:         plan = plan_swarm_sources(manifest=manifest, needed_indexes=None, sources=srcs)
 206:         elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
 207:         return {
 208:             "name": "swarm_scheduler",
 209:             "chunks": chunks,
 210:             "sources": sources,
 211:             "assigned": len([a for a in plan.assignments if a.status == "assigned"]),
 212:             "missing": len(plan.missing_indexes),
 213:             "chunks_per_s": round(chunks / max(elapsed, 1e-9), 3),
 214:             "assigned_bytes": plan.assigned_bytes,
 215:             "missing_bytes": plan.missing_bytes,
 216:             "source_count": len(plan.sources),
 217:         }
 218: 
 219:     return _time(run)

 281: def bench_compression(*, size_mib: int) -> BenchResult:
 282:     def run() -> dict:
 283:         data = (b"compressible-transfer-block\n" * ((size_mib * MiB) // 28 + 1))[: size_mib * MiB]
 284:         samples: list[float] = []
 285:         packed_size = 0
 286:         for _ in range(3):
 287:             t0 = time.perf_counter()
 288:             packed = zlib.compress(data, level=1)
 289:             samples.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
 290:             packed_size = len(packed)
 291:         med = statistics.median(samples)
 292:         return {
 293:             "name": "zlib_level1_compression",
 294:             "size_bytes": len(data),
 295:             "packed_bytes": packed_size,
 296:             "ratio": round(packed_size / max(1, len(data)), 6),
 297:             "mib_per_s": _mb_per_s(len(data), med),
 298:         }
 299: 
 300:     return _time(run)

 385: def bench_adaptive_runtime_scheduler(*, chunks: int) -> BenchResult:
 386:     def run() -> dict:

 388:             "chunk_size": MiB,
 389:             "window_chunks": 4,

 407:             "name": "adaptive_runtime_scheduler",
 408:             "chunks": int(chunks),
 409:             "chunks_per_s": 0,  # filled by _time wrapper below is not possible; use seconds outside metrics
 410:             "final_window_chunks": snap["window_chunks"],
 411:             "ack_count": snap["ack_count"],
 412:             "slow_events": slow_events,
 413:             "timeline_events": len(snap["timeline"]),
 414:             "ack_ema_ms": snap["ack_ema_ms"] or 0,
 415:         }
 416: 
 417:     result = _time(run)
 418:     metrics = dict(result.metrics)
 419:     metrics["chunks_per_s"] = round(float(metrics["chunks"]) / max(result.seconds, 1e-9), 3)
 420:     return BenchResult(
 421:         name=result.name,
 422:         metrics=metrics,
 423:         seconds=result.seconds,
 424:         notes="ACK-clocked live transfer window controller",
 425:     )
 426: 
 427: 
 428: def run_perf_lab(
 429:     *,
 430:     scale: str = "quick",
 431:     seed: int = 20260507,
 432: ) -> dict:
 433:     if scale not in {"quick", "standard", "heavy"}:
 434:         raise ValueError("scale must be quick, standard, or heavy")
 435:     cfg = {
 436:         "quick": {"cdc_mib": 4, "prior_mib": 4, "scheduler_chunks": 512, "ledger_rows": 500, "sim_mib": 256},
 437:         "standard": {"cdc_mib": 32, "prior_mib": 32, "scheduler_chunks": 4096, "ledger_rows": 5000, "sim_mib": 1024},
 438:         "heavy": {"cdc_mib": 256, "prior_mib": 256, "scheduler_chunks": 32768, "ledger_rows": 25000, "sim_mib": 10 * 1024},
 439:     }[scale]
 440:     started = time.time()
 441:     results = [
 442:         bench_hash_only(size_mib=cfg["cdc_mib"], seed=seed),
 443:         bench_fixed_indexing(size_mib=cfg["cdc_mib"], seed=seed),
 444:         bench_cdc_indexing(size_mib=cfg["cdc_mib"], seed=seed),
 445:         bench_prior_knowledge(size_mib=cfg["prior_mib"], mutation_bytes=4096, seed=seed + 1),
 446:         bench_swarm_scheduler(chunks=cfg["scheduler_chunks"], sources=12, seed=seed + 2),
 447:         bench_torture_sim(size_mib=cfg["sim_mib"], seed=seed + 3),
 448:         bench_sqlite_ledger(rows=cfg["ledger_rows"]),
 449:         bench_compression(size_mib=max(1, cfg["cdc_mib"] // 2)),
 450:         bench_transfer_brain(size_mib=cfg["sim_mib"]),
 451:         bench_stream_pipeline_profiles(),
 452:         bench_adaptive_runtime_scheduler(chunks=cfg["scheduler_chunks"]),
 453:     ]
 454:     return {
 455:         "schema": "one-link-perf-lab-v1",
 456:         "scale": scale,
 457:         "seed": seed,
 458:         "started_unix": started,
 459:         "duration_s": round(time.time() - started, 6),
 460:         "environment": {
 461:             "python": platform.python_version(),
 462:             "platform": platform.platform(),
 463:             "machine": platform.machine(),
 464:             "processor": platform.processor(),
 465:         },
 466:         "benchmarks": [r.to_dict() for r in results],
 467:     }
 468: 
 469: 
 470: def write_report(report: dict, output: Path) -> Path:
 471:     output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 472:     output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
 473:     return output

 475: 
 476: def compare_reports(old: dict, new: dict) -> dict:
 477:     """Return metric deltas from two perf-lab reports.
 478: 
 479:     Ratios greater than 1.0 mean the new report is higher. Whether higher is
 480:     better depends on the metric, so we keep this as raw math for now.
 481:     """
 482: 
 483:     old_by_name = {b["name"]: b for b in old.get("benchmarks", [])}
 484:     new_by_name = {b["name"]: b for b in new.get("benchmarks", [])}
 485:     benches: dict[str, dict] = {}
 486:     for name in sorted(set(old_by_name) & set(new_by_name)):
 487:         old_metrics = old_by_name[name].get("metrics", {})
 488:         new_metrics = new_by_name[name].get("metrics", {})
 489:         metrics: dict[str, dict] = {}
 490:         for key in sorted(set(old_metrics) & set(new_metrics)):
 491:             old_v = old_metrics[key]
 492:             new_v = new_metrics[key]
 493:             if isinstance(old_v, bool) or isinstance(new_v, bool):
 494:                 metrics[key] = {"old": old_v, "new": new_v, "changed": old_v != new_v}
 495:             elif isinstance(old_v, (int, float)) and isinstance(new_v, (int, float)):
 496:                 delta = float(new_v) - float(old_v)
 497:                 ratio = None if float(old_v) == 0 else float(new_v) / float(old_v)
 498:                 metrics[key] = {
 499:                     "old": old_v,
 500:                     "new": new_v,
 501:                     "delta": round(delta, 6),
 502:                     "ratio": round(ratio, 6) if ratio is not None else None,
 503:                 }
 504:             elif old_v != new_v:
 505:                 metrics[key] = {"old": old_v, "new": new_v, "changed": True}
 506:         benches[name] = metrics
 507:     return {
 508:         "schema": "one-link-perf-compare-v1",
 509:         "old_scale": old.get("scale"),
 510:         "new_scale": new.get("scale"),
 511:         "benchmarks": benches,
 512:     }

   3: Companion to ``perf_lab.py``. Surfaces the Phase A1 acceptance-gate numbers

  37: MiB = 1024 * 1024
  38: GiB = 1024 * 1024 * 1024
  39: 
  40: 
  41: def _xorshift_buf(seed: int, size: int) -> bytes:
  42:     state = seed & 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
  43:     out = bytearray(size)
  44:     for i in range(size):
  45:         state ^= (state << 13) & 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
  46:         state ^= state >> 7
  47:         state ^= (state << 17) & 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
  48:         out[i] = state & 0xFF
  49:     return bytes(out)
  50: 
  51: 
  52: @dataclass
  53: class BenchResult:
  54:     """One measured throughput data point.
  55: 
  56:     All times are wall-clock seconds. Throughput is reported in bytes per
  57:     second; callers convert to MiB/s or GiB/s as desired.
  58:     """
  59: 
  60:     name: str
  61:     bytes_processed: int
  62:     iterations: int
  63:     seconds_total: float
  64:     seconds_per_iter_median: float
  65:     bytes_per_second_median: float
  66:     metadata: dict[str, object]
  67: 
  68: 
  69: def _bench(
  70:     name: str,
  71:     fn: Callable[[], int],
  72:     iterations: int = 5,
  73:     metadata: dict[str, object] | None = None,
  74:     warmup_iterations: int = 0,
  75: ) -> BenchResult:
  76:     """Run ``fn`` ``iterations`` times. ``fn`` returns bytes processed.
  77: 
  78:     Reports median to suppress outliers from cold caches and OS scheduling.
  79:     """
  80:     for _ in range(max(0, warmup_iterations)):
  81:         fn()
  82:     durations: list[float] = []
  83:     bytes_one_iter = 0
  84:     for _ in range(iterations):
  85:         start = time.perf_counter_ns()
  86:         bytes_one_iter = fn()
  87:         elapsed_ns = time.perf_counter_ns() - start
  88:         durations.append(elapsed_ns / 1e9)
  89:     median_s = statistics.median(durations)
  90:     return BenchResult(
  91:         name=name,
  92:         bytes_processed=bytes_one_iter,
  93:         iterations=iterations,
  94:         seconds_total=sum(durations),
  95:         seconds_per_iter_median=median_s,
  96:         bytes_per_second_median=(bytes_one_iter / median_s) if median_s > 0 else 0.0,
  97:         metadata=metadata or {},
  98:     )

 206: def bench_native_aead(
 207:     kind: str = "aes",
 208:     chunk_size_kib: int = 64,
 209:     iterations: int = 200,
 210: ) -> tuple[BenchResult, BenchResult]:
 211:     """Encrypt + decrypt one chunk per iteration; return (enc_result, dec_result)."""
 212:     if not aead_native.HAS_NATIVE:
 213:         raise RuntimeError("aead_native unavailable")
 214:     n = chunk_size_kib * 1024
 215:     plaintext = _xorshift_buf(0xCAFE_AEAD ^ chunk_size_kib, n)
 216:     chunk_id = secrets.token_bytes(32)
 217:     key = secrets.token_bytes(32)
 218:     cipher = aead_native.AeadCipher.with_kind(key, kind)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
 219:     # warm-up
 220:     ct = cipher.encrypt_chunk(chunk_id, plaintext)
 221:     cipher.decrypt_chunk(chunk_id, len(plaintext), ct)
 222: 
 223:     def enc() -> int:
 224:         ct = cipher.encrypt_chunk(chunk_id, plaintext)
 225:         return len(plaintext)
 226: 
 227:     def dec() -> int:
 228:         cipher.decrypt_chunk(chunk_id, len(plaintext), ct)
 229:         return len(plaintext)
 230: 
 231:     enc_res = _bench(
 232:         f"native_aead_{kind}_encrypt_{chunk_size_kib}KiB",
 233:         enc,
 234:         iterations=iterations,
 235:         metadata={"input_bytes": n, "kind": kind},
 236:         warmup_iterations=min(20, max(1, iterations // 10)),
 237:     )
 238:     dec_res = _bench(
 239:         f"native_aead_{kind}_decrypt_{chunk_size_kib}KiB",
 240:         dec,
 241:         iterations=iterations,
 242:         metadata={"input_bytes": n, "kind": kind},
 243:         warmup_iterations=min(20, max(1, iterations // 10)),
 244:     )
 245:     return enc_res, dec_res

 311: def bench_native_chunk_store_locate(iterations: int = 1_000_000) -> BenchResult:
 312:     """Memtable + bloom lookup throughput (warm path)."""
 313:     if not chunk_store_native.HAS_NATIVE:
 314:         raise RuntimeError("chunk_store_native unavailable")
 315:     with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 316:         store = chunk_store_native.ChunkStore.open(d)
 317:         ids = []
 318:         ct = b"\xEE" * 80
 319:         for i in range(1024):
 320:             cid = i.to_bytes(4, "little") + b"\xBB" * 28
 321:             store.append_chunk(cid, b"\x33" * 16, 64, ct)
 322:             ids.append(cid)
 323:         store.flush()
 324: 
 325:         def go() -> int:
 326:             stride = 101
 327:             idx = 0
 328:             for _ in range(iterations):
 329:                 store.locate_chunk(ids[idx % len(ids)])
 330:                 idx = (idx + stride) % (len(ids) * stride)
 331:             return iterations * 32
 332: 
 333:         result = _bench(
 334:             "native_chunk_store_locate",
 335:             go,
 336:             iterations=1,
 337:             metadata={"chunks_indexed": len(ids), "lookups": iterations},
 338:         )
 339:         store.close()
 340:     return result
