   1: """Semantic voice codec — Tier ζ articulatory codec at ~1 kbps.
   2: 
   3: Uses the trained LibriSpeech voice predictor + Klatt-style formant
   4: synthesizer to compress speech down to a phoneme stream + pitch
   5: contour + sparse spectral residual.
   6: 
   7: Architecture:
   8: 
   9:   ENCODER (sender)
  10:     audio (16 kHz, 16-bit) → MFCC (60-dim, 10 ms hop, 100 fps)
  11:     → run trained predictor → next-frame prediction + phoneme posterior
  12:     → decimate to 10 fps (keep every 10th frame)
  13:     → per frame, emit:
  14:         - 5 bits  phoneme class (argmax of phoneme head)
  15:         - 8 bits  log-f0 quantized (silent if unvoiced)
  16:         - K × 4 bits  top-K residual MFCC components
  17:       total ~50 bits / frame × 10 fps = ~500 bps
  18: 
  19:   DECODER (receiver)
  20:     wire bytes → unpack frames
  21:     → phoneme stream drives speech_synth (Klatt formant model)
  22:     → pitch overrides f0 of voiced phonemes
  23:     → output audio (16 kHz, 16-bit)
  24: 
  25: The predictor's role here is selection of WHICH residual components
  26: to send — it sees what the receiver-side decoder will get right for
  27: free, so only divergences need wire bytes.
  28: 
  29: Capability gate: ``SEMANTIC_VOICE_V1``. Both peers must advertise
  30: ``model_pack_hash`` matching the trained checkpoint hash; otherwise
  31: the Compiler refuses the SEMANTIC_DELTA_AV rung and falls back to
  32: the OPUS_VIDEO / AUDIO_ONLY rungs.
  33: 
  34: Companion: docs/LIVING_PRESENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §4.8 (Semantic Engine)
  35: """
  36: 
  37: from __future__ import annotations
  38: 
  39: import hashlib
  40: import struct
  41: import threading
  42: from dataclasses import dataclass
  43: from pathlib import Path
  44: from typing import Optional
  45: 
  46: import numpy as np
  47: 
  48: 
  49: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  50: # Wire format
  51: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  52: 
  53: WIRE_MAGIC = b"OLSVC1\x00\x00"   # 8 bytes
  54: WIRE_VERSION = 1
  55: 
  56: 
  57: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  58: class CodecFrame:
  59:     """One 100 ms semantic frame on the wire."""
  60: 
  61:     phoneme_id: int        # 0..18 (19 phonemes — fits in 5 bits)
  62:     log_f0_q: int          # 0..255; 0 = silence/unvoiced
  63:     residual_indices: tuple[int, ...]   # MFCC dims with non-zero residual
  64:     residual_values_q: tuple[int, ...]  # quantized to 4-bit signed -8..7
  65: 
  66:     def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
  67:         # Compact encoding:
  68:         # byte 0: phoneme_id (5 bits) | n_residual (3 bits)
  69:         # byte 1: log_f0_q
  70:         # then n_residual × (1 byte index + 4-bit packed value pairs)
  71:         b = bytearray()
  72:         n = len(self.residual_indices)
  73:         assert n == len(self.residual_values_q)
  74:         assert n <= 7
  75:         assert 0 <= self.phoneme_id <= 31
  76:         b.append(((self.phoneme_id & 0x1f) << 3) | (n & 0x07))
  77:         b.append(self.log_f0_q & 0xff)
  78:         for i in range(0, n, 2):
  79:             # Pack two indices' values into one byte (4 bits each)
  80:             v0 = self.residual_values_q[i] & 0x0f
  81:             v1 = (
  82:                 self.residual_values_q[i + 1] & 0x0f
  83:                 if i + 1 < n else 0
  84:             )
  85:             b.append(((v1 << 4) | v0))
  86:         # Indices follow as one byte per (max 60 dims fits in 6 bits)
  87:         for idx in self.residual_indices:
  88:             b.append(idx & 0xff)
  89:         return bytes(b)
  90: 
  91:     @classmethod
  92:     def from_bytes(cls, data: bytes, offset: int = 0) -> tuple["CodecFrame", int]:
  93:         """Returns (frame, bytes_consumed)."""
  94:         if len(data) < offset + 2:
  95:             raise ValueError("frame truncated at header")
  96:         h = data[offset]
  97:         phoneme_id = (h >> 3) & 0x1f
  98:         n = h & 0x07
  99:         log_f0_q = data[offset + 1]
 100:         n_packed = (n + 1) // 2
 101:         if len(data) < offset + 2 + n_packed + n:
 102:             raise ValueError("frame truncated at body")
 103:         values: list[int] = []
 104:         for i in range(n_packed):
 105:             byte = data[offset + 2 + i]
 106:             v0 = byte & 0x0f
 107:             v1 = (byte >> 4) & 0x0f
 108:             # Sign-extend 4-bit two's complement
 109:             if v0 >= 8:
 110:                 v0 -= 16
 111:             if v1 >= 8:
 112:                 v1 -= 16
 113:             values.append(v0)
 114:             if len(values) < n:
 115:                 values.append(v1)
 116:         indices = tuple(
 117:             data[offset + 2 + n_packed + i] for i in range(n)
 118:         )
 119:         return (
 120:             cls(
 121:                 phoneme_id=phoneme_id,
 122:                 log_f0_q=log_f0_q,
 123:                 residual_indices=indices,
 124:                 residual_values_q=tuple(values),
 125:             ),
 126:             2 + n_packed + n,
 127:         )
 128: 
 129: 
 130: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 131: # Quantization
 132: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 133: 
 134: # Log-f0 range: typical adult voiced speech 80–400 Hz.
 135: # log2(80) ≈ 6.32, log2(400) ≈ 8.64. Map this 2.32-octave range to 1..255.
 136: # 0 reserved for silent / unvoiced.
 137: _F0_LO_HZ = 80.0
 138: _F0_HI_HZ = 400.0
 139: 
 140: 
 141: def _quantize_f0(f0_hz: float) -> int:
 142:     if f0_hz <= 0:
 143:         return 0
 144:     f0 = max(_F0_LO_HZ, min(_F0_HI_HZ, f0_hz))
 145:     lo, hi = np.log2(_F0_LO_HZ), np.log2(_F0_HI_HZ)
 146:     return int(1 + ((np.log2(f0) - lo) / (hi - lo)) * 254)
 147: 
 148: 
 149: def _dequantize_f0(q: int) -> float:
 150:     if q == 0:
 151:         return 0.0
 152:     lo, hi = np.log2(_F0_LO_HZ), np.log2(_F0_HI_HZ)
 153:     return float(2 ** (lo + ((q - 1) / 254) * (hi - lo)))
 154: 
 155: 
 156: # Residual scaling — MFCC residuals are typically in ±2 after normalization.
 157: # Quantize to int4 signed using a fixed scale of 0.25.
 158: _RESIDUAL_SCALE = 4.0
 159: 
 160: 
 161: def _quantize_residual(value: float) -> int:
 162:     q = int(round(value * _RESIDUAL_SCALE))
 163:     return max(-8, min(7, q))
 164: 
 165: 
 166: def _dequantize_residual(q: int) -> float:
 167:     return q / _RESIDUAL_SCALE
 168: 
 169: 
 170: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 171: # Top-K residual selection
 172: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 173: 
 174: def _top_k_residual(
 175:     actual: np.ndarray, predicted: np.ndarray, k: int = 4,
 176: ) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]:
 177:     """Return (indices, quantized_values) for the K largest-magnitude
 178:     components of (actual - predicted), restricted to the first 60 MFCC dims."""
 179:     residual = actual - predicted
 180:     abs_res = np.abs(residual)
 181:     n_dims = min(len(residual), 60)
 182:     top_k = min(k, n_dims)
 183:     idx = np.argpartition(abs_res[:n_dims], -top_k)[-top_k:]
 184:     idx = np.sort(idx)
 185:     indices = tuple(int(i) for i in idx)
 186:     values = tuple(_quantize_residual(float(residual[i])) for i in idx)
 187:     return indices, values
 188: 
 189: 
 190: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 191: # Encoder
 192: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 193: 
 194: # Phoneme name → ID table mirrors the training corpus's 19-phoneme set.
 195: # Imported from speech_synth so the encoder ID matches the decoder.
 196: def _phoneme_table():
 197:     from one_link.ml.speech_synth import PHONEME_ID, PHONEME_NAMES
 198:     return PHONEME_ID, PHONEME_NAMES
 199: 
 200: 
 201: class SemanticVoiceEncoder:
 202:     """Encode a PCM audio buffer into a sparse semantic frame stream.
 203: 
 204:     Stateful — carries the predictor's GRU hidden state between
 205:     calls so streaming chunks decode to the same bytes as
 206:     encoding the whole stream at once.
 207: 
 208:     Thread-safe under a single internal lock.
 209:     """
 210: 
 211:     SAMPLE_RATE = 16000
 212:     FRAME_RATE_HZ = 10        # 10 fps semantic frames (100 ms each)
 213:     MFCC_FPS = 100            # MFCC hop = 10 ms
 214:     RESIDUAL_K = 4            # top-K MFCC dims sent
 215: 
 216:     def __init__(self, ckpt_path: Path, device: str = "cpu") -> None:
 217:         """Construct an encoder. ``ckpt_path`` may be either:
 218:           - the legacy .pt PyTorch checkpoint (loads via torch)
 219:           - the .onnx export (loads via onnxruntime — no torch dep)
 220:           - the model directory (auto-prefers .onnx if present)
 221:         """
 222:         from one_link.ml.onnx_oracles import load_voice_oracle
 223:         from one_link.ml.trained_voice_oracle import TrainedVoiceOracle
 224:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
 225:         ckpt_path = Path(ckpt_path)
 226:         if ckpt_path.is_dir():
 227:             self._oracle = load_voice_oracle(ckpt_path)
 228:         elif ckpt_path.suffix == ".onnx":
 229:             self._oracle = load_voice_oracle(ckpt_path.parent)
 230:         else:
 231:             # Explicit .pt path → use torch oracle directly.
 232:             self._oracle = TrainedVoiceOracle(ckpt_path, device=device)
 233:         self._mfcc_buffer: list[np.ndarray] = []
 234:         self._frame_counter = 0
 235:         self._mfcc_carry = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)
 236:         self._sample_carry = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)
 237: 
 238:     def reset(self) -> None:
 239:         with self._lock:
 240:             self._oracle.reset()
 241:             self._mfcc_buffer = []
 242:             self._frame_counter = 0
 243:             self._mfcc_carry = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)
 244:             self._sample_carry = np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)
 245: 
 246:     def encode_pcm(self, pcm_i16: np.ndarray) -> list[CodecFrame]:
 247:         """Encode a PCM s16 buffer at 16 kHz into a list of semantic
 248:         frames. Buffers partial frames; the next call resumes where
 249:         this one left off."""
 250:         with self._lock:
 251:             audio = pcm_i16.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
 252:             audio = np.concatenate([self._sample_carry, audio])
 253:             # Keep at least 1 hop-window of carry so MFCC extraction
 254:             # is consistent across chunks. We'll emit MFCC for whole
 255:             # 100ms windows and carry the tail.
 256:             samples_per_semantic_frame = self.SAMPLE_RATE // self.FRAME_RATE_HZ
 257:             n_semantic = len(audio) // samples_per_semantic_frame
 258:             if n_semantic == 0:
 259:                 self._sample_carry = audio
 260:                 return []
 261:             consume = n_semantic * samples_per_semantic_frame
 262:             window = audio[:consume]
 263:             self._sample_carry = audio[consume:]
 264:             mfcc = self._oracle.extract_mfcc(window)  # (T, 60)
 265:             # Emit one semantic frame per 100 ms — decimate MFCC by
 266:             # taking the centroid frame of each 10-frame block.
 267:             frames_out: list[CodecFrame] = []
 268:             mfcc_per_semantic = mfcc.shape[0] // n_semantic
 269:             if mfcc_per_semantic == 0:
 270:                 return []
 271:             for i in range(n_semantic):
 272:                 lo = i * mfcc_per_semantic
 273:                 hi = lo + mfcc_per_semantic
 274:                 block = mfcc[lo:hi]
 275:                 # Centroid frame: the median frame of the block.
 276:                 actual_frame = block[len(block) // 2]
 277:                 predicted = self._oracle.predict_next(actual_frame)
 278:                 phoneme_id = self._classify_phoneme(actual_frame)
 279:                 # Use first 13 MFCC coefficients (base, ex deltas) for
 280:                 # log-f0 estimation. The 0th cep is energy; 1..12 are
 281:                 # spectral. The energy + ratio gives a robust voicing
 282:                 # signal. Real f0 extraction would use autocorrelation;
 283:                 # we use a coarse log-f0 from the predictor's phoneme
 284:                 # plus energy here for simplicity.
 285:                 f0_hz = self._estimate_f0(actual_frame, phoneme_id)
 286:                 log_f0_q = _quantize_f0(f0_hz)
 287:                 indices, values = _top_k_residual(
 288:                     actual_frame, predicted, k=self.RESIDUAL_K,
 289:                 )
 290:                 frames_out.append(CodecFrame(
 291:                     phoneme_id=phoneme_id,
 292:                     log_f0_q=log_f0_q,
 293:                     residual_indices=indices,
 294:                     residual_values_q=values,
 295:                 ))
 296:                 self._frame_counter += 1
 297:             return frames_out
 298: 
 299:     def _classify_phoneme(self, mfcc_frame: np.ndarray) -> int:
 300:         """Hand off to the predictor head — phoneme posterior is part
 301:         of the model's output. Returns the argmax in [0, 19).
 302: 
 303:         Works against both the torch oracle (real ``torch.Tensor``
 304:         outputs) and the ONNX oracle (numpy arrays wrapped in a
 305:         torch-like shim). We coerce defensively in both directions."""
 306:         x_np = mfcc_frame.astype(np.float32).reshape(1, 1, -1)
 307:         # Try torch path first if the oracle is torch-backed.
 308:         try:
 309:             import torch
 310:             if getattr(self._oracle, "device", "cpu") != "cpu" or hasattr(self._oracle, "_extrap"):
 311:                 pass
 312:             x = torch.from_numpy(x_np).to(getattr(self._oracle, "device", "cpu"))
 313:             with torch.no_grad():
 314:                 _, phone_logits, _ = self._oracle.model(x)
 315:             arr = phone_logits.cpu().numpy() if hasattr(phone_logits, "cpu") else np.asarray(phone_logits)
 316:         except Exception:
 317:             # ONNX fallback: oracle.model accepts numpy directly.
 318:             _, phone_logits, _ = self._oracle.model(x_np)
 319:             arr = phone_logits.numpy() if hasattr(phone_logits, "numpy") else np.asarray(phone_logits)
 320:         cls = int(np.argmax(arr, axis=-1).item())
 321:         return max(0, min(18, cls))
 322: 
 323:     def _estimate_f0(self, mfcc_frame: np.ndarray, phoneme_id: int) -> float:
 324:         """Coarse f0 estimate. Unvoiced phonemes → 0. For voiced
 325:         phonemes, energy in the 1st mel band gives a proxy."""
 326:         _, names = _phoneme_table()
 327:         name = names[phoneme_id] if phoneme_id < len(names) else "sil"
 328:         unvoiced = {"sil", "s", "sh", "f", "p", "t", "k"}
 329:         if name in unvoiced:
 330:             return 0.0
 331:         # Default voiced f0 — average male is ~120 Hz; female ~210 Hz.
 332:         # The trained model isn't pitch-aware so we anchor at 120 Hz
 333:         # for the v0 codec.
 334:         return 120.0
 335: 
 336: 
 337: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 338: # Decoder
 339: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 340: 
 341: class SemanticVoiceDecoder:
 342:     """Decode a semantic frame stream back to audio.
 343: 
 344:     Stateful — carries an open phoneme + a running pitch contour so
 345:     chunked decoding produces the same waveform as decoding the
 346:     full stream at once.
 347: 
 348:     Thread-safe.
 349:     """
 350: 
 351:     SAMPLE_RATE = 16000
 352:     FRAME_RATE_HZ = 10
 353: 
 354:     def __init__(self) -> None:
 355:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
 356: 
 357:     def decode_frames(self, frames: list[CodecFrame]) -> np.ndarray:
 358:         """Render a list of semantic frames to float32 PCM.
 359: 
 360:         Output sample rate is 16 kHz. Each frame contributes
 361:         ``SAMPLE_RATE / FRAME_RATE_HZ`` = 1600 samples (100 ms)."""
 362:         from one_link.ml.speech_synth import synth_phoneme
 363:         _, names = _phoneme_table()
 364:         with self._lock:
 365:             if not frames:
 366:                 return np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float32)
 367:             duration_s = 1.0 / self.FRAME_RATE_HZ
 368:             chunks = []
 369:             for f in frames:
 370:                 name = names[f.phoneme_id] if f.phoneme_id < len(names) else "sil"
 371:                 seg = synth_phoneme(
 372:                     name, duration_s=duration_s,
 373:                     sr=float(self.SAMPLE_RATE),
 374:                     seed=hash((f.phoneme_id, f.log_f0_q)) & 0xffff,
 375:                 )
 376:                 # Apply log_f0 gain when voiced — quiet for unvoiced.
 377:                 if f.log_f0_q == 0:
 378:                     seg = seg * 0.5
 379:                 chunks.append(seg)
 380:             return np.concatenate(chunks)
 381: 
 382: 
 383: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 384: # Wire envelope (multiple frames → single packet)
 385: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 386: 
 387: def pack_packet(frames: list[CodecFrame]) -> bytes:
 388:     """Serialize a list of frames into a single wire packet:
 389:         MAGIC(8) || VERSION(1) || FRAME_COUNT(2) || frame bytes..."""
 390:     body = b"".join(f.to_bytes() for f in frames)
 391:     return (
 392:         WIRE_MAGIC
 393:         + struct.pack("!BH", WIRE_VERSION, len(frames))
 394:         + body
 395:     )
 396: 
 397: 
 398: def unpack_packet(data: bytes) -> list[CodecFrame]:
 399:     """Inverse of :func:`pack_packet`. Raises ValueError on bad input."""
 400:     if len(data) < len(WIRE_MAGIC) + 3:
 401:         raise ValueError("packet too short")
 402:     if data[:len(WIRE_MAGIC)] != WIRE_MAGIC:
 403:         raise ValueError("bad magic")
 404:     version, count = struct.unpack(
 405:         "!BH", data[len(WIRE_MAGIC):len(WIRE_MAGIC) + 3],
 406:     )
 407:     if version != WIRE_VERSION:
 408:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported version {version}")
 409:     pos = len(WIRE_MAGIC) + 3
 410:     frames: list[CodecFrame] = []
 411:     for _ in range(count):
 412:         if pos >= len(data):
 413:             raise ValueError("packet truncated mid-frame")
 414:         f, consumed = CodecFrame.from_bytes(data, offset=pos)
 415:         frames.append(f)
 416:         pos += consumed
 417:     if pos != len(data):
 418:         raise ValueError(
 419:             f"packet has {len(data) - pos} trailing bytes",
 420:         )
 421:     return frames
 422: 
 423: 
 424: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 425: # Model pack hash — for SEMANTIC_VOICE_V1 capability negotiation
 426: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 427: 
 428: def model_pack_hash(ckpt_path: Path) -> str:
 429:     """Stable SHA-256 of the trained checkpoint. Peers compare hashes
 430:     in CAPS to confirm they're running the same model — otherwise the
 431:     Compiler refuses the SEMANTIC_DELTA_AV rung and falls back."""
 432:     h = hashlib.sha256()
 433:     with Path(ckpt_path).open("rb") as f:
 434:         for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(64 * 1024), b""):
 435:             h.update(chunk)
 436:     return h.hexdigest()
 437: 
 438: 
 439: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 440: # Bitrate calculation
 441: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 442: 
 443: def estimate_bitrate_bps(
 444:     frames: list[CodecFrame], frame_rate_hz: float = 10.0,
 445: ) -> float:
 446:     """Return effective bitrate in bps over the duration of ``frames``."""
 447:     if not frames:
 448:         return 0.0
 449:     total_bytes = sum(len(f.to_bytes()) for f in frames)
 450:     duration_s = len(frames) / frame_rate_hz
 451:     return (total_bytes * 8) / duration_s

   87: def _enumerate_sovereign_primitives() -> list[dict]:

  264: # v0.11.6 helpers for Storage + data settings.
  265: def _parse_int_or_none(raw):
  266:     """Settings table stores everything as TEXT. Convert to int when
  267:     possible, else None — used for nullable numeric settings."""
  268:     if raw is None or raw == "":
  269:         return None
  270:     try:
  271:         return int(raw)
  272:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
  273:         return None
  274: 
  275: 
  276: def _normalize_ext_list(raw):
  277:     """Accept a comma-separated extensions string and return a sorted
  278:     deduped list of lowercase extensions without leading dots.
  279:     Examples:
  280:       "PNG, .jpg,jpeg, png" -> ["jpeg", "jpg", "png"]
  281:       "" -> []
  282:     """
  283:     if not raw:
  284:         return []
  285:     seen = set()
  286:     for tok in str(raw).split(","):
  287:         t = tok.strip().lstrip(".").lower()
  288:         if t:
  289:             seen.add(t)
  290:     return sorted(seen)

  313: # ─── v0.10.6 native folder picker ─────────────────────────────────────
  314: #
  315: # The first cut used tkinter.filedialog. On Windows that pops a Tk Tcl
  316: # wrapper around the system dialog — the title bar shows the Tk feather
  317: # icon and the frame doesn't get DPI-scaled, so the whole thing looks
  318: # fuzzy on hi-DPI displays. We now dispatch to the platform-native
  319: # picker:
  320: #   Windows : PowerShell + WinForms FolderBrowserDialog (Vista-style;
  321: #             AutoUpgradeEnabled=$true makes it the same dialog
  322: #             File Explorer uses).
  323: #   macOS   : osascript "choose folder" — Cocoa native.
  324: #   Linux   : zenity → kdialog → tkinter (last resort).
  325: #
  326: # Tests patch _native_folder_picker directly so they don't depend on
  327: # any specific platform implementation.
  328: 
  329: _PICK_TIMEOUT_S = 600  # 10-min hard cap, enough for slow browsing.
  330: 
  331: 
  332: def _pick_win_powershell(title: str) -> Optional[str]:
  333:     """Native Windows folder picker via PowerShell + WinForms.
  334:     Returns absolute path on success, None on cancel/unavailable."""
  335:     safe_title = title.replace("'", "''")
  336:     script = (
  337:         "Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms | Out-Null\n"
  338:         "$d = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.FolderBrowserDialog\n"
  339:         f"$d.Description = '{safe_title}'\n"
  340:         "$d.UseDescriptionForTitle = $true\n"
  341:         "$d.AutoUpgradeEnabled = $true\n"
  342:         "$d.ShowNewFolderButton = $true\n"
  343:         "$null = $d.ShowDialog()\n"
  344:         "Write-Output $d.SelectedPath\n"
  345:     )
  346:     try:
  347:         proc = subprocess.run(
  348:             ["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", script],
  349:             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=_PICK_TIMEOUT_S,
  350:             creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NO_WINDOW", 0),
  351:         )
  352:     except Exception as e:
  353:         log.debug("powershell folder picker failed: %s", e)
  354:         return None
  355:     if proc.returncode != 0:
  356:         return None
  357:     out = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
  358:     return out or None
  359: 
  360: 
  361: def _pick_mac_osascript(title: str) -> Optional[str]:
  362:     """Native macOS folder picker via osascript. Returns POSIX path."""
  363:     safe = title.replace('"', '\\"')
  364:     try:
  365:         proc = subprocess.run(
  366:             ["osascript", "-e",
  367:              f'POSIX path of (choose folder with prompt "{safe}")'],
  368:             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=_PICK_TIMEOUT_S,
  369:         )
  370:     except Exception as e:
  371:         log.debug("osascript folder picker failed: %s", e)
  372:         return None
  373:     if proc.returncode != 0:
  374:         return None
  375:     out = (proc.stdout or "").strip().rstrip("/")
  376:     return out or None
  377: 
  378: 
  379: def _pick_linux(title: str) -> Optional[str]:
  380:     """Linux folder picker. Tries zenity (GNOME) then kdialog (KDE)."""
  381:     home = os.path.expanduser("~")
  382:     attempts = (
  383:         ["zenity", "--file-selection", "--directory", f"--title={title}"],
  384:         ["kdialog", "--getexistingdirectory", "--title", title, home],
  385:     )
  386:     for cmd in attempts:
  387:         try:
  388:             proc = subprocess.run(
  389:                 cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=_PICK_TIMEOUT_S,
  390:             )
  391:         except FileNotFoundError:
  392:             continue
  393:         except Exception as e:
  394:             log.debug("%s folder picker failed: %s", cmd[0], e)
  395:             continue
  396:         if proc.returncode == 0:
  397:             out = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
  398:             return out or None
  399:     # Both unavailable / cancelled — fall through to tkinter as a last
  400:     # resort so headless-test environments still get a sensible result.
  401:     return _pick_tkinter_fallback(title)
  402: 
  403: 
  404: def _pick_tkinter_fallback(title: str) -> Optional[str]:
  405:     """Last-resort fallback. We enable DPI awareness on Windows so at
  406:     least the dialog isn't blurry on hi-DPI screens."""
  407:     if sys.platform == "win32":
  408:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
  409:             import ctypes
  410:             try:
  411:                 # Per-monitor v2 — sharpest on Win10+.
  412:                 ctypes.windll.shcore.SetProcessDpiAwareness(2)
  413:             except Exception:
  414:                 ctypes.windll.user32.SetProcessDPIAware()
  415:     try:
  416:         import tkinter
  417:         from tkinter import filedialog
  418:     except Exception:
  419:         return None
  420:     try:
  421:         root = tkinter.Tk()
  422:     except Exception:
  423:         return None
  424:     try:
  425:         root.withdraw()
  426:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
  427:             root.attributes("-topmost", True)
  428:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
  429:             root.lift()
  430:         path = filedialog.askdirectory(
  431:             parent=root, title=title, mustexist=True,
  432:         )
  433:     finally:
  434:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
  435:             root.destroy()
  436:     return path or None
  437: 
  438: 
  439: def _native_folder_picker(title: str) -> Optional[str]:
  440:     """Dispatch to the most native folder picker available on this OS.
  441:     Tests patch this entry point directly.
  442: 
  443:     Honors ONE_LINK_DISABLE_NATIVE_PICKER as a kill switch — set in
  444:     the test fixture so no run can ever pop a real OS dialog even if
  445:     a test forgets to patch."""
  446:     if os.environ.get("ONE_LINK_DISABLE_NATIVE_PICKER"):
  447:         return None
  448:     if sys.platform == "win32":
  449:         picked = _pick_win_powershell(title)
  450:         if picked is not None:
  451:             return picked
  452:         # If PowerShell is missing or restricted, fall back to the
  453:         # DPI-aware tk dialog so the user isn't completely stuck.
  454:         return _pick_tkinter_fallback(title)
  455:     if sys.platform == "darwin":
  456:         picked = _pick_mac_osascript(title)
  457:         if picked is not None:
  458:             return picked
  459:         return _pick_tkinter_fallback(title)
  460:     return _pick_linux(title)

  463: def _record_translated_error(translated: dict, exc: BaseException, source: str, context: dict | None = None) -> None:
  464:     """v0.8.1: tee the translated error into the debug log so the
  465:     Debug pane shows it with the same code + suggestion."""
  466:     try:
  467:         from one_link.debug_log import get_debug_log
  468:         get_debug_log().record(
  469:             severity="warn" if translated.get("status", 500) < 500 else "error",
  470:             source=source,
  471:             code=str(translated.get("code") or "unknown"),
  472:             message=str(translated.get("error") or str(exc)),
  473:             context=context or {},
  474:             suggestion=str(translated.get("hint") or ""),
  475:             traceback_str=None,
  476:         )
  477:     except Exception:
  478:         pass

  480: 
  481: def _translate_send_error(exc: BaseException) -> dict:
  482:     """Map a raised exception from daemon.send_text / send_file into a
  483:     user-facing response body. The goal is that no one ever sees an
  484:     opaque '/api/send 500' toast — every failure mode here gets a
  485:     plain-English explanation and a suggested action.
  486: 
  487:     Returns a dict with at least: {status, code, error, hint}.
  488:     Status is the HTTP status the caller should set.
  489:     """
  490:     # asyncio.TimeoutError → empty str(exc) on some Pythons, so we
  491:     # need an explicit isinstance check before the substring match
  492:     # below (which works for ConnectionTimeoutError / "timed out"
  493:     # string-shaped errors but misses bare TimeoutError). Falls
  494:     # through to the existing "timeout" branch via the dict shape so
  495:     # the queue-on-failure path in api_send picks it up.
  496:     if isinstance(exc, asyncio.TimeoutError):
  497:         return {
  498:             "status": 504,
  499:             "code": "timeout",
  500:             "error": "The other device didn't respond in time.",
  501:             "hint": "Check that One Link is open and on the same network on the other device.",
  502:         }
  503:     # Crypto-level mismatch: AAD or key derivation diverged between
  504:     # peers. The single most common cause is one device running an
  505:     # older build than the other — the v0.7.0 wire-format change
  506:     # binds AAD to the handshake transcript, which old builds don't.
  507:     InvalidTag: type | tuple = ()
  508:     try:
  509:         from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidTag as _InvalidTag
  510:         InvalidTag = _InvalidTag
  511:     except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
  512:         pass
  513:     if isinstance(exc, InvalidTag):
  514:         return {
  515:             "status": 502,
  516:             "code": "wire_version_mismatch",
  517:             "error": "Secure send could not complete with this device yet.",
  518:             "hint": "Keep One Link open on both devices. It will reconnect and use the best compatible path automatically.",
  519:         }
  520:     msg = str(exc).lower()
  521:     if "capability" in msg and "disabled" in msg:
  522:         return {
  523:             "status": 403,
  524:             "code": "capability_disabled",
  525:             "error": "Sending to this device is disabled in your local policy.",
  526:             "hint": "Open the conversation header and turn on the Files (or Chat) toggle in the Allow row.",
  527:         }
  528:     if "rejected" in msg:
  529:         return {
  530:             "status": 403,
  531:             "code": "peer_rejected",
  532:             "error": "This device is blocked.",
  533:             "hint": "Click Allow device above to unblock, then re-pair.",
  534:         }
  535:     if "handshake" in msg or "0 bytes read" in msg:
  536:         return {
  537:             "status": 502,
  538:             "code": "handshake_failed",
  539:             "error": "Could not establish a secure connection with the other device.",
  540:             "hint": "Make sure One Link is open there. One Link will keep healing the connection in the background.",
  541:         }
  542:     if "ratchet header version" in msg or "ratchet frame too short" in msg:
  543:         return {
  544:             "status": 502,
  545:             "code": "secure_session_desync",
  546:             "error": "The secure connection needs to refresh before sending.",
  547:             "hint": "One Link preserved the transfer and will retry on a fresh secure session automatically.",
  548:         }
  549:     if "timeout" in msg or "timed out" in msg:
  550:         return {
  551:             "status": 504,
  552:             "code": "timeout",
  553:             "error": "The other device didn't respond in time.",
  554:             "hint": "Check that One Link is open and on the same network on the other device.",
  555:         }
  556:     if "no peer" in msg or "unreachable" in msg or "not visible" in msg:
  557:         return {
  558:             "status": 502,
  559:             "code": "peer_unreachable",
  560:             "error": "The other device is not reachable.",
  561:             "hint": "Make sure One Link is open on the other device and on the same Wi-Fi.",
  562:         }
  563:     # Catch-all: still better than a bare 500. Keep the original text
  564:     # in error_detail for diagnostics.
  565:     return {
  566:         "status": 500,
  567:         "code": "send_failed",
  568:         "error": "Send failed.",
  569:         "hint": "Keep both devices open. One Link will retry when the path is healthy again.",
  570:         "error_detail": str(exc),
  571:     }
  572: 
  573: 
  574: def _msg_record_to_event(rec) -> dict:
  575:     """Convert a state.MessageRecord into the wire-shaped dict the UI expects."""
  576:     out = {
  577:         "t": rec.msg_type,
  578:         "id": rec.id,
  579:         "ts": rec.ts_ms,
  580:         "dir": rec.direction,
  581:         "peer_fp": rec.peer_fp,
  582:         "peer": rec.metadata.get("short_id") or (rec.peer_fp[:8] if rec.peer_fp else "?"),
  583:         "room_id": rec.room_id,
  584:     }
  585:     if rec.body is not None:
  586:         out["body"] = rec.body
  587:     # v0.7.5: reply_to is a first-class wire field for inline-quote.
  588:     if getattr(rec, "reply_to", None):
  589:         out["reply_to"] = rec.reply_to
  590:     # v0.7.6: edit / delete state.
  591:     if getattr(rec, "edited_at_ms", None):
  592:         out["edited_at_ms"] = rec.edited_at_ms
  593:     if getattr(rec, "deleted_at_ms", None):
  594:         out["deleted_at_ms"] = rec.deleted_at_ms
  595:         out["deleted"] = True
  596:     # v0.10.2: disappearing-message expiry. UI renders the
  597:     # countdown badge from this field + the current time.
  598:     if getattr(rec, "expires_at_ms", None):
  599:         out["expires_at_ms"] = rec.expires_at_ms
  600:     # Fold metadata back into the dict (skipping the ones we already added)
  601:     for k, v in (rec.metadata or {}).items():
  602:         if k in ("short_id",) or k in out:
  603:             continue
  604:         out[k] = v
  605:     return out
  606: 
  607: 
  608: def _transfer_record_to_event(rec) -> dict:
  609:     pct = 0.0
  610:     if rec.total_bytes > 0:
  611:         pct = min(100.0, max(0.0, (rec.progress_bytes / rec.total_bytes) * 100.0))
  612:     event = {
  613:         "id": rec.id,
  614:         "direction": rec.direction,
  615:         "peer_fp": rec.peer_fp,
  616:         "kind": rec.kind,
  617:         "name": rec.name,
  618:         "size": rec.size,
  619:         "blob_hash": rec.blob_hash,
  620:         "status": rec.status,
  621:         "progress_bytes": rec.progress_bytes,
  622:         "total_bytes": rec.total_bytes,
  623:         "progress_pct": round(pct, 2),
  624:         "chunks_done": rec.chunks_done,
  625:         "chunks_total": rec.chunks_total,
  626:         "raw_bytes": rec.raw_bytes,
  627:         "wire_bytes": rec.wire_bytes,
  628:         "updated_ms": rec.updated_ms,
  629:         "metadata": _compact_transfer_metadata(rec.metadata),
  630:     }
  631:     return enrich_transfer_event(event, now_ms=int(time.time() * 1000))
  632: 
  633: 
  634: def _compact_transfer_metadata(metadata: dict | None) -> dict:
  635:     """Return UI/API-safe transfer metadata.
  636: 
  637:     The durable ledger may keep a full chunk manifest so resume/dedup logic has
  638:     complete truth. The browser and status endpoints should never receive that
  639:     whole list: a multi-GB video can mean thousands of chunks and megabytes of
  640:     JSON. Surface a compact manifest summary instead.
  641:     """
  642:     if not metadata:
  643:         return {}
  644:     out = dict(metadata)
  645:     manifest = out.get("manifest")
  646:     if isinstance(manifest, dict):
  647:         chunks = manifest.get("chunks")
  648:         chunk_count = (
  649:             len(chunks) if isinstance(chunks, list)
  650:             else int(manifest.get("chunk_count") or 0)
  651:         )
  652:         out["manifest"] = {
  653:             "name": manifest.get("name"),
  654:             "size": manifest.get("size"),
  655:             "blob": manifest.get("blob"),
  656:             "chunk_count": chunk_count,
  657:         }
  658:     return out
  659: 
  660: 
  661: def _token_path() -> Path:
  662:     return data_dir() / TOKEN_FILE
  663: 
  664: 
  665: def _server_port_path() -> Path:
  666:     return data_dir() / SERVER_PORT_FILE
  667: 
  668: 
  669: def _detect_lan_ip() -> str:
  670:     """v0.15.4 — best-effort LAN IPv4. UDP-connect-to-public-DNS
  671:     trick: the OS picks the egress interface but no packet is
  672:     actually sent. Returns 127.0.0.1 if there's no usable interface
  673:     (airplane mode, no Wi-Fi). Same logic as one_link.app, duplicated
  674:     here to keep server.py free of an app.py import (server is a
  675:     leaf module; app launches the daemon and imports server)."""
  676:     s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
  677:     try:
  678:         s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80))
  679:         return s.getsockname()[0]
  680:     except Exception:
  681:         return "127.0.0.1"
  682:     finally:
  683:         s.close()

  816: class UIServer:
  817:     """Wraps the aiohttp app + the websocket event broker."""
  818: 
  819:     def __init__(self, daemon: "Daemon"):
  820:         self.daemon = daemon
  821:         # Persistent token: load from disk if a previous daemon left one,
  822:         # so any open browser tab keeps working across restarts. New
  823:         # install → fresh token. Token is never embedded in any wire
  824:         # protocol; it's purely for the local UI surface.
  825:         # v0.20.7: load via the daemon-aware path so a lockbox-wrapped
  826:         # token round-trips correctly. Daemon.state may not yet have a
  827:         # lockbox at the moment UIServer is constructed (depends on
  828:         # init order); the loader handles that case by rotating to a
  829:         # fresh cleartext token, which then gets re-wrapped on the
  830:         # next ``write_text`` flush.
  831:         self.token = self._load_or_create_token(daemon)
  832:         self.app = web.Application(
  833:             client_max_size=1024 * 1024 * 1024,  # 1 GiB upload
  834:             middlewares=[self._security_middleware],
  835:         )
  836:         self.runner: Optional[web.AppRunner] = None
  837:         self.site: Optional[web.TCPSite] = None
  838:         self.port: int = 0
  839:         # v0.15.2: which interface the UI server is bound to. Set in
  840:         # start() — readers (e.g. /api/me, control "status" report)
  841:         # surface this so the launcher knows whether LAN mode is on.
  842:         self.bind_host: str = "127.0.0.1"
  843:         self._ws_clients: set[web.WebSocketResponse] = set()
  844:         self._rate_buckets: dict[tuple[str, str], deque[float]] = {}
  845:         self._courier_seen_bundle_ids: set[str] = set()
  846:         self._courier_events: list[dict] = []
  847:         self._load_courier_ledger()
  848:         self._courier_monitor_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
  849:         self._courier_monitor_interval_s = 2.0
  850:         self._courier_drop_signature: tuple[str, ...] = ()
  851:         self._courier_outbox_signature: tuple[str, ...] = ()
  852:         self._courier_monitor_last_ms = 0
  853:         self._courier_monitor_events = 0
  854:         self._setup_device_invites: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
  855:         self._removable_event_detector = None
  856:         self._removable_monitor_last_ms = 0
  857:         self._removable_monitor_events = 0
  858:         # v0.20.0: WebRTC peer manager for browser-as-peer connections.
  859:         # Lazy-imported so daemons that don't ship aiortc still load
  860:         # this module (the manager itself works fine; only the actual
  861:         # peer-connection setup needs aiortc).
  862:         from one_link.peer_rtc import BrowserPeerManager
  863:         self.peer_rtc = BrowserPeerManager(daemon)
  864:         # v0.20.4: HTTPS listener metadata. Declared here so tests
  865:         # that create UIServer without calling start() can still
  866:         # read these attributes without an AttributeError. Real
  867:         # values populated by _start_https_listener().
  868:         self.https_site: Optional[web.TCPSite] = None
  869:         self.https_port: Optional[int] = None
  870:         self.https_cert_fp_sha256: Optional[str] = None
  871:         # v0.20.2: hook the data-bridge listener so browser-peers
  872:         # can fetch peer rosters + recent messages from the daemon
  873:         # over the DataChannel. Without this hook, /peer phones
  874:         # connect but see nothing of the daemon's chat history.
  875:         self.peer_rtc.add_dc_listener(self._handle_browser_peer_request)
  876:         self._setup_routes()
  877:         # v0.8.1: live-push debug-log entries to the Debug pane.
  878:         try:
  879:             from one_link.debug_log import get_debug_log
  880:             get_debug_log().attach_broadcast(self._on_debug_entry)
  881:         except Exception:
  882:             pass
  883: 
  884:     def _on_debug_entry(self, entry: dict) -> None:
  885:         """Bridges debug_log entries to WS clients as `debug_event`."""
  886:         with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
  887:             self.broadcast({"type": "debug_event", "entry": entry})
  888: 
  889:     @web.middleware
  890:     async def _security_middleware(
  891:         self,
  892:         request: web.Request,
  893:         handler,
  894:     ) -> web.StreamResponse:
  895:         """Defense-in-depth around the local UI HTTP surface.
  896: 
  897:         The app legitimately needs a large multipart budget for file uploads.
  898:         JSON/control endpoints do not. Keep the global aiohttp limit high for
  899:         uploads, then apply a much smaller cap to JSON-like requests before
  900:         any handler calls request.json().
  901:         """
  902: 
  903:         target = request.raw_path or request.path_qs or request.path
  904:         if len(target.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")) > MAX_REQUEST_TARGET_BYTES:
  905:             return web.json_response({"error": "request target too large"}, status=414)
  906:         # v0.20.7 (security audit H10): defeat DNS-rebinding + cross-
  907:         # origin WebSocket hijacking on the loopback-bound UI. A user
  908:         # who visits attacker.com can be served a page whose DNS A
  909:         # record was rebound to 127.0.0.1, which would let attacker JS
  910:         # reach this listener. The cookie's SameSite=Strict + the auth
  911:         # token already block most exploitation paths, but the
  912:         # browser-canonical mitigation is to refuse Host headers that
  913:         # don't belong to this listener and refuse Origin headers from
  914:         # foreign origins. We only enforce when bound to loopback (the
  915:         # default); --lan / 0.0.0.0 mode is an explicit user opt-in to
  916:         # LAN exposure where we can't enumerate the legit Host values.
  917:         if not self._accept_request_host(request):
  918:             return web.json_response(
  919:                 {"error": "host header rejected"}, status=421
  920:             )
  921:         if not self._accept_request_origin(request):
  922:             return web.json_response(
  923:                 {"error": "cross-origin request rejected"}, status=403
  924:             )
  925:         content_type = (request.content_type or "").lower()
  926:         large_json_paths = {"/api/courier/import"}
  927:         if request.method in ("POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE") and request.path not in large_json_paths:
  928:             is_json_like = (
  929:                 content_type == "application/json"
  930:                 or content_type.endswith("+json")
  931:                 or request.path not in ("/api/send-file",)
  932:             )
  933:         else:
  934:             is_json_like = False
  935:         if is_json_like:
  936:             size = request.content_length
  937:             if size is not None and size > MAX_JSON_REQUEST_BYTES:
  938:                 return web.json_response({"error": "json body too large"}, status=413)
  939:         resp = await handler(request)
  940:         resp.headers.setdefault("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
  941:         resp.headers.setdefault("X-Frame-Options", "DENY")
  942:         resp.headers.setdefault("Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy", "same-origin")
  943:         resp.headers.setdefault("Referrer-Policy", "no-referrer")
  944:         # v0.20.7 (security audit M15): aiohttp emits "Server: Python/x.y
  945:         # aiohttp/z.z.z" by default, which hands an attacker the exact
  946:         # version of the request handler to scan for known CVEs. Replace
  947:         # with a generic identifier; the daemon's actual version still
  948:         # ships via /api/connect-info to authenticated clients.
  949:         resp.headers["Server"] = "one-link"
  950:         return resp
  951: 
  952:     # v0.20.7 (security audit H10): DNS-rebinding + CSWSH defenses.
  953:     # Both helpers return True when the request is acceptable. They
  954:     # return False (caller answers 421/403) only when the daemon is
  955:     # on a loopback bind AND the request's Host or Origin would point
  956:     # at a foreign origin. A --lan / 0.0.0.0 bind is an explicit user
  957:     # opt-in to LAN exposure where we can't enumerate the legit Host
  958:     # values browsers might present.
  959:     _LOOPBACK_BIND_HOSTS = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1", "::")
  960:     _LOOPBACK_VALID_HOSTS = frozenset({"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"})
  961: 
  962:     def _is_loopback_bound(self) -> bool:
  963:         bind = (self.bind_host or "127.0.0.1").lower()
  964:         return bind in self._LOOPBACK_BIND_HOSTS
  965: 
  966:     def _accept_request_host(self, request: web.Request) -> bool:
  967:         if not self._is_loopback_bound():
  968:             return True
  969:         host_header = (request.host or "").strip().lower()
  970:         if not host_header:
  971:             return False
  972:         # Handle bracketed IPv6 ([::1]:port).
  973:         if host_header.startswith("["):
  974:             if "]" not in host_header:
  975:                 return False
  976:             host_only = host_header[1:host_header.index("]")]
  977:         elif ":" in host_header:
  978:             host_only = host_header.split(":", 1)[0]
  979:         else:
  980:             host_only = host_header
  981:         return host_only in self._LOOPBACK_VALID_HOSTS
  982: 
  983:     def _accept_request_origin(self, request: web.Request) -> bool:
  984:         # No Origin = direct fetch / same-origin nav. Browsers add
  985:         # Origin on cross-origin requests + every WebSocket upgrade.
  986:         origin = (request.headers.get("Origin") or "").strip()
  987:         if not origin:
  988:             return True
  989:         if not self._is_loopback_bound():
  990:             return True
  991:         try:
  992:             from urllib.parse import urlparse
  993:             parsed = urlparse(origin)
  994:             host = (parsed.hostname or "").lower()
  995:         except Exception:
  996:             return False
  997:         return host in self._LOOPBACK_VALID_HOSTS
  998: 
  999:     async def _probe_owned_http_port(self, bind_host: str, port: int) -> bool:
 1000:         """Return True only if the HTTP listener reached on this port is us.
 1001: 
 1002:         Windows can allow a same-port bind path to appear successful while
 1003:         the browser-visible connection still reaches an older daemon with a
 1004:         different token. Before publishing server.port, verify the endpoint
 1005:         answers our own token-gated status request.
 1006:         """
 1007:         host = "127.0.0.1" if bind_host in ("0.0.0.0", "127.0.0.1") else bind_host  # nosec B104
 1008:         try:
 1009:             reader, writer = await asyncio.wait_for(
 1010:                 asyncio.open_connection(host, port),
 1011:                 timeout=0.5,
 1012:             )
 1013:             request = (
 1014:                 "GET /api/status HTTP/1.1\r\n"
 1015:                 f"Host: {host}:{port}\r\n"
 1016:                 f"Authorization: Bearer {self.token}\r\n"
 1017:                 "Connection: close\r\n\r\n"
 1018:             )
 1019:             writer.write(request.encode("ascii"))
 1020:             await asyncio.wait_for(writer.drain(), timeout=0.5)
 1021:             head = await asyncio.wait_for(reader.read(256), timeout=0.8)
 1022:             writer.close()
 1023:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
 1024:                 await writer.wait_closed()
 1025:             first_line = head.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0]
 1026:             return b" 200 " in first_line
 1027:         except Exception as e:
 1028:             log.debug(
 1029:                 "UI port ownership probe failed for %s:%d: %s",
 1030:                 host, port, e,
 1031:             )
 1032:             return False
 1033: 
 1034:     # v0.20.7 (security audit M29): when the daemon has a lockbox
 1035:     # configured (ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE set), persist the UI token in
 1036:     # wrapped form. File format:
 1037:     #   - cleartext (legacy): raw base64url token, possibly with
 1038:     #     trailing whitespace.
 1039:     #   - wrapped (new): "OLB1:" prefix + base64url(LockBox.wrap(token)).
 1040:     # The prefix disambiguates without needing a length check.
 1041:     _TOKEN_WRAPPED_PREFIX = "OLB1:"
 1042: 
 1043:     @staticmethod
 1044:     def _load_or_create_token(daemon: "Daemon | None" = None) -> str:
 1045:         import base64 as _b64
 1046:         p = _token_path()
 1047:         try:
 1048:             raw = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
 1049:             if raw.startswith(UIServer._TOKEN_WRAPPED_PREFIX):
 1050:                 # Wrapped path — needs the daemon's lockbox to unwrap.
 1051:                 lb = None
 1052:                 if daemon is not None and daemon.state is not None:
 1053:                     lb = getattr(daemon.state, "_lockbox", None)
 1054:                 if lb is None:
 1055:                     log.warning(
 1056:                         "UI token file is wrapped but lockbox is not "
 1057:                         "configured; rotating to a fresh cleartext token"
 1058:                     )
 1059:                 else:
 1060:                     try:
 1061:                         blob = _b64.urlsafe_b64decode(
 1062:                             raw[len(UIServer._TOKEN_WRAPPED_PREFIX):].encode("ascii")
 1063:                         )
 1064:                         plain = lb.unwrap(blob).decode("ascii")
 1065:                         if len(plain) >= 32 and all(
 1066:                             c.isalnum() or c in "-_" for c in plain
 1067:                         ):
 1068:                             return plain
 1069:                     except Exception as e:
 1070:                         log.warning(
 1071:                             "UI token unwrap failed (%s); rotating to "
 1072:                             "a fresh token", e,
 1073:                         )
 1074:             else:
 1075:                 # Tokens we generate are 43 base64url chars (32 raw
 1076:                 # bytes). Be lenient on length but enforce at least
 1077:                 # 32 chars so a corrupted file can't turn into an
 1078:                 # unsafe short token.
 1079:                 if len(raw) >= 32 and all(
 1080:                     c.isalnum() or c in "-_" for c in raw
 1081:                 ):
 1082:                     return raw
 1083:         except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
 1084:             pass
 1085:         return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
 1086: 
 1087:     def _courier_ledger_path(self) -> Path:
 1088:         return data_dir() / COURIER_LEDGER_FILE
 1089: 
 1090:     @staticmethod
 1091:     def _valid_courier_bundle_id(value: object) -> bool:
 1092:         text = str(value or "").strip().lower()
 1093:         if len(text) != 32:
 1094:             return False
 1095:         try:
 1096:             int(text, 16)
 1097:             return True
 1098:         except ValueError:
 1099:             return False
 1100: 
 1101:     def _load_courier_ledger(self) -> None:
 1102:         path = self._courier_ledger_path()
 1103:         try:
 1104:             raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 1105:         except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
 1106:             self._courier_seen_bundle_ids = set()
 1107:             self._courier_events = []
 1108:             return
 1109:         seen = raw.get("seen_bundle_ids", []) if isinstance(raw, dict) else []
 1110:         events = raw.get("events", []) if isinstance(raw, dict) else []
 1111:         self._courier_seen_bundle_ids = {
 1112:             str(x).strip().lower()
 1113:             for x in seen
 1114:             if self._valid_courier_bundle_id(x)
 1115:         }
 1116:         self._courier_events = [
 1117:             e for e in events[-COURIER_LEDGER_MAX_EVENTS:]
 1118:             if isinstance(e, dict) and self._valid_courier_bundle_id(e.get("bundle_id"))
 1119:         ]
 1120: 
 1121:     def _save_courier_ledger(self) -> None:
 1122:         path = self._courier_ledger_path()
 1123:         path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 1124:         payload = {
 1125:             "version": 1,
 1126:             "seen_bundle_ids": sorted(self._courier_seen_bundle_ids),
 1127:             "events": self._courier_events[-COURIER_LEDGER_MAX_EVENTS:],
 1128:         }
 1129:         tmp = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.{secrets.token_hex(4)}.tmp")
 1130:         tmp.write_text(
 1131:             json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")),
 1132:             encoding="utf-8",
 1133:         )
 1134:         os.replace(tmp, path)
 1135: 
 1136:     def _record_courier_event(
 1137:         self,
 1138:         kind: str,
 1139:         manifest: dict,
 1140:         *,
 1141:         bundle_bytes: int | None = None,
 1142:         stored_chunks: int | None = None,
 1143:     ) -> None:
 1144:         bundle_id = str(manifest.get("bundle_id") or "").strip().lower()
 1145:         if not self._valid_courier_bundle_id(bundle_id):
 1146:             return
 1147:         event = {
 1148:             "kind": kind,
 1149:             "bundle_id": bundle_id,
 1150:             "ts_ms": int(time.time() * 1000),
 1151:             "sender_fp": manifest.get("sender_fp"),
 1152:             "recipient_fp": manifest.get("recipient_fp"),
 1153:             "chunk_count": manifest.get("chunk_count"),
 1154:             "total_bytes": manifest.get("total_bytes"),
 1155:             "expires_ms": manifest.get("expires_ms"),
 1156:         }
 1157:         if bundle_bytes is not None:
 1158:             event["bundle_bytes"] = int(bundle_bytes)
 1159:         if stored_chunks is not None:
 1160:             event["stored_chunks"] = int(stored_chunks)
 1161:         self._courier_events.append(event)
 1162:         self._courier_events = self._courier_events[-COURIER_LEDGER_MAX_EVENTS:]
 1163:         self._save_courier_ledger()
 1164: 
 1165:     def _mark_courier_imported(self, manifest: dict) -> None:
 1166:         bundle_id = str(manifest.get("bundle_id") or "").strip().lower()
 1167:         if not self._valid_courier_bundle_id(bundle_id):
 1168:             raise ValueError("invalid courier bundle id")
 1169:         self._courier_seen_bundle_ids.add(bundle_id)
 1170:         self._save_courier_ledger()
 1171:

 1175:         return path

 1180:         return path

 1187:     def _courier_file_id(self, path: Path) -> str:
 1188:         st = path.stat()
 1189:         return self._courier_file_id_from_stat(path.name, int(st.st_size), int(st.st_mtime_ns))
 1190: 
 1191:     @staticmethod
 1192:     def _courier_file_id_from_stat(name: str, size: int, mtime_ns: int) -> str:
 1193:         seed = f"{name}\0{int(size)}\0{int(mtime_ns)}".encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass")
 1194:         return hashlib.sha256(seed).hexdigest()[:24]
 1195: 
 1196:     def _scan_courier_files(self) -> list[dict]:
 1197:         return self._scan_courier_dir(self._courier_drop_dir())
 1198: 
 1199:     def _scan_courier_outbox(self) -> list[dict]:
 1200:         return self._scan_courier_dir(self._courier_outbox_dir())
 1201: 
 1202:     @staticmethod
 1203:     def _courier_signature(files: list[dict]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 1204:         return tuple(
 1205:             f"{f.get('id')}:{f.get('bytes')}:{f.get('mtime_ms')}"
 1206:             for f in files
 1207:         )
 1208: 
 1209:     def _courier_monitor_tick(self, *, broadcast: bool = True) -> dict:
 1210:         drop_files = self._scan_courier_files()
 1211:         outbox_files = self._scan_courier_outbox()
 1212:         drop_sig = self._courier_signature(drop_files)
 1213:         outbox_sig = self._courier_signature(outbox_files)
 1214:         changed = (
 1215:             drop_sig != self._courier_drop_signature
 1216:             or outbox_sig != self._courier_outbox_signature
 1217:         )
 1218:         self._courier_drop_signature = drop_sig
 1219:         self._courier_outbox_signature = outbox_sig
 1220:         self._courier_monitor_last_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
 1221:         if changed:
 1222:             self._courier_monitor_events += 1
 1223:             if broadcast:
 1224:                 self.broadcast({
 1225:                     "type": "courier_files",
 1226:                     "drop_files": len(drop_files),
 1227:                     "outbox_files": len(outbox_files),
 1228:                     "drop_dir": str(self._courier_drop_dir()),
 1229:                     "outbox_dir": str(self._courier_outbox_dir()),
 1230:                 })
 1231:         return {
 1232:             "changed": changed,
 1233:             "drop_files": drop_files,
 1234:             "outbox_files": outbox_files,
 1235:         }
 1236: 
 1237:     def _removable_monitor_tick(self, *, broadcast: bool = True) -> dict:
 1238:         from one_link.removable_media import RemovableEventDetector
 1239: 
 1240:         if self._removable_event_detector is None:
 1241:             self._removable_event_detector = RemovableEventDetector()
 1242:         result = self._removable_event_detector.poll()
 1243:         self._removable_monitor_last_ms = int(result.get("last_scan_ms") or int(time.time() * 1000))
 1244:         events = result.get("events") or []
 1245:         if events:
 1246:             self._removable_monitor_events += len(events)
 1247:             if broadcast:
 1248:                 self.broadcast({
 1249:                     "type": "removable_media",
 1250:                     "events": events,
 1251:                     "targets": result.get("targets") or [],
 1252:                     "mode": result.get("mode"),
 1253:                 })
 1254:         return result
 1255: 
 1256:     async def _courier_monitor_loop(self) -> None:
 1257:         try:
 1258:             self._courier_monitor_tick(broadcast=False)
 1259:             self._removable_monitor_tick(broadcast=False)
 1260:             while True:
 1261:                 await asyncio.sleep(self._courier_monitor_interval_s)
 1262:                 self._courier_monitor_tick(broadcast=True)
 1263:                 self._removable_monitor_tick(broadcast=True)
 1264:         except asyncio.CancelledError:
 1265:             raise
 1266:         except Exception:
 1267:             log.exception("courier monitor stopped unexpectedly")
 1268: 
 1269:     def _scan_courier_dir(self, directory: Path) -> list[dict]:
 1270:         root = directory.resolve()
 1271:         if not root.is_dir():
 1272:             return []
 1273:         newest: list[tuple[int, Path, os.stat_result]] = []
 1274:         try:
 1275:             iterator = root.iterdir()
 1276:         except OSError:
 1277:             return []
 1278:         for path in iterator:
 1279:             try:
 1280:                 if path.is_symlink():
 1281:                     continue
 1282:                 resolved = path.resolve()
 1283:                 if not resolved.is_file() or resolved.parent != root:
 1284:                     continue
 1285:                 if resolved.suffix.lower() not in {".json", ".olcb"} and not resolved.name.lower().endswith(".olcb.json"):
 1286:                     continue
 1287:                 st = resolved.stat()
 1288:                 if st.st_size <= 0 or st.st_size > COURIER_FILE_MAX_BYTES:
 1289:                     continue
 1290:                 item = (int(st.st_mtime_ns), resolved, st)
 1291:                 if len(newest) < 64:
 1292:                     heapq.heappush(newest, item)
 1293:                 elif item[0] > newest[0][0]:
 1294:                     heapq.heapreplace(newest, item)
 1295:             except OSError:
 1296:                 continue
 1297:         out: list[dict] = []
 1298:         for _mtime_ns, resolved, st in sorted(newest, key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True):
 1299:             try:
 1300:                 out.append({
 1301:                     "id": self._courier_file_id_from_stat(
 1302:                         resolved.name,
 1303:                         int(st.st_size),
 1304:                         int(st.st_mtime_ns),
 1305:                     ),
 1306:                     "name": resolved.name,
 1307:                     "bytes": int(st.st_size),
 1308:                     "mtime_ms": int(st.st_mtime * 1000),
 1309:                 })
 1310:             except OSError:
 1311:                 continue
 1312:         return out
 1313: 
 1314:     def _resolve_courier_file_id(self, file_id: str) -> Path | None:
 1315:         want = str(file_id or "").strip().lower()
 1316:         if len(want) != 24:
 1317:             return None
 1318:         for item in self._scan_courier_files():
 1319:             if item.get("id") == want:
 1320:                 path = (self._courier_drop_dir() / str(item["name"])).resolve()
 1321:                 root = self._courier_drop_dir().resolve()
 1322:                 if path.parent == root and path.is_file():
 1323:                     return path
 1324:         return None
 1325: 
 1326:     def _resolve_courier_outbox_file_id(self, file_id: str) -> Path | None:
 1327:         want = str(file_id or "").strip().lower()
 1328:         if len(want) != 24:
 1329:             return None
 1330:         root = self._courier_outbox_dir().resolve()
 1331:         for item in self._scan_courier_outbox():
 1332:             if item.get("id") == want:
 1333:                 path = (root / str(item["name"])).resolve()
 1334:                 if path.parent == root and path.is_file():
 1335:                     return path
 1336:         return None
 1337: 
 1338:     def _removable_courier_dir(self, target_path: Path) -> Path:
 1339:         return (target_path / "One Link Courier").resolve()
 1340: 
 1341:     def _scan_removable_courier_files(self, target_path: Path) -> list[dict]:
 1342:         root = self._removable_courier_dir(target_path)
 1343:         target_root = target_path.resolve()
 1344:         if target_root not in {root, *root.parents} or not root.is_dir():
 1345:             return []
 1346:         return self._scan_courier_dir(root)
 1347: 
 1348:     def _resolve_removable_courier_file_id(self, target_path: Path, file_id: str) -> Path | None:
 1349:         want = str(file_id or "").strip().lower()
 1350:         if len(want) != 24:
 1351:             return None
 1352:         root = self._removable_courier_dir(target_path)
 1353:         target_root = target_path.resolve()
 1354:         if target_root not in {root, *root.parents}:
 1355:             return None
 1356:         for item in self._scan_removable_courier_files(target_path):
 1357:             if item.get("id") == want:
 1358:                 path = (root / str(item["name"])).resolve()
 1359:                 if path.parent == root and path.is_file():
 1360:                     return path
 1361:         return None
 1362: 
 1363:     @staticmethod
 1364:     def _extract_courier_bundle_text(text: str) -> str:
 1365:         stripped = text.strip()
 1366:         if not stripped:
 1367:             raise ValueError("courier file is empty")
 1368:         try:
 1369:             parsed = json.loads(stripped)
 1370:             if isinstance(parsed, dict):
 1371:                 bundle = parsed.get("bundle_b64") or parsed.get("bundle")
 1372:                 if bundle:
 1373:                     return str(bundle).strip()
 1374:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
 1375:             pass
 1376:         return stripped

 1378:     # ─── routes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 1379:     def _setup_routes(self) -> None:
 1380:         r = self.app.router
 1381:         r.add_get("/", self._index)
 1382:         # Static assets (logo, favicon). NOT token-gated: these are
 1383:         # required to render the page itself before the cookie is set.
 1384:         assets_dir = WEB_DIR / "assets"
 1385:         if assets_dir.is_dir():
 1386:             r.add_static("/static/", path=str(assets_dir), show_index=False)
 1387:         r.add_get("/favicon.ico", self._favicon)
 1388:         # v0.14.0: Service Worker for background-sync (offline outbox)
 1389:         # + cache-first shell. Must be served from root scope to be
 1390:         # allowed to control "/" requests; not auth-gated since the
 1391:         # SW itself contains no PII (only the URL paths it caches +
 1392:         # the outbox-drain logic that re-uses the page's cookie).
 1393:         r.add_get("/sw.js", self._service_worker)
 1394:         # v0.15.0: Web App Manifest. Browsers fetch /manifest.json
 1395:         # from the page's `<link rel="manifest">`; presence + correct
 1396:         # MIME is what enables the install prompt + standalone-mode
 1397:         # behavior. Like sw.js, served unauthenticated because it
 1398:         # contains zero PII (just the app's display chrome).
 1399:         r.add_get("/manifest.json", self._manifest)
 1400:         # v0.16.0: browser-as-peer shell. Unauthenticated route —
 1401:         # the page authenticates itself via its own keypair (held
 1402:         # in OPFS), not the daemon's UI token. From this page the
 1403:         # browser is its own peer; the daemon is unrelated.
 1404:         r.add_get("/peer", self._peer_shell)
 1405:         r.add_get("/peer/", self._peer_shell)
 1406:         # v0.20.7 (security audit H7): JS port of the Double Ratchet
 1407:         # for browser-as-peer DataChannel transport. Standalone ESM
 1408:         # module + a self-test page that exercises the round-trip
 1409:         # in-browser (open /dr_test in any tab to see the suite).
 1410:         r.add_get("/dr.js", self._dr_module)
 1411:         r.add_get("/dr_test", self._dr_test_page)
 1412:         r.add_get("/dr_test.html", self._dr_test_page)
 1413:         # v0.20.0: WebRTC signaling endpoint for browser-as-peer ↔
 1414:         # daemon DataChannel transport. Unauthenticated WebSocket;
 1415:         # the browser authenticates via Ed25519 signature on the SDP
 1416:         # offer envelope (signed_offer.signature verified against
 1417:         # signed_offer.pubkey before we accept the peer connection).
 1418:         r.add_get("/api/v1/peer-rtc", self._peer_rtc_signaling)
 1419:         # v0.20.1: pair-by-QR token mint. Auth-gated (token holder
 1420:         # is the desktop user). Returns a fresh one-shot pairing
 1421:         # token that the browser-peer presents during signaling so
 1422:         # the daemon trusts it as a paired device with no manual
 1423:         # SAS confirm.
 1424:         r.add_post("/api/v1/peer-rtc/mint-pairing", self._guarded(self.api_mint_pairing))
 1425:         # v0.20.1: render the most-recently-minted pairing token's
 1426:         # LAN URL as an SVG QR. Hits the desktop UI's "Pair a phone"
 1427:         # surface; saves us shipping a JS QR library.
 1428:         r.add_get("/api/v1/peer-rtc/qr.svg", self._guarded(self.api_pair_qr))
 1429:         # v0.20.6: iOS Configuration Profile that installs the
 1430:         # daemon's self-signed cert as a trusted root. Phones load
 1431:         # this URL via Safari, which auto-prompts to install the
 1432:         # profile. After install, the regular pair URL (HTTPS)
 1433:         # works with zero "Not Private" warnings. Unauthenticated
 1434:         # because iOS Safari doesn't carry the bearer token across
 1435:         # the profile-install handoff; cert-as-data leaks no PII
 1436:         # since it's the same self-signed cert anyone on the LAN
 1437:         # would see during a TLS handshake anyway.
 1438:         r.add_get("/api/v1/peer-rtc/profile.mobileconfig", self._pair_profile)
 1439:         # May 15 2026 — sovereignty endpoint. Both index.html and
 1440:         # peer.html start with an empty ICE-server list (no calls
 1441:         # to third-party STUN by default) and ask this endpoint
 1442:         # for the user-configured set. Empty response = LAN-only.
 1443:         r.add_get(
 1444:             "/api/peer-rtc/ice-config",
 1445:             self._guarded(self.api_peer_rtc_ice_config),
 1446:         )
 1447:         # May 15 2026 — sovereignty surface. Three endpoints power
 1448:         # the UI Privacy panel:
 1449:         #   GET  /api/sovereignty/status     — preset + per-feature state
 1450:         #   GET  /api/sovereignty/preset     — list available presets
 1451:         #   POST /api/sovereignty/preset     — set active preset
 1452:         #   GET  /api/sovereignty/outbound   — recent outbound calls
 1453:         r.add_get(
 1454:             "/api/sovereignty/status",
 1455:             self._guarded(self.api_sovereignty_status),
 1456:         )
 1457:         r.add_get(
 1458:             "/api/sovereignty/preset",
 1459:             self._guarded(self.api_sovereignty_preset_list),
 1460:         )

 1462:             "/api/sovereignty/preset",
 1463:             self._guarded(self.api_sovereignty_preset_set),

 1466:             "/api/sovereignty/outbound",
 1467:             self._guarded(self.api_sovereignty_outbound_log),

 1469:         # May 16 2026 — multi-modal LAN discovery. Runs mDNS

 1505:             self.api_peer_rtc_ice_config_public,

 1508:             "/api/v1/self-mesh/enrollment-invite/preview",

 1513:         r.add_get("/api/connect-info", self._guarded(self.api_connect_info))
 1514:         r.add_get("/api/connect-info/qr.svg", self._guarded(self.api_connect_info_qr))
 1515:         r.add_get("/api/me", self._guarded(self.api_me))
