11673:         safe = Path(name).name
11674:         if safe != name or not safe:
11675:             return web.json_response({"error": "bad name"}, status=400)
11676:         path = inbox_dir() / safe
11677:         if not path.is_file():
11678:             return web.json_response({"error": "not found"}, status=404)
11679:         ext = safe.rsplit(".", 1)[-1].lower() if "." in safe else safe.lower()
11680:         kind = self.PREVIEW_KINDS.get(ext)
11681:         if kind is None:
11682:             return web.json_response(
11683:                 {"error": "preview not available for this file type",
11684:                  "extension": ext},
11685:                 status=415,
11686:             )
11687:         try:
11688:             size = path.stat().st_size
11689:         except OSError as e:
11690:             return web.json_response({"error": f"stat: {e}"}, status=500)
11691:         # v0.9.5: PDFs render via the browser's built-in viewer
11692:         # (<iframe src=/api/files/{name}>), not by reading the
11693:         # bytes server-side. Return metadata only so a 100 MB PDF
11694:         # doesn't OOM the daemon.
11695:         if kind == "pdf":
11696:             return web.json_response({
11697:                 "name": safe,
11698:                 "extension": ext,
11699:                 "kind": kind,
11700:                 "size": size,
11701:                 "stream_url": f"/api/files/{safe}",
11702:             })
11703:         cap = self.PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES
11704:         truncated = size > cap
11705:         try:
11706:             with path.open("rb") as f:
11707:                 raw = f.read(cap)
11708:         except OSError as e:
11709:             return web.json_response({"error": f"read: {e}"}, status=500)
11710:         # Decode: prefer utf-8, fall back to latin-1 (which can't fail).
11711:         # Replace bad bytes with U+FFFD so the user sees that part is
11712:         # garbled rather than getting a 500.
11713:         try:
11714:             content = raw.decode("utf-8")
11715:             encoding = "utf-8"
11716:         except UnicodeDecodeError:
11717:             content = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
11718:             encoding = "utf-8-replace"
11719:         return web.json_response({
11720:             "name": safe,
11721:             "extension": ext,
11722:             "kind": kind,
11723:             "encoding": encoding,
11724:             "size": size,
11725:             "preview_bytes": len(raw),
11726:             "truncated": truncated,
11727:             "content": content,
11728:         })
11729: 
11730:     # Server-side debounce: explorer.exe spawns a new window each call,
11731:     # so repeated rapid clicks from the UI (or a runaway loop) would
11732:     # stack windows on top of the user's other work. One reveal per
11733:     # second is the most a human would intentionally do.
11734:     _last_reveal_ms: float = 0.0
11735: 
11736:     def _reveal_throttled(self) -> bool:
11737:         now = time.time() * 1000
11738:         if now - self._last_reveal_ms < 1000:
11739:             return True
11740:         self._last_reveal_ms = now
11741:         return False
11742: 
11743:     async def api_file_reveal(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
11744:         # Open the OS file manager with the inbox file selected.
11745:         # Same path-traversal defense as download.
11746:         name = request.match_info["name"]
11747:         safe = Path(name).name
11748:         if safe != name or not safe:
11749:             return web.json_response({"error": "bad name"}, status=400)
11750:         path = (inbox_dir() / safe).resolve()
11751:         if not path.is_file():
11752:             return web.json_response({"error": "not found"}, status=404)
11753:         if self._reveal_throttled():
11754:             return web.json_response({"ok": True, "throttled": True})
11755:         # v0.7.x: ONE_LINK_DISABLE_REVEAL=1 short-circuits the actual
11756:         # subprocess.Popen so test runs (which may exercise reveal
11757:         # endpoints via the integration suite) don't pop File Explorer
11758:         # windows on the developer's screen.
11759:         if os.environ.get("ONE_LINK_DISABLE_REVEAL") == "1":
11760:             return web.json_response({"ok": True, "disabled": True})
11761:         import subprocess
11762:         import sys
11763:         try:
11764:             if sys.platform == "win32":
11765:                 # v0.9.7: use list-form Popen — string form was
11766:                 # silently filing under "didn't work" for some users.
11767:                 # explorer.exe parses /select,<path> as a single
11768:                 # argv token (comma is part of the syntax, not a
11769:                 # separator), so pass it as one element.
11770:                 subprocess.Popen(
11771:                     ["explorer.exe", f"/select,{path}"],
11772:                 )
11773:             elif sys.platform == "darwin":
11774:                 subprocess.Popen(["open", "-R", str(path)])
11775:             else:
11776:                 subprocess.Popen(["xdg-open", str(path.parent)])
11777:         except OSError as e:
11778:             return web.json_response({"error": f"reveal failed: {e}"}, status=500)
11779:         return web.json_response({"ok": True, "path": str(path)})
11780: 
11781:     async def api_inbox_reveal(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
11782:         # Open the inbox folder itself (no specific file selected).
11783:         path = inbox_dir().resolve()
11784:         if self._reveal_throttled():
11785:             return web.json_response({"ok": True, "path": str(path), "throttled": True})
11786:         # See api_file_reveal — same env-gate so tests don't spawn
11787:         # actual Explorer windows.
11788:         if os.environ.get("ONE_LINK_DISABLE_REVEAL") == "1":
11789:             return web.json_response({"ok": True, "path": str(path), "disabled": True})
11790:         import sys
11791:         try:
11792:             if sys.platform == "win32":
11793:                 # v0.9.7: switch to os.startfile (ShellExecute under
11794:                 # the hood). Reuses an existing Explorer window if
11795:                 # one is open, displays significantly faster than
11796:                 # spawning a fresh explorer.exe via subprocess.
11797:                 os.startfile(str(path))
11798:             elif sys.platform == "darwin":
11799:                 import subprocess
11800:                 subprocess.Popen(["open", str(path)])
11801:             else:
11802:                 import subprocess
11803:                 subprocess.Popen(["xdg-open", str(path)])
11804:         except OSError as e:
11805:             return web.json_response({"error": f"reveal failed: {e}"}, status=500)
11806:         return web.json_response({"ok": True, "path": str(path)})
11807: 
11808:     # ─── /api/update/check ───────────────────────────────────────────
11809:     # Reads the latest GitHub Release for this repo and compares its
11810:     # tag against the local app_version. UI surfaces the result as an
11811:     # orange "Update available" banner. Never raises; failures
11812:     # (offline, rate-limited, repo private) return status='unknown' so
11813:     # the UI silently stays clean instead of showing a scary error.
11814:     #
11815:     # Cached in-process for 15 minutes per daemon-startup to avoid
11816:     # hammering the GitHub API on UI reloads. Force-bypass via
11817:     # ?fresh=1 (used by the Settings "Check now" button).
11818:     _update_cache: tuple[float, dict] | None = None
11819:     _update_cache_ttl_s: float = 900.0  # 15 minutes
11820: 
11821:     async def api_update_check(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
11822:         import time as _time
11823:         import os as _os
11824:         from one_link import __version__ as _local_ver
11825:         from one_link.update_check import fetch_latest
11826: 
11827:         # May 15 2026 — sovereignty default. /api/update/check is the
11828:         # path the UI's Settings panel and footer banner poll on
11829:         # tab-load. Honor the same opt-in gate the boot-time loop
11830:         # uses: env ONE_LINK_UPDATE_CHECK=1 OR setting
11831:         # update_check_enabled=1. Otherwise return status=disabled
11832:         # without touching the network.
11833:         env_on = _os.environ.get(
11834:             "ONE_LINK_UPDATE_CHECK", ""
11835:         ).strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
11836:         setting_on = False
11837:         if self.daemon.state is not None:
11838:             with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
11839:                 setting_on = (self.daemon.state.get_setting(
11840:                     "update_check_enabled"
11841:                 ) or "").strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")
11842:         if not (env_on or setting_on):
11843:             return web.json_response({
11844:                 "status": "disabled",
11845:                 "local_version": _local_ver,
11846:                 "reason": (
11847:                     "update-check disabled by default for sovereignty. "
11848:                     "Enable in Settings or set ONE_LINK_UPDATE_CHECK=1."
11849:                 ),
11850:             })
11851: 
11852:         force_fresh = request.query.get("fresh") in ("1", "true", "yes")
11853:         now = _time.monotonic()
11854:         if not force_fresh and self._update_cache is not None:
11855:             ts, payload = self._update_cache
11856:             if now - ts < self._update_cache_ttl_s:
11857:                 return web.json_response({**payload, "cached": True})
11858: 
11859:         # fetch_latest is synchronous (one urllib call). Bounce off the
11860:         # default executor so we don't block the event loop on slow
11861:         # networks; the timeout inside fetch_latest is the inner limit.
11862:         loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
11863:         try:
11864:             result = await loop.run_in_executor(
11865:                 None, lambda: fetch_latest(_local_ver)
11866:             )
11867:         except Exception as e:  # safety net — fetch_latest already swallows
11868:             log.warning("update_check unexpected error: %s", e)
11869:             payload = {
11870:                 "status": "unknown",
11871:                 "local_version": _local_ver,
11872:                 "error": str(e),
11873:             }
11874:         else:
11875:             payload = result.to_dict()
11876: 
11877:         self._update_cache = (now, payload)
11878:         return web.json_response({**payload, "cached": False})
11879: 
11880:     # ─── /api/update/plan ───────────────────────────────────────────
11881:     # Inspects the latest GitHub Release, picks the wheel for this
11882:     # OS+ABI, looks up its SHA-256 in SHA256SUMS. Read-only: does
11883:     # NOT download or install anything. The UI calls this to decide
11884:     # whether to show the "Update now" button as enabled, and to
11885:     # display the wheel filename + size to the user before they click.
11886:     async def api_update_plan(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
11887:         from one_link.updater import build_install_plan
11888:         loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
11889:         try:
11890:             plan = await loop.run_in_executor(None, build_install_plan)
11891:         except Exception as e:
11892:             log.warning("update_plan unexpected error: %s", e)
11893:             return web.json_response(
11894:                 {"status": "error", "error": str(e)}, status=200
11895:             )
11896:         return web.json_response(plan.to_dict())
11897: 
11898:     # ─── /api/update/install ────────────────────────────────────────
11899:     # GATED OFF by default. Setting ONE_LINK_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTOINSTALL=1
11900:     # in the daemon's environment enables it. The destructive parts
11901:     # (pip install + daemon respawn) need per-OS integration testing
11902:     # before going on by default; until then the UI's update banner
11903:     # falls back to the "View release" link and the user runs
11904:     # `pip install --upgrade one_link_native` manually.
11905:     #
11906:     # Flow when enabled:
11907:     #   1. Re-fetch the install plan (current OS, matched wheel).
11908:     #   2. Download wheel to a temp file.
11909:     #   3. SHA-256 verify against the release's SHA256SUMS.
11910:     #   4. Generate an updater script that:
11911:     #        a. Waits for THIS daemon's PID to exit
11912:     #        b. Runs pip install <wheel>
11913:     #        c. Relaunches the daemon
11914:     #   5. Spawn the updater script as a detached subprocess.
11915:     #   6. Return 202 to the UI.
11916:     #   7. Initiate daemon shutdown after sending the response.
11917:     #
11918:     # The client should expect the WebSocket to drop momentarily and
11919:     # auto-reconnect to the freshly-respawned daemon.
11920:     async def api_update_install(self, request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
11921:         import os as _os
11922:         gate = _os.environ.get("ONE_LINK_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTOINSTALL")
11923:         if gate not in ("1", "true", "yes"):
11924:             return web.json_response({
11925:                 "status": "disabled",
11926:                 "error": (
11927:                     "auto-install is experimental and disabled by default. "
11928:                     "Set ONE_LINK_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTOINSTALL=1 in the daemon's "
11929:                     "environment to enable, or run `pip install --upgrade "
11930:                     "one_link_native` manually."
11931:                 ),
11932:             }, status=503)
11933: 
11934:         from one_link.updater import (
11935:             build_install_plan, download_to_temp, sha256_file,
11936:             write_updater_script, spawn_detached,
11937:         )
11938:         loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
11939: 
11940:         # Step 1: plan
11941:         plan = await loop.run_in_executor(None, build_install_plan)
11942:         if plan.status != "ready" or plan.wheel is None:
11943:             return web.json_response({
11944:                 "status": "no_match",
11945:                 "error": plan.error or "no wheel available for this host",
11946:                 "plan": plan.to_dict(),
11947:             }, status=409)
11948: 
11949:         # Step 2: download
11950:         try:
11951:             wheel_path = await loop.run_in_executor(
11952:                 None,
11953:                 lambda: download_to_temp(
11954:                     plan.wheel.asset_url,
11955:                     expected_size=plan.wheel.size,
11956:                 ),
11957:             )
11958:         except Exception as e:
11959:             log.exception("update download failed")
11960:             return web.json_response({
11961:                 "status": "download_failed", "error": str(e),
11962:             }, status=502)
11963: 
11964:         # Step 3: SHA-256 verify (mandatory; abort if missing/mismatch)
11965:         expected = plan.wheel.expected_sha256
11966:         if not expected:
11967:             try:
11968:                 wheel_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
11969:             except OSError:
11970:                 pass
11971:             return web.json_response({
11972:                 "status": "unverified",
11973:                 "error": (
11974:                     "SHA256SUMS did not contain a hash for the wheel. "
11975:                     "Refusing to install an unverified binary."
11976:                 ),
11977:             }, status=409)
11978:         got = await loop.run_in_executor(None, sha256_file, wheel_path)
11979:         if got != expected:
11980:             try:
11981:                 wheel_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
11982:             except OSError:
11983:                 pass
11984:             return web.json_response({
11985:                 "status": "hash_mismatch",
11986:                 "error": f"expected {expected}, got {got}",
11987:             }, status=409)
11988: 
11989:         # Step 4: write updater script
11990:         script_path = await loop.run_in_executor(
11991:             None,
11992:             lambda: write_updater_script(
11993:                 wheel_path,
11994:                 parent_pid=_os.getpid(),
11995:             ),
11996:         )
11997: 
11998:         # Step 5: spawn detached
11999:         updater_pid = await loop.run_in_executor(
12000:             None, spawn_detached, script_path
12001:         )
12002: 
12003:         # Step 6: tell client we're going down
12004:         resp = web.json_response({
12005:             "status": "installing",
12006:             "tag": plan.tag,
12007:             "wheel": plan.wheel.filename,
12008:             "updater_pid": updater_pid,
12009:             "hint": (
12010:                 "The daemon is shutting down. The updater will install the "
12011:                 "new wheel and start a fresh daemon. Your browser tab will "
12012:                 "reconnect automatically once the new daemon is ready."
12013:             ),
12014:         })
12015: 
12016:         # Step 7: shut down AFTER the response is sent. Schedule on
12017:         # the event loop so the response is flushed first.
12018:         async def _shutdown_soon():
12019:             await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
12020:             log.info("auto-update: daemon exiting so updater can run")
12021:             # Hard exit — the updater is responsible for restart.
12022:             _os._exit(0)
12023:         asyncio.create_task(_shutdown_soon())
12024: 
12025:         return resp
12026: 
12027:     # ─── WebSocket events ─────────────────────────────────────────────
12028:     async def ws_events(self, request: web.Request) -> web.WebSocketResponse:
12029:         ws = web.WebSocketResponse(heartbeat=30)
12030:         await ws.prepare(request)
12031:         self._ws_clients.add(ws)
12032:         # Send an initial snapshot so the UI has state before any pushes.
12033:         await ws.send_json(
12034:             {
12035:                 "type": "hello",
12036:                 "me": {
12037:                     "short_id": self.daemon.me.short_id,
12038:                     "fingerprint": self.daemon.me.fingerprint,
12039:                     "hostname": self.daemon.me.hostname,
12040:                 },
12041:             }
12042:         )
12043:         try:
12044:             async for msg in ws:
12045:                 if msg.type == WSMsgType.ERROR:
12046:                     log.warning("ws error: %s", ws.exception())
12047:                 # Otherwise: we don't accept client→server messages; UI uses HTTP.
12048:         finally:
12049:             self._ws_clients.discard(ws)
12050:         return ws
12051: 
12052:     def broadcast(self, event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
12053:         """Push an event to all connected UI clients. Safe to call from any
12054:         coroutine; closed sockets are pruned."""
12055:         dead: list[web.WebSocketResponse] = []
12056:         for ws in list(self._ws_clients):
12057:             if ws.closed:
12058:                 dead.append(ws)
12059:                 continue
12060:             try:
12061:                 # send_str is synchronous-ish — schedule it but don't await.
12062:                 asyncio.create_task(ws.send_json(event))
12063:             except Exception:
12064:                 dead.append(ws)
12065:         for ws in dead:
12066:             self._ws_clients.discard(ws)
12067: 
12068:     # ─── lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
12069:     async def start(self) -> int:
12070:         self.runner = web.AppRunner(self.app, access_log=None)
12071:         await self.runner.setup()
12072:         # v0.15.2 — LAN-bind opt-in via env var. Default 127.0.0.1
12073:         # (loopback only, the historical safe default). Setting
12074:         # ONE_LINK_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 (or a specific LAN address)
12075:         # exposes the UI to the LAN so a phone on the same Wi-Fi
12076:         # can connect. The token still gates everything; the env
12077:         # var only changes which interface answers.
12078:         bind_host = os.environ.get("ONE_LINK_BIND_HOST") or "127.0.0.1"
12079:         # Try the well-known port first so browser tabs survive restarts.
12080:         # Fall through 7118..7132 if taken, then OS-assigned random as
12081:         # last resort.
12082:         #
12083:         # v0.20.5 — the previous "ownership probe" raced with TIME_WAIT
12084:         # entries from a just-killed daemon: bind() would succeed (so
12085:         # we own the port) but the probe's connect would briefly hit
12086:         # the kernel's TIME_WAIT-routing layer, fail to read a 200,
12087:         # and we'd fall through to a higher port. Result: every
12088:         # restart claimed a different port number, breaking every
12089:         # bookmark + previously-minted pair URL. On Windows + Linux,
12090:         # bind() succeeding ≠ "TIME_WAIT clear" but DOES mean "we
12091:         # own this listener now" — connections will route to us, not
12092:         # to the dead 5-tuples in TIME_WAIT. Probe removed.
12093:         bound = False
12094:         for candidate in range(
12095:             PREFERRED_UI_PORT, PREFERRED_UI_PORT + UI_PORT_FALLBACK_RANGE
12096:         ):
12097:             try:
12098:                 site = web.TCPSite(self.runner, host=bind_host, port=candidate)
12099:                 await site.start()
12100:                 self.site = site
12101:                 self.port = candidate
12102:                 bound = True
12103:                 break
12104:             except OSError:
12105:                 # Port in use by ANOTHER LISTENER — try the next.
12106:                 # TIME_WAIT entries don't cause this on Windows or
12107:                 # modern Linux; only an actively-listening rival
12108:                 # process does.
12109:                 continue
12110:         if not bound:
12111:             site = web.TCPSite(self.runner, host=bind_host, port=0)
12112:             await site.start()
12113:             sock = site._server.sockets[0]  # type: ignore[union-attr]
12114:             self.site = site
12115:             self.port = sock.getsockname()[1]
12116:         self.bind_host = bind_host
12117:         _server_port_path().write_text(str(self.port))
12118:         # v0.20.7 (security audit M29): wrap the UI token with the
12119:         # daemon's lockbox WHEN explicit passphrase mode is active.
12120:         # Silent-mode lockboxes (the default at-rest wrap for
12121:         # chain_keys) do NOT wrap the UI token because:
12122:         #   1. The on-disk lifetime is brief — every daemon restart
12123:         #      rotates the token.
12124:         #   2. The launcher and external tooling read the file as
12125:         #      raw text; wrapping silently would break that contract
12126:         #      without a corresponding security gain (an attacker
12127:         #      who can read the daemon's data dir during the
12128:         #      session can also read the daemon's memory).
12129:         # Explicit-passphrase mode is the user signaling "I want
12130:         # paranoid at-rest"; in that mode we wrap the token too.
12131:         import base64 as _b64
12132:         token_disk = self.token
12133:         try:
12134:             lb = (
12135:                 getattr(self.daemon.state, "_lockbox", None)
12136:                 if self.daemon.state is not None else None
12137:             )
12138:             if lb is not None and not getattr(lb, "is_silent", True):
12139:                 blob = lb.wrap(self.token.encode("ascii"))
12140:                 token_disk = self._TOKEN_WRAPPED_PREFIX + _b64.urlsafe_b64encode(
12141:                     blob
12142:                 ).decode("ascii")
12143:         except Exception as e:
12144:             log.warning(
12145:                 "UI token wrap failed (%s); falling back to cleartext", e,
12146:             )
12147:         _token_path().write_text(token_disk)
12148:         # POSIX permission tighten so a multi-user box doesn't read it.
12149:         with contextlib.suppress(OSError, NotImplementedError):
12150:             os.chmod(_token_path(), 0o600)
12151:         log.info("UI server up — http://%s:%d/", bind_host, self.port)
12152: 
12153:         # v0.20.4 — start a parallel HTTPS listener on port+1 so
12154:         # phones can hit the daemon over a secure context (Web
12155:         # Crypto Subtle requires HTTPS or localhost; a phone hitting
12156:         # http://<lan-ip> can't generate Ed25519 keys, breaking the
12157:         # whole browser-as-peer pair flow). The cert is self-signed,
12158:         # generated on first run, persisted to <data_dir>/peer_https/.
12159:         # Best-effort: if cert minting fails, log + skip; HTTP-only
12160:         # daemons still work (just not from phone Safari).
12161:         self.https_site = None
12162:         self.https_port = None
12163:         self.https_cert_fp_sha256 = None
12164:         await self._start_https_listener(bind_host)
12165:         self._courier_monitor_task = asyncio.create_task(self._courier_monitor_loop())
12166: 
12167:         return self.port
12168: 
12169:     async def _start_https_listener(self, bind_host: str) -> None:
12170:         """v0.20.4 — start the parallel HTTPS listener with the
12171:         self-signed cert. Lazy-imports peer_https so daemons that
12172:         don't have the module still boot."""
12173:         try:
12174:             from one_link.peer_https import build_ssl_context, cert_path, cert_fingerprint_sha256
12175:             from one_link.paths import data_dir
12176:         except ImportError as e:
12177:             log.info("peer-https unavailable: %s", e)
12178:             return
12179:         try:

   1: """Social recovery — your social graph IS your recovery layer.
   2: 
   3: The 24-word BIP-39 phrase (master_seed + mnemonic) is the canonical
   4: sovereignty backup: paper, in a drawer, restored by typing 24 words
   5: on a new device. It works, but it has well-known UX failure modes:
   6: 
   7:   - The user doesn't write it down (most common failure, by far)
   8:   - The user writes it down on the device they're backing up
   9:     (defeats the purpose)
  10:   - The user writes it down on a sticky note that gets thrown out
  11:   - The paper is destroyed (fire, flood, divorce, child with crayon)
  12: 
  13: Social recovery is a complementary backup layer that uses the user's
  14: existing trust graph (paired peers — friends, family, an old laptop
  15: on the same network) instead of paper. It works like this:
  16: 
  17:   - SETUP: split the 32-byte master seed into 5 Shamir shares with
  18:     threshold 3 (any 3 of 5 reconstruct the seed; 2 cannot). Each
  19:     share is encrypted with a key derived from the recipient peer's
  20:     Ed25519 identity, so only that specific peer can decrypt their
  21:     share. Distribute the encrypted shares to 5 trusted contacts
  22:     via the existing One Link channel — which the contacts already
  23:     have because they're paired peers.
  24: 
  25:   - RECOVERY: on a fresh device, the user contacts 3 of their 5
  26:     guardians (ideally in person). Each guardian's daemon decrypts
  27:     their share with the guardian's private key and surrenders it
  28:     via QR code (in-person flow, fully offline) or back over the
  29:     channel (online flow). The recovering daemon collects 3 shares,
  30:     runs Shamir combine, and reconstructs the original seed.
  31: 
  32: This combines well with the BIP-39 paper backup — they aren't
  33: exclusive. A paranoid user runs both. A typical user runs social
  34: recovery and skips the paper. The user is in charge.
  35: 
  36: Trust model
  37: -----------
  38: 
  39: The user trusts that 3 of their 5 chosen guardians won't all collude
  40: against them. With threshold 3-of-5, up to 2 malicious guardians
  41: gain nothing (they can't reconstruct the seed without a third
  42: honest share). Different from custodial recovery (Apple iCloud,
  43: Google account) where ONE entity holds everything; here no single
  44: guardian — and no single platform — can lock the user out.
  45: 
  46: Wire format for an encrypted share
  47: ----------------------------------
  48: 
  49: Each share that lands on a guardian's daemon is a self-describing
  50: blob the guardian can store + ship later:
  51: 
  52:   ``OLSR1`` (5 bytes magic) + ``\\x01`` (version)
  53:   + ``share_index`` (1 byte)              # 1..total
  54:   + ``threshold`` (1 byte)                 # K (e.g. 3)
  55:   + ``total`` (1 byte)                     # N (e.g. 5)
  56:   + ``setup_ms`` (8 bytes BE)              # ts when share was minted
  57:   + ``ephemeral_x25519_pub`` (32 bytes)    # for ECDH wrap
  58:   + ``nonce`` (12 bytes)                   # AES-GCM IV
  59:   + ``ciphertext+tag`` (dynamic)           # AES-GCM(ephemeral_dh, share_bytes)
  60: 
  61: Where ``share_bytes`` is the 32-byte share output of
  62: ``threshold.split`` over GF(256).
  63: 
  64: The wrap uses ECDH(ephemeral_x25519, contact_x25519_from_ed25519_pub)
  65: → HKDF-SHA256 → 32-byte AES-GCM key. The sender generates a fresh
  66: ephemeral X25519 keypair per share, derives the shared secret, then
  67: discards the ephemeral private. Forward-secrecy hygiene: a future
  68: compromise of the sender's long-term key cannot decrypt any past
  69: share that's still in a guardian's drawer.
  70: 
  71: The Ed25519 → X25519 conversion uses the standard Edwards-to-
  72: Montgomery curve map (the same trick libsodium and Signal both
  73: use): every Ed25519 public key has a unique X25519 equivalent
  74: that produces the same X-coordinate as the Edwards point's
  75: y-coordinate transformed via (1+y)/(1-y) mod p.
  76: """
  77: from __future__ import annotations
  78: 
  79: import secrets
  80: import struct
  81: import time
  82: from dataclasses import dataclass
  83: from typing import Iterable, Optional
  84: 
  85: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
  86: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.x25519 import (
  87:     X25519PrivateKey, X25519PublicKey,
  88: )
  89: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
  90:     Ed25519PrivateKey, Ed25519PublicKey,
  91: )
  92: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
  93: from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.hkdf import HKDF
  94: 
  95: from one_link import threshold
  96: 
  97: # Row 9 wiring: use the native Rust Shamir implementation when
  98: # available (45-84x faster reconstruct per F1.1 polish benches).
  99: # Falls back to pure-Python `threshold` module if the native crate
 100: # isn't installed.
 101: try:
 102:     from one_link import threshold_recovery_native as _native_tr
 103: 
 104:     _NATIVE_AVAILABLE = bool(_native_tr.HAS_NATIVE)
 105: except ImportError:
 106:     _NATIVE_AVAILABLE = False
 107:     _native_tr = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

 109: 
 110: SHARE_MAGIC = b"OLSR1"
 111: SHARE_VERSION = 1
 112: HEADER_LEN = 5 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 8 + 32 + 12  # 61 bytes
 113: NONCE_LEN = 12
 114: HKDF_INFO = b"OL/social-recovery/share-wrap|v1"
 115: DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 3
 116: DEFAULT_TOTAL = 5
 117: SEED_LEN = 32  # master seed bytes
 118: 
 119: 
 120: @dataclass(frozen=True)
 121: class WrappedShare:
 122:     """A guardian-deliverable encrypted share. ``encoded`` is the
 123:     bytes the guardian stores + ships; everything else is metadata
 124:     parsed from the header for UX (display "share 2 of 5 from
 125:     Alice's iPad")."""
 126:     share_index: int
 127:     threshold: int
 128:     total: int
 129:     setup_ms: int
 130:     encoded: bytes
 131: 
 132:     @classmethod
 133:     def parse(cls, blob: bytes) -> "WrappedShare":
 134:         if len(blob) < HEADER_LEN:
 135:             raise ValueError(
 136:                 f"share too short: {len(blob)} < {HEADER_LEN}"
 137:             )
 138:         if blob[:5] != SHARE_MAGIC:
 139:             raise ValueError("not a One Link social-recovery share (bad magic)")
 140:         if blob[5] != SHARE_VERSION:
 141:             raise ValueError(f"unsupported share version {blob[5]}")
 142:         share_index = blob[6]
 143:         threshold_k = blob[7]
 144:         total_n = blob[8]
 145:         setup_ms = struct.unpack(">Q", blob[9:17])[0]
 146:         return cls(
 147:             share_index=share_index,
 148:             threshold=threshold_k,
 149:             total=total_n,
 150:             setup_ms=setup_ms,
 151:             encoded=blob,
 152:         )
 153: 
 154: 
 155: # ── Ed25519 → X25519 conversion ──────────────────────────────────────
 156: #
 157: # Every Ed25519 keypair has a deterministic X25519 equivalent. The
 158: # *public* key conversion is the Edwards-to-Montgomery `u = (1+y)/(1-y)
 159: # mod p` formula on Curve25519. The *private* key conversion derives
 160: # the X25519 secret from the SHA-512 hash of the Ed25519 secret seed
 161: # and applies RFC 7748 clamping. This lets a peer use one keypair
 162: # for both signatures (Ed25519) and key agreement (X25519) without
 163: # storing a second private key.
 164: #
 165: # Reference: libsodium ``crypto_sign_ed25519_pk_to_curve25519`` +
 166: # ``crypto_sign_ed25519_sk_to_curve25519``. Pure Python here so we
 167: # don't add a libsodium dep.
 168: 
 169: 
 170: _P25519 = 2**255 - 19
 171: 
 172: 
 173: def _modinv(a: int, m: int) -> int:
 174:     return pow(a, -1, m)
 175: 
 176: 
 177: def ed25519_pub_to_x25519(ed_pub: bytes) -> bytes:
 178:     """Map an Ed25519 32-byte public key to its X25519 equivalent.
 179: 
 180:     The Ed25519 public key encodes a point ``(x, y)`` on the twisted
 181:     Edwards curve as ``y || sign-bit-of-x``. The X25519 (Montgomery)
 182:     u-coordinate of the equivalent point is ``(1 + y) / (1 - y) mod p``
 183:     (the birational map between the two curve forms)."""
 184:     if len(ed_pub) != 32:
 185:         raise ValueError("ed_pub must be 32 bytes")
 186:     # Decode y (little-endian). The high bit is the sign of x — we
 187:     # don't need the x sign for the u-coordinate map; mask it off.
 188:     y = int.from_bytes(ed_pub, "little") & ((1 << 255) - 1)
 189:     # u = (1 + y) / (1 - y) mod p
 190:     one_plus_y = (1 + y) % _P25519
 191:     one_minus_y = (1 - y) % _P25519
 192:     u = (one_plus_y * _modinv(one_minus_y, _P25519)) % _P25519
 193:     return u.to_bytes(32, "little")
 194: 
 195: 
 196: def ed25519_priv_to_x25519(ed_priv_seed: bytes) -> bytes:
 197:     """Derive the X25519 32-byte private key from an Ed25519 32-byte
 198:     private SEED (the value passed to Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes).
 199: 
 200:     Per libsodium's convention: take SHA-512 of the seed, keep the
 201:     first 32 bytes, apply RFC 7748 clamping (clear bit 0,1,2 of byte
 202:     0; clear bit 7 of byte 31; set bit 6 of byte 31)."""
 203:     if len(ed_priv_seed) != 32:
 204:         raise ValueError("ed_priv_seed must be 32 bytes")
 205:     import hashlib
 206:     h = hashlib.sha512(ed_priv_seed).digest()[:32]
 207:     h = bytearray(h)
 208:     h[0] &= 248
 209:     h[31] &= 127
 210:     h[31] |= 64
 211:     return bytes(h)
 212: 
 213: 
 214: # ── share wrap / unwrap ──────────────────────────────────────────────
 215: 
 216: 
 217: def _derive_aead_key(shared: bytes, *, info_extra: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
 218:     return HKDF(
 219:         algorithm=hashes.SHA256(),
 220:         length=32,
 221:         salt=None,
 222:         info=HKDF_INFO + info_extra,
 223:     ).derive(shared)
 224: 
 225: 
 226: def split_and_wrap(
 227:     *,
 228:     seed: bytes,
 229:     contact_ed_pubs: list[bytes],
 230:     threshold_k: int = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
 231:     total_n: int = DEFAULT_TOTAL,
 232:     setup_ms: Optional[int] = None,
 233: ) -> list[WrappedShare]:
 234:     """Split ``seed`` into Shamir shares + encrypt each share to one
 235:     contact's Ed25519 identity. Returns ``total_n`` WrappedShare
 236:     objects ready to ship to the corresponding contact.
 237: 
 238:     ``contact_ed_pubs`` MUST have length ``total_n``. The share at
 239:     index i is wrapped for contact_ed_pubs[i].
 240:     """
 241:     if len(seed) != SEED_LEN:
 242:         raise ValueError(f"seed must be {SEED_LEN} bytes")
 243:     if not (2 <= threshold_k <= total_n <= 255):
 244:         raise ValueError(
 245:             f"invalid threshold_k={threshold_k} / total_n={total_n} "
 246:             "(need 2 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 255)"
 247:         )
 248:     if len(contact_ed_pubs) != total_n:
 249:         raise ValueError(
 250:             f"contact_ed_pubs length {len(contact_ed_pubs)} != total_n {total_n}"
 251:         )
 252:     for i, p in enumerate(contact_ed_pubs):
 253:         if not isinstance(p, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(p) != 32:
 254:             raise ValueError(f"contact_ed_pubs[{i}] must be 32 bytes")
 255:     if setup_ms is None:
 256:         setup_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
 257: 
 258:     # Row 9 wiring: prefer the native Rust Shamir impl when available
 259:     # (45-84x faster reconstruct). Both paths produce the same share
 260:     # bytes for the same secret + the same set of x-values.
 261:     if _NATIVE_AVAILABLE:
 262:         native_shares = _native_tr.split_compat(
 263:             bytes(seed), threshold=threshold_k, num_shares=total_n
 264:         )
 265:         raw_shares = [
 266:             threshold.Share(x=x, y=y) for x, y in native_shares
 267:         ]
 268:     else:
 269:         raw_shares = threshold.split(
 270:             secret=bytes(seed), threshold=threshold_k, num_shares=total_n,
 271:         )
 272:     out: list[WrappedShare] = []
 273:     for i, share in enumerate(raw_shares):
 274:         share_idx = share.x
 275:         share_bytes = share.y
 276:         contact_ed_pub = bytes(contact_ed_pubs[i])
 277:         contact_x_pub = ed25519_pub_to_x25519(contact_ed_pub)
 278:         eph_priv = X25519PrivateKey.generate()
 279:         eph_pub = eph_priv.public_key().public_bytes_raw()
 280:         try:
 281:             shared = eph_priv.exchange(
 282:                 X25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(contact_x_pub),
 283:             )
 284:         except Exception as e:
 285:             raise ValueError(
 286:                 f"contact_ed_pubs[{i}] is not a valid Ed25519→X25519 "
 287:                 f"convertible pubkey: {e}"
 288:             ) from None
 289:         if shared == b"\x00" * 32:
 290:             raise ValueError(
 291:                 f"contact_ed_pubs[{i}] yielded zero shared secret "
 292:                 "(small-order point); refuse to wrap"
 293:             )
 294:         key = _derive_aead_key(shared)
 295:         nonce = secrets.token_bytes(NONCE_LEN)
 296:         header = (
 297:             SHARE_MAGIC
 298:             + bytes([SHARE_VERSION, share_idx, threshold_k, total_n])
 299:             + struct.pack(">Q", setup_ms)
 300:             + eph_pub
 301:             + nonce
 302:         )
 303:         # Plaintext is the full Shamir output: 1-byte index + share bytes.
 304:         # We re-include the index inside the AEAD so a guardian can't
 305:         # be tricked into shipping a renumbered share.
 306:         plaintext = bytes([share_idx]) + share_bytes
 307:         ct = AESGCM(key).encrypt(nonce, plaintext, header)
 308:         encoded = header + ct
 309:         out.append(WrappedShare(
 310:             share_index=share_idx,
 311:             threshold=threshold_k,
 312:             total=total_n,
 313:             setup_ms=setup_ms,
 314:             encoded=encoded,
 315:         ))
 316:     return out
 317: 
 318: 
 319: def unwrap_share(
 320:     *,
 321:     wrapped: bytes,
 322:     my_ed_priv_seed: bytes,
 323: ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
 324:     """Decrypt a wrapped share with the recipient's Ed25519 private
 325:     seed. Returns ``(share_index, share_bytes)`` ready to feed back
 326:     into ``threshold.combine`` along with K-1 other shares.
 327: 
 328:     Raises ValueError on tamper, wrong key, or version mismatch."""
 329:     if len(my_ed_priv_seed) != 32:
 330:         raise ValueError("my_ed_priv_seed must be 32 bytes")
 331:     if len(wrapped) < HEADER_LEN + 16:  # +16 for AEAD tag minimum
 332:         raise ValueError("wrapped share too short")
 333:     if wrapped[:5] != SHARE_MAGIC:
 334:         raise ValueError("not a One Link social-recovery share")
 335:     if wrapped[5] != SHARE_VERSION:
 336:         raise ValueError(f"unsupported version {wrapped[5]}")
 337:     share_idx = wrapped[6]
 338:     threshold_k = wrapped[7]
 339:     total_n = wrapped[8]
 340:     setup_ms = struct.unpack(">Q", wrapped[9:17])[0]
 341:     eph_pub = wrapped[17:49]
 342:     nonce = wrapped[49:61]
 343:     ct = wrapped[HEADER_LEN:]
 344:     header = wrapped[:HEADER_LEN]
 345: 
 346:     my_x_priv_bytes = ed25519_priv_to_x25519(my_ed_priv_seed)
 347:     my_x_priv = X25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(my_x_priv_bytes)
 348:     try:
 349:         shared = my_x_priv.exchange(
 350:             X25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(eph_pub),
 351:         )
 352:     except Exception as e:
 353:         raise ValueError(f"shared-secret derive failed: {e}") from None
 354:     if shared == b"\x00" * 32:
 355:         raise ValueError("ECDH yielded zero shared secret")
 356:     key = _derive_aead_key(shared)
 357:     try:
 358:         plaintext = AESGCM(key).decrypt(nonce, ct, header)
 359:     except Exception as e:
 360:         raise ValueError(
 361:             f"share decrypt failed (wrong key or tamper): {e}"
 362:         ) from None
 363:     if len(plaintext) < 1 + 1:  # share_idx + at least 1 byte of payload
 364:         raise ValueError("decrypted share too short")
 365:     inner_idx = plaintext[0]
 366:     if inner_idx != share_idx:
 367:         raise ValueError(
 368:             f"AEAD-bound share index mismatch: header says {share_idx}, "
 369:             f"plaintext says {inner_idx}"
 370:         )
 371:     share_bytes = plaintext[1:]
 372:     return inner_idx, share_bytes
 373: 
 374: 
 375: def combine_shares(shares: list[tuple[int, bytes]]) -> bytes:
 376:     """Reconstruct the original seed from K shares. Each tuple is
 377:     ``(share_index, share_bytes)`` — the same shape that
 378:     ``unwrap_share`` returns. Wraps ``threshold.combine`` with a
 379:     length check + a clearer error.
 380: 
 381:     Row 9 wiring: uses the native Rust Shamir reconstruct when
 382:     available (45-84x faster than pure-Python per F1.1 benches).
 383:     """
 384:     if not shares:
 385:         raise ValueError("need at least one share")
 386:     # Use native reconstruct when available.
 387:     if _NATIVE_AVAILABLE:
 388:         # Native expects exactly `k` shares; infer k from supplied count.
 389:         # If caller provided extras, split_compat-style we use first len(shares).
 390:         k = len(shares)
 391:         share_tuples = [(int(idx), bytes(payload)) for idx, payload in shares]
 392:         seed = _native_tr.combine_compat(share_tuples, threshold=k)
 393:     else:
 394:         threshold_shares = [
 395:             threshold.Share(x=int(idx), y=bytes(payload))
 396:             for idx, payload in shares
 397:         ]
 398:         seed = threshold.combine(threshold_shares)
 399:     if len(seed) != SEED_LEN:
 400:         raise ValueError(
 401:             f"reconstructed secret has wrong length {len(seed)}; "
 402:             f"expected {SEED_LEN}. Did you mix shares from different "
 403:             "setups?"
 404:         )
 405:     return seed
 406: 
 407: 
 408: # ── high-level recovery flow helpers ─────────────────────────────────
 409: 
 410: 
 411: def setup_social_recovery(
 412:     *,
 413:     seed: bytes,
 414:     guardians: list[tuple[str, bytes]],
 415:     threshold_k: int = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
 416: ) -> list[tuple[str, WrappedShare]]:
 417:     """Convenience: pair guardians (display_name, ed_pub) with their
 418:     respective wrapped shares. Returns ``[(display_name, WrappedShare),
 419:     ...]`` in input order — caller delivers each pair to its named
 420:     guardian via whatever transport (channel, QR, USB stick, sky-
 421:     writing — the wrap is sealed; the medium doesn't matter)."""
 422:     total_n = len(guardians)
 423:     pubs = [pub for _, pub in guardians]
 424:     shares = split_and_wrap(
 425:         seed=seed,
 426:         contact_ed_pubs=pubs,
 427:         threshold_k=threshold_k,
 428:         total_n=total_n,
 429:     )
 430:     return [(name, share) for (name, _pub), share in zip(guardians, shares)]
 431: 
 432: 
 433: def reconstruct_from_decrypted_shares(
 434:     decrypted: list[tuple[int, bytes]],
 435: ) -> bytes:
 436:     """Final step in the recovery ceremony: K guardians each shipped
 437:     their decrypted (share_index, share_bytes) tuple back to the
 438:     recovering device; combine them into the original seed."""
 439:     return combine_shares(decrypted)

 157: def get_preset(name: Optional[str]) -> SovereigntyPreset:
 158:     """Resolve a preset name to its definition. Unknown names fall
 159:     back to the default — the only thing that matters is that the
 160:     daemon NEVER crashes on a malformed setting."""
 161:     if not name:

 163:     return ALL_PRESETS.get(name.strip().lower(), ALL_PRESETS[DEFAULT_PRESET_NAME])

 166: def resolve_update_check_enabled(
 167:     *,
 168:     state_setting: Optional[str],
 169:     env_var: Optional[str],
 170:     preset_name: Optional[str],
 171: ) -> bool:
 172:     """Read order for the update-check flag.
 173: 
 174:     1. ``state_setting`` (explicit user setting) wins if not None / not empty.
 175:     2. ``env_var`` (operator override) wins if set.
 176:     3. Preset default.
 177:     """
 178:     # 1. Explicit setting wins. Strings "0"/"false"/"no"/"off" are
 179:     #    explicit OFF; "1"/"true"/"yes"/"on" are explicit ON.
 180:     s = (state_setting or "").strip().lower()
 181:     if s in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"):
 182:         return True
 183:     if s in ("0", "false", "no", "off"):
 184:         return False
 185:     # 2. Env var.
 186:     e = (env_var or "").strip().lower()
 187:     if e in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"):
 188:         return True
 189:     if e in ("0", "false", "no", "off"):
 190:         return False
 191:     # 3. Preset default.
 192:     return get_preset(preset_name).update_check_enabled

 195: def resolve_stun_servers(
 196:     *,
 197:     state_setting: Optional[str],
 198:     env_var: Optional[str],
 199:     preset_name: Optional[str],
 200: ) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 201:     """Read order for the STUN server list.
 202: 
 203:     Setting + env var are comma-separated lists of stun:host:port
 204:     URLs. Explicit empty string means "user wants NO stun even on a
 205:     preset that defaults to community STUN" — honored.
 206: 
 207:     1. ``state_setting`` (if not None) wins — empty string = []
 208:     2. ``env_var`` (if not None) wins next — empty string = []
 209:     3. Preset default.
 210:     """
 211:     def _parse(raw: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 212:         out = []
 213:         seen: set[str] = set()
 214:         for u in raw.split(","):
 215:             u = u.strip()
 216:             if u and u not in seen:
 217:                 out.append(u)
 218:                 seen.add(u)
 219:         return tuple(out)

 221:     # state_setting=None means "no override". Empty string means
 222:     # "explicit opt-out of even the preset default."
 223:     if state_setting is not None:
 224:         return _parse(state_setting)
 225:     if env_var is not None:
 226:         return _parse(env_var)
 227:     return get_preset(preset_name).stun_servers

 237:     except Exception:
 238:         return DEFAULT_PRESET_NAME
 239:     if v not in ALL_PRESETS:
 240:         return DEFAULT_PRESET_NAME
 241:     return v

   1: """Adapter for the Sphinx Coherence onion-routing primitive
   2: (`ol_onion::sphinx` via `one_link_native.sphinx`).
   3: 
   4: Per `One_link/native/ol_onion/SPHINX_COHERENCE_DESIGN.md`. Three
   5: layers:
   6: 
   7: 1. **Standard Sphinx (T1.1)**: Ristretto255 alpha blinding + filler-
   8:    byte construction. Single packet-level ephemeral pubkey BLINDED
   9:    at each hop so a global passive observer sees uncorrelated random
  10:    group elements at every relay. ~165 us 3-hop build.
  11: 
  12: 2. **PQ-hybrid (T1.2)**: ML-KEM-768 ciphertext addressed to the
  13:    entry hop. The PQ-binding propagates downstream via the
  14:    cumulative blinding chain, so a quantum adversary recording
  15:    today cannot decrypt the alpha chain tomorrow.
  16: 
  17: 3. **Field-bound (T1.3)**: derive_hop_keys_with_witness mixes the
  18:    relay's coherence-field PDE state into the blinding factor.
  19:    Daemon-side responsibility to source witnesses from
  20:    `ol_coherence_field` (not exposed at this Python layer yet).
  21: 
  22: Sphinx packets are FIXED SIZE at every hop (~1305 bytes standard,
  23: ~2393 bytes PQ-hybrid) so a network observer cannot infer hop count
  24: from packet length.
  25: 
  26: Typical daemon usage as sender:
  27: 
  28: .. code-block:: python
  29: 
  30:     from one_link import sphinx_native as sph
  31: 
  32:     eph_sk, _ = sph.generate_keypair()
  33:     circuit = [
  34:         (peer_a_id, peer_a_pubkey),  # first relay
  35:         (peer_b_id, peer_b_pubkey),  # middle relay
  36:         (dest_id, dest_pubkey),       # destination
  37:     ]
  38:     packet = sph.build_sphinx(eph_sk, circuit, payload=b"hello")
  39:     # Send packet to peer_a over the transport.
  40: 
  41: As a relay:
  42: 
  43: .. code-block:: python
  44: 
  45:     outcome, next_hop_id, inner = sph.peel_sphinx(
  46:         relay_sk=my_static_sk,
  47:         packet=received_bytes,
  48:     )
  49:     if outcome == "forward":
  50:         forward_to(next_hop_id, inner)
  51:     elif outcome == "deliver":
  52:         deliver(inner)
  53: """
  54: 
  55: from __future__ import annotations
  56: 
  57: import logging
  58: from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
  59: 
  60: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  61: 
  62: try:
  63:     from one_link_native import sphinx as _native_sphinx  # type: ignore[import-not-found,attr-defined]
  64: 
  65:     HAS_NATIVE: bool = True
  66:     HOP_ID_LEN: int = _native_sphinx.HOP_ID_LEN
  67:     MAX_HOPS: int = _native_sphinx.MAX_HOPS
  68:     SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD: int = _native_sphinx.SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD
  69:     SPHINX_PACKET_LEN: int = _native_sphinx.SPHINX_PACKET_LEN
  70:     PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN: int = _native_sphinx.PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN
  71:     ML_KEM_CT_LEN: int = _native_sphinx.ML_KEM_CT_LEN
  72:     ML_KEM_EK_LEN: int = _native_sphinx.ML_KEM_EK_LEN
  73:     COVER_SENTINEL: bytes = bytes(getattr(_native_sphinx, "COVER_SENTINEL", b"OL-COVER"))
  74:     COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN: int = int(getattr(_native_sphinx, "COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN", 64))
  75:     COVER_DEFAULT_RATE_HZ: float = float(getattr(_native_sphinx, "COVER_DEFAULT_RATE_HZ", 1.0))
  76: except (ImportError, AttributeError) as exc:
  77:     HAS_NATIVE = False
  78:     _native_sphinx = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
  79:     HOP_ID_LEN = 32
  80:     MAX_HOPS = 5
  81:     SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD = 1022
  82:     SPHINX_PACKET_LEN = 1305
  83:     PQ_SPHINX_PACKET_LEN = 2393
  84:     ML_KEM_CT_LEN = 1088
  85:     ML_KEM_EK_LEN = 1184
  86:     COVER_SENTINEL = b"OL-COVER"
  87:     COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN = 64
  88:     COVER_DEFAULT_RATE_HZ = 1.0
  89:     log.info(
  90:         "one_link_native.sphinx not installed (%s); Sphinx Coherence "
  91:         "routing unavailable. Build via "
  92:         "`cd native && maturin develop --release`.",
  93:         exc,
  94:     )
  95: 
  96: 
  97: class NativeMissingError(RuntimeError):
  98:     """Raised when the native sphinx surface is not available."""
  99: 
 100: 
 101: def _require_native() -> None:
 102:     if not HAS_NATIVE:
 103:         raise NativeMissingError(
 104:             "one_link_native.sphinx unavailable; rebuild via "
 105:             "`cd native && maturin develop --release`"
 106:         )
 107: 
 108: 
 109: # ── Standard Sphinx ─────────────────────────────────────────────
 110: 
 111: 
 112: def generate_keypair() -> Tuple[bytes, bytes]:
 113:     """Generate a fresh Ristretto255 keypair. Returns (sk, pk) both 32 bytes."""
 114:     _require_native()
 115:     sk, pk = _native_sphinx.generate_keypair()
 116:     return bytes(sk), bytes(pk)
 117: 
 118: 
 119: def derive_pubkey_from_scalar(sk: bytes) -> bytes:
 120:     """Derive the public Ristretto255 point from a 32-byte scalar."""
 121:     _require_native()
 122:     if len(sk) != 32:
 123:         raise ValueError(f"sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(sk)}")
 124:     return bytes(_native_sphinx.derive_pubkey_from_scalar(sk))
 125: 
 126: 
 127: def build_sphinx(
 128:     eph_sk: bytes, circuit: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]], payload: bytes
 129: ) -> bytes:
 130:     """Construct a standard Sphinx packet.
 131: 
 132:     `eph_sk`: 32-byte ephemeral Ristretto255 scalar (one per circuit).
 133:     `circuit`: list of (hop_id_32, pubkey_32) tuples in circuit order.
 134:     `payload`: up to `SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD` bytes.
 135: 
 136:     Returns the fixed-size `SPHINX_PACKET_LEN` wire bytes the sender
 137:     hands to `circuit[0]`.
 138:     """
 139:     _require_native()
 140:     if len(eph_sk) != 32:
 141:         raise ValueError(f"eph_sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(eph_sk)}")
 142:     if not circuit:
 143:         raise ValueError("circuit must have at least one hop")
 144:     if len(circuit) > MAX_HOPS:
 145:         raise ValueError(f"circuit has {len(circuit)} hops, max {MAX_HOPS}")
 146:     if len(payload) > SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD:
 147:         raise ValueError(
 148:             f"payload is {len(payload)} bytes, max {SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD}"
 149:         )
 150:     return bytes(_native_sphinx.build_sphinx(eph_sk, circuit, payload))
 151: 
 152: 
 153: def peel_sphinx(
 154:     relay_sk: bytes, packet: bytes
 155: ) -> Tuple[str, bytes, bytes]:
 156:     """Peel one Sphinx layer at this relay.
 157: 
 158:     Returns `(outcome, next_hop_id_or_empty, inner_or_payload)`:
 159:     - "forward": forward `inner_or_payload` to `next_hop_id_or_empty`.
 160:     - "deliver": this relay is the destination; `inner_or_payload`
 161:       is the user payload.
 162:     """
 163:     _require_native()
 164:     if len(relay_sk) != 32:
 165:         raise ValueError(f"relay_sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(relay_sk)}")
 166:     outcome, next_hop, inner = _native_sphinx.peel_sphinx(relay_sk, packet)
 167:     return str(outcome), bytes(next_hop), bytes(inner)
 168: 
 169: 
 170: # ── PQ-hybrid Sphinx ────────────────────────────────────────────
 171: 
 172: 
 173: def generate_pq_keypair() -> Tuple[bytes, bytes]:
 174:     """Generate a fresh ML-KEM-768 keypair. Returns (dk_2400, ek_1184)."""
 175:     _require_native()
 176:     dk, ek = _native_sphinx.generate_pq_keypair()
 177:     return bytes(dk), bytes(ek)
 178: 
 179: 
 180: def build_pq_sphinx(
 181:     eph_sk: bytes,
 182:     circuit: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes, Optional[bytes]]],
 183:     payload: bytes,
 184: ) -> bytes:
 185:     """Construct a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet.
 186: 
 187:     `circuit`: list of (hop_id_32, x25519_pk_32, pq_pk_1184_or_None).
 188:     The FIRST hop MUST supply a PQ pubkey; downstream hops MAY pass None.
 189:     """
 190:     _require_native()
 191:     if len(eph_sk) != 32:
 192:         raise ValueError(f"eph_sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(eph_sk)}")
 193:     if not circuit:
 194:         raise ValueError("circuit must have at least one hop")
 195:     if len(circuit) > MAX_HOPS:
 196:         raise ValueError(f"circuit has {len(circuit)} hops, max {MAX_HOPS}")
 197:     if circuit[0][2] is None:
 198:         raise ValueError("first hop must have a PQ pubkey")
 199:     if len(payload) > SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD:
 200:         raise ValueError(
 201:             f"payload is {len(payload)} bytes, max {SPHINX_MAX_USER_PAYLOAD}"
 202:         )
 203:     return bytes(_native_sphinx.build_pq_sphinx(eph_sk, circuit, payload))
 204: 
 205: 
 206: def peel_pq_sphinx_entry(
 207:     relay_x_sk: bytes, relay_pq_dk: bytes, packet: bytes
 208: ) -> Tuple[str, bytes, bytes]:
 209:     """Peel a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet at the ENTRY relay (decapsulates
 210:     the carried ML-KEM ciphertext into the hybrid shared secret)."""
 211:     _require_native()
 212:     if len(relay_x_sk) != 32:
 213:         raise ValueError(f"relay_x_sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(relay_x_sk)}")
 214:     outcome, next_hop, inner = _native_sphinx.peel_pq_sphinx_entry(
 215:         relay_x_sk, relay_pq_dk, packet
 216:     )
 217:     return str(outcome), bytes(next_hop), bytes(inner)
 218: 
 219: 
 220: def peel_pq_sphinx_intermediate(
 221:     relay_x_sk: bytes, packet: bytes
 222: ) -> Tuple[str, bytes, bytes]:
 223:     """Peel a PQ-hybrid Sphinx packet at a downstream/intermediate
 224:     relay (classical-only; ignores the carried PQ ciphertext)."""
 225:     _require_native()
 226:     if len(relay_x_sk) != 32:
 227:         raise ValueError(f"relay_x_sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(relay_x_sk)}")
 228:     outcome, next_hop, inner = _native_sphinx.peel_pq_sphinx_intermediate(
 229:         relay_x_sk, packet
 230:     )
 231:     return str(outcome), bytes(next_hop), bytes(inner)
 232: 
 233: 
 234: def build_cover_packet(
 235:     eph_sk: bytes, circuit: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]], cover_size: int
 236: ) -> bytes:
 237:     """Build a Sphinx cover packet — indistinguishable on the wire
 238:     from a real packet (same size, same blinding, same encryption).
 239:     Destination identifies it via `is_cover_payload`.
 240: 
 241:     `cover_size`: random-byte padding length after the cover sentinel
 242:     (≥ `COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN`).
 243:     """
 244:     _require_native()
 245:     if len(eph_sk) != 32:
 246:         raise ValueError(f"eph_sk must be 32 bytes, got {len(eph_sk)}")
 247:     if cover_size < COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN:
 248:         raise ValueError(
 249:             f"cover_size must be >= {COVER_PAYLOAD_MIN}, got {cover_size}"
 250:         )
 251:     return bytes(_native_sphinx.build_cover_packet(eph_sk, circuit, cover_size))
 252: 
 253: 
 254: def is_cover_payload(payload: bytes) -> bool:
 255:     """True iff `payload` carries the COVER_SENTINEL prefix."""
 256:     _require_native()
 257:     return bool(_native_sphinx.is_cover_payload(payload))
 258: 
 259: 
 260: class CoverScheduler:
 261:     """Poisson-rate scheduler for cover-traffic emission.
 262: 
 263:     Each call to `next_wait_ms()` returns the next inter-arrival
 264:     sleep in milliseconds. Pass the result to your event loop;
 265:     on wake, emit a cover packet built via `build_cover_packet`.
 266:     """
 267: 
 268:     def __init__(self, rate_hz: float, seed: bytes) -> None:
 269:         _require_native()
 270:         if len(seed) != 32:
 271:             raise ValueError(f"seed must be 32 bytes, got {len(seed)}")
 272:         if rate_hz <= 0:
 273:             raise ValueError(f"rate_hz must be positive, got {rate_hz}")
 274:         self._native = _native_sphinx.CoverScheduler(rate_hz, seed)
 275: 
 276:     def next_wait_ms(self) -> int:
 277:         return int(self._native.next_wait_ms())
 278: 
 279:     def rate_hz(self) -> float:
 280:         return float(self._native.rate_hz())
 281: 
 282:     def set_rate_hz(self, rate_hz: float) -> None:
 283:         if rate_hz <= 0:
 284:             raise ValueError(f"rate_hz must be positive, got {rate_hz}")
 285:         self._native.set_rate_hz(rate_hz)
 286: 
 287: 
 288: class RateEqualizer:
 289:     """Adaptive rate equalizer for cover traffic.
 290: 
 291:     Maintains a CONSTANT total emission rate (cover + real)
 292:     regardless of real-traffic load. When real traffic spikes, the
 293:     cover rate drops; when real traffic is idle, the cover rate
 294:     rises to fill the gap. An observer sees a uniform-rate output
 295:     stream and cannot infer "is there real traffic now?" from
 296:     packet timing alone.
 297: 
 298:     ## Usage
 299: 
 300:     .. code-block:: python
 301: 
 302:         eq = RateEqualizer(target_total_hz=5.0)
 303:         sched = CoverScheduler(rate_hz=5.0, seed=...)
 304:         while True:
 305:             # ... real traffic loop also calls eq.observe_real_emission
 306:             sched.set_rate_hz(max(eq.current_cover_rate(), 0.01))
 307:             sleep_ms(sched.next_wait_ms())
 308:             emit_cover_packet()
 309:             eq.observe_idle_tick(now_ms())
 310:     """
 311: 
 312:     def __init__(self, target_total_hz: float) -> None:
 313:         _require_native()
 314:         if target_total_hz <= 0:
 315:             raise ValueError(
 316:                 f"target_total_hz must be positive, got {target_total_hz}"
 317:             )
 318:         self._native = _native_sphinx.RateEqualizer(target_total_hz)
 319: 
 320:     def observe_real_emission(self, now_ms: int) -> None:
 321:         """Notify that a real packet was emitted at `now_ms`."""
 322:         self._native.observe_real_emission(int(now_ms))
 323: 
 324:     def observe_idle_tick(self, now_ms: int) -> None:
 325:         """Notify wall-clock has advanced without a real emission.
 326:         Lets the equalizer decay observed-real-rate toward zero."""
 327:         self._native.observe_idle_tick(int(now_ms))
 328: 
 329:     def current_cover_rate(self) -> float:
 330:         """Cover rate that maintains target total emission."""
 331:         return float(self._native.current_cover_rate())
 332: 
 333:     def observed_real_rate(self) -> float:
 334:         """Current EWMA-smoothed real-traffic rate (diagnostic)."""
 335:         return float(self._native.observed_real_rate())
 336: 
 337:     def target_total_hz(self) -> float:
 338:         return float(self._native.target_total_hz())
 339: 
 340:     def set_half_life_sec(self, half_life_sec: float) -> None:
 341:         if half_life_sec <= 0:
 342:             raise ValueError("half_life_sec must be positive")
 343:         self._native.set_half_life_sec(half_life_sec)
 344: 
 345:

   2: 
   3: A single sqlite database under ONE_LINK_HOME/data/state.db backs:
   4: 
   5: - peers (fingerprint, trust state, last seen)
   6: - messages (full chat history with FTS5 full-text search)
   7: - rooms (multi-party named conversations)
   8: - folders (designated sync folders)

  13: `check_same_thread=False` and `journal_mode=WAL`, guarded by a re-entrant

 316:     # forever (no auto-expire); N > 0 = muted until wall-clock ms N.

 329:         a side-channel SAS confirm. Independent of `trust` — trust
 330:         gates wire access; verification gates UI affordance."""
 331:         return self.verified_at_ms is not None
 332: 
 333:     def is_muted_at(self, now_ms: int) -> bool:
 334:         """v0.11.2: True iff the per-chat mute is active at `now_ms`.
 335:         muted_until_ms = 0 means muted forever; >0 means muted until
 336:         that timestamp. Falls back to the legacy `muted` boolean for
 337:         rows persisted under v0.7.3 schema before muted_until_ms
 338:         existed."""
 339:         if self.muted_until_ms is not None:
 340:             if self.muted_until_ms == 0:
 341:                 return True
 342:             return self.muted_until_ms > now_ms
 343:         return self.muted
 344:

 416: 
 417: class State:
 418:     """Singleton-style state handle. Construct once per daemon."""
 419: 
 420:     def __init__(self, db_path: Optional[Path] = None):
 421:         self.db_path = db_path or (data_dir() / DB_FILE)
 422:         self._conn: sqlite3.Connection = sqlite3.connect(
 423:             self.db_path, check_same_thread=False, isolation_level=None
 424:         )
 425:         self._conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
 426:         self._write_lock = threading.RLock()
 427:         # v0.20.7 (security audit H21 + partial C5): optional
 428:         # at-rest wrap for the highest-value secrets in the schema
 429:         # (group sender chain_keys). Daemon wires a LockBox here at
 430:         # boot when ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE is set; absent passphrase →
 431:         # None → values stored cleartext (legacy behavior). Wrapping
 432:         # is transparent to read paths via lockbox.maybe_unwrap so a
 433:         # mid-life passphrase opt-in coexists with legacy rows.
 434:         self._lockbox = None  # set via set_lockbox()
 435:         self._init_pragmas()
 436:         self._migrate()
 437: 
 438:     def set_lockbox(self, lockbox) -> None:
 439:         """v0.20.7: late-attach the at-rest wrap key. Daemon calls
 440:         this once at boot after constructing State + the LockBox.
 441:         Subsequent writes wrap; subsequent reads unwrap on demand."""
 442:         self._lockbox = lockbox
 443: 
 444:     # v0.20.7 (security audit M30): path-PII encryptor. Daemon late-
 445:     # attaches one of these at boot when the master seed is available;
 446:     # all chunk_sources / file_index_cache writes go through wrap, all
 447:     # reads go through unwrap. Legacy cleartext rows are detected by
 448:     # absence of the marker prefix and remain readable.
 449:     _path_pii = None
 450: 
 451:     def set_path_pii_encryptor(self, encryptor) -> None:
 452:         self._path_pii = encryptor
 453: 
 454:     # AAD strings: distinct per column so a path that exists in both
 455:     # tables encrypts to different ciphertext, ensuring a leak of one
 456:     # column doesn't help an attacker pivot via the other.
 457:     _PATH_PII_AAD_CHUNK_SOURCES = b"OL/state/chunk_sources/path|v1"
 458:     _PATH_PII_AAD_FILE_INDEX = b"OL/state/file_index_cache/path|v1"
 459: 
 460:     def _wrap_path(self, value: str, *, aad: bytes) -> str:
 461:         if self._path_pii is None or not value:
 462:             return value
 463:         return self._path_pii.wrap(value, aad=aad)
 464: 
 465:     def _unwrap_path(self, value: str, *, aad: bytes) -> str:
 466:         if self._path_pii is None or not value:
 467:             return value
 468:         out = self._path_pii.unwrap(value, aad=aad)
 469:         # If unwrap returned None, the value is wrapped but
 470:         # un-decryptable (tamper / wrong install). Surface the
 471:         # opaque marker so callers don't accidentally treat stale
 472:         # ciphertext as a real filesystem path.
 473:         return out if out is not None else value
 474: 
 475:     def _init_pragmas(self) -> None:
 476:         c = self._conn.cursor()
 477:         c.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
 478:         c.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL")
 479:         c.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
 480:         c.execute("PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY")
 481:         c.execute("PRAGMA cache_size = -8000")  # 8 MB
 482:         # v0.20.7 (security audit H22): zero freed pages on delete so
 483:         # the disappearing-messages reaper actually erases plaintext
 484:         # bodies from the file. Adds ~10% write cost; worth it.
 485:         c.execute("PRAGMA secure_delete = ON")
 486:         # v0.20.7: checkpoint WAL frequently so deleted-row plaintext
 487:         # does not linger in state.db-wal between application
 488:         # checkpoints. 50 pages ~= ~200KB worst case.
 489:         c.execute("PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 50")
 490:         c.close()
 491: 
 492:     def _migrate(self) -> None:
 493:         """Run schema migrations atomically.
 494: 
 495:         v0.20.7 (security audit H20): each migration step + its
 496:         version stamp run inside a single ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` /
 497:         ``COMMIT`` transaction. A SIGKILL between an ALTER TABLE and
 498:         the version-stamp INSERT used to leave the DB in a half-
 499:         migrated state (table already had the new column but
 500:         ``schema_version`` claimed the old version, so the next boot
 501:         re-ran the migration and either errored on duplicate column
 502:         or quietly mis-stamped). With per-step transactions, the WAL
 503:         rolls back on crash and the next boot retries the same step
 504:         from a clean baseline.
 505: 
 506:         SQLite's ``isolation_level=None`` (autocommit) still permits
 507:         explicit ``BEGIN``/``COMMIT`` to delimit a transaction, which
 508:         is what we want here — every other code path stays in
 509:         autocommit mode.
 510:         """
 511:         with self._write_lock:
 512:             c = self._conn.cursor()
 513:             try:
 514:                 # Bootstrap v1. SCHEMA_V1 is composed entirely of
 515:                 # ``CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`` statements (tables,
 516:                 # virtual tables, triggers, indexes), so a crash mid-
 517:                 # script is safe: the next boot re-runs the script and
 518:                 # idempotently fills in whatever is missing. We can't
 519:                 # wrap ``executescript`` in BEGIN IMMEDIATE because
 520:                 # SQLite's executescript implicitly commits the open
 521:                 # transaction — but the idempotency property keeps v1
 522:                 # bootstrap safe on its own.
 523:                 c.executescript(SCHEMA_V1)
 524:                 cur = c.execute("SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_version")
 525:                 row = cur.fetchone()
 526:                 current = row[0] if row and row[0] is not None else 0
 527:                 if current < 1:
 528:                     c.execute("INSERT INTO schema_version(version) VALUES(1)")
 529:                     current = 1
 530: 
 531:                 # vN+ migrations: each (apply_fn, target_version) pair
 532:                 # runs in its own transaction so a crash in the middle
 533:                 # of vN does not leave the schema with vN's tables but
 534:                 # vN-1's stamp.
 535:                 steps = [
 536:                     (2, self._migrate_v2_folder_sandboxes),
 537:                     (3, self._migrate_v3_peer_profile),
 538:                     (4, self._migrate_v4_messages_reply_to),
 539:                     (5, self._migrate_v5_edit_delete_read),
 540:                     (6, self._migrate_v6_group_reply),
 541:                     (7, self._migrate_v7_group_edit_delete),
 542:                     (8, self._migrate_v8_peer_verification),
 543:                     (9, self._migrate_v9_key_change_tracking),
 544:                     (10, self._migrate_v10_folder_conflicts),
 545:                     (11, self._migrate_v11_chunk_availability),
 546:                     (12, self._migrate_v12_disappearing_messages),
 547:                     (13, self._migrate_v13_prior_chunk_sources),
 548:                     (14, self._migrate_v14_mute_until),
 549:                     (15, self._migrate_v15_file_index_cache),
 550:                     (16, self._migrate_v16_route_memory),
 551:                     (17, self._migrate_v17_route_candidates),
 552:                     (18, self._migrate_v18_personal_device_mesh),
 553:                     (19, self._migrate_v19_self_mesh_enrollment),
 554:                     (20, self._migrate_v20_self_mesh_performance),
 555:                     (21, self._migrate_v21_device_guardian),
 556:                 ]
 557:                 for target_version, apply_fn in steps:
 558:                     self._run_atomic_migration(
 559:                         c,
 560:                         target_version=target_version,
 561:                         current_version=current,
 562:                         apply=apply_fn,
 563:                     )
 564:             finally:
 565:                 c.close()
 566: 
 567:     def _run_atomic_migration(
 568:         self,
 569:         c: sqlite3.Cursor,
 570:         *,
 571:         target_version: int,
 572:         apply,
 573:         current_version: Optional[int] = None,
 574:     ) -> None:
 575:         """Apply ``apply(cursor)`` and (if first-time-crossing) stamp
 576:         ``target_version`` in one transaction.
 577: 
 578:         Each migration step is idempotent — most use ``CREATE ... IF
 579:         NOT EXISTS`` and PRAGMA-introspected ``ALTER TABLE``, and a few
 580:         also serve as boot-time backfills (e.g. v2's root_id sweep).
 581:         We therefore always run ``apply`` so backfills keep healing
 582:         any drifted rows, but only INSERT the version stamp the first
 583:         time we cross the boundary. The whole thing is wrapped in a
 584:         single ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` so a crash mid-step rolls back
 585:         cleanly — no half-applied DDL with a stale version stamp.
 586:         """
 587:         if current_version is None:
 588:             row = c.execute("SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_version").fetchone()
 589:             current_version = (
 590:                 row[0] if row and row[0] is not None else 0
 591:             )
 592:         c.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
 593:         try:
 594:             apply(c)
 595:             if current_version < target_version:
 596:                 c.execute(
 597:                     "INSERT INTO schema_version(version) VALUES(?)",
 598:                     (target_version,),
 599:                 )
 600:             c.execute("COMMIT")
 601:         except Exception:
 602:             try:
 603:                 c.execute("ROLLBACK")
 604:             except Exception:
 605:                 pass
 606:             raise
 607:

 878:     def _migrate_v15_file_index_cache(self, c: sqlite3.Cursor) -> None:
 879:         """v0.12.4: durable file fingerprint/manifest cache.
 880: 
 881:         Large-file sends should not re-hash and re-index an unchanged file
 882:         every time the user sends it. The cache is keyed by canonical path and
 883:         guarded by file size + nanosecond mtimes/ctimes, so a stale row is
 884:         ignored automatically when the file changes.
 885:         """
 886:         c.execute(
 887:             """
 888:             CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS file_index_cache (
 889:                 path        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
 890:                 size        INTEGER NOT NULL,
 891:                 mtime_ns    INTEGER NOT NULL,
 892:                 ctime_ns    INTEGER NOT NULL,
 893:                 blob_hash   TEXT    NOT NULL,
 894:                 index_kind  TEXT    NOT NULL,
 895:                 chunks_json TEXT    NOT NULL,
 896:                 updated_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL
 897:             )
 898:             """
 899:         )
 900:         c.execute(

 954:     def _migrate_v12_disappearing_messages(self, c: sqlite3.Cursor) -> None:
 955:         """v0.10.2: per-peer disappearing-message TTL.
 956: 
 957:         peers.dm_ttl_ms — when set, every TEXT message exchanged with
 958:         this peer carries an expires_at_ms = ts_ms + dm_ttl_ms. None
 959:         = TTL off (default). Both ends must support v12 for end-to-end
 960:         expiry — receivers running older builds keep the message
 961:         forever; sender's local copy still expires.
 962: 
 963:         messages.expires_at_ms — wall-clock ms when this row should
 964:         be tombstoned. NULL = never expires (legacy + non-TTL chats).
 965:         Indexed for fast reaper sweeps."""
 966:         rows = c.execute("PRAGMA table_info(peers)").fetchall()
 967:         existing = {row[1] for row in rows}
 968:         if "dm_ttl_ms" not in existing:
 969:             c.execute("ALTER TABLE peers ADD COLUMN dm_ttl_ms INTEGER")
 970:         rows = c.execute("PRAGMA table_info(messages)").fetchall()
 971:         existing = {row[1] for row in rows}
 972:         if "expires_at_ms" not in existing:
 973:             c.execute("ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN expires_at_ms INTEGER")
 974:         # Partial index — only rows with non-NULL expires_at_ms are
 975:         # candidates for the reaper sweep, so a partial index keeps
 976:         # the index page footprint tiny on chats that never use TTL.
 977:         c.execute(
 978:             "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_expiry "
 979:             "ON messages(expires_at_ms) "
 980:             "WHERE expires_at_ms IS NOT NULL"
 981:         )

1139:     def schema_version(self) -> int:
1140:         """Return the latest applied schema version.
1141: 
1142:         Exposed through daemon status so launchers and UIs can detect a
1143:         stale backend before the user hits a broken feature path.
1144:         """

1146:             row = self._conn.execute(
1147:                 "SELECT MAX(version) AS version FROM schema_version"
