1211:     def upsert_peer(
1212:         self,
1213:         *,
1214:         fingerprint: str,
1215:         short_id: str,
1216:         pubkey: bytes,
1217:         hostname: Optional[str] = None,
1218:         address: Optional[str] = None,
1219:         port: Optional[int] = None,
1220:         trust_default: str = "pending",
1221:     ) -> PeerRecord:
1222:         now = _now_ms()
1223:         with self._write_lock:
1224:             c = self._conn.cursor()
1225:             try:
1226:                 c.execute(
1227:                     """
1228:                     INSERT INTO peers(fingerprint, short_id, pubkey, hostname,
1229:                         last_address, last_port, trust, first_seen_ms, last_seen_ms)
1230:                     VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1231:                     ON CONFLICT(fingerprint) DO UPDATE SET
1232:                         short_id     = excluded.short_id,
1233:                         pubkey       = excluded.pubkey,
1234:                         hostname     = COALESCE(excluded.hostname, peers.hostname),
1235:                         last_address = COALESCE(excluded.last_address, peers.last_address),
1236:                         last_port    = COALESCE(excluded.last_port, peers.last_port),
1237:                         last_seen_ms = excluded.last_seen_ms
1238:                     """,
1239:                     (
1240:                         fingerprint, short_id, pubkey, hostname,
1241:                         address, port, trust_default, now, now,
1242:                     ),
1243:                 )
1244:                 row = c.execute(
1245:                     "SELECT * FROM peers WHERE fingerprint = ?", (fingerprint,)
1246:                 ).fetchone()
1247:                 # v0.7.8: track hostname↔key history + raise a key-change
1248:                 # event whenever a hostname rotates fingerprints. The
1249:                 # detection happens here (post-INSERT) so it covers every
1250:                 # code path that upserts a peer (handshake, discovery,
1251:                 # snapshot rehydration). pubkey is bytes — convert once.
1252:                 # The new-event id (if any) is stashed on the returned
1253:                 # PeerRecord via `_pending_key_change_event_id` so the
1254:                 # daemon can broadcast it without a second query.
1255:                 new_event_id: Optional[int] = None
1256:                 if hostname:
1257:                     try:
1258:                         ed_pub_hex = pubkey.hex() if isinstance(pubkey, (bytes, bytearray)) else str(pubkey)
1259:                         new_event_id = self._record_hostname_key_seen_locked(
1260:                             c=c,
1261:                             hostname=hostname,
1262:                             ed_pub_hex=ed_pub_hex,
1263:                             fingerprint=fingerprint,
1264:                             now=now,
1265:                         )
1266:                     except Exception:
1267:                         # Detection failure must never block a peer
1268:                         # upsert — log via daemon if needed, but the
1269:                         # peer table is the source of truth.
1270:                         pass
1271:                 rec = self._row_to_peer(row)
1272:                 if new_event_id is not None:
1273:                     # Attach as a runtime-only attribute; the dataclass
1274:                     # itself is unchanged so callers that don't care
1275:                     # see no difference.
1276:                     object.__setattr__(rec, "_pending_key_change_event_id", new_event_id)
1277:                 return rec
1278:             finally:
1279:                 c.close()
1280: 
1281:     def set_peer_trust(
1282:         self,
1283:         fingerprint: str,
1284:         trust: str,
1285:         *,
1286:         actor: Optional[str] = None,
1287:         note: Optional[str] = None,
1288:     ) -> None:
1289:         if trust not in ("pinned", "pending", "rejected"):
1290:             raise ValueError(f"invalid trust state: {trust!r}")
1291:         applied_default_ttl = False
1292:         with self._write_lock:
1293:             row = self._conn.execute(
1294:                 "SELECT trust, dm_ttl_ms FROM peers WHERE fingerprint = ?",
1295:                 (fingerprint,),
1296:             ).fetchone()
1297:             before = row["trust"] if row else None
1298:             had_ttl = row and row["dm_ttl_ms"] is not None
1299:             self._conn.execute(
1300:                 "UPDATE peers SET trust = ? WHERE fingerprint = ?",
1301:                 (trust, fingerprint),
1302:             )
1303:             if before != trust:
1304:                 self._record_capability_audit(
1305:                     fingerprint=fingerprint,
1306:                     kind="trust_set",
1307:                     before=before,
1308:                     after=trust,
1309:                     actor=actor,
1310:                     note=note,
1311:                 )
1312:             # v0.11.6: when transitioning to "pinned" for the first
1313:             # time AND the user has a default disappearing-msg TTL
1314:             # set globally AND this peer has no per-chat TTL, copy
1315:             # the default in. This is the "applies to new pairings"
1316:             # promise from the Storage settings pane.
1317:             if (
1318:                 trust == "pinned"
1319:                 and before != "pinned"
1320:                 and not had_ttl
1321:             ):
1322:                 raw = self._conn.execute(
1323:                     "SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = 'default_dm_ttl_ms'"
1324:                 ).fetchone()
1325:                 if raw is not None:
1326:                     try:
1327:                         default_ttl = int(raw["value"])
1328:                     except (TypeError, ValueError):
1329:                         default_ttl = 0
1330:                     if default_ttl > 0:
1331:                         self._conn.execute(
1332:                             "UPDATE peers SET dm_ttl_ms = ? "
1333:                             "WHERE fingerprint = ?",
1334:                             (default_ttl, fingerprint),
1335:                         )
1336:                         applied_default_ttl = True
1337:         # Returning intentionally None to preserve existing call
1338:         # sites; applied_default_ttl is for tests + a future caller
1339:         # that wants the signal.
1340:

1359:     def set_peer_capabilities(self, fingerprint: str, caps: Iterable[str]) -> None:
1360:         values = sorted({str(c) for c in caps if str(c)})
1361:         with self._write_lock:
1362:             self._conn.execute(
1363:                 """
1364:                 INSERT INTO peer_capabilities(fingerprint, caps_json, updated_ms)
1365:                 VALUES(?, ?, ?)
1366:                 ON CONFLICT(fingerprint) DO UPDATE SET
1367:                     caps_json = excluded.caps_json,
1368:                     updated_ms = excluded.updated_ms
1369:                 """,
1370:                 (fingerprint, json.dumps(values), _now_ms()),
1371:             )
1372: 
1373:     def get_peer_capabilities(self, fingerprint: str) -> list[str]:
1374:         row = self._conn.execute(
1375:             "SELECT caps_json FROM peer_capabilities WHERE fingerprint = ?",
1376:             (fingerprint,),
1377:         ).fetchone()
1378:         if not row:
1379:             return []
1380:         try:
1381:             return list(json.loads(row["caps_json"]))
1382:         except Exception:
1383:             return []

1385:     def set_peer_capability_policy(
1386:         self,
1387:         fingerprint: str,
1388:         allowed: Iterable[str],
1389:         *,
1390:         actor: Optional[str] = None,
1391:         note: Optional[str] = None,
1392:     ) -> None:
1393:         values = sorted({str(c) for c in allowed if str(c)})
1394:         with self._write_lock:
1395:             before = self.get_peer_capability_policy(fingerprint)
1396:             self._conn.execute(
1397:                 """
1398:                 INSERT INTO peer_capability_policy(fingerprint, allowed_json, updated_ms)
1399:                 VALUES(?, ?, ?)
1400:                 ON CONFLICT(fingerprint) DO UPDATE SET
1401:                     allowed_json = excluded.allowed_json,
1402:                     updated_ms = excluded.updated_ms
1403:                 """,
1404:                 (fingerprint, json.dumps(values), _now_ms()),
1405:             )
1406:             if before != values:
1407:                 self._record_capability_audit(
1408:                     fingerprint=fingerprint,
1409:                     kind="cap_policy_set",
1410:                     before=before,
1411:                     after=values,
1412:                     actor=actor,
1413:                     note=note,
1414:                 )
1415: 
1416:     def clear_peer_capability_policy(
1417:         self,
1418:         fingerprint: str,
1419:         *,
1420:         actor: Optional[str] = None,
1421:         note: Optional[str] = None,
1422:     ) -> None:
1423:         with self._write_lock:
1424:             before = self.get_peer_capability_policy(fingerprint)
1425:             self._conn.execute(
1426:                 "DELETE FROM peer_capability_policy WHERE fingerprint = ?",
1427:                 (fingerprint,),
1428:             )
1429:             if before is not None:
1430:                 self._record_capability_audit(
1431:                     fingerprint=fingerprint,
1432:                     kind="cap_policy_clear",
1433:                     before=before,
1434:                     after=None,
1435:                     actor=actor,
1436:                     note=note,
1437:                 )
1438: 
1439:     def get_peer_capability_policy(self, fingerprint: str) -> Optional[list[str]]:
1440:         row = self._conn.execute(
1441:             "SELECT allowed_json FROM peer_capability_policy WHERE fingerprint = ?",
1442:             (fingerprint,),
1443:         ).fetchone()
1444:         if not row:
1445:             return None
1446:         try:
1447:             return list(json.loads(row["allowed_json"]))
1448:         except Exception:
1449:             return []
1450: 
1451:     # ─── capability / trust audit log (H1) ────────────────────────────
1452:     def _record_capability_audit(
1453:         self,
1454:         *,
1455:         fingerprint: str,
1456:         kind: str,
1457:         before: Any,
1458:         after: Any,
1459:         actor: Optional[str] = None,
1460:         note: Optional[str] = None,
1461:     ) -> None:
1462:         # Caller already holds _write_lock.
1463:         self._conn.execute(
1464:             """
1465:             INSERT INTO capability_audit(
1466:                 ts_ms, fingerprint, kind, before_json, after_json, actor, note
1467:             ) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1468:             """,
1469:             (
1470:                 _now_ms(),
1471:                 fingerprint,
1472:                 kind,
1473:                 None if before is None else json.dumps(before),
1474:                 None if after is None else json.dumps(after),
1475:                 actor,
1476:                 note,
1477:             ),
1478:         )
1479: 
1480:     def recent_capability_audit(
1481:         self,
1482:         *,
1483:         fingerprint: Optional[str] = None,
1484:         limit: int = 200,
1485:     ) -> list[dict]:
1486:         sql = (
1487:             "SELECT id, ts_ms, fingerprint, kind, before_json, after_json,"
1488:             " actor, note FROM capability_audit"
1489:         )
1490:         params: list[Any] = []
1491:         if fingerprint is not None:
1492:             sql += " WHERE fingerprint = ?"
1493:             params.append(fingerprint)
1494:         sql += " ORDER BY ts_ms DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?"
1495:         params.append(int(limit))
1496:         rows = self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall()
1497:         out: list[dict] = []
1498:         for r in rows:
1499:             def _parse(s: Optional[str]) -> Any:
1500:                 if s is None:
1501:                     return None
1502:                 try:
1503:                     return json.loads(s)
1504:                 except Exception:
1505:                     return s
1506:             out.append({
1507:                 "id": r["id"],
1508:                 "ts_ms": r["ts_ms"],
1509:                 "fingerprint": r["fingerprint"],
1510:                 "kind": r["kind"],
1511:                 "before": _parse(r["before_json"]),
1512:                 "after": _parse(r["after_json"]),
1513:                 "actor": r["actor"],
1514:                 "note": r["note"],
1515:             })
1516:         return out
1517: 
1518:     def activity_feed(
1519:         self,
1520:         *,
1521:         since_ms: Optional[int] = None,
1522:         kinds: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
1523:         peer_fp: Optional[str] = None,
1524:         limit: int = 200,
1525:     ) -> list[dict]:
1526:         """v0.9.1: cross-peer activity feed merging:
1527:           - capability_audit (verify_set, verify_clear, trust_set,
1528:             cap_policy_set, cap_policy_clear)
1529:           - key_change_events (in + out)
1530:           - transfers (file_send / file_recv complete + failed)
1531:           - manifest_conflicts (detected + resolved)
1532:           - peer first_seen synthetic events
1533: 
1534:         Returns newest-first rows, each shaped:
1535:           {ts_ms, kind, severity, label, detail, peer_fp,
1536:            peer_display_name, source}.
1537: 
1538:         Filters:
1539:           - since_ms: drop rows with ts_ms < since_ms
1540:           - kinds: keep only rows whose top-level kind matches
1541:             (one of: trust, key_change, transfer, conflict, peer)
1542:           - peer_fp: keep only rows attributable to this peer
1543:           - limit: cap final list (default 200, hard max 2000)"""
1544:         limit = max(1, min(int(limit), 2000))
1545:         kinds_set = set(kinds) if kinds else None
1546:         cutoff_raw = self.get_setting("activity_cleared_before_ms")
1547:         if cutoff_raw:
1548:             with contextlib.suppress(ValueError, TypeError):
1549:                 cutoff_ms = int(cutoff_raw)
1550:                 since_ms = max(int(since_ms or 0), cutoff_ms)
1551: 
1552:         events: list[dict] = []
1553:         peer_cache: dict[str, str] = {}
1554: 
1555:         def _peer_label(fp: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
1556:             if not fp:
1557:                 return None
1558:             if fp in peer_cache:
1559:                 return peer_cache[fp]
1560:             rec = self.get_peer(fp)
1561:             label = rec.display_name if rec else fp[:8]
1562:             peer_cache[fp] = label
1563:             return label
1564: 
1565:         # 1. capability_audit → trust kind
1566:         if kinds_set is None or "trust" in kinds_set:
1567:             sql = (
1568:                 "SELECT id, ts_ms, fingerprint, kind, before_json,"
1569:                 " after_json, actor, note FROM capability_audit"
1570:             )
1571:             params: list[Any] = []
1572:             wclauses: list[str] = []
1573:             if since_ms is not None:
1574:                 wclauses.append("ts_ms >= ?"); params.append(int(since_ms))
1575:             if peer_fp is not None:
1576:                 wclauses.append("fingerprint = ?"); params.append(peer_fp)
1577:             if wclauses:
1578:                 sql += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(wclauses)
1579:             sql += " ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
1580:             params.append(limit)
1581:             for r in self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall():
1582:                 k = r["kind"]
1583:                 if k == "verify_set":
1584:                     label, sev = "Verified in person", "good"
1585:                 elif k == "verify_clear":
1586:                     label, sev = "Verification revoked", "warn"
1587:                 elif k == "trust_set":
1588:                     after = json.loads(r["after_json"] or "null")
1589:                     label = f"Trust → {after}"
1590:                     sev = "info" if after == "pinned" else (
1591:                         "bad" if after == "rejected" else "warn"
1592:                     )
1593:                 elif k == "cap_policy_set":
1594:                     label, sev = "Permissions changed", "info"
1595:                 elif k == "cap_policy_clear":
1596:                     label, sev = "Permissions cleared (allow all)", "info"
1597:                 else:
1598:                     label, sev = k.replace("_", " ").title(), "info"
1599:                 events.append({
1600:                     "ts_ms": r["ts_ms"],
1601:                     "kind": "trust",
1602:                     "subkind": k,
1603:                     "severity": sev,
1604:                     "label": label,
1605:                     "detail": r["note"] or "",
1606:                     "peer_fp": r["fingerprint"],
1607:                     "peer_display_name": _peer_label(r["fingerprint"]),
1608:                     "source": "capability_audit",
1609:                 })
1610: 
1611:         # 2. key_change_events → key_change kind
1612:         if kinds_set is None or "key_change" in kinds_set:
1613:             sql = (
1614:                 "SELECT id, ts_ms, hostname, old_fingerprint,"
1615:                 " new_fingerprint, severity, acked_ms"
1616:                 " FROM key_change_events"
1617:             )
1618:             wclauses = []
1619:             params = []
1620:             if since_ms is not None:
1621:                 wclauses.append("ts_ms >= ?"); params.append(int(since_ms))
1622:             if peer_fp is not None:
1623:                 wclauses.append("(new_fingerprint = ? OR old_fingerprint = ?)")
1624:                 params.extend([peer_fp, peer_fp])
1625:             if wclauses:
1626:                 sql += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(wclauses)
1627:             sql += " ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
1628:             params.append(limit)
1629:             for r in self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall():
1630:                 sev = r["severity"] or "low"
1631:                 evsev = "bad" if sev == "high" else (
1632:                     "warn" if sev == "medium" else "info"
1633:                 )
1634:                 events.append({
1635:                     "ts_ms": r["ts_ms"],
1636:                     "kind": "key_change",
1637:                     "subkind": "detected",
1638:                     "severity": evsev,
1639:                     "label": f"Key change · {r['hostname']}",
1640:                     "detail": (
1641:                         f"old {r['old_fingerprint'][:8]}… → "
1642:                         f"new {r['new_fingerprint'][:8]}…"
1643:                         + (" (acknowledged)" if r["acked_ms"] else " (unacked)")
1644:                     ),
1645:                     "peer_fp": r["new_fingerprint"],
1646:                     "peer_display_name": _peer_label(r["new_fingerprint"]),
1647:                     "source": "key_change_events",
1648:                 })
1649: 
1650:         # 3. transfers → transfer kind. Only terminal states are
1651:         # interesting in the feed (mid-flight is the chat bubble's job).
1652:         if kinds_set is None or "transfer" in kinds_set:
1653:             sql = (
1654:                 "SELECT id, direction, peer_fp, kind AS tkind, name,"
1655:                 " size, status, updated_ms, metadata_json"
1656:                 " FROM transfers"
1657:                 " WHERE status IN ('complete', 'failed')"
1658:             )
1659:             params = []
1660:             if since_ms is not None:
1661:                 sql += " AND updated_ms >= ?"; params.append(int(since_ms))
1662:             if peer_fp is not None:
1663:                 sql += " AND peer_fp = ?"; params.append(peer_fp)
1664:             sql += " ORDER BY updated_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
1665:             params.append(limit)
1666:             for r in self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall():
1667:                 ok = (r["status"] == "complete")
1668:                 direction = r["direction"]
1669:                 verb = (
1670:                     "Received" if (ok and direction == "in") else
1671:                     "Sent" if (ok and direction == "out") else
1672:                     ("Receive failed" if direction == "in" else "Send failed")
1673:                 )
1674:                 label = f"{verb}: {r['name'] or '?'}"
1675:                 detail_parts = [r["tkind"] or "file"]
1676:                 if r["size"] is not None:
1677:                     bsz = r["size"]
1678:                     # Inline size formatting (KB/MB/GB) — same logic
1679:                     # as fmtBytes on the client.
1680:                     units = ["B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"]
1681:                     j = 0
1682:                     while bsz >= 1024 and j < len(units) - 1:
1683:                         bsz /= 1024
1684:                         j += 1
1685:                     fmt = f"{bsz:.1f} {units[j]}" if j > 0 and bsz < 10 else f"{int(bsz)} {units[j]}"
1686:                     detail_parts.append(fmt)
1687:                 events.append({
1688:                     "ts_ms": r["updated_ms"],
1689:                     "kind": "transfer",
1690:                     "subkind": "complete" if ok else "failed",
1691:                     "severity": "good" if ok else "bad",
1692:                     "label": label,
1693:                     "detail": " · ".join(detail_parts),
1694:                     "peer_fp": r["peer_fp"],
1695:                     "peer_display_name": _peer_label(r["peer_fp"]),
1696:                     "source": "transfers",
1697:                 })
1698: 
1699:         # 4. manifest_conflicts → conflict kind
1700:         if kinds_set is None or "self_mesh" in kinds_set:
1701:             sql = "SELECT * FROM self_mesh_audit"
1702:             wclauses = []
1703:             params = []
1704:             if since_ms is not None:
1705:                 wclauses.append("ts_ms >= ?"); params.append(int(since_ms))
1706:             if peer_fp is not None:
1707:                 wclauses.append("peer_fp = ?"); params.append(peer_fp)
1708:             if wclauses:
1709:                 sql += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(wclauses)
1710:             sql += " ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
1711:             params.append(limit)
1712:             for r in self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall():
1713:                 ev = r["event"]
1714:                 action = r["action"] or ""
1715:                 detail = r["detail"] or action.replace("_", " ")
1716:                 events.append({
1717:                     "ts_ms": r["ts_ms"],
1718:                     "kind": "self_mesh",
1719:                     "subkind": ev,
1720:                     "severity": r["severity"] or "info",
1721:                     "label": f"My devices · {ev.replace('_', ' ')}",
1722:                     "detail": detail,
1723:                     "peer_fp": r["peer_fp"],
1724:                     "peer_display_name": _peer_label(r["peer_fp"]),
1725:                     "source": "self_mesh_audit",
1726:                 })
1727: 
1728:         if kinds_set is None or "conflict" in kinds_set:
1729:             sql = (
1730:                 "SELECT id, folder_name, file_path, peer_fp,"
1731:                 " detected_ms, resolved_ms, resolution"
1732:                 " FROM manifest_conflicts"
1733:             )
1734:             wclauses = []
1735:             params = []
1736:             if since_ms is not None:
1737:                 wclauses.append("detected_ms >= ?"); params.append(int(since_ms))
1738:             if peer_fp is not None:
1739:                 wclauses.append("peer_fp = ?"); params.append(peer_fp)
1740:             if wclauses:
1741:                 sql += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(wclauses)
1742:             sql += " ORDER BY detected_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
1743:             params.append(limit)
1744:             for r in self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall():
1745:                 events.append({
1746:                     "ts_ms": r["detected_ms"],
1747:                     "kind": "conflict",
1748:                     "subkind": "resolved" if r["resolved_ms"] else "detected",
1749:                     "severity": "warn" if not r["resolved_ms"] else "info",
1750:                     "label": (
1751:                         f"Folder conflict ({r['resolution']})" if r["resolved_ms"]
1752:                         else "Folder conflict detected"
1753:                     ),
1754:                     "detail": f"{r['folder_name']}/{r['file_path']}",
1755:                     "peer_fp": r["peer_fp"],
1756:                     "peer_display_name": _peer_label(r["peer_fp"]),
1757:                     "source": "manifest_conflicts",
1758:                 })
1759: 
1760:         # 5. peer first_seen synthetic events
1761:         if kinds_set is None or "peer" in kinds_set:
1762:             sql = "SELECT fingerprint, hostname, first_seen_ms FROM peers"
1763:             wclauses = []
1764:             params = []
1765:             if since_ms is not None:
1766:                 wclauses.append("first_seen_ms >= ?"); params.append(int(since_ms))
1767:             if peer_fp is not None:
1768:                 wclauses.append("fingerprint = ?"); params.append(peer_fp)
1769:             if wclauses:
1770:                 sql += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(wclauses)
1771:             sql += " ORDER BY first_seen_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
1772:             params.append(limit)
1773:             for r in self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall():
1774:                 events.append({
1775:                     "ts_ms": r["first_seen_ms"],
1776:                     "kind": "peer",
1777:                     "subkind": "first_seen",
1778:                     "severity": "info",
1779:                     "label": f"Device first seen · {r['hostname'] or r['fingerprint'][:8]}",
1780:                     "detail": "",
1781:                     "peer_fp": r["fingerprint"],
1782:                     "peer_display_name": _peer_label(r["fingerprint"]),
1783:                     "source": "peers",
1784:                 })
1785: 
1786:         events.sort(key=lambda e: e["ts_ms"], reverse=True)
1787:         return events[:limit]
1788: 
1789:     def peer_trust_history(
1790:         self,
1791:         fingerprint: str,
1792:         *,
1793:         limit: int = 200,
1794:     ) -> list[dict]:
1795:         """v0.8.6: merged chronological trust history for one peer.
1796: 
1797:         Combines four sources into a single timeline (newest first):
1798:           - peers row's first_seen_ms (synthetic 'first_seen' event)
1799:           - capability_audit rows (verify_set, verify_clear, trust_set,
1800:             cap_policy_set, cap_policy_clear)
1801:           - key_change_events where this fingerprint is the new_fp
1802:             OR the old_fp (rotation events affect both ends)
1803:           - hostname_keys first_seen for any pubkey ever attached to
1804:             the peer's hostname (synthetic 'pubkey_first_seen' event)
1805: 
1806:         Each entry is a uniform dict with keys: ts_ms, kind, label,
1807:         detail, severity, source. The UI just renders the list — no
1808:         further classification needed."""
1809:         peer = self.get_peer(fingerprint)
1810:         if peer is None:
1811:             return []
1812:         events: list[dict] = []
1813: 
1814:         # 1. First-seen synthetic event from the peers row.
1815:         events.append({
1816:             "ts_ms": peer.first_seen_ms,
1817:             "kind": "first_seen",
1818:             "label": "Device first seen",
1819:             "detail": f"hostname: {peer.hostname or '(unknown)'}",
1820:             "severity": "info",
1821:             "source": "peers",
1822:         })
1823: 
1824:         # 2. capability_audit: rich. Translate each kind to a human label.
1825:         audit = self.recent_capability_audit(
1826:             fingerprint=fingerprint, limit=limit,
1827:         )
1828:         for row in audit:
1829:             kind = row["kind"]
1830:             if kind == "verify_set":
1831:                 method = (row["after"] or {}).get("verified_method") if isinstance(row["after"], dict) else None
1832:                 events.append({
1833:                     "ts_ms": row["ts_ms"],
1834:                     "kind": kind,
1835:                     "label": "Verified in person",
1836:                     "detail": (
1837:                         f"method: {method}" + (f" · note: {row['note']}" if row["note"] else "")
1838:                         if method else (row["note"] or "")
1839:                     ),
1840:                     "severity": "good",
1841:                     "source": "capability_audit",
1842:                 })
1843:             elif kind == "verify_clear":
1844:                 events.append({
1845:                     "ts_ms": row["ts_ms"],
1846:                     "kind": kind,
1847:                     "label": "Verification revoked",
1848:                     "detail": row["note"] or "",
1849:                     "severity": "warn",
1850:                     "source": "capability_audit",
1851:                 })
1852:             elif kind == "trust_set":
1853:                 before = row["before"]
1854:                 after = row["after"]
1855:                 events.append({
1856:                     "ts_ms": row["ts_ms"],
1857:                     "kind": kind,
1858:                     "label": f"Trust changed: {before or '?'} → {after or '?'}",
1859:                     "detail": row["note"] or "",
1860:                     "severity": "info" if after == "pinned" else (
1861:                         "bad" if after == "rejected" else "warn"
1862:                     ),
1863:                     "source": "capability_audit",
1864:                 })
1865:             elif kind in ("cap_policy_set", "cap_policy_clear"):
1866:                 before = row["before"]
1867:                 after = row["after"]
1868:                 if kind == "cap_policy_clear":
1869:                     label = "Permissions cleared (allow all)"
1870:                     detail = ""
1871:                 else:
1872:                     after_list = after if isinstance(after, list) else []
1873:                     detail = (
1874:                         f"now allow: {', '.join(after_list) or '(none)'}"
1875:                     )
1876:                     label = "Permissions changed"
1877:                 events.append({
1878:                     "ts_ms": row["ts_ms"],
1879:                     "kind": kind,
1880:                     "label": label,
1881:                     "detail": detail + ((" · " + row["note"]) if row["note"] else ""),
1882:                     "severity": "info",
1883:                     "source": "capability_audit",
1884:                 })
1885:             else:
1886:                 events.append({
1887:                     "ts_ms": row["ts_ms"],
1888:                     "kind": kind,
1889:                     "label": kind.replace("_", " ").title(),
1890:                     "detail": row["note"] or "",
1891:                     "severity": "info",
1892:                     "source": "capability_audit",
1893:                 })
1894: 
1895:         # 3. key_change_events: include any event where this peer is
1896:         # either the rotated-out fingerprint (old_fp) or rotated-in
1897:         # fingerprint (new_fp). Both contexts are useful: "this device
1898:         # used to be X, now it's Y" and "this device replaces Z".
1899:         kce_in = self.list_key_change_events(
1900:             new_fingerprint=fingerprint, limit=limit,
1901:         )
1902:         for ev in kce_in:
1903:             sev = ev["severity"]
1904:             events.append({
1905:                 "ts_ms": ev["ts_ms"],
1906:                 "kind": "key_change_in",
1907:                 "label": "Key change detected (this device replaces a prior one)",
1908:                 "detail": (
1909:                     f"prior fp: {ev['old_fingerprint'][:8]}… · severity: {sev}"
1910:                     + (" · acknowledged" if ev["acked_ms"] else " · UNACKNOWLEDGED")
1911:                 ),
1912:                 "severity": "bad" if sev == "high" else (
1913:                     "warn" if sev == "medium" else "info"
1914:                 ),
1915:                 "source": "key_change_events",
1916:             })
1917:         # rotated-out (this peer's fingerprint shows up as old_fp).
1918:         # No filter helper for old_fp; do a direct query.
1919:         old_rows = self._conn.execute(
1920:             "SELECT id, ts_ms, hostname, old_fingerprint, new_fingerprint,"
1921:             " severity, acked_ms FROM key_change_events"
1922:             " WHERE old_fingerprint = ? ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT ?",
1923:             (fingerprint, int(limit)),
1924:         ).fetchall()
1925:         for r in old_rows:
1926:             events.append({
1927:                 "ts_ms": r["ts_ms"],
1928:                 "kind": "key_change_out",
1929:                 "label": "This device was rotated out",
1930:                 "detail": (
1931:                     f"replaced by: {r['new_fingerprint'][:8]}…"
1932:                     + (" · acknowledged" if r["acked_ms"] else " · UNACKNOWLEDGED")
1933:                 ),
1934:                 "severity": "bad" if r["severity"] == "high" else (
1935:                     "warn" if r["severity"] == "medium" else "info"
1936:                 ),
1937:                 "source": "key_change_events",
1938:             })
1939: 
1940:         # Sort newest-first, cap to `limit`.
1941:         events.sort(key=lambda e: e["ts_ms"], reverse=True)
1942:         return events[:limit]
1943: 
1944:     # ─── key-change tracking (v0.7.8) ─────────────────────────────────
1945: 
1946:     def _record_hostname_key_seen_locked(
1947:         self,
1948:         *,
1949:         c: sqlite3.Cursor,
1950:         hostname: str,
1951:         ed_pub_hex: str,
1952:         fingerprint: str,
1953:         now: int,
1954:     ) -> Optional[int]:
1955:         """Internal: insert/update the hostname_keys row for this
1956:         observation, AND if the hostname has previously been seen with
1957:         a DIFFERENT pubkey, emit a key_change_events row.
1958: 
1959:         Severity is graded by the strongest prior trust observed:
1960:           - 'high'   ← any prior fingerprint for this hostname is pinned
1961:           - 'medium' ← any prior fingerprint exists in peers (pending)
1962:           - 'low'    ← only seen via discovery, never persisted in peers
1963:         Caller must hold self._write_lock and pass an open cursor.
1964:         Detection runs AFTER the upsert_peer INSERT so the new (hostname,
1965:         pubkey) pair sees its own peers row — we filter it out via the
1966:         `fingerprint != ?` clause below.
1967: 
1968:         Returns the integer id of the freshly-inserted key_change_events
1969:         row (so the caller can broadcast it in real time), or None if
1970:         no new conflict was logged."""
1971:         # 1. Find any conflicting prior observation.
1972:         prior_rows = c.execute(
1973:             "SELECT ed_pub_hex, fingerprint FROM hostname_keys"
1974:             " WHERE hostname = ? AND ed_pub_hex != ?"
1975:             " ORDER BY last_seen_ms DESC",
1976:             (hostname, ed_pub_hex),
1977:         ).fetchall()
1978:         # 2. Upsert the current (hostname, ed_pub_hex) row.
1979:         c.execute(
1980:             """
1981:             INSERT INTO hostname_keys(
1982:                 hostname, ed_pub_hex, fingerprint,
1983:                 first_seen_ms, last_seen_ms
1984:             ) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1985:             ON CONFLICT(hostname, ed_pub_hex) DO UPDATE SET
1986:                 last_seen_ms = excluded.last_seen_ms,
1987:                 fingerprint  = excluded.fingerprint
1988:             """,
1989:             (hostname, ed_pub_hex, fingerprint, now, now),
1990:         )
1991:         # 3. If we found a conflict AND haven't already logged this
1992:         # exact (old_fp, new_fp) pair, write a key_change_events row.
1993:         if not prior_rows:
1994:             return None
1995:         new_event_id: Optional[int] = None
1996:         for old in prior_rows:
1997:             old_fp = old["fingerprint"]
1998:             old_pub_hex = old["ed_pub_hex"]
1999:             if old_fp == fingerprint:
2000:                 # Hostname was reattached to a row we already wrote
2001:                 # under a different ed_pub_hex column — defensive guard,
2002:                 # shouldn't normally happen.
2003:                 continue
2004:             # Idempotency: have we already logged THIS specific
2005:             # (old_fp → new_fp) transition? If so, just bump nothing —
2006:             # the existing row stays, acked or not.
2007:             already = c.execute(
2008:                 "SELECT 1 FROM key_change_events"
2009:                 " WHERE hostname = ? AND old_fingerprint = ?"
2010:                 " AND new_fingerprint = ? LIMIT 1",
2011:                 (hostname, old_fp, fingerprint),
2012:             ).fetchone()
2013:             if already:
2014:                 continue
2015:             # Severity grading via prior peers row's trust state.
2016:             old_peer = c.execute(
2017:                 "SELECT trust FROM peers WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2018:                 (old_fp,),
2019:             ).fetchone()
2020:             if old_peer is not None and old_peer["trust"] == "pinned":
2021:                 severity = "high"
2022:             elif old_peer is not None:
2023:                 severity = "medium"
2024:             else:
2025:                 severity = "low"
2026:             cur = c.execute(
2027:                 """
2028:                 INSERT INTO key_change_events(
2029:                     ts_ms, hostname,
2030:                     old_fingerprint, new_fingerprint,
2031:                     old_pub_hex, new_pub_hex,
2032:                     severity, acked_ms
2033:                 ) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)
2034:                 """,
2035:                 (
2036:                     now, hostname,
2037:                     old_fp, fingerprint,
2038:                     old_pub_hex, ed_pub_hex,
2039:                     severity,
2040:                 ),
2041:             )
2042:             # First conflict (most-recent prior, if multiple) wins as
2043:             # the broadcast id. Subsequent prior_rows iterations will
2044:             # only fire when the hostname has rotated keys 3+ times,
2045:             # which is rare; keeping the freshest is the practical UX.
2046:             if new_event_id is None and cur.lastrowid is not None:
2047:                 new_event_id = int(cur.lastrowid)
2048:         return new_event_id
2049:

2071:     def list_key_change_events(
2072:         self,
2073:         *,
2074:         unacked_only: bool = False,
2075:         new_fingerprint: Optional[str] = None,
2076:         limit: int = 200,
2077:     ) -> list[dict]:
2078:         """Return key-change events, freshest first. UI surfaces use
2079:         `unacked_only=True` to drive the red banner; the device drawer
2080:         passes `new_fingerprint=fp` to list events targeting that
2081:         specific peer."""
2082:         sql = (
2083:             "SELECT id, ts_ms, hostname, old_fingerprint, new_fingerprint,"
2084:             " old_pub_hex, new_pub_hex, severity, acked_ms"
2085:             " FROM key_change_events"
2086:         )
2087:         clauses: list[str] = []
2088:         params: list[Any] = []

2090:             clauses.append("acked_ms IS NULL")

2095:             sql += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses)
2096:         sql += " ORDER BY ts_ms DESC, id DESC LIMIT ?"
2097:         params.append(int(limit))
2098:         rows = self._conn.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall()
2099:         return [
2100:             {
2101:                 "id": r["id"],
2102:                 "ts_ms": r["ts_ms"],
2103:                 "hostname": r["hostname"],
2104:                 "old_fingerprint": r["old_fingerprint"],
2105:                 "new_fingerprint": r["new_fingerprint"],

2107:                 "new_pub_hex": r["new_pub_hex"],
2108:                 "severity": r["severity"],
2109:                 "acked_ms": r["acked_ms"],
2110:             }
2111:             for r in rows
2112:         ]

2114:     def ack_key_change_event(self, event_id: int) -> bool:
2115:         """Mark a key-change event acknowledged. Returns True if a
2116:         previously-unacked row was just acked, False if the row didn't
2117:         exist OR was already acked."""
2118:         with self._write_lock:
2119:             cur = self._conn.execute(
2120:                 "UPDATE key_change_events SET acked_ms = ?"
2121:                 " WHERE id = ? AND acked_ms IS NULL",

2123:             )
2124:             return cur.rowcount > 0

2225:     # Sender chains.
2226:     def upsert_sender_chain(
2227:         self,
2228:         *,
2229:         group_id: bytes,
2230:         sender_pub: bytes,
2231:         direction: str,
2232:         epoch: int,
2233:         chain_key: bytes,
2234:         counter: int,
2235:     ) -> None:
2236:         if direction not in ("in", "out"):
2237:             raise ValueError(f"direction must be 'in' or 'out', got {direction!r}")
2238:         if len(chain_key) != 32:
2239:             raise ValueError("chain_key must be 32 bytes")
2240:         if len(sender_pub) != 32:
2241:             raise ValueError("sender_pub must be 32 bytes")
2242:         if len(group_id) != 16:
2243:             raise ValueError("group_id must be 16 bytes")
2244:         # v0.20.7 (security audit H21): wrap the chain_key at rest if
2245:         # the daemon was started with ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE. Reads
2246:         # detect the wrap marker and decrypt transparently; a stolen-
2247:         # disk attacker without the passphrase sees AEAD ciphertext.
2248:         # When no lockbox is configured this is a no-op passthrough
2249:         # (cleartext on disk — same as before this fix).
2250:         from one_link.lockbox import maybe_wrap as _lb_wrap
2251:         chain_key_at_rest = _lb_wrap(chain_key, self._lockbox)
2252:         with self._write_lock:
2253:             self._conn.execute(
2254:                 """
2255:                 INSERT INTO group_sender_chains(
2256:                     group_id, sender_pub, direction, epoch,
2257:                     chain_key, counter, updated_ms
2258:                 )
2259:                 VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
2260:                 ON CONFLICT(group_id, sender_pub, direction, epoch)
2261:                 DO UPDATE SET
2262:                     chain_key = excluded.chain_key,
2263:                     counter = excluded.counter,
2264:                     updated_ms = excluded.updated_ms
2265:                 """,
2266:                 (group_id, sender_pub, direction, int(epoch),
2267:                  chain_key_at_rest, int(counter), _now_ms()),
2268:             )
2269: 
2270:     def get_sender_chain(
2271:         self,
2272:         *,
2273:         group_id: bytes,
2274:         sender_pub: bytes,
2275:         direction: str,
2276:         epoch: Optional[int] = None,
2277:     ) -> Optional[dict]:
2278:         """Get the latest chain for (group, sender, direction). If
2279:         `epoch` is given, returns that exact epoch; otherwise the
2280:         highest known epoch."""
2281:         if epoch is not None:
2282:             row = self._conn.execute(
2283:                 "SELECT epoch, chain_key, counter FROM group_sender_chains "
2284:                 "WHERE group_id = ? AND sender_pub = ? AND direction = ? AND epoch = ?",
2285:                 (group_id, sender_pub, direction, int(epoch)),
2286:             ).fetchone()
2287:         else:
2288:             row = self._conn.execute(
2289:                 "SELECT epoch, chain_key, counter FROM group_sender_chains "
2290:                 "WHERE group_id = ? AND sender_pub = ? AND direction = ? "
2291:                 "ORDER BY epoch DESC LIMIT 1",
2292:                 (group_id, sender_pub, direction),
2293:             ).fetchone()
2294:         if not row:
2295:             return None
2296:         # v0.20.7 (security audit H21): unwrap if the stored value
2297:         # is lockbox-wrapped. Use length-based disambiguation: a
2298:         # cleartext chain_key is exactly 32 bytes (validated at
2299:         # write time), and a lockbox-wrapped one is 61 bytes
2300:         # (marker + nonce + ct + tag). This avoids the 1/256 false
2301:         # positive that a generic is_wrapped check would have on
2302:         # the small-marker-byte collision class.
2303:         chain_key = bytes(row["chain_key"])
2304:         if len(chain_key) != 32:
2305:             from one_link.lockbox import LockBox  # noqa: F401
2306:             if self._lockbox is None:
2307:                 raise RuntimeError(
2308:                     "found a non-cleartext chain_key but no lockbox is "
2309:                     "configured (was ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE removed?)"
2310:                 )
2311:             chain_key = self._lockbox.unwrap(chain_key)
2312:         return {
2313:             "epoch": row["epoch"],
2314:             "chain_key": chain_key,
2315:             "counter": row["counter"],
2316:         }
2317:

2399:     def edit_group_message(
2400:         self, *, id: str, new_body: str, edited_at_ms: int,
2401:     ) -> Optional[dict]:
2402:         cur = self.get_group_message(id)
2403:         if cur is None or cur.get("deleted_at_ms"):
2404:             return None
2405:         original = cur.get("original_body") or cur.get("body")
2406:         with self._write_lock:
2407:             self._conn.execute(
2408:                 "UPDATE group_messages SET body = ?, edited_at_ms = ?, "
2409:                 "original_body = COALESCE(original_body, ?) "
2410:                 "WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL",
2411:                 (new_body, int(edited_at_ms), original, id),
2412:             )
2413:         return self.get_group_message(id)
2414: 
2415:     def delete_group_message(
2416:         self, *, id: str, deleted_at_ms: int,
2417:     ) -> Optional[dict]:
2418:         cur = self.get_group_message(id)
2419:         if cur is None:
2420:             return None
2421:         if cur.get("deleted_at_ms"):
2422:             return cur
2423:         with self._write_lock:
2424:             self._conn.execute(
2425:                 "UPDATE group_messages SET body = NULL, deleted_at_ms = ? "
2426:                 "WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL",
2427:                 (int(deleted_at_ms), id),
2428:             )
2429:         return self.get_group_message(id)

2469:     def set_peer_profile(
2470:         self,
2471:         fingerprint: str,
2472:         *,
2473:         local_alias: Optional[str] = ...,  # type: ignore[assignment]
2474:         muted: Optional[bool] = ...,       # type: ignore[assignment]
2475:     ) -> Optional[PeerRecord]:
2476:         """v0.7.3: update per-device profile fields. Pass `Ellipsis`
2477:         (the default) to leave a field unchanged; pass None to
2478:         explicitly clear the alias. Returns the refreshed record."""
2479:         sets: list[str] = []
2480:         params: list[Any] = []
2481:         if local_alias is not Ellipsis:
2482:             v = local_alias
2483:             if v is not None:
2484:                 v = str(v).strip() or None
2485:             sets.append("local_alias = ?")
2486:             params.append(v)
2487:         if muted is not Ellipsis:
2488:             sets.append("muted = ?")
2489:             params.append(1 if muted else 0)
2490:         if not sets:
2491:             return self.get_peer(fingerprint)
2492:         params.append(fingerprint)
2493:         with self._write_lock:
2494:             self._conn.execute(
2495:                 f"UPDATE peers SET {', '.join(sets)} WHERE fingerprint = ?",  # nosec B608
2496:                 params,
2497:             )
2498:         return self.get_peer(fingerprint)

2500:     # ─── verification (v0.7.7) ────────────────────────────────────────

2502:     _ALLOWED_VERIFY_METHODS = ("sas-digits", "sas-qr", "sas-audio", "manual")
2503: 
2504:     def set_peer_verified(
2505:         self,
2506:         fingerprint: str,
2507:         *,
2508:         method: str,
2509:         note: Optional[str] = None,
2510:         actor: Optional[str] = None,
2511:     ) -> Optional[PeerRecord]:
2512:         """v0.7.7: mark a peer as verified-in-person via a side-channel
2513:         SAS confirm. `method` records HOW the user verified (digits
2514:         read aloud, QR scan, audio readback, manual override).
2515:         Records a capability_audit row so the trust transition is
2516:         forensically auditable. Returns the refreshed PeerRecord, or
2517:         None if the peer doesn't exist."""
2518:         if method not in self._ALLOWED_VERIFY_METHODS:
2519:             raise ValueError(
2520:                 f"verify method must be one of "
2521:                 f"{self._ALLOWED_VERIFY_METHODS!r}, got {method!r}"
2522:             )
2523:         clean_note: Optional[str] = None
2524:         if note is not None:
2525:             clean_note = str(note).strip() or None
2526:             if clean_note and len(clean_note) > 280:
2527:                 # Same upper bound as a tweet — long enough for a
2528:                 # location/context reminder, short enough to render
2529:                 # in the device drawer without truncation games.
2530:                 raise ValueError("verify note too long (max 280 chars)")
2531:         now = _now_ms()
2532:         with self._write_lock:
2533:             row = self._conn.execute(
2534:                 "SELECT verified_at_ms, verified_method FROM peers"
2535:                 " WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2536:                 (fingerprint,),
2537:             ).fetchone()
2538:             if row is None:
2539:                 return None
2540:             before = {
2541:                 "verified_at_ms": row["verified_at_ms"],
2542:                 "verified_method": row["verified_method"],
2543:             }
2544:             self._conn.execute(
2545:                 "UPDATE peers SET verified_at_ms = ?, verified_method = ?,"
2546:                 " verified_note = ? WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2547:                 (now, method, clean_note, fingerprint),
2548:             )
2549:             after = {
2550:                 "verified_at_ms": now,
2551:                 "verified_method": method,
2552:                 "verified_note": clean_note,
2553:             }
2554:             if before != {
2555:                 "verified_at_ms": after["verified_at_ms"],
2556:                 "verified_method": after["verified_method"],
2557:             } or row["verified_at_ms"] is None:
2558:                 self._record_capability_audit(
2559:                     fingerprint=fingerprint,
2560:                     kind="verify_set",
2561:                     before=before,
2562:                     after=after,
2563:                     actor=actor,
2564:                     note=clean_note,
2565:                 )
2566:         return self.get_peer(fingerprint)
2567: 
2568:     def clear_peer_verified(
2569:         self,
2570:         fingerprint: str,
2571:         *,
2572:         actor: Optional[str] = None,
2573:         note: Optional[str] = None,
2574:     ) -> Optional[PeerRecord]:
2575:         """v0.7.7: revoke a verified-in-person mark (e.g. user no
2576:         longer trusts the side channel, key changed, device changed
2577:         hands). Audit log captures the before-state so the timeline
2578:         survives the clear."""
2579:         with self._write_lock:
2580:             row = self._conn.execute(
2581:                 "SELECT verified_at_ms, verified_method, verified_note"
2582:                 " FROM peers WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2583:                 (fingerprint,),
2584:             ).fetchone()
2585:             if row is None:
2586:                 return None
2587:             before = {
2588:                 "verified_at_ms": row["verified_at_ms"],
2589:                 "verified_method": row["verified_method"],
2590:                 "verified_note": row["verified_note"],
2591:             }
2592:             if row["verified_at_ms"] is None:
2593:                 # Idempotent no-op — nothing to clear, no audit row.
2594:                 return self.get_peer(fingerprint)
2595:             self._conn.execute(
2596:                 "UPDATE peers SET verified_at_ms = NULL,"
2597:                 " verified_method = NULL, verified_note = NULL"
2598:                 " WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2599:                 (fingerprint,),
2600:             )
2601:             self._record_capability_audit(
2602:                 fingerprint=fingerprint,
2603:                 kind="verify_clear",
2604:                 before=before,
2605:                 after=None,
2606:                 actor=actor,
2607:                 note=note,
2608:             )
2609:         return self.get_peer(fingerprint)

2642:     # ─── disappearing messages (v0.10.2) ──────────────────────────────
2643: 
2644:     # Friendly TTL labels — UI presents these; values are the ms.
2645:     PEER_DM_TTL_PRESETS = {
2646:         None: "Off",
2647:         5 * 60 * 1000: "5 minutes",
2648:         30 * 60 * 1000: "30 minutes",
2649:         60 * 60 * 1000: "1 hour",
2650:         24 * 60 * 60 * 1000: "1 day",
2651:         7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000: "1 week",
2652:     }
2653: 
2654:     def set_peer_dm_ttl(
2655:         self,
2656:         fingerprint: str,
2657:         ttl_ms: Optional[int],
2658:     ) -> Optional[PeerRecord]:
2659:         """v0.10.2: set the per-peer disappearing-message TTL. Pass
2660:         None to clear (messages will no longer expire). Returns the
2661:         refreshed PeerRecord, or None if the peer doesn't exist."""
2662:         if ttl_ms is not None:
2663:             if not isinstance(ttl_ms, int) or ttl_ms <= 0:
2664:                 raise ValueError("ttl_ms must be a positive integer")
2665:             # Sanity cap: 30 days. Anything longer is "off" effectively;
2666:             # we don't persist it because the UI's preset list doesn't
2667:             # cover values that long.
2668:             if ttl_ms > 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000:
2669:                 raise ValueError("ttl_ms too large (max 30 days)")
2670:         with self._write_lock:
2671:             row = self._conn.execute(
2672:                 "SELECT 1 FROM peers WHERE fingerprint = ?", (fingerprint,),
2673:             ).fetchone()
2674:             if row is None:
2675:                 return None
2676:             self._conn.execute(
2677:                 "UPDATE peers SET dm_ttl_ms = ? WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2678:                 (ttl_ms, fingerprint),
2679:             )
2680:         return self.get_peer(fingerprint)
2681: 
2682:     def get_peer_dm_ttl(self, fingerprint: str) -> Optional[int]:
2683:         rec = self.get_peer(fingerprint)
2684:         return rec.dm_ttl_ms if rec else None
2685: 
2686:     def set_peer_muted_until(
2687:         self, fingerprint: str, until_ms: Optional[int],
2688:     ) -> None:
2689:         """v0.11.2: per-chat mute with duration.
2690: 
2691:         until_ms semantics:
2692:           None  → unmute (clear muted_until_ms + legacy muted=0)
2693:           0     → mute forever (muted_until_ms=0, legacy muted=1)
2694:           N > 0 → mute until wall-clock ms N
2695: 
2696:         We also keep the legacy `muted` boolean column in sync so
2697:         old read paths that haven't been ported still see a sane
2698:         derived state."""
2699:         if until_ms is not None and until_ms < 0:
2700:             raise ValueError("until_ms must be None, 0, or positive")
2701:         legacy_muted = 0 if until_ms is None else 1
2702:         with self._write_lock:
2703:             self._conn.execute(
2704:                 "UPDATE peers SET muted_until_ms = ?, muted = ? "
2705:                 "WHERE fingerprint = ?",
2706:                 (until_ms, legacy_muted, fingerprint),
2707:             )
2708: 
2709:     def get_peer_muted_until(self, fingerprint: str) -> Optional[int]:
2710:         rec = self.get_peer(fingerprint)
2711:         return rec.muted_until_ms if rec else None

2713:     def expire_due_messages(self, *, now_ms: Optional[int] = None) -> list[str]:
2714:         """v0.10.2: tombstone every message whose expires_at_ms has
2715:         passed. Returns the list of msg_ids that were just expired
2716:         so the daemon can broadcast msg_delete WS events.
2717: 
2718:         Idempotent — re-expiring a row that's already deleted is a
2719:         no-op (the AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL clause filters them out)."""
2720:         cutoff = now_ms if now_ms is not None else _now_ms()
2721:         with self._write_lock:
2722:             rows = self._conn.execute(
2723:                 "SELECT id FROM messages"
2724:                 " WHERE expires_at_ms IS NOT NULL"
2725:                 "   AND expires_at_ms <= ?"
2726:                 "   AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL",
2727:                 (cutoff,),
2728:             ).fetchall()
2729:             ids = [r["id"] for r in rows]
2730:             if not ids:
2731:                 return []
2732:             # Mark all expired in one statement.
2733:             self._conn.execute(
2734:                 "UPDATE messages SET body = NULL, deleted_at_ms = ?"
2735:                 " WHERE expires_at_ms IS NOT NULL"
2736:                 "   AND expires_at_ms <= ?"
2737:                 "   AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL",
2738:                 (cutoff, cutoff),
2739:             )
2740:         return ids

2742:     # ─── reactions (v0.7.5) ───────────────────────────────────────────
2743: 
2744:     def record_reaction(
2745:         self, *, target_msg_id: str, peer_fp: str, emoji: str,
2746:     ) -> bool:
2747:         """Add a reaction. Idempotent on (target, peer, emoji).
2748:         Returns True if a new row was inserted, False if it already
2749:         existed."""
2750:         if not target_msg_id or not peer_fp or not emoji:
2751:             raise ValueError("target_msg_id, peer_fp, emoji required")
2752:         # Bound emoji length — actual single grapheme can be up to
2753:         # ~50 bytes in Unicode, but a "reaction" with hundreds of
2754:         # combining marks is abuse.
2755:         if len(emoji) > 64:
2756:             raise ValueError("emoji too long")
2757:         with self._write_lock:
2758:             cur = self._conn.execute(
2759:                 """
2760:                 INSERT INTO message_reactions(
2761:                     target_msg_id, peer_fp, emoji, ts_ms
2762:                 ) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?)
2763:                 ON CONFLICT(target_msg_id, peer_fp, emoji) DO NOTHING
2764:                 """,
2765:                 (target_msg_id, peer_fp, emoji, _now_ms()),
2766:             )
2767:             return cur.rowcount > 0
2768: 
2769:     def remove_reaction(
2770:         self, *, target_msg_id: str, peer_fp: str, emoji: str,
2771:     ) -> bool:
2772:         with self._write_lock:
2773:             cur = self._conn.execute(
2774:                 "DELETE FROM message_reactions"
2775:                 " WHERE target_msg_id = ? AND peer_fp = ? AND emoji = ?",
2776:                 (target_msg_id, peer_fp, emoji),
2777:             )
2778:             return cur.rowcount > 0
2779: 
2780:     def list_reactions_for_messages(
2781:         self, msg_ids: Iterable[str],
2782:     ) -> dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]]:
2783:         """Return {target_msg_id: {emoji: [peer_fp, ...], ...}}.
2784:         Empty for messages with no reactions."""
2785:         ids = [str(m) for m in msg_ids if m]
2786:         if not ids:
2787:             return {}
2788:         placeholders = ",".join("?" for _ in ids)
2789:         rows = self._conn.execute(
2790:             f"SELECT target_msg_id, peer_fp, emoji FROM message_reactions"
2791:             f" WHERE target_msg_id IN ({placeholders}) ORDER BY ts_ms ASC",  # nosec B608
2792:             ids,
2793:         ).fetchall()
2794:         out: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = {}
2795:         for r in rows:
2796:             mid = r["target_msg_id"]
2797:             out.setdefault(mid, {}).setdefault(r["emoji"], []).append(r["peer_fp"])
2798:         return out

2800:     def search_messages(
2801:         self,
2802:         query: str,
2803:         *,
2804:         limit: int = 50,
2805:         peer_fp: Optional[str] = None,
2806:         room_id: Optional[str] = None,
2807:     ) -> list[MessageRecord]:
2808:         clauses = ["messages.rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM messages_fts WHERE messages_fts MATCH ?)"]
2809:         params: list[Any] = [query]
2810:         if peer_fp:
2811:             clauses.append("messages.peer_fp = ?")
2812:             params.append(peer_fp)
2813:         if room_id:
2814:             clauses.append("messages.room_id = ?")
2815:             params.append(room_id)
2816:         where = " AND ".join(clauses)
2817:         sql = (
2818:             f"SELECT * FROM messages WHERE {where} "  # nosec B608
2819:             f"ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT ?"
2820:         )
2821:         params.append(limit)
2822:         rows = self._conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
2823:         return [self._row_to_msg(r) for r in rows]
2824: 
2825:     def global_search(
2826:         self,
2827:         query: str,
2828:         *,
2829:         per_kind_limit: int = 10,
2830:     ) -> dict:
2831:         """v0.9.3: search across messages (FTS5), peers (LIKE), and
2832:         groups (LIKE). Returns a dict keyed by kind so the caller
2833:         can render each section.
2834: 
2835:         Query is escaped for FTS5 (`"…"` quoted) so user input
2836:         with operators like AND / OR / NEAR doesn't accidentally
2837:         change the search semantics. Empty query returns empty
2838:         results without hitting the DB."""
2839:         q = (query or "").strip()
2840:         out: dict = {"messages": [], "peers": [], "groups": []}
2841:         if not q:
2842:             return out
2843:         # 1. Messages via FTS5. Phrase-quoted so special chars don't
2844:         # error out the parser ("auth: user" would otherwise be
2845:         # parsed as field-restricted query).
2846:         try:
2847:             phrased = '"' + q.replace('"', '""') + '"'
2848:             msgs = self.search_messages(phrased, limit=per_kind_limit)
2849:         except Exception:
2850:             msgs = []
2851:         for m in msgs:
2852:             out["messages"].append({
2853:                 "id": m.id,
2854:                 "ts_ms": m.ts_ms,
2855:                 "direction": m.direction,
2856:                 "peer_fp": m.peer_fp,
2857:                 "msg_type": m.msg_type,
2858:                 "body": (m.body or "")[:200],
2859:                 "room_id": m.room_id,
2860:                 "reply_to": m.reply_to,
2861:             })
2862:         # 2. Peers by hostname / display alias / short_id / fingerprint
2863:         # prefix. Case-insensitive.
2864:         like = f"%{q}%"
2865:         peer_rows = self._conn.execute(
2866:             "SELECT * FROM peers"
2867:             " WHERE LOWER(IFNULL(hostname, '')) LIKE LOWER(?)"
2868:             "    OR LOWER(IFNULL(local_alias, '')) LIKE LOWER(?)"
2869:             "    OR LOWER(short_id) LIKE LOWER(?)"
2870:             "    OR LOWER(fingerprint) LIKE LOWER(?)"
2871:             " ORDER BY (trust = 'pinned') DESC, last_seen_ms DESC"
2872:             " LIMIT ?",
2873:             (like, like, like, like, int(per_kind_limit)),
2874:         ).fetchall()
2875:         for r in peer_rows:
2876:             rec = self._row_to_peer(r)
2877:             out["peers"].append({
2878:                 "fingerprint": rec.fingerprint,
2879:                 "short_id": rec.short_id,
2880:                 "hostname": rec.hostname,
2881:                 "display_name": rec.display_name,
2882:                 "trust": rec.trust,
2883:                 "is_verified": rec.is_verified,
2884:                 "last_seen_ms": rec.last_seen_ms,
2885:             })
2886:         # 3. Groups by name. groups.name was added in v0.6.2.
2887:         try:
2888:             grp_rows = self._conn.execute(
2889:                 "SELECT group_id, name, updated_ms FROM groups"
2890:                 " WHERE LOWER(IFNULL(name, '')) LIKE LOWER(?)"
2891:                 " ORDER BY updated_ms DESC LIMIT ?",
2892:                 (like, int(per_kind_limit)),
2893:             ).fetchall()
2894:         except Exception:
2895:             grp_rows = []
2896:         for r in grp_rows:
2897:             gid = r["group_id"]
2898:             try:
2899:                 gid_hex = gid.hex() if isinstance(gid, (bytes, bytearray)) else str(gid)
2900:             except Exception:
2901:                 gid_hex = ""
2902:             out["groups"].append({
2903:                 "group_id": gid_hex,
2904:                 "name": r["name"] or "",
2905:                 "updated_ms": r["updated_ms"],
2906:             })
2907:         return out
2908: 
2909:     def recent_messages(
2910:         self,
2911:         *,
2912:         peer_fp: Optional[str] = None,
2913:         room_id: Optional[str] = None,
2914:         limit: int = 50,
2915:     ) -> list[MessageRecord]:
2916:         clauses: list[str] = []
2917:         params: list[Any] = []
2918:         if peer_fp:
2919:             clauses.append("peer_fp = ?")
2920:             params.append(peer_fp)
2921:         if room_id:
2922:             clauses.append("room_id = ?")
2923:             params.append(room_id)
2924:         where = (" WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses)) if clauses else ""
2925:         sql = f"SELECT * FROM messages{where} ORDER BY ts_ms DESC LIMIT ?"  # nosec B608
2926:         params.append(limit)
2927:         rows = self._conn.execute(sql, params).fetchall()
2928:         return [self._row_to_msg(r) for r in reversed(rows)]

2930:     def _row_to_msg(self, row: sqlite3.Row) -> MessageRecord:
2931:         try:
2932:             md = json.loads(row["metadata_json"]) if row["metadata_json"] else {}
2933:         except Exception:
2934:             md = {}
2935:         cols = row.keys()
2936:         return MessageRecord(
2937:             id=row["id"],
2938:             ts_ms=row["ts_ms"],
2939:             direction=row["direction"],
2940:             peer_fp=row["peer_fp"],
2941:             msg_type=row["msg_type"],
2942:             body=row["body"],
2943:             room_id=row["room_id"],
2944:             metadata=md,
2945:             reply_to=row["reply_to"] if "reply_to" in cols else None,
2946:             edited_at_ms=row["edited_at_ms"] if "edited_at_ms" in cols else None,
2947:             original_body=row["original_body"] if "original_body" in cols else None,
2948:             deleted_at_ms=row["deleted_at_ms"] if "deleted_at_ms" in cols else None,
2949:             expires_at_ms=row["expires_at_ms"] if "expires_at_ms" in cols else None,
2950:         )

2952:     # ─── edit / delete (v0.7.6) ───────────────────────────────────────
2953: 
2954:     def edit_message(
2955:         self, *, id: str, new_body: str, edited_at_ms: int,
2956:     ) -> Optional[MessageRecord]:
2957:         """v0.7.6: replace a message's body and stamp edited_at_ms.
2958:         Preserves the original body in original_body the first time
2959:         an edit happens (subsequent edits don't overwrite it).
2960:         Returns the refreshed record, or None if not found / deleted."""
2961:         cur = self.get_message(id)
2962:         if cur is None or cur.is_deleted:
2963:             return None
2964:         original = cur.original_body or cur.body
2965:         with self._write_lock:
2966:             self._conn.execute(
2967:                 "UPDATE messages SET body = ?, edited_at_ms = ?,"
2968:                 " original_body = COALESCE(original_body, ?)"
2969:                 " WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL",
2970:                 (new_body, int(edited_at_ms), original, id),
2971:             )
2972:         return self.get_message(id)

2989: 
2990:         Tries `group_messages` table first; falls back to a no-op

2992:         with self._write_lock:

2999:             except Exception:
3000:                 return 0

3002:     def _delete_all_locked(self, table: str, where: str = "", params: tuple = ()) -> int:
3003:         sql = f"DELETE FROM {table}" + (f" WHERE {where}" if where else "")  # nosec B608
3004:         try:
3005:             cur = self._conn.execute(sql, params)
3006:             return int(cur.rowcount or 0)
3007:         except sqlite3.Error:
3008:             return 0

3014:                 "messages": self._delete_all_locked("messages"),
3015:                 "group_messages": self._delete_all_locked("group_messages"),
3016:                 "message_reactions": self._delete_all_locked("message_reactions"),
3017:                 "outbox": self._delete_all_locked("outbox"),

3099:     def storage_usage_by_peer(self) -> list[dict]:
3100:         """v0.11.6: per-peer usage rollup for the Storage pane.
3101:         Returns one entry per peer that has any messages, with
3102:         msg_count and file_bytes (sum of metadata.size for file
3103:         rows). The frontend joins this with peer display names."""
3104:         rows = self._conn.execute(
3105:             "SELECT peer_fp, COUNT(*) AS n, "
3106:             "  SUM(CASE WHEN msg_type='file' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS file_n "
3107:             "FROM messages WHERE deleted_at_ms IS NULL "
3108:             "GROUP BY peer_fp"
3109:         ).fetchall()
3110:         out: list[dict] = []
3111:         for r in rows:
3112:             fp = r["peer_fp"]
3113:             # Sum metadata.size across the file rows for this peer.
3114:             file_bytes = 0
3115:             file_rows = self._conn.execute(
3116:                 "SELECT metadata_json FROM messages "
3117:                 "WHERE peer_fp = ? AND msg_type = 'file' "
3118:                 "  AND deleted_at_ms IS NULL",
3119:                 (fp,),
3120:             ).fetchall()
3121:             for fr in file_rows:
3122:                 try:
3123:                     md = json.loads(fr["metadata_json"]) if fr["metadata_json"] else {}
3124:                 except Exception:
3125:                     md = {}
3126:                 size = md.get("size")
3127:                 if isinstance(size, (int, float)):
3128:                     file_bytes += int(size)
3129:             out.append({
3130:                 "peer_fp": fp,
3131:                 "msg_count": int(r["n"] or 0),
3132:                 "file_count": int(r["file_n"] or 0),
3133:                 "file_bytes": file_bytes,
3134:             })
3135:         # Largest by file_bytes first, then by msg_count.
3136:         out.sort(key=lambda d: (-d["file_bytes"], -d["msg_count"]))
3137:         return out

3139:     def storage_usage_by_group(self) -> list[dict]:
3140:         """v0.11.6: per-group rollup. Falls back to empty list when
3141:         the group_messages table doesn't exist on this build."""
3142:         try:
3143:             rows = self._conn.execute(
3144:                 "SELECT group_id, COUNT(*) AS n "
3145:                 "FROM group_messages GROUP BY group_id"
3146:             ).fetchall()
3147:         except Exception:
3148:             return []
3149:         out: list[dict] = []
3150:         for r in rows:
3151:             out.append({

3153:                             if isinstance(r["group_id"], str)
3154:                             else r["group_id"].hex(),
3155:                 "msg_count": int(r["n"] or 0),
3156:             })
3157:         out.sort(key=lambda d: -d["msg_count"])
3158:         return out

3172:     def delete_message(
3173:         self, *, id: str, deleted_at_ms: int,
3174:     ) -> Optional[MessageRecord]:
3175:         """v0.7.6: soft-delete. Body cleared; deleted_at_ms stamped.
3176:         Idempotent on already-deleted rows."""
3177:         cur = self.get_message(id)
3178:         if cur is None:
3179:             return None
3180:         if cur.is_deleted:
3181:             return cur
3182:         with self._write_lock:
3183:             self._conn.execute(
3184:                 "UPDATE messages SET body = NULL, deleted_at_ms = ?"
3185:                 " WHERE id = ?",
3186:                 (int(deleted_at_ms), id),
3187:             )
3188:         return self.get_message(id)

3198:     def record_read_marker(self, peer_fp: str, up_to_ts_ms: int) -> None:
3199:         """Mark all messages from `peer_fp` with ts ≤ `up_to_ts_ms`
3200:         as read by us. Monotonic — older markers can't overwrite a
3201:         newer one."""
3202:         if not peer_fp:
3203:             return
3204:         with self._write_lock:
3205:             self._conn.execute(
3206:                 """
3207:                 INSERT INTO peer_read_markers(peer_fp, up_to_ts_ms, updated_ms)
3208:                 VALUES(?, ?, ?)
3209:                 ON CONFLICT(peer_fp) DO UPDATE SET
3210:                     up_to_ts_ms = MAX(peer_read_markers.up_to_ts_ms, excluded.up_to_ts_ms),
3211:                     updated_ms = excluded.updated_ms
3212:                 """,
3213:                 (peer_fp, int(up_to_ts_ms), _now_ms()),
3214:             )
3215:

3231:     def upsert_transfer(
3232:         self,
3233:         *,
3234:         id: str,
3235:         direction: str,
3236:         peer_fp: str,
3237:         kind: str,
3238:         name: str,
3239:         size: int,
3240:         blob_hash: Optional[str] = None,
3241:         status: str = "queued",
3242:         progress_bytes: int = 0,
3243:         total_bytes: Optional[int] = None,
3244:         chunks_done: int = 0,
3245:         chunks_total: int = 0,
3246:         raw_bytes: int = 0,
3247:         wire_bytes: int = 0,
3248:         metadata: Optional[dict] = None,
3249:     ) -> TransferRecord:
3250:         if direction not in ("in", "out"):
3251:             raise ValueError(f"invalid transfer direction: {direction!r}")
3252:         if status not in (
3253:             "queued", "offered", "active", "complete", "failed", "paused",
3254:         ):
3255:             raise ValueError(f"invalid transfer status: {status!r}")
3256:         total = int(size if total_bytes is None else total_bytes)
3257:         now = _now_ms()
3258:         with self._write_lock:
3259:             self._conn.execute(
3260:                 """
3261:                 INSERT INTO transfers(
3262:                     id, direction, peer_fp, kind, name, size, blob_hash, status,
3263:                     progress_bytes, total_bytes, chunks_done, chunks_total,
3264:                     raw_bytes, wire_bytes, updated_ms, metadata_json
3265:                 ) VALUES(?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
3266:                 ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
3267:                     direction = excluded.direction,
3268:                     peer_fp = excluded.peer_fp,
3269:                     kind = excluded.kind,
3270:                     name = excluded.name,
3271:                     size = excluded.size,
3272:                     blob_hash = excluded.blob_hash,
3273:                     status = excluded.status,
3274:                     progress_bytes = excluded.progress_bytes,
3275:                     total_bytes = excluded.total_bytes,
3276:                     chunks_done = excluded.chunks_done,
3277:                     chunks_total = excluded.chunks_total,
3278:                     raw_bytes = excluded.raw_bytes,
3279:                     wire_bytes = excluded.wire_bytes,
3280:                     updated_ms = excluded.updated_ms,
3281:                     metadata_json = excluded.metadata_json
3282:                 """,
3283:                 (
3284:                     id, direction, peer_fp, kind, name, int(size), blob_hash,
3285:                     status, int(progress_bytes), total, int(chunks_done),
3286:                     int(chunks_total), int(raw_bytes), int(wire_bytes), now,
3287:                     json.dumps(metadata or {}, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True),
3288:                 ),
3289:             )
3290:             row = self._conn.execute(
3291:                 "SELECT * FROM transfers WHERE id = ?", (id,)
3292:             ).fetchone()
3293:         return self._row_to_transfer(row)
3294: 
3295:     def update_transfer(self, id: str, **fields: Any) -> Optional[TransferRecord]:
3296:         allowed = {
3297:             "status", "progress_bytes", "total_bytes", "chunks_done",
3298:             "chunks_total", "raw_bytes", "wire_bytes", "metadata",
3299:         }
3300:         bad = set(fields) - allowed
3301:         if bad:
3302:             raise ValueError(f"unknown transfer fields: {sorted(bad)!r}")
3303:         current = self.get_transfer(id)
3304:         if current is None:
3305:             return None
3306:         metadata = fields.pop("metadata", current.metadata)
3307:         data = {
3308:             "id": current.id,
3309:             "direction": current.direction,
3310:             "peer_fp": current.peer_fp,
3311:             "kind": current.kind,
3312:             "name": current.name,
3313:             "size": current.size,
3314:             "blob_hash": current.blob_hash,
3315:             "status": current.status,
3316:             "progress_bytes": current.progress_bytes,
3317:             "total_bytes": current.total_bytes,
3318:             "chunks_done": current.chunks_done,
3319:             "chunks_total": current.chunks_total,
3320:             "raw_bytes": current.raw_bytes,
3321:             "wire_bytes": current.wire_bytes,
3322:             "metadata": metadata,
3323:         }
3324:         data.update(fields)
3325:         return self.upsert_transfer(**data)

3331:         return self._row_to_transfer(row) if row else None
