 153: def diagnose_transfer(rec: Any, *, now_ms: int | None = None) -> TransferDiagnosis:
 154:     """Diagnose a transfer record into user-safe state.
 155: 
 156:     The labels are intentionally product language, not implementation language.
 157:     Raw errors stay in metadata/debug logs; the user sees what One Link is doing.
 158:     """
 159: 
 160:     status = str(_field(rec, "status", "queued") or "queued")
 161:     direction = str(_field(rec, "direction", "out") or "out")
 162:     md = _metadata(rec)
 163:     delivery_state = str(md.get("delivery_state") or "").lower()
 164:     err_class = str(md.get("error_class") or "")
 165:     err = str(md.get("error") or "")
 166:     code_src = " ".join((delivery_state, err_class, err)).lower()
 167:     next_retry = md.get("next_retry_ms")
 168:     next_retry_ms = int(next_retry) if isinstance(next_retry, (int, float)) else None
 169:     retry_in_ms = _now_delta(next_retry_ms, now_ms)
 170: 
 171:     if status == "complete":
 172:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 173:             code="done",
 174:             label="Done",
 175:             user_message="Verified and delivered.",
 176:             action="none",
 177:             automatic=True,
 178:             transient=False,
 179:             severity="ok",
 180:         )
 181: 
 182:     if status in ("queued", "offered") and delivery_state in ("queued", ""):
 183:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 184:             code="queued",
 185:             label="Sending",
 186:             user_message="One Link is preparing the send.",
 187:             action="retry_with_backoff",
 188:             automatic=True,
 189:             transient=True,
 190:             severity="info",
 191:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 192:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 193:         )
 194: 
 195:     if status == "active" or delivery_state == "sending":
 196:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 197:             code="sending",
 198:             label="Sending",
 199:             user_message="One Link is moving verified pieces now.",
 200:             action="continue",
 201:             automatic=True,
 202:             transient=True,
 203:             severity="info",
 204:         )
 205: 
 206:     if "ratchet" in code_src or "desync" in code_src or "invalidtag" in code_src:
 207:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 208:             code="secure_session_desync",
 209:             label="Resuming",
 210:             user_message="One Link is refreshing the secure session and will continue automatically.",
 211:             action="reopen_secure_session",
 212:             automatic=True,
 213:             transient=True,
 214:             severity="warn",
 215:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 216:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 217:             route_action="reopen_secure_session",
 218:         )
 219: 
 220:     if "version" in code_src or "compat" in code_src or "protocol" in code_src:
 221:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 222:             code="protocol_fallback",
 223:             label="Resuming",
 224:             user_message="One Link is switching to the best protocol both devices understand.",
 225:             action="fallback_protocol",
 226:             automatic=True,
 227:             transient=True,
 228:             severity="info",
 229:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 230:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 231:             route_action="fallback_protocol",
 232:         )
 233: 
 234:     if "chunk" in code_src or "integrity" in code_src or "hash" in code_src:
 235:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 236:             code="chunk_retry",
 237:             label="Resuming",
 238:             user_message="One Link is retrying only the piece that did not verify.",
 239:             action="retry_missing_chunk",
 240:             automatic=True,
 241:             transient=True,
 242:             severity="warn",
 243:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 244:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 245:             route_action="retry_missing_chunk",
 246:         )
 247: 
 248:     if "resum" in delivery_state:
 249:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 250:             code="resuming",
 251:             label="Resuming",
 252:             user_message="One Link is continuing from the verified pieces already delivered.",
 253:             action="retry_missing_chunk",
 254:             automatic=True,
 255:             transient=True,
 256:             severity="info",
 257:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 258:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 259:             route_action="retry_missing_chunk",
 260:         )
 261: 
 262:     if "offline" in code_src or "unreachable" in code_src or "timeout" in code_src:
 263:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 264:             code="waiting_for_device",
 265:             label="Waiting for device",
 266:             user_message="One Link is waiting quietly and will resume when the device is reachable.",
 267:             action="wait_for_peer",
 268:             automatic=True,
 269:             transient=True,
 270:             severity="info",
 271:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 272:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 273:             route_action="refresh_route",
 274:         )
 275: 
 276:     if "route" in code_src or "address" in code_src or "port" in code_src:
 277:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 278:             code="route_refresh",
 279:             label="Resuming",
 280:             user_message="One Link is refreshing the device route and trying again.",
 281:             action="refresh_route",
 282:             automatic=True,
 283:             transient=True,
 284:             severity="info",
 285:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 286:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 287:             route_action="refresh_route",
 288:         )
 289: 
 290:     if status == "paused" or bool(md.get("transient")):
 291:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 292:             code="retrying",
 293:             label="Waiting for device",
 294:             user_message="One Link saved the transfer and will retry automatically.",
 295:             action="retry_with_backoff",
 296:             automatic=True,
 297:             transient=True,
 298:             severity="info",
 299:             next_retry_ms=next_retry_ms,
 300:             retry_in_ms=retry_in_ms,
 301:         )
 302: 
 303:     if "source file" in code_src or "filenotfound" in code_src:
 304:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 305:             code="source_missing",
 306:             label="Needs attention",
 307:             user_message="The original file moved or was deleted before One Link could finish.",
 308:             action="choose_file_again",
 309:             automatic=False,
 310:             transient=False,
 311:             severity="error",
 312:         )
 313: 
 314:     if status == "failed":
 315:         return TransferDiagnosis(
 316:             code="needs_attention",
 317:             label="Needs attention",
 318:             user_message="One Link needs your attention before it can continue this transfer.",
 319:             action="manual_review",
 320:             automatic=False,
 321:             transient=False,
 322:             severity="error",
 323:         )
 324: 
 325:     return TransferDiagnosis(
 326:         code="unknown",
 327:         label="Sending" if direction == "out" else "Receiving",
 328:         user_message="One Link is tracking this transfer.",
 329:         action="observe",
 330:         automatic=True,
 331:         transient=True,
 332:         severity="info",
 333:     )

 336: def diagnose_exception(exc: BaseException) -> TransferDiagnosis:
 337:     """Classify a send exception before it becomes transfer metadata."""
 338: 
 339:     class _R:
 340:         status = "paused"
 341:         direction = "out"
 342:         metadata = {
 343:             "error": str(exc),
 344:             "error_class": type(exc).__name__,
 345:             "transient": not isinstance(exc, (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError)),
 346:         }
 347: 
 348:     if isinstance(exc, asyncio.TimeoutError):
 349:         _R.metadata["error"] = "timeout"
 350:     return diagnose_transfer(_R)

 353: def enrich_transfer_event(event: dict[str, Any], *, now_ms: int | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
 354:     """Attach doctor diagnosis to a transfer event dict."""
 355: 
 356:     diag = diagnose_transfer(event, now_ms=now_ms).to_dict()
 357:     out = dict(event)
 358:     out["doctor"] = diag
 359:     out["autopilot_truth"] = transfer_autopilot_truth(out, diagnosis=diag)
 360:     # Flatten the highest-value fields for older UI code and tests.
 361:     out["display_state"] = diag["label"]
 362:     out["user_message"] = diag["user_message"]
 363:     return out

 365: 
 366: def transfer_autopilot_truth(
 367:     rec: Any,
 368:     *,
 369:     diagnosis: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
 370: ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 371:     """Build the user-facing transfer intelligence contract.
 372: 
 373:     The daemon records rich engineering metadata: CDC decisions, binary frame
 374:     choices, performance reports, route observations, retry causes, and swarm
 375:     assists. This helper turns those details into a stable product surface the
 376:     UI can render directly. It is deterministic and side-effect free so tests,
 377:     WebSocket events, and REST snapshots all tell the same story.
 378:     """
 379: 
 380:     md = _metadata(rec)
 381:     plan = _as_mapping(md.get("autopilot_plan"))
 382:     perf = _as_mapping(md.get("performance_summary"))
 383:     report = _as_mapping(md.get("transfer_report"))
 384:     assist = _as_mapping(md.get("swarm_assist"))
 385:     brain = _as_mapping(md.get("transfer_brain"))
 386:     scheduler = _as_mapping(md.get("adaptive_scheduler"))
 387:     diag = dict(diagnosis or diagnose_transfer(rec).to_dict())
 388: 
 389:     status = str(_field(rec, "status", "") or "").lower()
 390:     direction = str(_field(rec, "direction", "out") or "out").lower()
 391:     progress_bytes = _as_int(_field(rec, "progress_bytes", 0))
 392:     total_bytes = _as_int(_field(rec, "total_bytes", _field(rec, "size", 0)))
 393:     wire_bytes = _as_int(_field(rec, "wire_bytes", report.get("wire_bytes_sent", 0)))
 394:     skipped_bytes = max(
 395:         _as_int(perf.get("skipped_bytes")),
 396:         _as_int(report.get("skipped_bytes")),
 397:         _as_int(md.get("skipped_bytes")),
 398:     )
 399:     saved_bytes = max(
 400:         _as_int(perf.get("saved_bytes")),
 401:         _as_int(report.get("saved_bytes")),
 402:         _as_int(md.get("saved_bytes")),
 403:         _as_int(assist.get("assisted_bytes")),
 404:     )
 405:     savings_ratio = max(
 406:         _as_float(perf.get("bandwidth_savings_ratio")),
 407:         _as_float(report.get("bandwidth_savings_ratio")),
 408:         _as_float(plan.get("estimated_savings_ratio")),
 409:         _as_float(md.get("bandwidth_savings_ratio")),
 410:         _as_float(md.get("prior_hit_rate_actual")),
 411:         _as_float(md.get("skipped_ratio")),
 412:     )
 413:     if savings_ratio <= 0 and total_bytes > 0 and (skipped_bytes > 0 or saved_bytes > 0):
 414:         savings_ratio = (skipped_bytes + saved_bytes) / max(1, total_bytes)
 415:     savings_ratio = _clamp01(savings_ratio)
 416: 
 417:     effective_mbps = max(
 418:         _as_float(perf.get("effective_mbps")),
 419:         _as_float(plan.get("estimated_mbps")),
 420:         (_as_float(report.get("effective_throughput_bps")) / 1_000_000.0),
 421:     )
 422:     wire_mbps = max(
 423:         _as_float(perf.get("wire_mbps")),
 424:         (_as_float(report.get("wire_throughput_bps")) / 1_000_000.0),
 425:     )
 426: 
 427:     route = (
 428:         perf.get("route")
 429:         or plan.get("route")
 430:         or md.get("route")
 431:         or brain.get("route")
 432:         or ("local_cache" if assist.get("strategy") == "multi_source_chunk_pull" else "")
 433:     )
 434:     route_label = _route_label(route)
 435:     frame_kind = str(
 436:         perf.get("frame_kind")
 437:         or plan.get("frame_kind")
 438:         or md.get("frame_kind")
 439:         or ""
 440:     ).lower()
 441:     fast_binary = bool(md.get("binary_frame")) or "binary" in frame_kind
 442:     sent_only_missing = skipped_bytes > 0 or saved_bytes > 0 or savings_ratio >= 0.01
 443: 
 444:     facts: list[str] = []
 445:     speed_fact = _mbps_fact("Finished at" if status == "complete" else "Sending at", effective_mbps)
 446:     if speed_fact:
 447:         facts.append(speed_fact)
 448:     if savings_ratio >= 0.01:
 449:         facts.append(f"{round(savings_ratio * 100):.0f}% already known")
 450:     if sent_only_missing:
 451:         facts.append("Only sent missing pieces")
 452:     if fast_binary:
 453:         facts.append("Using fast binary path")
 454:     if diag.get("automatic") and diag.get("action") not in {"none", "continue", "observe"}:
 455:         facts.append("Resuming automatically")
 456:     pulled = _as_int(assist.get("pulled"))
 457:     if pulled > 0:
 458:         source_count = max(1, _as_int(assist.get("source_count"), len(_as_mapping(assist.get("sources"))) or 1))
 459:         facts.append(
 460:             f"Pulled {pulled} chunk{'s' if pulled != 1 else ''} from "
 461:             f"{source_count} trusted device{'s' if source_count != 1 else ''}"
 462:         )
 463:     healed = _as_int(assist.get("healed"))
 464:     if healed > 0:
 465:         facts.append(
 466:             f"Healed {healed} chunk{'s' if healed != 1 else ''} by switching source"
 467:         )
 468:     facts.append(f"Route: {route_label}")
 469: 
 470:     seen: set[str] = set()
 471:     deduped = []
 472:     for fact in facts:
 473:         if fact and fact not in seen:
 474:             seen.add(fact)
 475:             deduped.append(fact)
 476: 
 477:     if diag.get("label") == "Done":
 478:         headline = "Verified and delivered"
 479:     elif speed_fact:
 480:         headline = speed_fact
 481:     else:
 482:         headline = str(diag.get("label") or ("Receiving" if direction == "in" else "Sending"))
 483: 
 484:     return {
 485:         "state": str(diag.get("code") or status or "unknown"),
 486:         "state_label": str(diag.get("label") or headline),
 487:         "headline": headline,
 488:         "message": str(diag.get("user_message") or ""),
 489:         "facts": deduped[:7],
 490:         "route": str(route or ""),
 491:         "route_label": route_label,
 492:         "speed_mbps": round(effective_mbps, 3),
 493:         "wire_mbps": round(wire_mbps, 3),
 494:         "known_pct": round(savings_ratio * 100.0, 1),
 495:         "sent_only_missing_pieces": bool(sent_only_missing),
 496:         "fast_path_label": "Fast binary path" if fast_binary else "Compatible path",
 497:         "self_healing_action": str(diag.get("action") or "observe"),
 498:         "automatic": bool(diag.get("automatic")),
 499:         "progress_bytes": progress_bytes,
 500:         "total_bytes": total_bytes,
 501:         "wire_bytes": wire_bytes,
 502:         "saved_bytes": saved_bytes,
 503:         "skipped_bytes": skipped_bytes,
 504:         "parallelism": _as_int(scheduler.get("parallelism"), _as_int(plan.get("parallelism"), 1)),
 505:     }

 507: 
 508: class RouteMemory:
 509:     """Tiny deterministic route scorer for a peer.
 510: 
 511:     This is intentionally independent from networking. The daemon can feed it
 512:     observations later; the simulator can already prove decisions.
 513:     """
 514: 
 515:     def __init__(self) -> None:
 516:         self._routes: dict[str, list[RouteObservation]] = {}
 517: 
 518:     def observe(self, obs: RouteObservation) -> None:
 519:         self._routes.setdefault(obs.route, []).append(obs)
 520: 
 521:     def candidates(self) -> tuple[RouteCandidate, ...]:
 522:         out: list[RouteCandidate] = []
 523:         for route, rows in self._routes.items():
 524:             attempts = len(rows)
 525:             successes = sum(1 for r in rows if r.ok)
 526:             failures = attempts - successes
 527:             latencies = [r.latency_ms for r in rows if r.ok and r.latency_ms is not None]
 528:             bandwidths = [r.bandwidth_bps for r in rows if r.ok and r.bandwidth_bps is not None]
 529:             reliability = successes / max(1, attempts)
 530:             latency = sum(latencies) / len(latencies) if latencies else None
 531:             bandwidth = sum(bandwidths) / len(bandwidths) if bandwidths else None
 532:             score = reliability * 100.0
 533:             if bandwidth:
 534:                 score += min(50.0, bandwidth / 10_000_000.0)
 535:             if latency is not None:
 536:                 score -= min(40.0, latency / 25.0)
 537:             score -= failures * 2.0
 538:             out.append(RouteCandidate(
 539:                 route=route,
 540:                 score=round(score, 4),
 541:                 attempts=attempts,
 542:                 successes=successes,
 543:                 failures=failures,
 544:                 latency_ms=latency,
 545:                 bandwidth_bps=bandwidth,
 546:             ))
 547:         return tuple(sorted(out, key=lambda c: (-c.score, c.route)))
 548: 
 549:     def best_route(self, fallback: str = "lan") -> str:
 550:         ranked = self.candidates()
 551:         return ranked[0].route if ranked else fallback

   1: """Receiver-side transfer admission control.
   2: 
   3: The transfer protocol is intentionally optimistic: a trusted peer can offer a
   4: huge file and the receiver replies with the exact chunks it wants. This module
   5: is the hard safety gate in front of that optimism. It keeps "send anything" from
   6: turning into "let anyone allocate anything".
   7: """
   8: 
   9: from __future__ import annotations
  10: 
  11: import shutil
  12: from dataclasses import dataclass

  14: from typing import Iterable
  15: 
  16: 
  17: TIB = 1024 ** 4
  18: 
  19: 
  20: DEFAULT_MAX_DECLARED_BYTES = 16 * TIB
  21: DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_RESERVE_BYTES = 2 * 1024 ** 3
  22: DEFAULT_FREE_RESERVE_RATIO = 0.05
  23: DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVE_INBOUND_TRANSFERS_PER_PEER = 3
  24: DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVE_INBOUND_BYTES_PER_PEER = 2 * TIB
  25:

  27:     "app",

  32:     "dll",
  33:     "dmg",
  34:     "exe",
  35:     "hta",
  36:     "jar",
  37:     "js",
  38:     "jse",
  39:     "lnk",
  40:     "msi",
  41:     "pkg",
  42:     "ps1",
  43:     "reg",
  44:     "scr",
  45:     "sh",
  46:     "sys",

 111: def _disk_free_bytes(path: Path) -> int:
 112:     try:
 113:         path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 114:         return int(shutil.disk_usage(path).free)
 115:     except Exception:
 116:         return 0

 119: def _clean_size(value: int | float | str | None) -> int | None:
 120:     if value is None:
 121:         return None
 122:     try:
 123:         size = int(value)
 124:     except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
 125:         return None
 126:     return size if size >= 0 else None
 127: 
 128: 
 129: def known_bytes_from_chunks(chunks: Iterable[dict], known_hashes: set[str]) -> int:
 130:     total = 0
 131:     seen: set[str] = set()
 132:     for c in chunks:
 133:         try:
 134:             h = str(c.get("hash") or "")
 135:             size = int(c.get("size") or 0)
 136:         except Exception:
 137:             continue
 138:         if not h or h in seen or h not in known_hashes or size <= 0:
 139:             continue
 140:         seen.add(h)
 141:         total += size
 142:     return total

 145: def classify_file_risk(name: str) -> dict:
 146:     """Return user-facing risk metadata for a received file.
 147: 
 148:     This is not antivirus and deliberately does not pretend to be. It is a
 149:     zero-trust UX guardrail: One Link can transfer any file, but files that are
 150:     commonly executable or scriptable should be surfaced as reveal/download
 151:     only and never treated like harmless media.
 152:     """
 153: 
 154:     safe_name = Path(str(name or "")).name
 155:     suffixes = [
 156:         part.lower().lstrip(".")
 157:         for part in Path(safe_name).suffixes
 158:         if part and part != "."
 159:     ]
 160:     ext = suffixes[-1] if suffixes else ""
 161:     risky_suffixes = [e for e in suffixes if e in HIGH_RISK_FILE_EXTENSIONS]
 162:     archive_suffixes = [e for e in suffixes if e in MEDIUM_RISK_FILE_EXTENSIONS]
 163:     if risky_suffixes:
 164:         return {
 165:             "level": "high",
 166:             "extension": ext,
 167:             "reason": "executable_or_script",
 168:             "label": "Executable file",
 169:             "user_message": (
 170:                 "One Link received this safely, but it can run code. "
 171:                 "Open it only if you trust the sender and expected this file."
 172:             ),
 173:             "open_policy": "reveal_only",
 174:         }
 175:     if archive_suffixes:
 176:         return {
 177:             "level": "medium",
 178:             "extension": ext,
 179:             "reason": "archive_or_macro_document",
 180:             "label": "Archive or macro-capable file",
 181:             "user_message": (
 182:                 "One Link received this safely. Check the contents before opening anything inside."
 183:             ),
 184:             "open_policy": "cautious",
 185:         }
 186:     return {
 187:         "level": "low",
 188:         "extension": ext,
 189:         "reason": "",
 190:         "label": "File",
 191:         "user_message": "",
 192:         "open_policy": "normal",
 193:     }
 194: 
 195: 
 196: def evaluate_transfer_admission(
 197:     *,
 198:     name: str,
 199:     size: int | float | str | None,
 200:     peer_fp: str,
 201:     policy: TransferAdmissionPolicy,
 202:     context: TransferAdmissionContext,
 203: ) -> TransferAdmissionDecision:
 204:     del name, peer_fp
 205:     clean_size = _clean_size(size)
 206:     if clean_size is None:
 207:         return TransferAdmissionDecision(
 208:             ok=False,
 209:             reason="invalid_size",
 210:             user_message="One Link blocked a file offer with an invalid size.",
 211:         )
 212:     if clean_size > int(policy.max_declared_bytes):
 213:         return TransferAdmissionDecision(
 214:             ok=False,
 215:             reason="declared_size_too_large",
 216:             user_message="One Link blocked a file offer that was too large to handle safely.",
 217:             declared_size=clean_size,
 218:         )
 219:     if (
 220:         policy.max_active_inbound_transfers_per_peer > 0
 221:         and context.active_inbound_count_for_peer
 222:         >= policy.max_active_inbound_transfers_per_peer
 223:     ):
 224:         return TransferAdmissionDecision(
 225:             ok=False,
 226:             reason="peer_inbound_transfer_quota",
 227:             user_message="One Link paused this sender because too many files are already incoming.",
 228:             declared_size=clean_size,
 229:         )
 230:     if (
 231:         policy.max_active_inbound_bytes_per_peer > 0
 232:         and context.active_inbound_bytes_for_peer + clean_size
 233:         > policy.max_active_inbound_bytes_per_peer
 234:     ):
 235:         return TransferAdmissionDecision(
 236:             ok=False,
 237:             reason="peer_inbound_byte_quota",
 238:             user_message="One Link paused this sender because their incoming queue is too large.",
 239:             declared_size=clean_size,
 240:         )
 241: 
 242:     already_known = max(0, min(clean_size, int(context.already_known_bytes)))
 243:     reserve_bytes = max(0, clean_size - already_known)
 244:     free_bytes = _disk_free_bytes(context.incoming_dir)
 245:     reserve_floor = max(
 246:         int(policy.min_free_reserve_bytes),
 247:         int(free_bytes * max(0.0, float(policy.free_reserve_ratio))),
 248:     )
 249:     required = reserve_bytes + reserve_floor
 250:     if reserve_bytes > 0 and free_bytes < required:
 251:         return TransferAdmissionDecision(
 252:             ok=False,
 253:             reason="insufficient_disk_space",
 254:             user_message=(
 255:                 "One Link is waiting for enough free space before accepting this file."
 256:             ),
 257:             reserve_bytes=reserve_bytes,
 258:             free_bytes=free_bytes,
 259:             required_free_bytes=required,
 260:             declared_size=clean_size,
 261:             already_known_bytes=already_known,
 262:         )
 263:     return TransferAdmissionDecision(
 264:         ok=True,
 265:         reserve_bytes=reserve_bytes,
 266:         free_bytes=free_bytes,

   1: """Deterministic never-lose transfer torture simulator.
   2: 
   3: The simulator uses synthetic manifests, so it can model multi-gigabyte sends
   4: without writing multi-gigabyte files. It exercises the same planning ideas as
   5: the live engine: rarest-first chunk scheduling, route memory, transient
   6: failures, corruption retry, offline waits, and legacy fallback.
   7: """
   8: 
   9: from __future__ import annotations
  10: 
  11: import hashlib
  12: import random
  13: from dataclasses import dataclass

  21: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  22: class SimSource:
  23:     peer_fp: str
  24:     route: str
  25:     chunk_indexes: frozenset[int]

  27:     latency_ms: float = 10.0
  28:     bandwidth_bps: float = 100_000_000.0
  29:     reliability: float = 0.99

  71: def synthetic_manifest(
  72:     *,
  73:     name: str = "huge-video.bin",
  74:     size: int,
  75:     chunk_size: int = 1024 * 1024,
  76: ) -> FileManifest:
  77:     if size < 0:
  78:         raise ValueError("size must be non-negative")
  79:     if chunk_size <= 0:
  80:         raise ValueError("chunk_size must be positive")
  81:     chunks: list[FileChunkManifest] = []
  82:     offset = 0
  83:     index = 0
  84:     while offset < size or (size == 0 and not chunks):
  85:         end = min(size, offset + chunk_size)
  86:         if size == 0:
  87:             end = 0
  88:         h = hashlib.blake2s(
  89:             f"{name}:{size}:{index}:{offset}:{end}".encode("utf-8"),
  90:             digest_size=32,
  91:         ).hexdigest()
  92:         chunks.append(FileChunkManifest(
  93:             index=index,
  94:             start=offset,
  95:             end=end,
  96:             size=end - offset,
  97:             hash=h,
  98:         ))
  99:         if size == 0:
 100:             break
 101:         offset = end
 102:         index += 1
 103:     blob = hashlib.blake2s(
 104:         f"{name}:{size}:{len(chunks)}".encode("utf-8"),
 105:         digest_size=32,
 106:     ).hexdigest()
 107:     return FileManifest(name=name, size=size, blob_hash=blob, chunks=tuple(chunks))
 108: 
 109: 
 110: def _default_sources(manifest: FileManifest) -> tuple[SimSource, ...]:
 111:     indexes = [c.index for c in manifest.chunks]
 112:     even = frozenset(i for i in indexes if i % 2 == 0)
 113:     odd = frozenset(i for i in indexes if i % 2 == 1)
 114:     all_chunks = frozenset(indexes)
 115:     return (
 116:         SimSource("a" * 64, "lan", even, trust_score=2.0, latency_ms=4, bandwidth_bps=250_000_000, reliability=0.97),
 117:         SimSource("b" * 64, "relay", odd, trust_score=1.5, latency_ms=80, bandwidth_bps=80_000_000, reliability=0.93),
 118:         SimSource("c" * 64, "prior", all_chunks, trust_score=2.0, latency_ms=1, bandwidth_bps=1_000_000_000, reliability=0.88),
 119:     )

 122: def _source_to_plan_source(source: SimSource, manifest: FileManifest) -> ChunkSource:
 123:     hashes = [c.hash for c in manifest.chunks if c.index in source.chunk_indexes]
 124:     return source_from_hashes(
 125:         source.peer_fp,
 126:         hashes,
 127:         trust_score=source.trust_score,
 128:         latency_ms=source.latency_ms,
 129:         bandwidth_bps=source.bandwidth_bps,
 130:         reliability=source.reliability,
 131:         route_kind=source.route,
 132:     )

 135: def simulate_never_lose_transfer(
 136:     *,
 137:     size: int = 10 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
 138:     chunk_size: int = 16 * 1024 * 1024,
 139:     seed: int = 20260507,
 140:     sources: Iterable[SimSource] | None = None,
 141:     drop_rate: float = 0.03,
 142:     corruption_rate: float = 0.01,
 143:     max_rounds: int = 50_000,
 144: ) -> TortureReport:
 145:     rng = random.Random(seed)
 146:     manifest = synthetic_manifest(size=size, chunk_size=chunk_size)
 147:     sim_sources = tuple(sources) if sources is not None else _default_sources(manifest)
 148:     by_hash = {c.hash: c for c in manifest.chunks}
 149:     delivered: set[int] = set()
 150:     needed = {c.index for c in manifest.chunks}
 151:     route_memory = RouteMemory()
 152:     attempts = retries = corruptions = offline_waits = fallback_events = 0
 153:     bytes_sent = 0
 154:     bytes_saved = 0
 155:     doctor_codes: list[str] = []
 156: 
 157:     for round_no in range(max_rounds):
 158:         if not needed:
 159:             break
 160:         active_sources: list[SimSource] = []
 161:         for src in sim_sources:
 162:             # Devices may sleep or routes may disappear for a round.
 163:             if rng.random() < drop_rate:
 164:                 offline_waits += 1
 165:                 route_memory.observe(RouteObservation(
 166:                     route=src.route, ok=False, error_code="offline", at_ms=round_no,
 167:                 ))
 168:                 diag = diagnose_transfer({
 169:                     "status": "paused",
 170:                     "direction": "out",
 171:                     "metadata": {
 172:                         "delivery_state": "waiting_for_device",
 173:                         "error_class": "PeerOffline",
 174:                     },
 175:                 })
 176:                 doctor_codes.append(diag.code)
 177:                 continue
 178:             active_sources.append(src)
 179:         if not active_sources:
 180:             continue
 181: 
 182:         plan = plan_swarm_sources(
 183:             manifest=manifest,
 184:             needed_indexes=needed,
 185:             sources=[_source_to_plan_source(s, manifest) for s in active_sources],
 186:         )
 187:         if not plan.assignments:
 188:             continue
 189: 
 190:         for assignment in plan.assignments:
 191:             if assignment.status != "assigned" or assignment.source_peer_fp is None:
 192:                 continue
 193:             src = next(s for s in active_sources if s.peer_fp == assignment.source_peer_fp)
 194:             attempts += 1
 195:             chunk = by_hash[assignment.chunk_hash]
 196:             if src.old_version and rng.random() < 0.5:
 197:                 fallback_events += 1
 198:                 route_memory.observe(RouteObservation(
 199:                     route=src.route, ok=False, error_code="legacy_fallback", at_ms=round_no,
 200:                 ))
 201:                 doctor_codes.append(diagnose_transfer({
 202:                     "status": "paused",
 203:                     "direction": "out",
 204:                     "metadata": {
 205:                         "delivery_state": "resuming",
 206:                         "error_class": "ProtocolVersionMismatch",
 207:                     },
 208:                 }).code)
 209:                 retries += 1
 210:                 continue
 211:             if rng.random() < corruption_rate:
 212:                 corruptions += 1
 213:                 retries += 1
 214:                 route_memory.observe(RouteObservation(
 215:                     route=src.route, ok=False, error_code="chunk_integrity", at_ms=round_no,
 216:                 ))
 217:                 doctor_codes.append(diagnose_transfer({
 218:                     "status": "paused",
 219:                     "direction": "out",
 220:                     "metadata": {
 221:                         "delivery_state": "resuming",
 222:                         "error_class": "ChunkIntegrityError",
 223:                     },
 224:                 }).code)
 225:                 continue
 226:             delivered.add(chunk.index)
 227:             needed.discard(chunk.index)
 228:             if src.route == "prior":
 229:                 bytes_saved += chunk.size
 230:             else:
 231:                 bytes_sent += chunk.size
 232:             route_memory.observe(RouteObservation(
 233:                 route=src.route,
 234:                 ok=True,
 235:                 latency_ms=src.latency_ms,
 236:                 bandwidth_bps=src.bandwidth_bps,
 237:                 at_ms=round_no,
 238:             ))
 239:             if not needed:
 240:                 break
 241: 
 242:     delivered_ok = len(delivered) == len(manifest.chunks)
 243:     if delivered_ok:
 244:         doctor_codes.append("done")
 245:     route_scores = tuple(c.__dict__ for c in route_memory.candidates())
 246:     return TortureReport(
 247:         seed=seed,
 248:         file_size=size,
 249:         chunks_total=len(manifest.chunks),
 250:         chunks_done=len(delivered),
 251:         delivered=delivered_ok,
 252:         attempts=attempts,
 253:         retries=retries,
 254:         corruptions=corruptions,
 255:         offline_waits=offline_waits,
 256:         fallback_events=fallback_events,
 257:         bytes_sent=bytes_sent,
 258:         bytes_saved=bytes_saved,
 259:         doctor_states=tuple(dict.fromkeys(doctor_codes)),
 260:         best_route=route_memory.best_route(),
 261:         route_scores=route_scores,
 262:     )
 263: 
 264: 
 265: def simulate_autopilot_torture_matrix(
 266:     *,
 267:     size: int = 2 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
 268:     chunk_size: int = 16 * 1024 * 1024,
 269:     seeds: Iterable[int] = (3, 7, 11, 19),
 270: ) -> dict[str, object]:
 271:     """Run a small deterministic matrix of hard transfer conditions.
 272: 
 273:     This is the benchmark harness for the product promise: big sends should
 274:     finish under drops, corruption, sleep/reconnect, and version fallback.
 275:     It stays synthetic so CI can model multi-GB videos without disk I/O.
 276:     """
 277: 
 278:     scenarios = {
 279:         "clean_lan": {"drop_rate": 0.0, "corruption_rate": 0.0},
 280:         "sleepy_wifi": {"drop_rate": 0.22, "corruption_rate": 0.01},
 281:         "hostile_wifi": {"drop_rate": 0.35, "corruption_rate": 0.06},
 282:         "prior_knowledge": {"drop_rate": 0.05, "corruption_rate": 0.01},
 283:     }
 284:     reports = []
 285:     for name, params in scenarios.items():
 286:         for seed in seeds:
 287:             manifest = synthetic_manifest(size=size, chunk_size=chunk_size)
 288:             sources = None
 289:             if name == "prior_knowledge":
 290:                 all_indexes = frozenset(c.index for c in manifest.chunks)
 291:                 sources = (
 292:                     SimSource(
 293:                         "p" * 64,
 294:                         "prior",
 295:                         all_indexes,
 296:                         trust_score=2.0,
 297:                         latency_ms=1.0,
 298:                         bandwidth_bps=2_000_000_000,
 299:                         reliability=0.97,
 300:                     ),
 301:                     SimSource(
 302:                         "l" * 64,
 303:                         "lan",
 304:                         frozenset(i for i in all_indexes if i % 3 == 0),
 305:                         trust_score=1.5,
 306:                         latency_ms=5.0,
 307:                         bandwidth_bps=700_000_000,
 308:                         reliability=0.98,
 309:                     ),
 310:                 )
 311:             report = simulate_never_lose_transfer(
 312:                 size=size,
 313:                 chunk_size=chunk_size,
 314:                 seed=int(seed),
 315:                 sources=sources,
 316:                 max_rounds=80_000,
 317:                 **params,
 318:             )
 319:             row = report.to_dict()
 320:             row["scenario"] = name
 321:             row["efficiency_multiplier"] = round(
 322:                 report.file_size / max(1, report.bytes_sent),
 323:                 3,
 324:             )
 325:             reports.append(row)
 326:     delivered = sum(1 for r in reports if r["delivered"])
 327:     retries = sum(int(r["retries"]) for r in reports)
 328:     offline_waits = sum(int(r["offline_waits"]) for r in reports)
 329:     avg_efficiency = (
 330:         sum(float(r["efficiency_multiplier"]) for r in reports) / max(1, len(reports))
 331:     )
 332:     return {
 333:         "runs": len(reports),
 334:         "delivered": delivered,
 335:         "delivery_rate": round(delivered / max(1, len(reports)), 6),
 336:         "retries": retries,
 337:         "offline_waits": offline_waits,
 338:         "avg_efficiency_multiplier": round(avg_efficiency, 3),
 339:         "reports": reports,
 340:     }
 341: 
 342: 
 343: def main() -> int:
 344:     report = simulate_never_lose_transfer()
 345:     print("One Link never-lose transfer torture simulator")
 346:     for key, value in report.to_dict().items():
 347:         print(f"  {key}: {value}")
 348:     return 0 if report.delivered else 1
 349: 
 350: 
 351: if __name__ == "__main__":
 352:     raise SystemExit(main())

   1: """Activation policy for the Universal Comms Fabric.
   2: 
   3: The fabric is allowed to be ambitious, but transport activation must be boring
   4: in the best possible way: deterministic, auditable, deny-by-risk, and easy for
   5: the UI to explain. This module decides whether a discovered path may be used
   6: automatically, requires a user ceremony, or must remain disabled.
   7: """
   8: 
   9: from __future__ import annotations
  10: 
  11: from dataclasses import dataclass
  12: from enum import Enum
  13: from typing import Iterable, Mapping
  14: 
  15: from .transport_adapters.base import AdapterProbe, RouteScore
  16: 
  17: 
  18: class ActivationState(str, Enum):
  19:     ACTIVE = "active"
  20:     READY = "ready"
  21:     ASK_USER = "ask_user"
  22:     BLOCKED = "blocked"
  23:     UNAVAILABLE = "unavailable"
  24: 
  25: 
  26: class ActivationRisk(str, Enum):
  27:     LOW = "low"
  28:     MEDIUM = "medium"
  29:     HIGH = "high"
  30:     CRITICAL = "critical"
  31: 
  32: 
  33: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  34: class ActivationIntent:
  35:     """What the caller wants to move over a path."""
  36: 
  37:     needs_bulk: bool = True
  38:     needs_control: bool = True
  39:     cross_internet_ok: bool = True
  40:     offline_ok: bool = True
  41:     allow_admin: bool = False
  42:     allow_user_ceremony: bool = True
  43:     min_bps: float = 0.0
  44:     trusted_peer: bool = False
  45:     verified_peer: bool = False
  46: 
  47: 
  48: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  49: class ActivationPlan:
  50:     adapter_id: str
  51:     route_name: str
  52:     state: ActivationState
  53:     risk: ActivationRisk
  54:     score: float
  55:     automatic: bool
  56:     needs_user: bool
  57:     reason: str
  58:     next_action: str
  59:     safeguards: tuple[str, ...]
  60: 
  61:     def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
  62:         return {
  63:             "adapter_id": self.adapter_id,
  64:             "route_name": self.route_name,
  65:             "state": self.state.value,
  66:             "risk": self.risk.value,
  67:             "score": round(self.score, 6),
  68:             "automatic": self.automatic,
  69:             "needs_user": self.needs_user,
  70:             "reason": self.reason,
  71:             "next_action": self.next_action,
  72:             "safeguards": list(self.safeguards),
  73:         }
  74: 
  75: 
  76: def activation_plan_for(
  77:     score: RouteScore,
  78:     probe: AdapterProbe | None = None,
  79:     *,
  80:     intent: ActivationIntent | None = None,
  81:     peer: object | None = None,
  82: ) -> ActivationPlan:
  83:     """Return the activation decision for one scored path.
  84: 
  85:     ``peer`` is intentionally duck-typed. Current daemon peer records are not a
  86:     stable cross-layer type, so callers can pass any object exposing useful
  87:     trust/verification hints; missing attributes simply keep the policy
  88:     conservative.
  89:     """
  90: 
  91:     intent = intent or ActivationIntent()
  92:     trusted = intent.trusted_peer or _truthy_attr(peer, "trusted") or _trust_is_pinned(peer)
  93:     verified = intent.verified_peer or _truthy_attr(peer, "verified")
  94:     safeguards = _base_safeguards(score, probe)
  95: 
  96:     if score.score <= 0.0 or (probe is not None and not probe.available):
  97:         return ActivationPlan(
  98:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
  99:             route_name=score.route_name,
 100:             state=ActivationState.UNAVAILABLE,
 101:             risk=ActivationRisk.LOW,
 102:             score=0.0,
 103:             automatic=False,
 104:             needs_user=False,
 105:             reason=score.reason or "path unavailable",
 106:             next_action="wait_for_path",
 107:             safeguards=safeguards,
 108:         )
 109: 
 110:     if intent.needs_bulk and not score.usable_for_bulk:
 111:         return ActivationPlan(
 112:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 113:             route_name=score.route_name,
 114:             state=ActivationState.ASK_USER if score.usable_for_control else ActivationState.BLOCKED,
 115:             risk=ActivationRisk.MEDIUM,
 116:             score=min(score.score, 0.25),
 117:             automatic=False,
 118:             needs_user=score.usable_for_control,
 119:             reason="control-only path cannot carry this transfer",
 120:             next_action="use_for_pairing_or_find_bulk_path" if score.usable_for_control else "find_bulk_path",
 121:             safeguards=safeguards + ("bulk payloads are never forced through control-only hardware",),
 122:         )
 123: 
 124:     if intent.needs_control and not score.usable_for_control:
 125:         return ActivationPlan(
 126:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 127:             route_name=score.route_name,
 128:             state=ActivationState.BLOCKED,
 129:             risk=ActivationRisk.HIGH,
 130:             score=0.0,
 131:             automatic=False,
 132:             needs_user=False,
 133:             reason="path cannot carry required control handshake",
 134:             next_action="find_control_path",
 135:             safeguards=safeguards,
 136:         )
 137: 
 138:     if score.estimated_bps < intent.min_bps:
 139:         return ActivationPlan(
 140:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 141:             route_name=score.route_name,
 142:             state=ActivationState.READY,
 143:             risk=ActivationRisk.MEDIUM,
 144:             score=min(score.score, 0.40),
 145:             automatic=False,
 146:             needs_user=False,
 147:             reason="path is below the requested speed floor",
 148:             next_action="prefer_faster_path",
 149:             safeguards=safeguards,
 150:         )
 151: 
 152:     if _is_cross_internet(score) and not intent.cross_internet_ok:
 153:         return ActivationPlan(
 154:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 155:             route_name=score.route_name,
 156:             state=ActivationState.BLOCKED,
 157:             risk=ActivationRisk.HIGH,
 158:             score=0.0,
 159:             automatic=False,
 160:             needs_user=False,
 161:             reason="internet route disabled for this intent",
 162:             next_action="use_local_or_offline_path",
 163:             safeguards=safeguards,
 164:         )
 165: 
 166:     if score.route_name == "courier" and not intent.offline_ok:
 167:         return ActivationPlan(
 168:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 169:             route_name=score.route_name,
 170:             state=ActivationState.BLOCKED,
 171:             risk=ActivationRisk.MEDIUM,
 172:             score=0.0,
 173:             automatic=False,
 174:             needs_user=False,
 175:             reason="offline courier route disabled for this intent",
 176:             next_action="wait_for_live_path",
 177:             safeguards=safeguards,
 178:         )
 179: 
 180:     if probe is not None and probe.requires_admin and not intent.allow_admin:
 181:         return ActivationPlan(
 182:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 183:             route_name=score.route_name,
 184:             state=ActivationState.ASK_USER if intent.allow_user_ceremony else ActivationState.BLOCKED,
 185:             risk=ActivationRisk.HIGH,
 186:             score=min(score.score, 0.35),
 187:             automatic=False,
 188:             needs_user=intent.allow_user_ceremony,
 189:             reason="path requires elevated OS permission",
 190:             next_action="ask_user_for_permission" if intent.allow_user_ceremony else "choose_non_admin_path",
 191:             safeguards=safeguards + ("admin-required paths cannot auto-start",),
 192:         )
 193: 
 194:     if probe is not None and probe.requires_user_action:
 195:         return ActivationPlan(
 196:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 197:             route_name=score.route_name,
 198:             state=ActivationState.ASK_USER if intent.allow_user_ceremony else ActivationState.READY,
 199:             risk=_risk_for(score, probe),
 200:             score=min(score.score, 0.65),
 201:             automatic=False,
 202:             needs_user=intent.allow_user_ceremony,
 203:             reason="path needs a user-visible device ceremony",
 204:             next_action="ask_user_for_ceremony" if intent.allow_user_ceremony else "wait_for_existing_path",
 205:             safeguards=safeguards + ("user-ceremony paths are explicit and revocable",),
 206:         )
 207: 
 208:     risk = _risk_for(score, probe)
 209:     automatic = trusted and verified and risk in {ActivationRisk.LOW, ActivationRisk.MEDIUM}
 210:     if not trusted:
 211:         reason = "peer is not trusted yet"
 212:         next_action = "pair_and_verify_peer"
 213:         state = ActivationState.ASK_USER
 214:         needs_user = True
 215:     elif not verified and _is_sensitive_route(score):
 216:         reason = "peer identity needs verification before automatic activation"
 217:         next_action = "verify_peer"
 218:         state = ActivationState.ASK_USER
 219:         needs_user = True
 220:     elif risk == ActivationRisk.HIGH:
 221:         reason = "route is high risk and needs explicit approval"
 222:         next_action = "ask_user_for_route"
 223:         state = ActivationState.ASK_USER
 224:         needs_user = True
 225:     else:
 226:         reason = score.reason or "path ready"
 227:         next_action = "open_route" if automatic else "keep_ready"
 228:         state = ActivationState.ACTIVE if automatic else ActivationState.READY
 229:         needs_user = False
 230: 
 231:     return ActivationPlan(
 232:         adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
 233:         route_name=score.route_name,
 234:         state=state,
 235:         risk=risk,
 236:         score=score.score,
 237:         automatic=automatic,
 238:         needs_user=needs_user,
 239:         reason=reason,
 240:         next_action=next_action,
 241:         safeguards=safeguards,
 242:     )
 243: 
 244: 
 245: def activation_plans_for(
 246:     scores: Iterable[RouteScore],
 247:     probes: Iterable[AdapterProbe] = (),
 248:     *,
 249:     intent: ActivationIntent | None = None,
 250:     peer: object | None = None,
 251: ) -> tuple[ActivationPlan, ...]:
 252:     probes_by_id = {p.adapter_id: p for p in probes}
 253:     plans = [
 254:         activation_plan_for(
 255:             score,
 256:             probes_by_id.get(score.adapter_id),
 257:             intent=intent,
 258:             peer=peer,
 259:         )
 260:         for score in scores
 261:     ]
 262:     return tuple(sorted(
 263:         plans,
 264:         key=lambda p: (
 265:             _state_rank(p.state),
 266:             _risk_rank(p.risk),
 267:             -p.score,
 268:             p.route_name,
 269:             p.adapter_id,
 270:         ),
 271:     ))
 272: 
 273: 
 274: def _base_safeguards(score: RouteScore, probe: AdapterProbe | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 275:     out = [
 276:         "peer identity is verified above transport",
 277:         "all payload chunks are cryptographically verified",
 278:         "route can be dropped and reopened without losing the send intent",
 279:     ]
 280:     if score.usable_for_bulk:
 281:         out.append("bulk path uses backpressure and chunk-level retry")
 282:     if probe is not None and probe.requires_user_action:
 283:         out.append("activation is gated by explicit local device state")
 284:     if _is_cross_internet(score):
 285:         out.append("internet paths stay end-to-end encrypted and relay-blind")
 286:     if score.route_name in {"lan", "wifi_direct"}:
 287:         out.append("local paths never require cloud storage")
 288:     return tuple(dict.fromkeys(out))
 289: 
 290: 
 291: def _risk_for(score: RouteScore, probe: AdapterProbe | None) -> ActivationRisk:
 292:     if probe is not None and probe.safety_state not in {"ok", "ready", ""}:
 293:         return ActivationRisk.CRITICAL
 294:     if probe is not None and probe.requires_admin:
 295:         return ActivationRisk.HIGH
 296:     if _is_cross_internet(score):
 297:         return ActivationRisk.MEDIUM
 298:     if score.privacy in {"same_machine", "direct_local", "proximity"}:
 299:         return ActivationRisk.LOW
 300:     if score.privacy == "offline_physical":
 301:         return ActivationRisk.MEDIUM
 302:     if score.privacy == "experimental_hardware":
 303:         return ActivationRisk.HIGH
 304:     return ActivationRisk.MEDIUM
 305: 
 306: 
 307: def _is_cross_internet(score: RouteScore) -> bool:
 308:     return score.route_name in {"relay", "webrtc"} or score.privacy == "direct_or_relayed_internet"
 309: 
 310: 
 311: def _is_sensitive_route(score: RouteScore) -> bool:
 312:     return _is_cross_internet(score) or score.route_name in {"onefield", "courier"}
 313: 
 314: 
 315: def _state_rank(state: ActivationState) -> int:
 316:     return {
 317:         ActivationState.ACTIVE: 0,
 318:         ActivationState.READY: 1,
 319:         ActivationState.ASK_USER: 2,
 320:         ActivationState.UNAVAILABLE: 3,
 321:         ActivationState.BLOCKED: 4,
 322:     }[state]
 323: 
 324: 
 325: def _risk_rank(risk: ActivationRisk) -> int:
 326:     return {
 327:         ActivationRisk.LOW: 0,
 328:         ActivationRisk.MEDIUM: 1,
 329:         ActivationRisk.HIGH: 2,
 330:         ActivationRisk.CRITICAL: 3,
 331:     }[risk]
 332: 
 333: 
 334: def _truthy_attr(obj: object | None, name: str) -> bool:
 335:     if obj is None:
 336:         return False
 337:     return bool(getattr(obj, name, False))
 338: 
 339: 
 340: def _trust_is_pinned(obj: object | None) -> bool:
 341:     if obj is None:
 342:         return False
 343:     return str(getattr(obj, "trust", "") or "").lower() in {"pinned", "trusted", "verified"}
<<<CONTENT_END>>>

   1: """OneField software-loopback transport adapter.
   2: 
   3: This is the safe OneField bridge: it proves One Link encrypted frames can pass
   4: through a OneField-shaped transport without enabling RF transmit. Hardware
   5: helpers can later attach beneath this adapter contract once their safety gates
   6: are proven.
   7: """
   8: 
   9: from __future__ import annotations
  10: 
  11: import asyncio
  12: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  13: from time import perf_counter
  14: 
  15: from one_link.hardware_inventory import HardwarePath
  16: 
  17: from .base import AdapterProbe, PreparedRoute, RepairResult, RouteScore, SessionStats
  18: from .static import score_probe
  19: 
  20: 
  21: ONEFIELD_LOOPBACK_MTU = 64 * 1024
  22: 
  23: 
  24: @dataclass
  25: class OneFieldLoopbackSession:
  26:     mtu: int = ONEFIELD_LOOPBACK_MTU
  27:     ordered: bool = True
  28:     reliable: bool = True
  29:     bulk_capable: bool = True
  30:     control_capable: bool = True
  31:     max_queued_frames: int = 1024
  32:     _queue: asyncio.Queue[bytes] = field(init=False, repr=False)
  33:     _created: float = field(default_factory=perf_counter, init=False)
  34:     _bytes_sent: int = 0
  35:     _bytes_received: int = 0
  36:     _frames_sent: int = 0
  37:     _frames_received: int = 0
  38: 
  39:     def __post_init__(self) -> None:
  40:         self._queue = asyncio.Queue(maxsize=self.max_queued_frames)
  41: 
  42:     async def send_frame(self, frame: bytes) -> None:
  43:         data = bytes(frame)
  44:         if not data:
  45:             raise ValueError("onefield loopback frame cannot be empty")
  46:         if len(data) > self.mtu:
  47:             raise ValueError("onefield loopback frame exceeds mtu")
  48:         await self._queue.put(data)
  49:         self._bytes_sent += len(data)
  50:         self._frames_sent += 1
  51: 
  52:     async def recv_frame(self) -> bytes:
  53:         data = await self._queue.get()
  54:         self._bytes_received += len(data)
  55:         self._frames_received += 1
  56:         return data
  57: 
  58:     async def stats(self) -> SessionStats:
  59:         elapsed = max(0.001, perf_counter() - self._created)
  60:         return SessionStats(
  61:             bytes_sent=self._bytes_sent,
  62:             bytes_received=self._bytes_received,
  63:             frames_sent=self._frames_sent,
  64:             frames_received=self._frames_received,
  65:             rtt_ms=1.0,
  66:             measured_bps=(self._bytes_sent + self._bytes_received) / elapsed,
  67:             loss=0.0,
  68:         )
  69: 
  70:     async def repair(self, reason: str) -> RepairResult:
  71:         return RepairResult(
  72:             repaired=True,
  73:             action="onefield_loopback_queue_preserved",
  74:             reason=str(reason or "operator_requested_repair"),
  75:         )
  76: 
  77: 
  78: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  79: class OneFieldLoopbackAdapter:
  80:     path: HardwarePath
  81: 
  82:     @property
  83:     def adapter_id(self) -> str:
  84:         return self.path.adapter_id or "onefield.loopback"
  85: 
  86:     @property
  87:     def kind(self) -> str:
  88:         return "onefield"
  89: 
  90:     def probe(self) -> AdapterProbe:
  91:         loopback_only = "software loopback" in " ".join(self.path.notes).lower()
  92:         return AdapterProbe(
  93:             adapter_id=self.adapter_id,
  94:             kind="onefield",
  95:             available=bool(self.path.available and loopback_only),
  96:             bulk_capable=bool(self.path.bulk_capable and loopback_only),
  97:             control_capable=bool(self.path.control_capable),
  98:             estimated_bps=float(self.path.estimated_bps or 5_000_000.0),
  99:             latency_ms=1.0 if loopback_only else 250.0,
 100:             loss=0.0,
 101:             privacy="same_machine" if loopback_only else "experimental_hardware",
 102:             range_hint="software_loopback" if loopback_only else self.path.range_hint,
 103:             requires_user_action=not loopback_only,
 104:             requires_admin=False,
 105:             safety_state="ok" if loopback_only else "rx_only_until_safety_gate",
 106:             notes=(
 107:                 "software loopback; RF transmit disabled",
 108:                 "frames remain encrypted above the adapter",
 109:                 *tuple(n for n in self.path.notes if n),
 110:             ),
 111:         )
 112: 
 113:     def score(self, *, intent: object | None = None, peer: object | None = None) -> RouteScore:

 115:

 117:         self,
 118:         probe: AdapterProbe,
 119:         *,
 120:         intent: object | None = None,
 121:         peer: object | None = None,

 123:         return score_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer)

 125:     async def prepare(
 126:         self,
 127:         *,
 128:         peer: object | None = None,
 129:         intent: object | None = None,
 130:     ) -> PreparedRoute:
 131:         probe = self.probe()

 133:             raise RuntimeError("onefield loopback is not enabled")

 136:             route_name=probe.route_name,
 137:             metadata={

 140:                 "safety_state": probe.safety_state,
 141:             },
 142:         )
 143: 
 144:     async def open(self, route: PreparedRoute) -> OneFieldLoopbackSession:
 145:         if route.adapter_id != self.adapter_id:
 146:             raise RuntimeError("prepared route belongs to another adapter")
 147:         if route.metadata.get("rf_transmit") is not False:
 148:             raise RuntimeError("onefield loopback refuses RF transmit routes")
 149:         return OneFieldLoopbackSession()

   1: """Durable route-memory adapters for the Universal Comms Fabric.
   2: 
   3: Route candidates are concrete, key-confirmed ways we have learned to reach a
   4: peer: host/port/transport plus success/failure history. This adapter lets the
   5: fabric route brain rank those remembered paths as real transport evidence
   6: instead of showing them only as diagnostics.
   7: """
   8: 
   9: from __future__ import annotations
  10: 
  11: from dataclasses import dataclass
  12: from typing import Mapping
  13: 
  14: from .base import AdapterProbe, PreparedRoute, RouteScore, TransportSession
  15: from .static import score_probe
  16: 
  17: 
  18: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  19: class DurableRouteCandidateAdapter:
  20:     candidate: Mapping[str, object]
  21: 
  22:     @property
  23:     def adapter_id(self) -> str:
  24:         peer = str(self.candidate.get("peer_fp") or "")[:8] or "unknown"
  25:         route = self.kind
  26:         transport = str(self.candidate.get("transport") or "tcp")
  27:         host = str(self.candidate.get("host") or "unknown")
  28:         port = int(self.candidate.get("port") or 0)
  29:         return f"remembered.{peer}.{route}.{transport}.{host}.{port}"
  30: 
  31:     @property
  32:     def kind(self) -> str:
  33:         route = str(self.candidate.get("route") or "lan").lower()
  34:         if route == "internet":
  35:             return "webrtc"
  36:         if route == "sealed_relay":
  37:             return "sealed_relay"
  38:         if route == "relay":
  39:             return "sealed_relay"
  40:         return route or "lan"
  41: 
  42:     def probe(self) -> AdapterProbe:
  43:         attempts = max(0, int(self.candidate.get("attempts") or 0))
  44:         successes = max(0, int(self.candidate.get("successes") or 0))
  45:         failures = max(0, int(self.candidate.get("failures") or 0))
  46:         verified = bool(self.candidate.get("verified"))
  47:         reliability = (
  48:             successes / max(1, attempts)
  49:             if attempts
  50:             else (0.98 if verified else 0.50)
  51:         )
  52:         reliability = max(0.05, min(0.995, float(reliability)))
  53:         bps = float(self.candidate.get("bandwidth_bps") or _default_bps(self.kind))
  54:         latency = self.candidate.get("latency_ms")
  55:         latency_ms = float(latency) if isinstance(latency, (int, float)) else _default_latency_ms(self.kind)
  56:         return AdapterProbe(
  57:             adapter_id=self.adapter_id,
  58:             kind=self.kind,
  59:             available=verified,
  60:             bulk_capable=self.kind not in {"qr_control", "audio_control", "ble_control"},
  61:             control_capable=True,
  62:             estimated_bps=max(0.0, bps),
  63:             latency_ms=latency_ms,
  64:             loss=max(0.0, min(0.95, 1.0 - reliability)),
  65:             privacy=_privacy_for_route(self.kind),
  66:             range_hint="remembered",
  67:             safety_state="ok" if verified else "needs_verification",
  68:             notes=(
  69:                 f"remembered route from {self.candidate.get('source') or 'runtime'}",
  70:                 f"{successes} success, {failures} failure",
  71:             ),
  72:         )
  73: 
  74:     def score(self, *, intent: object | None = None, peer: object | None = None) -> RouteScore:
  75:         probe = self.probe()
  76:         return self.score_from_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer)
  77: 
  78:     def score_from_probe(
  79:         self,
  80:         probe: AdapterProbe,
  81:         *,
  82:         intent: object | None = None,
  83:         peer: object | None = None,
  84:     ) -> RouteScore:
  85:         score = score_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer)
  86:         verified_bonus = 0.10 if bool(self.candidate.get("verified")) else 0.0
  87:         success_bonus = min(0.10, 0.025 * int(self.candidate.get("successes") or 0))
  88:         failure_penalty = min(0.20, 0.04 * int(self.candidate.get("failures") or 0))
  89:         return RouteScore(
  90:             adapter_id=score.adapter_id,
  91:             route_name=score.route_name,
  92:             score=max(0.0, min(1.0, score.score + verified_bonus + success_bonus - failure_penalty)),
  93:             estimated_bps=score.estimated_bps,
  94:             latency_ms=score.latency_ms,
  95:             reliability=score.reliability,
  96:             privacy=score.privacy,
  97:             reason=(
  98:                 "verified remembered route"
  99:                 if bool(self.candidate.get("verified"))
 100:                 else "remembered route awaiting verification"
 101:             ),
 102:             usable_for_bulk=score.usable_for_bulk,
 103:             usable_for_control=score.usable_for_control,
 104:         )
 105: 
 106:     async def prepare(
 107:         self,
 108:         *,
 109:         peer: object | None = None,
 110:         intent: object | None = None,
 111:     ) -> PreparedRoute:
 112:         return PreparedRoute(
 113:             adapter_id=self.adapter_id,
 114:             route_name=self.probe().route_name,

   1: """Safe initial adapters for the Universal Comms Fabric.
   2: 
   3: These adapters do not create networks yet. They expose existing or planned
   4: paths to the route brain in a deterministic way so daemon integration can
   5: begin without destabilizing current transfers.
   6: """
   7: 
   8: from __future__ import annotations
   9: 
  10: from dataclasses import dataclass
  11: 
  12: from one_link.hardware_inventory import HardwarePath
  13: 
  14: from .base import AdapterProbe, PreparedRoute, RouteScore
  15: 
  16: 
  17: _PRIVACY_WEIGHT = {
  18:     "same_machine": 1.0,
  19:     "direct_local": 0.95,
  20:     "offline_physical": 0.90,
  21:     "proximity": 0.82,
  22:     "in_person": 0.82,
  23:     "direct_or_relayed_internet": 0.62,
  24:     "experimental_hardware": 0.40,
  25: }
  26: 
  27: 
  28: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  29: class StaticPathAdapter:
  30:     """Adapter backed by a HardwarePath snapshot."""
  31: 
  32:     path: HardwarePath
  33: 
  34:     @property
  35:     def adapter_id(self) -> str:
  36:         return self.path.adapter_id or self.path.kind
  37: 
  38:     @property
  39:     def kind(self) -> str:
  40:         return self.path.kind
  41: 
  42:     def probe(self) -> AdapterProbe:
  43:         return AdapterProbe(
  44:             adapter_id=self.adapter_id,
  45:             kind=self.path.kind,
  46:             available=self.path.available,
  47:             bulk_capable=self.path.bulk_capable,
  48:             control_capable=self.path.control_capable,
  49:             estimated_bps=float(self.path.estimated_bps),
  50:             latency_ms=_default_latency_ms(self.path.kind),
  51:             privacy=self.path.privacy,
  52:             range_hint=self.path.range_hint,
  53:             requires_user_action=self.path.requires_user_action,
  54:             requires_admin=self.path.requires_admin,
  55:             safety_state=self.path.safety_state,
  56:             notes=self.path.notes,
  57:         )
  58: 
  59:     def score(self, *, intent: object | None = None, peer: object | None = None) -> RouteScore:
  60:         probe = self.probe()
  61:         return score_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer)
  62: 
  63:     def score_from_probe(
  64:         self,
  65:         probe: AdapterProbe,
  66:         *,
  67:         intent: object | None = None,
  68:         peer: object | None = None,
  69:     ) -> RouteScore:
  70:         return score_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer)
  71: 
  72:     async def prepare(
  73:         self,
  74:         *,
  75:         peer: object | None = None,
  76:         intent: object | None = None,
  77:     ) -> PreparedRoute:
  78:         return PreparedRoute(
  79:             adapter_id=self.adapter_id,
  80:             route_name=self.probe().route_name,
  81:             metadata={
  82:                 "kind": self.kind,
  83:                 "probe_only": True,
  84:                 "notes": list(self.path.notes),
  85:             },
  86:         )
  87: 
  88: 
  89: def score_probe(
  90:     probe: AdapterProbe,
  91:     *,
  92:     intent: object | None = None,
  93:     peer: object | None = None,
  94: ) -> RouteScore:
  95:     """Score a route candidate using only truthful probe-level evidence."""
  96: 
  97:     if not probe.available:
  98:         return RouteScore(
  99:             adapter_id=probe.adapter_id,
 100:             route_name=probe.route_name,
 101:             score=0.0,
 102:             estimated_bps=0.0,
 103:             latency_ms=probe.latency_ms,
 104:             reliability=0.0,
 105:             privacy=probe.privacy,
 106:             reason="adapter unavailable",
 107:             usable_for_bulk=False,
 108:             usable_for_control=False,
 109:         )
 110:     speed_score = min(1.0, max(0.0, probe.estimated_bps) / 1_000_000_000.0)
 111:     latency = probe.latency_ms if probe.latency_ms is not None else _default_latency_ms(probe.kind)
 112:     latency_score = 1.0 / (1.0 + max(0.0, latency) / 50.0)
 113:     privacy_score = _PRIVACY_WEIGHT.get(probe.privacy, 0.5)
 114:     friction = 0.22 if probe.requires_user_action else 0.0
 115:     admin = 0.20 if probe.requires_admin else 0.0
 116:     safety = 0.30 if probe.safety_state not in {"ok", "rx_only_until_safety_gate"} else 0.0
 117:     bulk_weight = 1.0 if probe.bulk_capable else 0.45
 118:     reliability = max(0.05, min(0.995, 1.0 - float(probe.loss)))
 119:     score = (
 120:         0.34 * speed_score * bulk_weight
 121:         + 0.22 * latency_score
 122:         + 0.20 * privacy_score
 123:         + 0.16 * reliability
 124:         + 0.08 * (1.0 if probe.control_capable else 0.0)
 125:         - friction
 126:         - admin
 127:         - safety
 128:     )
 129:     return RouteScore(
 130:         adapter_id=probe.adapter_id,
 131:         route_name=probe.route_name,
 132:         score=max(0.0, min(1.0, score)),
 133:         estimated_bps=max(0.0, float(probe.estimated_bps)),
 134:         latency_ms=latency,
 135:         reliability=reliability,
 136:         privacy=probe.privacy,
 137:         reason=_score_reason(probe),
 138:         usable_for_bulk=probe.available and probe.bulk_capable,
 139:         usable_for_control=probe.available and probe.control_capable,
 140:     )
 141: 
 142: 
 143: def adapters_from_paths(paths: tuple[HardwarePath, ...] | list[HardwarePath]) -> tuple[StaticPathAdapter, ...]:
 144:     return tuple(StaticPathAdapter(p) for p in paths)
 145: 
 146: 
 147: def _default_latency_ms(kind: str) -> float:
 148:     return {
 149:         "loopback": 1.0,
 150:         "lan": 6.0,
 151:         "ethernet": 2.0,
 152:         "wifi_direct": 7.0,
 153:         "private_hotspot": 10.0,
 154:         "webrtc": 70.0,
 155:         "sealed_relay": 120.0,
 156:         "ble_control": 45.0,
 157:         "qr_control": 500.0,
 158:         "audio_control": 700.0,
 159:         "storage_courier": 10_000.0,
 160:         "onefield": 250.0,
 161:     }.get(kind, 100.0)
 162: 
 163: 
 164: def _score_reason(probe: AdapterProbe) -> str:
 165:     if probe.bulk_capable and probe.control_capable:
 166:         return f"{probe.kind} can carry control and bulk data"
 167:     if probe.control_capable:
 168:         return f"{probe.kind} is control-plane only"
 169:     return f"{probe.kind} is visible but not usable yet"

   1: """TCP transport sessions for concrete fabric routes.
   2: 
   3: The fabric adapter contract sits below One Link's identity, capability,
   4: channel crypto, and chunk verification. This module therefore only opens a
   5: byte pipe and preserves frame boundaries with the existing wire framing.
   6: """
   7: 
   8: from __future__ import annotations
   9: 
  10: import asyncio
  11: import time
  12: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  13: 
  14: from one_link.wire import read_frame, write_frame
  15: 
  16: from .base import PreparedRoute, RepairResult, SessionStats
  17: 
  18: 
  19: @dataclass
  20: class TcpStreamSession:
  21:     reader: asyncio.StreamReader
  22:     writer: asyncio.StreamWriter
  23:     route: PreparedRoute
  24:     mtu: int = 16 * 1024 * 1024
  25:     ordered: bool = True
  26:     reliable: bool = True
  27:     bulk_capable: bool = True
  28:     control_capable: bool = True
  29:     _bytes_sent: int = 0
  30:     _bytes_received: int = 0
  31:     _frames_sent: int = 0
  32:     _frames_received: int = 0
  33:     _opened_ns: int = field(default_factory=time.perf_counter_ns)
  34: 
  35:     async def send_frame(self, frame: bytes) -> None:
  36:         await write_frame(self.writer, bytes(frame))
  37:         self._bytes_sent += len(frame)
  38:         self._frames_sent += 1
  39: 
  40:     async def recv_frame(self) -> bytes:
  41:         frame = await read_frame(self.reader)
  42:         self._bytes_received += len(frame)
  43:         self._frames_received += 1
  44:         return frame
  45: 
  46:     async def stats(self) -> SessionStats:
  47:         elapsed_s = max(1e-9, (time.perf_counter_ns() - self._opened_ns) / 1_000_000_000)
  48:         measured_bps = float((self._bytes_sent + self._bytes_received) * 8) / elapsed_s
  49:         return SessionStats(
  50:             bytes_sent=self._bytes_sent,
  51:             bytes_received=self._bytes_received,
  52:             frames_sent=self._frames_sent,
  53:             frames_received=self._frames_received,
  54:             measured_bps=measured_bps,
  55:         )
  56: 
  57:     async def repair(self, reason: str) -> RepairResult:
  58:         return RepairResult(
  59:             repaired=False,
  60:             action="reopen_route",
  61:             retry_after_s=0.0,
  62:             reason=str(reason or "tcp session must be reopened"),
  63:         )
  64: 
  65:     async def close(self) -> None:
  66:         self.writer.close()
  67:         await self.writer.wait_closed()
  68: 
  69: 
  70: async def open_tcp_route(route: PreparedRoute, *, timeout_s: float = 5.0) -> TcpStreamSession:
  71:     host, port = _endpoint_host_port(route.endpoint)
  72:     reader, writer = await asyncio.wait_for(
  73:         asyncio.open_connection(host, port),
  74:         timeout=max(0.1, float(timeout_s)),
  75:     )
  76:     return TcpStreamSession(reader=reader, writer=writer, route=route)
  77: 
  78: 
  79: def _endpoint_host_port(endpoint: str | None) -> tuple[str, int]:
  80:     if not endpoint:
  81:         raise ValueError("tcp route is missing endpoint")
  82:     if endpoint.startswith("["):
  83:         host, _, rest = endpoint[1:].partition("]")
  84:         if not host or not rest.startswith(":"):
  85:             raise ValueError("invalid bracketed IPv6 endpoint")
  86:         port_s = rest[1:]
  87:     else:
  88:         host, sep, port_s = endpoint.rpartition(":")
  89:         if not sep or not host:
  90:             raise ValueError("invalid tcp endpoint")
  91:     port = int(port_s)
  92:     if port <= 0 or port > 65535:
  93:         raise ValueError("tcp endpoint port must be 1..65535")
  94:     return host, port

   1: """Universal Comms Fabric route spine.
   2: 
   3: This module connects the new hardware/adapter world to One Link's existing
   4: AdaptiveTransferBrain. It does not replace the live daemon path yet; it
   5: produces deterministic route truth that the daemon can opt into.

  48: 
  49:     def route_truth(self) -> dict[str, object]:
  50:         best = self.best_score
  51:         activation = self.best_activation
  52:         decision = self.transfer_decision.to_dict()
  53:         return {
  54:             "route": best.route_name if best else decision.get("route"),
  55:             "adapter_id": best.adapter_id if best else None,
  56:             "kind": _user_route_kind(best) if best else "Waiting for device",
  57:             "state": _state_from_decision(decision),

  64:             "activation_risk": activation.risk.value if activation else "low",

  66:             "automatic": bool(activation and activation.automatic),
  67:             "needs_user": bool(activation and activation.needs_user),
  68:             "safeguards": list(activation.safeguards) if activation else [],
  69:             "transfer": decision,
  70:         }
  71: 
  72:     def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
  73:         return {
  74:             "probes": [p.to_dict() for p in self.probes],
  75:             "scores": [s.to_dict() for s in self.scores],
  76:             "activation": [a.to_dict() for a in self.activation],
  77:             "observations": [
  78:                 {

  82:                     "bandwidth_bps": o.bandwidth_bps,
  83:                     "energy_cost": o.energy_cost,

  91: 
  92: class UniversalCommsFabric:
  93:     """Probe adapters and feed route evidence into the transfer brain."""
  94: 
  95:     def __init__(self, adapters: Iterable[TransportAdapter]) -> None:
  96:         self._adapters = tuple(adapters)
  97: 
  98:     @classmethod
  99:     def from_inventory(cls, inventory: HardwareInventory | None = None) -> "UniversalCommsFabric":

 102: 
 103:     @classmethod
 104:     def from_inventory_and_candidates(

 108:     ) -> "UniversalCommsFabric":
 109:         inventory = inventory or collect_hardware_inventory()
 110:         remembered = adapters_from_route_candidates(tuple(candidates or ()))
 111:         return cls((*_adapters_from_inventory_paths(inventory.paths), *remembered))
