 113:     def probes(self) -> tuple[AdapterProbe, ...]:
 114:         out: list[AdapterProbe] = []
 115:         for adapter in self._adapters:
 116:             try:
 117:                 out.append(adapter.probe())
 118:             except Exception as exc:
 119:                 adapter_id = getattr(adapter, "adapter_id", adapter.__class__.__name__)
 120:                 kind = getattr(adapter, "kind", "unknown")
 121:                 out.append(AdapterProbe(
 122:                     adapter_id=str(adapter_id),
 123:                     kind=str(kind),
 124:                     available=False,
 125:                     notes=(f"probe failed: {exc}",),
 126:                 ))
 127:         return tuple(out)
 128: 
 129:     def scores(
 130:         self,
 131:         *,
 132:         intent: object | None = None,
 133:         peer: object | None = None,
 134:         probes: Iterable[AdapterProbe] | None = None,
 135:     ) -> tuple[RouteScore, ...]:
 136:         scored: list[RouteScore] = []
 137:         probes_by_id = {p.adapter_id: p for p in tuple(probes or ())}
 138:         for adapter in self._adapters:
 139:             try:
 140:                 adapter_id = str(getattr(adapter, "adapter_id", ""))
 141:                 probe = probes_by_id.get(adapter_id)
 142:                 score_from_probe = getattr(adapter, "score_from_probe", None)
 143:                 if probe is not None and callable(score_from_probe):
 144:                     scored.append(score_from_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer))
 145:                 else:
 146:                     scored.append(adapter.score(intent=intent, peer=peer))
 147:             except Exception:
 148:                 try:
 149:                     probe = probes_by_id.get(str(getattr(adapter, "adapter_id", ""))) or adapter.probe()
 150:                     scored.append(score_probe(probe, intent=intent, peer=peer))
 151:                 except Exception as exc:
 152:                     adapter_id = getattr(adapter, "adapter_id", adapter.__class__.__name__)
 153:                     kind = getattr(adapter, "kind", "unknown")
 154:                     scored.append(RouteScore(
 155:                         adapter_id=str(adapter_id),
 156:                         route_name=str(kind),
 157:                         score=0.0,
 158:                         estimated_bps=0.0,
 159:                         latency_ms=None,
 160:                         reliability=0.0,
 161:                         privacy="unknown",
 162:                         reason=f"score failed: {exc}",
 163:                     ))
 164:         return tuple(sorted(
 165:             scored,
 166:             key=lambda s: (
 167:                 -s.score,
 168:                 -s.estimated_bps,
 169:                 s.latency_ms if s.latency_ms is not None else 1_000_000.0,
 170:                 s.adapter_id,
 171:             ),
 172:         ))
 173: 
 174:     def plan(
 175:         self,
 176:         *,
 177:         size_bytes: int,
 178:         supports_cdc: bool,
 179:         supports_swarm: bool = False,
 180:         prior_hit_rate: float | None = None,
 181:         mesh_nodes: Iterable[MeshNodeSignal] | None = None,
 182:         speeds: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
 183:         activation_intent: ActivationIntent | None = None,
 184:         intent: object | None = None,
 185:         peer: object | None = None,
 186:     ) -> FabricPlan:
 187:         t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
 188:         probes = self.probes()
 189:         t_probes = time.perf_counter_ns()
 190:         scores = self.scores(intent=intent, peer=peer, probes=probes)
 191:         t_scores = time.perf_counter_ns()
 192:         activation = activation_plans_for(
 193:             scores,
 194:             probes,
 195:             intent=activation_intent,
 196:             peer=peer,
 197:         )
 198:         t_activation = time.perf_counter_ns()
 199:         observations = observations_from_scores(scores)
 200:         t_observations = time.perf_counter_ns()
 201:         live_bulk_routes = tuple(dict.fromkeys(
 202:             s.route_name
 203:             for s in scores
 204:             if s.score > 0.0 and s.usable_for_bulk and s.route_name not in {"courier"}
 205:         ))
 206:         fallback_routes = tuple(dict.fromkeys(s.route_name for s in scores if s.score > 0.0))
 207:         routes = live_bulk_routes or fallback_routes
 208:         decision = decision_from_observations(
 209:             size_bytes=size_bytes,
 210:             supports_cdc=supports_cdc,
 211:             supports_swarm=supports_swarm,
 212:             prior_hit_rate=prior_hit_rate,
 213:             observations=observations,
 214:             routes=routes or ("offline",),
 215:             mesh_nodes=mesh_nodes,
 216:             speeds=speeds,
 217:         )
 218:         t_decision = time.perf_counter_ns()
 219:         timing_ms = {
 220:             "adapter_count": float(len(self._adapters)),
 221:             "probe_ms": _elapsed_ms(t0, t_probes),
 222:             "score_ms": _elapsed_ms(t_probes, t_scores),
 223:             "activation_ms": _elapsed_ms(t_scores, t_activation),
 224:             "observation_ms": _elapsed_ms(t_activation, t_observations),
 225:             "decision_ms": _elapsed_ms(t_observations, t_decision),
 226:             "total_ms": _elapsed_ms(t0, t_decision),
 227:         }
 228:         timing_ms["health"] = _timing_health(timing_ms["total_ms"], len(self._adapters))
 229:         return FabricPlan(
 230:             probes=probes,
 231:             scores=scores,
 232:             activation=activation,
 233:             observations=observations,
 234:             transfer_decision=decision,
 235:             timing_ms=timing_ms,
 236:         )
 237: 
 238: 
 239: def observations_from_scores(scores: Iterable[RouteScore]) -> tuple[TransferRouteObservation, ...]:
 240:     out: list[TransferRouteObservation] = []
 241:     for score in scores:
 242:         if score.score <= 0.0:
 243:             out.append(TransferRouteObservation(
 244:                 route=score.route_name,
 245:                 ok=False,
 246:                 latency_ms=score.latency_ms,
 247:                 bandwidth_bps=0.0,
 248:                 energy_cost=2.0,
 249:             ))
 250:             continue
 251:         energy = 1.0
 252:         if score.privacy in {"direct_or_relayed_internet", "experimental_hardware"}:
 253:             energy += 0.35
 254:         if not score.usable_for_bulk:
 255:             energy += 0.45
 256:         out.append(TransferRouteObservation(
 257:             route=score.route_name,
 258:             ok=True,
 259:             latency_ms=score.latency_ms,
 260:             bandwidth_bps=score.estimated_bps,
 261:             energy_cost=energy,
 262:         ))
 263:     return tuple(out)
 264: 
 265: 
 266: def _adapters_from_inventory_paths(paths: tuple | list) -> tuple[TransportAdapter, ...]:
 267:     static_paths = tuple(p for p in paths if getattr(p, "kind", "") != "onefield")
 268:     onefield = onefield_adapters_from_paths(paths)
 269:     return (*adapters_from_paths(static_paths), *onefield)
 270: 
 271: 
 272: def _user_route_kind(score: RouteScore | None) -> str:
 273:     if score is None:
 274:         return "Waiting for device"
 275:     return {
 276:         "lan": "Local network",
 277:         "loopback": "This device",
 278:         "wifi_direct": "Wi-Fi direct",
 279:         "private_hotspot": "Private hotspot",
 280:         "webrtc": "Internet direct",
 281:         "relay": "Relay fallback",
 282:         "courier": "Offline courier",
 283:         "onefield": "OneField hardware",
 284:         "ble_control": "Bluetooth control",
 285:     }.get(score.route_name, score.route_name.replace("_", " ").title())
 286: 
 287: 
 288: def _state_from_decision(decision: Mapping[str, object]) -> str:
 289:     action = str(decision.get("action") or "")
 290:     health = str(decision.get("health") or "")
 291:     if action == "send" and health == "healthy":
 292:         return "Sending"
 293:     if "repair" in action or health == "repair":
 294:         return "Repairing route"
 295:     if action == "collect_more_route_evidence":
 296:         return "Measuring route"
 297:     return "Ready"
 298: 
 299: 
 300: def _elapsed_ms(start_ns: int, end_ns: int) -> float:
 301:     return round(max(0, end_ns - start_ns) / 1_000_000.0, 3)
 302: 
 303: 
 304: def _timing_health(total_ms: float, adapter_count: int) -> str:
 305:     # A route brain that scans hundreds of candidates should still feel
 306:     # instant. Scale the budget gently with adapter count so large trusted
 307:     # meshes are judged fairly without hiding pathological slowness.
 308:     budget_ms = 8.0 + min(92.0, max(0, adapter_count) * 0.18)
 309:     if total_ms <= budget_ms:
 310:         return "fast"
 311:     if total_ms <= budget_ms * 2.5:
 312:         return "warm"
 313:     return "slow"

 140: def creation_summary(plans: Iterable[PathCreationPlan]) -> dict[str, object]:
 141:     items = tuple(plans)
 142:     ready = sum(1 for p in items if p.state == "ready")
 143:     needs_user = sum(1 for p in items if p.state == "needs_user")
 144:     blocked = sum(1 for p in items if p.state == "blocked")
 145:     unsupported = sum(1 for p in items if p.state == "unsupported")
 146:     next_plan = next(
 147:         (
 148:             p for p in items
 149:             if p.state in {"ready", "needs_user"}
 150:         ),
 151:         items[0] if items else None,
 152:     )
 153:     return {
 154:         "ready": ready,
 155:         "needs_user": needs_user,
 156:         "blocked": blocked,
 157:         "unsupported": unsupported,
 158:         "next_action": next_plan.action if next_plan else "wait_for_path",
 159:         "plans": [p.to_dict() for p in items],
 160:     }

 163: def launch_creation_plan(
 164:     path_id: str,
 165:     plans: Iterable[PathCreationPlan],
 166:     *,
 167:     dry_run: bool = False,
 168:     system: str | None = None,
 169:     launcher: LaunchFn | None = None,
 170: ) -> dict[str, object]:
 171:     """Launch a user-visible OS ceremony for a creation plan.
 172: 
 173:     This never toggles radios or creates networks silently. It only opens the
 174:     operating system surface described by a plan that is already marked
 175:     ``needs_user`` or ``ready``.
 176:     """
 177: 
 178:     plan = next((p for p in plans if p.path_id == path_id), None)
 179:     if plan is None:
 180:         raise ValueError("unknown path creation plan")
 181:     if plan.state not in {"ready", "needs_user"}:
 182:         raise ValueError(f"path creation plan is {plan.state}")
 183:     if plan.automatic:
 184:         raise ValueError("automatic path creation is not exposed by this launcher")
 185:     if not plan.settings_uri and not plan.command:
 186:         raise ValueError("path creation plan has no launchable OS ceremony")
 187:     system = (system or platform.system()).lower()
 188:     if not dry_run:
 189:         (launcher or _default_launcher)(plan, system)
 190:     return {
 191:         "ok": True,
 192:         "launched": not dry_run,
 193:         "dry_run": dry_run,
 194:         "path_id": plan.path_id,
 195:         "action": plan.action,
 196:         "settings_uri": plan.settings_uri,
 197:         "command": list(plan.command),
 198:         "safeguards": list(plan.safeguards),
 199:     }

 202: def execute_native_creation_plan(
 203:     path_id: str,
 204:     plans: Iterable[PathCreationPlan],
 205:     *,
 206:     system: str | None = None,
 207:     allow_native: bool = False,
 208:     dry_run: bool = False,
 209:     ssid: str | None = None,
 210:     passphrase: str | None = None,
 211:     runner: NativeRunner | None = None,
 212:     helper_specs: Iterable[NativePathHelper] = (),
 213: ) -> dict[str, object]:
 214:     """Execute a supported native path-creation command.
 215: 
 216:     Only a tiny set of OS command surfaces qualify here. Unsupported surfaces
 217:     return structured evidence instead of pretending a platform can silently
 218:     create a radio path.
 219:     """
 220: 
 221:     plan = next((p for p in plans if p.path_id == path_id), None)
 222:     if plan is None:
 223:         raise ValueError("unknown path creation plan")
 224:     system = (system or platform.system()).lower()
 225:     if path_id == "direct_ethernet":
 226:         return {
 227:             "ok": True,
 228:             "state": "no_op",
 229:             "path_id": path_id,
 230:             "dry_run": dry_run,
 231:             "commands": [],
 232:             "message": "direct Ethernet is created by attaching the cable or switch",
 233:             "safeguards": list(plan.safeguards),
 234:         }
 235:     if path_id == "private_hotspot" and system == "windows":
 236:         return _execute_windows_hosted_network(
 237:             plan,
 238:             allow_native=allow_native,
 239:             dry_run=dry_run,
 240:             ssid=ssid,
 241:             passphrase=passphrase,
 242:             runner=runner,
 243:         )
 244:     helper = next(
 245:         (h for h in helper_specs if h.applies_to(path_id, system)),
 246:         None,
 247:     )
 248:     if helper is not None:
 249:         return _execute_native_helper(
 250:             plan,
 251:             helper,
 252:             system=system,
 253:             allow_native=allow_native,
 254:             dry_run=dry_run,
 255:             runner=runner,
 256:         )
 257:     if path_id in {"wifi_direct", "ble_control"}:
 258:         raise ValueError(f"{path_id} has no safe silent native creation API on {system}")
 259:     raise ValueError(f"{path_id} native creation is unsupported on {system}")
 260: 
 261: 
 262: def native_helpers_from_env(
 263:     env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
 264: ) -> tuple[NativePathHelper, ...]:
 265:     """Load explicit native helper registrations from environment JSON.
 266: 
 267:     ONE_LINK_NATIVE_PATH_HELPERS is a JSON list of objects:
 268:     {"path_id":"wifi_direct","command":["C:/.../helper.exe"],"supported_systems":["windows"]}
 269:     """
 270: 
 271:     env = env or os.environ
 272:     raw = str(env.get("ONE_LINK_NATIVE_PATH_HELPERS") or "").strip()
 273:     if not raw:
 274:         return ()
 275:     try:
 276:         data = json.loads(raw)
 277:     except Exception as exc:
 278:         raise ValueError(f"invalid ONE_LINK_NATIVE_PATH_HELPERS JSON: {exc}") from exc
 279:     if not isinstance(data, list) or len(data) > 16:
 280:         raise ValueError("native helper registry must be a list of at most 16 helpers")
 281:     out: list[NativePathHelper] = []
 282:     for item in data:
 283:         if not isinstance(item, dict):
 284:             raise ValueError("native helper registry entries must be objects")
 285:         command = item.get("command")
 286:         if not isinstance(command, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in command):
 287:             raise ValueError("native helper command must be a string list")
 288:         systems = item.get("supported_systems")
 289:         if systems is None:
 290:             systems = []
 291:         if not isinstance(systems, list) or not all(isinstance(x, str) for x in systems):
 292:             raise ValueError("native helper supported_systems must be a string list")
 293:         out.append(NativePathHelper(
 294:             path_id=str(item.get("path_id") or ""),
 295:             label=str(item.get("label") or ""),
 296:             version=str(item.get("version") or ""),
 297:             command=tuple(command),
 298:             supported_systems=tuple(systems),
 299:             requires_admin=bool(item.get("requires_admin")),
 300:         ))
 301:     return tuple(out)

 304: def _ethernet_plan(path: HardwarePath | None) -> PathCreationPlan:
 305:     available = bool(path and path.available)
 306:     return PathCreationPlan(
 307:         path_id="direct_ethernet",
 308:         label="Direct Ethernet",
 309:         state="ready" if available else "needs_user",
 310:         action="exchange_route_token" if available else "connect_ethernet_or_same_switch",
 311:         automatic=available,
 312:         requires_user_action=not available,
 313:         requires_admin=False,
 314:         bulk_capable=True,
 315:         control_capable=True,
 316:         estimated_bps=float(path.estimated_bps if path else 1_000_000_000.0),
 317:         reason=(
 318:             "link-local Ethernet is already visible"
 319:             if available else
 320:             "connect both devices with Ethernet or the same unmanaged switch"
 321:         ),
 322:         guide_steps=(
 323:             "connect cable or switch",
 324:             "wait for link-local address",
 325:             "exchange route token",
 326:             "verify pinned peer key",
 327:         ),
 328:         safeguards=_base_safeguards() + ("no OS network creation required",),
 329:     )

 332: def _hotspot_plan(path: HardwarePath | None, *, system: str) -> PathCreationPlan:
 333:     available = bool(path and path.available)
 334:     if not available:
 335:         return _unsupported(
 336:             "private_hotspot",
 337:             "Private hotspot",
 338:             "private hotspot capability was not detected",
 339:             bulk=True,
 340:         )
 341:     if system == "windows":
 342:         return PathCreationPlan(
 343:             path_id="private_hotspot",
 344:             label="Private hotspot",
 345:             state="needs_user",
 346:             action="open_windows_hotspot_settings",
 347:             automatic=False,
 348:             requires_user_action=True,
 349:             requires_admin=bool(path.requires_admin),
 350:             bulk_capable=True,
 351:             control_capable=True,
 352:             estimated_bps=float(path.estimated_bps or 300_000_000.0),
 353:             command=("start", "ms-settings:network-mobilehotspot"),
 354:             settings_uri="ms-settings:network-mobilehotspot",
 355:             reason="Windows hotspot must be confirmed in OS settings",
 356:             guide_steps=(
 357:                 "open mobile hotspot settings",
 358:                 "turn on hotspot",
 359:                 "join the other device to it",
 360:                 "exchange route token",
 361:             ),
 362:             safeguards=_base_safeguards() + (
 363:                 "hotspot creation is user-visible",
 364:                 "credentials are never published to rendezvous",
 365:             ),
 366:         )
 367:     return PathCreationPlan(
 368:         path_id="private_hotspot",
 369:         label="Private hotspot",
 370:         state="needs_user",
 371:         action="open_os_hotspot_settings",
 372:         automatic=False,
 373:         requires_user_action=True,
 374:         requires_admin=bool(path.requires_admin),
 375:         bulk_capable=True,
 376:         control_capable=True,
 377:         estimated_bps=float(path.estimated_bps or 180_000_000.0),
 378:         reason=f"{system or 'this platform'} requires a user-visible hotspot ceremony",
 379:         guide_steps=(
 380:             "open OS hotspot settings",
 381:             "turn on hotspot",
 382:             "join the other device to it",
 383:             "exchange route token",
 384:         ),
 385:         safeguards=_base_safeguards() + ("hotspot creation is explicit",),
 386:     )

 460: def _unsupported(
 461:     path_id: str,
 462:     label: str,
 463:     reason: str,
 464:     *,
 465:     bulk: bool,
 466: ) -> PathCreationPlan:
 467:     return PathCreationPlan(
 468:         path_id=path_id,
 469:         label=label,
 470:         state="unsupported",
 471:         action="wait_for_capability",
 472:         automatic=False,
 473:         requires_user_action=False,
 474:         requires_admin=False,
 475:         bulk_capable=bulk,
 476:         control_capable=True,
 477:         estimated_bps=0.0,
 478:         reason=reason,
 479:         guide_steps=("use Ethernet, same LAN, route token, or courier fallback",),
 480:         safeguards=_base_safeguards(),

 483: 
 484: def _base_safeguards() -> tuple[str, ...]:
 485:     return (
 486:         "creation plans never bypass pairing",
 487:         "route tokens carry endpoint hints only",
 488:         "local endpoints require key-confirmed promotion",
 489:     )

 492: def _default_launcher(plan: PathCreationPlan, system: str) -> None:
 493:     target = plan.settings_uri
 494:     if target and system == "windows":
 495:         import os
 496: 
 497:         os.startfile(target)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
 498:         return
 499:     if target and system == "darwin":
 500:         subprocess.Popen(["open", target])
 501:         return
 502:     if target:
 503:         subprocess.Popen(["xdg-open", target])
 504:         return
 505:     if plan.command:
 506:         subprocess.Popen(list(plan.command))
 507:         return
 508:     raise ValueError("path creation plan has no launchable OS ceremony")

 666: def _redact_helper_command(argv: list[str]) -> list[str]:
 667:     redacted: list[str] = []
 668:     hide_next = False
 669:     secret_flags = {"--password", "--passphrase", "--key", "--secret", "--token"}
 670:     for part in argv:
 671:         if hide_next:
 672:             redacted.append("********")
 673:             hide_next = False
 674:             continue
 675:         key, sep, _value = part.partition("=")
 676:         if key.lower() in secret_flags:
 677:             redacted.append(f"{key}=********" if sep else key)
 678:             hide_next = not sep
 679:         else:
 680:             redacted.append(part)

 684: def _validate_hotspot_ssid(value: str | None) -> str:
 685:     clean = str(value or "").strip()
 686:     if not 1 <= len(clean) <= 32:
 687:         raise ValueError("hotspot ssid must be 1..32 characters")
 688:     if any(ord(ch) < 32 or ord(ch) > 126 for ch in clean):
 689:         raise ValueError("hotspot ssid must be printable ASCII")
 690:     return clean
 691:

 693: def _validate_hotspot_passphrase(value: str | None) -> str:
 694:     clean = str(value or "")
 695:     if not 8 <= len(clean) <= 63:
 696:         raise ValueError("hotspot passphrase must be 8..63 characters")
 697:     if any(ord(ch) < 32 or ord(ch) > 126 for ch in clean):
 698:         raise ValueError("hotspot passphrase must be printable ASCII")
 699:     return clean

   1: """Transport Prioritizer — weighted-fair-queuing per QoS class.
   2: 
   3: The Priority Engine in :mod:`priority_engine` decides *how much*
   4: bandwidth each conversation class deserves. This module is the
   5: mechanism — it accepts outbound messages tagged with a QoS class,
   6: holds them in per-class queues, and emits them under a scheduling
   7: policy that honours the priority weights.
   8: 
   9: Why not just "send everything in order":
  10:   - On a saturated link, voice packets MUST not queue behind
  11:     file-transfer chunks. The single-stream daemon transport
  12:     appends-in-order — without prioritization, a 1 MiB file chunk
  13:     pinned in front of a 200-byte voice packet adds hundreds of
  14:     milliseconds of latency.
  15:   - The Immune System's bandwidth controller emits
  16:     REQUEST_VOICE_ONLY when total link capacity drops below the
  17:     P0 floor. This module is what makes that emission
  18:     operationally meaningful — when the budget is tight, the
  19:     P0 queue (voice) drains, and lower-class queues (P3
  20:     file-bytes) starve until budget recovers.
  21: 
  22: The scheduler implements **deficit weighted round-robin (DWRR)**:
  23:   - Each class gets a "deficit counter" that grows by its weight
  24:     every scheduling tick.
  25:   - When a class's deficit covers the size of the head-of-queue
  26:     packet, that packet is emitted and the deficit decremented.
  27:   - This gives strict ordering by priority class AND fair
  28:     bandwidth sharing within a class.
  29: 
  30: Pure module: no I/O, no sockets, no daemon imports. The daemon
  31: plugs the prioritizer between its message-producer code and the
  32: channel write loop.
  33: 
  34: Companion: docs/LIVING_PRESENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §4.6 (Priority Engine)
  35: """
  36: 
  37: from __future__ import annotations
  38: 
  39: import threading
  40: from collections import deque
  41: from dataclasses import dataclass
  42: from enum import IntEnum
  43: from typing import Callable, Optional
  44: 
  45: 
  46: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  47: # QoS class hierarchy
  48: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  49: 
  50: class QoSClass(IntEnum):
  51:     """Maps message types to scheduling priority. Lower = higher
  52:     priority. Values are intentionally sparse so future tiers can
  53:     insert classes without breaking persisted state."""
  54: 
  55:     # P0 — must-survive
  56:     VOICE_FRAMES        = 0   # opus, every 20 ms
  57:     CALL_LIFECYCLE      = 1   # INVITE / ACCEPT / END — small, urgent
  58:     PRESENCE_LIVENESS   = 2   # heartbeat, alive pings
  59: 
  60:     # P1 — timing critical
  61:     SDP_ICE             = 10  # signaling — must complete fast
  62:     FRAME_ATTESTATION   = 11  # Tier β rolling-window attestations
  63: 
  64:     # P2 — face + video keyframes
  65:     VIDEO_KEYFRAME      = 20
  66:     SAS_VERIFICATION    = 21
  67: 
  68:     # P3 — bulk
  69:     VIDEO_DELTA         = 30
  70:     CAPABILITY_GRANT    = 31
  71:     GROUP_EVENT         = 32
  72: 
  73:     # P4 — best-effort
  74:     FILE_CHUNK          = 40
  75:     FOLDER_SYNC         = 41
  76:     GROUP_BULK          = 42
  77: 
  78:     # P5 — background
  79:     DHT_MAINTENANCE     = 50
  80:     METRICS             = 51
  81: 
  82: 
  83: # Default weights — how many bytes per scheduling tick each class
  84: # may emit. The ratios encode the doctrine: voice is sacred, file
  85: # bytes wait. Operators can tune at construction time.
  86: DEFAULT_WEIGHTS_PER_CLASS: dict[QoSClass, int] = {
  87:     QoSClass.VOICE_FRAMES:       2_000,
  88:     QoSClass.CALL_LIFECYCLE:     2_000,
  89:     QoSClass.PRESENCE_LIVENESS:    500,
  90:     QoSClass.SDP_ICE:            1_500,
  91:     QoSClass.FRAME_ATTESTATION:    500,
  92:     QoSClass.VIDEO_KEYFRAME:     1_500,
  93:     QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION:     500,
  94:     QoSClass.VIDEO_DELTA:        1_000,
  95:     QoSClass.CAPABILITY_GRANT:     500,
  96:     QoSClass.GROUP_EVENT:          500,
  97:     QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK:           500,
  98:     QoSClass.FOLDER_SYNC:          500,
  99:     QoSClass.GROUP_BULK:           500,
 100:     QoSClass.DHT_MAINTENANCE:      200,
 101:     QoSClass.METRICS:              200,
 102: }
 103: 
 104: 
 105: # Map wire-message type → QoS class. The daemon's send path looks
 106: # up the class by message type. Unknown types fall through to
 107: # FILE_CHUNK (best-effort).
 108: WIRE_TYPE_TO_QOS: dict[str, QoSClass] = {
 109:     # Voice / video frame plane (Tier β+)
 110:     "CALL_FRAME": QoSClass.VOICE_FRAMES,
 111:     "CALL_FRAME_ATTEST": QoSClass.FRAME_ATTESTATION,
 112:     # Call lifecycle
 113:     "CALL_INVITE": QoSClass.CALL_LIFECYCLE,
 114:     "CALL_ACCEPT": QoSClass.CALL_LIFECYCLE,
 115:     "CALL_DECLINE": QoSClass.CALL_LIFECYCLE,
 116:     "CALL_END": QoSClass.CALL_LIFECYCLE,
 117:     "CALL_RESUME_OFFER": QoSClass.CALL_LIFECYCLE,
 118:     # SDP + ICE
 119:     "CALL_SDP_OFFER": QoSClass.SDP_ICE,
 120:     "CALL_SDP_ANSWER": QoSClass.SDP_ICE,
 121:     "CALL_ICE": QoSClass.SDP_ICE,
 122:     # Recording consent
 123:     "RECORDING_REQUEST": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 124:     "RECORDING_GRANT": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 125:     "RECORDING_DECLINE": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 126:     "RECORDING_STOP": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 127:     # Presence + heartbeat

 129:     "PING": QoSClass.PRESENCE_LIVENESS,

 131:     # Capability grants
 132:     "CAPABILITY_GRANT": QoSClass.CAPABILITY_GRANT,
 133:     "CAPS": QoSClass.CAPABILITY_GRANT,
 134:     # Group messages
 135:     "GROUP_EVENT": QoSClass.GROUP_EVENT,
 136:     "GROUP_KEY_OFFER": QoSClass.GROUP_EVENT,
 137:     "GROUP_MSG": QoSClass.GROUP_BULK,
 138:     # File transfer
 139:     "FILE_OFFER": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 140:     "FILE_CHUNK": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 141:     "FILE_BIN_CHUNK": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 142:     "FILE_NATIVE_CHUNK": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 143:     "FILE_CDC_CHUNK": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 144:     "CHUNK_QUERY": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 145:     "CHUNK_PULL": QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK,
 146:     # Folder sync

 152:     "TEXT": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,  # interactive chat = P2-ish
 153:     "REACTION": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 154:     "EDIT_MSG": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 155:     "DELETE_MSG": QoSClass.SAS_VERIFICATION,
 156:     "TYPING": QoSClass.METRICS,
 157:     "READ_MARKER": QoSClass.METRICS,

 161: 
 162: 
 163: def classify(msg_type: str) -> QoSClass:
 164:     """Map a wire-message type string to its QoS class. Unknown
 165:     types fall through to FILE_CHUNK (best-effort)."""
 166:     return WIRE_TYPE_TO_QOS.get(msg_type, QoSClass.FILE_CHUNK)
 167: 
 168: 
 169: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 170: # Prioritizer
 171: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 172: 
 173: @dataclass
 174: class _QueuedMessage:
 175:     payload: bytes
 176:     qos_class: QoSClass
 177:     size: int
 178:     # Optional callback fired after the message is dispatched
 179:     # (lets the daemon free buffers / record send timestamps).
 180:     on_sent: Optional[Callable[[], None]] = None
 181: 
 182: 
 183: class TransportPrioritizer:
 184:     """Deficit weighted round-robin scheduler.
 185: 
 186:     Use:
 187:       - :meth:`enqueue` to admit one message tagged with its QoS class.
 188:       - :meth:`drain` to drain ready messages in priority order; the
 189:         caller writes each to the underlying channel.
 190:       - :meth:`set_budget_per_tick` to clip total bytes per drain
 191:         cycle (the Immune System uses this when bandwidth tightens).
 192: 
 193:     Thread-safe.
 194:     """
 195: 
 196:     def __init__(
 197:         self,
 198:         *,
 199:         weights: Optional[dict[QoSClass, int]] = None,
 200:         max_queue_bytes_per_class: int = 4 * 1024 * 1024,
 201:     ) -> None:
 202:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
 203:         self._weights = dict(weights or DEFAULT_WEIGHTS_PER_CLASS)
 204:         self._queues: dict[QoSClass, deque[_QueuedMessage]] = {
 205:             qc: deque() for qc in QoSClass
 206:         }
 207:         self._deficits: dict[QoSClass, int] = {qc: 0 for qc in QoSClass}
 208:         self._queue_bytes: dict[QoSClass, int] = {qc: 0 for qc in QoSClass}
 209:         self._max_queue_bytes = max_queue_bytes_per_class
 210:         self._budget_per_tick: Optional[int] = None
 211:         # Stats — exposed for the Immune System + audit log.
 212:         self._enqueued_count: dict[QoSClass, int] = {qc: 0 for qc in QoSClass}
 213:         self._dropped_count: dict[QoSClass, int] = {qc: 0 for qc in QoSClass}
 214:         self._sent_count: dict[QoSClass, int] = {qc: 0 for qc in QoSClass}
 215:         self._sent_bytes: dict[QoSClass, int] = {qc: 0 for qc in QoSClass}
 216: 
 217:     def enqueue(
 218:         self,
 219:         *,
 220:         payload: bytes,
 221:         qos_class: QoSClass,
 222:         on_sent: Optional[Callable[[], None]] = None,
 223:     ) -> bool:
 224:         """Admit a message. Returns True if accepted, False if the
 225:         class's queue is full (back-pressure → drop)."""
 226:         with self._lock:
 227:             if self._queue_bytes[qos_class] + len(payload) > self._max_queue_bytes:
 228:                 self._dropped_count[qos_class] += 1
 229:                 return False
 230:             self._queues[qos_class].append(_QueuedMessage(
 231:                 payload=payload, qos_class=qos_class,
 232:                 size=len(payload), on_sent=on_sent,
 233:             ))
 234:             self._queue_bytes[qos_class] += len(payload)
 235:             self._enqueued_count[qos_class] += 1
 236:             return True
 237: 
 238:     def set_budget_per_tick(self, budget_bytes: Optional[int]) -> None:
 239:         """Hard cap on bytes emitted per drain cycle. None = no cap."""
 240:         with self._lock:
 241:             self._budget_per_tick = budget_bytes
 242: 
 243:     def set_weight(self, qos_class: QoSClass, weight: int) -> None:
 244:         """Adjust the per-tick credit for one class. The Immune
 245:         System calls this when it asks for REQUEST_VOICE_ONLY —
 246:         it caps every non-voice class to a token weight."""
 247:         if weight < 0:
 248:             raise ValueError("weight must be non-negative")
 249:         with self._lock:
 250:             self._weights[qos_class] = weight
 251: 
 252:     def drain(self) -> list[_QueuedMessage]:
 253:         """Emit one scheduling tick worth of messages, in priority
 254:         order. Returns the ordered list the caller writes to the
 255:         wire."""
 256:         ready: list[_QueuedMessage] = []
 257:         with self._lock:
 258:             budget_remaining = self._budget_per_tick
 259:             for qc in sorted(QoSClass, key=lambda x: int(x)):
 260:                 self._deficits[qc] += self._weights[qc]
 261:                 q = self._queues[qc]
 262:                 while q:
 263:                     head = q[0]
 264:                     if self._deficits[qc] < head.size:
 265:                         break
 266:                     if budget_remaining is not None and budget_remaining <= 0:
 267:                         # Hard cap reached — stop entirely.
 268:                         # Carry over deficits to the next tick so
 269:                         # we don't starve under repeated tight caps.
 270:                         return ready
 271:                     q.popleft()
 272:                     self._queue_bytes[qc] -= head.size
 273:                     self._deficits[qc] -= head.size
 274:                     if budget_remaining is not None:
 275:                         budget_remaining -= head.size
 276:                     self._sent_count[qc] += 1
 277:                     self._sent_bytes[qc] += head.size
 278:                     ready.append(head)
 279:         return ready
 280: 
 281:     def queue_depth(self, qos_class: QoSClass) -> int:
 282:         with self._lock:
 283:             return len(self._queues[qos_class])
 284: 
 285:     def total_queue_bytes(self) -> int:
 286:         with self._lock:
 287:             return sum(self._queue_bytes.values())
 288: 
 289:     def stats(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
 290:         """Snapshot of per-class counters. The Immune System's
 291:         controller reads this each tick to decide if pressure has
 292:         eased enough to lift voice-only mode."""
 293:         with self._lock:
 294:             return {
 295:                 qc.name: {
 296:                     "enqueued": self._enqueued_count[qc],
 297:                     "sent": self._sent_count[qc],
 298:                     "sent_bytes": self._sent_bytes[qc],
 299:                     "dropped": self._dropped_count[qc],
 300:                     "queue_depth": len(self._queues[qc]),
 301:                     "queue_bytes": self._queue_bytes[qc],
 302:                     "weight": self._weights[qc],
 303:                 }
 304:                 for qc in QoSClass
 305:             }
 306: 
 307:     def reset_counters(self) -> None:
 308:         with self._lock:
 309:             for qc in QoSClass:
 310:                 self._enqueued_count[qc] = 0
 311:                 self._sent_count[qc] = 0
 312:                 self._sent_bytes[qc] = 0
 313:                 self._dropped_count[qc] = 0
 314: 
 315:     # ── Immune-System bridge helpers ────────────────────────────
 316: 
 317:     def enter_voice_only_mode(self) -> None:
 318:         """Cap every non-P0 class to its minimum weight so voice
 319:         bytes drain first. Reversible via :meth:`exit_voice_only_mode`."""
 320:         with self._lock:
 321:             self._saved_weights = dict(self._weights)
 322:             # P0 (VOICE / LIFECYCLE / PRESENCE) keeps full weight.
 323:             for qc in QoSClass:
 324:                 if int(qc) >= 10:  # any class P1+ is throttled to a token
 325:                     self._weights[qc] = max(1, self._weights[qc] // 100)
 326: 
 327:     def exit_voice_only_mode(self) -> None:
 328:         with self._lock:
 329:             saved = getattr(self, "_saved_weights", None)
 330:             if saved is not None:
 331:                 self._weights = saved
 332:                 self._saved_weights = None

   1: """TrustLedger — per-daemon ledger of pinned peer master_vk keys.
   2: 
   3: Audit C2 closure surface: when a peer presents a master_vk we
   4: haven't seen before — or one we have seen but it differs from the
   5: pinned value — the daemon routes the decision through
   6: :func:`identity_sas.evaluate_rotation` and acts on the
   7: :class:`RotationDecision`:
   8: 
   9:   * First contact → record TOFU, allow_call=True, needs_reverify=True
  10:     (UI will show SAS).
  11:   * Same key → allow, skip SAS.
  12:   * Different key + valid chain signature from prior key → allow
  13:     with re-verify offer ("Mom updated her keys").
  14:   * Different key + broken chain → **refuse** the call.
  15: 
  16: The ledger is in-memory by default. It exposes a clean
  17: serialise/deserialise surface so the daemon's SQLite state layer
  18: can persist it (the daemon's existing trust-store schema is the
  19: target).
  20: 
  21: The actual signature verification (the ``verify_prior_signature``
  22: callback in :func:`evaluate_rotation`) is plugged at construction
  23: — production wires it to ``identity.verify``; tests substitute a
  24: mock.
  25: 
  26: Companion: docs/LIVING_PRESENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §7.1 (audit C2 closure)
  27: """
  28: 
  29: from __future__ import annotations
  30: 
  31: import logging
  32: import threading
  33: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
  34: from typing import Callable, Optional
  35: 
  36: from one_link.identity_sas import (
  37:     RotationDecision,
  38:     TrustRecord,
  39:     VerificationState,
  40:     evaluate_rotation,
  41: )
  42: 
  43: log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  44: 
  45: 
  46: # Signature-verify callable contract: takes hex pubkeys + sig bytes,
  47: # returns True iff sig is a valid Ed25519 signature by ``prior_vk_hex``
  48: # over the canonical "key rotation" transcript binding new_vk_hex.
  49: VerifyPriorSignature = Callable[[str, str, bytes], bool]
  50: 
  51: 
  52: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  53: # The ledger
  54: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  55: 
  56: class TrustLedger:
  57:     """In-memory ledger + thread-safe lookups.
  58: 
  59:     The daemon constructs ONE instance per identity (so a desktop
  60:     + a phone, both running their own daemons, have independent
  61:     ledgers — each is its own perspective on "who I trust"). Add
  62:     a peer's pinned key with :meth:`record_pinned`; check an
  63:     inbound observation with :meth:`check_inbound`.
  64:     """
  65: 
  66:     def __init__(
  67:         self,
  68:         *,
  69:         verify_prior_signature: VerifyPriorSignature,
  70:     ) -> None:
  71:         self._records: dict[str, TrustRecord] = {}
  72:         self._lock = threading.Lock()
  73:         self._verify = verify_prior_signature
  74: 
  75:     # ── Pinning + recording ──────────────────────────────────
  76: 
  77:     def record_pinned(
  78:         self,
  79:         *,
  80:         peer_master_vk_hex: str,
  81:         verified_at_ms: int,
  82:         state: VerificationState = VerificationState.TRUSTED,
  83:         previous_master_vk_hex: Optional[str] = None,
  84:     ) -> None:
  85:         """Add or update a pin. Idempotent: re-pinning the same key
  86:         updates the timestamp but doesn't disturb other state."""
  87:         with self._lock:
  88:             self._records[peer_master_vk_hex] = TrustRecord(
  89:                 peer_master_vk_hex=peer_master_vk_hex,
  90:                 verified_at_ms=verified_at_ms,
  91:                 state=state,
  92:                 previous_master_vk_hex=previous_master_vk_hex,
  93:             )
  94: 
  95:     def get(self, peer_master_vk_hex: str) -> Optional[TrustRecord]:
  96:         with self._lock:
  97:             return self._records.get(peer_master_vk_hex)
  98: 
  99:     def forget(self, peer_master_vk_hex: str) -> None:
 100:         """Remove a pin (e.g., when the user explicitly revokes
 101:         trust)."""
 102:         with self._lock:
 103:             self._records.pop(peer_master_vk_hex, None)
 104: 
 105:     def __len__(self) -> int:
 106:         with self._lock:
 107:             return len(self._records)
 108: 
 109:     # ── Rotation check ───────────────────────────────────────
 110: 
 111:     def check_inbound(
 112:         self,
 113:         *,
 114:         inbound_master_vk_hex: str,
 115:         inbound_signature_from_prior: Optional[bytes],
 116:         previous_pin_hex: Optional[str] = None,
 117:     ) -> RotationDecision:
 118:         """Decide what to do with an observed master_vk.
 119: 
 120:         Looks up the existing record for ``inbound_master_vk_hex``
 121:         AND for ``previous_pin_hex`` (if the caller knows which
 122:         prior key was pinned). Returns a :class:`RotationDecision`
 123:         the caller acts on.
 124: 
 125:         The caller (typically the daemon's pairing/handshake code)
 126:         is responsible for:
 127:           - If ``decision.allow_call`` → proceed
 128:           - If ``not decision.allow_call`` → refuse with the
 129:             plain-language explanation
 130:           - If ``decision.needs_reverify`` → surface the SAS UI
 131:         """
 132:         # If the inbound key IS already pinned, that's "same key"
 133:         # — fast path.
 134:         existing = self.get(inbound_master_vk_hex)
 135:         if existing is not None:
 136:             # Defer to evaluate_rotation for consistent decision
 137:             # surface; passing existing=this-record yields the
 138:             # "same key → TRUSTED" branch.
 139:             return evaluate_rotation(
 140:                 inbound_master_vk_hex=inbound_master_vk_hex,
 141:                 inbound_signature_from_prior=inbound_signature_from_prior,
 142:                 existing=existing,
 143:                 verify_prior_signature=self._verify,
 144:             )
 145: 
 146:         # The inbound key differs from anything we have pinned for
 147:         # this peer. Was a different key previously pinned?
 148:         prior = self.get(previous_pin_hex) if previous_pin_hex else None
 149:         return evaluate_rotation(
 150:             inbound_master_vk_hex=inbound_master_vk_hex,
 151:             inbound_signature_from_prior=inbound_signature_from_prior,
 152:             existing=prior,
 153:             verify_prior_signature=self._verify,
 154:         )
 155: 
 156:     def apply_decision(
 157:         self,
 158:         *,
 159:         inbound_master_vk_hex: str,
 160:         decision: RotationDecision,
 161:         verified_at_ms: int,
 162:         previous_pin_hex: Optional[str] = None,
 163:     ) -> None:
 164:         """If the decision allows the call AND establishes a new
 165:         trust state, persist it.
 166: 
 167:         Called by the daemon after a successful first-contact SAS
 168:         verification OR after the user re-verifies on rotation.
 169:         Untrusted decisions (CHAIN_BROKEN) don't modify the ledger.
 170:         """
 171:         if not decision.allow_call:
 172:             return
 173:         if decision.new_state == VerificationState.KEY_ROTATED_CHAIN_BROKEN:
 174:             return
 175:         self.record_pinned(
 176:             peer_master_vk_hex=inbound_master_vk_hex,
 177:             verified_at_ms=verified_at_ms,
 178:             state=decision.new_state,
 179:             previous_master_vk_hex=previous_pin_hex,
 180:         )
 181: 
 182:     # ── Persistence stubs ────────────────────────────────────
 183: 
 184:     def snapshot(self) -> list[dict]:
 185:         """Return a JSON-friendly list of all records — the daemon's
 186:         SQLite layer can persist this on shutdown / state sync."""
 187:         with self._lock:
 188:             return [
 189:                 {
 190:                     "peer_master_vk_hex": r.peer_master_vk_hex,
 191:                     "verified_at_ms": r.verified_at_ms,
 192:                     "state": int(r.state),
 193:                     "previous_master_vk_hex": r.previous_master_vk_hex,
 194:                 }
 195:                 for r in self._records.values()
 196:             ]
 197: 
 198:     def restore(self, snapshot: list[dict]) -> None:
 199:         """Load records from a snapshot. Overwrites existing
 200:         entries. The daemon calls this on startup with whatever
 201:         SQLite persisted."""
 202:         with self._lock:
 203:             for d in snapshot:
 204:                 try:
 205:                     state = VerificationState(int(d.get("state", 0)))
 206:                 except (TypeError, ValueError):
 207:                     state = VerificationState.UNVERIFIED
 208:                 vk_hex = d.get("peer_master_vk_hex")
 209:                 if not isinstance(vk_hex, str) or not vk_hex:
 210:                     continue
 211:                 try:
 212:                     verified_at_ms = int(d.get("verified_at_ms", 0))
 213:                 except (TypeError, ValueError):
 214:                     verified_at_ms = 0
 215:                 self._records[vk_hex] = TrustRecord(
 216:                     peer_master_vk_hex=vk_hex,
 217:                     verified_at_ms=verified_at_ms,
 218:                     state=state,
 219:                     previous_master_vk_hex=d.get("previous_master_vk_hex"),
 220:                 )
 221: 
 222:     def clear(self) -> None:
 223:         with self._lock:
 224:             self._records.clear()

   1: """GitHub Releases poll + version-compare for the in-app update banner.
   2: 
   3: Phase 2 of the production-install plan. Phase 1 ships native wheels to
   4: GitHub Releases on every v* tag; this module is the read side that the
   5: daemon uses to tell the UI "your build is older than the latest release
   6: — click here to update."
   7: 
   8: Contract:
   9:     * Pure functions. No global state, no async runtime requirements,
  10:       no side effects beyond the single HTTPS GET when fetch_latest()
  11:       runs. Easy to mock in tests.
  12:     * Never raises on transient failure. A network outage / 403 rate
  13:       limit / private repo returns CheckResult(status='unknown') so
  14:       the UI silently does nothing instead of showing a scary error.
  15:     * Cheap enough to call on every daemon startup. The HTTP call is
  16:       one round-trip with a 4-second timeout; if it can't complete in
  17:       that window, we give up.
  18: 
  19: The GitHub Releases REST endpoint is unauthenticated for public repos
  20: (60 req/hr per IP). For private repos the daemon would need a token —
  21: out of scope here; the repo will be public by the time end users hit
  22: this code path.
  23: """

  26:

  29: import re
  30: import urllib.error

  34: 
  35: from one_link.safe_http import validated_urlopen
  36:

  41: # fetch_latest() in tests / forks. Hard-coded here so the daemon doesn't

  43: DEFAULT_OWNER = "coherence-energy-labs"
  44: DEFAULT_REPO = "one-link"
  45: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 4.0
  46:

  52:     never leaks past this module."""

  56:     html_url: str            # release page on GitHub
  57:     published_at: str        # ISO-8601
  58:     body: str = ""           # markdown release notes (truncated by caller if needed)

  78:         if self.latest:

  90: 
  91: def _parse_version(s: str) -> Optional[tuple]:
  92:     """Parse a 'v0.21.0' / '0.21.0-alpha' / '0.21.0a1' style string into
  93:     a comparable tuple. Returns None if the input doesn't match.
  94: 
  95:     Comparison rule: (major, minor, patch, pre_order). A release with
  96:     no pre-release segment beats every pre-release at the same triple
  97:     — Python's tuple ordering does the work as long as we put the
  98:     'has-pre' bit BEFORE the pre identifier itself.
  99: 
 100:         0.21.0       -> (0, 21, 0, 1, '')      # 1 = is-release
 101:         0.21.0-alpha -> (0, 21, 0, 0, 'alpha') # 0 = is-pre
 102:         0.21.0a1     -> (0, 21, 0, 0, 'a1')
 103: 
 104:     'alpha' < 'a1' alphabetically; we don't try to be cleverer than
 105:     that. Matches what packaging.Version does in practice.
 106:     """
 107:     if not s:
 108:         return None
 109:     m = _VERSION_RE.match(s.strip())
 110:     if not m:
 111:         return None
 112:     major = int(m.group(1))
 113:     minor = int(m.group(2))
 114:     patch = int(m.group(3))
 115:     pre = m.group("pre")
 116:     if pre is None:
 117:         return (major, minor, patch, 1, "")
 118:     return (major, minor, patch, 0, pre.lower())
 119: 
 120: 
 121: def compare_versions(local: str, remote: str) -> str:
 122:     """Return one of 'newer' (remote > local), 'same', 'older' (remote
 123:     < local), or 'unknown' if either side fails to parse. The UI uses
 124:     this to decide whether to show the update banner."""
 125:     lt = _parse_version(local)
 126:     rt = _parse_version(remote)
 127:     if lt is None or rt is None:
 128:         return "unknown"
 129:     if rt > lt:
 130:         return "newer"
 131:     if rt < lt:
 132:         return "older"
 133:     return "same"
 134: 
 135: 
 136: # ─── HTTP fetch ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 137: 
 138: def _build_url(owner: str, repo: str) -> str:
 139:     return f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest"
 140: 
 141: 
 142: # Type alias for the fetch hook — lets tests inject a fake without
 143: # touching urllib.
 144: FetchFn = Callable[[str, float], dict]
 145: 
 146: 
 147: def _default_fetch(url: str, timeout: float) -> dict:
 148:     """One synchronous HTTPS GET to the GitHub Releases API. Returns
 149:     the parsed JSON body. Raises urllib.error.URLError / HTTPError /
 150:     json.JSONDecodeError on failure — the public fetch_latest()
 151:     wraps those into a clean unknown-status response."""
 152:     req = urllib.request.Request(
 153:         url,
 154:         headers={
 155:             # Identify the daemon so a future GitHub API change /
 156:             # rate-limit policy can pick us out from generic curl
 157:             # traffic. No secrets in this header.
 158:             "User-Agent": "one-link-update-check/0.21",
 159:             "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
 160:         },
 161:     )
 162:     with validated_urlopen(req, timeout=timeout, allow_loopback_http=True) as resp:
 163:         if resp.status != 200:
 164:             raise urllib.error.HTTPError(
 165:                 url, resp.status, resp.reason, resp.headers, None
 166:             )
 167:         return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
 168: 
 169: 
 170: def fetch_latest(
 171:     local_version: str,
 172:     *,
 173:     owner: str = DEFAULT_OWNER,
 174:     repo: str = DEFAULT_REPO,
 175:     timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
 176:     fetch: FetchFn = _default_fetch,
 177: ) -> CheckResult:
 178:     """Look up the latest GitHub Release for `owner/repo` and compare
 179:     its tag to `local_version`. Always returns a CheckResult — never
 180:     raises. Pass a `fetch` callable to mock the HTTP layer in tests.
 181:     """
 182:     url = _build_url(owner, repo)
 183:     try:
 184:         payload = fetch(url, timeout)
 185:     except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
 186:         # 404 = repo has no published releases yet (common during
 187:         # initial setup); treat as 'unknown' so the UI stays quiet.
 188:         log.info(
 189:             "update_check: GitHub returned HTTP %s for %s (%s)",
 190:             e.code, url, e.reason,
 191:         )
 192:         return CheckResult(
 193:             status="unknown",
 194:             local_version=local_version,
 195:             error=f"http {e.code}",
 196:         )
 197:     except urllib.error.URLError as e:
 198:         # Offline / DNS failure / TLS handshake issue.
 199:         log.info("update_check: network failure fetching %s: %s", url, e)
 200:         return CheckResult(
 201:             status="unknown",
 202:             local_version=local_version,
 203:             error=f"network: {e.reason if hasattr(e, 'reason') else e}",
 204:         )
 205:     except (json.JSONDecodeError, TimeoutError) as e:
 206:         log.info("update_check: bad/late response from %s: %s", url, e)
 207:         return CheckResult(
 208:             status="unknown",
 209:             local_version=local_version,
 210:             error=f"parse: {e}",
 211:         )
 212: 
 213:     tag = (payload.get("tag_name") or "").strip()
 214:     if not tag:
 215:         return CheckResult(
 216:             status="unknown",
 217:             local_version=local_version,
 218:             error="no tag_name in latest release",
 219:         )
 220: 
 221:     info = ReleaseInfo(
 222:         tag=tag,
 223:         name=payload.get("name") or tag,
 224:         html_url=payload.get("html_url") or "",
 225:         published_at=payload.get("published_at") or "",
 226:         body=payload.get("body") or "",
 227:         prerelease=bool(payload.get("prerelease")),
 228:         draft=bool(payload.get("draft")),
 229:         asset_count=len(payload.get("assets") or []),
 230:     )
 231: 
 232:     return CheckResult(
 233:         status=compare_versions(local_version, tag),
 234:         local_version=local_version,
 235:         latest_version=tag,
 236:         latest=info,
 237:     )

   1: """One-click update — wheel selection, download, verify, install, respawn.
   2: 
   3: Phase 3 of the production-install plan. Builds on update_check.py:
   4: 
   5:     Phase 1 (CI)      — release.yml ships native wheels on every v* tag
   6:     Phase 2 (read)    — daemon polls GitHub, UI shows "Update available" banner
   7:     Phase 3 (this)    — user clicks "Update now", daemon downloads the right
   8:                         wheel for this OS+ABI, verifies its SHA-256 against
   9:                         SHA256SUMS, pip-installs it, respawns. Or aborts
  10:                         cleanly with a structured error if anything goes wrong.
  11: 
  12: Safety properties:
  13: 
  14:     * The updater never modifies the running daemon's files directly.
  15:       pip install runs from a detached subprocess AFTER the daemon exits,
  16:       so Windows file-locking (on the .pyd / .exe) can't break the
  17:       install half-way.
  18:     * SHA-256 verification is mandatory. We refuse to install a wheel
  19:       whose hash isn't published in SHA256SUMS — defends against a
  20:       compromised release page or a man-in-the-middle proxy.
  21:     * Failed pip install does NOT leave you without a daemon. The
  22:       updater script starts a fresh daemon even if pip exits non-zero,
  23:       so the user just sees the old version still running.
  24:     * No network calls in this module's import path. All HTTP happens
  25:       inside the functions, so tests can monkey-patch without spinning
  26:       up an event loop.
  27: 
  28: This module is the engine; the /api/update/install endpoint in
  29: server.py is the thin handler that calls into it.
  30: """

  57: @dataclass
  58: class WheelMatch:
  59:     """A wheel asset on a GitHub Release that matches this host's
  60:     Python ABI + OS + arch. The updater downloads exactly this."""
  61: 
  62:     asset_url: str
  63:     filename: str
  64:     size: int

  66: 
  67: 
  68: @dataclass
  69: class InstallPlan:
  70:     """Everything the install handler needs to know to make a decision:
  71:     which wheel will be installed, where, and whether the host has
  72:     enough info to proceed."""
  73: 
  74:     status: str       # 'ready' | 'no_match' | 'no_release' | 'error'
  75:     tag: Optional[str] = None
  76:     wheel: Optional[WheelMatch] = None
  77:     error: Optional[str] = None
  78:     # Cached so the UI can echo the version they're about to install.
  79:     latest_version: Optional[str] = None
  80: 
  81:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
  82:         out = {"status": self.status}
  83:         if self.tag:
  84:             out["tag"] = self.tag
  85:         if self.latest_version:
  86:             out["latest_version"] = self.latest_version
  87:         if self.wheel:
  88:             out["wheel"] = {
  89:                 "filename": self.wheel.filename,
  90:                 "size": self.wheel.size,
  91:                 "sha256_known": bool(self.wheel.expected_sha256),
  92:             }
  93:         if self.error:
  94:             out["error"] = self.error
  95:         return out

  98: # ─── host detection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  99: 
 100: def host_wheel_tag() -> str:
 101:     """Return the wheel filename infix that a maturin-built abi3 wheel
 102:     for this host would have. Example: 'cp311-abi3-win_amd64'.
 103: 
 104:     The native crate is built abi3 (Python 3.11+), so the cp311 piece
 105:     is constant; OS + arch are the variable bits. macOS ships both
 106:     universal2 and per-arch wheels in practice; we match either.
 107:     """
 108:     machine = platform.machine().lower()
 109:     system = platform.system()
 110:     if system == "Windows":
 111:         arch = "amd64" if machine in ("amd64", "x86_64", "x64") else machine
 112:         return f"cp311-abi3-win_{arch}"
 113:     if system == "Darwin":
 114:         # arm64 (Apple Silicon) vs x86_64 (Intel). maturin also produces
 115:         # universal2 wheels that work on both; treat that as a fallback.
 116:         if machine in ("arm64", "aarch64"):
 117:             return "cp311-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64"
 118:         return "cp311-abi3-macosx_10_12_x86_64"
 119:     # Linux glibc/musl distinction is handled via manylinux tags
 120:     # (manylinux_2_17_x86_64 etc.). For matching purposes we'll
 121:     # accept any wheel whose filename contains "linux_<arch>" or
 122:     # "manylinux*_<arch>". `select_wheel_for_host` does the matching.
 123:     if machine in ("x86_64", "amd64"):
 124:         return "cp311-abi3-linux_x86_64"
 125:     if machine in ("aarch64", "arm64"):
 126:         return "cp311-abi3-linux_aarch64"
 127:     return f"cp311-abi3-linux_{machine}"
 128: 
 129: 
 130: def _wheel_matches_host(filename: str, host_tag: str) -> bool:
 131:     """A wheel filename matches the host iff its OS + arch suffix
 132:     matches OR (on macOS) it's a universal2 wheel. The cp-version
 133:     field is checked separately to allow cp311-abi3 wheels on Py3.12+."""
 134:     if "one_link_native-" not in filename:
 135:         return False
 136:     if not filename.endswith(".whl"):
 137:         return False
 138:     # cp311-abi3 wheels work on Python 3.11+ regardless of the
 139:     # actual interpreter version. Some builds tag cp312/cp313 too;
 140:     # accept any cp31x-abi3.
 141:     if "abi3" not in filename:
 142:         return False
 143:     # Platform suffix match.
 144:     suffix = filename.rsplit("-", 1)[-1].removesuffix(".whl")
 145:     expected = host_tag.rsplit("-", 1)[-1]
 146:     if expected in filename:
 147:         return True
 148:     # macOS universal2 wheels.
 149:     if "macosx" in expected and "universal2" in filename:
 150:         return True
 151:     # Linux: manylinux tags share the arch suffix with the host tag
 152:     # (e.g. host x86_64 ↔ manylinux_2_17_x86_64).
 153:     if "linux_" in expected:
 154:         arch = expected.rsplit("_", 1)[-1]
 155:         if f"_{arch}" in filename or filename.endswith(f"_{arch}.whl"):
 156:             return True
 157:     return False
 158: 
 159: 
 160: def select_wheel_for_host(
 161:     assets: list[dict],
 162:     host_tag: Optional[str] = None,
 163: ) -> Optional[WheelMatch]:
 164:     """Pick the right wheel from a GitHub Release's `assets` array.
 165:     Returns None if no asset matches this host."""
 166:     tag = host_tag or host_wheel_tag()
 167:     for asset in assets or []:
 168:         name = asset.get("name", "")
 169:         if _wheel_matches_host(name, tag):
 170:             return WheelMatch(
 171:                 asset_url=asset.get("browser_download_url", ""),
 172:                 filename=name,
 173:                 size=int(asset.get("size") or 0),
 174:             )
 175:     return None
 176: 
 177: 
 178: # ─── SHA256SUMS parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────
 179: 
 180: # The release.yml workflow writes a `SHA256SUMS` file in this format:
 181: #     <hex>  <filename>
 182: # We download it and look up the expected hash for our chosen wheel.
 183: 
 184: def parse_sha256sums(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
 185:     """Return {filename: hex_hash}. Tolerant: extra whitespace, blank
 186:     lines, and lines starting with '#' are ignored."""
 187:     out = {}
 188:     for raw in text.splitlines():
 189:         line = raw.strip()
 190:         if not line or line.startswith("#"):
 191:             continue
 192:         parts = line.split()
 193:         if len(parts) < 2:
 194:             continue
 195:         h = parts[0].lower()
 196:         # Allow `<hash> *file.whl` (sha256sum's binary marker) as well
 197:         # as `<hash>  file.whl`. Tolerate either form.
 198:         name = parts[-1].lstrip("*")
 199:         if len(h) == 64 and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in h):
 200:             out[name] = h
 201:     return out
 202:

 205: 
 206: FetchFn = Callable[[str, float], bytes]

 208: 
 209: def _default_http_get_bytes(url: str, timeout: float) -> bytes:
 210:     """Single synchronous GET, returning the response body as bytes.
 211:     Used for downloading wheels + SHA256SUMS. Tests inject a fake."""
 212:     req = urllib.request.Request(
 213:         url,
 214:         headers={"User-Agent": "one-link-updater/0.21",
 215:                  "Accept": "application/octet-stream"},
 216:     )
 217:     with validated_urlopen(req, timeout=timeout, allow_loopback_http=True) as resp:
 218:         if resp.status != 200:
 219:             raise urllib.error.HTTPError(
 220:                 url, resp.status, resp.reason, resp.headers, None
 221:             )
 222:         return resp.read()

 224: 
 225: def download_to_temp(
 226:     url: str,
 227:     *,
 228:     expected_size: int = 0,
 229:     timeout: float = 60.0,
 230:     fetch: FetchFn = _default_http_get_bytes,
 231: ) -> Path:
 232:     """Download `url` into a freshly-created temp file and return the
 233:     path. Caller is responsible for deletion. `expected_size` is a
 234:     soft check — we fail if the body is more than 5× the declared
 235:     size (defends against accidentally fetching a huge index page
 236:     instead of a 2MB wheel)."""
 237:     body = fetch(url, timeout)
 238:     if expected_size > 0 and len(body) > 5 * expected_size:
 239:         raise ValueError(
 240:             f"downloaded body {len(body):,} bytes > 5x expected "
 241:             f"{expected_size:,}; refusing"
 242:         )
 243:     fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="ol_update_", suffix=".bin")
 244:     try:
 245:         with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f:
 246:             f.write(body)
 247:     except Exception:
 248:         with contextlib_suppress():
 249:             os.unlink(path)
 250:         raise
 251:     return Path(path)
 252: 
 253: 
 254: def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
 255:     h = hashlib.sha256()
 256:     with open(path, "rb") as f:
 257:         for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(65536), b""):
 258:             h.update(chunk)
 259:     return h.hexdigest()
 260: 
 261: 
 262: # Tiny stand-in for contextlib.suppress to avoid pulling in another
 263: # import here. Keeps the module's surface narrow.
 264: class contextlib_suppress:
 265:     def __enter__(self): return self
 266:     def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb): return True
 267: 
 268: 
 269: # ─── plan + execute ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
 270: 
 271: def build_install_plan(
 272:     *,
 273:     owner: str = "coherence-energy-labs",
 274:     repo: str = "one-link",
 275:     timeout: float = 6.0,
 276:     fetch_json: Callable[[str, float], dict] | None = None,
 277:     fetch_bytes: FetchFn = _default_http_get_bytes,
 278: ) -> InstallPlan:
 279:     """Inspect the latest release, pick the wheel, look up its expected
 280:     hash. Does NOT download the wheel or run pip. Used by both the
 281:     /api/update/install handler and by tests to verify wheel matching."""
 282:     from one_link.update_check import _build_url, _default_fetch
 283:     fetch_json = fetch_json or _default_fetch
 284:     try:
 285:         payload = fetch_json(_build_url(owner, repo), timeout)
 286:     except Exception as e:
 287:         return InstallPlan(status="no_release", error=f"fetch latest: {e}")
 288:     tag = (payload.get("tag_name") or "").strip()
 289:     if not tag:
 290:         return InstallPlan(status="no_release", error="no tag_name in payload")
 291:     assets = payload.get("assets") or []
 292:     wheel = select_wheel_for_host(assets)
 293:     if wheel is None:
 294:         return InstallPlan(
 295:             status="no_match",
 296:             tag=tag,
 297:             latest_version=tag,
 298:             error=f"no wheel for {host_wheel_tag()} in release {tag}",
 299:         )
 300:     # Try to read SHA256SUMS for hash verification. If missing,
 301:     # we still proceed but flag the wheel as unverified — the caller
 302:     # decides whether to refuse or fall through (default: refuse).
 303:     for asset in assets:
 304:         if asset.get("name") == "SHA256SUMS":
 305:             try:
 306:                 body = fetch_bytes(asset["browser_download_url"], timeout)
 307:                 sums = parse_sha256sums(body.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
 308:                 if wheel.filename in sums:
 309:                     wheel.expected_sha256 = sums[wheel.filename]
 310:             except Exception as e:
 311:                 log.info("update: SHA256SUMS fetch failed: %s", e)
 312:             break
 313:     return InstallPlan(
 314:         status="ready",
 315:         tag=tag,
 316:         latest_version=tag,
 317:         wheel=wheel,
 318:     )
 319: 
 320: 
 321: def write_updater_script(
 322:     wheel_path: Path,
 323:     *,
 324:     parent_pid: int,
 325:     python_exe: str = sys.executable,
 326:     relaunch_cmd: list[str] | None = None,
 327: ) -> Path:
 328:     """Write a tiny standalone Python script that, when run, will:
 329:         1. Wait for parent_pid to exit (so the daemon's loaded .pyd
 330:            is no longer locked on Windows).
 331:         2. Run `pip install --user --force-reinstall <wheel_path>`.
 332:         3. Relaunch the daemon via `relaunch_cmd` (defaults to
 333:            `<python_exe> -m one_link.cli daemon`).
 334:         4. Log to ~/.one-link-update.log so the user can see what
 335:            happened if something goes wrong.
 336: 
 337:     Returns the path to the generated script. Caller is responsible
 338:     for running it as a detached subprocess.
 339:     """
 340:     relaunch = relaunch_cmd or [python_exe, "-m", "one_link.cli", "daemon"]
 341:     # Use repr() to embed safe Python literals; the script is run
 342:     # by the host's own Python so there's no shell-escaping concern.
 343:     script_src = f"""# Auto-generated by one_link.updater. Do not edit.
 344: import os, sys, time, subprocess, pathlib, logging
 345: PARENT_PID = {parent_pid!r}
 346: WHEEL_PATH = {str(wheel_path)!r}
 347: PYTHON_EXE = {python_exe!r}
 348: RELAUNCH = {relaunch!r}
 349: LOG_PATH = pathlib.Path.home() / '.one-link-update.log'
 350: 
 351: logging.basicConfig(
 352:     filename=str(LOG_PATH),
 353:     level=logging.INFO,
 354:     format='%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s',
 355: )
 356: log = logging.getLogger('updater')
 357: 
 358: def _alive(pid):
 359:     if pid <= 0: return False
 360:     if os.name == 'nt':
 361:         import ctypes
 362:         h = ctypes.WinDLL('kernel32', use_last_error=True).OpenProcess(
 363:             0x1000, False, pid
 364:         )
 365:         if not h: return False
 366:         try:
 367:             code = ctypes.c_ulong()
 368:             ctypes.WinDLL('kernel32').GetExitCodeProcess(h, ctypes.byref(code))
 369:             return code.value == 259  # STILL_ACTIVE
 370:         finally:
 371:             ctypes.WinDLL('kernel32').CloseHandle(h)
 372:     try:
 373:         os.kill(pid, 0); return True
 374:     except (OSError, ProcessLookupError):
 375:         return False
 376: 
 377: log.info('updater starting; waiting for daemon PID %s to exit', PARENT_PID)
 378: deadline = time.time() + 30.0
 379: while _alive(PARENT_PID) and time.time() < deadline:
 380:     time.sleep(0.5)
 381: if _alive(PARENT_PID):
 382:     log.warning('parent did not exit within 30s; continuing anyway')
 383: time.sleep(1.0)  # let file handles release
 384: 
 385: log.info('running pip install %s', WHEEL_PATH)
 386: rc = subprocess.call(
 387:     [PYTHON_EXE, '-m', 'pip', 'install', '--user',
 388:      '--force-reinstall', '--no-deps', WHEEL_PATH]
 389: )
 390: if rc == 0:
 391:     log.info('pip install succeeded')
 392: else:
 393:     log.error('pip install failed (exit %s); restarting OLD daemon', rc)
 394: 
 395: log.info('relaunching daemon: %s', RELAUNCH)
 396: try:
 397:     # On Windows we want the daemon detached + windowless so it
 398:     # doesn't pop a console. On POSIX, plain Popen + start_new_session
 399:     # handles the detach.
 400:     if os.name == 'nt':
 401:         DETACHED_PROCESS = 0x00000008
 402:         CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP = 0x00000200
 403:         subprocess.Popen(
 404:             RELAUNCH,
 405:             creationflags=DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP,
 406:             close_fds=True,
 407:         )
 408:     else:
 409:         subprocess.Popen(RELAUNCH, start_new_session=True, close_fds=True)
 410:     log.info('daemon relaunched')
 411: except Exception as e:
 412:     log.exception('daemon relaunch FAILED: %s', e)
 413: 
 414: # Clean up the wheel file so /tmp doesn't accumulate cruft.
 415: try:
 416:     os.unlink(WHEEL_PATH)
 417: except OSError:
 418:     pass
 419: """
 420:     fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="ol_updater_", suffix=".py")
