1136:   // ── v0.17.0 — Rendezvous client ─────────────────────────────────────
1137:   //
1138:   // Wire-format compat with desktop daemon's rendezvous_proto:
1139:   //   - PROTOCOL_VERSION = "OL-RDZ-1"
1140:   //   - canonical signing form: JSON.stringify with sorted keys,
1141:   //     separators ",", ":", ASCII-only (no Unicode escape-passthrough)
1142:   //   - signature: Ed25519 over canonical bytes of the dict MINUS
1143:   //     the "signature" field
1144:   //   - register endpoint: POST <rdzUrl>/api/v1/register, body is
1145:   //     the wire dict {v, type, pubkey_b64, timestamp_ms, ttl_s,
1146:   //     advertised_endpoints, nat_type, capabilities, signature}
1147:   //   - lookup endpoint: GET <rdzUrl>/api/v1/lookup/<pubkey_b64>
1148:   const RDZ_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "OL-RDZ-1";
1149:   const RDZ_DEFAULT_TTL_S = 300;
1150:   const RDZ_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS = 30 * 1000; // re-register 30s before expiry
1151: 
1152:   // Canonical JSON: keys sorted, no spaces, ASCII-safe. Mirrors
1153:   // Python `json.dumps(d, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
1154:   // ensure_ascii=True)` exactly. Used for both signing AND
1155:   // verification, so any drift breaks every signature.
1156:   function _canonicalJson(obj) {
1157:     if (obj === null) return "null";
1158:     if (typeof obj === "number") {
1159:       // Python json.dumps emits integers without trailing zeros
1160:       // and no scientific notation for typical ranges. Web JSON
1161:       // matches for safe-int range; bail loudly outside.
1162:       if (!Number.isFinite(obj)) {
1163:         throw new Error("non-finite numbers aren't canonical-JSON-safe");
1164:       }
1165:       // Integers stringified the same in Python + JS for ints.
1166:       // For floats: Python emits e.g. "1.5", JS emits "1.5". For
1167:       // exotic floats they may diverge; we never sign floats.
1168:       return Number.isInteger(obj) ? obj.toFixed(0) : String(obj);
1169:     }
1170:     if (typeof obj === "boolean") return obj ? "true" : "false";
1171:     if (typeof obj === "string") {
1172:       // Python ensure_ascii escapes any non-ASCII as \uXXXX.
1173:       // JSON.stringify on a string also produces \uXXXX for
1174:       // non-BMP chars but uses unescaped UTF-8 for BMP non-ASCII.
1175:       // We force \u escaping for ALL non-ASCII to match Python.
1176:       let out = '"';
1177:       for (let i = 0; i < obj.length; i++) {
1178:         const c = obj.charCodeAt(i);
1179:         if (c === 0x22) out += '\\"';
1180:         else if (c === 0x5c) out += "\\\\";
1181:         else if (c === 0x08) out += "\\b";
1182:         else if (c === 0x0c) out += "\\f";
1183:         else if (c === 0x0a) out += "\\n";
1184:         else if (c === 0x0d) out += "\\r";
1185:         else if (c === 0x09) out += "\\t";
1186:         else if (c < 0x20 || c >= 0x7f) {
1187:           out += "\\u" + c.toString(16).padStart(4, "0");
1188:         } else {
1189:           out += obj[i];
1190:         }
1191:       }
1192:       return out + '"';
1193:     }
1194:     if (Array.isArray(obj)) {
1195:       return "[" + obj.map(_canonicalJson).join(",") + "]";
1196:     }
1197:     if (typeof obj === "object") {
1198:       const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort();
1199:       return "{" + keys.map((k) =>
1200:         _canonicalJson(k) + ":" + _canonicalJson(obj[k])
1201:       ).join(",") + "}";
1202:     }
1203:     throw new Error(`uncanonicalable type: ${typeof obj}`);
1204:   }
1205: 
1206:   // Ed25519 sign via Web Crypto. Takes the JWK form and the bytes
1207:   // to sign; returns 64-byte raw signature.
1208:   async function _signEd25519(privateJwk, bytes) {
1209:     const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
1210:       "jwk",
1211:       privateJwk,
1212:       { name: "Ed25519" },
1213:       /*extractable=*/false,
1214:       ["sign"],
1215:     );
1216:     const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign(
1217:       { name: "Ed25519" },
1218:       key,
1219:       bytes,
1220:     );
1221:     return new Uint8Array(sig);
1222:   }
1223: 
1224:   // Verify Ed25519 signature for the lookup-result branch (we
1225:   // verify peer registers we look up). Public key is 32 bytes raw.
1226:   async function _verifyEd25519(pubkeyBytes, signature, message) {
1227:     const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
1228:       "raw",
1229:       pubkeyBytes,
1230:       { name: "Ed25519" },
1231:       /*extractable=*/false,
1232:       ["verify"],
1233:     );
1234:     return crypto.subtle.verify(
1235:       { name: "Ed25519" },
1236:       key,
1237:       signature,
1238:       message,
1239:     );
1240:   }
1241: 
1242:   // v0.20.7 (security audit C1): pull the DTLS-SRTP fingerprint
1243:   // out of an SDP blob. RFC 8122 a=fingerprint line. Mirrors
1244:   // peer_rtc.py's _extract_dtls_fingerprint exactly so both
1245:   // sides compute the same value from the same bytes.
1246:   function _extractDtlsFingerprint(sdp) {
1247:     if (typeof sdp !== "string") return "";
1248:     const m = /^a=fingerprint:(\S+)\s+([0-9A-Fa-f:]+)/m.exec(sdp);
1249:     if (!m) return "";
1250:     return m[1].toLowerCase() + ":" + m[2].toUpperCase();
1251:   }
1252: 
1253:   // v0.20.7 (security audit C1 + H6): verify a daemon-signed
1254:   // peer-rtc answer envelope. Throws on any failure so the
1255:   // caller's catch block surfaces the rejection to the UI
1256:   // instead of silently applying a tampered SDP.
1257:   // ``expectedFingerprint`` is the daemon_fingerprint the phone
1258:   // pinned at QR-scan time. When provided, the verifier also
1259:   // confirms the answer envelope claims the SAME fingerprint,
1260:   // closing the audit-H6 gap where peer.html ignored the
1261:   // ``&fp=`` field from the QR.
1262:   async function _verifySignedDaemonAnswer(envelope, expectedFingerprint) {
1263:     if (!envelope || envelope.t !== "answer") {
1264:       throw new Error("answer envelope expected");
1265:     }
1266:     if (typeof envelope.signature !== "string" || !envelope.signature) {
1267:       throw new Error(
1268:         "daemon answer is not signed (peer outdated). Please " +
1269:         "update the daemon to v0.20.7+ for MITM-resistant pairing."
1270:       );
1271:     }
1272:     const sigB64u = envelope.signature;
1273:     const pubB64u = envelope.daemon_pubkey_b64u;
1274:     if (typeof pubB64u !== "string" || !pubB64u) {
1275:       throw new Error("daemon answer is missing daemon_pubkey_b64u");
1276:     }
1277:     const claimedFingerprint = envelope.daemon_fingerprint || "";
1278:     const claimedDtls = envelope.dtls_fingerprint || "";
1279: 
1280:     const pubBytes = b64UrlToBytes(pubB64u);
1281:     if (!pubBytes || pubBytes.length !== 32) {
1282:       throw new Error("daemon_pubkey_b64u is not 32 bytes");
1283:     }
1284:     // Fingerprint cross-check #1: daemon_fingerprint in the
1285:     // envelope claims sha256:hex of pubBytes. Re-derive and
1286:     // require equality.
1287:     const derivedFp = await fingerprintOf(pubBytes);
1288:     if (claimedFingerprint && claimedFingerprint !== derivedFp) {
1289:       throw new Error(
1290:         "daemon_fingerprint does not match sha256(daemon_pubkey)"
1291:       );
1292:     }
1293:     // Fingerprint cross-check #2 (audit H6): the phone pinned
1294:     // a daemon fingerprint at QR-scan time. The signed answer
1295:     // envelope MUST claim that same fingerprint. A MITM serving
1296:     // a different daemon's signed answer (with a valid sig
1297:     // under THAT daemon's pubkey) would land here with a
1298:     // different fingerprint and we refuse.
1299:     if (expectedFingerprint &&
1300:         claimedFingerprint &&
1301:         expectedFingerprint !== claimedFingerprint) {
1302:       throw new Error(
1303:         "daemon answered with a different identity than the QR " +
1304:         "pinned at pair time (possible MITM or wrong daemon)"
1305:       );
1306:     }
1307:     // Build the canonical-bytes input for the signature: the
1308:     // envelope minus the signature field, JSON-serialized with
1309:     // sorted keys / no whitespace (matches peer_rtc._canonical).
1310:     const signing = Object.assign({}, envelope);
1311:     delete signing.signature;
1312:     const canonical = _canonicalJson(signing);
1313:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
1314:     const sig = b64UrlToBytes(sigB64u);
1315:     if (!sig || sig.length !== 64) {
1316:       throw new Error("daemon answer signature is not 64 bytes");
1317:     }
1318:     const ok = await _verifyEd25519(pubBytes, sig, enc.encode(canonical));
1319:     if (!ok) {
1320:       throw new Error("daemon answer signature does not verify");
1321:     }
1322:     // Cross-check: the SDP's a=fingerprint must match the claim
1323:     // the daemon cryptographically committed to. A MITM that
1324:     // rewrites the SDP fingerprint to point at their own DTLS
1325:     // cert invalidates this check.
1326:     const sdpDtls = _extractDtlsFingerprint(envelope.sdp || "");
1327:     if (claimedDtls) {
1328:       if (!sdpDtls) {
1329:         throw new Error(
1330:           "answer SDP is missing a=fingerprint (DTLS binding broken)"
1331:         );
1332:       }
1333:       if (sdpDtls !== claimedDtls) {
1334:         throw new Error(
1335:           "DTLS fingerprint in SDP does not match the daemon's " +
1336:           "signed claim (possible MITM)"
1337:         );
1338:       }
1339:     }
1340:   }
1341: 
1342:   // Build a RegisterReq matching the desktop daemon wire format.
1343:   // `advertised_endpoints` is a list of {host, port}. The browser
1344:   // can't easily know its public IP/port (NAT hides it; the rdz
1345:   // server tells us back via RegisterAck), so we usually pass
1346:   // an empty list and rely on the server's observation.
1347:   //
1348:   // Wire-format note on b64: despite the field name `pubkey_b64`,
1349:   // the daemon's rendezvous_proto uses urlsafe_b64encode().rstrip("=")
1350:   // — that's base64url WITHOUT padding. The JS bytesToB64Url helper
1351:   // already produces this exact form, so we use the keypair's
1352:   // public_key_b64u directly (no conversion). Same for the
1353:   // signature output.
1354:   async function _buildSignedRegister(rec, opts) {
1355:     opts = opts || {};
1356:     const ttl_s = opts.ttl_s || RDZ_DEFAULT_TTL_S;
1357:     const advertised_endpoints = opts.advertised_endpoints || [];
1358:     const nat_type = opts.nat_type || "unknown";
1359:     const capabilities = opts.capabilities || ["browser_peer", "webrtc_v1", "manual_signal_v1"]
1360:       .concat(window.WebTransport ? ["webtransport_v1"] : []);
1361:     const signing = {
1362:       v: RDZ_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
1363:       type: "register",
1364:       pubkey_b64: rec.public_key_b64u, // base64url, no padding
1365:       timestamp_ms: Date.now(),
1366:       ttl_s,
1367:       advertised_endpoints: advertised_endpoints.map((e) => ({
1368:         host: String(e.host),
1369:         port: Number(e.port),
1370:       })),
1371:       nat_type,
1372:       capabilities: capabilities.slice(),
1373:       transport_caps: browserTransportCapabilities(),
1374:     };
1375:     const canonical = _canonicalJson(signing);
1376:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
1377:     const sig = await _signEd25519(rec.private_key_jwk, enc.encode(canonical));
1378:     return Object.assign({}, signing, {
1379:       signature: bytesToB64Url(sig), // base64url, no padding
1380:     });
1381:   }
1382: 
1383:   function _normalizeRdzUrl(url) {
1384:     if (!url) return null;
1385:     let u = url.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
1386:     if (!/^https?:\/\//i.test(u)) {
1387:       // Default to https:// — never silently downgrade to http on
1388:       // a bare hostname. http requires the user to type it.
1389:       u = "https://" + u;
1390:     }
1391:     return u;
1392:   }
1393: 
1394:   async function registerWith(rdzUrl, opts) {
1395:     if (!state.rec) throw new Error("identity not unlocked");
1396:     const base = _normalizeRdzUrl(rdzUrl);
1397:     if (!base) throw new Error("rendezvous URL required");
1398:     const wire = await _buildSignedRegister(state.rec, opts);
1399:     const resp = await fetch(`${base}/api/v1/register`, {
1400:       method: "POST",
1401:       headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
1402:       body: JSON.stringify(wire),
1403:     });
1404:     const text = await resp.text();
1405:     let body;
1406:     try { body = JSON.parse(text); } catch { body = { raw: text }; }
1407:     if (!resp.ok) {
1408:       const err = body && body.error ? body.error : `HTTP ${resp.status}`;
1409:       throw new Error(err);
1410:     }
1411:     return body;
1412:   }
1413: 
1414:   async function lookupAt(rdzUrl, peerPubkeyB64u) {
1415:     const base = _normalizeRdzUrl(rdzUrl);
1416:     if (!base) throw new Error("rendezvous URL required");
1417:     // Daemon's _handle_lookup decodes via urlsafe_b64decode, so the
1418:     // URL path takes base64url. Identity already stores keys in
1419:     // base64url; pass through. encodeURIComponent is a belt-and-
1420:     // suspenders safety in case a future-ship key encoding sneaks
1421:     // in a non-URL-safe char.
1422:     const enc = encodeURIComponent(peerPubkeyB64u);
1423:     const resp = await fetch(`${base}/api/v1/lookup/${enc}`);
1424:     if (resp.status === 404) return null;
1425:     const text = await resp.text();
1426:     let body;
1427:     try { body = JSON.parse(text); } catch { body = { raw: text }; }
1428:     if (!resp.ok) {
1429:       const err = body && body.error ? body.error : `HTTP ${resp.status}`;
1430:       throw new Error(err);
1431:     }
1432:     return body;
1433:   }

1435:   // ── v0.19.0 — adaptive browser transport selector ──────────────────
1436:   //
1437:   // This is the browser-side transfer brain. It does not hide behind
1438:   // a static "use WebRTC" choice. It detects the live browser, scores
1439:   // every usable path, persists route memory in IndexedDB, and picks
1440:   // aggressively but safely. WebTransport is used when both the peer
1441:   // and browser support it; WebRTC remains the universal P2P path;
1442:   // manual signaling is the zero-server escape hatch.
1443:   const PATH_STATS_DB = "one-link-peer-path-stats";
1444:   const PATH_STATS_STORE = "path_stats.v1";
1445:   const PATH_STATS_VERSION = 1;
1446:   const PATH_EWMA_ALPHA = 0.28;
1447:   const PATH_EPSILON_BASE = 0.08;
1448:   const PATH_FAILURE_PENALTY = 0.70;
1449:   const WEBTRANSPORT_CAP = "webtransport_v1";
1450:   const WEBRTC_CAP = "webrtc_v1";
1451:   const MANUAL_SIGNAL_CAP = "manual_signal_v1";
1452: 
1453:   function browserTransportCapabilities() {
1454:     const caps = ["browser_peer", "manual_signal_v1"];
1455:     if (window.RTCPeerConnection) caps.push("webrtc_v1");
1456:     if (window.WebTransport) caps.push("webtransport_v1");
1457:     return caps;
1458:   }

1460:   function _pathStatKey(peerFp, pathKind) {
1461:     return `${peerFp || "unknown"}::${pathKind}`;
1462:   }

1464:   function _defaultPathStat(peerFp, pathKind) {
1465:     return {
1466:       peer_fp: peerFp || "unknown",
1467:       path_kind: pathKind,
1468:       ewma_throughput_bps: 0,
1469:       ewma_failure_rate: 0,
1470:       last_used_ms: 0,
1471:       samples: 0,
1472:     };
1473:   }

1475:   function _openPathStatsDb() {
1476:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
1477:       if (!window.indexedDB) {
1478:         reject(new Error("IndexedDB unavailable"));
1479:         return;
1480:       }
1481:       const req = indexedDB.open(PATH_STATS_DB, PATH_STATS_VERSION);
1482:       req.onupgradeneeded = () => {
1483:         const db = req.result;
1484:         if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(PATH_STATS_STORE)) {
1485:           db.createObjectStore(PATH_STATS_STORE, { keyPath: "id" });
1486:         }
1487:       };
1488:       req.onerror = () => reject(req.error || new Error("IndexedDB open failed"));
1489:       req.onsuccess = () => resolve(req.result);
1490:     });
1491:   }
1492: 
1493:   async function loadPathStats(peerFp) {
1494:     const db = await _openPathStatsDb();
1495:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
1496:       const tx = db.transaction(PATH_STATS_STORE, "readonly");
1497:       const store = tx.objectStore(PATH_STATS_STORE);
1498:       const req = store.getAll();
1499:       req.onerror = () => reject(req.error || new Error("path stats read failed"));
1500:       req.onsuccess = () => {
1501:         const prefix = `${peerFp || "unknown"}::`;
1502:         resolve((req.result || [])
1503:           .filter((r) => String(r.id || "").startsWith(prefix))
1504:           .map((r) => Object.assign({}, r, { id: undefined })));
1505:       };
1506:       tx.oncomplete = () => db.close();
1507:     });
1508:   }
1509: 
1510:   async function savePathStat(stat) {
1511:     const db = await _openPathStatsDb();
1512:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
1513:       const tx = db.transaction(PATH_STATS_STORE, "readwrite");
1514:       const store = tx.objectStore(PATH_STATS_STORE);
1515:       const row = Object.assign({}, stat, {
1516:         id: _pathStatKey(stat.peer_fp, stat.path_kind),
1517:       });
1518:       const req = store.put(row);
1519:       req.onerror = () => reject(req.error || new Error("path stats write failed"));
1520:       req.onsuccess = () => resolve(row);
1521:       tx.oncomplete = () => db.close();
1522:     });
1523:   }
1524: 
1525:   function observePathResult(prev, result) {
1526:     const stat = Object.assign(
1527:       _defaultPathStat(result.peer_fp, result.path_kind),
1528:       prev || {},
1529:     );
1530:     const bytes = Math.max(0, Number(result.bytes || 0));
1531:     const elapsedMs = Math.max(1, Number(result.elapsed_ms || 1));
1532:     const ok = result.ok !== false;
1533:     const throughput = ok && bytes > 0 ? (bytes * 8 * 1000) / elapsedMs : 0;
1534:     const oldBps = Number(stat.ewma_throughput_bps || 0);
1535:     const oldFail = Number(stat.ewma_failure_rate || 0);
1536:     stat.ewma_throughput_bps = oldBps <= 0
1537:       ? throughput
1538:       : ((1 - PATH_EWMA_ALPHA) * oldBps) + (PATH_EWMA_ALPHA * throughput);
1539:     stat.ewma_failure_rate = ((1 - PATH_EWMA_ALPHA) * oldFail) + (PATH_EWMA_ALPHA * (ok ? 0 : 1));
1540:     stat.samples = Number(stat.samples || 0) + 1;
1541:     stat.last_used_ms = Date.now();
1542:     return stat;
1543:   }
1544: 
1545:   function _pathSupported(pathKind, localCaps, peerCaps) {
1546:     const local = new Set(localCaps || browserTransportCapabilities());
1547:     const peer = new Set(peerCaps || []);
1548:     if (pathKind === "webtransport") {
1549:       return !!window.WebTransport && local.has("webtransport_v1") && peer.has("webtransport_v1");
1550:     }
1551:     if (pathKind === "webrtc") {
1552:       return !!window.RTCPeerConnection && local.has("webrtc_v1") && peer.has("webrtc_v1");
1553:     }
1554:     if (pathKind === "manual_webrtc") {
1555:       return !!window.RTCPeerConnection && local.has("manual_signal_v1");
1556:     }
1557:     return false;
1558:   }
1559: 
1560:   function pathScore(stat, pathKind) {
1561:     const s = stat || _defaultPathStat("unknown", pathKind);
1562:     const bps = Number(s.ewma_throughput_bps || 0);
1563:     const failure = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, Number(s.ewma_failure_rate || 0)));
1564:     const freshness = s.last_used_ms
1565:       ? Math.max(0.55, Math.exp(-(Date.now() - Number(s.last_used_ms)) / (30 * 60 * 1000)))
1566:       : 0.75;
1567:     const baseline = pathKind === "webtransport" ? 900_000_000
1568:       : pathKind === "webrtc" ? 450_000_000
1569:       : 180_000_000;
1570:     const learned = bps > 0 ? bps : baseline;
1571:     return learned * freshness * (1 - PATH_FAILURE_PENALTY * failure);
1572:   }
1573: 
1574:   function chooseTransportPath(opts) {
1575:     opts = opts || {};
1576:     const localCaps = opts.localCaps || browserTransportCapabilities();
1577:     const peerCaps = opts.peerCaps || [];
1578:     const statsByPath = opts.statsByPath || {};
1579:     const candidates = ["webtransport", "webrtc", "manual_webrtc"]
1580:       .filter((p) => _pathSupported(p, localCaps, peerCaps));
1581:     if (!candidates.length) {
1582:       return {
1583:         path_kind: "unavailable",
1584:         reason: "no shared browser transport",
1585:         score: 0,
1586:         candidates: [],
1587:       };
1588:     }
1589:     const scored = candidates.map((path) => ({
1590:       path_kind: path,
1591:       score: pathScore(statsByPath[path], path),
1592:       samples: Number((statsByPath[path] || {}).samples || 0),
1593:     })).sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score || a.path_kind.localeCompare(b.path_kind));
1594:     const epsilon = opts.epsilon == null ? PATH_EPSILON_BASE : Number(opts.epsilon);
1595:     if (scored.length > 1 && Math.random() < epsilon) {
1596:       const explore = scored.find((c) => c.samples === 0) || scored[scored.length - 1];
1597:       return Object.assign({}, explore, {
1598:         reason: "explore alternate path",
1599:         candidates: scored,
1600:       });
1601:     }
1602:     return Object.assign({}, scored[0], {
1603:       reason: "best observed path",
1604:       candidates: scored,
1605:     });
1606:   }
1607: 
1608:   async function openWebTransport(url) {
1609:     if (!window.WebTransport) {
1610:       throw new Error("WebTransport unavailable in this browser");
1611:     }
1612:     if (!/^https:\/\//i.test(String(url || ""))) {
1613:       throw new Error("WebTransport requires https://");
1614:     }
1615:     const wt = new WebTransport(url);
1616:     await wt.ready;
1617:     return wt;
1618:   }
1619: 
1620:   async function selectTransportForPeer(peerFp, peerCaps) {
1621:     let rows = [];
1622:     try {
1623:       rows = await loadPathStats(peerFp);
1624:     } catch {}
1625:     const statsByPath = {};
1626:     for (const row of rows) statsByPath[row.path_kind] = row;
1627:     return chooseTransportPath({ peerCaps, statsByPath });
1628:   }

1630:   // ── v0.18.0 — WebRTC DataChannel transport foundation ───────────────
1631:   const WRTC_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "OL-WRTC-1";
1632:   const WRTC_SIGNAL_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;
1633:   // May 15 2026 — sovereignty default: NO third-party STUN servers.
1634:   // Same-LAN pairing works without them (host candidates suffice).
1635:   // For cross-NAT pairing, the user can supply STUN via the
1636:   // daemon's /api/peer-rtc/ice-config endpoint (env var
1637:   // ONE_LINK_STUN_SERVERS or setting `stun_servers`). We fetch
1638:   // that asynchronously below and wire it into the RTC config.
1639:   // Empty list = host-only ICE = LAN-only fallback (no calls to
1640:   // Google / Cloudflare / Twilio / etc.).
1641:   const WEBRTC_STUN_SERVERS = [];
1642:   const WEBRTC_CONTROL_LABEL = "one-link-control-v1";
1643:   const WEBRTC_BULK_LABEL = "one-link-bulk-v1";
1644:   const WEBRTC_BULK_BUFFER_LOW_BYTES = 1 * 1024 * 1024;
1645:   const WEBRTC_BULK_BUFFER_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
1646: 
1647:   function assertWebRtcAvailable() {
1648:     if (!window.RTCPeerConnection) {
1649:       throw new Error("WebRTC unavailable in this browser");
1650:     }
1651:     if (!window.RTCSessionDescription) {
1652:       throw new Error("RTCSessionDescription unavailable in this browser");
1653:     }
1654:     return true;
1655:   }
1656: 
1657:   async function _signSignal(type, body) {
1658:     if (!state.rec) throw new Error("identity not unlocked");
1659:     const signing = {
1660:       v: WRTC_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
1661:       type: String(type),
1662:       sender_pubkey_b64: state.rec.public_key_b64u,
1663:       timestamp_ms: Date.now(),
1664:       body,
1665:     };
1666:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
1667:     const sig = await _signEd25519(
1668:       state.rec.private_key_jwk,
1669:       enc.encode(_canonicalJson(signing)),
1670:     );
1671:     return Object.assign({}, signing, { signature: bytesToB64Url(sig) });
1672:   }
1673: 
1674:   async function verifySignal(envelope, expectedType) {
1675:     if (!envelope || envelope.v !== WRTC_PROTOCOL_VERSION) {
1676:       throw new Error("not a One Link WebRTC signal");
1677:     }
1678:     if (expectedType && envelope.type !== expectedType) {
1679:       throw new Error(`expected ${expectedType}, got ${envelope.type}`);
1680:     }
1681:     if (Math.abs(Date.now() - Number(envelope.timestamp_ms || 0)) > WRTC_SIGNAL_TTL_MS) {
1682:       throw new Error("signal expired");
1683:     }
1684:     const pub = b64UrlToBytes(String(envelope.sender_pubkey_b64 || ""));
1685:     if (pub.byteLength !== 32) throw new Error("bad signal pubkey");
1686:     const sig = b64UrlToBytes(String(envelope.signature || ""));
1687:     if (sig.byteLength !== 64) throw new Error("bad signal signature");
1688:     const signing = {
1689:       v: envelope.v,
1690:       type: envelope.type,
1691:       sender_pubkey_b64: envelope.sender_pubkey_b64,
1692:       timestamp_ms: Number(envelope.timestamp_ms),
1693:       body: envelope.body,
1694:     };
1695:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
1696:     const ok = await _verifyEd25519(pub, sig, enc.encode(_canonicalJson(signing)));
1697:     if (!ok) throw new Error("signal signature does not verify");
1698:     return envelope;
1699:   }
1700: 
1701:   function encodeSignal(envelope) {
1702:     return bytesToB64Url(new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(envelope)));
1703:   }
1704: 
1705:   function decodeSignal(textValue) {
1706:     const s = String(textValue || "").trim();
1707:     if (!s) throw new Error("empty signal");
1708:     try {
1709:       return JSON.parse(s);
1710:     } catch {
1711:       const raw = b64UrlToBytes(s);
1712:       return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(raw));
1713:     }
1714:   }
1715: 
1716:   function createPeerConnection(opts) {
1717:     assertWebRtcAvailable();
1718:     opts = opts || {};
1719:     // May 15 2026 — sovereignty default. Start with whatever the
1720:     // top-level WEBRTC_STUN_SERVERS list contains (now [] — empty
1721:     // by default, no calls to third-party STUN). Asynchronously
1722:     // pull user-configured STUN from the daemon's
1723:     // /api/v1/peer-rtc/ice-config endpoint and wire it in if the
1724:     // user has set any. Silent on failure — LAN-only fallback is
1725:     // the intended default.
1726:     const pc = new RTCPeerConnection({
1727:       iceServers: WEBRTC_STUN_SERVERS,
1728:       bundlePolicy: "max-bundle",
1729:       rtcpMuxPolicy: "require",
1730:     });
1731:     (async () => {
1732:       try {
1733:         const r = await fetch("/api/v1/peer-rtc/ice-config", {
1734:           cache: "no-store",
1735:         });
1736:         if (!r.ok) return;
1737:         const cfg = await r.json();
1738:         if (Array.isArray(cfg.iceServers) && cfg.iceServers.length > 0) {
1739:           pc.setConfiguration({
1740:             iceServers: cfg.iceServers,
1741:             bundlePolicy: "max-bundle",
1742:             rtcpMuxPolicy: "require",
1743:           });
1744:         }
1745:       } catch (_) { /* LAN-only fallback is intentional */ }
1746:     })();
1747:     const session = {
1748:       pc,
1749:       control: null,
1750:       bulk: null,
1751:       signals: [],
1752:       opened_ms: Date.now(),
1753:       state: "starting",
1754:     };
1755:     const emitState = (label) => {
1756:       session.state = label;
1757:       if (opts.onState) opts.onState(label, session);
1758:     };
1759:     const wireChannel = (channel, kind) => {
1760:       channel.binaryType = "arraybuffer";
1761:       if (kind === "bulk") {
1762:         channel.bufferedAmountLowThreshold = WEBRTC_BULK_BUFFER_LOW_BYTES;
1763:       }
1764:       channel.onopen = () => emitState(`${kind}:open`);
1765:       channel.onclose = () => emitState(`${kind}:closed`);
1766:       channel.onerror = () => emitState(`${kind}:error`);
1767:       channel.onmessage = (event) => {
1768:         if (opts.onMessage) opts.onMessage(kind, event.data, session);
1769:       };
1770:       return channel;
1771:     };
1772:     if (opts.initiator) {
1773:       session.control = wireChannel(
1774:         pc.createDataChannel(WEBRTC_CONTROL_LABEL, { ordered: true }),
1775:         "control",
1776:       );
1777:       session.bulk = wireChannel(
1778:         pc.createDataChannel(WEBRTC_BULK_LABEL, {
1779:           ordered: false,
1780:           maxRetransmits: 0,
1781:         }),
1782:         "bulk",
1783:       );
1784:     } else {
1785:       pc.ondatachannel = (event) => {
1786:         if (event.channel.label === WEBRTC_CONTROL_LABEL) {
1787:           session.control = wireChannel(event.channel, "control");
1788:         } else if (event.channel.label === WEBRTC_BULK_LABEL) {
1789:           session.bulk = wireChannel(event.channel, "bulk");
1790:         }
1791:       };
1792:     }
1793:     pc.onicecandidate = async (event) => {
1794:       if (!event.candidate) return;
1795:       const signal = await _signSignal("ice", event.candidate.toJSON());
1796:       session.signals.push(signal);
1797:       if (opts.onSignal) opts.onSignal(signal, session);
1798:     };
1799:     pc.onconnectionstatechange = () => emitState(pc.connectionState || "unknown");
1800:     pc.oniceconnectionstatechange = () => emitState(`ice:${pc.iceConnectionState}`);
1801:     return session;
1802:   }
1803: 
1804:   async function createOfferSignal(opts) {
1805:     const session = createPeerConnection(Object.assign({}, opts, { initiator: true }));
1806:     const offer = await session.pc.createOffer({
1807:       offerToReceiveAudio: false,
1808:       offerToReceiveVideo: false,
1809:     });
1810:     await session.pc.setLocalDescription(offer);
1811:     const signal = await _signSignal("offer", session.pc.localDescription.toJSON());
1812:     session.signals.push(signal);
1813:     return { session, signal };
1814:   }
1815: 
1816:   async function acceptOfferSignal(envelope, opts) {
1817:     await verifySignal(envelope, "offer");
1818:     const session = createPeerConnection(Object.assign({}, opts, { initiator: false }));
1819:     await session.pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription(envelope.body));
1820:     const answer = await session.pc.createAnswer();
1821:     await session.pc.setLocalDescription(answer);
1822:     const signal = await _signSignal("answer", session.pc.localDescription.toJSON());
1823:     session.signals.push(signal);
1824:     return { session, signal };
1825:   }
1826: 
1827:   async function acceptAnswerSignal(session, envelope) {
1828:     if (!session || !session.pc) throw new Error("missing session");
1829:     await verifySignal(envelope, "answer");
1830:     await session.pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription(envelope.body));
1831:     return session;
1832:   }
1833: 
1834:   async function addIceSignal(session, envelope) {
1835:     if (!session || !session.pc) throw new Error("missing session");
1836:     await verifySignal(envelope, "ice");
1837:     await session.pc.addIceCandidate(envelope.body);
1838:     return session;
1839:   }
1840: 
1841:   function sendControl(session, obj) {
1842:     if (!session || !session.control || session.control.readyState !== "open") {
1843:       throw new Error("control channel not open");
1844:     }
1845:     session.control.send(JSON.stringify(obj));
1846:   }
1847: 
1848:   async function sendBulk(session, data) {
1849:     if (!session || !session.bulk || session.bulk.readyState !== "open") {
1850:       throw new Error("bulk channel not open");
1851:     }
1852:     while (session.bulk.bufferedAmount > WEBRTC_BULK_BUFFER_MAX_BYTES) {
1853:       await new Promise((resolve) => {
1854:         session.bulk.onbufferedamountlow = resolve;
1855:       });
1856:     }
1857:     session.bulk.send(data);
1858:   }

2002:   // ── v0.19.1 — SAS pairing over the control DataChannel ────────────
2003:   //
2004:   // Wire protocol over the control channel:
2005:   //
2006:   //   {"v":"OL-PAIR-1", "t":"hello", "pubkey":"<b64u>",
2007:   //    "fingerprint":"<algo>:<hex>", "nonce":"<b64u 16B>", "ts": <ms>,
2008:   //    "alias":"<optional display name>"}
2009:   //
2010:   //   {"v":"OL-PAIR-1", "t":"confirm",
2011:   //    "fingerprint":"<algo>:<hex>", "matched": true|false,
2012:   //    "ts": <ms>}
2013:   //
2014:   // Both sides send hello on control:open. Both compute SAS
2015:   // deterministically from canonical(SortedPubkeyPair, SortedNoncePair).
2016:   // First 6 decimal digits → human-readable SAS. SHA-256 of the same
2017:   // bytes → 6-cell visual art (one cell per byte → 256-color hue +
2018:   // shape). The user verifies face-to-face.
2019:   //
2020:   // Match path: each side sends `confirm matched=true`. Only when
2021:   // BOTH sides have local-confirmed AND received remote-confirmed
2022:   // do we persist the peer record. Either side answering false →
2023:   // tear down + close, no persistence.
2024:   //
2025:   // Replay defense: nonces are fresh per session; a captured
2026:   // hello/confirm pair from an old session won't match the new
2027:   // SAS computed against fresh nonces.
2028: 
2029:   const PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "OL-PAIR-1";
2030:   const PAIR_NONCE_BYTES = 16;
2031:   const PAIR_HELLO_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
2032: 
2033:   // OPFS peers store. One file per peer at /peers/v1/<short>.json so
2034:   // a single corrupt file doesn't poison the whole roster + a
2035:   // future ship can stream-load lazily.
2036:   const PEERS_DIR_NAME = "peers";
2037:   const PEERS_VERSION_DIR = "v1";
2038: 
2039:   async function _peersDir(create = false) {
2040:     const root = await _opfsRoot();
2041:     const peers = await root.getDirectoryHandle(PEERS_DIR_NAME, { create });
2042:     return peers.getDirectoryHandle(PEERS_VERSION_DIR, { create });
2043:   }
2044: 
2045:   function _peerFileName(fingerprint) {
2046:     // Strip the `algo:` prefix and grab a hex prefix as the on-disk
2047:     // filename. We DON'T trust the prefix to be unique — collisions
2048:     // get a numeric suffix on write. Keeping the file name a hex
2049:     // prefix means a casual filesystem peek doesn't reveal full
2050:     // pubkeys.
2051:     const hex = String(fingerprint).split(":").pop() || "unknown";
2052:     return `${hex.slice(0, 24)}.json`;
2053:   }
2054: 
2055:   async function listPeers() {
2056:     let dir;
2057:     try {
2058:       dir = await _peersDir(false);
2059:     } catch {
2060:       return [];
2061:     }
2062:     const out = [];
2063:     for await (const [name, handle] of dir.entries()) {
2064:       if (handle.kind !== "file") continue;
2065:       try {
2066:         const file = await handle.getFile();
2067:         const txt = await file.text();
2068:         const rec = JSON.parse(txt);
2069:         if (rec && rec.fingerprint && rec.public_key_b64u) out.push(rec);
2070:       } catch {
2071:         // Skip corrupt rows — better than zero peers.
2072:       }
2073:     }
2074:     out.sort((a, b) => Number(b.paired_ms || 0) - Number(a.paired_ms || 0));
2075:     return out;
2076:   }
2077: 
2078:   async function savePeer(rec) {
2079:     if (!rec || !rec.fingerprint || !rec.public_key_b64u) {
2080:       throw new Error("peer record requires fingerprint + public_key_b64u");
2081:     }
2082:     const dir = await _peersDir(true);
2083:     const fileName = _peerFileName(rec.fingerprint);
2084:     const file = await dir.getFileHandle(fileName, { create: true });
2085:     const writable = await file.createWritable();
2086:     await writable.write(JSON.stringify(rec));
2087:     await writable.close();
2088:     return rec;
2089:   }
2090: 
2091:   async function deletePeer(fingerprint) {
2092:     let dir;
2093:     try {
2094:       dir = await _peersDir(false);
2095:     } catch {
2096:       return false;
2097:     }
2098:     const fileName = _peerFileName(fingerprint);
2099:     try {
2100:       await dir.removeEntry(fileName);
2101:       return true;
2102:     } catch {
2103:       return false;
2104:     }
2105:   }
2106: 
2107:   // SAS derivation: canonical bytes of {alice_pubkey, bob_pubkey,
2108:   // alice_nonce, bob_nonce} where pubkeys + nonces are SORTED so
2109:   // both sides hash the same input regardless of role. Hash with
2110:   // SHA-256, take first 4 bytes → 6 decimal digits (mod 10^6).
2111:   // The same hash powers the visual art: bytes 4..10 each map to
2112:   // a (hue, shape) cell.
2113:   async function _computeSas(localPub, localNonce, remotePub, remoteNonce) {
2114:     const pubs = [localPub, remotePub].slice().sort();
2115:     const nonces = [localNonce, remoteNonce].slice().sort();
2116:     const dict = {
2117:       v: PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
2118:       pubkeys: pubs,
2119:       nonces,
2120:     };
2121:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
2122:     const bytes = enc.encode(_canonicalJson(dict));
2123:     const digest = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", bytes));
2124:     // 4-byte unsigned int → mod 10^6 → zero-padded to 6 digits.
2125:     const big =
2126:       ((digest[0] << 24) | (digest[1] << 16) | (digest[2] << 8) | digest[3]) >>> 0;
2127:     const six = (big % 1_000_000).toString().padStart(6, "0");
2128:     const display = six.slice(0, 3) + " " + six.slice(3);
2129:     const artBytes = digest.slice(4, 10); // 6 cells
2130:     return { digits: six, display, art: Array.from(artBytes), digest };
2131:   }
2132: 
2133:   function _renderSasArt(host, artBytes) {
2134:     if (!host) return;
2135:     host.innerHTML = "";
2136:     const SHAPES = ["●", "■", "▲", "◆", "★", "✚", "✦", "◐"];
2137:     for (const b of artBytes) {
2138:       const hue = (b * 360) / 256;
2139:       const shape = SHAPES[b & (SHAPES.length - 1)];
2140:       const cell = document.createElement("div");
2141:       cell.style.background = `hsl(${hue}deg 60% 28%)`;
2142:       cell.style.color = `hsl(${hue}deg 90% 75%)`;
2143:       cell.style.borderRadius = "8px";
2144:       cell.style.padding = "10px";
2145:       cell.style.textAlign = "center";
2146:       cell.style.fontSize = "20px";
2147:       cell.style.fontFamily = "ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace";
2148:       cell.textContent = shape;
2149:       host.appendChild(cell);
2150:     }
2151:   }

2153:   // Pair-session lifecycle. Per WebRTC session at most one pair
2154:   // attempt runs. `pairing` is mutually-driven state that closes
2155:   // out either by both-confirm or by mismatch / timeout / disconnect.
2156:   function _newPairing(session) {
2157:     return {
2158:       session,
2159:       version: PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
2160:       local_nonce: _randomBytes(PAIR_NONCE_BYTES),
2161:       remote_hello: null,
2162:       sas: null,
2163:       local_confirm: null,   // null | true | false
2164:       remote_confirm: null,  // null | true | false
2165:       sent_hello: false,
2166:       sent_confirm: false,
2167:       finished: false,
2168:       timeout: null,
2169:     };
2170:   }
2171: 
2172:   function _abortPairing(reason) {
2173:     const p = state.pairing;
2174:     if (!p || p.finished) return;
2175:     p.finished = true;
2176:     if (p.timeout) clearTimeout(p.timeout);
2177:     text($("#pair-status"),
2178:       reason ? `Pairing aborted: ${reason}` : "Pairing aborted.");
2179:     hide($("#pair-sas-wrap"));
2180:   }
2181: 
2182:   async function _sendPairHello() {
2183:     const p = state.pairing;
2184:     if (!p || p.sent_hello) return;
2185:     if (!state.rec) throw new Error("identity not unlocked");
2186:     const hello = {
2187:       v: PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
2188:       t: "hello",
2189:       pubkey: state.rec.public_key_b64u,
2190:       fingerprint: state.rec.fingerprint,
2191:       nonce: bytesToB64Url(p.local_nonce),
2192:       ts: Date.now(),
2193:     };
2194:     sendControl(p.session, hello);
2195:     p.sent_hello = true;
2196:   }
2197: 
2198:   async function _onPairHello(envelope) {
2199:     const p = state.pairing;
2200:     if (!p || p.finished) return;
2201:     if (p.remote_hello) {
2202:       // Duplicate hello (re-send by remote) — ignore. The first
2203:       // hello bound the SAS; later resends can't change it.
2204:       return;
2205:     }
2206:     if (envelope.v !== PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION) {
2207:       _abortPairing(`peer speaks ${envelope.v}, we speak ${PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION}`);
2208:       return;
2209:     }
2210:     if (!envelope.pubkey || !envelope.fingerprint || !envelope.nonce) {
2211:       _abortPairing("malformed hello (missing pubkey, fingerprint, or nonce)");
2212:       return;
2213:     }
2214:     const remoteNonce = b64UrlToBytes(envelope.nonce);
2215:     if (remoteNonce.byteLength !== PAIR_NONCE_BYTES) {
2216:       _abortPairing("malformed hello (bad nonce length)");
2217:       return;
2218:     }
2219:     p.remote_hello = envelope;
2220:     text($("#pair-peer-fp"), envelope.fingerprint);
2221:     show($("#pair-peer-wrap"));
2222: 
2223:     const sas = await _computeSas(
2224:       state.rec.public_key_b64u,
2225:       bytesToB64Url(p.local_nonce),
2226:       envelope.pubkey,
2227:       envelope.nonce,
2228:     );
2229:     p.sas = sas;
2230:     text($("#pair-status"),
2231:       "Compare the verification code + art with the other device. Confirm only if they match.");
2232:     text($("#pair-sas-digits"), sas.display);
2233:     _renderSasArt($("#pair-sas-art"), sas.art);
2234:     show($("#pair-sas-wrap"));
2235:   }
2236: 
2237:   async function _sendPairConfirm(matched) {
2238:     const p = state.pairing;
2239:     if (!p || p.sent_confirm || !state.rec) return;
2240:     p.local_confirm = matched;
2241:     const msg = {
2242:       v: PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
2243:       t: "confirm",
2244:       fingerprint: state.rec.fingerprint,
2245:       matched: !!matched,
2246:       ts: Date.now(),
2247:     };
2248:     sendControl(p.session, msg);
2249:     p.sent_confirm = true;
2250:     if (matched) {
2251:       text($("#pair-status"),
2252:         "You confirmed the match. Waiting for the other device to confirm…");
2253:     } else {
2254:       _abortPairing("you marked the codes as not matching");
2255:     }
2256:     await _maybeFinalizePairing();
2257:   }
2258: 
2259:   async function _onPairConfirm(envelope) {
2260:     const p = state.pairing;
2261:     if (!p || p.finished) return;
2262:     if (envelope.v !== PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION) return;
2263:     p.remote_confirm = !!envelope.matched;
2264:     if (!envelope.matched) {
2265:       _abortPairing("the other device marked the codes as not matching");
2266:       return;
2267:     }
2268:     text($("#pair-status"),
2269:       "Other device confirmed the match. Waiting for your confirmation…");
2270:     await _maybeFinalizePairing();
2271:   }
2272: 
2273:   async function _maybeFinalizePairing() {
2274:     const p = state.pairing;
2275:     if (!p || p.finished) return;
2276:     if (p.local_confirm !== true || p.remote_confirm !== true) return;
2277:     if (!p.remote_hello) return;
2278:     p.finished = true;
2279:     if (p.timeout) clearTimeout(p.timeout);
2280:     const rec = {
2281:       v: 1,
2282:       fingerprint: p.remote_hello.fingerprint,
2283:       public_key_b64u: p.remote_hello.pubkey,
2284:       alias: p.remote_hello.alias || "",
2285:       paired_ms: Date.now(),
2286:       last_seen_ms: Date.now(),
2287:       sas_digits: p.sas ? p.sas.digits : null,
2288:     };
2289:     try {
2290:       await savePeer(rec);
2291:     } catch (e) {
2292:       _abortPairing(
2293:         `paired but couldn't save peer record: ${e && e.message ? e.message : e}`
2294:       );
2295:       return;
2296:     }
2297:     text($("#pair-status"),
2298:       `Paired with ${rec.fingerprint}. Peer added to your roster.`);
2299:     hide($("#pair-sas-wrap"));
2300:     await _refreshPeersCard();
2301:   }
2302: 
2303:   function _routeControlMessage(session, kind, data) {
2304:     if (kind !== "control") return;
2305:     let msg;
2306:     try {
2307:       msg = typeof data === "string" ? JSON.parse(data) : null;
2308:     } catch {
2309:       return;
2310:     }
2311:     if (!msg || msg.v !== PAIR_PROTOCOL_VERSION) return;
2312:     if (msg.t === "hello") {
2313:       _onPairHello(msg);
2314:     } else if (msg.t === "confirm") {
2315:       _onPairConfirm(msg);
2316:     }
2317:   }
2318: 
2319:   async function _onControlChannelOpen(session) {
2320:     if (state.pairing && state.pairing.session === session) return;
2321:     state.pairing = _newPairing(session);
2322:     state.pairing.timeout = setTimeout(() => {
2323:       if (state.pairing && !state.pairing.finished && !state.pairing.remote_hello) {
2324:         _abortPairing("the other device didn't send a pair hello");
2325:       }
2326:     }, PAIR_HELLO_TIMEOUT_MS);
2327:     show($("#pair-card"));
2328:     text($("#pair-status"),
2329:       "Channel open. Waiting for the other device's identity claim…");
2330:     try {
2331:       await _sendPairHello();
2332:     } catch (e) {
2333:       _abortPairing(
2334:         `couldn't send pair hello: ${e && e.message ? e.message : e}`
2335:       );
2336:     }
2337:   }

2340:   $("#btn-pair-mismatch")?.addEventListener("click", () => _sendPairConfirm(false));

2410:   // ── v0.19.2 — message store + send/receive over control channel ─
2411:   //
2412:   // Wire protocol over the control DataChannel (post-pair only):
2413:   //
2414:   //   {"v":"OL-MSG-1", "t":"text", "id":"<uuid>",
2415:   //    "body":"<utf-8 text>", "ts":<ms>}
2416:   //
2417:   //   {"v":"OL-MSG-1", "t":"ack", "id":"<uuid>", "ts":<ms>}
2418:   //
2419:   // IndexedDB layout: store `messages.v1` with composite-ish key
2420:   // "<peer_fp>::<ts>::<id>" so per-peer reads sort cheaply by ts.
2421:   // Each record: {id, peer_fp, direction, body, ts, received_ms,
2422:   // ack_ms?}. Direction is "in" or "out". Outgoing rows track
2423:   // ack_ms once the peer ack arrives.
2424:   //
2425:   // Why IDB: messages are an indexed list (by peer, by ts), not
2426:   // a single blob. OPFS works for blobs; IDB works for sorted
2427:   // indexed records. Both are origin-private + survive Clear-
2428:   // Cookies.
2429:   //
2430:   // What this ship does NOT yet contain:
2431:   // - Multi-peer chat tabs (single-active-peer only)
2432:   // - Encryption-at-rest for messages (v0.16.1 wraps identity;
2433:   //   message wrap follows in v0.19.4)
2434:   // - Offline outbox (queued send when channel is closed)
2435:   // - Read receipts beyond ack
2436:   // - File transfer (v0.19.3 ships chunked send over bulk channel)
2437: 
2438:   const MSG_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "OL-MSG-1";
2439:   const MSG_DB_NAME = "one-link-peer-messages";
2440:   const MSG_STORE_NAME = "messages.v1";
2441:   const MSG_DB_VERSION = 1;
2442:   const MSG_BODY_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
2443: 
2444:   function _newMessageId() {
2445:     if (window.crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID();
2446:     // Fallback for very old browsers (we already require modern
2447:     // crypto/OPFS, so this should never fire — defensive only).
2448:     return bytesToB64Url(_randomBytes(16));
2449:   }
2450: 
2451:   function _msgKey(peerFp, ts, id) {
2452:     return `${peerFp || "unknown"}::${String(ts).padStart(15, "0")}::${id}`;
2453:   }
2454: 
2455:   function _openMessagesDb() {
2456:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
2457:       if (!window.indexedDB) {
2458:         reject(new Error("IndexedDB unavailable"));
2459:         return;
2460:       }
2461:       const req = indexedDB.open(MSG_DB_NAME, MSG_DB_VERSION);
2462:       req.onupgradeneeded = () => {
2463:         const db = req.result;
2464:         if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(MSG_STORE_NAME)) {
2465:           db.createObjectStore(MSG_STORE_NAME, { keyPath: "key" });
2466:         }
2467:       };
2468:       req.onerror = () => reject(req.error || new Error("IDB open failed"));
2469:       req.onsuccess = () => resolve(req.result);
2470:     });
2471:   }
2472: 
2473:   async function saveMessage(rec) {
2474:     if (!rec || !rec.peer_fp || !rec.id || !rec.ts) {
2475:       throw new Error("message record requires peer_fp, id, ts");
2476:     }
2477:     const db = await _openMessagesDb();
2478:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
2479:       const tx = db.transaction(MSG_STORE_NAME, "readwrite");
2480:       const store = tx.objectStore(MSG_STORE_NAME);
2481:       const row = Object.assign({}, rec, {
2482:         key: _msgKey(rec.peer_fp, rec.ts, rec.id),
2483:       });
2484:       const req = store.put(row);
2485:       req.onerror = () => reject(req.error || new Error("IDB put failed"));
2486:       req.onsuccess = () => resolve(row);
2487:       tx.oncomplete = () => db.close();
2488:     });
2489:   }
2490: 
2491:   async function loadMessages(peerFp, opts) {
2492:     opts = opts || {};
2493:     const limit = Number(opts.limit || 200);
2494:     const db = await _openMessagesDb();
2495:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
2496:       const tx = db.transaction(MSG_STORE_NAME, "readonly");
2497:       const store = tx.objectStore(MSG_STORE_NAME);
2498:       // Range over keys with the peer prefix. The composite-ish key
2499:       // sorts by ts naturally because ts is zero-padded to 15 chars.
2500:       const lower = `${peerFp}::`;
2501:       const upper = `${peerFp}::￿`;
2502:       const range = IDBKeyRange.bound(lower, upper);
2503:       const req = store.openCursor(range, "next");
2504:       const out = [];
2505:       req.onerror = () => reject(req.error || new Error("IDB cursor failed"));
2506:       req.onsuccess = () => {
2507:         const cursor = req.result;
2508:         if (!cursor) {
2509:           resolve(out);
2510:           return;
2511:         }
2512:         out.push(cursor.value);
2513:         if (out.length >= limit) {
2514:           resolve(out);
2515:           return;
2516:         }
2517:         cursor.continue();
2518:       };
2519:       tx.oncomplete = () => db.close();
2520:     });
2521:   }
2522: 
2523:   async function clearMessages(peerFp) {
2524:     const all = await loadMessages(peerFp, { limit: 100_000 });
2525:     if (!all.length) return 0;
2526:     const db = await _openMessagesDb();
2527:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
2528:       const tx = db.transaction(MSG_STORE_NAME, "readwrite");
2529:       const store = tx.objectStore(MSG_STORE_NAME);
2530:       let deleted = 0;
2531:       tx.onerror = () => reject(tx.error || new Error("IDB clear failed"));
2532:       tx.oncomplete = () => { db.close(); resolve(deleted); };
2533:       for (const row of all) {
2534:         store.delete(row.key);
2535:         deleted++;
2536:       }
2537:     });
2538:   }
2539: 
2540:   // ── chat send + receive ────────────────────────────────────────────
2541: 
2542:   async function sendChatMessage(body) {
2543:     const p = state.pairing;
2544:     if (!p || !p.finished || !p.remote_hello) {
2545:       throw new Error("no paired peer on the active connection");
2546:     }
2547:     if (!body || typeof body !== "string") {
2548:       throw new Error("message body required");
2549:     }
2550:     const trimmed = body.trim();
2551:     if (!trimmed) throw new Error("empty message");
2552:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
2553:     if (enc.encode(trimmed).byteLength > MSG_BODY_MAX_BYTES) {
2554:       throw new Error(`message exceeds ${MSG_BODY_MAX_BYTES} bytes`);
2555:     }
2556:     const id = _newMessageId();
2557:     const ts = Date.now();
2558:     const peer_fp = p.remote_hello.fingerprint;
2559:     const wire = {
2560:       v: MSG_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
2561:       t: "text",
2562:       id,
2563:       body: trimmed,
2564:       ts,
2565:     };
2566:     sendControl(p.session, wire);
2567:     const rec = {
2568:       id,
2569:       peer_fp,
2570:       direction: "out",
2571:       body: trimmed,
2572:       ts,
2573:       received_ms: ts,
2574:     };
2575:     await saveMessage(rec);
2576:     return rec;
2577:   }
2578: 
2579:   async function _onChatTextReceived(envelope) {
2580:     const p = state.pairing;
2581:     if (!p || !p.remote_hello) return;
2582:     if (envelope.v !== MSG_PROTOCOL_VERSION) return;
2583:     const id = String(envelope.id || "");
2584:     const body = String(envelope.body || "");
2585:     const ts = Number(envelope.ts || Date.now());
2586:     if (!id || !body) return;
2587:     const enc = new TextEncoder();
2588:     if (enc.encode(body).byteLength > MSG_BODY_MAX_BYTES) return;
2589:     const peer_fp = p.remote_hello.fingerprint;
2590:     const rec = {
2591:       id,
2592:       peer_fp,
2593:       direction: "in",
2594:       body,
2595:       ts,
2596:       received_ms: Date.now(),
2597:     };
2598:     try {
2599:       await saveMessage(rec);
2600:     } catch (e) {
2601:       console.warn("save message failed", e);
2602:     }
2603:     // Send ack back so the sender can mark it delivered.
2604:     try {
2605:       sendControl(p.session, {
2606:         v: MSG_PROTOCOL_VERSION,
2607:         t: "ack",
2608:         id,
2609:         ts: Date.now(),
2610:       });
2611:     } catch {}
2612:     _appendChatBubble(rec);
2613:   }
2614: 
2615:   async function _onChatAckReceived(envelope) {
2616:     const p = state.pairing;
2617:     if (!p || !p.remote_hello) return;
2618:     if (envelope.v !== MSG_PROTOCOL_VERSION) return;
2619:     const id = String(envelope.id || "");
2620:     if (!id) return;
2621:     // Update the existing outgoing record with ack_ms; tolerate
2622:     // missing rows (peer acks something we don't have on disk).
2623:     try {
2624:       const all = await loadMessages(p.remote_hello.fingerprint, { limit: 1000 });
2625:       const target = all.find((r) => r.id === id && r.direction === "out");
2626:       if (!target) return;
2627:       target.ack_ms = Number(envelope.ts || Date.now());
2628:       await saveMessage(target);
2629:       _markBubbleAcked(id);
2630:     } catch {}
2631:   }
2632:

2635:   function _appendChatBubble(rec) {
2636:     const log = $("#chat-log");
2637:     if (!log) return;
2638:     const bubble = document.createElement("div");
2639:     bubble.dataset.msgId = rec.id;
2640:     bubble.style.maxWidth = "85%";
2641:     bubble.style.padding = "8px 12px";
2642:     bubble.style.borderRadius = "12px";
2643:     bubble.style.whiteSpace = "pre-wrap";
2644:     bubble.style.wordBreak = "break-word";
2645:     if (rec.direction === "out") {
2646:       bubble.style.alignSelf = "flex-end";
2647:       bubble.style.background = "var(--accent)";
2648:       bubble.style.color = "white";
2649:     } else {
2650:       bubble.style.alignSelf = "flex-start";
2651:       bubble.style.background = "var(--bg-1)";
2652:       bubble.style.color = "var(--text)";
2653:       bubble.style.border = "1px solid var(--line)";
2654:     }
2655:     const body = document.createElement("div");
2656:     body.textContent = rec.body;
2657:     bubble.appendChild(body);
2658:     const meta = document.createElement("div");
2659:     meta.style.fontSize = "10px";
2660:     meta.style.opacity = "0.6";
2661:     meta.style.marginTop = "4px";
2662:     meta.style.textAlign = rec.direction === "out" ? "right" : "left";
2663:     const timeStr = new Date(rec.ts).toLocaleTimeString();
2664:     if (rec.direction === "out") {
2665:       meta.textContent = rec.ack_ms ? `${timeStr} · delivered` : timeStr;
2666:     } else {
2667:       meta.textContent = timeStr;
2668:     }
2669:     bubble.appendChild(meta);
2670:     log.appendChild(bubble);
2671:     log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight;
2672:   }

2674:   function _markBubbleAcked(id) {
2675:     const log = $("#chat-log");

2678:     if (!bubble) return;
2679:     const meta = bubble.querySelector("div:last-child");
2680:     if (meta && !meta.textContent.includes("delivered")) {
2681:       meta.textContent = `${meta.textContent} · delivered`;
2682:     }
2683:   }

2741:     _origRouteControlMessage(session, kind, data);

2770:   // ── v0.20.1 — auto-pair flow (browser ↔ daemon, no manual UX) ──
2771:   //
2772:   // The phone visits /peer?pair=<token>&fp=<algo>:<hex>&ws=<url>.
2773:   // The page detects the params, hides ALL the manual cards
2774:   // (identity provisioning, rendezvous, manual signaling, SAS),
2775:   // shows a single "Connecting…" status, and runs:
2776:   //
2777:   //   1. Provision identity silently (existing boot path; we just
2778:   //      don't render the identity card).
2779:   //   2. Open a RTCPeerConnection with multi-vendor STUN.
2780:   //   3. Create a control + bulk DataChannel (so the daemon side
2781:   //      can pin the channel labels).
2782:   //   4. createOffer() + setLocalDescription.
2783:   //   5. Build a signed offer envelope:
2784:   //        {v:"OL-PEER-RTC-1", t:"offer", sdp,
2785:   //         pubkey_b64u, fingerprint, pair_token, ts, signature}
2786:   //      Signature = Ed25519 over canonical(envelope minus signature).
2787:   //   6. Open WS to ws=, send envelope.
2788:   //   7. On answer, setRemoteDescription.
2789:   //   8. On control:open, mark this connection as paired with
2790:   //      the daemon's claimed fingerprint, save to OPFS.
2791:   //   9. Status: "Connected". Transition to chat (v0.20.2).
2792:   //
2793:   // Failure modes are surfaced as a single "Couldn't pair: <reason>"
2794:   // line + a Retry button. We do NOT fall back to manual SAS — if
2795:   // the QR pair flow fails, the user picks up their phone and
2796:   // taps Retry; if it still fails, they regenerate the QR on their
2797:   // laptop. Manual SAS is the advanced override path, not the
2798:   // recovery path.
2799: 
2800:   const AUTOPAIR_DAEMON_CONTROL_LABEL = "one-link-daemon-control-v1";
2801:   const AUTOPAIR_DAEMON_BULK_LABEL = "one-link-daemon-bulk-v1";
2802: 
2803:   // v0.20.7 (security audit M9): validate the WS URL the QR
2804:   // wants us to connect to. Without this check, an attacker who
2805:   // crafts (or substitutes) a QR can route a phone's signed
2806:   // pairing offer to an attacker-controlled WS endpoint. The
2807:   // attacker then either replays the captured offer against the
2808:   // real daemon (consuming the single-use token) or drops the
2809:   // offer + serves the phone an unsigned answer trying to steer
2810:   // it onto an attacker-controlled DataChannel.
2811:   //
2812:   // The defense: the QR is supposed to live alongside this page
2813:   // — both are served from the same daemon. So the WS URL's host
2814:   // MUST equal window.location.host. We additionally restrict
2815:   // the scheme to ws/wss so a "javascript:" or "file:" or
2816:   // "http:" URL can't be smuggled through.
2817:   function _isSafePairWsUrl(rawUrl) {
2818:     try {
2819:       const u = new URL(rawUrl);
2820:       if (u.protocol !== "ws:" && u.protocol !== "wss:") return false;
2821:       // host = hostname + (port if non-default). Compare ignoring
2822:       // case + folding default ports.
2823:       if (u.host.toLowerCase() !== window.location.host.toLowerCase()) {
2824:         return false;
2825:       }
2826:       return true;
2827:     } catch {
2828:       return false;
2829:     }
2830:   }
2831: 
2832:   function _detectPairQuery() {
2833:     try {
2834:       const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
2835:       const pair = params.get("pair");
2836:       const fp = params.get("fp");
2837:       const ws = params.get("ws");
2838:       if (!pair || !fp || !ws) return null;
2839:       if (!_isSafePairWsUrl(ws)) return null;
2840:       return { pair_token: pair, daemon_fingerprint: fp, ws_url: ws };
2841:     } catch {
2842:       return null;
2843:     }
2844:   }
2845:

2850:       pill.classList.add(pillKind);

2852:     }
2853:     text($("#autopair-status"), statusLine);
2854:   }

2916:   async function _previewSelfMeshInvite(query) {
2917:     const params = new URLSearchParams();
2918:     params.set("token", query.token);
2919:     if (state.rec && state.rec.public_key_b64u) {
2920:       params.set("device_pub_b64", state.rec.public_key_b64u);
2921:     }
2922:     const resp = await fetch(
2923:       `/api/v1/self-mesh/enrollment-invite/preview?${params.toString()}`,
2924:       { cache: "no-store" },
2925:     );
2926:     const body = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));
2927:     if (!resp.ok) {
2928:       throw new Error(body.hint || body.error || `HTTP ${resp.status}`);
2929:     }
2930:     return body;

2933:   async function _storeSelfMeshInvite(query, preview) {
2934:     if (!state.rec || !state.rec.public_key_b64u) {
2935:       throw new Error("device identity is not loaded");
2936:     }
2937:     if (preview.device_pub_b64 !== state.rec.public_key_b64u) {
2938:       throw new Error("this invite was minted for a different device key");
2939:     }
2940:     const record = {
2941:       v: 1,
2942:       claimed_ms: Date.now(),
2943:       token: query.token,
2944:       root_pub_b64: preview.root_pub_b64,
2945:       device_pub_b64: preview.device_pub_b64,
2946:       device_kind: preview.device_kind,
2947:       label: preview.label || preview.device_kind || "This device",
2948:       fingerprint: state.rec.fingerprint,
2949:     };
2950:     localStorage.setItem(SELF_MESH_CERT_KEY, JSON.stringify(record));
2951:     return record;
2952:   }

2989:           "claimed",
2990:           `${rec.label} is now trusted under this root identity.`,
2991:         );
2992:         hide($("#selfmesh-enroll-actions"));
2993:       } catch (e) {
2994:         _selfMeshEnrollSetState(
2995:           "bad",
2996:           "failed",

2998:         );
2999:       }
3000:     }, { once: true });

3031:       const record = {

3051:       _selfMeshEnrollSetState(

3054:         body.pending
3055:           ? `Check this code on the other device: ${body.trust_code || ""}`
3056:           : `${record.label} is now part of your One identity.`,
3057:       );
3058:     } catch (e) {
3059:       _selfMeshEnrollSetState(
3060:         "bad",
3061:         "failed",
3062:         `Couldn't add this device: ${e && e.message ? e.message : e}`,
3063:       );

3067:   async function _waitForIdentity(maxMs) {
3068:     const deadline = Date.now() + (maxMs || 8000);
3069:     while (Date.now() < deadline) {
3070:       if (state.rec) return state.rec;
3071:       // v0.20.4: if boot already failed, abort the wait early
3072:       // and let the caller surface the real error.
3073:       if (state.boot_error_msg) return null;
3074:       await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 80));
3075:     }
3076:     return state.rec || null;
3077:   }
3078: 
3079:   // v0.20.4 — preflight checks. Returns null if all good, or an
3080:   // {pill, status} object describing the specific failure mode.
3081:   // Most-common failure: insecure context. iOS Safari + most other
3082:   // browsers gate Web Crypto Subtle to HTTPS or localhost; a phone
3083:   // hitting http://<lan-ip>/peer can't generate Ed25519 keys at
3084:   // all. The QR generated by v0.20.4+ daemons is https://, so this
3085:   // should normally pass — but if the user got an http:// QR from
3086:   // an older daemon or hand-typed the URL, we surface the real
3087:   // reason instead of the generic "no identity" mystery.
3088:   function _autopairPreflight() {
3089:     if (!window.isSecureContext) {
3090:       return {
3091:         pill: "insecure",
3092:         status:
3093:           "This page is loaded over plain HTTP. Browsers block Web Crypto on " +
3094:           "non-HTTPS LAN addresses, so identity generation can't run. Reopen " +
3095:           "the QR on your laptop to get an https:// link, or open this on " +
3096:           "the laptop's localhost.",
3097:       };
3098:     }
3099:     if (!window.crypto || !crypto.subtle || !crypto.subtle.generateKey) {
3100:       return {
3101:         pill: "no web crypto",
3102:         status:
3103:           "Your browser doesn't expose Web Crypto. Try Chrome 113+, Edge 113+, " +
3104:           "Safari 17+, or Firefox 130+.",
3105:       };
3106:     }
3107:     if (!navigator.storage || !navigator.storage.getDirectory) {
3108:       return {
3109:         pill: "no opfs",
3110:         status:
3111:           "Your browser doesn't expose OPFS. The phone-as-peer architecture " +
3112:           "needs persistent origin-private storage. Try Chrome 86+, Safari " +
3113:           "15.2+, or Firefox 111+.",
3114:       };
3115:     }
3116:     return null;
3117:   }

3208:       // response routing and pull down the chat roster.
3209:       _registerDaemonDc(controlDc, pair.daemon_fingerprint);
3210:       try {

3222:     pc.onconnectionstatechange = () => {
3223:       if (pc.connectionState === "failed" || pc.connectionState === "closed") {
3224:         if (!dataChannelOpened) {

3250:     // complete offer (better LAN handshake reliability than

3252:     await new Promise((resolve) => {
3253:       if (pc.iceGatheringState === "complete") {
3254:         resolve();

3258:         if (pc.iceGatheringState === "complete") {

3260:           resolve();

3269:       v: "OL-PEER-RTC-1",
3270:       t: "offer",

3300:       );

3305:       try {

3324:       try { msg = JSON.parse(event.data); } catch { return; }

3330:           // See _verifySignedDaemonAnswer for the full rationale.
3331:           await _verifySignedDaemonAnswer(msg, pair.daemon_fingerprint);

3336:           state._pendingDaemonPubkey = msg.daemon_pubkey_b64u || "";

3368:   // ── v0.20.2 — daemon DataChannel router + roster + chat ───────────
3369:   //
3370:   // Once the auto-pair flow's controlDc opens, we register it as the
3371:   // live transport to the daemon. From there:
3372:   //
3373:   //   - Outgoing requests use _daemonRequest("fetch_peers", {})
3374:   //     which assigns a fresh rid (uuid), sends the envelope, and
3375:   //     returns a Promise that resolves on the matching response or
3376:   //     rejects on timeout (10s) / channel close.
3377:   //
3378:   //   - Incoming frames hit _routeDaemonDcMessage, which looks up
3379:   //     the pending Promise by rid and resolves/rejects it.
3380:   //
3381:   //   - The roster + chat UI build on top: _refreshDaemonRoster
3382:   //     fetches fetch_peers, renders rows. Tap a row → fetch_messages
3383:   //     for that peer → render the chat view.
3384:   //
3385:   // Browser-to-browser chat (v0.19.2) and browser-to-daemon chat are
3386:   // independent surfaces — different cards, different wires. v0.19.2's
3387:   // pairing/chat lives on the v0.18.0 control DataChannel between two
3388:   // browsers; v0.20.2's daemon-roster lives on the v0.20.0 daemon
3389:   // control DataChannel. They never collide.
3390: 
3391:   state.daemon_dc = null;
3392:   state.daemon_dc_fingerprint = null;
3393:   state.daemon_pending = new Map();   // rid → {resolve, reject, timer}
3394:   state.daemon_active_peer = null;     // currently-selected peer in the chat view
3395: 
3396:   const DAEMON_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;
3397: 
3398:   function _genRid() {
3399:     if (window.crypto && crypto.randomUUID) return crypto.randomUUID();
3400:     return bytesToB64Url(_randomBytes(16));
3401:   }
3402: 
3403:   function _registerDaemonDc(dc, daemonFingerprint) {
3404:     state.daemon_dc = dc;
3405:     state.daemon_dc_fingerprint = daemonFingerprint;
3406:     dc.addEventListener("close", () => {
3407:       state.daemon_dc = null;
3408:       // Fail any in-flight requests.
3409:       for (const [, pending] of state.daemon_pending) {
3410:         clearTimeout(pending.timer);
3411:         pending.reject(new Error("daemon channel closed"));
3412:       }
3413:       state.daemon_pending.clear();
3414:     });
3415:   }
3416: 
3417:   function _routeDaemonDcMessage(raw) {
3418:     let msg;
3419:     try {
3420:       msg = typeof raw === "string" ? JSON.parse(raw) : null;
3421:     } catch { return; }
3422:     if (!msg || msg.v !== "OL-PEER-1") return;
3423:     // First, route to the existing browser-to-browser handlers
3424:     // (pair/chat) — they're idempotent on non-matching version
3425:     // tags but we still want to keep them wired for the case where
3426:     // a browser-peer ALSO connects to this same page. In practice
3427:     // a phone in pair-by-QR mode talks only to the daemon, but we
3428:     // don't want to lose any v0.19.x dispatch coverage.
3429:     const rid = msg.rid || "";
3430:     if (rid && state.daemon_pending.has(rid)) {
3431:       const pending = state.daemon_pending.get(rid);
3432:       state.daemon_pending.delete(rid);
3433:       clearTimeout(pending.timer);
3434:       if (msg.t === "error") {
3435:         pending.reject(new Error(msg.message || msg.code || "daemon error"));
3436:       } else {
3437:         pending.resolve(msg);
3438:       }
3439:     }
3440:   }
3441: 
3442:   function _daemonRequest(t, params, opts) {
3443:     const dc = state.daemon_dc;
3444:     if (!dc || dc.readyState !== "open") {
3445:       return Promise.reject(new Error("no live daemon channel"));
3446:     }
3447:     const rid = _genRid();
3448:     const envelope = Object.assign(
3449:       { v: "OL-PEER-1", t, rid },
3450:       params || {},
3451:     );
3452:     const timeoutMs = (opts && opts.timeoutMs) || DAEMON_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS;
3453:     return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
3454:       const timer = setTimeout(() => {
3455:         if (state.daemon_pending.has(rid)) {
3456:           state.daemon_pending.delete(rid);
3457:           reject(new Error(`${t} timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`));
3458:         }
3459:       }, timeoutMs);
3460:       state.daemon_pending.set(rid, { resolve, reject, timer });
3461:       try {
3462:         dc.send(JSON.stringify(envelope));
3463:       } catch (e) {
3464:         state.daemon_pending.delete(rid);
3465:         clearTimeout(timer);
3466:         reject(e);
3467:       }
3468:     });
3469:   }

3641:   // Wrap createOfferSignal + acceptOfferSignal so they install our

 101: // ── Background sync (outbox) ──────────────────────────────────────
 102: //
 103: // When the user composes a message while offline OR the tab gets
 104: // suspended mid-send, we save the payload into IndexedDB and
 105: // register `sync.register("ol-outbox")`. The browser fires the sync
 106: // event when connectivity comes back; we drain the IDB queue.
 107: //
 108: // IDB is used instead of localStorage because:
 109: //   1. localStorage isn't available in service worker scope
 110: //   2. IDB has a richer API for queue semantics
 111: //   3. We can store binary payloads if we ever queue files
 112: const IDB_NAME = "one-link-outbox-v1";
 113: const IDB_STORE = "queue";
 114: 
 115: function openOutboxDB() {
 116:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
 117:     const req = indexedDB.open(IDB_NAME, 1);
 118:     req.onupgradeneeded = () => {
 119:       const db = req.result;
 120:       if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(IDB_STORE)) {
 121:         db.createObjectStore(IDB_STORE, { keyPath: "id", autoIncrement: true });
 122:       }
 123:     };
 124:     req.onsuccess = () => resolve(req.result);
 125:     req.onerror = () => reject(req.error);
 126:   });
 127: }
 128: 
 129: async function drainOutbox() {
 130:   let db;
 131:   try {
 132:     db = await openOutboxDB();
 133:   } catch {
 134:     return; // IDB unavailable; nothing to drain
 135:   }
 136:   const tx = db.transaction(IDB_STORE, "readwrite");
 137:   const store = tx.objectStore(IDB_STORE);
 138:   const allReq = store.getAll();
 139:   await new Promise((res, rej) => {
 140:     allReq.onsuccess = () => res(); allReq.onerror = () => rej(allReq.error);
 141:   });
 142:   const items = allReq.result || [];
 143:   for (const item of items) {
 144:     try {
 145:       const resp = await fetch(item.url, {
 146:         method: item.method || "POST",
 147:         headers: item.headers || { "content-type": "application/json" },
 148:         body: item.body,
 149:         credentials: "include",
 150:       });
 151:       if (resp.ok) {
 152:         store.delete(item.id);
 153:       }
 154:       // On non-2xx, leave it in the queue; the browser will retry
 155:       // the sync event later (or we drain on next activate).
 156:     } catch {
 157:       // Network still down; bail and let the browser retry.
 158:       return;
 159:     }
 160:   }
 161: }

 164:   if (event.tag === "ol-outbox") {
 165:     event.waitUntil(drainOutbox());
 166:   }

   1: """Wire protocol: length-prefixed binary frames + JSON message envelopes.
   2: 
   3: Frame format on the wire:
   4:     [4-byte big-endian length N] [N bytes payload]
   5: 
   6: Frames carry one of two payload kinds:
   7:     - handshake: raw bytes (HELLO/CHALLENGE/AUTH binary blobs, see channel.py)
   8:     - encrypted: ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext containing a JSON message
   9: 
  10: Inside an encrypted frame, the plaintext is a JSON object:
  11:     {"t": "<type>", "id": "<msg_id>", "ts": <unix_ms>, "from": "<short_id>", ...}
  12: 
  13: Message types (t):
  14:     TEXT       — chat message; "body": str
  15:     FILE_OFFER — sender announces a file; "name": str, "size": int, "blob": <hex sha256>
  16:     FILE_CHUNK — file content; "blob": <hex>, "seq": int, "data": <base64>, "eof": bool
  17:     ACK        — acknowledgement; "of": <msg_id>
  18:     PING       — keepalive
  19:     PONG       — keepalive reply
  20: """
  21: 
  22: from __future__ import annotations
  23: 
  24: import asyncio
  25: import json
  26: import time
  27: import uuid
  28: from typing import Any
  29: 
  30: MAX_FRAME = 16 * 1024 * 1024  # 16 MiB hard cap per frame; chunked above this
  31: 
  32: # v0.20.7 (security audit M7): cap JSON nesting on encrypted-frame
  33: # plaintexts. Without this, a malicious peer can ship `{"a":{"a":...}}`
  34: # nested 1000+ levels deep and drive CPython's recursive json
  35: # decoder into RecursionError. The receive loop catches that as a
  36: # generic Exception and closes the channel — annoying but bounded;
  37: # combined with slowloris-style pinning it becomes a cheap log-spam
  38: # / fd-churn primitive. 64 levels is well beyond any legitimate
  39: # One Link payload (the deepest live shape today is ~6 levels) and
  40: # below the CPython recursion floor with comfortable headroom.
  41: MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 64
  42: 
  43: 
  44: def _check_json_depth(data: bytes, max_depth: int = MAX_JSON_DEPTH) -> None:
  45:     """Pre-scan the JSON byte string for max nesting depth. Raise
  46:     ValueError if the max-nesting peak exceeds ``max_depth``. Honors
  47:     string boundaries so `{` inside a string literal does not count.
  48: 
  49:     Doing this BEFORE json.loads avoids the cost of full parsing for
  50:     obviously-malicious inputs and avoids tripping CPython's
  51:     recursion limit on the critical decode path."""
  52:     depth = 0
  53:     in_string = False
  54:     escape = False
  55:     for c in data:
  56:         if escape:
  57:             escape = False
  58:             continue
  59:         if in_string:
  60:             if c == 0x5c:  # backslash
  61:                 escape = True
  62:                 continue
  63:             if c == 0x22:  # closing quote
  64:                 in_string = False
  65:             continue
  66:         if c == 0x22:  # opening quote
  67:             in_string = True
  68:             continue
  69:         if c == 0x7b or c == 0x5b:  # { or [
  70:             depth += 1
  71:             if depth > max_depth:
  72:                 raise ValueError(
  73:                     f"JSON nesting too deep (>{max_depth}) — frame rejected"
  74:                 )
  75:         elif c == 0x7d or c == 0x5d:  # } or ]
  76:             if depth > 0:
  77:                 depth -= 1
  78: 
  79: 
  80: async def read_frame(reader: asyncio.StreamReader) -> bytes:
  81:     header = await reader.readexactly(4)
  82:     n = int.from_bytes(header, "big")
  83:     if n > MAX_FRAME:
  84:         raise ValueError(f"frame too large: {n} > {MAX_FRAME}")
  85:     return await reader.readexactly(n)
  86: 
  87: 
  88: def write_frame_nowait(writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, payload: bytes) -> None:
  89:     if len(payload) > MAX_FRAME:
  90:         raise ValueError(f"payload too large: {len(payload)} > {MAX_FRAME}")
  91:     writer.write(len(payload).to_bytes(4, "big") + payload)
  92: 
  93: 
  94: async def write_frame(writer: asyncio.StreamWriter, payload: bytes) -> None:
  95:     write_frame_nowait(writer, payload)
  96:     await writer.drain()
  97: 
  98: 
  99: def now_ms() -> int:
 100:     return int(time.time() * 1000)
 101: 
 102: 
 103: def new_msg_id() -> str:
 104:     return uuid.uuid4().hex
 105: 
 106: 
 107: def make_msg(t: str, sender_short_id: str, **fields: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
 108:     msg: dict[str, Any] = {
 109:         "t": t,
 110:         "id": new_msg_id(),
 111:         "ts": now_ms(),
 112:         "from": sender_short_id,
 113:     }
 114:     msg.update(fields)
 115:     return msg
 116: 
 117: 
 118: def encode_msg(msg: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
 119:     return json.dumps(msg, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
 120: 
 121: 
 122: def decode_msg(data: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]:
 123:     # v0.20.7 (security audit M7 + L3): bound JSON nesting before
 124:     # json.loads runs, then enforce that the top-level value is an
 125:     # object. Old behavior accepted JSON null / array / string and
 126:     # downstream `msg.get("t")` raised AttributeError or TypeError,
 127:     # which the recv loop swallowed and closed the channel —
 128:     # functional but log-noisy and cheap to drive.
 129:     _check_json_depth(data)
 130:     out = json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"))
 131:     if not isinstance(out, dict):
 132:         raise ValueError("frame must be a JSON object")
 133:     return out
<<<CONTENT_END>>>
